vt: In the beginning God created heaven and earth.
The earth was void and without form, darkness covered the face of the deep, and God's Spirit moved over the waters.
And God said, "Let there be light," and there was light.
God saw that the light was good, and he separated the light from the darkness.
God called the light day, and he called the darkness night, and that morning and that evening was the first day.
And God said, "Let there be a firmament in the middle of the waters, and it will divide the waters from the waters."
Then God made the firmament and divided the waters under the firmament from the waters above the firmament, and it was so.
God called the firmament heaven, and that morning and that evening was the second day.
And God said, "Let the waters under heaven be gathered together into one place and let the dry land appear," and it was so.
Then God named the dry land earth, and he named the waters the seas, and God saw that it was good.
And God said, "Let the earth bring forth every kind of seed-bearing plant, including grass, herbs, and fruit trees, each with their own kind of seed," and it was so.
And the earth brought forth all the seed bearing plants, including every kind of grass, herb, and fruit tree that there was, and God saw that it was good.
And that morning and that evening was the third day.
And God said, "Let there be lights in the heavens to divide the day from the night and let them be a sign for the seasons, to separate the days, months, and years.
Let the lights in the heavens give light on the earth," and it was so.
Then God made two great lights, the sun to rule the day, and the moon and stars to rule the night.
God placed the lights in the heavens to give light to the earth.
And to divide the light from the darkness and rule over the days and nights, and God saw that it was good.
And that morning and that evening was the fourth day.
And God said, "Let the waters bring forth abundant life with living creatures that move and birds that fly in the heavens above the earth."

Then God created an abundance of great whales and every kind of living moving creature that lived in the waters, plus every type of winged bird that flew above the earth, and God saw that it was good.
And God blessed them and said, "Be fruitful, multiply, and fill the waters of the seas with abundant life and let the birds multiply abundantly upon the earth."
And that morning and that evening was the fifth day.
And God said, "Let the earth bring forth every kind of living creature including cattle, animals, reptiles, and every other living thing on earth," and it was so.
God created animals of every kind, including cattle, reptiles, and every other living thing on the earth, and God saw that it was good.
And God said, "Let us make man in our image, a man who looks like us, and man will preserve and control all the fish, birds, cattle, reptiles, and every other living thing on earth."
So God created man in his image, both male and female.
Then God blessed them and said, "Be fruitful, multiply, and replenish the earth; Take control of the fish, birds, and every other living thing on earth."
And God said, "Behold, I have given you every green herb and every fruit tree on the earth that produces seed for you to eat.
I have given you every living thing on the earth, including every beast and bird, the reptiles, green herbs for food, and every other living thing on the earth," and it was so.
And God saw that everything he had created was very good, and that morning and that evening was the sixth day.
Then all of creation including heaven and earth was finished.
On the seventh day, God finished creating everything, and he rested from all the work that he had done.
God blessed and sanctified the seventh day because he rested on the seventh day.
This is the story of the history of the day that the Lord God created heaven and earth.
No plants had sprouted in the field because the Lord God had not yet brought the rains on the earth, and there were no men to til the ground.
God created a mist that went up from the earth and watered all the land on the face of the earth.
God created man from the dust on the ground, and he breathed the breath of life into his nostrils, and man became a living soul.
God planted a garden in the eastern part of Eden, and that's where he put the man he had created.
God made the pleasant looking living trees, and he made plants that were good for food. Then he put the 'Tree of Life', and the 'Tree of the Knowledge of Good and Evil', in the middle of the garden.
A river flowed from Eden to water the garden, and it was parted into four headwaters from the garden.
The first river was named Pishon, and it flowed around Havilah which is the land of gold.
The land there has an abundance of gold, and it also has precious stones including bdellium and onyx.
The name of the second river was Gihon which surrounds the land of Ethiopia.
The third river was named Hiddekel, and it flows east of Assyria. And the fourth river was named Euphrates.
The Lord God put man in the garden of Eden to care for and protect it.
And the Lord God said to the man, "You may eat freely from every tree in the garden.
But do not eat from the 'Tree of the Knowledge of Good and Evil,' because if you eat from it, you will surely die."
And God said, "It is not good for man to be alone, so I will make a companion for him."

And God gave everything he had made from the ground to Adam, including all the field animals and birds, because he wanted to see what Adam would name each living creature. Then Adam gave them all names.
Adam named all the cattle, all the birds of the air, and every field animal, but he had no companion.
So God put Adam into a deep sleep, and while he was sleeping, God took a rib from his body and closed the wound.
God took the rib he had taken from Adam and used it to make a woman then he brought her to Adam.
And Adam said, "This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh, she will be called Woman because she was taken out of Man."
That's why a man will leave his father and his mother and bond with his wife, and they will become one flesh.
The man and his wife were both naked, but they were not ashamed.
Now the serpent was more subtle and crafty than any of the field beasts that God had made, and one day he said to the woman, "Are you not allowed to eat from every tree in the garden?"
And the woman said, "We are allowed to eat the fruit from the trees in the garden.
But God told us not to touch or eat the fruit from the tree in the middle of the garden, because we will die if we do."
And the serpent said, "You will not die!

Because God knows, that when you eat the fruit from the tree in the middle of the garden, your eyes will be opened, and you will be like one of the gods, and you will know the difference between good and evil."

When the woman saw that the tree was pleasant to look at and the fruit looked like it was good for food, and she thought it was a tree that would make one wise, she ate its fruit. Then she gave some to her husband and he ate it too.
Immediately both of their eyes were opened, and they realized that they were naked, so they sewed fig leaves together and made aprons to cover themselves.
They heard God's voice while he was walking in the garden during the cool of the day, and they hid behind the trees in the garden.
And God called out to them and asked, "Where are you, Adam?"
And Adam said, "I heard your voice in the garden, and I was afraid because I was naked, so I hid from you."
And God said, "Who told you that you were naked? Did you eat fruit from the tree, that I told you not to eat from?"
And Adam said, "Eve gave me fruit from the tree and I ate it."
And the Lord said to the woman, "What have you done?" And the woman said, "The serpent deceived me and I ate it."
And God said to the serpent, "Because you have done this, you are more cursed than all the cattle and field animals, and you will crawl on your belly and eat dust all the days of your life.
I will also put hostility between you and the woman, between your seed and her seed, it will bruise your head, and you will bruise his heel."
And God said to the woman, "I will greatly multiply your sorrow during childbirth, you will desire your husband, and he will rule over you, but you will bear your children in sorrow"
And he said to Adam, "Because you listened to the woman and ate from the tree I told you not to eat from, the ground will be cursed, and you will eat sorrow from it all the days of your life.
It will bring you thorns and thistles, and you will eat herbs from the field.
Your face will be covered with sweat from the work you do making bread until you return to the ground. Because you were created from dust, so dust you are and to dust you will return!"
Adam named his wife Eve because she was the mother of every living thing.
Then God made leather coats for Adam and Eve to clothe them.

And God said, "Behold, the man has become like us, he knows the difference between good and evil, and he will be banished from the 'Garden of Eden' to prevent him from taking from the Tree of Life and living forever."
That's why the Lord God sent them out of the Garden of Eden and made man till the ground that he came from.
So he drove the man out of the garden, and on the east side of the Garden of Eden he placed Cherubim and a flaming sword that turned every which way, to guard the way to the Tree of Life.
Adam loved his wife Eve, then she conceived and gave birth to Cain and she said, "The Lord has given me a man."
Then she gave birth to Cain's brother Abel who became a shepherd, but Cain was a farmer and he tilled the ground.
Over time Cain labored over the ground and brought the fruits of his labor as an offering to the Lord.
Abel brought the fat and the best of his firstborn from his flocks to the Lord, and the Lord was very happy with Abel's offering.
But God did not respect Cain's offering, and that made Cain so angry that the look on his face soured.
And the Lord said to Cain, "Why are you so angry, and why has the expression on your face fallen?
If you are righteous your offering will be accepted, and if you are not righteous sin lies at the door. And you will be his desire, but you will rule over him."
Later Cain was talking to his brother Abel, and they went out to the field together, then Cain attacked his brother and killed him.
And the Lord said to Cain, "Where is your brother Abel?" Cain answered and said, "How should I know, am I my brother's keeper?"
And God said, "What have you done? The voice of your brother's blood cries out to me from the ground.
Because you killed Abel you are cursed; the earth has opened her mouth and swallowed his blood?
From now on, when you till the ground, the earth will produce no food for you. You will be a fugitive and a vagabond, and your days will be spent wandering the earth."
And Cain said to the Lord, "My punishment is greater than I can bear.
You have driven me out of the land, and you will no longer allow me in your presence. I will be a fugitive and a vagabond, and someday, somebody will kill me."
And the Lord said to Cain, "If anyone kills you, you will be avenged seven times." And the Lord God placed a mark on Cain to prevent anyone who finds him from killing him.
So, Cain left God's presence and lived in the land of Nod, which was east of Eden.
Cain loved his wife, and she conceived and gave birth to a son that she named Enoch. Then Cain built a city and named it after Enoch.
Enoch fathered a son named Irad, Irad fathered Mehujael, Mehujael fathered Methusael, and Methusael fathered Lamech.
Lamech married two wives, one was named Adah and the other was named Zillah.
Adah gave birth to Jabal, Jabal was the father of nomads who raised cattle and lived in tents.
Jabal's brother was named Jubal, Jubal was the father of musicians who played the harp and organ.
Zillah gave birth to Tubal-Cain and his sister Naamah, he was an instructor and taught craftsmen how to work with brass and iron.
One day Lamech spoke to his wives Adah and Zillah and said, "Listen to me, I was wounded by a young man who tried to kill me, so I had to kill him.
If God will avenge Cain's death seven times, surely I will be avenged seventy-seven times."
Then Adam loved his wife again and she gave him another son whom she named Seth. She said God had given her another son to replace her dead son Abel because Cain killed him.
Seth fathered a son that he named Enos, and that's when men began to call on the name of the Lord.
God created man in his likeness, and this is the history of Adam's descendants.
God created males and females, he blessed them and called them Adam on the day that he created them.
Adam fathered a son he named Seth when he was 130 years old, and Seth looked just like his father.
Adam lived for eight hundred years after he fathered Seth, and he fathered other sons and daughters.
Adam was 930 years old when he died.
Seth was 105 years old when his son Enos was born.
Seth lived another 807 years after his son Enos was born, and he had many other sons and daughters.
Seth was 912 years old when he died.
Enos was ninety years old when he fathered Cainan.
Enos lived another 815 years after his son Cainan was born, and he had many other sons and daughters.
Enos was 905 years old when he died.
Cainan was seventy years old when he fathered Mahalalel.
Cainan lived another 840 years after his son Mahalalel was born, and he had many other sons and daughters.
Cainan was 910 years old when he died.
Mahalaleel was 65 years old when his son Jared was born.
Mahalaleel lived another 830 years after his son Jared was born, and he had other sons and daughters.
Mahalaleel was 895 years old when he died.
Jared was 162 years old when his son Enoch was born.
Jared lived another 800 years after his son Enoch was born, and he had other sons and daughters.
Jared was 962 years old when he died.
Enoch was 65 years old when his son Methuselah was born.
Enoch walked with God for 300 years after his son Methuselah was born, and he had other sons and daughters.
Enoch lived for another 365 years.
Enoch walked with God and was not seen again after that, because God took him.
Methuselah was 187 years old when his son Lamech was born.
Methuselah lived another 782 years after his son Lamech was born, and he fathered other sons and daughters.
Methuselah was 969 years old when he died.
Lamech was 182 years old when he had a son.
When Lamech named his son Noah he said, "Noah will comfort us from all the hard work and labor we must do with our hands because the Lord has cursed the ground."
Lamech lived for 595 years after his son Noah was born, and he fathered other sons and daughters.
Lamech was 777 years old when he died.
Noah was 500 years old when his sons Shem, Ham, and Japheth were born.
At that time the men on earth began to multiply and they fathered many daughters.
God's sons saw that the men's daughters were beautiful and they chose them for their wives.
And the Lord said, "My spirit will not contend with man forever because he is made of flesh and he will only live to be about 120 years old."
In those days and later on there were giants on the earth, and when men's daughters began to bear children to God's sons, their sons became the famous mighty men of old.
God saw that man's wickedness on the earth was great and his mind constantly imagined evil thoughts in his heart.
The Good Lord's heart was grieved, and he regretted that he had created man on the earth.

And the Lord said, "I created man and I will destroy him and wipe him off the face of the earth. I will destroy the men, animals, all the reptiles, and the birds of the air because I regret ever creating them."
But Noah found grace in the eyes of the Lord.
This is the story of Noah and his descendants. During this time Noah walked with God, and he was a perfectly sinless and righteous man.
Noah fathered three sons, Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
But God saw that the earth was filled with corruption and violence.
And God saw that the earth and all the flesh on earth had become corrupt.
So God said to Noah, "I have seen the end of all flesh because they have filled the earth with violence, that's why I will destroy them and the earth.
Make an ark of gopher wood, then make some rooms in the ark and cover it with pitch inside and out.
The ark must be 300 cubits long, 50 cubits wide, and 30 cubits high.
Build a window one cubit below the roof with a door beside the window, the ark must be three stories tall, with first, second, and third floors.
Behold, I will destroy all life on the earth under heaven, I will flood the earth with water and destroy everything alive. Then all life including every breathing thing will die.
But I will make a covenant with you, and I want you to take your sons, your wife, and your son's wives into the ark.
They will be kept alive, and I want you to take two of every living thing, both male and female into the ark with you.
Take every kind of bird, cattle, and two of every creeping thing on earth will come to you to be saved.
Then gather all the food that you will need for you and everything else to eat."
So Noah did what God told him to do.
And the Lord spoke to Noah and said, "I have seen righteousness in you and your family, so I want you to move into the ark along with everyone in your household.
Take seven males and seven females of every kind of clean animal, and two males and two females of every kind of unclean animal into the ark.
Take seven male and seven female birds of every kind, and they will keep the earth's seeds alive.
In seven days it will begin to rain, and it will rain for forty days and forty nights, and every living thing that I made on the earth will be destroyed."
So Noah did everything that the Lord commanded him to do.
Noah was 600 years old when the earth was flooded.
When the flood began and the rains started, Noah took his wife, his sons and their wives into the ark with him.
He took the clean beasts, the unclean beasts, the birds, and every living thing that creeps on the earth into the ark with them.
Noah took two males and two females of each kind into the ark with him, just as God told him to.
After seven days, the flood waters began to cover the earth.
On the seventeenth day of the second month of the 600th year of Noah's life, God opened heaven's fountains and the heavy rains began to fall.
It rained for forty days and forty nights on the earth.
On the day it started raining, Noah took his wife and his sons Shem, Ham, Japheth, and their wives into the ark with him.
He took every kind of animal, every kind of cattle, every living thing on earth that creeps, and every sort of bird of every kind into the ark with him.
Noah brought them all into the ark including two males and two females of every living breathing thing on earth.
Noah brought all the males and females of every living thing into the ark as the Lord God had told him to, then he closed the door.
The flood lasted for forty days and forty nights, the rain raised the ark high above the earth, and it floated on top of the waters.
The waters on the earth increased dramatically and the ark floated on top of the waters.
The waters covered all the hills on the earth under the heavens.
The waters were fifteen cubits higher than the mountains.
Every living thing on the earth died, including men, birds, cattle, animals, and every living thing on earth that creeps.
Everything with the breath of life living on dry land died.
Everything living on the earth was destroyed including men, cattle, things that creep, and the birds of the heavens were all destroyed. Noah and everyone with him were the only ones to survive.
The earth was flooded for 150 days.
Then God remembered Noah and everything still living in the ark including the cattle. So, God made the winds blow over the earth to evaporate the flood waters.
The flood waters stopped, the windows of heaven closed and the rains were restrained.
The waters began to recede from the earth after 150 days.
On the seventeenth day of the seventh month, the ark came to rest on top of Mount Ararat.
The water continued to recede for ten months, and on the first day of the tenth month they could see the mountain tops.
After forty days, Noah opened the ark's window.
Noah sent out a raven that flew back and forth until all the waters on earth dried up.
He also sent out a dove to see if the waters had receded from the ground.
But the dove found nowhere to rest because the waters still covered the earth, and she returned to the ark. She landed on Noah's arm, and he brought her back into the ark.
So Noah waited another seven days and sent the dove out again.
The dove came back in the evening with an olive branch in her beak, that's when Noah knew that the waters were receding from the earth.
Noah stayed in the ark for seven more days and sent the dove out again, this time she did not return.
On the first day of the first month of the 601st year, Noah removed the ark's covering and saw that the water was gone and the ground was dry.
On the 27th day of the second month the earth was completely dry.
Then God spoke to Noah.
And God said, "Leave the ark and take your wife, your sons, and their wives with you.
Bring every living thing out of the ark including the birds, cattle, and every living thing that creeps so that they can breed, be fruitful, and multiply abundantly on the earth."
Noah left the ark with his wife and sons and their wives.
Every animal and everything that creeps on the earth including the birds and every other living thing of its own kind left the ark.
Then Noah built an altar and offered some of his clean beasts and birds as a burnt offering to the Lord on the altar.

The Lord smelled a sweet savory aroma and he said to himself, "I will never curse the earth again, and even though man's heart even from his youth is full of evil imaginations, I will never again destroy every living thing.
As long as the earth exists the time to plant, the time to harvest and the hot weather, cold weather, summer, spring, winter, and fall days and nights will never end."
God blessed Noah and his sons, and told them "Be fruitful, multiply, and replenish the earth.
I have given you every animal, every bird in the air, all the fish of the sea, and everything that moves on the earth. They will all be delivered into your hands, and they will dread and fear you.
I have given you every living thing on the earth that lives and moves for food, and the green herbs will also be your food.
But do not eat meat that has not had its blood drained from it.
I will require the life of anyone who kills or spills your lifeblood, whether it is spilled by someone's brother, another person, or an animal.
Since man was made in God's image, anyone who sheds a person's blood must forfeit their own blood to someone else.
You will be fruitful and bring forth life and multiply abundantly on the earth."
Then God spoke to Noah and his sons.
And God said, "I will establish my covenant with you and your descendants.
My covenant will be with you and every living creature on earth including the birds, cattle, every animal in the ark, and every other animal on earth.
I will establish my covenant with you, and I will never destroy every living thing with flood waters, and there will never again be a flood that destroys all life on earth."
And God said, "This is a token of my covenant with you and every living creature that lives on the earth. This covenant is with you, and your endless generations of descendants.
You will see my rainbow in the clouds, and it will be a token of the covenant between me and the earth.
You will see a rainbow in the clouds when I cover the earth with clouds.
Then, I will remember my covenant with you and all the living creatures, and the flood waters will never again destroy all life on earth.
The rainbow will shine in the clouds and when I see it, I will remember the everlasting covenant between me and every living creature on the earth."
And God said to Noah, "The rainbow is a token of the covenant that I have established between me and every living thing on the earth."
So Noah and his sons Shem, Japheth, and Canaan's father Ham left the ark.
Then Noah's three sons spread out all over the earth.
Noah became a shepherd and planted a vineyard.
One night Noah got drunk on wine and he was lying naked in his tent.
Canaan's father Ham, saw that his father Noah was naked, and he told his brothers about it.
So Shem and Japheth covered themselves with a blanket and walked backwards into the tent so they would not see their father's nakedness, and they covered their naked father.
Noah was sober by the time he woke up, and he knew what his youngest son had done.
Then Noah said, "Canaan is cursed and he will be a servant to his brothers' servants."
Furthermore Noah said, "May the Lord God bless Shem, but Canaan will be his servant.
God will enlarge Japheth and he will live in Shem's tents, and Canaan will be his servant."
Noah lived for another 350 years after the flood.
And Noah was 950 years old when he died.
This is the history of Noah's sons Shem, Ham, Japheth, and their descendants who were born after the flood.
Japheth's sons were Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras.
Gomer's sons were Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah.
Javan's sons were Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim.
Their islands were divided by language, lands, nations, and their families.
Ham's sons were Cush, Mizraim, Phut, and Canaan.
Cush's sons were Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah, Sabtechah, Raamah, Sheba, and Dedan.
Cush was Nimrod's father, who became a mighty one on earth.
Nimrod was a mighty hunter and people say that he is a mighty hunter before the Lord.
His kingdom began in the land of Shinar with Babel, Erech, Accad, and Calneh.
Assyria left that land and built the cities of Nineveh, Rehoboth, and Calah.
And the great city of Resen between Nineveh and Calah.
Mizraim's sons were Ludim, Anamim, Lehabim, and Naphtuhim.
And Pathrusim, Casluhim, who fathered Philistim and Caphtorim.
When Canaan went to Heth he named his firstborn son Sidon.
The families of the Jebusites, the Amorites, and the Girgashites.
And the Hivites, the Arkites, and the Sinites.
And the Arvadites, Zemarites, and the Hamathites were the families of Canaanites who were later spread abroad.
The Canaanite border stretched from Sidon near Gerar, to Gaza, towards Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, Zeboim, and Lasha.
These are all of Ham's sons and their families, divided by language, countries, and nations.
Shem, who was Japheth's older brother fathered all of Eber's children, and Japheth also fathered children.
Shem's children were Elam, Assyria, Arphaxad, Lud, and Aram.
Aram's children were Uz, Hul, Gether, and Mash.
Arphaxad fathered Salah and Salah fathered Eber.
Eber fathered two sons, one was named Peleg because the earth became divided during his lifetime, and Peleg's brother's name was Joktan.
Joktan fathered Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, and Jerah.
And Hadoram, Uzal, and Diklah.
And Obal, Abimael, and Sheba.
And Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab. These were the names of all of Joktan's sons.
Their homelands stretched from Mesha to Mount Sephar, which is towards east.
These are Shem's sons and their families divided by their languages, lands, and nations.
These are the families of Noah's sons, their descendants, and their nations. The nations on earth were all divided by these families after the flood.
At that time everyone on earth spoke the same language.
The people lived on the plains of Shinar after they migrated from the east.
And they said to each other, "Let us bake some bricks," then they had bricks for stone and tar for mortar.
And they said, "Let us build a city with a tower that reaches heaven, and we will make a name for ourselves so that we are not scattered all over the earth."
One day God came down to see the city and the tower the men built.
And God said, "Look at this, these people are united and they all speak the same language, and now they are beginning to do things, and nothing will prevent them from doing whatever they please.
Let us go down there and confound their language so they cannot understand each other."
So the Lord scattered them all over the earth, and they stopped building the city.
After the Lord confounded their language and scattered the people all over the earth, he named the city Babel (which means Confused).
This is the history of Shem and his descendants. Shem was 100 years old when his son Arphaxad was born two years after the flood.
Shem lived another 500 years after Arphaxad was born, and he had many other sons and daughters.
Arphaxad was 35 years old when his son Salah was born.
Arphaxad lived another 403 years after Salah was born, and he had other sons and daughters.
Salah was 30 years old when his son Eber was born.
Salah lived another 403 years after Eber was born, and he had other sons and daughters.
Eber was 34 years old when his son Peleg was born.
Eber lived another 430 years after Peleg was born, and he had other sons and daughters.
Peleg was 30 years old when his son Reu was born.
Peleg lived another 209 years after Reu was born, and he had other sons and daughters.
Reu was 32 years old when his son Serug was born.
Reu lived another 207 years after Serug was born, and he had other sons and daughters.
Serug was 30 years old when his son Nahor was born.
Serug lived another 200 years after his son Nahor was born, and he had other sons and daughters.
Nahor was 29 years old when his son Terah was born.
Nahor lived another 119 years after his son Terah was born, and he had other sons and daughters.
Terah was 70 years old when he fathered Abram, Nahor, and Haran.
This is the history of Terah and his descendants. Terah fathered Abram, Nahor, and Haran, and Haran fathered Lot.
Haran died where he was born in 'Ur of the Chaldeans' before his father Terah died.
Abram and Nahor took wives for themselves. Abram's wife was named Sarai, and Nahor's wife was named Milcah. Haran was Milcah's father and his son was named Iscah.
But Sarai was barren and she had no children.

Terah left 'Ur of the Chaldeans' and went to a place called Canaan, and he brought his son Abram, his grandson Lot (Haran's son), and Abram's wife Sarai (Terah's daughter-in-law). They settled in Haran when they arrived at their destination.
Terah was 205 years old when he died in Haran.
The Lord said to Abram, "Leave your country, your relatives, and your father's house, and I will lead you into a new land.
I will make you a great nation, I will bless you, make your name great, and you will be a blessing to others.
I will bless those who bless you and curse those who curse you. And through your descendants all the families of the earth will be blessed."
Abram was 75 years old when he left Haran as God had told him, and he took his nephew Lot with him.
Abram took his wife Sarai and his nephew Lot, and all of their possessions including all the servants they had acquired in Haran and went to the land of Canaan.
Abram passed through the land and stopped in Sichem at the plains of Moreh, where the Canaanites lived.
The Lord appeared to Abram and said, "I will give this land to your descendants." So, Abram built an altar to the Lord on that spot.
Then Abram traveled to the east side of Bethel and set up camp on a mountain. Bethel was on the west side, Hai was on the east side, and he built an altar to God and prayed to the Lord there.
And Abram continued to travel south.
There was a famine in the land, and Abram went down to Egypt because the famine was so terrible.
As Abram approached the border of Egypt, he spoke to his wife Sarai and said, "You are a beautiful woman.
When the Egyptians see you, they will kill me, but they will take you captive.
So I beg you to tell them that you are my sister, and they will spare my life."
When Abram arrived in Egypt, the Egyptians saw that Sarai was very beautiful.
Pharaoh's princes also saw her and told the Pharaoh how beautiful she was, and she was taken to Pharaoh's house.
Because of Sarai, Pharoah gave Abram some sheep, oxen, camels, male and female donkeys, and male and female servants.
The Lord plagued Pharaoh and his house with great plagues because of Abram's wife Sarai.
Pharaoh summoned Abram and said, "What have you done to me? Why did you not tell me she was your wife?
Why did you say she was your sister? I could have married her, so now you must take your wife and leave."
Then Pharaoh commanded his men to send Abram away, along with his wife and everything that he owned.
Abram left Egypt with his wife and his nephew Lot, along with everything that they owned and they traveled south.
Abram was very rich and he owned an abundance of cattle, silver, and gold.
Abram went south towards Bethel and stopped where he had first camped, somewhere between Bethel and Hai.
Abram went to the place where he built the altar to the Lord and prayed to God.
Lot was also rich and he had an abundance of flocks, herds, and tents.
They had so many dependents that the land could not support them both, and they could no longer live together.
There was constant conflict between Abram's herdsmen and Lot's herdsmen. Lot and Abram also had to share the land with the Canaanites and the Perizzites.
So Abram said to Lot, "I do not want there to be a conflict between us, or between my herdsmen and your herdsmen because I think of you as a brother.

The whole land lies before you, so I want you to take everyone in your household and leave. If you take the land to the left, I will go to the right, but if you take the land to the right, I will go to the left."

Lot looked out over the plains of Jordan, and he noticed that the plains had been well watered before the Lord destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah. The land was similar to the Lord's garden or the land of Egypt towards Zoar.
Lot chose the plains of Jordan, and he traveled east, so he and Abram were separated from each other after that.
Abram lived in the land of Canaan, and Lot lived in the cities of the plains and pitched his tent near Sodom.
But the men of Sodom were exceedingly wicked and sinned against the Lord.
After Lot and Abram separated, God spoke to Abram and said, "Look out at all the land that lies before you from north to south and east to west.
Because from now on, I will give you and your descendants all of this land as far as your eye can see forever.
I will make your family as numerous as the dust of the earth, and if someone can count the earth's dust, then your descendants will also be numbered.
So get up and walk the length and width of the land, because I am giving all of it to you."
Then Abram moved his tent to the 'Oaks of Mamre' where he built an altar to the Lord in Hebron.
When King Amraphel of Shinar, King Arioch of Ellasar, King Chedorlaomer of Elam, and Tidal the king of nations ruled.
They all went to war with King Bera of Sodom, King Birsha of Gomorrah, King Shinab of Admah, King Shemeber of Zeboiim, and King Zoar of Bela.
They all joined together in the valley of Siddim (Dead Sea).
And they served Chedorlaomer for twelve years and rebelled in the thirteenth year.
In the fourteenth year, Chedorlaomer and the kings who were with him defeated the Rephaims in Ashteroth Karnaim, the Zuzim in Ham, and the Emin in Shaveh Kiriathaim.
And the Horites on Mount Seir all the way to Elparan in the wilderness.
They returned to Enmishpat (Kadesh) and defeated the Amalekites and the Amorites in Hazezontamar.
The kings of Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, Zeboiim, and Bela (Zoar) joined them in battle in the valley of Siddim.
So these five kings joined King Chedorlaomer of Elam, King Amraphel of Shinar, King Arioch of Ellasar, and Tidal the king of nations.
The valley of Siddim was full of tar pits, so the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah fled there and they were defeated, but the survivors fled to the mountains.
Then Chedorlaomer and the other kings took all the stored food in Sodom and Gomorrah and left.
Abram's nephew Lot was living in Sodom, and Chedorlaomer and the other kings took Lot along with everything he owned with them when they left.
One of the survivors escaped and told Abram the Hebrew what happened. Abram lived near the plains of Mamre the Amorite, so he and his brothers' Eshcol and Aner were Abram's allies.
When Abram heard that his nephew Lot had been taken captive and since he thought of Lot as his brother, he led 318 trained soldiers and pursued Chedorlaomer and his allies to Dan.
Abram divided his armies against Chedorlaomer's army and defeated them during the night. Then he pursued them to Hobah north of Damascus.
Abram brought his nephew Lot and everything he owned, including the women and all the other people in his household back with him.

The king of Sodom went to meet Abram after he returned from the slaughter of Chedorlaomer. He brought all the kings who were allied with him to meet Abram in the valley of Shaveh, which is the king's valley.
King Melchizedek of Salem, who was also God's most high priest brought bread and wine.
Melchizedek blessed Abram and said, "Blessed is Abram of the Most High God, who possess both heaven and earth.
And blessed is God most high, because he has delivered your enemies into your hand," Then Abram gave Melchizedek 10% of everything that he owned as a tithe.
And the king of Sodom spoke to Abram and said, "Give me the people, and take the goods for yourself."
Abram replied to the king of Sodom and said, "I lift up my hand to the Most High God, who possesses all of heaven and earth.
And I will not take one thread, one shoestring, or anything else that belongs to you, because I do not want you to say that you have made Abram rich.
I will accept nothing from you except what my young men have eaten and the portion that belongs to Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre who joined me."
After all these things happened, Abram had a vision and the Lord's word came to him and said, "Fear not, Abram, I am your shield and your great reward."
And Abram said to the Lord God, "What can you do for me? I have no children, and my household manager Eliezer of Damascus will inherit everything I own."
Then Abram said, "You have made me infertile, and I have no heir to inherit my home."
Then God spoke to Abram and said, "An heir will be born to you Abram, and Eliezer will not inherit your home.
Then God took Abram outside and said, "Look up toward heaven and count the stars if you can, that's how numerous your descendants will be."
Abram believed in the Lord, and he believed that God's word was righteous for him.
Then God spoke to Abram and said, "I am the Lord God who brought you out of Ur of the Chaldeans, and I will give you this land as your inheritance."
But Abram asked, "Lord God, how do I know I will inherit it?"
So God replied to Abram and said, "Bring me a three-year-old heifer, a three-year-old female goat, a three-year-old ram, a turtledove, and a young pigeon."
Abram took all of these things to God, and he split all of them down the middle except for the birds, and he laid the pieces next to each other.
But when the vultures landed on the carcasses, Abram drove them away.
As the sun was going down, Abram fell into a deep sleep, and the horror of the great darkness overwhelmed him.
And the Lord said to Abram, "Know this for sure, your descendants will be strangers in a strange land, and they will be servants to cruel people who will afflict them for 400 years.
But I will judge the nation they serve, and afterwards they will leave that place with great wealth.
You will go to your fathers in peace, and you will live to a ripe old age before you are buried.
But the fourth generation will return here, because the immorality of the Amorites has not yet reached its peak."
When the sun set and it was dark; Abram saw a smoking furnace and a burning lamp that passed between the split carcasses.
That day, the Lord made a covenant with Abram and said, "I have given this land to your descendants, from the Nile River to the great Euphrates River.
Which includes all of the lands of the Kenites, Kenizzites, and the Kadmonites.
And the Hittites, the Perizzites, and the Rephaims.
And the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Girgashites, and the Jebusites."
Abram's wife Sarai was barren and they had no children, but she had an Egyptian housemaid named Hagar.
And Sarai said to Abram, "The Lord has prevented me from bearing children, so I want you to go to my maid, and maybe I can have children through her." Then Abram did what Sarai told him to do.
After Abram and his wife Sarai had lived in Canaan for ten years, Sarai gave her Egyptian maid to her husband Abram to be his wife.
So Abram went to Hagar and she got pregnant, but when Hagar realized that she was going to have a baby, she began to despise Sarai.
And Sarai said to Abram, "I have wronged you by giving you my maid, because when Hagar realized that she was pregnant, she started to despise me. And the Lord will judge both of us for our sins."
But Abram said to Sarai, "I place Hagar in your hands, and you can deal with her however you please." Then Sarai treated Hagar so harshly that she fled.
An angel of the Lord found Hagar along the road to Shur near a water fountain in the wilderness.
And the Lord's angel said, "Hagar, you are Sarai's maid, so why have you come here, and where are you going?" Hagar answered the angel and said, "I have fled from my mistress Sarai."
Then the Lord's angel said to Hagar, "Return to Sarai and serve her.
I will multiply your descendants, and they will become a people too numerous to count.
You are pregnant and you will soon give birth to a son, and you will name him Ishmael because the Lord has heard your sorrows.
Ishmael will be a wild man, he will be against everyone, and everyone will be against him, but he will live among his brothers.
So Hagar gave the Lord who spoke to her a name and she said, "You are the God who sees me, for I have seen the one who has seen me."
That's why the well was called Beer-Lahai-Roi, and it is located between Kadesh and Bered.
Hagar gave birth to Abram's son, and Abram named their son Ishmael.
Abram was 86 years old when Hagar gave birth to his son Ishmael.
When Abram was 99 years old, God appeared to him and said, "I am the Almighty God, walk with me and you will be made perfect.
I will make my covenant between you and me, and I will increase your numbers abundantly."
Then Abram fell face down on the ground, and God said to him.
"Behold, my covenant is with you, and you will be the father of many nations.
You will no longer be called Abram; your name will be changed to Abraham because I have made you the father of many nations.
I will make you extremely fruitful, and I will build you into nations, and your descendants will include kings.

I will establish my covenant between me and you, and your descendants after you, and their descendants after them. For it will be an everlasting covenant, and I will be your God and the God of your descendants after you.
I will give you and your descendants the entire land of Canaan as an everlasting possession, and I will be their God."
And God said to Abraham, "You and descendants will keep my covenant.
This is my covenant between me and you and your descendants. Every male child is to be circumcised.
Cut off his foreskin, and it will be proof of the covenant between us.
All of your biological or adopted male descendants, are to be circumcised when they are eight days old.
Those born in your house or adopted must be circumcised. This is my everlasting covenant between me and you and your descendants.
Any male child who is not circumcised, will be cut off from his people because he has broken my covenant."
And God said to Abraham, "Your wife Sarai's name will be changed to Sarah.
I will bless Sarah and she will give birth to a son for both of you. I will bless her and she will be the mother of nations, and the people's kings will come from her."

Then the expression on Abraham's face changed and he fell on the ground laughing, and in his heart, he thought, "I am 100 years old and Sarah is ninety years old, and nobody a hundred years old can have children."
And Abraham said to God, "Yes God, please bless Ishmael!"
And God said, "Your wife Sarah will give birth to a son for you, and you will name him Isaac. Then I will establish my everlasting covenant with Isaac and his descendants after him.
As for Ishmael, I have heard you and I have blessed him. I will make him fruitful and he will multiply abundantly. Ishmael will father twelve princes and I will make him into a great nation.
But my covenant is with Isaac, who Sarah will give birth to at about this time next year."
Then God stopped talking and left Abraham.
That same day, Abraham did what God told him to do, and he took his son Ishmael and had him circumcised along with all the other male children in his household.
Abraham was 99 years old when he was circumcised.
His son Ishmael was thirteen years old when he was circumcised.
Abraham and his son Ishmael were both circumcised on the same day.
And all the men of Abraham's household were circumcised with them.
God appeared to Abraham near the Oaks of Mamre, as he was sitting in the tent door during the heat of the day.
When Abraham looked up, he saw three men standing there. So, he got up and ran to meet them and greeted them with a warm welcome.
And Abraham said, "My Lord if I have found favor in your sight, please stay here with me and do not leave me.
I will go fetch some water for you to wash your feet, and you can rest here under the tree.
Before you leave, I will fetch some food to comfort your hearts since you have come to see me." And they said, "So do what you said you were going to do."
Abraham went into the tent and told Sarah to bake some bread on the hearth.
Then Abraham ran out to his herd, fetched a young and tender calf and gave it to one of his young men to be prepared.
Abraham gave the men some butter, milk, and the calf he had prepared, then stood beside the tree watching them eat.
And the men asked Abraham, "Where is your wife, Sarah?" And he said, "She is in the tent."
And the Lord spoke to Abraham and said, "I will return in the spring, and your wife Sarah will give you a son." Sarah was listening to them behind the tent door.
Abraham and Sarah were very old, and Sarah was much too old to have a baby.
Sarah laughed to herself and said, "Abraham and I are both too old to have a baby."
And the Lord said to Abraham, "Sarah laughed and said, 'As old as I am, are you sure I am going to have a child?'
Is anything too hard for the Lord? I will return in the spring, and Sarah will have a son."
Sarah was afraid, because she had laughed at the Lord and she denied laughing. But the Lord said to her, "Yes, you did laugh."
The men got up and headed towards Sodom, and Abraham went part of the way with them.
And the Lord said, "Should I hide what I have planned for Abraham.
Abraham will become a great and mighty nation, and all the nations on earth will be blessed because of him?

For I know that Abraham will tell his children and his entire household to keep the Lord's ways. To use good judgment and to be righteous, and I will bless Abraham with all the blessings I have promised him."
And God said to Abraham, "Sodom and Gomorrah are wicked and evil, and their sins are very great.
So I am going down there to see if their sin is as great as I have heard."
The men turned and headed towards Sodom, but Abraham still stood in front of the Lord.
Then Abraham asked God, "Are you going to destroy the righteous along with the wicked?
If there are fifty righteous people inside the city, are you going to destroy them along with the wicked?

It would not be like you to kill the righteous along with the wicked. You would be treating the righteous the same as you treat the wicked, and the earth's judge should not treat the righteous unfairly."
And the Lord said, "If I find fifty righteous people in Sodom, I will spare the whole place."
And Abraham said to the Lord again, "I am just dust and ashes.

But tell me, if there are only 45 righteous people in Sodom, will you destroy them and the whole city." And the Lord answered and said, "If I find only 45 righteous people there, I will not destroy it."
Abraham spoke to the Lord again and said, "What if there are only forty righteous people there?" And the Lord answered and said, "I will not destroy Sodom if there are forty righteous people there."

Then Abraham said to God, "Please do not be angry, but I have to ask you again. What if there are only thirty righteous people there?" And the Lord said, "I will not destroy Sodom if I find thirty righteous people there."
And Abraham said to God, "I have to ask you again, what if there are only twenty righteous people there?" And the Lord said, "I will not destroy Sodom if I find twenty righteous people there."

So finally Abraham said, "Please do not be angry, but I have to ask you one more time, what if there are only ten righteous people in Sodom?" And God said, "I will not destroy Sodom if I find ten righteous people there."
When God was finished talking to Abraham, he left and Abraham went home.
In the evening Lot was sitting at the gates of Sodom when he saw two angels approaching him, and he got up and went to meet them and bowed facedown toward them.

Lot greeted them and said, "My lords, I am your servant and I invite you into my home, where you can wash your feet and stay all night. Then you can get up early tomorrow morning and be on your way." But they answered him and said, "No thank you, we can stay out on the streets tonight."
But Lot insisted that they come to his house, so they went and he made them a feast with unleavened bread.
But before they went to bed, the men of Sodom and everyone living around Lot's house surrounded them.
And they shouted to Lot, "Where are the men you brought to your house tonight? Bring them out here, so we can have our perverted way with them."
And they shouted to Lot, "Where are the men you brought to your house tonight? Bring them out here, so we can pervert and abuse them.
Then Lot pleaded with them and said, "People please, do not do such a wicked thing.
I have two virgin daughters, and I will let you do whatever you want with them, but please leave these men alone and do not harm them, because they are under my roof."

And they said to Lot, "Who are you to tell us what to do? You were just a traveler, and we let you settle here among us, and now you want to judge us? We will we deal worse with you than we do with them!" Then they jumped at Lot and nearly broke down his door.
But the angels pulled Lot into the house and shut the door.
Then the angels blinded the men of Sodom, and they could not find the door.
And the angels said to Lot, "Take your possessions and everyone in your household including your sons and daughters and your son-in-law with you, and leave Sodom.
We are going to destroy this place, because Sodom's sins have been seen by the Lord, and God has sent us to destroy it."
So Lot went and spoke to his sons-in-law and said, "We must leave this place because the Lord is going to destroy the city of Sodom!" But Lot's sons-in-law just laughed at him.
At sunrise the angels spoke to Lot and said, "Get up and take your wife and daughters, and leave this place, or you will be consumed by the immorality in Sodom."
But Lot lingered too long, so the angels took the hands of his wife and his two daughters and led them out of the city. This is how God was merciful to Lot.
After the angels brought Lot and his family out of Sodom, they said, "Run for your life, do not look back, and do not stay on the plains, but go up into the mountains or you will be consumed.
And Lot said to them, "Please Lord do not make me go to the mountains.
You have been merciful to me, and you have saved my life, but I cannot go up into the mountain, because I fear that I will be overcome by some evil and I am afraid to die.
There is a little city nearby and I ask that you let me go there, and my soul will live."
And the Lord's angel replied to Lot and said, "OK, I have heard your concerns and I accept your plea, so I will not destroy that city for your sake.
You must hurry though because I cannot do anything until you get there." So, from that day forward, that city was named Zoar (which means Little City).
The sun was rising when Lot entered Zoar.
Then the Lord rained down fire and brimstone from heaven onto Sodom and Gomorrah.
God destroyed those cities, the plains, all the cities' inhabitants, and everything growing on the ground.
But Lot's wife turned and looked back, and she was turned into a pillar of salt.
Abraham was camped where he had stood before the Lord earlier, and he got up early that morning.
Abraham looked out over the plains, and he saw the smoke rising up from Sodom and Gomorrah like a smoking furnace.
When God destroyed the cities of the plains, he remembered Abraham and he protected Lot from all the death and destruction there.
But Lot was afraid to live in Zoar, so he moved into a cave in the mountains with his two daughters.
Lot's oldest daughter spoke to her younger sister and said, "Our father is old, and there are no men here for us to marry.
We can get our father drunk and sleep with him and have children to preserve his heritage."
So that night, they got their father drunk. Then Lot's oldest daughter went into his tent and had sex with him. But he was so drunk that he did not even know she had been there.
The next day, she told her younger sister all about it and she said, "We can get him drunk again tonight, then you can go in there to be with him."
That night they got their father drunk again, and his youngest daughter had sex with him. Once again, Lot was so drunk that he did not even know she had been there.
So Lot had impregnated both of his daughters.
Lot's oldest daughter had a son and named him Moab, who became the father of the Moabites.
His youngest daughter also had a son, and she named him Benammi, who became the father of the children of Ammon.
Abraham traveled south and lived between Kadesh and Shur for a while, and then he traveled to Gerar.
Abraham told King Abimelech of Gerar that his wife Sarah was his sister, so Abimelech took Sarah.
But God came to Abimelech in a dream and said, "You are a dead man because the woman you have taken is married to someone else."
But Abimelech had not slept with Sarah and he said, "Lord, are you going to kill a righteous nation?
Abraham did not tell me that Sarah was his sister! She told me that he was her brother, and in my heart, I am the innocent victim of all this.
And God said, "I know, that's why I stopped you from sinning against me and kept you from touching her.
Now send her back to her husband, because he is a prophet who will pray for you, and you will live. But if you do not send her back to her husband, then you and yours will surely die."
Abimelech got up early the next morning and told his servants what God had said, and they were all extremely frightened.

Then Abimelech sent for Abraham and said to him, "Look at what you have done to us! What have I ever done to offend you? You have brought a great sin against me and my kingdom, and you have done things to me that should never be done to anyone."
And Abimelech said to Abraham, "Why would you do something like this to me?"
And Abraham said, "I said this because I thought that you did not fear God, and I was afraid that your men would kill me and take my wife.
The truth is that Sarah really is my half-sister because she is my father's daughter, but she is not my mother's daughter, and we are also married.
When God told me to leave my father's house, I asked Sarah to be kind to me and tell everyone, everywhere that she was my sister."
Abimelech felt guilty, so he gave sheep and oxen plus male and female servants to Abraham and Sarah.
Then Abimelech said to Abraham, "My entire land lies before you, so leave and go live wherever you want."
And Abimelech said to Sarah, "I have given your brother a thousand pieces of silver, to make amends for any condemnation you or yours may have suffered from this, so that you will not be blamed."
So Abraham prayed to God and asked him to heal Abimelech, his wife, and his female servants. And Abraham asked God to heal their barren women, so they could have children.
Because the Lord had made all of Abimelech's women barren because he had taken Sarah from Abraham.
The Lord visited Sarah, and she had become pregnant just as the Lord said she would.
Sarah conceived, and gave birth to Abraham's son, exactly when God said it would happen.
Abraham and Sarah named their son, Isaac.
Abraham had Isaac circumcised when he was eight days old because that's what God told him to do.
Abraham was 100 years old when Isaac was born.
And Sarah said, "God has made me happy, and everyone that hears me laughing, will laugh with me."
And Sarah said, "Who would have ever thought that I would have a baby in my old age? But I have given Abraham a son in his old age."
Isaac grew older and was weaned from his mother, and Abraham prepared a great feast for him on the day that he was weaned.
Sarah saw the Egyptian Hagar's son, Ishmael, mocking Isaac.
So Sarah told Abraham to throw Hagar and Ishmael out of their camp. She did not want her son Isaac to share his inheritance with her slave Hagar and her son Ishmael.
This made Abraham very unhappy because he also loved his son Ishmael.
And God said to Abraham, "Do not grieve because of Ishmael and your slave woman Hagar. Listen to Sarah because Isaac and his descendants will be called to build a great nation.
I will also build a nation out of your slave woman Hagar's son Ishmael and his descendants because he is your son."
Abraham got up early in the morning and gave Hagar some bread and a bottle of water, then he sent her and Ishmael away. So, she left and wandered around in the wilderness of Beersheba.
When her water bottle was empty, she threw her child under one of the shrubs.
Hagar went and sat down beside her son Ishmael and started crying because she could not bear watching her only child die.
When God heard Ishmael's voice, his angel spoke to Hagar from heaven and asked, "Why are you worried Hagar? God has heard the boy crying.
Pick up Ishmael and carry him in your arms, because I am going to make him a great nation."
Then God opened Hagar's eyes and she saw a well appear, so she filled the bottle with water and gave it to her son Ishmael to drink.
God watched over Ishmael, and he grew up in the wilderness and became an archer.
Ishmael lived in the wilderness of Paran with his mother, and she found an Egyptian wife for him.
At the same time Abimelech and Phichol, the chief captain of Abimelech's army spoke to Abraham and said, "God is with you in all that you do.

Therefore, I want you to swear to me in front of God that you will deal honestly with me, my son, and my descendants. For I am only asking you to treat me with the same kindness that I have shown you, both here and in the other lands where you travel."
And Abraham said, "I swear I will do that."
Abraham blamed Abimelech for a well one of Abimelech's servants had violently stolen from him.
And Abimelech said, "I do not know what you are talking about, and I do not know who stole your well! You never told me about it, and I have not heard anything about this until today."
Then Abraham gave sheep and oxen to Abimelech, and they made a covenant.
Abraham picked seven ewe lambs out of his flock and set them aside.
Abimelech asked Abraham, "Why did you pick seven ewe lambs and set them out by themselves?"
Abraham said, "I want you to take these seven ewe lambs, as my testimony to you that I dug this well."
Abraham called that place Beersheba because both of them swore an oath.
They made a covenant at Beersheba, and then Abimelech and Phichol the chief captain of his army left, and they returned to the land of the Philistines.
Abraham planted olive trees in Beersheba, and he called on the name of the everlasting God there.
Then Abraham traveled throughout the land of the Philistines for days.
Then, God decided to tempt Abraham and he called out to him. Abraham answered and said, "Here I am."
And God said, "Take your only son Isaac whom you love, and go to Moriah. And I will show you a mountain where I want you to offer him up as a burnt offering."
Abraham got up early the next morning and cut enough wood for the burnt offering. He saddled his donkey, took Isaac along with two of his servants, and went where God told him to go.
Abraham looked up on the third day and saw that there was still a long way to go to the place that God had told him about.
So, Abraham said to his servants "Stay here with the donkey until we return. I am taking the boy to the place to worship."
Abraham loaded Isaac with enough wood for the burnt offering. Then the two left with a knife and a lit torch and went there alone.
Isaac spoke to Abraham and said, "I am here, the firewood is here, but where is the lamb for the burnt offering?"
And Abraham said, "God himself will provide a lamb for the burnt offering," and they went there together.
When they arrived in the place that God had told him about, Abraham built an altar, then he arranged the wood on the altar, tied his son and laid him on top of the woodpile.
Abraham took his knife and prepared to kill Isaac.
Then the Lord's angel called out to Abraham from heaven. So, Abraham answered him and said, "Here I am."
And the Lord's angel said, "Do not touch the boy or do anything to harm him. Now I know that you fear God because I can see that you are willing to sacrifice your only son to me."
Then Abraham saw a ram trapped in a thicket behind him, he took it and offered it to God as a burnt offering instead of his son.
Abraham named the mountain Jehovah-Jireh, and to this day people say, that the Lord can still be seen there.
Then the Lord's angel called out to Abraham from heaven again.
And the Lord's angel said, "Because you have offered to sacrifice your only son to me.
I will surely bless you and multiply your descendants like the stars in the heavens, they will multiply like the sands of the seas, and your descendants will possess their enemies' gates.
Your descendants and all the nations on earth will be blessed because you have obeyed my voice."
So Abraham returned to his servants, and they went back to Beersheba.
After that Abraham was told that his brother Nahor's wife Milcah had given birth to children.
Nahor's firstborn was Uz, then his brother Buz was born, then Aram's father Kemuel was born.
Then Chesed, Hazo, Pildash, Jidlaph, and Bethuel were born.
Bethuel fathered Rebekah, and Abraham's brother Nahor fathered eight children with his wife Milcah.
Reumah who was Nahor's concubine gave birth to Tebah, Gaham, Thahash, and Maachah.
Sarah was 127 years old when she died.
Sarah died in Kirjath-Arba (aka. Hebron) in the land of Canaan, and Abraham mourned and wept for Sarah.
Abraham stood before his dead wife and spoke to Heth's sons.
And Abraham said to Heth's sons, "I am a stranger here, please give me a place to bury my wife. I want to bury my dead out of my sight."
Then Heth's children answered Abraham.

And Heth's children said, "Hear us my Lord, you are a mighty prince among us, you can have any tomb of ours you want to bury your dead. No one will stop you and you will be allowed to bury your dead in any tomb.
Abraham stood up and bowed to the people of the land, including Heth's children.
Then Abraham spoke to them and said, "If you think I should bury my dead out of my sight, please speak to Zohar's son Ephron on my behalf.

Ephron owns the cave of Machpelah, and I would like you to ask him if he will sell me that piece of land at the end of his field. Tell him I will pay him whatever he says it is worth, because I need a place to bury my dead.
Ephron the Hittite lived among Heth's children, and he answered Abraham as they were watching, along with everyone else who had entered the city through the city gates.

Ephron the Hittite said, "No, my Lord, listen to me, I will give you the field and the cave. I freely give it to you in front of my people and their sons. I will give it to you free of charge so you can have a place to bury your dead."
Abraham bowed down to the people of the land.
Abraham spoke to Ephron in front of the people and said, "Listen to me, I will pay you for the field, please take my money so I can bury my dead there."
Then Ephron answered Abraham
And Abraham said, "My Lord, this land is worth 400 silver shekels, and what is 400 shekels between friends, please go and bury your dead."
Abraham agreed to Ephron's price in front of Heth's sons, and he weighed out 400 silver shekels to pay him.
Ephron's field was in Machpelah, which was on the way to Mamre. So, Abraham bought the field, the cave, all the trees growing there, and all the trees growing along the borders around the field.
Heth's children were there and they saw Abraham buy the field, and everyone that went through Ephron's city gates witnessed the transaction.
After this, Abraham buried his wife Sarah in the cave in the Machpelah field near Mamre, which is Hebron in the land of Canaan.
Abraham took possession of the field and the cave to be used for a cemetery, and it was witnessed by Heth's sons.
Abraham was very old, and the Lord had blessed him in all things.

Abraham lived among the Canaanites, and his oldest servant ruled over his household and everything that he owned. One day Abraham said to this servant, "Put your hand under my thigh, and swear to me before God and his covenant that you will fulfill this promise.
Swear to me by the Lord God of heaven and earth, that you will not allow my son Isaac to marry a Canaanite woman.
I want you to go to my home country where my relatives live to find a wife for my son Isaac."
And the servant said, "What if the woman does not want to move here, do you want me to take Isaac there?"
Abraham replied to him and said, "No, do not take him there.

The Lord God of heaven told me to leave my father's house and the land of my relatives, and he swore to me that he would give me this land for my descendants. The Lord also said that he would send one of his angels there before I arrived, and that I would find a wife for my son Isaac in my homeland.
If the woman is not willing to come here, then I release you from this oath but do not take my son there.
Then the servant put his hand under Abraham's thigh and swore an oath to him about his son's future wife.
Abraham's servant left and took ten of Abraham's camels, along with many of Abraham's good things, and went to Nahor's city in Mesopotamia.
Abraham's servant arrived in the evening and made his camels kneel beside the well outside the city. This was about the same time in the evening that the women would come to draw water from the well.
Then Abraham's servant prayed and said, "Lord God of my master Abraham, I pray that you will show kindness to Abraham and let me find a wife for his son.
I am standing here before the city well, and the daughters from the city will come here to draw water.

When I speak to one of the girls and say, 'May I have a drink of water from your pitcher.' And she says, 'You and your camels both can have some water to drink.' Then I will know that you have shown kindness to my master and she is the wife you have chosen for your servant Isaac."

Before he was finished speaking, Rebekah came out to the well with a water pitcher on her shoulder. Abraham's brother Nahor and his wife Milcah had a son named Betheul, and Rebekah was Betheul's daughter.
Rebekah was very pretty and she was a virgin. She had come down to the well to fill her pitcher, and when she pulled the pitcher out of the well,
Abraham's servant ran to meet her and said, "May I have some water to drink."
And she said, "Drink, my Lord," and she gave him a drink of water.
He drank some water, and she said, "I will also draw some water for your camels to drink."
She quickly emptied her pitcher into the trough and ran back to the well to draw enough water for all of his camels.
Abraham's servant said nothing, but he wondered to himself if this was the woman the Lord had sent.
When the camels finished drinking, the man took a golden earring that weighed half a gold shekel, and two wrist bracelets that weighed ten gold shekels and gave them to her.
Then Abraham's servant asked Rebekah, "Who is your father? Do you think your father has enough room in his house for us to stay?"
And she said, "I am Bethuel's daughter, his parents are Nahor and Milcah and they are my grandparents.
I think we have enough room for you and enough straw and feed for your camels."
Then Abraham's servant bowed his head and worshipped the Lord.
And he said, "Blessed be Abraham's Lord God, who has blessed him with love, mercy, and truth. I am also blessed because God has led me to the house of my master's brother."
Rebekah ran to her mother's house and told everyone what happened.
Rebekah had a brother named Laban, when he saw the bracelets on her wrists and heard what she had to say, he ran out to the well to meet the man.
When Laban got to the well, he saw the man standing there with his camels.
And Laban said, "You are blessed by the Lord, so why are you standing out here? I have prepared a place in the house for you, and there is also room for your camels."
Abraham's servant entered the house and unloaded his camels, and Laban brought some straw and hay to feed them, then he gave all of Abraham's servants some water to wash their feet.
Abraham's servant was given some food to eat, but he said, "I will not eat before I tell you why I am here."
And he said, "I am Abraham's servant.
The Lord has blessed him abundantly, Abraham has become a great man, and his God has given him flocks, herds, silver, gold, male and female servants, camels, and donkeys.
Abraham's wife Sarah gave him a son when she was very old, and Abraham has given everything he owns to his son Isaac.
My master made me swear that I would not let his son Isaac marry a Canaanite woman.
But Abraham told me to go to his father's house where his relatives live, to find a wife for his son."
And I asked Abraham, "What if the woman does not want to follow me home?"

And Abraham said, "The Lord that I walk with, will send his angel with you to my father's house, he will make your way prosperous, and you will find a wife for my son from one of my relatives in my father's house.
If you do not find the right woman to marry my son, you will be released from this oath.
When I arrived at the well, I prayed and said, "Lord God of my master Abraham, please let me find a wife for Abraham's son Isaac.
I am standing by the city well and when a virgin comes to draw water, I will ask her, 'May I have some water to drink?'
And if she replies back to me and says, 'You and your camels both can have some water to drink,' then I will know that the Lord God has chosen a wife for my master's son to marry.
Before I finished praying, Rebekah showed up with her pitcher, she drew some water from the well, and I asked her, 'May I please have some water to drink?'
So she handed me her pitcher and said, 'You and your camels both can have some water to drink,' so I drank and she also watered my camels.

Then I asked her, 'Who is your father?' And she said, I am Bethuel's daughter, his parents are Nahor and Milcah and they are also my grandparents. Then I gave her the earring and put the bracelets on her wrists.
And I bowed my head and worshipped the Lord, and I blessed my master Abraham's Lord God, who led me to Abraham's brother Nahor, who is Rebekah's father.
Please be kind and tell me honestly if you will allow Rebekah to marry my master's son. And if not, I will know whether to turn left or right and look somewhere else."
Rebekah's father Bethuel and her brother Laban both answered and said, "This request comes from the Lord, we cannot tell you yes or no.
God has spoken, so take Rebekah and go and she will marry your master's son."
When Abraham's servant heard this, he bowed and worshipped the Lord.
Then he gave Rebekah some clothes, silver jewelry, and gold jewelry. He also gave precious gifts to her mother and her brother.
That night they all stayed up late and ate and drank with Abraham's servant and his men. Then they got up early the next morning, and Abraham's servant said, "Now you can send me back to my master."
And Rebekah's mother and brother said, "Let Rebekah stay with us at least ten more days, then she can go with you."
And Abraham's servant said to them, "The Lord has made my trip successful, so please do not delay my departure and let me return to my master."
And Rebekah's mother and brother said, "We will let Rebekah decide.
So they sent for Rebekah and asked her if she wanted to leave with him. And Rebekah said, "Yes, I want to go with him."
Then Rebekah and her nurse left with Abraham's servant and his men.
Rebekah's family blessed her and said, "Rebekah, you are our sister and we hope you are blessed with thousands of descendants, and may they take possession of their enemies' gates.
Rebekah and her girlfriends got up and rode away on their camels with Abraham's servant.
Isaac lived in the south country, and he came from the direction of the Lahairoi well.
In the evening Isaac was out meditating in the field, when he looked up, he saw camels coming his way.
When Rebekah saw Isaac, she jumped off her camel.
Rebekah had asked Abraham's servant, "Who is that man coming to meet us from the field?" And Abraham's servant said, "It is my master's son Isaac." So, Rebekah covered herself with a veil.
Then Abraham's servant told Isaac everything that happened on his trip
Isaac brought Rebekah to meet his mother Sarah in her tent, then Rebekah and Isaac were married and Isaac loved Rebekah. And Rebekah comforted Isaac after his mother died.
After Sarah died, Abraham got remarried to a woman named Keturah.
Keturah gave birth to Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah.
Jokshan fathered Sheba and Dedan. Then Dedan fathered Assyriaim, Letushim, and Leummim.
Keturah had many descendants including Midian, Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abidah, and Eldaah.
Abraham gave everything he owned as an inheritance to Isaac.
But Abraham had other sons with his concubines, so he gave them gifts while he was still living and sent them away to the eastern country.
Abraham lived to be 175 years old.
Then Abraham gave up the ghost and died an old man at the ripe old age of 175, and everyone gathered together for his funeral.
His sons Isaac and Ishmael buried him in the Machpelah cave in Ephron's field near Mamre. Ephron's father was Zohar the Hittite.
The field where Abraham and his wife Sarah were buried was the field that Abraham purchased from Heth's sons.
After Abraham died, God blessed his son Isaac who lived near the Lahairoi well.
This is the history of Abraham's son, Ishmael. Hagar the Egyptian was Ishmael's mother, she was also Abraham's wife Sarah's housemaid.
These are the names of Ishmael's sons in the order in which they were born. Ishmael's firstborn was Nebajoth, followed by Kedar, Adbeel, and Mibsam.
Then Mishma, Dumah, and Massa were born.
After that Hadar, Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah were born.
These are Ishmael's sons, who were the twelve princes that God had promised to Hagar. Their nations are listed in the order of their names, towns, and castles.
Ishmael was 137 years old when he died, and his people gathered together for his funeral.
Ishmael's sons lived near Egypt, and they were scattered from Havilah to Shur which is towards Assyria. And Ishmael was surrounded by his brothers when he died.
This is the history of Abraham's son, Isaac.
Isaac was forty years old when he married Rebekah, and she was the daughter of Bethuel the Syrian of Padan-Aram and Laban the Syrian's sister.
Isaac's wife Rebekah could not have children, and he pleaded with the Lord for his wife to be made fertile, and she conceived twins.
The children in her womb struggled against each other in her womb, and she asked the Lord, "Why is this happening to me?"

And the Lord said to her, "There are two nations within your womb, and you will give birth to two different people, the younger son will be stronger than the older son, and the eldest son will serve the younger one.
After nine months, she gave birth to twin boys.
The first one to come out was red and hairy, and they named him Esau.
Then his brother came out holding onto Esau's heel, they named him Jacob, and Isaac was sixty years old when they were born.
The boys grew older, and Esau was a man of the field and a skillful hunter, but Jacob was a plain man who stayed at home in the tents.
Isaac loved Esau because Esau supplied the venison that he ate, but Rebekah loved Jacob.
One day Jacob was cooking some bean soup, and Esau was very hungry when he came in from the fields.
And he asked Jacob, "Can I have some of that bean soup, because I am really hungry," and that's why Esau is also called Edom.
And Jacob said, "Sell me your inheritance, and I will give you some soup."
And Esau said, "I am starving, and my birthright is worth nothing to me?"
And Jacob said, "Swear to me that you have sold your inheritance to me for this bean soup!" So, Esau swore an oath and sold his birthright to Jacob
Jacob gave Esau some bread and lentil soup to eat. When Esau finished eating, he got up and left unworried about losing his inheritance.

While Abraham was living there was a famine throughout the land, and after he died there was another famine. Because of the famine, Isaac went to see King Abimelech who ruled over the Philistines in Gerar.
And God appeared to Isaac and said, "Do not go to Egypt, and I will tell you where there's a better place to live.

Go where I tell you to go, and I will be with you, and bless you. I will keep the promises I made to your father Abraham because I swore an oath and promised him, that I would give you, and your descendants all of these countries.
I will multiply your descendants like the stars of heaven, and I will give all these countries to your descendants, and all their nations on earth will be blessed.
All your nations will be blessed, because Abraham obeyed me, and kept my commandments, statutes, and laws."
Isaac lived in Gerar.

The men in Gerar asked Isaac about his wife, and he told them that she was his sister. He was afraid to tell them that she was his wife, because Rebekah was a beautiful woman, and he was afraid that if they knew she was his wife, they would kill him and take her.
Isaac had been in Gerar for a long time when Abimelech King of the Philistines looked out the window and saw him kissing Rebekah.

Abimelech summoned Isaac and said, "Rebekah's your wife, and you lied to me. You told me she was your sister." And Isaac answered him, "I said it because I thought the men here would kill me and take her."
And Abimelech said, "What have you done to us? What if someone had sex with your wife, you would have brought sin and judgment down on us."
And Abimelech spoke to his people and said, "Anyone that touches this man or his wife will be put to death."
Then Isaac planted his fields and harvested a hundred times more crops than he planted, because God had blessed him.
Over time Isaac's wealth increased, and as his wealth continued to grow, he became a very great man.
He owned flocks, herds, and many servants, and that's why the Philistines envied him.
Isaac had inherited wells that his father Abraham's servants had dug, but during his lifetime, the Philistines had filled them full of dirt.
Abimelech spoke to Isaac and said, "You're mightier than we are, so we want you to leave."
Isaac left and moved to the Gerar valley to live, and that's where he set up his camp.
