So the people rested on the seventh day.
The Israelis called it manna, it was white and looked like coriander seed, but it tasted like honey wafers.

And Moses said, "This is what the Lord says to do, 'Fill a container with an omer of manna to be kept for your descendants so they can see the bread that I fed you in the wilderness when I brought you out of Egypt.'"
Then Moses spoke to Aaron and said, "Put an omer of manna in a pot and store it for the Lord, to be kept for your descendants."
The Lord told Moses what to do so Aaron stored it with the Testimony to be kept for future generations.
And the sons of Israel ate manna for forty years until they arrived in an inhabited land at the borders of Canaan.
An omer is 1/10th of an ephah or about 3.6 liters.
The entire Israeli congregation did what the Lord told them to do, they left the Sin wilderness and camped in Rephidim, but there was no drinking water there.
So the people complained to Moses and said, "We are thirsty and we need drinking water." And Moses said to them, "Why are you complaining to me? Do you really want to test the Lord?"

The people were thirsty and they wanted water, and they complained to each other about Moses and they said to him, "Why did you bring us out of Egypt, do you want us, our children, and our cattle to die of thirst?"
Moses cried out to the Lord and said, "What should I do with these people? They are almost ready to stone me."
And the Lord said to Moses, "Go ahead of the people, take the Israeli elders and the staff you used to strike the Nile River with you.

I will stand in front of you on the rock in Horeb, and I want you to strike the rock, and drinking water will come out of it." Moses did what the Lord told him to do in front of the Israeli elders so that they could see it for themselves.

He named the place Massah which means 'trial or temptation' and Meribah which means 'quarreling or strife', because the Israelis complained, and they tempted the Lord and said, "Is the Lord with us or not?"
Then Amalek came and fought Israel in Rephidim.
And Moses said to Joshua, "Choose our best men and go fight Amalek. Tomorrow I will stand on top of the hill with God's staff in my hand."
So Joshua did what Moses told him to do and fought against Amalek. Moses, Aaron, and Hur went up to the top of the hill.
When Moses held up his hand Israel would win, but when he lowered his hand Amalek started winning.

But Moses was tired and his hand was heavy, so they put a stone under him to sit on. So, Aaron and Hur lifted Moses' hands up, and they stood on either side of him and held his hands steady until the sun went down.
Joshua humiliated Amalek and his people and defeated them on the battlefield.
And the Lord said to Moses, "Write this in a history book and make sure that Joshua hears this because I am going to completely erase the memory of Amalek from under heaven."
And Moses built an altar and named it Jehovah-Nissi, which means 'The Lord is our banner.'
He said it was because the Lord has sworn that he would make war with Amalek from one generation to the next.
Jethro was Moses' father-in-law and the priest in Midian, and he heard what God had done for Moses and the Israelis when he brought them out of Egypt.
Jethro was also Zipporah's father and Zipporah was Moses' wife. Jethro let Zipporah move back home after Moses sent her back.
Zipporah had two sons, one named Gershom because Moses said, "I have been an alien in a strange land."
The other one was named Eliezer because Moses said, "The God of my father helped me and delivered me from Pharaoh's sword."
Jethro was also Gershom and Eliezer's grandfather, and he went to visit Moses where they were camped at God's mountain. Jethro brought Moses' wife Zipporah and their two sons with him.
And Jethro said to Moses, "I have brought your wife and sons with me to come to visit you."
Moses went to meet his father-in-law and paid tribute to him and kissed him. They asked each other how they were doing, then they went into the tent.
Moses told his father-in-law about Israel's enslavement. He told him about everything that the Lord had done to Pharaoh and the Egyptians when he brought the people out of Egypt.
Jethro was happy and rejoiced when he heard about all the good things the Lord did for Israel when he delivered them from the Egyptians.
And Jethro said, "Blessed be the Lord, who has delivered you and the Israeli people from the hand of Pharaoh and the Egyptians.
Now I know that the Lord is greater than all the other gods because of the way he dealt with the proud and arrogant Egyptians for treating the Israelis that bad.
Moses' father-in-law took a burnt offering and other sacrifices to God. Aaron came and he brought the Israeli elders with him, and they all ate bread together in God's presence.
The next day, Moses sat as the people's judge, and they stood around him all day from morning to evening.

When Moses' father-in-law saw everything that Moses had done for the people, he said, "Why are you sitting and judging these people all by yourself? Every day they wait from morning until evening for you to hear their case."
And Moses answered his father-in-law and said, "Because the people come to me to ask questions of God.
When they have something in dispute, they come to me and I judge between them and I teach them God's laws."
And Moses' father-in-law said to him, "This is not good.
This will exhaust both you and these people because it is too much for you to handle all by yourself.
Listen to me and let me give you some advice and God will be with you, you are the people's advocate, so that you may bring their causes to God.
Teach them God's legal decrees and laws and show them the way they must walk and the work that they must do.

Choose able, truthful, honest, and God-fearing men who hate covetousness and teach them God's law. Then let them moderate disputes between the people. They should be organized by groups of 1000, 100, 50, and 10.
Let them judge the people for small everyday disputes, and you will decide any major controversies. They will bear the burden with you and reduce the heavy load that you carry.
If you do what God has told you to do, then you will endure and the people will all go home in peace."
So Moses listened to his father-in-law and did what he suggested.
Moses chose wise and able men and made them the people's leaders. The officials were appointed by rank to be leaders of 1000's, 100's, 50's, and 10's.
They judged the people's everyday disputes, but they brought the difficult cases to Moses, everything else they judged by themselves.
Then Moses father-in-law left and went back to his own land.
Three months after the Israelis left Egypt they reached the Sinai wilderness.
The Israelis left Rephidim and traveled to the Sinai desert where they camped in the wilderness before the mountain.
Moses went to God's mountain and the Lord called out to Moses from the mountain and said, "This is what I want you to say to Jacob's house and the Israelis.
Speak to them and say, 'You have seen what I did to the Egyptians when I brought you to me on eagles' wings.
So if you obey me and keep my covenant, you will be a special treasure to me above all other people because the earth belongs to me.
You will be my kingdom of priests and a holy nation. And this is what I want you to tell the Israelis."
Moses called for the people's elders and laid out God's words in front of them.
They all answered unanimously and said, "We will do everything the Lord has told us to do." Then Moses returned to the Lord and told him everything the people said.
And the Lord said to Moses, "I come to you in a thick cloud so that the people may hear and forever believe you when I speak to you." And Moses told the people what the Lord said.
And the Lord said to Moses, "Go to the people, and declare today and tomorrow as holy days and let them wash their clothes.
Be ready on the third day, because on that day the Lord will come down to Mount Sinai where the people can see him.
Set borders around the mountain to keep the people from going to the mountain or touching its border because whoever touches the mountain will be put to death.
When the trumpet sounds come up to the mountain, but do not let any man nor beast touch it or they will be stoned or shot with arrows and killed."
Then Moses left the mountain and went down to the people, he sanctified the people and they washed their clothes.
And he said to the people, "Be ready on the third day but do not touch your wives."
On the morning of the third day, a thick cloud enveloped the mountain, there was thunder and lightning, and a very loud trumpet blast, and all the people in the camp trembled.
Moses brought the people out of the camp to meet with God, and they stood at the lower part of the mountain.
Mount Sinai was covered with smoke because the Lord descended in fire and smoke billowed up like a smoking furnace, the whole mountain shook like there was an earthquake.
When the trumpet sounded the sound grew louder and louder. Then Moses spoke, and God answered him with a powerful voice.
The Lord came down to the top of Mount Sinai and called Moses to come up to the top of the mountain, and Moses went.
And the Lord said to Moses, "Go down there and tell the people not to cross the border to see the Lord or many of them may perish.
The priests who come near the Lord must sanctify themselves, or else the Lord's anger will suddenly burst out against them."
And Moses said to the Lord, "The people cannot come up to Mount Sinai because you told us to set borders around the mountain and sanctify it."

And the Lord said to him, "Go get Aaron and bring him back with you but do not let the priests or the people break through the borders to come see the Lord or his anger will suddenly burst out against them."
So, Moses went down and spoke to the people.
Then God spoke to the people and said,
"I am your Lord God, and I brought you out of Egypt and bondage to the Egyptians.
Do not worship other gods before me.
Do not make graven images or likenesses of anything in heaven above, the earth below, or the water underneath the earth.
Do not bow down nor worship them because I am a jealous God. I will punish the children for the sins of the fathers to the third and fourth generation of those who hate me.
The Lord God will show mercy to the thousands who keep my commandments and love me.
Do not take your Lord God's name in vain, because I will not hold those who take my name in vain guiltless.
Remember to keep the Sabbath day holy.
You must labor and do all of your work in six days.

But the seventh day is your Lord God's Sabbath, and you must not do any work on the seventh day. Do not let your sons, daughters, male or female servants, your cattle, or any strangers that live with you do any work either.
Because your Lord God made the heavens, the earth, the oceans, and everything in them in only six days, and he rested on the seventh day because he blessed the Sabbath day and made it holy.
Honor your father and mother, so that you may live a long life on the land which your Lord God has given you.
Do not kill.
Do not commit adultery.
Do not steal.
Do not tell lies about your neighbor.
Do not covet your neighbors' wife, house, male or female servants, oxen, donkeys nor anything else that belongs to your neighbors."
The people saw the thunder and lightning, and they heard the trumpet, and when they saw the smoking mountain they stood way back.
And they said to Moses, "Talk to us and we will listen but do not let God speak to us or we will all die."
And Moses said to the people, "Fear not, because God has come to test you, so that you will fear him and you will not sin."
The people stood far away, and Moses moved closer to the thick darkness where God was.
And the Lord said to Moses, "Tell the Israelis that you have seen and talked with me from heaven.
Do not cast silver or gold gods for yourselves.
Make an earthen altar where you can sacrifice your burnt offerings, peace offerings, sheep, and your oxen to me. And wherever I record my name I will come to you and bless you.
If you build a stone altar for me, do not build it out of carved stone because carving the stone you will pollute it.
Do not walk up to my altar on steps or your nakedness will be exposed.
And God said, "These are the laws that I want you to give the people.
If you buy a male Hebrew servant, he may serve you for six years but in the seventh year he must be allowed to leave and pay you nothing.
If he came alone, he must leave alone but if he was married when he came to you, then his wife will be allowed to leave with him.
If his master gave him a wife and she gave birth to his children, then the wife and her children will belong to her master and he must leave alone.
If the servant plainly states, 'I love my master, my wife, and my children, and I am not going to leave them behind to become a free man.'
If he stays, he must go to court with his master and stand next to the court's door post, and the judge will publicly bore a hole in his ear with an awl, and he will serve his master forever.
If a man sells his daughter as a servant, she will not be allowed to leave her master the way the male servants do.
If she marries her master and she does not please him, then he must let her be redeemed. He will not be allowed to sell her in a foreign country because he did not deal honestly with her.
If she marries her master's son, he must treat her like a daughter.
If he takes another wife, he must not diminish her food, clothes, or marital duties.
If he does not provide these things for her, then she will be given her freedom and allowed to leave without having to pay him money.
Anyone who kills another person must be put to death.
If they did not plan to kill that person but God let it happen anyway, then God will provide them a place to flee.
But if an arrogant person deceitfully plans to kill their neighbor, they must be removed from my altar and put to death.
Anyone who kills their father or mother must be put to death.
Anyone who steals a servant for their own profit or sells them must be put to death.
Anyone who curses their father or mother must be put to death.
If two people fight and one of them beats the other person with a stone or their fists, and the loser is bedridden but does not die.
And if the injured party can walk around outside, even if they have to use a staff, then the responsible party will have to pay for their loss of time until they are completely healed.
If someone beats their servants or maids to death with a rod, they must be punished.
But, if their servant recovers after a day or two, they will not be punished because the servant is his master's property.
If anyone fights and hurts a pregnant woman and her child is born prematurely, the guilty party must pay whatever the woman's husband demands, if the judge determines that it is a fair settlement.
If any further injury happens, then you must give a life for a life.
An eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth, a hand for a hand, and a foot for a foot.
Burning for burning, wound for wound, and injury for injury.
If someone blinds their servant or their maid, they must set them free because they blinded them.
If someone knocks their servant or maid's tooth out, they must set them free because they knocked their tooth out.
If an ox gores someone and they die, then the ox will be stoned to death and his flesh must not be eaten, but the owner of the ox will be held responsible.
But, if an ox gores someone because the owner did not keep it fenced in and it kills someone else, the ox and his owner must both be stoned to death.
If financial compensation is demanded from the ox's owner, they must pay whatever is demanded in order to redeem themselves.
Even if the ox gored the owner's son or daughter, the owner must be judged in accordance with this law.
If an ox gores a servant, the ox's owner must give the servant's master thirty silver shekels, and the ox must be stoned to death.
If a man opens or digs a pit, and leaves it uncovered and an ox or donkey falls into it.
The owner of the pit will make it good and pay restitution to the damaged party, and the dead beast will belong to the owner of the pit.
If anyone's ox hurts someone else's ox and it dies, then they must sell their own live ox and divide the money between them, and the meat from the dead ox will be divided between them.
If anyone's ox gored anything in the past and the ox's owner did not keep it fenced in, the owner must repay the injured party with a living ox, and the dead ox will belong to them."
And God said, "If someone steals an ox or a sheep and kills it or sells it, they must repay the victim with five oxen for each stolen ox, and four sheep for each stolen sheep.
If a thief is caught breaking into a place and is killed, the person who killed the thief will be innocent of shedding the thief's blood.

If the sun has risen and the thief is killed; the homeowner will be guilty of killing the thief. If a thief is caught, they must make full restitution for what they have stolen, but if they have nothing they may be sold into slavery for stealing.
If a stolen ox, donkey, or sheep is found alive in the thief's possession the thief must repay twice the value of what was stolen.
If someone lets their animal overgraze their field or vineyard and puts the animal in someone else's field, they must make restitution to the owner from the best of their own field or vineyard.
If a fire breaks out and spreads to the berry bushes, stacked wheat, standing wheat, or any other fields and it is consumed, then whoever started the fire will be required to make restitution.
If someone gives money or something of value to someone else to manage and it is stolen and the thief is caught, then the thief must repay twice the amount they stole.
If the thief is not found, then the homeowner must be brought to court to determine whether or not they stole their neighbor's possessions.

If there is a dispute over who owns something whether it is an ox, a donkey, a sheep, clothes, or anything else of value, both parties must appear in court. Whoever the judge decides against must repay the owner twice the value of the property in dispute.
If someone brings a donkey, an ox, a sheep, or any other animal to their neighbor to care for and it dies, or it is hurt or driven away and there are no witnesses.

They must make an earnest promise to each other and the neighbor must promise the Lord that they did not lose or steal their neighbor's property. The owner must accept it, and they will not be required to pay restitution to their neighbor.
If it is stolen, the neighbor must make restitution to the owner.
If the owner's animal is torn to pieces by a predator, they must take it for their neighbor to see it, and they will not be required to pay restitution.
If someone borrows an animal from their neighbor, and it gets hurt while it is in their possession, the borrower must pay restitution to the owner.
But if the owner is present, the borrower is not required to pay restitution. If the owner is paid for the use of the animal, then the payment made to hire the animal will cover any losses.
If a man tempts an unmarried woman into having sexual intercourse, he must marry the woman.
If her father absolutely refuses to let her marry him, he must pay her the full amount of a virgin's dowry.
Do not allow a witch to live.
Anyone who has sex with any kind of animal must be put to death.
Anyone who sacrifices to any god except for the Lord will be destroyed.
Do not mistreat strangers nor oppress them because you were once strangers in Egypt.
Do not take advantage of a widow or an orphan.
If you take advantage of them in any way and they cry out to me, I will surely hear them.
Which will kindle my anger, and I will kill you with a sword, your wives will become widows, and your children will be orphaned.
If you lend money to poor people, do not make them pay interest and do not be a greedy banker.
If you take your neighbor's garments as collateral for a loan, return the garments to them before the sun goes down.
If those garments are the only clothes that they own, what will they sleep in? When they cry out to me, I will hear them because I am a gracious God.
Do not curse the gods nor the leaders of your people.
Do not delay in offering me your first ripe fruits, your first wine, or your firstborn sons, because you must bring them to me.
And do not delay in offering me your oxen and sheep either, you can leave them with their mothers for seven days, but on the eighth day, you must bring them to me.
You will be my holy people, but you must not eat the meat from an animal killed by predators, throw it to the dogs instead."
And God said, "Do not make false reports and do not lie for the wicked.
Do not follow the crowd or participate in their evil. Do not support a dishonest or deceitful cause or side with the crowd to force a dishonest judgment.
Do not show favoritism to poor people just because they are poor.
If you see your enemy's ox or donkey going astray, you must bring it back to them.
If someone hates you and you see that their heavily loaded donkey has collapsed, do not ignore them but help them with their animal.
Do not deny justice to the cause of the poor.
Stay away from false claims, and do not kill an innocent righteous person, because I will not justify the wicked.
Do not accept a gift because the gift blinds the wise and perverts the words of the righteous.
Do not oppress strangers, for you know what is in their heart because you were once a stranger in Egypt.
Sow your land for six years and gather the fruit at harvest time.
But in the seventh year let your field, vineyard, and olive groves rest and lie fallow, so that your people may eat from it and the field animals can have whatever is left.
You must work for six days, and rest on the seventh day so that your ox, donkey, your maid's son, and any of your employees can rest and be refreshed.
You must be cautious about everything I have warned you about, and do not call on other gods or even mention their names.
Hold a feast for me three times a year.

Celebrate the Seven Day Feast of Unleavened Bread in the first month of the year. As I told you, it must be celebrated in the month of Abib because that is the month you left Egypt. Bring me an offering for the feast when you come.
At the end of the year, gather and harvest your first fruits and everything else you have sown in the field and celebrate the harvest feast.
Your males must appear before the Lord God three times a year.
Do not offer my blood sacrifice with leavened bread, and none of the leftovers from my fat sacrifice must be left until the next morning.
Bring the first fruits of your harvest into your Lord God's house. Do not boil a kid goat in its mother's milk.
Behold, I will send an angel to guide you and show you the way to the place I have prepared for you.
Listen to this angel, do what he says, and do not provoke him because my name is in him and he will not pardon you.
If you listen to the angel and do everything I tell you to do, then I will be an enemy to your enemies.
And, I will cut them off when my angel leads you to the land of the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
Do not bow down to their gods, do not serve them or do the things that they do, but overthrow them and destroy their graven images.
If you serve your Lord God, I will bless you with food and water and take away any sickness among you.
And your women will not be barren or have miscarriages, and I will give you a long full life.
I will send my fear ahead of you and confuse the people you encounter, and I will make your enemies run away.
I will send hornets ahead of you to drive the Hivites, Canaanites, and Hittites away from you.
I will not drive all of them out of the land at the same time because the land would become desolate because too many field animals would multiply, and you would have too many animals to care for.
Little by little I will drive them out ahead of you until you have increased enough to inherit the land.
Your borders will range from the Red Sea to the Mediterranean Sea, and from the desert to the Euphrates River. I will deliver the inhabitants to you, and you will drive them out of the land.
Do not make covenants with them or their gods.
They must not live in your land because they may make you sin against me, and if you serve their gods, you will be caught in a trap."
The Lord spoke to Moses and said, "I want Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and seventy of Israel's elders to come here and worship me from a distance.
Moses is the only one allowed to come near the Lord, he must come alone because other people are not allowed to come near me."
Moses told the people about the Lord's judgments, and they all answered with one voice and said, "We will do whatever the Lord wants."
Moses wrote down everything the Lord said, and he got up early the next morning, and built an altar with twelve stone columns at the foot of the mountain to represent the twelve tribes of Israel.
Then Moses sent Israel's young men to sacrifice their oxen and make burnt offerings and peace offerings to the Lord.
Moses took half of the sacrificial blood and poured it in the sinks and sprinkled the other half on the altar.
He read God's Book of the Covenant to the people and they said, "We will do whatever the Lord wants."
Then Moses took the sacrificial blood and sprinkled it on the people and said, "This is the blood that binds the Lord's word between you and him."
Then Moses, Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and seventy of Israel's elders went to see the Lord.
When they got there, they saw Israel's God and under his feet was a path paved with sapphires and it was as clear as the heavens.
God did not touch Israel's noble children and when they saw him, they ate and drink with him.

And the Lord said to Moses, "Come up into the mountains with me and I will give you stone tablets engraved with the laws and commandments that I have written for you, and you can teach them to the people.
So Moses and Joshua left and went up into God's mountain.
And Moses spoke to the elders and said, "Wait for us here, Aaron and Hur will stay with you and if any of you have any disagreements with each other, you can ask them about it.
Then Moses went up into God's cloud covered mountain.
God's glory lived high up on Mount Sinai, and it was covered by the cloud for six days, on the seventh day he spoke to Moses from the middle of the cloud.
To the Israelis, God's glory looked like a fire devouring the top of the mountain.
Moses stayed on top of God's cloud covered mountain for forty days and forty nights.
Then the Lord spoke to Moses again and said,
"Speak to the Israelis and tell them that everyone must willingly give you a heartfelt offering to bring to me.
These are the offerings that you may accept from them; Gold, silver, and brass.
Blue, purple, and scarlet fine linen and goat's hair.
Red dyed ram skins, badger skins, and shittim wood.
Lamp oil, spices the for anointing oil and sweet incense.
And bring onyx stones and other stones that will be used to set in the priest's jeweled robe and vest.
And they can build a sanctuary for me, so that I may live among them.
I will give you a design and show you how to build the sanctuary and its furnishings.
Tell them to build a shittim wood ark two and one-half cubits long, one and one-half cubits wide, and one and one-half cubits high.
Overlay it inside and out including the crown moldings with pure gold.
Cast four gold rings and put them in the four corners of the ark, two of them on each side of the ark.
Make two shittim wood poles overlaid with gold.
Put the poles into the rings on each side of the ark to carry it.
The poles must be permanently attached to the ark's rings so they cannot be removed.
Put the testimony that I am going to give you into the ark.
Make a solid gold Mercy Seat, two and one-half cubits long, and one and one-half cubits wide to cover the ark.
Make two cherubs out of hammered gold for the ends of the Mercy Seat.
Attach one cherub to each end of the Mercy Seat.
The cherubs and the Mercy Seat should be made from one solid piece of gold with a cherub on each end of the Mercy Seat.
Put the Mercy Seat on top of the ark and put the testimony that I am going to give to you in the ark.

I will meet with you and speak with you there between the two cherubs above the Mercy Seat. The Mercy Seat will cover the ark that will contain all the commandments I am going to give to the Israelis.
You must also make a shittim wood table, two cubits long, a cubit wide, and one and one-half cubits tall.
Overlay it with pure gold and decorate it with gold crown moldings.
Make a border all around it that is one hand wide with a crown molding made of gold attached to the border.
Make four gold rings and attach them to the four corners above its four feet.
Attach the rings to the table's border and the poles will be inserted in the rings to carry the table.
Make the poles out of shittim wood, overlay them with gold and they will be used to carry the table.
Make solid gold dishes, spoons, and vessels for the drink offering.
Set the priest's bread offerings on the table before me.
Hammer a pure gold metal sheet into the shape of a lampstand including its shaft, cup, branches, buds, and flowers.
Make six branches for the lampstand with three branches on each side.
Make three cups that look like almond flower blossoms for each of the lampstand's six branches, attach three of them to each branch.
The lampstands must have four cups shaped like almond flower blossoms.
Make and attach flower buds under each of the lampstand's branches.
The branches and buds must be identical and all of them must be hammered out of one solid sheet of pure gold
Make seven lamps and arrange them so that they illuminate the space in front of the ark.
Make the ark's tongs and candle snuffers out of pure gold.
Make each cup out of one talent's worth of pure gold.
Use the designs you were shown on the mountain to make the cups."
And the Lord said, "Along with the skillfully crafted tabernacle cherubs that you make, you must also make ten blue, purple, and scarlet fine twined linen curtains.
Each curtain must be 28 cubits long and 4 cubits wide.
Sew five curtains together to make one curtain.
Sew blue loops to the end edge of each curtain where they are sewn together.
Attach fifty loops to each curtain, so that the loops are interconnected with each other.
Make fifty gold buckles and clip the tabernacle curtains together with them so that all the curtains joined together make one curtain.
Make eleven goat hair curtains as a tent to cover the tabernacle.
All the curtains must be identical, make them thirty cubits long and four cubits wide.
Join five curtains together, join the other six curtains together and fold the edge of the last curtain twice and put it on the front of the tabernacle.
Make fifty loops on the outer edge of each curtain to join them together.
Make fifty brass buckles and put the buckles into the loops to couple them together into one tent.
The half curtain that remains will hang over the back of the tabernacle.
The remaining tent curtains will hang down one cubit or about eighteen inches on each side of the tabernacle.
Cover the tent with red dyed ram skins and cover the top with badger skins.
Construct a rigid framework for the tabernacle out of shittim wood boards.
The framework boards must be ten cubits long, and a cubit and a half wide.
Make all of the tabernacle boards identical with two tenons on each end of each board.
Make twenty boards for the south side of the tabernacle.
Make forty silver foundations and put two of them under each board on the south side.
Make twenty boards for the northern side of the tabernacle.
Make forty more silver foundations and put two of them under each board on the north side.
Make six more boards for the west side of the tabernacle.
Make two boards for each corner of the tabernacle's west side.
Connect the top and bottom of each of the corner boards together with one ring.
Make five shittim wood crossbars for each board on the east side of the tabernacle.
Make five shittim wood crossbars for each board on the west side of the tabernacle.
Make five shittim wood crossbars for each of the boards on west side of the tabernacle.
The middle crossbar will reach from the middle of each board from one end to the other.
Make gold rings to fit the crossbars and overlay the boards and crossbars with gold.
Erect the tabernacle the way the Lord showed you on the mountain.
Make a blue, purple, and scarlet veil of fine twined linen with cherubs skillfully woven into it.
Hang it on four gold overlaid shittim wood columns with gold hooks that sit on four silver bases.
Hang the veil under the buckles and place the Ark of the Covenant behind the veil to separate the Holy Place from the Most Holy Place.
Put the Mercy Seat on the ark in the Most Holy Place.
Place the table outside the veil on the tabernacle's north wall and place the lampstand next to the tabernacle's south wall.
Make the tent door out of blue, purple, and scarlet fine twined linen embroidered with fine needlework.
Make five gold overlaid shittim wood columns with five brass bases and gold hooks for the tent door."
And the Lord said, "Make a square shittem wood altar five cubits long, five cubits wide, and three cubits high.
Make equal sized brass overlaid horns for each of the altar's four corners.
Make bronze ash pans and utensils to remove the ashes from the altar.
Make a brass grate with four brass rings attached to its four corners.
Put it under the altar's ledge about halfway down.
Make brass overlaid shittim wood poles for the altar.
Put the poles into the rings on each side of the altar to support it.
Use the boards to make the hollow altar the way you were shown on the mountain.
Make the curtains that cover the tabernacle court's south wall 100 cubits long and weave them out of fine linen thread.
Attach twenty brass bases with hooks and silver bands to the columns for hanging the linen curtains.
Make the linen curtains for the north side wall 100 cubits long, each with 20 columns and 20 brass hooks with silver bands.
On the tabernacle court's west side hang linen curtains that are fifty cubits long with ten columns and ten bases.
The east side of the tabernacle court must be fifty cubits long.
The linen curtains on each side of the gate will be fifteen cubits long with three columns and three bases.
Both sides of the tabernacle gate must have linen curtains that are fifteen cubits long, both with three columns and three bases.
The linen curtains for the court gate must be twenty cubits long and are to be made out of embroidered blue, purple, and scarlet fine twined linen with four columns and four bases.
All the columns around the court must be decorated with silver hooks and brass bases.
The court will be 100 cubits long and 50 cubits wide and it must be decorated with fine twined linen and brass bases.
All the tabernacle cups and pegs for the court will be made of brass.
Tell the Israelis to bring pure pressed light olive oil to you for the lamp so it can burn forever.

Aaron and his sons will bring the lamp before the Lord in the congregation's tabernacle outside the veil in front of the ark. It must burn every evening until the morning; this law must be observed by the Israelis and their descendants forever."
And the Lord said to Moses, "Separate your brother Aaron and his sons Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar apart from the other Israelis so that they may minister to me in the priest's office.
Make some beautiful, glorious, and holy garments for Aaron.
Speak to the wise hearted craftsmen and ask them to make these garments for Aaron so that he may be ordained as a priest and serve me in the priest's office.

Tell them that the holy garments they make for Aaron and his sons must include a jeweled vest, a robe, an embroidered coat, a ceremonial crown, and a belt so that they may minister to me in the high priest's office.
Tell them to use fine linen embroidered with gold, blue, purple, and scarlet yarn.
Tell them to carefully and skillfully make the robe out of gold, blue, purple, and scarlet fine twined linen.
It must be joined together at the edges with two shoulder pieces.
The robe's belt must be woven from the same fine twined gold, blue, purple, and scarlet linen and attach it to the vest.
Engrave the names of Israel's twelve children on two onyx stones.
Engrave six names on each stone in the order of their birth.
Engrave the two stones the way a jeweler would engrave a document seal and set them in gold settings like fine jewelry.
Put the two stones on each of the robe's two shoulders as a memorial to the Israelis, and Aaron will carry their names on his shoulders before the Lord.
Then make gold settings.
And two pure gold chains and fasten them to the ends of the settings.
Make the high priest's jeweled judgment vest the same way you make the robe. Use the same fine twined linen woven with gold, blue, purple, and scarlet yarn.
Make a double-folded pouch that is one span long and one span wide or about nine inches square.
Place four rows of stone settings on the pouch. The first row of stones should include a sardius, a topaz, and a carbuncle.
The pouch's second row should have an emerald, a sapphire, and a diamond.
The pouch's third row should have a ligure, an agate, and an amethyst.
And the pouch's fourth row should have a beryl, an onyx, and a jasper and they must be decorated with gold filigree.
Engrave the names of Israel's twelve children that the twelve tribes of Israel were named after on the stones like a finely engraved seal.
Make pure gold rope vest chains and attach them to the high priest's jeweled vest.
Make two gold rings for the high priest's jeweled vest and put one on each end of the vest.
Put the two gold chains in the two rings on the ends of the high priest's jeweled vest.
The other two ends of the gold chains must be fastened in two settings and attached to the robe's shoulder pieces.
Attach the gold rings to the high priest's jeweled vest on the inner side of the robe's border.
Attach the other two gold rings below the shoulder pieces near the seam where the robe is joined together above the belt.
Bind the rings of the high priest's jeweled vest to the robe's rings with blue lace above the robe's belt, to hold the vest securely to the robe.
Aaron will carry the names of the Israelis in the high priest's jeweled judgement vest over his heart when he goes into the Holy Place as an eternal memorial before the Lord.

Put the Urim and the Thummim in the high priest's jeweled judgement vest, and Aaron will carry them over his heart when he goes in before the Lord. Aaron will carry the judgment of the Israelis over his heart eternally before the Lord.
Make the entire robe blue.
Make an opening in the robe and weave a collar around it to prevent it from being torn apart.
Make blue, purple, and scarlet pomegranates all around the robe's hem with gold bells between them.
Attach the gold bells and pomegranates all around the robe's hem, alternating between the bells and the pomegranates.

Aaron must wear this robe when he goes into the Holy Place to minister before the Lord, and the sound of the tinkling bells will be heard by everyone when he goes in and when he comes out so that he will not die.
Make a solid gold plate and engrave "HOLINESS TO THE LORD"on it, like the engravings on a signet or document seal.
Attach a blue lace to it so it can be attached to the front of the priest's turban

Aaron will always wear it on his forehead to carry the iniquity of the holy gifts which the Israelis bring before the Lord. And it shall always be on his forehead so that the Lord may accept the gifts.
Embroider the priest's fine linen coat, turban, and belt with skillful needlework.
Make glorious and beautiful coats, belts, and hats for Aaron's sons
Your brother Aaron and his sons will anoint, consecrate, and sanctify them, so that they may minister to me in the priest's office.
Make short linen breeches that reach from their waist to their thighs to cover their nakedness.

This will be an eternal law for Aaron and his sons and descendants. They must wear the holy garments when they enter the congregation's tabernacle or come near the altar to minister in the Holy Place, so that they do not bear the full weight of sin and die."
And God said, "Take a young bull and two unblemished rams so Aaron and his sons can be made sacred in the Holy Place and serve me in the priest's office.
Make unleavened wheat bread, cakes, and wafers tempered and anointed with oil.
Put them in a basket, then bring the basket, the bull, and the rams to the Holy Place.
Aaron and his sons will wash them with water and bring them to the congregation's tabernacle door.
Then they must put the holy garments including the jeweled vest, coat, robe, and belt on Aaron.
Then put the ceremonial turban with the holy crown on his head.
Pour the anointing oil on Aaron's head and anoint him.
And put coats his sons.
Then they must consecrate Aaron and his sons and clothe them with belts and put hats on them, and by law they will be given the priest's office for all of eternity.
And bring a bull before the congregation's tabernacle where Aaron and his sons will lay their hands on the bull's head.
Then kill the bull before the Lord by the door of the congregation's tabernacle.
Dip your finger in the bull's blood and use it to mark the horns of the altar and pour the rest of the blood at the bottom of the altar.
Take the bull's fat above the liver that covers the intestines and the kidneys and burn them on the altar.
Burn the bull's flesh, skin, and dung in a fire outside the camp as a sin offering.
Aaron and his sons will lay their hands on the head of the ram that you bring them.
Kill the ram and sprinkle his blood all around and on the altar.
Cut the ram into pieces, wash the legs and internal organs and put them aside with the head and other parts.
Burn the whole ram on the altar as a sweet and savory offering to the Lord.
Aaron and his sons will lay their hands on the head of the other ram.
Then kill the ram and mark the tip of Aaron and his sons' right ear and thumb and the big toe on their right foot, then sprinkle the blood on and all around the altar.
Take some of the blood that is on the altar, mix it with the anointing oil and sprinkle it on Aaron and his sons' and their garments. Then he and his sons and their garments will be holy.
Then take the ram's fat, rump, the fat that covers its inner organs, the caul above its liver, its kidneys, its right shoulder, and all the other fat because its a consecration ram.
Take a loaf of bread, an oiled bread cake, and a wafer out of the basket of unleavened bread that is before the Lord.
Put it all into Aaron and his sons' hands and they will wave it as a wave offering before the Lord.
Take their bread offering and burn it on the altar as a burnt offering, because it will be a sweet and savory offering to the Lord.
Take the breast from Aaron's consecration ram and wave it before the Lord as a wave offering and it will be your portion.

Sanctify the breast of the wave offering which is waved before the Lord and the shoulder of the sacred offering which is lifted up to the Lord from the consecration ram from Aaron and his sons' portion.
By law Aaron, his sons', and the Israelis must make the sacred sacrificial offerings and peace offerings to the Lord.
Aaron's holy garments will be anointed and declared sacred and passed down to his sons and his descendants.
The son that replaces him as the priest will wear the holy garments for seven days when he comes into the congregation's tabernacle to minister in the Holy Place.
Take the consecration ram and boil his flesh in the Holy Place.
Aaron and his sons will eat the meat from the ram and the bread that is in the basket near the congregation's tabernacle door.
They may eat whatever they want from the atonement's consecrated offering. Sanctify and ordain them because they are holy and nobody else is allowed to eat from the consecrated offering.
If any of the meat or bread from the consecrations is leftover the next morning, burn it in a fire and do not eat it because it is holy.
You must do everything I have told you to do to Aaron and his sons and consecrate them for seven days.
Offer a bull every day as a sin offering to cleanse the altar and for the atonement of sin. After you have made the sin atonement, anoint the altar to sanctify it.
Make atonement for the altar and sanctify it for seven days and it will be the holiest altar, and anything that touches it will be holy.
Every day you must offer two, one year old lambs on the altar.
One lamb in the morning and one in the evening.
With the morning lamb offer 1/10th of a deal of flour mixed with 1/4th of a hin of olive oil.
Offer the other lamb in the evening the same way you do in the morning because the burnt offerings are sweet and savory aromas to the Lord.
Aaron and his descendants must continue to make this burnt offering at the congregation's tabernacle door throughout eternity, because that's where I will meet with you and speak to you.
And I will meet with the Israelis there and the tabernacle will be sanctified by my glory.
I will sanctify Aaron and his sons, the congregation's tabernacle, and the altar, and they will minister to me in the priest's office.
And I will live among the Israelis, and I will be their God.
And they will know that I am the Lord their God, the God that brought them out of captivity in Egypt so that I may live among them, because I am their Lord God."
And God said, "Make an altar of shittim to burn incense on.
Make a cube two cubits long, two cubits wide, and two cubits high and make horns for it out of the same kind of wood.
Overlay its top, sides, and horns with pure gold and adorn it with gold crown moldings.
Make two gold rings and attach them to each side under the crown moldings for places to put the poles to carry it.
Make the poles out of shittim wood and overlay them with gold.
Put the altar in front of the veil that is next to the Ark of the Covenant in front of the Mercy Seat that covers the testimony, and that's where I will meet with you.
Every morning after Aaron fills the lamps he must burn sweet incense on the altar.
Aaron and his descendants must burn incense on the altar for God when they light the lamps every night, for all of eternity.
Do not offer anything else on the altar after lighting the lamps, do not make any sacrificial burnt offerings, no bread offerings, and no drink offering.
Aaron or his descendants must forever make atonement for the blood of sin on the altar's horns once a year because it is the holiest offering to the Lord."
Then the Lord spoke to Moses and said,
"Every year to prevent the spread of disease when you take the annual census of the Israelis, every man must pay a ransom to the Lord for his soul.
Everyone who is counted in the census must give 1/2 of a sanctuary shekel as a sin offering to the Lord.
Everyone counted in the census who is twenty years old or older must give an offering to the Lord.
Both the rich and poor, must give no more or no less than 1/2 of a shekel when they give an offering to the Lord as a sin atonement for their souls.
Take the atonement money from the Israelis and use it for the congregation's tabernacle service as a memorial to the Israelis, and to make a sin atonement for their souls before the Lord."
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said,
"Make a brass sink with brass feet and fill it with water to wash with and place it between the congregation's tabernacle and the altar.
Aaron and his sons will use it to wash their hands and feet.
They must wash their hands and feet when they go into the congregation's tabernacle, or they go near the altar to make a burnt offering before the Lord to prevent them from dying.
It shall be an eternal law for Aaron, his sons, and his descendants for generations to come to wash their hands and feet so that they do not die."
Then the Lord spoke to Moses and said,
"You should also take these spices, 500 silver, sanctuary shekels worth of pure myrrh, 250 shekels worth of sweet cinnamon, and 250 shekels worth of sweet calamus.
500 sanctuary shekels worth of cassia, and a hin of olive oil.
Make a holy oily ointment like the pharmacist makes, as a holy anointing oil.
Use the oil to anoint the congregation's tabernacle and the Ark of the Covenant that is inside it.
Anoint the table and lampstand along with all its vessels, utensils, and the incense altar.
Anoint the altar for burnt offerings with all of its vessels and utensils, and the brass sink with brass feet.
Sanctify them so they will be most holy and whatever touches them will be holy.
Anoint Aaron and his sons, consecrate them so they may minister to me in the priest's office.
Speak to the Israelis and say, 'This will be an eternal holy anointing oil to me from Aaron, his sons, and their descendants.'
There must not be any other compound like it, and it must not be poured onto a man's flesh because it is holy to you.
Whoever makes a compound like it or puts it on anyone other than a priest will be cut off from their people."
Then the Lord spoke to Moses again and said, "Take an equal measure of the sweet fragrant perfumes made from stacte, onycha, galbanum.
Make a perfume like a confection tempered together to be pure and holy the way the pharmacist does.
Grind some of it into very fine powder and put it in front of the Testimony in the congregation's tabernacle, where I will meet with you and it will be most holy to you.
Do not use this formula to make any of this perfume for yourselves because it will be holy for the Lord.
If anyone uses the formula to make something similar or they make something that smells like it, they will be cut off from their people."
Then the Lord spoke to Moses and said,
"Behold, I have called Bezalel the son of Uri and Hur from the tribe of Judah by his name.
I have filled him with the spirit of God and given him wisdom, understanding, knowledge, and all kinds of skill.
To skillfully work with gold, silver, and brass.
And cutting and setting stones, timber carving, and all kinds of other skills.
I have given him Ahisamach's son Aholiab from the tribe of Dan, and I have given many skills to everyone who is wise hearted, so that they can make everything that I have asked you to make.
Including the congregation's tabernacle, the Ark of the Covenant, the Mercy Seat behind the ark, and all the tabernacle's furniture.
And its table, the pure gold lampstand, its furniture, and the altar for incense.
And the burnt offerings altar, its furniture, and the brass sink with brass feet.
And the service clothes, the holy priest's garments for Aaron and his sons to minister in the priest's office.
And the anointing oil and sweet incense for the Holy Place made the way I told you to make them."
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said,

"You should also speak to the Israelis and say, 'Truly I tell you that you must keep my Sabbath because it is a sign between me, you, and your descendants so that you will know that I am the Lord who sanctifies you.
That's why you must keep the Sabbath because it is holy to you and anyone who defiles it will be put to death. Anyone who does any work on the Sabbath will surely be cut off from their people.
You may work for six days, but the seventh day is the Sabbath, and you must rest. The Sabbath is Holy to the Lord, and whoever does any work on the Sabbath will surely be put to death.'
That's why the Israelis and their descendants must keep the Sabbath and observe it for all of eternity because it is an eternal covenant between me, you, and them.
It is a sign that will last forever between me and the Israelis because in six days the Lord made heaven and earth, and on the seventh day he rested and was refreshed."
When God finished speaking to Moses on Mount Sinai, he gave Moses two stone tablets with ten commandments written on them that God himself had written with his finger.

When the people noticed that Moses was late returning from the mountain, they gathered together and went to Aaron and said, "Moses brought us out of Egypt, and now we do not know what happened to him. Cast some golden gods for us to carry out in front of us."
And Aaron replied to them and said, "Have your wives, sons, and daughters bring their gold earrings to me."
So all the people removed their gold earrings and brought them to Aaron.
Aaron took their gold earrings and cast a calf of molten gold and engraved it with an engraving tool. And they said, "O Israel, these are the gods who brought you out of Egypt."
When Aaron saw how exuberant the people were, he built an altar for the golden calf. Then he made a proclamation to the people and said, "Tomorrow there will be a feast for the Lord."
They got up early the next day and brought peace offerings and burnt offerings. Then the people sat down to eat and drink and began playing around.
And the Lord said to Moses, "The people that you brought out of Egypt have corrupted themselves. So go back down to them.

They have quickly turned away from what I have taught them, they made a calf of molten gold, and they have worshipped and made sacrifices to it and they said, "O Israel, these are the gods who brought us out of Egypt."
And the Lord said to Moses, "Behold, I have seen those stubborn people.
That's why I want you to leave me alone so that my anger can grow hot, then I will consume them and I will make you a great nation."
But Moses implored his Lord God and said, "Lord, why does your anger grow hot against the people you brought out of Egypt with great power and a mighty hand?

The Egyptians will speak against you and say that you brought them out of Egypt just to kill them in the mountains. That you consumed them and wiped them off the face of the earth. Please, control your fierce anger and do not do this evil to your people.

Remember your servants Abraham, Isaac, and Israel whom you swore to protect when you said to them, 'I will multiply your descendants like the stars of heaven, and I promise to give all of this land to your descendants, and they will inherit it forever.'"
Then the Lord changed his mind and decided not to bring the evil against his people which he had thought about and planned.
Then Moses left the mountain with the two stone tablets that God had written his commandments on.
The tablets were God's work; he had written them and carved them himself with his own two hands.
Joshua heard all the noise that the people were making as they shouted, and he said to Moses, "There is the noise of war within the camp."
And Moses said, "It is not the sound of victory or defeat that I hear, but it is the sound of singing.
Then as soon as he was near the camp, Moses saw them dancing around the calf and he was very angry, and he threw the tablets on the ground and broke them into pieces.
He took the calf that they had made, burned it in the fire, ground it into powder, scattered it on the water, and made the Israelis drink it.
And Moses said to Aaron, "What did these people tell you that made you bring such a great a sin against them?"
And Aaron replied, "Do not be so angry my Lord, you know that these people are intent on doing evil.
All the people came to me and said, 'Make gods for us to carry before us, because Moses brought us out of Egypt and we do not know what has happened to him.'
And I said to them, 'If anyone has any gold bring it to me. So, they gave me their gold, and I melted it in the fire and cast a golden calf.'"
Then Moses saw that Aaron had let the people run naked and out of control much to the amusement of their enemies.
Then Moses stood at the camp gate and said, "Whoever is on the Lord's side come to me," and all of Levi's sons gathered around him.
And he said to them, "The Lord God of Israel says for you to go throughout the camp and kill every man, his neighbor, his friends, and his brother with your swords."
Then Levi's children did what Moses told them to do and about 3,000 men died that day.
Because Moses had said, "Today you have been enlisted into the Lord's service and he will bestow a blessing upon every man, his sons, and his brothers."
The next day, Moses spoke to the people and said, "You have committed a great sin and now I am going up to the Lord, and maybe I can make atonement for your sins."
Moses returned to the Lord and said, "Oh Lord, these people have committed a great sin, and they made golden gods for themselves.
Please forgive their sin if you can, but if you cannot, I ask that you erase my name from that book you have written."
And the Lord said to Moses, "I will erase the name of whoever has sinned against me from my book.
So go and my Angel will guide you and lead the people to the place I told you about, but when I come to visit, I will discipline them for their sin."
And the Lord plagued the people because they made Aaron cast a golden calf to worship.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said, "Leave this place and take the people that you brought out of Egypt, and go to the land that I promised to give Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and their descendants.
I will send an angel to lead you, and I will drive out the Canaanites, Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
It is a land flowing with milk and honey, but I am not going there with you because you are stubborn people, and I might get angry with you along the way."
When the people heard these sober words they began to mourn, and nobody wore their dress clothes or jewelry.

Because the Lord had said to Moses, "Tell the Israelis that they are stubborn people, and I am not going to spend time with them right now because they will make me very angry. Tell them to remove their jewelry and fine clothes and I will decide what to do with them later."
The Israelis were near Mount Horeb, and they removed their jewelry and dress clothing.
Then Moses pitched the congregation's tabernacle tent far away from the camp and he called it the congregation's tabernacle and everyone who sought the Lord went there.
When Moses went to the tabernacle everyone got up and stood in their tent doorway and watched him go into the tabernacle.
As Moses entered the tabernacle, a column of cloud descended and stood by the tabernacle door where the Lord talked with Moses.
All the people saw the column of cloud standing at the tabernacle door, and they all stood up and worshipped the Lord in their tent doorway.
Then the Lord spoke to Moses face to face as a friend would speak to a friend. When Moses left the tabernacle to return to the camp, his servant Joshua, who was Nun's son did not leave with him.

Moses said to the Lord, "Look, you told me to bring these people up here, but you have not told me who you will send with me. You also said, 'I know you by name Moses, and you have found favor in my sight.'

That's why I have been praying for your approval of me and for you to teach me your ways, so I will know you and I will know that you approve of me, and then you will consider this nation to be your people."
And the Lord said, "I will go with you, and my presence will give you rest."
And Moses said to him, "If you do not go with me, please do not make us leave this place.

Because all the people on earth will know that this is where your people and I have found grace in your sight? Everyone on earth will know that you are with us, and there will be a distinct difference between them and us."
And the Lord said to Moses, "I will do what you ask, because you have found grace in my sight and I know you by name."
And Moses said, "I beg you to show me your glory."

And God said, "I will show you all my goodness and I will proclaim the name of the Lord before you, and I will have mercy for those to whom I will have mercy, and I will have compassion for those to whom I will have compassion."
And God said, "You cannot see my face, because no man can see me and live."
And the Lord said, "Behold there is a place for you by my side, and you will stand on a rock.
And I will put you in a cleft of the rock and cover you with my hand while my goodness passes by.
Then I will move my hand, and you will see me from behind, but you will not see my face."
Then the Lord said to Moses, "Carve two stone tablets like the ones you broke, and I will rewrite them with the same words that were on the first tablets.
Get up early in the morning and come to me on top of Mount Sinai.
Make sure you come alone, I do not want to see anyone else on the mountain, and I do not want them feeding their flocks or herds at the foot of the mountain either."

Moses did what the Lord told him to do, and he carved two stone tablets just like the first two. The next morning, he got up early in the morning and went to Mount Sinai and he took the tablets with him.
The Lord descended in a cloud and Moses stood with him and proclaimed the name of the Lord.
The Lord passed before him and Moses declared the Lord God to be merciful, gracious, long suffering, with an abundance of goodness and truth.

He has mercy for thousands, he forgives immorality and transgression, he corrects the guilty and he reveals the immorality of the fathers to the children and their children's children, all the way down to the third and fourth generations.
Then Moses bowed facedown and worshipped God.

And Moses said, "O Lord, if you have found me to be a good person, I pray that you will go with us because these are stubborn people and I beg you to pardon our immorality and sin and accept us as we are."

And God said," Behold, I will make a covenant with you and your people. I will show them miracles that have never been seen by any nation on earth before. I will show you and everyone with you the amazing power of the Lord.
And if you do everything that I told you to do, I will drive the Amorites, Canaanites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and the Jebusites out before you.
Do not make a covenant with the people living there because it could be a trap.
Destroy their altars, break their images, and cut down their Asherah poles.
You must not worship other gods because the Lord is a jealous God.
This is to prevent you from making covenants with the people there and to prevent you from whoring and sacrificing to their gods and eating from the sacrifices to their gods.
And when their daughters marry your sons, and their daughters go whoring after their gods, they will make your sons go whoring after their gods too.
Do not cast any gods of molten metal.
Keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread for seven days in the month of Abib because you left Egypt in the month of Abib.
The firstborn male from the matrix is mine including all of your firstborn oxen, cattle, or sheep.

You must rescue a firstborn donkey by offering a lamb as payment and if you do not rescue it, you must break its neck. You must rescue all your firstborn sons and none of them will be allowed to appear before me empty-handed.
You must work for six days and rest on the seventh day, even during the plowing and harvest seasons.
Celebrate the Feast of Weeks when the first wheat harvest comes in and celebrate the Feast of Final Harvest at the end of the year.
Three times a year, all of your male children must appear before the Lord God of Israel.
I will drive the nations out in front of you and enlarge your borders, nobody will want your land if you appear before the Lord God three times a year.
Do not offer the Passover blood sacrifice with leavened bread and do not leave any leftovers from the feast until the next morning.
Bring the first fruits of your harvest to your Lord God's house, and do not boil a kid goat in his mother's milk."
And the Lord spoke to Moses again and said, "Write this down because I have made a covenant with you and Israel with these words."
Moses spent forty days and forty nights with the Lord God and he did not eat nor drink. And God wrote the ten commandments on the stone tablets, which is the covenant with the Lord God.

When Moses came down from Mount Sinai he carried the stone tablets with the ten commandments with him, and he had no idea that his face and skin were glowing because he had been talking with the Lord.
When Aaron and all the Israelis saw Moses, his face and skin glowed brilliantly, and they were afraid to go near him.
Moses called out to Aaron and all the rulers from the congregation, and they all came and talked with him.
Then all of the Israelis people came near, and he gave them the commandments that the Lord had given him on Mount Sinai.
Moses put a veil over his face until he had finished speaking with them.
But when he went to talk to the Lord, he removed the veil and when he came out, he told the Israelis everything that the Lord had told him.
When the Israelis saw that Moses' face and skin were glowing, he put the veil back over his face until he went back to speak to the Lord again.
Moses gathered the entire Israeli congregation together and said to them, "These are the ten commandments which the Lord wants you to keep.
You must work for six days and rest on the seventh day which is the Sabbath. The Sabbath will be a holy day for the Lord to rest, anyone who works on that day will suffer the consequences.
You must not build a fire in your homes on the Sabbath day."
And Moses spoke to all of the Israelis and said, "The Lord has told us.
That whoever is willing should take an offering of gold, silver, and brass to the Lord.
And fine linen made of blue, purple, and scarlet goats' hair.
And red dyed ram skins, badger skins, and shittim wood.
And lamp oil and spices for the anointing oil and sweet incense.
And onyx stones for the high priest's robe and jeweled vest.
Every wise hearted person among you must make everything that the Lord commands.
Including the tabernacle and its tent, clothes, buckles, boards, crossbars, columns, and bases.
The ark and its poles, the Mercy Seat, and the covering veil.
The table and its poles, all of its vessels and the priest's bread offering.
The lampstand for the lamps and its furniture, and lamps with oil for the light.
The incense altar and its poles, anointing oil, sweet incense, and curtains for the tabernacle's entrance door.
The altar for burnt offerings with its brass grate, poles, vessels, and the brass sink with brass feet.
The court's wall curtains and its columns, the column's bases, and the curtains for the court's door.
The pegs and cords for the tabernacle's court.
Service clothes for the holy lace and holy garments for Aaron and his sons to wear when they minister in the priest's office."
Then the Israeli congregation left Moses and went to work.
And everyone with a willing heart and spirit brought offerings for the Lord's work, for the service of the congregation's tabernacle, and for the sacred garments.
Men and women who were willing brought gold bracelets, earrings, rings, tablets, and jewelry as a gold offering to the Lord.
Everyone who had woven fine linen with blue, purple, and scarlet goats' hair, red ram skins, and badger skins brought them to the Lord.
Everyone who was willing made a brass and silver offering to the Lord, and everyone who had shittim wood brought it for the tabernacle.
All the wise hearted women spun blue, purple, and fine scarlet linens, and brought it to the Lord.
And all the wise hearted women also spun goats' hair.
All the rulers brought onyx stones ready to be set for the priest's robe and jeweled vest.
They all brought spices, lamp oil, and anointing oil for the sweet incense.
All the Israeli children who were willing, brought an offering to the Lord. Everyone with a willing heart brought all kinds of work which the Lord had asked Moses to have hand made.
And Moses spoke to the Israeli children and said, "Look, the Lord has called Uri and Hur's son Bezalel from the tribe of Judah.
And God has filled Bezalel with a wise understanding spirit, and the knowledge of all types of skillful workmanship.
God has given him the ability to do all types of creative work in gold, silver, and brass.
God has taught him how to cut and set stones, carve wood, and how to do many other kinds of skillful work.
Besides Bezalel, God also had it in his heart to teach Ahisamach's son Aholiab, who was from the tribe of Dan.

God endowed both of them with wise hearts and the skills to do all types of creative work. God taught them engraving, how to weave fine linen and how to embroider it with blue, purple, and scarlet thread. And God gave them all the skills they needed to create all types of skillful work.
Then Bezalel, Aholiab, and every other man that God had endowed with a wise and understanding heart went to work. They started building the sanctuary the way the Lord wanted it built.
Moses asked Bezalel, Aholiab, and all the other men to whom the Lord had given wisdom to come and help build the sanctuary.
Moses gave them the offerings that the Israelis had brought for them to use to build the sanctuary, and the Israelis freely brought more offerings to them every morning.
One day everyone working on the sanctuary stopped and went to see Moses.
They spoke to Moses and said, "The people have brought us more offerings than we need to build the Lord's sanctuary."

Then Moses spoke to them and word was spread throughout the camp that Moses said, "Do not bring any more offerings to build the temple." So, they stopped making things and did not bring anything else for the sanctuary.
Because everything they had already made was more than enough to finish the job.
The many wise hearted men who worked on the tabernacle skillfully made ten blue, purple, and scarlet fine twined linen curtains with cherubim.
All the curtains were the same size, 28 cubits long and 4 cubits wide.
Five curtains were connected together, and the other five curtains were also connected together.
Then Bezalel made blue fabric loops which were attached along the seam of the curtains where they were joined together.
And he made 50 loops for each curtain that held them all together.
And he also made 50 gold buckles that connected all the curtains together into one continuous piece as one tabernacle.
And he made 11 goat hair curtains for the tent that covered the tabernacle.
Each of the 11 curtains were 34 cubits wide.
Bezalel connected five curtains together into one assembly, and six curtains into the other assembly.
And he made 50 loops on the outermost edge of the first curtain, and 50 loops along the edge of the second curtain where the two curtains were connected.
And he made 50 brass buckles to connect the tent into one piece.
And he dyed a ram skin red, to cover the tent and he used a badger skin as a cover above that.
And he made shittim wood boards to support the tabernacle.
Each board was ten cubits long and one and one-half cubits wide.
All the boards for the tabernacle had two equally spaced tenons at the bottom.
And he made 20 boards for the south side of the tabernacle.
And he made 40 silver bases, one for each of the two tenons for the bottom of each board.
And he made 20 boards for the north side of the tabernacle.
And 40 silver bases for the bottom of each board.
Bezalel made six boards for the west side of the tabernacle.
And he made two boards for the corners of two sides of the tabernacle.
hey were connected together with one ring at the top and the bottom of each corner.
There were eight boards and 16 silver bases with two bases under the bottom of each board.
Bezalel made five shittim wood crossbars for the boards on one side of the tabernacle.
And five crossbars for the boards on the west side of the tabernacle.
And he made the middle crossbar to go through the boards from one end to the other.
And he overlaid the boards with gold, he made gold rings for the boards to hold the crossbars, and the crossbars were overlaid with gold.
And he made a fine twined linen woven with blue, purple, and scarlet for the veil and skillfully covered it with cherubim.
And he made four shittim wood columns overlaid with gold with gold hooks and cast four silver bases for it.
And he made a fine twined linen curtain embroidered with blue, purple, and scarlet to hang over the tabernacle door.
Finally, Bezalel overlaid the five column caps and the hooks and bands with pure gold, but the five bases were made of brass.
Bezalel made a shittim wood ark two and one-half cubits long, one and one-half cubits wide, and a one and one-half cubits high.
He overlaid it inside and out with pure gold and made gold crown moldings all around it.
He cast four gold rings for its four corners, two rings on each side.
He made shittim wood poles overlaid with gold.
He put the poles into the rings on each side of the ark to carry it.
He made the Mercy Seat out of pure gold, two and one-half cubits long and one-half cubit wide.
He forged two cherubs out of one piece of gold for each end of the Mercy Seat.
He made the cherubs to attach to each end of the Mercy Seat.
The cherubs were made facing each other with their wings spread high over the Mercy Seat.
He made the shittim wood table two cubits long, one cubit wide, and one and one-half cubits high.
He overlaid it with pure gold and made gold crown moldings all the way around it.
He made the border one hand width or about two and one half to four inches wide all the way around, and he made a gold crown molding for the border.
Bezalel cast four gold rings and put them on the feet of the table's four corners.
The rings were attached to the border to hold the poles for carrying the table.
He made the poles out of shittim wood and overlaid them with gold to carry the table.
He made everything on the table including its cups, dishes, spoons, and covers out of pure gold.
He hand forged the pure gold lampstand out of one solid gold sheet including its shaft, branches, cups, buds, and flowers which were all made the same way.
It had six branches altogether, with three branches that spread out from each side.
He fashioned three cups to look like flowering almonds with a bud and flower on each branch, there were a total of six branches spreading out from the lampstand.
There were four almond shaped bowls with bulbs and flowers on the lampstand.
There was a bulb attached to the bottom of each of the six branches.
All of the bulbs and branches were forged the same way out of hand hammered pure gold.
Bezalel made seven lamps, candle snuffers, and ash pans out of pure gold.
It took about one talent or approximately 75 pounds of pure gold for everything on the table.
He made the incense altar out of shittim wood, it was cube shaped one cubit long, one cubit wide, and two cubits high, and it was made all in one piece including the horns.
He overlaid it all including the top, sides, crown moldings, and its horns with gold.
He made two gold rings under its crown moldings that he attached to the two corners on each side to insert the poles to carry it with.
He made the poles out of shittim wood and overlaid them with gold.
And he made the holy anointing oil and the pure incense of sweet spices the way a pharmacist would make it.
Bezalel made the altar for the burnt offering out of shittim wood. It was square in shape, and it was 5 cubits long, 5 cubits wide, and 3 cubits high.
He attached its horns to the four corners, and all the horns were identical, and they were overlaid with brass.
He made all of the altar's vessels, pots, shovels, sinks, flesh hooks, and firepans out of brass.
He made a brass grate all around the altar and beneath its middle.
He cast four brass rings for the grate's four corners for the carrying poles.
He made the poles out of shittim wood and overlaid them with brass.
He put the poles into the rings on the altar's sides to carry it because it was made with boards and it was hollow.
He made the sink and its feet out of the brass from the mirrors that the women brought to the tabernacle door.
He made the court's south wall 100 cubits long and covered them with fine twined linen wall hangings.
It had 20 columns with 20 brass bases and hooks, and the columns had silver bands around them.
The court's north wall was 100 cubits long, with 20 columns with silver bands, 20 brass bases with hooks, and they were covered with fine twined linen curtains.
The west wall was 50 cubits long and was covered with fine twined linen curtains. It had ten columns with ten bases and ten hooks, and the columns had silver bands all around them.
The east wall was 50 cubits long.
One side of the court's gate was 15 cubits long, and it had three columns with three bases and was covered with curtains.
The other side of the court's gate was 15 cubits long, and it had three columns with three bases and was covered with curtains.
All the curtains around the court were made of fine twined linen.
All the bases for the court's columns were made of brass, but the bands and hooks for the columns were made of silver, and the column caps were overlaid with silver.

The curtain for the court's gate was 20 cubits long and it was made of fine twined linen embroidered with blue, purple, and scarlet needlework, and just like the curtains in the court it was five cubits wide.
There were four columns with four brass and silver hooks, and the column caps were overlaid with silver.
And all the pegs around the tabernacle's court were made of brass.
Aaron's son Ithamar the Levite, kept the construction records for the tabernacle and he recorded them the way that Moses had told him to.
Uri and Hur's son Bezalel from the tribe of Judah, made everything that the Lord told Moses to make.
Ahisamach's son Aholiab from the tribe of Dan who was a skillful engraver, weaver and embroiderer in blue, purple, and scarlet fine linen.
There were 29 gold talents and 730 gold sanctuary shekels collected from offerings for the construction of the Holy Place.
They collected 100 silver talents, and 1,775 silver sanctuary shekels.
There were 603,550 men counted at the census. Every one of them that were 20 years old or older gave one bekah which is 1/2 of a sanctuary shekel.
From the 100 silver talents, they used one talent to cast each base for the sanctuary and the veil.
From the 1,775 shekels Bezalel made hooks for the columns, banded them with silver, and overlaid the column caps.
And the people offered 70 brass talents and 2,400 brass shekels.
Finally Bezalel made the altar bases, all the altar vessels, the tabernacle door and its grate from brass.
Plus, the brass bases around the court, the court gate, and all the pegs for the tabernacle and the court.
They made holy garments for Aaron to perform the services in the Holy Place with blue, purple, and scarlet cloth the way the Lord asked Moses to make it.
Bezalel made the ephod out of gold, blue, purple, and scarlet fine twined linen.
They skillfully hand forged the gold into thin wires. They wove the wire into the blue, purple, and scarlet fine linen.
They made shoulder pieces and attached them to each side of the ephod.
The ephod's belt was attached to the ephod, and it was made the same way out of gold, blue, purple, and scarlet fine twined linen, just like the Lord had asked Moses to make it.
They set onyx stones in gold settings and engraved them like signets with the names of the Israelis.
They attached the stones to the ephod's shoulders as a memorial to the Israelis, the way the Lord told Moses that he wanted it done.
Bezalel skillfully made the high priest's jeweled vest the same way he made the ephod. He made it out of gold, blue, purple, and scarlet fine twined linen.
They made the high priest's jeweled vest one span or about nine inches long and one span or about nine inches wide and folded it in half.
