They sewed four rows of stones to the vest, and each row had a sardius, a topaz, and a carbuncle.
On the second row was an emerald, a sapphire, and a diamond.
On the third row was an agate, a ligure, and an amethyst.
On the fourth row was an onyx, a beryl, and a jasper, and they were all set in gold settings.
There were twelve stones, each one was engraved like a signet with the name of one of the Israelis. The twelve stones represented Israel's twelve tribes.
They made gold chain ropes for each end of the high priest's jeweled vest.
They made two gold settings and two gold rings and attached them to each end of the high priest's jeweled vest.
They fastened the two gold rope chains to the rings that were attached to each end of the high priest's jeweled vest.
They fastened the other two gold rope chains to the two settings that were attached to the front of the ephod's shoulder pieces.
They made two gold rings and put them on the ephod's side border that were attached to the two ends of the high priest's jeweled vest.
They made two other gold rings and attached them close to the seam, underneath the shoulder pieces and above the ephod's belt.

They bound the high priest's jeweled vest by its rings to the ephod's rings with blue lace above the ephod's belt to hold the high priest's jeweled vest to the ephod, the way the Lord had asked Moses to make it.
The ephod's robe was woven from blue thread.
There was a hole in the middle of the top of the robe with a collar around it so that it would not tear.
They embroidered the robe's hems with blue, purple, and scarlet twined linen that made them look like pomegranates.
They made solid gold bells and attached them between each of the pomegranates on the robe's hem.
There was a bell between each pomegranate all around the robe's hem for Aaron to wear when he ministered, the same way the Lord told Moses to make it.
They made woven coats of fine linen for Aaron and his sons.
They made the turban, caps, and undergarments out of fine twined linen.
They made the sash out of fine twined linen with blue, purple, and scarlet embroidery, the way the Lord told Moses to make it.
They made the emblem of the holy crown out of solid gold and like a signet, they engraved an inscription on it that said, "HOLINESS TO THE LORD."
They tied a blue lace to it to fasten it high up on the turban, the way the Lord told Moses to make it.
The congregation's tabernacle was finished, and this was the last work to be done for it, and the Israelis had done everything that the Lord had asked Moses to do.
Then they brought the tabernacle tent including all the furniture, buckles, boards, poles, columns, and bases to Moses.
Including the red dyed ram skin coverings, the badger skin coverings, and the covering veil.
And the Ark of the Covenant, its poles, and the Mercy Seat.
And the table and its vessels and the priest's bread offering.
And the solid gold lampstand with its rows of lamps, cups, and oil for the lamps.
And the gold altar, anointing oil, sweet incense, and the curtain for the tabernacle door.
And the brass altar with its brass grate, poles, cups, and the brass sink with its feet.
And the tabernacle tent's court curtains and its columns, cords, pegs, bases, gate, and service vessels.
And the clothes for the services in the holy place, and the holy garments for Aaron and his sons to wear when they minister to the Lord in the priest's office.
So the Israelis had done all the work to make everything that the Lord asked Moses to make.
Finally, Moses looked at all the work they had done and behold, they had made everything the way the Lord had asked them to make it, so Moses blessed them.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said,
"On the first day of the first month, set up the tabernacle tent for the congregation.
Put the Ark of the Covenant in the tent and cover it with the veil.
Bring in the table and arrange things on top of it in the proper order, then bring in the lampstand and light its lamps.
Set the gold incense altar in front of the Ark of the Covenant and hang the tabernacle door curtain.
Set the burnt offering altar in front of the congregation's tabernacle tent door.
Set the brass sink between the congregation tent and the altar and fill it with water.
Set up the court and hang the curtains at the court gate.
Anoint the tabernacle and everything in it with anointing oil including all of its vessels and it will be holy.
Anoint the burnt offering altar and all of its vessels and sanctify it, and it will be the altar of the Most Holy.
Anoint the brass sink and its feet and sanctify it.
Bring Aaron and his sons to the tabernacle's door and wash them with water.
Put the holy garments on Aaron, anoint him and sanctify him, so that he may minister to me in the priest's office.
Clothe his sons with coats.

Anoint them the same way their father was anointed so that they may minister to me in the priest's office because their anointing will surely be an everlasting priesthood throughout all of their descendants."
Moses did everything that the Lord asked him to do.
On the first day of the first month of the second year, they erected the tabernacle.
Moses erected the tabernacle and he fastened its bases, set up its boards, installed the poles, and set up the columns.
Moses spread the tent over the tabernacle, and put the tent covering above it, the way the Lord told him to erect it.
Moses put the ten commandments into the ark, set the ark's poles, and put the Mercy Seat upon the ark.
Moses brought the ark into the tabernacle and covered it with the covering veil, the way the Lord told him to.
He put the table in the tabernacle tent on its northern wall outside the veil.
Moses arranged the bread before the Lord in the order that the Lord had told him to.
He put the lampstand in the tabernacle tent beside the table, on the tabernacle's south wall.
Moses lit the lamps before the Lord, the way the Lord told him to.
He put the golden altar in the congregation tent in front of the veil.
Then Moses burned sweet incense the way the Lord told him to.
He hung the curtain at the tabernacle door.
Moses put the altar next to the tabernacle door, the way the Lord told him to, and he made the burnt offering on it.
He set the brass sink between the congregation and the altar and filled it with water to wash with.
That's where Moses, Aaron and Aaron's sons washed their hands and feet.
When they went near the altar in the congregation tent, they washed, the way the Lord told them to.
Moses erected the court around the tabernacle and altar and hung the court's gate curtain. So, Moses' work was finished.
Then a cloud covered the congregation tent and the Lord's glory filled the tabernacle.
Moses was unable to enter the congregation tent because the cloud settled on it, and the Lord's glory filled the tabernacle.
When the cloud ascended from the tabernacle, the Israelis continued on their journeys.
But if the cloud did not ascend from above the tabernacle, they did not continue their journey until it did.
Because the Lord's cloud covered the tabernacle by day and it was covered by fire at night, and everyone in the House of Israel saw it throughout all their journeys.
Then the Lord called out to Moses from the tabernacle and said,
"Speak to the Israelis children and say, 'If anyone brings an offering to the Lord, bring it from your livestock, herds, or flocks.
If the offering is a sacrificial burnt offering from the herd, it must be an unblemished male animal and it must be offered voluntarily at the tabernacle door before the Lord.
They must put their hand on the head of the burnt offering, and it will be accepted as an atonement for their sin.
They must kill the bull in front of the Lord and Aaron's sons, then the priests must bring the blood to the tabernacle door and sprinkle it around and on the altar.
They must filet the burnt offering and cut it into pieces.
Priest Aaron's sons must build a fire on the altar and stack the wood on the fire.
Aaron's sons, who are the priests, must arrange the animal's parts including its head and the fat on the burning wood on the altar.
But its innards and legs must be washed in water, and the priest must burn all of it on the altar as a sweet savory sacrificial burnt offering to the Lord.
Whether the sacrificial burnt offering is from the flock, from the sheep, or from the goats, it must be an unblemished male.
It must not be killed before the Lord on the north side of the altar, and Aaron's sons, the priests, must sprinkle its blood on the altar and all around it.
It must be cut into pieces, and the priest must arrange its head and fat in the fire on the altar.
But the priest must wash its innards and legs with water and burn it on the altar as a sweet savory burnt offering to the Lord.
But if the sacrificial burnt offering to the Lord is birds, they must bring turtledoves or young pigeons.
The priest must bring it to the altar and wring off his head and burn it on the altar, and its blood must be drained beside the altar.
The priest must pluck its crop and feathers and throw them in the ashes beside the east side of the altar.
The priest must tear its wings without tearing it apart and burn it in the fire on the altar as a sweet savory burnt offering to the Lord.'"
And God said, "When anyone brings a bread offering to the Lord, it must be made with fine flour, oil, and frankincense.

Bring it to Aaron's sons, the priests, and they will mix a handful of flour, oil, and frankincense together and burn a memorial portion of it in the fire on the altar, and it will be a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
Whatever remains of the bread offering will belong to Aaron and his sons; it is the holiest of all the Lord's burnt offerings.
If you bring a donation of baked bread, it must be unleavened cakes made with fine flour and oil, or unleavened wafers anointed with oil.
If your donation is bread baked in a pan, it must be made of fine unleavened flour and mixed with oil.
You must cut it into pieces, then pour oil on it and it will be a bread offering.
If your donation is a fried bread offering cooked in the frying pan, it must be made with fine flour and oil.
When you bring these types of bread offerings to the Lord, offer it to the priest who will bring it to the altar.
The priest must take a memorial portion of the bread offering, and burn it in the fire on the altar, and it will be a sweet savory aroma to the Lord.
If there are any leftovers from the bread offering, give it to Aaron and his sons, for it is the most holy part of the offering to the Lord.
Do not bring a leavened bread offering to the Lord, because he does not want a burnt offering made with leavening or honey.
Do not burn the first fruits on the altar as a sweet and savory offering.
Season your bread offering with salt, for your covenant with God requires all your offerings to be offered with salt.
If you make a bread offering to the Lord from the first fruits of your harvest, it must be made from roasted green wheat heads and ripe wheat kernels from the threshing floor.
You must put oil and frankincense on it as a bread offering to the Lord.
The priest must burn the flailed wheat as the memorial portion of the burnt offering with oil and frankincense, as an offering to the Lord."
And God said, "If your peace offering to be sacrificed before the Lord comes from your herd, it does not matter if it is a male or female animal, but it must be an unblemished animal.
You must lay your hand on the head of your offering and kill it at the tabernacle door. Then priest Aaron's sons, the priests, must sprinkle the blood on and all around the altar.
Offer its internal organs and the fat that covers them as a burnt peace offering to the Lord.
And the kidneys with the fat that covers them near the flanks, and you must remove the caul above the liver along with the kidneys.
Aaron's sons must burn them on the altar as a sweet savory sacrificial burnt offering to the Lord.
If your sacrificial peace offering to the Lord comes from your flock, whether it is male or female, it must be an unblemished animal.
If you offer a lamb, then you must offer it before the Lord.
The priest must lay his hand on the head of the offering, and kill it in front of the tabernacle, and Aaron's sons must sprinkle the blood on and all around the altar.
The priest must offer the sacrificial burnt peace offering to the Lord, including the fat, the whole boneless rump, and the fat that covers the internal organs.
Its kidneys and the fat that covers them near the flanks and the caul above the liver must be removed.
And the priest must burn the food offering in the fire on the altar, as an offering to the Lord.
And if the offering is a goat, then it will be offered in front of the Lord.
The priest must lay his hand on its head and kill it in front of the tabernacle, and Aaron's sons must sprinkle its blood on and all around the altar.
Then the priest must burn all the fat that covers the internal organs as an offering to the Lord.
Including its kidneys and the fat that covers them, near the flanks and the caul above the liver will all be removed.
The priest must burn them on the altar because it is a sweet savory burnt offering, and all the fat belongs the Lord.
For all of eternity there will be law for your descendants, wherever they live, that they must not eat the fat nor blood of the offering."
Then the Lord spoke to Moses and said,
"Speak to the Israelis and say, 'If anyone is ignorant of God's laws and commits a sin, or willingly does something that God says not to do.
Or if an anointed priest sins and brings guilt on the people, then he must bring an unblemished young bull to the Lord as a sin offering.
He must bring the bull to the tabernacle door before the Lord, and he must lay his hand on the bull's head and kill it before the Lord.
The anointed priest must take the bull's blood and bring it to the congregation tabernacle.
The priest must stand before the veil and dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle it seven times before the Lord.

The priest must enter the tabernacle and put some of the blood on the sweet incense altar horns before the Lord and pour the rest of the bull's blood at the bottom of the burnt offering altar near the tabernacle door.
The priest must remove all of the bull's fat for the sin offering including the fat that covers the internal organs.
And its kidneys and the caul fat above the liver near the flanks.
The priest must burn the sacrificial bull on the burnt offering altar.
Including the bull's hide, flesh, head, legs, internal organs, and dung.
The priest must carry the whole bull outside the camp to a clean place where the ashes are dumped and build a wood fire and burn it on top of the ashes.
If the whole Israelis congregation unintentionally sins and no one notices that they have broken any of the Lord's commandments, and they are guilty of doing things which should not be done.
When the sin becomes known the congregation must offer a young bull for the sin and bring it in front of the tabernacle.
Then the congregation elders must lay their hands on the bull's head and kill it before the Lord.
And the anointed priest must bring some of the bull's blood to the tabernacle.
The priest must dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle it seven times in front of the veil before the Lord.
The priest must put some of the blood on the tabernacle altar's horns and pour the rest of it out at the bottom of the burnt offering beside the tabernacle door before the Lord.
The priest must take all the bull's fat and burn it on the altar.
The priest must do this in the same way that he did with the bull for a sin offering, that will atone for their sin, and they will be forgiven.
Then the priest must take the bull outside the camp away from the congregation, and burn it as a sin offering, just as he burned the first bull.
If or when a ruler has unintentionally sinned through ignorance of any of the Lord God's commandments and he is guilty of doing something that he should not have done.
When he becomes aware of the sin, he must bring an unblemished male kid goat as his sin offering.
And the priest must take the sin offering and lay his hand on the goat's head and kill it before the Lord, in the same place that they kill the burnt offerings.
The priest must dip his finger in the sin offering's blood and wipe it on the burnt offering altar's horns, then pour the rest of it out at the bottom of the altar.
The priest must burn all of the fat on the altar the same way he did the peace offerings, and this will make an atonement for his sin, and he will be forgiven.
If any of the common people ignorantly sin and breaks any of the Lord's commandments, and they are guilty of doing things which should not be done.
If or when they become aware of their sin then they must offer an unblemished female kid goat for their sin.
And the priest must lay his hand on the sin offering's head and kill it at the burnt offering altar.
And the priest must dip his finger in the blood and wipe it on the burnt offering altar's horns and pour the rest of it out at the bottom of the altar.

The priest must remove all of its fat the same way he does the peace offerings, then burn it on the altar as a sweet savory offering to the Lord to make atonement for their sin, and they will be forgiven.
If they bring a lamb for their sin offering, it must be an unblemished female.
And the priest must lay his hand on the lamb's head and kill it in the same place that they kill the other burnt offerings.
Then the priest must dip his finger in the sin offering's blood and wipe it on the altar's horns and pour the rest of it out at the bottom of the altar.

The priest must remove all of the lamb's fat the same way that it is removed from the sacrificial peace offering and burn it on the altar. This is the same way that the burnt offering is made to the Lord, that way the priest can make an atonement for their sin, and they will be forgiven.'"
Then the Lord spoke to Moses and said, "If someone sins because they witness or have seen or know of something sinful and they do not speak out about it, then they shall bear its iniquity.
If someone touches anything unclean, whether it is an unclean animal or an unclean reptile, even if they are unaware of it, they will also be guilty.
Or if they touch an unclean man no matter what that man is defiled by, even if they are unaware of it, when they do finally realize it then they will also be guilty.
If someone thoughtlessly speaks and swears an oath to do something foolish whether it is good or bad, then later when they realize what they have said, they must confess their guilt.
If they are guilty of one of these sins, they must confess their sin.
Then they must bring a female lamb or kid goat as a trespass offering to the Lord for this sin, and the priest will make an atonement for it.
If they are unable to bring a lamb, then they must bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons to the Lord, one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering.
When they bring them to the priest, he must wring off its neck and make the sin offering first, but he must not cut it into pieces.
The priest must sprinkle some of the sin offering blood beside the altar and pour the rest of it out at the bottom of the altar.
The priest must offer the second one as a burnt offering to atone for their sin, and they will be forgiven.

If they are unable to bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons as an offering for their sin, they must bring 1/10th of an ephah of fine flour with no oil or frankincense mixed with it, as a sin offering.
Then they must bring it to the priest, and he will take a handful of it as a sin offering and burn it on the altar, because that is how the Lord wants the offerings to be made.
This way the priest can make an atonement for any of the sins that they've committed, and they will be forgiven. The rest of the bread offering will belong the priest."
And the Lord spoke to Moses again and said,

"If someone unintentionally sins against the Lord, they must bring an unblemished ram from their flocks to the Lord, or they can buy something of equal value with silver shekels, to offer the Lord as a trespass offering.

They must then make amends for the harm that they have done to the Lord's holy things, plus they must add an additional 20% more for the priest. The priest must then offer their ram trespass offering as an atonement for their sin, and they will be forgiven.
Someone who unknowingly commits any sin forbidden by God's word is guilty and must be held responsible.

As a trespass offering, they must bring an unblemished ram from their flock or one that they bought of equal value to the priest, and the priest will make an atonement for the sins they have unknowingly committed, and they will be forgiven.
And it will be their offering for trespassing against the Lord."
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said,
"If someone commits a sin and trespasses against the Lord and lies about it to his neighbor or deceives a friend or violently takes something from his neighbor.
Or they find something that was lost and they lie about it or they falsely swear that they are telling the truth, or they commit any other such sin.

They are guilty because they have sinned and they must return anything that was stolen, or they took something through violence, or they stole something that they were loaned, or they lied about something that they found which was lost that they took.
They must return anything that they have falsely sworn to the owner about plus they must add 20% more to its value on the day that they make their guilt offering.
They must bring an appropriately valued unblemished lamb from their flock to the priest as a sin offering to the Lord.
When the priest makes an atonement for their sin before the Lord, they will be forgiven for any sins they may have committed."
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said,
"Tell Aaron and his sons, this is the burnt offering law, it must be burned in the fire on the altar all night long until the next morning.
The priest must wear his linen clothing and take the ashes from the altar fire and put them beside the altar.
Then he must change his clothes and carry the ashes to a clean place outside the camp.
The altar fire must never be extinguished, every morning the priest must add wood to the fire and lay out the burnt offerings in the proper order and burn the fat from the peace offerings.
The fire on the altar must burn forever and it can never be extinguished.
This is the law of the bread offering that Aaron's sons must make in front of the altar, before the Lord.
The priest must take some of the flour, oil, and frankincense that are part of the bread offering and burn them on the altar as a savory sweet, scented memorial to the Lord.
Aaron and his sons will the eat the rest of it along with the unleavened bread in the Holy Place inside the tabernacle court.
The bread must not be baked with leavening. I have given it to Aaron and his sons as their portion of my fire offering, and just like the sin offering and trespass offering, it is most holy.
All of Aaron's male children will be allowed to eat it, his descendants will share in the Lord's fire offering forever, and anyone who touches them must be holy."
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said,

"On the day that Aaron is anointed, he and his descendants must forever bring a 1/10th part of an ephah of fine flour for a bread offering. They must bring half of it in the morning and half of it in the evening.
Bake it in a pan with oil and then bring some of it to the Lord as a sweet savory bread offering.
And Aaron's descendant's anointed priest must forever offer it to the Lord, and it must be completely burnt.
From now on, the priest's bread offering must not be eaten, and it must be completely burned in the fire."
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said,
"Speak to Aaron and his sons and say, 'This is the law of the burnt offering and the sin offering, for they are most holy. Both offerings must be killed in the same place before the Lord.
The priest that offers it for sin must eat it in the Holy Place in the tabernacle court.
Anything that touches its flesh will become holy, and if any of the blood is splashed on the garments, they must be washed in the Holy Place.
If it was cooked in a clay pot the pot must be broken, but if it was cooked in a brass pot, it must be scrubbed and rinsed in water.
All the male priests must eat from it, and it is most holy.
None of the blood from the sin offering brought to the tabernacle must be eaten in the Holy Place, it must be burned in the fire.'"
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said, "This is the law of God's most holy trespass offering.
They must kill both the trespass offering and the burnt offering in the same place and then sprinkle the blood on and all around the altar.
The priest must offer its rump and all of its fat including the fat that covers the internal organs.
The priest must remove the kidneys, the fat by the flanks on the kidneys and the caul above the liver.
The priest must burn them on the altar for a burnt offering as a trespass offering to the Lord.
Every male priest must eat from it in the Holy Place, for it is most holy.
The same law applies to both the trespass offering and the sin offering, and it belongs to the priest who makes atonement with it.
The hides from anyone's burnt offering belongs to the priest.
The bread offering whether it was cooked in the oven or the frying pan, will belong to the priest who offers it.
Aaron and his sons will share equally in every bread offering, whether it is baked dry or mixed with oil.
By law this is the way to make a sacrificial peace offering to the Lord.

If the priest makes a sacrificial thanksgiving peace offering, then he must offer it with unleavened cakes mixed with fine flour and oil, plus fried unleavened wafers made with fine flour anointed with oil.
The priest must offer the cakes along with leavened bread for the sacrificial thanksgiving peace offering.
He must bring one offering of each kind and donate it as a sacred offering to the Lord, it will belong to the priest who sprinkles the peace offering's blood.
The meat from the priest's thanksgiving peace offering must be eaten the same day it is offered; he must not leave any leftovers until the next morning.
However, if the sacrificial offering is a voluntary offering that was previously promised, it can be eaten the same day and the next day too.
But on the third day anything left over from the offering must be burned.
If any of the meat from the peace offering is eaten on the third day, they will not be accepted by God. The meat will be disgusting and the soul who ate it will be considered to be unclean.
Any meat that touches anything unclean must not be eaten, but it must be burned in the fire, as for the other meat anyone who is clean may eat it.
But anyone who is unclean and eats the Lord's portion of the sacrificial meat offering, will be cut off from their people.
If anyone touches anything unclean whether it is a human, an animal, or any other unclean thing, and they eat the Lord's portion of the meat offering, they will be cut off from their people."
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said,
"Speak to the Israeli children and tell them not to eat any fat from an ox, sheep, or goat.
The fat from any animal that dies of natural causes, or it is torn to pieces by a predator must not br eaten, but it may be used for anything else.
Anyone who eats fat from an animal that was offered as a burnt offering to the Lord, will be cut off from their people.
Besides that, no matter where you live you must not eat blood of any kind, whether it is from a bird or an animal.
Anyone who eats any kind of blood, will be cut off from their people."
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said,
"Speak to the Israelis and tell them that, when they bring their sacrificial peace offerings to the Lord they must donate part of it as the Lord's portion.
They must bring their burnt offerings to the Lord in person including the breast's fat, and wave it as a wave offering before the Lord.
The priest must burn the fat on the altar, but the breast will belong to Aaron and his sons.
Give the right shoulder to the priest as your sacred offering for the sacrificial peace offering.
Any of Aaron's sons that offer the animal's blood and fat as a peace offering will have the right shoulder for their part.
It is by eternal law that I the Lord have given part of the Israelis' peace offerings, including the wave offering and the sacred offering to Aaron and his sons as the priest's portion.
That portion of the Lord's burnt offerings is for the anointing of Aaron and his sons on the day that they were presented to the Lord to minister to him in the priest's office."
On the day that Moses anointed Aaron and his sons, the Lord told the Israelis that by law, this offering was to be given to Aaron and his descendants forever.
These are the eternal laws of the burnt offering, bread offering, sin offering, trespass offering, consecrations, and the sacrificial peace offerings.
These are the laws that the Lord gave to Moses out in the wilderness, on top of Mount Sinai. And on that day Moses told the Israelis that the Lord said to give their sacrifices to the Lord.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said,
"Take the garments you prepared to Aaron and his sons along with the anointing oil, a bull for the sin offering, two rams, and a basket full of unleavened bread.
And assemble the congregation together at the tabernacle door."
Moses did what the Lord told him to do, and the entire assembly gathered together at the tabernacle door.
And Moses said to the congregation, "This is what the Lord wants us to do."
Then he washed Aaron and his sons with water.
Moses put the coat, belt, robe, and ephod on Aaron and he attached the high priest's jeweled vest to the robe with a decorative sash.
When Moses put the high priest's jeweled vest on Aaron, he attached the Urim and Thummim to the vest.
Moses did what the Lord wanted him to do, and he put the turban on Aaron's head and attached the golden plate to the front of the turban, and it was the holy crown.
Moses anointed the tabernacle and everything in it with anointing oil and sanctified them.
He sprinkled anointing oil on the altar seven times to anoint it, its vessels, and the brass sink and feet to sanctify them.
He poured anointing oil on Aaron's head and anointed him in order to sanctify him.
Moses put coats on Aaron's sons, wrapped them with belts, and put hats on their heads the way the Lord told him to.
He brought the bull for the sin offering, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on the head of the bull sin offering.

Moses killed it, then he took the blood and wiped it on the altar's horns with his finger to purify it. Then he poured the rest of blood at the bottom of the altar to consecrate and sanctify it, and to make atonement for sin.
Moses took all the fat on the internal organs, the two kidneys, their fat, and the caul above the liver and burned it on the altar.
But he burned the bull's hide, flesh, and dung outside the camp, the way the Lord told him to burn it.
Moses brought the ram for the burnt offering, then Aaron and his sons laid their hands on the ram's head.
Moses killed it and sprinkled the blood on and all around the altar.
He cut the ram into pieces and burned its head, fat, and its cut pieces.
Moses washed the legs and internal organs in water, and he burned the whole ram on the altar as a sweet, savory, burnt sacrificial offering, exactly the way the Lord told him to.
Moses brought the other consecration ram, then Aaron and his sons laid their hands on its head.
Moses killed it and took some of its blood and wiped it on the tip of Aaron's right ear, his right-hand thumb, and the big toe of his right foot.

Moses wiped some of the ram's blood on the tip of Aaron's sons' right ear, their right-hand thumb, and the big toe of their right foot, then he sprinkled the rest of the blood on and all around the altar.
Moses took its rump, right shoulder, and kidneys, plus the fat on the internal organs including the kidneys and the caul above the liver, and the rest of the fat.
Moses took one unleavened cake, a cake of oiled bread, and one wafer from the basket of unleavened bread before the Lord and laid them on the fat and right shoulder.
Moses put all of this in Aaron and his sons' hands, who waved them as a wave offering before the Lord.
Then Moses took it all from their hands and consecrated it, then he burned it on the altar as a sweet savory offering to the Lord.
Moses took his part of the consecrated ram's breast and waved it as a wave offering before the Lord, the way the Lord told him to.
Moses took the anointing oil and the blood which was on the altar and sprinkled it on Aaron and his sons and their garments. So, this is how Moses sanctified all of them and their garments.
Then Moses said to Aaron and his sons, "Boil the meat and eat it at the tabernacle door along with the bread that is in the consecration basket the way I commanded you to eat it.
Burn any meat or bread that is leftover in the fire.
Do not leave the congregation tabernacle door for seven days because it takes seven days before you are consecrated.
The Lord told us to do what we have done today to make atonement for you.
That's why you must endure seven days and seven nights at the tabernacle door, in order to do your duty to the Lord, so that you do not die, for that is what the Lord commanded of me."
So Aaron and his sons did everything which the Lord commanded through Moses.
And on the eighth day Moses called Aaron, his sons, and Israel's elders.
Moses spoke to Aaron and said, "Take a young unblemished calf as a sin offering and a ram as a burnt offering, and offer them before the Lord.
Then speak to the Israelis and say, 'Take an unblemished kid goat as a sin offering, and an unblemished year-old calf and a lamb, as a burnt offering.
Also offer a bull and a ram as peace offerings, along with a bread offering mixed with oil to sacrifice before the Lord because today the Lord will appear to you.'"
And they brought everything that Moses told them to bring to the tabernacle, and the entire congregation moved closer to stand before the Lord.
And Moses said, "This is what the Lord told me to command you to do, and the glory of the Lord will appear to you."

And the Lord spoke to Moses and said,

If she cannot afford to bring a one-year-old lamb so the priest can make atonement for her, then she must bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons, one as a burnt offering and one as a sin offering, then she will be clean.'"
And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron and said,
"When anyone has a swollen skin infection, such as a scab, or bright spot, and it appears to be the plague or leprosy, then they must go to priest Aaron or one of his priestly sons.

After the priest reexamines them on the seventh day, and the infection has not spread, then the priest must quarantine them for seven more days.

But if the skin infection spreads after they have already seen the priest for their cleansing, the priest must reexamine them.
If the priest sees that the skin infection has spread, then it is leprosy and the priest must declare them to be unclean.

If the priest sees that an infection has broken out and covers anyone's entire body from head to toe.

When the priest sees that the raw infected flesh is leprosy, he must declare them unclean.

When the priest sees the infected person again, and if the infection has turned white, then the priest must declare them clean and they will be clean.

But if the priest looks at it, and there are no white hairs and it has not spread beneath the skin, and it is somewhat dark colored, then the priest must quarantine them for seven days.
If the infection spreads, then it is a plague and the priest must declare the person to be unclean.
But if the infection has not moved or spread, then it is a boil and the priest must declare the person to be clean.
If part of the infected flesh is hot and feverish, and the swollen area is a somewhat white or reddish color.

If the priest looks at it and the hair on the infected area has turned white, and the infection appears to have spread beneath the skin, it is leprosy that has spread from the infected area, and the priest will pronounce him to be unclean.

But if the priest looks at it, and there is no white hair in the infected area and it has not spread beneath the skin, but it is somewhat dark colored, then the priest will have the person quarantined for seven days.
When the priest looks at them on the seventh day, and the infection has spread, then the priest must declare the person to be unclean because it is leprosy.
And if the infected area has not spread or moved, but it is kind of dark colored, then it is just a swollen inflamed spot, and the priest must declare the person to be clean.
If a man or woman has an infection on their head or beard and goes to the priest.

If the priest looks at it and it appears to have spread beneath the skin, and it is covered with thin yellow hair, then the priest must pronounce the person unclean, because it is a dry scaly skin disease and it may even be leprosy.

But if the priest sees that the disease is just a scaly skin infection, and it has not spread beneath the skin and there is no black hair growing from it, then he must have the person quarantined for seven days.
After seven days if the priest sees that the disease has not spread, and there is no yellow hair growing there, and it does not appear to have infected the area beneath the skin.
Then the area around the infection must be shaved without shaving the scaly infected area, and the priest must have the person quarantined for seven more days.

On the seventh day the priest must inspect the infection, and if the infection has not spread on the skin, nor raw flesh is seen beneath the skin, then the priest will pronounce them to be clean, and when they wash their clothes, they will be clean.
But if the infection continues to spread after it has been cleaned.
When the priest sees that the person's infection has continued to spread, the priest does not even have to check for yellow hair, and he must declare the person to be unclean.
But if the scaly skin has not spread and there is black hair growing there, then the skin is healed and the person is clean, and the priest will declare him to be clean.
If a man or woman has a skin infection with white spots or bright white spots.
If the priest inspects the spots and they are freckled or a darkish white color, then the person is clean.
Even if the hair has fallen off of their head and they are bald; they are still clean.
If they have lost the hair on the front part of their head and their forehead is bald; they are still clean.
But if their bald head or forehead has a white reddish sore on it, then they have leprosy growing on their bald head.
When the priest sees that the swollen sore on their bald head is a white reddish color, and it appears to be leprosy.
The person is leprous and unclean, and the priest will pronounce them to be completely unclean because they have a plague on their head.
The leper who suffers with the plague must tear their clothes, uncover their head, and put a mask over their face. And they must cry out, 'Unclean, unclean!'
The entire time that a person suffers from a poisonous plague they will be unclean and defiled, and they will have to live all alone outside the camp.
The garments of a leprosy infected person, whether it is a wool or linen garment.
Or whether it is woven from linen, leather, or wool.
And if the infected clothes have a green or reddish bacteria growing on it, then it is leprosy and it must be shown to the priest.
If the priest sees that it is the plague, then the clothes must be quarantined for seven days.
When the priest looks at the garment on the seventh day, if the plague on the cloth or leather garment has spread, then the plague is a consuming leprosy, and it is unclean.
Then the priest must burn the infected garment in the fire because it is a consuming leprosy.
If the priest looks at the clothes and the plague has not spread.
Then the priest must order the infected things to be washed and quarantined for seven more days.

After the garment has been washed and quarantined for seven days and the priest has inspected it inside and out and it appears that the infected cloth has not changed color or the disease has spread, it is still unclean and it must be burned in the fire.
If the priest sees that the infected area fades after being washed, then he must tear the infected part out of the garment, and it does not matter whether it was made of woven cloth or leather.
If the bacteria in the infected garment still appears to be spreading, then you must burn it in the fire.
If the garment was washed, and it appears that the infection is gone, then it must be washed a second time, and it will be clean.
This is the leprosy infection law for infected wool, linen, or leather garments, and how to determine if they must be declared clean or unclean."
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said,

The priest must wave the guilt offering lamb and the log of oil before the Lord.
The priest must then sacrifice the guilt offering lamb and apply its blood to the right ear, thumb, and big toe of the infected person who is being cleansed.

The priest must place some of the oil in their left hand on the unclean person's right earlobe, right thumb, and the big toe on their right foot in order to cleanse them.

If the unclean person can afford them, they must sacrifice one turtledove or one young pigeon.

This is the law that God has given to those who suffer from leprosy and cannot afford the purification process."

You will eat and be satisfied, and you will bless your Lord God for the good land that he has given you.
But if you ask, 'What can we eat in the seventh year if we do not sow or reap our crops?'
The answer is this, I will bless you in the sixth year, and the land will yield enough produce to last you for three years.
You can then plant your crops again in the eighth year, but you will still be eating from the old harvest that you stored until the ninth year when the new harvest comes in.
The land belongs to me and can never be sold, and you are only strangers and guests living with me.
You must allow for the redemption of all the land that you own.
If your brother becomes poor and sells some of his property, you can redeem him and buy it back for him.
If he has no one to help him and he can help himself, then he must help himself.
He can calculate the number of years since he sold it, then return the surplus to the man who bought it and return to his property.
If he is unable to repay the buyer, then the property will remain in the possession of the buyer until the year of Jubilee, when the property is returned to the original owner.
If a man sells a house inside a walled city, he can buy it back within one year of selling it.

If the house inside the city walls is not bought back within one year after it is sold, it will belong to the buyer and their descendants forever. It will not be returned to its original owner in the year of Jubilee.
But the houses inside an unwalled village will be treated like open fields, they can be redeemed and their people can return in the year of Jubilee.
The Levites can redeem their cities and houses at any time.

If someone buys a house from a Levite, the house and the city it is built in will revert back to them in the year of Jubilee, because the houses in the Levites' cities are their inheritance as Israelis.
The fields in the pastures outside the Levites' cities cannot be sold because they belong to them forever.
If your brother becomes poor and is unable to support himself, you must help him, even if he is a stranger or a traveler.
Fear your God and do not charge your brother interest for a loan, so that he can continue to live with you.
Do not charge your brother interest if you lend him money, and do not charge him extra for food either.
I am your Lord God! I brought you out of Egypt and gave you the land of Canaan.
If your brother lives near you and becomes poor, and he sells himself to you as a servant, do not treat him like a slave.
Treat him like a hired servant and he can live with you as if he were a foreigner until the year of Jubilee.
After working for you for a year, your brother will be allowed to leave with his children and return to his own family and his father's land.
They are my servants, and I brought them out of bondage in Egypt, and I do not want them to be sold as slaves.
Fear your God, and do not rule over your brother with an iron fist.
You may buy male and female slaves from their fellow countrymen in the other nations around you, or from foreigners who live among them.
In addition to buying slaves from the nations around you, you may also buy slaves from the foreigners' families and children who live among you, who were born in your land.
You will own your slaves forever, and you may pass them down to your children as their inheritance, but you must not rule over your fellow Israelis with an iron fist.
If a stranger or a foreigner becomes wealthy while living among you, and your fellow Israelite who lives near them becomes poor and sells themselves to them or their family.
After selling himself, one of his brothers may redeem him.
If he is able, he can redeem himself, or his uncle or his uncle's son can redeem him.

The Israelite who sold himself into slavery and his redeemer can calculate the sale price based on the number of years they were enslaved until the year of Jubilee, and during that time they will be treated like a hired servant.
If there are very many years left before the year of Jubilee, then the person who was sold into slavery must repay the cost of their freedom to their redeemer.

If there is only a few years left until the year of Jubilee, the person who sold themselves into slavery and their owner must calculate the price of their freedom, and they must pay their owner an appropriate amount based on the number of years that they were enslaved.
The person who sold himself into slavery must be treated like a hired worker for the remaining years, and their owner must not rule over them with an iron fist.

If the person who sold himself into slavery is not redeemed before the year of Jubilee, then in the year of Jubilee they will be free and they will be allowed to leave their owner's household with their children and family.
The Israelis are my servants, and I brought them out of Egypt. I am their God!"
And the Lord spoke to Moses at Mount Sinai and said, "You must not make idols or carved images, nor should you set up a standing statue or sacred stone to bow down to. I am your Lord God!
You must keep my Sabbaths and respect my sanctuary. I am the Lord!
If you keep my laws and commandments.
I will send the rains at the right time, and the land will produce crops, and the trees will bear fruit.
You will have enough food from your harvests to last you until the next planting season, and you will live in your land in peace and security.
You will have peace, and you will lie down and sleep soundly without fear of being attacked. I will remove the dangerous animals from your land, and no enemies will be allowed to invade your country.
You will defeat and kill your enemies.
With God's help, you will be victorious in battle, five of you will defeat 100, 100 of you will defeat 10,000, and all of your enemies will fall before you.
If you keep my laws and commandments, I will respect you, I will make you prosperous, I will increase your numbers, and I will renew my covenant with you.
You will eat food that you have stored from the previous harvest, and you will have so much food that you will have to get rid of some of it to make room for the new harvest.
I will live with you, and I will never reject you.
I will walk with you, I will be your God, and you will be my people.
I am your Lord God! I rescued you from Egyptian slavery, I broke the chains that bound you and I allow you to live in freedom.
But if you do not listen to me, and you do not do everything that I command you to do.
Or you reject my laws, or if you hate my judgments and you do not obey all of my commandments, then you will break my covenant.

And I will send fear, disease, and fever to you. They will make you weak and sick, and they will cause you great sorrow. You will sow your seed in vain, because your enemies will eat your harvest before you can harvest your crops.
I will turn against you, and you will be defeated by your enemies. They will rule over you and you will be forced to flee even when no one is chasing you.
If you still do not listen to me, I will punish you even more severely for your sins.
I will break your pride; I will make your land as hard as iron and your crops will be as brittle as brass.
Your hard work will be a waste of time, because your land will not produce crops and your trees will not bear fruit.
If you disobey me and refuse to listen to me, I will punish you with seven times more plagues for each of your sins.
I will also send wild animals among you; they will steal your children and kill your livestock. Your numbers will dwindle and your roads will become deserted.
And if I do not correct you for these things and you continue to disobey me.
Then I will not do what you want, and I will punish you seven more times for your sins.
I will use a sword to take revenge against you. I will send a plague to your cities, and you will be delivered into your enemy's hand.
When I break your ability to make a living, ten women will not be able bake enough bread for you. They will give you the bread in measured amounts, but still you will not be satisfied.
But if you still do not listen to me about these things and walk contrary to my ways.
Then I will also walk contrary to you in fury, and I will chastise you seven times for your sins.
You will eat the flesh of your sons and daughters.
I will destroy your high places and tear down your images. I will throw your carcass over your idol's carcass, and my soul will abhor you.
I will lay waste to your cities, I will destroy your sanctuaries, and I will not smell the savor of your sweet scents.
I will destroy your lands, and your enemies will be astonished.
I will scatter you among the heathen and I will draw my sword against you. Your land will be destroyed, and your cities will be laid waste.
The land will enjoy her Sabbaths for as long as it lies desolate while you are exiled in your enemies' land. Then the land will be able to rest and enjoy her Sabbaths.
As long as it lies desolate it will rest, because when you lived there you did not let it rest on your Sabbaths.

For those of you who survive, I will fill your hearts with fear in the land of your enemies. You will run scared at the sound of a rustling leaf as if you were running from a sword, you will trip and fall even though no one is chasing you.

You will fight amongst yourselves, as if you were being attacked with a sword, and you will flee in fear, even though no one is chasing you. You will be so weak and afraid that you will be unable to stand up to your enemies.
You will perish among the heathen, and your land will consume you.
The survivors will be punished for their sins in their enemy's land, and they will also be punished for the sins of their fathers.
If they confess their immorality and sins, the sins of their fathers and how they have rebelled against me and opposed my teachings.
And if they opposed me and I brought them into the land of their enemies, but their uncircumcised hearts are humbled, and they accept the punishment for their sins.
Then I will remember the land and my covenants with Jacob, Isaac, and Abraham.
The land will lie empty and enjoy its Sabbaths while they are gone. They will accept the punishment for their sins because they despised my judgments and rejected my laws.
Even though they are in their enemy's land, I will not abandon them nor despise them. I will not completely destroy them nor break my covenant with them, because I am their Lord God!
But for their sake, I will remember the covenant I made with their ancestors. I brought them out of Egypt in front of all the other nations, so that I could be their God. I am the Lord!"
These are the laws and judgements that the Lord God gave to Moses on Mount Sinai. This is God's covenant between him and the Israelis in order to govern them.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said,
"Speak to the Israelis and tell them that when a man promises to devote himself to the Lord, he will be one of God's people.
A man between the ages of twenty and sixty years old is worth about fifty silver sanctuary shekels.
A female the same age is worth about thirty shekels.
If the person is between the ages of five and twenty, then a male is worth about twenty shekels, and a female is worth about ten shekels.
If they are a child between one month and five years old, a male is worth about five silver shekels, and a female is worth about three silver shekels.
If the person is 60 years old or older, then a male is worth about 15 shekels, and a female is worth about 10 shekels.
If the person is not worth what you thought they were worth, then you should both go to the priest, and the priest will decide what their proper value should be.
If someone brings an animal as an offering to the Lord, anything that person gives to the Lord will be holy.
If someone exchanges an animal for another animal good or bad, then both animals are holy.
If it is an unclean animal that cannot be offered as a sacrifice to the Lord, then the person must offer the animal to the priest.
The priest will decide whether the offering is good or bad and it will be worth whatever the priest says it is worth.
If the person decides to buy it back, then a fair price would be about 20% more than its estimated value.
If a man dedicates his house to the Lord, then the priest must decide whether it is good or bad and the house will be worth whatever the priest says it is worth.
If the person who dedicated the house to the Lord wants to buy it back, they must pay 20% more than its estimated value, then the house will belong to them.

If a man dedicates a portion of his land to the Lord, then the priest must determine its value based on how much seed it takes to sow its fields. For example, a field that takes 10 1/2 bushels of seed to sow will be valued at fifty silver shekels.
If a man dedicates his field to the Lord in the year of Jubilee, its estimated value will stand.

If someone sets their field apart as holy after the Jubilee year, the priest must calculate the field's valued based on how many years are left until the next year of Jubilee, and the owner must pay the priest its determined value.
If the person who dedicated the field wants to buy it back, they must pay an additional 20% of its estimated value to buy it back.
If the person who dedicated the field does not buy it back or they sell it to someone else, they will never be able to buy it back.
When the field is released in the year of Jubilee, it becomes a holy field devoted to the Lord and it will belong to the priests.
If a man dedicates a field to the Lord, that he bought and did not inherit.

The priest must calculate the field's value based on how many years are left until the next year of Jubilee, and that's how much the owner must pay the priest. This payment will be a holy offering to the Lord.
In the year of Jubilee, the field must be returned to its original owner.
All values will be based on the official weight of the sanctuary shekel, which is equal to twenty gerahs.
No one is allowed to dedicate one of their firstborn sheep or oxen, because it already belongs to the Lord.

If it is an unclean animal, the owner can buy it back for whatever the priest says it is worth. If the owner wants to buy it back, they must add 20% to its estimated value. If it is not redeemed, it can be sold for whatever the priest says it is worth.
Nothing devoted to the Lord whether it is a person, an animal, or a field can be sold or redeemed. For it is holy and it belongs to the Lord.
Nothing devoted to men can be redeemed but must be put to death.
All tithes paid from the land, whether from seed crops or fruit trees, belong to the Lord and they are sacred and holy.
If a man wants to redeem part of his tithe, he must pay 20% more than what the priest appraised it for.
Every tenth animal in the herd or flock that passes under the shepherd's staff is holy to the Lord.
The man must not inspect the animal good or bad or substitute one animal for another. But if he does, then both animals become holy and they cannot be redeemed."
The Lord gave these commandments to Moses on Mount Sinai for the Israelis to follow.
On the first day of the second month of the second year after the Israelis left Egypt, the Lord spoke to Moses in the tabernacle in the Wilderness of Sinai and said,

Count every able-bodied man who is at least 20 years old and fit for military service, then you and Aaron can organize them by the armies they control.

These are the names of the men from Reuben's tribe who will stand with you, first there is Elizur, who is Shedeur's son.

There were 62,700 people in Dan's tribe.

There were 41,500 people in Asher's tribe.
Naphtali's descendants were sorted and organized by their names, families, and ancestors. Everyone who was 20 years old or older and could go to war were counted in the census.
There were 53,400 people in Naphtali's tribe.
So Moses and Aaron and the twelve Israeli princes counted the people, and each prince represented his own father's house.
So these were the Israelis men who were counted by their fathers' houses who were at least 20 years old and fit for military service.
The total number of people that were counted was 603,550.
But the men who were from their father Levite's tribe, were not included in the census.
Because the Lord had spoken to Moses and said,
"Do not include the Levite tribe in the census when you count the Israelis.

Assign the Levites the responsibility of managing the congregation tabernacle and all of its contents. They will be needed to transport the tabernacle and its equipment, and they will serve in and encamp around it.
When the tabernacle is moved, the Levites will disassemble it, move it, and reassemble it in its new location. Any outsiders who come near it, can be put to death.
When the Israelis set up their tents, each man in the army will be assigned to their own camp with their own flag.
The Levites must pitch their tents around the tabernacle, so that the Lord's anger does not affect them. The Levites will be responsible for guarding the tabernacle of the testimony."
And the Israelis did everything that the Lord told Moses to do.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron and said,
"The Israelis men must camp with their tribes far from the tabernacle, under their father's flag."
Amminadab's son Nahshon was the captain of Judah's tribe, and they camped on the eastern side of the tabernacle, where they raised their flag facing the rising sun.
And there were 64,600 men in Nashon's army.
Zuar's son Nathaniel was the captain of Issachar's tribe, and they camped next to Nashon's camp.

There was a total of 603,550 men in the Israelis armies, which were organized by their father's house and his tribe's flag.
But the Lord commanded Moses not to count the Levites among the children of Israel, so they were not counted.

The Israelis did everything that Moses told them to do, because that was how the Lord wanted it done. So, they organized their tribes by their fathers' houses and their tribe's flag, and they moved their camp in this order.
This is a record of Moses and Aaron's descendants, recorded on the day that the Lord spoke with Moses on Mount Sinai.
The names of Aaron's sons are Nadab who was the firstborn, then Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
Aaron had sons whom he declared sacred and anointed as priests so they could be ministers in the priest's office, and these are their names.

Aaron's sons Nadab and Abihu died childless in the wilderness of Sinai when they offered strange fire before the Lord. So, during Aaron's lifetime, his sons Eleazar and Ithamar ministered in the priest's office with him.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said,
"Bring Levi's family here and present them to priest Aaron, so that they may minister to him.
They will control the congregation's tabernacle and perform their services before the entire congregation.
They must also control all of the tabernacle's tools and instruments, so they can maintain them and perform their services before the entire congregation.
The Levites must work with Aaron and his sons, because the children of Israel will completely dedicate them to Aaron's service.

Merari started the Mahlite and Mushite families, and this is a list of all of Merari's families.

The total number of Levites who were a month old and older that Moses and Aaron counted at the Lord's command were 22,000 males.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said, "Count all of the Israelis firstborn males who are a month old and older, and number them by their names.
And the Levites are reserved for God instead of all of Israel's firstborn children. The Levite's cattle are also reserved for God instead of all of Israel's firstborn cattle. Because I am the Lord!"
And Moses counted and numbered all the firstborn in Israel, as the Lord had commanded him.
There were 22,273 firstborn males, who were a month old and older and numbered by their names.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said,
"The Levites will take the place of all of Israel's firstborn children and cattle, and they will be mine. Because I am the Lord!
They will redeem the 273 firstborn Israelis who outnumber the Levites.
Take five sanctuary shekels apiece to redeem those counted by the census. Five sanctuary shekels are worth twenty gerahs.
Give the money to Aaron and his sons, to be used to redeem those who are numbered with an odd number."
Moses took the redemption money for the 273 Israelis that outnumbered the firstborn Levites.
And he took in 1,365 sanctuary shekels to redeem the firstborn children of Israel.
And Moses gave the redemption money of those who were redeemed to Aaron and his sons, as the Lord had commanded him.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron and said,
"Count Kohath's sons from the Levite tribe, by their tribe and their father's houses.
Every son from thirty years old to fifty years old in the tribe will be counted to do the work in the tabernacle's congregation.
Kohath's sons will perform the services of the most holy things in the congregation's tabernacle.
When the camp moves forward, Aaron and his sons will come, and take down the covering vail, and cover the Ark of Testimony with it.
Then put it in a badger skin bag, spread a blue cloth over it, and insert its carrying poles.
They must spread a blue cloth over the priest's bread offering table, and put the dishes, spoons, and vessels on the covering, then place the regular bread offering there.
They must then cover them with a scarlet cloth, and cover that with a badger skin covering, and insert the poles to carry it.
They must cover everything that they use to minister and perform the tabernacle's services under a blue cloth, including the lampstand, its lamps, tongs, snuff dishes, and all of its oil cups.
Put the lampstand and all of its accessories in a badger skin bag and lay it on the bar.
Spread a blue cloth on the golden altar, put it in a badger skin bag, and insert its carrying poles.
Take all the ministry instruments that are used to minister in the sanctuary, and wrap them in a blue cloth, and put them in a badger skin bag, and put them on the bar.
Then remove the ashes from the altar and cover it with a purple cloth.
They must put everything from the sanctuary that they use to minister in a badger skin bag, including all of its vessels, censers, fleshhooks, shovels, and hides, then insert its carrying poles.

When Aaron and his sons finish covering the sanctuary, and all of its vessels, the camp will be ready to move forward. Kohath's sons must carry it forward, but they must not touch anything holy, otherwise they will die. These are the things that Kohath's sons are responsible for moving in the congregation's tabernacle.

Aaron's son Eleazar and his office is responsible for managing and organizing the tabernacle and everything in it, including the lamp oil, the sweet incense, the daily bread offering, the anointing oil, and all of its utensils."
And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron and said,
"Do not separate the tribal families of the Kohathites from the Levites.
But they must approach the most holy things this way, in order to live and not die. Aaron and his sons will enter and appoint the service jobs to each man, and it will be each man's burden to carry.
But they must not go into the sanctuary to see the most holy things unless they are covered, otherwise they may die."

Count everyone thirty to fifty years old, that enters into the service of the congregation's tabernacle to do the work.

Plus the columns all around the court, their bases, pins, cords, accessories, and anything else used in the services. Assign the responsibility of managing each item, to each man by name.
Merari's family will perform these services for the congregation's tabernacle under the supervision of Ithamar, who was the son of priest Aaron."
Then Moses, Aaron, and the congregation's leaders counted, numbered, and organized Kohath's sons by their father's house and their families.
They counted everyone who was between the age of thirty and fifty years old, who entered into the service to do the work of the congregation's tabernacle.
And there were 2,750 from those families.
These were all of the Kohathite families that Moses and Aaron counted and numbered to perform the tabernacle services, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
And they counted, numbered, and organized the families of Gershon's sons by their fathers' houses.
They counted everyone who was between the age of thirty and fifty years old, who entered into the service to do the work of the congregation's tabernacle.
And there were 2,630 from those families that were counted, numbered, and organized by their fathers' houses.
These were all the Gershonite families that Moses and Aaron counted, numbered, and organized to perform the tabernacle services, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
They counted, numbered, and organized the families of Merari's sons by their fathers' houses.
They counted everyone who was between the age of thirty to fifty years old, who entered into the service to do the work of the congregation's tabernacle.
And there were 3,200 from those families.
These were all the Merari families that Moses and Aaron counted, numbered, and organized to perform the tabernacle services, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
And Moses, Aaron, and Israel's leaders counted, numbered, and organized the families of Levite's sons by their fathers' houses.
They counted everyone who was between the age of thirty to fifty years old, who entered into the service to do the work of the congregation's tabernacle.
And overall, there were 80,580.
So, Moses counted, numbered, organized, and assigned all of them to their jobs, burdens, and services, as the Lord had commanded him.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said,
"Tell the Israelis that they must send anyone with a disease or leprosy, and anyone who was defiled by touching a dead body out of the camp.
Put both the males and females out of the camp, so that they do not defile the camps where I live."
And the Israelis put them out of the camp, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said,
"Tell the Israelis that if a man or woman commits a sin against the Lord and they are found guilty.
Then they must confess their sin, and compensate the person that they have sinned against, with the full amount of the damages plus an additional 20%.
But if they have no family to compensate, the Lord will be compensated through the priest when they bring the ram of the atonement to God.
All of the holy things that the Israelis offer and bring to the priest, will belong to God.
And all of the holy things that they give to the priest, will belong to God."
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said,
"Tell the Israelis that if a man's wife sins against him.
And she has sex with another a man but there are no witnesses against her, she is still guilty of adultery even if her husband does not know about it.
If her husband becomes suspicious and jealous, and he wants to find out if she has been unfaithful and defiled herself.

Then the man must bring his wife to the priest, along with an offering of 1/10th of an ephah of barley flour which is not mixed with oil or frankincense, as a jealousy offering to find out whether or not she is guilty of adultery.
Then the priest must present her to the Lord.
The priest must then mix some dirt from the tabernacle floor with some holy water in a clay bowl.
Then the priest will uncover her head, and set her before the Lord, and put the memorial jealousy offering in her hands. But the priest will hold the bitter water that curses the guilty in his hands.

The priest will swear an oath and say to the woman, 'If you have not committed adultery and defiled yourself by having sex with a man other than your husband, then you will be free of the curse that the bitter water causes.
But if you have been with another man and defiled yourself by having sex with a man other than your husband.'
Then the priest will swear the oath of the curse and say to the woman, 'The Lord will make you a curse among your people, your womb will rot, you will become infertile, and your stomach will swell.
And the water that causes the curse will enter your bowels and it will make your stomach swell and your womb rot!' And the woman will say, "Amen, amen!"
Then the priest will write these curses in a book and blot them out with the bitter water.
The priest will give the bitter water to the woman to drink. After she drinks and swallows some of the water that causes the curse, it will become bitter.
Then the priest will take the jealousy offering from the woman's hand, and wave it before the Lord and offer it on the altar.
The priest must then take a handful of the offering and burn it on the altar, and then the woman must drink the rest of the bitter water.

After she drinks the water, if she has defiled herself and sinned against her husband, the water in her stomach will become bitter and begin to swell, her womb will rot, she will be infertile, and she will be cursed among her own people.
But, if she has not defiled herself, she will be clean and free from the curse, and she will be fertile and able to bear children.
This is the law of jealousy when a wife goes off and has sex with a man other than her husband.
This law is also for the husband who becomes jealous or suspicious that his wife is cheating on him, then he will present her to the Lord, and the priest will perform the law's services upon her.
Then the husband will be innocent of any immorality, but she will be held accountable for her sin."
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said,
"Speak to the Israelis and tell them, if a man or woman makes a vow to devote themselves to the Lord as a Nazarite.
They must not drink any wine, distilled spirits, wine vinegar, distilled vinegar, liquor made from grapes, nor are they allowed to eat grapes or raisins.
During the time they spend in service to the Lord, they are not allowed to eat grape seeds, grape skins, or anything else that comes from the grape vine.
They must let their hair grow and they must not shave their head until their service is up, because during that time they will be holy to the Lord.
And they are not allowed to be around any dead bodies during the time of their service.
They are not allowed to go near their father, mother, brother, or sister when they die because God's consecration is upon their head.
And they will be holy during the entire time of their service to the Lord.
If someone near them suddenly dies and defiles their consecrated head, they must shave their head to cleanse and reconsecrate it seven days later.
On the eighth day, they must bring two turtle doves or two young pigeons to the priest at the tabernacle door.
The priest must offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering to atone for being defiled by the dead, and on that day, they will be made holy again.

The priest must consecrate their days of service to the Lord, but their days of service to the Lord before they were defiled will be lost, and they must bring a one-year-old lamb as a sin offering, because they were defiled.
This is the Nazarite law for those whose days of service to the Lord are satisfied, they must come to the congregation's tabernacle door.
And bring with them an unblemished one year old male lamb as a burnt offering, an unblemished one year old ewe lamb as a sin offering, and one unblemished ram as peace a offering to the Lord.
Plus a basket of unleavened bread, cakes made from fine flour mixed with oil, unleavened crackers anointed with oil, a bread offering, and their drink offering.
The priest must bring them before the Lord to make their sin and burnt offerings.
Then the priest must offer the ram as peace offerings to the Lord, along with the basket of unleavened bread as their bread offering, plus their drink offering.
The Nazarite must shave their head at the congregation's tabernacle door and put their hair in the fire under the peace offerings.
And the priest must put the hair from the Nazarites shaved head in their hands, along with the ram's shoulder, one unleavened cake, and one unleavened cracker from the basket.

Then the priest must wave them before the Lord, and this is a holy portion for the priest along with the breast wave offering and the sacred shoulder heave offering. Then the Nazarite will be allowed to drink wine.

This is the law for the Nazarites and their offerings who have vowed to devote themselves to the Lord's service. They may also bring other offerings in additional to what they promised to fulfill their vow to serve the Lord."
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said,
"Speak to Aaron and his sons and tell them to bless the Israelis and say,
'May the Lord bless you and keep you.
May the Lord make his face shine upon you and be gracious to you.
May the Lord lift up his face to you and give you peace.'
And when Aaron and his sons bless the Israelis in my name, I will also bless them."
When Moses finished setting up, anointing, and sanctifying the tabernacle including the altar, its vessels, and all of its accessories.
The princes of Israel and the tribal leaders from their fathers' houses, who had counted and numbered their armies.
Brought their offering before the Lord in front of the tabernacle, and they brought six covered wagons and twelve oxen. There was one wagon for two of the princes, and an ox for each prince.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said,

"Take their gifts and give them to the Levites, and use the oxen and wagons for transporting the congregation's tabernacle, and distribute them among the people in accordance with the services they are to perform."
So Moses gave the wagons and oxen to the Levites.
He gave Gershon's sons two wagons and four oxen, to help with the work they were responsible for.
He gave Merari's sons who worked for Aaron's son Ithamar, four wagons and eight oxen to help with their responsibilities.
But Kohath's sons were given nothing to help them with their services, because they were required to carry the sanctuary items on their shoulders.
And the princes made their offering before the altar for its dedication.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said, "Each prince must make his offering for the dedication of the altar on his appointed day."
So on the first day, Amminadab's son, Nashon, prince of the tribe of Judah made his offering.

Nashon offered one silver charger that weighed as much as 130 silver sanctuary shekels, and one silver bowl that weighed 70 shekels. Both of them were full of fine flour mixed with oil as a bread offering.
Plus one gold spoon full of incense, that was worth as much as ten gold sanctuary shekels.
And a young bull, one ram, and a one year old lamb as a burnt offering.
And one kid goat as a sin offering.
And Amminadab's son, Nashon, brought 2 oxen, 5 rams, 5 male goats, and 5 one year old lambs as his peace offering.

On the day that the altar was anointed, the twelve princes of Israel brought 12 silver chargers, 12 silver bowls, and 12 gold spoons that were dedicated to the altar.
Each silver charger weighed 130 sanctuary shekels, each bowl weighed 70 shekels, and all the silver bowls together weighed 2,400 shekels.
The 12 gold spoons each weighed 10 sanctuary shekels, which was a total of 120 shekels altogether.
They brought 12 young bulls, 12 rams, 12 one year old lambs, and 12 kid goats as the burnt offering, sin offering, and the bread offering.
The peace offering consisted of 24 oxen, 60 rams, 60 male goats, and 60 one year old lambs to dedicate the altar after it was anointed.
When Moses went into the congregation's tabernacle to speak with God, he heard the voice of the One True God speaking to him from the Mercy Seat between the two cherubim on the Ark of Testimony.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said,
"Speak to Aaron and tell him to light the seven lamps, so their light will shine above the lampstand."
So Aaron did as the Lord had commanded Moses, and he lit the seven lamps above the lampstand.
The lampstand was made the way that the Lord told Moses to make it and it was forged from pure gold. Everything from its stalk to its flowers were made from the pattern that the Lord had given Moses.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said,
"You must cleanse the Levites and separate them from Israelis.
In order to do this, you must sprinkle them with purifying water, they must shave off all the hair on their body, then they must wash their clothes. After they do all this, they will be clean.
Then they must take a young bull along with a bread offering of fine flour mixed with oil, and a second young bull as a sin offering.
Bring the Levites before the congregation tabernacle and assemble the whole Israeli congregation together.
Present the Levites before the Lord and the Israelis must lay their hands on the Levites.
Then Aaron must offer the Levites before the Lord as an offering from the Israelis, so they may perform the Lord's services.
The Levites must lay their hands on the bulls' heads, and they will offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering as an atonement to the Lord for the Levites.
Then present the Levites to Aaron and his sons as an offering to the Lord.
And the Levites you separate from among the Israelis will be mine.
Then the Levites may enter into the service of the congregation's tabernacle. After you cleanse them, they may be offered as a wave offering.
Because I have separated them from among the other Israelis to be completely dedicated to me, instead of the first-born male of everything that is born from all the children of Israel.

I have sanctified the firstborn males of both man and beast from the children of Israel for myself, because of the day that I killed all the firstborn male offspring of everything living in the land of Egypt.
And I have taken the Levites as a replacement for all the firstborn males of Israel.
