And I have given the Levites to Aaron and his sons, as a gift to perform the Lord's services for the Israelis in their congregation tabernacle. In order to make an atonement for the people, so that they do not have to suffer a plague when they come near the sanctuary."
Then Moses, Aaron, and the entire Israeli congregation did everything that the Lord had commanded Moses.
So the Levites were purified and they washed their clothes. Then Aaron offered them up as an offering before the Lord and made an atonement to cleanse them.
After that the Levites went to perform their services in the congregation tabernacle before Aaron and his sons, just as the Lord had instructed Moses to have the Levites do things.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said,
"This is what belongs to the Levites: Every man twenty-five years old and older will enter into the service of the congregation tabernacle.
Everyone fifty years old and older will retire and no longer serve or perform the tabernacle services.

But the Levites over fifty, may assist their brothers with their obligations in the congregation's tabernacle, but they must not perform any services in the tabernacle. This is how you must deal with the Levites and their responsibilities to the congregation tabernacle.
In the first month of the second year after the Israelis left Egypt, the Lord spoke to Moses in the Sinai wilderness and said,
"Let the Israelis keep the Passover in the appointed season.
Tell them that they must celebrate in the evening of the fourteenth day of the month during the appointed season and keep all of its rites and ceremonies."
So Moses spoke to the Israelis and told them to keep the Passover.
And the Israelis kept the Passover in the evening of the fourteenth day of the first month out in the Sinai wilderness, just as the Lord had commanded Moses.
But some men who could not keep the Passover came to Moses and Aaron because they had been defiled by the body of a dead man.

They said to Moses, "We have been defiled by a dead man's body, and we need to know if we are allowed to celebrate the Passover. And we need to know if we are allowed to make an offering to the Lord in the appointed season along with the other Israelis?"
Moses replied to them and said, "Wait here, and I will go and ask the Lord what to do about your situation."
And the Lord answered Moses and said,

"Speak to the Israelis and tell them, that if any of you or your descendants are unclean because of a dead body, or you are travelling in a foreign land, you are still allowed to observe the Lord's Passover.
They can celebrate it in the evening of the fourteenth day of the second month, and they must eat unleavened bread and bitter herbs.
They must not leave any leftover lamb until the next morning nor break any of its bones, and they must keep all of the Passover's legal decrees.

But a clean person who is not traveling and fails to keep the Passover, must bear their sin and they must be cut off from their people, because they did not bring their offering to the Lord in the appointed season.

If there are any foreigners living among you who want to keep the Lord's Passover, they must follow the same legal decrees. Everyone including both foreign and native-born Israelis is required to follow these same legal decrees."
The day that the tabernacle was erected, God covered the tent of testimony with a cloud, and it was covered by a column of fire from the evening until the next morning.
So it was covered by a cloud during the day, and it was covered by a column of fire in the evening.
When the cloud rose above the tabernacle, the Israelis moved forward and they camped wherever the cloud stopped.
At the Lord's command the Israelis moved, and they pitched their tents when the Lord commanded them. And they rested in their tents as long as the cloud covered the tabernacle.
When the cloud covered the tabernacle for a long time, the Israelis obeyed the Lord's command not to move, and as long as it was covered by the cloud they rested in their tents.
And that is how it was as long as the cloud covered the tabernacle, they obeyed the Lord and rested in their tents and at the Lord's command they moved forward.
So, when the cloud covered the tabernacle they rested in their tents, and when the cloud rose above the tabernacle, they moved their camp whether it was day or night.

It did not matter how long the cloud remained and covered the tabernacle. Whether it was two days, a month, or a year, the Israelis would not move, but as soon as it rose above the tabernacle, they moved their camp.
At the Lord's command they rested in their tents, and at the Lord's command they moved their camp. The Israelis kept every commandment that Moses gave them from the Lord.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said,
"Make two silver trumpets from a single piece of silver. Use them to call the assembly together and signal the camps when it is time to move.
When they blow the trumpets, the entire assembly will know to assemble at the congregation tabernacle door.
But if only one trumpet is blown, then everyone will know that Israel's princes are being summoned to Moses.
When the trumpets sound an alarm, the camps that lie on the eastern side of the tabernacle will move forward.
When the trumpets sound a second alarm, then the camps that lie on the south side will move forward, because the trumpets will sound off when it is time to move the camp.
But when you want to assemble the congregation, the trumpets will make a different sound than the sound of an alarm.
Aaron's sons, who are the priests will blow the trumpets, and you and your descendants must observe this law forever.
If you must go to war against an oppressive enemy in your own land, blow the trumpets to sound the alarm. Then God will remember you and you will be saved from your enemies.

You can also sound the trumpets to announce the beginning of the holidays, the beginning of the solemn days, the beginning of the months, and over the sacrificial peace offerings. And they will be a memorial to remind your Lord God of this covenant. I am your Lord God!"
On the twentieth day of the second month in the second year, the cloud rose above the congregation tabernacle of testimony.
And the Israelis left the Sinai wilderness and traveled until the cloud rested in the wilderness of Paran.
The people began their first journey when the Lord commanded Moses to move.
Amminadab's son Nashon, from the tribe of Judah moved his camp first and they raised the flag for their army to follow.
And Zuar's son Nathaniel, was over the people in the tribe of Issachar.
And Helon's son Eliab, was over the people in the tribe of Zebulun.
Gershon and Merari's sons took down the tabernacle and carried the tabernacle forward.
Then Shedeur's son Elizur, from the tribe of Reuben moved his camp and they raised the flag for their army to follow.
And Zurishaddai's son Shelumiel, was over the people in the tribe of Simeon.
And Deuel's son Eliasaph, was over the people in the tribe of Gad.
Next the Kohathites moved forward carrying the sanctuary items, and by the time they arrived at the new camp, the tabernacle would be setup.
Then Ammihud's son Elishama, from the tribe of Ephraim moved his camp and they raised the flag for their army to follow.
And Pedahzur's son Gamaliel, was over the people in the tribe of Manasseh.
And Gideoni's son Abidan, was over the people in the tribe of Benjamin.
The last to move forward was the tribe of Dan because they were camped at the rear of the tabernacle, and Ammishaddai's son Ahiezer, was over the people in the tribe of Dan.
And Ocran's son Pagiel, was over the people in the tribe of Asher.
And Enan's son Ahira, was over the people in the tribe of Naphtali.
This was the order in which the Israelite armies moved their camp forward.

When the time to move came, Moses spoke to his brother-in-law Hobab son of Raguel the Midianite and said, "We are moving to the Promised Land which the Lord has promised to give Israel, and I would like for you to come with us because the Lord has promised to give Israel many wonderful blessings."
And Hobab replied to Moses and said, "No, I am going to return to my own land where my relatives live."
And Moses said, "Please do not leave us because you know the way through the wilderness, and you can show us the way.
If you come with us, we will share all the good things with you, that the Lord has promised us."
Then the Israelis left the Lord's mountain and journeyed out into the wilderness for three days. They carried the Ark of the Covenant before them, and it showed them where to find a place to rest.
On the days that they moved forward, the Lord's cloud hovered above the tabernacle as they traveled.
When it was time to move, Moses stood before the ark and said, "Rise up Lord, scatter your enemies and make those who hate you flee before you."
When they stopped and set the Ark down, Moses would say, "Return to us Lord, and protect the many thousands of Israelis."

When the Lord heard the people complaining, he was very angry and upset. Their complaints kindled the Lord's fiery anger which burned among them. And it consumed those who were in the furthest parts of the camp.
The people cried out to Moses, so he prayed to the Lord and the fire was extinguished.
And Moses named the place Taberah, which means the burning place because the Lord's fiery anger burned among them.
The foreigners who mixed with the Israelis began to lust after the things that they had left behind in Egypt. The Israelis also began to cry out and said, "Who will give us some meat to eat?
We remember the fish, cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions, and garlic which we freely ate in Egypt.
But now our soul has dried up, and we have nothing at all to eat but this manna."
The manna looked like coriander seed, and it was a whitish color or about the same color as bdellium.
The people gathered and ground it into flour, then they made cakes and baked them in pans, and it tasted like it was baked in fresh oil.
The manna fell every evening when the dew fell on the camp.
Then Moses heard the people weeping from their tent doors. This made the Lord very angry and Moses was also displeased.
And Moses said to the Lord, "These people are the reason you have afflicted me. Why have I not found favor in your sight, why have you laid the burden of all of these people on me?

Did I conceive all of these people, am I the one who fathered them? Why did you tell me, that I have to carry them like a father carries his children, into the land that you swore to give to their fathers?
Where can I find enough meat to feed all of these people? They weep and ask me to give them some meat to eat.
I am unable to carry all of these people alone because it is too heavy a load for me.
If this is what you intend for my life, I pray that you will kill me and spare me from a lifetime of misery."
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said, "Bring me seventy Israeli elders who are officers over the people. Bring them to the congregation tabernacle to stand next to you.

Then I will come down and talk with you, and I will remove some of the spirit of responsibility which is on you and put it on them. They will help you bear the people's burdens, so that you are not alone and you will not have to bear all of their burdens alone.

And tell the people to sanctify themselves for tomorrow, because their cries have reached the Lord's ears, for the Lord has heard them crying out for meat. He has heard their complaints of how much happier they were in Egypt because of everything they left behind. Therefore, the Lord is going to give you all the meat you can eat.
You will not eat meat for just one day, two days, five days, ten days, nor even twenty days.

But you will eat meat for a whole month, until it comes out of your nostrils and you begin to loathe it. For you have despised the Lord who is among you, and he has heard your weeping, crying, and saying, 'Why did we ever leave Egypt?'"
And Moses responded to the Lord and said, "But there are 600,000 soldiers among all these people, and you said that you would give them enough meat to eat for a whole month.
If we kill all the flocks and herds and catch all the fish in the sea, would that even be enough to satisfy them all?"
And the Lord answered Moses and said, "Has the Lord's hand grown weak? Now you will see whether or not my words are true."
So Moses left and went to tell the people everything that the Lord had said, and he assembled seventy elders around the tabernacle.

And the Lord came down in a cloud and spoke to Moses and removed some of the spirit that was on him and gave it to the seventy elders, and when the spirit rested on them, they began to prophesy continuously.
Eldad and Medad were two of the seventy elders, but even though they had not gone to the tabernacle meeting, the spirit also rested on them, and they began to prophesy in their camp.
And a young man ran out to Moses and told him that Eldad and Medad were prophesying in the camp.
Joshua, son of Nun was one of Moses' young assistants, and he asked Moses to forbid Eldad and Medad from prophesying.
And Moses said to him, "Are you jealous of them for my sake? I wish God would make all of his people into prophets and put his spirit onto all of them!"
Then Moses returned to camp with all the Israeli elders.

And the Lord sent the winds to bring quail from the sea, and they fell in the camp. And they were scattered all over the camp for a day's ride in all directions, and they were piled up on the ground two cubits deep.
And the people were up on their feet all that day, all that night, and all the next day gathering quail. The least that was gathered was ten homers, and they spread them all over the camp.
Before they began to eat or even chewed their first bite, the Lord's anger was kindled against them, and he sent a great plague to strike the people down.
And he named that place Kibroth-Hattaavah, which means grave of gluttony, because they buried the people there who lusted after the things that were left behind in Egypt.
And the people moved to Hazeroth, where they lived when they left Kibroth-Hattaavah.
Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses because he had married an Ethiopian woman.
And they said, "Does the Lord only speak to Moses, or does he not also speak to us?" And the Lord heard them talking.
Now Moses was a very humble man, much humbler than all the other men on earth.
Then suddenly the Lord spoke to Moses, Aaron, and Miriam and said, "I want the three of you to come to the congregation tabernacle, so they went.
And the Lord came down in a column of cloud and stood in the tabernacle door, and he called Aaron and Miriam, and they both came.
And the Lord said to them, "Hear my words, if there were a prophet among you, I would make myself known to him in a vision and I would speak to him in a dream.
But my servant Moses is not that way, he is the most faithful of my whole house.
So I speak to him face to face and not in dark speech, because he sees the Lord the way he is, so why are you unafraid to speak against my servant Moses?"
And the Lord was very angry with them and he left.
The cloud left the tabernacle, and Miriam turned as white as snow and Aaron saw that she had now become leprous.
And Aaron said to Moses, "Please help us, I beg you not to lay our foolish sin on us.
Do not let her be like a dead person, whose flesh is half consumed when they come out of their mother's womb."
And Moses cried to the Lord and said, "O God, I beg you, please heal her."
And the Lord said to Moses, "If her father had spit in her face for her sin, would she not be ashamed of herself for seven days? Send her out of the camp for seven days, after that she can return."
And Miriam was sent out of the camp for seven days, and the people's camp did not move until she was allowed to return.
Then the people left Hazeroth and camped in the Paran wilderness.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said,
"Have each prince send a leader from each of the twelve tribes of Israel, to search and explore the land of Canaan which I have given them."
And Moses did as the Lord commanded and sent some of the leaders from the tribes of Israel, who were camped in the wilderness of Paran.
And these are the names of those who were sent, beginning with Zaccur's son Shammua, who was sent from Reuben's tribe.
And Hori's son Shaphat was sent from Simeon's tribe.
And Jephunneh's son Caleb was sent from Judah's tribe.
Joseph's son Igal was sent from Issachar's tribe.
Nun's son Oshea was sent from Ephraim's tribe.
Raphu's son Palti was sent from Benjamin's tribe.
Sodi's son Gaddiel was sent from Zebulun's tribe.
Susi's son Joseph Gaddi was sent from Manasseh's tribe.
Gemalli's son Ammiel was sent from Dan's tribe.
Michael's son Sethur was sent from Asher's tribe.
Vophsi's son Nahbi was sent from Naphtali's tribe.
Machii's son Geuel was sent from Gad's tribe.
Moses sent these men out to explore the land, and he named Nun's son Oshea, Jehoshua.
Moses sent them out to survey the land of Canaan, and he told them to go southward toward the mountain.
To see what was in the land there, to find out who the people were that lived there, and to find out if they were strong, weak, few, or many.
To see if the land there was good or bad, and to find out if the people lived in walled cities or tents.

He wanted them to see what type of land it was, whether it was fertile or barren, or whether there were forests there. And he told them to try and bring back crop samples, because it was time for the first grape harvest.
So they searched the land in the wilderness of Zin from Rehob to Hamath.
They traveled north to Hebron, where Anak's descendants Ahiman, Sheshai, and Talmai lived. Hebron had been built seven years before the Egyptian city of Zoan.
They came upon the Eshcol brook, and they took a sample cluster of grapes so large that it took two men to carry it, and they took samples of the pomegranates and figs too.
They called the place the Eshcol brook, because of the grape cluster they took from there.
After searching the land for forty days, they returned.

They returned to the Israeli congregation of Kadesh, in the wilderness of Paran, and went to Moses, Aaron, and the entire congregation with word of what they had found, and they showed them the samples they had brought back.
And they said to them, "We went where you sent us, and it is a land that flows with milk and honey, and these samples are part of the land's fruit there.
But the people living there are strong, and they live in great walled cities, and we also saw Anak's descendants.
The Amalekites live in the south but the Hittites, Jebusites, and Amorites live in the mountains, and the Canaanites live by the sea near the Jordan coastline."
And Caleb tried calm the people and he said to Moses, "Let us go right now and take the land, because there is no doubt that we are strong enough to overcome the people there."
But the men with him said, "We cannot go up against these people, because they are stronger than us."

And they began to spread rumors about the land they had just searched to the Israelis and said, "The land we explored, is a land that will consume anyone who tries to live there, because we saw a huge mass of very powerful people there.
We also saw Anak's descendants who come from giants there, and we looked like tiny grasshoppers compared to them."
And the entire congregation of people cried out and wept throughout the night.

All the Israelis were whispering behind Moses and Aaron's backs, and they all went to them and said, "Why did God not just let us die in Egypt, and why does he not just let us die out here in the wilderness?
The Lord has brought us to this land, to be killed in battle, so that our wives and children would be captured and preyed upon, it would be better if we just return to Egypt."
And they said one to another, "Let us appoint a new leader and return to Egypt."
Then Moses and Aaron bowed facedown before the whole Israelis congregation.
And Nun's son Joshua, and Jephunneh's son Caleb who were two of the men who had scouted the land, stood before the people and tore their clothes.
And they spoke to the entire Israeli congregation and said, "The land which we have just scouted, is an exceptionally good land.
If the Lord is pleased with us, he will give us this land which is a land flowing with milk and honey.
Do not rebel against the Lord, and do not fear the people of this land because they are our bread. For they are defenseless and the Lord is with us, so do not fear them."
But the congregation decided to stone them, and the Lord's glory appeared to them in the tabernacle.

And the Lord said to Moses, "How long are these people going to provoke me, how long will it be before they believe me? Even after all the signs and wonders I have shown them, they still do not believe me.
I will disinherit them and send a pestilence to destroy them, and I will make you a greater and mightier nation than them."
Then Moses replied to the Lord and said, "If you do that, the Egyptians will hear that you used your power to bring these people out of Egypt.

And the Egyptians will tell the inhabitants here that the Lord is among the Israeli people. For they have seen you face to face and your cloud stands above them. And you move before them in a column of a cloud during the day and they see you in a column of fire at night.
If you kill all of these people as one man now, then the nations that have heard of you will speak against you and say,
"The Lord was unable to bring these people into the land which he swore to give them, so he killed them in the wilderness."
Therefore I beg you Lord, show the people that the Lord's power is as great as you promised it would be when you said,

"The Lord is merciful and long suffering, he forgives immorality and sin, and he will not clear the guilty. And the immorality of the fathers will be visited on the children to the third and fourth generation."
O Lord, please forgive the immorality of these people through your great mercy. You forgave them when they were in Egypt and you continue to forgive them until this very day.
And the Lord said, "I have forgiven them as you have asked because of the words you have spoken.
But as truly as I live, the entire earth will be filled with the glory of the Lord.
But everyone who has seen my glory and the miracles I have performed, both in Egypt and out in the wilderness, have now tempted me ten times and they refuse to listen to my voice.
So they will not see the land that I promised to give their fathers, nor will anyone else who has provoked me.
But my servant Caleb's spirit was very different, and he completely believed God, so he and his descendants will take possession of the land that they explored.
The Amalekites and Canaanites live in the valley, so tomorrow I want you to move out into the wilderness by way of the Red Sea."
And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron and said,
"How long must I tolerate this evil Israelis congregation that I have heard murmuring against me.
So speak to them today and say, 'As surely as the Lord God lives, he will judge you by your own words.
Therefore anyone counted in the census who is twenty years old or older who has murmured against me will fall and die in this wilderness.
None of you will be given the promised land in which to live, except for Jephunneh's son Caleb and Nun's son Joshua.
But I will bring your children whom you said would be plundered, into the land and they will enjoy the land which you despise.
But as for you, your dead bodies will fall in this wilderness.
And your children will wander in the wilderness for forty years and suffer for your unfaithfulness until your dead bodies have decayed in the wilderness.

You explored the land for forty days, so you will bear your sin for forty years. You will wander in the wilderness for one year for each day you spent exploring the land, and you will know that your suffering comes from my unhappiness with you.
I the Lord have spoken, and I will surely do everything to this evil congregation that they have spoken against me, and they will die and decay in the wilderness.'"
For when the men whom Moses sent to explore the land returned, they had the entire congregation gossiping against Moses, by slandering the land.
So the men who brought the evil report about the land, died by the plague before the Lord.
But Nun's son Joshua and Jephunneh's son Caleb who were two of the men sent to explore the land, were not harmed and they did not die.
After Moses told the Israeli people all of these things, they were greatly grieved and they mourned.
So they got up early in the morning, and went up into the mountains and said, "We are here, and we will go to the place which the Lord has promised, because we have sinned."
But Moses answered them and said, "Do you want to violate the Lord's commandment? For you know that if you violate the Lord's commandment, it will not prosper.
So do not go up there, because the Lord is not with you and you will be defeated before your enemies.
You know that the Amalekites and Canaanites are there, and you will fall by the sword because you have turned away from the Lord, and the Lord will not be with you."
But they went up to the mountain top anyway, and neither Moses nor the Lord's Ark of the Covenant left the camp with them.
Then the Amalekites and Canaanites came down from the mountain, defeated them, embarrassed them, and pursued them all the way to Hormah.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said,
"Speak to the Israelis and tell them; 'When you enter the land I gave you for your home.
You must make a sweet savory burnt offering to the Lord by fire to fulfill a vow, a freewill offering, or for your solemn feasts from your herds or flocks.
When you bring these offerings to the Lord, you must also bring a bread offering of 6 1/4 ounces of a measure of flour mixed with 1 1/2 quarts of oil.
And with each lamb offered as a burnt offering, you must also bring 1 1/2 quarts of wine as a drink offering.
Or for a ram offering, you must prepare a bread offering using 12 1/2 ounces of flour mixed with 2 quarts of oil.
And you must bring two quarts of wine as a drink offering, and the aroma will be very pleasing to the Lord.
When you prepare a bull as a burnt offering, a sacrifice to fulfill a vow, or a peace offering to the Lord.
You must also bring with the bull offering a 3/10th deal of flour mixed with 1/2 hin of oil.
And you must bring 1/2 hin of wine as a drink offering along with the fire offering, as a sweet savory aroma to the Lord.
This is how it must be done, whether it is for a bull, ram, lamb, or a kid goat.
You must prepare every offering this way, no matter how many are offered.
Everyone born in Israel must prepare their fire offerings this way, as a sweet savory aroma to the Lord.
If there are strangers visiting or living with you or your descendants, and they want to make a sweet savory offering by fire to the Lord, then let them do it this way.

There must be only one law that forever applies to everyone in the congregation including any foreigners among you and your descendants. So, foreigners must be treated the same as native-born Israelis.
There will be only one law concerning this matter, for both you and any foreigners visiting or living among you.'"
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said,
"Speak to the Israelis and tell them; 'When you enter the land where I am bringing you.
And you eat the bread of the land; you must make a sacred offering to the Lord.
You must offer a cake from your first dough as a sacred offering to the Lord, just as you offer the grain from your threshing floor.
You and all of your descendants must give the Lord your first dough as a sacred offering.
If you have mistakenly failed to observe all of the commandments that the Lord spoke to Moses.
Including the laws the Lord gave to Moses, from the day that the Lord commanded Moses, which are also for all of your descendants to come.

Then if one of these laws is broken because of the congregation's ignorance of the law, the congregation must offer a young bull as burnt offering and a sweet savory aroma to the Lord. Along with the meat offering and drink offering prepared this way, the congregation must offer one kid goat as a sin offering.

The priest must make an atonement for the entire Israeli congregation, and their sin will be forgiven. They must bring their burnt offering and their sin offering before the Lord, to make amends for their ignorance of the law.
Then everyone will be forgiven for their ignorance, including the entire Israeli congregation and any foreigners visiting or living among them, because all of the people were ignorant of the law.
If anyone sins through their ignorance, they must bring a one-year-old female goat for a sin offering.
The priest can make an atonement before the Lord for the ignorant soul who sins because of their ignorance of the law, and they will be forgiven.
There will be only one law for anyone who sins through ignorance, including both native born Israelis and foreigners who are visiting or living among them.
But anyone who is overconfident in their sin and disrespects the Lord, whether native born or a foreign visitor living among them, will be cut off from their people.
So the soul who has despised the Lord's word and broken God's commandment, will be completely cut off and their immorality will be on them.'"
While they were out in the wilderness, the Israelis found a man who had gathered some sticks on the Sabbath.
So they brought him to Moses, Aaron, and the congregation.
And they locked him away, because they did not know what to do with him.
And the Lord said to Moses, "The man must be put to death, and the congregation must stone him to death outside the camp."
So the congregation took him out of the camp and stoned him to death as the Lord had commanded Moses.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said,
"Speak to the Israelis and tell them; 'You must attach a fringe made with a blue ribbon and beads along the borders of their garments, and this should be done throughout all generations.

This fringe will be a reminder to them, so that when they see it, they will remember and keep all of the Lord's commandments, and they will not seek out what their own heart and eyes desire, which causes them to go a whoring.
This will help you remember to keep all of my commandments, and you will be holy to your God.
Because I am your Lord God! For I brought you out of Egypt to be your God, and I am your Lord God! Amen!'"
Korah was Izhar's son, who was Kohath's son from Levi's tribe, began making plans to revolt, along with Eliab and On's sons Dathan and Abiram. On was Peleth's son from Reuben's tribe.
They rose up against Moses with 250 princes from the Israeli assembly, who were famous leaders within the congregation.

They all gathered together against Moses and Aaron and said to them, "You have taken on too much on yourselves, since everyone in the congregation is Holy, and the Lord is among them, why do you lift yourselves up above everyone else in the Lord's congregation?"
When Moses heard this, he laid facedown.
And he spoke to Korah and his company and said, "Tomorrow the Lord will make clear who his people are, who is Holy, and he will choose the one that is allowed to come near him.
Do this, Korah and all his company must take their censers.
Then tomorrow, light the fire in them, and sprinkle incense in them before the Lord, and the Lord will choose that man to be Holy, because you sons of Levi have taken on too much upon yourselves."
And Moses said to Korah, "I pray that you sons of Levi listen and hear.

It may seem to be a small thing to you, that the God of Israel has separated you from the Israeli congregation, in order to bring you close to him, to perform the services of the Lord's tabernacle, and to stand before the congregation to minister to them?
He has brought you and all your brothers from Levi's tribe close to him, and now you also want to be priests too?
And now all of you have come together against the Lord, and that's why you cry out against Aaron?"
Moses sent for Eliab's sons Dathan and Abiram, but they refused to come.
Did you bring us out of a land flowing with milk and honey, to kill us in the wilderness, just so you could make us your servants?
Besides that, you have not brought us to a new land flowing with milk and honey, or given us new fields and vineyards, and we think you're planning to trick these men, so we will not come up.
This made Moses very angry, and he said to the Lord, "Do not accept their offering, I have not taken as much as even a donkey from them, nor have I hurt any of them."
And Moses said to Korah, "You and Aaron must come here tomorrow along with your entire company and present yourselves before the Lord.
Aaron, and all 250 of them must bring their incense filled censers and present them before the Lord.
Moses and Aaron and every one of them must then light their censer on fire, and sprinkle incense on them in the congregation's tabernacle doorway."
Korah stirred up the congregation against them, and they assembled themselves before the door of the congregation's tabernacle, and the Lord in all his glory appeared to the whole congregation.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron and said,
Separate yourselves from these people, and I will instantly destroy them.
And they fell facedown and said, "O God, the God of the spirits of all flesh, will you allow yourself to be angry with the whole congregation because one man has sinned?"
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said,
"Tell the people to leave Korah, Dathan, and Abiram's tabernacle."
Then the Israeli elders got up and went with Moses to see Dathan and Abiram.
Moses spoke to the congregation and said, "I beg you to get up and touch nothing, and leave these wicked men's tents, or else you will also be consumed by their sins."
So they got up and left Korah, Dathan, and Abiram's tents, then Dathan and Abiram came out, and stood in the doorway of their tents, along with their wives, sons, and children.
And Moses said, "So that you will know that the Lord has sent me to do this work, and because none of it has come from my own mind.
If these men die of natural causes, or they do not suffer an unusual fate, then the Lord has not sent me.

But if the Lord creates something new, and the earth opens her mouth and swallows them up, along with everything they own, and they quickly fall into the pit, then you will understand that these men have provoked the Lord."
And just as he finished speaking, the ground opened up beneath them, and the earth was torn apart.
The earth opened her mouth and swallowed the men from Korah and their families, their houses, and everything they owned.
They all went down into the pit alive, and the earth closed in on them, and they disappeared from the congregation.
All the Israelis fled when they heard the people's screams, because they were afraid the earth would swallow them up also.
And a fire came out from the Lord and consumed the 250 men that offered incense.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said,
Speak to priest Aaron's son Eleazar, and tell him, that because they are Holy, they must remove the censers from the fire and scatter the ashes all around over there.

Recycle the censers that belonged to these sinners and make some large platters from them to cover the altar, it is because they were offered before the Lord that they are considered to be holy and it will be as a sign to the Israelis.
The priest Eleazar took the brass censers that belonged to the men that were burnt, and he had them forged into large platters to cover the altar.

This will be a reminder to the Israelis, that only Aaron's descendants are allowed come near the Lord to offer incense before him, and they are not to be like Korah and as his company," this is the word that the Lord gave to Moses, for him to give to the congregation.
But the next day the whole congregation of the Israelis murmured against Moses and Aaron, and said, "You have killed the Lord's people."
And when the congregation gathered together to protest against Moses and Aaron, they looked toward the congregation's tabernacle, and behold a cloud covered it, and the glory of the Lord appeared.
Then Moses and Aaron went before the congregation's tabernacle.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said,
"Leave this congregation, so that I may immediately destroy them," and they fell facedown.

And Moses said to Aaron, "Take a censer and put fire in it taken from the altar, and sprinkle incense on it, and go quickly to the congregation, and make an atonement for them, because the Lord's anger has gone out from here, and the plague has begun."
So Aaron ran out into the middle of the congregation as Moses commanded, and, behold the plague had begun, and he sprinkled incense on the censer, and he made an atonement for the people.
And he stood between the living and the dead, and the plague was stopped.
And 14,700 more people died from the plague because of what Korah had started.
Aaron returned to Moses in the congregation's tabernacle doorway, and the plague was stopped.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said,
"Speak to the Israelis and tell them to engrave twelve rods with the names of each of the chiefs of the twelve tribes of their fathers and give one to each chief.
Write Aaron's name on the rod for Levi's tribe, because one staff will be given to the each of the chiefs of their fathers' house.
Place the rods in the congregation's tabernacle before the 'Ark of Testimony', where I will meet with you.
And the staff of the man that I have chosen will bud and bloom, and I will silence the Israelis cries and complaints against you when they see this."
So Moses spoke to the Israelis, and together they all gave him a staff for each chief of their fathers' tribes, and there were a total twelve rods, including the one for Aaron.
And Moses laid the rods before the Lord in the tabernacle of witness.
The next day Moses went into the congregation's tabernacle of witness and behold Aaron's staff for Levi's tribe had sprouted buds, and it bloomed and produced almonds.
Moses brought all the staffs from before the Lord and presented them to the Israelis as they watched him present a rod to each of the chiefs.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said, "Place Aaron's staff before the testimony as a token to remember the rebels that cried out against me to stop their complaints and rumors, so they do not die."
And Moses did what the Lord commanded.
And the Israelis spoke to Moses and said, "Behold death has overtaken us.
Whoever comes anywhere near the Lord's tabernacle will die, we will be consumed by death?"
And the Lord said to Aaron, "You, your sons, and your father's tribe along with you will bear the sanctuary's immorality, and you and your sons will also bear the immorality of the priesthood.
And bring your brothers from your father Levi's tribe with you, so that they may be joined with you to serve you, but you and your sons will minister before the congregation's tabernacle of witness.
They will do whatever you ask them to do to maintain the tabernacle, but they are not allowed to come near the sanctuary vessels or the altar, or both you and them will die.
And they will help you keep and maintain the congregation's tabernacle, to do whatever is needed for the tabernacle, and nobody from the other tribes will be allowed to come near you.
You will responsible for the sanctuary and altar, so that there will be no anger on the Israelis anymore.
And behold, I have taken your Levite brothers from the Israelis tribes, to be given as a gift for the Lord, to do the work of the congregation's tabernacle.

And that's why you and your sons will serve as priests for everything concerning the altar, including what's inside the vail, I have given the priest's office to you as a gift of service, and anyone else that comes near must be put to death."

And the Lord spoke to Aaron and said, "Behold I will make you responsible for my sacred offerings from the Israelite's Holy things, I have given them to you to anoint you and your sons, by legal decree forever.

This will be your portion of the most Holy things, every burnt offering, every bread offering, every sin offering, and every trespass offering that they give to me will be most Holy for you and for your sons.
You and the other males will eat it in the Most Holy Place, and it will be Holy to you.

This is the portion of the sacred offering and wave offerings of the Israelis gifts. I have given them to you, your sons, and your daughters, which by law will be forever, and every clean person in your house will be allowed to eat it.
I give you all of the best oil, wine, wheat, and the first fruits which the Israelis offer to the Lord.
And anything in the land that ripens first which they bring to the Lord, will be yours, and every clean person in your house will be allowed to eat it.
Everything that Israel donates will be yours.

Every living thing that is born of flesh whether man or beast, which they bring to the Lord, will be yours. But the firstborn of man must be redeemed, and the firstborn of the unclean beasts must be redeemed.
Payment for those to be redeemed must be paid when they are a month old. The price will be determined by you based on the value of five sanctuary shekels, which is worth twenty gerahs.

But you are not allowed to redeem firstborn cows, sheep, or goats, because they are Holy, so you must sprinkle their blood on the altar, and burn their fat as a burnt offering, to make a sweet savory aroma for the Lord.
And their flesh will be yours, like the wave offering and right shoulder are yours.

I have given you, your sons, and your daughters all the sacred offerings of holy things, which the Israelis offer to the Lord. They will be yours by law forever, for it is a covenant made with salt which will last forever before the Lord for you and your descendants."
And the Lord spoke to Aaron and said, "You will have no inheritance in their land, or any part among them, I am your part and your inheritance among the Israelis.
And, behold I have given Levi's children the one-tenth tithes offered by the Israelis as their inheritance, as payment for the services they perform for the congregation's tabernacle.
And the Israelis must not come near the congregation's tabernacle from now on, so that they do not die because of their sin.

But the Levites will service the congregation's tabernacle, and they will bear the immorality of their sin, and this law will last forever for their descendants, and from among the Israelis, they will have no inheritance.

But I have given the sacred tithe offerings to the Lord from the Israelis to the Levites for their inheritance, that's why I have said to them, that among all of Israel they will have no other inheritance."
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said,

"Speak to the Levites and tell them, when you collect the tithes from the Israelis which I have given you for your inheritance, then you must make it a sacred offering for the Lord of 1/10th of the tithe.
And you must calculate your sacred offering, as though it were the wheat from the threshing room floor, or the fullness of the winepress.
You must also offer a sacred offering to the Lord from the tithes which you receive from the Israelis and give the Lord's portion to priest Aaron.
Out of all the gifts you offer as a sacred offering to the Lord, let the best holiest part of it be lifted up to the Lord.
That's why you must tell them, when you have lifted up the best of it, then it will be given to the Levites like the increase from the threshing room floor and the winepress.
And it will be your food for you and your households, because it is your reward for your service in the congregation's tabernacle.
And you will bear no sin from it, because when you have lifted up the best, and you do not pollute the Israelis' Holy things, you will not die."
And the Lord spoke to Moses and to Aaron and said,
This is a legal decree which the Lord commanded when he said, "Speak to the Israelis, and tell them to bring you an unblemished red heifer, that has never been yoked.
Give her to priest Eleazar and he will take her outside the camp, where he will have her slaughtered before him.
Eleazar must then dip his finger in her blood and sprinkle it directly in front of the congregation's tabernacle seven times.
He will then have the heifer including her hide, flesh, blood, and dung burned before him.
The priest must throw cedar wood, hyssop, and scarlet into the fire with the burning heifer.
Then the priest must wash his clothes, and take a bath in fresh clean water, and afterwards he will go back to the camp, where he will be unclean until the evening.
The man that actually burned her must wash his clothes, and take a bath in fresh clean water, and he will be unclean until the evening.

And a clean man will gather the heifer's ashes and lay them up outside the camp in a clean place, and it will be kept for the Israeli congregation, and they will use it to make the water of separation for the purification of sin.

And the one who gathers the heifer's ashes must wash his clothes, and he will be unclean until the evening. This law will last forever and is to be kept for the Israelis or any foreigners living among them.
And anyone that touches a man's dead body, will be unclean for seven days.
He must purify himself this way on the third day, and on the seventh day he will be clean, but if he does not purify himself on the third day, then he will not be clean on the seventh day.

Anyone that touches a man's dead body, and does not purify themselves, defiles the Lord's tabernacle, and their soul will be cut off from Israel, because the water of separation was not sprinkled on them, they will still be unclean.
This law is to be invoked when a man dies in his home, and anyone and everyone that comes into or is already in the home, will be unclean for seven days.
And every uncovered open bowl will be unclean.
Anyone that touches someone who is killed in battle, or any other dead body, or a dead man's bones, or they touch a grave, will be unclean for seven days.
The unclean person must take the burnt heifer's ashes and put them in a bowl with clean running water to make the water of separation for the purification for sin.

A clean person must take a hyssop branch, dip it in the water, and sprinkle it on the tent, the bowls, anyone that was there, anyone that touched a bone, anyone that touched someone killed in battle, anyone that touched any other dead bodies, or even if they touched a grave.

The clean person must sprinkle the water of separation on the unclean person on the third and seventh day, and on the seventh day they must purify themselves by washing their clothes, taking a bath in clean water, and they will be clean in the evening.

But the unclean person that does not purify themselves, will be cut off from the congregation, because they have defiled the Lord's sanctuary, and the water of separation was not sprinkled on them, and they are still unclean.
This law that lasts forever states, that anyone who sprinkles or touches the water of separation must wash their clothes, and they will be unclean until evening.
And whatever the unclean person touches will be unclean, and if they touch another soul, that soul will be unclean until evening."
Then in the first month, the entire Israeli congregation, went out into the desert of Zin, and the people lived in Kadesh, and Miriam died and was buried there.
And there was no water for the congregation, and they gathered together to complain against Moses and Aaron.
The people were angry with Moses and they said, "If only God would have let us die when our brothers died before the Lord!
Why have you brought the Lord's congregation into this wilderness, was it just so that we and our cattle should die here?
That's why you made us leave Egypt, it was to bring us into this evil place! This place has no seed, no figs, no grapevines, no pomegranates, and not even any water to drink."
Moses and Aaron left the assembly and went to the congregation's tabernacle door, and when they fell facedown, the Lord's glory appeared to them.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said,

Take the staff, and gather your brother Aaron and the assembly together, and speak to the rock while they watch, and water will flow from the rock for you to give to the congregation and their beasts to drink.
And Moses took the staff, as the Lord commanded him.
Then Moses and Aaron gathered the congregation together before the rock, and Moses said to them, "Hear this you rebels; must we fetch water for you from this rock?"
Moses lifted up his hand, and struck the rock twice with his staff, the water flowed abundantly, and the congregation and their beasts drank.
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron and said, "Because you did not believe me, or sanctify me in the eyes of the Israelis, you will not lead them into the land which I have given them."
And this place will be known as the water of Meribah, because the Israelis struggled with the Lord, and they found him to be Holy.
Moses sent messengers from Kadesh to the king of Edom with this message, "You know of all the hardships your brothers from Israel have suffered.
You saw how it was when our fathers moved to Egypt, and how we had to live in Egypt for a long time, and how the Egyptians mistreated us, and our fathers.
And the Lord heard us when we cried out to him, and he sent an angel who brought us out of Egypt, and now we are in Kadesh, which is a city near your border.

I ask that you give us safe passage through your country, and we will not travel through any of your fields or vineyards. We will not drink your well water, but we will travel straight through on the king's highway, and we will not turn to the left or the right, until we have passed completely through your land and have reached the other side of your borders."
Edom answered him and said, "You may not pass through my land, or else I will meet you on the battlefield with the sword."

The Israelis said to him, "We will only travel by the highway, and if we or our cattle drink any of your water, then I will pay for it, I only ask that you please let us go through and we will do nothing more than walk through on our own two feet."
And he answered him and said, "You will not be allowed to pass through," then Edom went out to meet them with an army of great strength.
So Edom refused to let Israel pass through his land, and they turned away and went in a different direction.
And the whole Israelis congregation traveled from Kadesh and went to Mount Hor.
On Mount Hor near the coastal land of Edom, the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron and said,
"Aaron and his people will stay here, because they will not be allowed to enter into the land which I have given to Israel, because they rebelled against my word at the waters of Meribah.
So bring Aaron and his son Eleazar up to Mount Hor.
And strip Aaron of his garments, and put them on his son Eleazar, because Aaron and his people will die and be put to rest there."
And Moses did what the Lord commanded, and they went to Mount Hor, then in front of the entire congregation.
He stripped Aaron of his garments, and put them on his son Eleazar, and Aaron died right there on the mountain top, and Moses and Eleazar came down from the mountain.
And when the congregation saw that Aaron was dead, the entire House of Israel mourned him for thirty days.
When the Canaanite King Arad, who lived in the south heard that Israel had sent spies, he fought against them and took some of them as prisoners.
And Israel made a promise to the Lord and said, "If you deliver these people into my hands, then I will completely destroy their towns and cities."
And the Lord heard Israel, and delivered the Canaanites to them, and they completely destroyed their towns and cities, and he named the place Hormah.
Then they left Mount Hor and traveled by the Red Sea around the land of Edom, and the people became very discouraged along the way.
And the people cried out against God and Moses and said, "Why have you brought us out of Egypt to die in the wilderness? There is no bread or water, and our soul loathes this awful bread."
And the Lord sent fiery serpents among the people, and they bit the people, and many Israelis died.
So the people went to Moses and said, "We have sinned and spoken against you and the Lord, please pray to the Lord and ask him to take serpents away from us," and Moses prayed for the people.
And the Lord said to Moses, "Make a fiery serpent, and set it on a staff, and anyone who is bitten by a snake will live when they look at it."
And Moses made a brass serpent and put it on a staff, and when someone was bitten by a snake they would live after they looked at it.
And the Israelis moved forward, and they camped in Oboth.
They moved again from Oboth to Ije-Abarim near Moab, and they camped in the wilderness facing the rising sun.
They moved from there and camped in the valley of Zared.
From there they moved and camped on the other side of the Arnon river, which is in the wilderness along the Amorite coast, because the Arnon river is on the border between Moab and the Amorites.
Therefore it is said in the Book of the Wars of the Lord, "What he did in the Red sea and in the brooks of Arnon.
And at the stream of the brooks that go down to the home of Ar, which lies on the border of Moab."
From there they went to Beer, which is near the well where the Lord spoke to Moses and said, "Gather the people together, and I will give them water."
Then Israel sang this song, "Spring up, O well, all of you sing to it.
Sing of the people's leaders who dug the well with their staffs, as they were directed by the lawgiver, and they left the wilderness and went to Mattanah.
And then they traveled from Mattanah to Nahaliel, and from Nahaliel to Bamoth.
And from the Bamoth valley, which is in the country of Moab, to the top of Pisgah which looks toward Jeshimon.
And Israel sent messengers to Sihon King of the Amorites and said,

"Please let us pass through your land, if you do, we will not walk through your fields or vineyards, we will not drink water from your well, but we will travel by the king's highway, until we reach the borders on the other side of your land."
And Sihon refused to let Israel pass through his land, but he assembled his army, and went to confront them in the wilderness, and when he met them in Jahaz, he fought them there.
Israel defeated him in battle and took possession of his land from the river Arnon to Jabbok, all the way to the border of Ammon, because the Ammonites were too strong.
Israel took all of their cities, and they lived in Heshbon and all of the Amorite's cities, towns, and villages.
For Heshbon was the city of Sihon the king of the Amorites, who had fought against the former King of Moab, and taken his land all the way to the river Arnon.
That's why the wise people who speak in proverbs say, "Come to Heshbon, let the city of Sihon be built and prepared.
For a fire has gone out of Heshbon, a flame from the city of Sihon, it has consumed Ar of Moab, and the lords of the high places of Arnon.
Sorrow to you Moab! You have been undone, O people of Chemosh, he has given his sons that escaped death as fugitives, and the daughters of Sihon king of the Amorites, have been taken into captivity.
We have shot at them, Heshbon has perished all the way to Dibon, and we have laid waste to Nophah, which reaches all the way to Medeba."
Thus Israel lived in the land of the Amorites.
Moses sent spies to Jaazer, and they captured its villages and drove out the Amorites living there.
And they turned and went by Bashan, where King Og of Bashan and all his people went to fight against them at Edrei.

And the Lord said to Moses, "Do not fear him, because I have delivered him, his land, and all of his people into your hand, and you will defeat him just as you did the Amorite's King Sihon, who lived at Heshbon."
So they defeated him, his sons, and all his people, and they fought until there were none of them left alive, and they took possession of his land.
The Israelis moved forward, and set up camp in the plains of Moab, on this side of the Jordan River, near Jericho.
And Zippor's son Balak saw everything that Israel had done to the Amorites.
Moab was extremely distressed and frightened of the Israeli people, because there were so many of them.

And Zippor's son Balak, who was the Moabite King at that time, spoke to the Midian elders and said, "These people will consume everything around us, and they will devour us like an ox eats the grass out in the fields."

So he sent messengers to Pethor, which is near the river in the land of his people's children. He sent them with a message for Beor's son Balaam which said, "Behold there are some people who have come here from Egypt, that are so numerous that they cover the face of the earth, and they have set up camp near me.

Please answer my prayer and put a curse on these people, because they are too greater than I am. If you come and help me, perhaps we will be strong enough to defeat them and drive them out of the land, because I know that when you bless someone, they are blessed, and when you curse someone, they are cursed."
And the elders of Moab and Midian left with the rewards of divination for the prophet in their hands, and they went to Balaam, and told him what Balak had said.
And he said to them, "Rest here tonight, and I will give you an answer in the morning, after I hear from the Lord," and the Moab elders stayed with Balaam that night.
And God came to Balaam and said, "Who are these men with you?"
And Balaam said to God, "Moab's King Balak, the son of Zippor, has sent me a message that says,

There are some people who have come to their land from Egypt, that are so numerous that they cover the face of the earth, they want me to come and curse them, and maybe they will be able to defeat them, and drive them away."
And God said to Balaam, "Do not go with them, and do not curse the people, because they are blessed."
And Balaam rose up early in the morning, and went to Balak's elders and said, "Go back to your land, because the Lord refuses to let me help you."
The Moab elders rose up, and went back to Balak and said, "Balaam refuses to come help us."
And Balak sent another group of elders, who were more honorable than the first delegation he sent.
They went to Balaam and said, Zippor's son Balak says, "I pray that you let nothing hinder you from coming here.
Because I will bestow a great honor upon you, and I will do whatever you tell me to do, so please come in answer to my prayer, and put a curse on these people."
And Balaam answered Balak's servants and said, "Even if Balak gave me his house full of silver and gold, I still could not do anything more or less than what the Lord my God tells me to do.
So I pray that you will stay here tonight, so that I may speak to the Lord and see if he has anything more to say to me."
And God came to Balaam that night and said to him, "If these men have come for you, rise up and go with them, but you must only do what I tell you to do."
So Balaam rose up early in the morning, saddled his donkey, and went with the Moab elders.
But God was very angry because he went with them, and an angel of the Lord stood in his way to interfere with his purpose. He was riding his donkey and two of his servants were with him.
And the donkey saw the Lord's angel standing in the road with his sword drawn, and the donkey turned away and went out into the field, and Balaam beat the donkey, to get her back on the road.
But the Lord's angel stood in the road through the vineyards, and there was a wall on each side.
And when the donkey saw the Lord's angel, she slammed herself up against the wall, and crushed Balaam's foot against the wall, and he beat her again.
Then the Lord's angel went little further, and stood in a narrow place, where there was no room to turn either to the left or the right.
And when the donkey saw the angel of the Lord, she fell down under Balaam, and Balaam grew very angry, and he beat the donkey with a staff.
And the Lord opened the donkey's mouth and she said to Balaam, "What have I done to you for you to beat me these three times?"
So Balaam said to the donkey, "Because you disobeyed me, and if I had a sword in my hand, I would kill you."
And the donkey said to Balaam, "I am your donkey and you have ridden me since the very first day that you bought me until today? Have I ever behaved this way before?" And Balaam said, "No."
Then the Lord opened Balaam's eyes, and when he saw the Lord's angel standing in the road, with a sword in his hand, he bowed his head and fell flat on his face.
And the Lord's angel said to him, "Why have you have beaten your donkey these three times? Behold, I stand here blocking your way, because your way is perverse to me."
But the donkey saw me, and turned away from me these three times, and if she had not turned away from me, I would have surely killed you and kept her alive.
And Balaam said to the Lord's angel, "I have sinned, because I did not know that you were standing in my way, so if it displeases you, I will go back home."
And the Lord's angel said to Balaam, "Go with these men, but you must only speak the words that I give you." So, Balaam went with Balak's elders.
When Balak heard that Balaam had come, he went to meet him in the city of Moab, which is on the border of the furthest coastline of the Arnon river.
And Balak said to Balaam, "Did I not send for you and earnestly request that you come to me? Why did you not come, am I unable to give you a place of honor?"
And Balaam said to Balak, "Now I have come to you, but I have no power to say anything at all, except the words that God puts in my mouth.
Then Balaam and Balak went to Kirjath-Huzoth.
And Balak offered sheep and oxen and sent them to Balaam and the princes that were with him.
The next day, Balak took Balaam up into the high places of Baal, where he could see the farthest borders of the people.
And Balaam said to Balak, "I want you to build seven altars for me here and prepare seven oxen and seven rams here."
And Balak did as Balaam asked, and they offered a bull and a ram on each altar.
And Balaam said to Balak, "Stand by your burnt offering, and I will go and see if the Lord will meet with me, and whatever he shows me I will tell you." And he went to a place high up on the hill.
When Balaam met with God he said to him, "I have prepared seven altars, and I have offered a bull and a ram on each altar."
And the Lord put these words in Balaam's mouth and said, "Return to Balak, and tell him this."
So he returned to the spot where Balak stood by his burnt offering with all the Moab elders.
Then he spoke the Lord's parables and said, "King Balak of Moab has brought me from the eastern mountains of Syria and said, 'Come, defy Israel and curse Jacob for me.'
How can I curse those whom God has not cursed, and how can I be angry with anyone that the Lord is not angry with?
For I see him from the top of the rocks, and I behold him from the hills, they are the people who will live alone and will not be counted among the world's nations.
Who can count Jacob's dust, or number the one-fourth part of Israel? Let me die the death of the righteous and let my last days end like his!"
Then Balak said to Balaam, "What have you done to me? I asked you to curse my enemies, and you have blessed them instead."
And he answered and said, "I told you before that I must take heed of the Lord, and I can only speak the words that he has put in my mouth?"
So Balak said to him, "I beg you to come with me to another place where you will not be able to see them all, and you can curse them for me from there."
And he brought him to the top of Mount Pisgah at the fields of Zophim, and he built seven altars there, on which he offered a bull and a ram on each altar.
Then Balaam said to Balak, "Stand here by your burnt offering, while I meet with the Lord over there."
And the Lord met with Balaam, and put more words in his mouth and said, "Go back to Balak, and tell him this."
And when he returned, Balak and the Moab elders were standing by their burnt offering and Balak asked him, "What did the Lord say?"
Then he spoke the Lord's parables and said, "Rise up Balak son of Zippor and listen to what I have to say.
God is not a man and he does not lie, neither is he the Son of Man that must repent from sin, and he will do whatever he says he will do.
Behold, I have received a commandment from God to bless them, because he has blessed them, and I cannot reverse it.
He has seen no immorality in Jacob, and he has seen no perverseness in Israel, his Lord God is with them, and the shout of a king is among them.
God brought them out of Egypt, and he has the strength of a wild ox.
Surely there is no magic spell that will prevail against Jacob, neither will any divination work against Israel, and it will be said of Jacob and Israel at the appointed time, see what God has done!
Behold, these people will rise up as a great lion, and as a young lion, they will not lie down again until they eat their prey and drink the blood of those they have killed."
And Balak said to Balaam, "Well then do not curse them, but please do not bless them either."
But Balaam answered him and said, "Did I not tell you, that I must do whatever the Lord says?"
And Balak said to Balaam, "I beg you to come with me to another place, perhaps it will please God that you may curse them for me from there."
And Balak brought Balaam to the top of Mount Peor, looking towards Jeshimon.
And Balaam said to Balak, "Build seven altars for me here, and prepare seven bulls and seven rams."
And Balak did as Balaam said, and he offered a bull and a ram on each altar.
When Balaam saw that it pleased the Lord to bless Israel, he gave up and decided not to ask him to curse them again, but he turned toward the wilderness.
Balaam looked up and saw the Israelis were in their tents camped by tribe, and the spirit of God came upon him.
Then Balaam spoke the Lord's parable and said, "Boer's son Balaam, the man who has his eyes open has spoken.
Balaam's ears are open to the words of God, and have seen the vision of the Almighty and fallen into a trance, but his eyes are still open.
O Jacob and O Israel! Your tents and tabernacles are beautiful.
They are spread out like the valleys or gardens near the river, and like the flowering aloe trees which the Lord has planted, and like cedar trees beside the water.
He will pour the water out of his buckets, his seed will be spread across many waters, his king will be higher than Agag, and his kingdom will be glorified.
God brought him out of Egypt, and he has the strength of a wild ox. He will eat up his enemies nations, then he will break their bones and pierce them with his arrows.
He layed down like a lion, but who will stir up this great lion? Blessed is the one who blesses you and cursed is the one who curses you.

King Balak's anger was kindled against Balaam and he waved his hands together in frustration. Then King Balak said to Balaam, "I asked you to curse my enemies, but instead you have blessed them three times.
So go back to where you came from, because I was going to give you a great honor, but the Lord has taken this honor from you."
Then Balaam spoke to Balak and said, "When I first spoke to your messengers I warned them.

And I told them, 'Even if Balak were to give me his house full of silver and gold, I cannot go against the Lord's commandment. I could not say anything either good or bad from my own mind, but I must say only what the Lord has told me to say?
So now I must go back to my people, but before I go I must tell you what these people will do to your people in the coming days."
Then he spoke the Lord's parables and said, "Beor's son Balaam, the man whose eyes are open has spoken."
And Balaam said, "I Balaam have heard Gods words, and I was given knowledge from the Most High and saw the vision of the Almighty. Even though I fell into a trance, my eyes are still open.
I see a rising star coming from Jacob but not now and not in the near future. A sceptre will rise from Israel that will defeat all of Moab's territories and destroy all of Seth's children.
Edom will become Israel's possession, and they will courageously take possession of Seir from his enemies.
Jacob will will rule with strength and destroy any of his enemies that remain in the city."
Then Balaam spoke the Lord's parables when he looked at Amalek and said, "Amalek was the first of the nations, but in the end it he will perish forever."
Then Balaam spoke the Lord's parables when he looked at the Kenites and said, "Your home is strong, and you have built your nest on a rock.
Nevertheless the Kenites will waste away until Assyria carries you away as captives."
Balaam spoke the Lord's parables and said, "Alas, who will survive when God does this?
Ships will sail here from the coast of Cyprus to attack Assyria and Eber, and both will also perish forever."
Then Balak and Balaam got up and returned to their own homes.
And Israel lived in Shittim, and the people began to commit prostitution with the daughters of Moab.
The religious leaders called the people to make sacrifices to their false gods, and they feasted and bowed down to their false gods.
The men of Israel had sex with the women of Moab to honor 'Baal of Peor', and the Lord became very angry with them.
And the Lord said to Moses, "Take the people's chief's heads, and hang them up on a pole in the sun before the Lord, so that the Lord's fierce anger is turned away from Israel."
And Moses said to Israel's judges, "Kill all the men that had sex to honor 'Baal of Peor'."
And, behold one of the Israelis came to see his brothers and brought a Midian woman for Moses and the Israelis to see, as they were weeping before the congregation's tabernacle door.
When Phinehas the son of Eleazar, who was the son of priest Aaron saw it, he rose up from among the congregation and took a spear in his hand.
And he followed the Israeli man into the tent and drove the spear through the man and through the woman's stomach, and the plague against Israel was stopped.
But 24,000 people died from the plague before it was stopped.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said,
"Because of Phinehas' deep belief in my honor, my anger towards the Israelis has been satiated, and I did not totally destroy them in my jealous rage.
So, behold I have given him my peace covenant.
And this agreement gives him and his descendants the rights to an everlasting priesthood, because he was respectful of his God, and made an atonement for the sins of the Israelis."
Now the name of the Israeli man who was executed with the Midianite woman, was Salu's son Zimri; a chief of one of the Simeonite families.
And the Midianite woman's name that was killed was Cozbi, the daughter of Zur; he was a chief in the house of Midian."
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said,
"Frustrate and defeat the Midianites.

Because their tricks and deceptions have caused sin to come on you regarding the question of Peor and their sister Cozbi, the daughter of a Midianite prince, who was executed when the plague caused by Peor came upon you."
After the plague, the Lord said to Moses and Eleazar the son of priest Aaron,
"Count everyone in the House of Israel, who are twenty years old and older, by their fathers' house, who are able to make war in Israel."
Moses and priest Eleazar said to the people on the plains of Moab by the Jordan River near Jericho,
Count the Israelis, from twenty years old and older, who left Egypt, the way the Lord commanded Moses and the Israelis to do.
Beginning with Israel's oldest son Reuben's children were, Hanoch from the family of the Hanochites of Pallu, and the family of the Palluites.
And Hezron, from the family of the Hezronites, Carmi, from the family of the Carmites.
And there was a total of 43,730 from Reuben's family.
Then there were Pallu and Eliab's sons.
And Eliab's sons were, Nemuel, Dathan, and Abiram. Dathan and Abiram were famous in the congregation, because they rebelled against Moses, Aaron, and the Lord along with Korah.
And the earth swallowed them up together with Korah, whose entire company died, at same time that the 250 men were devoured by fire.
Although Korah's sons did not die at that time.
And Simeon's sons by their families were, Nemuel, from the family of the Nemuelites, Jamin, from the family of the Jaminites, and Jachin, from the family of the Jachinites.
And Zerah, from the family of the Zerahites, and Shaul, from the family of the Shaulites.
And there was a total of 22,200 from Simeon's family.
Then there were Gad's sons that are listed here by their families, Zephon, from the family of the Zephonites, Haggi, from the family of the Haggites, and Shuni, from the family of the Shunites.
And Ozni, from the family of the Oznites, and Eri, from the family of the Erites.
And Arod, from the family of the Arodites, and Areli, from the family of the Arelites.
And there was a total of 40,500 from Gad's family.
Judah's sons were Er and Onan, who died in the land of Canaan.
And Judah's sons by their families were, Shelah, from the family of the Shelanites, Pharez, from the family of the Pharzites, and Zerah, from the family of the Zerahites.
And Pharez's sons were, Hezron, from the family of the Hezronites, and Hamul, from the family of the Hamulites.
And there was a total of 66,500 from Judah's family.
And Issachar's sons by their families were, Tola, from the family of the Tolaites, and Pua, from the family of the Punites.
And Jashub, from the family of the Jashubites, and Shimron, from the family of the Shimronites.
And there was a total of 64,300 from Issachar's family.
And from Zebulun's sons by their families were, Sered, from the family of the Seredites, Elon, from the family of the Elonites, and Jahleel, from the family of the Jahleelites.
And there was a total of 60,500 from Zebulun's family.
And Joseph's sons by their families were Manasseh and Ephraim.
Manasseh's descendants by their families were, the Machirites from Machir who was Gilead 's father, and Gilead was the head of the Gileadite family.
These are Gilead's sons, Jeezer, from the family of the Jeezerites, and Helek, from the family of the Helekites.
And Asriel, from the family of the Asrielites, and Shechem, from the family of the Shechemites.
And Shemida, from the family of the Shemidaites, and Hepher, from the family of the Hepherites.
But Hepher's son Zelophehad, had daughters but no sons, and his daughters' names were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
And there was a total of 52,700 from Manasseh's family.
And Ephraim's sons by their families were, Shuthelah, from the family of the Shuthalhites, Becher, from the family of the Bachrites, and Tahan, from the family of the Tahanites.
And Shuthelah's son was Eran, from the family of the Eranites.
And there was a total of 32,500 from Ephraim's family.
And Benjamin's sons by their families were, Bela, from the family of the Belaites, Ashbel, from the family of the Ashbelites, and Ahiram, from the family of the Ahiramites.
And Shupham, from the family of the Shuphamites, and Hupham, from the family of the Huphamites.
And Bela's sons Ard and Naaman by their families were, Ard, from the family of the Ardites, and Naaman, from the family of the Naamites.
And there was a total of 45,600 from Benjamin's family.
And Dan's sons by their families were, Shuham, from the family of the Shuhamites, and these are Dan's families by their families.
And there was a total of 64,400 from Shuham's family.
And Asher's sons by their families were, Jimna, from the family of the Jimnites, Jesui, from the family of the Jesuites, and Beriah, from the family of the Beriites.
And Beriah's sons by their families were, Heber, from the family of the Heberites, and Malchiel, from the family of the Malchielites.
And Asher's daughter's name was Sarah.
And there was a total of 53,400 from Asher's family.
And Naphtali's sons by their families were, Jahzeel, from the family of the Jahzeelites, and Guni, from the family of the Gunites.
And Jezer, from the family of the Jezerites, and Shillem, from the family of the Shillemites.
And there was a total of 45,400 from Naphtali's family.
And there was a total of 601,730 Israelis.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said,
"The land will be divided among all of them as their inheritance by the number of names.

The size of the inheritance must be determined by the size of each family, to those with many the inheritance will be greater, and to those with few the inheritance will be less, and the size of everyone's inheritance is based on the size of their family.
The land will be divided by casting lots to determine who gets which parcel of land as their inheritance based on the names of their father's tribe.
The casting of lots will determine the way that the possession is to be divided between the many and the few."
And the Levites by their families were, Gershon, from the family of the Gershonites, Kohath, from the family of the Kohathites, and Merari, from the family of the Merarites.
This is a list of the Levite families, beginning with the Libnites, the Hebronite family, the Mahlite family, the Mushite family, the family of the Korathites, and Kohath fathered Amram.
Amram's wife's name was Jochebed, she was Levi's daughter whose mother gave birth to her in Egypt, and she gave birth to Amram, Aaron, Moses, and their sister Miriam.
And Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar were fathered by Aaron.
But Nadab and Abihu died, when they made an improper burnt offering before the Lord.
And there were 23,000 males from a month old and older, but Nadab and Abihu were not counted among them, and they were not given any part of Israel's inheritance.
These are the Israelis that Moses and priest Eleazar counted in the plains of Moab by the Jordan River near Jericho.
But none of them from Nadab or Abihu's families were counted, when Moses and priest Aaron, counted the Israelis in the Sinai wilderness.
Because when the Lord said to them, "They will surely die in the wilderness!" Not one of them survived, except for Jephunneh's son Caleb, and Nun's son Joshua."

Then the daughters of Hepher's son Zelophehad, Gilead's son, Machir's son, and Manasseh's son, from the families of Joseph's son Manasseh, whose daughters' names were, Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
And they stood before Moses and priest Eleazar, and all the leaders of the congregation, by the tabernacle door and said,
"Our father died in the wilderness, and he was not one of those from Korah that gathered together to rebel against the Lord, but he died from his own sin, and he had no sons.
Why should our father's name be removed from among his family, only because he has no son? So, give us an inheritance from among the brothers of our father."
So Moses brought their cause before the Lord.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said,
Zelophehad's daughters speak the truth, and you must surely give them an inheritance among their father's brothers and let their father's inheritance be passed on to them.
And you must speak to the Israelis and say, "If a man dies, and he has no son, then his inheritance must be passed down to his daughter.
And if he has no daughter, then you must give his inheritance to his brothers.
And if he has no brothers, then you must give his inheritance to his father's brothers.

And if his father has no brothers, then give his inheritance to his closest family that is next of kin to him, and it will be their possession, and this decision will be made by law for Israel's descendants, like the Lord commanded Moses."
