And the Lord said to Moses, "Go up into Mount Abarim, where you will see the land which I have given to Israel's descendants.
And when you have seen it, your people will come together, the same as when your brother Aaron came to you.
Because when you were in the Zin wilderness, you rebelled against my commandment when the people were angry, and both of you failed to sanctify me before them at the waters of Meribah in Kadesh."
And Moses spoke to the Lord and said,
"Let the Lord God of the spirits of all flesh, appoint a man to lead the congregation.
To lead them and to go in before them, to bring them in, and to lead them out, so that the Lord's congregation does not wander around in the wilderness, like sheep without a shepherd."
And the Lord said to Moses, "Take Nun's son Joshua, a man filled with the spirit, and lay your hands on him.
And bring him before priest Eleazar and the entire congregation, and while they are watching, give him his orders.
And give him some of your honor, so that the entire Israelis congregation may be under his authority.

And he will stand before priest Eleazar, and ask for the Lord's judgment of the Urim, and when he tells them to leave, they will leave, and when he tells them to come in, they come in, along with all of Israel's descendants, and the entire congregation."
And Moses did as the Lord commanded him, and he brought Joshua before priest Eleazar, and the entire congregation.
And he laid his hands on him, and gave him his orders, like the Lord commanded Moses.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said,
"Tell the Israelis to make their sin offering, bread offering, and burnt offering as a sweet savor to me, must be observed in their due season.
And tell them, that this continuous burnt offering to the Lord, must include two unblemished year-old lambs.
One lamb must be offered in the morning, and the other lamb is to be offered in the evening.
And 1/10th of an ephah of flour for a bread offering, mixed with 1/4th of a hin of filtered oil.
This burnt offering must be offered continuously, because it was ordained on Mount Sinai as a sweet savory sacrificial offering made by fire to the Lord.
And as the drink offering to the Lord, you must pour 1/4th of a hin of strong wine per lamb in the Holy Place.

And you must offer the other lamb in the evening, and it must be prepared in the same way as the morning bread offering and the drink offering, and it will be a sweet savory sacrificial offering made by fire to the Lord.
On the Sabbath, you must offer two unblemished year-old lambs, and a 2/10th measure of flour mixed with oil for a bread offering, and a drink offering.
This burnt offering must be offered every Sabbath, and it is in addition to the continuously offered burnt offering and drink offering.
At the beginning of each month, you must offer two young bulls, one ram, and seven unblemished year-old lambs, as a burnt offering to the Lord.
And 3/10th of a deal of flour mixed with oil as a bread offering per bull, and 2/10th of a measure of flour mixed with oil as a bread offering per ram.
And several 1/10th deals of flour mixed with oil as a bread offering per lamb, and it will be a sweet savory burnt offering sacrifice made by fire to the Lord.

As their drink offering, they must offer, a half hin of wine per bull, 1/3rd of a hin of wine per ram, and 1/4th of a hin of wine per lamb, and this burnt offering must be made every month of the year.
And one kid goat must be offered to the Lord as a sin offering, in addition to the continuous burnt offering and drink offering.
And the Lord's Passover is to be observed on the fourteenth day of the first month of the year.
And on the fifteenth day of this month, the seven-day feast must be observed, and all bread eaten during this time must be unleavened.
On the first day the people must gather for a Holy assembly, and no type of servant work is allowed to be done there.
But you must offer a sacrificial burnt offering made by fire to the Lord, of two young bulls, one ram, and seven one year-old lambs, and they must all be unblemished.
And as their bread offering, which must be made from flour mixed with oil, with 3/10 of a deal per bull, and 2/10 of a measure per ram.
And you must offer 1/10th of a deal for each of the seven lambs.
And one goat as a sin offering, to make an atonement for yourself.
You must make these offerings in addition to the continuously offered morning burnt offering.

This is the way that you must make your daily offering for those seven days, as a sacrificial sweet savory meat burnt offering made by fire to the Lord, and it must be offered in addition to the continuously offered burnt offering and drink offering.
And you must gather the people as a holy assembly, and you must do no servant work.

Also on the day of the first fruits, when you bring a new bread offering to the Lord at your Feast of Weeks, you must gather the people for a holy assembly, during which time you must do no servant work.
But you must offer a sweet savory burnt offering to the Lord, consisting of two young bulls, one ram, and seven one year-old lambs.
And their bread offering is to be made of flour mixed with oil, with 3/10th of a deal per bull, and 2/10th of a measure per ram.
And 1/10th of a deal for each of the seven lambs.
And one kid goat, to make an atonement for yourself.
You must make these unblemished offerings in addition to the continuous burnt offering, bread offering, and drink offering."

And the Lord said, "You must gather the people together for a holy assembly on the first day of the seventh month, and you must do no servant work that day because it is a day of celebration and trumpet blowing.
And you must make a sweet savory burnt offering to the Lord, of one young bull, one ram, and seven unblemished year-old lambs.
And their bread offering must be made of flour mixed with oil, with 3/10th of deal per bull, and 2/10th of a measure per ram.
And 1/10 of a deal for each of the seven lambs.
And one kid goat as a sin offering, to make an atonement for yourself.

This is in addition to the monthly burnt offering, bread offering, drink offering, bread offering, and the daily burnt offering, properly prepared as a sweet sacrificial savor, made by fire to the Lord.
On the tenth day of the seventh month you must gather the people for a Holy assembly, and your soul must abstain from pleasure, and you must not do any work while you're there.
But you must offer as a sweet savory burnt offering to the Lord, one young bull, one ram, and seven one year-old lambs, they must all be unblemished.
And their bread offering must be made of flour mixed with oil, with 3/10th of a deal per bull, and 2/10th of a measure per ram.
And 1/10th of a deal for each of the seven lambs.
One kid goat as a sin offering, in addition to the sin offering of atonement, the continuous burnt offering, the bread offering, and the drink offering.
And on the fifteenth day of the seventh month you must gather the people for a holy assembly, at which time you will do no servant work. You must observe this feast to the Lord for seven days.

You must offer a sacrificial sweet savory burnt offering made by fire to the Lord, which will include thirteen young bulls, two rams, and fourteen one year old lambs, and all of them must be unblemished.
Their bread offering must be made of flour mixed with oil, with 3/10th of a deal per bull for all thirteen bulls, and 2/10th of a measure per ram for both of the two rams.
And 1/10th of a deal per lamb of the 14 lambs.
And one kid goat as a sin offering, in addition to the continuous burnt offering, the bread offering, and the drink offering.
On the second day, you must sacrifice twelve young bulls, two rams, and fourteen unblemished year-old lambs.
And the total bread offering and drink offering depends on the number of bulls, rams, and lambs, as it was ordered.
And one kid goat as a sin offering, in addition to the continuous burnt offering, the bread offering, and their drink offering.
And on the third day eleven bulls, two rams, plus fourteen one year-old unblemished lambs.
And the total bread and drink offering will be determined by the total number of bulls, rams, and lambs, as it was ordered.
And one goat as a sin offering, in addition to the continuous burnt offering, bread offering, and drink offering.
And on the fourth day ten bulls, two rams, and fourteen one year-old unblemished lambs.
The total bread offering and drink offering will be determined by the total number of bulls, rams, and lambs, as it was ordered.
And one kid goat as a sin offering, in addition to the continuous burnt offering, bread offering, and drink offering.
And on the fifth day nine bulls, two rams, and fourteen unblemished year-old lambs.
The total bread and drink offering will be determined by the total number of bulls, rams, and lambs, according to the number ordered.
And one goat as a sin offering, in addition to the continuous burnt offering, bread offering, and drink offering.
And on the sixth day eight bulls, two rams, and fourteen unblemished year-old lambs.
And the total number of bread and drink offerings, will be determined the total number of bulls, rams, and lambs, as it was ordered.
And one goat as a sin offering, in addition to the continuous burnt offering, bread offering, and drink offering.
And on the seventh day seven bulls, two rams, and fourteen unblemished year-old lambs.
And the total number of bread and drink offerings, will be determined the total number of bulls, rams, and lambs, as it was ordered.
And one goat as a sin offering, in addition to the continuous burnt offering, bread offering, and drink offering.
On the eighth day you must gather the people together for a solemn assembly, and you must do no servant work in there.
But you must make a sacrificial sweet savory burnt offering made by fire to the Lord, of one bull, one ram, and seven unblemished year-old lambs.
And the total number of bread and drink offerings, will be determined the total number of bulls, rams, and lambs, as it was ordered.
And one goat as a sin offering, in addition to the continuous burnt offering, bread offering, and drink offering.

You must do all of these things for the Lord on your set feast days, in addition to fulfilling your promises, and making your voluntary offerings, plus your burnt offerings, bread offerings, drink offerings, and your peace offerings."
And Moses told the Israelis everything that the Lord commanded him to tell them.
And Moses spoke to the tribal leaders of Israel's descendants and said, "This is what the Lord has commanded.
If a man makes a promise to the Lord, or swears an oath to bind his soul, he must not break his word, and he must do everything that he promised.
If a young woman makes a promise to the Lord that binds her soul, and she still lives in her father's house.
And if her father hears her promise, and he does not speak out against her, then every promise she made will stand.
But if her father hears any of the promises that she made to bind her soul, and he rejects them, then none of them will stand, and the Lord will forgive her.
If she ever had a husband, and if she ever made a promise to bind her soul.
And if her husband hears her promises and accepts them, then her promises will stand, and everything she said to bind her soul will stand.
But if her husband rejects the promises she made to bind her soul, it will be ineffective, and the Lord will forgive her.
But every promise made by a widow or divorced woman, will stand against her.
And if she made a promise in her husband's house or bound her soul with an oath.
If her husband hears her promise, and he does not reject it, then every promise she made will stand.

But if her husband has completely rejects them the day he hears them, then whatever she promised to bind her soul, will not stand, because her husband has made them void, and the Lord will forgive her.
And every one of the promises or binding oaths she made to afflict the soul, may be accepted or voided by her husband.
But if her husband never speaks about the promises or bonds that she made, then this will confirm them, because he held his peace when he heard them.
But if he in any way makes them void after he has heard them, then he will be burdened by her immorality."
These are the laws which the Lord gave Moses, about the relationships between a man and his wife, and a father and his young daughter if she is still living in his house.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said,
"Punish the Midianites for what they have done to Israel's descendants, then gather all your people together."
And Moses spoke to the people and said, "Arm yourselves, because we are going to war with the Midianites, to avenge the Lord for what they have done.
Each one of Israel's tribes, must send 1,000 men armed and ready for war.
So they sent a total of 12,000 men from all the tribes, that were armed and ready for war.
Moses sent 12,000 of them to the war, a thousand men from each tribe. He sent priest Eleazar's son Phinehas with them, who carried the holy instruments and the war trumpets to blow.
They did what the Lord commanded Moses to do, and they went to war with the Midianites, and killed every male.
And besides all the others that were killed, they killed the five Midianite kings which included Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba, plus Beor's son Balaam who was killed with a sword.
And the Israelis took the Midianite women and their children captive, and they took all of their cattle, flocks, and goods as spoils of war.
And they burned all the cities and castles where they had been living.
And they carried away all the plunder from both men and beasts, as the spoils of war.

And they brought the captives, the plunder, and all the spoils of war to Moses and priest Eleazar, and it was presented to the Israelis congregation in their camp on the plains of Moab, near the shores of the Jordan River and Jericho.
Moses and priest Eleazar, and the congregation's princes left to meet them outside the camp.
Moses became very angry with all the officers who returned from the battle.
And he said to them, "Why did you save these women, and why are they still alive?

Behold, these are the people that caused the Israelis to listen Balaam, and to sin against the Lord with the idolatry and immorality of Peor, and this brought a plague to the midst of Lord's congregation.
So now, you must kill every male among the children, and every one of the women who have had sex with a man.
But all the females, that have not had sex with a man, may be allowed to live for yourselves.

And any of you who have killed a someone or touched anyone that was killed must stay outside the camp for seven days, and you must purify both yourselves and your captives on the third and the seventh day.
You must purify your clothes, no matter whether they are made of hides or goat hair, and also everything made of wood."
Priest Eleazar spoke to the soldiers who went into battle and said, "The Lord gave Moses this legal decree.
Only the gold, silver, brass, iron, tin, and lead.

And anything else that can be melted in the fire, must be melted to be made clean, and it must also be washed in the water of separation to be purified, and if it can not be melted, it must be washed and cleaned with water.
When you wash your clothes on the seventh day, you will be clean, and then you will be allowed to come into the camp."
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said,
"Take the prey of both man and beast that was taken, for yourself, priest Eleazar, and the congregation's chief fathers.
Separate the plunder into two parts, one part for the men that went to war, and the other part for the congregation.
The surviving soldiers should give a portion of everything that they took, as the Lord's tribute and it should include one of every 500 people, cattle, donkeys, and sheep.
Take it from their half, and give it to priest Eleazar, as a sacred offering of the Lord.
And take 1/50th of the people, cattle, donkeys, flocks, and of every type of beast, from the Israelis half, and give it to the Levites who manage the Lord's tabernacle.
So Moses and priest Eleazar did what the Lord commanded Moses to do.
And there were 675,000 sheep, in addition to the other plunder that the men of war had captured.
And there was a total number of 72,000 cattle.
And there was a total number of 61.000 donkeys.
And there was a total number of 32,000 women who had not had sex with a man.
And as their half, the soldiers were given 337,500 sheep.
And 675 sheep were donated to the Lord.
And from the 36,000 cattle, 72 were donated as the Lord's tribute.
And from the 30,500 donkeys, 61 were donated as the Lord's tribute.
And from the 16,000 people, 32 of them were donated as the Lord's tribute.
Moses gave the Lord's sacred offering as a tribute to priest Eleazar, the way that the Lord had commanded Moses.
And Moses separated the Israelis congregation's half, from the half that was given to the soldiers.
So the congregation's half, included 337,500 sheep.
And 36,000 cattle.
And 30,500 donkeys.
And 16,000 people.
So Moses took one out of every fifty of both of man and beast, from the Israelis half, and gave them to the Levites, who managed the Lord's tabernacle, like the Lord had commanded him.
And the officers over the thousands of the armies, the captains of thousands, and captains of hundreds, came to Moses.
And they said to Moses, your servants have counted the soldiers under our command, and they are all present and accounted for.

So, we have brought a donation for the Lord, of jewels, gold, chains, bracelets, rings, earrings, and tablets, from everything that each man has taken, to make an atonement for our souls before the Lord.
And Moses and priest Eleazar took their gold and jewelry.
And the total value of the gold and jewelry that the captains of 1,000's, and the captains of 100's offered to the Lord, was 16,750 shekels.
Because the each of soldiers had taken some spoils of war for themselves.
Then Moses and priest Eleazar took the officers gold, and brought it into the congregation tabernacle, as a memorial for the Israelis before the Lord.
Reuben and Gad's descendants had a very large herd of cattle, and when they saw that the land of Jazer and Mount Gilead, was a good place for grazing cattle.
Then Gad and Reuben's descendants came and spoke to Moses, priest Eleazar, and the congregation's princes and said,
"Ataroth, Dibon, Jazer, Nimrah, Heshbon, Elealeh, Shebam, Nebo, and Beon.
Even the country the Lord conquered before the Israelis congregation, is a land for cattle and for your servants who have cattle.
So they said, "If we have found grace in your sight, give us this land, and do not make us cross over the Jordan River."
And Moses said to Gad and Reuben's descendants, "Are you going to just sit here when your brothers go to war?
Why would you discourage the hearts of the Israelis from going over into the land that the Lord has given them?
Your fathers did the same thing when I sent them from Kadesh-Barnea to go see the land.
For when they went into the Eshcol valley and saw the land, they discouraged the heart of the Israelis and told them not go into the land which the Lord had given them.
And that kindled the Lord's anger at the same time, and he swore an oath and said,

"Surely none of the men twenty years old and older that I brought out of Egypt, will see the land which I swore to give to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Because they did not trust the Lord and they did not completely follow me.
Except for Jephunneh the Kenezite's son Caleb, and Nun's son Joshua, because they trusted in the Lord, and completely followed me.
And the Lord's anger was kindled against Israel, and he made them wander around out in the wilderness for forty years, until the entire generation who had done evil in his sight had been consumed.
And, behold you have raised a new generation of sinful men in your father's houses, and you have increased The Lord's fierce anger toward Israel.
For if you turn away from him, he will leave them to wander around out in the wilderness again, and you will have destroyed all of these people."
And they came back to him and said, "We will build sheep pens here for our cattle, and cities for our children.
But we will go armed and ready for battle before the Israelis, until we have brought them to their place, and our children will live safely in walled cities protected from the other people there.
We will not return to our homes, until every man has received his inheritance.
For we will not have an inheritance with them over on the other side of the Jordan River, because our inheritance has come to us here on the east side of the Jordan River"
And Moses said to them, "If you do this thing, and go to war, armed and ready for battle before the Lord.
And all of you cross the Jordan River armed before the Lord, until he has driven all of his enemies out from before him.
And the land before the Lord is conquered, then afterwards you will be allowed to return, and be forgiven before the Lord and Israel, and this land will be your inheritance from the Lord.
But if you fail to do so, behold you will have sinned against the Lord, and you can be sure that your sin will find you out.
So Build cities for your children, and sheds for your sheep, and do everything that you said you would do.
And Gad and Reuben's descendants spoke to Moses and said, "We are your servants my Lord, and we will do whatever you command us to do.
We will leave our children, our wives, and all of our flocks and cattle, in the cities of Mount Gilead.
But, just as my Lord says, we are your servants and every man among us will arm ourselves for war and go into battle before the Lord.
So Moses sent them their orders through priest Eleazar, Nun's son Joshua, and the chief fathers of the tribes of Israel.

And Moses said to them, "If Gad and Reuben's descendants arm themselves for battle and cross the Jordan River, with you before the Lord, and they conquer the land there, then you may give them the land of Gilead as their inheritance.
But if they do not arm themselves and go with you, then they will have settle for an inheritance from among you in the land of Canaan.
And Gad and Reuben's descendants answered and said, "We are your servants, so will we do what you have ordered us to do.
We will arm ourselves and go before the Lord into the land of Canaan, so that we may claim our inheritance on this side of the Jordan River."

So Moses gave Gad and Reuben's descendants, and half the tribe of Joseph's son Manasseh, the land from the Amorite kingdom of King Sihon, and the land from the Bashan kingdom of King Og, along with its coastal cities, including the cities in the country all around them.
And Gad's descendants built Dibon, Ataroth, and Aroer.
And Atroth, Shophan, Jaazer, and Jogbehah.
And Beth-Nimrah, Beth-Haran, fenced cities, and sheds for their sheep.
And Reuben's descendants built Heshbon, Elealeh, and Kirjathaim.
And they changed the names of Nebo, Baal-Meon, Shibmah, and they gave names to the cities that they built.
And the descendants of Manasseh's son Machir went to Mount Gilead and took possession of it, and they displaced the Amorites there.
And Moses gave Mount Gilead to Manasseh's son Machir, and that's where he lived.
And Manasseh's son Jair went and took its small towns, and the town of Havoth-Jair was named after him.
And Nobah went and took Kenath and its villages, and the village of Nobah was named after him.
These are the stories of the Israelis after they left Egypt with their armies under the direction of Moses and Aaron.
This is what Moses wrote about their adventures, when they left to begin their journey to the places the Lord had commanded them to go.
The Israelis left Rameses on the fifteenth day of the first month which was the day after Passover, and the power of the Lord brought them out of Egypt while all of the Egyptians watched.
Because the Egyptians had to bury all of their firstborn sons, who the Lord had destroyed, along with their gods on whom the Lord had passed judgment.
So the Israelis left Rameses and camped in Succoth.
And they left Succoth and camped on the edge of the wilderness in Etham.
And they left Etham and turned back toward Pi-Hahiroth near Baal-Zephon, and they camped near Migdol.
And they left Pi-Hahiroth, and passed through the sea into the wilderness, and traveled three days into the Etham wilderness, and camped in Marah.
And they left Marah, and camped in Elim, where there were twelve water fountains, and 70 palm trees there.
And they left Elim and camped by the Red Sea.
And they left the Red Sea and camped in the wilderness of Sin.
And they left the wilderness of Sin and camped in Dophkah.
And they left Dophkah and camped in Alush.
And they left Alush and camped in Rephidim which had no water for the people to drink.
And they left Rephidim and camped in the Sinai desert.
And they left the Sinai desert and camped in Kibroth-Hattaavah.
And they left Kibroth-Hattaavah and camped in Hazeroth.
And they left Hazeroth and camped in Rithmah.
And they left Rithmah and camped in Rimmon-Parez.
And they left Rimmon-Parez and camped in Libnah.
And they left Libnah and camped in Rissah.
And they left Rissah and camped in Kehelathah.
And they left Kehelathah and camped on Mount Shapher.
And they left Mount Shapher and camped in Haradah.
And they left Haradah and camped in Makheloth.
And they left Makheloth and camped in Tahath.
And they left Tahath and camped in Tarah.
And they left Tarah and camped in Mithcah.
And they left Mithcah and camped in Hashmonah.
And they left Hashmonah, and camped in Moseroth.
And they left Moseroth, and camped in Bene-Jaakan.
And they left Bene-Jaakan and camped in Hor-Hagidgad.
And they left Hor-Hagidgad and camped in Jotbathah.
And they left Jotbathah and camped in Abronah.
And they left Ebronah and camped in Ezion-Geber.
And they left Ezion-Geber and camped in the Zin wilderness of Kadesh.
And they left Kadesh, and camped on Mount Hor, near the border of Edom.
And priest Aaron went up into Mount Hor and died at the Lord's commandment, in the fortieth year after the Israelis left Egypt, on the first day of the fifth month.
And Aaron was 123 years old when he died on Mount Hor.
And King Arad the Canaanite, who lived in the southern land of Canaan, heard that the Israelis were coming.
And they left Mount Hor and camped in Zalmonah.
And they left Zalmonah and camped in Punon.
And they left Punon and camped in Oboth.
And they left Oboth, and camped in Lye-Abarim, on the border of Moab.
And they left Lye-Abarim and camped in Dibongad.
And they left Dibongad, and camped in Almon Diblathaim.
And they left Almon Diblathaim, and camped in the Abarim mountains, before Nebo.
And they left the Abarim mountains, and camped in the plains of Moab, by the Jordan River, near Jericho.
And they camped next to the Jordan River, from Beth-Jeshimoth all the way to Abel-Shittim in the plains of Moab.
And the Lord spoke to Moses in the plains of Moab by the Jordan River, near Jericho and said,
"Speak to the Israelis and tell them; when they cross the Jordan River and go into Canaan.
They must drive out all the inhabitants of the land there, and destroy all their pictures and cast images, and tear down all their high places.
And you must take the land from the inhabitants, and live there, because I have given the land to you.

And you must cast lots to divide the land among your families, and you must give a larger inheritance to the families with more people, and to those with less people you must give a smaller inheritance, every man's inheritance will be however his lot falls, and each of your fathers tribe's inheritance will be distributed accordingly.

But if you do not drive the inhabitants out of the land before you, then those that you allow to remain will prick your eyes, and they will be a thorn in your sides and frustrate you in your own land.
Besides that, I will do to you, what I thought I would do to them.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said,
"Order the Israelis and tell them; when they enter Canaan, that the land will be their inheritance, all the way to the coasts of Canaan.
Then their south quarter will be from the wilderness of Zin along by the coast of Edom, and their southern border will be the furthest most coast of the eastern Dead Sea.
And their border will stretch from south of the Akrabbim ridge, then on to Zin, and south to Kadesh-Barnea, and on to Hazar-Addar, and then to Azmon.
And their border will stretch around Azmon to the Nile River, and out to the ocean.
And the western border will stretch all the way to the Mediterranean Sea for a border; this will be their western border.
And their northern border, will go from the Mediterranean Sea all the way to Mount Hor.
Their border will point from Mount Hor to the entrance of Hamath, to the farthest point of the border at Zedad.
And the border goes on to the farthest point of Ziphron at Hazar-Enan, which will be their northern border.
And their eastern border will stretch from Hazar-Enan to Shepham.
And the coast will go down from Shepham to Riblah, along the east side of Ain, and the border will descend to the eastern side of the Sea of Galilee.
And the border of their land will go down to the Jordan River, all way to the Dead Sea, and this will be their land with all of its coasts."
And Moses gave orders to the Israelis and said, "This is the land that you will inherit chosen by lot, which the Lord said to give to the nine tribes and the half tribe.
Because Reuben's descendants and Gad's descendants, have received their inheritance in accordance with what was allotted to their father's houses, and so has Manasseh's half tribe.
The two tribes and the half tribe have received their inheritance on this side of the Jordan River near Jericho, and eastward toward the rising sun."
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said,
"Priest Eleazar and Nun's son Joshua, will be responsible for dividing up the land for you.
And you must pick one prince from every tribe, to divide the land for their inheritance.
These are the names of the men from each tribe, and from Judah's tribe, will be Jephunneh's son Caleb.
And from Simeon's tribe, will be Ammihud's son Shemuel.
And from Benjamin's tribe, will be Chislon's son Elidad.
And the chosen prince from Dan's tribe, will be Jogli's son Bukki.
The chosen prince from Joseph's tribe, from the children of Manasseh, will be Ephod's son Hanniel.
And the chosen prince from Ephraim's tribe, will be Shiphtan's son Kemuel.
And the chosen prince from Zebulun's tribe, will be Parnach's son Elizaphan.
And the chosen prince from Issachar's tribe, will be Azzan's son Paltiel.
And the chosen prince from Asher's tribe, will be Shelomi's son Ahihud.
And the chosen prince from Naphtali's tribe, will be Ammihud's son Pedahel.
These are the ones whom the Lord has chosen to divide their inheritance from the land of Canaan among the Israelis."
And the Lord spoke to Moses on the plains of Moab by the Jordan River near Jericho and said,
"Tell the Israelis, to give the cities, fields, and the pastures surrounding them to the Levites as their inheritance to live in.
And they will have cities to live in, and the fields and pastures around them will be for their cattle, goods, and all their animals.
And the fields around the cities to will be given to the Levites, will reach out a thousand cubits all around the city walls.
The fields around city spread 2,000 cubits from each of the city borders on the north, south, east, and west sides, and the city must be located within the center of the fields.
You must give 42 cities to the Levites, in addition there must be six refuge cities, as places where the murderers can flee.
So there will be a total of 48 cities given to the Levites, along with their fields and pastures.
The cities to be given to the Levites will come from the Israelis' inheritance. And from those who have many you will give many, but from those who have few you will give few."
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said,
"Speak to the Israelis and tell them; when they cross over the Jordan River into Canaan.
They must designate certain cities to be cities of refuge, so that a murderer who accidentally kills a person may flee to a place of safety.
And those cities will be a place for refuge and protection for murderers from someone who wants revenge, so that the murderer is not killed, where they can stand before the congregation in judgment.
And you must give six cities as a place for refuge.
You must give three refuge cities on this side of the Jordan River, and three refuge cities on the other side of the river in the land of Canaan.
These six cities will be a refuge for both the Israelis and any foreigners among them, so that anyone who accidentally kills a person may have a place to flee.
And if they have beaten someone to death with an iron weapon, then they are a murderer, and murderers will surely be put to death.
And if they throw a stone at someone and it kills them, then they are a murderer, and murderers will surely be put to death.
And if they have beaten someone to death with a wooden weapon, then they are a murderer, and murderers will surely be put to death.
And when an officially appointed executioner confronts someone who has been legally judged to be a murderer, they may put them to death.
But if in their hatred, a murderer spears someone with a sword, or they lay in wait to ambush someone to throw a stone at them and kill them.

And if in their hatred they beat someone to death with their hands, they will surely be put to death, because they are a murderer, and it will be the appointed official's responsibility to put the murderer to death.
But if the accused murderer accidentally kills someone without malice, or they did not plan to ambush and kill the victim.
Or the accused murderer threw a stone, and someone was killed, and they were not enemies, and the person who threw the stone was not trying to harm anyone, and the accused did not see the victim.
Then the congregation must judge the case between the accused murderer and the officially appointed executioner based on these judgments.

And the congregation must deliver the accused murderer from the hands of the executioner, and the congregation will restore them to the refuge city, where they fled, and they must live there until the death of the anointed high priest, who was anointed with Holy oil.
But if the accused murderer ventures outside the border of the refuge city, where they had fled.
And the executioner finds the accused murderer outside the refuge city borders, then they may kill the accused, and they will not be guilty of murder.

Because the accused murderer should have remained in their refuge city until the death of the high priest, but after the death of the high priest the murderer will be return to the land of their inheritance.
So these things are for a law of judgment to you and your descendants in all your homes.
Whoever kills anyone, may be put to death by the testimony of multiple witnesses, but the testimony of only one witness is not enough to convict someone of murder.
Furthermore there is no payment or fine, sufficient to save the life of a convicted murderer, but they must surely be put to death.
And there is no payment or fine, sufficient for anyone that has fled to their refuge city, that would allow them to return the land of their inheritance, until after the death of the high priest.
So you must not pollute the land where you live, because blood defiles the land and the land cannot be cleansed of the blood that is shed there, except by the blood of the person who shed blood.
Therefore do not defile the land where you live, for I the Lord live in that land with the Israelis."

And the chief fathers of the families of Gilead's descendants, who was Machir's son, who was Manasseh's son, from the families of Joseph's sons, came and spoke to Moses, and the princes, and the chief fathers of the Israelis.
And they said, "The Lord commanded you to give the land by lot as an inheritance to the Israelis, and he also commanded you to give our brother Zelophehad's inheritance to his daughters.

And if they married one of the sons from one of the other Israelis tribes, then their inheritance will be taken from our fathers' inheritance. It will be added to the inheritance of the tribe that they married into, so it will be taken from the lot of our inheritance.
Then at the time of the Israeli Jubilee, their inheritance will be added to the tribal inheritance that they married into and removed from their fathers' tribe's inheritance."
And Moses spoke to the Israelis and said, "The tribe from Joseph's sons has spoken well, and this is the commandment that the Lord has given us about this."
The Lord has given us a commandant about Zelophehad's daughters and he has said, 'Let them marry whoever they think best, but they are only allowed to marry someone from their father's tribe.
So the Israelis inheritance, will not pass from one tribe to another, because everyone of the Israelis will keep their own fathers' inheritance for themselves.

And every daughter, that possesses an inheritance in any of the Israelis tribes, will only be able to marry someone from her father's family tribe, so that all Israelis may enjoy the inheritance of their fathers.
No inheritance will pass from one tribe to another, but everyone from the Israelis tribes will keep their own father's inheritance for themselves.'"
So Zelophehad's daughters did what the Lord commanded Moses to do.
And his daughters, Mahlah, Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Noah, married their father's brothers' sons.
And they were married into the families from the sons of Manasseh who was Joseph's son, and their inheritance remained in the tribe of the family of their father.
These are the Lord's commandments and judgments which he gave to the Israelis through Moses in the plains of Moab by the Jordan River near Jericho.
Moses spoke to all of Israel on the east side of the Jordan River in the wilderness, on the plain by the Red Sea coast, in the area between Paran, Tophel, Laban, Hazeroth, and DizAhab.
It is an eleven-day journey from Horeb by the way of Mount Seir to Kadesh-Barnea.
Now on the first day, of the eleventh month of the fortieth year Moses spoke to all of Israel, about the things that the Lord had given to him as commandments for them to live by.
This was after he killed King Sihon the Amorite, who ruled over Heshbon, and King Og of Bashan, who ruled Astaroth in Edrei.
And on this side of the Jordan River, in the land of Moab, Moses began to declare this law and he said,
"The Lord our God spoke to us in Horeb and said, 'You have lived on this mountain long enough.

Move to Mount Amorite, and to all the places near it, including the plains, the hills, and the vale. Then travel southward by the seashore to Canaan, Lebanon, the great river, and the Euphrates River.
See the lands before you, and go take possession of them, because the Lord has sworn to give them to your fathers Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and their descendants.'
And I spoke to you at that time and said, 'I am alone, and I cannot support you by myself.
Because your Lord God has increased your numbers so much, that you have now become as numerous as the stars in heaven.
May the Lord God of your fathers, make you a thousand times more numerous than you are, and bless you as he has promised that he would!
How can I support you all alone, and carry the weight of all your troubles and burdens, and settle your conflicts all by myself?
Find your wise men, those among you who are famous for their understanding, and bring them to me, and I will appoint them to be your governing officials.'
And you answered me and said, 'You have asked us to do something, that sounds like it would be good for us.'

So, I took your tribal chiefs and your famous wisemen and appointed them as your governing officials. And a chain of command will be established from the officers appointed to govern your tribes. Some officers will govern thousands, some will govern hundreds, some will govern fifty, and some will govern ten.
At that time, I charged your judges with hearing the causes of your brothers and I said, 'Judge everyone righteously, including every man and his brother, and any foreigners with them.

When you pass judgment over someone, make sure you treat everyone equally. Whether the issue you are hearing is a small matter or a great one, do not be afraid of anyone who comes before your court. For the judgment will be God's, and any causes that are too hard for you to decide, bring them to me, and I will hear it and decide for you.'
Also at that time, I gave you every commandment of everything that you must do.

As our Lord God commanded us, we left Horeb and traveled through the terrible wilderness, and you saw all the great and awesome things God did on our way to Mount Amorite, but we finally arrived in Kadesh-Barnea.
And I said to you, 'You have come to Mount Amorite, which our Lord God has given to us.
Behold your Lord God has given you the land before you, so go and take possession of it, and do not fear nor be discouraged, because the Lord God of your fathers has told you to do this.'
And all of you came to me and said, 'We must send men to search out the land before us, so they can determine which way we should go, and which cities are the best places for us to go.'
And I thought that was a good idea, so I took twelve men one from each tribe.
And I sent them up into the mountains, where they searched and explored the Eshcol valley.
And they took some of the fruit of the land, and brought it down to us, and they gave us their account of the lands there and said, 'The Lord our God has given us a good land.'
But you refused to go up into the land and rebelled against your Lord God's commandment.
And you were gossiping in your tents and when you said, 'The Lord hates us, because he has brought us out of Egypt, just to deliver us into the hands of the Amorites, who want to destroy us.

Where can we go? Our brothers discouraged our heart when they said, 'The people are greater and taller than we are, the great cities have walls, all the way up to heaven, and besides that, we saw Anakim's sons there.'
Then I said to you, 'Do not fear nor be afraid of them.
The Lord your God goes before you, and he will fight for you, the same way that he did all those other things for you before your very own eyes in Egypt.'
And you saw how your Lord God supported you in the wilderness, as a man supports his own son, and he has continued to support you until you arrived in this place.
But you did not believe your Lord God.
Who went before you, to search for a place for you to set up camp, who guided you with a column of fire by night, and a cloud by day to show you which way to go.
And the Lord heard what you were saying, and it made him angry, and he swore an oath and said,
'Surely not one man from this evil generation will see the good land, which I swore to give to your fathers.
Except for Jephunneh's son Caleb, who will see it, and I will give the land that he has walked on to him and his children, because he has completely followed the Lord.'
The Lord was also angry with me because of you and he said, 'You will not be allowed to go into the promised land either.
But Nun's son Joshua, who is standing before you, will be allowed to go there, so you must encourage him, because he is the reason that Israel will inherit the promised land.

And your children, who you said would be captured, and your children, who do not know the difference between good and evil, will be allowed to go into the promised land, and I will give it to them as their inheritance.
But as for you, go back out into the wilderness by the coast of the Red Sea.'

Then you answered me and said, 'We have sinned against the Lord, and we will go and fight, the way that our Lord God commanded us,' and when every man had armed himself with weapons of war, you were ready to go up into the hills.
And the Lord said to me, 'Tell them not go up into the hills and fight, because I am not with them, and if you do, you will be defeated by your enemies.'
So I spoke to you, and you would not listen to me, but you rebelled against the Lord's commandment, and you overconfidently went up into the hills.
And the Amorites living on that mountain, came out and chased you, like a swarm of bees, and destroyed you in Seir, all the way to Hormah.
And you returned and wept before the Lord, but the Lord would not hear you, nor listen to you.
So, you waited in Kadesh and lived there for a long time."
Then we turned and went out into the wilderness along the coast of the Red Sea, like the Lord told to me, and we lived around Mount Seir for a long time.
And the Lord spoke to me and said,
"You have lived around this mountain for long enough, turn and head north.

Give this command to the people and say, 'Pass through the land along the coast of your brothers from Esau's descendants, who are living in Seir, and be careful how you behave, because they will be afraid of you.
Do not attack them, because I will not give you their land, not even as much as a foot wide strip of land, because I have given Mount Seir to Esau as his inheritance.
You will be allowed to buy meat and water from them with money, so that you may have food and water to eat and drink.'"

For your Lord God has blessed all the works of your hands, he knows you have been wandering through this great wilderness, your Lord God has been with you for these last forty years, and you have lacked nothing.

When we passed through our brothers' land, where Esau's descendants lived in Seir, we went all the way through to the plain from Elath and Ezion-Geber, then we turned and passed through the wilderness of Moab.
And the Lord said to me, "Do not distress the Moabites, or attack them in battle, because I will not give you their land, because I have given Ar to Lot's descendants as their inheritance."
The Emims lived there in the past, they were as great and tall a people as the Anakims, and there were many of them.
They were counted among the giants, like the Anakims, but the Moabites called them Emims.

In the past the Horims also lived in Seir, but Esau's descendants succeeded them. They defeated them and took their place, the same way that Israel did when they took possession of the land which the Lord gave them as their inheritance.
And I said, "Now rise up, and cross over the Zered brook." And we crossed the Zered brook.

And it took thirty-eight years from the time we arrived in Kadesh-Barnea, until we crossed over the Zered brook. Which was after the entire generation of warriors from among the camp died off, just as the Lord had promised them.
Because the hand of the Lord was indeed against them, and he destroyed them from among the camp, until they were all consumed.
So, when all the men of war died, and were consumed from among the people.
The Lord spoke to me and said,
"Today, I want you to pass through Ar, along the coast of Moab.

And when you approach the Ammonites, do not distress or attack them, because I will not give you any of their land, because I have given it to Lot's descendants as their possession as an inheritance."
That land was also counted among the land of the giants, because giants lived there in the past, and the Ammonites called them Zamzummims.
They were a great tall people, and there were many of them like the Anakims, but the Lord destroyed them. The Ammonites succeeded them and took their place in the land.

Just as God had done to Esau's descendants who lived in Seir, when he destroyed the Horims from before them. Then Esau's descendants succeeded them, and took their place, and they have lived in the land to this very day.
And the Avims who lived in Hazerim, as far away as Gaza, were destroyed by the Caphtorims, who came from Caphtor to destroy them, and took their place in the land.

Now I say, "Get up and cross the Arnon River, because I have delivered King Sihon the Amorite king of Heshbon, and his lands into your hands. So go and defeat him in battle and take possession of the land.
Today I will begin to put the fear and dread of you in all the nations that under the heavens. They will hear reports of you, and they will tremble, worry and be anguished because of you."
I sent messengers from the wilderness of Kedemoth to King Sihon of Heshbon with words of peace and said,
"Let us use your road to pass through your land, and we will not turn to the left or right, but we will stay on the road.
If you let us pass through your land on foot, we will use our money to buy meat and water to eat and drink from you.
Please let us pass through like Esau's descendants did for us in Seir, and the Moabites did for us in Ar, until we cross the Jordan River into the land which our Lord God has given us."
But King Sihon of Heshbon would not let us pass, because your Lord God hardened his heart and made him obstinate, so that God could deliver him into your hands on this day.
And the Lord said to me, "Behold I have begun to give Sihon and his land to you, so you can begin to take possession of his land as your inheritance."
Then Sihon and all of his people came out to fight at Jahaz.
And our Lord God delivered him to us, and we defeated him, his sons, and all his people.
And at that time we took all of his cities, and completely destroyed his men, women, and children, in every city until none remained.
And we took their cattle and everything in their cities for ourselves, as the spoils of war.
From Aroer on the banks of the Arnon river, all the way to Mount Gilead, there were no cities too strong for us to capture, and our Lord God delivered them all to us.
But we did not go near the land of the Ammonites, nor to any other place along the Jabbok River, nor any of the mountain cities, that our Lord God had forbidden us to go near.
Then we turned toward Bashan, and King Og of Bashan came out with all of his people, to do battle with us at Edrei.
And the Lord said to me, "Do not fear King Og, because I will deliver him, his people, and his land into your hands, and you will defeat him as you defeated King Sihon of the Amorites in Heshbon."
So our Lord God delivered King Og of Bashan and all of his people, into our hands, and we defeated him, and none of his people survived.
And at that time, we took all of his cities including sixty cities in the Argob region of the kingdom of Og in Bashan.
All of those cities had high city walls with bars on the gates, and we also took many unsecured towns and villages without walls.
We completely destroyed them, the same way we defeated King Sihon of Heshbon, when we completely wiped out the men, women, and children in every city.
But we took everything in the cities as the spoils of war for ourselves, including all the cattle.
We took all the land from the two Amorite kings, that was on this side of the Jordan River, from the Arnon River to Mount Hermon.
The Sidonians name for Mount Hermon is Sirion, and the Amorites call it Shenir.
We took all the plains cities, all of Gilead, and all of Bashan as far as Salchah and Edrei, which are cities in Bashan kingdom of Og.
Because King Og of Bashan was all that was left of the giants of Rephaim. His iron bed was nine cubits long, and four cubits wide, and it still remains in Rabbath of the Ammonites.
And at that time, I gave the land we took from beyond Aroer near the Arnon River, which included all of their cities and half of Gilead, to the Reubenites and the Gadites.
And I gave the half-tribe of Manasseh the rest of Gilead and all of Bashan from the kingdom of Og, and all of the Argob region which was called the land of giants.
Manasseh's son Jair took the Argob country all the way to the coasts of Geshuri and Maachathi, and he named them Bashan-Havoth-Jair after himself, which is still their name to this day.
And I gave Gilead to Machir.
And I gave the Reubenites and the Gadites the land from Gilead to the Arnon river and half of the valley, and the border stretched all the way to the Jabbok River, which is on the Ammonite border.
As well as the plains from Chinnereth and the Jordan River, all the way to the Dead Sea plain, under the eastern slopes of Ashdoth-Pisgah.
At that time I gave you commands and said, "Your Lord God has given you this land, all of you must arm yourselves, and pass before your Israelis brothers on your way to war.
But you must leave your wives, your children, and your cattle in the cities I have given you, because I know that you have a lot of cattle.
Until the rest of your brothers have taken possession of the land beyond the Jordan River which your Lord God has given them, then all of you may return to the inheritance which I have given you."
At that time I gave Joshua an order and said, "You have seen everything that your Lord God has done to these two kings, and he will do the same to every kingdom that you pass through.
Do not fear them, because your Lord God will fight for you."
At that time, I implored the Lord and asked,
"O Lord God, you have begun to show your great and mighty hand to your servant. For what other god in heaven or on earth, can do the mighty works that you do?
I pray you will let me go and see the good land beyond the Jordan River, that good mountain. and Lebanon."
But the Lord was angry with because of you, and would not listen to me, and the Lord spoke to me and said, "Be satisfied, and speak to me no more about this matter.
Go to the top of Mount Pisgah, and look west, north, south, and east. You will see the land with your own eyes, but you will not be allowed to cross the Jordan River.
But you must give the military command to Joshua, encourage him, and strengthen him because he will cross over and lead these people, and he will lead them to the land they will inherit."
So, we stayed in the valley along the border of Beth-Peor.
O Israel, listen to the laws and judgements which I will teach you, because if you obey them, you may live to go and take possession of the land that the Lord God of your fathers has given you.
Do not add one word to the commands that I have given you, and do not diminish from them either, so that you may keep your Lord God's commandments which I have given you.
You saw with your own eyes what your Lord God did when he destroyed all the men, because they followed Baal-Peor.
But those of you that held loyally to your Lord God are alive today because of it.
Behold, I have taught you the laws and judgments that you should obey when you take possession of the promised land, just as my Lord God has commanded me.

That's why you should keep these commandments, because this will show your wisdom and understanding to other nations. When they hear these laws, they will say, "Surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people.
For what other nation is as great as ours, whose god is as near to them as our Lord God is to us in everything that we ask of him?
And what other nation is so great or has laws and judgments, as righteous as the laws which I have given you today?

Pay attention to the things that you have seen very diligently and teach them to your sons and your son's sons, and make sure that your soul does not forget them, otherwise these lessons may fade from your heart, soul, and memory.

Especially remember the day that you stood before your Lord God in Horeb, when he said to me, "Gather the people together, and I will let them hear my words, so that they may learn to fear me all the days of their lives here on earth, and they may also teach these things to their children."
And you came near and stood at the foot of the mountain, and the mountain erupted with fire that went up into the heart of heaven, and everything was covered with thick dark clouds.
And the Lord spoke to you from the middle of the fire, and you heard his words, but you saw no physical form, you only heard his voice.
And he gave you his covenant of the ten commandments that he commanded you to obey, which he had written on two stone tablets.
And the Lord ordered me to teach you these laws and judgments, so that you might keep them in the land that he sent you to possess.
So keep watch over yourselves, because you did not see the Lord, when he spoke to you in Horeb from the middle of the fire.
Otherwise, you may corrupt yourselves by carving an image in the likeness of any living thing male or female.
Such as the likeness of any of the animals on the earth, or the likeness of any winged birds that fly in the air.
Or the likeness of anything that creeps on the ground, or the likeness of any fish beneath the waters on the earth.

Otherwise you may one day look up to heaven, and when you see the sun, the moon, or all the stars in heaven, you may be driven to worship them, or become the servants of the things which your Lord God has given equally to all nations under the heavens.
But the Lord has taken you out of the Egyptian iron furnace, to be his people of inheritance, as you are today.

Furthermore the Lord was angry with me because of you, and he swore that I would never cross the Jordan River, and I would never enter into that good land which your Lord God has given you as an inheritance.
But I must die here, and I will never cross the Jordan River, but you will cross over and take possession of that good land.
So take heed, pay attention, and make sure that you do not forget the covenant, which your Lord God has made with you. Do not carve an image or likeness of anything which your Lord God has forbidden.
For your Lord God is a consuming fire, and a jealous God.

After you have fathered children and grandchildren, and you have lived in the land a long time, and you corrupt yourselves and carve an image or likeness of anything, and you do evil in your Lord God's sight to provoke his anger.

May heaven and earth be my witness against you on that day, so that destruction overtakes you, cutting you off from the land which you crossed the Jordan River to possess. And your days there will not last long and you will be completely destroyed.
And the Lord will scatter you among the nations, and only a small number of you will survive among the heathen, where the Lord leads you.
And you will serve manmade gods of wood and stone, which neither see, hear, eat, nor smell.
But if seek your Lord God from there with all of your heart and soul, you will find him.
When you suffer tribulation, and all of these things come upon you in the latter days. If you turn to your Lord God and listen to his voice.
Because your Lord God is a merciful God, he will not destroy you nor forsake you and he will not forget the covenant which he swore to your fathers.

Ponder the days and times past which came before you, when God first created man on earth, and ask from one side of heaven to the other if there has ever been anything as great as this, or if anything like it has ever been heard of before?
And ask yourself if any other people have ever heard God's voice speaking to them from the middle of a fire, as you have, and lived?

Or has God ever attempted to take a nation for himself from the middle of another nation, by temptations, signs, wonders, and war, with his mighty hand, his outstretched arm, and great terrors, as your Lord God did for you in Egypt before your very own eyes?
He let you see all of this, so that you might know that he is the Lord God, and there are no other gods besides him.
From the heavens he let you to hear his voice, so that he might instruct you, and he showed you his great fire on earth, and you heard his words coming from the middle of the fire.
And because he loved your fathers, he chose their descendants after them to be his people, and he brought them out of Egypt, in his sight with his mighty power.
He drove greater and mightier nations out from before you and brought you into their land and gave it to you as an inheritance, and to this day it still belongs to you.
So consider in your heart and know that he is the Lord God in heaven above, and on the earth beneath heaven, and there are no other gods.

So keep God's laws and commandments which I have given you on this day, so that everything may go well for you and your children. So that you may also prolong your days on earth which your Lord God has given you forever.
Then Moses severed three cities that were facing the sun, from the others on this side of the Jordan River.
As a place of sanctuary for anyone to flee who may have accidentally killed a neighbor, who they had not hated in the past, and a place where someone like this can live in safety.

The names of these cities are: From Reuben's tribe there is Bezer on the wilderness plains, and from Gad's tribe is Ramoth in Gilead, and from the Manassite tribe are the Golan Heights which is in Bashan.
These are the laws Moses has given to the Israelis.
These are the laws, testimonies, and judgments which Moses gave to the Israelis after they left Egypt.
On this side of the Jordan River, in the valley along the border of Beth-Peor, in King Sihon's land of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon, whom Moses and the Israelis defeated, after they left Egypt.
And they took possession of his land, and the land of King Og of Bashan, who were the two kings of the Amorites on this side of the Jordan River facing the rising sun.
From Aroer, which is near the bank of the Arnon River, all the way to Mount Zion which is also called Mount Hermon.
And all the plains on the far eastern side of the Jordan River, as far as the Dead Seas, under the slopes of the Pisgah springs.
And Moses spoke to all of Israel and said, "O Israel, listen to the laws and judgments which I am giving you today, so that you may learn, keep, and do them.
The Lord our God made a covenant with us in Horeb.
The Lord did not make this covenant with our fathers, but he made it with us, all of us who are alive today.
The Lord spoke to you face to face on the mountain, from the middle of the fire.
I stood between you and the Lord at that time, to show you the Lord's word, because you were afraid of the fire, and you did not go up into the mountain, when he said,
'I am your Lord God, who brought you out of Egypt, from the house of bondage.
You shall have no other gods before me.
You shall not carve an image or likeness of anything that is in heaven above, on the earth below, or beneath the waters on the earth.

You shall not bow down to their idols nor serve them, because I am your Lord God and I am a jealous God, who visits the immorality of the fathers on their children to the third and fourth generations of those who hate me.
And I will show mercy to the thousands of those who love me and keep my commandments.
You shall not take the name of the Lord your God in vain, because whoever takes the Lord's name in vain will not be found guiltless.
You shall keep the Sabbath day holy to sanctify it, like your Lord God has commanded you.
You shall do all your work and labor in six days.

But the seventh day is your Lord God's Sabbath day, it is a day of rest, and you will do no work of any kind on that day, nor should your son, your daughter, your male or female servant, your oxen, your donkey, any of your cattle, nor any foreigners living within your walls, so that your male and female servants may get as much rest as you.'

Remember that you were a servant in the land of Egypt, and that your Lord God brought you out of there with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm, so your Lord God commands you to keep the Sabbath day.
Honor your father and mother, because this is what your Lord God has commanded you, so that your days may be prolonged and everything will go well for you, in the land your Lord God has given you.
You shall not kill.
You shall not commit adultery.
You shall not steal.
You shall not you bear false witness against your neighbor.
You shall not covet your neighbor's wife, nor his house, field, male servant, female servant, oxen, donkey, or anything else that belongs to your neighbor.'

These are the words that the Lord spoke with a great voice, from the middle of the fire, when all of you were assembled on the mountain in the thick cloudy darkness, and he wrote them all on two stone tablets that he gave me.
When you heard his voice from the middle of the darkness, and because the mountain was on fire, you, your elders, and all of your tribal leaders came to me.
And you said, 'Behold our Lord God has shown us his glory and greatness, and we have heard his voice from the middle of the fire, and today we have seen that God does talk to man, and he lives.
So why should we die? Because his great fire will consume us, and if we hear our Lord God's voice again, we will surely die.
For who has survived that has heard the voice of the living God speaking from the middle of the fire, as we have?
You must go and hear what our Lord God has to say, then you can return and tell us everything he says, and we will do whatever he says.'
And the Lord heard you when you spoke to me and he said, 'I have heard what these people said to you, and they have spoken well with what they have said.
If only they had such a heart to fear me, and always keep all of my commandments, so that everything might go well for them and their children forever!
Go and tell them to go back to their tents.
But I want you to stay here with me, and I will give you all of the commandments, laws, and judgments you must teach them, so that they may keep them in the promised land which I have given them.'
So you must keep and observe all of your Lord God's commandments, and you must not leave the narrow path, or turn to the right or to the left.
You must walk in all the ways which your Lord God has commanded you, so that you may live and everything will go well for you, so that your days may be prolonged in the land which you will possess."
These are the commandments, laws, and judgments which your Lord God commanded me to teach you to obey in the land you will possess.
So that you, your son, and your son's son will fear your Lord God and keep all the laws and commandments I have given you so that all the days of your life may be prolonged.

O Israel, listen, observe, and keep his commandments, laws, and judgments, so that everything may go well for you, and your numbers may greatly increase, as your fathers' Lord God promised you, in a land that flows with milk and honey.
O Israel, hear this, our Lord God is one Lord.
And you must love your Lord God with all your heart, all your soul, and all your strength.
And the commandments I have given you today will be in your heart.
And you must diligently teach them to your children and tell them about these things when you are sitting in your house, or you are taking a walk, or you lie down, or when you get up in the morning.
And you must bind them with your handshake as a sign, that you will think of them at the front of your mind.
You must write them on the door posts of your house, and your gate posts.
When your Lord God brings you into the land he promised to give your fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. The land where he also promised to give you great and good cities that you did not build.

A place with houses filled with every good thing that you did not make, and wells that you did not dig. And vineyards and olive trees which you did not plant, in a land where you will eat your fill and be full.
Then be careful that you do not forget the Lord, who brought you out of the house of bondage in Egypt.
You must fear your Lord God, and serve him, and swear by his name.
You must not chase after other gods, especially the gods of other people that are all around you.

Because your Lord God is with you, and he is a jealous God, and if you are unfaithful toward him, his anger will be kindled against you, and it will destroy you and remove you from the face of the earth.
You will not tempt your Lord God, as you tempted him in Massah.
You will diligently keep your Lord God's commandments, testimonies, and the laws he has given you.
You will do what is good and righteous in God's sight, so that everything goes well for you. Then you will go in and take possession of the good land that God promised to give your fathers.
You will throw out all your enemies before you, just as the Lord has said.
And in the future when your children ask you about the testimonies, laws, and judgments that our Lord God has given us?
Then you can answer them and say, "We were Pharaoh's slaves in Egypt, and the Lord brought us out of bondage with a mighty hand.
And we saw with our own eyes, the many great and sorrowful signs and wonders, that the Lord performed against the Pharaoh, Egypt, and everyone else in his household.
God brought us out of Egypt, to bring us into the land that he promised to give to our fathers.
And the Lord commanded us to fear him and keep all of his laws, so that we would be safe, and he could protect us, and keep us alive to this very day.
And if we observe and obey all of the commandments that our Lord God has given us, then we will be righteous in his sight."

When your Lord God brings you into a land to possess and he throws out seven greater and mightier nations before you, including the Hittites, Girgashites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and the Jebusites.
And when your Lord God delivers them to you, you will defeat and completely destroy them, and you must not make any concessions toward them, nor show them any mercy.
You must not pledge your sons or daughters to them in marriage.
Because they will turn your sons and daughters away from me, they will not follow me and they may serve other gods, so the Lord's anger will be kindled against you which will suddenly destroy you.
But this is the way you must deal with them, you must destroy their altars, crush their images, cut down their Asherah poles, and burn their carved images in a fire.
Because you are a holy people to your Lord God, and he has chosen you for himself, to be his special people, above all other people living on the face of the earth.
The Lord did not give you his love nor choose you because there were more of you than any other people, but it was because you were the fewest of all people.
But because the Lord loved you, and because he wanted the promise that he made to your fathers, he brought you out of Egypt with a mighty hand and rescued you from slavery under Pharaoh.
So know that your Lord God is God, the faithful God, who keeps his promises and grants mercy to those who love him, and keep his commandments to a thousand generations.
And repays those who hate him to their face with destruction, he will have no mercy on anyone who hates him, and he will repay him to his face.
So you must keep and obey these commandments, laws, and judgments which I have given you today.
Because, if you hear and keep these judgments your Lord God will keep his promises to you and show you the mercy which he swore to your show fathers.

And he will love you, bless you, and multiply you, he will also bless your children, your land, your wheat, your wine, your oil, and the increase of your cows and sheep flocks, in the land that he swore to your fathers that he would give to you.
You will be blessed above all other people, and there will be no barren males or females among you, or your cattle.
And the Lord will remove you from all sickness, and he will not put any of the evil diseases you know from Egypt on you, but he will lay them on all of those who hate you.
And you will consume whoever your Lord God delivers to you. You will have no pity on them, nor serve their gods, because that will be a snare to you.
And if you say in your heart, that these nations are stronger than I am, how can I dispose of them?
You must not be afraid of them, but just remember what your Lord God did to Pharaoh, and all of Egypt.
The great temptations you saw, the signs, the wonders, and the Lord's mighty hand and outstretched arm which your Lord God used to bring you out of bondage, he will do to all the people who you fear
Furthermore, your Lord God will send a hornet's nest among them, until everyone who is left runs and hides from you, and they will be destroyed.
You must not be frightened of them, because your Lord God is with you, a mighty God to be terribly feared.
And your Lord God will push those nations out before you little by little, and they will not be defeated all at once because if they were, the field beasts would increase against you.
But your Lord God will deliver them to you and devastate them with complete destruction.
He will deliver their kings into your hands, and you will remove their name from under heaven, and they will not stand before you until you have destroyed them.

You must burn the carved images of their gods in a fire, and you must not keep the gold or silver they are made of, nor take it with you, otherwise you will be trapped by it, because it is an abomination to your Lord God.
And you must not bring an abomination into your home, or else you will be cursed like it is, but turn away from it and completely abhor it, because it is a cursed thing.

You must observe and obey all the commandments which I have given you today, so that you may live and multiply your descendants, and go and take possession of the land the Lord swore he would give your fathers.

Remember your Lord God led you through the wilderness for forty years, in order to humble and test you, so that he would know what was in your heart, and whether or not you would keep his commandments.

God humbled you and allowed you to suffer, but when you were hungry, he fed you with manna from heaven, which you nor your fathers knew anything about. He did this to teach you that man does not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds from the mouth of the God.
Your clothes did not wear out, and your feet did not swell up during those forty years.
You must also remember in your heart, that in the same way a man disciplines his son, so your Lord God will discipline you.
So you must keep your Lord God's commandments, walk in his ways, and fear him.
Because your Lord God brings you into a good land, a land of brooks flowing with water, with fountains and springs that trickle out of the depths of the valleys and hills.
A land of wheat, barley, grapevines, fig trees, and pomegranates, it is also a land of olive oil and honey.
A land where there is no scarcity of bread and you will lack nothing, a land rich with iron ore and you can mine brass from the hills.
When you have eaten your fill, you will bless your Lord God for the good land which he has given you.
Be very careful that you do not forget your Lord God, and fail to keep his commandments, judgments, and laws which I have given you today.
Otherwise, after you have eaten your fill, built good houses, and lived there.
And after your herds and flocks multiply, and your silver and gold multiplies, and everything that you have has multiplied.
When your heart becomes proud, and you forget your Lord God, who brought you out of the house of bondage in Egypt.
The God who led you through that great and terrible wilderness full of fiery serpents, scorpions, and drought. And where there was no water, he made water pour out of the rock for you.
He fed you manna in the wilderness, which your fathers knew nothing about in order to humble and test you, so that you may prosper later on.
And you say in your heart, I have prospered and acquired all of this wealth all by myself, by my own hand.

But you will remember your Lord God, because he is the one who has given you the power to acquire your wealth, in order to establish his covenant, which he swore to your fathers, that has lasted to this very day.
And if you forget your Lord God, and chase after other gods, serve them, and worship them, I will testify against you, and you will surely perish.
So you will perish, like the nations that the Lord God destroys before you, because you would not obey his voice.
O Israel hear this, cross over the Jordan River today, and take possession of nations greater and mightier than yourself, great cities with walls all the way up to heaven.
A great and tall people, who as you know are the descendants of the Anakims, and about whom you have heard it said, "Who can stand before the descendants of Anak!"

But understand this today, your Lord God crosses the Jordan River before you as a consuming fire. God will destroy them, and bring them down before your very eyes, so that you can quickly drive them out and destroy them, just as he has promised you.
After your Lord God drives them out before you, do not say you in your heart, that the Lord gave me this land because I am righteousness, but he drove them out because they are wicked nations.

Your Lord God did not send you to take possession of their land because you are righteous, or you have an honest heart. God drove them out because they are wicked nations, and to keep the promises that he made to your fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
So understand this, you are stubborn people, and your Lord God did not give you this good land because you are righteous.
Do not forget that you provoked your Lord God to anger in the wilderness and remember that from the very first day you left Egypt until you arrived here today, you have rebelled against him.
You also provoked your Lord God to anger in Horeb, and he was so angry that he could have destroyed you.
I had gone up into the mountain to receive the stone tablets with the Lord's covenant written on them. I lived on the mountain for forty days and forty nights, and I ate no bread and drank no water.

Your Lord God gave me a covenant that he wrote and carved on two stone tablets with his own fingers, every word that he spoke to you on the mountain from the middle of the fire, when everyone was assembled before him.
After forty days and forty nights, the Lord gave me the covenant which he had written on the two stone tablets.

And the Lord said to me, "Quick, return to the people you brought out of Egypt, because they have sinned and corrupted themselves. O how quickly they turned against me and strayed from the path that I commanded them to take, because they have made a molten image."
Furthermore the Lord spoke to me and said, "I have seen these stubborn people.
Leave me alone, so I can destroy them and erase their names from under heaven, and I will make you a mightier and greater nation than them."
So I descended the burning mountain, and I carried the covenant written on the two stone tablets in my hands.
When I looked, behold I saw that you had sinned against your Lord God and made a molten calf, and I saw that you had turned away from the path that he commanded you to take.
And I threw the stone tablets on the ground and broke them right in front of you.

Then I bowed down before the Lord for forty days and forty nights. During that time, I ate no bread and drank no water, because you had committed so many wicked sins in his sight that it provoked his anger.
I was afraid of the Lord's burning anger and displeasure with you, and of his plans to destroy you. But at that time the Lord listened to me on your behalf.
And at that time the Lord was also very angry with Aaron and wanted to destroy him, so I prayed for Aaron.
And I took your sinful calf and burned it in the fire, then I crushed it, ground it into powdery dust, and threw the dust into the brook that was flowing down the mountain.
And at Taberah, Massah, and Kibroth-Hattaavah, you provoked the Lord to anger even more.

When your Lord God sent you away from Kadesh-Barnea he said, "Go and take possession of the land I have given you." But you rebelled and refused to obey him, because you did not believe him and you would not listen to him.
