You have rebelled against the Lord from the very first day that I met you.
So I bowed down before the Lord for forty days and forty nights, because he said that he was going to destroy you.

And I prayed to the Lord and said, "O Lord God, do not destroy your people, for they are your inheritance which you rescued through your greatness. And they are the people you brought out of Egypt with a mighty hand.
Remember your servants Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and do not look at the stubborn sinful wickedness of these people.

Otherwise the people in the land you brought us from will say, their Lord God was unable to bring them into the land which he promised them and he hated them, so he brought them out into the wilderness to kill them.
Yet they are your people and your inheritance, and you brought them out of Egypt with your mighty power and outstretched arm.
At that time the Lord said to me, "Carve two stone tablets like to the first two, and bring them to me up on the mountain, and make a wooden ark.
I will rewrite the tablets with the same words that were written on the first tablets which you broke, and you can put them in the ark to protect them."
So I made a shittim wood ark, and carved two stone tablets like the first two, and carried them in my hands up into the mountain.

And the Lord wrote the ten commandments on these two tablets, with the same words that he wrote on the first two tablets, these commandments are the same ones that the Lord spoke of on the mountain from the middle of the fire while you were all assembled before him.
I came down from the mountain and put the tablets in the ark I built, and they are still there now, the way the Lord commanded me.

And the Israelis left Beeroth which was part of Jaakan's tribe and traveled to Mosera where Aaron died and was buried. Then Aaron's son Eleazar began to minister in the priest's office instead of him.
From there they journeyed to Gudgodah, and from Gudgodah to Jotbath, a land of rivers and lakes.
At that time the Lord separated Levi's tribe to stand before the Lord and carry his Ark of the Covenant, and to minister to him and bless others in his name, which they still do, to this day.
So Levi and his brothers have no inheritance, because the Lord God is their inheritance, and this is what he promised them.
I stayed up on the mountain, like I did the first time for forty days and forty nights, and the Lord listened to me at that time, and he decided not to destroy you.
And the Lord said to me, "Rise up, and lead the people into the land I promised to give their fathers, so that they may take possession of it."
And now Israel, your Lord God requires nothing from you, but to fear him, to walk in his ways, to love him, and to serve your Lord God with all of your heart and soul.
And to keep your Lord God's commandments and laws which I have given you today, for your own good.
Behold, the heaven, the heaven of the heavens, the earth and everything on it, all belong to your Lord God.
Only your Lord God delighted in and loved your fathers, and he chose their descendants after them, including you, above all other people, and it is still that way to this day.
So circumcise the foreskin of your heart, and do not be stubborn any longer.
Because your Lord God is God of gods, and Lord of lords, the great, mighty, and awesome God who shows no preferential treatment to his people, who cannot be bribed.
He executes judgment of the fatherless and widows, he loves strangers and gives them food and clothes.
So love strangers, because you were strangers in the land of Egypt.
Fear your Lord God, serve him, be loyal to him, and swear by his name.
He is your praise, he is your God, and he has done all of these great and awesome things for you, and you have seen it with your own two eyes.
Your fathers went down into Egypt with seventy people, and now your Lord God has multiplied you like the stars of heaven.
So you must love your Lord God and always do everything that he says, and keep his laws, judgments, and commandments.
And today you know that unlike your children who have not seen your Lord God's punishments, or his great mighty hand, and outstretched arm.
Or the miracles and plagues that he sent against the Egyptians and Pharaoh the king.
Or what he did to the Egyptian army and their horses and chariots, or how he made the water of the Red Sea crash down on them as they pursued you, or how he has continued to destroy them to this day.
Or what he did for you in the wilderness, until you arrived here.

Eliab was Reuben's son, and your children have not seen what God did to Eliab's sons Dathan and Abiram in Israel, when the earth opened her mouth and swallowed them, their households, their tents, and everything else that they owned.
But you yourselves have seen all the great and wonderous things that your Lord God has done.
So, keep the commandments I have given you today to make you strong, and go and take possession of the land you have inherited.
And your days will be prolonged in the land that the Lord promised to give to your fathers and their descendants, a land flowing with milk and honey.
Because the land you are going to take possession of is nothing like the land you are coming from in Egypt, where you sowed your seed, and carried water to it as you would an herb garden.
But the land, where you are going, is a land of hills and valleys, and it is watered by the rains from heaven.
A land your Lord God cares for and watches over all year long.
And if you diligently listen to the commandments I have given you today, to love your Lord God and serve him with all your heart and soul.
Then I will provide the rains for your land in the proper seasons, from the first rains to the harvest rains, so that you may harvest your wheat and crops, so you can press your oil and wine.
And I will put grass for your cattle in your fields, so that you may eat your fill.
So be careful that your heart is not deceived, and you turn away from your Lord God, and you are tricked into serving and worshiping other gods.

Because the Lord's anger will be kindled against you, and he will close the heavens and there will be no rain. The land will not yield her fruit; you will quickly perish and the good land which the Lord has given you will be taken away.
Therefore, store my words in your heart and soul, and bind them as a sign on your hand, so that they may always be remembered at the front of your mind.
Teach these things to your children and speak of them when you are sitting in your home, or when you go for a walk, or when you lie down, and when you rise up.
Write them on the door posts of your home and your gates.
So that you and your children's days may be multiplied in the land the Lord promised to give to your fathers, like the old days of heaven on earth.
Because if you diligently keep all the commandments which I have given you, and you love your Lord God, and walk in his ways, and loyally follow him.
Then the Lord will drive out all these nations before you, and you will take possession of nations greater and mightier than you.
Everywhere you walk will be yours, and your land will extend from the wilderness to Lebanon, and from the Euphrates River to the coast of the farthest sea.
No man will be able to stand against you, because your Lord God will put the dread and fear of you upon all the lands where you walk, as he has told you.
Behold, today I give you both a blessing and a curse.
You will receive a blessing if you obey your Lord God's commandments, which I have given to you this day.
But you will be cursed if you do not obey God's commandments, and you turn away from the path which I have commanded you to take this day, and you chase after gods that you do not know.
When your Lord God brings you in to take possession of the land you are entering, you must declare a blessing on Mount Gerizim, and a curse on Mount Ebal.
Are these mountains not on the other side of the Jordan River, along the road that faces the sunset, in the land of the Canaanites, who live in the desert beside Gilgal, near the plains of Moreh?
Because you will cross over the Jordan River, to enter and take possession of the land that your Lord God has given you, and that's where you will live.
And you must observe and obey all the laws and judgments which I have given you today.
These are the laws and judgments that you must observe and obey in the land, which your fathers' Lord God gave you to live in for all the days of your life on earth.
When you take possession of these nations, you must completely destroy every place that they used to serve their gods, including high up on the mountains, or the hills, and under every green tree.
Tear down their altars, break their columns, burn their Asherah poles, remove the carved images of their gods, and totally eliminate every one of their names.
You shall not worship your Lord God in this way.
But your Lord God will choose a place from all of your tribes for his home and a place to establish his name, and he will bring you to this place.
That's where you must bring your burnt offerings, your sacrifices, your tithes, your hand's sacred offerings, your promises, your voluntary offerings, and the yearlings from your herds and flocks.
That's where you will eat before your Lord God, and you will rejoice because your households, and everything that you put your hand to, will prosper, because your Lord God has blessed you.
You must not behave in the way that we do today, where everyone does whatever seems right in their own eyes.
Because you have not yet arrived in the place of rest and the inheritance, which your Lord God has given you.
When you cross the Jordan River and live in the land your Lord God has given you as an inheritance, he will give you rest from all your enemies that surround you, and you will live securely.

Then your Lord God will choose a place for his name to live, and that place is where you must bring everything that I told you to bring, including your burnt offerings, your sacrifices, your tithes, your hand's sacred offerings, and everything that you promised to the Lord.
You, your sons and daughters, your male and female servants, and the Levites living within your gates because they have no other inheritance, will rejoice before your Lord God.
Take heed that you do not offer your burnt offerings in every place that you see.
But make your burnt offerings in a place the Lord will chooses for you from one of your tribes, and that's where you must do everything that I command you to do.

You may kill and eat whatever meat your soul desires within your gates, because your Lord God has given you his blessing, and you may eat the clean and the unclean animals including the deer and the gazelle.
But do not eat the blood, instead pour it out on the ground like water.

Within your gates, you must not eat any of your tithes of wheat, wine, oil, yearlings from your herds or flocks, your voluntary offerings, your hand's sacred offerings, nor any of your other promised gifts.

But instead you, and your sons and daughters, your male and female servants, or any Levites living within your gates must eat them before your Lord God, in a place that he will choose, and you will rejoice before him in all that you do.
Be careful that you do not forsake the Levites as long as you are living on the earth.
When your Lord God enlarges your border as he promised, and you crave meat and say, "I will eat meat, because my soul longs for meat," then you may eat meat or whatever your soul desires.

If the place where your Lord God has chosen to establish his name is too far from you, then you can slaughter anything from the herds or flocks that the Lord has given you, and as I have told you, you may eat it or whatever your soul desires within your gates.
You may eat it the way the gazelle and deer are eaten, so you can also eat the clean and the unclean animals in the same way.
Make sure you do not eat the blood, because the blood is the life, and you must not eat the life with the flesh.
You must not eat it, but you must pour it out on the ground like it is water.
You must not eat it, so that everything goes well for you and your children, because you have done everything that you thought was righteous in the Lord's sight.
But you must take only your holy things and your promised gifts to the place the Lord has chosen.
You must offer your sacrificial burnt offerings, both the meat and the blood on your Lord God's altar, and the blood must be poured out on his altar, and then you may eat the meat.

Listen to and obey everything I have said to you, so that everything may go well for you and your children forever, and you will be doing everything that is good and righteous in your Lord God's sight.
When your Lord God cuts off the nations before you, and you enter their nation to take possession of their land, and you drive them out to live there.

Take care that you are not snared by following their ways, after that they have been destroyed before you, do not ask about their gods and ask, "How did these nations serve their gods? I will do likewise."

You must not worship your Lord God the same way, because he hates every abomination that they practice for their gods, because they have even burnt their own sons and daughters in the fire to their gods.
So do everything I have commanded you to do, observe and obey your Lord God's commandments, do not add to it, nor diminish from it.
If a prophet or dreamer rises up among you, and gives you signs or wonders.
And if the signs or wonders they have told you about come to pass and they say, "Let us chase after and serve other gods that you do not know."
You must not listen to that prophet or dreamer, because your Lord God is testing you, to know whether you love your Lord God with all your heart and soul.
You must walk after your Lord God, fear him, keep his commandments, obey his voice, serve him, and loyally follow him.

And that prophet or dreamer, must be put to death, because they have tried to turn you away from your Lord God, who brought you out of Egypt, and rescued you from the house of bondage. They tried to turn you away from the path that your Lord God commanded you to walk in, so you must purge that evil from your midst.
If your brother, your son or daughter, the wife you embrace, or your closest friend secretly tempts you and says, "Let us go and serve other gods," which you nor your fathers have ever known.
Especially the gods of the people around you, whether they are near or far from you, from one end of the earth to the other.
You must not consent nor listen to them, you must not pity them, and you must neither spare nor conceal them.
But you must surely kill them, your hand must be the first to put him to death, and then the hands of all the other people.
You must stone them with stones and kill them, because they have sought to lure you away from your Lord God, who brought you out of the Egyptian house of bondage.
And all of Israel will hear about it and be fearful, and they will no longer do this type of wickedness among you.
But if you are living in one of the cities that your Lord God gave you to live in and you hear someone say,
"Some men from Belial's descendants led the inhabitants of their city astray and said, 'Let us go and serve other gods (which you have not known).'"
Then you must diligently ask questions and investigate to determine the truth, and if you discover for certain, that such an abomination has been committed among you.
You must surely defeat the people of that city with the sword, and completely destroy it and everything there, including the cattle.

Take all the spoils and pile them in the middle of the street and burn the city along with every scrap of the spoils in the fire, this will be a burnt offering to your Lord God, and it will remain a pile of ruins forever, never to be rebuilt.

Do not hold any of these cursed things in your hand, so that the Lord may turn from his fierce anger, and show you mercy, have compassion on you, and multiply you as he promised your fathers he would.
Because you listen to your Lord God's voice, you keep all of his commandments that I have given you today, and you do everything that is righteous in God's eyes.
You are your Lord God's children, and you must not cut yourselves, nor shave your forehead for the dead.
For you are a holy people to your Lord God, and he has chosen you to be his special people, above all the other nations on earth.
You must not eat anything abominable.
The beasts that you are allowed to eat include the cow, sheep, and goat.
The deer, gazelle, red deer, wild goat, white antelope, wild ox, and wild sheep.
And you are allowed to eat any other beast with a two-toe split hoof, that chews the cud.

Nevertheless you must not eat any of the beasts without a two-toe split hoof that chews the cud, or it has a two-toe split hoof but does not chew the cud, like the camel, the hare, and the rabbit, because they are unclean to you.
And because pigs have a split hoof, yet does not chew the cud, it is unclean to you, so you must not eat its meat, nor touch its dead carcass.
You may eat anything living in the water that has fins and scales.
But you must not eat anything living in the water that does not have fins and scales, because it is unclean to you.
And you may eat all of the clean birds.
But you are not allowed to eat these birds: The eagle, bearded vulture, and osprey.
The glede, kite, and any kind of vulture.
Any kind of raven.
The owl, night hawk, cuckoo, and any kind of hawk.
The little owl, great owl, and the swan.
The pelican, Egyptian vulture, and the cormorant.
The stork, any kind of heron, lapwing, and the bat.
Anything that flies and creeps on the ground like insects, is unclean to you and they must not be eaten.
But you may eat any of the clean birds.

You must not eat anything that dies of natural causes, you must give it to any foreigners living within the gates of your city to eat, or you may sell it to a foreigner, because you are a holy people to your Lord God. You must not boil a kid goat in its mother's milk.
You must set aside an honest tithe of ten percent of everything your field produces each year.

And you must eat before your Lord God, in a place that he will choose to place his name, from your tithes of wheat, wine, oil, and the firstlings of your herds and flocks, so that you may learn to always fear your Lord God.
And when your Lord God blesses you, and the place where your Lord God chooses to place his name, is too far away for you, and you are unable to carry it.
Then you must sell it and carry the money in your hand to the place your Lord God has chosen.

And you may spend that money for whatever your soul desires, oxen, sheep, wine, strong drink, or for anything else you want, and you must eat it there before your Lord God, and you will celebrate with your household.
And you must not forsake the Levite living inside your gates, because he has no other inheritance from you.
At the end of every three years bring a tithe consisting of your entire fields production for the year and lay it up inside your gates.

And because the Levites have no other inheritance from you, and the foreigners, the fatherless, and the widows inside your gates will come and eat and be satisfied. So that your Lord God may bless you for all the work your hands have done.
At the end of every seven years you must cancel all debts.

This is how the debts must be cancelled, every creditor shall cancel everything he has loaned to his neighbor or brother, and he must release them from their obligations to repay their debt, and he must not collect anything, because it is called the Lord's release from debt.
You may collect what is owed from a foreigner, but you must release your brother from his obligations to repay his debt.
There will be no poor among you, because the Lord will greatly bless you in the land that he gives you to take possession of as your inheritance.
But only if you carefully listen to your Lord God's voice and strive to observe and obey all of his commandments which I have given you today.
Because your Lord God will bless you as he promised, and you will lend to many nations, but you will not borrow, and you will govern many nations, but they will not govern you.
If you have any poverty stricken brothers living within your city gates, in the land your Lord God gives you, you must not harden your heart against them, nor refuse to help them.
But you must be generous and lend them whatever they need.

Be careful and do not let wicked thoughts enter your heart, because if you turn a blind eye to your poor brothers and loan them nothing during the seventh year of release, and he cries out to the Lord against you, it will be counted as a sin against you.
You must lend them whatever they need without complaining about it, because your Lord God will bless you in everything that you do for your generosity.
Because the poor will always be with you, so I command you to open your hand wide to the needy and your poor brothers living in your land.
And if you purchase a male or female Hebrew slave, and they serve you for six years, then you must set them free in the seventh year.
And when you set them free, do not send them away empty handed.
You must liberally give to them from your flock, your threshing floor, your winepress, and anything else your Lord God has blessed you with.
You must remember that you were once a slave in Egypt, and your Lord God rescued you, so I am ordering you to do this thing today.
But if one of your male or female servants says, "I do not want to leave," because they are happy, and they love you and your household.
Then you must take an aul and punch a hole through their ear into the door, and they will be your servant forever.

It will not seem like a hardship to you when you set them free and send them away, because their six years of service was worth twice what a hired hand would have cost, and your Lord God will bless everything you do.
You must set aside all the first-born males from your herd or flock to be sanctified to your Lord God, and you must not use your first-born bull for work, nor shear your first-born sheep.
Each year, you and your household must eat the offering before your Lord God, in the place that he chooses.
But if an animal is blemished, lame, blind, or has any other type of defect or illness, then you must not sacrifice it to your Lord God.
Both the clean and unclean people can eat it inside your gates, as if it were a gazelle or deer.
But you must not eat the blood, and you must pour it out on the ground as if it were water.
Observe the month of Abib, and celebrate your Lord God's Passover, because in the month of Abib he brought you out of Egypt by night.
So, you must sacrifice to your Lord God's Passover from your flock and herd, in the place where he chooses to place his name.

You must not eat any leavened bread with it, and you must eat the unleavened bread of affliction for seven days, because you left the land of Egypt in haste, this is so that you remember that day for all the days of your life.

And you must allow no leavened bread throughout your land for those seven days, and you must not keep any leftovers from the meat that you sacrificed in the evening of the first day, until the next morning.
You must not sacrifice the Passover animal inside the gates of your cities or towns, which your Lord God has given you.
But you must make the Passover sacrifice in the evening where your Lord God chooses to place his name, when the sun sets in the season that you came out of Egypt.
You must roast and eat it in the place that your Lord God chooses, and in the morning, you may go back to your tents.
For six days you must eat unleavened bread, and on the seventh day you must gather for a solemn assembly before your Lord God, and you must do no work in there.
Seven weeks after you first begin to harvest the wheat.
At which time you must celebrate the Feast of Weeks to your Lord God with a voluntary offering from your hand to his, in accordance with how he has blessed you.

You and your wife, son, daughter, male servants, female servants, foreigners, fatherless children, widows, or Levites living within your gates must join you in rejoicing before your Lord God, in the place that your Lord God chose to place his name.
And you must remember that you were once a slave in Egypt, and you must observe and obey these laws.
You must celebrate the Feast of Tabernacles seven days after you have harvested and threshed your wheat and pressed your wine.
You and your wife, son, daughter, male servants, female servants, foreigners, fatherless children, widows, or Levites living within your gates must rejoice in your feast.

So you must rejoice and celebrate a solemn feast to your Lord God for seven days, in the place that he chooses, because your Lord God will bless you with abundance, and everything that you do will prosper.

So three times a year, all of your men must appear before your Lord God in the place that he chooses for the Feast of Unleavened Bread, the Feast of Weeks, and the Feast of Tabernacles, but they must not show up emptyhanded.
Each man must give whatever he can according to the blessings your Lord God has given you.
You must appoint judges and officers within the gates of all the cities of each tribe your Lord God has given you. And they will judge the people with true justice.
Justice must prevail, judge and respect all people fairly, do not show partiality to anyone, do not take bribes, because a bribe blinds the eyes of the wise, and corrupts the words of the righteous.
You must pursue all that is just, so that you may live in and inherit the land your Lord God has given you.
You must build an altar to your Lord God, but do not plant any type of tree near it.
And you must not set up any type of image that your Lord God hates.
You must not sacrifice any blemished, ugly, or deformed bulls or sheep to your Lord God, because it is an abomination to him.
If a man or woman inside the city gates of the city that your Lord God gave you, has done wicked things in God's sight and transgressed against his covenant.
And they have served and worshipped other gods, or even the sun, the moon, or any of the stars in the heavens which I have forbidden.
And you have been told or heard about it, and you diligently investigate the rumor, and it turns out to be true, that such an abomination was committed in Israel.
Then you must bring the wicked man or woman who has committed such wickedness, and stone them to death at the city gates.
There must be more than one witness against the accused person, there must be at least two or three witnesses to testify of their guilt, before they can be sentenced to death.
The witnesses that testify against the accused must cast the first stones to put them to death, after that all the other people must throw their stones to remove that evil from amongst you.
If controversial matters arise among you, that are too difficult for you to judge between the truth and lies, then you must go to the place that your Lord God chose.
You must go to the Levite priest who presides over such matters at that time, and when you ask for their judgement, they will give you, their verdict.
And you must carry out the sentence that was given to you at the place the Lord chose, according to what they said.
You must carry out the laws and judgments they proclaim to you, and you must not decline to carry out the sentence they give you, and you must not waver from the left or the right.
But the arrogant man who acts overconfidently must be put to death, if he will not listen to the priest that ministers before your Lord God, or to the judge. You must purge that evil from Israel.
And the people will hear and be afraid and will no longer behave arrogantly.
When you enter and take possession of the land your Lord God will give you to settle in and you say, "Let us appoint a king, like all the other nations around us."
You must appoint the king, whom your Lord God chooses for you from among your brothers, you must not appoint a foreigner over you who is not one of your brothers.
But he must not acquire a large herd of horses for himself, nor send the people back to Egypt to buy more horses, because the Lord has said to you, "You must not return there, nor go that way again."
He must not take lots of wives for himself, otherwise his heart may go astray, and he must not accumulate lots of gold and silver.
And when he is seated on his kingdom's throne, he must write a copy of this law in a book for himself, before the Levite priests.
And he must read from it all the days of his life, so that he may learn to fear his Lord God, to keep and obey all of God's laws and his laws.

So that his heart does not think he is better than his brothers, and he does not turn to the left or the right from the commandment, so that he may prolong the days to the end for himself and his children in his kingdom within Israel.
The Levite priests and their entire tribe, shall have no inheritance with Israel, instead they will eat the Lord's burnt offerings made by fire, because that is their inheritance.
That's why they will they have no inheritance among their brothers, because the Lord is their inheritance, as he promised them.
The priests will collect what they are due from the people that offer sacrifices, and when an ox or a sheep is offered, the priest must be given the shoulder, the two cheeks, and the stomach.
You must also give them the first harvest of your wheat, your new wine, your oil, and the first fleece from your sheared sheep.
Because your Lord God has chosen them and their sons from all of your tribes, to stand and minister in the name of the Lord, forever.
If any Levite, no matter where they come from in Israel, earnestly desires to come to the place which the Lord has chosen.
Then he will be allowed to stand before his Lord God, and minister in his name, as all the other Levites do.
They shall be given an equal portion to eat, even if they have received money from the sale of their father's estate.
When you enter the land your Lord God has given you, you must not learn to do the abominable things that they do in those nations.
None of you are allowed to sacrifice you son or daughter in a fire, or use divination or practice witchcraft, and they must not become soothsayers or sorcerers.
Or warlocks, spirit guides, wizards, or necromancers.
Because everyone that does these things are an abomination to the Lord, and your Lord God drives them out from before you, because they are an abomination.
You must be perfect before your Lord God.
Because the nations you will possess, listened to their spirit guides and diviners, but as for you, your Lord God has not allowed you to do this.
Your Lord God will raise up a prophet like me from among your brothers, and you must listen to everything he says to you

This is what you desired from your Lord God in Horeb on the day you were all assembled when you said, "Do not let me hear my Lord God's voice, nor let me see this great fire anymore, so that I will not die."
And the Lord said to me, "They have spoken well.
I will raise up a prophet from among their brothers like you, and I will put my words in his mouth, and he will tell them everything that I will command him.
And I will deal sternly with anyone who does not listen to what I tell the prophet to say in my name.
But any prophet, who delivers a message in my name which I have not commanded him to speak, or he speaks in the name of other gods will die.
And if you say in your heart, 'How will we know if the prophets word comes from the Lord?'

When a prophet speaks in the name of the Lord, if the things they say do not come to pass or come true, that is a message that the Lord has not spoken, but the prophet has spoken overconfidently, and do not be afraid of him."
When your Lord God cuts off the nations and gives you their land, and you drive them out and live in their cities and houses.
You shall separate three cities for yourselves in the middle of your land, which your LORD God gives you to possess.
You shall build roads and divide your land into three parts, where a murderer may flee to those cities, which your LORD God has given you as an inheritance.
And this is how to handle the case of a murderer, who flees there to live: Whoever ignorantly kills his neighbor, whom he had not hated in the past;

Such as when someone has an accident, when they go out into the woods with a neighbor to chop firewood. If they swing the axe to cut down a tree, and the head slips off the handle, and hits the neighbor in the head and kills them, then they can flee to one of the sanctuary cities and live there safely.

Otherwise, a vengeful accuser may pursue the murderer and overtake them along the way with a heart full of rage and kill an innocent person who did not intentionally kill or hate the victim. And the fugitive who did not deserve to die, was killed because it was such a long way to the sanctuary cities.
That's why I gave you this command and said, "You must set three cities aside for yourselves."
And if your Lord God enlarges your borders, as he promised your fathers he would, and he gives you all the land he promised to give your fathers.
If you keep and obey all the commandments I have given you today, to love your Lord God and walk in his ways forever, then you will need three more sanctuary cities in addition to these three.
So that innocent blood is not shed in your land that your Lord God has given you as an inheritance, and you will not be guilty of spilling their blood.
But if someone hates their neighbor, and lies in wait for them, attacks, mortally wounds, and kills them, and they flee to one of these cities.
Then the city elders must send for him and deliver him into the hands of the vengeful accuser, so that he may be put to death.
You must not have pity on them, but you must purge the guilt of shedding innocent blood from Israel, so that all may go well for you.
You must not move nor remove your neighbor's border markers, which were set up by your ancestors to mark the borders of the land that your Lord God has given you as an inheritance.

One witness is not enough to convict a person of any immorality or sin, but it will require two or more witnesses to convict someone of any immorality or sin, before guilt is established beyond a shadow of doubt.
If a false witness testifies against someone and accuses them of wrongdoing.
Then both parties will stand before the Lord, the priests, and the judges who are serving at that time to hear the controversy between the two.
And the judges will diligently investigate, and if there is a false witness, who has testified falsely against his brother.
Then you must do to him, what he wanted to do to his brother, so that you can purge the evil from among you.
And the rest of the people will hear and be afraid, and they will never commit such an evil act among you again.
And you must not show any pity, but you must demand a life for a life, an eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth, a hand for a hand, and a foot for a foot.

When you go out to do battle against your enemies, and you see horses, chariots, and an army larger than yours, do not be afraid of them, because your Lord God, who brought you out of Egypt is with you.
And when you are near enough to join the battle, then the priest will approach and speak to the people.

And the priest will say to them, "O Israel hear this, today you approach to do battle against your enemies, do not let your hearts be faint, fear not, and do not tremble, nor should you be terrified of them.
For your Lord God goes to fight your enemies for you in order to save your life."

And the officers are to speak to the people and say, "Have any of you built a new house, and not dedicated it to the Lord? If so, return home, otherwise you may die in battle, and another man will dedicate your home.
If any of you have planted a vineyard, and not eaten from it then return home, otherwise you may die in battle, and another man will eat your crops.
If any of you have proposed marriage to a wife and not married her, then return home, otherwise you may die in battle, and another man will marry her."
Then the officers are to speak to the people again and say, "If you are fearful or frightened, return home, otherwise you may frighten your brother in arms, and he will be as afraid as you."
When the officers have finished speaking to the people, they must appoint captains to lead the people's army.
When you approach a city ready to fight, you must first offer them a peaceful settlement.
If their answer is peace, and they open their gates to you, then everyone there will be your slaves, and they will serve you.
But if they refuse to make peace with you, and decide to wage war with you, then you must lay siege to their city.
When your Lord God has delivered them into your hands, you must kill every male there with a sword.
But you can take the spoils of war for yourself, including the women, children, cattle, and everything else in the city, and you will eat from the enemies' spoils, that your Lord God has given you.
This is how you must deal with the cities that are a long way from you, that are not part of the cities in your neighboring nations.
But when it comes to the cities that your Lord God has given you as an inheritance, do not leave anything alive that breathes.
But destroy them completely, especially the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and the Jebusites, as your Lord God has commanded you.
So that they do not teach you to chase after their abominations and worship their gods. For this will cause you to sin against your Lord God.

When you lay siege to a city for a long time while making war against them, you must not chop down and destroy the trees there because you can eat their fruit and the trees are not human, and they can be used in the siege.
But you may cut down any trees that do not produce fruit, because they can be used to build bulwarks to defeat the besieged city, until it is subdued.
If you find a dead person lying out in the field that your Lord God has given you, and you do not know who killed them.
Then your elders and judges must come and measure the distance from the victim to the cities all around where the victim was found.
And the elders from the city nearest to the dead person, must take a heifer that has never been worked or yoked.
And they must bring that heifer down into a rough valley, that has neither been plowed nor sown and break its neck there in the valley.

And Levi's sons the priests must come, because they have been chosen by your Lord God to minister to him, and to bless in his name, and to settle every controversy and every case of assault to be tried,
And all the elders from the city next to the where the dead man was found, must wash their hands over the heifer that was beheaded in the valley.
And they will answer and say, "Our hands have not shed this blood, and we have not seen who has done this.
O Lord, be merciful to your people whom you have redeemed in Israel, and do not hold them responsible for shedding this innocent blood." And the bloodshed will be forgiven.
So the guilt of shedding innocent blood shall be purged from among you, when you do what is right in the Lord's sight.
When you go out to wage war against your enemies, and your Lord God delivers them into your hands, and you take them captive.
If you see a beautiful woman among the captives, and you desire her so much that you want to make her your wife.
Then you must bring her home to your home, and she must shave her head and trim her nails.

She must put aside the clothes she wore in her captivity. After she has lived in your house for a full month and mourned her father and mother, then you may go to her and become her husband, and she will be your wife.
And if she does not delight you, then you must let her go, but you must not sell her for money, nor shall you make merchandise of her, because you have humbled her.
If a man has two wives, and he loves one but hates the other, and they have both given birth to his children, and the firstborn son was born to the one that was hated.

When the man prepares his sons' inheritance from what he owns, he must not put the firstborn son from the wife that he loves before the son of the wife that he hates. Because the son from the wife that he hates is indeed his firstborn son.

But he must acknowledge the firstborn son from the wife that he hates, by giving him a double portion of everything that he owns. Because that son is the beginning of his father's strength, and the right of the firstborn belongs to him.
If a man has a stubborn and rebellious son, who will not obey the voice of his father or mother, and he will not listen to them when they chasten him.
Then his father and mother must take him to the city elders' courtroom.
And they will tell the city elders that their son is stubborn and rebellious, and he will not obey them, and he is a glutton and a drunk.
Then all the men in the city must come and stone him to death. This is how you will purge evil from among you, and all of Israel will hear about it and be afraid.
If someone has committed a sin worthy of death, and they are to be put to death, and you hang them on a tree.

Their body must not remain hanging on the tree all night, but you must bury them that day, because anyone hanged on a tree is cursed by God'. This is so that the land which your Lord God has given you as an inheritance, is not defiled.
If you see someone's ox or sheep running loose, you must not ignore it, but you must bring it back to its owner.
And if they do not live near you, or you do not know who owns it, then you must bring it home with you, and keep it until its owner comes looking for it, and you can return it to them at that time.
You must do the same thing with their donkey, or their clothes, or anything else they may have lost that you have found, you must not just ignore it.
If you see your brother's donkey or ox has fallen by the wayside, do not just ignore it, you must surely help him lift it up.
Women must not wear men's clothes, and men must not wear women's clothes, because this is an abomination to your Lord God.
If you find a bird's nest with chicks or eggs in a tree or on the ground along the road, and the mother hen is sitting on them, you must not take the hen with the young.
You may take the young, but not the hen, so that everything goes well for you, and you may prolong your life.
When you build a new house, make sure you build a guardrail around your roof, so that you are not held responsible of causing their death if someone falls from the roof of your house.
You must not sow your vineyard with different varieties of seed, otherwise the fruit of your vineyard will be defiled.
You must not hitch an ox and a donkey together to plow.
You must not wear clothes with different types of wool and linen mixed together.
You must make tassels for the four corners of the cloak you wear.
If a man marries a wife and he grows to hate her.
And he begins to complain against and accuse her of doing bad things and he says, "I married this woman and I have since discovered that she was not a virgin."
Then the young woman's father and mother must bring proof of her virginity to the city elders.
And her father will say to the elders, "I gave my daughter to this man as his wife, and he hates her.

And he has been complaining against her and he said, 'I discovered that your daughter is not a virgin,' but here is proof of my daughter's virginity," and they will spread the cloth before the city elders.
Then the city elders must chastise the man.

And they must fine him a hundred silver shekels, and give them to the young woman's father, because her husband has put an evil name on one of Israel's virgins. She will remain his wife, and he will not be allowed to divorce her for the rest of his life.
But if it turns out to be true, and no proof of her virginity can be found.

Then they must bring the young woman to the door of her father's house, and the men from her city will stone her to death, because she has been promiscuous in her father's house, and you must purge the evil from among you.
If a man is discovered to be having sexual relations with a woman married to another man, then both of them must be put to death, because you must purge this evil from Israel.
If a young virgin woman has been promised in marriage to a husband, and another man finds her in the city, and has sexual relations with her.

Then you must bring both of them to the city gates, and stone them to death. The young woman because she did not cry out in the city, and the man because he violated his neighbor's wife, and you must purge this evil from among you.
But if a man finds an engaged young woman out in the fields, and he forces himself on her and has sexual relations with her, then only the man must be put to death.
You must not do anything to the young woman, because she has not committed a sin that is worthy of death, this should be treated just like when a man attacks and kills his neighbor.
Because he attacked her in the field, and the engaged girl cried out but no one was there to help her.
If a man meets a young unengaged virgin woman, and they lie together and have sexual relations, and they are discovered.
Then the man that had sexual relations with her must give her father fifty silver shekels, and she will be his wife, because he has violated her, and he cannot divorce her for his entire life.
A man must not marry his father's wife, so that he does not dishonor his father.
If a man who has damaged genitals or he has been castrated, he is not allowed to enter the Lord's sanctuary.
Bastards even to the tenth generation of their descendants, are not allowed to enter the Lord's sanctuary.
No Ammonites or Moabites even to the tenth generation of their descendants, are allowed to enter the Lord's sanctuary.
Because they did not meet you with bread and water along the road when you left Egypt, and because they hired Balaam son of Beor of Pethor from Mesopotamia to curse you.
But your Lord God would not listen to Balaam, and he turned the curse into a blessing, because he loved you.
You must not seek peace nor prosperity from them for as long as you live forever.
You must not despise an Edomite, because they are your brothers, nor should you despise Egyptians, because you were a stranger in their land.
Their descendants will be allowed to enter the Lord's sanctuary in their third generation.
When you send your army to war against your enemies, stay away from everything wicked.
If any man among you becomes unclean for any reason during the night, then he must leave the camp, and stay outside the camp.
But in evening after he bathes with clean water, he will be allowed to return to the camp when the sun goes down.
When you are required to leave camp, you must have a place outside the camp to stay.
You must have a shovel built into your weapon, so you can dig a hole where you can bury your excrement when you relieve yourself.
Because your Lord God walks throughout your camp to deliver you from your enemies. Your camp must be kept holy, so that he does not see your uncleanliness, and turn away from you.
You must not return a servant who has escaped to their master if they have taken refuge with you.
You must allow them to live with you, wherever they choose within your gates, and you must not oppress them.
You must not allow any of Israel's sons or daughters to become whores or homosexual prostitutes.
You must not bring money earned by a whore, or proceeds from the sale of a dog, into your Lord God's house to fulfill any promises. Because they are both an abomination to your Lord God.
You must not charge interest for anything that you lend, including money, food, or anything else that you lend.

If you lend to a foreigner, you may charge interest, but if you lend to your brother, you must not charge interest. So that your Lord God may bless you in everything that you put your hand to, in the land that he gave you to possess.
When you make a promise to your Lord God, you must not delay in fulfilling it. For your Lord God will surely require it from you if you do, and you will be guilty of a sin.
But if you refrain from making promises, you will not be guilty of a sin.
You must do whatever you said you would do, even if it is a voluntary offering, because whatever you promised the Lord, must be fulfilled.
Whenever you enter your neighbor's vineyard, you may eat your fill of their grapes, but do not put any in your basket.
When you enter your neighbor's field of standing wheat, you may pick some of the grain heads with your hands, but do not use a sickle to harvest their wheat.

When a man marries a woman, but he is not happy with her, because he has found something unclean about her. He may divorce her by writing and giving her divorce papers and sending her out of his house.
When she leaves his house, she may go and become another man's wife.
And if her new husband hates her and divorces her by writing and giving her divorce papers, and sending her out of his house, or he dies after he took her to be his wife.

Then her former husband who divorced her, may not remarry her because she has been defiled, and it is abomination to the Lord. You must not cause any sin to come upon the land that your Lord God has given you as an inheritance.

When a man takes a new wife, he must not be sent away to war nor forced to perform other duties for the army. He will be allowed to remain free to stay home with his new wife for one year, to bring her happiness.
Do not take millstones as the security pledge for a debt, because if it is not repaid and it must be taken as payment for the debt, the debtor will lose his ability to earn a living.
If a man is caught kidnapping one of his Israelis brothers, and sells him as a slave, then the thief must be put to death, because you must purge this evil from among you.
Beware of leprosy, you must carefully observe and obey everything that the Levite priests teach you, make sure you do what I have commanded them to do.
Remember what your Lord God did to Miriam by the side of the road, when you left Egypt.
When you lend anything to your brother, you must not enter his house to retrieve his security pledge.
You must stand outside his house and wait for him to bring his security pledge to you.
And if he is a poor man, you must not sleep with his security pledge in your possession.
You must return his pledge to him before the sun goes down, so that he may sleep in his own clothes and bless you, and you will be righteous before your Lord God.
You must not oppress any poor or needy hired servants, whether they are one of your brothers or a foreigner living in your land within your city gates.
You must give them their pay when it is due before the sun goes down, because they are poor and they need it. Otherwise, they may cry out to the Lord against you, and it will be a sin on you.
The fathers must not be put to death for the sins of the children, nor shall the children be put to death for the father's sin, everyone will be put to death for their own sin.
You must not pervert the judgment of a foreigner nor the fatherless, and you must not take a widow's clothes as a security pledge.
Remember, you were once a slave in Egypt, and your Lord God rescued you from there, so I command you to do this thing.

When you harvest your fields, and you see that you have forgotten to cut a sheaf, do not go and cut it, but leave it for a foreigner, the fatherless, or a widow, so that your Lord God may bless all the work of your hands.
When you harvest the olives from your trees, do not go through them more than once, but leave whatever is left for a foreigner, the fatherless, or a widow.
When you gather the grapes from your vineyard, do not glean it afterward, but leave whatever is left for a foreigner, the fatherless, or a widow.
Remember you were once a slave in Egypt. Therefore, I command you to do this thing.
If there is a dispute between men, they must go to court where the judges can judge them, to justify the righteous and condemn the wicked.
And if a wicked person deserves to be beaten, the judge will order them to lie down, to be flogged before him. The number of lashes he receives will depend on his offense.
The guilty party must receive no more than forty lashes, and if they are given more than forty lashes, they will be shamed and humiliated before you.
You must not muzzle an ox while it is treading the wheat.
If brothers live together and one of them dies childless, the dead brother's wife must not marry outside the family. Her husband's brother must marry her and fulfill his duty as her brother-in-law.
And their firstborn son will be given the dead brother's name, so that his name will not be forgotten in Israel.

If the man does not like his brother's wife and refuses to marry her, then she can go to the city elders at the gate and say, "My husband's brother refuses to stand up for his brother's name in Israel, and he will not fulfill the duties of a brother-in-law."
Then the city elders will speak to him, and if he stands by his decision and says, "I do not like her, and I do not want to marry her."
Then his brother's wife must come to him in the presence of the elders, and remove his shoe from his foot, spit in his face and say, "So be it, this man will not build up his brother's house."
And the name of his house in Israel will be known as "The House of Someone with No Shoe."
When two men are fighting with one another, and one of their wives reaches out to help her husband, and she grabs hold of the other man's genitals.
Then you must cut off her hand and have no pity for her.
You must not use different measures, such as one big and one small for the contents of your bags.
You must not use different measures, such as one big and one small in your house.
But you must use perfect, honest, and just weights and measures, so that your days may be lengthened in the land your Lord God has given you.
Because anyone who deals dishonestly and does unrighteousness things, is an abomination to your Lord God.
Remember what Amalek did to you by the roadside, as you left Egypt.
How he met you along the road when you were faint and weary and defeated you, and attacked all the stragglers following behind you, and he did not fear God.
When your Lord God gives you rest from the enemies all around you, in the land which he has given you as an inheritance, you must erase Amalek's memory from under heaven. Do not forget!
When you enter, take possession of and live in the land which your Lord God has given you as an inheritance.

You must take some of the earth's first fruit you have harvested from the land that your Lord God has given you and place it in your basket. Then carry it to the place that your Lord God has chosen to place his name.
Then go to the current priest there and say to him, "I profess this day to your Lord God, that I have come to the country which he promised to give to our fathers for us."
The priest will take your basket and place it before your Lord God's altar.
You must speak to your Lord God and say, "My father was a wandering Syrian about to die, and he went down to Egypt with just a few people, and became a great, mighty, and very crowded nation.
And the evil Egyptians afflicted us, and treated us with evil, and forced us into hardship and slavery.
And when we cried to the Lord God of our fathers, he heard our voice, and he looked and saw our affliction, labor, and oppression.
And the Lord brought us out of Egypt with a mighty hand and outstretched arm, with great terror, signs, and wonders.
He brought us here and gave us this land, a land flowing with milk and honey.
O Lord, now I have brought the first fruits from the land which you have given me," then you must place it before your Lord God and worship him.
So, you must rejoice over every good thing which your Lord God has given you, your house, the Levite, and the foreigner living among you.

After you have finished preparing all of your tithes from the third year during the year of tithing, and you have given it to the Levite, the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow so that they may eat their fill inside of your gates.

Then you must say before your Lord God, "I have brought the holy things from my home, and I have given them to the Levite, the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow, just as you commanded me, and I have not transgressed nor forgotten your commandments.

I have not eaten from the sacred portion while I was in mourning, nor have I used any of it while unclean, and I have not offered any of it for the dead. I have listened to my Lord God's voice, and I have done everything just as you commanded me.
Look down from your holy home in heaven and bless your people of Israel, and the land which you have given us. For it is just as you promised our fathers, a land flowing with milk and honey."
Your Lord God has commanded you to obey these laws and judgments today, so you must keep and obey them with all your heart and soul.
Today you have proclaimed that the Lord is your God, and that you will walk in his ways and keep and obey his laws, commandments, and judgments, and to listen to his voice.
And the Lord has proclaimed to you today that you are his treasured people as he promised, and that you should keep all of his commandments.
And he will raise you up in praise, name, and honor high above all the nations which he created, so that you may be your Lord God's holy people, just as he promised.
Moses and the Israeli elders gave their commandments to the people and said, "You must keep all of the commandments I am giving you today.
On the day you cross the Jordan River and enter the land your Lord God has given you, you must erect large stones and cover them with plaster.

After you have crossed the Jordan River, you must write down all of these laws on those stones, as soon as you arrive in the land your Lord God has given you. For it is a land flowing with milk and honey, just as the Lord God of your fathers promised you.
So today I give you this command, when you cross the Jordan River you must erect these stones on Mount Ebal, and cover them with plaster.
Furthermore, you must build a stone altar to your Lord God there, but you must not use any iron tools on them.
You must build your Lord God's altar with uncut stones, then you must offer burnt offerings on it to your Lord God.
You must offer peace offerings there and eat them and rejoice before your Lord God.
And you must clearly write all of these laws on the stones."
Then Moses and the Levite priests spoke to all of Israel and said, "O Israel, take heed and listen; on this day you have become your Lord God's people.
So, you must obey your Lord God's voice, and all of his commandments and laws which I have given you today."
That same day Moses charged the people and said,
"After you have crossed the Jordan River, these leaders will stand on Mount Gerizim to bless the people; Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph, and Benjamin.
And these leaders will stand on Mount Ebal to pronounce the curse; Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan, and Naphtali.
Then the Levites will speak to all of the Israelis in a loud voice and say,
'Cursed is the man who makes carved idols or molten images, it is an abomination to the Lord for the craftsman who makes one and hides it in a secret place. Let everyone say, Amen!
Cursed is he who dishonors his father or mother. Let everyone say, Amen!
Cursed is he who moves or removes his neighbor's boundary marker. Let everyone say, Amen!
Cursed is he who lets a blind person wander around out in the road. Let everyone say, Amen!
Cursed is he who perverts the judgment of the foreigner, the fatherless, and widows. Let everyone say, Amen!
Cursed is he who has sexual relations with his father's wife, because he has defiled his father's bed. Let everyone say, Amen!
Cursed is he who has sexual relations with any type of beast. Let everyone say, Amen!
Cursed is he who has sexual relations with his sister, his father or mother's daughter. Let everyone say, Amen!
Cursed is he who has sexual relations with his mother-in-law. Let everyone say, Amen!
Cursed is he who secretly murders his neighbor. Let everyone say, Amen!
Cursed is he who accepts payment for killing an innocent person. Let everyone say, Amen!
Cursed is he who does not continue to do all things written in the Book of the Law. Let everyone say, Amen!'"

If you faithfully listen to the voice of your Lord God, and you observe and keep all of his commandments I have given you today, then your Lord God will set you high above all the other nations on earth.
All of these blessings will come upon you and overtake you, if you listen to your Lord God's voice.
You will be blessed in the city and blessed in the field.
You will be blessed in the fruit of your womb, the fruit of your ground, the fruit of your cattle, the increase in the number of your cows, and your sheep flocks.
You will be blessed in your basket and in your storehouse.
You will be blessed when you come in and when you go out.
Your Lord God will cause any enemies who rise up against you to be defeated, they will come out united against you and flee before you in seven different ways.
Your Lord God will command the blessings to come upon you in your storehouses, and everything that you set your hand will prosper. And God will bless you in the land which he has given you.
Your Lord God will establish you as his holy people as he promised you, if you keep his commandments, and walk in his ways.
And all people of the earth will see that you are called in the name of the Lord, and they will be afraid of you.
Your Lord God will make you abundantly prosperous in the fruit of your womb, your cattle's offspring, and the fruit of your land, in the land that God promised to give your fathers.

Your Lord God will open the storehouse of his heavens for you; he will give you good rain in the growing season and bless everything that you do. You will lend to many nations, but you will not borrow.

Your Lord God will make you the head, not the tail, and you shall only be above. You will only move upward and never downward, if you listen to, observe, and obey all of God's commandments that I have given you today.
And you must not turn away to the left or the right from any of the words I have given you today, nor chase after other gods to serve them.
But, if you do not listen to your Lord God's voice and observe and obey all of his commandments and laws I have given you today, then all of these curses will come upon you and overtake you.
You will be cursed in the city and cursed in the field.
You will be cursed in your basket and in your storehouse.
The fruit of your body will be cursed, as well as the fruit of your land, the increase in your number of cows, and your flocks of sheep.
You will be cursed when you come in and when you go out.

And the Lord will send curses upon you, with frustration and reprimand in everything that you do until you are destroyed and you quickly perish, because of the wickedness you committed when you abandoned him.
The Lord will make pestilences cling to you, until you have been consumed and removed from the land that you go to take possession of.

The Lord will strike you down with disease, fever, inflammation, extreme burning, and the sword. Your crops will be destroyed by drought, blight, and mildew, and these things will pursue you until you perish.
The heavens above your head will be like brass, and the earth beneath your feet will be like iron.
The Lord will turn the rain from heaven into powder and dust, and it will come down on you, until you are destroyed.

The Lord will cause you to be defeated before your enemies. You will unite to attack them and flee in seven different directions before them. Then you will be scattered into all the kingdoms on the earth.
And your carcass will be meat for the birds and beasts of the earth, and nobody will chase them away.
The Lord will defeat you with Egyptian boils, hemorrhoids, scabies, and the itch that cannot be healed.
The Lord will defeat you with madness, blindness, and an astonished heart.
At noon you will grope around like a blind man in the dark. Your ways will not prosper, you will only be persecuted and deceived forever, and no one will come to save you.
You will marry a wife, and another man will have sexual relations with her. You will build a house, BUT you will not live there. You will plant a vineyard, but you will not gather its grapes.

Your ox will be killed right before your eyes, but you will not eat from it. Your donkey will be violently stolen from you, and it will not be returned. Your sheep will be given to your enemies, and nobody will help you rescue them.
Your sons and daughters will be given to other people, and your eyes will look for them all day long, but you will not find them and there will be nothing you can do about it.
A foreign nation will consume your crops and everything else you produce, and you will only be persecuted and oppressed.
You will be driven mad and insane by everything you see.
The Lord will cause great pain in your knees and your legs, and he will give you sore boils that cannot be healed, from the soles of your feet to the top of your head.
The Lord will exile you and your chosen king to a foreign nation which you and your fathers have never known. And there you will serve their strange gods of wood and stone.
And you will become an astonishment, a proverb, and an example, among all nations where the Lord leads you.
You will carry much seed out into the field, but harvest very little, because the locust will consume it.
You will plant vineyards and dress them, but you will neither drink the wine, nor gather the grapes, because the worms will eat them.
You will have olive trees throughout your land, but you will never anoint yourself with the oil, because your olive trees will drop their fruit on the ground.
You will father sons and daughters, but you will not enjoy them, because they will be taken into captivity.
All your trees and the fruit of your land will be consumed by locusts.
The foreigner living among you will rise high above you, and you will sink very low.
They will lend to you, but you will not lend to them, they will be the head, and you will be the tail.

All of these curses will come on you, pursue you, and overtake you until you have been destroyed. For you did not listen to your Lord God's voice, or keep his laws and commandments which he commanded you to obey.
And they will be a curse on you and your descendants, as a sign and wonder forever.
Because you did not serve your Lord God with a joyful and happy heart, for the abundance of all things.
So you will serve the enemies your Lord will send against you, in hunger, thirst, nakedness, and lacking everything. For God will put an iron yoke around your neck until he has destroyed you.
The Lord will bring a nation whose language you do not understand against you from the far ends of the earth, as swift as the eagle flies.
A ruthless fierce appearing nation, with no regard for old people, and they will show favor to the young.

They will eat your cattle and the fruit of your land, until you have been destroyed. They will leave you no wheat, wine, oil, or increase in calves from your cows, or lambs from your flocks, until they have destroyed you.
They will lay siege to your city gates, until all of your trusted, high, and fenced walls come tumbling down throughout the entire land your Lord God has given you.
And in the siege and distress your enemies inflict upon you, you will eat the fruit of your own womb, and the flesh of the sons and daughters your Lord God has given you.
So that the most gentle and tender man among you, will look toward his brother, his wife, and the rest of his surviving children, with evil in his eyes.
He will not share the flesh of his children he plans to eat with any of them. Because he will have nothing left in him from the siege and the distress, that your enemies will inflict on you.

And the tender and delicate woman among you, who are so gentle and tender they would not venture to set the soles of their feet on the ground, will look toward their husbands, sons, and daughters with evil in their eye.
And she will secretly eat the afterbirth and her children because of a lack of anything else to eat in the siege and distress, that your enemy will inflict upon you within the gates of your city.
If you do not observe and obey all of his laws that are written in this book, so that you may fear his glorious and fearful name, the Lord your God.
Then the Lord will make even greater, longer lasting plagues for you and your descendants. Miserable plagues which are severe, sore, and long-lasting chronic sicknesses.
God will afflict you with all the diseases that you feared in Egypt, and they will cling to you.
The Lord will also bring every sickness and plague upon you not written in the laws of this book, until you have been destroyed.
And you who were once as numerous as the stars of heaven will have your numbers depleted, because you would not obey your Lord God's voice.

And as the Lord once rejoiced over you and did good things for you and multiplied your numbers, he will rejoice over destroying you and bring you down to nothing. Then you will be removed from the land that you went to possess.
The Lord will scatter you among all the people, from one end of the earth to the other, and you will serve other wood and stone gods there that you nor your fathers have ever known.
And among those nations you will find no rest, not even a place to rest your feet, but the Lord will give you a trembling heart there, with failing eyes, and a sorrowful mind.
And your life will hang in doubt before you, and you will be afraid night and day, and you will have no assurance of your life.

In the morning you will say, "God I wish it was evening!" and in the evening you will say, "God it I wish it was morning!" Because of the fear in your heart, and the terrifying things you will see with your eyes.

And the Lord will bring you back to Egypt in ships, by a route that I told you that you would never have to travel again, and you will be offered for sale to your enemies as slaves, but nobody will buy you.
This is the covenant that contains the agreement the Lord commanded Moses to make with the Israelis in the land of Moab, in addition to the covenant he made with them in Horeb.
And Moses assembled all of Israel together and said, "You have seen everything that the Lord did to Pharaoh before your eyes in Egypt, and to all of his servants and his entire land.
And your eyes have seen the temptations, signs, and those great miracles.
Yet to this day, the Lord has not given you an understanding heart, eyes to see, or ears to hear.
I led you through the wilderness for forty years and during that time the clothes you wear, and the shoes on your feet did not grow old.
You have eaten no bread and drank no wine or strong drink, so that you might know that I am your Lord God.
And when you came to this place, King Sihon of Heshbon and King Og of Bashan, came out against us to do battle, and we defeated them.
We took their land and gave it to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half tribe of Manasseh as their inheritance.
So you must keep and obey everything this covenant says, in order for you to prosper in everything that you do.
Today all of you stand before your Lord God; your leaders, your elders, your officers, and all the men of Israel.
Plus your children, your wives, and any foreigners living in your camp, from your wood carvers to the people who draw your water.
So that you can enter into a covenant with your Lord God, with the promises that he makes with you today.
In order for him to establish you as his people today, so that he may be your God as he promised you and your fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
And I am not only making this covenant and this oath with you.
But with everyone who stands here with us before our Lord God, and anyone that is not here with us today.
Because you know how we lived in Egypt, and how we passed through the other nations on our way to this place.
And you have seen their abominations, including the wood, stone, silver, and gold idols, that they worshipped.

Otherwise a man, woman, family, or tribe among you, whose heart turns away from our Lord God, may go to serve the gods of other nations. Which will cause a root that bears gall and wormwood to rise up among you.
And when they hear this curse, they will bless themselves in their heart and say, 'I will have peace, even though I walk in the imagination of my heart.' This is what adds drunkenness to thirst.
The Lord will not spare them, but his anger and jealousy will burn against them, and all the curses that are written in this book will come upon them, and he will erase their name from under heaven.
And the Lord will separate him and his evil ways from all the tribes of Israel, in accordance with all the curses of the covenant written in this Book of the Law.
So that the generations to come that rise up after you, and the foreigners that come from a far-off land, see the plagues of the land and the sicknesses the Lord has inflicted on it.

And the whole land will be like burning salt and brimstone, unsown and unproductive, where no grass grows. Just like the destruction of Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboim which the Lord destroyed in his fierce anger.
And all the nations will ask, 'Why has the Lord done these things to this land? What caused his outburst of great burning anger?'
Then men will say, 'It is because they abandoned the covenant of the Lord God of their fathers, that he made with them when he brought them out of Egypt.
Because they served and worshipped other gods whom they did not know, gods that the Lord had not have given them.
Therefore, the Lord's anger was kindled against this land, which brought all the curses on it that are written in this book.
And in anger with great indignation the Lord rooted them out of their land, and threw them into another land, and that's how it is to this day.'
The secret things belong to our Lord God, but those things which are revealed belong to us and our children forever, so that we may keep all the words in his law."

And Moses spoke to the people as they stood on the plains of Moab and said, "When these things happen to you among all the nations where your Lord God has driven you, you will remember all the blessings and curses I have set before you.
When you and your children return to your Lord God with all your heart and soul, and you obey his voice in accordance with everything I am telling you on this day.
Then your Lord God will save you from your captivity, and he will have compassion on you and bring you back together from all the nations where he scattered you.
Even if you have been driven to the farthest parts under heaven, your Lord God will gather you and bring you back together from there.
And your Lord God will bring you into the land your fathers possessed, and you will take possession of it. Then God will do only good for you, and you will be multiplied more than your fathers.
And your Lord God will circumcise your heart and the hearts of your descendants, to love your Lord God with all your heart, and with all your soul, so that you may live.
And your Lord God will put all of these curses on your enemies, and on those who hate and persecute you.
And you will return and obey the Lord's voice and commandments and do everything that I have commanded you to do today.

And your Lord God will make everything you do abundantly prosperous, including the works of your hands, the fruit of your womb, the fruit of your cattle, and the fruit of your land for good. For the Lord will rejoice over you for good, just as he rejoiced over your fathers.
If you listen to your Lord God's voice and keep all of his laws and commandments written in the Book of the Law, and you return to him with all of your heart, mind, and soul.
For this commandment I give you today is not hidden from you, nor is it far away.
For it is not in heaven that you should ask, 'Who will ascend into heaven and retrieve it for us, so that we may hear and obey?'
And it is not beyond the sea that you should ask, 'Who will sail across the sea and retrieve it for us, so that we may hear and obey?'
But the word is very near to you, it is in your mouth and in your heart, so that you may listen and obey.
Behold, I have shown you everything about life today including the good, the evil, and death.

For today I give you this commandment 'You shall love your Lord God, walk in his ways, and keep all of his laws, commandments, and judgments,' so that you may live and multiply abundantly, and your Lord God will bless you in the land you are going to take possession of.
But if your heart turns away from him, and you refuse to hear him, but you are lured away from him, and you worship and serve other gods.
I will denounce you today, and you will surely perish, and your days will not be prolonged on the land, when you cross the Jordan River to take possession of it.

I will call heaven and earth to record this day against you, because I have shown you the difference between life and death, blessing and curse. Therefore, you should choose life, so that both you and your descendants may live.

So that you may love your Lord God and obey his voice and cling loyally to him. For the Lord is your life, and he increases your number of days in the land he promised to give to your fathers Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob."
Moses went and spoke to all of Israel.
And he said to them, "I am 120 years old today, I can no longer come and go as I please, and the Lord has said to me, 'You will not cross the Jordan River.'
Your Lord God will cross ahead of you and destroy these nations before you, and you will take possession of their land. Joshua will cross ahead of you, as the Lord said.
And the Lord will treat them as he did Sihon and Og the Amorite kings, when he destroyed their land.
And the Lord will deliver them to you, so that you may do everything to them exactly as I have ordered you.
Be strong and courageous, fear not, nor be afraid of them, because your Lord God, goes with you, he will not fail you, nor forsake you."

Then Moses called for Joshua in front of all of Israel and said, "Be strong and courageous, for you must go with these people to the land the Lord has promised to give their fathers, and you must give it to them as their inheritance.
And the Lord will go before you, he will be with you, and he will not fail you nor will he forsake you, so fear not and do not be dismayed."
So Moses wrote down this law and delivered it to the Israelis elders, and Levi's sons the priests, who carried the Lord's Ark of the Covenant.
And Moses gave them another commandment and said, "At the end of every seven years, in the year of solemn debt release, during the Feast of Tabernacles.
When all of Israel comes to appear before your Lord God in the place that he chose, you must read this law before all of Israel where they can hear it.

Gather all the people together including the men, women, children and any foreigners within your gates, so that they may hear, learn, and fear your Lord God. So that they may listen, observe, and obey everything that his laws say.
Then their children who have known nothing, may hear and learn to fear your Lord God, as long as you live in the land you are crossing the Jordan River to take possession of."
