And the Lord spoke to Moses and said, "Behold the day of your death approaches. Summon Joshua and present yourselves in the congregation's tabernacle, so that I may transfer your responsibilities to him." Then Moses and Joshua presented themselves in the congregation's tabernacle.
The Lord appeared as a column of cloud in the tabernacle, and the column of cloud stood over the tabernacle door.

And the Lord spoke to Moses and said, "Behold you will sleep with your fathers, and these people will rise up, and they will go whoring after the foreign gods in the strange land they are entering. They will forsake me and break the covenant I have made with them.

Then my anger will be kindled against them in those days, and I will forsake them, and I will hide my face from them. They will be devoured and many evils and troubles will happen to them, that will cause them to say, 'Our God is not among us, have not these evils come upon us because of this?'
And I will surely hide my face in those days, because of everything evil work they have been involved in, when they turned to other gods.
So write this song, and teach it to Israel's descendants, let them sing out, so that this song may be a witness for me against all of Israel.

After I have brought them into the land that I swore to give their fathers, a land flowing with milk and honey. But after they have eaten their fill and grown fat, they will turn to other gods and serve them and provoke me and break my covenant.

When many evils and troubles begin to happen to them, this song will testify as a witness against them. For their descendants will sing it and they will not forget. For even now, I know what is in their hearts before I bring them into the land I promised to give them."
So that same day Moses wrote this song and taught it to the Israelis.
Then he gave Nun's son Joshua an order and said, "Be strong and courageous, because you will bring the Israelis into the land I promised to give them, and I will be with you."
When Moses finished writing the Lord's laws in the Book of the Law, from start to finish.
He gave this command to the Levites, who carried the Lord's Ark of the Covenant and said,
"Take this Book of the Law and put it inside your Lord God's Ark of the Covenant, so that it may be kept there as a witness against you.
Because I know you are stubborn and rebellious people, and you are already rebelling against the Lord today while I am still living. How much more rebellious will you be after my death?
Bring all your tribal elders and officers to me, so that I may speak to them and they can hear these words, and call heaven and earth to record this witness against them.

Because I already know that after my death you will completely corrupt yourselves and turn away from the ways which I have commanded you to follow. And evil things will happen to you in the latter days, because you will do evil in sight of the Lord and provoke his anger through the works of your own hands."
And Moses spoke to the entire Israelis congregation, and he repeated this whole song to them, to the very end.
Listen O heavens and I will speak, O earth, hear the words of my mouth.
My doctrine will fall like rain, my speech descends like dew, or a gentle rain falling on the tender herbs and the showers falling on the green grass.
Because I will publish our Lord God's name and acknowledge his greatness.
He is the rock, his work is perfect, for all of his ways are just and righteous judgements. He is a God of truth and without immorality.
They have corrupted themselves, the spot on them is not that of his children, because they are a perverse and crooked generation.
O foolish and unwise people, do you repay the Lord in this way? Is he not your father who has bought and redeemed you? Has he not made and established you?
Remember the old days, consider the many years of your past descendants. Ask your father, and he will show you your elders, and they will tell you.

When the Most High divided up and gave the nations their inheritance and he separated the sons of Adam. The Lord set the boundaries of the people in accordance with the number of Israel's descendants.
For the Lord's portion is his people, and Jacob is the Lord's allotted inheritance.
God found him in a desert wasteland and howling wilderness. The Lord led him, guided him, instructed him, and guarded him as the apple of his eye.
As an eagle stirs up her nest, she flutters over her young, spreads her wings, takes them up, and carries them on her wings.
So the Lord alone led him, and there were no strange gods with him.
He made him ride high up on the earth's hills, so that he might eat the bounty from the fields, he made honey that he could eat from the rocks and drew oil from flinty rock.
Cows butter, sheep milk, goats, with lamb's fat from the rams of Bashan, with the choicest wheat grain, and you drank wine made from the purest grape juices.
But Jeshurun kicked back and grew fat. He grew fat, bloated, and was covered with fat, then he abandoned the God who made him, and scorned the rock of his salvation.
You have made him very jealous with strange gods and provoked him to anger with your abominations.
You sacrificed to devils, not God, and you sacrificed to unknown gods, new gods that your fathers did not fear.
You ignored the rock that fathered you, and you have forgotten the God who formed you.
When the Lord saw this; he abhorred you, because his sons and daughters had provoked him to anger.
And the Lord said, "I will hide my face from them, and I will see their end. For they are a very stubborn generation, children in whom there is no faith.

They have provoked my jealousy by that which is not of God, and they have provoked my anger with their vanities. So, I will make them jealous by those who are not a people, and I will provoke them to anger with a foolish nation.
Because a fire has been kindled by my anger, and it will burn to the lowest hell. It consumes the earth along with everything it has produced and sets fire to the mountains' foundations.
I will pile mischief upon them and fire my arrows at them.
They will burn with hunger, and they will be devoured with burning heat and bitter destruction, I will also send the teeth of beasts against them, and poison from the serpents of the dust.
Out in the streets the sword will destroy both the young men and the virgins, there will be terror within their homes, and babies and old men with gray hair will die of fright.
I said I would scatter them to the four corners of the earth, and I would make their memory disappear from among men.
Had I not feared the enemy's anger, their adversaries would not have misunderstood and behaved strangely and said, 'We have prevailed, and it was not the Lord who did all this.'"
For Israel is a nation void of counsel, with no understanding among them.
O if only they were wise and understood, then they would consider their coming fate!
How could one man chase one thousand, or two men could cause 10,000 to flee, unless their rock had sold them, and the Lord had shut them down?
Because their rock is not like our rock, even our enemies understand this.
Because their vine is from Sodom's vine and from Gomorrah's fields, their grapes are grapes of gall, and their clusters are bitter.
Their wine is the poison of dragons, and the cruel venom of asps.
Have I not stored up these things with me, and sealed them among my treasures?
Vengeance and repayment is mine, their foot will slip in due time, for their day of disaster is here, and these things will come upon them quickly.
Because the Lord will judge his people, and have compassion for his servants, when he sees that their power is gone, and there are no slave or free people left.
And the Lord will say, "Where are their gods, and the rock that they trusted,
Who ate their sacrificial fat, and drank the wine of their drink offering? Let them rise up before you to help you and be your protector.
You can now see that I am he, and there is no other God besides me, I bring death and I give life, I wound and I heal, and there is nobody that can deliver from my hand.
Because I will lift up my hand to heaven, and I will say that I live forever.
If I sharpen my glittering sword, and my hands take hold of it in judgment, I will give vengeance to my enemies and repay those who hate me.
I will make my arrows drunk with blood, and my sword will devour the flesh and blood of the slain and captives, and this will be the beginning of my revenge on the enemy."
O nations rejoice with God's people, because he will avenge his servants' blood, and give vengeance to his adversaries, but he will be merciful to his land and his people.
And Moses came with Nun's son Joshua and recited the words of this song where all the people could hear.
And Moses finished reciting this song to all of Israel.
Then Moses spoke to them and said, "Take these words to heart that I testify to you today, so that you may command your children to observe and obey, all the words of this law.

For these words are not a vain thing for you, because they are your life and through them you will prolong the days of your life, when you cross the Jordan River to take possession of the land where you are going."
And that same day the Lord spoke to Moses and said,
"Go up into the Abarim mountain range to Mount Nebo in the land of Moab next to Jericho, and look out over the land of Canaan, which I am giving to the Israelis as their inheritance.
You will die on that mountain, and your people can gather around you there, just as they gathered around your brother Aaron when he died on Mount Hor.
Because both of you trespassed against me in the Zin wilderness at the waters of Meribah-Kadesh, because you did not sanctify me in the midst of the Israelis.
You will be allowed to see the promised land, but you will not be allowed to go into the land I have given to the descendants of Israel."
And Moses the man of God gave this blessing to the Israelis, just before his death.

And Moses said, "The Lord came from Mount Sinai, and rose up like the sun from Mount Seir to shine before the people of Mount Paran. The Lord came with tens of thousands of saints, and a fiery law for them flew out from his right hand.
Yes, you loved your people; all of your saints are in your hand, and they sit at your feet, and they all receive your words.
Moses gave us God's law, and the inheritance of Jacob's congregation.
And the Lord was a king in Jeshurun, when the people's leaders gathered the tribes of Israel together.
Let Reuben live and not die and make sure the number of his men grows and increases."

And Moses gave Judah his blessing and said, "O Lord, hear Judah's voice and bring him to his people, let his hands be sufficient for him to defend himself, and may you also defend him from his enemies."
And Moses spoke of Levi and said, "Let your Thummim and Urim be with your holy one, whom you tested at Massah and struggled with at the waters of Meribah.
Who said to his father and mother, 'I have not seen him.' Nor did he acknowledge his brothers, and he did not know his own children; for they have observed and kept your word and your covenant.
They will teach your judgments to Jacob, and your law to Israel, they will place incense before you, and they will put whole burnt offerings on your altar.
O Lord, bless his substance, and accept the work of his hands, crush the waists of those who hate and rise up against him, so that they do not rise up against him again."
And of Benjamin Moses said, "The Lord's beloved will live in safety with him, and the Lord will shield him all day long and he shall live between his shoulders."
And of Joseph Moses said, "The Lord has blessed his land with heaven's precious dew, and with the waters from the depth below.
And with the precious fruits the sun brings forth, and the precious things put forth by the moon.
And with the finest things from the ancient mountains, and with the precious things from the everlasting hills.

And with the precious things from the fullness of the earth, and with the good will of the one who lived in the burning bush. May all of these blessings rest on Joseph's head, who was separated from his brothers.

His glory is like a young bull, and his horns are like the horns of a wild ox. He will push the people together to the ends of the earth, and they will come from Ephraim's tens of thousands, and Manasseh's thousands."
And of Zebulun and Issachar Moses said, "Rejoice in your tents, and in your coming in and your going out.
Call our people to the mountain where they must offer righteous sacrifices, because they will harvest the seas abundance and the treasures hidden in the sand."
And of Gad Moses said, "Blessed is he who enlarges Gad's domain, because he lives as a lion and tears an arm or a head loose.
And he kept the first part for himself, because he was seated with the lawgiver's portion, and he came with the people's leaders, and he executed the Lord's justice and judgments with Israel."
And of Dan Moses said, "Dan is a lion cub, he will leap from Bashan."
And of Naphtali Moses said, "Naphtali is filled with favor and the Lord's blessing, he shall take possession of the west and the south."
And of Asher Moses said, "Let Asher be blessed with children, let him be most favored to his brothers, and let him dip his foot in oil.
Your shoes will be made of brass and iron, and may your strength last you all the days of your long life.
There are none like Jeshurun's God, who rides on the heavens and the clouds to your aid, in all of his majesty.
The eternal God is your refuge, and underneath are his everlasting arms. He will drive the enemy out from before you and he will say, 'Destroy them!'
So Israel alone will live in safety, and Jacob's fountain will flow upon on a land of wheat and wine, where the dew will fall from God's heavens.

O Israel, who else is like you, your people are blessed with happiness and saved by your Lord's shield, whose sword is your sword of excellency! You will prove that your enemies are liars, and you will walk on their high places."
Moses went from the Moab plains to Mount Nebo, and the top of Mount Pisgah near the Jericho border. And the Lord showed him the entire promised land from the land of Gilead to Dan.
Which included all the lands of Naphtali, Ephraim, Manasseh, and Judah, and as far away as the coast of Mediterranean Sea.
And from the southern plains of the Valley of Jericho, the City of Palms, all the way to Zoar.

And the Lord spoke to Moses and said, "This is the land which I swore to give Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob when I said, 'I will give this land to your descendants, I have allowed you to see it with your own eyes, but you will not go there.'"
So the Lord's servant Moses died in Moab, just as the Lord said he would.
And the Lord buried Moses in a valley in Moab, along the border of Beth-Peor, but to this day nobody knows where his tomb is located.
Moses was 120 years old when he died, but his eyes were not dim, and his natural life force had not diminished.
And the Israelis wept for Moses in the plains of Moab for thirty days, until his time of weeping and the mourning period ended.
And Nun's son Joshua was full of the spirit of wisdom, because Moses had laid his hands on him, and the Israelis did as the Lord commanded Moses and listened to Joshua.
And there has never been anyone in Israel since then like Moses, a prophet who spoke to the Lord face to face.
There have been no prophets that have performed all the signs and wonders the Lord sent Moses to do to Egypt, Pharaoh, and Pharaoh's servants.
And Moses showed that mighty hand and great terror to everyone in Israel.
After his servant Moses died, the Lord spoke to Nun's son Joshua who had been assisting Moses and said,
"My servant Moses is dead, so get up and lead the Israelis across the Jordan River into the Promised Land which I have given to you and to them.
I have given you all the land where the soles of your feet shall tread, as I promised Moses.
Your lands will stretch from the wilderness and Lebanon to the great Euphrates River, throughout all the Hittite lands, all the way to the coast of the Mediterranean Sea facing the setting sun.
No one will be able to stand against you all the days of your life, because I will be with you as I was with Moses, so that you do not fail, and I will never fail you nor abandon you.
Be strong and courageous, because you will divide the Promised Land among these people as their inheritance, which I swore to their fathers that I would give them.

Be strong and very courageous, so that you may observe and obey all of my laws which my servant Moses gave you. Do not stray from the true path or turn from the left or the right, so that you may be prosperous wherever you go.
Meditate on this Book of the Law, day and night, so that you may observe and obey everything written in it, in accordance with the law, because these laws will make you successful and prosperous.
Have I not commanded you to be strong and courageous? Do not be afraid, do not be dismayed, because your Lord God is with you wherever you go."
Then Joshua gave these orders to his officers and said,

"Spread the word throughout the camp and tell the people to prepare their food, because within the next three days we will be crossing the Jordan River to enter and take possession of the land which our Lord God has given us."
And Joshua spoke to the Reubenites, Gadites, and the half tribe of Manasseh and said,
"Remember what the Lord's servant Moses commanded us, when he said, 'Our Lord God had given you rest, and he is giving you this land.'

Your wives, your children, and your cattle may remain in the land which Moses gave you on this side of the Jordan River. But you must arm yourselves and cross over the Jordan River with your brothers, because you are the mighty men of valor and you must help them.

Until the Lord gives your brothers the same rest that he has given you, and they have taken possession of the land your Lord God has given them. After that you can return to and enjoy your land, which the Lord's servant Moses gave you on this side of the Jordan River facing the rising sun."
And they answered Joshua and said, "We will do everything you command us to do, and we will go wherever you send us.
We will listen to you about everything the same way that we listened to Moses, and may your Lord God be with you, as he was with Moses.
We will be strong and courageous, and we will put to death anyone who refuses to listen to your word and rebels against any of your commands."

And Nun's son Joshua sent two men from Shittim to secretly spy, and he spoke to them and said, "Go and search the land all the way to Jericho." So, they left and when they came to Rahab the prostitute's house, they stayed there.
When the king of Jericho was told about them, he said, "Behold some men came here tonight from the people of Israel to spy on the country."
The King of Jericho sent a message to Rahab and said, "Bring me the men who are staying in your house, because they have come to spy on the country."
But Rahab had hidden the two men, and she said to the messenger, "Two men did come here, but I did not know where they were from.
After it was dark, they closed the gates and the men left, but I do not know where they went. If you quickly pursue them now, you should be able to overtake them."
But Rahab had hidden them on the roof of her house with the flax stalks, that she had stored on her roof.
So they pursued the men all the way to the fjords of the Jordan River, and as soon as they left the city the guards closed the gates.
And before they could lay down to rest, Rahab came to the men on the roof.
And Rahab said to the men, "I know that the Lord has given you the land, and that your terror has fallen on us, and everyone living in the land here is weak and dizzy because of you.

Because we heard that the Lord dried up all the water of the Red Sea, when you left Egypt. And we heard what you did when you completely destroyed the two Amorite kings, Sihon and Og on the other side of the Jordan River.
As soon as we heard these things, our hearts melted and our men lost their courage, because your Lord God is the God in heaven above and on the earth below.
So, I pray that since I have shown you kindness that you will promise me by the Lord, that you will also show kindness to my father's house, and give me a true token.
I ask you to allow my father, mother, brothers, and my sisters to live and that you will protect everything that they own and deliver us from death."

And the men answered Rahab and said, "Our life for your lives is a fair deal, as long as you do not tell anyone about our business, and after the Lord has given us this land, we will deal kindly and honestly with you."
Then Rahab lowered them down with a rope through the window, because the house where she lived was built along the city wall.
And Rahab said to them, "Go to the mountain and hide there for three days, otherwise the king's soldiers may find you, and when they return here then you may go on your way."
And the men spoke to Rahab and said, "We cannot be bound by this oath you have made us swear.

Unless you tie this scarlet thread in the window through which you lowered us down from your roof. And you must bring your father, mother, brothers, and everyone else in your father's household into your home with you.

If anyone leaves your house and goes out into the street, their blood will be on their heads, and we will not be guilty. But if anyone is injured or killed while they are in your house, their blood will be on our head.
And if you report what we are up to, then we will not be bound by the oath you have made us swear."
And Rahab said, "It will be as you have said." Then Rahab sent them away, and after they left, she tied the scarlet ribbon in her window.
Then they went up into the mountain and stayed there for three days until the soldiers returned. They had looked for them throughout the land, but they could not find them.
After the three days, the men descended from the mountain and returned home. When they went to see Nun's son Joshua, they told him everything that had happened.
And they said to Joshua, "Truly the Lord has delivered all the land into our hands, because the country's inhabitants are weak and completely terrified of us."
Joshua rose early in the morning, and they left Shittim and went to the Jordan River, where he and all the Israelis stayed before they crossed over.
After three days, the camp's officers went throughout the troops.
And they gave orders to their soldiers and said, "When you see the Levite priests carrying your Lord God's Ark of the Covenant, then leave and follow it.

But keep a distance of about 2,000 cubits between you and the Ark of the Covenant. Do not come near it. Follow the ark and it will lead the way through the land, since you have not been this way before."
After this Joshua spoke to the people and said, "Sanctify yourselves, because tomorrow the Lord will do wonders among you."
Then Joshua spoke to the priests and said, "Pick up the Ark of the Covenant, and carry it before the people," and they carried it out in front of them.
And the Lord spoke to Joshua and said, "Today I will begin to magnify you before all of Israel, so they will know that just as I was with Moses, I will also be with you.
When you order the priests that carry the Ark of the Covenant, tell them when they reach the banks of the Jordan River, they must stop and wait before crossing the river."
And Joshua spoke to the Israelis and said, "Come and hear your Lord God's words."

And Joshua said, "This is how you will know that the living God is among you and that he will, without fail, drive out from before you the Canaanites, Hittites, Hivites, Perizzites, Girgashites, Amorites, and the Jebusites.
Behold, the Ark of the Covenant of the Lord of all the earth crosses over the Jordan River before you.
So, I want you to pick twelve men from the tribes of Israel, one man from each of the twelve tribes.

As soon as the priests' feet who carry the Lord of all the earth's ark touches the water of the Jordan River, the water will stop flowing and the river will be cut off from the upstream waters and they will pile up."
Then the people left their camp to cross the Jordan River, and the priests carried the Ark of the Covenant before them.
As soon as the priests' feet that carried the ark touched the water in the Jordan River, which usually overflows its banks at harvest time.

The river water flowing from upstream stood still all the way up to the city of Adam, which is beside Zarethan. So, the water flowing toward the Dead Sea was cut off, and the people crossed over the river near Jericho.
And the priests carrying the Lord's Ark of the Covenant stood firm on dry ground in the middle of the Jordan River, and all of the Israelis crossed over the Jordan River on dry ground.
After all the people crossed the Jordan River, the Lord spoke to Joshua and said,
"Pick twelve men, one from each of the twelve tribes.

And give them this command, 'Take twelve stones from the middle of the Jordan River where the priests are firmly standing. Carry them across the river with you and leave them in the camp where you will be spending the night.'"
Then Joshua summoned the twelve men, whom he had chosen from the twelve tribes of Israel.

And Joshua spoke to them and said, "Go back out into the middle of the Jordan River in front of your God's Ark of the Covenant, and each of you must pick up a stone and carry it on your shoulder, one stone for each of the tribes of Israel.
And this will be a memorial among you, so that when your children ask what these stones mean.

You can answer them and say, 'It is to remind us of the time that the waters of the Jordan River were cut off before the Lord's Ark of the Covenant as it crossed over the Jordan. These stones are a memorial for Israel's descendants to remember forever.'"
And the Israelis did as Joshua commanded and pulled twelve stones from the middle of the Jordan River to represent the twelve tribes of Israel and carried them back to the camp and laid them down.
Then Joshua stacked twelve stones in the middle of the Jordan, where the priests who carried the Ark of the Covenant stood, and they are still there to this day.

Because the priests who carried the ark stood in the middle of the Jordan River, until they finished doing everything that the Lord ordered them to do. This was just as Moses had instructed Joshua, and the people hurried across the river.
After everyone crossed the river, the priests crossed the river carrying the Lord's Ark of the Covenant as the people watched.
Then the armed soldiers from Reuben's descendants, Gad's descendants, and the half tribe of Manasseh crossed the river before all of the Israelis, armed for battle as Moses had instructed them.
About 40,000 troops prepared for war passed before the Lord to do battle on the plains of Jericho.
That day the Lord magnified Joshua in sight of all of the Israelis and they feared him, as they had feared Moses all the days of his life.
And the Lord spoke to Joshua and said,
"Order the priests who carry the Ark of the Covenant to come up out of the Jordan."
So Joshua ordered the priests to come up out of the Jordan River.

When the priests carrying the Lord's Ark of the Covenant came up out the middle of the Jordan River and the soles of their feet touched dry land, the river's water began to overflow its banks again as it had before.
It was the tenth day of the first month when the people crossed the Jordan River and camped in Gilgal along the eastern border of Jericho.
Joshua camped in Gilgal, where he set up the twelve stones they had taken from the Jordan River.
And Joshua spoke to the Israelis and said, "In the future when your children ask you, 'What do these stones mean?'
Then you can say to them, "Israel crossed the Jordan River to dry land on the other side of the river in this spot.
Because your Lord God dried up the Jordan River's water until we crossed over, the same way that he had done when he dried up the Red Sea for us until we crossed.
So that all the people of the earth will know that the Lord's hand is mighty, and to help you fear your Lord God forever.

After all the Amorite kings on the western side of the Jordan River, and the Canaanite kings by the sea, heard that the Lord had dried up the waters of the Jordan River for the Israelis to cross, their hearts melted and they no longer had a fighting spirit within them, because of the Israelis.
At that time the Lord said to Joshua, "Make some knives, and circumcise Israel's descendants a second time."
So Joshua made some knives, and circumcised Israel's descendants at the Hill of Foreskins.
Joshua circumcised all the males who came from Egypt, because of all the men of war who had died along the road in the wilderness after they left Egypt.
Now everyone who left Egypt had already been circumcised, but no one born in the wilderness along the road from Egypt had been circumcised.

And the Israelis had to walk in the wilderness for forty years, until all the men of war who had come from Egypt died because they would not obey the Lord's voice. So, the Lord promised that he would not show them the Promised Land, a land flowing with milk and honey that he had promised to give to their fathers for them to give us.
Joshua circumcised the children who had taken their place, because they were uncircumcised and had not been circumcised along the way.
After they finished circumcising all the people, they all stayed in the camp until they had healed.
And the Lord spoke to Joshua and said, "Today I have rolled Egypt's disgrace away from you. And that's why that place is still called Gilgal to this day."
The Israelis camped in Gilgal, and they kept the Passover on the fourteenth day of the month on the plains of Jericho.
The day after Passover, they ate roasted wheat and unleavened cakes made from wheat which had been harvested from the land, then dried and stored.

Then the manna from heaven ceased the day after they ate the stored wheat that was harvested from the land, and the Israelis never ate manna again, but they ate from the land's abundance in Canaan that year.
When Joshua was camped near Jericho, he looked up and saw a man standing in front of him with a drawn sword in his hand, so he approached the man and said, "Are you for us, or against us?"
And the man said, "Neither, but I have now come as the captain of the Lord's multitudes," and Joshua fell facedown in respect and said, "What message do you have for this servant of the Lord?"
Then the captain of the Lord's multitude said to Joshua, "Loosen your shoe and remove it from your foot, for the place where you are standing is holy," and Joshua did what he was told.
Now the gates of Jericho were closed shut because of the Israelis, and no one could leave or enter.
And the Lord spoke to Joshua and said, "Behold, I have put the fate of Jericho and their king into the hands of your mighty men of valor.
Surround the city with your mighty men of war and march them around the city once a day for six days.
March seven priests around the city each one carrying a ram's horn trumpet before the ark. On the seventh day march them around the city seven times while the priests blow their trumpets.

When you hear a long blast from their ram's horn trumpets, tell the people to shout a great shout, and the city walls will come tumbling down. Then the men can climb over the walls and go straight into the city.
Nun's son Joshua assembled the priests and said, "Carry the Ark of the Covenant before you, and give seven ram's horn trumpets to seven priests to carry behind the ark."
And he spoke to the people and said, "March around the city with the mighty men armed for war leading the way for the Lord's Ark of the Covenant."
When Joshua finished speaking to the people, the seven priests marched before the Lord blowing their trumpets, and the Lord's Ark of the Covenant followed them.
And the mighty men armed for war led the way, as the priests followed constantly blowing their trumpets followed by The Ark of the Covenant.
Then Joshua gave his orders to the people and said, "You must not shout, speak, nor make any noise with your voice until the day I tell you to shout, then you must shout as loud as you can."
So the men carrying the Lord's Ark of the Covenant surrounded the city and marched around it once, then they returned to their camp and waited.
And Joshua and the priests who carried the Ark of the Covenant, rose early the next morning.

Then the mighty men armed for war led the way for the seven priests constantly blowing their seven ram's horn trumpets as they marched around the city. And the priests carrying the Lord's Ark of the Covenant followed.
On the second day they surrounded the city and marched around it once, then returned to camp, and they did this for six days.
On the seventh day they rose early and went out at dawn to march around the city, but on that day, they marched around it seven times.
The seventh time around as the priests blew their trumpets, Joshua said to the people, "Shout, because the Lord has given you the city!

This city is cursed by the Lord including everyone and everything in it, and it must all be destroyed except for Rahab the prostitute's house. She will be spared and everyone in her house will be allowed to live, because she hid the messengers that we sent here.
You must not touch any of the cursed things, otherwise you will be cursed and cause the entire camp of Israel to be cursed and bring great trouble on us.
But the Lord has declared anything made of silver, gold, brass, or iron to be sacred and they must all be brought into the Lord's treasury."

So the people shouted a great shout when they heard the priests blow the trumpets for the last time, and the walls came tumbling down. Then the people charged straight into the city and took the city.
They completely destroyed everything in the city with the sword, including the men and women both young and old, and the oxen, sheep, and donkeys.

But Joshua told the two men who had spied out the country to go to the prostitute's house, and bring her along with everything that she owned, and her people out of the city, to protect her as they had promised they would.
So the young spies brought Rahab and her father, mother, brothers, and everything that she owned out of the city, and they left her relatives outside the Israelis camp.
Then they burnt the city and everything in it to the ground, but they brought everything made of silver, gold, brass, and iron to the Lord's house and put it in his treasury.

Joshua spared Rahab the prostitute along with her father's household, and saved everything that she owned, because she had hidden the messengers that Joshua sent to spy out the land in Jericho, and she lives in Israel to this day.

Then Joshua formally and sincerely warned the people at that time and said, "Anyone who rebuilds Jericho will be cursed before the Lord. If they rebuild its foundation, it will cost them their firstborn, and if they rebuild its gates, it will cost them their youngest son."
So the Lord was with Joshua, and his fame spread throughout the entire country.

But some of the Israelis committed a sin against the Lord, because Carmi's son Achan stole the cursed thing, and the Lord's anger was kindled against Israel. Carmi was the son of Zabdi and Zerah from Judah's tribe

Joshua sent some men from Jericho to Ai, which is east of Bethel near Bethaven, and he gave them their orders and said, "Go and explore the country," and the men traveled through Ai exploring the land.

They returned to bring their report to Joshua and they said, "You only need to send 2,000 or 3,000 men to defeat Ai, because there are very few people there, and it will not be necessary to send the whole army for such a small place."
So about 3,000 men were sent, but they were defeated by the men of Ai and they had to flee.

And the men of Ai killed about 36 of them, and they chased them from the city gates all the way to Shebarim and killed more of them along the way. As a result, the people's hearts melted and they lost their courage.
When Joshua heard this, he tore his clothes and fell facedown before the Ark of the Covenant, where he and the Israelis elders put dust on their heads, and they remained there until evening.

And Joshua cried out and said, "O Lord God, why did you bring all these people over the Jordan River? Did you deliver us into the hands of the Amorites just to destroy us and show us that we should have been content living on the other side of the river!
O Lord, what can I say now that the Israelis have turned and fled from their enemies!

Because the Canaanites and all the inhabitants of the land will hear about it. When they do, they will surround us and wipe our name from the face of the earth, and what will that do to your great name?"
Then the Lord spoke to Joshua and said, "Get up from there, why are you lying on your face?
Israel has sinned, and they have broken my covenant that I told them to keep. They have stolen and dissembled things, and they even tried to hide some of them among their own personal possessions.

Therefore, the Israelis could not stand before their enemies, they lost their courage, turned and fled from their enemies because they were cursed, I will no longer be with you unless you destroy the cursed things in your camp.

So get up, sanctify the people then speak to them and say, 'Sanctify yourselves and prepare for what will come tomorrow, for the Lord God of Israel says, "There are cursed things in the midst of Israel, and you cannot stand before your enemies until you remove them from your camp."
So in the morning each tribe must be brought forward tribe by tribe, and whichever tribe the Lord chooses must come forward family by family, household by household, and man by man.
And the man that stole the cursed thing along with everything that he owns must be burned, because he has broken the Lord's covenant, and he did something foolish in Israel.'"
So Joshua rose up early in the morning and brought all the tribes of Israel forward tribe by tribe, and Judah's tribe was chosen.
And he brought Judah's family forward, and the Zerahite family was chosen, and Joshua brought the Zerahite family forward man by man, and Zabdi was chosen.
And Zabdi's household was brought forward man by man, and Achan was chosen. Achan was the son of Carmi, who was the son of Zabdi and Zerah, from Judah's tribe.
Then Joshua said to Achan, "My son, I pray that you give glory to the Lord God of Israel, and confess your sin to him, and tell me what you have done, and do not try to hide it from me."
And Achan answered Joshua and said, "I have sinned against the Lord God of Israel, and I have indeed done this thing.

When I saw a good Babylonian garment, and 200 silver shekels, and a 50-shekel gold bar among the spoils of war, I coveted them and I took them. I buried them under the gold bar in the middle of my tent."
So, Joshua sent messengers to Achan's tent, and they found it and the silver buried under the gold bar in his tent.
They took them from the tent and brought them to Joshua for all the Israelis to see, and they spread them out before the Lord.

So, Joshua and all of the Israelis took Zerah's son Achan, the silver, the garment, and the gold bar, plus his sons, daughters, oxen, donkeys, sheep, tent, and everything else that he owned to the Valley of Achor.
And Joshua said, "Because have you troubled us, the Lord will trouble you today." Then all of the Israelis stoned them to death, then they burned their bodies.
And they stacked a great pile of stones over them as a monument that is still there. This calmed the Lord's fierce anger, and they call that place the Valley of Achor to this day.

And the Lord spoke to Joshua and said, "Do not be afraid or surprised! Take all of your soldiers and attack Ai, because I have put the king of Ai and his people, his city, and his lands into your hands.
Go and do to Ai and her king what you did to Jericho and her king. Prepare an ambush behind the city, but this time you will be allowed to take all the spoils of war and their cattle for yourselves.
So, Joshua planned to attack Ai with 30,000 mighty men of valor in the middle of the night.
Then Joshua addressed the army and said, "You must lie in wait behind the city, right outside the city walls, but be ready for action.
I will approach to the city from the other side with the rest of the soldiers, when they come out to attack us, we will flee from them.
They will come after us and we will draw them away from the city. They will think that we are fleeing from them, as we did the first time we attacked them.
When that happens, rise up from your hiding place, then ambush and seize the city, because your Lord God will deliver it into your hands.
After you have taken the city, set it on fire as the Lord commanded. Now I have given you your orders and you know what to do."
So Joshua sent them out and they went to lie in wait and prepare for the ambush on the western side of Ai, between Bethel and Ai. But Joshua spent that night among the people.
Early the next morning Joshua and the Israelis elders mobilized the remaining soldiers and led them to Ai.

Then the troops who were the mighty men of war marched with Joshua, and they approached Ai from the north. They stopped and set up camp on the north side of the city with a valley between them and the city.
And Joshua had prepared an ambush with about 5,000 men between Bethel and Ai, on the west side of the city.
After Joshua stationed the troops on the north side of the city, and rear troops stationed on the west side of the city, he went down into the valley that night.

When the king of Ai saw what was happening, they got up early and quickly left the city to do battle against the Israelis at the appointed time and place overlooking the plains. But the king did not know that an ambush had been planned by the troops who were lying in wait behind the city.
Joshua and all the Israelis with him acted as if they were being beaten, and they fled out into of the wilderness before them.
All of the king's men in Ai had assembled to pursue Joshua, and they chased him and they were drawn away from the city.
So there were no men left in Ai or Bethel, because they had left to pursue the Israelis, and the city was wide open.
Then the Lord spoke to Joshua and said, "Point your spear toward Ai, because I am going to put that city into your hands," and Joshua pointed his spear toward the city.
As soon as he pointed his spear toward Ai, the ambushers quickly left their hiding place, and they ran to the city and entered it. Once the city had been captured, they hurriedly set fire to it.
And when the men of Ai looked back, they saw the smoke from the city, and they were powerless to flee this way or that, and Israel's fleeing soldiers turned to face their pursuers in the wilderness.
When Joshua and all of the Israelis saw that the ambushers had taken the city, and they saw the smoke from the city, they turned and killed the men of Ai.
And the others that had come out of the city against them, were trapped in the middle of the Israelis. So, the men from Ai were surrounded and defeated, and none of them escaped or survived.
But they took the king of Ai alive and brought him to Joshua.

When Israel finished killing all of the inhabitants of Ai who had followed them into the fields and wilderness, and after their pursuers had all fallen and died by the sword, the Israelis returned to Ai and used their swords to finish off whatever enemy was left.
And 12,000 men and women from Ai died that day.
Because Joshua did not lay down his spear until he had completely destroyed Ai and killed everyone living there.
The Israelis only took the cattle and the other spoils of war for themselves from the city, that the Lord told Joshua they could have.
So, Joshua burned Ai, and made it an eternal pile of ashes, and it is still a devastation to this day.

Joshua hanged the king of Ai on a tree until the evening, and as soon as the sun went down, he ordered them to throw the king's body at the entrance of the city gates, then stack a great pile of stones there as a memorial that remains to this day.
Then Joshua built an altar to the Lord God of Israel on Mount Ebal.

The altar was built using whole uncut stones as the plans that the Lord's servant Moses had laid out in his Book of the Law. When they finished building the altar they offered their sacrificial burnt offerings and peace offerings on it to the Lord.
And in the presence of all of Israel Joshua wrote a copy of the Law of Moses on the altar's stones.

All of Israel and their elders, officers, judges, both citizens and the foreigners living among them stood on both sides the Lord's Ark of the Covenant before the Levite priests who carried it. Half of them stood before Mount Gerizim and half of them stood before Mount Ebal. This was as the Lord's servant Moses had commanded them before he died, so they could bless the people of Israel.
Afterward Joshua read all of the laws, blessings, and curses, exactly the way they were written in the Book of the Law.

There were no commandments that Moses had written that Joshua did not read before the entire Israelis congregation, including the women, children, and the foreigners living among them who understood the language.

When this news reached the kings west of Jordan, and those in the hills and valleys, and everyone along the coasts of the Mediterranean Sea by the Lebanese border, including the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and the Jebusites.
They united to form an alliance to fight Joshua and Israel as one army.
When the inhabitants of Gibeon heard what Joshua had done to Jericho and Ai.
They cunningly schemed and disguised themselves as ambassadors, and they carried worn-out sacks with old and mended wineskins on their donkeys.
They wore old, patched sandals on their feet and old frayed clothing, and all the bread in their provisions was dry and moldy.
And they went to see Joshua at his camp in Gilgal, and they spoke to him and the Israelis men and said, "We have come from a far country to offer you a treaty of alliance with us."
The Israelis men replied to the Hivites and said, "Where are you from, do you live near us, how can we make a treaty of alliance with you if we do not know anything about you?"
And they answered Joshua and said, "We are your servants," and Joshua said to them, "Who are you, and where have you come from?"

And they said to him, "We are your servants, and we have come from a country from very far away, we have come here because we have heard the famous name of your Lord God, and everything that he has done in Egypt.
Everything that he did to the two Amorite kings on the other side of the Jordan, King Sihon of Heshbon, and King Og of Bashan who reigned in Ashtaroth.

So, our elders and all the people in our country spoke to us and said, "Take some prepared food for the journey, and go meet with them. Tell them, that we are your servants, and we want to make a treaty with you.
This bread that we took hot from the ovens in our homes for our provisions, on the day that we left to come meet with you, is now moldy and dried out.
These wineskins were new when we filled them and now, they are worn-out, and our shoes and clothes are also worn-out because we have traveled such a very long distance."
The men of Israel accepted their gift of prepared food, but they did not consult the Lord about it.
So Joshua signed a peace treaty with them, and decided to let them live, and the congregation's leaders swore an oath to them.
Three days after the Israelis signed a treaty with them, they heard that the Gibeonites were their neighbors, and they were living among them.
So the Israelis traveled to their cities where they arrived on the third day. Their cities were Gibeon, Chephirah, Beeroth, and Kiriath-Jearim.

The Israelis did not attack them, because the congregation's leaders had sworn an oath to them by the Lord God of Israel. But the entire Israelis congregation started complaining about their leaders because of this.
But the congregation's leaders answered them and said, "We have sworn an oath to them by the Lord God of Israel, so we cannot touch them now.
This is what we have to do, we must let them live so that the Lord's anger is not brought down on us, because we swore an oath to them in his name."
And their leaders said, "We promised to let them live, but their leaders said that they would be our servants, so let them be the wood carvers and water carriers for the entire congregation.
And Joshua summoned the deceivers and he spoke to them and said, "Because you deceived us when you told us that you were from a place far away from us, when you actually lived among us!
So now you are cursed, and you will never be freed from the slavery you have imposed on yourselves, and you will be wood carvers and water carriers for my God's house forever."

And they answered Joshua and said, "We are your servants, and we feared for our lives, because we had heard that your Lord God commanded Moses to give you all of the land, and to destroy everyone that lived in the land before you, and that's why we have done this thing.
And now, behold we are at your mercy, so do to us whatever you think is right and just."
So he delivered them from the hands of the Israelis, and they did not kill them.
And from that day forward to this very day, Joshua made them wood carvers and water carriers for the entire congregation and the Lord's altar, at the place that the Lord would choose.

When King Adoni-Zedek of Jerusalem heard that Joshua had conquered and destroyed Ai, the same way that he had destroyed Jericho and killed their king. And after the king heard that the inhabitants of Gibeon had made peace with Israel, and they were now living among them.
He was extremely afraid, because Gibeon was one of the great royal cities and they were more powerful than Ai, because all their men were mighty warriors.
So King Adoni-Zedek of Jerusalem sent word to King Hoham of Hebron, King Piram of Jarmuth, King Japhia of Lachish, and King Debir of Eglon and said,
"I need you to come help me defeat Gibeon, because they have made peace with Joshua and the Israelis."

And the five Amorite kings including the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, and the king of Eglon, assembled their armies together and set up camped where they attacked Gibeon.

And the Gibeonites sent messengers to Joshua who was camped in Gilgal and said, "We need you to come quickly and help us, because all the Amorite kings from the mountains have arrayed their armies against us."
So Joshua left Gilgal with his soldiers who were mighty men of valor, and they were armed and ready for war.
And the Lord spoke to Joshua and said, "Do not fear them, because I have delivered them into your hands, and not one of them will be left standing when you are done."
Joshua left Gilgal and traveled all night, because he had a sudden surprise attack planned.
The Lord confused them and they panicked as Israel attacked and mercilessly slaughtered them at Gibeon, then Joshua followed them to Beth-Horon, and attacked them all the way to Azekah and Makkedah.
As they fled Israel to Beth-Horon, the Lord threw meteorites from heaven at them all the way to Azekah. More of them died from the meteorites than the Israelis killed with their swords.

That day the Lord delivered the Amorites into the hands of the Israelis, and Joshua spoke to the Lord where the Israeli soldiers could see him and said, "O sun, stand still over Gibeon! O moon, stand still over the Valley of Ajalon!"

And the sun and the moon stood still until the Israelis had taken vengeance against their enemies. For is it not written in the Book of Jasher? "The sun stood still in the middle of the sky, and it did not set for almost a whole day."
There had never been a day like that before or since, a day when the Lord listened to a man and fought for Israel.
And Joshua returned to the camp in Gilgal with all the Israeli soldiers.
But the five kings fled and hid in a cave at Makkedah.
And Joshua was told that the five kings were found hiding in a cave at Makkedah.
And Joshua said, "Cover the mouth of the cave with great stones, and put guards there to keep them.
Do not stop there but pursue the enemy until you have defeated the last of them, and do not let them enter their cities, because your Lord God has delivered them into your hands."
When Joshua and the Israelis had defeated and slaughtered the last of them, some of them survived and retreated to their walled cities.
Then the army safely returned to Makkedah where Joshua was camped, and all the other nations were afraid to speak against Israel.
Then Joshua said, "Open the cave and bring me the five kings."
So they brought him the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, and the king of Eglon from the cave.
When they brought the kings to Joshua, he summoned the Israeli army and spoke to their leaders and said, "Come and put your feet on the necks of these kings," and they put their feet on their necks.
And Joshua said to them, "Fear not, and do not be dismayed, be strong and courageous, because this is the way the Lord will deal with all of your enemies who fight against you."
Afterward Joshua had them executed and hanged them on five trees, and they hung on those trees until the evening.

When the sun went down Joshua gave the order to his men, and they took their bodies down from the trees and threw them into the cave where they had hidden. Then they sealed the cave's entrance with large stones, where they remain to this very day.

That day Joshua conquered Makkedah with the sword, and he completely destroyed the king and everyone living there. He had no mercy on their people and none of them survived, and he treated to the king of Makkedah the same as he treated the king of Jericho.
Then Joshua left Makkedah and took all the Israeli troops with him to Libnah, and they attacked Libnah.

And the Lord also delivered Libnah and their king into Israel's hands, and Joshua slaughtered everyone living there with the sword. No one survived, and he treated their king the same as he treated the king of Jericho.
Joshua left Libnah and took all the Israeli troops with him to Lachish, and he camped on their border and attacked them.
And the Lord took Lachish on the second day and delivered it into Israel's hands, and he slaughtered everyone living there with the sword, just as he had done in Libnah.
Then King Horam of Gezer came to help Lachish, and Joshua defeated him and his people, until none of them were left.
Joshua left Lachish and took all of the Israeli troops with him to Eglon, where they camped along its border and attacked them.
They took Eglon that day, and he slaughtered everyone living there with the sword, just as he had done in Lachish.
Joshua left Eglon along with all of the Israel and went to Hebron, where they fought them.
Joshua took Hebron, and they slaughtered everyone living there with the sword, just as he had done in Eglon, and nothing remained when he was finished.
Then Joshua returned to Debir with all the Israeli troops and fought them.
Joshua took Debir and slaughtered everyone living there with the sword, just as he had conquered Hebron and their king, and Libnah and their king.

So, Joshua defeated all the mountain countries from the south to the vale, and to the springs. He conquered all of their kings and left no survivors, but he completely destroyed everything that breathed, as the Lord God of Israel commanded.
Joshua defeated them from Kadesh-Barnea all the way to Gaza, and the entire country of Goshen all the way to Gibeon.
Joshua conquered these kings and their lands all at one time, because the Lord God of Israel fought for Israel.
And Joshua safely returned with all the Israeli troops to their camp in Gilgal.
When King Jabin of Hazor heard about these things, he sent messengers to King Jobab of Madon and the kings of Shimron and Achshaph.
Then he sent messengers to the northern mountain kings, the plains kings south of Galilee, the valley kings, and the kings along the western borders of Dor.
He also sent messengers to the eastern and western Canaanites and the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, and the mountain Jebusites, and the Hivites under Mount Hermon in Mizpah.

So, they assembled their armies and went to meet King Jabin of Hazor. There were so many of them that they appeared to be as numerous the grains of sand on the beach, and they had many horses and chariots.
When all these kings came together, they camped at the waters of Merom to fight the Israelis.

And the Lord spoke to Joshua and said, "Do not be afraid of them, because tomorrow at about this time I will deliver them up to be killed before Israel. Then you will be able to hobble their horses and burn their chariots."
So Joshua brought the entire Israeli army with him and launched a sudden surprise attack against them by the waters of Merom, and they all fell before Israel.

The Lord delivered them into the Israelis hands, who defeated them and chased them to great Sidon, then to Misrephoth-Maim, and to the eastern Valley of Mizpah. They attacked them until there were no survivors.
Then Joshua did what the Lord told him to do, and he hobbled their horses and burned their chariots.
Then Joshua turned back to defeat and conquer the king of Hazor with the sword, because Hazor had been the head of all those kingdoms in the past.
They defeated every living soul there with the sword and completely destroyed them. They left no breathing thing alive, then they burned Hazor to the ground.
So Joshua defeated and conquered all of those kings with the sword, and he completely destroyed them, just as Moses the servant of the Lord commanded.
But Israel did not burn any of the other fortified cities, except for Hazor which Joshua burned.

And the Israelis took all the spoils of war from these cities for themselves, including their cattle and children. But they killed the men and every other living thing with their sword, until nothing that breathed was left alive.
And as the Lord had commanded his servant Moses, Moses gave his orders to Joshua. And Joshua did everything that Moses said, and he left nothing undone that the Lord had commanded Moses to do.
So Joshua took all the land, the hills, the south country, all the land of Goshen, the valley, the plains, the mountain and the valley of Israel.
All the way from Mount Halak, that goes up to Seir, to Baalgad in the Lebanon Valley under Mount Hermon. So, Joshua defeated, conquered, and killed all of their kings.
Joshua made war for a long time against those kings.
None of those cities made peace with Israel except for the Hivites who lived in Gibeon, and Joshua all of the others in battle.

Because the Lord hardened their hearts, so that they would come out to do battle with Israel. This was so Joshua could completely destroy and annihilate them, and they would receive no mercy, just as the Lord commanded Moses.
Then Joshua cut off the Anakims from the mountains of Hebron, Debir, Anab, Judah, and all the mountains of Israel. Joshua completely destroyed them, along with all of their cities.
There were no Anakims left in Israel except for in Gaza, Gath, and Ashdod.

So, Joshua took the whole land, just as the Lord told Moses it would happen. Then Joshua gave it as an inheritance to Israel according to the way that their tribes were divided up. Then the land rested from war.
These are the kings that Israel defeated when they took the land on the other side of the Jordan River, all the way from the Arnon River to Mount Hermon to the eastern plains, toward the rising sun.

King Sihon the Amorite lived in Heshbon, and he ruled from Aroer on the banks of the Arnon River, and from the middle of the river halfway up to Mount Gilead, all the way to the Jabbok River, which is along the Ammonite border.
From the eastern plains to the Sea of Galilee, all the way to the eastern shore of the Dead Sea, then toward east Beth-Jeshimoth, and southward to just below the slopes of Ashdoth-Pisgah.
And King Og of Bashan, whose citizens were the descendants of the giants who lived in Ashtaroth and Edrei.
King Og reigned over Mount Hermon, Salcah, all of Bashan all the way to the Geshurite and Maachathite borders, and half of Mount Gilead to the borders of King Sihon of Heshbon.
The Lord's servant Moses and the Israelis defeated them, and Moses gave their land to the Reubenites, Gadites, and the half tribe of Manasseh as their inheritance.

These are the kings that Joshua and the Israelis defeated on the west side of the Jordan River, from Baalgad in the Lebanon Valley all the way to Mount Halak which rises toward Seir. And Joshua gave these lands to the Israelis as an inheritance, which he divided up and distributed to their tribes.

And Joshua defeated the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and the Jebusites in the mountains, valleys, plains, springs, wilderness, and the south country. And the Israelis defeated the king's armies of the following cities.
The king of Jericho, and the king of Ai which is beside Bethel.
The king of Jerusalem and the king of Hebron.
The king of Jarmuth and the king of Lachish.
The king of Eglon and the king of Gezer.
The king of Debir and the king of Geder.
The king of Hormah and the king of Arad.
The king of Libnah and the king of Adullam.
The king of Makkedah and the king of Bethel.
The king of Tappuah and the king of Hepher.
The king of Aphek and the king of Lasharon.
The king of Madon and the king of Hazor.
The king of Shimron-Meron and the king of Achshaph.
The king of Taanach and the king of Megiddo.
The king of Kedesh and the king of Jokneam of Carmel.
The king of Dor along the coast of Dor and the king of Gilgal.
The king of Tirzah and the other thirty kings.
Now Joshua was old and worn-out, and the Lord spoke to him and said, "You are an old man and there is still much more land to take possession of.
This is the land that remains to be taken, all of Philistine and Geshuri.

From Sihor which is before Egypt, all the way to the borders of northern Ekron which belongs to the Canaanites. The five lords of the Philistines and the land of the Gazathites, Ashdothites, Eshkalonites, Gittites, Ekronites, and the Avites.
From the south, all the Canaanite lands, and Mearah that is beside the Sidonians to Aphek, to the Amorite borders.
All of the Giblite lands, all of Lebanon facing the rising sun, and from Baalgad under Mount Hermon to the entrance of Hamath.

I will drive out all the inhabitants from the hill country of Lebanon to Misrephoth-Maim, and all the Sidonians before the Israelis. And I will divide up the land by lot among them as an inheritance, as I have commanded you.
So I want you to divide up this land as an inheritance among the nine tribes, and the half tribe of Manasseh."

The other half tribe of Manasseh along with the Reubenites and the Gadites had already received their inheritance, which the Lord's servant Moses had given to them along the eastern shore of the Jordan River.
From Aroer along the banks of the Arnon river, along with the city in the middle of the valley, and the whole Medeba plateau all the way to Dibon.
And all of King Sihon's Amorite cities all the way to the Ammonite border, and he reigned in Heshbon.
Also Gilead, and the Geshurites and Maachathites territories, all of Mount Hermon, and all of Bashan all the way to Salcah.
Moses defeated and drove out King Og of Bashan's entire kingdom, he reigned in Ashtaroth and Edrei, and his people were the descendants of giants.
But the Israelis did not expel the Geshurites, nor the Maachathites, and they live among the Israelis to this day.
Levi's tribe was the only one that did not receive an inheritance, the sacrifices of burnt offerings to the Lord God of Israel are their inheritance, as he had told them it would be.
This is what Moses gave to Reuben's tribe as an inheritance to be distributed among their families.
The land from Aroer on the banks of the Arnon river, plus the city in the middle of the valley, and the whole plateau near Medeba.
To Heshbon and all the cities on the plains, including Dibon, Bamoth-Baal, and Beth-Baal-Meon.
And Jahaza, and Kedemoth, and Mephaath.
And Kirjathaim, Sibmah, and Zareth-Shahar on the mountain overlooking the valley.
And Beth-Peor, Ashdoth-Pisgah, and Beth-Jeshimoth.

And all the plains cities, and the entire kingdom of King Sihon of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon until Moses defeated him along with the princes of Midian, Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba, who were Sihon's princes in their home country.
The Israelis also killed the prophet Beor's son Balaam with the sword, along with the others that were killed.
The border of Reuben's descendants ran along the Jordan River, and his descendants' inheritance was distributed among their families, including their cities and villages.
This is the inheritance that Moses gave to Gad's tribe and his descendants to be distributed among their families.
Their border began at Jazer, and their lands included all of the cities of Gilead, and half of the Ammonite lands, all the way to Aroer near Rabbah.
The lands from Heshbon to Ramath-Mizpah and Betonim, and from Mahanaim to the border of Debir.

And in the valley, Beth-Haram, Beth-Nimrah, Succoth, and Zaphon. And what remained of King Sihon of Heshbon's kingdom to the eastern side of the Jordan River, whose border stretched all the way to the Sea of Galilee on the eastern side of the Jordan River.
This is what Gad's descendants inherited and distributed by their families, including their cities and villages.
This is the inheritance that Moses gave to the half tribe of Manasseh, to be distributed among their descendants' families.
Their lands stretched from Mahanaim throughout the entire kingdom of King Og of Bashan, and all the towns of Jair in Bashan, which is sixty cities in all.

And it included half of Gilead, Ashtaroth, Edrei, and the cities that belonged to King Og of Bashan. All of this was given to Manasseh's son Machir's descendants, or up to one half of Machir's descendants which was distributed by family.
These are the countries on the eastern side of the Jordan River near Jericho that Moses distributed to them as an inheritance on the plains of Moab.
But Moses did not give an inheritance to Levi's tribe, because the Lord God of Israel was their inheritance, as he had told them.
These are the countries that the Israelis inherited in Canaan that priest Eleazar, Nun's son Joshua, and the leaders of the tribes of Israel distributed among their fathers as an inheritance.
Their inheritance was chosen by lot for the nine and a half tribes, as the Lord had commanded through Moses.
Because Moses had given the inheritance on the other side of the Jordan River to the other two and a half tribes, but he gave no inheritance to the Levites among them.

Joseph's descendants became the two tribes Manasseh and Ephraim, so they gave the Levites no part of the land, except for the cities where they lived along with the city's fields and pastures for their cattle and herds.
The Israelis divided the land and did everything else just as the Lord had commanded Moses.

Then Judah's descendants went to Joshua in Gilgal, and Caleb who was the son of Jephunneh the Kenezite said to him, "You know what the Lord said about you and me in Kadesh-Barnea to Moses who was the man of God.
I was forty years old when the Lord's servant Moses sent me from Kadesh-Barnea to explore the land, and I brought him an honest report that was in my heart.
Nevertheless my brothers who went with me made the hearts of the people melt with fear, but I remained loyal to my Lord God.
And that day Moses swore to me and said, 'Surely the land on which you have walked will be yours and your descendant's inheritance forever, because you have completely followed my Lord God.'

And now, behold the Lord has kept me alive for the last forty-five years as he said he would when he spoke to Moses, while Israel wandered around in the wilderness and today, I am eighty-five years old.
But I am as strong today as I was the day that Moses sent me out, and my strength and readiness for war or for whatever else is to come, is the same as it was then.

So give me this mountain which the Lord spoke of in those days, for you have heard about the Anakims and their great walled cities who were there at that time. If the Lord is with me, I will drive them out as the Lord promised."
And Joshua blessed Jephunneh's son Caleb and gave Hebron to him as his inheritance.
So from that day until today, Hebron has belonged to Caleb who was the son of Jephunneh the Kenezite, because he completely followed the Lord God of Israel.
And Hebron used to be known as Kirjath-Arba which was named after the great leader Arba of the Anakims. And the land rested from war.

This was the inheritance chosen by lot for Judah's descendant's tribe and distributed by their families. The furthest part of their border stretched southward all the way to Edom in the Zin wilderness along the southern coast.
Their southern border started along the southern bay of the Dead Sea.
And it proceeded along the south side of Maaleh-Acrabbim and passed through to Zin and ascended over the south side to Kadesh-Barnea and passed through Hezron to Adar where it turned toward Karkaa.
From there it went toward Azmon, and then toward the Nile River, and down the river ending at the southern coastal sea.
And the eastern border was along the Dead Sea to the end of the Jordan River, and their northern quarter border stretched from the Dead Sea Bay at the furthest part of the Jordan.
The border turned toward Beth-Hogla north of Beth-Arabah and then to the stone of Bohan, which was named after Reuben's son.

The border went toward Debir from the Valley of Achor and northward toward Gilgal, which lies before the slope to Adummim on the south side of the river. Then it turned toward the waters of En-Shemesh and ended at En-Rogel.

From there the border went by Hinnom's son's valley just south of the Jebusites, which is also called Jerusalem Then the border went to the top of the mountain that lies westward before the Hinnom Valley, which is at the end of the valley of the northern giants.
And the border turned from the hilltop to the fountain at the Waters of Nephtoah, then turned toward the cities of Mount Ephron and Baalah, which is also called Kiriath-Jearim.
The border curved around western Baalah to Mount Seir, and passed along to the side of Mount Jearim, which is on the north side Chesalon, then down to Beth-Shemesh and on to Timnah.
And the border turned toward the northern side of Ekron, and the border turned toward Shicron, and then to Mount Baalah, and from there to Jabneel, then on to the Sea of Galilee where it ended.
And the western border stretched along the coast of the Mediterranean Sea. These are the boundaries of the lands of Judah's descendants, that stretch around their families.
And the Lord told Joshua to give some land from Judah's descendants' inheritance to Jephunneh's son Caleb, which included Arba's father's city Kirjath-Arba, which is also called Hebron.
And Caleb drove out the families of Anak's three sons Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai.
From there he went on to attack the inhabitants of Debir, which was formerly known as Kirjath-Sepher.
And Caleb said, "I will give my daughter Achsah's hand in marriage to whoever defeats and captures Kirjath-Sepher."
So Caleb's brother Kenaz's son Othniel captured it, and Caleb gave him his daughter Achsah to be his wife.
When she came to him, she urged him to ask her father for a field, and when she jumped off her donkey, Caleb asked her, "What do you want?"
She answered him and said, "I came to ask you for another blessing, because you have given me southern land, I also ask you to give me some water springs," so he gave her the upper and lower springs.
These are the lands given to the descendants of Judah's tribe which were distributed among their families.
The farthest cities given to Judah's tribe's descendants toward the southern coast of the Dead Sea in Edom were Kabzeel, Eder, and Jagur.
Then there was Kinah, Dimonah, Adadah,
Kedesh, Hazor, Ithnan,
Ziph, Telem, Bealoth,
Hazor-Hadattah, Kerioth-Hezron, which is also called Hazor.
And after that there was Amam, Shema, Moladah,
Hazar-Gaddah, Heshmon, Beth-Palet,
Hazar-Shual, Beersheba, Bizjothjah,
Baalah, Iim, Azem,
Eltolad, Chesil, Hormah,
Ziklag, Madmannah, Sansannah,
Lebaoth, Shilhim, Ain, and Rimmon, and in that territory there were twenty-nine cities and villages.
And the cities and villages in the valley were Eshtaol, Zoreah, and Ashnah.
Then there was Zanoah, En-Gannim, Tappuah, Enam,
Jarmuth, Adullam, Socoh, Azekah,
Sharaim, Adithaim, Gederah, and Gederothaim, and in that territory there were fourteen cities and villages.
Then there was Zenan, Hadashah, Migdal-Gad,
Dilean, Mizpah, Joktheel,
Lachish, Bozkath, Eglon,
Cabbon, Lahmam, Kithlish,
Gederoth, Beth-Dagon, Naamah, and Makkedah, and in that territory there were sixteen cities and villages.
Then there was Libnah, Ether, Ashan,
Jiphtah, Ashnah, Nezib,
Keilah, Achzib, Mareshah, and in that territory, there were nine cities and villages.
Then there was Ekron's towns and villages.
Ekron's land stretched all the way to the Mediterranean Sea and included all the land near Ashdod and its villages.
There was Ashdod and its towns and villages, Gaza and its towns and villages, as far as the Nile River, and along the coast of the Mediterranean Sea.
And in the mountains there was Shamir, Jattir, and Socoh.
Then there was Dannah, Kirjath-Sannah, which is also called Debir.
And Anab, Eshtemoh, Anim,
Goshen, Holon, and Giloh, and in that territory there were eleven cities and villages.
Then there was Arab, Dumah, Eshean,
Janum, Beth-Tappuah, Aphekah,
Humtah, Kirjath-Arba, which is also called Hebron, and Zior. There were nine cities and villages in that territory.
Then there was Maon, Mount Carmel, Ziph, Juttah,
Jezreel, Jokdeam, Zanoah,
Cain, Gibeah, and Timnah, and there were ten cities and villages in that territory.
Then there was Halhul, Beth-Zur, and Gedor.
Maarath, Beth-Anoth, and Eltekon, and there were six cities and villages in that territory.
Then there was Kirjath-Baal also called Kiriath-Jearim, and Rabbah, which were two cities and their villages.
In the wilderness there was Beth-Arabah, Middin, Secacah,
Nibshan, and the city of Salt, and En-Gedi, and there were six cities and villages in that territory.
And Judah's descendants could not drive the Jebusites out of Jerusalem, and the Jebusites live with Judah's people in Jerusalem to this day.

The land that was chosen by lot for Joseph's descendants to inherit went from the Jordan River near Jericho, to the eastern Jericho waters, then on to the wilderness that goes from Jericho and throughout Mount Bethel.
From there it goes from Bethel to Luz and passes along the borders of Archi to Ataroth.
And it descended westward toward the border of Japhleti, then to the coast of lower Beth-Horon to Gezer, and it ended at the sea.
So Joseph's sons, Manasseh and Ephraim received their inheritance.

These are the borders of the land that Ephraim's descendants received as their inheritance which was divided up among their families. Their eastern border stretched from Ataroth-Addar to upper Beth-Horon.
And the border went toward the sea to the north side of Michmethah, and from there it went eastward to Taanath-Shiloh and passed by its eastern border, and then on to Janoah.
From Janoah the border went down to Ataroth, then to Naarah and on to Jericho, and it ended at the Jordan River.
Then from Tappuah the border went westward to the Kanah river, and it ended at the sea. This is the land that the descendants of Ephraim's tribe inherited that was distributed among their families.
Plus all the cities and villages that were designated for Ephraim's descendants that was part of Manasseh's descendants' inheritance.
But they did not drive out the Canaanites living in Gezer, so the Canaanites live as slaves among the Ephraimites to this day.

There was also a plot of land chosen by lot to give to Manasseh's tribe because Machir was Joseph's firstborn son and he was also Gilead's father, and Gilead received the lands of Gilead and Bashan, because Machir was a man of war.

There was also a plot of land chosen by lot for the rest of Manasseh's descendants that was distributed among their families for Abiezer's descendants, Helek's descendants, Asriel's descendants, Shechem's descendants, Hepher's descendants, Shemida's descendants, and these were the names of Joseph's son Manasseh's male heirs.

But Zelophehad, who was Hepher's son, who was Gilead's son, who was Machir's son, who was Manasseh's son had no sons. But he did have daughters, and their names were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.

Zelophehad's daughters presented themselves to priest Eleazar, Nun's son Joshua, and the princes and said, "The Lord commanded Moses to give us an inheritance from our brothers allotment." So, Joshua gave them an inheritance, as the Lord had commanded.
Manasseh received ten additional plots of land chosen by lot in addition to Gilead and Bashan, which were on the other side of the Jordan River.
Because Manasseh's daughters were given an inheritance among his sons, and the rest of Manasseh's sons received the land of Gilead.
Manasseh's borders stretched from Asher to Michmethah near Shechem, then south to include the inhabitants of Tappuah.
Now Manasseh owned the land near Tappuah, but the city of Tappuah along the border of Manasseh's land belonged to Ephraim's descendants.

And the border descended to the southern side of the Kanah River, and Ephraim's cities are among the cities of Manasseh. But Manasseh's border stretched along the north banks of the river that flowed into the sea.
Ephraim's lands were to the south, and Manasseh's land was toward the north, with the sea as its border. Their borders met at Asher which was on the north side and Issachar on the east side.
Manasseh was given Beth-Shean, Ibleam, Dor, Endor, Taanach, and Megiddo along with their inhabitants, towns, and villages which were within the borders of Asher and Issachar.
But Manasseh's army could not drive out the inhabitants of those cities, so the Canaanites continued to live there.
So, when the Israelis had grown strong, they made slaves out of the Canaanites, but they could not completely drive them out.
One day Joseph's descendants spoke to Joshua and said, "The Lord has blessed us, and our people have multiplied and there are many of us. So, why have you given us just one small piece of land?"

Joshua answered them and said, "If the lands on Mount Ephraim are too small for your great people, then go out into the wooded countryside, and clear the land for yourselves in the land of the giants and the Perizzites.

And Joseph's people said, "Mount Ephraim is not enough land for us, and the Canaanites who live in the valley have iron chariots, and so do the people who live in Beth-Shean and its towns, and in the Jezreel valley."
So Joshua spoke to the people of Joseph's house and said, "Ephraim and Manasseh are a great people with great power, and you will not have only one plot.
