The mountain will be yours as well, and since it is covered with woods, you can clear it all the way to its furthest borders. And even though the Canaanites are strong and they have iron chariots, you can drive them out."
Then the entire Israelis congregation assembled together at Shiloh, and set up the congregation's tabernacle there, and the land was subdued before them.
There were seven Israelis tribes, which had not yet received their inheritance.
So Joshua spoke to the Israelis and said, "How long will you postpone going to take possession of the land, which your fathers' Lord God has given you?

Appoint three men from each of your tribes to send out to survey, explore, and map the land in accordance with each of their inheritances. When they are done, tell them to return and report back to me.
Tell them to divide it into seven parts, Judah's house shall remain within their southern borders, and Joseph's house will remain within their northern borders.
After you divide the land into seven parts, bring the maps to me, so that I may cast lots for your plots of land before our Lord God.

But the Levites will have no inheritance among you, because the Lord's priesthood is their inheritance. Gad, Reuben, and the half tribe of Manasseh have received their inheritance on the east side the Jordan River, which the Lord's servant Moses gave them."

And the men got up and left, after Joshua assigned them the job of mapping out and describing the land and he said, "Walk throughout the land, describe it, map it, and return to me, so that I may cast lots for your inheritance before the Lord here in Shiloh.

So the men traveled throughout the land mapping and describing its cities. They divided it up into seven parts which were recorded in a book. When they finished, they returned to Joshua and the people in Shiloh.
Then Joshua cast lots for the land before the Lord in Shiloh. Then he divided the land among the seven Israeli tribes and distributed it among their families.

And the first lot cast came up for Benjamin's tribe, and it was divided up in accordance with their families. The boundaries of their allotted tract of land was located between Judah's descendants and Joseph's descendants.
Their northern border stretched from the north side of the Jordan River to the northern side of Jericho, through the western mountains, and out to the Bethaven wilderness.

And the border crossed the Jordan River and went from there toward the side of Luz near Bethel. The border descended southward from there to Ataroth-Adar, near the hill on the south side of lower Beth-Horon.

Then the border was drawn southward around the sea, from the hill that lies south of Beth-Horon, and it ended at Kirjath-Baal, which is also known as Kiriath-Jearim, a city for Judah's people, and this was the western quarter.
The south quarter went from the end of Kiriath-Jearim, on out to the west, and then to the well at the Waters of Nephtoah.

Then the border descends to the end of the mountain that lies before the valley of Hinnom's son, which is in the valley of the northern giants. From there it descends into the Hinnom valley to the south side of Jebus, and on down to En-Rogel.

It was drawn from the north to En-Shemesh, and from there it went toward Geliloth, which is near the Ascent of Adummim. Then it descends to the stone of Bohan which was named after Reuben's son Bohan.
From there the border passed along the northern slope against Beth-Arabah, then down into the valley.
The border passed along to the north side of Beth-Hoglah and reached all the way to the north bay of the Dead Sea at the south end of the Jordan River. And this was the southern border.
Its eastern border ran along the Jordan River. These are the borders of the land that Benjamin's descendants inherited, that they divided among their families.
Now the names of the cities of Benjamin's descendants which were established by their family names were Jericho, Beth-Hoglah, and the valley of Keziz.
Then there was Beth-Arabah, Zemaraim, Bethel,
Avim, Pharah, Ophrah,
Chephar-Haammonai, Ophni, and Gaba were their twelve cities and villages.
Then there was Gibeon, Ramah, Beeroth,
Mizpah, Chephirah, Mozah,
Rekem, Irpeel, Taralah,

And Zelah, Eleph, and Jebusi which is also called Jerusalem, Gibeath, and Kirjath were their fourteen cities and villages. This is the land that Benjamin's tribe inherited and divided among their families.
Simeon drew the second lot for his tribe's inheritance, and it was divided among their families, and it lay within the boundaries of Judah.
Included in their inheritance was Beersheba, Sheba, and Moladah.
Then there was Hazar-Shual, Balah, Azem,
Eltolad, Bethul, Hormah,
Ziklag, Beth-Marcaboth, Hazar-Susah,
Beth-Lebaoth, and Sharuhen which were thirteen of their cities and villages.
Then there was Ain, Remmon, Ether, and Ashan which were four of their cities and villages.
And all of the villages surrounding these cities all the way to Baalath-Beer which is Ramath to the south. This was Simeon's tribe's inheritance, which was divided up among their families.

The Simeonite's inheritance was taken from the lands of Judah's descendants, because their share was too large for them. So, Simeon's descendants received their inheritance from within Judah's borders.
And the third lot cast came up for Zebulun's descendants, which was divided up based on the size of their families. And the border of their inheritance stretched all the way to Sarid.
Their border went toward the sea to Maralah, and it reached all the way to Dabbasheth and the river before Jokneam.
From Sarid it turned eastward toward the rising sun along the border of Chisloth-Tabor, and then on to Daberath and up to Japhia.
From there it passed along the east to Gath-Hepher and Eth-Kazin, then out to Remmon-Methoar toward Neah.
Then the border circled around the north side of Neah to Hannathon and ended in the Iphtah-El Valley.
Which also included Kattath, Nahalal, Shimron, Idalah, and Bethlehem and their twelve cities and villages.
These were the cities and villages that Zebulun's descendants inherited, which were distributed among them based on the size of their families.
The fourth lot cast came up for Issachar's descendants, in accordance with their families.
Their border stretched toward Jezreel and included Chisloth-Tabor and Shunem.
Then there was Haphraim, Shihon, Anaharath,
Rabbith, Kishion, Abez,
Remeth, En-Gannim, En-Haddah, Beth-Pazzez,
And their border reached to Tabor, Shahazimah, and Beth-Shemesh, and it ended at the Jordan River. There were sixteen cities along with their villages altogether.
These were the cities and villages that Issachar's descendants inherited, which were distributed among their families.
The fifth lot cast came up for Asher's descendants, which was distributed among their families.
Their borders included Helkath, Hali, Beten, Achshaph,
Alammelech, Amad, Misheal, and it reached westward all the way to Carmel and Shihor-Libnath.

Then it turned toward the rising sun and on to Beth-Dagon and it reached Zebulun. Then the border went on to the valley of Jiphthah-El toward the north side of Beth-Emek and Neiel, from there it passed by Cabul on the left.
And Hebron, Rehob, Hammon, Kanah, all the way to great Sidon.
Then it turned toward Ramah as far as the fortified city of Tyre, where it turned toward Hosah, and it ended at the sea's coastline in Achzib.
And it also included Ummah, Aphek, and Rehob, which were 22 cities and villages altogether.
These were the cities and villages that Asher's descendants inherited, which were distributed among their families.
The sixth lot cast came up for Naphtali's descendants, which was distributed among their families.
And their borders began at Heleph, and stretched from Allon to Zaanannim, then to Adami, Nekeb, and Jabneel as far as Lakum, and it ended at the Jordan River.

Then the coast turned westward to Aznoth-Tabor, and ran from there to Hukkok, and reached all the way to the south side of Zebulun, and it stretched all the way to the west side of Asher, then toward the rising sun to Judah along the Jordan River.
And the walled cities were Ziddim, Zer, Hamath, Rakkath, and Galilee,
Adamah, Ramah, Hazor,
Kedesh, Edrei, En-Hazor,
Iron, Migdal-El, Horem, Beth-Anath, and Beth-Shemesh, and there were nineteen walled cities and villages altogether.
These were the cities and villages that Naphtali's descendants inherited, which were distributed among their families.
The seventh lot cast came up for Dan's descendants, which was distributed among their families.
Included within the borders of their inheritance were Zorah, Eshtaol, Ir-Shemesh,
Shaalabbin, Ajalon, Jethlah,
Elon, Timnah, Ekron,
Eltekeh, Gibbethon, Baalath,
Jehud, Bene-Berak, Gath-Rimmon,
Me-Jarkon, and Rakkon, including the areas before Joppa.

When the borders of the land that Dan's descendants inherited became too small for them, they attacked and fought against Leshem. They captured and defeated them, then they took possession of and settled in the land of Leshem, and renamed it after their father Dan.
These were the cities and villages that Dan's descendants inherited, which were distributed among their families.
When the Israelis finished dividing up the borders of their lands, they gave Nun's son Joshua an inheritance from among their own inheritance.
And in accordance with the Lord's word, they gave him the city of Timnath-Serah on Mount Ephraim, where he rebuilt the city and lived there.

These are the inheritances, which priest Eleazar, Nun's son Joshua, and the leaders among the fathers of the tribes of Israel distributed by lot in Shiloh at the door of the congregation's tabernacle before the Lord. Then they were finished dividing up the country by lot.
The Lord also spoke to Joshua and said,
"Speak to the Israelis and say, 'Appoint cities of refuge for yourselves that I spoke to you about through Moses.
So that murderers who unintentionally and accidentally kill someone will have a place to flee. Those cities will be a city of refuge from the person who seeks blood vengeance against murderers.

When someone flees to one of those cities, they will stand at the city's entrance gate and declare their cause to that city's elders. The elders will accept them into their city and give them a place to live among them.

And if the blood avenger pursues them to the city of refuge, then the elders must not deliver the accused murderer into the avenger's hands, because it was an accident, and they had not intentionally killed anyone.

And they will be allowed to live there, until they stand before the congregation for judgment and the high priest at the time dies. After that the murderer will be allowed to return to their own city from where they had come, and they may return to their own home.'"
So they appointed Kedesh in Galilee on Mount Naphtali, Shechem on Mount Ephraim, and Kirjath-Arba in Hebron on Mount Judah as cities of refuge.

On the eastern side of the Jordan River by Jericho, they designated Bezer which was on the plains in the wilderness from Reuben's tribe, and Ramoth in Gilead from Gad's tribe, and Golan in Bashan from Manasseh's tribe as cities of refuge.

These were the cities of refuge appointed for everyone in Israel and foreigners traveling among them. So that if anyone accidentally kills someone, they will have a safe place to flee where they will be safe from the avenger of blood, until they stand trial before the congregation.
Then the leaders among the Levite fathers came to see priest Eleazar, Nun's son Joshua, and the leaders of the fathers of the tribes of Israel.

The Levite leaders spoke to Eleazar, Joshua, and the Israelis leaders at Shiloh in Canaan and said, "The Lord commanded through Moses, that you were to give us cities along with their adjacent fields and pastures for our cattle.
Then the Israelis did as the Lord commanded, and the Levites were given these cities chosen by lot, along with their fields and pastures to the Levites from their inheritance.
Thirteen cities were chosen by lot from the tribes of Judah, Simeon, and Benjamin for the Kohathite families, who were Levites that had descended from priest Aaron.
The rest of Kohath's descendants were given ten cities, chosen by lot from the families of the tribes of Ephraim, Dan, and the half tribe of Manasseh.
Gershon's descendants were given thirteen cities, chosen by lot from the families of the tribes of Issachar, Asher, Naphtali, and the other half tribe of Manasseh in Bashan.
Merari's descendants were given twelve cities, chosen by lot by from the families of the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and Zebulun.
And the Israelis gave all of these cities along with their fields and pastures chosen by lot to the Levites, as the Lord had commanded them through Moses.
And they were given these cities which are mentioned here by name, from the tribes of Judah and Simeon.
The first lot chosen, fell to Aaron's descendants from the Kohathite families.
They were given the city of Hebron located in the hill country of Judah, along with all the fields and pastures around it which came from Anak's father Arba.
But they gave the city's fields and villages to Jephunneh's son Caleb as his possession.
Priest Aaron's descendants were given Hebron along with its fields and pastures as a refuge city for murderers, and they were also given Libnah along with its fields and pastures.
Plus Jattir and Eshtemoa, along with their fields and pastures.
And Holon along with her fields and pastures, and Debir with her fields and pastures.
And Ain, Juttah, and Beth-Shemesh, along with their fields and pastures, which were nine cities from Judah and Simeon's tribes.
From Benjamin's tribe they were given Gibeon and Geba, along with their fields and pastures.
And Anathoth and Almon along with their fields and pastures, which were four cities.
Altogether there were thirteen cities, along with their fields and pastures given to these descendants of priest Aaron from Benjamin's tribe.
The other families of Kohath's descendants who were Levites were given cities, that were chosen by lot from Ephraim's tribe.
They gave them Shechem on Mount Ephraim along with its fields and pastures, as a refuge city where murderers could flee and live safely, and Gezer along with its fields and pastures.
And they were given Kibzaim and Beth-Horon along with their fields and pastures, which were four cities.
And they were given Eltekeh and Gibbethon from Dan's tribe, along with their fields and pastures.
And they were given Aijalon and Gath-Rimmon along with their fields and pastures, which were four cities.
And they were given Tanach and Gath-Rimmon along with their fields and pastures from the half tribe of Manasseh, which were two cities.
There were a total of ten cities along with their fields and pastures given to the remaining families of Kohath's descendants from Ephraim's tribe.

Gershon's descendants who were descended from Levi were also given cities with fields and pastures. They were given Golan in Bashan along with its fields and pastures, as a refuge city for a place that a murderer could flee and live safely. Plus Be-Eshterah along with its fields and pastures, which were two cities from the other half of Manasseh's tribe.
From Issachar's tribe, they were given Kishon and Dabareh, along with their fields and pastures.

They were also given Jarmuth and En-Gannim along with their fields and pastures, which were two cities from Issachar's tribe, plus the two cities from the other half tribe of Manasseh, which were four cities altogether.
From Asher's tribe, they were given Mishal and Abdon, along with their fields and pastures.
Plus Helkath and Rehob along with their fields and pastures, which were four cities from Asher's tribe.

They were also given three cities from Naphtali's tribe, including Kedesh in Galilee, along with its fields and pastures, as a refuge city for a place that a murderer could flee and live safely. They were also given Hammoth-Dor and Kartan, along with their fields and pastures.
Altogether there were thirteen cities, along with their fields and pastures, distributed among Gershon's descendants.
The remaining Levite families who were Merari's descendants, were given Jokneam and Kartah along with their fields and pastures, from Zebulun's tribe.
Plus they were given Dimnah and Nahalal along with their fields and pastures, which were four cities.
From Reuben's tribe, they were given Bezer and Jahaz, along with their fields and pastures.
And Kedemoth and Mephaath along with their fields and pastures, which were four cities.

And from Gad's tribe, they were given Ramoth in Gilead, along with its fields and pastures, as a refuge city for a place that a murderer could flee and live safely, plus Mahanaim along with its fields and pastures.
And Heshbon and Jazer along with their fields and pastures, which were four cities.
Altogether there were twelve cities chosen by lot that were given to the remaining Levites, who were Merari's descendants which were distributed among their families.
There were a total of forty-eight cities, along with their fields and pastures given to the Levite's from all of Israel's possessions.
Each of these cities had fields and pastures all around them.
So, the Lord gave Israel all the land that he swore to give their fathers, and they took possession of the land and lived there.
Then the Lord gave them the rest of the land he had promised to give their fathers. None of their enemies could stand before them, and the Lord delivered all of their enemies into their hands.
None of the good things the Lord promised the House of Israel failed, and they all came to pass.
Then Joshua summoned the Reubenites, Gadites, and the half tribe of Manasseh.
And he spoke to them and said, "You have done everything that the Lord's servant Moses commanded you, and you have obeyed every order that I gave you.
You did not abandon your brothers during all this time, and you have obeyed your Lord God's commandment's.
And now as your Lord God promised, he has given rest to your brothers. So return to your homes and the land, which the Lord's servant Moses has given you on the other side of the Jordan River.

But be careful that you observe and obey the laws and commandments that the Lord's servant Moses gave you which are: Love your Lord God, walk in his ways, keep his commandments, hold loyally to him, and serve him with all your heart, mind, and soul."
So, Joshua blessed them and sent them away, then they all went home.

Moses had given land in Bashan to the half tribe of Manasseh. But Joshua gave the other half tribe of Manasseh land from among their brothers on the west side of the Jordan River, then he blessed them and sent them home.

And Joshua spoke to them and said, "Return to your homes with abundant wealth, go home with your cattle, silver, gold, brass, iron, and clothes. And when you go home, share the spoils of war you have taken from your enemies with your brothers."

Then the Reubenites, Gadites, and half tribe of Manasseh left the Israelis in Shiloh in the land of Canaan and returned to their own country in Gilead. The land they were given was in accordance with the Lord's word which had been given to them through Moses.
When they reached the borders of Canaan near the banks of the Jordan River, Reuben and Gad's descendants, and the half tribe of Manasseh built a great altar there.
The Israelis got word that Reuben and Gad's descendants, and the half tribe of Manasseh had built an altar on the borders of Canaan by the Jordan River, on the Israelis side of the river.
And when the Israelis heard about it, the whole Israelis congregation massed their troops at Shiloh, to go to war against them.
And the Israelis sent priest Eleazar's son Phinehas to Gilead to see Reuben and Gad's descendants, and the half tribe of Manasseh.
He took ten princes with him, one from each family of the tribes of Israel, and each one was the head of their father's house among the thousands of Israelis.
So they went to Gilead and spoke to Reuben and Gad's descendants, and the half tribe of Manasseh and said,

"The Lord's whole congregation wants to know why you have committed this trespass against the God of Israel. Why have you turned away from him, and why have you built this rebellious altar against him?
Was the immorality of Peor not enough for us? Because you know there was a plague placed upon the Lord's congregation, and to this day we have not been cleansed of those sins.
But now you have turned away from the Lord, and when he sees you rebelling against him today, tomorrow he will be angry with the entire Israelis congregation.

If the land you inherited is unclean, then cross over to the land where the Lord's tabernacle lives and take possession of it. But do not rebel against the Lord or us by building an altar other that is not our Lord God's altar.
Did not Zerah's son Achan commit a trespass with the cursed thing, and God's anger fell on the entire Israelis congregation. For Achan was not the only one who perished for his immorality."
Then Reuben and Gad's descendants, and the half tribe of Manasseh answered the Israelis leaders and said,
"The Lord God is the God of gods, and he is our Lord God! He knows and Israel will also know, that if we have done this as a rebellion or transgression against him, then do not spare our lives today.
If we have built an altar and turned away from the Lord, or we have offered a burnt offering, bread offering, or peace offering, then let the Lord himself hold us responsible.
But we have in fact built this altar out of fear so that your descendants would not say, 'What do you have to do with the Lord God of Israel?
For the Lord has put the Jordan River between us as a border, and Reuben and Gad's descendants have no part of the Lord,' and your descendants will make our descendants stop fearing the Lord.
Therefore we said, 'Let us build an altar, not for burnt offerings nor sacrifices.

But to remind us, and our descendants after us, that we will worship the Lord with our burnt offerings, sacrifices, and peace offerings. Then in the future your descendants will be unable to tell our descendants, that we have had no part of the Lord.

So we said, 'When they tell our descendants in the future that we have had no part in the Lord, we can tell them about our altar to the Lord which our fathers built, was not for burnt offerings nor sacrifices, but it is simply a witness between us and you.'

God forbid we should turn away from the Lord and rebel against him today, by building an altar for burnt offerings, bread offerings, sacrifices, or to replace our Lord God's altar before his tabernacle."
So priest Phinehas and all of the Israelis congregation princes were pleased when they heard what Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh's descendants said.

Priest Eleazar's son Phinehas spoke to Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh's descendants and said, "Today we know that the Lord is among us, because you have not committed this trespass against him. Therefore, you have delivered Israel from the hand of the Lord."
Then priest Eleazar's son Phinehas, and all of the Israelis princes left Reuben and Gad's descendants in the land of Gilead and returned to Canaan. And they brought word of this to the people.

The people of Israel were pleased to hear this and they blessed God. They were happy that they did not have to go to war against Reuben and Gad's descendants, and they were happy that they did not have destroy the land where they lived.
So Reuben and Gad's descendants said, "This altar will be named Ed; for it is a witness between us that the Lord is God!"
A long time after the Lord had given rest to Israel from all their enemies that surrounded them, Joshua grew old and frail with age.
Then one day Joshua summoned all of Israel's elders, family leaders, judges, and officers, and said to them, "I am old and stricken with age.
You have seen everything that your Lord God has done to all of these nations because of you, because he is your Lord God who fought for you.

Behold, I have divided up by lot these remaining nations, along with all the nations that I cut off from the western side of the Jordan River all the way to the Mediterranean Sea, as an inheritance for your tribes.
Your Lord God will expel them and drive them out before you, and you will take possession of their land, as your Lord God has promised to you.
Therefore be very courageous and do everything written in the Book of the Law of Moses, and do not turn away from the Lord.
So do not associate with these remaining nations among you. Do not mention the names of their gods or swear by them, and do not serve them nor bow down to them.
But remain loyal to your Lord God, as you have done to this day.
For the Lord has driven out great and strong nations before you, and to this day no one has been able to stand against you.
One of you can chase a thousand fleeing before you, because your Lord God fights for you, just as he promised.
Therefore be very careful and make sure that you love your Lord God.

Otherwise, you may turn away from your Lord God, and cling to the remaining nations among you, then you will marry into their beliefs, you will be lured into their ways, and you will be bound to them.

So, know this for a certain, your Lord God will no longer drive these nations out from before you. But they will become snares and traps to you, and they will be an affliction in your sides and thorns in your eyes, until you perish from this good land that your Lord God has given you.

And behold, today I am going the way of all the earth, and you know with all your hearts, minds, and souls that not one of all the good things which your Lord God promised has failed you. Everything he promised you has come to pass, and not one thing has failed.

So it will come to pass, that just as all good things that your Lord God promised has come to you, so will all the evil things that he promised you, until he has destroyed you and completely removed you from the good land which he has given you.

If you transgress against your Lord God's covenant which he gave you, and you worship and bow down to other gods, then your Lord's anger will be kindled against you, and you will quickly perish. And God will completely remove you from the good land he has given you."
Joshua assembled all of the Israelis tribes to Shechem. He summoned their elders, family leaders, judges, and officers to present themselves before God.

And Joshua spoke to all the people and said, "This is what the Lord God of Israel says, 'Long ago before the flood, your fathers Terah, the father of Abraham and Nachor lived beyond the river, and they served other gods.
But I brought your father Abraham from the other side of the river, and led him throughout the land of Canaan, and multiplied his descendants, and I gave him Isaac.
And this is what I gave Isaac, Jacob, and Esau. I gave Mount Seir to Esau as his inheritance, but Jacob and his descendants went down to Egypt.
Then I sent Moses and Aaron, and I plagued the Egyptians with what I did there, then I brought you out of there.
I brought your fathers out of Egypt, but the Egyptians pursued them with chariots and horsemen to the Red Sea.'

When they cried out to the Lord, he put darkness between them and the Egyptians and brought the sea crashing down on them and covered them with water. Their eyes saw what God did in Egypt, and they lived in the wilderness for a long time.

I brought you into the Amorite's land who lived on the other side of the Jordan River where they fought you. But I delivered them into your hands, so that you could take possession of their land, and I destroyed them before you.
Then Zippor's son King Balak of Moab, rose up and went to war against Israel, and he summoned Beor's son Balaam to come and curse you.
But I would not listen to Balaam. So, all that Balaam could do was bless you over and over again, and I delivered you from Balak's hand.

And you crossed the Jordan River, and you went to Jericho and fought against the men of Jericho and the Amorites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hittites, Girgashites, Hivites, and the Jebusites, and the Lord delivered them into your hands.
And the Lord sent swarms of hornets which drove all of them out before you, including the two Amorite kings, but they were not defeated by your sword or your bow.
And I have given you a land for which you did not labor, and cities to live in which you did not build, and you will eat from their vineyards and olive groves which you did not plant.
So fear your Lord God, serve him with honest sincerity and truth, and put away the gods that your fathers served on the other side of the river and in Egypt, and serve your Lord God.

If it seems evil to you to serve the Lord, then you must choose who you will serve today, whether it is the gods your fathers served on the other side of the river, or the Amorite's gods where you live. But as for me and my house, we will serve the Lord."
And the people replied and said, "God forbid that we should forsake the Lord to serve other gods.

For our Lord God brought us and our fathers out of the land of the house of bondage in Egypt. And he did those great signs in our sight, and protected us wherever we went, and among all the people through whom we passed.
And the Lord drove out all the people, even the Amorites who lived in the land, so we will also serve the Lord, because he is our God."
And Joshua spoke to the people and said, "You cannot serve the Lord, because he is a holy and jealous God, and he will not forgive your transgressions or your sins.
If you forsake the Lord and serve strange gods, he will turn on you and bring disaster to you and consume you, even after he has done good things for you."
And the people replied to Joshua and said, "No, we will serve the Lord!"
Then Joshua said to the people, "You are witnesses against yourselves that you have chosen to serve the Lord," and they said, "We are witnesses."
And Joshua said, "So now put away the strange gods among you and incline your heart to the Lord God of Israel."
And the people said to Joshua, "We will serve our Lord God, and we will obey his voice."
So that day, Joshua made a covenant with the people in Shechem, and he gave them a law and legal decree.
Then Joshua wrote these words in the Book of the Law of God and set a great stone there under an oak tree near the Lord's sanctuary.

And Joshua spoke to all the people and said, "Behold this stone will be a witness for us, because it has heard all the words the Lord has spoken to us, and it will be a witness against you if you deny your God."
After that Joshua let all the people leave, and everyone returned to their own inheritance.
Then after all these things, Nun's son Joshua who was the Lord's servant died, he was a hundred and ten years old.
And they buried Joshua along the border of Timnah-Serah on the northern side of Mount Gaash, which was his inheritance on Mount Ephraim.
Israel served the Lord all the days of Joshua's life, and all the days of the elders who outlived him and those who had seen everything the Lord had done for Israel.

And Joseph's bones, which the Israelis had brought from Egypt, were buried in Shechem on a plot of land which Jacob had bought from Shechem's father Hamor's sons for a hundred pieces of silver. And it became an inheritance for Joseph's descendants.
And Aaron's son Eleazar died, and they buried him on a hill on Mount Ephraim which had been given to Eleazar's son Phinehas.
After Joshua died the Israelis spoke to the Lord and asked, "Who will be the first to go and fight against the Canaanites for us?"
And the Lord said, "Judah will go first because I have delivered the land into his hand."

Then Judah spoke to his brother Simeon and said, "Come up to my land which was chosen for me by lot, and help me fight the Canaanites. Then I will also go with you to your chosen lot." So Simeon went with him.
When Judah attacked the Canaanites and Perizzites, the Lord delivered them into their hands, and they killed 10,000 of them in Bezek.
When they found Adoni-Bezek in Bezek, they fought against him and killed the Canaanites and the Perizzites.
But Adoni-Bezek fled, so they pursued him and when they caught him, they cut off his thumbs and big toes.

Then Adoni-Bezek said, "I had my army cut off the thumbs and big toes of seventy kings, then I forced them to eat the scraps from my table. Now God has repaid me for what I have done," and they brought him to Jerusalem, where he died.
Now Judah's descendants fought against Jerusalem; they defeated and conquered it with the sword and set the city on fire.
Afterward Judah's descendants fought against the Canaanites who lived on the mountains, in the south, and in the valleys.
Judah also attacked the Canaanites that lived in Hebron, which had previously been called Kirjath-Arba, and they killed Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai.
And from there he attacked the people living in Debir, which had previously been called Kirjath-Sepher.
And Caleb said, "I will give my daughter Achsah in marriage to whoever defeats and conquers Kirjath-Sepher."
And Kenaz's son Othniel who was Caleb's younger brother conquered it, and he was given Caleb's daughter Achsah to be his wife.
One day she went to see Othniel to ask her father for a field, and as she was getting down from her donkey, Caleb asked her, "What do you want?"

She answered him and said, "I came to ask you for another blessing, because you have given me land in the south, I ask that you also please give me springs for water," So Caleb gave her the upper and lower springs.
The descendants of Moses' father-in-law the Kenite, left the city of palm trees with Judah's descendants and went out into the wilderness of Judah south of Arad to live among the people.
Judah and his brother Simeon went and killed the Canaanites that inhabited Zephath. They completely destroyed it, so they renamed the city Hormah.
Judah also captured Gaza, Askelon, and Ekron along with the lands around them.
The Lord was with Judah, and they drove out the mountain's inhabitants, but they could not drive out the valley's inhabitants, because they had iron chariots.
And as Moses had promised, Judah gave Hebron to Caleb, and he expelled the descendants of Anak's three sons.
But Benjamin's descendants failed to drive out the Jebusites that inhabited Jerusalem, so they live in Jerusalem with the Jebusites to this day.
Joseph's house also attacked Bethel, and the Lord was with them.
Joseph's house sent spies to observe Bethel, which had previously been known as Luz.
When the spies saw a man coming from the city they said to him, "Please show us the best way for our armies to enter the city, and we will show you mercy."
After he showed them the best way into Bethel, they defeated and conquered the city with the edge of the sword, but they let the man and his family go.
And the man went to the land of the Hittites, and he built a city that he named after Luz, which is still its name today.
Manasseh also failed to drive out the inhabitants of Beth-Shean, Taanach, Dor, Ibleam, and Megiddo, and their towns, fields, and pastures, because the Canaanites were determined to live there.
After Israel became strong, they made slaves out of the Canaanites, and they did not completely drive them out.
Ephraim also failed to drive out the Canaanites that lived in Gezer, but they allowed the Canaanites to live among them in Gezer.
Zebulun also failed to drive out the inhabitants of Kitron and Nahalol, but they allowed them to live among them as slaves.
Asher also failed to drive out the inhabitants of Accho, Sidon, Ahlab, Achzib, Helbah, Aphik, and Rehob.
So the Asherites lived among the Canaanites who inhabited the land, because they did not drive them out.
Naphtali also failed to drive out the inhabitants of Beth-Shemesh and Beth-Anath, so he lived among the Canaanites who inhabited the land, but the people there became their slaves.
The Amorites forced the Danites into the mountains, because they would not allow them to come through their valley.
The Amorites were determined to live on Mount Heres, and in Aijalon and Sha-Albim, but Joseph's house grew strong and prevailed, and the Amorites became slaves.
The Amorite border stretched from the rock of Akrabbim and upward.

An angel of the Lord came up from Gilgal to Bochim and said, "I brought you out of Egypt, and led you into the land that I promised to give to your fathers and I said, 'I will never break my covenant with you.
Do not make an alliance with these people, and tear down their altars,' but you did not obey my voice. What have you done?
So now, because of this, I will not drive them out before you, and they will be thorns in your sides, and their gods will be a snare to you."
When the angel of the Lord said all of these things to Israel's descendants, they all began to weep.
They named that place Bochim, and they offered sacrifices to the Lord there.
When Joshua let the people go, Israel's descendants returned to their own land which they had received as their inheritance.
And the people who had seen all the great works that the Lord had done for Israel, served the Lord as long as Joshua and the elders who outlived him were alive.
When Nun's son Joshua, who was the Lord's servant, turned 110 years old, he died.
And they buried Joshua on the northern hillside of Mount Ephraim in Gaash, along the border of Timnath-Heres.

After that generation passed away and went to be with their fathers, another generation rose up after them. This new generation of Israelis that rose up, did not know the Lord, and they had not seen what he had done for Israel.
Those Israelis descendants committed evil transgressions in the Lord's sight and served Baal.

They abandoned their fathers' Lord God who had brought them out of Egypt. They followed other gods, who were the gods of the people around them, and they bowed down to those gods which provoked the Lord's anger.
They abandoned the Lord and served Baal and Ashtaroth.

So the Lord's anger grew hot against Israel, and he delivered them into the hands of people that ruined them. He sold them into the hands of their enemies all around them, and they were no longer strong enough to stand before their enemies.
Wherever they went, the hand of the Lord was against them, and he brought disaster upon them. And they were greatly distressed, just as the Lord had promised them.
Then the Lord raised up judges, who delivered them from the hands of those who ruined them.

But they would not listen to their judges, and they went whoring after other gods, and bowed down to them. They had quickly turned from the ways of their fathers, who had walked obediently with the Lord as they obeyed his commandments, but this new generation did not.

When the Lord began to feel sorry for his people, because they were groaning and they were frustrated by those who oppressed them, he raised up a judge to protect them. And God was with that judge, who delivered them from the hands of their enemies until the judge died.

When that judge died, they returned to their evil ways, and they were more corrupt than their fathers. They followed, served, and bowed down to other gods, and they would not stop practicing their own selfish and stubborn ways.
The Lord's anger grew hot against Israel once again and he said, "Because these people have not listened to me, and they have broken the covenant which I gave their fathers.
I will no longer drive out before them any of the nations, that Joshua left behind when died.
This is how I will test whether or not the Israelis will keep and walk in the way of the Lord as their fathers did.
Therefore, the Lord left those nations intact, nor did he immediately drive them out or deliver them into Joshua's hands.
These are the nations that the Lord left to test the Israelis that had not experienced any of the wars in Canaan.
Just to teach the Israelis descendants about war, especially those who had never experienced war before.
These five rulers of all the Canaanites, Philistines, Sidonians, and the Hivites that lived on Mount Lebanon from Mount Hermon to the entrance of Hamath.
The Lord left these rulers to test whether or not Israel would keep the Lord's commandments, which God had given their fathers through Moses.
Israel's descendants continued to live among the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
And the Israelis men married the daughters of these people, and those people's sons married the Israeli daughters, and served their gods.
So the Israelis did evil in sight of the Lord, they forgot their Lord God and served Baal and Asherah.
Therefore the Lord's anger grew hot against Israel, and he sold them into the hand of King Chushan-Rishathaim of Mesopotamia, and the Israelis descendants served him for eight years.
When the Israelis cried to the Lord; God raised up Caleb's younger brother Kenaz's son Othniel, to be their deliverer.
The Lord's Holy Spirit came upon Othniel, and he was Israel's judge and he went to war. The Lord delivered King Chushan-Rishathaim of Mesopotamia into Othniel's hands, who prevailed against him.
And the land rested for forty years, and Kenaz's son Othniel died.
Then the Israelis did evil in sight of the Lord, so he gave King Eglon of Moab power over the Israelis, because they had done evil in his sight again.
King Eglon persuaded the Ammonites and Amalekites to join forces with him, and he attacked and defeated Israel, and took possession of the city of palm trees.
So the Israelis served King Eglon of Moab for eighteen years.
But when the Israelis cried to the Lord, the Lord raised up Ehud son of Gera, a lefthanded Benjamite as their deliverer. Then the Israelis sent Ehud to King Eglon of Moab with a present.
But Ehud made himself a double-edged dagger that was a cubit long, and he strapped it to his right thigh and hid it underneath his clothes.
And he brought the present to King Eglon of Moab, who was a very fat man.
After Ehud presented the present, the king sent the gift bearers away.

But when Ehud arrived at the stone quarries near Gilgal, he turned around and went back to King Eglon. When Ehud returned, he said, "O king, I have a secret message for you." The king then said to his servants, "Silence," and everyone standing near the king left.
Ehud approached the king who was sitting alone in his summer parlor and said, "I have a message for you from God," and the king got up out of his seat.
Ehud took the dagger from his right thigh with his left hand and thrust it into the king's stomach.
The blade's handled was covered by the king's fat which closed in around the blade, and he could not pull the dagger out of the king's stomach. And the king defecated all over himself.
Then Ehud closed and locked the parlor doors and left through the entrance hall.
After Ehud left, the king's servants came to the parlor, but its doors were locked and they said to each other, "He must be using the bathroom in his summer chamber."
They waited as long as they could and the king still had not opened the parlor doors. So, they went and got a key and opened the doors, and they saw their Lord lying dead on the floor.
While they were standing around waiting for the king to open the parlor doors, Ehud escaped and passed by the stone quarries and went on to Seirah.
When Ehud arrived on Mount Ephraim, he blew a trumpet and led the Israelis down the mountain.

And Ehud said to them, "Follow me, because the Lord has delivered your Moabite enemies into your hands." So, they followed Ehud down the mountain and captured the fjords of the Jordan River toward Moab, and they would not allow anyone to cross the river.
They killed about 10,000 valiant, lusty Moabite men, and nobody escaped.
So the Israelis conquered Moab that day, and the land rested for 80 years.
The Lord raised up Anath's son Shamgar after Ehud, who also delivered Israel and killed 600 Philistine men with an ox goad.
After Ehud died, the Israelis once again did evil in the Lord's sight.
Then the Lord sold them into the hands of King Jabin of Canaan who reigned in Hazor. Captain Sisera who lived in the Gentile city of Harosheth commanded King Jabin's armies.
The Israelis cried to the Lord, because King Jabin had 900 iron chariots, and he severely oppressed them for twenty years.
The prophetess Deborah who was married to Lapidoth judged Israel at that time.
She lived under the Palm of Deborah between Ramah and Bethel on Mount Ephraim, and the Israelis would come to hear her decisions.

Deborah summoned Abinoam's son Barak from Kedesh in Naphtali and spoke to him and said, "Did not the Lord God of Israel give you a command and say, 'March to Mount Tabor with 10,000 men from Naphtali and Zebulun.
Then I will lure Sisera, the commander of King Jabin's army along with his chariots and soldiers to the Kishon river and deliver them into your hands.'?"
And Barak replied to Deborah and said, "If you go with me then I will go, but if you do not go with me, then I will not go."
And Deborah said, "I will go with you, but the road you take will bring you no honor, because the Lord will sell Sisera into the hands of a woman," and Deborah got up and went with Barak to Kedesh.
So Barak summoned Zebulun and Naphtali to Kedesh, then he and Deborah left with 10,000 men.
Now Heber the Kenite, was a descendant of Hobab, who was the father-in-law of Moses moved away from the Kenites and pitched his tent on the plains of Zaanaim, which was near Kedesh.
When Sisera learned that Abinoam's son Barak had gone up to Mount Tabor.
He assembled all of his 900 iron chariots and summoned all of his soldiers from the Gentile city of Harosheth, and they marched to the Kishon river.

Then Deborah spoke to Barak and said, "Get up, because today the Lord has delivered Sisera into your hands, and the Lord has gone out before you!" So, Barak descended from Mount Tabor with his 10,000 men.
Then the Lord went before Barak, and humiliated Sisera along with his chariots and soldiers with the edge of the sword, and Sisera jumped off his chariot and fled on foot.
But Barak pursued the chariots and the soldiers all the way back to the Gentile city of Harosheth, then all of Sisera's soldiers fell by the sword, and none of them survived.
However Sisera fled by foot to Heber the Kenite's wife Jael, he wanted to hide in her tent because there was peace between King Jabin of Hazor and the house of Heber the Kenite.
Jael met with Sisera and she said to him, "Come in my Lord and do not be afraid." When he entered her tent, she covered him with a blanket.
Then Sisera said to Jael, "Can I please have a little water to drink because I am thirsty," and she gave him some milk to drink, then covered him up again.
Sisera spoke to Jael again and said, "Please stand in the tent door and if anyone asks if there are any men here, I beg you to tell them no."
Then Heber's wife Jael took a hammer and a tent stake and quietly crept into the tent as Sisera slept and drove the stake through his temples into the ground, and he died.

As Barak pursued Sisera, Jael came out to meet him and said, "Come with me, I have the man you are searching for." When Barak entered her tent, he saw Sisera lying there dead, with a tent stake through the temples of his head.
So God defeated King Jabin of Canaan before the Israelis that day.
And the Israelis prospered and prevailed against King Jabin of Canaan until they destroyed him.
Then that day, Deborah and Abinoam's son Barak sang this song,
"Praise you Lord for avenging Israel, when the people willingly offered themselves.
Hear this O Kings and listen O princes, as I sing praises to the Lord God of Israel.
Lord, when you left Seir and marched from the field of Edom, the earth trembled, the heavens dropped, and the clouds poured out their water.
The mountains shook all the way to Sinai before the Lord God of Israel.
In the days of Anath's son Shamgar and in the days of Jael, the highways were deserted and the travelers walked by the side roads.
Life for the villagers ceased in Israel, until I Deborah arose as a mother in Israel.
When they chose new gods, war came to their gates, and there was not a shield or spear found among the 40,000 Israelis.
My heart is with the governors of Israel, who willingly volunteered from among the people. Bless the Lord!
You who ride white donkeys, who sit in judgment and walk the road must ponder and speak,

Those who were delivered from the archer's noise in the places for drawing water, shall remember the Lord's righteous acts toward his people's villages in Israel. Then the Lord's people will go down to gates.
O Deborah, awake, awake and sing a song! O Barak son of Abinoam, arise and lead your captives to freedom!
Then the survivors were given dominion over the people's nobles, and the Lord gave me authority over the mighty.

Some came from Ephraim which is a land that used to belong to the Amalekites, and some came from Benjamin's people. Governors came from Machir, and writers that know how handle a pen came from Zebulun.
Issachar's princes were with Deborah and Barak, and he sent Issachar into the valley on foot. But Reuben's divisions thought great thoughts from their hearts.
Reuben, do you live among the sheep pens to hear the bleating flocks? For Reuben's divisions greatly searched their hearts.
Gilead lived beyond the Jordan River, and why did Dan's people remain in their ships? Asher stayed on the seashore and lived in his breached defenses.
Zebulun and Naphtali's people risked their lives in the high places of the battlefield.
Kings came and fought the kings of Canaan in Taanach by the waters of Megiddo, but they took no plunder of money.
They fought from heaven, the stars from heaven fought against Sisera.
The ancient Kishon river swept them away. O my soul, you have walked down with strength.
Then their horse hoofs were broken by their prancing mighty ones.
And the Lord's angel said, 'Curse Meroz, bitterly curse her inhabitants, because they did not come to help the Lord against the mighty.'
Heber the Kenite's wife Jael will be blessed above all other women in the tent.
Sisera asked for water and Jael gave him milk, and she brought him butter in a noble dish.
Jael took a tent stake in her left hand and the workmen's hammer in her right hand, and drove the tent stake through Sisera's head, when she pierced his temples.
He fell at her feet and laid there dead.
Sisera's mother looked out a window and cried out through the lattice and said, 'Why has Sisera's chariot not returned? What has delayed the return of his chariots?'
Sisera's mother kept telling herself, and her wisest ladies kept answering her and saying,

'Are they not speedily dividing the spoils of war and giving a girl or two to each man. Are Sisera and his soldiers not the victors who are collecting a plunder of multicolored colored cloth and embroidery to wear on both sides of their necks?'
O Lord, let all of your enemies perish, but let those who love you be like the sun when its brilliant light shines." And the land rested for forty years.
Then the Israelis did evil in the Lord's sight again, and he delivered them into Midian's hand for seven years.
The hand of Midian prevailed against Israel. And because of the Midianites, the Israelis prepared shelters in the mountains, caves, and strongholds.
And so it was that when the Israelis planted their crops, the Midianites, Amalekites, and the eastern people would come and attack them.
They would camp next to them and destroy the land's bountiful produce all the way to Gaza. They left no nourishment for the Israelis, nor for their sheep, oxen, and donkeys.

For the Midianites came upon them with their cattle and tents like a great swarm of locusts. There were so many of them with their camels that they could not be counted, and they entered the land to destroy it.
The Israelis had become greatly impoverished because of the Midianites, and they cried out to the Lord.
When the Israelis cried to the Lord because of the Midianites.
The Lord sent a prophet to Israel who said, "This is what the Lord God of Israel says, 'I brought you out of Egypt, and I freed you from the house of bondage.
I delivered you from the hands of the Egyptians who oppressed you, and I drove them out before you, and I gave you their land.'
And the Lord God said, 'I am your Lord God, and I told you not to fear the Amorite gods in the land where you live, but you did not obey my voice.'"

And the Lord's angel came and sat under an oak tree in Ophrah that belonged to Joash the Abiezrite. And Joash's son Gideon was threshing wheat near the winepress to keep it hidden from the Midianites.
And the Lord's angel appeared to Gideon and said, "You are a mighty man of valor, and the Lord is with you."

And Gideon replied, "Oh my Lord, if the Lord is with us, then why have all these things happened to us? And where are all the miracles that our fathers told us about when they told us that the Lord brought us out of Egypt? And now the Lord has forsaken us and delivered us into the hands of the Midianites."
Then the Lord looked at him and said, "Am I not sending you? So, take your strength and go save Israel from the hands of the Midianites."
And Gideon said to the Lord, "Oh my Lord, how can I save Israel? My family in Manasseh lives in poverty, and I am the least in my father's house."
And the Lord said to him, "I will be with you, and you will defeat the Midianites as one man."
And Gideon said to the Lord, "If I have found grace in your sight, then show me a sign that you are the one talking with me.
I pray that you will not leave until I return and bring my offering to set before you." And the Lord said, "I will stay until you return."
Then Gideon went and prepared a kid goat and unleavened cakes made with an ephah of flour, he put the meat in a basket and poured the broth in a pot and presented it to the Lord under the oak tree.
And God's angel said to Gideon, "Take the meat and unleavened cakes and lay them on this rock, and then pour out the broth." So, Gideon did what he was told.
Then the Lord's angel touched the meat and unleavened cakes with the staff in his hand, and fire flashed out from the rock and consumed the meat and cakes, then the Lord's angel left.
When Gideon realized that he was speaking to one of the Lord's angels he said, "O Lord God! Alas, I have seen an angel of the Lord face to face."
And the Lord said to Gideon, "Peace be to you, fear not, for you will not die."
Then Gideon built an altar to the Lord there and called it Jehovah-Shalom, and it is still in Ophrah of the Abiezrites to this day.
That night the Lord said to Gideon, "Take one of your father's young bulls, and a seven-year-old bull, and tear down your father's altar to Baal, and cut down the Asherah pole beside it.
Build an altar to your Lord God on top of this rock where it was ordered. Cut some wood from the Asherah poles and use it to build a fire to sacrifice the second bull as a burnt offering."
Then Gideon and ten of his servants did what the Lord had commanded him to do, but he could not do it during the day because he was afraid of his father, so he did it at night.

When the men from the city rose early in the morning, they saw that Baal's altar had been torn down, and the Asherah pole next to it had been cut down, and the second bull had been offered on the new altar.
And they asked one another, "Who has done this?" After they asked themselves over and over again, they decided that Joash's son Gideon had done it.
Then the city men said to Joash, "Bring us your son, so we can put him to death! He has torn down Baal's altar and cut down the Asherah pole next to it."

Joash replied to everyone and said, "Are you pleading for Baal? Do you have to save him? Whoever pleads for him must be put to death by morning, and if he is a God, let him plead for himself against whoever tore down his altar."
That day Joash called his son Jerub-Baal and said, "So let Baal plead against him, because he has torn down his altar."
Then all the Midianites, Amalekites, and the people from the east crossed the river and camped in the Jezreel valley.
But the Lord's Spirit came upon Gideon and he blew a trumpet, and Abiezer came to join him.
Gideon sent messengers throughout all Manasseh summoning the people to come join him. And Gideon also sent messengers to Asher, Zebulun, Naphtali, and they came to meet them.
And Gideon said to God, "If you intend to use me to save Israel as you said you would.

Then I will know you are planning to use me to save Israel when I put a wool fleece on the floor. If it is wet the next morning from the morning dew but the ground underneath it is dry, then I will know that you are planning to use me to save Israel, as you said you would."
So, Gideon got up early the next morning and squeezed the fleece together, and when he wrung the dew out of it, it filled a bowl full of water.

And Gideon said to God, "Do not be angry with me and I will only ask you this one more time, but I pray that you will please let me test this fleece one more time. This time let the fleece be dry and let the ground be wet with dew."
That night God did as he was asked, because the fleece was dry, and the ground was wet with dew.

Then Jerub-Baal, who is Gideon, and all the people with him got up early and set up camp beside the well of Harod. The Midianite armies were camped on their north side in the valley near the Hill of Moreh.

The Lord spoke to Gideon and said, "There are too many people with you for me to put the Midianites into their hands, otherwise the Israelis will boast about themselves and say, 'We were saved by our own hands.'
So go to your people and say, "Whoever is fearful and afraid can leave Mount Gilead and return home!" So, 22,000 soldiers returned home, but 10,000 remained.

And the Lord spoke to Gideon and said, "There are still too many soldiers, bring them down to the water, and I will separate them for you. Whoever I say is to go with you will go with you, and whoever I say is not to go with you will not go with you."
So Gideon brought the soldiers down to the water, and the Lord said to Gideon, "Whoever laps water with their tongue like a dog will be separated from those that bow down on their knees to drink."
There were 300 of them that lapped water like a dog, but the rest of them all bowed down on their knees to drink.
The Lord spoke to Gideon and said, "I will use the 300 men that lapped water like a dog to deliver the Midianites into your hands, and all the others can return home."

So, Gideon sent all of the Israelis except the 300 men back to their tents, but the 300 prepared their food and took the other people's trumpets. And the Midianite armies were below them in the valley.
That night, the Lord spoke to Gideon and said, "Get up and go down and attack the Midianites, because I have delivered them into your hand.
But if you are afraid to go down there, take your servant Phurah down there with you.

Go down there and listen to what they are saying to each other. Then you will know the best way to attack them." Then Gideon and his servant Phurah went down to the outposts of the Midianite army's camp.
The Midianites, Amalekites, and all the eastern people were arrayed along the valley like a swarm of locusts. They had too many camels to count, and their armies were like the sand on the beach.

When Gideon arrived in their camp, a man was telling his friend about a dream he had and he said, "I saw a barley bread cake come tumbling into our camp, and it hit the tent so hard that the tent overturned and collapsed."
His friend replied and said, "It is nothing but the sword of Joash's son Gideon a man of Israel, because God has delivered Midian and all of its armies into Gideon's hands."
When Gideon heard the dream and its interpretation, he worshipped the Lord and returned to the Israelis camp and said, "Get up, because the Lord has delivered the Midianite armies into your hands."
Then Gideon divided the 300 men into three companies, and he put a trumpet in each soldier's hand along with a pitcher containing a lit torch in their other hand.
And Gideon said to them, "Look at me, and when I get to their camp outposts, watch me and do what I do.
When I blow the trumpet, all of you must also blow your trumpets on every side of the camp, then shout, 'The sword of the Lord and Gideon is with us.'"

Gideon and the 100 men with him came to the camp outposts at the beginning of the middle watch. They blew their trumpets right after the changing of the guard, then they broke the pitchers in their hands.

The three companies blew their trumpets and broke their pitchers. They held the torches in their left hand and blew the trumpets with their right hand and shouted, "The sword of the Lord and Gideon is with us."
They stood their ground all around the camp and the Midianite soldiers panicked and cried as they fled.

When the 300 the trumpets sounded the Lord caused panic in the Midianite camp, and they turned their swords against each other. Then they fled to Beth-Shittah in Zererath and the Abel-Meholah border near Tabbath.
The Israelis soldiers from Naphtali, Asher, and Manasseh all pursued the Midianites.

Gideon sent messengers throughout all of Mount Ephraim and said, "Come down and attack the Midianites, and protect the waterways to Beth-Barah and the Jordan River. Then the soldiers from Mount Ephraim defended the waterways to Beth-Barah and the Jordan River.

They captured two Midianite princes, Oreb and Zeeb. They killed Oreb on the Oreb rock, and they killed Zeeb at the Zeeb winepress. They pursued Midian, and they brought the leaders of Oreb and Zeeb to Gideon on the other side of the Jordan River.
Then the men of Ephraim spoke to Gideon and said, "Why have you treated us this way? You did not call us for help when you went to fight the Midianites?" And they got violent with him.
And Gideon answered them and said, "What have I done compared to you? Are not the gleanings from the grape vines on Mount Ephraim better than the best harvests in Abiezer?
God delivered the princes of Midian, Oreb and Zeeb into your hands, and what can I do compared to you?" When he had said that their anger toward him abated.
Then Gideon and the 300 men with him arrived at the Jordan River and crossed over. Even though they were exhausted they continued to pursue the fleeing armies.
Gideon spoke to the men of Succoth and said, "Can you give some loaves of bread to my soldiers, because they are tired and hungry, and I am pursuing King Zebah and King Zalmunna of Midian."
But the Succoth princes asked, "Are the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna now in your possession, so that we should give bread to your army?"
And Gideon said, "When the Lord delivers Zebah and Zalmunna into my hands, I am going to tear the flesh off of your bones with thorns and briars from the wilderness."
Then Gideon went to Penuel and told them the same thing. And they gave him the same answer that the men of Succoth had given him.
When Gideon spoke to the men in Penuel he said, "When I triumphantly return here, I will tear down this tower."
Zebah and Zalmunna were in Karkor with their army of about 15,000 soldiers that were all that was left from the armies of the east. For 120,000 soldiers had already been slain in battle.
Gideon traveled the road that passed by the people who lived in tents east of Nobah and Jogbehah, and attacked and defeated their army, because they were taken by surprise.
When Zebah and Zalmunna fled, Gideon pursued them, and captured King Zebah of Midian and King Zalmunna, and they routed and embarrassed their entire army.
Joash's son Gideon returned from battle before sunrise.
They caught and interrogated a young man from Succoth, and he gave them the names and descriptions of the 77 leaders and elders of Succoth.

Gideon went to the men in Succoth and said, "Behold, Zebah and Zalmunna are here, and you rebuked me over them and said, 'Are Zebah and Zalmunna in your hands right now? Why should we give you bread for your weary men?'"
Then Gideon punished the city elders with thorns and briers from the wilderness to teach them a lesson.
And Gideon tore down the tower of Penuel and killed all the men in the city.
Then Gideon spoke to Zebah and Zalmunna and asked, "What kind of men did you kill on Mount Tabor?" And they answered him and said, "They were just like you, each one resembled the son of a king."
And Gideon said, "They were my brothers and my mother's sons. And as surely as the Lord lives, if you had not killed them, I would let you live."
Then Gideon spoke to his firstborn son Jether and said, "Get up and kill them." But the young man did not draw his sword, because was young and scared.
Then Zebah and Zalmunna said, "Get up and kill us yourself, show us what kind of a man you are!" So, Gideon got up and killed them and took the ornaments hanging around their camels' necks.
Then the men of Israel spoke to Gideon and said, "We want you, your son, and your son's son to rule over us, because you have delivered us from Midian's hands."
Gideon answered them and said, "Neither my son nor I will not rule over you, the Lord will rule over you."
But Gideon spoke to them again and said, "I would like to make a request of you, I would ask you to give me the earrings from your plunder, because they were Ishmaelites and they had gold earrings."
And they answered him and said, "We will gladly give them to you." And they spread a blanket on the ground, and each man threw the earrings from their spoils on the blanket.

Altogether the gold earrings that he asked for weighed 1,700 gold shekels, that was in addition to the ornaments, pendants, and purple clothing that belonged to the Midian kings, plus all the chains hanging around their camels' necks.
Gideon had an ephod made from it, and he kept it in Ophrah where he lived. But soon all of Israel went whoring after it there, and it became a snare to Gideon and his household.
This was how Midian was conquered by Israel. They never raised their heads again, and the land rested for forty years in the days of Gideon.
And Joash's son Jerub-Baal went home, where he lived in his own home.
Gideon fathered 70 sons because he had many wives.
Gideon also kept a concubine in Shechem, who gave birth to his son that he named Abimelech.
Joash's son Gideon died at a good old age and was buried in his father Joash's tomb, in Ophrah of the Abiezrites.
As soon as Gideon died, the Israelis turned away from God again, and went a whoring after Baal, and they made Baal-Berith their God.
And the Israelis forgot their Lord God, who had delivered them from the hands of their enemies on all sides.
And they did not show kindness to Jerub-Baal's house, for all of the good things he had done for Israel. Jerub-Baal was Gideon.
Jerub-Baal's son Abimelech went to Shechem to see his mother's brothers and her father's family, and he spoke to them and said,
"Please ask the men of Shechem, 'Would it be better for you for just one-man to reign over you or 70 of Jerub-Baal's sons?' Remember this, I also come from your flesh and bones.
Abimelech's mother's brothers spoke to the men of Shechem about Abimelech, and their hearts were inclined to follow him, because he was their brother.
Then they gave Abimelech seventy silver pieces from Baal-Berith's house, which he used to hire some vain and lazy people to follow him.
Abimelech went to his father's house in Ophrah, and on a single stone he killed 70 of Jerub-Baal's sons who were his brothers. But Jothan, Jerub-Baal's youngest son survived because he had hidden.
So all the leaders inside the city fortifications in Shechem went out to the plains of Shechem beside the pillar and made Abimelech their king.
When they told Jotham, he went and stood on top of Mount Gerizim and cried out to them in a loud voice and said, "Men of Shechem listen to me, so that God will listen to you.
The trees set out to anoint a king for themselves, and they said to the olive tree, 'Reign over us.'
But the olive tree responded to the trees and asked, 'Should I abandon what honors both God and man, just to be elevated above the trees?'
Then the trees responded to the fig tree and asked, 'Will you come and reign over us?'
But the fig tree responded and asked, 'Should I forsake my sweetness and good fruit, just to be elevated above the trees?'
Then the trees said to the vine, 'Will you come, and reign over us?'
But the vine responded and asked, 'Should I leave my wine, which cheers God and man, just to be elevated above the trees?'
Finally all the trees asked the thornbush, 'Will you come, and reign over us?'
But the thornbush said, 'If you truly want to anoint me king over you, then come and put your trust in my shadow. If not, let fire come from the thornbush, and devour the cedars of Lebanon.'
So, if you have truly and sincerely made Abimelech your king, and you have dealt well with Jerub-Baal and his household, and you have treated him as he deserves to be treated.
Because my father fought for and risked his life for you, and he delivered you from the hand of Midian.

And you have risen up against my father's house today and killed 70 of his sons on one stone. Then you made the son of Jerub-Baal's female servant Abimelech, king over the men of Shechem, because he is your brother.
If you have dealt truly and sincerely with Jerub-Baal and his household today, then rejoice in Abimelech and let him rejoice in you.
But if not, let fire come from Abimelech, and devour the men of Shechem and Millo, and let fire come out from the men of Shechem and Millo, and devour Abimelech."
Then Jotham fled to Beer, where he lived because he feared his brother Abimelech.
After Abimelech had reigned over Israel for three years,
God sent an evil spirit to come between Abimelech and the Shechem men, and they began to deal deceitfully with Abimelech.

In order to bring justice for the cruelty done to Jerub-Baal's seventy sons. So that vengeance for their blood was taken against their brother Abimelech and the Shechem men who helped him kill his brothers.
Then the Shechem men sent outlaws to ambush Abimelech in the mountains, and they robbed everyone that came through there, and Abimelech was told about it.
Ebed's son Gaal went with his brothers and crossed into Shechem, and the men there put their trust in Gaal.
After they went out into the fields to gather grapes from their vineyards, they trampled them to make wine. Then they went into their God's house and ate, drink, and made merry and cursed Abimelech.

Then Ebed's son Gaal said, "Who is Abimelech and who is Shechem, and why should we serve him? Is he not the son of Jerub-Baal, and is not Zebul his officer? We must serve the men of Hamor, who was Shechem's father. Why should we serve Abimelech?
If God would only put these people under my authority, I would remove Abimelech!" And I would say to Abimelech, "Muster your army and come out!"
When Zebul the city ruler heard what Ebed's son Gaal had said, his anger was kindled.
He secretly sent messengers to Abimelech and said, "Ebed's son Gaal and his brothers have come to Shechem, and they are fortifying the city against you.
You must bring your soldiers at night and set an ambush in the field.
Then that morning you can get up at sunrise and march on the city, when Gaal and his men come out against you, you may do to them whatever you see fit."
So Abimelech and his soldiers left at night and divided into in four companies, then they laid in wait against Shechem.
Ebed's son Gaal went and stood in the entrance of the city gates, as Abimelech and his men were getting up and coming out of hiding.
When Gaal saw the people, he said to Zebul, "Behold, people are coming down from the mountains," But Zebul replied to him and said, "The mountain shadows look like men to you."
Gaal spoke again and said, "Look people are coming down through the middle of the land, and another company is coming through the Plain of Meonenim."

Then Zebul replied to him and said, "Where is your gloating mouth now, I heard that you said, 'Who is Abimelech, and why should we serve him?' Are these not the people that you despise? So, go and fight them now!"
So, Gaal went and fought against Abimelech and the Shechem men.
But Gaal fled and Abimelech chased him all the way back to the entrance of the city gates, and many were overthrown and wounded.
Afterwards Abimelech lived in Arumah, and Zebul drove Gaal and his brothers out of Shechem.
The next day, the Shechem people went out into the field, and Abimelech was told about this.
Abimelech divided his men into three companies and laid in wait out in the field. When he saw the people coming out of the city, he rose up and attacked them.
Abimelech and the company with him rushed forward, and they stood their ground at the entrance of the city gates, and the two other companies rushed the people out in the fields and killed them all.
Abimelech fought against the city all day long, and he captured it and killed its people, then he demolished the city and sowed it with salt.
When the leaders in the Shechem tower heard what was happening, they entered the temple of El-Berith.
Abimelech was told about all the men that had gathered together in the Shechem tower.

So Abimelech went up into Mount Zalmon with his men, and he took an axe and cut a branch from the trees and laid it on his shoulder. Then he spoke to everyone with him and said, "Go quickly and do what I have done."

Abimelech's men then cut their own branches and followed him back to the Shechem tower, and they piled them up against the tower and set them on fire, and about 1,000 men and women were burned alive in the tower.
After that Abimelech went to Thebez, where he set up camp, then he attacked and captured Thebez.
But there was a strong tower inside the city where all the men and women there fled. Then everyone in the city locked themselves into the tower and climbed up to its top floors.
Abimelech approached the tower entrance to attack it, and he set it on fire.
A woman in the tower threw a piece of millstone at Abimelech's head and smashed his skull.
Then he called one of his young armor-bearers to him and said, "Draw your sword and kill me, so that nobody can say that a woman killed me," and the young man thrust him through and he died.
When the Israelis men saw that Abimelech was dead, they all left and returned to their own home.
This was how God repaid Abimelech for the wickedness he had done to his father, by killing his seventy brothers.
And God also put the evil that the Shechem men had done back on their own heads, and the curse of Jerub-Baal's son Jotham was on them.
After Abimelech died, Puah's son Tola, son of Dodo from Issachar's tribe who lived in Shamir on Mount Ephraim, rose up to defend Israel.
He judged Israel for 23 years, and he was buried in Shamir when he died.
After Tola died, Jair rose up from Mount Gilead, and judged Israel for 22 years.
Jair had 30 sons that rode on 30 donkeys, and they had 30 cities in the land of Gilead, which are called Havoth-Jair to this day.
Jair died and was buried in Camon.

Then the Israelis did evil in the Lord's sight again. They served Baal, Ashtaroth, and the gods of Syria, Sidon, Moab, the Ammonites, and the Philistines. They abandoned the Lord and did not serve him.
The Lord's anger grew hot against Israel, and he sold them into the hands of the Philistines and the Ammonites.

That year the Philistines and Ammonites began to frustrate and oppress all of the Israelis on Mount Gilead on the other side of the Jordan River in the land of the Amorites. And they continued this oppression for eighteen years.
The Ammonites also crossed the Jordan to fight against Judah, Benjamin, and the house of Ephraim so that Israel was in deep distress.
And the Israelis cried out to the Lord and said, "We have sinned against you, both because we have forsaken our God, and we have also served Baal."
And the Lord spoke to the Israelis and said, "Did I not deliver you from the Egyptians, the Amorites, the Ammonites, and the Philistines?
And the Sidonians, the Amalekites, and the Maonites who oppressed you, and you cried to me, and I delivered you from their hands.
Yet you have forsaken me and served other gods, so I will no longer deliver you.
Go and cry to the gods you have chosen and let them deliver you from the time of tribulation."
Then the Israelis said to the Lord, "We have sinned, do to us whatever seems good to you, but we pray that you will deliver us today."
And the Israelis got rid of their strange gods and served the Lord, and the Lord's soul was grieved by their misery.
Then the Ammonites gathered together and set up camp on Mount Gilead, and the Israelis assembled their people together and camped in Mizpah.
And the rulers of Mount Gilead said one to another, "Whoever attacks the Ammonites, will be the leader of all the people who live on Mount Gilead."
Jephthah from Mount Gilead was a mighty man of valor, he was the son of a whore and Gilead was his father.
Gilead's wife gave birth to his sons and they grew up. They defeated Jephthah and said to him, "You will not inherit from our father's house because you are the son of a different woman."
Then Jephthah fled from his brothers and settled in the land of Tob, where he attracted vain men who traveled with him.
As time passed, Ammon's descendants went to war against Israel.
When Ammon's descendants declared war against Israel, Gilead's elders went to fetch Jephthah from Tob.
They asked Jephthah to come and take control of their army, so they could fight and defeat Ammon's descendants.
Then Jephthah spoke to the elders of Gilead and said, "Did you not hate me and expel me from my father's house? Why do you come to me now when you are in distress and need my help?"
Gilead's elders spoke to Jephthah and said, "The reason we turn to you now, is so that you may go with us to fight the Ammonites. Then you will be our leader and rule over everyone in Gilead."
And Jephthah replied to Gilead's elders and asked, "If I return home with you to fight the Ammonites, and the Lord delivers them into my hands, will you really allow me to be your leader?"
And the elders of Gilead answered Jephthah and said, "The Lord will be our witness between us, if we do not do whatever you say."
Then Jephthah went with Gilead's elders, and the people made him their leader, and Jephthah repeated all of his conditions before the Lord in Mizpah.
Then Jephthah sent messengers to the Ammonite king and said, "Why have you come to my land and attacked me?"

The Ammonite king answered Jephthah's messengers and said, "Because the Israelis stole my land when they came here from Egypt. They took everything from the Arnon river all the way to the Jabbok and the Jordan Rivers. Therefore, I am now giving you a chance to restore those lands peaceably."
Jephthah sent messengers back to the Ammonite king.
Who said this is what Jephthah says, "Israel did not take the land from the Moabites or the Ammonites.
But, when Israel came up from Egypt and walked through the wilderness to the Red Sea and came to Kadesh.

Israel sent messengers to the king of Edom and said, 'Please let me pass through your land. But the king of Edom would not listen, and they also sent messengers to the king of Moab, but he would not consent.' So, Israel settled in Kadesh.

Then the Israelis traveled through the wilderness around the lands of Edom and Moab and camped on the east side of Moab on the other side of the Arnon river. But they did not cross the border or go into Moab, because the Arnon river was the border of Moab.
And Israel sent messengers to King Sihon of the Amorites from Heshbon who said, 'Please let us pass through your land to our home.'
