But Sihon did not trust Israel to pass through his borders, so he assembled his troops and camped in Jahaz where he attacked Israel.
Then Israel's Lord God delivered Sihon and all of his troops into the hands of the Israelis, and they defeated him. So, the Lord God gave the land from the Amorites who lived there to the Israelis.
And they took possession of all the land within the Amorite borders, from the Arnon river all the way to the Jabbok River, and from the wilderness all the way to the Jordan River.
So now that Israel's Lord God has driven the Amorites out of the land before his people of Israel, should it now be given to you?
Do you not own what your God Chemosh has given to you? Because our Lord God gives us whatever he wants us to have.
Are you that much better than Zippor's son King Balak of Moab? Did he ever struggle or fight against Israel?
Israel has lived in Heshbon and Aroer and their towns, and all the cities along the banks of the Arnon river for 300 years? Why did you not take the land at that time?
So I have not sinned against you, but you have done me wrong by waging war against me and my Lord, the judge who will be the judge between us today."
However the Ammonite king did not listen to Jephthah's message.
Then the Spirit of the Lord came upon Jephthah, and he passed through Gilead and Manasseh then through Mizpah of Gilead, and from there he approached the Ammonites.
And Jephthah made a promise to the Lord and said, "If you deliver the Ammonites into my hands.
Then whatever comes out of the door of my house to meet me when I return in peace from fighting the Ammonites, I will give to the Lord and offer it up as a burnt offering."
So Jephthah crossed over to fight against the Ammonites, and the Lord delivered them into his hands.
He defeated them from Aroer all the way to Minnith. He slaughtered 20 of their cities all the way to the plains of their vineyards. This was how the Lord defeated the Ammonites before the Israelis.
When Jephthah arrived at his house in Mizpah, his daughter, who was his only child came out dancing with tambourines to meet him.

When Jephthah saw her, he tore his clothes and said, "Alas, not my only daughter! You have brought me to my knees, and you have brought me great misery, because I have opened my mouth, and I have made a promise to the Lord, that I cannot take back!"

And she said to Jephthah, "Father, if you have made a promise to the Lord, you must do to me what you promised the Lord you would do, because the Lord has taken vengeance for you against your Ammonite enemies."
And she said to her father, "Let me do this one thing, let me wander around the mountains with my companions for two months, and mourn my virginity."
And Jephthah replied to her and said, "Go then," and he sent her away. Then she and her companions wandered around the mountains and grieved her virginity for two months.
After the two months, she returned to her father, and Jephthah did to her what he promised the Lord he would do. And she had never had sex with a man, because it was the custom in Israel.
So now the daughters of Israel go yearly to mourn Jephthah's daughter from Mount Gilead for four days every year.

Then the men of Ephraim assembled their troops and went northward and said to Jephthah, "Why have you crossed over to fight against the Ammonites without asking us to go with you? We are going to burn your house to the ground, with you in it."
Jephthah answered them and said, "My people and I were involved in a great conflict with the Ammonites, and when I called on you, you did not deliver me from their hands.
When I saw that you would not help me, I risked my life to cross over and confront the Ammonites. The Lord delivered them into my hands, so why then have you come to fight against me today?"

Then Jephthah assembled all of his troops together in Gilead and they fought Ephraim, and the Gilead army defeated Ephraim. The Ephraimites said, "You Gileadites are fugitives living among the descendant of Ephraim and Manasseh."

The Gileadites captured the passages of the Jordan River before the Ephraimites. When the Ephraimites tried to escape and said, "Please let me pass," the men of Gilead would ask him, "Are you an Ephraimite?" And he would say, "No."

Then they spoke to him again and said, "Please say Shibboleth," and if he said, "Sibboleth," because he could not pronounce it properly. Then they killed him at the passages of the Jordan River, and 42,000 Ephraimites were killed there at that time.
Jephthah from Mount Gilead judged Israel for six years, then he died and was buried in one of Mount Gilead's cities.
After Jephthah died, Ibzan of Bethlehem judged Israel.
Ibzan had 30 sons and 30 daughters, and he sent his daughters abroad, and imported 30 daughters from abroad for his sons, and he judged Israel for seven years.
Then Ibzan died and was buried in Bethlehem.
After Ibzan died, Elon the Zebulonite judged Israel for ten years.
Then Elon the Zebulonite died and was buried in Aijalon in the country of Zebulun.
After Elon died, Abdon the son of Hillel a Pirathonite judged Israel.
He had 40 sons and 30 nephews that rode on 70 donkeys, and he judged Israel for eight years.
Then Abdon the son of Hillel the Pirathonite died and was buried in Pirathon in the land of Ephraim on Mount Amalekite.
The Israelis did evil in the Lord's sight again, and he delivered them into the hands of the Philistines for 40 years.
A certain Danite man named Manoah from Zorah was married to a woman that could not have children.
An angel of the Lord appeared to the woman and spoke to her and said, "Behold, you are barren and cannot bear children, but you will conceive and give birth to a son.
Therefore, please do not drink any wine or strong drink, and do not eat anything unclean.

For Behold, you will conceive and give birth to a son, and no razor will ever touch his head. For the child will be a Nazarite to God from the womb, and he will begin to deliver Israel from the hands of the Philistines."
Then the woman went to her husband and said, "A man of God came to me, and he appeared like a very terrible angel of Go. I did not ask him where he was from, and he did not tell me his name.

But he spoke to me and said, 'Behold you will conceive and give birth to a son. You must not drink any wine or strong drink, nor eat anything unclean, because the child will be a Nazarite to God from the womb to the day he dies.'"
Then Manoah pleaded with the Lord and said, "O my Lord, let the man of God you sent, come back to us and teach us how to raise the child who is to be born."
God heard and listened to Manoah, and the angel of God returned to the woman as she sat out in the field, but her husband Manoah was not with her.
And the woman hurriedly ran to her husband and said, "Behold the man who came to me the other day has returned!"
So Manoah got up and followed his wife back out into the field, and he approached the man and said, "Are you the man who spoke to my wife the other day?" And he said, "I am."
Then Manoah asked him, "When your words come to pass, how can we teach and show the boy his life's mission?"
And the Lord's angel answered Manoah and said, "Make sure that your wife does not do any of the things I warned her about.
She must not eat anything that comes from a vine, she must not drink any wine or strong drink, nor eat anything unclean. And she must observe everything that I warned her about."
And Manoah said to the Lord's angel, "I ask you to please stay with us until we have prepared a kid goat for dinner."

And the Lord's angel replied to Manoah and said, "Even if I wait for your dinner, I will not eat your food, and if you prepare a burnt offering, you must offer it to the Lord." For Manoah did not know that the man was the Lord's angel.
Then Manoah spoke the Lord's angel again and asked, "What is your name, so that when what you have said comes to pass, we may honor you?"
The Lord's angel replied to him and said, "Why do you ask my name, since it is a secret?"
Then Manoah took a kid goat along with a bread offering, and offered it on a rock to the Lord, and as Manoah and his wife watched, the Lord's angel did an amazing thing.
As the flame rose up from the altar toward heaven, the Lord's angel ascended in the flame, and when Manoah and his wife saw this, they fell facedown on the ground.
And the Lord's angel never appeared to Manoah and his wife again. Then Manoah knew that he was the Lord's angel.
Then Manoah spoke to his wife and said, "We will surely die, because we have seen God."

But his wife said to him, "If the Lord wanted to kill us, he would not have accepted the burnt offering and bread offering from our hands. And he would not have shown us all these things, nor would he have told us about these things at this time."
The woman gave birth to a son and named him Samson, and as the child grew, the Lord blessed him.
And at times, the Lord's spirit began to move in Samson at Dan's camp between Zorah and Eshtaol.
Samson went down to Timnah one day, where he saw a Philistine woman.
And Samson went to his father and mother and said, "I have seen a Philistine woman in Timnah, and I want to ask her to be my wife."

Then Samson's father and mother said to him, "Can you not find a woman among your brother's daughters, or among our people? Must you take a wife from the uncircumcised Philistines?" And Samson replied to his father and said, "Get her for me, for she is pleasant to me."

But Samson's father and mother did not know that this was of the Lord. They did not know that the Lord was seeking an occasion to move against the Philistines; for at that time the Philistines ruled over Israel.
Then Samson along with his father and mother went down to the vineyards of Timnah, and a young lion roared and charged Samson.
And the Lord's spirit came upon Samson very powerfully, and he tore the lion apart with his bare hands as if it were a kid goat. But he did not tell his father or mother about it.
Then Samson went down and talked with the woman, and he was well pleased with her.
Later when Samson returned to take her, he saw the lion's carcass laying on the side of the road, and there was a swarm of bees and honey in its carcass.
Samson took some of the honey and ate some of it on his way to father and mother. He gave his parents some honey to eat, but he did not tell them that he had taken it from the lion's carcass.
So his father went to see the woman, and Samson prepared a feast there because that's what the young men used to do in those days.
When the Philistines saw Samson, they brought 30 men to accompany him.
Samson spoke to them and said, "Now, I will tell you a riddle; if you can solve it for me during the next seven days of feast, I will give you 30 sheets and 30 garments.
But if you cannot tell me what it means, then you must give me 30 sheets and 30 garments." And they said to him, "Tell us your riddle, we want to hear it."
So Samson told them the riddle and said, "From the eater came meat to eat, and from the strong came something sweet." But after three days they still could not explain the meaning of the riddle.

Then on the seventh day they spoke to Samson's wife and said, "Entice your husband into explaining the riddle for us, or we will burn you and your father's house! Did you invite us here to take advantage of us and take what we have?"

And Samson's wife wept before him and said, "You do not love me you hate me! You told my people a riddle, but you did not explain it to me." And he said to her, "Behold, I have not even explained it to my father and mother, so why would I tell you?"
She was so upset that she wept before him for the seven days of their feast. So, on the seventh day Samson finally answered the riddle for her, then she went and explained it to her people.

Before sunset on the seventh day, the men of the city went to answer Samson and said, "What is sweeter than honey and stronger than a lion?" And Samson said to them, "If you had not plowed with my heifer, you would not have solved my riddle!"

Then the Lord's spirit came upon Samson, and he went down to Ashkelon where he killed 30 of their men. He took their clothes and gave them to the men who had solved his riddle. And he was burning with anger when he returned to his father's house.
But Samson's wife was given to his companion, whom he thought was his friend.

But after a while, during the time of the wheat harvest, Samson prepared a kid goat and took it with him to visit his wife and he said to her father, "I want to visit my wife in her bedroom." But her father would not let him see her.
And her father said, "I honestly thought that you hated her, so I gave her to your friend. Do you not think that her younger sister is prettier than her? Please take her instead of her older sister."
Samson replied to them and said, "No, this time I will be blameless for the displeasure I cause the Philistines."
And Samson went and caught 300 foxes, and took torches, and tied the foxes tail to tail, and put a torch between their two tails.
Then he lit the torches and released the foxes into the Philistines standing wheat so that their stored grain, standing wheat, vineyards, and olive groves were completely burned up.

Then the Philistines asked, "Who did this?" They answered themselves and said, "It was the Timnite's son-in-law Samson, because they gave his wife to his friend." So, they went and burned her and her father to death.
And Samson said to them, "Even though you have done this, I will not stop until I have taken revenge against you."
Then Samson mercilessly attacked and slaughtered them, and he went to live on top of the rock of Etam.
After that the Philistines moved and camped in Judah; they spread out from there into Lehi.
And the men of Judah asked them, "Why have you invaded us?" And they answered, "We have come to capture Samson, and repay him for what he has done to us."

Then 3,000 men left Judah and went to the top of the rock of Etam and confronted Samson and said, "What have you done to us? Do you not know that the Philistines are our rulers?" And he answered them and said, "I have only done to them, what they have done to me."
And they said to him, "We have come to capture you, and deliver you into the hands of the Philistines." And Samson said to them, "Swear to me, that you will not kill me yourselves."

In response to his request they said, "No, we swear that we are not going to kill you, but we are going to restrain you and deliver you into their hands." So, they tied him up with two new ropes and brought him down off the rock.

When they arrived in Lehi, the Philistines came out shouting against him, and the Lord's spirit came upon him in great power. Then the ropes tied around his arms burned from his hands and fell to the ground.
He found a donkey jawbone laying on the ground, so he grabbed it and used it to kill 1,000 Philistine men.
And Samson said, "With a donkey's jawbone, I have piled them into heaps. And with the jawbone of a donkey, I have killed 1,000 men."
When he finished speaking, he threw the jawbone from his hand and named that place Ramath-Lehi.
And he was so thirsty that he called on the Lord and said, "You have delivered this great victory into your servant's hand. I am dying of thirst; must I now fall into the hands of the uncircumcised?"

But God opened a hollow place in the donkey's jaw and water came rushing out. And after he drank all that he could, his spirit was revived. So, he named that place En-Hakkore, which is still in Lehi to this day.
And Samson judged Israel for 20 years in the days of the Philistines.
Then Samson went to Gaza where he met a prostitute and spent the night with her.

When the Gazites heard that Samson was there they said, "Samson is here!" Then they surrounded the city gates, and they quietly lay in wait for him all night long and they said, "We will kill him in the morning at daybreak."

But Samson only laid there until midnight, then he got up and pulled the two gateposts from the city gates and carried them away bars and all. Then he carried them on his shoulders to the top of the hill before Hebron.
Later on Samson fell in love with a woman named Delilah, who lived in the Valley of Sorek.

But the Philistine leaders went to her and said, "We will each give you 1,100 pieces of silver if you use your sexual prowess to tempt Samson into revealing where he gets his great strength. We need to know how to defeat, overpower, and capture him."
So Delilah spoke to Samson and said, "Please tell me where you get your great strength, and how can you be restrained and captured."
Samson replied to her and said, "If they tie me up with seven green undried bowstrings, I will be as weak as any other man."
Then the Philistine leaders brought her seven green undried bowstrings, and she tied him up.

Delilah let the men hide in her bedroom and she went to Samson and said, "Samson, the Philistines are here!" Then he broke the strings as if they were just burnt threads, and they still did not know where his strength came from.
And Delilah said to Samson, "You mocked me and lied to me, please tell me how you can be restrained and captured."
And Samson replied to her and said, "If they tie up me with new unused ropes, then I will be as weak as any other man."

Delilah took new unused ropes and tied him up and she said, "Samson, the Philistines are here!" And she knew they were lying in wait for him in her bedroom, and he broke the ropes from his arms like they were just a thread.

Then Delilah said to Samson, "You are still mocking me and telling me lies, tell me how you can be tied up and captured!" And he said to her, "You must weave seven locks of my hair into the web of a loom."
She fastened it with the pin and said to him, "Samson, the Philistines are here!" And Samson awoke from his sleep and pulled the beam's pin loose along with the web.
And Delilah said to Samson, "How can you say you love me, when your heart is not with me? You have mocked me three times, and you still have not told me where your great strength comes from."
But Delilah continued to press Samson every day with her constant nagging to discover his secret, and his soul was frustrated almost to death.

Samson finally told Delilah everything in his heart and said, "My head has never been touched by a razor, because I have been a Nazarite to God since the day I was born. If I shave my head, I will lose my strength, and I will be as weak as any other man."

When Delilah realized that Samson had told her everything in his heart, she sent for the Philistine lords and said, "Come at once, because he has told me everything in his heart." Then they came and brought Delilah the money they promised her.
Delilah let Samson fall asleep on her lap, and she called a man to come and shave seven locks of hair from his head, then she tied him up and his strength left him.
And Delilah said, "Samson, the Philistines are here!" Then he awoke from his sleep and said, "I will shake my bonds loose and leave as I did before," but he did not know that the Lord had left him.
So the Philistines captured him and gouged his eyes out, then they brought him down to Gaza, where he was bound with brass shackles and forced to grind wheat in prison.
However, after they shaved his head. his hair began to regrow.
Then the Philistine leaders gathered to offer a great sacrifice to their god Dagon. They all rejoiced and said, "Our god has delivered our enemy Samson into our hands."
When the people saw him, they praised their god and said, "Our God has delivered our enemy, who has killed many of us and destroyed our country into our hands."
When their hearts were merry, they said, "Send for Samson so we can ridicule him." So, they brought Samson from the prison and made fun of him, and they tied him between the columns.
Samson spoke to the boy who held his hand and asked him, "Can you bring me to the columns that support the temple roof, so I can lean up against them?"
The house was full of men and women, and all the Philistine leaders were there. There were also about 3,000 men and women sitting on the roof watching them ridicule Sampson.

Then Samson called out to the Lord and said, "O Lord God, I pray you remember me and give me strength. O God, I pray just this once, that I may have vengeance against the Philistines for the loss of my eyes."
Then Samson took hold of the two middle columns supporting the temple roof, one in each hand.

And Samson said, "Lord God, let me die with the Philistines!" Then Samson pushed with all of his might, and the temple fell on the people and the Philistine leaders. So, there were more dead Philistines there than Samson had previously killed in his entire life.
Then Samson's brothers and his father's entire house came and took him to be buried between Zorah and Eshtaol in his father Manoah's cemetery. Samson had judged Israel for 20 years.
There was a man named Micah from Mount Ephraim.

And Micah spoke to his mother and said, "I have the 1,100 silver shekels that I heard you cursing about that you said were stolen because I took it." And Micah's mother said, "May the Lord bless you, my son."

When Micah returned the 1,100 silver shekels to his mother she said, "I will completely dedicate this silver to the Lord for my son to use to make a carved and molten image. Therefore, I will now return it to you."
After Micah returned the money to his mother, she gave 200 silver shekels to a man at the foundry, who used them to make a carved and molten image, which they kept in Micah's house.
Then Micah built a shrine to the gods, and he made an ephod and a teraphim, and he declared one of his sons to be a sacred priest.
In those days there was no king in Israel, but everyone did whatever they thought was right in their own eyes.
There was a young Levite man from Bethlehem-Judah who was part of Judah's family living there.
And the young Levite man left the city of Bethlehem-Judah to his own place, and as he was traveling, he came upon Micah's house on Mount Ephraim.
And Micah spoke to him and asked, "Where do you come from?" And the man responded and said, "I am a Levite from Bethlehem-Judah, and I am traveling looking for my own place."
And Micah said to him, "Stay with me, and be a father and a priest to me, and I will give you ten silver shekels per year, a suit of clothes, and your food." So, the Levite went in.
The young Levite was content to live with Micah, and he was like one of his own sons.
Micah declared the Levite to be sacred, and the young man became his priest, and he lived in Micah's house.
Then Micah said, "Now I know that the Lord will do me good, since I have a Levite as my priest."
In those days there was no king in Israel, and the Danites were looking for a place to live, because up until then they had been given no inheritance from the tribes of Israel.

The Danites sent five men of valor from their tribes in Zorah and Eshtaol, to explore and search the land and they gave them instructions and said, "Go search and explore the land." When they arrived at Micah's house on Mount Ephraim, they stayed there.
When they were near Micah's house, they recognized the young Levite man's accent, and they went over to him and asked, "Who brought you here, why are you here, and what are you doing here?"
The young Levite man answered them and said, "Micah does things for me, he made a deal with me and hired me as his priest."
And then they asked him, "We need you to ask God for his counsel, so we will know whether or not, the journey we are undertaking will be prosperous."
The priest answered them and said, "Go in peace, for the Lord goes before you, and he will be with you wherever you go."

Then the men left and went to Laish, and they saw that the that people living there were as carefree as the Sidonians. They lived quietly and securely, and they had no strong magistrates to judge them and shame them for the bad things they did. They lived a long way from the Sidonians, they did no business with other people, and they did not have alliances with any other communities.
When the men returned to their brothers in Zorah and Eshtaol they were asked, "What did you learn?"
And the men said, "We surveyed the land and it looks very good, we need to go and attack them now! There is nothing to worry about because they are weak, and we can go and take over their land.
When you get there, you will see that the people there live securely in a large land. God has put this land into our hands, and it is a place where they lack nothing that the earth provides."
So 600 Danite soldiers armed and ready for war left Zorah and Eshtaol.
They camped in Kiriath-Jearim which is in Judah, and they named the place behind Kiriath-Jearim, Mahaneh-Dan which it is still called to this day.
As they traveled through Mount Ephraim, they came across Micah's house.

The five men who had explored the country of Laish said to their brothers, "Do you know that there is an ephod, a carved image, an idol, and a molten image in one of those houses? We think you know what to do."
So they went towards the house where the young Levite man lived in Micah's house, and when they saw him, they saluted him.
The 600 armed Danite soldiers stood guard by the entrance of the city gates.
The five men who had explored the land went in and took the carved image, the ephod, the idol, and the molten image, as the priest stood at the gate's entrance with the 600 soldiers.
When they entered Micah's house, they grabbed the carved image, ephod, idol, and the molten image. Then the young priest spoke to them and asked, "What are you doing?"

They answered him and said, "Put your hand over mouth and come with us and be our father and priest. Are you better off as the priest over the house of one man, or would you be better off as the priest of an entire Israelis family and tribe?"
The priest's heart was glad, and he was relieved to hear their plan, so he took the ephod, the idol, and the carved image and went with the soldiers.
So the Danites left and put the children, cattle, and a carriage out in front of them.
After the Danites traveled a good distance from Micah's house, the men living near Micah's house gathered together, and overtook them.
When they cried out to the Danites, they turned toward Micah and asked, "What is the matter with you, why have you come to us with such a company?"
And Micah said, "You took my priest and the gods I made and left. What do I have left? So how can you ask, 'What is the matter with you?'"
The Danites responded to him and said, "Do not scream at us, or some angry fellows might run you over and take your life, along with the lives of the people in your household."
So the Danites went their own way when Micah realized that they were too strong for him and turned around and went home.

So they took Micah's priest and his idols and went to Laish where the people lived quietly and secure. And they attacked and defeated them with the edge of the sword and burned the city to the ground.

The people there had no deliverer because they were a long way from Sidon, and they had no trade or alliances with other cities. The Danites rebuilt and lived in the city in the valley near Beth-Rehob.
They changed the name of the city of Laish to Dan, which was named after their father Dan who was a descendant of Israel.
The Danites set up the carved image, and Jonathan who was Gershom's son, who was the son of Manasseh, and his sons were priests for the Danite tribe until the day their lands were captured.
And the Danites set up the carved image that Micah had made for themselves, where it remained the entire time that the house of God was in Shiloh.
So in the days when Israel had no king, there was a Levite traveling along the side of Mount Ephraim, who took a concubine from Bethlehem-Judah.
She began to be unfaithful to him with other men, then she left and returned to her father's house in Bethlehem-Judah, where she stayed for four months.

Her husband followed her and he went to speak pleasantly with her, to bring her back home, and he took his servant and a couple of donkeys with him. She took him into her father's house, and her father was happy to meet him when he met him.
The girl's father, who was his father-in-law invited him in, so he stayed there for three days, and they got to know each other as they ate and drink together.
They got up early on the fourth day, and the man was ready to leave, but the girl's father told his son-in-law to relax and have something to eat before he left.
So they sat down and ate and drink together some more, because the girl's father had said to the man, "I pray that you will be content and stay here all night and let your heart be merry."
When the Levite got up to leave, his father-in-law urged him again to stay, so he stayed there another night.
The Levite got up early on the fifth day and the girl's father said to him, "I hope you will stay a while longer," so they stayed until the afternoon and they both ate.

When the Levite, his concubine, and his servant got up to leave, the man's father-in-law the girl's father said to him, "It is getting late in the day, I pray that you will stay the night, the day is almost over. So, make your heart merry and stay here, and you can get up early tomorrow, and be on your way home in the morning."
But the Levite would not stay the night, and he left with his servant, his two saddled donkeys, and his concubine. And they were passing by Jebus which is also known as Jerusalem.
When they were near Jebus, the day was almost spent, and the servant said to his master, "I pray that you will let us stay in this Jebusite city tonight."
His master responded to him and said, "No we cannot stay in this strange city, it is not part of Israel. We will go on to Gibeah."
Then the Levite man said to his servant, "Come, let us go on to Gibeah or Ramah where we can find a place to stay the night."
So they passed on by, and the sun went down when they were near Gibeah, which belonged to Benjamin.
And they stopped near Gibeah, and when they went into the city to find a place to stay, they had to sit down on one of the city streets, because no one would take them into their home for the night.
But an old man came by who had been working out in the field on Mount Ephraim, and he lived in Gibeah, where the men were Benjamites.
When the old man saw a traveler out on the city streets, he asked, "Where have you come from, and where are you going?"

And the Levite man replied to the old man and said, "We come from Bethlehem-Judah, and we are on our way to the side of Mount Ephraim. Now I am on my way to the Lord's house, but nobody will invite me in.
But we have both straw and feed for our donkeys, and there is enough bread and wine for me and your housemaid, and the young man who is with us, and we lack or need nothing."
And the old man said, "Peace be with you, please do not stay in the streets, but let me provide what you need."
So the old man brought the Levite into his house and fed their donkeys, and they washed their feet and ate and drink.

As they were making their hearts merry, some men from the city who were Belial's sons, surrounded the house and beat the door and spoke to the old master of the house and said, "Bring us that man in your house, so that we may know him."
The old master of the house went out and spoke to them and said, "No my brothers, do not do this wicked thing to this man staying in my house, do not do this foolishness.
I will bring my daughter who is a young woman and his concubine out to you, and you can do with them whatever seems good to you, but do not such a vile thing to this man."
But the men would not listen to him, so the man took his concubine out to them, and they abused her all night long until morning, and at daybreak they let her go.
The woman came back at dawn and fell at the door of the old man's house where her lord was staying until daylight.
Her lord got up that morning and when he opened the doors to leave and go on his way, he saw his concubine laying in front of the house, and her hands were laying across the threshold.
He said to her, "Get up, let us be on our way." But she did not answer, so the man put her on one of his donkeys, and they left to return home.
When they entered his house, he took a knife and cut up his concubine and divided her body and bones into twelve parts, and he sent her body parts throughout all of Israel.
And everyone who saw it said, "Until today, nothing like this has ever happened in Israel, not even since the day the Israelis left Egypt. Think it over, take advice, and speak your minds!"
Then the Israelis, all the way from Dan to Beersheba left Mount Gilead, and they assembled the congregation together as one man before the Lord in Mizpah.
All the people's leaders from all the Israelis tribes, presented themselves in the people's assembly of God, where there were 400,000 footmen armed with swords.
The Benjamites heard that the Israelis had gone up to Mizpah. Then the Israelis said, "Tell us, how did this wickedness happen?"
So the Levite who was married to the woman who was killed answered them and said, "I went to Gibeah and stayed in Benjamin with my concubine.
And the men of Gibeah surrounded the house where I stayed that night. They were planning to kill me, but they took my concubine and forced her to have sex, and she died.
So I cut her up into pieces, and sent her throughout the inherited country of Israel, because they had committed such an obscenity and foolishness in Israel.
Now behold this you people of Israel and give me your advice and counsel right here right now."
All the people made a unanimous decision, and spoke as one man and said, "Not one of us will go to his tent or his house.
But we will cast lots to decide what to do against Gibeah.
We will take 1/10th of the men in Israel, to supply provisions for the army when they enter Gibeah in Benjamin to punish them for the senseless wickedness they have done in Israel."
So all of Israel's soldiers united and marched against Gibeah.
Israel's tribes sent soldiers throughout Benjamin and said, "What is this wickedness you have done?
So deliver all the Belial men in Gibeah, so that we may put them to death and remove this evil from Israel." But the Benjamites would not listen to the voice of their Israelis brothers.
But the Benjamites from Gibeah assembled their armies and went to attack the Israelis.
And there were 26,000 armed men from the Benjamite cities, besides the 700 armed men from Gibeah.
Among all these people were 700 lefthanded soldiers who could sling stones at a target the width of a hair and not miss.
But there were 400,000 sword carrying armed soldiers from Israel without men from the Benjamite tribe.
So the Israelis went to God's house to ask for his counsel and they asked, "Who will be the first to go and do battle against the Benjamites?" And the Lord said, "Judah will go up first."
The Israelis got up early the next morning and camped outside Gibeah.
Then the Israelis arrayed their armies to do battle against the Benjamites in Gibeah.
The Benjamites came out of Gibeah and killed 22,000 Israelis troops that day.
But the Israelis men summoned all of their courage and set their battle array in the same place where they had arrayed themselves the first day.

The Israelis wept as they went before the Lord that evening to seek his counsel again and they asked, "Should we fight our Benjamite brothers in battle again?" And the Lord said, "Go up against them!"
So, the Israelis advanced against the Benjamites the second day.
On the second day of battle, Benjamin's army came from Gibeah and killed another 18,000 Israelis soldiers armed with swords.
Then the Israeli people went to the house of God. They wept and sat before the Lord, and fasted that day until evening, and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before the Lord.
Because, in those days God's Ark of the Covenant was there, so the Israelis went there to ask for the Lord's counsel.

Aaron's son Eleazar had a son named Phinehas who stood before the ark in those days and asked God, "Should we attack our Benjamite brothers again, or should we stop?" And the Lord said, "Go and fight, because tomorrow I will deliver them into your hands."
So Israel laid an ambush, where they hid and lay in wait all around Gibeah.
On the third day, the Israelis arrayed their army against Gibeah the same as before and attacked the Benjamites.

The Benjamites went to attack the Israelis, but they were drawn away from the city. They began to defeat the Israelis and killed about 30 of them on the highways. One road led to the house of God, and the other led to a field in Gibeah.
The Benjamites said, "We have defeated them again just as before." But the Israelis said, "We will flee, and draw them out onto the highways and away from the city."
Then the Israelis rose up from their hiding places and arrayed their army at Baal-Tamar. All of the soldiers lying in wait came out of hiding all the way to the Meadows of Gibeah.
And 10,000 Israelis soldiers attacked Gibeah and fought a fierce battle, but the Benjamites did not know what God had planned for them.
The Lord defeated the Benjamites before Israel, and they slaughtered 25,100 armed sword carrying Benjamite men that day.
Then the Benjamites realized that they had been defeated. And the Israelis fled knowing that they had a hidden ambush waiting for the Benjamites beside Gibeah.
The ambushers rushed and attacked Gibeah with their swordsmen and defeated the entire city.
The Israelis soldiers had prearranged a smoke signal from the city with the ambushers.

When the Israelis saw the signal, they turned and back went into the battle. The Benjamites began to defeat them, and killed about 30 Israelis men and they said, "Surely we have defeated them again, as we did in the first battle."
But when the smoke began to rise up from the city, the Benjamites looked behind them, and saw the flames from the city ascending up to heaven.
When the Israelis turned again, the Benjamites were amazed at the disaster that had come upon them.
So they turned and fled the Israelis into the wilderness, but the battle overtook them and they were struck down and destroyed by the men coming from the cities.
They chased and surrounded the Benjamites and trampled them down with ease near Gibeah facing the rising sun.
And 18,000 Benjamite men fell that day, and they were all men of valor.
But the Benjamites fled to the Rock of Rimmon in the wilderness. The Israelis killed 5,000 men along the highway and pursued them to Gidom, where they killed another 2,000.
So there was a total of 25,000 Benjamite soldiers armed with swords that were killed that day, all of them were men of valor.
But 600 men fled to the Rock of Rimmon in the wilderness, where they lived for four months.

Then the Israelis turned their swords on the Benjamites again and defeated them, as well as all the men from every city including all of their animals, and everything else that they owned. And they set fire to every city they found.
The Israelis had sworn an oath in Mizpah and said, "Not one of us will allow our daughters to marry Benjamite men."
So the people came to the house of God, and sat before God until the evening, and they bitterly wept and cried out to the Lord.
And they said, "O Lord God of Israel, why has this happened to Israel. Today there is one tribe missing in Israel!"
The next day the people got up early and built an altar, where they offered burnt offerings and peace offerings.

And the Israelis asked, "Who among all the tribes of Israel did not come to the congregation before the Lord? For they had made a great oath that anyone who did not come up before the Lord in Mizpah will surely be put to death."
Then the Israelis grieved for their Benjamite brothers and said, "One tribe has been cut off from the tribes of Israel today.
How can we find wives for those who survived, for we have sworn an oath by the Lord that we will not allow them to marry any of our daughters?"
And they asked, "Which tribe of Israel did not come up to Mizpah before the Lord?" And they saw that no one from Jabesh-Gilead had come to the camp assembly.
Because when they counted the people, they found that no inhabitants from Jabesh-Gilead were there.
So the congregation sent 12,000 of their most valiant men and gave them their orders and said, "Take your swords and go destroy the inhabitants of Jabesh-Gilead including the women and children.
You must completely destroy every man, and every woman who has had sexual relations with a man."
But they found 400 young virgins who had not had relations with a man in Jabesh-Gilead, and they brought them to the camp at Shiloh, in the land of Canaan.
And the congregation sent a delegation of people to speak peaceably to the remaining Benjamites living at the Rock of Rimmon.
So at that time the Benjamite men came, and they were given wives from the surviving women of Jabesh-Gilead, but there were not enough of them to satisfy all of the men.
And the people grieved for the Benjamites, because the Lord had made a broken defense among the tribes of Israel.
Then the congregation elders said, "How can we find wives for the remaining men, because all of the women in Benjamin have been destroyed?"
And they said, "There must be an inheritance for the Benjamites who escaped the destruction, so that no Israelis tribe is destroyed.
However we cannot give them wives from our daughters, because the Israelis have sworn an oath and said, 'Cursed is the man who gives a wife to Benjamin.'"

Then they said, "Behold we will have a feast to the Lord in Shiloh every year on the north side of Bethel, beside the eastern highway that goes up from Bethel to Shechem, on the south side of Lebonah."
So they commanded the Benjamites and said, "Go and lie in wait in the vineyards.
When the daughters of Shiloh come out to dance in the vineyards, each man can catch a wife for himself from the daughters of Shiloh and return to the land of Benjamin with them.

When their fathers or brothers come to us to complain, we will say, "Please do us a favor by helping them, because we did not save any wives for them in the war. And since you did not actually give them wives at this time, you will not be guilty of violating your promise to God."

And the Benjamite descendants did what they were told. They took the women they needed for wives from the dancers that they captured. And they returned to the land of their inheritance, and they strengthened the cities where they lived.
And at that time the Israelis left, and each man returned to his tribe, his family, and their own inheritance.
In those days there was no king in Israel, and each man did whatever he thought was right in his own eyes.
In the days that the judges ruled, there was a famine in the land, and a man from Bethlehem-Judah was traveling in the country of Moab, with his wife and their two sons.
The man's name was Elimelech and his wife's name was Naomi, and his two sons were named Mahlon and Chilion. They were Ephrathites from Bethlehem-Judah, and they settled in Moab.
Then Naomi's husband Elimelech died, and she was left with her two sons.
Their sons married women from Moab, one was named Orpah and the other was named Ruth, and they lived there for about ten years.
Mahlon and Chilion both died, and Naomi was left without her husband and her two sons.
Then she heard in Moab that the Lord had visited his people and was providing them with bread, so she and her daughters-in-law prepared to leave Moab.
So Naomi left that place with her two daughters-in-law, and they set out to return to the land of Judah.
But Naomi spoke to her two daughters-in-law and said, "Both of you should return to your mother's house. May the Lord deal kindly with you, because you have dealt kindly with your dead and with me.
May the Lord allow each of you to find rest in a house with your new husband." Then she kissed them, and they cried and wept aloud.
Orpah and Ruth responded to their mother-in-law and said, "Surely you will let us return to your people with you."
But Naomi replied and said, "No my daughters, you must return home. Why would you want to go with me? There are no sons left in my womb to be your husbands.
So, my daughters you must go your own way and return to your home, because I am too old to find another husband. Even if there was hope that I could find another husband tonight and had more sons.
Would you stay and wait for them to grow up? Would you wait for them without having husbands? No, my daughters it grieves me very much for your sakes that the hand of the Lord has turned against me."
And they all cried and wept again, then Orpah kissed her mother-in-law, but Ruth clung to her.
And Naomi spoke kindly to Ruth and said, "Behold your sister-in-law Orpah is going back to her people and her gods, so you must return with your sister-in-law."
But Ruth said, "Please do not ask me not to follow you or leave you, for I will go where you go, and I will stay where you stay. Your people will be my people, and your God will be my God.
Where you die, I will die and I will be buried there, may the Lord severely punish me and more, if anything but death separates us."
When Naomi realized that Ruth was determined to go with her, she quit trying to convince her to leave.
So they both went to Bethlehem and when they arrived, the whole city was excited to see them and they asked, "Is this Naomi? (Naomi means pleasant or delightful)"
And she replied to them and said, "Do not call me Naomi, call me Mara because the Almighty has dealt very bitterly with me.
I left full of life, and the Lord has brought me home empty. So why do you call me Naomi? You can see that the Lord has testified against me, and the Almighty has afflicted me?"
So Naomi returned home from Moab and Ruth the Moabite who was her daughter-in-law returned with her. And they arrived in Bethlehem at the beginning of the barley harvest.
Naomi's dead husband Elimelech had a powerful and wealthy family member named Boaz.
And Ruth the Moabite spoke to Naomi and said, "Let me go out into the field and glean some wheat, and I may find grace in the owner's sight." And Naomi answered Ruth and said, "Go, my daughter."
So Ruth went out into the field to glean grain behind the harvesters, and she happened upon a field that belonged to Boaz, who was one of Elimelech's relatives.
Boaz had come from Bethlehem, and he spoke to the harvesters and said, "May the Lord be with you." And they answered him and said, "And may the Lord bless you."
Then Boaz spoke to his foreman who supervised the harvesters and asked, "Who is that girl?"
The harvester's foreman answered him and said, "It is the Moabite girl that returned from Moab with Naomi."

She came to me and said, "I pray you will let me glean and gather sheaves of grain after the harvesters." She began working this morning, and she has been working all day until now, except for a short rest she took in the house.
Then Boaz spoke to Ruth and said, "Listen my daughter? Do not leave here to glean in other fields but stay here close to my other young women.

Keep your eyes on the field and follow the other girls and harvest where they harvest. I told the young men not to bother you or touch you. If you get thirsty, go and drink from the vessels that they filled."
Then Ruth fell facedown and bowed to the ground and said to Boaz, "What have I done to find such grace in your eyes that would make you take notice of a stranger like me?"

And Boaz answered Ruth and said, "I have seen everything that you have done for your mother-in-law since the death of your husband. I also learned that you left your father and mother, and the land where you were born to come and live among people that you did not know.
May the Lord reward your work and give you the full rewards of the Lord God of Israel, under whose wings you have come to trust."
Then Ruth said, "My Lord, you have comforted me and may I continue to find favor in your sight because you have spoken favorably toward me, even though I am not like one of your other servant girls."

At mealtime Boaz spoke to Ruth and said, "Come and eat some bread dipped in vinegar with us?" So, Ruth sat down beside the other harvesters, and Boaz offered her dried grain which she ate, and she had some leftovers when she finished.
When Ruth got up to work and glean the field, Boaz gave his young men their orders and said, "Let her glean the fields even among the standing sheaves, and do not interfere with her.
Leave some handfuls of whole wheat stalks laying on the ground on purpose for her to glean, and do not reprimand her."
So Ruth worked out in the field gleaning grain until the evening, when she threshed out what she had gleaned, she had about an ephah of barley.
Then Ruth picked up her grain and carried it to the city where her mother-in-law saw what she had gleaned. And Ruth gave Naomi the leftover grain she had from her lunch.

Ruth's mother-in-law Naomi spoke to Ruth and said, "Where did you work and glean today? Blessed be the man who noticed you." So, Ruth told her mother-in-law where she had worked and she said, "I worked with a man named Boaz today."

Then Naomi replied to her daughter-in-law and said, "Blessed be the man of the Lord, who has not withheld his kindness from the living or the dead." And Naomi said to her, "That man is close family to us, he is one of our next of kin."
Ruth the Moabite replied to Naomi and said, "Boaz also said to me, "Stay close to my young men, until they finish harvesting my fields."
Naomi replied to her daughter-in-law Ruth and said, "My daughter, it is good that you are working with Boaz's young women, that way nothing will happen to you in one of the other fields."
So Ruth stayed close to Boaz's young women to glean the fields until the end of the barley and wheat harvest, and she continued to live with her mother-in-law.
One day Ruth's mother-in-law Naomi said to her, "My daughter, should I find a husband for you so that you may rest, and things may go well for you?"
Boaz is one of our relatives and you have been working closely with his young women, and he is winnowing barley on the threshing room floor tonight.
So clean yourself up and take a bath, put on some perfume, wear your best clothes, and go down to the threshing room, but do not let him see you until he has finished eating and drinking.
Watch him when he goes in to lay down so you will know where he sleeps, then go in and uncover his feet, and lay down and he will tell you what you what to do next."
Then Ruth said to Naomi, "I will do everything that you have told me to do."
So she went down to the threshing room and did everything that her mother-in-law told her to do.
When Boaz finished eating and drinking and his heart was merry; he went to lie down at the end of the grain pile. Then she softly came to him and uncovered his feet, and she laid down.
At midnight, Boaz woke up and turned over, and he was afraid because there was a woman laying at his feet.
And Boaz said, "Who are you?" Ruth answered him and said, "I am your servant Ruth, please spread your blanket over me, because you are a close family member."

Boaz replied to Ruth and said, "My daughter may the Lord bless you, because you have shown more kindness today than you did in the beginning, since you did not chase the young men, whether they were rich or poor.
So now my daughter do not be afraid, because I am going to do whatever you require, since all of my people in the city know that you are a virtuous woman.
Although it is true that I am your close family member, there is a family member closer to you than me.

Stay here tonight, and in the morning, and if he wants to do his family duty and redeem you, good. But if he does not want to redeem you, then as surely as the Lord lives, I will. So, lie here until morning.
And Ruth lay at his feet until morning, and she got up early so no one else would see her, and Boaz said, "Do not tell anyone that a woman came into the threshing room."
Boaz also said, "Bring your vail over here and hold it out." And when she did, he put six measures of barley in it and laid it on her shoulder, and she went into the city.
When Ruth returned her mother-in-law Naomi asked, "What happened last night my daughter?" And Ruth told her everything that Boaz had done for her.
And Ruth said, "Boaz gave me these six measures of barley because he said to me, 'Do not go back to your mother-in-law empty handed.'"
Then Naomi said, "Wait patiently my daughter, until you know which way things are headed. For Boaz will not rest until he has resolved this matter today."

Then Boaz went up to the gate and sat down, and the family member that Boaz had spoken of came by. And Boaz spoke to him and said, "Hello friend, come and sit over here." And the man went and sat down beside Boaz.
Boaz spoke to the ten men who were city elders and said, "Sit here with us." And they came and sat down.
Boaz spoke to his family and said, "Naomi has come home from Moab, and she is selling a parcel of land that belonged to our brother Elimelech.

I thought I would come to let you know, so you can buy it back in the presence of everyone here including the elders of my people, and if you want to redeem it is yours to redeem. But if not, let me know because if none of you want to redeem it, I will buy it and redeem it since I am the next closest family member."

Then Boaz said, "The day you buy the field from Naomi and Ruth the Moabite, you must also take in Ruth the Moabite who is the dead man's wife in order to keep the deceased man's name on his inheritance."
And the family said, "I cannot redeem it for myself, because it would ruin my own inheritance, you may redeem my right to yourself, because I cannot redeem it."

In the past it used to be that when property was redeemed or exchanged in Israel, in order to confirm the transaction, a man would take off his shoe and gave it to his neighbor, and this was how a deal was confirmed in Israel.
So the family said to Boaz, "Buy it for yourself." And Boaz removed his shoe.

Then Boaz spoke to the elders and said, "All of you are my witness today, and you can testify that I have bought everything from Naomi that belonged to Elimelech, including everything Chilion and Mahlon owned.

In addition, I have purchased Mahlon's wife Ruth the Moabitess to be my wife, to raise up the name of the deceased through his inheritance. So that the name of the dead will not be cut off from among his brothers or from the gates of his home, and you are witnesses to this today."

Everyone at the gates and the elders said, "We are your witnesses. May the Lord make the woman who is coming into your house be like Rachel and Leah, who helped build up the House of Israel. May you be worthy in Ephratah, and famous in Bethlehem.
And let your house be like Pharez's house whom Tamar bore to Judah, because of the children which the Lord will give you from this young woman."
So Boaz took Ruth as his wife and when he went into her bedroom, the Lord caused her to conceive, and she gave birth to a son.
And the women said to Naomi, "Blessed be the Lord, who has not left you without a family today, so that this child's name may become famous in Israel.
This child will restore your life and nourish you in your old age. For your daughter-in-law who loves you and is better to you than seven sons, has given birth to him."
So Naomi took the child, embraced him and she became his nurse.
The neighborhood women gave the child a name and said, "A son has been born to Naomi." They named him Obed, and he became Jesse's father, who was the father of David.
Now this is the history of Pharez, Pharez fathered Hezron.
And Hezron fathered Ram, and Ram fathered Amminadab.
And Amminadab fathered Nahshon, and Nahshon fathered Salmon.
And Salmon fathered Boaz, and Boaz fathered Obed.
And Obed fathered Jesse, and Jesse fathered David.
Now there was a man from Ramathaim-Zophim which is on Mount Ephraim. His name was Elkanah and he was Jeroham's son, who was Elihu's son, who was Tohu's son, who was Zuph the Ephrathite's son.
Elkanah had two wives; one was named Hannah and the other was named Peninnah. Peninnah had children, but Hannah had none.
Elkanah left his hometown every year to go worship and sacrifice to the Lord of Hosts in Shiloh. And Eli's two sons Hophni and Phinehas were the Lord's priests there.
When it was time for Elkanah to present his offering, he gave some of it to his wife Peninnah and some to her sons and daughters.
But he gave a larger portion to Hannah because he loved her, even though she had no children because the Lord had closed her womb.
And because the Lord had closed Hannah's womb, her adversary provoked her just to upset her and make her worry.
Year after year when Hannah went to the Lord's temple, her adversary provoked her to tears until she could not eat.
Then her husband Elkanah spoke to her and said, "Hannah, why are you weeping, why do you not eat, and why is your heart grieved? Am I not better to you than ten sons?"
So after they had finished eating and drinking in Shiloh, Hannah got up. Now Eli the priest was sitting near the entrance of the Lord's temple.
But Hannah's soul was very distressed as she prayed and wept bitterly to the Lord.

And Hannah made a promise to the Lord and said, "O Lord of Hosts, please see my affliction and do not forget me. And if you remember me, then give me a baby boy and I will dedicate him to you for all the days of his life, and his head will never be shaved."
As Hannah continued praying before the Lord, Eli could see her lips moving.
Hannah spoke to the Lord in her heart, and her lips were moving but her voice could not be heard, so Eli thought she was drunk.
Then Eli spoke to her and said, "How long are you going to stay drunk? Put your wine away."
And Hannah answered him and said, "No my Lord, I am not drunk. I am a woman with a spirit full of sorrow, and I have been pouring out my soul before the Lord.
Please do not mistake me for a daughter of Belial, because I have spoken from the abundance of complaints and grief in my life until now."
Then Eli answered and said, "Go in peace, and may the God of Israel grant you the petition that you have asked of him."
And Hannah said, "May I find grace in your sight." So, she went on her way and began to eat again, and she was no longer sad.

Elkanah and Hannah got up early the next morning and worshipped before the Lord. Then they returned to their home in Ramah, and Elkanah had sexual relations with his wife Hannah, and the Lord remembered her.

That's why after she conceived when the time had come for her to give birth to a son, Hannah named him Samuel and said, "I have named him Samuel because I asked the Lord for him. (Samuel means Delightful)"
Then Elkanah and his entire household went to offer the Lord their annual sacrifice and to fulfill his promise.
But Hannah did not go because she said to her husband, "I cannot go until the child has been weaned, after that I will bring him to appear before the Lord, and he will stay there forever."

Hannah's husband Elkanah said to her, "Do what you think is right, and stay home until you have weaned him, because only the Lord can establish his word." So, she stayed home and breastfed her son until he was weaned.
After she had weaned him, she took her young child, along with three bulls, an ephah of flour, and a bottle of wine to the Lord's house in Shiloh.
Then they killed a bull and brought the child to Eli.
And Hannah spoke to Eli and said, "Oh my Lord, as your soul lives I am the woman who stood before you, praying to the Lord.
I prayed for this child, and the Lord has given me what I asked for.
So I have dedicated him to the Lord, and as long as he lives, he will belong to the Lord." And they worshipped the Lord there.
And Hannah prayed and said, "My heart rejoices in the Lord, my horn is glorified by the Lord, my mouth speaks boldly against my enemies, because I rejoice in your salvation.
No one is as holy as the Lord because there is no one besides you, nor is there a rock like our God.
Do not speak foolish pride anymore, do not let arrogance come from your mouth because the Lord is a God of knowledge, and he weighs every action.
The mighty men's bows and arrows are broken, but those who stumble are strengthened.
Those who are full have hired out themselves for bread, and the hungry no longer starve. The barren woman gives birth to seven children, but the woman who has many children grows feeble.
The Lord brings death and makes life, he brings down to the grave and he raises up.
The Lord makes poor and he makes rich; he brings low and lifts up.

The Lord raises the poor from the dust; he lifts up the beggar from the dunghill. He sets them among princes to inherit the throne of glory, because the earth's pillars belong to the Lord, and he has placed the world on them.
The Lord protects the feet of his saints, and the wicked are silenced in the darkness, because no man prevails through his own strength.

The Lord's adversaries will be broken into pieces, he will bring thunder on them from heaven, he will judge the ends of the earth, and he will give strength to his king, and glorify the horn of his anointed."
Then Elkanah went to home to Ramah, and the child Samuel began to minister to the Lord before Eli the priest.
Eli's sons were wicked men of Belial, and they did not know the Lord.
It was the priest's custom with the people when a man offered a sacrifice, his servant came while the meat was boiling with a three-pronged meat hook in his hand.

And would stick it into the pan, kettle, caldron, or pot, and the priest kept for himself all the meat that was brought up by the hook. This was how they treated all the Israelis who came to Shiloh with their offerings.
Before they burned the fat the priest's servant came to tell the man offering a sacrifice, to give him some raw meat for the priest to roast, because he did not want boiled meat.

And if a man said to him, "The fat must be burned first, then you can take as much as your soul desires." Then the servant would answer him and say, "No, you must give it to me now, and if you refuse, I will take it by force!"
So the young men's sins were very great before the Lord, because they abhorred the Lord's offering.
But young Samuel was still a child, and he ministered before the Lord wearing a linen ephod.
Every year Samuel's mother Hannah made him a little robe and brought it to him when she came to offer the yearly sacrifice with her husband.
Then Eli would bless Elkanah and his wife Hannah and say, "May the Lord give you more children from this woman for the child she dedicated to the Lord," and they would go back home.
So the Lord visited Hannah, and she conceived and gave birth to three more sons and two daughters. And Samuel continued to grow before the Lord.

Eli was very old, and he heard about everything that his sons had done to Israel. He heard how they had been having sexual relations with the women who assembled at the entrance of the congregation's tabernacle.
And Eli said to them, "Why do you do such things? I have heard about all of the evil dealings you have had with these people.
No, my sons, I have heard no good reports about you, but I have heard that you make the Lord's people transgress.

If a man sins against another man, God can intervene for him; but if a man sins against the Lord, who can intervene for him?" But they would not listen to their father, because the Lord intended to kill them.
And the child Samuel grew up, and he found favor both with the Lord and also with men.
And a man of God came to Eli and said, "This is what the Lord says, 'Did I not plainly appear to your father's house when they were under Pharaoh's house in Egypt?

And from all the tribes of Israel, I chose your father to be my priest and offer sacrifices on my altar, to burn incense and to wear an ephod before me. And did I not also give your father's house all the burnt offerings that the Israelis made by fire?

So why do you kick at the sacrifices and offerings that I have commanded for my home, and honor your sons above me? Why do you make yourselves fat with the best parts of all the offerings from my people in Israel?'

That's why the Lord God of Israel says, 'I did indeed say that your house and the house of your father would walk before me forever.' But now the Lord says, 'Far be it from Me! For I will honor those who honor me and show little esteem for those who despise me.
Behold the days are coming, when I will cut off your arm and the arm of your father's house, so that there will be no old men in your household.
You will see an enemy in my home, and in all the wealth which God will give Israel. And there will be no old men in your house forever.
And any of your men that I do not cut off from my altar, will make your eyes weep and grieve your heart. And all of your descendants will die in the prime of their life.
And this will be a sign to you; this curse will fall on your two sons Hophni and Phinehas. And both of them will die on the same day.
And I will raise up a faithful priest, who will do whatever is in my heart and mind. And I will build a trustworthy house for him, and he will walk before my anointed one forever.

And everyone left in your house will come and bow down to him for a piece of silver and a morsel of bread. And they will beg him to put them to work in one of the priests' offices, so they can afford a piece of bread to eat.'"
Samuel was still a child when he ministered to the Lord before Eli, and the Lord's word was rare in those days, and nobody was having visions.
At that time, Eli's eyes had begun to grow dim and he could not see, and he laid down in his room.
Before the lamp of God was snuffed out, Samuel was lying down trying to sleep in the Lord's temple where God's Ark of the Covenant was kept.
Then the Lord called out to Samuel and he answered and said, "I am here."
Then Samuel ran to Eli and asked, "Here I am, did you call me?" And Eli said, "I did not call you, go and lay back down," so he went and laid down again.

But the Lord called out again and said, "Samuel!" So, Samuel got up and went back to Eli and said, "Here I am, because you called me again," and Eli answered him and said, "I did not call out to you my son, go and lie down."
Now Samuel did not know the Lord at that time, because the Lord's word had not yet been revealed to him.

And the Lord called out to Samuel a third time, so he got up and went to Eli and said, "Here I am, because I heard you call out to me," and Eli realized that it was the Lord who had been calling the child.
So, Eli said to Samuel, "Go and lie down, and if the Lord calls out to you again you should say, 'Speak Lord, because your servant hears you.'"So, Samuel went back to his room and laid down.
Then the Lord came and stood nearby, and he called out as before and said, "Samuel, Samuel." Then Samuel answered and said, "Speak Lord, because your servant hears you."
And the Lord said to Samuel, "Behold I will do something in Israel, that will cause the ears of everyone who hears it to tingle.
On that day, I will do everything against Eli which I have spoken about his house, and I will do it all from beginning to end.
Because I told him that I would judge his house forever for the immorality that he knows all about, because his sons have made themselves vile, and he did not restrain them.
So I have sworn to Eli, that the immorality of his house cannot be purged by sacrifices or offerings forever."
Samuel laid in his room until the morning, and he opened the doors of the Lord's house, and he was afraid to tell Eli about his vision.
Then Eli called for Samuel and said, "Samuel my son," and he answered, "I am here."
And Eli said, "What did the Lord say to you? I beg you not to hide anything that he said from me, if you hide anything from me may God treat you the same way and more."
Samuel told Eli everything and did not hide anything from him. And Eli said, "He is the Lord, he can do whatever seems good to him."
And as Samuel grew up the Lord was with him, and he made sure that all of Samuel's words were trustworthy.
All of Israel all the way from Dan to Beersheba knew that Samuel was the Lord's established prophet.
The Lord would appear in Shiloh, because he revealed himself and delivered his word to Samuel in Shiloh.
Samuel's word was heard throughout all of Israel. One day the Israelis went to do battle against the Philistines. They camped near Ebenezer and the Philistines camped in Aphek.
The Philistines arrayed themselves against the Israelis and when they joined the battle, Israel was defeated and about 4,000 Israelis soldiers were killed on the battlefield.

When the Israelis army returned to camp the elders said, "Why has the Lord allowed us to be defeated by the Philistines today? Let us bring the Lord's Ark of the Covenant from Shiloh, and we will carry it with us to save us from our enemies' hands."

So the army sent messengers to Shiloh and asked them to bring the Lord of Hosts' Ark of the Covenant whose throne lives between the cherubim. And Eli's two sons Hophni and Phinehas were there with God's Ark of the Covenant.
When the Lord's Ark of the Covenant was brought into camp, all of Israel shouted such a great shout, that it shook the earth.

When the Philistines heard such a great noise they said, "Why are the Hebrews shouting and making so much noise in their camp?" Then they realized that the Ark of the Covenant had come into the Israelis camp.
And the Philistines were so afraid, they said, "God has come into their camp, this will only bring us sorrow! Nothing like this has ever happened before.
Woe unto us! Who will deliver us from the hand of their mighty Gods? These are the same Gods that defeated the Egyptians out in the wilderness with all kinds of plagues.
O you Philistines, be strong and act like men, otherwise you may become the Hebrews servants, just as they have been you servants, so be men and fight."

Then the Philistines fought and they defeated Israel, and the Israelis army was routed, and they fled to their tents. There was a great slaughter that day and 30,000 Israelis soldiers were killed as they fled.
God's Ark of the Covenant was taken, and Eli's two sons Hophni and Phinehas were killed.
A Benjamite man from the army ran from the battlefield to Shiloh that day with his clothes torn, and he had dirt on his head.

When he arrived, Eli was sitting by the side of the road watching, because his heart trembled for God's Ark of the Covenant. And when the man entered the city and told them what had happened, the whole city cried out.
When Eli heard all of the crying he said, "What is all this noise and tumult about?" And the man quickly came and told Eli what happened.
Now Eli was 98 years old, and his eyes were dim and he could not see.
And the man said to Eli, "I have come from the army, and I fled the battle today," And Eli asked, "What has happened my son?"

The messenger answered Eli and said, "Israel fled from the Philistines, and there was a great slaughter among the soldiers. Your sons Hophni and Phinehas are dead, and God's Ark of the Covenant has been taken."

As soon as he mentioned God's Ark of the Covenant, Eli fell backwards from his seat beside the city gate, and because he was a fat old man, his neck was broken and he died. Eli had judged Israel for forty years.

Phinehas' wife was Eli's daughter-in-law, and she was pregnant with a baby that was nearly ready to be delivered. When she heard that God's Ark of the Covenant had been taken, and that her father-in-law and her husband were both dead, she went into labor and collapsed because she was overwhelmed by her labor pains.
As she lay dying the women with her said, "Do not be afraid, because you have given birth to a son." But she did not answer or respond.
She named the child Ichabod and said, "Glory has left Israel, for God's Ark of the Covenant was taken!" And her father-in-law and husband were both dead.
And she said, "Glory has left Israel, for God's Ark of the Covenant has been taken."
And the Philistines took God's Ark of the Covenant and brought it from Ebenezer to Ashdod.
When the Philistines took God's Ark of the Covenant, they brought it into the house of Dagon and set it next to Dagon.
When the people of Ashdod got up early the next morning, Dagon had fallen facedown on the ground in front of the Ark of the Covenant, so they put Dagon back in his place.

When they got up early the morning after that, Dagon had fallen facedown again, and he was laying on the ground in front of the Ark of the Covenant again. Dagon's head and hands had been cut off and only the stump of his body was laying on the threshold.
That's why when the priests or anyone else comes to Dagon's house in Ashdod, they will not walk on the threshold of Dagon's house to this day.
But the Lord's hand lay heavily on the people of Ashdod and he destroyed them. He afflicted them and the people living near their borders with tumors.
When the men of Ashdod saw that, they said, "The Ark of the God of Israel cannot remain here, because their God's hand lays heavily upon us and our god Dagon!"

So, they sent for the Philistine leaders and spoke to them and asked, "What can we do with the Ark of the God of Israel?" And they answered them and said, "Carry the Ark of the God of Israel to Gath," so they took it there.
After they carried it to Gath, the Lord's hand was against that city too. He brought a great destruction against both the great and small men there, and they were also afflicted with tumors.

So they sent God's Ark of the Covenant to Ekron and the Ekronites cried out and said, "They have brought God's Ark of the Covenant from Israel to us, in order to kill us and our people, the way it killed them."

So they sent for the Philistine leaders and said, "Send the God of Israel's Ark of the Covenant away, it must be returned to its own place, so that it does not kill all of our people!" Because a deadly destruction moved throughout the city, and God's hand lay very heavily on them.
Those who did not die were afflicted with tumors, and the city's cries were heard heaven.
The Ark of the Covenant had been in Philistine for seven months.
So the Philistines summoned the priests and diviners and said, "What should we do with the Ark of the Covenant? Tell us how to send it back to its place."

And the priests and diviners said, "If you send the ark of the God of Israel away, do not send it away empty, but return it to him with a trespass offering, then you will be healed. And you will know why his hand has not left you."

Then the Philistines asked, "What trespass offering must we send back to God?" The priests and diviners answered, "Five golden tumors, and five golden mice which represents the number of Philistine lords. Because the same plague that was placed on you was also placed on your Lords.
So, make gold images of your tumors and mice that are ruining your land and give glory to the God of Israel. Maybe he will lift his hand from you, your gods, and your land.
Why harden your hearts like Pharaoh and the Egyptians? When he worked his wonders among them, did they not let the people go when they departed?
So now, build a new cart with two milk cows that have never been yoked. Tie the cows to the cart but separate their calves from them and bring them home.
When you return it to him, lay the Ark of the Covenant on the cart, and put gold jewels in a chest beside it as a trespass offering. Then let it go and send it away.

But keep an eye on it and see if it goes up the road toward its home in Beth-Shemesh. If it does, then the Lord has done this great evil to us. If not then we will know that we were not defeated by his hand, but it just happened by chance."
So they took two milk cows and tied them to the cart and took their calves home.
Then they laid the Lord's Ark of the Covenant and the chest with the gold images of the mice and tumors on the cart.

And the cows went straight to the road to Beth-Shemesh, and stayed on that highway, mooing as they went. They did not turn to the left or the right, and the Philistine lords followed them to the border of Beth-Shemesh.
The people of Beth-Shemesh were harvesting their wheat in the valley, and when they looked up, they saw the ark and they began to rejoice.
And the cart came into the field of a Beth-Shemite named Joshua and stopped near a large stone. The people there took the cart's wood and offered the cows as a burnt offering to the Lord.

The Levites took the Ark of the Covenant and the chest that held the gold jewels and lowered them down from the cart. They set them on the stone, and the men of Beth-Shemesh offered burnt offerings and made sacrifices to the Lord that same day.
After the five Philistine lords saw this, they returned to Ekron that same day.
The Philistines had returned one gold tumor as a trespass offering to the Lord for each of the five cities Ashdod, Gaza, Askelon, Gath, and Ekron.

They also sent enough gold mice to represent the number of Philistine cities that belonged to the five lords. Both their fortified cities and their country villages, all the way to the great stone of Abel, on which they sat the Ark of the Covenant. And this stone remains in Joshua the Beth-Shemite's field to this day.
But God struck down 50,070 men of Beth-Shemesh, because they looked into his Ark of the Covenant. And the people mourned because the Lord had defeated many of them with a great slaughter.
The men of Beth-Shemesh said, "Who can stand before the Holy Lord God, and to whom should we send the ark from here?"
They sent messengers to the inhabitants of Kiriath-Jearim and said, "The Philistines have returned the Ark of the Covenant, so come down and take it back up with you."
The men of Kiriath-Jearim came and carried the Ark of the Covenant back to Abinadab's house up on the hill and sanctified his son Eleazar to keep the Ark of the Covenant.
From that day forward the ark had been in Kiriath-Jearim for twenty years, and the entire House of Israel mourned and sought the Lord for a long time.

Samuel spoke to all the Israelis and said, "If you return to the Lord with all your hearts, and get rid of Ashtaroth and the strange gods, and prepare your hearts to only serve the Lord, and he will deliver you from the hands of the Philistines."
So the Israelis put away Baal and Ashtaroth, and they only served the Lord.
Then Samuel said, "Assemble all of the Israelis in Mizpah, and I will pray to the Lord for you."

So they gathered together in Mizpah, where they drew water, and poured it out before the Lord. They fasted that day and said, "We have sinned against the Lord!" And Samuel judged the Israelis in Mizpah.
When the Philistines heard that the Israelis had gathered together in Mizpah, the Philistine lords marched toward Israel, and when the Israelis heard it, they were afraid of the Philistines.
Then the Israelis pleaded with Samuel and said, "Do not stop crying out to our Lord God for us, so that he will save us from the hands of the Philistines."
So Samuel offered a suckling lamb as a whole burnt offering to the Lord, and he cried out to the Lord for Israel, and the Lord heard him.

As Samuel offered up the burnt offering, the Philistines moved in closer to do battle against Israel. But the Lord thundered loudly against them that day, and the Israelis embarrassed and defeated them.
The Israelis army left Mizpah and pursued and defeated the Philistines all the way to Beth-Car.
And Samuel set up a stone between Mizpah and Shen where he named it Ebenezer and said, "Until now the Lord has helped us."
