And he said, "Lord God of Israel, there is no God like you in heaven above or on earth below, you keep your covenant with your servants and show mercy to those who walk before you with all their heart.
You have kept the promise which you spoke with your mouth to your servant, my father David. And you have fulfilled it with your hands this very day.

So now O Lord God of Israel, keep the promise you made to your servant my father David when you said, 'You shall never fail to have a descendant sitting on the throne of Israel before me, if your they take heed to walk before me as you have walked before me.'
O God of Israel, I pray that you will confirm the words that you spoke to your servant my father David.
But can God live on the earth? Behold, even the highest heaven and heaven of heavens cannot contain you, much less this temple I have built you?
O Lord my God, respect your servant's prayers and plea, so that you may hear the cry and prayers that your servant pleads before you today.
May your eyes be open toward this temple both night and day which is where you have said, 'My name will be there,' so that you may hear the prayers that your servant prays for this place.
Listen to the plea of your servant and your people of Israel, when they pray about this place, and please forgive when you hear these prayers in your home in heaven.
If a man sins against his neighbor, and he must come before your altar to swear an oath in this temple.

And when you hear this in heaven, please listen to us and judge your servants, condemn the wicked and bring everything he has done down on his own head, but justify the righteous and give to them in accordance with their righteousness.
When your Israelis people are defeated before the enemy, because they have sinned against you, and they turn back to you and confess your name and they pray and plead to you in this temple.
When you hear this in heaven and forgive the sins of your people of Israel, and bring them back to the land that you gave their fathers.
When heaven is closed and there is no rain because they have sinned against you, if they turn toward this temple to pray and confess your name, and turn from their sins when you afflict them.

When you hear this in heaven and forgive the sins of your servants the people of Israel, and you teach them the good ways they should walk, and let it rain on your land, which you have given to your people as an inheritance.
If there is a famine, pestilence, blight, mildew, locusts, or caterpillars in the land, or if their enemy besieges them in their cities, or any other plague or sickness that comes.
Then whatever prayer or plea of any kind is made by anyone or by all of your Israelis people, and each man knows the plague of his own heart, and he spreads his hands out toward this temple.

When hear you this in your home in heaven, please forgive and listen to us, and give to each man whose heart you already know everything about his ways, because only you know the hearts of all of men's descendants.
So that they will fear you for their entire life in the land you gave to our fathers.
As for the foreigner that is not one of your Israelis people, but they come here from a country far away because of your name.
Because they will hear of your great name, your strong hand and your out stretched arm, and when they comes to pray toward this temple.

Hear them from your home place in heaven, and listen to everything that the foreigner asks of you when you know their ways, so that all people of the earth may know your name and fear you, as do your Israelis people. So that they may also know that the temple I built, is dedicated only to you and your name.
If your people leave to do battle against their enemy wherever you send them, and they pray to the Lord toward your chosen city and the temple that I built in your name.
Then hear their prayers and pleas in heaven, and maintain their cause.

If they sin against you, because there are no men without sin, and you are angry with them and deliver them to the enemy, so that they are carried away as captives to the enemies land, whether near or far.
If they return to their senses in their land of captivity, and they repent and plea with you in their captors land and they say, 'We have sinned and have been perverse, and we have been wicked.'

If they return to you with all their heart and soul while in their enemy's land where they were led as captives. If they pray to you for the land you gave to their fathers and your chosen city, and the temple which I built in your name.
Then hear their prayer and plea in your home in heaven, and maintain their cause.
And forgive your people and all the sins that they have committed against you, and give compassion to their captors, so that they may show your people compassion and mercy.
Because they are your people and your inheritance, and you brought them out of Egypt from the middle of the iron furnace.
So that your eyes are open to your servant's and your Israelis people's plea, and listen to everything that they ask of you.
Because, O Lord God you did separate them from all the other people of the earth as your inheritance, as you spoke through your servant Moses, when you brought our fathers out of Egypt."
When Solomon finished this prayer and plea to the Lord, he got up from before the Lord's altar, where he had been kneeling with his hands spread up toward heaven.
He stood up and blessed the entire Israelis congregation with a loud voice and said,
"Blessed is the Lord for giving rest to his people of Israel as he promised, and not one word of his good promise which he promised through his servant Moses has failed.
May the Lord our God be with us as he was with our fathers, let him not leave us nor forsake us.
So that he may incline our hearts to walk with him in all his ways and keep his commandments, laws, and judgments that he commanded our fathers to keep.
Let my words I have pled before the Lord be near to our Lord God day and night, so that he may maintain his servants and the cause of his Israeli people at all times, as each day requires.
So that everyone on earth may know that the Lord is God, and there is no other.
Therefore let your heart be as devoted to our Lord God as it is today, to walk in his laws and keep his commandments."
Then the king and all the Israelis with him offered sacrifices before the Lord.
Solomon offered 22,000 oxen and 120,000 sheep as his peace offering sacrifice to the Lord. So that's how the king and all of the Israelis dedicated the Lord's temple.

That same day the king consecrated the middle court in front of the Lord's temple, because that's where he offered burnt offerings, bread offerings, and the fat from the peace offerings. Because the brass altar that was before the Lord was too small to hold all those sacrificial offerings.

At that time Solomon and all of the Israelis with him held a feast, a great congregation came from the entrance of Hamath all the way to the Nile River to feast before our Lord God for seven days, and then another seven days after that for a total of fourteen days.

On the eighth day he sent the people away and they blessed the king and went back home joyful and with a happy heart for all the goodness that the Lord had done for his servant David, and his Israelis people.
When Solomon finished building the Lord's temple and the king's palace, and everything else that Solomon wanted.
The Lord appeared to Solomon a second time, as he had appeared to him in Gibeon.

And the Lord said to him, "I have heard the prayer and plea that you have made before me, I have consecrated this temple you have built and placed my name there forever, and I will watch over it with my eyes and my heart forever.
If you walk before me as your father David walked with honest integrity of heart, in accordance with everything that I have commanded, and you keep my laws and judgments.
Then I will establish the throne of your kingdom over Israel forever, as I promised your father David when I said, 'There will never fail to be one of your descendants to govern Israel.'
But if you or your descendants turn away from following me, and you do not keep my commandments and laws I have set before you, but you go to worship and serve other gods.

Then I will cut Israel off from the land which I have given them, and this temple which I have consecrated in my name will be thrown out of my sight, and Israel will become a lesson and an example to all nations.
This high temple will become a pile of rubble, and everyone that passes by it will be astonished and they will hiss and say, 'Why has the Lord done this to this land and this temple?'

Then they will answer and say, 'Because they have forsaken their Lord God, who brought their fathers from the land of Egypt, and have they have held to other gods, worshipped, and served them, so the Lord has brought all this evil on them.'"
It took Solomon twenty years to build the Lord's temple and the king's palace.
Now King Hiram of Tyre furnished Solomon with as many cedar trees and fir trees, and as much gold as he desired, so King Solomon gave King Hiram twenty cities in Galilee.
And Hiram left Tyre and went to see the cities Solomon had given him, and he was not happy.
And he said, "What kind of cities have you given me my brother?" And he named them the Land of Cabul, as they are still called to this day.
Then Hiram sent 120 gold talents to the king.
King Solomon had to raise an army of workers to build the Lord's temple, his own palace, Jerusalem's walls, Millo, Hazor, Megiddo, and Gezer.
Because Pharaoh the king of Egypt had gone up and taken Gezer, then burned it and killed the Canaanites living in the city, and he gave it to his daughter who was married to Solomon as a present.
So Solomon rebuilt Gezer and lower Beth-Horon.
Baalath and Tadmor in the wilderness of Judah.
As well as the cities where Solomon stored everything he had including his chariots and horses, and whatever else he desired to build in Jerusalem, Lebanon, and the entire lands of his domain.
As for all the surviving Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites who were not descendants of Israel.
Solomon placed all the people left in the land whom the Israelis were unable to completely destroy, into slavery and they remain slaves to this very day.
But Solomon did not make any Israelis into slaves, because they were his soldiers, servants, officials, officers, and the commanders of his chariots and cavalry.
Overall, Solomon had 550 supervisors and chief officers that supervised all the workers that did his work.
When Pharaoh's daughter came up from the City of David to the palace that Solomon built for her, he built the Millo (city fortifications).
Three times a year after the temple was finished Solomon offered burnt offerings, peace offerings, and he burned incense to the Lord on the altar he built.
King Solomon built a navy with ships from Ezion-Geber, which was beside Eloth on the shores of the Red Sea in Edom.
Hiram sent servants from his navy, to help Solomon's servants with their knowledge of the seas.
They went to Ophir and brought 420 gold talents from there, and gave it to King Solomon.
When the queen of Sheba heard of Solomon's fame concerning the name of the Lord, she came to test him with difficult questions.
She arrived in Jerusalem with a very large caravan of camels carrying spices, lots of gold, and precious stones. Then she went to Solomon and spoke to him about everything that was in her heart.
Solomon answered all her questions, and there was nothing that he could not tell her.
When the queen of Sheba saw all of Solomon's wisdom for herself, and the palace that he had built.

Plus all the food on his table, how his servants, ministers, and attendants lived and attended to his needs and their apparel, and the burnt offerings he presented at the Lord's temple, it took her breath away.
And she said to the king, "Everything I heard in my own land about your accomplishments and wisdom is all true.
But I did not believe it until I came here and saw it with my own eyes, and now I see that I was not even told half the story, your wisdom and prosperity far exceeds everything I ever heard.
How blessed are your people and your servants who stand before you listening to your wisdom everyday.
Blessed is your Lord God who delighted in you and set you on the throne of Israel, because the Lord love Israel forever, so he made you king, to make judgments and bring justice."

Then the queen of Sheba gave King Solomon 120 gold talents, and a great quantity of spices and precious stones, there was never again such an abundance of spices ever given to the king like what she had given to the him.
Hiram's navy also brought gold, plenty of almug trees, and precious stones from Ophir.

The King made columns for the Lord's temple, the king's palace, and harps for singers from the almug trees. There had never before been seen such high quality almug trees, nor have they been seen since, even to this very day.

King Solomon gave the queen of Sheba whatever her heart desired, and whatever she asked for, besides what he had already given her from his royal bounty. So she and her servants left and went back to their own country.
One year, King Solomon collected gold that weighed as much as 666 gold talents.
In addition to the revenues he collected from his merchants who trafficked in spices, and all of the Arabian kings, and the country's governors.
King Solomon had 200 hammered gold shields made that weighed 600 gold shekels each.
The king had 300 hammered gold shields made, and each shield contained three minas of gold, and he put them in the palace of the Forest of Lebanon.
Besides that the king had a great ivory throne made, and he had it overlaid with the finest gold.
The throne had six steps, and the top of the throne was curved around the back, and there were armrests on either side of the seat, with two lions standing beside the armrests.
There were twelve lions, one stood on each side of the six steps, and there had never been anything like it made in any kingdom before.

All of King Solomon's drinking cups, and all the vessels for the palace of the Forest of Lebanon were made of pure gold. In Solomon's day they did not make anything of silver because it was thought to be worthless.

Because the king had a navy that sailed from the port of Tarshish along with Hiram's navy, and once every three years ships from Tarshish would arrive bringing gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks.
So King Solomon far exceeded all the earthly kings in riches and wisdom.
Everyone on earth sought the wisdom of Solomon which God had put in his heart.
Every year they brought him their tributes of gold and silver bowls, garments, armor, spices, horses, and mules.
Solomon accumulated 1,400 chariots and 12,000 horses, that he stationed in his chariot cities of Jerusalem.
The king made silver as common as stones in Jerusalem , and cedar was as abundant as the sycamore trees in the foothills.
Solomon's merchants had horses and linen yarn brought in from Egypt, that were purchased at a fair price.
Chariots from Egypt could be purchased for 600 silver shekels, and a horse for 150. And all the Hittite and Syrian kings also imported their chariots and horses from there.
But King Solomon loved many foreign women besides Pharaoh's daughter including Hittite women and women from Moab, Ammon, Edom, and Sidon.

These women were from the nations that the Lord had warned the Israelis not to marry into when he said, "You must not marry them and you must not mix with them, because they will surely turn your hearts toward their gods." But, Solomon was in love and clung loyally to these women.
He had 700 royal princess wives and 300 concubines, and his wives turned his heart away from his God.
When Solomon grew old, his wives had turned his heart to other gods, and his heart was not perfect with his Lord God, as his father David's heart was.
Because Solomon followed the Sidonian goddess Ashtoreth and Milcom the Ammonite's abomination.
Solomon did evil in the Lord's sight and did not fully follow after the Lord, as did his father David.
Then in the hills before Jerusalem, Solomon built a high place for Chemosh the abomination of Moab, and Molech the abomination of the Ammonites.
And he did this for all of his foreign wives who burned incense and made sacrifices to their gods.
The Lord was angry with Solomon, because his heart had turned away from the Lord God of Israel, who had appeared to him twice.
Solomon had been given a commandment about this, and he was warned not to chase after other gods, but he did not keep the Lord's commandment.
So the Lord said to Solomon, "Because you have done this and you have not kept my covenant and the laws I have given you, I will surely tear the kingdom from you and give it to your servant.
However for your father David's sake, I will not tear it from your hands, but I will tear it from your son's hands.
But I will not tear away the entire kingdom, I will give one tribe to your son for my servant David's sake and for the sake of Jerusalem, which I have chosen.
Then the Lord stirred up an adversary against Solomon, Hadad the Edomite one of the king's descendants in Edom.
Because when David was in Edom, Joab the army commander had gone up to bury the dead, after he had killed every male in Edom.
For six months Joab and all the Israelis remained there, until he had cut off every male in Edom.
But Hadad had fled to Egypt when he was just a little child with certain of his father's Edomite servants.
So they left Midian and went to Paran, where they took men from Paran with them on to Pharaoh king of Egypt, who gave him a house, prepared food, and land.
Hadad had found such great favor in Pharaoh's sight, that he gave his own wife queen Tahpenes' sister to him to be his wife.
Tahpenes' sister gave birth to Hadad's son who they named Genubath. Tahpenes weaned him in Pharaoh's house, and Genubath lived there among Pharaoh's sons.
When Hadad heard in Egypt that David slept with his fathers and that Joab the commander of the army was dead, Hadad said to Pharaoh, "Let me go, so that I may return to my own country."
Then Pharaoh asked him and said, "But what have you lacked here with me, that you suddenly want to return to your own country?" And he answered, "I have lacked nothing, but let me go anyway."
God stirred up another adversary against Solomon, Eliadah's son Ezron who had fled from his Lord King Hadadezer of Zobah.
Ezron had put together a group of raiders and became their leader. When David killed the Zobaites, Ezron and his men went to Damascus, where they settled and took control.
He abhorred Israel and he was their adversary all the days of Solomon's life. He added to the mischief that Hadad caused, and he reigned over Syria.
Even Nebat's son Jeroboam an Ephrathite from Zereda who was Solomon's servant, and whose mother was a widow named Zeruah, turned against the king.
This is what caused him to turn against the king, Solomon had built fortifications, and strengthened the broken defenses of the city of his father David.
So, Jeroboam was a mighty man of valor, and Solomon saw that he was very industrious, and he put him in charge of the work force in Joseph's house.
One day Jeroboam met the prophet Ahijah the Shilonite along the road as he left Jerusalem. Ahijah was wearing a new robe, and the two of them found themselves all alone by the field.
Then Ahijah grabbed hold of his new robe and tore it into twelve pieces.

And he spoke to Jeroboam and said, "Take ten pieces of this robe, because this is what the Lord God of Israel says, 'Behold, I will tear Solomon's kingdom from his hands, and I will give you ten tribes.
But Solomon's descendants will keep one tribe for my servant David's sake and for the sake of Jerusalem, the city I have chosen from among all the tribes of Israel.

Because they have forsaken me and worshipped Ashtoreth the Sidonian goddess, Chemosh the Moabite God, and Milcom the God of the Ammonite's descendants. They have not walked in my ways, nor have they done that which is right in my eyes. And unlike Solomon's father David, they do not keep my laws and judgments.

However I will not remove the whole kingdom from Solomon's hands, but I will make him a ruler all the days of his life for my servant David's sake, whom I chose because he kept my commandments and my laws.
But I will take the kingdom from his son's hand, and give ten tribes of it to you.
I will give his son one tribe, so that my servant David may always have a light before me in Jerusalem, the city I have chosen to put my name upon.
And as for you, I will make you the king of Israel and you will reign over all the land that your heart desires.

And if you listen to everything that I command you, and walk in my ways, and do what is right in my sight, and you keep my laws and commandments, as my servant David did, then I will be with you. I will build you a stable kingdom just as I did for David, and I will give Israel to you.
And I will humble David's descendants, but not forever.'"
That's why Solomon tried to kill Jeroboam, and Jeroboam fled to King Shishak of Egypt, and lived in Egypt until Solomon died.
As for the rest of the acts of Solomon, and everything that he has done as well as his wisdom, are all written in the book of the Acts of Solomon.
So, Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all of Israel for forty years.
After that, Solomon slept with his fathers and he was buried in the city of his father David, and his son Rehoboam reigned in his place.
Rehoboam went to Shechem, because all of Israel went to Shechem to make him king.
When Nebat's son Jeroboam heard about this, he was still in Egypt where he had lived ever since he had fled from King Solomon.
So they sent for Jeroboam and he and the entire Israelis congregation came and spoke to Rehoboam.
And they said, "Your father put a grievous yoke on us, but if you lighten the burden and heavy yoke your father put on us, we will serve you."
And he said to them, "Leave here for three days then come back to me," and the people left.
King Rehoboam consulted with the old men that advised his father Solomon while he was still living and said, "Give me your advice and tell me how you think I should answer these people?"
And they spoke up and said, "If you will be these people's servant today, and you serve them and answer them with good words, then they will be your servants forever."
But he rejected the old men's counsel, and he consulted the young men that he grew up with who had served him.
And he asked them, "What advice can you give me about how I should answer these people, who have spoken to me and said, 'Make the yoke your father put on us lighter'?"

The young men that grew up with him said, "This is how you should speak to these people that said, 'Your father made our yoke heavy, but you must make our yoke lighter than your father's yoke,' and this is what you should say to them, 'My little finger will be thicker than my father's waist!
In fact my father did load you with a heavy yoke, but I will add to your yoke, my father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions."
So Jeroboam and all the people returned to Rehoboam on the third day, at the time the king had appointed when he said, "Return here in three days."
The king ignored the old men's advice and he answered the people harshly.

And he spoke to them as the young men advised him and said, "My father made your yoke heavy, and I will add to your yoke, my father also chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions."
So the king did not listen to the people, in order to fulfill what the Lord had said when he spoke to Jeroboam through Nebat's son Ahijah the Shilonite.

When all the Israelis saw that the king would not listen to them, they answered him and said, "What portion have we in David? And what inheritance do we have in the son of Jesse? Return to your tents, O Israel! Now take care of your own house, O David!" So the Israelis went home.
But Rehoboam reigned over the Israelis who lived in the cities of Judah.
Then King Rehoboam sent Adoram, who was in charge of his workers, and the Israelis stoned him to death. So King Rehoboam hastily climbed up into his chariot and fled to Jerusalem.
So to this day the Israelis still rebel against the house of David.

When the Israelis heard that Jeroboam had returned, they summoned him to the congregation, and made him king over all of Israel, none of them followed the house of David, except for the tribe of Judah.

And when Rehoboam went to Jerusalem, he assembled 180,000 chosen warriors from the house of Judah and the tribe of Benjamin to fight against the House of Israel, to bring the kingdom back to Solomon's son Rehoboam.
But the word of God came to Shemaiah the man of God.
And he said, "Speak to Solomon's son King Rehoboam of Judah, and the entire house of Judah and Benjamin, and to all that remains of the people.

And say this, 'This is what the Lord says, "You must not go fight against your Israelis brothers, so return to your homes because this word is from me."' So they listened to the him, and returned home.
Then Jeroboam built Shechem on Mount Ephraim and lived in there for a while, then he left to go build Penuel.
And Jeroboam said in his heart, "Now the kingdom will return to the house of David.
If these people go up to make sacrifices in the Lord's temple at Jerusalem, their hearts will return to their lord King Rehoboam of Judah, and they will kill me and return to King Rehoboam of Judah."

After the king took counsel, he had two gold calves made and he said to the people, "It is too much for you to go up to Jerusalem. Behold O Israel here are the gods that brought you up out of the land of Egypt."
He had one put in Bethel and the other in Dan.
And it became a sin, because the people walked as far as Dan to worship before one of the calves.
Jeroboam built shrines in high places, and made priests from the lowest class of people who were not even Levites.

And Jeroboam ordained a feast on the fifteenth day of the eighth month, like the feast that was in Judah, and he offered sacrifices on the altar. So he made this sacrifice in Bethel to his golden calves, and he put the priests in Bethel in the high places he had made.
So on the fifteenth day of the eighth month in the month that Jeroboam designated, he ordained a feast for the Israelis, and offered sacrifices on the altar he had built, and burned incense.
One day as Jeroboam was stood by the altar burning incense, a man of God sent by the Lord's word came to Bethel from Judah.

Then he cried out the Lord's word against the altar and said, "O altar, this is what the Lord says, 'A child named Josiah will be born into the house of David, and he will sacrifice to you the priests of the high places that burn incense on you, and the people's bones will be burned on you.'"
That same day he gave a sign and said, "This is the sign of which the Lord has said, 'Behold the altar will be torn apart, and the ashes on it will be poured out.'"

When King Jeroboam heard what the man of God who cried against the altar in Bethel said, he stretched out his hand from the altar and said, "Seize him!" But the king's outstretched hand shriveled up, and he could not pull it back.
Suddenly the altar was torn apart and ashes poured out from it, and this was the sign which the Lord's word spoke of through the man of God.

The king responded to the man of God and said, "Plead with your Lord God, and pray for me, so that my hand may be restored." And the man of God implored to the Lord, and the king's hand was restored to normal as it was before.
Then the king spoke to the man of God and said, "Come home with me and refresh yourself, and I will reward you."
And the man of God replied to the king and said, "Even if you were to give me half of your house, I would not go with you, nor will I not eat or drink in this place either.
Because the Lord's word came to me and said, 'Eat no bread, drink no water, nor return home by the same way that you came.'"
So he went in another direction, and he did not return home the same way that he had come to Bethel.

Now there was an old prophet who lived in Bethel, and his sons came and told him everything that the man of God had done in Bethel. They also told their father what the man of God said to the king that day.
And their father said to them, "Which way did he go?" Because his sons had seen which way the man of God went when he left Judah.
Then he said to his sons, "Saddle my donkey." So they saddled his donkey, and he rode off in that direction.
So he followed the man of God and when he found him sitting under an oak tree he said to him, "Are you the man of God that came from Judah?" And he said, "I am."
Then he said to him, "Come home with me and eat some bread."
And he said, "I can not go with you, nor will I eat or drink with you in that place.
Because the Lord's word came to me and he said, "You must not eat or drink there, and you must not return home the same way that you came."

And the old prophet said to him, "I am also a prophet just like you, and an angel came to me and brought me the Lord's word and said, Bring the Lord's prophet back to your house, so that he may eat some bread and drink water with you." But this was a lie.
So he went back with him, and ate bread and drank water in his house.
As they sat at the table, the Lord's word came to the old prophet that brought him back.
And he cried to the man of God that came from Judah and said, "This is what the Lord says, 'Because you have disobeyed the Lord's word, and you have not kept your Lord God's commandment.
But you went back with him and ate his bread and drank his water in the place that the Lord told you not to eat or drink there, your body will not reach the tomb of your fathers.'"
After he ate and drank, the old prophet saddled the man of God's donkey whom he had brought back.
After he left, a lion met the man of God by the side of the road and killed him, his body was thrown by the wayside, and the donkey and lion both stood by the man's carcass.
Then some men passed by and saw the body laying along the roadside and the lion standing next to the carcass, and they went to the city where the old prophet lived and told everyone there about it.

When the old prophet who had brought him back to the city heard of it he said, "It is the man of God, who was disobedient to the Lord's word, and the Lord delivered him to the lion that tore him apart and killed him, since he ignored the Lord's word."
The old prophet spoke to his sons and said, "Saddle my donkey," and they saddled it for him.
He went and found the man of God's body by the roadside with the donkey and lion standing next to the carcass, he saw that the lion had not eaten the man's carcass nor torn the donkey apart.
The old prophet laid the man of God's body on the donkey and brought it back, and he carried it back to the city to mourn and bury him.
The he laid the man's body in his own grave and they mourned over him and said, "Alas, this is my brother!"
After the old prophet buried him he spoke to his sons and said, "When I am dead, bury me in the tomb where the man of God is buried, and lay my bones beside his bones.
Because of the Lord's word which he cried out against the altar in Bethel, and all the shrines in the high places of the Samaritan cities, will surely come to pass.

After all this, Jeroboam still did not turn from his evil ways. But once again he ordained his priests of the high places from among the lowest classes of people. He declared anyone sacred that wanted to be a priest of the high places.
This action became the sin in the house of Jeroboam, that led to its destruction and its removal from the face of the earth.
At that time Jeroboam's son Abijah fell sick.

And Jeroboam said to his wife, "Please get up and disguise yourself, so that nobody knows that you are my wife, and go to Shiloh. Look for Ahijah the prophet there, because he told me that I should be these people's king.
Take ten loaves of bread, hard biscuits, and a small cup of honey with you. Go to him, and he will tell you what is to become of the child."
So Jeroboam's wife left and went to the house of Ahijah in Shiloh. But Ahijah was blind and could not see because of his age.
And the Lord said to Ahijah, "Behold, Jeroboam's wife has come to ask you about her sick son, and this is what you must tell her, because she is coming to you disguised as another woman."

When Ahijah heard the sound of her footsteps as she came in the door, he said, "Come in, you must be Jeroboam's wife, why have you disguised yourself as someone else? Because now I have to give you some sad news.
Go and tell Jeroboam, this is what the Lord God of Israel says, 'Because I have glorified you from among the people, and made you the ruler of my people of Israel.

I tore the kingdom away from the house of David and gave it you, but you have not been like my servant David who kept my commandments and followed me with all his heart, who only did what he thought was righteous in my eyes.
But you have done evil above everyone else that came before you, and because you have made other gods and molten images to provoke me to anger, and you have thrown me away behind your back.

Therefore, I will bring down evil upon the house of Jeroboam, and I will cut you off from Jeroboam any male descendants who piss against the wall. Any of Jeroboam's descendants left in Israel will be removed like a man carries away dung until it is all gone.

Any of Jeroboam's descendants that die in the city will be eaten by dogs, and any of his descendants that die out in the field will be eaten by the birds of the air.' Because this is what the Lord has said.
So get up and go home, but when you enter the city, the child will die.

All of Israel will mourn and bury him, because he is the only descendant of Jeroboam who will be given a proper burial. Because from among the house of Jeroboam, he is the only one in which the Lord God of Israel has found something good.
Besides that, the Lord will raise up another king over Israel for himself, who will cut off the house of Jeroboam this very day.

Because the Lord will defeat Israel as a reed is shaken in the water, and he will root Israel out from this good land, which he gave to their fathers. He will scatter them beyond the Euphrates River, because they have made the Asherah poles that have provoked the Lord's anger.
So he will give up on Israel because of Jeroboam's sins, who also caused Israel to sin."
Jeroboam's wife got up and went back to Tirzah, and when she arrived at the door's threshold, the child died.
They buried him and all of Israel mourned for him, just as the Lord had said when he spoke through his servant the prophet Ahijah.
The rest of the acts of Jeroboam, including his wars and how he reigned, are all written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
Jeroboam reigned for twenty-two years. When he died and was buried, his son Nadab took his place as the next king.

Solomon's son Rehoboam was 41 years old when he began to reign over Judah, and he reigned for 17 years from Jerusalem, which is the city the Lord chose from all the other tribes of Israel to put his name on. Rehoboam's mother's name was Naamah and she was an Ammonite.
The city of Judah did evil in the Lord's sight, and they provoked his jealousy through their sins which were far above anything that their fathers had done.
Because they also built high places, graven images, and Asherah poles on every high hill and under every green tree.
There were also Sodomites in the land, and they committed every abomination of the nations that the Lord had thrown out before the Israelis.
In the fifth year of King Rehoboam, King Shishak of Egypt attacked Jerusalem.
Shishak took all the treasures from the Lord's temple and the king's palace including all of the gold shields which Solomon had made.
King Rehoboam had brass shields made to replace them and turned them over to the commander of the guard, who protected the king's palace door.
Whenever the king entered the Lord's temple, the guards carried them, and afterwards they brought them back into the guards' chamber.
Now the rest of the acts of Rehoboam, and all that he did, are all written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah.
And there was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam for their whole entire lives.
Rehoboam died and slept with his fathers and was buried with them in the city of David. His mother's name was Naamah and she was an Ammonite, and his son Abijam reigned in his place.
Now in the eighteenth year of the reign of Nebat's son King Jeroboam, Abijam became the king of Judah.
He reigned in Jerusalem for three years. His mother's name was Maachah who was Absalom's daughter.
He practiced all the sins that his father committed before him. His heart was not as perfect with his Lord God as his forefather David's heart had been
Nevertheless, for David's sake the Lord God gave him a lamp in Jerusalem by raising up his son after him, to help establish Jerusalem.

Because David had always done what he thought was righteous in the Lord's eyes, and he did not turn away from anything that the Lord commanded him in his entire life, except for the matter of Uriah the Hittite.
And there was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam for Abijam's whole entire life.
Now the rest of the acts of Abijam and everything that he did, are all written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah, including the war's between Abijam and Jeroboam.
Abijam died and slept with his fathers. They buried him in the city of David and his son Asa reigned in his place.
In the twentieth year of King Jeroboam reign over Israel, Asa reigned over Judah.
Asa reigned from Jerusalem for forty-one years, and his grandmother Maachah was Absalom's daughter.
Asa did whatever he thought was righteous in the Lord's eyes, just like his father David had done.
He removed the Sodomites from the land, and all the idols that his forefathers had made.
He also removed his grandmother Maachah as queen, because she had built an Asherah pole idol. Asa destroyed and burned it near the Brook of Kidron.
Even though the shrines built in the high places were not removed, Asa's heart was perfect with the Lord for all of his days.
Then he brought everything that he and his father had dedicated, into the Lord's temple including the silver and gold vessels.
There was war between Asa and King Baasha of Israel for all the days of their lives.
King Baasha of Israel attacked Judah and built Ramah, so that nobody could enter or leave the territory of King Asa of Judah.

Then King Asa took all the silver and gold that remained in the treasuries of the Lord's temple and the king's palace, and handed it over to his servants. Then he sent them to Tabrimon and Hezion's son King Ben-Hadad of Syria, who lived in Damascus with a message.

They delivered their message and said, "Let us make a treaty between you and me, and between your father and my father. I have sent you a present of silver and gold, so that you will go and break your treaty with King Baasha of Israel, so that he will withdraw from me."
Ben-Hadad listened to King Asa and sent the commanders of his armies to attack the cities of Israel and he defeated Ijon, Dan, Abel-Beth-Maachah, and all of Naphtali including Chinneroth.
When Baasha heard about it, he stopped building Ramah and withdrew to Tirzah.

Then King Asa made a proclamation and summoned all the men throughout Judah, with no exceptions. They carried away all the stones and timber that Baasha had used to build in Ramah, and King Asa used them to build Geba of Benjamin and Mizpah.

The rest of all the acts of Asa, along with all his might, and everything else that he did, and the cities he built, are all written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah. However he suffered in his old age with diseased feet.
Asa died and slept with his fathers, and he was buried with his forefathers in the city of his father David, and his son Jehoshaphat reigned in his place.
Jeroboam's son Nadab began to reign over Israel in the second year of King Asa of Judah, and reigned over Israel for two years.
He did evil in the Lord's sight, and committed the same sins that his fathers did, that he also made Israel commit.
Ahijah's son Baasha from the house of Issachar conspired against Nadab, and while Nadab and the Israelis laid siege to the Philistine city of Gibbethon, Baasha killed Nadab.
Baasha killed Nadab in the third year of King Asa of Judah's reign, and reigned in his place.

During Baasha's reign, he killed all of Jeroboam's family, he did not leave any of them alive. He destroyed them all, to fulfill what the Lord had said when he spoke through his servant Ahijah the Shilonite.
Because of Jeroboam's sins, Israel also sinned and because he provoked the Lord God of Israel's anger.
The rest of all the acts of Nadab, and everything else that he did are all written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
And there was war between Asa and King Baasha of Israel for all the days of their lives.
Ahijah's son Baasha became the king of Israel during the third year of Asa's reign over Judah. Baasha ruled from Tirzah for twenty-four years.
But he did evil in the Lord's sight, and committed all the sins of Jeroboam which he also made Israel commit.
Then the Lord's word came to Hanani's son Jehu against Baasha.

And he said, "Because as I glorified you from the dust, and made you ruler over my people Israel, you have walked in the way of Jeroboam, and you have made my people of Israel sin, and provoked me to anger with their sins.
Behold, I will take away the posterity of Baasha and his house, and I will make your house like the house of Nebat's son Jeroboam.
Anyone from Baasha's family that dies in the city will be eaten dogs, and anyone from his family that dies in the fields will be eaten by the birds of the air."
The rest of the acts of Baasha, and everything that he did, and his might, are all written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
So Baasha died and slept with his fathers and was buried in Tirzah, and his son Elah reigned in his place.

The Lord's word came through Hanani's son Jehu the prophet against Baasha and his house, because of all the evil that he had done in the Lord's sight, and by provoking him to anger with the work of his hands, just like the house of Jeroboam and also because he killed Jeroboam.
In the twenty-sixth year of King Asa of Judah's reign, Baasha's son Elah began to reign over Israel in Tirzah, and he reigned for two years.
While Elah was in Tirzah getting drunk in his household manager Arza's house, his servant Zimri, who was the commander of half his army of chariots conspired against him.
Zimri attacked and killed Elah, in the twenty-seventh year of King Asa of Judah's reign, and he reigned in his place.

As soon as Zimri was seated on his throne and began to reign, he killed everyone in the house of Baasha. He did not leave even one man that pisses against the wall alive, and none of his friends or family survived.
Zimri destroyed the entire house of Baasha, just as the Lord had said when he spoke against Baasha through the prophet Jehu.
All of this happened because of Baasha and his son Elah's sins, and because they also made Israel commit their sins, and provoked the Lord God of Israel to anger with their vanities.
The rest of the acts of Elah, and everything that he did, are all written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
In the twenty-seventh year of King Asa's reign over Judah, Zimri reigned for only seven days in Tirzah. The Israelis armies were camped next to the Philistine city of Gibbethon.
And the troops in the camp heard that Zimri had conspired against and killed the king. So all the Israelis made Omri, who was the commander of the army, king of Israel that day in the camp.
Omri left Gibbethon and took all the Israelis with him, and they laid siege to Tirzah.
When Zimri saw that the city had been captured, he went into the inner court of the king's palace, and burned it down around himself and died.
All of this was because of the sins he committed and his evil doings in the Lord's sight, by walking in the ways of Jeroboam, and the sins which he made Israel commit.
The rest of the acts of Zimri, and the treason he committed, are all written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
Then the people of Israel were divided into two parts, half of the people followed Ginath's son Tibni who they made king, and the other half followed Omri.
But the people that followed Omri defeated the people that followed Ginath's son Tibni, so Tibni died and Omri reigned.
In the thirty-first year of the reign of King Asa of Judah, Omri began to reign over Israel, and he reigned for twelve years, and for six of them he reigned in Tirzah.
He bought the hill of Samaria from Shemer for two silver talents, then he built a city on top of the hill. He named the city Samaria after Shemer, who had owned the hill.
But Omri worked evil in the Lord's sight, and did worse things than anyone who had come before him.
Because he walked in all the ways of Nebat's son Jeroboam, and he also made Israel commit all his sins, and they provoked the Lord God of Israel's anger with their vanities.
The rest of the acts of Omri, and everything else that he did, and the might that he had shown, are all written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
So Omri died and slept with his fathers, and was buried in Samaria, and his son Ahab reigned in his place.
In the thirty-eighth year of the reign of King Asa of Judah, Omri's son Ahab began to reign over Israel, and Omri's son Ahab reigned over Israel in Samaria for twenty-two years.
Omri's son Ahab did more evil in the Lord's sight than everyone that came before him.
As if it were not enough for him to walk in the sins of Nebat's son Jeroboam, he married Jezebel the daughter of King Ethbaal of Sidonia, then he went and served and worshipped Baal.
Then he built an altar for Baal in the house of Baal, which he had built in Samaria.
King Ahab erected an Asherah pole, and he did more to provoke the Lord God of Israel's anger than all the other kings of Israel that came before him.

In Ahab's day, Hiel the Bethelite rebuilt Jericho, he laid its foundation at the cost of his firstborn son Abiram, and set up its gates at the cost of his youngest son Segub. All of this was to fulfill the Lord's word, which he had spoken through Nun's son Joshua.

Elijah the Tishbite from Mount Gilead spoke to Ahab and said, "I stand before the living Lord God of Israel, and he has told me that there will be no dew or rain in these years, except what comes from my word."
And the word of the Lord came to him and said.
And he said, "Leave here and head east, and hide near the Brook of Cherith before the Jordan River.
You will drink from the brook, and I have commanded the ravens to feed you there."
So he went and did everything the Lord told him, and he lived next to the Brook of Cherith before the Jordan River.
The ravens brought him bread and meat in the morning and the evening, and he drank from the brook.
After a while, the brook dried up because there had been no rain in the land.
And the word of the Lord came to him and said.
And he said, "Get up and go to Zarephath of Sidon, and live there. Behold I have commanded a widow woman there to sustain you."

So he got up and went to Zarephath, and when he arrived at the city gate, he saw the widow woman gathering sticks, and he called out to her and said, "I pray you will bring me a little cup of water to drink."
As she went to get him some water, he called out to her and said, "I pray you will bring me a morsel of bread too."

And she said, "As your Lord God lives, I do not have a cake, but I do have a handful of meal in a barrel and a small bottle of oil, and I am gathering some sticks, to take home to prepare a meal for me and my son, so that we may eat and then die."
And Elijah said to her, "Fear not, go and do as you have said but make a little bread cake and bring it to me first, then make some for you and your son.
Because this is what the Lord God of Israel says, 'The barrel of meal will not go to waste, the small bottle of oil will not run dry, until the day that the Lord sends rain on the earth.'"
So she did what Elijah told her to do, then both of them and her family ate for many days.
The flour barrel never went empty, and the bottle was never without oil. And everything was just as the Lord said it would be when he spoke through Elijah.
After all these things, the woman's son fell sick. She was the mistress of the house, and he was so sick that he could barely breathe.
And she said to Elijah, "O man of God, what have you done to me? Have you come to remind me of my sin, and kill my son?"
And he said to her, "Give me your son!" And he took him from her embrace, and carried him up into the loft where he lived, and he laid him on his own bed.
Then Elijah cried out to the Lord and said, "O my Lord God, have you brought evil upon the widow I travel with by killing her son?"
He stretched his body out over the top of child three times, and cried out to the Lord and said, "O my Lord God, I pray you will let this child's soul return to him."
The Lord heard Elijah's voice, and the child's soul returned to him and he was revived.
Then Elijah brought the child back down from the loft into the house, and delivered him to his mother. And Elijah said, "Look, your son still lives!"
Then the woman said to Elijah, "Now I know that you are a man of God by what you have done, and that the Lord's words in your mouth are truth."
After a long time, the Lord's word came to Elijah in the third year and said, "Go and show yourself to Ahab, and I will make it rain on the earth."
Elijah went to meet Ahab during a terrible famine in Samaria.
Ahab had summoned Obadiah who was the manager of his house, and he also greatly feared the Lord.
Because when Jezebel killed the Lord's prophets, Obadiah hid a hundred prophets in caves, with fifty of them in each cave, and gave them food and water.
Then Ahab said to Obadiah, "Go throughout the land to all fountains and brooks, and perhaps we can find enough grass to save the horses and mules, so that we do not lose all of our animals."
So Ahab and Obadiah each went in opposite directions to search the land.
Obadiah was walking along the road when Elijah met up with him and Obadiah knew him, and he bowed facedown and said, "Are you my Lord Elijah?"
He answered him and said, "I am, go and tell your Lord that Elijah is here."
Obadiah replied and said, "What sin have I committed, that you would deliver your servant into Ahab's hand to kill me?

As surely your Lord God lives, there is no nation or kingdom where my Lord has not looked for you. When they said, 'He is not here,' he made each kingdom or nation swear an oath that they had not found you.
Now you say, go and tell your Lord that Elijah is here.

And as soon as I am gone, the Lord's Spirit will carry you somewhere that I do not know. So when I go tell Ahab and then he cannot find you, he will kill me. But I am your servant and I have feared the Lord from my youth.
Were you not told about what I did when Jezebel killed the Lord's prophets? How I hid a hundred of them with fifty in each cave, and fed them bread and water?
Now you say, 'Go and tell your Lord that Elijah is here!' And if I do that, he will kill me."
And Elijah said, "As the Lord of Hosts lives who I stand before, I will surely show myself to him today."
So Obadiah went to tell Ahab, and Ahab went to meet Elijah.
When Ahab saw Elijah he said to him, "Are you the one that troubles Israel?"
Elijah answered him and said, "I have not troubled Israel, but you and your father's house have. You have forsaken the Lord's commandments, and you have followed Baalim.
So gather all of the Israelis together and send them to me at Mount Carmel, plus 450 of Baal's prophets, and the 400 Asherah prophets who eat at Jezebel's table."
So Ahab sent all of the Israelis and the prophets to Mount Carmel.

Elijah came to all the people and said, "How long will you swing back and forth between two opinions? If the Lord is God follow him, but if it is Baal then follow him," and the people did not say a word.
Then said Elijah to the people, "I am the only remaining prophet of the Lord, but Baal has 450 prophets.

So let them give us two bulls, and let them choose one for themselves and cut it in pieces, and lay it on the wood with no fire under it, and I will dress the other bull and lay it on the wood with no fire under it.
Then you call on the name of your gods, and I will call on the name of the Lord, then let the god that answers with fire be God!" All the people answered and said, "That is a good idea."
Elijah then said to Baal's prophets, "Choose you one bull for yourselves to prepare first, because there are many of you. Then call on the name of your gods, but put no fire under it."

They dressed the bull which was given to them, and they called on the name of Baal from morning to noon until evening and said, "O Baal, hear us!" But there was no sound, and no one answered as they leaped around the altar they had made.
At noon Elijah mocked them and said, "Cry louder because he is a god is he not, maybe he is thinking, or maybe he is on a journey, or perhaps he is just asleep and must be awakened!"
So they cried louder and cut themselves with knives and lancets, until their blood gushed out all over them.
When midday had passed, they prophesied until the time of the evening sacrificial offering, but no voice was heard, no one was answered, and no one was paying attention.
Then Elijah said to all the people, "Come near to me." And all the people moved closer to him, and he repaired the Lord's altar that had broken down.
Elijah took twelve stones, which represented the number of tribes from Jacob's sons, to whom the Lord's word came when he said, "Israel will be your name."
With those stones he built an altar in the Lord's name, and he dug a trench around the altar that could hold two measures of seed.
He put the wood in order and cut the bull into pieces, and laid it on the wood and said, "Fill four barrels with water, and pour it on the burnt sacrifice and the wood."
And he said, "Do the same thing again, and they did it the second time and he said, "Do it a third time," and they did it the third time.
The water ran all around the altar and the trench also filled with water.

At the time of the evening sacrificial offering, Elijah the prophet came near and said, "Lord God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, let it be known this day that you are God in Israel, and that I am your servant, and that I have done all of these things as you have said.
O Lord hear me, so that these people may know that you are the Lord God, and that you have turned their heart back to you."
Then the Lord's fire fell and consumed the burnt sacrifice, the wood, the stones, the dust, and evaporated the water in the trench.
When everyone saw that, they fell on their faces and said, "The Lord is God, the Lord is God."
And Elijah said to them, "Do not let Baal's prophets escape," and they brought them down to the Brook of Kishon, where Elijah had them killed.
Then Elijah said to Ahab, "Get up and eat and drink, because I hear the sound of abundant rain coming."
So Ahab went to eat and drink, and Elijah went to the top of Mount Carmel, and he threw himself down on the ground, and put his face between his knees.
And said to his servant, "Go and look out toward the sea." So he went and looked out and said, "There is nothing," and he told him seven times to go and look again.

Then the seventh time Elijah's servant said, "Behold there is a little cloud rising up out of the sea, it looks like a man's hand." And he said, "Run to Ahab and say, 'Prepare your chariot, and go down now so that the rain does not stop you.'"
In the mean while, the heavens were blackened with clouds and wind, and there was a great rain, and Ahab rode to Jezreel.
And the Lord's hand was on Elijah, and he wrapped his belt around his waist, and he ran before Ahab all the way to the entrance of Jezreel.
Ahab told Jezebel everything that Elijah had done, and with how he had killed all the prophets with the sword.
Then Jezebel sent a messenger to Elijah and said, "So let the gods do more to me by tomorrow if I do not make not your life like the life of one of those that you killed."
When Elijah heard that, he got up and fled for his life to Beersheba in Judah, and left his servant there.

But he himself traveled a day's journey out into the wilderness. He sat down under a juniper tree and prayed that God would let him die and he said, "O Lord, enough is enough, please take my life because I am no better than my fathers."
Then behold, as he lay down to sleep under a juniper tree an angel touched him and said, "Get up and eat."
He looked up and saw a cake baking on some coals and a small cup of water, so he ate and drank and laid back down.
The Lord's angel came to him a second time and touched him and said, "Get up and eat, because you have a long journey ahead of you."
He got up and ate and drank, and the strength he got from that food was all he needed to walk for forty days and forty nights to Mount Horeb, which is God's mountain.
He came to a cave there where he stayed, and behold the Lord's word came to him and said, "Why are you here Elijah?"

And he said, "I have been very jealous for the Lord God of Hosts. For the Israelis have forsaken your covenant, torn down your altars and killed your prophets. And now I am the only one left, and they want to take my life away as well."

And the Lord said, "Go and stand upon the mountain before the Lord." Then the Lord passed by and a great strong wind tore the mountains apart, and broke the rocks into pieces before the Lord. But the Lord was not in the wind, and after the wind there was an earthquake, but the Lord was not in the earthquake.
After the earthquake there was a fire, but the Lord was not in the fire, and after the fire there came a still small voice.
So, when Elijah heard it, he wrapped his face in his cloak and left. As he stood in the cave's entrance, behold a voice came to him and said, "Why are you here Elijah?"

And he said, I have been very jealous for the Lord God of Hosts, because the children of Israel have forsaken your covenant, thrown down your altars, and killed your prophets with the sword, and I, even I only, am left, and they seek my life, to take it away.
The Lord said to him, "Return the way you came to the wilderness of Damascus, and when you get there anoint Hazael as the king of Syria.
You must then anoint Nimshi's son Jehu as the king of Israel, and anoint Shaphat's son Elisha of Abel-Meholah to take your place as prophet.
Then anyone that escapes Hazael's sword will be killed by Jehu, and anyone that escapes Jehu's sword will be killed by Elisha.
But I have 7,000 people left in Israel who have not bowed to Baal or kissed him with their lips.
When Elijah left he found Shaphat's son Elisha plowing the field with twelve yokes of oxen, and he was standing next to the twelfth yoke of oxen. Elijah passed by him and threw his cloak on him.

Elisha left the oxen and ran after Elijah and said, "I pray you will let me kiss my father and mother goodbye, then I will follow you." And he replied to him and said, "Then go on back, what have I ever done for you?"

Elisha left and took a yoke of his oxen and killed them, then he boiled their meat with the wood from his oxen's yoke, and gave to the people and they ate. Then he got up, and followed Elijah and served Elijah.
King Ben-Hadad of Syria gathered his armies together, and he had thirty-two other kings with him plus their horses and chariots, and he went to war against Samaria.
And he sent messengers to Ahab King of Israel into the city, and said to him, in this says Ben-Hadad.
'Your silver and gold is mine, your best wives and children are also mine.'"
The king of Israel replied and said, "O my lord king, it is just as you have said, I am yours and so is everything that I have."
The messengers returned and said, "This is what King Ben-Hadad says, 'Even though I sent you a message and told you to deliver your silver, gold, wives, and your children to me.
But at about this time tomorrow I will send my servants to search your house, and your servant's houses, and they will seize and carry away anything that you value.

Then the king of Israel summoned all the elders of the land and said, "See how this man wants to create mischief? Because he sent me a message demanding my wives, my children, and my silver and gold, and I did not deny him."

Then the king of Israel summoned all the elders of the land and said, "See how this man wants to create mischief? Because he sent me a message demanding my wives, my children, and my silver and gold, and I did not deny him."

So Ahab replied to Ben-Hadad's messengers and said, "Tell my Lord the king, 'Everything you demanded from your servant at first I will do, but I can not do this thing.'"So the messengers returned to Ben-Hadad and gave him the message.
Ben-Hadad sent a message back to him and said, "May the gods punish me so much more severely, if any dust remains in Samaria for each man that follows me to have a handful."
The king of Israel answered and said, "Tell him, anyone putting on their armor, should not boast like the one who is taking theirs off.
Ben-Hadad and the other kings were drinking on their pavilions when they heard this and he said to his servants, "Prepare for battle," and they arrayed their armies against the city.

Behold a prophet came to King Ahab of Israel and said, "This is what the Lord says, 'Have you seen this great army? Behold, I will deliver it into your hands today, and you will know that I am the Lord.'"
Ahab asked, "By whom?" And the prophet replied, "This is what the Lord says, 'By the young provincial officers.' Then Ahab asked, "Who will start the battle?" And he answered, "You will."
When he counted his troops, he had 232 young provincial officers, and 7,000 soldiers from Israel.
The Israelis left at noon, but at the same time Ben-Hadad and the other thirty-two kings were drunk on their pavilions.
The young provincial officers left first. Ben-Hadad had sent out scouts who reported back to him and said, "There are men marching this way from Samaria."
And he said, "Whether they have come for peace or war, take them alive."
So these young provincial officers came from the city with the army that followed them.
Each Israelis man killed their adversary and the Syrians fled, and were pursued by the Israelis, and King Ben-Hadad of Syria escaped on a horse with the cavalry.
Then the king of Israel attacked the horses and chariots, and slaughtered the Syrians.

Later the prophet went to see the king of Israel and said, "Go and see what you need to do to reinforce your positions, because at the beginning of the year the king of Syria will come and attack you."
The king of Syria's servants said to him, "Their gods are gods of the hills, that's why they were stronger than us, but if we fight them on the plains, we will surely defeat them.
You must also remove the kings from their thrones and replace them with other officers.

You must also raise an army like the one that you just lost, horse for horse, and chariot for chariot. Then we will fight against them on the plains, and we will surely be stronger than them." And the king listened to them and did what they said.
At the beginning of the year Ben-Hadad mobilized the Syrians and went to fight the Israelis in Aphek.
And the Israelis marched out to meet them, and they pitched their tents before them like two little flocks of kid goats, but the Syrians filled the countryside.

A man of God spoke to the king of Israel and said, "This is what the Lord says, 'Because the Syrians have said, "The Lord is a God from the hills but not the valleys," I will deliver their entire army into your hands, and you will know that I am the Lord.'"
The two armies were camped opposite each other for seven days. Then on the seventh day the battle began, and the Israelis killed 100,000 Syrian foot soldiers in one day.
But the rest fled to the city of Aphek where a wall fell on 27,000 of their men, and Ben-Hadad fled into an inner chamber of the city.

And his servants said to him, "Behold, we have heard that the Israelis kings are merciful kings, I pray you will let us put sackcloth around our waist and ropes on our heads, and go to the king of Israel, and perhaps he will spare your life."

So they strapped sackcloth around their waist, and put ropes on their heads, and went to see the king of Israel and said, "Your servant Ben-Hadad says, 'I pray you will let me live.'"And the king answered them and said, "Is he still alive? He is my brother."

Now the men diligently looked to see whether anything good would come from him, and they quickly caught on to what he just said, and they said, "Yes, your brother Ben-Hadad." Then he said, "Go you and bring him here." Then Ben-Hadad came to him, and Ahab made him come up to his chariot.

Ben-Hadad said to him, "I will restore the cities that my father took from your father, and make streets for you in Damascus, as my father made in Samaria." Then Ahab said, "I will send you away with this treaty." So he made a treaty with him and sent him away.
A certain man from the sons of the prophets through the Lord's word said to his friend, "I pray you will kill me." but the man refused to kill him.
Then he said to him, "Because you have not obeyed the Lord's word, behold as soon as you leave me a lion will kill you!" And as soon as he left a lion found him and killed him.
Then he found another man and said, "I pray you will kill me." So the man struck him and wounded him.
So the prophet left and waited by the roadside for the king, and he disguised himself with ashes on his face.

As the king passed by he cried out to the king and said, "Your servant marched out into the middle of the battle, and a man brought a captive to me and said, 'Watch this man, if he goes missing for any reason, then will your life be traded for his life, unless you pay a silver talent.'
And as your servant was busy here and there, the man disappeared." And the king of Israel said to him, "You have pronounced your own judgment on yourself."
He hurriedly removed the ashes from his face, and the king of Israel immediately recognized that he was of the prophets.

And the prophet said to him, "This is what the Lord says, 'Because you have let a man whom I appointed to utter destruction escape from your hands, your life will be forfeited for his life, and your people for his people.'"
So, the king of Israel returned to his home in Samaria heavy hearted and unhappy.
After all this, Naboth the Jezreelite had a vineyard in Jezreel next to the palace of King Ahab of Samaria.

Ahab spoke to Naboth and said, "Give me your vineyard, so that I may use it for an herb garden. It is near my house, and I will give you a better vineyard for it, or I will pay you whatever it is worth in money if that seems better to you."
And Naboth said to Ahab, "God forbid, that I should give my father's inheritance to you."

Ahab returned to his house heavy hearted and depressed because Naboth the Jezreelite had said to him, "I will not give you my father's inheritance." So Ahab laid down on his bed, and turned away and he would not eat.
But his wife Jezebel came to him and asked, "Why is your spirit so sad that you do not eat?"

He answered her and said, "Because I spoke to Naboth the Jezreelite and asked him to sell me his vineyard or to trade it for another vineyard, and he answered me and said, 'No, I will not give you my vineyard.'"
His wife Jezebel said to him, "Do you not govern the kingdom of Israel? So, get up and eat and let your heart be merry, and I will give you Naboth the Jezreelite's vineyard."
So she wrote letters in Ahab's name and sealed them with his seal, and sent them to the elders and nobles who lived near Naboth in his city.
In these letters she wrote, "Proclaim a fast, and give Naboth a seat of honor among his people."
But seat two sons of Belial before him to testify against him and say, "You have blasphemed God and the king, then carry him out and stone him to death."
So the men, elders, and nobles of his city did as Jezebel instructed them in the letters she had written them.
They proclaimed a fast and gave Naboth a seat of honor among his people.

Two sons of Belial, came in and sat before him, and testified against Naboth in the presence of the people and said, "Naboth has blasphemed God and the king." Then they carried him out of the city, and stoned him to death.
Then they sent word to Jezebel and said, "Naboth has been stoned to death."
When Jezebel heard that Naboth had been stoned to death she said to Ahab, "Get up and go take possession of Naboth the Jezreelite's vineyard which he refused to sell you, because he is dead.
When Ahab heard that Naboth was dead, he got up to go down and take possession of Naboth the Jezreelite's vineyard.
Then the Lord's word came to Elijah the Tishbite.
And the Lord said, "Get up and go down to meet King Ahab of Israel in Samaria. Behold he has gone down to take possession of Naboth's vineyard.

Speak to him and say, 'This is what the Lord says, "Have you killed someone and taken possession of his land? In the place where dogs licked Naboth's blood, they will also lick your blood from the ground!"'"
When Elijah found him Ahab said, "O my enemy, you have found me." And Elijah answered and him and said, "I have found you, because you sold yourself and worked evil in the Lord's sight.

And this is what the Lord says, 'Behold, I will bring evil down on you and take away your descendants, and I will cut Ahab off from any men left in Israel who piss against the wall, whether they are free or slave.
I will make your house like the house of Nebat's son Jeroboam or Ahijah's son Baasha's house, because what you have done has provoked my anger and caused Israel to sin.'
And the Lord also spoke of Jezebel and said, 'The dogs will eat Jezebel by the wall of Jezreel.'
Any descendants of Ahab who die in the city will be eaten by dogs, and anyone that dies in the field will be eaten by the birds of the air."
But there were none like Ahab, who sold himself to work wickedness in the Lord's sight, who was stirred up by his wife Jezebel.
He committed every Amorite abomination and chased after their idols, and he did everything like the Amorites, whom the Lord had driven out before the Israelis.
When Ahab heard those words, he tore his clothes and covered himself with sackcloth and fasted. Then he laid down in sackcloth and walked softly.
And the word of the Lord came to Elijah the Tishbite again.

And the Lord said, "Do you see how Ahab humbles himself before me? It is because he humbles himself before me, that I will not bring this evil in his days, but I bring the evil on his house in his son's days."
And three years passed without a war between Syria and Israel.
In the third year, King Jehoshaphat of Judah came down to meet with the king of Israel.
The king of Israel said to his servants, "Do you know that Ramoth-Gilead is ours, and we have not taken it from the hands of the Syrian king?"

And he said to Jehoshaphat, "Will you go with me into battle in Ramoth-Gilead?" And Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, "I am just like you, my people are your people, and my horses are your horses."
But Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, "I pray that you will ask the Lord for his word today."

Then the king of Israel gathered about 400 prophets together and said to them, "Should I go to war against Ramoth-Gilead, or should I refrain?" And they said, "Go to war, because the Lord will deliver them into your hands."
And Jehoshaphat asked, "Is there not a prophet of the Lord here that we can ask?"

The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "There is still one man Imlah's son Micaiah through whom we may ask of the Lord. But I hate him, because he does not prophesy good things about me, but prophecies evil against me. And Jehoshaphat replied, "The king should not say such things."
Then the king of Israel summoned an officer and said, "Bring Imlah's son Micaiah here quickly."

The king of Israel and King Jehoshaphat of Judah each put on their robes and sat on their thrones in an empty place in the entrance of the gate of Samaria, and all the prophets prophesied before them.
Chenaanah's son Zedekiah the son made iron horns for himself and he said, "This is what the Lord says, 'With these horns you will push the Syrians out until you have consumed them.'"
And all the prophets prophesied the same and said, "Go up to Ramoth-Gilead and prosper, because the Lord will deliver them into the king's hands."

And the messenger that went to bring Micaiah spoke to him and said, "Behold, all the prophets declare good things to the king as one voice, I pray you will let your words be like theirs and speak that which is good."
And Micaiah said, "As the Lord lives, what the Lord says to me is what I will speak."

So he came to the king and the king asked him, "Micaiah, should we go to war against Ramoth-Gilead, or should we refrain?" And he answered and said, "Go and prosper, because the Lord will deliver them into the hands of the king."
And the king said to him, "How many times must I adjure you to tell me nothing but the truth in the name of the Lord?"
And he said, "I saw all of Israel scattered on the hills, like sheep without a shepherd and the Lord said, 'These have no master, let each man return home in peace.'"
And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "I told you that he would not prophesy anything good about me, but only evil?"
And Micaiah continued and said, "So hear the Lord's word, I saw the Lord sitting on his throne, and all the angels of heaven standing next to him on his right and his left.
And the Lord said, 'Who will persuade Ahab to march up and fall at Ramoth-Gilead?' And one said one thing, and another said something else.
And a spirit came and stood before the Lord and said, 'I will persuade him.'

And the Lord said to him, 'How will you do this?' And he said, "I will go out and be a lying spirit in the mouths of all his prophets.' And the Lord said, 'You will persuade him and prevail, so go and do it.'
So now, behold the Lord has put a lying spirit in the mouths of all of your prophets, and the Lord has spoken evil against you."
But Chenaanah's son Zedekiah went and smacked Micaiah on the cheek and said, "Which way did the Lord's Spirit go when it left me to speak to you?"
And Micaiah said, "Behold, in those days when you try to hide in the inner chamber, you will see the truth for yourself."
And the king of Israel said, "Take Micaiah back to city governor Amon, and the king's son Joash.
And tell them the king says, "Put this fellow in the prison, and feed him only affliction bread and water until I return in peace."
And Micaiah said, "If you return at all, the Lord has not spoken through me." And he said, "O you people, listen and take heed."
So the king of Israel and King Jehoshaphat of Judah went to Ramoth-Gilead.
The king of Israel spoke to Jehoshaphat and said, "I will disguise myself and go into battle, but you should put on your robes." And the king of Israel disguised himself and went into battle.
But the king of Syria gave the 32 captains over his chariots their orders and said, "Do not fight anyone great or small except the king of Israel."
When the chariot captains saw Jehoshaphat they thought, "Surely he is the king of Israel." When they turned to fight him Jehoshaphat cried out.
When the chariot captains figured out that he was not the king of Israel, they stopped pursuing him.

But, a certain man drew his bow without taking aim, and hit the king of Israel between the joints of his armor. So he turned to his chariot driver and said, "Carry me out of the battle because I am badly wounded!"
The battle continued to rage throughout the day, but the king stayed in his chariot facing the Syrians. He died that evening, and his blood ran out of the wound into the chariot.
At about sundown a proclamation was sent throughout the Israelis army which said, "Everyone return to your own city in your own country."
So the king died, and he was brought back to Samaria where he was buried.
Someone washed the king's armor and his chariot in the pool of Samaria, and the dogs licked his blood, just as the Lord said it would be.

The rest of the acts of Ahab, and everything else that he did, and the ivory house that he built, and all the cities that he built, are all written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
So Ahab died and slept with his fathers and his son Ahaziah reigned in his place.
In the fourth year of King Ahab's reign over Israel, Asa's son Jehoshaphat began to reign over Judah.
Jehoshaphat was thirty-five years old when he began to reign in Jerusalem, and he reigned for twenty-five years. His mother's name was Azubah and she was Shilhi's daughter.

He walked in all the ways of his father Asa, and he did not turn away from doing what he thought was righteous in the Lord's eyes. But the high places were not removed, because the people continued to burn incense and offer sacrifices in the high places.
And Jehoshaphat made peace with the king of Israel.
The rest of the acts of Jehoshaphat, and the might that he showed and his wars, are all written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah.
And he removed the Sodomites from the land who remained from the days of his father Asa.
Then there was no King in Edom and a deputy served as king.
Jehoshaphat built ships in Tarshish to travel to Ophir for gold, but they did not go because they were wrecked at Ezion-Geber.
Then Ahab's son Ahaziah offered to help Jehoshaphat and said, "Let my servants go with your servants in the ships." But Jehoshaphat refused.
So Jehoshaphat died and slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the city of his father David, and his son Jehoram reigned in his place.
Ahab's son Ahaziah began to reign over Israel in Samaria in the seventeenth year of King Jehoshaphat of Judah's reign, and he reigned for two years over Israel.
And he did evil in the Lord's sight, and walked in the ways of his father, mother, and in the ways of Nebat's son Jeroboam who had made Israel sin.
Because he served and worshipped Baal, and he provoked the Lord God of Israel's anger, just as his father had done.
Then after Ahab died Moab rebelled against Israel.
Ahaziah was and sick fell through the lattice in his upper chamber in Samaria, and he sent messengers and said to them, "Go and ask Ekron's god Beelzebub whether I will recover from this disease."

But the Lord's angel spoke to Elijah the Tishbite and said, "Get up and go meet the king of Samaria's messengers and say to them, "Is it because there is no God in Israel, that you go to ask for advice from Ekron's god Beelzebub?
So now, the Lord says this, 'You will surely die, and you will not leave the bed you are lying on!'"And then Elijah left.
When the messengers returned to the king he asked them, "Why have you returned?"

They answered him and said, "A man came to meet us on the road and said, "Return to the king and say to him, 'This is what the Lord says, "Is it because there is no God in Israel, that you go to ask for advice from Ekron's god Beelzebub? And you will surely die, and you will not leave the bed you are lying on!"'"
