Then the king asked them, "What kind of man came to meet you and told you these things?"
So they answered him and said, "He was a hairy man, with a leather belt strapped around his waist." And the king said, "It was Elijah the Tishbite."
Then the king sent a platoon captain with fifty men to find him, and they found him sitting on top of a hill, and the captain spoke to him and said, "You man of God the king says, 'Come down here.'"

Elijah answered him and said to the captain, "If I am a man of God, then let fire come down from heaven and consume you and your platoon!" And fire came down from heaven and consumed the captain and the fifty men in his platoon.
So the king sent another platoon captain with fifty men, and the captain found him and said, "O man of God, the king said for you to come down here quickly."

Elijah answered him again and said, "If I am a man of God, then let fire come down from heaven and consume you and your platoon!" And fire came down from heaven and consumed the captain and the fifty men in his platoon again.

And the king sent a third platoon captain with fifty men, and the captain found him and fell on his knees before Elijah and implored him, "O man of God, I pray you will let my life and these fifty servants of yours lives be precious in your sight.
Behold, fire came down from heaven, and burned up the first two captains and all their men, so please let my life now be precious in your sight."
Then the Lord's angel said to Elijah, "Go down and meet him, do not be afraid of him." So he got up and went with him to meet the king.

When they arrived Elijah said to the king, "This is what the Lord says, 'You have sent messengers to ask Ekron's god Beelzebub for advice because there is no God in Israel to ask him for his word, so you will surely die, and you will not leave the bed that you are lying on.'"
So he died just as the Lord had told Elijah he would. And because he had no son, Jehoram began to reign in his place in the second year of King Jehoshaphat's son Jehoram of Judah's reign.
The rest of all the acts of King Ahaziah are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
Elijah and Elisha were leaving Gilgal shortly before the Lord took Elijah up into heaven in a whirlwind.

Elijah spoke to Elisha and said, "I pray you will stay here because the Lord has sent me to Bethel." And Elisha said to him, "As the Lord lives and as your soul lives, I will not leave you." So they went down to Bethel.
The prophets sons in Bethel came out to meet Elisha and said to him, "Do you know that the Lord will take your master away from you today?" And he said, "Yes I know that so hold your peace."
And Elijah said to Elisha, "I pray you will stay here because the Lord has sent me to Jericho." And he said, "As the Lord lives and as your soul lives, I will not leave you." So they went to Jericho.

And the sons of the prophets that were at Jericho came to Elisha, and said to him, do you know that the Lord will take away your master from your head today, and he answered, yes, I know it, hold you your peace.
And Elijah said to him, stay, I pray you, here, because the Lord has sent me to Jordan, and he said, like the Lord lives, and as your soul lives, I will not leave you, and they two went on.
Fifty of the prophets' sons stood far away to see the two men as they stood by the Jordan River.
Elijah rolled up his cloak and struck the waters, and the waters were divided, so that the two men crossed the river on dry ground.
After they crossed the river Elijah said to Elisha, "Tell me what I can do for you before I am taken away?" And Elisha said, "I pray you will let me inherit a double portion of your spirit."
And he said, "You have asked a difficult thing. Nevertheless, if you see me as I am taken from you, it will be so, but if you do not see me, then it will not be so."
As they continued onward and talked to each other, a chariot of fire with horses of fire appeared and split the two of them apart, and Elijah was carried into heaven by a whirlwind.
Elisha saw this and he cried out, "My father, my father, the chariot and horsemen of Israel!" Then he no longer saw Elijah, so he tore his own clothes into two pieces.
Elijah's cloak fell from his body, and Elisha picked it up and took it back and stood on the banks of the Jordan River with it.
And he took Elijah's cloak and struck the waters with it and said, "Where is Elijah's Lord God?" And after he struck the waters, they parted and he crossed the river.
When the prophets' sons from Jericho who were watching him saw what happened they said, Elijah's spirit does rest on Elisha." And they went to meet him, and bowed facedown to the ground before him.

And they said to Elisha, "We your servants have fifty strong men with us, we pray you will let them go and look for your master. Perhaps the Lord's Spirit has taken him up, and thrown him on some mountain or into some valley, And he replied, "Do not send them."
They continued to push him until he was ashamed and he said, "Go ahead and send them." So they sent the fifty men to look for him for three days, but they could not find him.
When they returned to Elisha who was staying in Jericho he said to them, "Did I not tell you not go?"
The men of the city replied to Elisha and said, "I pray you will look and see that this city's situation is pleasant, but there is no water and the ground is barren."
So Elisha said, "Bring me a small cup with salt in it," and they brought it to him.
He went out to the water springs and threw the salt in them and said, "This is what the Lord says, "I have healed these waters, and there will be no more death or barren land from them."
So the waters have been healed to this very day, just as Elisha said they would be.
Elisha left and went to Bethel, and as he was going up the road, there some little children came out from the city and mocked him and said to him, "Go on up you bald head! Go up you bald head!"
He turned around and looked at them and cursed them in the name of the Lord. Then two female bears came out of the woods, and tore forty-two of the children apart.
He left and went to Mount Carmel and then he returned to Samaria.
Now in the eighteenth year of King Jehoshaphat's reign over Judah, Ahab's son Jehoram began to reign over Israel from Samaria, and he reigned for twelve years.
But he worked evil in sight of the Lord, but not the way his father and mother did, because he had the image of Baal that his father made removed.
Nevertheless he clung to the sins that Nebat's son Jeroboam committed and made Israel commit, and he did not depart from them.
King Mesha of Moab bred sheep and he gave 100,000 lambs, 100,000 rams, and their wool to the king of Israel.
But after Ahab died, the king of Moab rebelled against the king of Israel.
So King Jehoram left Samaria at that same time, and mobilized all the Israelis armies.

As he left he sent messengers to King Jehoshaphat of Judah and said, "The king of Moab has rebelled against me, will you join me in battle against Moab?" And he said, "I will go with you because I am like you. My people are like your people, and my horses are your horses."
Then Jehoshaphat asked, "Which way should we go?" And Joram answered, "We will go through the wilderness of Edom."
So the kings of Israel, Judah, and Edom left and they wandered around in circles for seven days, and there was no water for their armies or cattle.
Then the king of Israel said, "Alas! The Lord has brought us three kings together, just to deliver us into Moab's hands!"

But Jehoshaphat said, "Is there not a prophet of the Lord here to give us the Lord's word? One of the servants of king of Israel answered him and said, "There is Shaphat's son Elisha who poured water on Elijah's hands."
And Jehoshaphat said, "The word of the Lord is with him." So Jehoshaphat, and the kings of Israel and Edom went down to him.

However, Elisha spoke to the king of Israel and said, "What do I have to do with you? Go ask your father and mother's prophets." But the king of Israel replied to him and said, "No, because the Lord has summoned these three kings together, to deliver them into the hands of Moab."
Then Elisha said, "As surely as the Lord of Hosts lives whom I stand before, were it not for the high esteem in which I hold King Jehoshaphat of Judah, I would not look at you or acknowledge you."
And Elisha said, "But for now bring me a musician." When the musician began to play his harp, the Lord's hand came upon Elisha.
And he said, "This is what the Lord says, 'Fill this valley full of ditches.'
Because the Lord says this, 'You will not see wind nor rain, but that valley will be filled with water so that you, your cattle, and your animals will drink.'
This is a small thing in the Lord's sight, and he will deliver the Moabites into your hands.
You will defeat every important fortified city. You will fell every good tree, and fill in all the water wells, and ruin every good field with stones.
In the morning when the bread offering was made, water began to flow from Edom and the country was filled with water.
When the Moabites heard that all the kings had come to fight them, they summoned everyone who was big and strong enough to wear armor and stationed them along the border.
So the Moabites got up early in the morning as the sun reflected off the water, and they could see that the water on the other side of the river was as red as blood.
And they said, "This is blood of the kings, they have surely killed each other now to Moab goes the spoils."
But when they got to the Israelis camp, they attacked and defeated the Moabites, and they fled before them. But the Israelis marched forward killing the Moabites, even into their own country.

They defeated the cities, and they threw stones on every good piece of land, and they filled in all the water wells, and felled all the good trees. Kir-Haraseth was the only place left with stones, however the men with slings went in and defeated it.
When the king of Moab saw that the battle was nearly lost for him, he took 700 swordsmen with him to break through to the king of Edom, but they could not get through.

Then he took his oldest son who should have inherited his kingdom, and offered him as a burnt offering on the city wall. And there was a great indignation against Israel, so they left and returned to their own land.

The wife of one of the prophet's sons went to Elisha and cried out and said, "Your servant my husband is dead, and you know that he feared the Lord, and now his creditor has come to take my two sons away as slaves."
And Elisha said to her, "Tell me what can I do for you? What do you have in your house?" And she said, "Your housemaid has nothing in the house, except a pot of oil."
Then he said, "Go and borrow as many empty jars as you can from all of your neighbors.
Then you and your sons go into the house and shut the door behind you, and pour oil into all those jars and set the full ones aside.
So she left him, and went home and shut the door behind her and her sons, and they brought the jars to her which she poured oil into.
When all the jars were full, she said to her son, "Bring me another jar." And he said to her, "There is not another jar," and the oil stopped flowing.
Then she returned and told the man of God and he said, "Go and sell the oil to pay your debt, then you and your children can live on the rest."
One day Elisha passed through Shunem, where a great woman asked him to stop and eat some bread with her, after that whenever he was passing through he would stop by and eat with her.
She spoke to her husband and said, "Behold, I think this is a Holy man of God, who passes through here all the time.
I hope you will build a small room for him along the wall and we can put a bed, a table, a stool, and a lampstand in there for him for when he passes through here.
One day Elisha was passing through Shunem and he went to lie down in his room.
He said to his servant Gehazi, "Call this Shunammite woman." So when he called her, she came and stood before him.

He told Gehazi what to say and he said, "Say this to her, 'Behold you have been good for us with all this care. What can I do for you? Would you like me to speak to the king or the army commander for you?'"And she answered, "No, I live with my own people."
Then Elisha spoke to Gehazi and said, "So what can we do for her?" And Gehazi answered, "Honestly she has no children, and her husband is an old man."
And Elisha said, "Call her," and when he called her, she came and stood in the doorway.
Elisha spoke to her and said, "By this about this time next year, you will embrace your own son!" And she said, "No my Lord, you are a man of God, so do not lie to me."
Then the woman conceived and gave birth to a son at the time of year that Elisha said she would.
One day after the child was grown, he went to see his father who was in the fields with the harvesters.
And he said to his father, "My head, my head," and his father said to a boy, "Take him to his mother."
After he had taken him to his mother, the boy sat on his mother's knees until noon, and then died.
She carried him to the man of God's room and laid they boy on his bed, then she shut the door and left.
She called out to her husband and said, "I pray you will send me one of the young men and a donkey, so I can run to the man of God, and return."
And her husband said, "Why do you need to go see him today? It is not the new moon or the Sabbath?" And she said, "Do not worry, everything will be alright."
Then she saddled a donkey and said to her servant, "Drive forward, and do not slow down because of me, unless I tell you to."
So she went to see the man of God on Mount Carmel, and when he saw her approaching from afar, he said to his servant Gehazi, "Behold here comes the Shunammite woman.
I pray you will run out to meet her and say, 'Is everything alright with you, your husband, and the child?'"And she answered, "All is well."

When she reached the man of God on top of the hill, she came and grabbed Elisha's feet, but Gehazi came to push her away. But the man of God said, "Leave her alone because her soul is very frustrated. The Lord has hidden the reason from me, and he has not told me what's wrong."
Then she said, "I did desire a son from my Lord? And I did say, 'Do not deceive me?'"

Then he said to Gehazi, Get dressed and take my staff and go! !f you meet anyone along the way do not salute him, and if anyone salutes you, do not answer him. When you get there lay my staff on the child's face."
And the child's mother said, "As the Lord lives and as your soul lives, I will not leave you." So Elisha got up and followed her.
Gehazi ran ahead of them, and when got there he laid the staff on the child's face, but the child did not make a sound or move. So he went back to meet Elisha and told him, "The child is not awake."
When Elisha arrive at the house, the child was laying dead on his bed.
So he went into the room and shut the door behind him and the two of them were alone, and he prayed to the Lord.

He went over and laid on top of the child and put his mouth on the boys mouth, and his eyes on the boys eyes, and his hands on the boys hands, and stretched himself over the child, and the child body began to get warm.
Elisha began to pace in and out and around the room. Then he stretched out over the child again, and the boy sneezed seven times and opened his eyes.
He called out to Gehazi and said, "Call the Shunammite woman." So he called her, and when she came in he said, "Take your son."
Then she went in and fell at his feet and bowed facedown to the ground, and she took her son and left.
When Elisha returned to Gilgal, there was a shortage in the land, and the prophets' sons came and sat before him. Then he said to his servant, "Put on a large pot of stew for the prophets' sons."

One servant went out into the field to gather herbs, and found a wild vine and gathered all the wild gourds he could carry. He went back and shredded them into the pot of stew, even though they did not know what they were.
So they ladled out the stew for the men to eat, and as they were eating, they cried out and said, "O man of God, there is death in the pot!" And they could not eat it.
But then he said, "Bring me some meal." Then he threw it into the pot and said, "Pour some out for the people to eat," and this time there was nothing harmful in the pot.
One day a man came from Baal-Shalisha and brought bread from the first fruits, twenty loaves of barley, and some ripe wheat heads to the man of God and he said, "Give this to the people to eat."

And his servant said, "How can I set out just twenty loaves of bread for a hundred men to eat?" And he said again, "Give it to the people to eat, because this is what the Lord says, 'They will eat and there will be leftovers.'"
So he set it before them and they ate, and there were leftovers just as the Lord said there would be.

Now Naaman the Syria king's army commander was a great and honorable man in his master's sight, because the Lord had delivered the victory to Syria through him, and he was a mighty man of valor, but he was also a leper.
The Syrians had sent companies of raiders out, and brought captives back from Israel, including a young girl who waited on Naaman's wife.
One day the girl said to her mistress, "If my master would go to the prophet of my Lord God in Samaria, he would cure him of his leprosy."
Someone went and told the king and said, "This is what the young girl from the land of Israel said."
Then the king of Syria said, "Go now and I deliver this letter to the king of Israel." So he left and took ten silver talents, 6,000 gold pieces, and ten clothing changes with him.
He delivered the letter to the king of Israel that said, "I have sent my servant Naaman to you with this letter, so that you may cure him of his leprosy."

When the king of Israel read the letter he tore his clothes and said, "Am I God, who can kill and bring back to life? This man thinks I can cure a man of his leprosy? So I pray that you will consider that this man wants to quarrel with me!"

When Elisha the man of God heard that the king of Israel had torn his clothes, he sent a message to the king that said, "Why have you torn your clothing? Let him come to me and he will know that there is a prophet in Israel."
So Naaman came with his horses and chariot and stood at the door of Elisha's house.
And Elisha sent a messenger to him and said, "Go and wash in the Jordan River seven times, and your flesh will come return and you will be clean."

But Naaman was angry and he left and said, "Behold I thought he would come out to see me, and stand with me, and call on the name of his Lord God, and wave his hand over me and cure me of this leprosy.
Are not the Abana and Pharpar rivers part of Damascus? Are they not better than all the waters of Israel? I could have washed in them to be clean." So he turned and left in a rage.

But his servants came and spoke to him and said, "My father, if the prophet had asked you to do some great thing, would you not have done it? How much more then should you listen to him when he says, 'Go wash and be clean?'"
Then he went down and dipped himself in the Jordan River seven times, as the man of God asked him to, and his flesh became like that of a little child, and he was clean.

Naaman returned to the man of God with his entire company and stood before him and said, "Behold, now I know that there is no God on earth, except in Israel. So I pray you will accept a blessing from your servant."
But Elisha said, "As the Lord lives before whom I stand, I will accept nothing." Naaman urged him to take it, but he refused.

And Naaman said, "If you will not accept my gift, then I ask you to give your servant enough dirt for two mules to carry? Because from now on I will offer no burnt offering or sacrifice to other gods, but only to the Lord God of Israel."

But, may the Lord God pardon your servant of this one thing, when my master goes into the house of Rimmon to worship, and he leans on my arm, and I bow down in the house of Rimmon, may your Lord God pardon me for this."
And Elisha said, "Go in peace." So he left, but he had not traveled very far.

But the man of God Elisha's servant Gehazi thought, "Behold my master has spared Naaman the Syrian by not accepting the gifts he brought, but as the Lord lives, I am going to run out and ask him for something."
So Gehazi followed Naaman and when Naaman saw him running his way, he jumped off the chariot to meet him and said, "Is everything alright?"

And he said, "Everything is alright, but my master sent me and he said, "Behold two young men who are the prophets' sons have come here from Mount Ephraim. So I ask if you can give them a silver talent and two clothing changes?"

Naaman urged him to take them and said, "Please take two talents." Then he put two silver talents in two bags and tied them shut, and gave them and two clothing changes to two of his servants, and they carried them home for Gehazi.
When Gehazi returned to the hill, he took the gifts from them and put them in the house, and he let the men go, and they left.
But he went in and stood before his Elisha he asked, "Where have you been Gehazi?" And he said, "Your servant has been nowhere."

Then Elisha asked him, "Did you not know that my heart went with you, when the man got down from his chariot to meet you? Is it the right time to receive money, garments, olive groves, vineyards, sheep, oxen, and male and female servants?
So Naaman's leprosy will cling to you and your descendants forever, and Gehazi left Elisha's presence as a leper white as snow.
Now the prophets' sons said to Elisha, "Behold, the place where we live with you is too small for us.
We pray that you will let us go to the Jordan River where we can each cut enough beams to build a place to live there, and he answered them and said, "Go ahead."
But one of them said, "I pray you will come with us." And he answered and said, "I will go with you."
So he went with them and when they arrived at the Jordan River, they cut down some trees.
But as one man was felling a tree, the axe head fell into the water, and he cried out and said, "Alas master, it was borrowed."
The man of God asked, "Where did it fall?" And his servant showed him where it fell, and the man of God cut a stick, and threw it in the water, and the axe head floated to the top.
So the man of God handed it to his servant and said, "Here take it with you."
Then the Syrian king declared war against Israel, and he asked his servants for their advice and he said, "I want to set up my camp in a particular place."
But the man of God sent a message to the Israelis king and said, "You must not try to pass through this particular place, because the Syrians have set up camp there."
Then the Israelis king sent word to the place that Elisha warned him about, and saved himself from their traps more than once.
So the Syrian king's heart was terribly troubled about this and he called his servants and said, "Show me, which one of us is on the Israelis king's side?"
And one of his servants said, "O Lord my king, God's prophet Elisha in Israel tells Israel's king everything you say in your own bedroom."
And he said, "Send some spies to find out where where he is, so I can send some troops to capture him," and someone said, "Behold he is in Dothan."
So he sent horses, chariots, and a large powerful army at night to surround the city.
Elisha's servant got up early that morning and went out, and when he saw that an army had surrounded the entire city, he went to Elisha and said, "Master, what are we going to do?"
And he answered, "Fear not, because the army that's with us, is larger than the army that's with them."

Then Elisha prayed and said, "Lord, I pray that you will open my servant's eyes so that he may see." So the Lord opened the young man's eyes, and he saw that the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire all around Elisha.
When they came down to Elisha, he prayed to the Lord and said, "I pray you will defeat these people with blindness!" So God blinded them just as Elisha had asked.
And Elisha said to them, "This is not the way and this is not the city you are looking for. Follow me, and I will bring you to the man you are trying to find. But he led them to Samaria.
When they arrived in Samaria Elisha said, "Lord, open their eyes so that they may see." The Lord opened their eyes, and they looked around and saw that they were standing in the middle of Samaria.
When he saw them the Israelis king spoke to Elisha and asked, "My father, should I kill these men and defeat them?"

Elisha answered and said, "Do not kill them, should you kill prisoners you have captured with your sword and your bow? Give them some bread and water to eat and drink, then send them back to their master."
Then he prepared great meal for them, and after they ate and drank, he sent them away. They returned to their master, and the Syrian armies no longer ventured into the land of Israel.
After all this, King Ben-Hadad of Syria assembled his entire army and went to besiege Samaria.

There was a great famine in Samaria and they besieged it so long that a donkey's head sold for food for eighty silver shekels, and a fourth of a cup of dove's dung for fuel sold for five silver shekels.
As the Israelis king was passing by the wall, a woman cried out to him and said, "My Lord, O king, please help me!"
And he said, "If the Lord does not help you, where will I find help for you, from the barn floor or the winepress?"
Then the king questioned her and asked, "What ails you?" And she answered and said, "This woman said to me. 'If we eat your son today, we can eat my son tomorrow.'
So we boiled and ate my son and the next day I said to her, "Now it is time to eat your son, and she has hidden her son."
When the king heard what the woman said, he tore his clothes, and he walked by the wall wearing sackcloth underneath, and all the people saw this.
Then the king said, "God punish me even more severely, if Shaphat's son Elisha's head is still attached to his body by the end of this day."

But Elisha sat in his house with the elders and the Israelis king sent a messenger to him, but before the messenger arrived Elisha said to the elders, "See you how this son of a murderer has sent someone to take off my head? So when the messenger gets here shut the door, and shut and bar the door. Because, is not that the sound of his master's feet right behind him?"
While Elisha was talking with them the messenger arrived and he said, "Behold this evil is from the Lord, why should I wait for the Lord any longer?"
Then Elisha said, "Hear what the Lord has to say, 'At about this time tomorrow a measure of fine flour and two measures of barley will be sold for a shekel each at Samaria's gate.'"

Then the officer whose hand the king leaned on answered the man of God and said, "Behold can the Lord make windows in heaven?" And Elisha replied and said, "Behold you will see it with your own eyes, but you will not eat from it."
Now there were four leprous men at the entrance of the city gate and they said to each other, "Why should we sit here until we die?

If we enter the city with the famine there, then we will die there. If we sit here, we will also die. So let us fall to the Syrian armies, if they save us we will live, and if they kill us we will die."
So they got up in the middle of the night and they went to the Syrian camp. When they got to the farthest part of the Syrian camp, behold there were no men there.

Because the Lord made the Syrian armies hear the noise of chariots, horses, and even a massive army and they said to one another, "The Israelis king has hired the Hittite and Egyptian kings to attack us."
So they got up and fled in the middle of the night and left their tents, horses, and donkeys and they left the camp as it was, and fled for their lives.

When the lepers came to the farthest part of the camp, they went into one of the tents and ate and drink. Then they carried their silver, gold, and clothes away and hid it, and they went into another tent and took what was there, and carried it away and hid it also.

Then they said one to another, "We are not doing the right thing! This is a day of good news and we have not told anyone. If we stay until the morning light, some mischief will come on us, so we must go and tell the king's palace."

So they went and told the city's gatekeepers what was happening and they said, "We went to the Syrian camp, and there was no one there. We heard no men's voices but the horses and donkeys were tied up, and the tents were full of stuff."
The king heard about it and summoned the gatekeepers, and they told everyone inside the king's palace.

The king got up in the night and said to his servants, "Now I will show you what the Syrians have done to us. They know that we are hungry, so they left their camp to hide from us in the field and they think, "When they come from the city, we will catch them and get into the city."

But one of his servants said, "I pray you will send some scouts with five of the remaining horses, whatever happens to them will be no worse than what will happen to the rest of the Israelis. I say all the Israelis will be consumed so let us send them out to see what's happening."
So they took two chariot horses, and the king sent them to see what the Syrians were up to and said, "Go and see what's happening."

The scouts followed them all the way to the Jordan River, and the road was full of clothes and bottles that the Syrians had discarded in their haste. So the messengers returned and told the king what they found.
Then the people went and took the spoils from the Syrians' tents. So a measure of fine flour and two measures of barley were sold for a shekel apiece that day, as the Lord had said.
The king's officer was put in charge of the gate, and the people trampled him to death at the gate, just as the man of God said would happen when the king came down to visit him.

And it happened just like the man of God told the king it would happen when he said, "Two measures of barley and a measure of fine flour will be sold for a shekel apiece, will be tomorrow at about this time at Samaria's city gate."

When the king's officer answered the man of God and said, "Behold could the Lord make windows in heaven?" And Elisha replied and said, "Behold you will see it with your own eyes, but you will not eat from it."
So his fate was sealed because the people trampled him at the gate, and he died.

Then Elisha spoke to the woman whose son he had restored to life and said, "Go with the people in your household and travel wherever you can go, because the Lord has called for a seven year famine on the land."
And the woman got up and did what the man of God said, and she took her household to the Philistine lands for seven years.
At the end of seven years the woman returned from the Philistine lands, and she went to ask the king for her house and land.
The king talked to the man of God's servant Gehazi and said, "I pray you will tell me all the great things that Elisha has done."

As he was telling the king how Elisha had brought a dead body back to life, he saw the woman whose son's life had been restored when she came to ask the king for her house and land to be returned, and Gehazi said, "My Lord O king, this is the woman, and this is her son that Elisha restored to life."

When the king asked the woman about it she said it was true. So the king appointed one of his officers to her and said, "Restore everything to her that was hers, including everything that the field produced since the day she left until now."
Then when Elisha went to Damascus, King Ben-Hadad of Syria was sick and someone told him Elisha was there and they said, "The man of God has come here."
The king spoke to Hazael and said, "Take a present and go meet the man of God, and ask him to speak to the Lord for me and ask, 'Will recover from this disease?'"

So Hazael went to meet him and took a presents with him of every good thing from Damascus. Forty loaded camels came and stood before him and said, "Your son King Ben-Hadad of Syria has sent me to ask you, 'Will I recover from this disease?'"
Elisha responded and said, "Go and tell him, 'You may certainly recover,' however the Lord has shown me that he will surely die."
Elisha looked very sternly at him which made him feel ashamed, and the man of God began to weep.

And Hazael asked, "Why does my Lord weep?" And he answered, "Because I know the evil that you will do to Israel, their fortified cities that you will you set on fire, their young men you will kill, their children you will crush, and their pregnant women you will rip up."
But Hazael said, "Is your servant a dog? Am I someone that would do such a terrible thing? And Elisha answered, "The Lord has shown me that you will be the Syrian king."
Then he left Elisha and returned to his master who asked him, "What did Elisha say to you?" And he answered and said, "He told me that you will surely recover."
The next day, Hazel spread a thick damp cloth over the king's face and he died, then Hazael reigned in his place.
In the fifth year of Ahab's son King Joram's reign over Israel, Jehoshaphat's son King Jehoram began to reign in his father's place.
He was thirty-two years old he when he began to reign, and he reigned over Jerusalem for eight years.
So he walked in the ways of the kings of Israel just like Ahab's house, because Ahab's daughter was his wife, and he did evil in sight of the Lord.
But the Lord would not destroy Judah for his servant David's sake, because he had promised to always give David and his descendants a guiding light.
In Jehoram's days, Edom revolted against Judah, and made themselves a King to rule over them.

So Jehoram went over to Zair with all of his chariots and their commanders. He got up in the middle of the night, and defeated the Edomites who had him surrounded. But his army fled back to their tents.
But Edom has revolted against Judah to this day, and Libnah revolted at the same time.
The rest of the acts of King Joram, and everything that he did, are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah.
And Jehoram died and slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the city of David, and his son Ahaziah reigned in his place.
In the twelfth year of the reign of Ahab's son King Joram of Israel, King Jehoram's son Ahaziah began to reign over Judah.
Ahaziah was twenty-two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned for one year in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Athaliah, she was the daughter of King Omri of Israel.
He walked in the ways of the house of Ahab, and did evil in the Lord's sight, just like the house of Ahab, because he was Ahab's son-in-law.
Ahaziah and Ahab's son Joram went to the war against King Hazael of Syria in Ramoth-Gilead, and the Syrians wounded Joram.

King Joram returned to Jezreel so the wounds he got from the Syrians, when he fought King Hazael of Syria at Ramah could heal. King Jehoram's son Ahaziah of Judah went down to see Ahab's son Joram in Jezreel, because he was wounded.
The prophet Elisha summoned one of the prophet's sons and said, "Get dressed and take this box of oil to Ramoth-Gilead.
When you get there look for Jehoshaphat's son Jehu and get him to move to an inner chamber with you away from his brothers. Jehoshaphat was Nimshi's son.
Then pour the oil from the box on his head and say, "This is what the Lord says, "I have anointed you king of Israel. Then open the door and flee, do not stay there."
So the young prophet went to Ramoth-Gilead.
When he arrived, he saw all the military captains sitting around and he said, "I have an errand for you O captain," and Jehu said, "A message for who?" And he said, "For you, O captain."

Jehu got up and went into the house, and the young prophet poured the oil on his head, and said to him, "This is what the Lord God of Israel says, 'I have anointed you king over the Lord's people of Israel.
You will defeat your master Ahab's house, so that I may avenge the blood of my prophets and all of the Lord's servants at the hand of Jezebel.
Because the whole house of Ahab will perish, and I will cut Ahab off from any man left in Israel who pisses against the wall, whether they are free men or slaves.
I will make Ahab's house like the house of Nebat's son Jeroboam or Ahijah's son Baasha.
The dogs of Jezreel will eat Jezebel's corpse, and there will be no one to bury her!'"Then he opened the door and fled.
Then Jehu returned to his Lord's servants and one of them asked, "Is everything alright? Why did this mad fellow come to you?" And he said, "You know those kinds of people and their nonsense."
And they said, "That's a lie tell us the truth!" Jehu replied and said, "He spoke to me and said, 'This is what the Lord says, "I have anointed you king of Israel."'"
Then they hurriedly put their garments on the top of the stairs under Jehu's feet, and they blew trumpets and proclaimed, "Jehu is king!"
So Jehoshaphat's son Jehu the grandson of Nimshi conspired against Joram. Joram and all of Israel protected Ramoth-Gilead from King Hazael of Syria's attacks.

But King Joram had returned to Jezreel to be healed from the wounds which the Syrians had given him, when he fought with King Hazael of Syria. But Jehu said, "If you are thinking of making me king, then go to tell it in Jezreel and do not let anyone escape alive from the city."
So Jehu rode a chariot to Jezreel because Joram lay there wounded, and King Ahaziah of Judah had also come down to see Joram.

A watchman was standing on the tower in Jezreel, and he saw Jehu and his company coming his way and said, "I see a company coming!" And Joram said, "Send a horseman out to meet them, and tell him to say, 'Do you come in peace?'"

So a messenger rode out on horseback to meet Jehu and said, "This is what the king says, "Do you come in peace?" And Jehu said, "What do you have to do with peace? Get behind me, and the watchman went to Joram and said, "The messenger is not coming back."
Then he sent out a second messenger on horseback who went to them and said, "This is what the king says, "Do you come in peace?" And Jehu answered, "What do you have to do with peace? Get behind me."
The watchman went to Joram and said, "He rode out to them, but he is not coming back. The driver is driving like Nimshi's son Jehu, because he's driving furiously."
And Joram said, "Get my chariot ready," and they got it ready. Then King Joram of Israel and King Ahaziah of Judah left in their chariots and met Jehu at Naboth the Jezreelite's place.
When Joram saw Jehu he said, "Do you come in peace, Jehu?" And he answered, "What peace, there can be no peace as long as your mother Jezebel has so many whores and witches?"
Joram turned and fled and yelled to Ahaziah and said, "O Ahaziah, there is treachery!"
Jehu drew his bow with his full strength and hit Joram between his arms, and the arrow went straight through his heart, and he sunk down into his chariot.

Then Jehu turned to his captain Bidkar and said, "Pick him up and throw him into Naboth the Jezreelite's field. Because do you remember when you and I rode together behind his father Ahab, and the Lord laid this burden on him.
As surely as the Lord said, 'Yesterday I saw the blood of Naboth and his sons, and I will repay you on this plot of land.' Now throw him on that plot of land, just like the Lord said."

But when King Ahaziah of Judah saw this, he fled through the garden house. But Jehu followed him and said, "Kill him in the chariot!" And they caught up with him and shot him at Gur near Ibleam, and he fled to Megiddo, where he died.
His servants carried him to Jerusalem in a chariot and buried him in his tomb with his fathers in the city of David.
In the eleventh year of Ahab's son King Joram's reign, Ahaziah's began to reign over Judah.
When Jezebel heard that Jehu arrived in Jezreel, she painted her face, adorned her head, and looked out of the window.
As Jehu entered the gate she said, "O Zimri, who killed his master have you come in peace?"
He looked up to the window and said, "Who is on my side?" And two or three eunuchs looked out at him.
And Jehu said, "Throw her down!" So they threw her down, and some of her blood was sprinkled on the wall and the horses, and he trampled her under foot.
When he went in, he ate and drink and said, "Go and see to this cursed woman and bury her, because she was a king's daughter."
They went to bury her, but they only found her skull, feet, and the palms of her hands.

So they returned to Jehu and told him what they found and he said, "This is what the Lord said when he spoke through his servant Elijah the Tishbite and said, 'Dogs will eat Jezebel's flesh on a piece of land in Jezreel.'
And Jezebel's carcass will lay in the field in Jezreel like dung, so that no one can say, 'This is Jezebel.'"
Ahab had seventy sons in Samaria. So Jehu sent letters to the officials, elders, and the guardians of Ahab's sons in Samaria.
And he wrote, "As soon as you get this letter, since your master's sons are with you, and you have chariots, horses, armor, and fortified cities.
Pick the best one of your master's sons, and put him on his father's throne to fight for your master's house."
But they were terrified and said, "Behold if two kings could not stand before him, then how can we?"

Then the palace manager, the city overseer, the elders, and the children's guardians, sent a message to Jehu and said, "We are your servants, and we will do whatever you tell us to do, we will not make any kings. So do whatever you think is right."

Then he wrote a second letter that said, "If you are on my side and you want to follow me, then bring your master's sons' heads to me in Jezreel by this time tomorrow." Now the king had seventy sons, who were raised by the great men of the city.
When they received letter, they killed the king's seventy sons. Then they put their heads in baskets and sent them to Jehu in Jezreel.
A messenger went to Jehu to tell him and said, "They brought the king's sons' heads." And he said, "Lay them in two piles at the gate entrance until morning."
In the morning, Jehu went out and stood before all the people and said, "You are righteous, behold I am the one who conspired against and killed my master, but who killed all these people?"
You must know by now that not one of the Lord's word which he spoke against the house of Ahab will fall to the ground, because the Lord has done what he promised through his servant Elijah."
So Jehu killed everyone that remained from the house of Ahab in Jezreel, including all his great men, family, and priests until not one remained.
Then he got up and went to Samaria, and he stopped at the shearing house along the way.
Jehu met with the brothers of King Ahaziah of Judah and said, "Who are you?" And they answered, "We are Ahaziah's brothers, and we have come to meet the king and queen's sons."
And he said, "Take them alive!" So they took them alive and killed forty-two men at the shearing house pit, and they left none of them alive.

After Jehu left, he saw Rechab's son Jehonadab coming to meet him and he saluted him and said, "Is your heart as righteous with me, as mine is with you?" And Jehonadab answered, "It is, so give me your hand," and Jehu gave him his hand and he pulled him up into the chariot with him.
And he said, "Come with me, and see my zeal for the Lord." So they made him ride in his chariot.
When Jehu arrived in Samaria, he killed all of Ahab's people remaining in Samaria, until he had completely destroyed them, just as the Lord had said to Elijah.
Jehu gathered all the people together and addressed them and said, "Ahab served Baal a little bit, but Jehu will serve him much more."

So bring all of Baal's prophets, servants, and priests to me because I have a great sacrifice for Baal. Make sure you bring all of them to me because whoever does not show up will not live. But Jehu was deceiving them because his intent was to destroy all of Baal's worshippers.
And Jehu said, "Proclaim a solemn assembly for Baal," and they proclaimed it.

So Jehu's message was sent throughout the land of Israel, and all of Baal's worshippers showed up, and none of his worshippers failed to appear. They all went to the house of Baal, and Baal's house was full of worshippers from one end to another.
Jehu spoke to the ceremonial wardrobe keeper and said, "Bring out the ceremonial vests for all of Baal's worshippers," so he brought them their vests.

Jehu went into the house of Baal with Rechab's son Jehonadab and addressed Baal's worshippers and said, "Look around and make sure only Baal's worshippers are here and there are no servants of the Lord's here."

Before they went in to offer sacrifices and burnt offerings, Jehu addressed eighty men outside and said, "If any of these men that I have delivered into your hands escapes, whoever lets them go, will forfeit his life for the life of whoever was spared."

As soon as Jehu finished making the burnt offering, he spoke to the guards and captains and said, "Go in and kill them, do not let anyone escape!" So they killed them with their swords, and they threw the bodies out into the city streets, then they went back into the house of Baal.
Then they brought out the images from the house of Baal and burned them.
They demolished the house of Baal and his images, and they made it into a house of sewage which it is to this day.
This is how Jehu destroyed Baal and removed him from Israel.
However, Jehu did not turn away from the sins of Nebat's son Jeroboam, who had made Israel sin by worshipping the golden calves in Bethel and Dan.

And the Lord said to Jehu, "Because you have done well and done that which is right in my eyes, and you have done to Ahab's house everything that was in my heart, your descendants will sit on the throne of Israel to the fourth generation."
But Jehu was not careful to walk in the Law of the Lord God of Israel with all his heart, because he did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam that he made Israel commit.
In those days the Lord began to reduce Israel's territory, and Hazael killed them all along the borders of Israel.
From Jordan eastward, throughout all the lands of Gilead and the Gadites, Reubenites, and the Manassites, from Aroer near the Arnon river through Gilead and Bashan.
The rest of the acts of Jehu, and everything that he did, and all his might, are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
Jehu died and slept with his fathers, and they buried him in Samaria, and his son Jehoahaz reigned in his place.
Jehu reigned over Israel in Samaria for twenty-eight years.
When Ahaziah's mother Athaliah saw that her son was dead, she got up and killed all the royal heirs.
But King Joram's daughter Jehosheba, who was Ahaziah's sister hid Ahaziah's son Joash and his nurse from Athaliah in a bedroom, to keep him from being killed.
She hid him in the Lord's temple for six years while Athaliah reigned over the land.

In the seventh year priest Jehoiada summoned the commanders of hundreds along with the captains and the guards to the Lord's temple. He made a covenant and an oath with them in the Lord's temple, and showed them the king's son.
He gave them a commandment and said, "This is what you must do, a third of you that come on the Sabbath will guard the king's palace.
A third of you will be stationed at the gate of Sur, and a third of you at the gate behind the guards, to keep the watch over the Lord's house, to make sure that it is not destroyed.
Two thirds of you that leave on the Sabbath, will keep the watch over the Lord's temple for the king.
Then all of you men will be armed and you will surround the king. Whoever comes within range must be killed, and you must stay with the king wherever he goes, whether he goes in or out."
The commanders of the hundreds did everything that priest Jehoiada ordered. They took all their men whether they were coming in or leaving on the Sabbath to priest Jehoiada.
The priest gave King David's spears and shields, that were in the Lord's temple to the commanders of hundreds.
The armed guards surrounded the king near the altar, from the right corner to the left corner of the temple.
Priest Jehoiada put the crown on the king's son, then they gave him the testimony and anointed him king, and they clapped their hands and said, "God save the king."
When Athaliah heard all the noise that the guards and the people were making, she came to the Lord's temple to see the people.

Then Athaliah looked and saw the king standing beside a column and the princes and trumpeters were standing with the king which was custoMary. All the people rejoiced and blew trumpets, and she tore her clothes and cried, "Treason, treason!"

But priest Jehoiada gave orders to the commanders of the hundreds in control of the armies, and said, "Take her outside and kill anyone that follows her with the sword. Because the priest had said, "Do not kill her in the Lord's temple."
So they seized her near the entrance where the horses came into the king's palace, and killed her there.
That day Jehoiada made a covenant between the Lord, the king, and the people that they would be the Lord's people. He also made a covenant between the king and the people.

All the people of the land went into the house of Baal, and destroyed his altars and his images broke they into pieces. They killed Baal's priest Mattan before the altars, and priest Jehoiada appointed officers over the Lord's temple.

He took the commanders oof the hundreds, the captains, the guards, and all the people of the land, and they brought the king down from the Lord's temple, and entered the gate by the guards of the king's palace, and Joash took his seat on the king's throne.
All of the people rejoiced and then the city was quiet, and they killed Athaliah with the sword beside the king's palace.
Joash was seven years old when he began to reign.
Joash began to reign in the seventh year of King Jehu's reign, and he reigned for forty years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Zibiah of Beersheba.
Joash did what he thought was righteous in the Lord's sight for all the days of his life while priest Jehoiada guided him.
But the high places were not removed, and the people still sacrificed and burned incense in the high places.

Joash spoke to the priests and said, "Bring all the money and dedicated things here that is brought into the Lord's temple, including the census money, the tithe money that everyone has pledged, and all the money that anyone brings voluntarily into the Lord's temple.
Let the priests receive it from their congregations, and use it to repair any damage found in the temple."
But in the 23rd year of the reign of King Joash, the priests had not repaired the damage to the temple.

Then King Joash summoned priest Jehoiada and the other priests and he said to them, "Why have you not repaired the damaged temple? From now on you may take no more money from your congregations, but deliver here to repair the damage to the temple."
The priests consented to take no more money from the people, and they would not attempt to repair the temple themselves.

So priest Jehoiada bored a hole in the chest for the collections lid and set it on the right side of the altar you come into the Lord's temple. And the priest doormen put all the money that was brought into the Lord's temple in it.
When they saw that the chest was full of money, the king's scribe and the high priest came to the Lord's temple to collect it, count it, and put up in bags.

And they gave the money, being told, into the hands of those that did the work, that had the oversight of the Lord's temple, and they laid it out to the carpenters and builders, that worked on the Lord's temple.
They also used the money to hire masons and stone carvers and to buy timbers, carved stones, and everything else that was needed to repair the Lord's temple.
However they did not make any silver bowls, candle snuffers, sinks, trumpets, or any gold bowls with the money that was brought into the Lord's temple.
But they gave that money to the workmen who repaired the Lord's temple instead.
They did not require the men who were given the money to account for how it was spent, because they were honest and dealt they faithfully.
The trespass and sin money was not brought into the Lord's temple, it was given to the priests.
Then King Hazael of Syria attacked and captured Gath, then he went to attack Jerusalem.

King Joash of Judah took all the Holy things dedicated by Jehoshaphat, Jehoram, Ahaziah, his fathers who were kings of Judah, along with his own Holy things and all the gold found in the treasuries of the Lord's temple and the king's palace, and he sent it to King Hazael of Syria, then he left Jerusalem.
The rest of the acts of Joash, and everything that he did, are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah.
Joash's servants conspired against him, and they rose up and killed him in the house of Millo, which lies along the road to Silla.
Because Shimeath's son Jozachar and Shomer's son Jehozabad his servants, killed him and he died. They buried him with his fathers in the city of David, and his son Amaziah reigned in his place.
In the twenty-third year of the reign of Ahaziah's son King Joash of Judah, Jehu's son Jehoahaz began to reign over Israel in Samaria, and he reigned for seventeen years.
He did evil in the Lord's sight, and committed the same sins as Nebat's son Jeroboam, who made Israel sin, and he did not turn away from them.
The Lord's anger was kindled against Israel, and he delivered them into the hands of King Hazael of Syria and Hazael's son Ben-Hadad, for all the days of their lives.
Jehoahaz implored the Lord and the Lord listened to him, because he saw the king of Syria's oppression of Israel.
So the Lord gave Israel a savior who freed them from the oppression of the Syrians, and the Israelis lived in their tents, just as they had in the past.
Nevertheless, they did not walk away from the sins that the house of Jeroboam made Israel commit, and they still walked in them, and they even allowed the Asherah poles to remain in Samaria.
Jehoahaz had no army left except for fifty horsemen, ten chariots, and 10,000 foot soldiers because the Syrian king had destroyed them, and ground them down like threshing room dust.
The rest of the acts of Jehoahaz, everything that he did, and his might are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
Jehoahaz died and slept with his fathers, and they buried him in Samaria and his son Joash reigned in his place.
Jehoahaz's son Joash began to reign over Israel in Samaria in the thirty-seventh year of the reign of King Joash of Judah, and he reigned for sixteen years.
He did evil in the Lord's sight, and he did not turn away from the sins that Nebat's son Jeroboam made Israel commit, but he walked in them.
The rest of the acts of Joash, and everything that he did, and his might when he fought against King Amaziah of Judah, are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
Joash die and slept with his fathers, so Jeroboam sat on his throne and Joash was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel.
When Elisha fell sick from his illness from which he died, King Joash of Israel came down to see him and wept over his him and said, "O my father, my father the chariots and horsemen of Israel."
Elisha said to him, "Take a bow and arrows," and he took his bow and arrows.
Then he said to the king of Israel, "Put your hand on the bow," and he put his hand on the bow, and Elisha put his hands on the king's hands.

And he said, "Open the east window," and he opened it. Then Elisha said, "Shoot," so he shot. And he said, "This is the arrow of the Lord's deliverance and the victory over Syria, because you will attack and kill the Syrians in Aphek, until you have consumed them."
And Elisha said, "Take the arrows," and he took them." And he said to the king of Israel, "Stab the ground," and he stabbed it three times and stopped.

The man of God was angry with him and said, "You should have stabbed the ground five or six times, then you would have defeated Syria until they were destroyed, but now you will only defeat Syria three times."
Elisha died, and they buried him. Moabite raiders used to invade the land at the beginning of each year.

One day as the Israelis were burying a man, they saw a band of raiders coming their way. They threw the body into Elisha's tomb, but when the body was being lowered, it touched the bones of Elisha, and the man was revived and stood up on his feet.
But King Hazael of Syria oppressed Israel all the days of the reign of King Jehoahaz.
The Lord was gracious, compassionate, and respectful to Israel because of his covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. And he would not destroy them or remove them from his presence to this day.
So King Hazael of Syria died, and his son Ben-Hadad reigned in his place.
Jehoahaz's son Joash took back the cities from Hazael's son Ben-Hadad, which he had taken from his father Jehoahaz by war. Joash beat him three times and recovered the cities of Israel.
In the second year of Jehoahaz's son King Joash's reign over Israel, Joash's son King Amaziah began to reign over Judah.
Amaziah was twenty-five years old when he began to reign in Jerusalem, and he reigned for twenty-nine years. His mother's name was Jehoaddan and she was also from Jerusalem.
Amaziah did everything that he thought was righteous in the Lord's sight, but unlike King David he did the things his father Joash had done.
However the high places were not removed, and the people continued to sacrifice and burn incense on the high places.
As soon as the kingdom was firmly under his control, he killed his servants who had killed his father the king.

But he did not kill the murderers' because it was written in the Book of the Law of Moses, in which the Lord gave this commandment and said, "The fathers will not be put to death for the sins of the children, nor will the children be put to death for the sins of the fathers, but every man will be put to death for his own sin."
Amaziah killed 10,000 people of Edom in the Valley of Salt, then he captured Sela in battle and he renamed it Joktheel, which is its name to this very day.
Then he sent messengers to King Joash of Israel, who was the son of Jehoahaz, the son of Jehu and said, "Come, let us meet face to face."

But King Joash of Israel replied to King Amaziah of Judah and said, "A thistle in Lebanon sent a message to a cedar in Lebanon and said, 'Give your daughter to my son to be his wife.' And a wild beast was passing by and trampled the thistle.
You have defeated Edom and your heart is proud, take glory in this and stay home. Why do you want to meddle and stir up trouble that would cause you and Judah to fall?"
But Amaziah would not listen, so King Joash of Israel went and met King Amaziah of Judah face to face at Beth-Shemesh in Judah.
Judah was routed by Israel, and all the men fled to their own homes.

King Jehoash of Israel captured King Amaziah of Judah, who was the son of Joash, the son of Ahaziah at Beth-Shemesh. Then he went to Jerusalem and tore down 400 cubits of the wall of Jerusalem from the Gate of Ephraim to the corner gate.
He took all the gold, silver, valuable vessels, and other treasures found in the Lord's temple and the king's palace, and he returned to Samaria with hostages.
The rest of the acts of Joash and everything that he did, his might and how he fought with King Amaziah of Judah, are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
Joash died and slept with his fathers, and was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel, and his son Jeroboam reigned in his place.
King Joash's son Amaziah lived for fifteen years after King Jehoahaz's son King Joash of Israel died.
The rest of the acts of Amaziah, are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah.
Some conspirators conspired against Amaziah in Jerusalem and he fled to Lachish, but they sent assassins to Lachish and they killed him there.
Then they brought him back to Jerusalem on horses, and he was buried with his fathers in the city of David.
All the people of Judah made sixteen year old Azariah the king instead of his father Amaziah.
He rebuilt Elath and returned it to Judah, after that the king slept with his fathers.
After Joash's son Amaziah of Judah reigned for fifteen years, one of his other sons Jeroboam became the king of Israel in Samaria, and he reigned for forty-one years.
He did evil in the Lord's sight, and he did not turn away from all the sins of Nebat's son Jeroboam who made Israel commit sin.

Jeroboam restored Israel's borders from the entrance of Hamath to the Dead Sea, just as the Lord God of Israel said when he spoke through his servant Jonah, who was the prophet Amittai's son from Gath-Hepher.
The Lord saw that Israel's affliction was very bitter for both the free and slaves, and there was no one to help Israel.
Then the Lord said he would not erase Israel's name from under heaven, so he used Joash's son Jeroboam save them.

The rest of the acts of Jeroboam, and everything that he did, his might, how he waged war and recovered Damascus and Hamath for Israel from Judah, are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
Jeroboam died and slept with his fathers who were the kings of Israel, and his son Zachariah reigned in his place.
In the twenty-seventh year of the reign of King Jeroboam of Israel, King Amaziah's son Azariah of Judah began to reign.
He was sixteen years old when he began to reign, and he reigned for fifty-two years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jecholiah and she was from Jerusalem.
He did everything that he thought was righteous in the Lord's sight, just like his father Amaziah had.
Except he did not remove the high places, and the people continued to sacrifice and burn incense on the high places.
The Lord afflicted the king with leprosy until the day of his death. He lived in a separate house from the palace, and the king's son Jotham was over the palace and judged the people of the land.
The rest of the acts of Azariah, and everything that he did are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah.
So Azariah died and slept with his fathers, and they buried him with his fathers in the city of David, and his son Jotham reigned in his place.
In the thirty-eighth year of King Azariah of Judah's reign, Jeroboam's son Zachariah reigned over Israel in Samaria for six months.
He did evil in the Lord's sight, just like his fathers had done, he did not turn away from the sins of Nebat's son Jeroboam who made Israel sin.
Jabesh's son Shallum conspired against Zachariah and killed him before the people, and reigned in his place.
The rest of the acts of Zachariah are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
So the Lord's word was fulfilled when he spoke through Jehu and said, "Your descendants will sit on Israel's throne for four generations." And that's exactly what happened.
Jabesh's son Shallum began to reign in the thirty-ninth year of the reign of King Uzziah of Judah, and he reigned for a full month in Samaria.
Because Menahem the son of Gadi left Tirzah and went to Samaria, then he defeated and killed Jabesh's son Shallum, and reigned in his place.
The rest of the acts of Shallum, and his conspiracy against Zachariah are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
Then Menahem attacked and defeated everyone within the borders Tirzah, because they would not open their gates for him. So he defeated Tirzah, and had all the pregnant women ripped apart.
In the thirty-ninth year of the reign of King Azariah of Judah, Gadi's son Menahem began to reign over Israel in Samaria, and he reigned for ten years.
He did evil in the Lord's sight, for the entire time of his reign he did not turn away from the sins of Nebat's son Jeroboam, who made Israel sin.
King Pul of Assyria attacked the land, and Menahem gave Pul a thousand silver talents to garner his support in order to consolidate his power over the kingdom.
Menahem exacted money from the wealthy men of Israel, he demanded fifty silver shekels from each one to give to the Assyrian king. So the Assyrian king turned back, and did not stay in the land.
The rest of the acts of Menahem, and everything that he did are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
Menahem died and slept with his fathers, and his son Pekahiah reigned in his place.
In the fiftieth year of the reign of King Azariah of Judah, Menahem's son Pekahiah began to reign over Israel in Samaria, and he reigned for two years.
He did evil in the Lord's sight, and he did not turn away from the sins of Nebat's son Jeroboam who made Israel sin.

But Remaliah's son Pekah, one of his officers conspired against Pekahiah along with Argob, Arieh, and fifty men from Mount Gilead. Pekah attacked and killed him in Samaria in the king's palace, and he reigned in his place.
The rest of the acts of Pekahiah, and everything that he did are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
In the fifty-second year of Azariah King of Judah Pekah the son of Remaliah began to reign over Israel in Samaria, and he reigned for twenty years.
He did evil in the Lord's sight, and he did not turn away from the sins of Nebat's son Jeroboam who made Israel sin.

In the days of King Pekah of Israel, King Tiglath-Pileser of Assyria attacked and captured Ijon, Abel-Beth-Maachah, Janoah, Kedesh, Hazor, Mount Gilead, Galilee, and all of Naphtali's lands and carried them to Assyria.
In the twentieth year of Uzziah's son Jotham's reign, Elah's son Hoshea conspired against Remaliah's son Pekah and killed him, and reigned in his place.
The rest of the acts of Pekah, and everything that he did are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
In the second year of King Remaliah's son Pekah of Israel's reign, King Uzziah's son Jotham of Judah began to reign.
He was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned for sixteen years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jerusha and she was Zadok's daughter.
He did everything that he thought was righteous in the Lord's sight, and he did everything just like his father Uzziah had done.
However he did not remove the high places, and the people continued to sacrifice and burn incense in the high places. He built the higher gate of the Lord's temple.
The rest of the acts of Jotham, and everything that he did are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah.
In those days the Lord began to send King Rezin of Syria and Remaliah's son Pekah against Judah.
Jotham died and slept with his fathers, and he was buried with his fathers in the city of his father David, and his son Ahaz reigned in his place.
In the seventeenth year of the reign of Remaliah's son Pekah, Jotham's son King Ahaz of Judah began to reign.
Ahaz was twenty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned for sixteen years in Jerusalem and unlike his father David, he did not do what was righteous in his Lord God's sight.
But he walked in the ways of Israel's kings, and yes he sacrificed his son in the fire, just like the heathen's abominations, whom the Lord driven out before the Israelis.
He sacrificed and burned incense in the high places, on the hills, and under every green tree.
Then King Rezin of Syria and King Remaliah's son Pekah of Israel went to war in Jerusalem, and they besieged Ahaz but they could not overcome him.
At that time the Syrian King Rezin recovered and drove the Jews out of Elath and returned it to Syria. Then the Syrians moved to Elath where they live to this day.

So Ahaz sent messengers to the Assyrian King Tiglath-Pileser and said, "I am your servant and your son, so come and save me from the hands of the Syrian king and the Israelis king, who rise up against me."
Ahaz took all the gold and silver that he could find in the Lord's temple and the king's palace, and sent it to the Assyrian king as a present.
The Assyrian king listened to him and marched to Damascus, where he attacked and captured the people and then took them to Kir, and executed King Rezin.
King Ahaz went to Damascus to meet King Tiglath-Pileser of Assyria where he saw an altar. Then King Ahaz sent priest Urijah a detailed model of the altar, that displayed its fine quality workmanship.
And priest Urijah built an altar from the plans and detailed instructions that King Ahaz sent him from Damascus. So, priest Urijah had it built and finished before King Ahaz returned from Damascus.
The king returned from Damascus, and when he saw the new altar he approached it.
He burned his burnt offering and bread offering, and poured his drink offering, and sprinkled the blood of his peace offerings on the new altar.
He moved the brass altar which was before the Lord, from the front of the temple between the new altar and the Lord's temple to the north side of the new altar.

King Ahaz gave an order to priest Urijah and said, "Burn the morning burnt offering, the evening bread offering, and the king's burnt offering and bread offering, along with the burnt offerings, grain offerings, and drink offerings from people of the land on the new altar. Then sprinkle all the blood from the burnt offerings and sacrifices on the new altar. But the brass altar will be for me to ask for guidance."
So, priest Urijah did everything that King Ahaz commanded.
King Ahaz cut the borders off of the foundations and removed the brass sink from each of them. He removed the sea from the brass oxen that were under it, and put it on the stone pavement.
He removed the Sabbath canopy that they had built in the temple, and closed the king's entrance outside the Lord's temple for the Assyrian king.
The rest of the acts of Ahaz, and everything that he did, are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah.
Ahaz died and slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the city of David, and his son Hezekiah reigned in his place.
In the twelfth year of the reign of King Ahaz of Judah, Elah's son Hoshea began to reign over Israel in Samaria, and he reigned for nine years.
He did evil in the Lord's sight, but not like the Israelis kings who came before him.
King Shalmaneser of Assyria attacked him, then Hoshea became his servant and gave him presents.

The Assyrian king found out that Hoshea was conspiring against him because he sent messengers to the Egyptian king. And he brought no presents to the Assyrian king, as he had every year before that. So the Assyrian king put him in prison.
Then the Assyrian king marched throughout the land and went to Samaria, and he besieged it for three years.

In the ninth year of the reign of King Hoshea, the Assyrian king captured Samaria and carried the Israelis back to Assyria. He brought them to Halah, where he settled them by the Habor river of Gozan, and also in the cities of the Medes.
All this happened, because the Israelis had sinned against their Lord God, who had brought them out of Egypt, and freed them from Pharaoh the Egyptian king, and they had feared other gods.
They also walked in the laws of the heathens that the Lord had driven out before the Israelis, and they did the abominable things the kings of Israel taught them.
The Israelis secretly did those unrighteous things against their Lord God, and from the watchtower to the fortified city, they built high places in all their cities.
They set up images and Asherah poles on every high hill and under every green tree.
They burned incense in all the high places, just like the heathen that the Lord carried away before them, and they worked wicked things to provoke the Lord's anger.
Because they served idols that the Lord had told them, "Do not do this thing."

But the Lord warned Israel and Judah through all the prophets and wise men and said, "Turn away from your evil ways and keep my laws and commandments, obey everything in the law which I gave your fathers, which I also sent to you through my servants the prophets."
Even so, they would not listen, but they were just as stubborn as their fathers who did not believe in their Lord God.

So they rejected God's laws and his covenant that he made with their fathers, as well as his testimonies which he gave them. But they chased after vanity and became vain, and they followed the heathen all around them, whom the Lord had told them not to do what they did.

They abandoned their Lord God's commandments, and they made two molten images of calves and an Asherah pole. Then they worshipped the sun, the moon, and the stars of the heavenly hosts and they served Baal.
They sacrificed their sons and daughters in the fire and used divination and magic spells to sell themselves to do evil in the Lord's sight, which provoked his anger.
That's why the Lord was very angry with Israel and removed them from his sight, and there was no one left except the tribe of Judah.
Judah did not keep their Lord God's commandments either, but they walked in the laws of Israel which they made.
Then the Lord rejected all of Israel's descendants. He afflicted them and delivered them into the hands of spoilers, until he had completely banished them from his sight.

Because the Lord ripped Israel from the house of David, and the Israelis made Nebat's son Jeroboam their new king. Jeroboam drove Israel away from following the Lord, and made them commit a great sin.
So the children of Israel walked in all the sins of Jeroboam, and they did not turn away from them.

Until the Lord removed Israel from his sight, as he said he would through all his servants the prophets. So Israel was carried away from their own land to Assyria, where they remain until this very day.

The Assyrian king brought men from Babylon, Cuthah, Ava, Hamath, and Sepharvaim and placed them in the Samaritan cities instead of the Israelis, and they took possession of Samaria and lived in its cities.
When they first began to settle there and make their homes there, they did not fear the Lord, so he sent lions among them which killed some of them.

So they spoke to the Assyrian king and said, "The nations which you have removed and placed in the Samaritan cities, do not know anything about the God of the land. And because they do not know anything about the God of the land, he has sent lions to kill them."
Then the Assyrian king said, "Take one of the priests that you brought from that place back with you to live there, and let him teach them about the God of the land."
Then one of the priests whom they had carried away from Samaria went to live in Bethel, and he taught them to fear the Lord.
However every nation made their own gods in every city where they lived, and they put them in the shrines of the high places that the Samaritans had built.
And the men of Babylon made Succoth-Benoth, and the men of Cuth made Nergal, and the men of Hamath made Ashima.
And the Avites made Nibhaz and Tartak, and the Sepharvites sacrificed their children in a fire to Adrammelech and Anammelech, the gods of Sepharvaim.
So the occupiers feared the Lord, but they also appointed all types of priests who made sacrifices for them in the shrines of the high places.
They feared the Lord, but served their own gods, as it was ordered by the nations that carried them away from there.

To this very day they practice all their former ways, they do not fear the Lord, and they do not observe their laws, legal decrees, or the laws, and commandments which the Lord gave to Jacob's descendants, whom he named Israel.
With whom the Lord has made a covenant when he said, "You will not fear other gods, nor bow down to them, nor serve them, nor sacrifice to them.
But you will fear, worship, and sacrifice to the Lord who brought you out of the land of Egypt with great power and an outstretched arm.
And you will observe forever the laws, legal decrees, statutes, and commandments which he wrote down for you, and you will fear no other gods.
And you will not forget the covenant that I have made with you, nor will you fear other gods.
But you will fear your Lord God, and he will deliver you from the hands of all your enemies.
However they did not listen, and they practiced their former abominations.
So these nations feared the Lord but they also served their carved images, and to this day both their children and their grandchildren continue to do as their fathers did.
In the third year of the reign of Elah's son King Hoshea of Israel, Ahaz's son King Hezekiah of Judah began to reign.
He was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned for twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Abi and she was Zachariah's daughter.
He did what he thought was righteous in the Lord's sight, just like his father David had done.

He removed the high places, broke all the carved images, cut down the Asherah poles, and destroyed the brass serpent that Moses had made, because up until that time the Israelis burned incense to it and called it Nehushtan.
Hezekiah trusted in the Lord God of Israel, and none of the kings of Judah before or after him was ever like him.
Because he faithfully clung to the Lord, and did not turn away from following him, but he kept all the Lord's commandments that he had given Moses.
The Lord was with Hezekiah and he prospered wherever he went, and he rebelled against the Assyrian king and refused to serve him.
He defeated the Philistines to the borders Gaza, and from the watchtower all the way to the fortified city.
In the fourth year of the reign of King Hezekiah, which was the seventh year of the reign of Elah's son King Hoshea of Israel, King Shalmaneser of Assyria attacked and besieged Samaria.
After three years of siege which was the sixth year of King Hezekiah's reign, and the ninth year of King Hoshea's reign of Israel, the Assyrians captured Samaria.
So the Assyrian king captured Samaria and carried the Israelis back to Assyria. He brought them to Halah, where he settled them by the Habor river of Gozan, and also in the cities of the Medes.

All of this happened because they would not obey their Lord God, but they transgressed against his covenant, and ignored everything that the Lord's servant Moses had commanded, and they would neither listen to or obey his commandments.
In the fourteenth year of the reign of King Hezekiah, the Assyrian King Sennacherib attacked and captured all the fortified cities of Judah.

King Hezekiah of Judah sent a message to the Assyrian king in Lachish that said, "I have offended you, if you withdraw your troops, I will pay you whatever you want." Then the Assyrian king collected 300 silver and 30 gold talents from King Hezekiah of Judah.
Hezekiah gave him all the silver that could be found in the Lord's temple and in the treasuries of the king's palace.
At that time, King Hezekiah of Judah also removed the gold from Lord's temple doors and columns, which his craftsmen had previously overlaid on them, and gave it to the Assyrian king.

The Assyrian king sent the Tartan, Rab-Saris, and Rabshakeh with a great army from Lachish to attack King Hezekiah in Jerusalem. When they reached Jerusalem, they stationed their men by the conduit of the upper pool, which is in Jerusalem along the highway that runs beside the field where they wash laundry.
When they had called out to the king, Hilkiah's son Eliakim who was near the palace, Shebna the scribe, and Asaph's son Joah the record keeper went out to meet them.
And the Rabshakeh said to them, "Speak to Hezekiah and tell him that the great Assyrian king says this, 'What makes you trust your own confidence?'
