You say you have a strategy and the strength for war. Who do you trust, that caused you to rebel against me?
Now behold! You are trusting the staff of the Egyptian broken reed, which will pierce any man's hand that leans on it, because this is what happens to anyone that trusts Pharaoh king of Egypt.

But if you say to me, 'We trust in our Lord God!' then I ask you is not Hezekiah the one who tore down and removed the altars in the high places, and then said to Judah and Jerusalem, 'You will worship at this altar in Jerusalem!'?
That's why, I pray you will accept my Lord the Assyrian king's pledge to give you 2,000 horses, if you can find enough riders for them!
How will you even defeat one captain from the weakest of my master's army, and put your trust in Egypt for chariots and horsemen?
So now, would I come to attack and destroy this place without the Lord's word? Because it was the Lord himself that said to me, "Go and attack this land and destroy it.'"

Then Hilkiah's son Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah said to the Rabshakeh, "I pray you will speak to us your servants in the Syrian language because we understand it, do not talk to us in the language of the Jews because the people on the wall are listening."

But the Rabshakeh said, "Has my master sent me just to speak to you and your master? Or has he not sent me to speak to the men sitting on the wall, because just like you will they have to eat their own dung, and drink their own piss?"
Then the Rabshakeh cried out in the language of the Jews with a loud voice and said, "Hear the words of the great Assyrian king.
This is what the king says, "Do not let Hezekiah deceive you, because he will not be able to deliver you from my hands.
Do not believe Hezekiah when he tells you to trust in the Lord when he said, 'The Lord will surely deliver us, and this city will not be delivered into the hand of the Assyrian king.'

Do not listen to Hezekiah, because this is what the Assyrian king says, 'Make peace and surrender to me.' Then everyone will eat from his own vine and his own fig tree, and drink water from his own well.

I will take you to a land that's like your own land, a land of wheat and wine, a land of bread and vineyards, a land of olive trees and honey, so that you may live and not die. But do not listen to Hezekiah when he tries to persuade you and says, 'The Lord will deliver us.'
Have any of the gods of any of the nations delivered their lands from the hands of the Assyrian king?
Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivah? Have they delivered Samaria from my hands?
Who are they among all the gods of all the countries, that have delivered their country from my hands, so that the Lord would deliver Jerusalem from my hand?"
But the people held their peace and did not answer him, because the king ordered them not to speak and said, "Do not answer him."

Then Hilkiah's son Eliakim who supervised the palace, along with Shebna the scribe and Asaph's son Joah the recorder went to meet King Hezekiah with torn clothes, and told him what the Rabshakeh said.
When King Hezekiah heard what was said he tore his clothes, and covered himself with sackcloth, and went into the Lord's temple.
And he sent Eliakim who was over the palace, Shebna the scribe, and the elders priests covered with sackcloth, to Amoz's son Isaiah the prophet.

He told them to speak to Isaiah and say, "This is what King Hezekiah says, 'Today is a day of trouble, rebuke, and blasphemy because the children have come to be born, and there is no strength to deliver them.'

Maybe your Lord God will listen to what the Rabshakeh has to say, whom his master the Assyrian king has sent to defy the living God. And maybe your Lord God will blame him for the words he has heard, so lift up your prayer for whoever still survives."
So King Hezekiah's servants went to speak to Isaiah.

And Isaiah spoke to them and said, "This is what you must say to your master, 'This is what the Lord says, "Do not be afraid of the blasphemous words you have heard the Assyrian king's servants say about me.
Behold, I will blast him with a rumor and he will be worried and return to his own land, then I will cause him to fall by the sword in his own land.'"
Then the Rabshakeh heard that the Assyrian king had left Lachish, so he returned and found the king waging war against Libnah.
When King Sennacherib received a letter warning him about King Tirhakah of Ethiopia that said, "Behold he has come to attack you," he sent messengers with a letter back to Hezekiah.
And the letter said, "Speak to King Hezekiah of Judah and say, 'Do not let your God in whom you trust deceive you by saying, "Jerusalem will not be delivered into the hands of the Assyrian king."
Behold, you have heard what the Assyrian kings have done to all lands that they invade, they have completely destroyed them! Do you really think you will be delivered?
Have the gods of the nations that my fathers destroyed delivered them? Such as the gods of Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and the descendants of Eden who lived in Telassar?
Where is the king of Hamath, the king of Arpad, the king of the city of Sepharvaim, the king of Hena, or the king of Ivah?'"
When Hezekiah received the letter from the messengers he read it, then he went into the Lord's temple, and spread it out before the Lord.
He prayed before the Lord and said, "O Lord God of Israel, who lives between the cherubims, you alone are the God of all the kingdoms on earth, you are the creator of heaven and earth.
Please listen and hear Lord, open your eyes and see Lord, and hear Sennacherib's message which he sent to defy the living God.
The truth is Lord, the Assyrian kings have destroyed these nations and their lands.
They threw their gods into the fire because they were not gods, but just the wood and stone work of men's hands, that's why they were destroyed.
So, O Lord our God, I beg you to save us from his hands, so that all the kingdoms on earth will know that you are the only Lord God."
Then Amoz's son Isaiah sent a message to Hezekiah and said, "This is what the Lord God of Israel says, 'I have heard the prayer prayed to me against the Assyrian king Sennacherib.'
This is the word that the Lord has spoken about him, the virgin Daughter of Zion has despised, laughed at, and scorned you. The Daughter of Jerusalem has shaken her head at you.
Who have you blasphemed and disapproved of, and against whom have you glorified yourself, and looked up at with prideful eyes? You have defied the Holy One of Israel.'

You have used your messengers to disapprove of the Lord and have said, 'I have ascended to the heights of the mountains to the remote peaks of Lebanon with all my chariots. I will cut down its tall cedar trees and its choice fir trees. I will enter into the lodgings of his borders and the Carmel forests.
I have dug wells and drunk foreign waters, and with the soles of my feet have I dried up all the rivers of Egypt.'
And the Lord replied, "Have you not heard how I have done it? How I planned and formed it long ago? Now I will allow you to lay waste to the fortified cities and pile them into ruinous heaps.

Because their inhabitants are powerless, dismayed, and confused. They are like the field grass or the green herbs, like the grass growing on the house tops, and like wheat scorched before it is grown.
But I know where you live, I know about your coming in and going out, and I know your rage against me.

Because your rage and anger against me has come up to my ears, so I will put my hook in your nose, and my bridle in your mouth, and I will force you to turn back and return the same way that you came."

This will be a sign to you that proves this is true Hezekiah, 'This year you will eat whatever grows by itself, in the second year you will eat whatever springs forth of the previous crop, in the third year you will sow, reap, plant vineyards, and eat its fruit.
Whatever remains that escaped from Judah will take root below and bear fruit above.
Because the remnants of Jerusalem will come out along with those that escaped from Mount Zion, and the zeal of the Lord of Hosts make sure this happens.
That is why the Lord says this concerning the Assyrian king, 'He will not enter this city or shoot an arrow there, nor will he advance on it with a shield, or throw a siege ramp against it.
He will return the same way he came, and he will not enter this city!'
Because the Lord says, 'I will defend and save this city, for my own sake and for the sake of my servant David.'"
So that night the Lord's angel went to the Assyrian camp and killed 145,000 men, and when they got up early the next morning, behold there was nothing there but dead corpses.
So Sennacherib the Assyrian king returned to Nineveh where he lived.

And it happened, as he was worshipping in the house of Nisroch his God, that Adrammelech and Sharezer his sons defeated him with the sword, and they escaped into the land of Armenia, and Esarhaddon his son reigned instead of him.
In those days King Hezekiah was sick until his death, and Amoz's son the prophet Isaiah came to him and said, "This is what the Lord says, 'Get your house in order because you are going to die.'"
Then Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed to the Lord.
And Hezekiah said, "O Lord, I beg you to remember how I have walked before you in truth and with a perfect heart, and I have done everything that is good in your sight," and he wept sorely.
And before Isaiah could leave and go out into the middle court, the Lord's word came to him.

And the Lord said, "Go back and tell Hezekiah the leader of my people that this is what the God of your father David says 'I have heard your prayer, I have seen your tears, and behold I will heal you, then on the third day go up to the Lord's temple.
And I will add fifteen years to your days, and I will deliver you and this city from the hands of the Assyrian king, and I will defend this city for my own sake and for my servant David's sake.'"
And Isaiah said, "Take some mashed up figs and lay it on the boil," and the king recovered.
Then Hezekiah said to Isaiah, "What will be the Lord's sign that I will be healed, and when to go to the Lord's temple on the third day?"
Isaiah replied and said, "This will be the sign from the Lord, that he will do what he has promised, would you like the shadow on the sundial to go forward ten degrees or back ten degrees?"
Hezekiah answered and said, "It is an easy thing for the shadow to go forward ten degrees, so let the shadow go back ten degrees."
So the prophet Isaiah cried out to the Lord, and the shadow on the Ahaz sundial went backwards ten degrees.
At that time Baladan's son King Merodach-Baladan of Babylon, sent letters and a present to King Hezekiah, because he had heard that Hezekiah had been sick.

Hezekiah listened to them, and showed them all of the precious things in his warehouses, including the silver, gold, spices, precious ointments, his armor, and all of his other treasures. There was nothing in his warehouses, or in his entire kingdom that he did not show them.
Then the prophet Isaiah came to King Hezekiah and said, "What did these men say to you and where did they come from?" And Hezekiah said, "They came here all the way from Babylon."
The Isaiah asked, "hat did they see in your warehouses?" And Hezekiah answered, "They have seen everything in my warehouses, there is nothing among my treasures that I have not shown them."
And Isaiah said to Hezekiah, "Hear the Lord's word.
The Lord says, 'Behold, the day has come, that everything in your warehouses that your fathers have stored up to this day will be carried to Babylon, and there will be nothing left.
And the sons that you will father will be carried away, and they will be eunuchs in the king of Babylon's palace.'"
But Hezekiah said to Isaiah, "The Lord's word you have spoken to me is good." Because he thought to himself, "At least there will be peace and truth during my lifetime and that's good."
The rest of the acts of Hezekiah, and all of his might, plus how he built the pool and a conduit to bring water into the city, are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah.
Then Hezekiah died and slept with his fathers, and his son Manasseh reigned in his place.
Manasseh was twelve years old when he began to reign, and reigned for fifty-five years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Hephzibah.
He did evil in the Lord's sight, and committed the abominations of the heathen, who the Lord drove out before the Israelis.

Because he rebuilt the high places which his father Hezekiah had destroyed, and he raised up altars for Baal and built an Asherah pole, just like King Ahab of Israel. He also worshipped and served the sun, the moon, the planets, and the all stars of heaven as gods.
And he built altars in the Lord's temple of which the Lord had said, "I will put my name in Jerusalem."
He built altars for the sun, the moon, the planets, and the all the stars of heaven in the two courts of the Lord's temple.
He sacrificed his son in the fire, practiced sorcery, used magic spells, and dealt with familiar spirits and wizards, he worked much wickedness in the Lord's sight and provoke his anger.

He made and set a carved Asherah pole in the temple where the Lord spoke to David and his son Solomon and said, "I have chosen this temple in Jerusalem from all tribes of Israel to establish my name forever.

I will never again make Israel move out of the land I gave their fathers, if they will only observe and obey everything that I have commanded them, as it is recorded in all the laws that my servant Moses gave them."
But they did not listen, and Manasseh seduced them into doing more evil than all the nations did whom the Lord destroyed before the Israelis.
Then the Lord spoke through his servants the prophets.
And the Lord said, "Because King Manasseh of Judah has done these abominations, and was more wicked than the Amorites who were before him, and he also made Judah sin with his idols.
So, this is what the Lord God of Israel says, 'Behold I am going to bring such evil on Jerusalem and Judah, that both ears of whoever hears about it will tingle.
I will stretch the measuring line over Jerusalem that I used to destroy Samaria and I will wipe out Jerusalem as one wipes a dish clean and turns it upside down.
I will forsake what remains of my inheritance, and deliver them into the hand of their enemies, and they will become all of their enemies prey and spoils.
Because they have done evil in my sight and provoked my anger, from the day their fathers came out of Egypt, until this very day.'"

Besides that Manasseh shed a lot of innocent blood, until he filled the streets of Jerusalem with blood from one end to another. He did this in addition to doing evil in the Lord's sight and making Judah sin.
The rest of the acts of Manasseh, and everything that he did, and the sins he committed, are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah.
Manasseh died and slept with his fathers, and was buried in the garden of his own house, in the Uzza garden, and his son Amon reigned in his place.
Amon was twenty-two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned for two years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Meshullemeth, and she was the daughter of Haruz from Jotbah.
He did evil in the Lord's sight, just like his father Manasseh.
He walked in all the ways of his father, and he served and worshipped all the idols that his father served and worshipped.
He had forsaken the Lord God of his fathers, and he did not walk in the ways of the Lord.
King Amon's servants conspired against him, and killed him in his own house.
The people of the land killed everyone that had conspired against King Amon, and they made his son Josiah king to take his place.
The rest of the acts of everything that Amon did, are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah.
He was buried in his tomb in the garden of Uzza, and his son Josiah reigned in his place.
Josiah was eight years old when he began to reign, and he reigned for thirty-one years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jedidah, she was Adaiah of Bozkath's daughter.
He did what he thought was righteous in the Lord's sight, and he walked in all the ways of his father David, and he did not turn to the left or the right.
In the eighteenth year of the reign of King Josiah, the king sent Shaphan the son of Azaliah, who was Meshullam the scribe's son to the Lord's temple and said,
"Go to the high priest Hilkiah, and have him count the silver that the people brought into the Lord's temple, that the gatekeepers collected.
Then give it to the people who supervise the work rebuilding the Lord's temple, to pay those who are working to repair the damage done to the Lord's temple.
To carpenters, and builders, and masons, and to buy timber and carved stone to strengthen the house.
However there is no need to audit the money given to them because they deal faithfully."
And Hilkiah the high priest spoke to Shaphan the scribe and said, "I have found the Book of the Law in the Lord's temple." And Hilkiah gave the book to Shaphan which he read.

Once again Shaphan the scribe brought word to the king and said, "Your servants have collected the money from the temple, and they gave it to the people who are supervising and doing the work on the Lord's temple."
Shaphan the scribe showed the book to the king and said, "Hilkiah the priest gave me this book," then he read it to the king.
When the king heard the words from the Book of the Law, he tore his clothes.
And the king commanded priest Hilkiah, Shaphan's son Ahikam, Micaiah's son Achbor, Shaphan the scribe, and Asahiah the king's servant said.

"Go and ask the Lord for me, the people, and all the people of Judah about the words found in this book. The Lord's great anger has been kindled against us, because our fathers did not listen to the words of this book, and they did not obey everything that was written about us."

So priest Hilkiah, Ahikam, Achbor, Shaphan, and Asahiah went to speak to the prophetess Huldah who was married to Tikvah's son and Harhas' grandson Shallum, who was the keeper of the wardrobe. She lived in the suburbs of Jerusalem.
And she said to them, "Tell the man who sent you."
"This is what the Lord says, 'Behold I will bring evil on this place and its inhabitants, and fulfill all the words of the book which the king of Judah has read.

Because they have forsaken me and burned incense to other gods, and they have provoked my anger by all the evil works of their hands, so my anger will be kindled against this place, and it will not be quenched.'
But say this to the king of Judah who sent you to ask the Lord, 'This is what the Lord God of Israel says, "As touching the words are which you have heard.

Because your heart was tender, and you humbled yourself before the Lord when you heard what I spoke against this place and its people, so that they would become a devastation and a curse, and because you have torn your clothes and wept before me, I have heard you," says the Lord.
So I will bring you to your fathers and you will go to your grave in peace, and you will not see all the evil which I will bring on this place,'"and they brought her response back to the king.
One day King Josiah sent for all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.

The king went into the Lord's sanctuary with all the men of Judah, the priests, the prophets, and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem both great and small. Then he read the whole Book of the Covenant to them, which was found in the Lord's sanctuary.

The king stood near a column and made a covenant before the Lord. He promised to follow the Lord and keep the Lord's commandments, testimonies, and laws with all his heart and soul. He promised to do everything that was written in his Book of the Covenant, and all the people stood by his covenant with the Lord.

The king commanded high priest Hilkiah, the second order priests, and the doorkeepers to bring all the bowls that were made for Baal and the Asherah pole, and all the stars of heaven out of the Lord's temple. Then he burned them in the fields of Kidron outside Jerusalem, and he carried their ashes to Bethel.

King Josiah put down the idolatrous priests that the kings of Judah had ordained to burn incense in the high places in the cities of Judah and all around Jerusalem. He also put down those that burned incense to Baal, the sun, the moon, the planets, and all the stars of heaven.
He brought the Asherah pole from the Lord's temple to the Brook of Kidron outside of Jerusalem and burned it, and ground it into powder, and threw the powder on the graves of the people's children.
He tore down the Sodomites' houses that were near the Lord's temple, where the women wove hangings for the Asherah pole.

He brought all the priests from Judah's cities and defiled the high places from Geba to Beersheba where the priests had burned incense. He also tore down the gate's high places at the entrance gates of Joshua the governor of the city, which was on the left side of the city gate.
Nevertheless, the priests of the high places did not come to the Lord's altar in Jerusalem, but they ate the unleavened bread with their brothers.
He also defiled Topheth in the valley of Hinnom's descendants, so that no one could sacrifice his son or daughter in the fire to Molech.

He removed the horses that the kings of Judah had given to the sun from the entrance of the Lord's temple. They were in the fields and pastures near the chamber of the eunuch Nathan-Melech. And he burned the chariots of the sun.

The king tore down the altars located on top of the upper chamber of Ahaz and the altars which the kings of Judah and Manasseh had setup in the two courtyards of the Lord's temple. He tore them down and crushed them, and threw the dust into the Brook of Kidron.

The king also defiled the high places before Jerusalem, south of Mount Corruption, which Israel's King Solomon built for Ashtoreth the Sidonian's abominable god, and Chemosh the abominable god of Moab, and Milcom the abominable god of Ammon's descendants.
He broke the images into pieces and cut down the Asherah poles, then he filled their places with human bones.

Besides that, he tore down the altar at Bethel and the high place built by Nebat's son Jeroboam who made Israel sin. He tore down both that altar and the high place, and burned them and the Asherah pole, and ground them into powder.

As King Josiah turned around, he saw the tombs up on the mountain. He sent some men to remove the bones from the tombs, and he burned them on the altar to pollute it, just as the Lord's man of God had proclaimed.

Then the king asked, "Whose monument is this that I see?" The men of the city replied and said, "It is the tomb of the man of God who came from Judah and proclaimed the things that you have done to the altar of Bethel."
And he said, "Leave him alone and do not move his bones." So they did not disturb his bones, or the prophet's bones that came from Samaria.
Then King Josiah removed every house in the high places in Samaria's cities, which the Israelis kings made to provoke the Lord's anger, and he did everything to them that he had done in Bethel.
He killed all the priests there on the altars of the high places, and burned men's bones on them and returned to Jerusalem.
The king gave a command to all the people and said, "Keep your Lord God's Passover, as it is written in the Book of the Covenant."
Surely no such a Passover had been celebrated from the days of the judges that judged Israel, nor in all the days of the kings of Israel or the kings of Judah.
But in the eighteenth year of the reign of King Josiah, the Passover was celebrated to the Lord in Jerusalem.

Besides that, Josiah removed the mediums and spiritualists who workers with familiar spirits and the wizards, carved images, idols, and all the abominations that were found in the land of Judah and in Jerusalem. He did this so that he could carry out what was written in the book that priest Hilkiah found in the Lord's sanctuary.
There had been no kings like him before and there have been none since, a king that turned to the Lord with all his heart, soul, and might as it was written in all the laws of Moses.
But the Lord did not turn away from the fierceness of his great anger, which was kindled against Judah because of everything that Manasseh had done to provoke him.

And the Lord said, "I will also remove Judah from my sight just like I removed Israel, and I will cast my chosen city of Jerusalem away along with its temple of which I said, 'My name will always be there!'"
The rest of the acts of Josiah, and everything that he did, are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah.
In his day Pharaoh King Necho of Egypt attacked the Assyrian king at the Euphrates River, then King Josiah saw him at Megiddo, and he attacked and killed him.

His servants brought his dead body from Megiddo to Jerusalem in a chariot. They buried him in his own tomb, and the people of the land anointed Josiah's son Jehoahaz as their king to replace his father.
Jehoahaz was twenty-three years old when he began to reign, and he reigned for three months in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Hamutal, she was the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah.
He did evil things in the Lord's sight, just like his fathers had done.
Pharaoh Necho imprisoned Jehoahaz in chains at Riblah in Hamath, so he could not reign in Jerusalem. Then he levied a one hundred silver talent and a one gold talent tax on the land.
Then Pharaoh Necho made King Josiah's son Eliakim the new king in place of his father Josiah, and changed his name to Jehoiakim. But Necho took Jehoahaz away and carried him to Egypt, where he died.
And as Pharaoh had commanded him, King Jehoiakim gave Necho the all money, silver, and gold collected from the people of the land, which was based on each person's wealth.
Jehoiakim was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned for eleven years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Zebudah, she was the daughter of Pedaiah of Rumah.
And he did everything that was evil in the Lord's sight, just like his fathers had done.
In his day King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon invaded Judah, and King Jehoiakim became his servant for three years until he rebelled.
he Lord sent Chaldean, Syrian, Moabite, and Ammonite armies against Judah to destroy it, Just as the Lord had said it would happen when he spoke through his servants the prophets.
Surely the Lord's commandment to remove Judah from his sight came upon them, because of everything Manasseh had done and the sins he had committed.
Also for the innocent blood that Manasseh shed, because he filled Jerusalem with innocent blood which the Lord would not pardon.
The rest of the acts of Jehoiakim, and everything that he did, are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah.
So Jehoiakim died and slept with his fathers, and his son Jehoiachin reigned in his place.
The king of Egypt did not come out of his land anymore, because the king of Babylon had taken all the land that the king of Egypt had, from the Nile River all the way to the Euphrates River.
Jehoiachin was eighteen years old when he began to reign, and he reigned in Jerusalem for three months. His mother's name was Nehushta, she was Elnathan's Daughter of Jerusalem.
He did everything that was evil in the Lord's sight, just like his father had done.
At that time, King Nebuchadnezzar's Babylonian armies attacked Jerusalem and laid siege to the city.
King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon came to Jerusalem as his armies attacked and besieged it.
King Jehoiachin of Judah surrendered to the king of Babylon along with his mother, his servants, his officers and commanders. And the king of Babylon captured him in the eighth year of his reign.

Nebuchadnezzar also carried off all the treasures from the Lord's temple and the king's palace. And he cut up all the gold bowls which King Solomon of Israel had made in the temple of the Lord, just like the Lord had said it would be.

He carried away the people of Jerusalem, including 10,000 captive officers and mighty men of valor. And he carried away all the craftsmen and blacksmiths, no one remained except the poorest people of the land.
Nebuchadnezzar captured Jehoiachin and carried him from Jerusalem to Babylon along with his mother, his wives, his officers, and the mighty men of the land.
The king of Babylon also brought 7,000 mighty men and craftsmen and 1,000 blacksmiths, and anyone else that was strong enough for war into captivity in Babylon.
Then the king of Babylon made Jehoiachin's father's brother Mattaniah king to reign in his brother's place, and changed Mattaniah's name to Zedekiah.
Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned for eleven years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Hamutal, she was the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah.
He did everything that was evil in the Lord's sight, just like Jehoiakim had done.
All of this happened in Jerusalem and Judah because the Lord's anger burned until he had thrown them from his presence. So that Zedekiah also rebelled against the king of Babylon.

It was on the tenth day of the tenth month of the ninth year of his reign, that King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon brought his armies to attack Jerusalem, and they camped next to it and built siege forts all around it.
The city was under sieged until the eleventh year of the reign of King Zedekiah.
On the ninth day of the fourth month, the famine in the city was so bad that the people had no food or bread.

Then the city walls were breached, and all the men of war fled by night through the gates between the two walls near the king's garden. Even though the Chaldeans had that side of the city surrounded, the king and his men fled toward the plains.
The Chaldean army pursued the king and overtook him on the plains of Jericho, and his entire army was scattered away from him.
So they captured the king and brought him up to the king of Babylon in Riblah, where they passed judgment on him.
They mercilessly killed Zedekiah's sons before him, then they gouged out Zedekiah's eyes, and bound him with brass shackles and carried him to Babylon.
On the seventh day of the fifth month of the nineteenth year of the reign of King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon, Nebuzaradan a servant of the king of Babylon and captain of the guard went to Jerusalem.
He burned the Lord's temple, the king's palace, all the houses, and all the great buildings in Jerusalem.
The Chaldean army that came with the captain of the guard, tore down all the city walls surrounding Jerusalem.

Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard carry away the rest of the people left in the city, including the fugitives who had gone over to the king of Babylon's side, as well as whatever remained of the army.
But the captain of the guard let the poor people stay there to manage the vineyards and ranches.
The brass columns, brass foundations, and the brass sea that was in the Lord's temple were broken to pieces by the Chaldeans, and carried back to Babylon.
The pots, shovels, candle snuffers, spoons, and all the brass bowls that were used to minister in the Lord's temple were carried away.
The gold and silver firepans, bowls, and anything else made of gold or silver was carried away by the captain of the guard.
The two brass columns, brass sea, brass bowls, and brass foundations which Solomon had made for the Lord's temple, were too heavy to weigh.

One of the columns was eighteen cubits high, and the brass ornamental capital on top of it was three cubits high. The interwoven work and the pomegranates on top of the ornamental capital were all made of brass. And all the brass work of the second column was identical to the first column.
The captain of the guard took Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the second priest, and the three temple doorkeepers captive.

He took an officer that was over the men of war, and five men that were in the king's court who were found in the city, and the army's principal scribe who mustered the people, and sixty other men of the land that were found in the city.
Then Nebuzaradan who was the captain of the guard brought them to the king of Babylon to Riblah.
The king of Babylon had them killed at Riblah in Hamath. So, this was how the people of Judah were carried away from their land.
As for the people that King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon left in Judah, he appointed Ahikam's son and Shaphan's grandson Gedaliah their governor.

When all of Judah's army captains and their soldiers who had not surrendered found out that King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah as governor, they met the governor at Mizpah. These army captains were Nethaniah's son Ishmael, Kareah's son Johanan, Tanhumeth's son Seraiah of Netophah, and Jaazaniah from the Maacah region.
And Gedaliah swore to them and their men and said, "Do not fear becoming the servants of the Chaldeans, live in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and all will go well for you."

But in the seventh month, Elishama's grandson and Nethaniah's son Ishmael of the royal family came with ten men and killed Gedaliah. So he died at Mizpah, along with the Jews and the Chaldeans that were with him.
Then all the people there both great and small and the captains of the armies, got up and fled to Egypt because they were afraid of the Chaldeans.

On the twenty-seventh day of the twelfth month of the thirty-seventh year after Judah's king Jehoiachin was taken prisoner by the Babylonians, King Nebuchadnezzar's son Evil-Merodach became the new king of Babylon, and he decided to be kind to Jehoiachin, and set him free.
He spoke kindly to Jehoiachin, and held him in higher esteem than all the other kings that were exiled with him in Babylon.
He exchanged Jehoiachin's prison garments for new clothes, and allowed him to eat bread at the king's table for the rest of his life.
King Evil-Merodach gave Jehoiachin a daily allowance every day for the rest of his life.
Adam, Sheth, Enosh,
Kenan, Mahalalel, Jered,
Henoch, Methuselah, Lamech,
Noah, Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
Japheth's sons were Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras.
Gomer's sons were Ashchenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah.
Javan's sons were Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim.
Ham's sons were Cush, Mizraim, Put, and Canaan.
Cush's sons were Seba, Havilah, Sabta, Raamah, Sabtecha. Raamah's sons were Sheba, and Dedan.
Cush fathered Nimrod, who became mighty on the earth.
Mizraim fathered Ludim, Anamim, Lehabim, Naphtuhim,
Pathrusim, Casluhim from whom came the Philistines and the Caphthorim.
Canaan fathered his firstborn son Sidon, and Heth,
Also the Jebusites, Amorites, and Girgashites,
Also the Hivites, Arkites, and Sinites,
Also the Arvadites, Zemarites, and Hamathites.
Shem's sons were Elam, Assyria, Arphaxad, Lud, Aram, Uz, Hul, Gether, and Meshech.
Arphaxad fathered Shelah, and Shelah fathered Eber.
Eber had two sons, one was named Peleg because during his time the earth was divided up, and his brother's name was Joktan.
Joktan fathered Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah,
Hadoram, Uzal, Diklah,
Ebal, Abimael, Sheba,
Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab.
Joktan's sons were Shem, Arphaxad, Shelah,
Eber, Peleg, Reu,
Serug, Nahor, Terah,
and Abram, whose name was later changed to Abraham.
Abraham's sons were Isaac and Ishmael.
These are their descendants. Ishmael had twelve sons and his firstborn was Nebaioth and then Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam,
Mishma, Dumah, Massa, Hadad, Tema,
Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah.
Abraham's sons from his concubine Keturah were Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah. Jokshan's sons were Sheba, and Dedan.
Midian's sons were Ephah, Epher, Henoch, Abida, and Eldaah. These are all of Keturah's sons.
Abraham fathered Isaac, and Isaac's sons were Esau and Israel.
Esau's sons were Eliphaz, Reuel, Jeush, Jaalam, and Korah.
Eliphaz's sons were Teman, Omar, Zephi, Gatam, Kenaz, Timna, and Amalek.
Reuel's sons were Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah.
Seir's sons were Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah, Dishon, Ezar, and Dishan.
Lotan's sons were Hori and Homam, and Timna was Lotan's sister.
Shobal's sons were Alian, Manahath, Ebal, Shephi, and Onam. Zibeon's sons were Aiah and Anah.
Dishon was Anah's son. Dishon's sons were Amram, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran.
Ezer's sons were Bilhan, Zavan, and Jakan. Dishan's sons were Uz and Aran.
Now these are the kings that reigned in Edom before any kings reigned over Israel, Beor's son Bela in the city of Dinhabah.
When Bela died, Zerah's son Jobab of Bozrah reigned in his place.
When Jobab died, Husham of the Temanites reigned in his place.
When Husham died, Bedad's son Hadad, who defeated Midian in the field of Moab, reigned in his place, and his city was named Avith.
When Samlah died, Shaul of Rehoboth by the river reigned in his place.
And when Samlah was dead, Shaul of Rehoboth by the river reigned instead of him.
When Shaul died, Baal-Hanan the son of Achbor reigned in his place
When Baal-Hanan died, Hadad reigned in his place and his city was named Pai. His wife's name was Mehetabel, and she was Matred's daughter and Mezahab's granddaughter.
Hadad also died and the dukes of Edom were Duke Timnah, Duke Aliah, Duke Jetheth,
Duke Aholibamah, Duke Elah, Duke Pinon,
Duke Kenaz, Duke Teman, Duke Mibzar,
Duke Magdiel, and Duke Iram. These were all the dukes of Edom.
Israel's sons were Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Zebulun,
Dan, Joseph, Benjamin, Naphtali, Gad, and Asher.
Judah's sons were Er, Onan, and Shelah and their grandmother was Shua the Canaanite. Judah's firstborn son Er did evil in the Lord's sight and the Lord killed him.
His daughter-in-law Tamar gave birth to Pharez and Zerah, and altogether Judah had five sons.
Pharez's sons were Hezron and Hamul.
Zerah's five sons were named Zimri, Ethan, Heman, Calcol, and Dara.
Carmi's son Achar caused much trouble for Israel by taking the cursed thing.
Ethan's son was Azariah.
The sons born to Hezron were Jerahmeel, Ram, and Chelubai.
Ram fathered Amminadab. Amminadab fathered Nahshon, who was a leader of Judah's descendants.
Nahshon fathered Salma, and Salma fathered Boaz.
Boaz fathered Obed, and Obed fathered Jesse.
Jesse's firstborn son was Eliab, his second born was Abinadab, his third born was Shimma,
his fourth born was Nathaniel, his fifth born was Raddai,
his sixth born was Ozem, and his seventh born was David.
Their sisters were Zeruiah and Abigail. Zeruiah's three sons were Abishai, Joab, and Asahel.
Abigail gave birth to Amasa, and Amasa's father was Jether the Ishmaelite.
Hezron's son Caleb had children by his wives Azubah and Jerioth. Azubah's sons were Jesher, Shobab, and Ardon.
When Azubah died, Caleb married Ephrath who gave birth to Hur.
Hur fathered Uri, and Uri fathered Bezalel.
Afterward when he was sixty years old, Hezron married Machir's daughter who gave birth to his son Segub. Machir was Gilead's father.
Jair's father Segub owned twenty-three cities on Mount Gilead.
But Geshur and Aram captured its towns Jair and Kenath, and sixty of its cities. All of them belonged to the descendants of Gilead's father Machir.
After that Hezron died in Caleb-Ephratah, then Hezron's wife Abiah gave birth to Ashur who was Tekoa's father.
Hezron's firstborn son Jerahmeel sons were Ram who was his firstborn then Bunah, Oren, Ozem, and Ahijah.
Jerahmeel also had another wife named Atarah, she was Onam's mother.
Jerahmeel's firstborn son was Ram then Maaz, Jamin, and Eker.
Onam's sons were Shammai and Jada. Shammai's sons were Nadab and Abishur.
Abishur's wife's name was Abihail, and she gave birth to his sons Ahban and Molid.
Nadab's sons were Seled and Appaim, but Seled died childless.
Ishi was Appaim's son, Sheshan was Ishi's son, and Ahlai was Sheshan's son.
Shammai's brother Jada's sons were Jether and Jonathan, and Jether died childless.
Jonathan sons were Peleth and Zaza. These were all the sons of Jerahmeel.
Now Sheshan had daughters and no sons, but he had an Egyptian servant named Jarha.
Sheshan gave his daughter in marriage to his servant Jarha, and she gave birth to Jarha's son Attai.
Attai fathered Nathan, and Nathan fathered Zabad.
Zabad fathered Ephlal, and Ephlal fathered Obed.
Obed fathered Jehu, and Jehu fathered Azariah.
Azariah fathered Helez, and Helez fathered Eleasah.
Eleasah fathered Sisamai, and Sisamai fathered Shallum.
Shallum fathered Jekamiah, and Jekamiah fathered Elishama.
Now Jerahmeel's brother Caleb's sons were his firstborn son Mesha who was Ziph's father, and his second son Mareshah who was Hebron's father.
Hebron's sons were Korah, Tappuah, Rekem, and Shema.
And Shema fathered Raham, the father of Jorkeam, and Rekem fathered Shammai.
Shammai's son was Maon, and Maon was Beth-Zur's father.
Caleb's concubine Ephah, gave birth to Haran, Moza, and Gazez. And Haran was Gazez's father.
Jahdai's sons were Regem, Jotham, Gesham, Pelet, Ephah, and Shaaph.
Caleb's concubine Maachah gave birth to Sheber and Tirhanah.
She also gave birth to Shaaph who was Madmannah's father, and Sheva who fathered Machbenah and Gibea. And Caleb was Acsah's daughter.
These were Caleb's descendants. The sons of Hur Ephratah's firstborn son Hur were Shobal who was Kiriath-Jearim's father,
Bethlehem's father Salma, Beth-Gader's father Hareph.
Kiriath-Jearim's father Shobal's sons were Haroeh, and half of the Manahethites.
Kiriath-Jearim's descendants were the Ithrites, Puhites, Shumathites, and the Mishraites who spawned the Zareathites and the Eshtaulites.
Salma's sons were Bethlehem and the Netophathites, Ataroth from the house of Joab, half the Manahethites, and the Zorites,
And the families of the scribes who lived in Jabez including the Tirathites, Shimeathites, and Suchathites. These are the Kenites who were descended from Hamath, the father of the house of Rechab.

These were the names of David's sons who were born in Hebron. His firstborn son was Amnon, whose mother was Ahinoam the Jezreelite. His second born son was Daniel, whose mother was Abigail the Carmelite.
His third born son was Absalom the son, whose mother was Maachah and her father was King Talmai of Geshur. His fourth born son was Adonijah, whose mother was Haggith.
His fifth born son was Shephatiah, whose mother was Abital. His sixth born son was Ithream, whose mother was his wife Eglah.
He had six sons born in Hebron, and he reigned there for seven years and six months, and then for thirty-three years in Jerusalem.
The names of David's four children born in Jerusalem were Shimea, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon, whose mother was Ammiel's daughter Bathsheba.
There was also nine more starting with Ibhar, Elishama, Eliphelet,
Nogah, Nepheg, and Japhia,
Elishama, Eliada, and Eliphelet.
These were the names of all of David's sons, beside the sons of his concubines who were Tamar's sister.
Solomon's sons were Rehoboam, Abia, Asa, Jehoshaphat,
Joram , Ahaziah, Joash,
Amaziah, Azariah, Jotham,
Ahaz, Hezekiah, Manasseh,
Amon, and Josiah.
Josiah's sons were Johanan who was his firstborn, Jehoiakim who was his second born, Zedekiah was his third born, and Shallum was his fourth born son.
Jehoiakim's sons were Jeconiah and Zedekiah.
Jeconiah sons were Assir and Salathiel,
Malchiram, Pedaiah, Shenazar, Jecamiah, Hoshama, and Nedabiah.
Pedaiah's sons were Zerubbabel and Shimei. Zerubbabel's children were Meshullam and Hananiah, and their sister was Shelomith.
And five others were Hashubah, Ohel, Berechiah, Hasadiah, and Jushab-Hesed.
Hananiah's sons were Pelatiah, Jesaiah, Rephaiah's sons, Arnan's sons, Obadiah's sons, and Shechaniah's sons.
Shecaniah had six descendants including Shemaiah and his sons Hattush, Igeal, Bariah, Neariah, and Shaphat.
Neariah's three sons were Elioenai, Hezekiah, and Azrikam.
Elioenai's seven sons were Hodaiah, Eliashib, Pelaiah, Akkub, Johanan, Dalaiah, and Anani.
Judah's sons were named Pharez, Hezron, Carmi, Hur, and Shobal.
Shobal fathered Reaiah. Reaiah fathered Jahath. Jahath fathered Ahumai and Lahad. They were the families of the Zorathites.
Etam's sons were named Jezreel, Ishma, and Idbash and their sister's name was Hazelelponi.
Penuel fathered Gedor. Ezer fathered Hushah. Hur's firstborn son was named Ephratah and his second born was named Bethlehem.
Tekoa's father Ashur had two wives Helah and Naarah.
Naarah gave birth to his sons Ahuzam, Hepher, Temeni, and Ha-Ahashtari. They were all Naarah's sons.
Helah's sons were named Zereth, Jezoar, and Ethnan.
Coz fathered Anub and Zobebah. He was the forefather of Harum's son Aharhel's descendants.
Jabez was more honorable than his brothers. His mother named him Jabez because she said, "Jabez means pain, and I endured much pain and sorrow when I gave birth to him."

Jabez prayed to the God of Israel and said, "Please bless me and enlarge my borders, and let your mighty hand be with me. Remain with me and protect me from evil, so that I do not suffer and grieve!" And God granted his request.
Shuah's brother Chelub fathered Mehir. Mehir was Eshton's father.
Eshton fathered Beth-Rapha, Paseah, and Irnahash's father Tehinnah. They were the men of Rechah.
Kenaz's sons were named Othniel and Seraiah. Othniel's sons were named Hathath and Meonothai.
Meonothai fathered Ophrah. Seraiah fathered Joab who was the father of the inhabitants living in the Valley of Charashim, which was also called the Valley of Craftsmen.
Jephunneh's son Caleb's sons were named Iru, Elah, and Naam. Elah's son was named Kenaz.
Jehaleleel's sons were named Ziph, Ziphah, Tiria, and Asareel.
Ezra's sons were named Jether, Mered, Epher, and Jalon. Mered's wife Bithiah gave birth to Miriam, Shammai, and Ishbah who was Eshtemoa's father.
Mered's wife Jehudijah gave birth to Gedor's father Jered, Socho's father Heber, and Zanoah's father Jekuthiel. These are Mered and his wife Pharaoh's daughter Bithiah's sons.
The sons of Hodiah's wife, who was the sister of Naham, were the fathers of Keilah the Garmite and of Eshtemoa the Maachathite.
Shimon's sons were named Amnon, Rinnah, Ben-Hanan, and Tilon. Ishi's sons were named Zoheth and Ben-Zoheth.
The sons of Judah's son Shelah were named Er who was the father of Lecah and Laadah who was the father of Mareshah, and the families of those who worked fine linen from the house of Beth-Ashbea.
And Jokim and the men of Chozeba, Joash, Saraph who ruled in Moab, and Jashubi-Lehem. These names are from the ancient records.
These were the names of the potters and those that lived among plants and hedges, and they lived in there in service of the king.
Simeon's sons were named Nemuel, Jamin, Jarib, Zerah, Shaul,
Shallum, Mibsam, and Mishma.
Mishma's sons were named Hamuel, Zacchur, and Shimei.
Shimei had sixteen sons and six daughters, but his brothers did not have many children and their families did not multiply like Judah's descendants.
They lived in Beersheba, Moladah, Hazar-Shual,
Bilhah, Ezem, Tolad,
Bethuel, Hormah, Ziklag,
Beth-Marcaboth, Hazar-Susim, Beth-Birei, and Shaaraim. These were their cities until the reign of David.
Their five cities and villages were named Etam, Ain, Rimmon, Tochen, and Ashan.
Plus all the villages around their cities all the way to Baal. This is where their homes were, and their genealogical history.
And Meshobab, Jamlech, and Joshah who was Amaziah's son,
And Joel, Josibiah's son Jehu. Josibiah was Seraiah's son and Asiel's grandson.
And Elioenai, Jaakobah, Jeshohaiah, Asaiah, Adiel, Jesimiel, Benaiah,
And Shiphi's son Ziza who was Allon's grandson. Allon was Jedaiah's son, Jedaiah was Shimri's son, and Shimri was Shemaiah's son.
Those mentioned here by name were their families leaders, and their fathers' descendants increased greatly.
They went outside the city of Gedor, toward the east side of the valley to find pastureland for their sheep flocks.
They found rich fat pastures and good land that was wide, quiet, and peaceful because Ham's descendants had lived there from ancient times.

Those written here by name came during the days of King Hezekiah of Judah, and they attacked and defeated the people there. They completely destroyed their tents and homes that were found there, and lived in their land because there was good pastures there for their flocks.
Five Hundred of Simeon's descendants led by Ishi's sons' Pelatiah, Neariah, Rephaiah, and Uzziel, went to Mount Seir.
They defeated the rest of the Amalekites that had escaped, and they live there to this very day.

Israel's firstborn son was named Reuben. Reuben's birthright as firstborn son was given to Joseph's sons, and Reuben's birthright status as firstborn son was not counted as his inheritance because he had defiled his father's bed. Joseph was Israel's eleventh son.
Even though Judah prevailed over his brothers and the chief ruler came from him, the birthright belonged to Joseph.
Reuben's sons were named Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
Joel's sons were named Shemaiah, Gog, Shimei,
Micah, Reaia, Baal,
And his son Beerah, who King Tilgath-Pilneser of Assyria captured and carried away, was a Reubenite leader.
His brothers' genealogical record which was recorded by their families were chief Jeiel, Zechariah, and
Bela was Azaz's son, Azaz was Shema's son, and Shema was Joel's son who lived in Aroer as far away as Nebo and Baal-Meon.
Bela expanded as far east as the edge of the wilderness all the way to the Euphrates River, because their cattle had multiplied in the land of Mount Gilead.
In Saul's day, they made war with and defeated the Hagarites, and they lived in their tents throughout the eastern lands of Mount Gilead.
Gad's descendants lived in the land of Bashan next to Reuben's tribe all the way to Salcah.
Joel was the chief, Shapham was next, then Jaanai and Shaphat who lived in Bashan.
Their seven brothers from the house of their fathers were Michael, Meshullam, Sheba, Jorai, Jachan, Zia, and Heber.
These were the descendants of Abihail who was Huri's son, who was Jaroah's son, who was Gilead's son, who was Michael's son, who was Jeshishai's son, who was Jahdo's son, who was Buz's son,
Ahi who was Abdiel's son, who was Guni's son and the chief of their fathers' house.
They lived in Gilead in Bashan and the surrounding towns of Sharon, and all the fields and pastures along their borders.
They were all counted by their genealogies in the days of King Jotham of Judah and King Jeroboam of Israel.

There were 44,760 skilled warriors and courageous men from Reuben's sons, the Gadites, and half the tribe of Manasseh who were trained for battle that were strong enough to carry a shield and a sword and shoot a bow.
They went to war with the Hagarites, Jetur, Nephish, and Nodab.

Then because they cried to God in battle he helped them, and the Hagarites were delivered into their hands, along with everyone else that was with them. And God was pleased with them because they trusted him.
They seized the Hagarites cattle and carried away 50,000 camels, 250,000 sheep, 2,000 donkeys, and 100,000 men.
Many more were killed because the war was of God, and they lived in there until the time of the captivity.
The people from half the tribe of Manasseh lived in the land, and they had spread from Bashan to Baal-Hermon and Senir, and all the way to Mount Hermon.
The heads of their fathers' house were Epher, Ishi, Eliel, Azriel, Jeremiah, Hodaviah, and Jahdiel. They were the famous mighty men of valor and the leaders of their families.
But they transgressed against the God of their fathers, and they went whoring after the gods of the people of the land, whom God had destroyed before them.

So the God of Israel stirred up the spirit of King Pul of Assyria also known as King Tilgath-Pilneser of Assyria, and he carried the Reubenites, Gadites, and the half tribe of Manasseh into exile and brought them to Halah, Habor, Hara, and to the Gozan River where they remain to this very day.
Levi's sons names were Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
Kohath's sons names were Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
Amram's children's names were Aaron, Moses, and Miriam. Aaron's sons names were Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
Eleazar fathered Phinehas, and Phinehas fathered Abishua.
Abishua fathered Bukki, and Bukki fathered Uzzi.
Uzzi fathered Zerahiah, and Zerahiah fathered Meraioth.
Meraioth fathered Amariah, and Amariah fathered Ahitub.
Ahitub fathered Zadok, and Zadok fathered Ahimaaz.
Ahimaaz fathered Azariah, and Azariah fathered Johanan.
Johanan fathered Azariah, who served the priest's office in the temple that Solomon built in Jerusalem.
Azariah fathered Amariah, and Amariah fathered Ahitub.
Ahitub fathered Zadok, and Zadok fathered Shallum.
Shallum fathered Hilkiah, and Hilkiah fathered Azariah.
Azariah fathered Seraiah, and Seraiah fathered Jehozadak.
Jehozadak went into captivity when the Lord sent Judah and Jerusalem into exile by the hand of Nebuchadnezzar.
Levi's sons were named Gershom, Kohath, and Merari.
Gershom's sons were named Libni and Shimei.
Kohath's sons were named Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
Merari sons were named Mahli and Mushi.
These are the names of the Levite families listed by their fathers. Gershom's sons were named Libni, Jahath, Zimmah,
Joah, Iddo, Zerah, and Jeaterai.
Kohath's sons were named Amminadab, Korah, Assir,
Elkanah, Ebiasaph, Assir,
Tahath, Uriel, Uzziah, and Shaul.
Elkanah's sons were named Amasai, Ahimoth,
Zophai, Nahath,
Eliab, and Jeroham.
Samuel's firstborn son's name was Vashni, and his second born was Abiah.
Merari's sons were named Mahli, Libni, Shimei, Uzza,
Shimea, Haggiah, and Asaiah.
These were the musicians David appointed to direct the music in the service of the Lord's temple, after that the ark had been setup.

They ministered before the home place of the congregation's tabernacle with singing, until Solomon built the Lord's house in Jerusalem. They served their office and they followed the orders they were given.
hese are the men that served the tabernacle along with their children. From the sons of the Kohathites there was a singer named Heman, and then there was Joel's son, Shemuel's son,
Elkanah's son, Jeroham's son, Eliel's son, Toah's son,
Zuph's son, Elkanah's son, Mahath's son, Amasai's son,
Elkanah's son, Joel's son, Azariah's son, Zephaniah's son,
Tahath's son, Assir's son, Ebiasaph's son, Korah's son,
Izhar's son, Kohath's son, Levi's son, and Israel's son,
And Heman's brother Asaph, who served as his right hand man. Asaph was Berachiah's son, and Berachiah was Shimea's son.
Then there was Michael's son, Baaseiah's son, Malchiah's son,
Ethni's son, Zerah's son, Adaiah's son,
Ethan's son, Zimmah's son, Shimei's son,
Jahath's son, Gershom's son, and Levi's son.
And their brothers who were Merari's sons that stood at Heman's left hand were Kishi's son Ethan , Abdi's son, Malluch's son,
Hashabiah's son, Amaziah's son, Hilkiah's son,
Amzi's son, Bani's son, Shamer's son,
Mahli's son, Mushi's son, Merari's son, and Levi's son,
And Their brothers who were also Levites were appointed to all types of service for the Lord God's tabernacle.

But Aaron and his sons made their offerings on the burnt offering altar and the incense altars. They were appointed to do all the work of the Most Holy Place, to make an atonement for Israel's sins, and to perform all the duties that God had commanded them through his servant Moses.
Aaron's sons names were Eleazar, Phinehas, Abishua,
Bukki, Uzzi, Zerahiah,
Meraioth, Amariah, Ahitub,
Zadok, and Ahimaaz.
Now these are the lands and castles from throughout Israel's borders that were assigned to Aaron's sons, beginning with the Kohathite families, because theirs was the first lot cast.
They were given Hebron in the land of Judah, including the suburbs surrounding it.
But the fields and villages around the city were given to Jephunneh's son Caleb.
They gave Aaron's sons the cities of Judah. Which were Hebron the city of refuge, Libnah along with her fields and pastures, then Jattir and Eshtemoa along with their fields and pastures.
Then Hilen with her fields and pastures and Debir with her fields and pastures.
And Ashan with her fields and pastures, then Beth-Shemesh with her fields and pastures.
They were also given thirteen cities from Benjamin's tribe including Geba, Alemeth, and Anathoth, all of which included all of their surrounding fields and pastures.
The rest of the sons of Kohath were given ten cities chosen by lot from the half tribe of Manasseh.
Gershom's sons and their families were given thirteen cities from the tribe of Issachar, the tribe of Asher, the tribe of Naphtali, and the tribe of Manasseh in Bashan.
Merari's sons and their families were given twelve cities chosen by lot from the tribe of Reuben, the tribe of Gad, and the tribe of Zebulun.
The Israelis descendants gave these cities along with their fields and pastures to the Levites.
These above named cities were chosen and assigned by lot from the tribes of Judah, Simeon, and Benjamin.
The rest of the families from the sons of Kohath were given cities from within the borders of Ephraim's tribe.
They gave them the refuge cities of Shechem on Mount Ephraim along with its fields and pastures, and they also gave them Gezer with its fields and pastures.
Plus Jokmeam with her fields and pastures, Beth-Horon with her fields and pastures,
Aijalon with her fields and pastures, and Gath-Rimmon with her fields and pastures.
The rest of Kohath's sons were given Aner and Bileam, along with their fields and pastures from the half tribe of Manasseh.
Gershom's sons were given Golan in Bashan and Ashtaroth, along with their fields and pastures from the family of the half tribe of Manasseh.
Issachar's tribe also gave them Kedesh and Daberath, along with their fields and pastures.
And Ramoth and Anem, along with their fields and pastures.
Asher's tribe also gave them Mashal and Abdon, along with their fields and pastures.
Plus Hukok and Rehob, along with their fields and pastures.
And Kedesh in Galilee, Hammon, and Kirjathaim along with their fields and pastures from Naphtali's tribe.
The rest of Merari's children were given Rimmon and Tabor, along with their fields and pastures from Zebulun's tribe.
On the other side of the Jordan River near Jericho, they were given Bezer in the wilderness and Jahzah, along with their fields and pastures from Reuben's tribe.
They were also given Kedemoth and Mephaath, along with their fields and pastures.
And they were given Ramoth in Gilead and Mahanaim, along with their fields and pastures from Gad's tribe.
Plus Heshbon and Jazer, along with their fields and pastures.
Issachar's four sons were named Tola, Puah, Jashub, and Shimrom.

Tola's sons were named Uzzi, Rephaiah, Jeriel, Jahmai, Jibsam, and Shemuel, were the heads of their father's house. Tola's genealogy recorded 22,600 courageous mighty men of valor and their descendants during King David's day.
Uzzi's son was named Izrahiah. Izrahiah's four sons were named Michael, Obadiah, Joel, and Ishiah. And all five of them were leaders.
In addition to them, from the house among their fathers descendants were 36,000 warriors prepared for battle, because they had many wives and children.
Their brothers from among all of Issachar's family were 87,000 courageous mighty men of valor, counted by their genealogies.
Benjamin's three sons were named Bela, Becher, and Jediael.
Bela's five sons were named Ezbon, Uzzi, Uzziel, Jerimoth, and Iri and they were the heads of the their fathers' house. And there were 22,034 mighty men of valor counted by their genealogies.
Becher's sons were named Zemira, Joash, Eliezer, Elioenai, Omri, Jerimoth, Abiah, Anathoth, and Alameth. These are the names of all of Becher's sons.
There were 22,200 mighty men of valor from the heads of the house of their fathers house counted among the genealogy of their descendants.
Jediael's son was named Bilhan. Bilhan's sons were named Jeush, Benjamin, Ehud, Chenaanah, Zethan, Tarshish, and Ahishahar.
There were 17,200 soldiers from Jediael's sons who were the heads of their fathers' house. They were mighty men of valor prepared to do battle and go to war.
Ir's children were named Shuppim and Huppim. And Hushim's son was named Aher.
Naphtali's sons were named Jahziel, Guni, Jezer, and Shallum, and they were descendants of Bilhah.
Manasseh's sons that his Aramean concubine gave birth to were named Ashriel and Machir. Machir was Gilead's father.
Machir married Maachah who was Huppim and Shuppim's sister, and his second wife came from Zelophehad's descendants. Zelophehad only had daughters and no sons.
Machir's wife Maachah gave birth to a son and she named him Peresh. His brother's name was Sheresh, and his sons were named Ulam and Rakem.
Ulam's son was named Bedan. All of the men listed above were Gilead's descendants, who was Machir's son and Manasseh's grandson.
Machir's sister was named Hammoleketh, and she gave birth to Ishod, Abiezer, and Mahalah.
Shemidah's sons were named Ahian, Shechem, Likhi, and Aniam.
Ephraim's sons names were named Shuthelah, Bered, Tahath, Eladah, Tahath,
Zabad, Shuthelah, Ezer, and Elead. Ezer and Elead were killed by the men of Gath when they came down to steal their cattle.
Their father Ephraim mourned for many days, and his brothers came to comfort him.
When he went in to be with his wife she conceived and gave birth to a son, and he named him Beriah, because of the evil that had fallen upon his house.
His daughter's name was Sherah, who built upper and lower Beth-Horon and Uzzen-Sherah.
Ephraim also had sons named Rephah, Resheph, Telah, Tahan,
Laadan, Ammihud, Elishama,
Non, and Jehoshuah.

Their possessions and homes were located in Bethel and its surrounding towns, from east of Naaran and westward toward Gezer and its towns, and also Shechem and its towns all the way to Gaza and its towns.
Near the borders of Manasseh's descendants including Beth-Shean, Taanach, Megiddo, and Dor and all their towns, where Israel's son and all of his descendants lived.
Asher's sons were named Imnah, Isuah, Ishuai, Beriah, and their sister was named Serah.
Beriah's sons were named Heber and Malchiel, and Malchiel was Birzavith's father.
Heber fathered Japhlet, Shomer, Hotham, and Shua.
Japhlet's sons were named Pasach, Bimhal, and Ashvath. These are the names of Japhlet's children.
Shamer's sons were named Ahi, Rohgah, Jehubbah, and Aram.
Shamer's brother Helem's sons were named Zophah, Imna, Shelesh, and Amal.
Zophah's sons were named Suah, Harnepher, Shual, Beri, Imrah,
Bezer, Hod, Shamma, Shilshah, Ithran, and Beera.
Jether's sons were named Jephunneh, Pispah, and Ara.
Ulla's sons were named Arah, Haniel, and Rezia.

All of the above listed men were Asher's descendants who were the heads of their father's house. They were brave mighty men of valor and the leaders of their tribes. There were 26,000 soldiers trained and prepared for war that were recorded in their families genealogical records.
Benjamin's firstborn son was named Bela, Ashbel was his second, Aharah was his third,
Nohah was his fourth, and Rapha was his fifth.
Bela's sons were named Addar, Gera, Abihud,
Abishua, Naaman, Ahoah,
Gera, Shephuphan, and Huram.
These are the names of Ehud's descendants who were the heads of their families living in Geba, then exiled to Manahath.
Naaman, Ahiah, and Gera who exiled them and fathered Uzza and Ahihud.
Shaharaim fathered children in Moab, after he divorced his wives Hushim and Baara.
The names of the children he fathered with his wife Hodesh were Jobab, Zibia, Mesha, Malcham,
Jeuz, Shachia, and Mirma. These were his sons that were the heads of their families.
With his wife Hushim he fathered Abitub and Elpaal.
Elpaal's sons were named Eber, Misham, and Shamed who built Ono and Lod along with the towns surrounding it.
Plus Beriah and Shema, who were heads of the families of Aijalon, who also drove Gath's inhabitants away.
Then there was Ahio, Shashak, Jeremoth,
Zebadiah, Arad, Ader,
Michael, Ispah, and Joha were Beriah's sons.
Then there was Zebadiah, Meshullam, Hezeki, Heber,
Ishmerai, Jezliah, and Jobab who were Elpaal's sons.
Then there was Jakim, Zichri, Zabdi,
Elienai, Zilthai, Eliel,
Adaiah, Beraiah, and Shimrath who were Shimhi's sons.
Then there was Ishpan, Heber, Eliel,
Abdon, Zichri, Hanan,
Hananiah, Elam, Antothijah,
Iphedeiah, and Penuel who were Shashak's sons.
And Shamsherai, and Shehariah, and Athaliah.
And Jaresiah, and Eliah, and Zichri, the sons of Jeroham.
These were heads of the families, who were the chief men by their genealogies that lived in Jerusalem.
Gibeon's father was married to Maachah and lived in Gibeon.
His firstborn son was named Abdon, Zur, Kish, Baal, Nadab,
Gedor, Ahio, Zacher,
And Mikloth who fathered Shimeah. And they all lived near their brothers in Jerusalem.
Ner fathered Kish and Kish fathered Saul. Saul fathered Jonathan, Malchishua, Abinadab, and Esh-Baal.
And the son of Jonathan was Meribbaal, and Meribbaal fathered Micah.
Micah's sons were named Pithon, Melech, Tarea, and Ahaz.
Ahaz fathered Jehoadah. Jehoadah fathered Alemeth, Azmaveth, and Zimri. And Zimri fathered Moza.
Moza fathered Binea. Binea's sons were named Rapha, Eleasah, and Azel.
Azel had six sons who were named Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, and Sheariah, and Obadiah, and Hanan.
Azel's brother Eshek sons were named Ulam who was his firstborn, Jehush was his second born son, and Eliphelet who was his third born son.
Ulam's sons were archers and mighty men of valor, and he had 150 sons and descendants. And these were all of the descendants of Benjamin.
So all the genealogies of Israel were counted and written in the Book of the Kings of Israel. But Judah was carried away in captivity to Babylon for their transgression.
The first inhabitants who returned from Babylon to live in their cities in the land of their inheritance, were Israel's Levite priests and their tabernacle servants.
Some of the descendants of Judah, Benjamin, Ephraim, and Manasseh who lived in Jerusalem were,
Uthai was Ammihud's son, Ammihud was Omri's son, and Omri was Imri's son. Imri was Bani's son, and Bani was a descendant of Judah's son Pharez.
And from the Shilonites came the firstborn son Asaiah and his sons.
Zerah had a son named Jeuel and 690 other descendants.
From Benjamin's sons came Sallu who was Meshullam's son, Hodaviah was Sallu's son, and Hodaviah was Hasenuah's son.
And Jeroham's son Ibneiah, Elah was Uzzi's son, Uzzi was Michri's son. Meshullam was Shephatiah's son, Shephatiah was Reuel's son, and Reuel was Ibnijah's son.
There were 956 descendants from their generations, and all of these men were the chief leaders of their father's tribes.
From the priests were Jedaiah, Jehoiarib, Jachin,
Azariah was Hilkiah's son, Hilkiah was Meshullam's son, Meshullam was Zadok's son, Zadok was Meraioth's son, Meraioth was Ahitub's son, and Ahitub was the ruler of God's tabernacle.

Adaiah was Jeroham's son, Jeroham was Pashur's son, and Pashur was Malchijah's son. Maasiai was Adiel's son, Adiel was Jahzerah's son, Jahzerah was Meshullam's son, Meshullam was Meshillemith's son, and Meshillemith was Immer's son.
Altogether there were 1,760 priests who returned to Judah. They were the leaders of their tribes, and they were responsible for performing the services of God's tabernacle.
From the Levite's descendants were Hasshub's son Shemaiah. Hasshub was Azrikam's son, Azrikam was Hashabiah's son, Hashabiah was Merari's son,
Bakbakkar, Heresh, Galal, and Micah's son Mattaniah. Micah was Zichri's son, Zichri was Asaph's son,
Shemaiah was Obadiah's son, Shemaiah was Galal's son, Galal was Jeduthun's son. Berechiah was Asa's son, and Asa was Elkanah's son who lived in the Netophathite villages.
And the gatekeepers were Shallum who was the chief and also Akkub, Talmon, Ahiman, and their brothers,
Who until now stood guard at the eastern king's gate, they were gatekeepers from the descendants of Levi.

Shallum was Kore's son, Kore was Ebiasaph's son, and Ebiasaph was Korah's son. Shallum and his brothers from the Korahite house of his father served the Lord's armies as guardians of the tabernacle gates just like their fathers had done.
The Lord was with Eleazar's son Phinehas who had ruled over them in the past.
Meshelemiah's son Zechariah was the Congregation Tabernacle's gatekeeper.
There were 212 of them chosen and ordained by David and the prophet Samuel to be the Congregation Tabernacle's gatekeepers. They were counted and recorded by their genealogy in their villages.
So they and their descendants oversaw the gates of the Lord's tabernacle by their divisions.
The gatekeepers were divided into four quarters to guard the gates to the east, west, north, and south sides.
Their brothers would come from their villages to serve with them for seven days from time to time.
But the four chief Levite gatekeepers were responsible for the security of the chambers and treasuries of the house of God.
They were stationed all around the house of God, because they were in charge of protecting and opening it every morning.
Some of them were in charge of bringing the ministering vessels in and out.
Some of them were also appointed to oversee the bowls and all of the sanctuary instruments, fine flour, wine, oil, frankincense, and spices.
Some of the priests' sons made the ointment of spices.
Mattithiah the Levite who was Shallum the Korahite's firstborn son, was responsible for the office in charge of baking the sacrificial bread.
Some of their other brothers who were Kohath's descendants, were over the priests who prepared the bread offering for every Sabbath.
Some of the chief fathers of the Levites were musicians who stayed in the chambers for free, because they were employed to work as musicians both day and night.
These were the descendants of the Levite chief fathers who lived in Jerusalem.
Gibeon's father Jehiel lived in Gibeon. His wife's name was Maachah,
And his firstborn son was named Abdon, then Zur, Kish, Baal, Ner, Nadab,
Gedor, Ahio, Zechariah, and Mikloth.
Mikloth fathered Shimeam, and they lived near their brothers in Jerusalem.
Ner fathered Kish and Kish fathered Saul. Saul fathered Jonathan, Malchishua, Abinadab, and Esh-Baal.
Jonathan's son was named Meribbaal, and Meribbaal fathered Micah.
Micah's sons names were Pithon, Melech, Tahrea, and Ahaz.
Ahaz fathered Jarah. Jarah fathered Alemeth, Azmaveth, and Zimri. And Zimri fathered Moza.
Moza fathered Binea. Rephaiah was Binea's son, Eleasah was Rephaiah's son, and Eleasah's son was Azel.
Azel had six sons whose names were Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan.
The Philistines attacked Israel, and the Israelis fled and were killed on Mount Gilboa.
The Philistines chased Saul and his sons, and they killed his sons Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchishua.
The pitched battle went against Saul, and the Philistine archers hit and wounded him with their arrows.

Then said Saul to his armor-bearer, "Draw your sword and thrust me through with it, or else these uncircumcised will come and abuse me!" But his armor-bearer would not do it because he was extremely frightened. So Saul took a sword, and fell on it.
When his armor-bearer saw that Saul was dead, he also fell on a sword and died.
So Saul, his three sons, and his entire household all died together.
When all the Israelis men in the valley saw that Saul and his sons were dead and the army had fled, they also abandoned their cities and fled. Then the Philistines moved in and lived in their homes.
The next day, when the Philistines came to strip the dead, they discovered that Saul and his sons had fallen on Mount Gilboa.
After they stripped Saul, they sent his head and his armor throughout the Philistine lands, to carry the news of his death to the people in their idol's temples.
They put his armor in the house of their gods, and nailed his head to the temple of Dagon.
When all of Jabesh-Gilead heard what the Philistines had done to Saul.
All the courageous men got up and went to retrieve the bodies of Saul and his sons. They brought them to Jabesh, and buried their bones under the oak in Jabesh. Then they fasted for seven days.
So Saul died for his transgressions against the Lord, for not keeping the Lord's word, and also for consulting with a familiar spirit and asking it for advice.
And for not asking the Lord for his word, the Lord killed him and turned the kingdom over to David's son Jesse.
Then all the Israelis went to see David in Hebron and said, "Behold we are your flesh and your blood.

Besides that, even in the past when King Saul ruled, you were the one that led Israel into battle and brought them back. And your Lord God said to you, 'Feed my people of Israel, and you will be the ruler of Israel.'"

So all the Israelis elders went to the king of Hebron, where David made a covenant with them before the Lord. Then they anointed David as king of Israel, just as the Lord had said when his word was given to them through Samuel.
David and all the Israelis went to Jerusalem which is also called Jebus, where the Jebusites inhabited the land.
And the inhabitants of Jebus confronted David and said, "You must not come here!" Nevertheless David captured the castle of Zion, which is the city of David.
And David said, "Whoever defeats the Jebusites first will be the chief commander." So Zeruiah's son Joab was first to defeat the Jebusites and became chief commander.
David moved into the castle, so they called it the city of David.
David built up the city including city fortifications all around it, and Joab rebuilt the rest of the city.
David grew greater and greater, because the Lord of Hosts was with him.
These were David's chiefs of the mighty men who made him king, and strengthened themselves along with his kingdom, and all of Israel, according to the Lord's word concerning Israel.
This is an accounting of David's mighty men. First there was Jashobeam the Hachmonite who was the chief commander, he raised his spear and attacked and killed three hundred men, all at one time.
After him was Dodo's son Eleazar the Ahohite, who was one of the three mighty men.
He was with David at Pasdammim where the Philistines gathered for battle, where the people fled from the Philistines in a field full of barley.
Eleazar and David stationed themselves in the middle of the field and defended it. They killed the Philistines, and the Lord saved them through a great victory.
Three of the thirty commanders went down to the rock to David, into the cave of Adullam, and the Philistine armies were camped in the Valley of Rephaim.
David was barricaded in his stronghold, and the Philistine garrison was stationed at Bethlehem.
David longed for water and he said, "If only someone would bring me a drink of water from the well at the gate of Bethlehem!"

So the three mighty men broke through the Philistines, and drew water from the Bethlehem well near the gate, and brought it to David. But David would not drink it, but instead he poured it out to the Lord.

And David said, "My God far be it for me to do this thing! How can I drink the blood of these men who have put their lives in jeopardy for me?" Because they had risked their lives to bring the water, David would not drink it. These were the kind of things that the three mighty men did.
Joab's brother Abishai was the three mighty men's chief, because he lifted up his spear against the three hundred and killed them, and he made a name for himself among the three.
Abishai was more honorable than the other two because he was their commander, however he was not one of the first three.
Jehoiada's son Benaiah was a courageous man from Kabzeel, who had done many great things. He killed two men from Moab who were as strong as lions, and he also killed a lion in a pit on a snowy day.

Benaiah killed a five cubit tall Egyptian man of great stature. The Egyptian had a spear in his hand that was as wide as weaver's beam. Benaiah confronted him with only a staff, and he took the spear out of the Egyptian's hand, and killed him with his own spear.
These are some of the things that Jehoiada's son Benaiah did that made a name for him among the three mighty men.
Benaiah was the most honorable from among the thirty commanders, and even though he was not one the first three, David put him in charge of his guards.
Some of the other courageous men of his armies were Joab's brother Asahel, Dodo's son Elhanan of Bethlehem,
Shammoth the Harorite, Helez the Pelonite,
Ikkesh the Tekoite's son Ira, Abiezer the Antothite,
Sibbecai the Hushathite, Ilai the Ahohite,
Maharai the Netophathite, Baanah the Netophathite's son Heled,
Ribai of Gibeah's son Ithai from the Benjamites, Benaiah the Pirathonite,
Hurai from the Brooks of Gaash, Abiel the Arbathite,
Azmaveth the Baharumite, Eliahba the Sha-Albonite,
Hashem the Gizonite's sons, Shage the Hararite's son Jonathan,
Sacar the Hararite's son Ahiam, Ur's son Eliphal,
Hepher the Mecherathite, Ahijah the Pelonite,
Hezro the Carmelite, Ezbai's son Naarai,
Nathan's brother Joel, Haggeri's son Mibhar,
Zelek the Ammonite, Naharai the Berothite, Zeruiah's son Joab the armor-bearer,
Ira the Ithrite, Gareb the Ithrite,
Uriah the Hittite, Ahlai's son Zabad,
Shiza the Reubenite's son Adina who was a Reubenite commander, and thirty men with him,
Maachah's son Hanan, and Joshaphat the Mithnite,
Uzzia the Ashterathite, Hothan the Aroerite's sons Shama and Jehiel,
Shimri the Tizite's sons Jediael and Joha,
Eliel the Mahavite, Elnaam's sons Jeribai and Joshaviah, Ithmah the Moabite,
Eliel, Obed, and Jasiel the Mesobaite.
These are the names of the mighty men of war that came to help David in Ziklag, while he was still exiled from the kingdom of Kish's son Saul.
They were archers armed with bows, who could use both their right and left hand to sling stones and shoot arrows. Some of them were Saul's brothers from Benjamin.
Their chief was Ahiezer and Joash was next in command, they were both Shemaah the Gibeathite's sons. Then there was Azmaveth's sons Jeziel and Pelet, Berachah, and Jehu the Antothite,
Ismaiah the Gibeonite who was a mighty man and the leader of the thirty, Jeremiah, Jahaziel, Johanan, Josabad the Gederathite,
Eluzai, Jerimoth, Bealiah, Shemariah, and Shephatiah the Haruphite,
The five Korhites Elkanah, Jesiah, Azareel, Joezer, Jashobeam,
Jeroham of Gedor's sons Joelah and Zebadiah.

Some Gadites were with David in his stronghold in the wilderness. They were warriors and mighty men of valor who were prepared for battle. They were strong and they could handle a shield and spear. They had faces like the faces of lions, who were as swift as the deer on the mountains.
The first one was Ezer then Obadiah was the second, and Eliab the third,
Mishmannah the fourth, Jeremiah the fifth,
Attai the sixth, Eliel the seventh,
Johanan the eighth, Elzabad the ninth,
Jeremiah the tenth, Machbanai the eleventh,
These were the Gadite army commanders, one of the least commanded a hundred soldiers, and the greatest commanded over a thousand.
They are the ones that crossed the Jordan river in the first month as its banks were overflowing, and everyone living in the valleys fled both toward the east and the west.
And descendants from both Benjamin and Judah came to David's stronghold.

David went to meet them and he said to them, "If you have come in peace to help me, my heart will be with you, but if you have come to betray me to my enemies, seeing that there is no blood on my hands, the God of our fathers see you and reprimand you."

Then the spirit came upon Amasai who was the chief commander and he said, "We are yours David son of Jesse, and we are on your side. Peace be with you, and peace to your helpers because your God helps you." Then David received them and made them leaders of his army.
