Some of Manasseh's men defected to David, when he went with the Philistines to attack Saul, but David did not help them. The Philistine lords met and they sent David away and said, "He will return to his master Saul, and we will lose our heads."
As David marched to Ziklag, the men of Manasseh defected to him including Adnah, Jozabad, Jediael, Michael, Jozabad, Elihu, and Zilthai who were the commanders of thousands from Manasseh.
They helped David defeat the band of raiders, because they were all mighty men of valor, and they were commanders of the armies.
Because at that time, men came to join David and help him day after day, until he had a great army, like the armies of God.
And these are the numbers of men who were armed and ready for war, and came to David to Hebron, to turn the kingdom of Saul to him, in accordance with the Lord's word.
There were 6,800 descendants of Judah who were armed with shields and spears, who were ready for war.
There were 7,100 mighty men of valor trained for war from Simeon's descendants.
There were 4,600 from Levi's descendants.
Jehoiada was the leader of 3,700 Aaronite soldiers.
Zadok was a young mighty man of valor, and he had twenty-two captains with him from his father's house.
Benjamin had 3,000 descendants of Saul, because until that time the greatest part of them remained loyal to the house of Saul.
Ephraim's tribe had 20,800 mighty men of valor, who were famous throughout the house of their fathers.
The half tribe of Manasseh had 18,000, who were called by name to come and make David king.
Issachar's descendants were men that understood the times, and knew what Israel should to do. There were two hundred leaders among them who led their brothers at their command.
Zebulun had 50,000 warriors trained for battle, who were experts at war, armed with all kinds of weapons, who were very disciplined and devoted to David.
Naphtali had 1,000 captains, and they led 37,000 warriors who were armed with shields and spears.
There were 28,600 Danites who were experts in warfare.
Asher had 40,000 warriors trained for battle, who were experts in warfare.

There were 120,000 warriors on the other side of the Jordan River from the Reubenites, Gadites, and the half tribe of Manasseh. All of them were armed with all kinds of weapons of war and trained for battle.

All these men of war could maintain their discipline, came to Hebron with a perfect heart, to make David the king over all of Israel. The rest of the people of Israel were also united to make David the king of Israel.
They stayed with David for three days eating and drinking, because their brothers had prepared a table for them.

Besides that, their neighbors from as far away as Issachar, Zebulun, and Naphtali brought food on their donkeys, camels, mules, and oxen. They brought an abundance of meat, meal, fig cakes, raisin clusters, wine, oil, oxen, and sheep because Israel was overwhelmed with joy.
David consulted with every one of his commanders of the thousands and hundreds.

Then David spoke to the entire Israelis congregation and said, "If it seem good to you, and if it is from our Lord God, let us send word abroad to our brothers everywhere throughout the land of Israel, and also to the priests and Levites in their cities, fields, and pastures, and offer them the opportunity to join us.
Let us bring our God's Ark of the Covenant back, because we did not ask about it during Saul's reign.
The entire congregation agreed because it was righteous in the eyes of the people.
So David gathered all the Israelis people together, from Shihor of Egypt all the way to the entrance of Hamath, to bring God's Ark of the Covenant home from Kiriath-Jearim.

David went with all of Israel to Baalah of Judah which is also called Kiriath-Jearim to bring back the Lord God's Ark of the Covenant, who lives between the cherubims that is called by the name on it.
They carried God's Ark of the Covenant in a new cart from Abinadab's house. Uzza and Ahio drove the cart.
David and all the Israelis sang and played their musical instruments before God with all their might. So they all played their harps, tambourines, cymbals, and trumpets.
As they passed the threshing room floor of Chidon, Uzza steadied the Ark with his hand because the oxen stumbled.
This caused the Lord's anger to be kindled against Uzza, and God killed him because he put his hand on the ark, and he died right there before God.
David was upset with the Lord because of his violent outburst against Uzza, so he called that place Perez-Uzza, which it is still called to this day.
David was afraid of God that day and said, "How can I bring God's Ark of the Covenant home with me?"
So David did not bring the ark home with him to the city of David, but he carried it away to the Obed-Edom the Gittite's house.
And God's Ark of the Covenant remained in Obed-Edom's house with his family for three months, and the Lord blessed the house of Obed-Edom, and everything that he had.
King Hiram of Tyre sent messengers to David with cedar timbers, masons, and carpenters to build his house.
David realized that the Lord had confirmed him as the king of Israel, because his kingdom was lifted up above all others for the sake of the Lord's Israelis people.
David married more wives in Jerusalem and fathered more sons and daughters.
These are the names of David's children born in Jerusalem, his firstborn was Shammua, then Shobab, Nathan, Solomon,
Ibhar, Elishua, Elpalet,
Nogah, Nepheg, Japhia,
Elishama, Beeliada, and Eliphalet.
When the Philistines heard that David had been anointed king over all of Israel, they went to looking for him, but David heard about it and went out to confront them.
The Philistines came and spread their troops throughout the Valley of Rephaim.
David asked God what to do and he said, "Should I attack the Philistines, and will you deliver them into my hands?" And the Lord said to him, "Go, and I will deliver them into your hands."
David and his men went to Baal-Perazim where they defeated the Philistines. Then David said, "God has broken my enemies by my hand like the breaking waves." So they named that place Baal-Perazim.
Then David ordered his men to burn their gods in a fire, after they were abandoned.
Once again the Philistines spread throughout the valley.
So David asked God what to do and God said to him, "Do not chase after them, but turn and attack them over near the mulberry trees.
When you hear the sound of the troops marching in the tops of the mulberry trees, then you will leave to meet them in battle, because God has gone out before you to defeat the Philistine armies."
Then David did as God commanded him, and they defeated the Philistine armies from Gibeon all the way to Gazer.
And David's fame spread throughout all the lands, and the Lord brought the fear of him on all nations.
David built buildings for himself in the city of David, and prepared a place for God's Ark of the Covenant and pitched a tent for it.
Then David said, "No one should carry God's Ark of the Covenant except the Levites, because the Lord has chosen them to forever minister to him and carry his ark."
David gathered all of Israel together in Jerusalem to bring the Ark of the Covenant to the place which he had prepared for it.
Then David assembled Aaron's descendants and the Levites together.
From Kohath's sons there was chief Uriel and 120 of his brothers.
From Merari's sons there was chief Asaiah and 220 of his brothers.
From Gershom's sons there was chief Joel and 130 of his brothers.
From Elizaphan's sons there was chief Shemaiah and 200 of his brothers.
From Hebron's sons there was chief Eliel and 80 of his brothers.
From Uzziel's sons there was chief Amminadab and 112 of his brothers.
David summoned the priests Zadok and Abiathar and the Levite descendants Uriel, Asaiah, Joel, Shemaiah, Eliel, and Amminadab.

And he spoke to them and said, "You are the chief fathers of the Levites, and you and your brothers must sanctify yourselves, so that you may bring the God of Israel's Ark of the Covenant to the place that I have prepared for it.
It is because we did not seek our Lord God's advice in due order the first time we tried to bring it here, he broke our defenses."
Then the priests and the Levites sanctified themselves so they could bring the God of Israel's Ark of the Covenant back home.
Afterwards, Levi's descendants carried God's Ark of the Covenant on their shoulders with poles, as the Lord had commanded through Moses.
David spoke to the Levite chiefs and appointed their brothers to be the musicians and singers who joyfully sang and played their musical instruments including harps and cymbals.
So the Levites appointed Joel's son Heman and from his brothers was Berechiah's son Asaph, and from the brothers of Merari was Kushaiah's son Ethan.

Also with them were their brothers who were the second degree gatekeepers Zechariah, Ben, Jaaziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattithiah, Elipheleh, Mikneiah, Obed-Edom, and Jeiel.
So the singers Heman, Asaph, and Ethan were appointed to play the brass cymbals.
Zechariah, Aziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Maaseiah, and Benaiah played the harps in the style of Alamoth.
Mattithiah, Elipheleh, Mikneiah, Obed-Edom, Jeiel, and Azaziah excelled at playing harps in the style of Sheminith.
Chenaniah lead the Levites in song, and instructed the singers because he was a very skillful musician.
Berechiah and Elkanah were the ark's custodians.

The priests Shebaniah, Jehoshaphat, Nathaniel, Amasai, Zechariah, Benaiah, and Eliezer blew their trumpets before God's Ark of the Covenant, and Obed-Edom and Jehiah were also appointed as custodians of the ark.
So David and Israel's elders and his commanders of thousands, joyfully went to bring the Lord's Ark of the Covenant from Obed-Edom's house.
Because God helped the Levites who carried the Lord's Ark of the Covenant, they sacrificed seven bulls and seven rams.
David wore a fine linen robe, so did all the Levites who carried the ark, the singers, and Chenaniah the master of music who led the singers. David also wore a fine linen apron.
Israel did all this as they brought the Lord's Ark of the Covenant back. They shouted, maracad their maracas, blew trumpets, struck their cymbals, and made a joyful noise with their harps.
As the Lord's Ark of the Covenant entered the city of David, Saul's daughter Michal was looking out a window at King David dancing and playing, and she despised him in her heart.
So they brought God's Ark of the Covenant and set it in the middle of the tent that David had prepared for it, and they offered sacrificial burnt offerings and peace offerings before God.
After David finished offering his burnt offerings and peace offerings, he blessed the people in the name of the Lord.
David gave every man and woman of Israel a loaf of bread, a good piece of meat, and a jug of wine.
David appointed certain Levites to minister before the Ark of the Covenant, to keep the records, and to thank and praise the Lord God of Israel.
Asaph was in charge then there was Zechariah, Jeiel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Mattithiah, Eliab, Benaiah, Obed-Edom, and Jeiel. They all played music with their harps, but Asaph played the cymbals.
The priests Benaiah and Jahaziel also regularly blew their trumpets before God's Ark of the Covenant.
Then that day David delivered his first psalm to thank the Lord to Asaph and his brothers.
Which went like this, "Give thanks to the Lord, call on his name, make his deeds known among the people.
Sing psalms to him, talk about all his wonderous works.
Glory in his Holy name, let the heart of those that seek the Lord rejoice.
Seek the Lord and his strength, and seek his face regularly.
Remember the marvelous works he has done, his wonders, and the judgments from his mouth.
O you seed of his servant Israel, you children of Jacob, his chosen ones.
He is our Lord God, his judgments are in all the earth.
Always remember his covenant, the word which he has given to a thousand descendants.
Remember the covenant he made with Abraham, and his oath to Isaac.
He has confirmed the law to Jacob, and to Israel as an everlasting covenant.
And he said, 'I will give you the land of Canaan as your inheritance.'
When you were just a few strangers in the land.
When the people wandered from nation to nation, and from one kingdom to another.
He warned no man to do them wrong, and he blamed kings on their behalf.
And he said, 'Do not touch my anointed and do no harm to my prophets!'
Sing to the Lord and all the earth, reveal his salvation from day to day.
Declare his glory among the heathen, proclaim his marvelous works among all nations.
Because the Lord is great, and he is to be greatly praised, he is to be feared above all other gods.
For all the other people's gods are idols, but the Lord made the heavens.
Glory and honor are in his presence, strength and happiness are in his home.
People of all nations people give thanks to the Lord, you relatives of the people give thanks for the Lord's glory and strength.
Give thanks to the Lord for the glory his name is due. Come before him and bring an offering, and worship the Lord's beautiful Holiness.
Everyone on earth should fear him, he made the world stable and it will not be moved.
Let heaven and earth rejoice and be glad, and let the men among the nations say, 'The Lord reigns.'
Let the fullness of the sea roar, and let the fields and everything in them rejoice.
Then the trees in the woods will sing out in the Lord's presence, because he comes to judge the earth.
O give thanks to the Lord, because he is good and his mercy endures forever.
Cry out to him and say, 'Save us O God of our salvation, gather us together and deliver us from the heathen. So that we may give thanks to your Holy name, and we may glory in your praise.'
Blessed be the Lord God of Israel forever and ever!" Then all the people said, "Amen, and praised the Lord!"
So David left Asaph and his brothers there to continuously minister before the Lord's Ark of the Covenant, and to perform the every day work required by the temple.
Along with Obed-Edom and sixty-eight of his brothers. Jeduthun's son Hosah and Obed-Edom were the temple gatekeepers.
David also left priest Zadok and his priestly brothers before the Lord's tabernacle, in the high place in Gibeon.
To regularly offer burnt offerings to the Lord on the altar of the burnt offerings from morning until evening. And to do it as it was written in the Lord's laws, which he had given Israel to keep.
With them were Heman, Jeduthun, and the rest of those chosen expressly by name to give thanks to the Lord because his mercy endures forever.
Heman and Jeduthun had their trumpets, cymbals, and musical instruments with them to make music for God. And Jeduthun's sons were the gatekeepers.
Then all the people left and went back to their homes, and David returned home to bless his house.
One day as David sat in his house he spoke to Nathan the prophet and said, "I live in a house built of cedar trees, but the Lord's Ark of the Covenant remains under a tent."
Then Nathan said to David, "Do whatever is in your heart, because God is with you."
And it happened the same night, that the word of God came to Nathan and said.
Go and tell David my servant, in this says the Lord, you will not build me a house to live in.
Because from the day that I brought Israel out of Egypt to this day, I have not lived in a house, but I have moved from tent to tent, and from one tabernacle to another.
Wherever I have walked with the Israelis, I have never spoken a word to any of the judges of Israel whom I commanded to feed my people and said, 'Why have you not built me a house of cedar?'
That's why you must speak to my servant David and say, 'The Lord of Hosts says, "I took you from the sheep pen, from following the sheep, to be the ruler over my people Israel.
I have been with you wherever you have walked, and I have cut off all your enemies from before you. I have made a name for you like the names of the greatest men on the earth.

I will also provide a place for my people Israel and plant them there so they can live in their own place, and they will no longer have to move. And the children of wickedness will not waste them anymore, as they did at the beginning.
Which they have done since the time that I appointed judges over my people of Israel. Besides that, I will subdue all your enemies. Furthermore I tell you that the Lord will build you a house.
Then when your days have expired and you must go to be with your fathers, I will raise up your descendant after you, which will be of your sons, and I will establish his kingdom.
And he will build me a house, and I will establish his throne forever.
I will be his father and he will be my son, and I will not take my mercy away from him, as I took it from those who came before you.
But I will settle him in my house and kingdom forever, and his throne will be established forever."'"
So Nathan spoke to David about everything the Lord said and all his visions.
King David went and sat before the Lord and said, "Who am I, O Lord God, and what is my house, that you have brought me this far?
And yet O Lord God, as if this was a small thing to you, because you have spoken about far off into the future of your servant's house, and you regard me as a man of high esteem.
What more can David say about the honor you have bestowed on your servant? For you know your servant.
O Lord, for the sake of your servant and according to your own heart, you have done all these great things, and you have revealed your greatness.
O Lord, there are none like you, and there is no other God. We have heard all about this with our own ears.

What other nation on earth is like your people Israel? The one nation whom God went to rescue to be his own people. You made a great and awe inspiring name for yourself by driving out the other nations before your people when you rescued them from Egypt.
Because you made your people of Israel your own people forever, and you became their Lord God.
So now Lord, let the things you have said about your servant and about establishing his house forever be done as you have promised.
When the people say, 'The Lord of Hosts is the God of Israel,' let your name be established and magnified forever, and let your servant David's house be established before you.
Because you O my God, you have told your servant that you will build him a house, that's why your servant has found it in his heart to pray before you.
And now Lord, you are God and you have promised this goodness to your servant.
So let it please you to bless the house of your servant, so that it may be before you forever. Because if you bless it O Lord, it will be blessed forever."
After all this happened, David defeated and subdued the Philistines, then he captured the Philistine city of Gath and her surrounding towns.
Then David defeated the Moabites and they became his servants, and they brought him tribute.
David defeated King Hadarezer of Zobah all the way to Hamath, who had gone out to establish his authority along the Euphrates River.
David took 1,000 chariots, 7,000 horsemen, and 20,000 foot soldiers from him. He also crippled all their chariot horses, except for 100 that he kept for his chariots.
When the Syrians from Damascus came out to help King Hadarezer of Zobah, David killed 22,000 Syrian men.
Then David stationed garrisons in Syria of Damascus. The Syrians became David's servants, and brought tribute to him, and this is how the Lord protected David wherever he went.
David brought the gold shields that Hadarezer's servants carried to Jerusalem.
Likewise, David also brought much of the brass from Hadarezer's cities Tibhath and Chun that Solomon servants made, including the brass sea, brass columns, and brass vessels.
When King Tou of Hamath heard how David defeated all of King Hadarezer of Zobah's armies.

He sent his son Hadoram to King David, to ask about his welfare and to congratulate him for defeating Hadarezer, because Hadarezer had waged war against Tou. Hadoram brought all kinds of gold, silver, and brass items.
King David also dedicated these items to the Lord, along with the silver and gold that he brought from all these nations including the Philistines, Edom, Moab, Ammon, and Amalek.
Besides that, Zeruiah's son Abishai killed 18,000 Edomites in the Valley of Salt.
David stationed garrisons in Edom, and the Edomites became his servants. This is how the Lord protected David wherever he went.
So David reigned over all of Israel, and executed judgment and justice among all of his people.
Zeruiah's son Joab was over the armies, and Ahilud's son Jehoshaphat was the record keeper.
Ahitub's son Zadok and Abiathar's son Abimelech were the priests, and Shavsha was a scribe.
Jehoiada's son Benaiah was over the Cherethites and Pelethites, and David's sons were the chief officials around the king.
After all this, King Nahash the Ammonite died and his son reigned in his place.

And David said, "I will show kindness to Nahash's son Hanun because his father shown kindness to me." Then David sent messengers to comfort him over his father's death. So David's servants went to comfort Hanun the Ammonite in the land of his descendants.
But the Ammonite princes said to Hanun, "Do you think David has sent comforters to you to honor your father? Or, have his servants come to search and spy out the land to overthrow you?
So Hanun had David's servants shaved, then he had their clothes cut off up to their buttocks, and sent them away.

Someone told David how his men had been treated, so he sent messengers to meet them. Hanun had humiliated David's me by the way they were treated so the king said, "Stay in Jericho until your beards have grown back before you return."

When the Ammonites realized that they had become repulsive to David, Hanun and the Ammonites sent a thousand talents of silver to hire chariots and horsemen from Mesopotamia, Syria-Maachah, and Zobah.
So they hired the king of Maachah and 32,000 chariots and his people who came and pitched their tents before Medeba. And the Ammonites brought their armies from their cities to battlefield.
When David heard about it, he sent Joab and all mighty men of valor.
The Ammonites marched out and arrayed themselves for battle before the city gate, and the kings that came with them stayed out in the field.
When Joab saw the battle lines that were set before him and behind him, he selected his best men of Israel, and arrayed them against the Syrians.
He turned control of the rest of his army over to his brother Abishai, and they arrayed themselves against the Ammonites.
Then Joab said, "If the Syrians are too strong for me, you must come and help me, but if the Ammonites are too strong for you, then I will help you.
Be courageous for our people and for the cities of our God, and let the Lord do what he thinks is good in his sight."
So when Joab and the people with him approached the Syrians to join the battle, they fled before him.
When the Ammonites saw that the Syrians fled, they also fled into the city from his brother Abishai, then Joab went to Jerusalem.
When the Syrians realized that they were loosing to Israel, they sent messengers to bring the Syrians that were beyond the river, and Captain Shophach of Hadarezer came and led them.

David was told about this new development, and he gathered all the Israelis troops and crossed the Jordan River, and came and arrayed his men for battle against them. When David marched into battle against the Syrians, they fought him.
But the Syrians fled before Israel and David killed Captain Shophach, 7,000 Syrian chariot drivers, and 40,000 footmen from their armies.
When Hadarezer's servants realized that they had lost the battle to Israel, they made peace with David and became his servants, and the Syrians would never help the Ammonites anymore.

After the end of the year when time came for the kings to march out to the battlefield, Joab led the powerful Israeli army. He laid waste to the Ammonite country and surrounded Rabbah. But David stayed in Jerusalem while Joab defeated and destroyed Rabbah.

David took their king's crown from his head. It weighed one gold talent and it also had precious stones on it. David placed it on his head, and he also brought great and bountiful spoils of war from the city.

David brought the people living there out and put them to work with saws, iron plows, and axes. He dealt with all the Ammonite cities the same way, then David and all the people returned to Jerusalem.
After all this, war broke out in Gezer with the Philistines, and at that time Sibbechai the Hushathite killed Sippai, who was a descendant of the giant, and the Philistines were subdued.
Once again there was war with the Philistines, and Jair's son Elhanan killed Lahmi who was Goliath the Gittite's brother, and his spear was as thick as a weaver's beam.
And there was war in Gath again, where a man of great stature lived who was the son of the giant. He had twenty-four fingers and toes, six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot.
But when he defied Israel, David's brother Shimea's son Jonathan killed him.
These descendants of the giant in Gath, fell by the hand of David and his servants.
Then Satan stood up against Israel, and provoked David to take a census of Israel.
David spoke to Joab and the people's leaders and said, "Go and count all the Israelis from Beersheba to Dan, and report back to me with the numbers."

Joab answered him and said, "My Lord, the Lord makes his people a hundred times more than they are, and all of them are your servants. Why do you want to require this thing, and why do you want to cause Israel to trespass against the Lord?"
But the king decided against Joab, so Joab left and traveled throughout all of Israel, and returned to Jerusalem.
Joab gave the total count of the people to David, and there were 1,100,000 men armed with swords in Israel, and 470,000 men armed with swords in Judah.
But Joab did not count the Levites or Benjamin's tribe because the king's word was an abomination to him.
God was displeased with this thing, so he defeated Israel.
And David said to God, "I have done this thing and sinned greatly, but I beg you to do away with the immorality of your servant, because I have been very foolishly."
And the Lord spoke to Gad, David's prophet and said.
And the Lord said, "Go and tell David this is what the Lord says, 'I offer you three choices, and you can choose one of them for me to do to you.'"
So Gad came to David, and said to him, in this says the Lord, choose thee

Either three years of famine, three months of being destroyed by your enemies while their swords overtake you, or three days the Lord's sword will bring a pestilence in the land, and the Lord's angel will go destroying throughout the borders of Israel.' So now, how should I reply to the one that sent me."
David Gad and said, "I am in great straits, let me fall into the Lord's hands because he is very merciful, but do not let me fall into the hands of men."
So the Lord sent a pestilence on Israel, and 70,000 Israelis men died.

Then God sent an angel to destroy Jerusalem, and as he was destroying it the Lord saw the destruction and he repented from the evil. And he said to the destroying angel, "It is enough, stay your hand!" And the Lord's angel stood by Ornan the Jebusite's threshing room floor.

David looked up and saw the Lord's angel standing between the earth and heaven with his sword stretched out over Jerusalem. Then David and the Israeli elders who were clothed in sackcloth, fell facedown.

And David said to God, "Was it not I who ordered the people to be counted? I am the one that has sinned and done evil, but what have these sheep done? O my Lord God, I pray you will let your hand be against me and my father's house, but do not continue this plague on your people."
Then the Lord's angel commanded Gad to tell David to set up an altar to the Lord on Ornan the Jebusite's threshing room floor.
So David went by what Gad said in the Lord's name.
Ornan was threshing wheat and when he looked back he saw the angel, then he and his four sons that were with him hid themselves.
As David came toward Ornan, Ornan looked up and saw David, then he left the threshing room floor, and bowed facedown to David.
Then David spoke to Ornan and said, "Sell me this threshing room because I must build an altar to the Lord in there to stop the plague against the people, and I will pay you full price."

Ornan replied to David and said, "Take it and do whatever is good in the king's eyes. I will also give you the oxen for burnt offerings, the threshing instruments for wood, and the wheat for the bread offering, I will give it all to you."

King David replied to Ornan and said, "No, I will buy it from you and I will pay you a full and honest price for it, because I will not take anything from you to give to the Lord, or offer burnt offerings without paying for them."
So David gave Ornan 600 gold shekels for the place.
David built an altar to the Lord and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings there. Then he called on the Lord, and the Lord answered him with fire from heaven on the burnt offering altar.
The Lord ordered the angel to sheath his sword and the angel put his sword away.
When David saw that the Lord had answered his prayers on Ornan the Jebusite's threshing room floor, he sacrificed there.
Because the Lord's tabernacle that Moses built in the wilderness and the altar of burnt offering, were in the high place at Gibeon.
But David could not go there to talk to God, because he feared the Lord's angel's sword.
Then David said, "This is the Lord God's temple, and this is the altar for the burnt offerings of Israel."
David ordered the foreigners in the land of Israel to gather together, and from them he appointed masons and stonecutters to do the work building the house of God.
David had an abundance of iron prepared to make the nails and hinges for the gate doors, and so much brass that it could not be weighed.
The Sidonians and the people of Tyre brought so much cedar wood to David, that he also had an abundance of cedar.

And David said, "My son Solomon is young and inexperienced, and the house that will be built for the Lord must be exceedingly magnificent, famous, and glorious throughout all the countries. So I will make preparations for it now." And David made abundant preparations for it before he died.
Then he summoned his son Solomon, and told him to build a house for the Lord God of Israel.
And David said to Solomon, "My son, I thought I would build a house and dedicate it to my Lord God.

But the Lord's word came to me and he said, 'You have shed a lot of blood, and you have made great wars, you will not build a house dedicated to my name, because you have shed too much blood on the earth in my sight.

Behold, a son will be born to you who will be a man of rest, and I will give him rest from all his enemies that surround him because his name will be Solomon. I will give peace and quiet to Israel in the days of his rule.
He will build a house dedicated to my name. He will be my son and I will be his father, and I will establish the throne of his kingdom over Israel forever.'
Now my son, may the Lord be with you and prosper you, and build the house of your Lord God as he has asked of you.
May the Lord give you wisdom and understanding, and give you control of all of Israel, so that you may keep the law of your Lord God.
Then, if you take heed to satisfy the laws and judgments which the Lord gave Moses concerning Israel you will prosper. Be strong and courageous, do not dread nor be discouraged.

Now behold, I have taken great pains to prepare for the Lord's temple. I have stored 100,000 gold talents and 1,000,000 silver talents, and too much brass and iron to weigh. I have also prepared stone and timber in great abundance that you may add to if needed.
Besides that, there is an abundance workmen with you, including stone and timber carvers and workmen, and all types of skillful men for every type of work.
And workers of gold, silver, brass, and iron beyond number. So begin doing the work, and may the Lord be with you.
David also ordered all the Israelis leaders to help his son Solomon.

And he said to them, "May your Lord God be with you, and he has given you rest from war on every side. Because he has given the inhabitants of the land into my hand, and the land has subdued before the Lord and his people.

Now set your heart and soul to seek your Lord God, and go build the Lord God's sanctuary, as a place to bring the Lord's Ark of the Covenant. Then bring God's Holy vessels into the house that will be built and dedicated to the name of the Lord.
So when David was old and full of days, he made his son Solomon king of Israel.
He gathered all the Israel princes together, along with the priests and Levites.
All the male Levites aged 30 years old and older were counted, and altogether there were 38,000 men.
Of these, 24,000 were assigned to work on the Lord's temple, and 6,000 were appointed to be officers and judges.
And David said, "Besides that, 4,000 were gatekeepers and 4,000 praised the Lord with the instruments which I had made to give praise."
David divided and organized Levi's descendants from Gershon, Kohath, and Merari into divisions.
From the Gershonites there was Laadan and Shimei.
Laadan's three sons were Jehiel the chief, Zetham, and Joel.
Shimei's three sons were Shelomith, Haziel, and Haran. All of these were the chief fathers of Laadan's family.
These were Shimei's four sons Jahath, Zina, Jeush, and Beriah.
Jahath was the firstborn and Zizah was born second, but Jeush and Beriah did not have many sons, so their inheritance from their father's house was calculated as one family.
Kohath's four sons were Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.

Amram's sons were Aaron and Moses. Aaron and his descendants were forever separated to sanctify the most Holy things, to burn incense before the Lord, to minister to him, and to bless in his name forever.
As for Moses the man of God, his sons were named among Levi's tribe.
Moses' sons were Gershom and Eliezer.
From Gershom's sons there was Shebuel the chief.
Eliezer only had one son who was Rehabiah the chief, but Rehabiah had numerous sons.
From Izhar's sons there was Shelomith the chief.
From Hebron's sons there was Jeriah the firstborn, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third, and Jekameam the fourth.
From Uzziel's sons there was Micah the firstborn and Jesiah was the second.
Merari's sons were Mahli and Mushi. Mahli's sons were Eleazar and Kish.
When Eleazar died he had daughters but no sons, and their cousins the sons of Kish married them.
And Mushi's three sons were Mahli, Eder, and Jeremoth.
These were Levi's sons from the chiefs among house of their fathers, as they were counted in the census by name, who worked in the service of the Lord's temple, who were twenty years old and older.
Because David said, "The Lord God of Israel, has given rest to his people, so that they may live in Jerusalem forever.
And the Levites will no longer have to carry the tabernacle, nor any of its vessels for its services.
Because David's last words were to count the Levites who were twenty years old and older.

Because their office was to wait on Aaron's sons in the service of the Lord's temple. They worked in the courts and the chambers purifying of all Holy things, and they performed all the other work in the service of the house of God.

They also helped the priests with the bread offering and the fine flour for bread offering. They helped with the unleavened cakes, which were baked in pans, or it was fried, and all measurements for quantities and size.
They would also stand every morning and evening to thank and praise the Lord.
Whenever the Lord's burnt offerings were offered during the Sabbaths, new moons, and celebratory feasts, the priests determined how many of them were needed to serve regularly before the Lord.
The Levites were responsible for all the work done in the service of the Lord's Congregation Tabernacle and the Holy Place, under the supervision of their brothers who were Aaron's sons.
These are the divisions from Aaron's sons. Aaron's sons were Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
But Nadab and Abihu died before their father, and had no children, so Eleazar and Ithamar served in the priest's office.

David separated his descendants into two groups, each with their own duties to perform, one group was from Zadok who was a descendant of Eleazar, and the other was from Ahimelech who was a descendant of Ithamar.

There were more leaders from Eleazar's descendants than there was from Ithamar's descendants, and they were divided accordingly. So, there were sixteen leaders from Eleazar's descendants, and eight from Ithamar's descendants.
Their positions were divided by lot, because the sanctuary officers and officers of the house of God came from Eleazar and Ithamar's sons.

Nathaniel the scribe's son Shemaiah the Levite recorded their names before the king and his officers. Those present were priest Zadok and Abiathar's son Ahimelech, and the leaders of the families of the priests and Levites. One family was chosen from Ithamar and one from Eleazar.
Now the first lot cast chose Jehoiarib and Jedaiah was the second chosen by lot.
The third lot chosen went to Harim, the 4th to Seorim.
The 5th went to Malchijah and the 6th went to Mijamin.
The 7th went to Hakkoz and the 8th went to Abijah.
The 9th went to Jeshuah and the 10th went to Shecaniah.
The 11th went to Eliashib and the 12th went to Jakim.
The 13th went to Huppah and the 14th went to Jeshebeab.
The 15th went to Bilgah and the 16th went to Immer.
The 17th went to Hezirand the 18th went to Aphses.
The 19th went to Pethahiah and the 20th went to Jehezekel.
The 21st went to Jachin and the 22nd went to Gamul.
The 23rd went to Delaiah and the 24th went to Maaziah.
They were the men chosen by their father Aaron to serve in the Lord's house, in accordance with everything that the Lord God of Israel had commanded him.
These are some of Levi's remaining descendants: From Amram's sons there was Shubael, and from Shubael's sons there was Jehdeiah.
Rehabiah's firstborn son was Isshiah.
Izhar was Shelomoth's father and Shelomoth was Jahath's father.
Hebron's sons were Jeriah who was the firstborn, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third, and Jekameam the fourth.
From Uzziel's sons there was Michah, and Michah's son Shamir.
Michah's brother was Isshiah, and from Isshiah's sons there was Zechariah.
Merari's sons were Mahli, Mushi, and Jaaziah.
Merari's son Jaaziah had four sons named Beno, Shoham, Zaccur, and Ibri.
Mahli's son was Eleazar who had no sons.
Kish's son was Jerahmeel.
Mushi's sons were Mahli, Eder, and Jerimoth. These were the sons of the Levites according to their families.
As their brothers who were Aaron's descendants did, they cast lots in the presence of King David, Zadok, Ahimelech, the leaders of the families of the priests and Levites, and their younger brothers.

David and the temple commanders chose some of the descendants of Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun to deliver the Lord's words to the people, and some were chosen to play lyres, harps, and cymbals. These are some of the workmen required to perform these services.
From Asaph's sons they chose Zaccur, Joseph, Nethaniah, and Asarelah. Asaph supervised them, and the king appointed him to be a prophet to deliver the Lord's word.

From Jeduthun's sons there were Gedaliah, Zeri, Jeshaiah, Shimei, Hashabiah, and Mattithiah who were the six sons under their father Jeduthun's supervision, who prophesied with a harp to give thanks and praise to the Lord.
From Heman's sons there were Bukkiah, Mattaniah, Uzziel, Shebuel, Jerimoth, Hananiah, Hanani, Eliathah, Giddalti, Romamtiezer, Joshbekashah, Mallothi, Hothir, and Mahazioth.
All of these fourteen sons and three daughters were given to Heman the king's prophet through God's promises to honor him.
All of them were supervised by their fathers as they made music in the Lord's house with cymbals, harps, and lyres as the king had ordered Asaph, Jeduthun, and Heman.
So there were 288 of them, along with their brothers who were taught and trained to skillfully perform the Lord's songs.
They all cast lots for their duties, both young and old, great and small, teacher, scholar, and student alike.
The first lot cast was for Asaph's family which went to Joseph, the second went to Gedaliah, he and his brothers and sons were twelve.
The third went to Zaccur, he, his sons, and his brothers were twelve.
The 4th went to Izri, he, his sons, and his brothers were twelve.
The 5th went to Nethaniah, he, his sons, and his brothers were twelve.
The 6th went to Bukkiah, he, his sons, and his brothers were twelve.
The 7th went to Jesharelah, he, his sons, and his brothers were twelve.
The 8th went to Jeshaiah, he, his sons, and his brothers were twelve.
The went 9th to Mattaniah, he, his sons, and his brothers were twelve.
The 10th went to Shimei, he, his sons, and his brothers were twelve.
The 11th went to Azareel, he, his sons, and his brothers were twelve.
The 12th went to Hashabiah, he, his sons, and his brothers were twelve.
The 13th went to Shubael, he, his sons, and his brothers were twelve.
The 14th went to Mattithiah, he, his sons, and his brothers were twelve.
The 15th went to Jeremoth, he, his sons, and his brothers were twelve.
The 16th went to Hananiah, he, his sons, and his brothers were twelve.
The 17th went to Joshbekashah, he, his sons, and his brothers were twelve.
The 18th went to Hanani, he, his sons, and his brothers were twelve.
The 19th went to Mallothi, he, his sons, and his brothers were twelve.
The 20th went to Eliathah, he, his sons, and his brothers were twelve.
The 21st went to Hothir, he, his sons, and his brothers were twelve.
The 22nd went to Giddalti, he, his sons, and his brothers were twelve.
The 23rd went to Mahazioth, he, his sons, and his brothers were twelve.
The 24th went to Romamtiezer, he, his sons, and his brothers were twelve.
These were the divisions of the gatekeepers. From the Korhites was Kore's son Meshelemiah from Asaph's descendants.
Meshelemiah's sons were: Zechariah was the firstborn, Jediael was the second, Zebadiah was the third, Jathniel was the fourth,
Elam was the fifth, Jehohanan was the sixth, and Elioenai was the seventh.
Besides that Obed-Edom's sons were: Shemaiah who was the firstborn, Jehozabad was the second, Joah was the third, Sacar was the fourth, and Nathaniel was the fifth,
Ammiel was the sixth, Issachar was the seventh, and Peulthai was the eighth because God blessed Obed-Edom.
Obed-Edom's son Shemaiah fathered sons that ruled throughout their father's house, because they were mighty men of valor.
Shemaiah's sons were: Othni, Rephael, Obed, and Elzabad and his brothers Elihu and Semachiah who were courageous men.
All of Obed-Edom's descendants and their sons and brothers were strong capable men for the service, and there were sixty-two of them altogether.
Meshelemiah had eighteen strong sons and brothers.
Merari's descendant Hosah also had sons including Simri who was the leader, and even though he was not the firstborn his father made him the leader.
Hilkiah was the second, Tebaliah the third, Zechariah the fourth, and altogether Hosah had thirteen sons and brothers.
Among these sons and brothers were the divisions of gatekeepers, even among the leaders the men had responsibilities to minister in the Lord's temple.
The leaders of each small or large family from their fathers' houses cast lots to see which gate they would guard.
The lot cast for the Eastern Gate fell to Shelemiah. Then they cast lots for his son Zechariah the wise counsellor, and he won the lot that was cast for the Northern Gate.
Obed-Edom won the lot cast for the Southern Gate, and his sons won the lot for the storehouses.
Shuppim and Hosah won the lots cast for the Western Gate and the Shallecheth Gate near the upper causeway, and they stationed guards at every outpost.
Six Levites were stationed on the east side, four a day were stationed on the north side, four a day on the south side, and two pairs of Levites were stationed at the storehouses.
At the western suburb there were four stationed at the causeway, and two at the suburb.
These were the divisions of gatekeepers from among Kore and Merari's sons.
From the Levites, Ahijah was over the treasures of the house of God and the dedicated things.
From the descendants of Laadan the Gershonite, who were the leaders of his family there was Jehieli who was the leader of one Gershonite family.
Jehieli's sons were Zetham and his brother Joel, who were over the treasures of the Lord's temple.
Others who helped were from the Amramites, Izharites, Hebronites, and the Uzzielites.
Moses' son Gershom fathered Shebuel who was over the treasuries.
Eliezer's descendants included his sons Rehabiah, Jeshaiah, Joram, Zichri, and Shelomith.
Shelomith and his brothers were over all the treasures of all the things dedicated by King David, the leading fathers, the commanders over thousands and hundreds, and the army commanders.
Some of the spoils of war that they won in battle were dedicated to maintain the Lord's temple.

Everything that had been dedicated by Samuel the prophet, Kish's son Saul, Ner's son Abner, and Zeruiah's son Joab, along with anything else that was dedicated was cared for by Shelomith and his brothers.
From the Izharites, Chenaniah and his sons had the outside official duties as officers and judges over Israel.

From the Hebronites, Hashabiah and his brothers there were 1,700 courageous men of valor. They were officers in charge of the Lord's business in Israel on the western side of the Jordan River, and in the service of the king.

Jerijah was the leader of the Hebronites, in accordance with his fathers' descendants. In the fortieth year of David's reign they searched the records and found mighty men of valor in Jazer of Gilead.

His brothers, 2,700 men of valor were chief fathers whom King David appointed to rule over the Reubenites, Gadites, and the half tribe of Manasseh in everything pertaining to God, and the affairs of the king.

The total number of Israelis counted from every division were 24,000, including the leading fathers and the commanders of the 1,000s and 100s, and their officers who served the king in any way, came and went month by month throughout the year.
Zabdiel's son Jashobeam son was in charge of the first division, which was assigned the first month. There were 24,000 men in his division.
Perez, who was the commander over all of his descendants who were the army commanders the first month.
Dodai, who was part of the Ahohite tribe, was in charge of the army the second month. His second in command was Mikloth, and they had 24,000 soldiers in their division.
The third commander of the army for the third month was Jehoiada the chief priest's son Benaiah who had 24,000 men under his command.
This is the same Benaiah who was mighty among the thirty and was over the thirty, and his son Ammizabad commanded his division.
The commander of the fourth army division in the fourth month was Joab's brother Asahel, and he was succeeded by his son Zebadiah. He had 24,000 soldiers under his command.
The commander of the army in the fifth month was Shamhuth, who came from Izrah's tribe. He had 24,000 soldiers under his command.
The commander of the army in the sixth month was Ira the son of Ikkesh the Tekoite, and he had 24,000 soldiers under his command.
The seventh commander in the seventh month was Helez the Pelonite, from the tribe of Ephraim. He commanded 24,000 men.
Sibbecai of the Zerahites was the eigth commander of the army in the eighth month, he belonged to the Hushah tribe. He had 24,000 soldiers under his command.
The army's nineth commander for the nineth month was Abiezer the Anetothite, from the Benjamites tribe. He had 24,000 soldiers under his command.
Maharai the Netophathite was the Zerahite tribe's army commander in the tenth month. He had 24,000 soldiers in his division.
Benaiah the Pirathonite from the Ephraim tribe was the army commander in the tenth month. He had 24,000 soldiers in his division.
Heldai the Netophathite from the Othniel tribe was the twelfth army commander in the twelfth month. He had 24,000 soldiers under his command.
In addition the ruler over the Reubenite tribes of Israel was Zichri's son Eliezer, and over the Simeonites was Maachah's son Shephatiah.
From the Levites there was Kemuel's son Hashabiah, and from the Aaronites there was Zadok.
From Judah there was Elihu one of David's brothers, and from Issachar there was Michael's son Omri.
From Zebulun there was Obadiah's son Ishmaiah, and from Naphtali there was Azriel's son Jerimoth.
From Ephraim's descendants there was Azaziah's son Hoshea, and from the half tribe of Manasseh was Pedaiah's son Joel.
From the half tribe of Manasseh in Gilead there was Zechariah's son Iddo, and from Benjamin there was Abner's son Jaasiel.
From Dan there was Jeroham's son Azareel. These were all the princes of the tribes of Israel.
But David did not take the census of the people who were younger than twenty years old, because the Lord had said he would increase the Israelis numbers like the stars in the heavens.
Zeruiah's son Joab began to take the census but he did not finish, because the Lord's anger fell on Israel, nor was the number recorded in the records of the chronicles of King David.
Adiel's son Azmaveth was over the king's treasures, and Uzziah's son Jehonathan was over the storehouses in the fields, cities, villages, and castles.
Chelub's son Ezri was over the people who worked in the fields tilling the ground.
Shimei the Ramathite was over the vineyards, and Zabdi the Shiphmite was over the vineyard production for the wine cellars.
Baal-Hanan the Gederite was over the olive and sycamore trees in the lower plains, and Joash was over the oil cellars.
Shitrai the Sharonite was over the herds that grazed in Sharon, and Adlai's son Shaphat was over the herds in the valleys.
Obil the Ishmaelite was over the camels, and Jehdeiah the Meronothite was over the donkeys.
And Jaziz the Hagerite was over the flocks. These were all the rulers of everything that belonged to King David.
King David's uncle Jonathan was a wise counsellor and a scribe, and Hachmoni's son Jehiel attended to the king's sons.
Ahithophel was also the king's counsellor, and Hushai the Archite was the king's companion.
After Ahithophel there was Benaiah's son Jehoiada and then Abiathar, and Joab was the general of the king's army.

David summoned and assembled in Jerusalem all the princes of the tribes of Israel, and the company captains that ministered to the king by division, including the captains over the thousands and hundreds. He also summoned the people who watched over the king's sons and managed everything that he owned, along with the officers, the mighty men, and all the courageous men.

Then King David stood on his feet and said, "Hear me, my brothers and my people, I had it in my heart to build a house of rest for the Lord's Ark of the Covenant, and for the footstool of our God. And I had made preparations to begin building the temple.
But God said to me, 'You must not build a house dedicated to my name, because you have been a man of war, and have shed blood.'

However the Lord God of Israel has chosen me before all others from my father's house to be the king of Israel forever. Because he has chosen Judah to be the ruler, and from the house of Judah he chose my father's house, and from my father's sons he chose me to be the king over all of Israel.
The Lord has given me many sons, and he has chosen my son Solomon to sit on the throne of the kingdom of the Lord over Israel.
And he said to me, 'Your son Solomon, will build my house and courts because I have chosen him to be my son, and I will be his father.
Besides that, I will establish his kingdom forever, if he remains true and obeys my commandments and judgments, as it is being done today.'

So in front of all Israel the Lord's congregation and audience of our God, you must look for and keep all of your Lord God's commandments, so that you may possess this good land, and leave it as an inheritance for your children after you forever.

And you my son Solomon, know your father God and serve him with a perfect heart and with a willing mind. Because the Lord searches all hearts, and understands all the imaginations and thoughts. If you seek him, you will find him, but if you forsake him he will throw you away forever.
Take heed now, because the Lord has chosen you and to build a house for the sanctuary. So be strong and do it."
Then David gave his son Solomon the plans for the entrance hall, its houses, treasuries, upper chambers, inner parlors, and the place for the Mercy Seat.

The plans contained all the designs that the spirit had given David for the courts of the Lord's temple, and all the chambers surrounding the treasuries of the dedicated things and the other treasuries of the house of God.
He also gave him for the divisions of the priests and Levites, and all the service work of the Lord's temple, and for all the service vessels in the Lord's temple.
He also gave him all the gold and silver by weight that was needed for all the service instruments needed for all types of services.
He even gave him enough gold and silver for the lamps and lampstands, based on how each lamp or lampstand was used.
He gave Solomon enough gold for the priests bread offering table, and also enough silver for the silver tables.
He also gave him pure gold for the fleshhooks, bowls, cups, and the golden sinks, plus enough silver for every silver sink.
For the incense altar and the cherubim chariots with spread out wings he gave enough refined gold for what the plans called for, including enough gold to cover the Lord's Ark of the Covenant.
Then David said, "All this, the Lord has made me understand. He has shown me everything in his plans in writing with his hand upon my shoulder."

And David said to his son Solomon, "Do this, and be strong and courageous, do not fear, and do not be dismayed, because my Lord God will be with you. He will not fail you nor forsake you, until you have finished all the work for the service of the Lord's temple.

And, behold the divisions of the priests and Levites, they will even be with you for all the services of the house of God. There will be many skillful men with you to do all types of skillful workmanship and services. All the princes and people will also be completely at your commandment."

Furthermore King David spoke to the entire congregation and said, "Solomon my son, whom God alone has chosen is still young and inexperienced. The work is great, because this palace is not for man, but for the Lord God.

Now I have with all my might prepared all these resources for the house of my God. I have stored the gold, silver, brass, iron, wood, turquoise, onyx for jewelry settings, stones of many different colors, all types of other precious stones, and marble slabs in abundance.

Besides that, because I have such an affection to build the house of my God, I am giving my own personal treasures of gold and silver to the house of my God, above and beyond everything else that I have prepared for his Holy house.
I have even provided 3,000 gold talents from the gold of Ophir, and 7,000 refined silver talents, to overlay the walls of the buildings.

I have given the gold and the silver for the things made of gold and silver, and for all types of work done by the hands of artisans. So who is willing to consecrate their services to the Lord's temple today?
Then the chief of the fathers and princes of the tribes of Israel and the captains of thousands and of hundreds, with the rulers of the king's work, offered willingly.
They also donated toward the service of God's house 5,000 talents and 10,000 drams of gold, 10,000 silver talents, 18,000 brass talents, and 100,000 iron talents.
Anyone who had precious stones donated them to the treasury of the Lord's temple, where it was under Jehiel the Gershonite's care.
This caused the people to rejoice, because their leaders had willingly offered all this to the Lord with a perfect heart, and King David also rejoiced with great joy.
So David blessed the Lord before the entire congregation and said, "Blessed be you our father, O Lord God of Israel forever and ever.
Your power, glory, victory, and majesty, O Lord is the greatest, because everything that is in heaven and on the earth is yours. Yours is the kingdom O Lord, and you are glorified as head above all.
Both riches and honor come from you, and you reign over everything. You hold all the power and might in your hand, and it is within your power to make everything great and give strength to all.
That's why O Lord our God, that we thank you and praise your glorious name.
But who am I, and who are my people, that we should be able to offer all this so willingly? Because everything comes from you, and from your own hand we have given all this to you.
Because we are foreigners and travelers before you, as all our fathers were. Our days on earth are just like shadows, and there are none among us that endure here.
O Lord our God, everything that we have stored and prepared in order to build a house dedicated to your Holy name comes from your hand, and all of it already belongs to you.

I also know my God, that you test the heart, and find pleasure in honesty. As for me, in the honesty of my heart I have willingly offered all these things, and now I have seen the joy in your people who are present and joyfully giving willingly to you.
O Lord God of our fathers Abraham, Isaac, Israel keep this desire forever in the imagination and thoughts of the hearts of your people, and turn their hearts toward you.
And give my son Solomon a perfect heart to keep and obey all of your commandments, testimonies, laws, and to build your palace for which I have made provisions."

Then David addressed the entire congregation and said, "Now bless your Lord God!" So the entire congregation blessed the Lord God of their fathers and bowed their heads, and worshipped the Lord, and paid homage to the king.

After that they offered sacrifices and burnt offerings to the Lord. The day after that they offered 1,000 bulls, 1,000 rams, and 1,000 lambs, along with their drink offering, and other sacrifices in abundance for all of Israel.

They ate and drink before the Lord that day with great happiness. Then they made King David's son Solomon their king again for a second time, and anointed him before the Lord to be their ruler, and Zadok as their priest.
Solomon prospered and all of Israel obeyed him.
All the princes, the mighty men, and all of King David's other sons submitted themselves to the rule of King Solomon.
The Lord greatly magnified Solomon's influence over Israel, and bestowed on him such royal majesty as had never been seen on any of Israel's kings before him.
This was how Jesse's son David reigned over all of Israel.
He reigned over Israel for forty years. He reigned from Hebron for seven years, and then from Jerusalem for another thirty-three years.
He died at a ripe old age, full of years, riches, and honor. Then his son Solomon reigned in his place.
All the acts of King David from first to last, are written in the books of Samuel, Nathan, and Gad the prophets.
Along with all the details of his reign and his might, and the circumstances that came upon him and Israel, and all the other kingdoms of the land.
King David's son Solomon was firmly established in his kingdom, and his Lord God was with him, and the Lord greatly exalted him.
Then Solomon spoke to all of the Israelis including all of the leading fathers, commanders of the 1,000s and the 100s, judges, and governors.
3 So Solomon and the entire congregation went up into the high place in Gibeon, because that's where the Lord's servant Moses built the congregation's tabernacle of God in the wilderness.
But David had already brought God's Ark of the Covenant up from Kiriath-Jearim to the place he had prepared for it, because he had pitched a tent for it in Jerusalem.
Besides that, he had already erected the brass altar that Hur's son Bezalel had made before the Lord's Congregation Tabernacle. So Solomon and the congregation looked for it there.
Then Solomon went to the place where the Lord's brass altar was in front of the congregation's tabernacle, and offered 1,000 burnt offerings on it.
That night God appeared and spoke to Solomon and said, "Whatever you ask I will give to you."
And Solomon said to God, "You have shown great mercy to my father David, and you have made me king in his place.
Now O Lord God, let your promise to my father David be established, because you have made me king over a people who are as numerous as the dust of the earth.
Give me the wisdom and knowledge that I need to lead these people because who can govern such a great people as yours?"

And God said to Solomon, "Because you asked for what was in your heart, and did not ask for riches, wealth, honor, long life, or the life of your enemies, but you have instead asked for the wisdom and knowledge you need to judge my people wisely, over whom I have made you king.

Wisdom and knowledge is granted to you, and I will give you riches, wealth, and honor such as none of the kings that have come been before you has ever had, and there will be none so great after you either."
Then Solomon returned to Jerusalem from his journey to the congregation's tabernacle in the high place in Gibeon, and reigned over Israel.
King Solomon accumulated 1,400 chariots and 12,000 horsemen which he stationed with him in Jerusalem and also in the other chariot cities.
The king made gold and silver as plentiful as stones in Jerusalem, and cedar trees as abundant as the sycamore trees in the vale.
Solomon had horses imported from Egypt, and the king's merchants purchased linen yarn at a good price.
Chariots could be purchased from Egypt for 600 silver shekels, and a horse sold for 150 silver shekels. So they exported enough horses for all the Hittite and Syrian kings.
And Solomon determined to build a house for the name of the Lord, and a house for his kingdom.
Solomon put 70,000 men to work transporting heavy loads, and he sent 80,000 stone carvers to the mountain, along with 3,600 managers to oversee them.
Then King Solomon sent King Hiram of Tyre a message and said, "I would like to deal with you the same way you dealt with my father David, when you sent cedar to him to build a palace.

Behold, I am building a house dedicated to my Lord God's name, so I can burn sweet incense before him. Also as a place to offer the regular priests bread offerings, the Sabbath's morning and evening burnt offerings, the new moon offerings, and the solemn feasts for our Lord God. This is a legal decree to Israel forever.
Because the house I am building is great, because our God is great and above all other gods.
But who is able to build him a house, seeing how the highest of heavens cannot contain him? So who am I, that I should build him a house, except as a place to burn sacrifices before him?

So send me a skillful engraver who can work with gold, silver, brass, iron, plus purple, crimson, and blue yarn. Someone that can work with my craftsmen here in Judah and Jerusalem, whom my father David provided.
I also need you to send me cedar, fir, and algum trees from Lebanon because I know that your servants are skilled timber cutters, and I will send my servants to help them.
I will need an abundance of timber, because the house I am about to build will be great and wonderful.
In return, I will give your timber cutting servants and carvers 20,000 measures of threshed wheat, 20,000 measures of barley, 20,000 jugs of wine, and 20,000 jugs of oil."
Then King Hiram of Tyre answered Solomon in writing and said, "Because the Lord loves his people, he has made you their king."

King Hiram also said, "Blessed be the Lord God of Israel that made heaven and earth, who has given King David a wise son who is filled with prudence and understanding, so that he might build a house for the Lord, and a palace for his kingdom.
Now I have sent my father's servant Huram, who is a skillful man full of understanding and knowledge.

He is one of Dan's grandsons and his father was a citizen of Tyre who skillfully worked in gold, silver, brass, iron, stone, and timber plus purple, blue, and crimson fine linen. He is also experienced in all types of engraving and he can create any design given to him. He will work with your craftsmen, and your father my Lord David's craftsmen.
So send us the servants, wheat, barley, oil, and wine that you have spoken of.
And we will cut as much wood as you will need from Lebanon, and we will float it to Joppa by sea where you can pick it up and carry it to Jerusalem."
Then Solomon counted all the foreigners in Israel, the same way that his father David had counted them, and there was a total of 153,600 of them.
He put 70,000 of them to work as manual laborers, 80,000 of them went to work as carvers on the mountain, and 3,600 experienced men managed the people a work.

Then Solomon began building the Lord's house in Jerusalem on Mount Moriah, where the Lord appeared to his father David. It was the same place that David had prepared from the former threshing room floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
He began building on the second day of the second month of the fourth year of his reign.
Solomon instructed them to the build the house of God sixty cubits long and twenty cubits wide.
The entrance hall along the front side of the house was built twenty cubits long and twenty cubits high. He covered the inside of the entrance hall with pure gold.
The main house was paneled with fir overlaid with fine gold, and carved images of palm trees and chains.
He decorated the house with beautiful precious stones and gold from Parvaim.
He had the beams, posts, walls, and doors of the house overlaid with gold, and they engraved cherubims on the walls.
He built the most Holy house 20 cubits long and 20 cubits wide, and he overlaid it with 600 talents worth of fine gold.
The gold nails weighed fifty shekels, and he overlaid the upper chambers with gold.
In the most Holy house he carved two cherubims, and overlaid them with gold.

All the cherubim's wings were a total of twenty cubits long, one wing of one cherub was five cubits long and it touched one wall of the house. The other wing was five cubits long and it touched the other cherub's wing.
One wing of the other cherub was five cubits long and it touched the other wall of the house, and the other wing was five cubits long and it touched the wing of the other cherub.
The cherub's wings all spread a total of twenty cubits, they stood on their feet and they faced inward toward each other.
He made the vail of fine linen with embroidered cherubs of blue, purple, and crimson thread.
He also built two 35 cubit tall columns in front of the house, and on top of each column was a five cubit high ornamental capital.
He made chains like the ones in the inner sanctuary, and hung them on the column heads, and he had a hundred craved pomegranates hung from the chains.
He raised the columns on the right and left sides on the front of the temple. He named the column on the right side Jachin, and the one on the left was named Boaz.
Besides all that, he made a brass altar twenty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and ten cubits high.
He also made a bowl shaped cast metal sea that was ten cubits in diameter, five cubits high, and thirty cubits in circumference.
It had two rows of ten cast ornamental oxen per cubit underneath the sea that surrounded it when it was cast.

The brass sea stood on a foundation of twelve brass oxen that were looking outward on each side with three on each of four sides facing north, south, east, and west with their hindquarters toward the center.
It was a handbreadth thick, and its rim was shaped like lily flowers or the brim of a cup, and it held 3,000 bathtubs of water.
He also made ten washbasins, and placed five on the right side and five on the left, where they washed things that were offered for the burnt offering, but the priests washed in the brass sea.
He made ten gold lampstands in the form that was specified, and set them in the temple, five on the right side and five on the left.
He made also ten tablets and placed them in the temple, five on the right side and five on the left, and he made a hundred gold sinks.
He also made the priests' court, the great court, and doors for the court which were overlaid with brass.
He set the brass sea on the right side of the eastern end, against the south wall.
And Huram made the pots, and the shovels, and the sinks, and Huram finished the work that he was to make for King Solomon for the house of God.
He was finished making the two columns, pommels, the ornamental capitals, and the two wreaths that covered the two pommels of the ornamental capitals which were on top of the columns.
He finished the 400 pomegranates on the two rows of pomegranates on each of two wreaths, to cover the two pommels of the ornamental capitals on the columns.
He also made the foundations, and the washbasins on top of the foundations.
He made one brass sea with twelve oxen underneath it.
His father Huram also made the brass pots, shovels, meat hooks, and all the other instruments for King Solomon for the Lord's temple.
The king had them cast in clay molds on the plains of the Jordan River between Succoth and Zeredathah.
Solomon had all these brass bowls made in such great abundance, and they kept no record of how much the brass weighed.
Solomon also had all the gold bowls, gold altar, and gold tablets where the priests placed the bread offering made for the house of God.
Besides that, he had the all the pure gold lamps and lampstands made that would burn before the inner sanctuary when needed.
He had all the flowers, lamps, and tongs made perfectly of pure gold.
And he had the candle snuffers, sinks, spoons, censers, entrance way to the Lord's house, the inner doors of Most Holy Place, and the temple's entrance doors all made of pure gold.

After all this, Solomon's work on the Lord's temple was finished. Then he had everything that his father David had dedicated to the Lord brought and placed among the other treasures of God's house, including all the gold and silver instruments.
Then Solomon assembled the Israelis elders, the tribal leaders, and the chief fathers of Israel to Jerusalem, to bring the Lord's Ark of the Covenant there from the city of David in Zion.
So all the Israelis men gathered together before the king for the feast in the seventh month.
All the Israelis elders came, and the Levites carried the ark.
The priests and Levites carried the ark, and they brought the congregation's tabernacle and all of its Holy vessels.
King Solomon and the entire Israelis congregation assembled with him before the ark, and they sacrificed so many sheep and oxen that no one kept count.
The priests brought the Lord's Ark of the Covenant to his place in the Most Holy Place of the temple's inner sanctuary and placed it under the wings of the cherubims.
The cherubims wings were spread above the ark and they covered it and its carrying poles.
They pulled the ark's poles in, so that the ends of the poles could be seen from the front of the inner sanctuary, but they could not be seen outside the Holy Place, just as it is to this day.
There was nothing in the ark except the two stone tablets that Moses put in there in Horeb, when the Lord made a covenant with the Israelis, after they left Egypt.
Then all the priests present left the Holy Place, after they had all been sanctified regardless of their division.

All the Levite musicians including Asaph, Heman, Jeduthun, and their sons and brothers were all dressed in fine white linen. They had their cymbals, lyres, and harps and they stood at the east end of the altar, as they and 120 priests with them sounded their trumpets.

Then as the trumpeters and singers came together united as one sound praising and thanking the Lord. When they lifted up their voices with trumpets, cymbals, and musical instruments they praised the Lord and said, "Because God is good, his mercy endures forever and the Lord's temple was filled with a cloud.
And because of the cloud, the priests could not stand there to minister as the glory of the Lord filled God's house.
Then Solomon said, "The Lord has said that he would live in thick darkness.
But I have built a house for you, and a place for your home forever."
Then the king turned and blessed the whole Israelis congregation, and they all stood up.
And he said, blessed be the Lord God of Israel, who has with his hands satisfied that which he spoke with his mouth to my father David and said.

When God said, 'Since the day I brought my people out of the land of Egypt I chose no city from the tribes of Israel as a location to build a house, so that my name might be established there, nor did I chose anyone to be a ruler over my people Israel.
But I have chosen Jerusalem to be the place to establish my name there, and I have chosen David to be over my people Israel.'"
And it was in my father David's heart to build a house dedicated to the name of the Lord God of Israel.
But the Lord said to my father David, 'Because you have in your heart the idea to build a house dedicated to my name, you did well to have this in your heart.
But you are not going to build the house, because you will have a son of your own flesh and blood, and he will build the house dedicated to my name.'

So the Lord has kept his word, because I have been raised in my father David's house, and as the Lord has promised I have been set on the throne of Israel, and I have built a house dedicated to the name of the Lord God of Israel.
And I have put the Lord's Ark of the Covenant in it, which contains the Lord's covenant that he made with the Israelis."
And he stood before the altar of the Lord in the presence of all the congregation of Israel, and spread out his hands.

Solomon had made a brass scaffolding five cubits long, five cubits wide, and three cubits high that was sitting in the middle of the court. And he stood on the scaffolding, then he knelt down before the Israelis congregation, and spread out his hands toward heaven.
And Solomon said, "O Lord God of Israel, there is no God like you in heaven or on earth, who keeps your covenant and shows mercy to your servants, who walk before you with all their hearts.
You have kept your promise with your servant my father David that you spoke with your mouth, and satisfied with your hand, on this day.

So O Lord God of Israel, keep the promise you made with your servant my father David when you said, 'You will never fail to have a man sit before me on the throne of Israel, if your descendants take heed to walk in my law, as you have walked before me.'
O Lord God of Israel, let your word which you have spoken now be verified to your servant David.
But will God indeed live with men on the earth? For behold, even heaven and the highest heavens cannot contain you, so how can this temple I have built!
So have respect O Lord my God, for the prayers of your servant and listen to his cries and prayers which are prayed before you.

So that your eyes may be open on this house day and night, so you may keep an eye on the place which you said that you would put your name there, and listen to the prayers which your servant prays toward this place.
So listen to your servant's pleas, and the pleas of your people Israel, which they will pray toward this place. Listen to them from your home place even in heaven and when you hear them, forgive.
If a man sins against his neighbor, and an oath is laid on him to make him swear an oath to come before your altar in this house.

Then when you hear from heaven and judge your servants and repay the wicked and bring on his own head what he has done, and justifying the righteous by rewarding him in accordance with his righteousness.
And if your people Israel are defeated by the enemy because they have sinned against you, and they return and confess your name, and pray and make a plea before you in this house.
Then hear them from the heavens, and forgive your people Israel's sin, and bring them back to the land that you have given them and their fathers.

When the heavens are closed shut, and there is no rain because they have sinned against you, but if they pray toward this place and confess your name, and they turn from their sin, after you have afflicted them.

Then hear them from heaven and forgive your servant people Israel's sins, when you have taught them the good way in which they should walk, and send rain on your land, which you have given to your people as an inheritance.
If there is a shortage in the land or a plague, pestilence, blight, mildew, locusts, caterpillars and their enemies besiege them in their cities, and no matter what sickness or plague comes.
Then whatever prayer or plea that your people Israel make, when each person knows their own grief and affliction, and when they spread out their hands in this temple.
Then hear them from your home place in heaven and forgive, and reward each man in accordance with their own way of life, because you know their hearts and their true character.
So that they may fear you and walk in your ways, as long as they live in the land which you have given our fathers.
As for the foreigner who is not of your people Israel, but has come from a far country for your great name's sake, your mighty hand, and your stretched out arm, if they come and pray in this house.

Then hear them from your home place in the heavens, and answer the foreigner's prayers and do what they asks of you. This way everyone on earth will know your name and fear you, as do your people in Israel, and you will know that this house I have built is called by your name.
If your people go to war against their enemies wherever you send them, and they pray to you toward the city you have chosen, and the house which I have built and dedicated to your name.
Then hear their prayers and pleas from the heavens, and maintain their cause.
If they sin against you, because there is no man who does not sin and you are angry with them, and deliver them over to their enemies, and they are carried away as captives to a land far or near.

But if they come to their senses in the land where they were carried as captives, and they repent and pray to you in the land of their captivity and say, 'We have sinned, done wrong, and dealt wickedly.'

If they return to you with all their heart and soul in the land of their captivity, where they were carried away as captives, and pray toward their land which you have given to their fathers and the city you have chosen, and toward the house which I have built that I dedicated to your name.
Then hear their prayers and pleas even from your home place in the heavens, and maintain their cause and forgive your people who have sinned against you.
Now my God, I beg you will open your eyes and let your ears hear the prayers that are made in this place.
So Lord God, enter your resting place along with the ark of your strength. Then O Lord God, may your priests be clothed in salvation, and let your saints rejoice in your goodness.
O Lord God, do not turn away from the face of your anointed, and remember the mercies of your servant David."
When Solomon finished praying, fire came down from heaven and consumed the burnt offering and sacrifices, and the Lord's glory filled the house.
