The priests could not enter the Lord's house, because the Lord's glory filled the Lord's house.

When all the Israelis saw the fire come down and the Lord's glory on the temple, they bowed facedown to the ground and worshipped and praised the Lord and said, "Because he is good, his mercy endures forever."
Then the king and all the people offered sacrifices before the Lord.
King Solomon offered a sacrifice of 22,000 oxen and 120,000 sheep, and that's how the king and all the people dedicated the house of God.

The priests waited at their post along with the Levites with their musical instruments of the Lord, which King David had made to praise the Lord when he said, "Because his mercy endures forever," when David was praised by their ministry. All the priests sounded their trumpets before them, as all of Israel stood by.

Then Solomon consecrated the Holy middle of the courtyard in front of the Lord's temple, because that's where he offered burnt offerings and the fat of the peace offerings, because the brass altar Solomon had built could not contain all the burnt offerings, bread offerings, and the fat.
Also at that time Solomon and all of Israel, which was a very great congregation of people who came from the entrance of Hamath and all the way to the Nile River, kept the feast for seven days.
On the eighth day, they held a solemn assembly to dedicate the altar that lasted for seven more days, and the feast lasted for seven more days after that.
On the twenty-third day of the seventh month he sent the people home. They were cheerful, glad, and happy because they saw how good the Lord was to Solomon, David, and all his people of Israel.
After this, Solomon was finished with all the work on the Lord's temple, the king's palace, and everything else that his heart led him to make in the Lord's temple, and his own house prospered.
The Lord appeared to Solomon at night and said, "I have heard your prayer, and I have chosen this place for myself as a house of sacrifice.
If I close the heavens and it does not rain, or if I command the locusts to devour the land, or if I send a pestilence among my people.
If my people, who are called by my name humble themselves and pray to me, and turn from their wicked ways, then I will hear from heaven and forgive their sin, and I will heal their land.
Now my eyes will be open, and my ears will pay attention to the prayers that are made in this place.
Because as of now, I have chosen and sanctified this house, so that my name will be here forever, and my eyes and heart will always be there.
As for you, if you walk before me as your father David did, and do everything that I have asked of you, and observe my laws and judgments.
Then I will establish your kingdom's throne as I promised your father David when I and said, 'One of your descendants will always be a ruler in Israel.'
But if you turn away from me and forsake my laws and commandments, and you go serve and worship other gods.

I will pull them out by the roots and throw them out of the promised land. Then I will throw this house that I sanctified in my name out of my sight, and I will make it an example of my wrath among all nations of the world.
Everyone will be astonished when this highly respected temple becomes a pile of rubble, and whoever passes by will say, 'Why has the Lord done these terrible things to this land and this house?'

And they will be answered, 'It is because they have forsaken their fathers' Lord God, who brought them out of Egypt. They have held to other gods which they have worshipped and served, so he has brought all of this evil on them.'"
It took Solomon twenty years to build the Lord's temple and his own palace.
Solomon rebuilt the cities which Hiram had given him, and he sent some Israelis to live there.
Then Solomon took his troops to Hamath-Zobah and conquered it.
He built Tadmor in the wilderness and he also built the storehouse cities in Hamath.
He also built upper and lower Beth-Horon the fortified cities with walls and barred gates.

Solomon also built Baalath and the storehouse cities, chariot cities, cities of horsemen, and everything else that Solomon desired to build in Jerusalem and Lebanon, and throughout his entire kingdom.
There were some people were not of Israel, and they remained with the Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and the Jebusites.
But their descendants who were left in the land that the Israelis did not consumed, were made to pay taxes by Solomon to this day.
But Solomon did not make the Israelis his servants for the work, instead he made them his men of war, commanders over his captains, and captains over his chariots and horsemen.
They were also King Solomon's 250 civilian officers, who supervised the people.

Then Solomon brought Pharaoh's daughter from the city of David to the palace that he had built for her. Because he said, "My wife will not live in the house of King David of Israel, because anywhere that the Ark of the Covenant has been is Holy ground."
After that, Solomon offered burnt offerings to the Lord on the Lord's altar which he had built before the entrance hall.

He made the daily offerings as Moses ordered for the Sabbaths, new moons, and the solemn feasts three times a year. He even observed the Feast of Unleavened Bread, the Feast of Weeks, and the Feast of Tabernacles.

And as his father David had ordered he appointed the divisions of priests to their service, and the Levites to their responsibilities to praise and minister before the priests, as their every day duties required. He also appointed the gatekeepers by their divisions at every gate, because David the man of God had commanded it.
They obeyed King David's commandments regarding the priests and Levites, and anything having to do with the treasuries.
King Solomon's work had been prepared for him until the day that the Lord's temple foundation was laid, and the work continued until it was finished. And that's how the Lord's temple was perfected.
Then Solomon went to Ezion-Geber and Eloth in Edom, near the seashore.

King Hiram sent ships with servants under the command of his own officers along with sailors who had knowledge of the sea. And Solomon's servants sailed with them to Ophir where they loaded 400 gold talents, that they brought back to King Solomon.

When the queen of Sheba heard Solomon's fame, she came to Jerusalem to test Solomon with difficult questions. She brought a huge company with camels carrying an abundance of spices, gold, and precious stones. When she arrived she went to see Solomon, and when she spoke with him she told him everything that was in her heart.
Solomon answered all of her questions truthfully, and he hid nothing from her.
When the queen of Sheba saw Solomon's wisdom, and the house that he had built.

When she also saw all the meat on his table, and all his ministers and servants seated with him and their fine clothing, his cupbearers and their apparel, and the way he ascended and went into the Lord's temple, she was totally overwhelmed.
And she said to the king, "I can see that all the reports I have received of your accomplishments and wisdom in my own land are all true.

However, I did not believe it until I came and saw it with my own eyes, and I was astonished to see that I was only told about half of your greatness and wisdom, because the truth is that you have exceeded the fame and wisdom that I have heard.
Your people are happy, and your servants who stand before you must be happy to hear your wisdom everyday!

Blessed be your Lord God, who was delighted so much in you he set you on his throne, to be your Lord God's king of Israel, and because he loved Israel he has established them forever. So he made you their king in order to judge them and give justice to them."
Then she gave King Solomon 120 gold talents, an abundance of spices, and precious stones. And there had never been such spices like those that the Queen of Sheba gave King Solomon.
King Hiram's servants and Solomon's servants who brought gold from Ophir, also brough algum trees and precious stones.

And the king added algum tree terraces to the Lord's temple and the king's palace. They used some of the wood to build lyres and harps for musicians like had never before been seen in the land of Judah.
So King Solomon gave the Queen of Sheba whatever she desired and whatever she asked of him. Then she and her servants left and went back to her own land.
Now the gold that was brought to Solomon in one year weighed 666 talents.
That did not include what the traders and merchants brought to Solomon, or all the gold and silver brought by the kings of Arabia and governors of the land.
King Solomon had 200 shields made of hammered gold, and it took gold that weighed 600 shekels to make one shield.
He had another 300 shields made of hammered gold, and it took gold that weighed 300 gold shekels to make one shield. The king had them put in the palace in the Forest of Lebanon.
Besides that, the king had a great throne made of ivory, and overlaid it with pure gold.
There were six steps to the throne which had a gold footstool attached to it, and there were armrests on each side of the throne, with lions standing beside each armrest.
There were twelve lions, two standing on each side of the six steps. Never before had anything like that ever been made in any kingdom.

All of King Solomon's drinking cups and all the bowls for Lebanon's house of the forest were made of pure gold. Nothing was made of silver in King Solomon's day because silver was considered to be worthless back then.
This was because the king's ships sailed to and from Tarshish with Hiram's servants, and once every three years they would return carrying gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks.
King Solomon exceeded all the other kings on earth in riches and wisdom.
All the kings on earth sought out Solomon, to hear the wisdom that God had put in his heart.
Year after year they all brought presents including gold and silver bowls, clothes, harnesses, spices, horses, and mules.
King Solomon had 4,000 stalls for horses and chariots and 12,000 horses, which he stationed in chariot cities, and also with him in Jerusalem.
Solomon reigned over all the kings from the river all the way to the land of the Philistines, as far as the Egyptian border.
The king made silver in Jerusalem as plentiful as stones, and he made the cedar trees as abundant as the sycamore trees in the lower plains.
They brought horses to Solomon from all the lands of Egypt.
The rest of Solomon's acts from first to last, are written in the book of Nathan the prophet, the prophecies of Ahijah the Shilonite, and Iddo the prophet's visions against Nebat's son Jeroboam.
And Solomon reigned over Israel in Jerusalem for forty years.
Solomon died and slept with his fathers, and he was buried in the city of his father David, and his son Rehoboam reigned in his place.
Rehoboam went to Shechem, because all of Israel went to Shechem to make him king.
When Nebat's son Jeroboam heard this he returned from in Egypt where he had fled earlier from King Solomon.
And they sent and called him. So Jeroboam and all Israel came and spoke to Rehoboam and said.
And Jeroboam said, "Your father made our life burdensome, but if you ease the burden your father put on us, we will serve you."
Rehoboam answered them and said, "Return to me in three days," and they all left.
King Rehoboam conferred with the old men that had counseled his father Solomon when he was living and said, "How do you think I should answer these people when they return?"
They spoke to him and said, "If you are kind to these people and make them happy, and speak good words to them, they will be your servants forever."
But he ignored their counsel, and he consulted the young men that he brought with him.

He spoke to them and said, "These people spoke to me and said, 'Your father made our life burdensome, but if you ease the burden your father put on us, we will serve you.' So, how do you think I should answer these people when they return?"

The young men that he brought with him spoke to him and said, "This is how you should answer the people that spoke to you and said, 'Your father made our life burdensome, but if you ease the burden your father put on us, we will serve you.' This is what you must say to them, 'My little finger will be thicker than my father's waist.
Because it is indeed true that my father put a heavy burden on you, but I will put a larger burden on you, my father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions.'"
So Jeroboam and all the people returned to King Rehoboam on the third day, as he had asked them.
The king answered them rudely, and he ignored the old men's counsel.

He answered them the way the young men told him to and he said, "My father gave you a heavy burden, but I am going add to it, my father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions."
But the king did not listen to the people because God had other plans. This was so the Lord could fulfill his word, when he spoke through Ahijah the Shilonite to Nebat's son Jeroboam.

When all the Israelis realized that the king would not listen to them, the people answered him and said, "What do we have to do with David, and we have no inheritance in Jesse's son either. So now go to your tents, O Israel! Look now, David and tend to your own house!" So all the Israelis went home to their tents.
But Rehoboam reigned over Israel's descendants who lived in the cities of Judah.
Then King Rehoboam sent Hadoram the forced labor superintendent to them, and the children of Israel stoned him to death. And King Rehoboam quickly mounted his chariot and fled to Jerusalem.
And Israel rebels against the house of David to this very day.
When Rehoboam arrived in Jerusalem he conscripted 180,000 warriors chosen from the house of Judah and Benjamin. He planned to attack Israel, so that he could regain control of the kingdom.
But the word of the Lord came to Shemaiah the man of God and said.
Speak to Rehoboam the son of Solomon, king of Judah, and to all Israel in Judah and Benjamin and said.

And say this, 'This is what the Lord says, you must not go and fight against your brothers! Return to your homes, because this thing comes from me!'"They obeyed the Lord's words, and they did not go to attack Jeroboam.
Rehoboam lived in Jerusalem, and built fortified cities to defend Judah.
He even built Bethlehem, Etam, Tekoa,
Beth-Zur, Shoco, Adullam,
Gath, Mareshah, Ziph,
Adoraim, Lachish, Azekah,
Zorah, Aijalon, Hebron which are in Judah and Benjamin's fortified cities.
Rehoboam fortified the stronghold cities, and stationed military commanders and stored supplies including oil and wine there.
He put shields and spears in every city, and reinforced them making them exceedingly strong. And Judah and Benjamin remained on his side.
And the priests and Levites throughout the borders of Israel remained loyal to Rehoboam.
The Levites left their fields, pastures, and possessions and moved to Judah and Jerusalem. Because Jeroboam and his sons had rejected them as the priests of the Lord's office.
Jeroboam ordained his own priests for the high places, devils, and calf idols that he made.
Everyone from all the tribes of Israel whose hearts were determined to seek the Lord God of Israel, went to Jerusalem to sacrifice to their fathers' Lord God.
So they strengthened the kingdom of Judah and followed Solomon's son Rehoboam for three years, because for three years they walked in the ways of David and Solomon.
Rehoboam married Mahalath, and her parents were Jerimoth and Abihail. Jerimoth was David's son, and Abihail was the daughter of Jesse's son Eliab.
She gave birth to his children Jeush, Shamariah, and Zaham.
After her, he married Absalom's daughter Maachah who gave birth to his children Abijah, Attai, Ziza, and Shelomith.
Rehoboam loved Absalom's daughter Maachah above all his other wives and concubines. Altogether he had eighteen wives and sixty concubines, and fathered twenty-eight sons and sixty daughters.
Rehoboam appointed Maachah's son Abijah the chief and ruler from among his brothers, because he intended to make him king.
He wisely dispersed all of his children throughout all the countries of Judah and Benjamin. They were sent to every fortified city where he abundantly supplied them, and he desired many wives.
When Rehoboam had the kingdom firmly established and he had consolidated his power, he abandoned the Lord's law, and took all Israel with him.
In the fifth year of King Rehoboam's reign, King Shishak of Egypt attacked Jerusalem because the Israelis had sinned against the Lord.
They came with 1,200 chariots, 60,000 horsemen and an army too numerous to count came with him from Egypt plus the Libyans, the Sukkiims, and the Ethiopians.
He captured the fortified cities in Judah, then went to Jerusalem.

Then Shemaiah the prophet went to Rehoboam and the princes of Judah, who had gathered together in Jerusalem to escape King Shishak and said to them, "This is what the Lord says, 'You have forsaken me, so I have left you in Shishak's hands.'"
On hearing this the king and the Israelis leaders humbled themselves and said, "The Lord is righteous!"

When the Lord saw that they had humbled themselves, the Lord's word came to Shemaiah and said, "They have humbled themselves, so I will not destroy them, but I will grant them deliverance, and my anger will not be poured out on Jerusalem through Shishak.
Nevertheless they will be his servants, so that they will know the difference between serving me and serving the kingdoms of other countries."

So King Shishak of Egypt attacked Jerusalem, and took the treasures from the Lord's temple and the king's palace, he took everything and he also carried away all the gold shields that Solomon had made.
Then King Rehoboam had brass shields made to replace them, and gave them to the guards commanders, who were stationed at the entrance of the king's palace.
Whenever the king entered the Lord's temple, the guards went with him carrying the shields, and then they returned them to the guard' armory.
After King Rehoboam humbled himself, the Lord's anger turned away from him, so that he was not completely destroyed, and things also went well in Judah.

So King Rehoboam established himself in Jerusalem. He was forty-one years old when he began to reign and he reigned in Jerusalem for seventeen years. He reigned in the city which the Lord had chosen from all the other tribes of Israel, to put his name on. His mother's name was Naamah the Ammonite.
Rehoboam did evil, because he did not prepare his heart to seek the Lord.

All the acts of Rehoboam, from first to last, are written in the book of Shemaiah the prophet, and the records of Iddo the prophet concerning the genealogies. There were wars between Rehoboam and Jeroboam continuously throughout their days.
Then Rehoboam died and slept with his fathers, and was buried in the city of David, and his son Abijah reigned in his place.
In the eighteenth year of King Jeroboam's reign, Abijah began to reign over Judah.
Abijah reigned for three years in Jerusalem, and his mother's name was Micaiah the daughter of Uriel of Gibeah. And there was war between Abijah and Jeroboam.
Abijah assembled an army of 400,000 courageous men conscripted and prepared for war. Jeroboam also conscripted an army with 800,000 mighty men of valor who were arrayed in formation against him.
Abijah stood on Mount Zemaraim, which is part of Mount Ephraim and said, "Hear me, O Jeroboam, and everyone in Israel.
You should know by now that the Lord God of Israel has given the kingdom of Israel to King David and his descendants forever, which was established by a covenant of salt!
But Nebat's son Jeroboam, the servant of King David's son Solomon has risen up and rebelled against his Lord.
Jeroboam has assembled an army of vain men from Belial's descendants, and they attacked Solomon's son Rehoboam when he was young and inexperienced, and he could not defend himself.

And now you think you can withstand the Lord's kingdom, which is in the hands of David's descendants. Yes, you are a great army, and you have your golden calves with you that Jeroboam made to be your gods.

You drove out the Lord's priests, the Levites, and Aaron's sons. And you made priests for yourselves like the people from other nations do. Now whoever wants, can come and consecrate himself with a young bull and seven rams and become a priest of those that are not gods.
But as for us, the Lord is our God and we have not forsaken him, and the priests who minister to the Lord are Aaron's sons, and the Levites attend to their business.

They burn sweet incense and burnt offerings to the Lord every morning and every evening. The priests also set their bread offerings in order on the purified table. Every evening they light the lamps on the gold lampstands, because we perform the services required by our Lord God, but you have forsaken him.
And behold, God himself is with us as our leader, and his priests sound the battle trumpets to warn you O children of Israel, do not attack the Lord God of your fathers, because you will not win."
But Jeroboam had laid an ambush behind them, so as they were facing Judah the ambush was behind them.
When Judah looked back, he saw that the battle was behind him and in front of him, and they cried out to the Lord, and the priests sounded the trumpets.
Then the men of Judah gave a great shout and as they shouted, God defeated Jeroboam and all of Israel before Abijah and Judah.
The Israelis fled before Judah, and God delivered them into Judah's hands.
Abijah and his people slaughtered them, and 500,000 Israelis men of war died.
This was how the Israelis were brought down at that time and Judah's descendants prevailed because they relied on the Lord God of their fathers.
Abijah pursued Jeroboam and captured the cities of Bethel with its towns, Jeshanah with its towns, and Ephraim with its towns from him.
During the days of Abijah, Jeroboam never did recover his strength and the Lord struck him down, and he died.
But Abijah grew mighty and married fourteen wives, he had twenty-two sons and sixteen daughters.
All the acts of Abijah, his ways and his sayings are written in the records of Iddo the prophet.
Then Abijah died and slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the city of David, and his son Asa reigned in his place. In his day the land was at peace for ten years.
King Asa did that which was good and righteous in the eyes of his Lord God.
Because he removed the altars of the strange gods and the high places, he tore down the images and he cut down the Asherah poles.
He commanded Judah to seek the Lord God of their fathers, and to obey the law and commandments.
He also removed the high places and the images from all the cities of Judah, and his kingdom was at peace.
King Asa built fortified cities in Judah because the land was at peace. In those days there was no war because the Lord had given him rest.

So Asa said to the people of Judah, "Let us build these cities and surround them with walls and install towers and gates with bars, and the land is still before us, because we sought our Lord God. We have sought him and he has given us rest on every side." So they built and prospered.
Asa had an army of 300,000 men that carried shields and spears from Judah 300,000, and 280,000 men from Benjamin that carried shields and drew bows. And they were all mighty men of valor.
One day Zerah the Ethiopian attacked them with an army of 1,000,000 men and 300 chariots, and they advanced all the way to Mareshah.
Then Asa marched against him arrayed for battle in the valley of Zephathah at Mareshah.

Asa cried to his Lord God and said, "O Lord, it is nothing for you to help the powerless against the many. Help us O Lord our God, because we rely on you, and in your name we are going up against this vast army. O Lord, you are our God, do not let them prevail against you."
So the Lord defeated the Ethiopians before Asa and Judah, and they fled.

Asa and his army pursued them to Gerar, and the Ethiopians were overpowered, and they could not recover because they had been destroyed before the Lord and his army, and they carried away tremendous spoils of war.
Then they defeated all the cities around Gerar because the Lord's fear came upon them, and they took vast amounts of the spoils of war from all the cities, because there was so much there to take.
They also attacked the herdsmen's tents and carried away an abundance of cattle, sheep, and camels and returned to Jerusalem.
And the Spirit of God came upon Oded's son Azariah.

Azariah went to speak Asa and said, "Asa, I want you and all of Judah and Benjamin to listen to me, the Lord is with you as long as you are with him. If you seek him you will find him, but if you forsake him, he will forsake you.
For a long time now Israel has been without the true God, without a teaching priest, and without the law.
But when they were in trouble they turned to the Lord God of Israel, and when they sought him they found him.
In those times there was no peace for travelers, nor anyone else because there were many conflicts throughout the land.
And nation destroyed nation city by city, because God frustrated them with all kinds of adversity.
So be strong, and do not be discouraged because your work will be rewarded."

When Asa heard Oded's son's prophecy, he was encouraged and had all the abominable idols removed from the land of Judah, Benjamin, and the cities which he had captured on Mount Ephraim. And he restored the Lord's altar that stood before the Lord's entrance hall.

Then Asa gathered everyone together from Judah and Benjamin, and the foreigners from Ephraim, Manasseh, and Simeon. Because great numbers of people came to join him from Israel, when they saw that his Lord God was with him.
So they gathered together in Jerusalem in the third month of the 50th year of the reign of King Asa.
At the same time they offered the Lord all the spoils of war they had captured, including 700 oxen and 7,000 sheep.
And they entered into a covenant to seek the Lord God of their fathers with all their heart and soul.
They passed a law that whoever refused to seek the Lord God of Israel would be put to death, whether they were great or small, or whether they were man or woman.
And they swore an oath to the Lord with a loud voice with trumpets, much shouting, and maracas.
Everyone in Judah rejoiced over the oath, because they swore with all their heart and soul to seek God, and they found him and the Lord gave them rest all around.
King Asa also removed his grandmother Maachah as queen, because she had made an idol of an Asherah pole and Asa cut it down, ground it up, and burned it at the Brook of Kidron.
But he did not remove the high places from Israel, nevertheless King Asa's heart was perfect with the Lord for all his days.
And he brought the things that his he and his father had dedicated into the house of God, including all the gold and silver vessels.
And there was no more war to the 35th year of the reign of Asa.
In the 36th year of the reign of King Asa, King Baasha of Israel attacked Judah and built Ramah, his intent was to prevent anyone from going to or leaving from King Asa of Judah.
Then Asa sent gold and silver from the treasuries of the Lord's temple and the king's palace to King Ben-Hadad of Syria in Damascus.

And he sent them a message and said, "Let us make a treaty between me and you, as there was between my father and your father. Behold the gold and silver I have sent you to break your treaty with King Baasha of Israel, then he will withdraw his troops from me."
Ben-Hadad listened to King Asa, and sent his commanders and armies to attack the cities of Israel. Then they defeated Ijon, Dan, Abelmaim and all the storehouse cities of Naphtali.
When King Baasha heard what had happened, he stopped building in Ramah and his work ceased.
Then King Asa captured all of Judah, and they carried away the stones and timber that King Baasha was using to build with in Ramah, Geba, and Mizpah.
At that time Hanani the prophet came to King Asa of Judah and said, "Because you have relied on the king of Syria and not your Lord God, the king of Syria's armies have escaped from your hands.
Were not the Ethiopians and Lubims a huge army with many chariots and horsemen? But, because you relied on the Lord, he delivered them into your hands.

For the eyes of the Lord run back and forth throughout the earth, to show himself strong in the behalf of those whose hearts are perfect toward him. You have acted foolishly, so from now on you will have wars."
Then King Asa became angry with the prophet and put him in prison, because he was enraged at him for what he said, and Asa also oppressed some of the people at the same time.
And behold all of the acts of Asa from the first to the last are written in the Book of the Kings of Judah and the Book of the Kings of Israel.
In the 39th year of King Asa's reign his feet became miserably diseased, but he never sought the Lord's help with his disease, but he turned to the physicians instead.
And Asa died and slept with his fathers in the 41st year of his reign.

They buried him in his own tomb which he'd had made for himself in the city of David. They laid him in a casket filled with sweet scents and various spices prepared by the apothecaries, and they burned a great fire in his honor.
Asa's son Jehoshaphat reigned in his place, and he consolidated his power against Israel.
He stationed garrisons of troops in all the fortified cities and throughout Judah, and in all the cities his father Asa had captured from Ephraim.
The Lord was with Jehoshaphat, because he walked in the first ways of his father David, and did not seek Baalim.
But he sought the Lord God of his father and walked in his commandments, and did not commit the abominations of Israel.
So the Lord established the kingdom in his hand, and all of Judah brought presents to Jehoshaphat, and he had an abundance of riches and honor.
His heart was delighted with the ways of the Lord, plus he removed the high places and Asherah poles from Judah.
In the 3rd year of his reign he also sent his wise officials Benhail, Obadiah, Zechariah, Nathaniel, and Micaiah to teach in the cities of Judah.
And he sent with them the Levites: Shemaiah, Nethaniah, Zebadiah, Asahel, Shemiramoth, Jehonathan, Adonijah, Tobijah, and Tob-Adonijah. The Levite priests Elishama and Jehoram also went with them.
They taught the people from the Book of the Law of the Lord throughout all the cities of Judah.
All the kingdoms around Judah feared the Lord so greatly, that they were too afraid to make war against Jehoshaphat.
Some of the Philistines also brought Jehoshaphat tribute and gifts of silver, and the Arabians brought him 7,700 rams and 7,700 male goats from their flocks.
Jehoshaphat's kingdom grew tremendously, and he built fortresses and city storehouses throughout Judah.
He had tremendous business and storehouses in the cities of Judah, and warriors who were mighty men of valor in Jerusalem.
These are their numbers according to their father's house: Judah was the commander of 1,000's, and Adnah was the chief commander of 300,000 mighty men of valor.
Next to him was captain Jehohanan who commanded 280,000 warriors.
Next to him was Zichri's son Amasiah, who willingly offered himself to the Lord along with his 200,000 mighty men of valor.
Eliada came from Benjamin, he was a mighty man of valor, and he commanded 200,000 men armed with bow and shields.
Next him was Jehozabad who commanded 180,000 men ready and prepared for the war.
These men served the king, in addition to those who the king stationed in the fortified cities throughout Judah.
King Jehoshaphat had an abundance of riches and honor, and he had an alliance with King Ahab.

A few years later Jehoshaphat went to visit King Ahab in Samaria, and Ahab sacrificed an abundance of sheep and oxen for him and the people with him, and he asked Ahab to go with him to Ramoth-Gilead.

King Ahab of Israel spoke to King Jehoshaphat of Judah and asked, "Will you go with me to Ramoth-Gilead?" And Jehoshaphat replied, "I am like you, and my people are like your people, and we will fight with you in the war."
Then Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, "I pray you will first ask for the Lord's word on this matter before you commit."

So the king of Israel summoned 400 prophets and said to them, "Should we or should we not go to war in Ramoth-Gilead? They answered him and said, "Go, because God will deliver them into the king's hands."
But King Jehoshaphat said, "Is there not a different prophet of the Lord here that we can ask?"

The king of Israel responded to King Jehoshaphat and said, "There is one more man that we can inquire about the Lord, but I hate him, because he never prophesied anything good to me, but always evil. His name is Micaiah the son of Imla and King Jehoshaphat said, "The king should not say such things about a prophet of God."
So the king of Israel summoned one of his officers and said, "Bring Imla's son Micaiah to me quickly."

The king of Israel and King Jehoshaphat of Judah sat together on their thrones, dressed in their royal robes near the threshing room floor by the entrance of the gates of Samaria, and all the prophets prophesied before them.
Chenaanah's son Zedekiah made some iron horns and said, "This is what the Lord says, 'You can use these horns to push Syria until they have been consumed.'"
Then all the prophets prophesied and said, "Go to Ramoth-Gilead and prosper, because the Lord will deliver it into the king's hands."

The messenger sent to summon Micaiah spoke to him and said, "Behold the prophets speak with one voice to the king and they all declare good things, so I pray you will also say good things to the king."
And Micaiah said, "As the Lord lives, I will speak whatever my God says."

When Micaiah went to the king, the king asked him, "Micaiah, should we or should we not go to war in Ramoth-Gilead?" And he replied and said, "Go and you will prosper, and they will be delivered into your hands."
And the king spoke back to him and said, "Micaiah, how many times must I tell you to tell me nothing but the truth in the Lord's name?"
Then Micaiah said, "I saw all of Israel scattered on the mountains as sheep without a shepherd. And the Lord said, 'They have no master, let them return to their homes in peace.'"
And the king of Israel said to King Jehoshaphat, "Did I not tell you that he would not prophesy anything good to me, but only evil?"
Again Micaiah said, "So, hear the word of the Lord, I saw the Lord sitting on his throne, and all the armies of heaven standing at his right and left hand.
And the Lord said, 'Who will tempt King Ahab of Israel into going up to fall at Ramoth-Gilead?' And each one spoke up one after the other saying different things.
Then a spirit there came and stood before the Lord and said, 'I will tempt him!' And the Lord said to him, 'How will you do this?'
And he replied, 'I will leave go to be a lying spirit in the mouths of all his prophets.' And the Lord said, 'You will tempt him and you will prevail, so go and do this thing.'
Now behold, the Lord has put a lying spirit in the mouths of your prophets, and the Lord has spoken evil against you."
Then Chenaanah's son Zedekiah smacked Micaiah across the cheek and said, "Which way did the Lord's Spirit go when he left me to speak to you?"
And Micaiah said, "Behold, you will see that on the day that you try to hide yourself in an inner chamber."
Then the king of Israel said, "Take Micaiah back to Amon the governor of the city and the king's son Joash
And tell them that the king says, 'Put this fellow in prison, and feed him nothing but the bread and water of affliction, until I return in peace.'"
But Micaiah spoke up and said, "If you return in peace then the Lord has not spoken through me!" He also said, "Everyone, please listen to me!"
So the king of Israel and King Jehoshaphat of Judah went to Ramoth-Gilead.
The king of Israel spoke to Jehoshaphat and said, "I will disguise myself and go into battle, but you should wear your royal robes." So the king of Israel disguised himself and they went into battle.
Now the king of Syria had given his chariot commanders their orders and said, "Do not attack anyone great or small, except the king of Israel."

When the chariot commanders saw King Jehoshaphat they said, that is the king of Israel, so they surrounded him to attack. But Jehoshaphat cried out and the Lord helped him, and God moved them away from him.
When the chariot commanders realized that he was not the king of Israel, they turned back and stopped pursuing him.

However, an archer drew his bow and fired an arrow without aiming, and struck the king of Israel between the joints of his armor. Then the king said to his chariot driver, "Turn around and carry me out of the battle, because I am wounded."
The battle continued to intensify that day, but the king of Israel stayed in his chariot fighting the Syrians until the evening, and at about sunset he died.
King Jehoshaphat of Judah returned in peace to his house in Jerusalem.
Hanani the prophet's son Jehu went to meet King Jehoshaphat and said to him, "Should you help the ungodly and love those that hate the Lord? That's why, the Lord's wrath has come upon you.
Nevertheless, there are good things about you because you have removed the Asherah poles from the land, and you have prepared your heart to seek God."
Jehoshaphat lived in Jerusalem, and he went out among the people from Beersheba to Mount Ephraim, and returned them to the Lord God of their fathers.
He assigned judges throughout the land in all the fortified cities of Judah.
And said to the judges, "Be careful of what you decide because you do not judge for man, but you judge for the Lord who is with you when you make your judgments.
So let the fear of the Lord be with you and consider your judgements carefully, because there is no immorality, partiality, or bribery with our Lord God."
Besides that, Jehoshaphat appointed some of the Levites, priests, and chief fathers of Israel in Jerusalem to judge on the Lord's behalf and settle disputes, when they returned to Jerusalem.
Jehoshaphat addressed them and said, "You must serve faithfully and with a perfect heart in fear of the Lord."

Because whatever dispute comes before you, whether it comes from your brothers who live in your cities, or it is between blood relatives, or it is about the law, commandments, judgments, or ordinances you must warn them not to trespass against the Lord, so that his anger does not come upon you and your brothers. Do this and you will not trespass against the Lord.

Amariah the chief priest will be over you in everything that matters to the Lord. Ishmael's son Zebadiah the ruler of the house of Judah will be over anything that matters to the king, and the Levites will also be officers before you. Deal courageously, and the Lord will be with the good!"
After all this, Moab's descendants, Ammon's descendants, and others with them besides the Ammonites attacked Jehoshaphat in battle.

Then some men came to Jehoshaphat and said, "There is a vast army coming to attack you from beyond the sea on this side Syria, and they are already in Hazazon-Tamar." Hazazon-Tamar is also known as En-Gedi.
Jehoshaphat was afraid, and he went to seek the Lord and proclaimed a fast throughout all of Judah.
All of Judah gathered together to ask the Lord for his help, and they came from every city in Judah to seek the Lord.
Jehoshaphat stood before the new courtyard in the Lord's temple, in the midst of the congregation of Judah and Jerusalem.

And Jehoshaphat spoke to the Lord and said, "O Lord God of our fathers, are you not God in heaven, and do you not rule over all the kingdoms of the heathen, and is there not the power and might in your hands, so that no one can withstand you?
Are you not our God, who drove the inhabitants of this land out before your people Israel, and gave it to your friend Abraham's descendants forever?
And they lived in there, and have built you a sanctuary in there for your name and said.

And they said, 'If evil comes upon us, whether it is the sword, judgment, pestilence, or famine, we will stand before this temple in your presence, because your name is here. And we will cry out to you in our affliction, and you will hear us and help us.'
And now, these people from Ammon, Moab, and Mount Seir who you would not let Israel invade when they left Egypt. So they turned away from them, and they did not destroyed them.
Behold, how they reward us by coming to drive us out of your possession, that you gave us as an inheritance.
O our God, will you not judge them? Because, we do not have the strength to confront this great company that comes to attack us, nor do we know what to do, so our eyes are on you."
Everyone in Judah stood before the Lord with their children and their wives.

Then the Lord's Spirit came upon Zechariah's son Jahaziel who was a Levite from the sons of Asaph, as he stood in the middle of the congregation. Zechariah was Benaiah's son, who was Jeiel's son, who was Mattaniah's son.

And Jahaziel said, "Listen to King Jehoshaphat, all you who live in Judah and Jerusalem because this is what the Lord says, 'Do not be afraid nor discouraged by this great army, because this battle is not yours, but it is God's.
Tomorrow you will go down to attack them. They will be coming up by the cliff of Ziz, and you will find them at the end of the brook facing the wilderness of Jeruel.

You will not need to fight in this battle, just setup your formation and stand still, and you will see the Lord's salvation with you. O Judah and Jerusalem, fear not nor be discouraged, tomorrow leave to attack them, because the Lord will be with you.
Then Jehoshaphat bowed his head facedown to the ground, and all the inhabitants of Judah and Jerusalem fell facedown on the ground worshipping the Lord.
And the Levites, Kohathites, and Korhites stood up to praise the Lord God of Israel with a loud voice on high.

They got up early in the morning and went out into the wilderness of Tekoa. As they were leaving Jehoshaphat stood up and said, "Hear me O Judah and you inhabitants of Jerusalem, believe in your Lord God so you will be established, and believe his prophets so you will prosper."

After he consulted with the people, he appointed singers to the Lord to praise the beauty of his Holiness. As they went out before the army they sang, "Praise the Lord, because his mercy endures forever."
As they began to sing and praise the Lord, the Lord set ambushes against the people of Ammon, Moab, and Mount Seir who had attacked Judah, and they were defeated.

Because the people of Ammon and Moab attacked and completely destroyed the inhabitants of Mount Seir. After they destroyed the inhabitants of Mount Seir, they turned on each other and destroyed one another.
When Judah marched toward the watch tower in the wilderness, they looked toward the army, and they saw dead bodies on the ground everywhere, and no one escaped.

When Jehoshaphat and his people came to take away the spoils of war from them, they found an abundance of both riches and precious jewels with the dead bodies. They stripped off more riches than they could carry away for themselves, and there was so much spoils of war that it took them three days to gather it all up.
On the fourth day they gathered together in the Valley of Berachah to bless the Lord. That's why that place is called the Valley of Berachah to this very day.
Then all the men of Judah and Jerusalem returned with Jehoshaphat leading the way, and they joyfully returned to Jerusalem, because the Lord had made them rejoice over their enemies.
So they returned to the Lord's temple in Jerusalem with lyres, harps, and trumpets.
And the fear of God was upon all the kingdoms of the defeated countries, when they heard that the Lord had fought against the enemies of Israel.
So the realm of Jehoshaphat was quiet, because his God gave him rest all around.
Jehoshaphat reigned over Judah for twenty-five years in Jerusalem, he was thirty-five years old when he began to reign. His mother's name was Azubah and she was Shilhi's daughter.
He walked in the ways of his father Asa, and never stopped doing what he thought was righteous in the Lord's sight.
However he had not removed the high places, because the people had not yet prepared their hearts to accept the God of their fathers.
The rest of the acts of Jehoshaphat from the first to the last, are all written in the Book of Jehu who was Hanani's son, which is also recorded in the Book of the Kings of Israel.
After all this, King Jehoshaphat of Judah formed an alliance with King Ahaziah of Israel, who did very wicked things.
Jehoshaphat formed an alliance with Ahaziah to build ships to go to Tarshish, and they built the ships in Ezion-Geber.

Then Dodavah's son Eliezer of Mareshah prophesied against Jehoshaphat and said, "Because you have allied yourself with Ahaziah, the Lord has destroyed your work!" So the ships wrecked and they were unable to sail to Tarshish.
Jehoshaphat died and slept with his fathers, and he was buried with his fathers in the city of David, and his son Jehoram reigned in his place.
Jehoram's brothers who were Jehoshaphat's sons were: Azariah, Jehiel, Zechariah, Azariah, Michael, and Shephatiah. They were all King Jehoshaphat's sons of Israel.
Their father gave them tremendous gifts of gold, silver, and other precious things along with fortified cities in Judah. But he gave the kingdom to Jehoram, because he was his firstborn son.
When Jehoram took over his father's kingdom, he consolidated his power by killing all his brothers and other Israelis leaders with the sword.
Jehoram was thirty-two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned for eight years in Jerusalem.
Jehoram walked in the ways of the kings of Israel, just like the house of Ahab. Because he had married Ahab's daughter and worked evil in the eyes of the Lord.
However, the Lord did not want to destroy the house of David, because of the covenant that he had made with David, and as he had promised to give a light to David and his sons forever.
In his day the Edomites revolted against the rule of Judah, and made a king for themselves.
Then Jehoram, his princes, and all his chariots marched with him into Edom by night, and defeated the Edomites when they surrounded him and his chariot commanders.
So to this day the Edomites have revolted from under the rule of Judah. And at the same time Libnah also revolted from under his hand, because he had forsaken the Lord God of his fathers.
Besides that, he built high places in the mountains of Judah and caused the inhabitants of Jerusalem to chase after false gods, which caused Judah to veer away from the path of truth.

One day Elijah the prophet wrote a letter to Jehoram which and said, "This is what the Lord God of your father David says, 'Because you have not walked in the ways of your father Jehoshaphat, nor in the ways of King Asa of Judah.

But you have walked in the ways of the kings of Israel, and you have caused Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem to go a whoring, just as the house of Ahab prostituted itself. And because you have also killed your brothers from your father's house, who were better than you.
Behold, the Lord will defeat your people, your children, and your wives with a great plague, and everything you own will be destroyed.
Day after day, you will be overcome with a terrible bowel disease until your bowels fall out on the ground.'"
Besides that, the Lord stirred up the spirits of the Philistines and the Arabians who lived near the Ethiopians against Jehoram.

And they marched into Judah and tore it down, and they carried away anything of substance that they found in the king's palace. Including his sons and wives, so that he had no sons left except for his youngest son Jehoahaz.
After all this the Lord attacked his bowels with an incurable disease.
Two years later, his diseased bowels fell out and he died of many terrible diseases. His people did not build a memorial fire to burn for him, like they had for his fathers.

Jehoram was thirty-two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned in Jerusalem for eight years, but when he died nobody cared. However they did bury him in the city of David, but not in the tombs of the kings.

The people of Jerusalem made King Jehoram's son Ahaziah their king instead of him, because the raiders who came with the Arabs to attack them had killed all his other sons. So King Jehoram's son Ahaziah became the king of Judah.
Ahaziah was forty-two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned for one year in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Athaliah and she was Omri's daughter.
He also walked in the ways of the house of Ahab, because his mother taught him to be a wicked man.
So he did evil in the Lord's sight just like the house of Ahab, and he was destroyed because they were his counselors after his father died.
Joram also walked in their ways and followed their counsel, and he went to war with King Ahab's son Joram of Israel against King Hazael of Syria at Ramoth-Gilead, and the Syrians wounded him.

Joram returned to Jezreel so the wounds he received in Ramah when he fought King Hazael of Syria could heal. And King Jehoram's son Azariah of Judah went down to see Ahab's son Joram in Jezreel because he was sick.
Ahaziah's destruction came from God when he went to see Joram. Because when he arrived he went with Joram to attack Nimshi's son Jehu, whom the Lord had anointed to destroy the house of Ahab.
While Jehu was executing judgment on the house of Ahab, he found the leaders of Judah and the sons of Ahaziah's brothers who ministered to Ahaziah, and he killed them.

He searched for Ahaziah and caught him, because he had hidden in Samaria. They brought him to Jehu, and they buried him after they killed him because they said, "He is the son of Jehoshaphat, who sought the Lord with all his heart." So there was no one left from the house of Ahaziah with the power to rule the kingdom.
But when Ahaziah's mother Athaliah saw that her son was dead, she got up and destroyed all the royal descendants from the house of Judah.

But King Jehoram's daughter Jehoshabeath rescued Ahaziah's son Joash, and she hid him and his nurse from Athaliah in a bedroom away from the king's other sons who were killed. So King Jehoram's daughter Jehoshabeath who was married to priest Jehoiada was Ahaziah's sister, and she hid Joash from Athaliah, and she could not find him to kill him.
And they hid him and the others in the house of God for six years, while Athaliah reigned over the land.

In the seventh year the priest Jehoiada consolidated his power and made a covenant with the commanders of hundreds, Jeroham's son Azariah, Jehohanan's son Ishmael, Obed's son Azariah, Adaiah's son Maaseiah, and Zichri's son Elishaphat.
After that they went to Judah where they assembled the Levites and the chief fathers of Israel from all the cities of Judah, then they went to Jerusalem.

The entire congregation made a covenant with the king in the house of God and Jehoiada said to them, "Behold King David's descendant Joash must reign, because the Lord promised this for his descendants.
This is what you must do: One third of the priests and Levites on duty during the Sabbath will be the entrance gatekeepers.
One third will be stationed at the king's palace, and one third will be stationed at the foundation gate, while everyone else is in the courtyards of the Lord's temple.
But no one will be allowed to enter the Lord's temple except the priests and the Levites who serve them because they are Holy, but all people are required to obey the Lord.
The Levites must surround the king with their weapons in their hands, and anyone else that enters the temple must be put to death. But you must stay with the king as he enters and leaves the temple."

So the Levites and everyone in Judah did everything that the priest Jehoiada commanded. And the commanders kept all their men there on the Sabbath including those who were off duty, because Jehoiada had not dismissed any of the divisions.
Besides that, Jehoiada the priest large and small shields and spears delivered to the commanders that King David had stored in the house of God.
He stationed all his men with their weapons in their hands, surrounding the king in the temple along the altar, and outside all around the temple.
Then they brought out the king's son and put the crown on his head, and declared him as king, and Jehoiada and his sons anointed him and said, "God save the king!"
When Athaliah heard all the noise that the people made while they were running around and praising the king, she went to the people in the Lord's temple.

She looked and saw the king standing at his column at the entrance. The officers and trumpeters stood beside the king, and everyone rejoiced and blew their trumpets, as the singers with their musical instruments sang praises. Then Athaliah tore her clothes and screamed, "Treason, treason!"

Then Jehoiada the priest sent the army commanders to remove her from the temple and he said to them, "Remove her from this area and kill all her followers with the sword. The priest also said, "Do not kill her or her followers in the Lord's temple!"
So they seized her as she reached the entrance of the horse gate at the king's palace, and that's where they killed her.
Then Jehoiada made a covenant between him, the people, and the king that promised that they would be the Lord's people.
Then the people marched to the house of Baal and tore it down. They smashed all of Baal's altars and images into pieces, and killed his priest Mattan before the altars.

Jehoiada also appointed the officers of the Lord's temple who would be supervised by the Levite priests, whom David appointed over the Lord's temple to offer the Lord's burnt offerings as it is written in the Law of Moses, with rejoicing and singing as it was ordained by David.
He stationed the gatekeepers at the gates of the Lord's temple, so that no one who is unclean in any way could enter the temple.

Jehoiada and the army commanders, the nobles, the people's governors, and all the people brought King Joash down from the Lord's temple. When they entered the king's palace through the upper gates, they seated him on the kingdom's royal throne.
All the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was quiet and at peace after they killed Athaliah with the sword.
Joash was seven years old when he began to reign, and he reigned for forty years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Zibiah of Beersheba.
Joash did what he thought was righteous in the Lord's sight for all the days of priest Jehoiada's life.
Jehoiada married two wives, and he fathered sons and daughters.
A short time after this, Joash decided to strengthen the Lord's temple.

King Joash summoned the priests and Levites and said, "Go to the cities of Judah and collect all the annual tax money needed from Israel to rebuild the house of your God, and do it quickly." However the Levites were in no hurry to get this done.

So the king summoned Jehoiada the high priest and said, "Why have you not required the Levites to collect the taxes for the Tabernacle of Witness, from the Israelis congregation in Judah and Jerusalem as the Lord's servant Moses commanded which is also required by the assembly of Israel?"
Because the wicked Athaliah's sons had left the house of God in a pile of ruble, and they had also used all the dedicated things from the Lord's temple to worship Baalim.
The king ordered them to build a chest, and they set it outside the gates of the Lord's temple.
Then they proclaimed throughout Judah and Jerusalem for the people to bring to the Lord, the taxes that God's servant Moses had imposed on Israel in the wilderness.
All the leaders and the people rejoiced, and they brought in their taxes and threw them into the chest, until it was full.

When the Levites brought the chest to the king's office and they saw all the money, the king's scribe and the high priest's officer came and emptied the chest. Then they carried it back out to its place at the gate, and this was how they collected such an abundance of money day after day.

The king and Jehoiada gave the money to the people who supervised the work in the service of the Lord's temple and they used it to hire masons, carpenters, iron workers, and brass workers to rebuild the Lord's temple.
So the workmen worked and their work progressed, and they restored the house of God to its former glory and reinforced its structure.

When they finished the work, they brought the rest of the money to the king and Jehoiada. They had many gold and silver vessels, spoons, and bowls made to minister in the Lord's temple. And they regularly offered burnt offerings in the Lord's temple during Jehoiada's entire lifetime.
But Jehoiada was 130 years old when he died.
And they buried him in the city of David among the kings, because he had done many good things in Israel, for both God and God's house.
After Jehoiada died the leaders of Judah went to the king and paid tribute to him. Then the king listened to them.
And they abandoned the Lord's temple, the God of their fathers, and they worshipped Asherah poles and idols. This caused the Lord's anger to come upon Judah and Jerusalem for their trespass.
But the Lord sent prophets to bring the people back to the Lord, and they testified against their sin, but the people would not listen.

The Spirit of God came upon priest Jehoiada's son Zechariah. He stood on a pulpit above the people and said, "This is what the Lord God says, 'Why have you transgressed against the commandments of the Lord, so that you cannot prosper?' It is because you have forsaken the Lord, that he has also forsaken you!"
Then they conspired against Zechariah, and at the king's command they stoned him to death in the courtyard of the Lord's temple.

King Joash had not remembered the kindness which Zechariah's father Jehoiada had shown him, and the king killed Jehoiada's son. And as he died he said, "May the Lord see you and repay you for what you have done!"

At the end of the year, the Syrian army came and attacked King Joash. They invaded Judah and Jerusalem and killed the people's leaders, and they sent all the spoils of war back to their king in Damascus.

The Syrian army came with a small company of men, and the Lord delivered a vast army into their hands, because Judah had forsaken the Lord God of their fathers. So they executed judgment against Joash.

After the Syrians left, he was grievously wounded and in great distress. But his own servants conspired against him for murdering the priest Jehoiada's son, and they killed him on his bed. He died, and they buried him in the city of David, but they did not bury him in the tombs of the kings.
These are the ones that conspired against Joash, there was Shimeath's whose mother was Zabad the Ammonite and Jehozabad whose mother was Shimrith the Moabite.
The story of Joash's sons, and the great burden laid on him to rebuild the house of God, are all written in the Book of the Kings, and his son Amaziah reigned in his place.
Amaziah was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned for twenty-nine years in Jerusalem, and his mother's name was Jehoaddan of Jerusalem.
He did what he thought was righteous in the Lord's sight, but not with a perfect heart.
After he established his kingdom, he killed his servants that had killed his father King Joash.

But he did not kill their children, because he obeyed what was written in the law in the Book of Moses, where the Lord's commandment said, "The fathers will not die for the sins of the children, and the children will not die for the sins of the fathers, but each man will die for his own sin."

Then Amaziah gathered everyone from Judah together and appointed army commanders over 1000's and 100's, in accordance with their fathers' houses throughout Judah and Benjamin. He had everyone counted that was 20 years old and older, and conscripted 300,000 men who he trained for war so they could handle a spear and shield.
He also hired 100,000 mighty men of valor from Israel for 100 silver talents.
But a man of God came to him and said, "O king, do not take the army of Israel with you, because the Lord is not with Israel or the descendants of Ephraim.
But even if you go and fight bravely the battle, God will make you fall before the enemy, because God has power to help and power to overthrow."

Amaziah replied to the man of God and said, "But what should we do about the hundred talents which I have already given the army of Israel?" And the man of God answered, "The Lord can give you much more than this."
Then Amaziah divided up the army and he sent those who had come from Ephraim back home. This made them very angry at Judah, and they returned home in great anger.
Amaziah consolidated his power, then he led his people into the valley of salt and defeated 10,000 of Seir's tribesmen.
The army of Judah captured 10,000 men alive and carried them away as captives. They took them to the top of the rock, and threw them off the cliff, and they were all broken into pieces.

But the soldiers that Amaziah removed from the ranks and sent home attacked the cities of Judah from Samaria all the way to Beth-Horon. They killed 3,000 of them, and carried away a tremendous amount of the spoils of war.
After Amaziah returned from the slaughter of the Edomites, he brought the gods from the descendants of Seir and set them up as his gods. He bowed down before them, and burned incense to them.

This kindled the Lord's anger against Amaziah, and he sent a prophet to him who said, "Why have you been worshipping the gods of those people, who could not even deliver their own people from your hands?"

As he talked with him the king asked, "Did we make you the king's counselor? Stop now, why should you be killed?" Then the prophet held back and said, "I know that God has decided to destroy you, because you have done this and you have not listened to me."

Then King Amaziah of Judah took his counselors advice and sent a message to King Joash of Israel and said, "Come, let us meet face to face." King Joash was King Jehoahaz's son, and King Jehoahaz was King Jehu's son.

King Joash of Israel replied to King Amaziah of Judah and said, "A thistle in Lebanon sent a message to the cedar in Lebanon and said, "Give your daughter's hand in marriage to my son to be his wife, and a wild beast was passing through Lebanon, and trampled all over the thistle.

You say you have defeated the Edomites, and your conceited heart makes you boast. So you should just stay home. Why should you meddle in your neighbor's affairs which will only cause you to fall and take Judah with you?"
But Amaziah would not listen because his overconfidence came from God, so that he could deliver Judah into the hands of their enemies, because they worshipped Edom's gods.
So King Joash of Israel and King Amaziah of Judah attacked each other face to face at Beth-Shemesh in Judah.
Judah was defeated by Israel, and they all fled to their tents.

King Joash of Israel captured King Amaziah of Judah at Beth-Shemesh and brought him to Jerusalem. Joash tore down 400 cubits of the wall of Jerusalem from the gates of Ephraim to the gate corners. King Amaziah was King Joash's son, who was King Jehoahaz's son.

Joash took all the gold and silver, and all the vessels he found in the house of God that Obed-Edom managed, plus all the treasures in the king's palace. He also took hostages and returned to Samaria.
King Joash's son Amaziah of Judah lived another fifteen years after the death of Joash who was King Jehoahaz's son of Israel.
The rest of the acts of King Amaziah from the first to the last are all written in the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel.
After King Amaziah turned away and stopped following the Lord they conspired against him in Jerusalem, and he fled to Lachish. But they sent assassins to Lachish and killed him there.
They put his body on a wagon pulled by horses, and brought him to be buried with his fathers in the city of Judah.
Then the people of Judah coronated sixteen year old Uzziah, and made him their king in his father Amaziah's throne room.
King Uzziah rebuilt Eloth and returned it to Judah, after Amaziah died and slept with his fathers.
Uzziah was 16 years old when he began to reign and he reigned for 52 years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jecoliah of Jerusalem.
He did everything that he thought was righteous in the Lord's sight, just like his father Amaziah had done.
Uzziah sought God all the while that Zechariah lived, who taught him to understand the visions of God. And as long as he sought the Lord, God made him prosperous.
He went to war against the Philistines and tore down the walls of Gath, Jabneh, and Ashdod. Then he built cities around Ashdod and among the Philistines.
God helped him against the Philistines, the Arabians living in Gurbaal, and the Mehunims.
The Ammonites gave gifts to Uzziah, and his name spread abroad all the way to Egypt, because his power grew and was greatly consolidated.
Besides that, Uzziah built and fortified towers in Jerusalem at the corner gate, the valley gate, and at the wall's corners.

He also built towers in the desert and dug many wells, because he had many herds of cattle in the low country and out on the plains. He also had ranchers and vintners in Mount Carmel because he loved the soil.

King Uzziah maintained a vast army that was trained and ready for war when necessary. The size of the divisions were organized based on the numbers that the scribe Jeiel and the official Maaseiah recorded. They worked under the leadership of Hananiah who was one of the king's army commanders.
There was a total of 2,600 chief fathers of the mighty men of valor.
They commanded a vast army of 307,500 men trained for war, who used their mighty power to help the king against his enemies.
King Uzziah prepared this vast army with everything they needed to defend themselves including shields, helmets, armor, spears, bows, and slings for throwing stones.

In Jerusalem he built siege engines invented by skillful men, that were designed to breach the towers and bulwarks. He also built machines to shoot arrows and catapults to heave great stones. His name spread far and wide, because he had a tremendous amount of help consolidating his power.
But as Uzziah's power grew, his conceited heart led to his own destruction, because he transgressed against his Lord God, and he went into the Lord's temple to burn incense on the incense altar.
Azariah and eighty of the Lord's courageous priests followed him into the Lord's temple.

They confronted King Uzziah and said, "Uzziah, it is not your place to burn incense to the Lord. That Job is only for the priests who are the sons of Aaron, because they have been declared sacred to burn incense. "Leave this sanctuary, because you have trespassed and you will receive no honor from the Lord God."
This made Uzziah angry and had an incense censer burner in his hand. Then leprosy began to grow on his forehead as he stood beside the incense altar before the priests in the Lord's temple.

Azariah the chief priest and all the priests looked at him and saw the leprosy growing on his forehead, and they threw him out of the temple. And yes, he was also in a hurry to leave because the Lord had defeated him with leprosy.

After that King Uzziah was a leper until the day of his death. He lived in isolation in several houses because he was a leper. And he was cut off from the Lord's temple, and his son Jotham took control of the king's palace and governed the people of the land.
Now the rest of the acts of Uzziah, first and last, did Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz, write.

So Uzziah died and slept with his fathers, and they buried him near where his fathers were buried in the field where the kings were buried, because they said, "He was a leper." And his son Jotham reigned in his place.
Jotham was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned for sixteen years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jerushah who was Zadok's daughter.
He did what he thought was righteous in the Lord's sight, just like his father Uzziah had done, however he did not enter into the Lord's temple. But the people had become corrupt.
He built the high gates of the Lord's temple, and he did extensive work on the wall of Ophel.
Besides that, he built cities on Mount Judah and he built castles and towers in the forests.
Jotham won the war against the Ammonites and the citizens of Ammon paid him 100 pieces of silver, 10,000 bags of wheat, and 10,000 bags of barley as war reparations every year for three years.
So Jotham became very powerful because he was dedicated in his ways to follow his Lord God.
The rest of the acts of Jotham including all his wars and his ways, are written in the Book of the Kings of Israel and Judah.
He was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned for sixteen years in Jerusalem.
Jotham died and slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the city of David, and his son Ahaz reigned in his place.
Ahaz was twenty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned for sixteen years in Jerusalem, but unlike his father David, he did not do what was righteous in the Lord's sight.
Because he walked in the ways of the kings of Israel, and he also made molten images for Baalim.

Besides that, he burned incense in the Valley of Ben Hinnom, and he sacrificed his children in a fire. He followed the abominable practices of the heathen who the Lord had driven out before the Israelis.
He also sacrificed and burned incense in the high places, on the hills, and under every green tree.

So his Lord God delivered him into the hands of the Syrian king and they defeated him. Then they carried away a great number of captives and brought them to Damascus. He was also delivered into the hands of the king of Israel, who defeated him and slaughtered his army.
Because Remaliah's son Pekah killed 120,000 courageous men in just one day in Judah, because they had forsaken the Lord God of their fathers.
Zichri, who was a warrior from Ephraim killed the king's son Maaseiah, Azrikam the palace governor, and the king's assistant Elkanah.
Then the Israelis carried away 200,000 of their captive brothers, women, sons, and daughters. They also took tremendous amount of the spoils of war from them, and brought it all to Samaria.

But Oded the Lord's prophet who was in Samaria went out to meet the returning army and said, "The Lord God of your fathers was angry with Judah, so he delivered them into your hands, and you have killed them in a rage that reaches all the way up to heaven.
And now you propose to make slaves out of these people from Judah and Jerusalem, but does this not also make you guilty of sinning against your Lord God?
So hear me and return these captives to their own land, because the fierce anger of the Lord is coming upon you."

Then some of the leaders from the tribe of Ephraim including Johanan's son Azariah, Meshillemoth's son Berechiah, Shallum's son Jehizkiah, and Hadlai's son Amasa stood up to oppose those that were returning from the war.

And they said to them, "Do not bring those captives here, because we have in fact already offended the Lord God, and you intend to add to our sins and trespasses. Our trespasses are great and the Lord's fierce anger already burns against Israel."
So the soldiers left the captives and their spoils of war with the leaders and the congregation.

The above named men who had objected helped the captives and clothed the naked and gave them shoes, food, and drink from the spoils that were left and then they anointed them. Anyone who could not walk was placed on a donkey and they brought them to Jericho the city of palms, where they were close to their brothers, then they returned to Samaria.
At that time King Ahaz sent word to the kings of Assyria to ask for their help.
Because the Edomites had once again come and defeated Judah, and carried away captives.

The Philistines had also invaded the cities of the low country and south of Judah. And they captured Beth-Shemesh, Ajalon, Gederoth, Shocho with its villages, Timnah with its villages, and Gimzo with its villages where they lived.
The Lord brought Judah low because of King Ahaz of Israel, who had made Judah weak and naked, and sorely transgressed against the Lord.
So King Tilgath-Pilneser of Assyria took advantage of him, and attacked him instead of helping him.
Then Ahaz took some of the valuables from the Lord's temple, the king's treasury, and the leaders and gave it to the king of Assyria, but it did not help him.
And in his distress King Ahaz trespassed even more against the Lord.

Because he sacrificed to the gods of Damascus who defeated him and he said, "Because the gods of the kings of Syria help them, I will sacrifice to them, so that they will help me." But instead they were the ruin of all of Israel and him.
Ahaz collected all the vessels from the house of God and cut them all into pieces, and he closed the doors of the Lord's temple, and made altars in every corner of Jerusalem.
Then he made high places to burn incense to other gods in every city throughout Judah, and provoked the anger of his fathers' Lord God.
The rest of the acts of King Ahaz including all of his ways from the first to the last, are all written in the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel.
And Ahaz died and slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the city of Jerusalem, but they did not bury him in the tombs of the kings of Israel. And his son Hezekiah reigned in his place.
Hezekiah began to reign when he was twenty-five years old, and he reigned for twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Abijah who was Zechariah's daughter.
He did everything that he thought was righteous in the Lord's sight, just like his father David.
In the first month of the first year of his reign, he opened the doors of the Lord's temple and reinforced them.
Then he brought the priests and Levites together in the street on the eastern side of the temple.
And he said to them, "All you Levites listen to me, sanctify yourselves and sanctify the Lord's temple that belongs to the God of your fathers and remove all the filth from the Holy Place.

Because our fathers have trespassed against our Lord God, and done that which is evil in the Lord's eyes and forsaken him. They have turned their faces from the house of the Lord, and they have turned their backs on him.
They have also closed the entrance doors to the hall and extinguished the lamps, and they have not burned incense nor offered burnt offerings to the God of Israel in the Holy Place.
So the Lord's anger was on Judah and Jerusalem, and he delivered them over to trouble, astonishment, and hissing, as you can see with your own eyes.
Our fathers have fallen by the sword and our sons, daughters, and wives are all in captivity because of this.
Now it is in my heart to make a covenant with the Lord God of Israel, so that his fierce anger may turn away from us.
My sons, do not be negligent now because the Lord has chosen you to stand before him, to serve him, and to minister to him and burn incense."

Then the Levites rose, Mahath the son of Amasai, and Joel the son of Azariah, from the sons of the Kohathites, and from the sons of Merari, Kish the son of Abdi, and Azariah the son of Jehalelel, and of the Gershonites, Joah the son of Zimmah, and Eden the son of Joah.
Shimri and Jeiel from the Elizaphanites; Zechariah and Mattaniah from the Asaphites;
Jehiel and Shimei from the Hemanites; and Shemaiah and Uzziel from the Jeduthunites.
Then they assembled their brothers and sanctified themselves and went to clean the Lord's house, as the Lord commanded them through the king's commands.

The priests went into the inner sanctuary of the Lord's temple to clean it. They brought out all the filth that they found in the Lord's temple out into the temple courtyard, and the Levites carried it out to the Brook of Kidron in the valley.

They began the work to sanctify the temple on the first day of the first month, and on the eighth day of the month they reached the Lord's entrance hall. So they worked to sanctify the Lord's temple for eight more days, and they were finished by the sixteenth day of the first month.

Then they went to King Hezekiah and said, "We have cleaned the Lord's entire temple, the burnt offering altar along with all of its vessels, and the priests bread offering table with all of its bowls.
Besides that, we have prepared and sanctified everything that King Ahaz threw away when he transgressed against the Lord, and as you will see they are back before the Lord's altar."
Then King Hezekiah got up early the next morning and assembled the city leaders, and they all went to the Lord's temple.

They brought seven bulls, seven rams, seven lambs, and seven male goats with them as a sin offering for the kingdom, the sanctuary, and for Judah. Then he commanded Aaron's sons the priests to offer them on the Lord's altar.
So they killed the bulls and the priests sprinkled the blood on the altar, they also killed the rams and the lambs and sprinkled the blood on the altar.
Then they brought the male goats for the sin offering before the king and the congregation, and they laid their hands on them.

The priests killed the goats and sprinkled the blood on the altar to make an atonement for all of Israel, because the king commanded the burnt offering and the sin offering to be made for all of Israel.
King Hezekiah sent the Levites to the Lord's house with cymbals, lyres, and harps as the Lord had commanded through King David after he was given the Lord's word from the prophets Gad and Nathan.
The Levites stood with David's instruments, and the priests stood with their trumpets.

Then King Hezekiah ordered the burnt offering to be sacrificed on the altar. When the burnt offering began, they began singing the Lord's song accompanied by trumpets and the instruments ordained by King David of Israel.
The entire congregation worshipped the Lord and the singers sang, the trumpeters sounded, and it all continued until the burnt offering was finished.
As they finished the offering, the king and everyone present with him bowed and worshipped the Lord.

Besides that, King Hezekiah and his officials ordered the Levites to sing praises to the Lord with the words of David and Asaph the prophet. So they joyously sang praises and bowed their heads and worshipped.

Then Hezekiah said, "You have declared yourselves sacred to the Lord, come near and bring sacrifices and thanksgiving offerings into the Lord's temple." Then everyone in the congregation with a free heart brought their sacrifices, thanksgiving and burnt offerings.
And the congregation brought seventy bulls, one hundred rams, and two hundred lambs for their burnt offerings to the Lord.
There were 600 oxen and 3,000 sheep declared to be sacred sacrificial offerings.

But there were not enough priests to prepare all the burnt offerings. So their Levite brothers helped them until the work was finished, and the other priests had been sanctified. This was because the Levites sanctified themselves with more honest hearts and they worked more diligently than the priests.

Also there was an abundance of burnt offerings, along with the fat of the peace offerings and the drink offerings for every burnt offering. And this is how the service of the Lord's temple was reestablished and organized.
King Hezekiah and all the people rejoiced at what God had prepared for them, because all of this had happened so suddenly.
