King Hezekiah wrote letters and sent them throughout all of Israel, Ephraim, and Manasseh, to invite the people come to the Lord's temple in Jerusalem, to celebrate the Lord God of Israel's Passover.
Because the king, his princes, and the entire congregation in Jerusalem had decided to celebrate the Passover in the second month.
They could not keep it at the regular time, because not enough priests had sanctified themselves sufficiently, and the people had not come together in Jerusalem.
This proposal pleased the king and the entire congregation.

So they established a decree to distribute a proclamation throughout Israel from Beersheba all the way to Dan, to invite the people to come celebrate the Lord God of Israel's Passover in Jerusalem. Because they had not observed the Passover the way that it was written to be kept in such a long time.

The couriers went throughout all of Israel and Judah, with the letters from the king and his officials as the king commanded which read, "People of Israel return to the Lord God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, and God will return to those of you who have escaped from the hands of the Assyrian kings.
Do not be like your fathers and brothers who trespassed against the Lord God of their fathers, and who because of that were given up to devastation, as you can see.

Do not be stubborn like your fathers, but yield to the Lord and enter into his sanctuary, which he has sanctified forever. And serve your Lord God, so that his fierce anger will be turned away from you.

Because if you turn back to the Lord, your brothers and children will find compassion from their captors and they will return to this land. Because your Lord God is gracious and merciful, and he will not turn his face away from you, if you return to him."
So the couriers carried the letters from city to city throughout the country of Ephraim, Manasseh, and even to Zebulun, but the people laughed at them and mocked them.
Nevertheless various people from Asher, Manasseh, and Zebulun humbled themselves, and went to Jerusalem.
The hand of God was also in Judah and he gave the people one heart to obey the Lord's word sent to them by the king and his officials.
Then a vast congregation of people assembled in Jerusalem to celebrate the Feast of Unleavened Bread in the second month.
They removed all of Baal's altars in Jerusalem and the incense altars and carried them away, then threw them in the Brook of Kidron.
On the fourteenth day of the second month they killed the Passover lamb. The priests and Levites were ashamed, and they sanctified themselves and brought the burnt offerings into the Lord's temple.
They stood their ground at their assigned posts, as the Law of Moses the man of God described. And the priests sprinkled the blood which they had received from the Levites.
There were many in the congregation who were not sanctified, so the Levites took charge of killing the Passover lambs for everyone who was unclean, to sanctify the lambs to the Lord.

A vast number of people, many from Ephraim, Manasseh, Issachar, and Zebulun had not have sanctified themselves, but did they eat the Passover contrary to what was written. But Hezekiah prayed for them and said, "May the good Lord forgive every one of you,
Who prepares his heart to seek the Lord God of his fathers, even if he is not clean as required in the sanctuary's purification."
And the Lord listened to Hezekiah, and healed the people.

And all the Israelis present in Jerusalem celebrated the Feast of Unleavened Bread for seven days with great joy. The Levites and priests praised the Lord every day, singing praises to the Lord accompanied by loud instruments.

King Hezekiah spoke comfortably to all the Levites who taught the Lord's good knowledge, and they ate throughout the seven days feast. They made peace offerings and confessions to the Lord God of their fathers.
And the whole assembly decided to celebrate for seven more days, and they happily celebrated for seven more days.

King Hezekiah of Judah gave 1,000 bulls and 7,000 sheep to the congregation, and his officials gave 1,000 bulls and 10,000 sheep to the congregation, and a great number of priests sanctified themselves.
The entire congregations from Judah and Israel including the foreigners who came from Israel and Judah rejoiced, along with the priests and Levites.
So there was great joy in Jerusalem, because nothing like this had happened since the days of King David's son Solomon of Israel.
Then the Levite priests stood and blessed the people, and God heard their voice, and their prayers rose all he way up to his Holy home in heaven.

After all this was finished, the Israelis present went to the cities of Judah, and destroyed the abominable images, cut down the Asherah poles, and tore down the high places and altars throughout Judah, Benjamin, Ephraim, and Manasseh, until they had completely destroyed them all. Then all the Israelis returned to their homes in their own cities.

King Hezekiah assigned the priest's and Levite's the duties they are to perform for the burnt offerings and peace offerings, and the services they are to perform to minister and give thanks and praises to the Lord within the gates of the Lord's dwelling.

The king also donated from his own property for the morning and evening burnt offerings, the Sabbath burnt offerings, the new moon burnt offerings, and the ceremonial feasts, as it is written in the Law of the Lord.
Besides that, he commanded the people living in Jerusalem to give to the priests and Levites, so that they could serve as the Lord's law stated.
As soon as the order was made public, the Israelis brought an abundance of first fruits, wheat, wine, oil, honey, produce from the field, and all the tithes to the temple.

The descendants of Israel and Judah who lived in the cities of Judah brought the tithes of oxen, sheep, and Holy things which were declared sacred to the Lord their God, and piled them up at the temple.
In the third month they began storing the piles of donated goods, and they finished in the seventh month.
When King Hezekiah and his officers came and saw the piles of donated goods, they blessed the Lord, and his people of Israel.
Then Hezekiah questioned the priests and Levites about the piles of donations.

Azariah the chief priest of the house of Zadok answered him and said, "Since the people began bringing their offerings into the Lord's temple, we have had more than enough to eat, because the Lord has blessed his people, and this great abundance is what is leftover."
Then Hezekiah commanded them to prepare storehouses in the Lord's temple, and they prepared them.
They brought the faithfully donated offerings, tithes, and dedicated things into the storehouse. And Cononiah the Levite supervised the storehouse and his brother Shimei was his assistant.

Jehiel, Azaziah, Nahath, Asahel, Jerimoth, Jozabad, Eliel, Ismachiah, Mahath, and Benaiah were very wise men. They were appointed by King Hezekiah to serve under Cononiah, his brother Shimei, and Azariah the chief official of the house of God.
Kore was the eastern gatekeeper, and he managed and distributed the voluntary offerings and the most Holy things given to the Lord God. Kore was Imnah the Levite's son.

Under Kore's authority Eden, Miniamin, Jeshua, Shemaiah, Amariah, and Shecaniah faithfully distributed the contributions to the priests in their own cities according to their designated office, by their brothers divisions, to great and small equally.

In addition they distributed portions to the males by genealogy who were three years old or older, and to anyone that entered into the Lord's house to perform the daily duties and services of their appointed responsibilities.

And to both the priests according to the genealogy of their fathers' house, as well as the Levites who were twenty years old and older, according to their appointed responsibilities by their divisions.
And to the genealogy of their children, wives, sons, and daughters throughout the entire congregation, because they sanctified themselves in Holiness in their assigned office.

As for the priests who are the descendants of priest Aaron, who lived in the fields and pastures of their cities or in other cities, the men were designated by name, to give portions to every male among the priests, and to anyone that was listed by genealogy to be among the Levites.
Hezekiah did this throughout all the districts of Judah, and he worked that which was good, righteous, and truthful before his Lord God.
He did all the work that he began in the service of the house of God, the law, the commandments, and he sought his God with all his heart and he prospered.
After all these acts of faith King Sennacherib of Assyria invaded Judah. He planned to conquer Judah for himself and he laid siege to the fortified cities.
When King Hezekiah realized that Sennacherib had come to attack Jerusalem.
He met with his officers and military men to stop the flow of water to the fountains outside the city, and they helped him.

So many people worked together to stop the water to all the fountains, and they also dammed brook that ran through the land and said, "Why should the Assyrian kings come here and find plenty of water?"

He reinforced his army and rebuilt all the damaged walls, and raised towers and another outer wall. He also strengthened the fortifications in the city of David, and he had an abundance of arrows and shields produced.
And he appointed generals over war over the people, and gathered them together to him in the street of the gate of the city, and spoke comfortably to them and said.
And King Hezekiah said, "Be strong and courageous, do not be shocked or afraid of the king of Assyria. Do not fear the army with him, because there are more with us than there are with him.
With him is an arm of flesh, but our Lord God is with us to help us fight our battles." And the people were relieved after they heard the words of King Hezekiah of Judah.

After this did Sennacherib King of Assyria send his servants to Jerusalem, but he himself laid siege against Lachish, and all his power with him, to Hezekiah King of Judah, and to all Judah that were at Jerusalem and said.
And the message read, "This is what King Sennacherib of Assyria says, 'Do you trust someone that makes you endure the siege in Jerusalem?'
Did not Hezekiah persuade you to die by famine and thirst when he said, "Our Lord God will deliver us from the hand of the Assyrian king?"
Has not that same Hezekiah removed his high places and altars, and commanded Judah and Jerusalem and said, "You must only worship before one altar, and burn incense on it?"
Do you not know what my fathers and I have done to the people in other lands? Were any of the gods of those countries in any way able to deliver their lands from my hands?
Who was there among all the gods of those nations that my fathers completely destroyed, that could deliver his people from my hands. Will your God be able to deliver you from my hands?

So now I say, do not let Hezekiah deceive you in this manner and do not believe him. Because no god of any nation or kingdom has ever been able to deliver their people from my hands or from my father's hands. How much less will your god be able to deliver you from my hands?"
And Sennacherib's servants also spoke even more against the Lord God, and against his servant Hezekiah.

Sennacherib wrote letters that screamed against the Lord God of Israel and he also spoke against him and said, "The gods of other nations have not delivered their people from my hands, so the God of Hezekiah will not deliver his people from my hands."
Then they cried out in Hebrew in a loud voice to the people of Jerusalem who were standing on the wall, to frighten them and destroy their moral so they could take the city.
And they spoke against the God of Jerusalem, as they had spoken against the gods of the other people of the earth, saying they were only idols made by the work of men's hands.
King Hezekiah and Amoz's son Isaiah the prophet responded by praying and crying out to heaven.

And the Lord sent an angel, who cut off all the mighty men of valor from their commanders and captains in the king of Assyria's camp, and killed them. The king was humiliated and he returned to his own land, and when he entered the house of his own gods, his own sons killed him with the sword.
The Lord saved Hezekiah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem from the hands of King Sennacherib of Assyria and all the others, and he guided them in every direction.
Many people brought gifts to the Lord in Jerusalem, and they also brought presents to King Hezekiah of Judah, so much so that he was magnified in sight of all nations from then on.
In those days Hezekiah was sick to the death, and he prayed to the Lord who spoke to him and gave him a sign.
But Hezekiah's heart was proud, and his gratitude was not equal to the gifts that he had been given. So the Lord's wrath came upon him, and also upon Judah and Jerusalem.
But Hezekiah humbled his prideful heart, and so did the inhabitants of Jerusalem. After that, the Lord's anger never fell on them again during Hezekiah's lifetime.
Hezekiah was extremely rich and highly honored, and he built treasuries and storehouses for his gold, silver, precious stones, spices, shields, and all kinds of valuable jewelry.
And he built storehouses for the wheat, wine, and oil. He also built barns and stalls for all kinds of animals, and pens and coups for his flocks.
Besides that, he provided his cities with an abundance of flocks and herds because God had made him so very wealthy.
This is the same Hezekiah that diverted the water from the upper Gihon River, and he made it flow straight down to the west side of the city of David, and he prospered in everything that he did.

However, when the ambassadors from the leaders of Babylon came to him about the wonder that had happened there, God left him to himself to test him, so he could know what was really in Hezekiah's heart.
The rest of the acts of Hezekiah including his goodness, are recorded in the Visions of Isaiah the prophet, and in the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel. Isaiah was Amoz's son.

Hezekiah died and slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the chief tombs with the sons of David. All of the inhabitants of Judah and Jerusalem honored him when he died. And his son Manasseh reigned in his place.
Manasseh was twelve years old when he began to reign, and he reigned for 55 years in Jerusalem.
But he did evil things in the Lord's sight. He practiced the abominable things of the heathen who the Lord had driven out of the land before the Israelis.
Manasseh rebuilt the high places that his father Hezekiah had torn down. He raised altars for Baalim and made Asherah poles, and worshipped the sun, moon, and stars of heaven and served them.
He also built altars in the Lord's temple, of which the Lord had said, "My name in will be in Jerusalem forever."
He also built altars to worship the sun, moon, and stars of heaven in two courtyards of the Lord's temple.

He sacrificed his children in the fire in the Valley of Hinnom. He practiced sorcery, astrology, and witchcraft, and consulted wizards and familiar spirits. He did a great deal of evil in the sight of the LORD, which provoked his anger.

Manasseh had a carved idol image made that he had setup in the house of God. In the same place where God had said to David and his son Solomon, "I have chosen to put my name forever, on this house and Jerusalem before all the other tribes of Israel.

I will never again remove the Israelis from the land that I have given your fathers, if you will only listen and carefully do everything that I have commanded, and passed down through Moses with all the laws, judgements, and the legal decrees."
So Manasseh led the inhabitants of Judah and Jerusalem away from God, and caused them to do worse things than the heathen who the Lord had destroyed before the Israelis.
The Lord spoke to Manasseh and his people, but they would not listen.
So the Lord sent the Assyria King's military commanders and armies to attack Manasseh, who captured him among the thorns and bound him with shackles, and carried him to Babylon.
While he was in captivity, he implored his Lord God for forgiveness, and he earnestly humbled himself before the God of his fathers.
Manasseh prayed and pleaded with God and God heard his pleas, and brought him back to his kingdom in Jerusalem. After that he knew that the Lord was God.

After this, Manasseh built a wall outside the city of David in the valley on the west side of the Gihon River, all the way to the entrance at the fish gate. The wall also surrounded the Hill of Ophel, and he had it built up to a very great height. And he assigned military commanders to all the fortified cities of Judah and prepared to defend against any type of attack.

He removed all the strange gods and idols from the Lord's temple and dumped them outside the city. Then he tore down all the altars that he'd had built on the mountain of the Lord's temple and in Jerusalem.
After that, he restored the Lord's altar and sacrificed peace offerings and thanksgiving offerings, and commanded Judah to serve the Lord God of Israel.
Nevertheless the people still sacrificed in the high places, but only to their Lord God.
The rest of the acts of Manasseh and his prayers to his God, and the words of the wise men who spoke to him in the name of the Lord God of Israel, are written in the Book of the Kings of Israel.

Manasseh's prayers and how pleased God was with him are also written among the sayings of the wise men. As well as the things he did before he was humbled including his sins, his trespasses, and the locations where he built the high places and set up Asherah poles and carved images.
So Manasseh died and slept with his fathers, and they buried him in his own house. And his son Amon reigned in his place.
Amon was twenty-two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned for two years in Jerusalem.
Amon did evil in the Lord's sight just like his father Manasseh Because Amon sacrificed to all the carved images which his father Manasseh had made, and served them.
But Amon did not humble himself before the Lord as his father Manasseh had, but instead he trespassed more and more.
And his servants conspired against him, and killed him in his own house.
But the people of the land killed everyone that conspired against King Amon, and they made his son Josiah king instead of him.
Josiah was eight years old when he began to reign, and he reigned in Jerusalem for thirty-one years.
He did what he thought was righteous in the Lord's sight, and he walked in the ways of his father David, and he did not waiver to the left or the right.

Because in the eighth year of his reign, while he was still young, he began to seek the God of his father David. In the twelfth year of his reign he began to purge the high places, the Asherah poles, carved images, and molten images from Judah and Jerusalem.

In Josiah's presence, they tore down Baalim's altars and the images that were high above them. He cut down the Asherah poles, and he broke the carved and cast images into pieces, and ground them into dust, then strew the dust all over the graves of the people that had sacrificed to them.
And he burned the priest's bones on their altars, and cleansed Judah and Jerusalem.
He did this with their mattocks in the cities of Manasseh, Ephraim, Simeon, and even all the way to Naphtali and all around it.

After Josiah had the altars and Asherah poles torn down, and after he'd had the carved images ground into dust, and after he cut down all the idols throughout the entire land of Israel, he returned to Jerusalem.

In the eighteenth year of Josiah's reign after he'd had the land and the temple purged, he sent Azaliah's son Shaphan, and Maaseiah the governor of the city, and Joahaz the recorder's son Joah, to rebuild the house of his Lord God.

After they delivered the money to Hilkiah the high priest that was brought into the house of God, that the Levites collected at the temple doors from the people of Manasseh, Ephraim, Judah, Benjamin, and whatever else remained of Israel, they returned to Jerusalem.
Hilkiah put the money in the hands of the men who supervised the work in the Lord's temple, who gave it to the workmen who did the work in the Lord's temple, to rebuild and repair the temple.
They even gave money to the artists and builders to buy carved stone and timber for couplings, and beams to repair the temple floor, which the kings of Judah had destroyed.

And the men worked faithfully to move things forward. The very wise Levites supervising them were Merari's descendants Jahath and Obadiah, and Zechariah and Meshullam the Kohathites. And other Levites, who were skilled musicians with their musical instruments.
They also supervised the manual laborers, and there were very wise men who performed all types of work and services, and from the Levites there were scribes, officers, and gatekeepers.
When they brought out the money that was donated in the Lord's temple, priest Hilkiah found a book of the Lord's law given by Moses.
Hilkiah spoke to Shaphan the scribe and said, "I have found the Book of the Law in the Lord's temple!" And Hilkiah delivered the book to Shaphan.
Shaphan carried the book back to King Josiah and reported, "Your servants are doing all the work that was assigned to them.
And they have collected all the money in the Lord's temple, and delivered it to the very wise supervisors, and their workmen."
Then Shaphan the scribe said to the king, "Priest Hilkiah has given me a book, and he read it to the king."
After King Josiah heard the words of the law, he tore his clothes.
Then the king gave his orders to Hilkiah, Shaphan's son Ahikam, Micah's son Abdon, Shaphan the scribe, and one of the king's servants named Asaiah.

And he said, "Go ask the Lord for me and the people who are left in Israel and Judah, about the words in this book that was found. Because the Lord's anger that has been poured out on us is great, because our fathers have not kept the word of the Lord by doing what is written in this book."

So Hilkiah and the men that the king appointed to go with him went to speak to Huldah the prophetess, she lived in the lower section of Jerusalem and she was married to Shallum the keeper of the wardrobe. Shallum was Tikvath's son who was Hasrah's son.
And she answered them, in this says the Lord God of Israel, you tell the man that sent you to me.
This is what the Lord says, "Behold I will bring evil on this place and its inhabitants, and they will know the curses written in the book which they read to the king of Judah.

Because they have forsaken me, and burned incense to other gods. They have provoked my anger with all the works of their hands, so my anger will be poured out on this place, and will not be quenched."
But tell the king of Judah who sent you to ask me about the Lord, this is what the Lord God of Israel says about what you have read:

And the Lord says, "Because your heart was tender and you humbled yourself before God when you heard his words against this place and its inhabitants. So I have heard you because you humbled yourself, tore your clothes, and wept before me, .

Behold, I will bring you to your fathers, and you will be brought to your grave with your fathers in peace. Your eyes will not see all the evil that I will bring on this place and its inhabitants.'"So they brought God's word back to the king.
Then the king assembled all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem together.

The king went into the Lord's house along with all the men of Judah, the people of Jerusalem, the priests, the Levites, and everyone else great and small. And he read everything to them written in the Book of the Covenant that had been found in the Lord's house.

Then the king stood at the podium and made a covenant before the Lord, to follow the Lord, to keep his commandments, his testimonies, and his laws with all his heart and soul, and to do everything in the covenant that was written in this book.

He had everyone in Jerusalem and Benjamin stand up to show their agreement with the covenant that was written in the book. Then all the people of Jerusalem fulfilled their covenant with the God of their fathers.

Josiah had all the abominations removed from all the countries of Israel, and made everyone in Israel serve their Lord God, and they followed the Lord God of their fathers all the days of King Josiah.
Besides that, Josiah kept the Passover to the Lord in Jerusalem, and they killed the Passover lamb on the fourteenth day of the first month.
He assigned the priests their duties, and encouraged them to work in the service of the Lord's temple.

Josiah spoke to the Levites who taught everyone in Israel who were Holy to the Lord and said, "Put the Holy Ark in the temple built by King David's son Solomon of Israel. You will no longer have to carry it around on your shoulders. You will now serve your Lord God and his people Israel.
Organize yourselves by your families and your divisions, the way that King David of Israel and his son Solomon wrote.
Stand in the Holy Place and help the families and people of your father's brothers, separated into the divisions of the Levite families.
So slaughter the Passover sacrifice, sanctify yourselves and prepare your brothers to do everything that was written in the Lord's word which was given to you through Moses."
Josiah donated 30,000 lambs and 3,000 bulls and kids from his own flocks and herds as Passover offerings for everyone present.

His officials also willingly gave to the people, the priests, and the Levites. Hilkiah, Zechariah, Jehiel, and the administrators of the house of God gave the priests 2,600 calves and 300 oxen for the Passover offerings.
Conaniah and his brothers Shemaiah and Nathaniel, as well as Hashabiah, Jeiel, and Jozabad the Levite chiefs donated 5,000 calves and 500 oxen to the Levites for Passover offerings.
So the service was prepared, the priests stood in their place, and the Levites stood in columns by their divisions, the king ordered.
They killed the Passover lambs as the priests sprinkled the blood with their hands, and the Levites skinned them.

They set aside the burnt offerings to give them to the divisions of the people's families. Then they offered it to the Lord, as it was written in the Book of Moses, and they did the same thing with the oxen.
Then they roasted the Passover sacrifice as required by the legal decree, but they boiled the other holy offerings in pots, kettles, and pans and quickly divided them among the people.

Afterwards, they made preparations for themselves and the priests, because Aaron's sons the priests were busy offering the burnt offerings and the fat until nighttime. So the Levites prepared everything for themselves and Aaron's sons the priests.

Asaph's descendants the singers were in place as King David, Asaph, Heman, and the king's prophet Jeduthun had commanded them. But the gatekeepers who waited at all the gates did not have to leave their posts, because their Levite brothers prepared food for them.
So the Lord's entire Passover service was prepared that same day, including the burnt offerings on the Lord's altar, as King Josiah commanded.
The children of Israel present at that time, kept the Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread for seven days.

There was never a Passover like that ever kept in Israel from the days of Samuel the prophet. All the kings of Israel never keep such a Passover as Josiah kept along with the priests, the Levites, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and everyone from Judah and Israel who were present then.
This Passover kept in the eighteenth year of King Josiah's reign.
After all this, and after Josiah had prepared the temple, King Necho of Egypt came to attack Charchemish near the Euphrates River, and Josiah went to confront him.

Necho sent ambassadors to Josiah who said, "King of Judah, is there a problem between you and me? I have not come to attack you today, but I have come to fight a war against another kingdom. Because God is with me and has commanded me to hurry here, and you must stop meddling with God, so that he does not destroy you!"

Nevertheless Josiah would not turn away from him, he disguised himself and went to fight against him. He would not listen to Necho's words that came from the mouth of God, but he went to fight in the Valley of Megiddo.
The archers fired arrows at King Josiah, and he screamed to his servants, "Take me away from here, because I am mortally wounded!"

So his servants moved him from one chariot to another chariot, and they brought him to Jerusalem where he died, and he was buried in one of his fathers' tombs. Then all of Judah and Jerusalem mourned the death of King Josiah.

Jeremiah mourned for Josiah, and to this day all the men and women in the choir sing lamentations mourning Josiah. And in Israel they made the lamentations a legal decree, and they are written in the Book of Lamentations.
As for the rest of the acts of Josiah and his goodness and good deeds, which are in compliance with what was written in the Lord's law.
And his deeds from the first to the last, are written in the Book of the Kings of Israel and Judah.
Then the people of the land made Josiah's son Jehoahaz the new king to take his father's place in Jerusalem.
Jehoahaz was twenty-three years old when he began to reign, and he reigned for three months in Jerusalem.
The king of Egypt deposed him in Jerusalem, and demanded that Judah pay a hundred silver talents and one gold talent.
Then King Necho of Egypt crowned Jehoahaz's brother Eliakim king of Judah and Jerusalem, and he changed Eliakim's name to Jehoiakim. Then Necho carried Eliakim's brother Jehoahaz away to Egypt.
Jehoiakim was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned for eleven years in Jerusalem. And he did evil in the sight of his Lord God.
Then King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon attacked and captured Jehoiakim and bound him in shackles to take him to Babylon.
Nebuchadnezzar also carried off the vessels from the Lord's temple, and put them in his temple in Babylon.
The rest of the acts of Jehoiakim including his abominations and everything else against him, are written in the Book of the Kings of Israel and Judah. And his son Jehoiachin reigned in his place.
Jehoiachin was eight years old when he began to reign, and he reigned for three months and ten days in Jerusalem, and he did evil in sight of the Lord.

At the end of the year, King Nebuchadnezzar had Jehoiachin brought to Babylon, along with the valuable vessels from the Lord's temple, and crowned Jehoiachin's brother Zedekiah the king of Judah and Jerusalem.
Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he began to reign, and reigned for eleven years in Jerusalem.
And he did what was evil in his Lord God's sight, and did not humble himself before Jeremiah the prophet who spoke for the Lord.
But Zedekiah rebelled against King Nebuchadnezzar, who made him swear by God. He also stiffened his neck, and hardened his heart and refused to turn to the Lord God of Israel.
Besides that, all the chief priests and the people transgressed in all the abominations of the heathen even more, and they polluted the Lord's house which he had made holy in Jerusalem.
The Lord God of their fathers sent his messengers to them with his message over and over again, because he had compassion for his people and his home temple.
But they mocked God's messengers and they despised his words and abused his prophets, until the Lord's anger at his people was so intense that there was no remedy.

So God sent the king Nebuchadnezzar of the Chaldeans to attack them. He killed their young men with the sword in their sanctuary, and had no compassion for young or old, man or woman, or the elderly. So God put them all into the hands of the Chaldeans.
He had all the vessels great or small from the house of God, the treasures in the Lord's temple, and the treasures of the king and his officer were brought to Babylon.
And they burned the house of God, and tore down the walls of Jerusalem, and burned all the palaces there, and destroyed all its valuable vessels.
King Nebuchadnezzar had anyone who escaped the sword carried away to Babylon, where they served him and his sons until the Persian kingdom rose to power.
This was to satisfy the Lord's word from the mouth of Jeremiah, it would be seventy years of desolation until the land would enjoy the Sabbaths again.

In the first year of King Cyrus of Persia, so that the Lord's word spoken through the mouth of Jeremiah would be fulfilled, the Lord stirred the spirit of King Cyrus of Persia. Then he wrote a proclamation and sent it throughout his entire kingdom.

And it read, "This is what King Cyrus of Persia says, 'The Lord God of heaven has given me all the kingdoms on earth, and he has asked me to buildi his house in Jerusalem of Judah. And he has told me to let anyone among you who are his people who want to can go there.'"

In the first year of King Cyrus of Persia, to fulfill the Lord's word spoken through the mouth of Jeremiah, the Lord stirred up King Cyrus of Persia's spirit, so much so that he put a proclamation in writing and sent it throughout his entire kingdom.
And the proclamation read, "This is what King Cyrus of Persia says, 'The Lord God of heaven has given me all the kingdoms on earth, and he has asked me to build his house in Jerusalem of Judah.'"
Is there anyone among you who are his people? If so, may his God be with you and you may go up to Jerusalem in Judah, and build the Lord God of Israel's temple because he is the God in Jerusalem.
So let any remaining survivors wherever they are, be helped by those with gold, silver, property, and livestock, along with their voluntary offerings for the house of God in Jerusalem.'"
Then the chief fathers of Judah and Benjamin stood up along with the priests and Levites, and all of those whose spirit God had stirred up, left to go build the Lord's house in Jerusalem.
All their neighbors gave them silver and gold vessels along with property, livestock, and other precious things, in addition to everything else that was willingly offered.
King Cyrus also brought the vessels from the Lord's temple, which Nebuchadnezzar had taken from Jerusalem and had put in the house of his gods.
King Cyrus of Persia had Mithredath the treasurer bring them out by hand, and he counted them to Sheshbazzar the leader of Judah.
The total inventory count was 1,000 silver chargers, 30 gold chargers, 29 knives,
30 gold sinks, 410 silver sinks, and 1,000 other types of vessels.
There were 5,400 total number of gold and silver vessels that Sheshbazzar brought with them from their captivity in Babylon to Jerusalem.
These are the descendants of the people who were captured and carried away to Babylon by King Nebuchadnezzar, who left the province and returned to their own cities in Jerusalem and Judah.
The total number of men from Israel who left with Zerubbabel, Jeshua, Nehemiah, Seraiah, Reelaiah, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mizpar, Bigvai, Rehum, and Baanah was:
From Parosh's descendants there were 2,172.
Shephatiah had 372 descendants.
Arah had 777 descendants.
Pahath-Moab, Jeshua, and Joab altogether had 2,812 descendants.
Elam had 1,254 descendants.
Zattu had 945 descendants.
Zaccai had 760 descendants.
Bani had 640 descendants.
Bebai had 623 descendants.
Azgad had 1,222 descendants.
Adonikam had 666 descendants.
Bigvai had 2,056 descendants.
Adin had 454 descendants.
Ater of Hezekiah had 98 descendants.
Bezai had 323 descendants.
Jorah had 112 descendants.
Hashum had 223 descendants.
Gibbar had 95 descendants.
Bethlehem had 123 descendants.
Netophah had 56 descendants.
Anathoth had 128 men.
Azmaveth had 42 descendants.
Kirjatharim, Chephirah, and Beeroth altogether had 743 descendants.
Ramah and Gaba altogether had 621 descendants.
Michmas had 122 men.
Bethel and AI altogether had 223 men.
Nebo had 52 descendants.
Magbish had 156 descendants.
The other Elam had 1,254 descendants.
Harim had 320 descendants.
Lod, Hadid, and Ono altogether had 725 descendants.
Jericho had 345 descendants.
Senaah had 3,630 descendants.
The priests: Jedaiah of Jeshua's house had 973 descendants.
Immer had 1,052 descendants.
Pashur had 1,247 descendants.
Harim had 1,017 descendants.
The Levites: Jeshua, Kadmiel, and Hodaviah altogether had 74 descendants.
The singers: Asaph had 128 descendants.
The gatekeepers: Shallum, Ater, Talmon, Akkub, Hatita, and Shobai altogether had 139 descendants.
The temple assistants: Ziha, Hasupha, and Tabbaoth's descendants.
Keros, Siaha, and Padon's descendants.
Lebanah, Hagabah, and Akkub's descendants.
Hagab, Shalmai, and Hanan's descendants.
Giddel, Gahar, and Reaiah's descendants.
Rezin, Nekoda, and Gazzam's descendants.
Uzza, Paseah, and Besai's descendants.
Asnah, Mehunim, and Nephusim's descendants.
Bakbuk, Hakupha, and Harhur's descendants.
Bazluth, Mehida, and Harsha's descendants.
Barkos, Sisera, and Thamah's descendants.
Neziah and Hatipha's descendants.
The descendants of Solomon's servants including Sotai, Sophereth, and Peruda's descendants.
Jaalah, Darkon, and Giddel's descendants.
Shephatiah, Hattil, Pochereth of Zebaim, and Ami's descendants.
Altogether the temple assistants and Solomon's servants had 392 descendants.
The following people left Telmelah including Telharsa, Cherub, Addan, and Immer but they could not prove that they were Israel's descendants.
Delaiah, Tobiah, and Nekoda had 652 descendants.
From the priest's descendants there was: Habaiah, Koz, and Barzillai's descendants. Barzillai married one of Barzillai's daughters from Mount Gilead and he took his father-in-law's name.
These men searched their for family records but could not find them, so they were considered to be polluted and they were not allowed to join the priesthood.
The governor said that they should not eat the most holy things until there was a priest who could consult Urim and Thummim.
There was a total of 42,360 altogether from the entire congregation.
Beside that they had 7,337 servants and maids, and 200 singing men and women.
They also had 736 horses and 245 mules.
And they had 435 camels and 6,720 donkeys.
When they arrived in Jerusalem, some of the chief fathers freely offered donations to rebuild the Lord's Temple in the place where God originally wanted it built.
They donated what they could afford to the work treasuries which was 61,000 gold drams, 5,000 silver minas, and 100 priest garments.
So the priests, the Levites, the singers, the gatekeepers, and the temple assistants, and some of the other people went back to the cities they came from. Others also returned to their own cities.
In the seventh month after the Israelis had returned to their cities, the people together as one in Jerusalem.

After that, Jozadak's son Jeshua and his priest brothers, together with Shealtiel's son Zerubbabel, and his brothers began building the altar of Israel's God, so they could offer burnt offerings as it was written in the Law of Moses, the man of God.
They set the altar on its original foundation, and even though they were afraid of the local people, they offered both morning and evening burnt offerings on it to the Lord.
They also celebrated the Feast of Tabernacles as it was written in the law, and they offered the customarily required daily number of burnt offerings every day.

After that they also offered the daily burnt offerings and new moon offerings, as well as all of the Lord's feasts that were declared sacred, and for everyone who voluntarily brought offerings to the Lord.
On the first day of the seventh month they began to offer burnt offerings to the Lord, but the foundation for the Lord's temple had not yet been laid.

They also gave money to the masons and carpenters, and provided meat, drink, and oil to the people from Sidon and Tyre who brought cedar logs from Lebanon to Joppa by the sea, as King Cyrus of Persia had requested.

In the second month of the second year after their return to God's temple in Jerusalem, Shealtiel's son Zerubbabel and Jozadak's son Jeshua, plus all their other priest brothers, the Levites, and everyone else who returned from the captivity to Jerusalem began the work to move the construction of the Lord's temple forward. Every Levite twenty years old and older was appointed to supervise the construction of the Lord's temple.

So Jeshua along with his sons and brothers, Kadmiel and his sons the descendants of Judah, together with Henadad's sons and their Levite sons and brothers, began supervising the work to move the construction of house of God forward.

When the builders laid the foundation of the Lord's temple, they dressed the priests in their apparel with their trumpets, and Asaph the Levite sons with their cymbals to praise the Lord, as required by the legal decree of Israel's King David.

When the foundation of the Lord's temple had been laid, they sang together in their divisions praising and giving thanks to the Lord, because he is good, and his mercy toward Israel endures forever. All the people shouted with a great shout when they praised the Lord.
But many of the ancient men who were Levites, priests, and chief fathers who had seen the foundation of the first house of God laid, wept loudly and many shouted for joy.
They were so loud, that the people could not tell the difference between the people's shouts of joy and their weeping, because everyone shouted loudly and the noise was heard very far away.
When Judah and Benjamin's adversaries heard that the descendants from captivity had rebuilt the Lord God of Israel's temple.

Then they went to Zerubbabel and the chief fathers and said, "Let us help you build because we seek your God just as you do, and we have sacrificed to him since the days of King Esarhaddon of Assur who brought us up here."

But Zerubbabel, Jeshua, and the rest of the chief fathers of Israel replied to them and said, "You cannot help us build a house for our Lord God of Israel, because we must build it ourselves as King Cyrus of Persia has commanded us."
Then the people living in the land before the Israelis returned, tried to weaken the resolve and discourage the people of Judah from building.
As long as King Cyrus of Persia lived, those people bribed government officials to frustrate the Israelis plans, even until King Darius the son of Ahasuerus of Persia began to reign.
In the beginning of the reign of King Ahasuerus son of King Cyrus of Persia, they wrote accusations against the inhabitants of Judah and Jerusalem and sent them to him.

During the reign of King Artaxerxes son of Ahasuerus of Persia, the king received a letter written by Bishlam, Mithredath, Tabeel, and their companions that was written in the Syrian language and translated for the him.
Rehum the chancellor and Shimshai the scribe wrote a letter of accusations against Jerusalem to King Artaxerxes with their complaints.

So Rehum the chancellor, Shimshai the scribe, and their companions: the Dinaites, the Apharsathchites, the Tarpelites, the Apharsites, the Archevites, the Babylonians, the Susanchites, the Dehavites, and the Elamites wrote.
Along with the rest of the nations whom the great and noble Asnapper deported to the cities of Samaria, and other places on the west side the Euphrates river wrote a letter to King Artaxerxes.
The text of the letter that they sent to King Artaxerxes read, "Your servants the men on this side the river, at such a time as this.

Let it be known to the king, that the Jews who came from your land to our land, are rebuilding a rebellious and bad city in Jerusalem. They have rebuilt its fortified walls and repaired its foundations.
And let it also be known to the king, that if this city and the walls are rebuilt, they will not pay tribute, tolls, or duties which will damage the royal treasuries.
Now because we maintain the king's palace, and because we do not want to see the king dishonored, we have we sent this certified letter to inform the king.

That you should search the record books of your fathers, and you will find that this city is a rebellious city. You will also discover that his city has been harmful to kings and provinces, and they have incited sedition since ancient times, which is why this city was destroyed.
We certify to the king that, if this city is rebuilt and its walls are reinforced again, you will have no power over this side of the Euphrates river."

Then King Artaxerxes sent an answer back to Rehum the chancellor and Shimshai the scribe, their companions who live in Samaria, and the rest of the people who live beyond the Euphrates river which read, "Peace be with you at this time.
The letter which you sent to us has been clearly translated to me.
I ordered the scribes to search the records, and they found that this ancient city has indeed incited sedition and rebellion against the kings.
There have also been mighty kings that ruled over Jerusalem, who also ruled over all the countries beyond the Euphrates river, and tribute, toll, and duties were paid to them.
So order these men to cease construction and tell them that this city must not be rebuilt, until they receive further orders from me.
Proceed carefully and do not fail not to take care of this matter. Why should we allow the damage to grow that will cause damage to the kings?"
When King Artaxerxes' letter was read to Rehum, Shimshai the scribe, and their companions, they quickly went to the Jews in Jerusalem and forced them to cease their construction.
Then, work on the house of God in Jerusalem ceased. So work was stopped until the second year of the reign of King Darius of Persia.
Then the prophets Haggai and Iddo's son Zechariah prophesied in the name of the God of Israel, to the Jews in Judah and Jerusalem.
Then Shealtiel's son Zerubbabel and Jozadak's son Jeshua began to build the house of God in Jerusalem, with the prophets of God helping them.

At that time Tatnai governor on the west side of the Euphrates river, Shethar-Boznai, and their companions went to speak to the Israelis and said, Who gave you permission to rebuild this temple and this wall?"
Then they also asked them, "What are the names of the men rebuilding this building?"

But the eye of their God was on the elders of the Jews, so that the governor and his associates could not stop their construction, until a report was sent to King Darius and he sent a letter back to them with instructions.
Governor Tatnai, Shethar-Boznai, and the Apharsachites on the west side of the Euphrates river composed the report sent to King Darius.
The text in the letter they sent to King Darius read, "All peace to you.

Let it be it known to the king, that we went to the province of Judea, to the house of the great God. The Israelis are rebuilding it with great stones and timber walls. Construction of this temple proceeds rapidly and everything prospers in their hands.
Then we spoke to the elders and asked, 'Who gave you permission to rebuild this temple, and repair these walls?'
We also asked them their names, so that we could record the names of their supervisors for you.
They answered us and said, 'We are the servants of the God of heaven and earth, and we are rebuilding the temple that was built many years ago, which a great king of Israel built.

But after that, our fathers provoked the God of heaven to anger, and he placed them into the hands of the Chaldean King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon, who destroyed this temple and carried the people away to Babylon.
But in the first year of King Cyrus of Babylon, he made a decree to rebuild this house of God.

King Nebuchadnezzar had also taken all the gold and silver vessels from the house of God in Jerusalem, and brought to the temple of Babylon. And King Cyrus removed them from the temple of Babylon and sent them to Sheshbazzar, whom he had appointed governor.
And King Cyrus said to him, 'Take these vessels, and carry them to the temple in Jerusalem, and let the house of God be rebuilt in his city.'
Then Sheshbazzar came and laid the foundation to the house of God in Jerusalem, and since that time until now it is being rebuilt, but it is not finished.

So, if it pleases the king, let a search be made of the king's records in Babylon, to see if King Cyrus made a decree to rebuild this house of God in Jerusalem, and may the king at his leisure return an answer back to us concerning this matter."
Then King Darius ordered a search to be made of the palace records, that were kept in Babylon's treasuries.
And they found a written record in the palace in Achmetha in the province of the Medes.

It was written that in the first year of King Cyrus that he made a decree about the house of God in Jerusalem. He allowed the house of God to be rebuilt, along with the place where they offered sacrifices, and he allowed the foundations to be restored. According to the records it was sixty cubits high, and sixty cubits wide.
With three rows of great stones, and a row of new timbers, and the expenses were paid from the king's palace treasuries.

Nebuchadnezzar also took gold and silver vessels from the house of God and brought them to Babylon. But King Darius allowed them to be returned to the temple in Jerusalem, and they were placed in the proper place in the house of God in Jerusalem.
That's why King Darius gave Tatnai governor of the region beyond the river, Shethar-Boznai, and their companions the Apharsachites his decree that said, "Stay far away from that place!
Leave this work on the house of God alone! You must allow the Jewish governor and their elders to build this house of God in his city.

Besides that, I hereby decree that you must help the Jewish elders by financing the rebuilding of this house of God. You must pay the entire cost of rebuilding this temple from the king's goods and the tribute collected from beyond the river must be immediately given to these men, so that their work is not hindered.

In addition, whatever the priests in Jerusalem need and request for the burnt offerings to the God of heaven will be given to them daily without fail including the young bulls, rams, lambs, wheat, salt, wine, and oil.
So they can offer sweet savory sacrifices to the God of heaven, and pray for the life of the king and of his sons.

I also hereby decree that whoever interferes with these orders, will have a timber pulled from their house and planted in the ground where he will be impaled on it, and his house will be made into a dunghill for this offense.
May the God who caused his name to live there, destroy any kings or people who lift a hand to destroy this alter or this house of God in Jerusalem. I Darius, have made this decree, so do it quickly."
Then Tatnai the governor on this side the river, Shethar-Boznai, and their companions quickly did everything that King Darius ordered.

The Jewish elders built and prospered through the prophesying of Haggai the prophet and Iddo's son Zechariah. They finished building it at the commandment of the God of Israel and the decrees of Cyrus, Darius, and King Artaxerxes of Persia.
The Lord's house was finished on the third day of the month of Adar, which was in the sixth year of the reign of King Darius.
The Israelis, the priests, the Levites, and the rest of the descendants from the captivity joyfully celebrated the dedication of this house of God.

At the dedication of the house of God they offered one hundred bulls, two hundred rams, four hundred lambs and as a sin offering for all the sins of Israel they offered twelve male goats, to match the number of tribes of Israel.
They appointed the priests and Levites in the service of God in Jerusalem by their divisions, as it is written in the Book of Moses.
The descendants of the captivity celebrated the Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month.
Because the priests and Levites were all purified together. They were all pure and they killed the Passover for all the descendants of the captivity, for their priest brothers, and for themselves.

The descendants of Israel who had returned from captivity ate it together, along with everyone that separated themselves from the filthiness of the heathen of the land, to seek the Lord God of Israel.

And they joyously kept the Feast of Unleavened Bread for seven days, because the Lord had made them joyful, and turned the Assyrian king's heart to them, to strengthen their hands in the work on the house of the God of Israel.
After all this, during the reign of King Artaxerxes of Persia Ezra arrived in Jerusalem. Ezra was Seraiah's son, Seraiah was Azariah's son, and Azariah was Hilkiah's son,
Hilkiah was Shallum's son, Shallum was Zadok's son, Zadok was Ahitub's son.
Ahitub was Amariah's son, Amariah was Azariah's son, Azariah was Meraioth's son,
Meraioth was Zerahiah's son, Zerahiah was Uzzi's son, Uzzi was Bukki's son,
Bukki was Abishua's son, Abishua was Phinehas' son, Phinehas was Eleazar's son, Eleazar was Aaron the chief priest's son.

Ezra came to Jerusalem from Babylon. He was a scribe skilled in the laws which the Lord God of Israel had given that were written in the Book of the Laws of Moses. The king always granted Ezra's requests, because the hand of his Lord God was upon him.
In the seventh year of King Artaxerxes reign some of the Levites, Israelis, temple assistants, priests, singers, and gatekeepers went to Jerusalem.
Ezra arrived in Jerusalem in the fifth month of the seventh year of the reign of King Artaxerxes.
Ezra left Babylon on the first day of the first month, and he arrived in Jerusalem on the first day of the fifth month, because the good hand of his God was upon him.
Because Ezra had prepared his heart to seek and keep the Lord's Laws, and to teach his laws and judgments in Israel.
Now King Artaxerxes gave a letter to priest Ezra the scribe and the text of this letter read, "Priest Ezra the scribe has studied the written word of the Lord's commandments and laws for Israel.
From King Artaxerxes king of kings, to priest Ezra a scribe in the laws of God in heaven, with perfect peace and greetings.
I hereby make this decree, that all the people of Israel including his priests and Levites in my realm, may voluntarily go with you to Jerusalem.
You were sent from the king and his seven counselors to determine if Judah and Jerusalem, are in compliance with the laws of your God which are in your hand.
To deliver the gold and silver, which the king and his counselors have freely offered the God of Israel, whose home is in Jerusalem.
Plus any voluntary offerings of gold and silver for the house of their God in Jerusalem which the people and priests willingly give from the provinces of Babylon.
So that you can quickly purchase with this money all the bulls, rams, lambs along with with their bread and drink offerings. And offer them up on the altar of the house of your God in Jerusalem.
And to do whatever seems to be the good will of your God to you and your brothers, with the rest of the gold and silver.
You must also deliver all the vessels that have been given to you for the service in the house of your God in Jerusalem.
And whatever else is needed for the house of your God that you may have the occasion to provide, may be paid for from the king's treasuries."

I King Artaxerxes do hereby make this decree to all the treasurers beyond the river, "Whatever priest Ezra the scribe of the law of the God of heaven requires of you, you will take care of it immediately.
Up to one hundred silver talents, one hundred measures of wheat, one hundred baths of wine, one hundred baths of oil, and unlimited salt.
Let whatever the God of heaven commands be diligently done for the house of the God of heaven. Because why should the anger of the God of heaven be against the realm of the king and his sons?
We also certify that it will be unlawful to impose any tolls, tributes, or duties on the Levites, priests, temple assistants, singers, gatekeepers, or ministers from this house of God.

And you Ezra, with the wisdom of your God that is in your hand, will appoint magistrates and judges to judge all the people west of the Euphrates river who know the laws of your God. And you must teach the laws to those who do not know them.
Whoever does not obey the law of your God and the king's law, let the judgment be speedily executed against him whether it is death, banishment, confiscation of goods, or imprisonment."
And Ezra said, "Blessed be the Lord God of our fathers, who has put this in the king's heart, to beautify the Lord's temple in Jerusalem.

Who has extended mercy to me before the king, and his counselors, and before all the king's mighty leaders. I was strengthened as the hand of the Lord my God was upon me, and I gathered the chief men of Israel to go with me."
My name is Ezra, and I am writing this account of the chief fathers and the genealogy of those who left Babylon with me, during the reign of King Artaxerxes.
From the descendants of Phinehas was Gershom, from Ithamar's descendants was Daniel, and from David's descendants was Hattush.
From Shechaniah and Pharosh's descendants, Zechariah had 150 men with him.
From Pahath-Moab's descendants, Zerahiah's son Elihoenai had 200 men with him.
Jahaziel's son Shechaniah had 300 men with him.
From Adin's descendants, Jonathan's son Ebed had 50 men with him.
From Elam's descendants, Athaliah's son Jeshaiah had 70 men with him.
From Shephatiah's descendants, Michael's son Zebadiah had 80 men with him.
From Joab's descendants, Jehiel's son Obadiah had 218 men with him.
And from the sons of Shelomith, the son of Josiphiah, and with him a hundred and sixty males.
From Bebai's descendants, the other Bebai's son Zechariah had 28 men with him.
From Azgad's descendants, Hakkatan's son Johanan had 110 men with him.
From the last of Adonikam's sons, Eliphelet, Jeiel, and Shemaiah who had 60 men with them.
Bigvai's sons Uthai and Zabbud, also had 70 men with them.
I gathered the returning exiles together at the Ahava Canal. We camped there for three days, and as I reviewed the people and priests there, I discovered that there were no Levites among us.
Then sent I for the chief leaders: Eliezer, Ariel, Shemaiah, Elnathan, Jarib, Elnathan, Nathan, Zechariah, and Meshullam. I also summoned the wise teachers Joiarib and Elnathan.
Then I sent them to Iddo the chief father and his brothers the Temple assistants in Casiphia, with a message that instructed them to bring those who minister in our God's house to meet with us.

Because the good hand of God was upon us, they brought us a wise teacher named Sherebiah and 18 of his sons and brothers. Sherebiah was a descendant of Mahli, Mahli was Levi's son, and Levi was Israel's son.
They also sent Hashabiah, Jeshaiah, and 20 of their sons and brothers from Merari's descendants.
They also sent 220 temple assistants, that were the descendants of the men appointed by David and his officials to serve the Levites, and I recorded all of their names.
Then I proclaimed a fast by the Ahava River, so that we could humble ourselves before our God to seek a safe journey from him for us, our children, and all our possessions.

Because I was ashamed to ask the king for soldiers and horsemen to protect us from our enemies along the way. Because we had spoken to the king and said, "The good hand of our God is upon anyone that seeks him, but his power and anger is against anyone that abandons him."
So we fasted and implored our God for this, and he answered our prayers.
Then I separated 12 chief priests from the others including Sherebiah, Hashabiah, and ten of their brothers.
I weighed out the gold, silver, vessels, and even the offering from the house of our God which the king, his counselors and lords, and everyone else from Israel that was present had offered.
I even weighed out 650 silver talents, 100 gold talents, and 100 talents worth of silver vessels into their hand.
Also twenty gold sinks that weighed 1,000 drams each, and two fine copper bowls that were as precious as gold.
And I said to them, "You are holy to the Lord and these vessels are holy, and the gold and silver are voluntary offerings to the Lord God of your fathers.
Watch over them and keep them with you until you weigh them out in the chambers of the Lord's temple before the chief priests, Levites, and Israel's chief fathers in Jerusalem."
So the priests and Levites took the gold, silver, and vessels with them to our God's house in Jerusalem.

Then on the twelfth day of the first month we left the Ahava River to go to Jerusalem. The good hand of our God was upon us and he delivered us from the hand of any enemies waiting to attack us along the way.
When we arrived in Jerusalem, we stayed there for three days.

On the fourth day priest Uriah's son Meremoth was in our God's house weighing the silver, gold, and vessels. Phinehas' son Eleazar, Jeshua's son Jozabad, and Binnui's son Noadiah of the Levites were also with him.
Everything was weighed and counted and weights and numbers were recorded at that time.

The descendants of those that had been carried away into captivity also offered burnt offerings to the God of Israel which numbered for all of Israel 12 bulls, 96 rams, 77 lambs, and 12 male goats as a sin offering.
Then they delivered the king's decrees to the king's officers and governors on the west side of the Euphrates River, who further assisted the people and the house of God.

Later, after all these things happened, the officials came to me and said, "The Israelis including the priests and Levites have not separated themselves from the local people. They have been participating in the abominable practices of the Canaanites, Hittites, Perizzites, Jebusites, Ammonites, Moabites, Egyptians, and Amorites.

Because the Israelis men and their sons have been marrying their daughters, and the Holy Seed has been mingled with the people of those lands. Even the leaders, officials, and chief fathers have been participating in this trespass."
When I heard about this, I was shocked and I tore my clothes and pulled some hair from my head and beard, and I sat down astonished.

I sat there astonished until the evening sacrifice, as everyone who trembled at the words of the God of Israel gathered around me, because they were terrified of the sins of the exiles who had returned from the captivity.
At the evening sacrifice I rose up from my sadness, and after having torn my clothes I fell on my knees and spread my hands out to my Lord God.
And I said, "O my God, I am ashamed and embarrassed to look up to you. My God, because our wickedness has increased over our head, and our sins have reached all the way up to heaven.

Since the days of our fathers our sins have been great trespass until today. Because of our wickedness our kings and priests have been delivered into the hand of kings of the other nations. And we have faced death by the sword, and we have been exiled into captivity. Our nations have become the spoils of war and ruled by mass confusion to this day.

But now, our Lord God from above has shown us the grace to allow the survivors to escape captivity and he has given us a place in his holy land. Even in our bondage, our God has given us a new life and a new light for our eyes.

We were slaves, but our God did not forsake us in our bondage. But he has extended his mercy to us through the kings of Persia, and he has given us a chance for revival. He has allowed us to rebuild the destroyed house of our God, and he has given us fortified borders in Judah and Jerusalem.
Now O our God, what can we say after this? Because we have abandoned your commandments.

We have abandoned the commandments that you gave us through your servants the prophets which said, 'The land that you go to possess is an unclean land corrupted by the filth from the people of the nations there. They have filled it from one end to another with their filth and abominations.'

And you said 'Do not allow your daughters to marry their sons, nor allow their daughters to marry your sons. Do not seek their peace or wealth forever, so that you may be strong and eat from the good of the land, and leave it as an inheritance to your children forever.'
After you punished us because of our evil deeds and our great sins, you still allowed some of us to survive. Because our God has punished us much less than our wickedness deserved.

Should we break your commandments once again, and marry into the people who practice these abominations? Would you not be so angry with us that you would destroy us, so that no one would remain or escape?
O Lord God of Israel, you are righteous because today we are all that survived. So behold we come to you in our sins, but we cannot stand before you because of this."

When Ezra finished praying, confessing, weeping, and bowing before the house of God, a vast crowd of Israelis men, women, and children assembled around him and wept bitterly, because they were very sorry.

Then Jehiel's son Shechaniah the Elamite answered Ezra and said, "We have trespassed against our God, and have taken foreign wives from the people of the land, but now there is hope for us in Israel for this.
So let us make a covenant with our God to divorce all those wives and their children, as my Lord and those who tremble at God's commandments, and let it be done according to with the law.
Get up, because this is your responsibility, and we will support you. So be courageous and do what God says!"
Then Ezra got up and made the chief priests, Levites, and all the Israelis swear an oath that they would do everything required by this promise.

Then Ezra withdrew from the house of God and went into Eliashib's son Johanan's chamber, and when he arrived there, he ate no bread and drank no water, because he mourned the sins of the exiles that had returned from the captivity.
They made a proclamation throughout Judah and Jerusalem which said, "All exiles who have returned from the captivity should come to Jerusalem.

And whoever does not come within three days, as the counsel of the leaders and elders requires will forfeit everything they own, and they will be separated from the congregation of those who had returned from captivity."

Then all the men of Judah and Benjamin went to Jerusalem within three days, on twentieth day of the ninth month. Everyone sat outside in the rain, on the street in front of the house of God, trembling with fear because of this.
And priest Ezra stood up and spoke to them and said, "You have transgressed and taken strange wives, which has increased Israel's trespasses.
So, confess to the Lord God of your fathers, and do as his will and separate yourselves from the people of the land, and from your foreign wives."
Then the entire congregation answered in a loud voice and said, "We must do what you say!

But there are lots of people here and it is the rainy season, and we can not stand outside in the rain. And this is not one or two days of work, because there are so many of us that have sinned in this way.

So let the leaders of the congregation, along with the city elders and judges stand and make appointments with anyone married to a foreign woman to meet at an appointed time, until the fierce anger of our God about this is turned from us."
Asahel's son Jonathan and Tikvah's son Jahaziah were employed to take care of this matter, and Meshullam and Shabbethai the Levite helped them.

Then the exiles from captivity did as they were told. Priest Ezra, along with certain chief fathers identified by name to represent their families, separated and met on the first day of the tenth month to investigate the matter.
And they finished the divorces of all the men who had married foreign wives by the first day of the first month.
Some of the names of the priests' sons who were found to have married foreign wives were from the sons of Jozadak's son Jeshua and his brothers, Maaseiah, Eliezer, Jarib, and Gedaliah.
They said they would divorce their wives, and they each offered a ram from their flock as their guilty sin offering.
From Immer's sons there was Hanani and Zebadiah.
From Harim's sons there was Maaseiah, Elijah, Shemaiah, Jehiel, and Uzziah.
From Pashur's sons there was Elioenai, Maaseiah, Ishmael, Nathaniel, Jozabad, and Elasah.
From the Levites there was Jozabad, Shimei, Kelaiah who was also called Kelita, Pethahiah, Judah, and Eliezer.
From the singers there was Eliashib. From the gatekeepers there was Shallum, Telem, and Uri.
Besides that, from Israel there was Parosh's descendants Ramiah, Jeziah, Malchiah, Miamin, Eleazar, Malchijah, and Benaiah.
From Elam's sons there was Mattaniah, Zechariah, Jehiel, Abdi, Jeremoth, and Eliah.
From Zattu's sons there was Elioenai, Eliashib, Mattaniah, Jeremoth, Zabad, and Aziza.
From Bebai's sons there was Jehohanan, Hananiah, Zabbai, and Athlai.
From Bani's sons there was Meshullam, Malluch, Adaiah, Jashub, Sheal, and Ramoth.
From Pahath-Moab's sons there was Adna, Chelal, Benaiah. Maaseiah, Mattaniah, Bezalel, Binnui, and Manasseh.
From Harim sons there was Eliezer, Ishijah, Malchiah, Shemaiah, Shimeon,
Benjamin, Malluch, and Shemariah.
From Hashum's sons there was Mattenai, Mattathah, Zabad, Eliphelet, Jeremai, Manasseh, and Shimei.
From Bani sons there was Maadai, Amram, Uel,
Benaiah, Bedeiah, Chelluh,
Vaniah, Meremoth, Eliashib,
Mattaniah, Mattenai, Jaasau,
Bani, Binnui, Shimei,
Shelemiah, Nathan, Adaiah,
Machnadebai, Shashai, Sharai,
Azareel, Shelemiah, Shemariah,
Shallum, Amariah, and Joseph.
From Nebo's sons there was Jeiel, Mattithiah, Zabad, Zebina, Jadau, Joel, and Benaiah.
All of these men had married foreign wives, and some of them had children with those wives.
Nehemiah's son Hachaliah spoke out and said, "In the month of Chisleu of the twentieth year, I was in the Shushan palace.
My brother Hanani and some men arrived from Judah. So I asked them about the Jews who had escaped the captivity, and also about Jerusalem."

And they answered me and said, "The survivors who survived the captivity are in the province and they are greatly afflicted and disgraced. The wall of Jerusalem has also been torn down, and its gates have been burned with fire."
After I heard this, I sat down, wept and mourned for days, I fasted and prayed before the God of heaven.
Then I prayed and said, 'I beg you, O Lord God of heaven, the great and terrible God who keeps promises and shows mercy to those who love him and observe his commandments.

Please open your eyes and ears and listen attentively, so that you hear your servant's prayer, which I pray night and day before you. Because your servants the Israelis are now confessing their sins before you, that we, both me and my father's house have sinned against you.
We have dealt very corruptly against you and we have not kept your commandments, laws, and judgments, which you gave us through your servant Moses.
I beg you to remember the promise you made through your servant Moses when you said, 'If you transgress, I will scatter you abroad among the nations.

But if you return to me and keep my commandments, even though you were thrown out into the farthest reaches of heaven. I will gather them from there, and I will return them to the place that I have chosen as the place to establish my name.'
You have rescued these people, who are your people and your servants with your strong hand and great power.

O Lord I beg you, please listen attentively to my prayers and the prayers of your other servants, who love to worship you and prosper. I pray this day for your servant, and ask that you grant him mercy. Because I was the king's cupbearer."
In the month of Nisan of the twentieth year of King Artaxerxes' reign, I, Nehemiah, was the one who gave the king his wine. And never before had I appeared sad in the king's presence.

The king noticed that I was sad and that's why he spoke to me and said, "Why is the expression on your face so sad, are you sick, or is something troubling your heart?" Then I was very extremely frightened.
I responded to the king and said, "May the king live forever, how can I not appear sad? The city of my fathers' tombs has been wasted, it lies in ruins and its gates have been consumed by fire?"
Then the king asked me, "What would you like to ask?" So I prayed to the God of heaven.

I answered the king and said, "If it pleases the king, and if your servant has found favor in your sight, I would ask you to send me to the city of my fathers' tombs in Judah, so I can help rebuild it."
The king was sitting beside the queen and he said to me, "How long will your trip take, and when will you return?" So, I told the king how long I thought it would take, and he let me go.
Besides that, I said to the king, "If it please the king, can you give me letters to give the governors beyond the river, to provide me with safe passage to Judah?

And a letter to Asaph the keeper of the king's forest, so he can give me timber to make beams for the temple gates, the city walls, and for the house that I will live in." And because the good hand of my God was upon me, the king granted my request.
Then I went to the governors beyond the river and gave them the king's letters. The king had also sent army captains and horsemen with me.
When Sanballat the Horonite and Tobiah the Ammonite official heard about me, they were extremely upset that someone had come to help the Israelis.
So after I had arrived and rested in Jerusalem for three days.

Then I got up in the middle of the night with a few of the other men and left. I did not tell any of them what my God had put in my heart to do in Jerusalem. And I only took one horse with me to ride.
I left at night and rode through the valley gates toward the dragon well and the dung port. I went to inspect Jerusalem's walls that had been torn down and the gates that were burned down.
Then I rode toward the fountain gate and the king's pool, but I could not get through because I could not find a place that was safe and had enough room for the horse to pass.
So I rode up near the valley brook in the dark and inspected the wall, then I returned through the valley gates.
The city leaders did not know where I went or what I was doing, because I had not yet told the Jews, priests, nobles, city leaders, or any of the workers why I was in Jerusalem.

Then I said to them, "Do you see the distress that we are in, how Jerusalem lies in waste, and its gates are burned down? "Come, let us rebuild the wall of Jerusalem, so that we no longer have to live in disgrace."
Then I told them that the good hand of my God was upon me, and so were the words that king spoke to me. And they said, "Let's go rebuild Jerusalem." And they immediately began the good work.

But when Sanballat the Horonite, Tobiah the Ammonite official, and Geshem the Arabian heard about it, they laughed at us and despised us and said, "What are you going to do? Are you going to rebel against the king?"
Then I answered them and said, "The God of heaven will make us prosperous, so we who are his servants will get up and rebuild. But you have no portion, right, or memorial in Jerusalem."

Then the high priest Eliashib and his priest brothers began rebuilding the city. They sanctified the sheep gate and installed its doors, and they continued building from the tower of Meah all the way to the tower of Hananeel.
The men of Jericho built next to Eliashib, and Imri's son Zaccur built next to them.
But Hassenaah's sons rebuilt the fish gate, and they also laid its beams and installed its doors, locks, and bars.

Next door to them Meremoth began making repairs, next door to him Meshullam began making repairs, and next door to him Zadok began making repairs. And Meremoth was Urijah's son, Urijah was Koz's son, Meshullam was Berechiah's son, Berechiah was Meshezabel's son, and Zadok was Baana's son.
Next to them the Tekoites began making repairs, but their nobles thought they were above manual labor, and they refused to help with their Lord's construction work.
Besides rebuilding the old gate, Jehoiada and Meshullam laid its beams and installed its doors, locks, and bars. Jehoiada was Paseah's son and this particular Meshullam was Besodeiah's son.
Next other men who began the work to rebuild were Melatiah the Gibeonite, Jadon the Meronothite, and the men of Gibeon and Mizpah, who were under the governor west of the Euphrates.

Next to him Harhaiah's son Uzziel, one of the goldsmiths began work to help them rebuild. Also next to him Hananiah who was the son of one of the apothecaries, began work to broaden and fortify the wall in Jerusalem.
Next to them Hur's son Rephaiah who governed half of Jerusalem, began work rebuilding the city.
Next to them Harumaph's son Jedaiah began repairs to the wall next to his house, and his neighbor Hashabniah's son Hattush helped.
Harim's son Malchijah and Pahath-Moab's son Hashub worked on another part of the wall, and the furnace chimneys.
Next to him Halohesh's son Shallum, who governed the other half of Jerusalem and his daughters helped with the repairs.
Hanun and the inhabitants of Zanoah rebuilt the valley gate and installed its doors, locks, and bars and they repaired 1,000 cubits of the wall all the way down to the gate of the city landfill.
But the city landfill gate was repaired by Rechab's son Malchiah who governed part of Beth-Haccerem. He rebuilt it and installed its doors, locks, and bars.

But the fountain gate was repaired by Colhozeh's son Shallun who rebuilt it, covered it, installed its doors, locks, and bars. He also worked on the wall of the pool of Siloah near the king's garden, and the stairs that descend from the city of David. Shallum also governed part of Mizpah.

After him was Azbuk's son Nehemiah who governed half of Beth-Zur, began repairs at a place next to King David's tombs, and rebuilt the wall all the way to the manmade pool and the House of the Mighty.
After him were the Levites under Bani's son Rehum. Next to him was Hashabiah who governed half of Keilah, who began repairs in his district.
After him their brothers supervised by Henadad's son Bavai who governed the other half of Keilah, began repairs in his district.
Next to him Jeshua's son Ezer who governed another part of Mizpah, began the repairs to the wall that went up towards the armory at the corner of the wall.
After him Zabbai's son Baruch earnestly repaired another part of the wall from the corner to the door of high priest Eliashib's house.
After him Meremoth repaired another part of the wall from the door of Eliashib's house to the end of Eliashib's house. Meremoth was Urijah's son and Urijah was Koz's son.
After him the priests from the plains made repairs.
After him Benjamin and Hashub made repairs to the wall next to their house. After him Azariah began repairing the wall next to his house. Azariah was Maaseiah's son and Maaseiah was Ananiah's son.
After him Henadad's son Binnui began repairing another part of the wall from where it turned next to Azariah's house all the way to the corner.
Uzai's son Palal made repairs next to where the wall turned and the tower near the king's high house by the prison courtyard. After him Parosh's son Pedaiah made repairs.
Besides that, the temple servants who lived in Ophel, began repairs next to the place near the eastern water gate toward the tower that lies outside the city.
After them the Tekoites repaired another part of the wall next to the great tower that lies outside the city, all the way to the wall of Ophel.
Above the horse gate the priests worked to make repairs to the wall near their own house.
After them Immer's son Zadok made repairs next his house. After him Shechaniah's son Shemaiah the eastern gatekeeper made repairs.
