After him Shelemiah's son Hananiah and Zalaph's sixth son Hanun repaired another part of the wall. After him Berechiah's son Meshullam began repairs next to his room.
After him Malchiah the goldsmith's son made repairs to the wall near the temple assistants and merchants, next to the Miphkad gate that goes up to the corner of the wall.
The goldsmiths and merchants began to make repairs to the upper wall, between the upper corner and the sheep gate.
But when Sanballat heard that we were rebuilding the wall, he was angry and filled with indignation, and he mocked the Jews.

He spoke to his brothers and the Samarian army and said, "What are these feeble Jews doing? Can they rebuild everything by themselves, and will they make sacrifices? Will they be finished in a day? Can they restore the stones from the piles of burnt rubble?"
Then Tobiah the Ammonite standing next to him spoke up and said, "Even if a fox were to climb up on their wall, it would cause their stone wall to fall."
Hear us O our God because we are despised. Turn their spite back on their own head, and give them over to captivity and let them be carried away to another land as prey.
And cover not their immorality, and do not let their sin be erased from before you, because they have provoked you to anger before the builders.
So we rebuilt the wall, and joined it all together up to half its original height, because the people decided to work.
But when Sanballat, Tobiah, the Arabians, Ammonites, and Ashdodites heard that the walls of Jerusalem were being built up. And after the broken defenses began to be repaired, they became very angry.
And they all conspired together to come to attack and hinder Jerusalem.
Nevertheless, because of them we prayed to our God, and stood watch against them day and night.
Then the people of Judah said, "The manual laborers' strength has decayed, and there is so much rubble there that we will never rebuild the wall."
And our adversaries said, "They will not know we are there nor see us coming, until we are in the middle of them, and we will kill them to stop their work."
When the Jews who lived near them came to us said ten times over, "Wherever you return from they will be on you and attack you."
So I assigned people hidden behind the wall by their families to protect the lower and higher places armed with their swords, spears, and bows.

After I inspected the defenses, I stood before the nobles, leaders, and the rest of the people and said, "Do not be afraid of them, remember the great and awesome Lord and fight for your brothers, sons, daughters, wives, and homes."
When our enemies heard that we knew about their plans to attack us, and God had brought their counsel to nothing, we all returned to our work on the wall.
From that time on, half of my servants worked on the wall, and the other half of them held stood guard with spears, shields, bows, and armor. The officers stood behind all of Judah's people.
Everyone who labored and worked rebuilding the wall, worked with one hand and held a weapon in the other hand.
Each of the builders had their sword strapped to his side. And this is how they built, but the trumpeter stood next to me.
Then I addressed the nobles, leaders, and everyone else and said, "The work is great and large, and we are separated far from each other on the wall.
So wherever you hear the trumpet sound coming from, run to us at that place, because our God will fight for us.
So we labored on, and half of them held their spears from the morning sunrise until the stars appeared at night.
At the same time I said to the people, "Everyone and their servants must stay inside Jerusalem at night so they can stand guard at night, and labor by day."
So neither I nor my brothers, servants, or the guards who followed me removed our clothes except when they took them off for washing.
There was a great cry from the people and their wives against their Jewish brothers.
Because some people there said, "We have many sons and daughters, and we need wheat for them to eat and live."
Others there also said, "We have mortgaged our lands, vineyards, and houses just to buy wheat because of the shortage."
And still others said, "We have borrowed money for the king's taxes on our lands and vineyards.

But now we are like our brothers and their children, and we are bringing our sons and daughters into bondage. Some of our daughters are already in bondage, but we are powerless to rescue them, because other men own our lands and vineyards."
I was very angry when I heard these words and their cries.
Then I thought about the situation and I reprimanded the nobles and leaders and said, "You exact usury from every one of your brothers!" So I assembled a great crowd against them.

So I spoke to the nobles and leaders and said, "We have done our best to rescued our Jewish brothers who were sold to foreigners. But it seems that you are selling your own brothers, so you can sell them back to us!" Then held they their peace, because they were speechless and unable to answer.
I also said, "It is not a good that you do not walk in the fear of our God. Do you not want to avoid the same reproach that our foreign enemies receive?
Me, my brothers, and servants have been lending money and wheat to the people. I pray you will please let us stop this usury.

I pray you will restore their lands, vineyards, olive groves, and their houses to them this day. I also ask you to return the percentage of the money, wheat, wine, and oil that you have been exacting from them.

Then they said, "We will restore everything to them and require nothing more from them. And we will do as you say." Then I summoned the priests, and the nobles and leaders took an oath, that they would do everything that they promised.

I also shook the wrinkles from my robe and said, "May God shake every man from his house and possessions that does not keep this promise, and may he have everything shaken out until he is completely empty. Then all the congregation said, "Amen, and praise the Lord!" And the people did everything that they promised.

I was the Jewish governor in Judah for twelve years, from the twentieth to the thirty-second year of the reign of King Artaxerxes. During that time, my brothers and I never took food or money from the people as the other leaders did.

But the former governors that came before me burdened the people, and they took their bread and wine plus forty silver shekels. Yes, even their servants burdened the people, but I did not because I feared God.
Instead, I continued doing the work on this wall, we did not buy any land and all of my servants worked on that place.
Besides that, there were 150 Jews and leaders at my table plus the others that came to us from among the heathen all around us.

They prepared one ox, six choice sheep, and birds for me every day. Once every ten days they brought all sorts of wine from the storehouse. But for all this I did not require the bread allotted for the governor, because the burden on these people was very heavy.
Think favorably of me my God, because of all the good that I have done for these people.

When Sanballat, Tobiah, Geshem the Arabian, and the rest of our enemies heard that I had built the wall, and all the broken defenses had been repaired except for the doors on the gates that had not yet been installed.
Sanballat and Geshem sent me a message that said, "Come meet us in one of the villages on the plains of Ono." But I knew they were planning to attack me.
And I sent a message back to them that said, "I am doing a great work and I cannot come down. Why should I stop work to leave and come down to see you?"
But they sent me four messages like this, and I always gave them the same answer.
Then Sanballat sent his servant to me a fifth time with an open letter in his hand.

In which was written, "It is being reported among the foreigners, and Gashmu is also saying that you and the Jews are thinking about rebelling, and that you are building the wall, in order to become their king.

It is also being said that you have appointed prophets to preach about you in Jerusalem who are saying, 'There is a king in Judah, and soon this will be reported to the king.' So come, and let us discuss this together."
Then I sent a message back to him that said, "There is no truth to the rumors you are spreading, you just invent them from your own heart."
Because they are all trying to frighten us by saying, "Their hands will be weakened from the work, and the work will never be done." So I ask O God, that you strengthen my hands.

Afterward, I went to see Shemaiah who was confined to his house and he said, "Let's meet inside the temple of God's house, and we can shut the temple doors because they will be coming to kill you in the middle of the night!" Shemaiah was Delaiah's son and Delaiah was Mehetabeel's son.
And I said, "I am not the kind of man to flee, should a man such as me go into the temple to save his own life? I will not go in there!"
Then I realized that God had not given this message to Shemaiah for me, but he pronounced this false prophecy against me because Tobiah and Sanballat had hired him.
He was hired to scare me to make me commit a sin by doing what he said, so he could make an evil report against me.
O My God, remember forever what Tobiah, Sanballat, the prophetess Noadiah, and the rest of the prophets have done, in order to put fear in my heart.
So the wall was finished in 52 days on the 25th day of the month of Elul.
When all our enemies heard about it, and all the foreign heathens around us saw these things, they were afraid and depressed, because they realized that all this was the work of our God!
Besides that, in those days the nobles of Judah sent many letters to Tobiah, and Tobiah sent many letters back to them.

Many people in Judah had sworn an oath to Tobiah, because he was Shechaniah's son-in-law, and his son Johanan was also married Meshullam's daughter. Shechaniah was Arah's son and Meshullam was Berechiah's son.
They also reported Tobiah's good deeds to me, and told him everything I said, and he sent me letters to put fear in my heart.
After I built the wall and installed the doors, and after I had appointed the gatekeepers, singers, and Levites.
I let my brother Hanani govern Jerusalem along with Hananiah the palace commander, because he was a faithful man who feared God more than most other men.

And I said to them, "Do not open the gates of Jerusalem until the sun is hot. While the guards stand by bar the doors and keep them closed. Appoint the inhabitants of Jerusalem to keep watch, some at their post and some at their house."
Now the city was large and great, but the people were few in there, and the houses were not built.
Then my God put it in my heart to assemble the nobles, leaders, and the people to be counted by their genealogy. I found the following written genealogical record of the first people to return.
These are the people from the provinces that King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon carried away as slaves, who returned to their own cities in Jerusalem and Judah.

These people returned with Zerubbabel, Jeshua, Nehemiah, Azariah, Raamiah, Nahamani, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispereth, Bigvai, Nehum, and Baanah. The following is a count sorted by their families of the people who returned to Israel:

Keros, Sia, Padon,

There was a total of 302 descendants from the temple assistants and Solomon's servants.
These were the undocumented people who returned from Telmelah: Tel-Haresha, Cherub, Addon, and Immer. But they could not prove who their forefathers were, or that they were descendants of Israel.
Delaiah, Tobiah, and Nekoda had 642 descendants.
From the priests there was Habaiah, Koz, and Barzillai's descendants. Barzillai took his father-in-law's name and he was married to Barzillai the Gileadite's daughter.
These men searched for their genealogical records, but they could not find them. That's why they were considered to be polluted and they were excluded from the priesthood as unclean.
The governor spoke to them and told them that they should not eat the most Holy things until a priest could consult the Urim and Thummim on their behalf.
Altogether the entire congregation totaled:42,360.
Beside that they had 7,337 male and female servants, and they also had 245 male and female singers.
They had 736 horses and 245 mules.
They had 435 camels and 6,720 donkeys.
Some of the chief fathers also donated to the work, including the Governor who donated 1,000 gold drams 50 sinks, and 530 thirty robes for the priests.
Some of the other chief fathers donated 22,000 gold drams and 2,200 silver minas to the work treasury.
The rest of the people donated 20,000 gold drams, 2,000 silver minas, and 67 robes for the priests.

So the Levites, temple assistants, priests, gatekeepers, singers, some of the other people, and all of the Israelis settled in their own cities. And by the end of the seventh month all the Israelis had settled in their cities.
All the people gathered together in the street before the water gate, and they spoke to Ezra the scribe as one voice and asked him to bring out the Lord's Book of the Law of Moses for Israel.
On the first day of the seventh month, Ezra the priest brought the law before the congregation of men and women, and everyone else that could hear and understand.

So right there in the street before the water gate Ezra the priest read the law from morning till noon, before the men and women and everyone else that could understand. And the people were very attentive as they listened to the reading of the Book of the Law of Moses.

Ezra the scribe stood on a wooden pulpit which had been made for that purpose. Mattithiah, Shema, Anaiah, Urijah, Hilkiah, and Maaseiah stood beside him at his right side. Pedaiah, Mishael, Malchiah, Hashum, Hashbadana, Zechariah, and Meshullam stood at his left side.
Ezra opened the book in plain sight of all the people, and because he was above everyone else when he opened it, they all stood up.
Ezra blessed the great Lord God, and all the people answered, "Amen, amen!" Then they lifted up their hands, and bowed their heads and worshipped the Lord facing the ground.
Also Jeshua, Bani, Sherebiah, Jamin, Akkub, Shabbethai, Hodijah, Maaseiah, Kelita, Azariah, Jozabad, Hanan, Pelaiah, and the Levites helped the people understand the law as they all stood there.
So they read from the book of God's law, and they helped the people make sense of the law, as they tried to help them understand the meanings of it.

Then Nehemiah the local governor, priest Ezra the scribe, and the Levites all taught the people and said, "Do not mourn or weep as you listen because this is a holy day to your Lord God!" Because all the people wept as they heard the words of the law.

Then Nehemiah said to them, "Go your own way, eat the rich food and drink the sweet drinks, and send portions to those who have prepared nothing, because this is a holy day to our Lord, and do not grieve because the Lord's joy is your strength."
So the Levites comforted the people and said, "Hold your peace and do not grieve because this day is holy."
Then everyone left and went their own way to eat, drink, and send portions to the unprepared, and they rejoiced greatly, because they understood the words that they had just heard.
On the second day Ezra the scribe assembled the people's chief fathers, priests, and Levites together to help them understand the words of the law.
And they discovered written in the law which the Lord had given through Moses, that the Israelis were supposed to live in huts during the feast of the seventh month.

So they published an order and sent it throughout all of Jerusalem and their other cities which read, "Go to the mountains and fetch some olive, pine, myrtle, and palm branches along with branches from other trees to build huts as it is written in the law.

So the people went and brought back branches to make huts for themselves. Everyone built huts on the roofs of their houses, in their courtyards, in the courtyards of God's temple, in the street by the water gate, and in the street by the Gate of Ephraim.

The entire congregation of those who had returned from the captivity made huts, and they sat in them. Because since the days of Nun's son Jeshua no one in Israel had celebrated this way, and they were happy and rejoiced greatly.

So day after day from the first day to the last, Ezra read from the Book of the Law of God and they kept the feast for seven days. Then on the eighth day they assembled a solemn assembly as it was required by the law.
On the 24th day of that month the Israelis descendants assembled together to fast and they wore sackcloth with dust on their heads.
The Israelis separated themselves from all the foreigners, and they confessed their sins and the wickedness of their fathers.
As they stood they read from their Lord God's Book of the Law for 1/4th of the day, and they confessed their sins and worshipped their Lord God for another 1/4th of the day.
Then the Levites: Jeshua, Bani, Kadmiel, Shebaniah, Bunni, Sherebiah, Bani, and Chennai stood on the stairs and cried out with a loud voice to their Lord God.

Then the Levites: Jeshua, Kadmiel, Bani, Hashabniah, Sherebiah, Hodijah, Shebaniah, and Pethahiah said, "Stand up and forever praise and bless your Lord God and his glorious name which is glorified above all others.

You alone are the Lord God, you made the heaven and the heaven of heavens with all their sun, moon, stars, and the earth with everything on it including its seas and everything in them. You protect them all and the hosts of heaven worship you.
You are the Lord God who chose Abram, who brought him out of Ur of the Chaldeans and changed his name to Abraham.

You found his heart to be faithful before you, and you made a covenant with him to give him the lands of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Jebusites, and Girgashites to give to his descendants. And you have kept your promises because you are righteous.
You saw the affliction of our fathers in Egypt, and heard their cries by the Red Sea.

You showed signs and wonders to Pharaoh, all his servants, and all the people of his land. Because you knew they dealt proudly against our fathers. So you established your name that survives to this very day.
You divided the Red Sea before them, and they walked through the middle of the sea on dry land. You threw their persecutors into the ocean depths like a stone thrown into turbulent waters.
Besides that, you led them by day with a column of clouds and by night with a column of fire, to light their way and lead them.
You also came down to Mount Sinai and spoke with them from heaven. You gave them your true and righteous judgments, laws, and commandments.

You did not abandon them when they refused to obey and did not remember the signs and wonders that you showed them. Instead they were stubborn and rebellious and they appointed a leader to lead them back into bondage. But you are a forgiving God, who is always kind, gracious, merciful, ready to pardon, and slow to anger.
You gave them bread from heaven for their hunger, and water from the rock for their thirst. You told them to take possession of the land that you promised and swore an oath to give them.
But they and our fathers were stubborn and dealt proudly, and they did not listen to your commandments.

They refused to obey and did not remember the signs and wonders that you showed them. Instead they were stubborn and rebellious and they appointed a leader to lead them back into bondage. But you are a forgiving God, who is always kind, gracious, merciful, ready to pardon, slow to anger, and you did not abandon them.
Even after they cast a molten calf and said, 'This is your God who brought you up out of Egypt!' And you did not abandon them even after they greatly provoked you.

Yet in your many mercies you did not forsake them in the wilderness. The column of clouds that lead their way by day did not leave them, nor did the column of fire by night that showed them the light and the way to go.
You also gave them your good spirit to instruct them, you did not withhold your manna from them for food, and you gave them water to drink.
You sustained them in the wilderness for forty years, and they lacked nothing, their clothes did not grow old, and their feet did not swell up.
Besides that, you gave them kingdoms and nations, and you gave them every corner of land. And they took possession of the lands that belonged to King Sihon of Heshbon and King Og of Bashan.
You multiplied their children like the stars of heaven, and you brought them into the land that you promised to their fathers, so that they could go in and take possession of it.

So the children went in and took possession of the land, and you subdued the inhabitants of the land before them. You put the Canaanites into their hands, along with their kings and the people of the land, so they could do with them whatever they wanted.

They captured reinforced cities, and they took possession of a rich land full of vineyards, olive groves, houses full of goods, wells that were already dug, and an abundance fruit trees. So they ate their fill and became fat, and they delighted in your great goodness.

But they were disobedient and rebellious, and they turned their backs on your law. They killed your prophets who testified against them and tried to turn them back to you, they also blasphemed and provoked you.

So you delivered them into the hands of their enemies, who oppressed them. And in their time of trouble, after they cried out to you, you heard them from heaven, and with your many mercies you gave them saviors, who saved them from their enemies.

But after they rested, they committed evil acts before you again, so you left them in their enemies land and they had the complete control over them. But when they returned and cried out to you, you heard them from heaven, and with your mercies you delivered them from evil many times.

You testified against them and tried to bring them back to your law, but they were too proud and they refused to listen to your commandments. They sinned against your judgments, which men live by if they obey them. They were just stubborn and shrugged their shoulders, and would not listen.
But you restrained them for many years, and your spirit testified against them through your prophets. But they would not listen, so you gave them over into the hands of the people of the lands.
Nevertheless, because you are a gracious and merciful God full of great mercies, you did not completely consume them nor abandon them.

So our great, mighty, and awesome God who keep his covenant and mercies, do not think little of or overlook all our troubles that have come upon us or our kings, princes, priests, prophets, our fathers, and all your people since the time of the Assyrian kings until today.
However you have been true in everything that has come upon us, because you have been righteous, but we have been wicked.
We have not kept your law, nor have we listened to your commandments and testimonies that you testified against us, and neither have our kings, princes, priests, nor our fathers.
In your great goodness you gave them a kingdom where they did not serve you, and you gave them a large rich land, but they still did not turn away from their wicked works.
Behold, today we are servants in the land that you gave to our fathers to eat and enjoy its good fruit, and we are their servants!
The land produces much bounty for the kings whom you have put over us because of our sins. They treat our bodies and cattle as they please, and we are in great distress.
Because of all this we are making a binding covenant with you in writing and our princes, Levites, and priests will place their seal on it.
Those who sealed the covenant were: Nehemiah, the governor, Hachaliah's son, Zidkijah,
Seraiah, Azariah, Jeremiah,
Pashur, Amariah, Malchijah,
Hattush, Shebaniah, Malluch,
Harim, Meremoth, Obadiah,
Daniel, Ginnethon, Baruch,
Meshullam, Abijah, and Mijamin.
The priests: Maaziah, Bilgai, and Shemaiah.
The Levites: Azaniah's son Jeshua, Henadad's descendant Binnui, and Kadmiel.
And their Levite brothers: Shebaniah, Hodijah, Kelita, Pelaiah, Hanan,
Micha, Rehob, Hashabiah,
Zaccur, Sherebiah, Shebaniah,
Hodijah, Bani, and Beninu.
And the leaders of the people: Parosh, Pahath-Moab, Elam, Zatthu, Bani,
Bunni, Azgad, Bebai,
Adonijah, Bigvai, Adin,
Ater, Hizkijah, Azzur,
Hodijah, Hashum, Bezai,
Hariph, Anathoth, Nebai,
Magpiash, Meshullam, Hezir,
Meshezabeel, Zadok, Jaddua,
Pelatiah, Hanan, Anaiah,
Hoshea, Hananiah, Hashub,
Hallohesh, Pileha, Shobek,
Rehum, Hashabnah, Maaseiah,
Ahijah, Hanan, Anan,
Malluch, Harim, and Baanah.

The rest of the people including the Levites, priests, gatekeepers, singers, temple assistants, and everyone else who separated themselves from the people of the lands to obey the law of God, along with their wives, sons, and daughters who are knowledgeable and understanding.

They joined their noble brothers and entered into a curse and an oath to walk in God's law, which was given through Moses the servant of God. They also promised to observe and obey all our Lord God's commandments, judgments, and laws.
We promised not allow our daughters to marry the people of the land, and not to allow their daughters to marry our sons.

We promised if the people of the land brought merchandise or prepared food to sell on the Sabbath day or the holy day, that we would not buy it from them. We also promised that every seventh year we would cancel every debt we are owed.
We also made a law to annually charge ourselves 1/3rd of a shekel to service our God's house.

That money is for the priest's bread offering, the regular bread offering, and the daily burnt offerings. It is also for the Sabbaths, new moons and appointed feasts, the holy things, and the sin offerings to make an atonement for Israel. Plus all the work that must be done to maintain the house of our God.

Then we cast lots among the Levites, priests, and the people to determine which families will bring the wood offering into our God's house at the appointed time every year. This offering will be used to burn the offerings on our Lord God's altar, as it is written in the law.
We also cast lots to decide who will bring the first fruits from our ground, and the first fruits from all the trees to the Lord's temple every year.
We will also bring the firstborn of our sons, cattle, herds, and flocks to the priests that minister in our God's house, as it is written in the law.

In addition we should bring the first fruits of our dough, grain, fruit from all types of trees, wine, and oil to the priests in the chambers of our God's house. And we will give our tithes from ground to the Levites, so they can have all the tithes from the cities where we till the ground.
And a priest from Aaron's descendants will be with the Levites when they take the tithes, and the Levites must bring 1/10th of the tithes to the storehouses and treasuries our God's house.

Because the Israelis and the Levites must bring the wheat, new wine, and oil offerings into the storerooms where the sanctuary vessels are kept, and where the ministering priests, gatekeepers, and singers stay. And we will not forsake our God's house.

The leaders of the people who lived in Jerusalem and everyone else, cast lots to determine which 1/10th of the people would live in the holy city of Jerusalem, and the rest were to live to other cities.
And the people blessed all the men who willingly offered to live at Jerusalem.

These are the provincial chiefs who settled in Jerusalem. But the Israelis, Levites, priests, temple assistants, and Solomon's servants' descendants lived in Judah, on their own land in their own cities.

Some of Judah and Benjamin's descendants lived in Jerusalem. From Judah's descendants there was Uzziah's son Athaiah. Uzziah was Zechariah's son, Zechariah was Amariah's son, Amariah was Shephatiah's son, Shephatiah was Mahalalel's son, and Mahalalel was one of Perez's descendants.

And there was Baruch's son Maaseiah. Maaseiah was Colhozeh's son, Colhozeh was Hazaiah's son, Hazaiah was Adaiah's son, Adaiah was Joiarib's, Joiarib was Zechariah's son, and Zechariah was one of Shiloni's descendants.
Perez's courageous descendants who lived in Jerusalem totaled 468 mighty men of valor.

From Benjamin's descendants there was Meshullam's son Sallu. Sallu was Joed's son, Joed was Pedaiah's son, Pedaiah was Kolaiah's son, Kolaiah was Maaseiah's son, Maaseiah was Ithiel's son, and Ithiel was Jesaiah's son.
After him there was Gabbai and Sallai with 928 descendants.
Zichri's son Joel was their supervisor, and Senuah's son Judah was the city's assistant supervisor.
The priests were: Joiarib's son Jedaiah and Jachin.
Hilkiah's son Seraiah was the leader of the house of God. Seraiah was Meshullam's son, Meshullam was Zadok's son, Zadok was Meraioth's son, and Meraioth was Ahitub's son.

The brothers who did the work at the temple totaled 822 men, and Adaiah was another priest who settled in Jerusalem. Adaiah was Jeroham's son, Jeroham was Pelaliah's son, Pelaliah was Amzi's son, Amzi was Zechariah's son, Zechariah was Pashur's son, and Pashur was Malchiah's son.

Altogether there were 242 brothers who were the chief fathers that settled in Jerusalem, and Amashai was another priest there. Amashai was Azareel's son, Azareel was Ahasai's son, Ahasai was Meshillemoth's son, and Meshillemoth was Immer's son.
The brothers who were the mighty men of valor there totaled 128 men, and Zabdiel who was the son of one of the great men was their commander.
Also of the Levites, Shemaiah the son of Hashub, the son of Azrikam, the son of Hashabiah, the son of Bunni.
The Levite chiefs were Shabbethai and Jozabad, they supervised the public services of God's house.

Another Levite brother was Micha's son Mattaniah who was the principal who began the thanksgiving in prayer, and Bakbukiah was his assistant. Micha was Zabdi's son and Zabdi was Asaph's son. Bakbukiah was Abda's son, Abda was Shammua's son, Shammua was Galal's son, and Galal was Jeduthun's son.
Altogether there were 284 Levites in the holy city.
Besides that, there were 172 brothers who were gatekeepers in Jerusalem including Akkub and Talmon.
The other Israelis including the Levites and priests all lived on their own land in the other cities of Judah.
But the temple servants lived in Ophel, and Ziha and Gispa supervised the temple servants.

Uzzi was the Levite supervisor in Jerusalem who helped the priests there. Uzzi was Bani's son, Bani was Hashabiah's son, Hashabiah was Mattaniah's son, and Mattaniah was Micha's son. Uzzi was one of Asaph's descendants, they were the singers who helped supervise the services of God's house.
Because it was the king who ordered that the singers should be allowed to perform at certain times every day.
Pethahiah was the king's ambassador to the Israelis people. Pethahiah was Meshezabel's son, they were descended from Judah's son Zerah.
As for the villages and their fields, some of Judah's descendants lived in Kirjath-Arba, Dibon, Jekabzeel, and their villages.
They also lived in: Jeshua, Moladah, Beth-Phelet,
Hazar-Shual, Beersheba, and their villages.
They also lived in Ziklag, Mekonah, and their villages.
And they lived in: Enrimmon, Zareah, Jarmuth,
Zanoah, Adullam, Azekah, and in their villages, and they lived in Lachish and its fields, from Beersheba all the way to the Valley of Hinnom.
Benjamin's descendants from Geba lived in Michmash, Aija, Bethel, and their villages.
And they lived in: Anathoth, Nob, Ananiah,
Hazor, Ramah, Gittaim,
Hadid, Zeboim, Neballat,
Lod, and Ono the Valley of Craftsmen.
And some Levite divisions lived in Judah and Benjamin.
These are the Levites and priests who went with Shealtiel's son Zerubbabel: Jeshua, Seraiah, Jeremiah, Ezra,
Amariah, Malluch, Hattush,
Shechaniah, Rehum, Meremoth,
Iddo, Ginnetho, Abijah,
Miamin, Maadiah, Bilgah,
Shemaiah, and Joiarib, Jedaiah,
Sallu, Amok, Hilkiah, and Jedaiah were their brothers and chief priests in the days of Jeshua.
The Levites Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel, Sherebiah, Judah, and Mattaniah. And Mattaniah supervised the thanksgiving along with his brothers.
Their brothers Bakbukiah and Unni stood near them in the audience.
And Jeshua fathered Joiakim, Joiakim fathered Eliashib, Eliashib fathered Joiada,
Joiada fathered Jonathan, and Jonathan fathered Jaddua.
In Joiakim's day, these were the priests and chief fathers: from Seraiah there was Meraiah, and from Jeremiah there was Hananiah.
From Ezra there was Meshullam, and from Amariah there was Jehohanan.
From Melicu there was Jonathan, and from Shebaniah there was Joseph.
From Harim there was Adna, and from Meraioth there was Helkai.
From Iddo there was Zechariah, and from Ginnethon there was Meshulla.
From Abijah there was Zichri, and from Miniamin and Moadiah there was Piltai.
From Bilgah there was Shammua, and from Shemaiah there was Jehonathan.
From Joiarib there was Mattenai, and from Jedaiah there was Uzzi.
From Sallai there was Kallai, and from Amok there was Eber.
From Hilkiah there was Hashabiah, and from Jedaiah there was Nathaniel.
The chief fathers and priests of the Levites in the days of Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan, and Jaddua were recorded during the reign of King Darius of Persia.
The chief fathers of the Levite descendants up until the days of Eliashib's son Johanan were written in the Book of the Chronicles.
And the Levite chiefs Hashabiah, Sherebiah, and Kadmiel's son Jeshua along with their brothers who stood next to them, took turns praising and giving thanks, as King David the man of God had ordered.
Mattaniah, Bakbukiah, Obadiah, Meshullam, Talmon, and Akkub were the gatekeepers who stood guard by the gateway thresholds.
They served during the days of priest Ezra the scribe, Governor Nehemiah, and Jeshua's son Joiakim. Joiakim was Jozadak's son.

At the dedication of Jerusalem's wall they looked everywhere for Levites to bring them to Jerusalem, to celebrate the dedication with thanksgiving, happiness, and singing accompanied by cymbals, lyres, and harps.
The musicians all came together from Netophathi's villages and the plains country all around Jerusalem.
They also came from the house of Gilgal and the fields of Geba and Azmaveth, because the musicians had built villages all around Jerusalem.
After the priests and Levites purified themselves, the people, the gates, and the wall.
I, Nehemiah, brought the leaders of Judah up on the wall, and appointed two great companies of musicians to gave thanks. One company moved to the right on top of the wall toward the dung gate.
Hoshaiah and half the leaders of Judah followed them.
Along with Azariah, Ezra, Meshullam,
Judah, Benjamin, Shemaiah, and Jeremiah.
And some of the priests' sons who had trumpets, including Jonathan's son Zechariah, and Shemaiah's son, Mattaniah's son, Micaiah's son, Zaccur's son, and Asaph's son.
Along with his brothers Shemaiah, Azarael, Milalai, Gilalai, Maai, Nathaniel, Judah, and Hanani who brought the musical instruments that David the man of God prescribed. And Ezra the scribe led them.
At the Fountain Gate they climbed the steps that ascended to the wall of City of David where they could look down at David's house above the east water gate.
The other company of musicians who gave thanks went with the other half of the people on the wall to the left. I, Nehemiah, followed them past the furnace tower all the way to the broad wall.
And they marched above the Ephraim gate, the old gate, the fish gate, the Tower of Hananeel, and the Tower of Meah, all the way to the sheep gate. Then they stopped at the prison gate.
So I, Nehemiah, the two companies of musicians, and half the leaders with me stood in the house of God and gave thanks.
Along with these priests Eliakim with their trumpets: Maaseiah, Miniamin, Micaiah, Elioenai, Zechariah, and Hananiah.
Then Maaseiah, Shemaiah, Eleazar, Uzzi, Jehohanan, Malchijah, Elam, and Ezer along with their supervisor Jezrahiah and the other musicians, all sang loudly.

That day they also rejoiced and offered great sacrifices, because God had made them rejoice with great joy. All the wives and the children also rejoiced, and the joy of Jerusalem was heard very far away.

At that time some people were appointed over the treasury storerooms, because of all the offerings of the first fruits and tithes. The law required the portions to be collected from the cities fields and stored for the priests and Levites. Because all of Judah rejoiced for the priests and Levites who served God.
Then both the singers and gatekeepers performed their God's services of purification, as King David and his son Solomon had ordered.
Because in the old days, King David and Asaph the head musician, and their singers sang songs of praise and thanksgiving to God.

So all the Israelis in the days of Zerubbabel and Nehemiah, gave daily portions of the offerings to the singers and gatekeepers. They sanctified the holy things to the Levites, and the Levites sanctified them to Aaron's descendants.

One day they were reading to the audience from the Book of Moses, and they discovered that it was written in the book that the Ammonites and Moabites were forever banned from joining God's congregation.
Because they did not meet the Israelis with bread and with water, but they hired Balaam to attack them, so he could curse them, however our God turned the curse into a blessing.
After they heard what was written in the law, they separated all the mixed foreigners from Israel.
Before this, one of Tobiah's allies, Priest Eliashib, had been appointed to manage the storehouses of our God's house.

Eliashib had prepared a large storeroom for Tobiah, where they had previously laid the bread offerings, frankincense, vessels, tithes of wheat, new wine, and oil donations which the king had ordered to be given to the Levites, singers, gatekeepers, as well as the priest's offerings.
But during all this time, I, Nehemiah, was not in Jerusalem because I had returned to King Artaxerxes of Babylon in the 32nd year of his reign. Later, I obtained permission from the king to leave.
When I returned to Jerusalem, I discovered the evil things that Eliashib had done for Tobiah by preparing a storeroom for him in the courts of God's house.
And I was terribly grieved, so I threw all of Tobiah's household stuff out of the storeroom.
Then I ordered them to clean the storerooms and I had them bring the vessels, bread offering, and frankincense back into the storerooms of God's house.
I realized that the donations to the Levites and singers had not been given to them for their services, so they had all gone back to their own fields.
Then I dealt harshly with the leaders and asked, "Why has God's house been abandoned?" Then I brought all the Levites and singers back together, and stationed them in their assigned places.
After that, all of Judah brought their tithes of wheat, new wine, and oil to the treasuries.

And because they were trustworthy, I appointed these treasurers over the treasuries: Shelemiah the priest, Zadok the scribe, Pedaiah the Levite, and Hanan was their assistant. Their Job was to manage and distribute the supplies to their fellow Levites. Hanan was Zaccur's son and Zaccur was Mattaniah's son.
Remember me for this, O my God and do not wipe out the good deeds I have done for the house of my God, and its offices.

In those days I saw some people working on the Sabbath in Judah. I saw some treading wine presses, harvesting sheaves, and loading donkeys with wine, grapes, figs, and all types of goods to bring to Jerusalem. So I, Nehemiah testified against them and warned them about selling food on the Sabbath.
There were also men from Tyre who brought fish and all types of merchandise to sell in Judah and Jerusalem, on the Sabbath.
Then I dealt harshly with the nobles of Judah and said, "What is this evil thing that you have done to profane the Sabbath?
Did not your fathers do this very same thing, and did not our God bring all this evil on us, and on this city for this? But you bring more anger on Israel by profaning the Sabbath!

The night before the Sabbath as it began to get dark, I ordered the gates of Jerusalem to be closed shut, and not to be reopened until after the Sabbath. I posted some of my servants at the gates to make sure that nothing could be brought into the city on the Sabbath.
Then the merchants and sellers camped outside Jerusalem a couple of times.
Then I testified against them and said, "Why are you camping outside the wall? If you do it again, I will arrest you!" From that time forward, they no longer came on the Sabbath.
I, Nehemiah, ordered the Levites to purify themselves and stand guard at the gates to keep the Sabbath day holy. O my God, please remember me for this as well, and protect me with your great mercy.
In those days I also noticed that Jews had married wives from Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab.
Half of their children spoke the languages of Ashdod or other people, and they could not speak the language of the Jewish people.

And I dealt with them, and cursed them, and defeated certain of them, and took off their hair, and made them swear by God and said, you will not give your daughters to their sons, nor take their daughters to your sons, or for yourselves.

Did not King Solomon of Israel commit these very same sins? Even though there was no king like him who was so beloved by his God among many nations, and God made him king of all Israel. Nevertheless foreign women lured him into sin.
Do we now have to hear, that you are committing all this great evil and transgression against our God by marrying foreign wives?"
Joiada was Priest Eliashib's son and one of his sons was Sanballat the Horonite's son-in-law. So I drove him away from me.
So remember them, O my God, because they have defiled the priesthood and the covenant of the Levites and the priesthood.
I, Nehemiah, have purified the Levites and priests and removed everything foreign from the temple, and I assigned specific duties to each one of them.
I also scheduled the wood offering and first fruit offerings at the appointed times. So remember me O my God, for all the good that I have done.
King Ahasuerus reigned over 127 provinces, from India to Ethiopia.
In those days King Ahasuerus sat on the throne in his royal palace in Shushan.

In the third year of his reign, King Ahasuerus prepared a feast for all his princes and servants. Military leaders from Persia and Media were there with him along with the nobles and princes of the provinces.
Then King Ahasuerus put his riches, glorious kingdom, and majestic honor on display for 180 days.
After the 180 day period, the king prepared a seven day feast for everyone in the courtyard garden of the king's Shushan palace, and everyone great and small were invited to attend.

The palace was decorated with white, green, and blue wall hangings, fastened with purple fine linen cords to silver rings and marble columns. The sofas were made of gold and silver, and they were arranged on a red, white, black, and blue marble pavement.
The people were served an abundance of royal wine in a variety of gold drinking vessels, which were appropriate for a king.
The king had also ordered his palace servants to serve the people whatever they wanted to drink, there was no limit on how much they were allowed drink, as the law required.
Queen Vashti also prepared a feast for the women in King Ahasuerus' royal palace.

On the seventh day, when the heart of the king was merry with wine, he commanded Mehuman, Biztha, Harbona, Bigtha, and Abagtha, Zethar, and Carcas, the seven eunuchs that served in the presence of Ahasuerus the king.
He told them to bring Queen Vashti to him with the crown royal, to show the people and princes her beauty, because she was very beautiful to look at.
But the queen Vashti refused to come at the king's commandment by his eunuchs, and for that reason was the king very angry, and his anger burned in him.
Then the king asked the wise men who knew the times, because it was the king's custom to consult the wise men who understood the law and judgement.

The king's closest advisors were Carshena, Sethar, Admatha, Tarshish, Meres, Marsena, and Memucan, the seven princes of Persia and Media. They were the his most trusted advisors and highest ranking officials.
What does the law allow us to do to punish Queen Vashti for disobeying an order from King Ahasuerus, that the eunuchs gave her?
Memucan answered the king before his princes and said, "Queen Vashti has not only wronged the king, but she also wronged all the princes and people in all of King Ahasuerus' provinces.

Because when the queen's conduct is reported throughout the kingdom and the women hear about it, they will despise their husbands and say, 'King Ahasuerus ordered Queen Vashti to come to him, but she refused to go.'
Plus this very day all the royal ladies of Persia and Media will hear about the queen's behavior and refuse to listen to the king's princes. This will cause much contempt and anger in the kingdom.

So if it pleases the king, you should issue a royal decree and have it written as an irrevocable law among the laws of the Persians and Medes that says, 'Vashti will never again be allowed to come before King Ahasuerus, and her royal estate will be given to a woman better than her.'
When the king's decree is published throughout the king's great empire, all the wives will honor their husbands, both great and small."
This pleased King Ahasuerus and his princes, and the king did what Memucan said.

He sent letters throughout all the king's provinces, written and published in every script and language in each province to all the people, and it read that every man should be the master of his own house.
After all this King Ahasuerus' anger was appeased, he remembered what Vashti had done and what had been decreed against her.
Then the king's minister spoke to him and said, "We will search for beautiful young virgins for the king.

The king should appoint officers in all his kingdom's provinces, to find and bring the beautiful young virgins to the women's quarters in the Shushan Palace. They will be placed in the custody of Hege the king's eunuch who supervises the women, where they can be given the things they need for their purification.
And the king can choose a young woman that pleases him to replace Queen Vashti. This idea pleased the king, so that's what he did.
Now there was a certain Jew in the Shushan Palace named Mordecai. And Mordecai was Jair's son, Jair was Shimei's son, and Shimei was Kish the Benjamite's son.
Mordecai had been carried away into captivity from Jerusalem with King Jeconiah of Judah, whom King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon had captured and carried away.

Mordecai raised his uncle's daughter Hadassah as his own daughter, because her parents were dead and she had no father or mother. Hadassah was also called Esther and she was a very beautiful young woman.

So after the king's decree had been heard throughout the land, many beautiful young women been brought to the Shushan Palace and placed in Hegai the women's supervisor's custody. And Esther was one of the young women brought to the king's palace and placed in Hegai's custody.

Esther pleased King Ahasuerus and she obtained his kindness and he preferred her above all the others, so he quickly gave her the things she needed for the purification. He also gave her seven young servant women selected from the king's palace. Then she and her maids were moved to the best place in the women's quarters.
Esther had not told them who her people or relatives were, because Mordecai had told her not to.
Mordecai walked to the women's quarters courtyard every day, to find out how Esther was doing and what had become of her.

After every other young woman had met King Ahasuerus and she had been there for twelve months, it was her turn to meet the king. This was because the purification process required six months of beauty treatments with oil of myrrh, then six months of perfume and cosmetic treatments.
Whenever a young woman went to the king, she was given whatever she desired to take with her from the women's quarters to the king's palace.

Each woman went to the king in the evening, and she returned to the women's quarter's the next day, to the custody of the king's eunuch Shaashgaz who took care of the king's concubines. If the king was delighted with her and he summoned her by name she went back to the king, otherwise she was not invited back.

When it was Esther's turn to go to the king, she took nothing except what Hegai the king's eunuch who supervised the women's quarters advised her to take, and Esther found favor in the sight of everyone who saw her. Esther was Abihail's daughter and Mordecai was her uncle who had adopted her as his daughter.
So Esther was taken to King Ahasuerus in his royal palace in Tebeth the tenth month of the seventh year of his reign.

The king loved Esther above all the other women, and she found grace and favor in his sight more than all the other virgins. So he placed the royal crown on her head, and made her his queen instead of Vashti.
Then King Ahasuerus prepared a great feast for Esther and all his princes and servants, and he proclaimed tax relief to all the provinces and gave gifts worthy of a king.
When the virgins were assembled a second time, Mordecai was seated at the king's gate.
Esther had not yet introduced her relatives or her people to the king. Because Esther did what Mordecai had told her to do, just as she had always done while he was raising her.
In those days, while Mordecai sat at the king's gate, Bigthan and Teresh, two of the king's eunuchs who guarded the gates, were angry and conspired to kill the king Ahasuerus.
And Mordecai heard about their plot and he told Queen Esther about it, and she informed the king of what Mordecai had said.
When the accusations were investigated, they were found to be true, so they were both hanged on a tree, and the trial was recorded in the Book of the Chronicles before the king.
After all these things happened King Ahasuerus promoted Hammedatha the Agagite's son Haman, and advanced his seat above all the princes that were with him.
All the king's servants within the king's gate, bowed and respected Haman because the king had ordered it, but Mordecai did not bow nor respect him.
Then the king's servants at the king's gate said to Mordecai, "Why do you disobey the king's commandment?"
Day after day they spoke to him, but he would not listen to them. So they told Haman to see if Mordecai would be allowed to stand without bowing, because he had told them that he was a Jew.
When Haman saw that Mordecai would not bow nor respect him, he was filled with anger.
When he discovered that Mordecai's people were Jews, he rejected the idea of only punishing Mordecai. Instead, he decided to destroy all of Mordecai's people throughout the kingdom of King Ahasuerus.
In Nisan, the first month of the twelfth year of King Ahasuerus' reign, they cast lots before Haman for the Pur to determine the exact date. And the lot fell on the twelfth month of Adar.

Then Haman spoke to King Ahasuerus and said, "There are certain people scattered and dispersed among the people in all the provinces of your kingdom, whose laws differ from all the other people. They do not keep the king's laws, so it is not in your best interest to allow them to behave that way.
If it pleases the king, issue a written decree to destroy them, and I will pay 10,000 silver talents into the treasury to pay the soldiers who carry out these orders."
The king took his ring from his hand, and gave it to Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, who was the enemy of the Jews.
The king said to Haman, "The silver and the people have been turned over to you, to do with them whatever seems right to you."

Then King Ahasuerus' scribes were summoned on the thirteenth day of the first month, and everything that Haman ordered the king's lieutenants to do was written down, and the decree was sent to the governors and other leaders throughout every province. The orders were all written in their own language, and sealed in the king's name, with the king's ring.

The letters were sent by postal carriers throughout all the king's provinces, with orders to destroy and kill all the young, old, and Jewish men, women, and children on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month which was Adar, and to carry away their spoils as plunder.
A copy of the written order was published and given to all the people in every province, so that they would be prepared to attack on that day.
The postal carriers left, hastened by the king's orders, and the decree was delivered to the Shushan Palace, and the king and Haman sat down to drink, but the city of Shushan was baffled.
When Mordecai realized everything that had happened, he tore his clothes, put on sackcloth with ashes, went out into the middle of the city, and cried out with a loud and bitter cry.
He even stood before the king's gate, because it was illegal to enter King Ahasuerus' palace gates wearing sackcloth.
So every province wherever the king's decree and orders went, there was great mourning, fasting, weeping, and wailing among the Jews, and many lay in the streets wearing sackcloth and ashes.
So Esther's maids and eunuchs came and told her what was happening. Then the queen was extremely grieved and she sent clothes to Mordecai to replace his sackcloth, but he would not accept them.
Then Esther sent for Hatach who was one of the eunuchs the king had appointed to attend to her. She gave him an order to go to Mordecai to find out what was going on, and why.
So Hatach went to Mordecai on the city streets before the king's gate.
Mordecai told him everything that had happened, and about the money that Haman had promised to pay the king's treasuries to destroy the Jews.

He also gave him a copy of the written decree that was delivered to the Shushan Palace to destroy them, to show to Esther. He also asked her to go to the king, and declare her people to him and he requested that she would plead with the king on their behalf.
Hatach returned to Esther and told her what Mordecai said.
Again Esther spoke to Hatach, and gave him commandment to Mordecai.

And she told him to say, "All the king's servants and the people in the king's provinces know that any man or women, who approaches the king in the inner court who is not summoned, may be put to death. Unless the king holds out the golden scepter, that allows that person to live. And I have not been summoned to come to king for the past thirty days."
And they told to Mordecai what Esther said.
Then Mordecai ordered Hatach to answer Esther this way, "Do not think only of yourself, and think that you will escape the fate of the Jews in the king's palace.

Because if you hold your peace now, then salvation and deliverance for the Jews will rise up from another place, but you and your father's house will be destroyed. And who knows, perhaps you were sent to this kingdom for just such a time as this?"
Then Esther sent them back to Mordecai with an answer.

And she said, "Go, gather all the Jews in Shushan together, and fast for me, and do not eat nor drink night or day for three days. My young women and I will also fast, and I will go in to see the king, which is against the law, and if I perish, I perish."
So Mordecai went on his way, and did everything that Esther had asked him to do.
On the third day Esther put on her royal apparel, and stood in the inner courtyard next to King Ahasuerus' palace. The king sat on his royal throne in the royal palace, next to the palace gates.

When the king saw Queen Esther standing in the courtyard, he looked upon him favorably and held out the golden scepter in his hand to Esther. So Esther moved closer, and touched the top of the scepter.
Then the king to Esther, "Queen Esther, what would you like to request? Ask and it will be given to you up to half of my kingdom."
And Esther answered, "If you think it is a good idea, I would like for the king and Haman to come to a banquet that I have prepared for you today."
Then the king said, "Tell Haman to come quickly, so he that may do as Esther has asked." And the king and Haman went to the banquet that Esther prepared.
As they drank the banquet wine the king said to Esther, "What is your petition and what is your request? Ask and it will be granted to you, even up to the half the kingdom will be given to you."
Then Esther answered and said, "My petition and my request is this.

If I have found favor in sight of the king, and if it pleases the king to grant my petition and fulfill my request. I will answer the king's question, if the king and Haman would come to the banquet that I will prepare for them tomorrow."

Then Haman left that day with a joyful and glad heart. But when Haman saw Mordecai sitting in the king's gate, and he did not stand up, nor move out of his way, he was filled with indignation against Mordecai.
Nevertheless Haman restrained himself and when he got home, he summoned his friends and his wife Zeresh.

Haman told them glorious stories of his riches, and about all of his children, and all the things the king had promoted him to, and how he had advanced above all the other princes and servants of the king.
And Haman said, "Besides that, Queen Esther had prepared a banquet no one else but the king and myself, and tomorrow I am also invited back to her banquet with the king.
But all of this profits me nothing, as long as I see Mordecai the Jew sitting at the king's gate."

Then his wife Zeresh and all his friends said to him, "Build a gallows fifty cubits high, and ask the king to hang Mordecai. Then go merrily with the king to the banquet." This idea pleased Haman, and he had the gallows built.
That night King Ahasuerus could not sleep, and he commanded them to bring him the Book of the Chronicles, and they read the records before the king.
And it was found written in the book, that Mordecai had told of Bigthana and Teresh, two of the king's eunuchs who were the keepers of the door, had planned to assassinate King Ahasuerus.
And the king asked, "What honor and dignity has been bestowed on Mordecai for this?" Then the king's servants who ministered to him said, "Nothing has been done for him."
And the king said, "Who is that in the courtyard?" Haman had just come into the outer courtyard of the king's palace, to ask the king to hang Mordecai on the gallows that he'd had built for him.
And the king's servants answered him and said, "Haman is standing in the courtyard," and the king said, "Let him come in."
So Haman came in and the king spoke to him and asked, "What can be done for a man that the king wants to honor?" And Haman thought to himself, "Who would the king want to honor more than me?"
Haman answered the king and said, "For the man the king would like to honor,
Let the king's royal apparel be brought to him to wear, let him ride the king's royal horse, and let him wear the royal crown on his head.

Let this royal apparel and horse be given to one of the king's most noble princes, so that they may array the man that the king wants to honor and parade him on horseback through the city streets. And let them proclaim before him, 'And this is how a man is treated that the king wants to honor!'"
Then the king said to Haman, "Hurry and take the royal apparel and horse to Mordecai the Jew, who sits at the king's gate just as you have said, and do not forget to do anything that you have said."

Then Haman took the apparel and horse, and arrayed the honors on Mordecai, and paraded him on horseback through the city streets. And proclaimed before him, "This is how a man is treated that the king wants to honor!"
Mordecai returned to the king's gate. But Haman hurried home, with his head covered mourning himself.

Haman told his wife Zeresh and all his friends everything that had happened to him. Then his wise men and his wife Zeresh spoke to him and said, "If Mordecai is one of the Jews, and you have begun to fall before him, you will not prevail against him and you will surely fall before him."
As they were talking, one of the king's eunuchs hurriedly came to bring Haman to the banquet that Esther had prepared.
So King Ahasuerus and Haman went to Queen Esther's banquet.

Once again, at the second banquet as they were drinking wine the king spoke to Esther and asked, "Queen Esther, what is your petition, and what is your request. Ask and it will be granted, even as much as half of my kingdom."
Then Queen Esther answered and said, "O king, if I have found favor in your sight, and if it pleases the king, let my life be given to me as my petition, and my people's lives as my request.

Because my people and I have been sold out by the enemy of the king to be killed and destroyed, and to perish. But if we had just been sold into slavery, I would have held my tongue, and I would not have burdened the king."
Then King Ahasuerus answered Queen Esther and said, "Who is he, and where is he who would dare devise such a scheme as this in his heart?"
And Esther said, "The adversary and enemy is this wicked Haman!" Then Haman was terrified of the king and queen.

The King got up from the wine banquet table and went out into the palace garden very angry. Then Haman begged and made a request for his life to Queen Esther, because he realized that the king was contemplating evil against him.

King Ahasuerus returned from the palace garden to the wine banquet hall, and Haman had fallen on Queen Esther's bed. Then the king said, would he actually attack the queen while I am still in the palace? As soon as the words left the king's mouth, they covered Haman's face.

Harbonah, one of the eunuchs spoke to the king and said, "Look at this, Haman built a fifty cubits high gallows at his house to hang Mordecai, the man who saved the king's life with his report." Then the king said, "Hang him on it."
So they hanged Haman on the gallows that he had built for Mordecai. Then was the king's anger pacified.
That day King Ahasuerus gave Haman's house who was the enemy of the Jews to Queen Esther, and Mordecai appeared before because Esther had told the king who Mordecai was to her.
The king took off his ring, which he had taken from Haman and gave it to Mordecai, and Esther appointed Mordecai over the house of Haman.
Once again Esther spoke to the king and bowed down at his feet, and tearfully implored him not to allow Haman the Agagite to move forward with his scheme that he devised against the Jews.
Then the king pointed his golden scepter toward Esther, so she rose and stood before the king.

And she said, "If it pleases the king, and if I have found favor in your sight, and you find me pleasing to look upon, and it seems right to you, I ask you to reverse the orders that Haman who was Hammedatha the Agagite's son devised to destroy all the Jews in the king's provinces.
Because, I can not endure watching the evil that is going to come upon my people or family?"
Then King Ahasuerus spoke to queen Esther and Mordecai the Jew and said, "Behold I have given Haman's house to Queen Esther, and he was hanged on the gallows because he abused the Jews.
So you can write whatever you want about the Jews and seal it with the king's ring, because whatever is written in the king's name and sealed with the king's ring, cannot be reversed."

On the 23rd day of the 3rd month of Sivan, the king's scribes wrote whatever Mordecai told them to write. Then they sent letters to the Jews, officials, and governors of the 127 provinces that stretched from India to Ethiopia. And each province received letters written in their own language, including the Jewish provinces.
Mordecai wrote the orders in the name of King Ahasuerus, and sealed them with the king's ring, and sent them out by postal carriers who rode horses, mules, and camels.

The letters included new orders from the king that granted the Jews in every city the right to organize their defenses to defend their life from the power of any people or province that would assault them or try to destroy, kill, or cause their men, women, or children to perish. They were also granted the power to defend their property from being plundered as the spoils of war.
The day that King Ahasuerus appointed for this in all the provinces, was the 13th day of the 12th month of Adar.
A copy of these written orders were published and sent to all the people in every province, so the Jews would be ready to avenge themselves against their enemies on that day.
So the postal carriers left in haste on their on horses, mules, and camel, because the king's decree had to be delivered to the Shushan Palace in time.
Then Mordecai left the king's presence in royal blue and white apparel wearing a great golden crown, and a fine purple linen robe, and the whole city of Shushan gladly rejoiced.
So the Jews saw the light and had happiness, joy, and honor.

And in every province, and in every city, wherever the king's orders and decree went, the Jews had a good happy day and they rejoiced and feasted. Many people of the land became Jews because they feared the Jews.

On the 13th day of the 12th month of Adar, when the date of the king Ahasuerus' decree moved closer to its time of execution, when the enemies of the Jews hoped to have power over them, it turned out that the Jews had the power and ruled over those who hated them.

The Jews assembled together in their cities throughout all of King Ahasuerus' provinces. They attacked those who wanted to hurt them, and no one could stand against them, because the fear of the Jews fell upon all the people.
All of King Ahasuerus' provincial rulers, lieutenants, deputies, and officers helped the Jews, because they feared Mordecai.
Because Mordecai had become great in the king's palace, and his fame grew greater and greater throughout all the provinces.
This was how the Jews defeated all their enemies with one stroke of the sword, and they were able to slaughter and destroy anyone who hated them.
And in the Shushan Palace the Jews killed and destroyed 500 men.
And Parshandatha, Dalphon, Aspatha,
Poratha, Adalia, Aridatha,
Parmashta, Arisai, Aridai, Vajezatha.
They killed these previously named ten sons of Haman, but they did not plunder their property or take their spoils of war. Haman was Hammedatha's son and he was the enemy of the Jews.
That day, they brought the number of people killed in the Shushan Palace to the king.

So King Ahasuerus went to Queen Esther and said, "The Jews have killed 500 men in the Shushan Palace, including Haman's ten sons. I am not sure what have they done in the rest of the provinces? So what are your further petitions or requests, ask and it will be done."
Then Esther replied and said, "If it pleases the king, let the Jews in Shushan do tomorrow what they have done by today's decree, and let them hang the bodies of Haman's ten sons on the gallows."
And the king ordered it to be done, and the decree was sent to Shushan, and they hanged Haman's ten sons.
On the fourteenth day of the month of Adar, the Jewish people in Shushan attacked and killed 300 men in Shushan. But they did not take any of their property.
But the other Jews in the king's other provinces gathered together to protect themselves from their enemies, and they killed 75,000 of their enemies, but they did not take their property.
That happened on the 13th day of Adar, and on the 14th day they rested and celebrated with a day of feasting and happiness.
But the Jews in Shushan assembled together on the 13th and 14th day of the month. Then they rested on the 15th day and celebrated with a day of feasting, joy, and happiness.
That's why, the Jews who lived in the villages and unwalled cities made the fourteenth day of Adar a good day of happiness and feasting, and they sent gifts one to another.
Mordecai wrote all these things down, and sent letters to all the Jews in all of King Ahasuerus' provinces, both near and far.
To establish a holiday among them, to celebrate annually the 14th and 15th day of Adar.

To remember the days when the Jews rested from their enemies, and the month of sorrow and mourning that was turned into good joyous days of celebration. In order to feast, rejoice, and send presents to one another, and give to the poor.
The Jews decided to do what Mordecai had written to ask them to do, and they continued this custom.
Because Hammedatha the Agagite's son Haman who was the enemy of all the Jews, had devised a plan to destroy them, by casting lots for the Pur to consume and destroy them.

But when Esther appealed to the king, he had orders written that would turn Haman's wicked scheme against the Jews, against on his own head. So that he and his sons wound up being hanged on the gallows.
That's why they named these days the Purim after the Pur, because of everything they had seen and experienced that was written in this letter.
So the Jews ordained and established this custom for themselves, their descendants, and everyone who would join them to celebrate these two days as it was written at their appointed time every year.

So that these days would be remembered and celebrated throughout every generation, every family, every province, and every city. To always remember and memorialize these days of Purim among the Jews and their descendants.
Then Queen Esther and Mordecai the Jew, wrote with full authority to confirm this second letter of Purim. And Queen Esther was Abihail's daughter.
Mordecai sent the letters to all the Jews in the 127 provinces of King Ahasuerus' kingdom, with words of peace and truth.

In order to confirm the days of Purim at their appointed times, and as Mordecai the Jew and Queen Esther wanted. Because they established and committed themselves and their descendants to the practices of fasting and lamentation during those days.
And Esther's decree confirmed the days of Purim, and it was written in the book.
And King Ahasuerus taxed the land, and the sea islands.
All the acts of Mordecai's power, might, and the declaration of his greatness to which King Ahasuerus had advanced him, are all written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Media and Persia?

Because Mordecai the Jew was King Ahasuerus' most trusted, and great among the Jews, and he was accepted by his army of brothers. He was always seeking wealth for his people and speaking peace to everyone around him.
There was a man named Job in the land of Uz, who was perfect and honest. He was someone who feared God and avoided evil.
And he fathered seven sons and three daughters.
His property included 7,000 sheep, 3,000 camels, 500 yoke of oxen, 500 female donkeys, and a very large household. He was the greatest man of all the men in the east.
Job's sons took turns feasting in their homes, and they invited their three sisters to come eat and drink with them.

After they finished their feasts, Job would send for his children to sanctify them, and he would get up early in the morning to offer burnt offerings for all of them. Job did this regularly because he thought, "Maybe my children have sinned and cursed God in their hearts."
One day when the sons of God came to present themselves before the Lord, Satan also came with them.
And the Lord said to Satan, "Where did you come from?" Then Satan answered the Lord and said, "I have been walking up and down and roaming all over the earth."
And the Lord said to Satan, "Have you seen my servant Job? There is no one else like him on all the earth, he is a perfect and honest man who fears God and avoids evil."
Then Satan answered the Lord and said, "Does Job fear God for no reason?
Have not you built a hedge around him, his house, and around everything that he owns on every side? You have blessed the work of his hands, and his possessions have increased in the land.
But if you put out your hand and touch everything that he has, he will curse you to your face."
And the Lord said to Satan, "Behold I put everything that he has is in your power, but do not physically harm him." So Satan left the Lord's presence.
Then one day Job's sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine in their oldest brother's house.
And a messenger came to Job and said, "The oxen were plowing, and the donkeys were feeding beside them.
And the Sabean people captured them and carried them away, and they killed the servants with their swords, and I am the only one that survived."
While he was speaking another messenger came to him and said, "God's fire has fallen from heaven, and it has burned up and consumed the sheep and the servants, and I am the only one that survived."

While he was speaking another messenger came to him and said, "Three bands of Chaldeans captured the camels and carried them all away. They also killed all the servants with their swords, and I am the only one that survived."
While he was speaking another messenger came to him and said, "Your sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine in their oldest brother's house.
And, behold a great wind blew in from the wilderness and destroyed the house, and it fell on the young men and killed them, and I am the only one that survived."
Then Job got up, tore his clothes and shaved his head, then he fell on the ground worshipping God.
And he said, "I came out of my mother's womb naked, and that's where I will return naked, the Lord gives and the Lord takes away, blessed be the name of the Lord."
During all this Job did not sin nor foolishly blame God.
Another day, when the sons of God once again came to present themselves before the Lord, Satan also came with them to present himself before the Lord.
And the Lord spoke to Satan and said, "Where did you come from?" And Satan answered the Lord and said, "I have been walking up and down and roaming throughout the earth."

And the Lord said to Satan, "Have you seen my servant Job? There is no one else like him on all the earth, because he is a perfect and honest man who fears God and avoids evil. But he still retains his integrity, even though you moved me to destroy him without cause."
And Satan answered the Lord and said, "Skin for skin, a man will give everything he has for his life.
But if you reach out and touch his flesh and bone, he will curse you to your face."
And the Lord said to Satan, "Behold, I place him in your hands, but do not kill him."
So Satan left the Lord's presence, and infected Job with boils and sores from the soles of his feet to the top of his head.
Job scrape himself with a piece of broken pottery as he sat among the ashes.
Then Job's wife said to him, "Do you still have your integrity? Why don't you just curse God and die!"

But he said to her, "You sound like a foolish woman speaking. What good are we if we only accept God with good things, and we do not receive him with evil?" After all this, Job still did not sin with his lips.

When three of Job's friends heard about all the evil that had come upon him, they all came from their own place to see him. So Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite made an appointment to come together to mourn with him and comfort him.
When they looked up they did not recognize Job from a distance. They began to weep loudly and tore their clothes, then they sprinkled dust on the tops of their heads toward heaven.
So they sat with him for seven days and seven nights, and no one spoke a word to him, because they saw that his grief was very great.
After this Job opened his mouth and cursed the day he was born.
Then Job spoke.
And he said, "Let the day I was born perish, and the night in which it was said, 'A boy has been conceived.'
May that day be turned to darkness. May God ignore that day from above, so that no light shines upon it.
Let the shadow and darkness of death stain it, let a cloud settle on it and let the blackness of that day terrify it.
As for that night, let the darkness seize it, do not let it become one of the days of the year, and do not let it become one of the days of the months.
Behold, let that night be solitary, and let no joyful voice be heard there.
Let those who are ready to raise up their mourning and curse the day, curse that day.
Let the stars of the twilight go dark, let that day look for light and find none, do not let it see the morning dawn of that day.
Because that day did not shut the doors of my mother's womb, nor did it hide the sorrow from my eyes.
Why did I not die in my mother's womb? Why did I not give up the ghost when I came out of her stomach?
Why did her knees not prevent my birth, and why did her breasts feed me?
I should have been quiet and still born, then I would have slept and been at rest.
Then I would be at rest with the kings and counselors of the earth, who built the now deserted palaces for themselves.
Or I would be at rest with the princes who filled their houses with gold and silver.
Or why was my untimely birth not hidden so that I was not born, like an infant who never saw light.
Where the troubles of the wicked cease, and the weary are at rest.
Where the prisoners rest together, and they do not hear their oppressor's voice.
Where the great and small stay, and servants are set free from their masters.
Why is light given to those in misery, and life is given to the bitter soul.
And to those who long for death that never comes, and to those who search for death more than hidden treasures.
And to those who rejoice and are happy when they can find the grave?
Why is light given to a man whose way is hidden, and who God has surrounded?
Because I sigh before I eat, and my groans pour out like water.
Because everything I have greatly feared has come upon me, and what I am afraid of has come to me.
I was not safe and I have had no quiet rest, because trouble has come."
Then Eliphaz the Temanite replied to Job.
And he said, "If we try to speak to you, will you be grieved? But who can not speak out?
Behold, you have instructed many and you have given strength to the weak.
Your words have upheld the fallen, and you have strengthened feeble knees.
But now trouble has come upon you and you faint, it touches you and you are troubled.
Is this not your own confident honest ways, and your fears and hopes?
I pray that you will remember that no one innocent ever perished. And do you remember anyone righteous who has been destroyed?
Because I have seen, that those who plow and sow immorality and wickedness, reap the same.
By the blast of God's breath they perish, and by the wind from his nostrils they are consumed.
The voice of the fierce roaring lion and the teeth of the young lions, are broken.
The old lion perishes for lack of prey, and the stout lion's cubs are scattered abroad.
A secret was brought to me, and my ear heard part of it.
From the thoughts, dreams, and visions of the night when men sleep deeply.
Fear and trembling came upon me, which made all my bones shake.
Then a spirit passed before my face, and the hair of my flesh stood on edge.
It stood still, but I could not recognize the form of it, an image was before my eyes, there was silence, and I heard a voice and said.
And the voice said, 'Can mortal man be more just than God, can a man be more pure than his maker?
Behold, God puts no trust in his servants, and he filled his angels with foolishness.
How much less will God trust in those who live in clay houses with dust foundations, which is crushed like a moth?
They are destroyed from morning to evening, and when they perish forever nobody notices.
Does not their excellency go away when they die without wisdom?'"
And Eliphaz the Temanite further stated, "So call out now and who will answer, and to which of the saints will you turn?
