Because anger kills the foolish man, and envy kills the silly one.
I have seen the foolish take root, but suddenly his home was cursed.
His children are far from safety, they are crushed in the gate and they have no savior to deliver them.
The hungry eat his harvests and even takes from the thorns, and the robber swallows his wealth.
Although affliction does not come from the dust, and trouble does not spring from the ground.
But man is born into trouble as surely as sparks fly upward.
I would look to God, and I would commit my cause to God.
Who does great, marvelous, and unsearchable things too numerous to count.
Who gives rain on the earth, and pours water on the fields.
He sets those who are low on up high, so that those who mourn may be glorified in safety.
He disappoints the devices of the crafty, so that their hands find no successful enterprise.
He captures the wise in their own craftiness, and the counsel of the stubborn is carried away head first.
They meet in darkness during the day, and they grope at noon during the day as if it were night.
But he saves the poor from the sword of their own mouth, and from the traps of the powerful.
So the poor have hope, and immorality stops her mouth.
Behold, happy is the man who God corrects, so that his reasoning does not despise the Almighty's discipline.
Because he wounds, makes sore, and binds up, but his hands also heal and make whole.
He will deliver you from six troubles, and no seventh evil will touch you.
He will rescue you from the death of famine, and in war he will save you from powerful weapons.
You will be hidden from the scourge of the tongue, nor will you fear destruction when chaos comes.
You will laugh at destruction and famine, and you will not be afraid of the beasts of the earth.
Because you will be allied with the field stones, and the field beasts will be at peace with you.
You will know that your home is at peace, and when you visit your home you will not sin.
You will know also that your descendants will be many, and your offspring as numerous as the grass of the earth.
You will come to your grave in old age, like the shock to the wheat when harvest season comes.
And behold, we have searched this out and it is true! So hear it, and know it is for your own good."
But Job answered Eliphaz the Temanite.
And he said, "Oh if only my grief and disasters could be thoroughly weighed on the scales of justice!
Because they would be heavier than the ocean sands, and that's why my words have been so harsh.
The Almighty's poisoned arrows are inside of me and they drink my spirit, and the terrors of God have arrayed themselves against me.
Does the wild donkey bray when it has grass, and do the oxen moo over their fodder?
Can unsavory food be eaten without salt, or does an egg white have any taste?
The things that my soul refused to touch are as loathsome as rotten meat.
Oh, if only God would grant my request and give me what I long for the most!
If only God would just be willing to destroy me, and unleash his hand to cut me off!
Then I would be comforted, and I would harden myself in sorrow even though he has not spared me, because I have not denied the words of the Holy One.
What strength gives me hope, and what will cause my end, and why should I prolong my life?
Does my strength come from stones, or is my flesh made of brass?
Is my help not within me and has wisdom been driven away from me?
Anyone afflicted should be shown pity from his friend, unless he forsakes the fear of the Almighty.
My brothers have dealt as deceitfully as a brook, and like a brooks stream they pass away.
Which are blackened because of the ice which the snow has hidden.
But when it is hot and they grow warm, they vanish as they melt away.
Their paths are turned away, so they perish and turn to nothing.
Tema's troops looked for water, and Sheba's companies waited for them.
They had hope, but they were confused and ashamed because they found nothing.
But now you are nothing, you see my problems and you are afraid.
Did I say, 'Bring me something or reward me from your wealth?'
Or did I say, 'Deliver me and rescue me from the hands of my powerful enemies?'
Teach me, and I will hold my tongue if you help me understand where I have erred.
Your righteous words are forceful, but who do your arguments blame?
Do you imagine to blame my words and speech, and treat my cries as wind?
You overwhelm the fatherless, and dig a pit for your friend.
So be content when you look at me, because if I lie to you it will be evident.
I pray you will return and not blame the immorality on me, because my righteousness is at stake.
Is there any immorality in my tongue? Can I not taste and recognize perverse things in my mouth?"
Then Job spoke further and said, "Has not man's time on earth been appointed to labor? Are not his days like the days of a hired hand?
He labors like a slave who desires the shade of the day, or a hired hand who works for the rewards of his labor.
So I have been forced to endure months of vanity, and exhausting nights make me weary.
When I lie down I ask myself, 'When will I get up?' And the night goes on and on, and I toss and turn back and forth until the day dawns.
My flesh is infested with worms and covered with dust, my skin is broken with festering sores.
My days pass swifter than a weaver's shuttle, and end hopelessly.
Remember that my life is simply wind, and my eye will see no more good.
Anyone looking for me will see no longer see me, you will look for me but I will be gone.
As the morning cloud is burned away and vanishes, so will the one who goes down to the grave and no longer returns.
He will no longer return to his house, and anyone in his home will no longer know him.
So I will not restrain my mouth, I will speak of the anguish of my spirit, and I will complain of the bitterness in my soul.
Am I the ocean or a whale that you have to keep watch over?
When I say, 'My bed will comfort me, and my couch will ease my complaints.'
Then you scare me with dreams, and terrify me through visions.
That causes my soul to choose strangling and death, rather than life.
I loathe my life, and I know that I will not always be alive. So leave me alone, because my days are just vanity.
What is a man, that you should magnify him and set your heart on him?
Why should you visit him every morning, and test him every moment?
How long will it be before you leave me alone long enough to swallow my own spit?
How have I sinned, and what have I done to you, O protector of men? Why have you made me a target against you, and made me a burden to myself?
Why do you not pardon my transgression and remove my immorality? Because soon I will sleep in the dust, and you will look for me in the morning, but I will not be there."
Then Bildad the Shuhite answered Job.
And he said, "How long will you say these things, and how long will your words be like a strong wind?
Does God pervert judgment, or does the Almighty pervert justice?
If your children have sinned against him, and he has thrown them away for their transgression.
If you had looked to God ahead of time, and made your plea to the Almighty.
If you were pure and honest, he would surely awaken now and restore your righteousness home to prosperity.
Even though you're beginning with nothing, your latter days will increase with prosperity.
Because I pray that you ask about former generations, and prepare yourself to search for their fathers.
Because were just born yesterday and we know nothing, and our days on earth are just a shadow.
Will they not teach you, tell you, and utter the words from their heart?
Can a rush grow without the marsh, or can reeds grow without water?
Even though it is still green and it has not been cut, it withers before any other herb.
So are the paths of anyone who forgets God, and the hypocrite's hope will perish.
His hope will be destroyed, and his trust will become a spider's web.
He leans on his house, but it will not stand, he holds fast to it, but it does not endure.
He is green before the sun, and his branch shoots out in his garden.
His roots are wrapped around the pile, and looks for a place among the stones.
If he is removed from his place it will deny him and say, 'I have not seen you!'
Behold, this is the joy of his way, and from the earth will others grow.
Behold, God will not throw away a perfect man and he will not help the evildoers.
He will fill your mouth with laughter and your lips with rejoicing.
And anyone who hates you will be clothed in shame, and the wicked's home place will come to nothing."
Then Job answered and said.
And he said, "I know the truth, but how can a man be righteous with God?
If God deals with man, he cannot answer God once out of a thousand times.
God is wise in heart and mighty in strength. Has anyone hardened his heart against God and prospered?
He removes the mountains without their knowledge, and overturns them in his anger.
He shakes the earth from her place, and its foundations tremble.
He commands the sun and it does not rise, and he seals off the stars.
He alone can expand the heavens and walk on the ocean waves.
He created Arcturus, Orion, Pleiades, and all the southern constellations.
He does great things beyond finding the uncountable wonders of the universe.
He passes by me and I do not see him. He passes on but I do not comprehend his presence.
Behold, when he takes something away, who can hinder him? Who can say to him, 'What are you doing?'
If God does not restrain his anger, the proud helpers of chaos cower beneath him.
How can I answer him or choose my words to reason with his word?
Even though I was righteous, I could not answer, but I would plea to my judge for mercy.
If I had called to him and he had answered, I still would not believe he had heard my voice.
Because he breaks my soul with a violent storm, and multiplies my wounds without cause.
He does not let me catch my breath, but he fills me with bitterness.
If I speak from strength he is stronger, and if I ask for judgment, who can make him give me a time to plead?
If I justify myself, my own mouth will condemn me. And if I say, 'I am perfect,' my own mouth will also prove me to be perverse.
Even if I were perfect, I would still not know my own soul and I would despise my life.
That's why I said of this one thing that he destroys both the perfect and the wicked.
If the plague kills suddenly, he will laugh at the trial of the innocent.
The earth was placed into the hands of the wicked, he covers the faces of its judges. If not him, then where and who is it?
Now my days move faster than a postal rider, they flee and they see no good.
They pass away like a swift ship, or an eagle that pounces quickly on its prey.
If I say, 'I will forget my complaint, so I can ignore my sadness and comfort myself.'
Then I am still afraid of all my sorrows, because I know that you will not declare me innocent.
So if I am wicked, then why should I labor in vain?
If I wash myself with water from melted snow, and thoroughly cleanse my hands.
You would still push me into a ditch, and my own clothes will despise me.
Because he is not a man like me, that I can answer and we could judge each other.
Nor are there any mediators between us, that could punish both of us.
Let him take his staff away from me, and do not let his fear terrify me.
Then would I speak without fear, but that is not the way it is for me."
Then Job further stated, "My soul is weary of my life, I will complain about myself and speak of the bitterness in my soul.
I will say to God, do not condemn me, show me for that reason you deal with me.
Does it make you feel good to oppress me, and despise the work of your hands, and shine a light on the counsel of the wicked?
Do you have eyes of flesh, and do you see the same way a man sees?
Are your days the same as the days of man? Or are your years the same as the days of man.
So that you enquire of my immorality and search for my sin?
You know that I am not wicked, but there is no deliverance from your hand.
Your hands made me and fashioned me all together, but now you destroy me.
I beg you remember that you made me like the clay, so will you turn me into dust again?
Have you not poured me out like milk, and curdled me like cheese?
You have clothed me with skin and flesh, and braced me with bones and sinews.
You have granted me life and favor, and your visitation has protected my spirit.
You have hidden these things in your heart, so that I know this is with you.
If I sin you mark me, and you do not acquit my immorality.
If I am wicked then I am filled with sorrow. If I am righteous I can not lift my head, and I am full of confusion, and that's why see you my affliction.
You hunt me like a fierce lion because my pride increases, and once again you show your marvelous self to me.
You renew your witnesses against me, and increase your indignation with me, changes and war attack me.
Why have you brought me out of the womb? If only I had given up the ghost, and no one had ever seen me!
It should have been as if I had never existed, and I should have been carried from the womb to the grave.
Are not my days numbered? So stop and leave me alone, so that I may have a little comfort.
Before I leave and never return, and I go to the land of the shadow of death and darkness.
To a land of darkness as dark as darkness itself and the confusion of the shadow of death, and where light is like the darkness."
Then Zophar the Naamathite answered Job.
And he said, "Should not all of these words be answered, and should the speaker be justified?
Should your lies silence others, and should you not be made to feel ashamed for your mockery?
Because you have said, 'My doctrine is pure, and I am clean in your eyes.'
If only God would speak out against you.
So that you could see the secrets to both sides of what wisdom truly is! In order for you to know that God takes less from you than your immorality deserves.
Can you find God's secrets by searching for them? Can you limit the perfection of the Almighty?
It is as high as heaven and deeper than hell, so what can you do and what can you know?
God's wisdom is longer than the earth, and broader than the sea.
If he cuts you off and imprisons you or convenes a court against you, then who can stop him?
Because he knows vain men and he also sees wickedness, so do you not think he will consider it?
Because vain men will become wise, when a wild donkey's colt is born as wise as a man.
If you prepare your heart, and stretch out your hands toward him.
If there is immorality in your hand, put it away and do not let it live in your tabernacles.
Then you will steadfastly look up without shame, and you will be fearless.
Because you will forget your misery and remember that time passes away like flowing water.
Your age will shine like the noon day, and you will be as bright as the morning.
You will be secure because there is hope, you will dig and rest in safety.
You will also lie down because you will not be afraid of anyone, and many will request your help.
But the eyes of the wicked will fail and they will not escape, and they will hopelessly want to give up the ghost."
And Job answered and said.
And he said, "No doubt, you are one of the people with whom wisdom will die.
But I understand as well as you that I am not your inferior, nor am I one who does not know these things?
I am like someone mocked by their neighbor who calls on God. When God answers him, the honest righteous man is laughed at and ridiculed.
His feet are ready to slip, and he is like a lamp despised by anyone whose thoughts are at ease.
The thieves tabernacles prosper, and those who provoke God are secure and God brings them great abundance.
But ask the animals and they will teach you, and ask the birds of the air and they will tell you.
Or speak to the earth and it will teach you, and the fish of the sea will inform you.
Who does not know that the Lord's hand of has done all of this work?
The soul of every living thing is in his hand, and so is the breath of all mankind.
Does not the ear test words, as the mouth tastes its meat?
Wisdom is found in the ancient, and understanding comes with old age.
Wisdom and strength are with God, counsel and understanding belong to him.
Behold, what he tears down cannot be rebuilt again, and any man he shuts in cannot be reopened.
He withholds the waters and the rivers dry up, he sends the rain and it overwhelms the earth.
He has strength and wisdom with him, the deceived and the deceiver belong to him.
He leads lawyers away spoiled and makes fools out of the judges.
He loosens the shackles of kings, and wraps a belt around their waists.
He leads princes away spoiled, and overthrows the mighty.
He removes the speech of the trusted, and takes away the understanding of the aged.
He pours contempt on princes, and weakens the strength of the powerful.
He discovers deep things from the darkness and brings light to the shadow of death.
He creates and destroys great nations. He enlarges nations and straitens them out.
He removes the heart of the earth's great leaders, and makes them wander around in a wilderness where there is no way out.
They grope around in the dark without light, and he makes them to stagger like a drunk man."
And Job said, "My eyes have seen all of this, and my ears have heard and understood.
I know what you know and I am not inferior to you.
Surely I would speak to the Almighty, and it is my desire to reason with God.
But you forge lies, and you are all worthless physicians.
If you would only hold your peace! It would benefit your wisdom.
Listen to the pleas and reasoning coming from my lips.
Will you speak wickedly and talk deceitfully for God?
Will you accept God's people and deal honestly in his behalf?
Is it good that God had to search you out, or do you mock him like one man mocks another?
He will surely blame you if you secretly accept such people.
Do you not fear his excellency when his dread falls on you?
Your memories are like ashes, and your bodies are like clay statues.
Hold your peace and leave me alone, so that when I speak whatever comes on me comes on me.
That's why I chew my flesh in my teeth, and put my life in my hand?
Even if he kills me I will still trust in him, but I will maintain my own ways before him.
He is also my salvation, because a hypocrite will not come before him.
Listen diligently to my speech and declarations with your ears.
Behold, I have prepared my cause and I know that I will be justified.
Who will plead with me? Because, if I hold my tongue I will give up the ghost.
If you only grant me two things, I will not hide from you.
Withdraw your hand from me, and do not let your dread make me afraid.
When you call I will answer, or let me speak and you can answer me.
How much wickedness and sin am I responsible for? Make me understand my transgression and sins.
Why do you hide your face and make me your enemy?
Will you break a wind driven leaf, and will you pursue dry straw?
Because you write bitter things against me, and make me possess the wickedness of my youth.
You also put my feet in stocks and watch over all my paths, and you set footprints on the ground from the heels of my feet.
And a man is consumed like something rotten, or like a moth eaten garment."
And Job said, "The days are few and full of trouble for a man born from a woman.
He blooms like a flower then he's cut down, he also flees like a shadow and does not endure.
Do you open your eyes to one such as this, and bring me into judgment before you?
Can anyone bring something clean from the unclean? No not one!
Since his days are finite and his months are numbered with you, you have established his boundaries which he cannot pass.
Turn away from him and let him rest, until he finishes all the duties of his days as a hired hand.
There is hope for a tree, because if it is cut down, it will sprout again and its tender branches will not stop growing.
Even though its root grows old in the earth, and its fallen branches die on the ground.
At the scent of water it will bud and sprout twigs like a sapling.
But man dies, gives up the ghost and wastes away, so where is he now?
Like water that evaporates from the oceans, and floods that decay and dry up.
So men lay down and they do not get up. And until the heavens no longer exist, they will not be awakened from their sleep.
If only you would hide me in the grave or keep me secret until your anger has passed, so that you can appoint a special time to remember me!
If a man dies, will he live again? I will wait until things change for all the days of my appointed time here on earth.
You call and I will answer, and you will desire the works of your hands.
Because you number my steps, do you not now watch over my sin?
My transgressions are sealed in a bag, and you sew up my immorality.
But truly, falling mountains come to nothing and the rocks are removed from their place.
Rushing water wears the stones away, you wash away the things which grow from the earth's dust, and you destroy the hopes of man.
You prevail forever against man and he passes away, so you change his appearance and send him away.
If his sons are honored, he does not know it and if they are brought low, but he is not aware of them.
But his flesh will give him pain, and his inner soul will mourn him.
And he said, "Should a wise man utter vain knowledge, and fill his stomach with the east wind?
Should a wise man utter vain knowledge, and fill his stomach with the east wind?
Should he reason with unprofitable talk or speeches that serve no good purpose?
You throw off fear and restrain your prayers to God.
Because your mouth utters your immorality, and you choose to speak like the wicked and crafty.
I do not condemn you, but your own lips and mouth condemns and testifies against you.
Were you the first man born, or were you created before the hills?
Have you heard God's secrets and do you limit wisdom to yourself?
What do you know that we do not know? What do you understand that we do not understand?
We have the gray headed and very ancient men with us, who are much older than your father.
Are God's comforts not enough for you, has he kept anything secret from you?
Why does your heart carry you away, and what are your eyes winking at.
What makes you turn your spirit against God, and why do such words leave your mouth?
What is man that should make him clean, and should a man born of a woman be made righteous?
Behold, he puts no trust in his saints, and even the heavens are not clean in his sight.
How much more abominable and filthy is a man who drinks immorality like water?
Listen to me and I will declare it and tell you what I have seen.
I will tell you what the wise men have said and not concealed from their fathers.
To whom alone the earth was given and no foreigner passed among them.
The wicked man labors with his whole life, and his numbered years are hidden from the oppressor.
A sound of terror is in his ears, when he is prosperous the destroyer comes to attack him.
He does not believe that he will return from darkness, and he is waiting for the sword.
He wanders abroad looking for bread and says, 'Where is the bread?' He knows that the day of darkness is at hand, and it is ready for him.
Trouble and anguish fill a man with fear, and they will prevail against him like a king ready to do battle.
Because he stretched out his hand against God, and he tries to stand against the Almighty.
He runs at him headfirst with his thick studded shields.
Because his face is covered with fat, and his thighs bulge with fat.
He lives in desolate cities, and he inhabits abandoned houses which are piles of rubble that no one wants.
He will not be rich nor will his wealth continue, and he will not prolong its perfection on the earth.
He will not leave the darkness, the flames will dry his branches, and the breath of life will disappear from his mouth.
Do not let the deceived one trust in vanity, because vanity will be his reward.
His reward will be accomplished before its time, and his branch will not flourish.
He will be like an unripe grape shaken from the vine, and he will shed his flowers like the olive tree.
Because the congregation of hypocrites will be desolate, and fire will consume the tabernacles of bribery.
They conceive mischief and produce vanity, and their stomach prepares deceit.
Then Job answered Eliphaz the Temanite.
And he said, "I have heard many things from you, and all I can say is that you are all miserable comforters.
Will your vain words never end, and what emboldens you to answer that way?
I could also speak the same way as you. If your soul were in my soul's place, I could pile up words against you and shake my head at you.
But I would strengthen you with my mouth, and the words from my lips would console your grief.
Even though I speak, my grief is not consoled, and I am restrained but where is my comfort?
But now he has made me weary, and you have desolated my all family and company.
You have filled me with wrinkled faces which witnesses against me, and my lean and frail body bears witness to my face.
He tears me and hates me with his anger, he grinds his teeth on me and my enemies glare at me.
Their mouths gape wide open at me, they have slapped me contemptuously on the cheek and they unite together against me.
God has delivered me to the ungodly and turned me over to the wicked.
I was at ease, but he has torn me apart. He grabbed me by the neck and shook me into pieces, and he set me up as his target.
His archers surround me, he holds me, restrains me, and he does not spare me, then he pours my gall out on the ground.
He destroys me with broken defense after broken defense, and he runs at me like a giant.
I have sewn sackcloth over my skin and buried my horn in the dust.
My face is red from weeping, and the shadow of death is upon my eyelids.
None of this is because of any injustice from my hands, and my prayers are also pure.
O earth, do not cover yourself with my blood, and may my cries for help have no place to rest.
Even now my witness and my record are high in heaven.
My friends scorn me, but my eyes pour out tears to God.
If only someone would plead to God the way a man pleads with his neighbor!
After a few years have passed, I will go away and not return.
Then Job said, "My breath is corrupt and my days are extinct, and the grave is ready for me.
Are there no mockers around me, and must my eyes continue to see their provocation?
Now lay me down and take responsibility for me, who else will shake hands with me?
Because you have hidden understanding from their hearts, and you will not glorify them.
Whoever flatters his friends, will cause the eyes of his children to fail.
He has also made me a perfect example for the people, and I was beaten like a drum.
My eyes have grown dim with sorrow, and all parts of my body are just shadows.
Honest men will be astonished by this, and the innocent will be stirred up against the hypocrites.
The righteous will also hold on his way, and whoever has clean hands will grow stronger and stronger.
But all of you can return now, because I cannot find one wise man among you.
My days have passed, and even my purposes and the thoughts of my heart are broken.
My thoughts change the night into day, the light is short because of the darkness.
If I wait the grave is my house, and I have made my bed in the darkness.
I have called my father corruption, and my mother and sister are the worm.
And now where is my hope and who will see it?
It will go down to the bars of the pit, when we rest together in the dust.
Then Bildad the Shuhite answered Job.
And he said, "How long will it be before you stop talking? Mark my words, and then we can speak.
So why are we treated like animals and called vile in your sight?
You who tear yourself in his anger, will the earth be forsaken because of you and will the rock be removed from its place?
Yes, the light of the wicked will be extinguished, and the spark of his fire will not shine.
The light will be dark in his tabernacle, and his candle will be extinguished with him.
The steps of his strength will be straightened, and his own counsel will throw him down.
Because his own feet have thrown him into a net, and he wanders into a trap.
The trap grabs his heel, and the robber will take everything he has.
The snare is laid on the ground for him, and a trap waits him along the road.
Terrors frighten him in every direction and hinder his every step.
His strength will be starved, and destruction will be ready at his side.
It will devour his skin's strength, and the firstborn of death devours his strength.
His confidence will be removed from his tabernacle and bring him to the king of terrors.
Terror will live in his tabernacle, because fire and brimstone will be scattered over his home.
His roots will dry up beneath him, and his branches will be cut off above him.
His memory will perish from the earth, and he will have no name on the street.
He will be driven out of the light into darkness, and chased out of the world.
He will never have a son or nephew among his people, and no one will remain in his home.
Those that come after him will be astonished by his fate, just as those before him were frightened.
This is surely like the homes of the wicked, and this place is the place of someone who does not know God."
Then Job answered Bildad the Shuhite.
And he said, "How long will you frustrate and break my soul into pieces with words?
You have disapproved of me ten times, are you not ashamed of the way that you have treated me.
And if I have indeed erred, then my error remains with me.
If you magnify yourselves against me, and plead my disgrace against me.
Know now that God has overthrown me, and he has surrounded me with his net.
Behold, even though I cry out of wrongful accusations, I am not heard. When I cry out loud there is no justice.
He has blocked my way and I cannot pass, he has set darkness along my paths.
He has stripped me of my glory, and taken the crown from my head.
I am gone and he has destroyed me on every side, then he removed my hope like a tree.
He also kindled his anger against me, and he counts me as one of his enemies.
His troops unite together, they construct their ramparts against me and bivouac all around my tabernacle.
He carried my brothers far away from me and to be honest, my acquaintances are strangers to me.
My family has failed, and my closest friends have forgotten me.
Those living in my house including my maids, count me as a stranger, I am an illegal alien in their sight.
I called and pleaded with my servant, but he would not answer me.
My breath smells strange to my wife, and even though I pleaded with her for the children's sake, my own body is repulsive to them.
Yes, young children despised me and when I got up they spoke against me.
All my best friends abhor me, and the ones I loved turned against me.
My bones cling to my skin and flesh, and I have escaped by the skin of my teeth.
Oh have pity on me my friends, because the hand of God has touched me.
Why do you persecute me as God does, and will you never be satisfied by my pound of flesh?
Oh how I wish my words were written and printed in a book!
Oh if only my words were carved with an iron pen and chiseled into the rock forever!
Because I know that my savior lives, and that he will stand up for me in the latter days on the earth.
Even after the worms have destroyed my skin and this body, yet I will see God in my flesh.
I will see him for myself and my eyes will behold him, and not as a stranger, even though my heart is consumed within me.
But you should say, 'Why do we not persecute him?' Since the root of the matter is found in me?
Be afraid of the sword, because anger brings the punishments of the sword, so that you will know there is justice."
Then Zophar the Naamathite answered Job.
And he said, "That's why my thoughts cause me to answer, and that's why I hurry.
I have heard your disrespect against me, and the spirit of my understanding makes me answer.
Do you not know that since the ancient times when man was placed on earth.
That the triumph of the wicked is short lived, and the joy of the hypocrite lasts but a moment?
Though his excellency reaches up to the heavens and his head reaches into the clouds.
But he will forever perish like his own dung rots, and anyone who has seen him will say, 'Where is he?'
He flies away like a dream that can not be found, and he will be chased away like a vision of the night.
The one who saw him will no longer see him, nor will the people in his own home.
His children will seek to please the poor, and his hands will restore their goods.
His bones are full of the sin of his youth, which will be buried with him in the dust.
Though wickedness tastes sweet in his mouth, and even though he hides it under his tongue.
Even though he spares it and does not forsake it, but he still keeps it in his mouth.
The meat in his bowels will turn bitter, and it will become the venom of asps inside of him.
He has swallowed riches and he will vomit them back up again, and God will force it out of his system.
He will suck the poison of asps, and the viper's tongue will kill him.
He will not see the rivers, the floods, or the brooks of honey and butter.
He must return the fruits of his labor along with his wealth, and he will not be able to swallow it, nor will he be able to rejoice in it.
Because he has oppressed and forsaken the poor, because he has violently taken away a house which he did not build.
Surely his stomach will not feel quietness and nothing he desired will be saved.
He will have nothing left, so no one will look for his prosperity.
In the fullness of his serenity he will be in dire straits, and the hand of the wicked will come upon him.
When he is about to fill his stomach, God will throw the fury of his anger upon him, and will rain it down on him while he is eating.
He will flee from iron weapons and the steel arrow will pierce him.
The arrow is drawn from his body, the glittering sword is pulled from his liver and he is overcome by terrors.
His hidden secret place will be filled with darkness, an unfanned flame will consume him and anyone or anything left in his tabernacle.
Heaven will reveal his immorality, and the earth will rise up against him.
The increase of his prosperity will leave him, and his property will fly away on the day of his anger.
This is what a wicked man receives from God, and his heritage is appointed to him by God."
But Job answered Zophar the Naamathite.
And he said, "Listen diligently to what I say, and let this be your consolations to me.
Bear with me while I speak, and after I have spoken you can continue to mock me.
As for me, is my complaint against someone else, and even if it were, why should my spirit not be troubled?
Mark my words, and cover your astonished mouth with your hand.
Because whenever I remember what has happened to me, I am afraid and begin to tremble with fear.
So why do the wicked live to an old age, and even become mighty and powerful?
They watch their children and grandchildren grow up before their own eyes.
Their houses are safe from fear, and the staff of God does not touch them.
Their bulls mate successfully, and their cows conceive and never give birth to stillborn calves.
They send their children out like lambs, and they dance and play.
They play the tambourine and harp, and rejoice at the sound of the organ.
They spend their days in wealth, and they die quickly and go down to the grave.
And that's why they say to God, 'Leave us alone because we do not want to know your ways.
Who is the Almighty, that we should have to serve him, and what would it profit us to pray to him?'
Unfortunately, they think they have earned everything they have with their own hands, but I do not accept the counsel of the wicked.
How often God puts wicked candle out, and their destruction comes on them unexpectedly! God distributes sorrows in his anger.
They are like stalks blowing in the wind, and chaff that storms carry away.
God lays up his immorality for the children of the wicked, he rewards their immorality and they will know it.
His own eyes will see his destruction, and he will drink from the anger of the Almighty.
Because he does not care what happens in his house after his time is cut short, and he is dead?
Can anyone teach God anything he does not already know? Since he even judges those who are in heaven.
One man dies in perfect health, while he is completely at ease and quiet.
He is fat and full of milk, his bones and marrow are still moist and strong.
Another dies in the bitterness of his soul, and never eats with pleasure.
They will lay down in the dust the same way, and the worms will cover them.
Behold, I know your thoughts, and the devices which you wrongfully imagine against me.
Because you ask, 'Where is the prince's house, and where are the homes of the wicked?'
Have you not asked travelers about their princes, and have you not accepted their coins?
Are the wicked not reserved for the day of destruction? And they will be brought forth on the day of wrath.
Who will declare the wicked man's ways to his face, and who will repay him for what he has done?
But he will be brought to the grave, where he will remain in the tomb.
The valley clods are sweet to him, and there will be an endless horde of people following him.
So why do you comfort you me in vain, since your answers remain a lie?"
Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered Job.
And he said, "Can any man be profitable to God, can even a wise man be profitable to him?
Does it please the Almighty if you are righteous, or does he gain anything if you make your ways perfect?
Will he blame you because he fears you? Or will he enter into judgment against you?
Is not your wickedness great and infinite?
Because you have taken pledges from your brother for nothing, and left him stripped naked.
You have not given water to the weary, and you have withheld bread from the hungry.
But while the mighty man had the earth, an honorable man lived on it.
You have sent widows away empty handed, and the arms of the fatherless have been broken.
So there are snares all around you, and suddenly fear troubles you.
Or it is so dark that you can not see, and the flood waters cover you.
Is not God in the heights of heaven, and behold see how high the stars are!
And you say, 'How does God know? Does he judge through the dark cloud?
Thick clouds cover him, so that he does not see us, and he walks in the circuit of heaven.'
Will you walk in the old ways which the wicked men have walked?
Who were cut down before their time, and whose foundations were swept away by a flood.
Who said to God, "Leave us alone, what can the Almighty do to us?'
Still he filled their houses with good things, but I keep the counsel of the wicked far away from me.
The righteous see it and they are glad, and the innocent hysterically laugh at them.
In fact our property is not destroyed, but their remains are consumed by fire.
Now you should acquaint yourself with him and be at peace, that way good will come to you.
I pray you will receive the law from his mouth, and store his words in your heart.
If you return to the Almighty he will build you back up, if you remove any immorality far from your tabernacles.
Then you will store gold like dust, and the gold of Ophir will be as abundant as the stones in the streams.
The Almighty will be your defender and you will have plenty of silver.
Because then you will delight in the Almighty, and lift up your face to God.
You must pray to him, and when he hears you, you must pay what you promised.
When you decide something, it will be established for you, and light will shine on all your ways.
When men are downtrodden you will say, 'Lift them up Lord,' and he will save the humble people.
He will deliver the innocent's island to them through your clean hands.
Then Job answered Eliphaz the Temanite.
And he said, "Even today my complaint is bitter, my suffering is heavier than my groaning.
Oh if I only knew where to find him, so that I could even go to where he sits!
I would plead my cause before him, and fill my mouth with arguments.
I would listen to the words he used to answer me, and I would understand what he said to me.
Will he plead against me with his great power? No, but he would listen to me.
The righteous could reason with him there, and I would forever be delivered from my judge.
But wherever I go he is not there, no matter whether I go forward or backward, I do not feel his presence.
When he works at my left hand I do not feel his presence, and when he hides at my right hand I cannot see him.
But he knows the road I take, and after he tests me I will come forth like gold.
My feet have followed in his footsteps, I have kept his ways, and I have not declined to acknowledge him.
Nor have I departed from the commandments from his lips, I have treasured his words more than my daily bread.
But he is of one mind and no one can oppose him, and he does whatever his soul desires.
Because he performs the judgement that has been assigned to me, and he has many such plans.
So I am troubled by his presence, and when I think about it I am afraid of him.
Because God makes my heart soft and the Almighty troubles me.
Because I was not silenced by the darkness, nor by the darkness that covers my face.
Then Eliphaz the Temanite said, "Since judgement time is not hidden from the Almighty, why is it that those who know him do not see his days?
Some remove boundary landmarks and violently steal flocks, that they feed off of.
They drive away the donkeys of the fatherless, and they take the widow's oxen as a security.
They turn the needy away, the earth's poor hide together from them.
And like the wild donkeys in the desert, the poor go to work early searching for food and the wilderness provides food for them and their children.
Everyone reaps their wheat in the field, and the poor glean the vineyards of the wicked.
They cause the naked to live without clothing, and they have no warm clothing in the cold weather.
They are wet from the mountain showers, and embrace the rocks for lack of a shelter.
They snatch the fatherless from their mother's breast, and take the poor as collateral.
They make him go naked without clothing, and they take sheaves of wheat from the hungry.
They make oil in their homes, tread in their winepresses, and suffer from thirst.
Men groan from the city, and the wounded soul cries out, but God does not charge them with foolishness.
They are the ones who rebel against the light, they do not know the ways of the light, nor do they endure in the paths of light.
The murderer who rises with the light kills the poor and needy, and he is like a thief in the night.
The eye of the adulterer also waits for the twilight and says, 'No one will see me,' and they disguise their face.
In the dark they dig through houses, which they marked for themselves in the daytime, they do not know the light.
Because the morning to them is like the shadow of death, and if someone knows them they are friends with the terrors of the shadow of death.
He is swift as flowing water, his portion on the earth is cursed, and he does not see his way through the vineyards.
Drought and heat consume the snow's melting waters, so does the graves of those who have sinned.
The womb will forget him, the worm will feed sweetly on him, he will no longer be remembered, and wickedness will be as broken as a fallen tree.
He treats the childless barren woman with evil, and does nothing good for the widow.
God attracts the mighty with his power, but when the mighty rise they have no guarantee of life.
Even though God gives them life in safety, he always keeps an eye on their ways.
They are glorified for a little while, but soon they are gone and brought low. They are taken from the road and just like everyone else, they are cut off like the tops of the ripe wheat heads.
And if it is not so, who can prove I am a liar and make what I say worthless?"
Then Bildad the Shuhite answered Job.
And he said, "Authority and fear are with him, he makes peace in his high places.
His armies are too numerous to count, and is there anyone on whom his sunlight does not rise?
How can man be justified with God, or how can anyone born of a woman ever be clean?
Behold even the moon and the stars are not pure in his sight, and their light does not shine to him.
How much less is a worm than a man, and is not a son of man more important than a worm?"
But Job answered Bildad the Shuhite.
And he said, "How have you helped the powerless, and how have you saved the feeble arm?
How have you counseled the unwise, and how have you completely declared the insightful truth?
To whom have you uttered these words, and whose spirit spoke through you?
Dead things and its inhabitants are formed under the waters.
Hell is naked before him, and its destruction is not covered.
He stretches out the north star over the empty place, and he hangs the earth on nothing.
He draws the waters up into his thick clouds, and the waters do not burst the cloud under them.
He withholds the face of his throne, and spreads his cloud over it.
He surrounds the waters with shores as boundaries until the days and nights come to an end.
Heaven's columns tremble and are astonished by his blame.
He divided the sea with his power, and by his understanding he defeats through the proud.
By his spirit he has decorated the heavens, his hands have formed the crooked serpent.
Lo, these are just a few of his ways, but how little of a portion is heard from him? But who can understand the thunder of his power?"
Then Job continued his parable to Bildad the Shuhite.
And he said, "As surely as God lives, who has taken away my judgment and frustrated my soul, the Almighty.
For the entire time my breath is in me and God's spirit is in my nostrils.
My lips will not speak wickedness, nor will my tongue utter deceit.
God forbid that I should justify you, and until I die my integrity will not be removed from me.
I hold fast to my righteousness and I will not let it go, and my heart will not disapprove of me as long as I live.
Let my enemy be like the wicked, and let anyone that rises up against me be like the unrighteous.
For what hope does the hypocrite have, and what has he gained when God takes his soul away?
Will God hear his cries when trouble comes his way?
Will he delight himself in the Almighty, and will he always call on God?
I will teach you by the hand of God, and what is with the Almighty I will not conceal.
Behold, you yourselves have seen it all, why then do you continue this vain talk?
This is a wicked man's portion with God, and what the heritage of the oppressors will receive from the Almighty.
His children are only multiplied for the sword, and his offspring will not be satisfied with just bread.
Those that remain of him will be buried in death, and his widows will not weep.
Even though he piles up silver like dust, and prepares clothes like clay.
He may prepare it, but the righteous will wear it, and the innocent will divide the silver.
He builds his house like a moth's cocoon or a vendor's market booth.
The rich man will lie down, but not for long because when he opens his eyes it will all be gone.
Terrors take hold of him like rushing water, a violent storm steals him away in the night.
The east wind carries him away, and he disappears as the storm hurls him from his home.
Because God will not spare him, and he would gladly flee from God's hands.
Men will clap their hands at the rich, and they will be hissed from their place."
Then Job continued speaking to Bildad the Shuhite and said, "Surely there is a silver vein in the mine, and a place where they can refine the gold.
Iron is mined from the earth, and molten brass pours out of the stone.
Man puts an end to darkness and he searches for perfection in the dark, including precious stones and the shadow of death.
The floods break the inhabitants, then even the waters forgotten by the foot are dried up, and they have gone far away from men.
As for the earth, bread comes from it and underneath it is turned up as if it were plowed by fire.
Its stones have a place for sapphires and it also has a place for gold dust.
There is an unknown path that no bird knows, and the vulture's eyes have not seen.
The lion's cubs have not walked that path, nor has the fierce lion passed through that way.
He puts his hand on the rock, and overturns the mountains by their roots.
He cuts rivers through the rocks, and his eye sees every precious thing.
He prevents the overflowing floods, and he brings anything that is hidden out into light.
But where is wisdom found, and where is the place of understanding?
Man does not know the price of wisdom, nor is it found in the land of the living.
The deep waters say, 'It is not in me!' And the sea says, 'It is not with me!'
It cannot be bought with gold, nor can it be purchased for any amount of weighed silver.
It cannot be purchased with the gold of Ophir, onyx, or sapphires.
Wisdom cannot be bought with gold or crystal, nor can it be exchanged for jewels set in fine gold.
Not to mention anything made of coral or pearls, because the price of wisdom is far above rubies.
Ethiopian topaz or pure gold will not equal its value.
So where does wisdom come from, and where is the place of understanding?
Since it is hidden from the eyes of every living thing, and even withheld from the birds of the air.
Death and destruction say, 'We have heard of its fame with our ears.'
God understands its ways, and he knows where its found.
Because he sees the ends of the earth, and everything under the entire heavens.
He gives weight to the winds, and he weighs and measures the waters.
When he created the rain, he decreed a path for the lightning and made the rumble of thunder.
Then he did see and declare its wisdom when he prepared it and searched it out.
And to man he said, 'Behold fear of the Lord is wisdom, and to leave evil behind is understanding.'"
Then Job continued his parable to Bildad the Shuhite.
And he said, "Oh if only things for me were like they were before, when God protected me.
When his candle shone on my head, and his light led me through the darkness.
Like I was when I was young, when God's secret mark was on my tabernacle.
When the Almighty was still with me, and my children were still around me.
When I washed my feet with butter, and the grindstone poured out rivers of olive oil.
When I left through the city gate, and prepared my seat in the streets!
When the young men saw me and hid, and the aged respectfully stood up.
When the princes stopped talking, and they covered their mouth with their hand.
When the nobles held their peace, and their tongues were stuck to the roofs of their mouths.
When they heard me then blessed me, and when their eyes saw me and gave witness on my behalf.
Because I delivered the poor who cried out, the fatherless, and anyone who had no one else to help them.
Anyone who was dying and ready to perish blessed me, and I helped the widow's heart sing for joy.
I was dressed in righteousness, and my judgments were like a royal robe and a jeweled crown.
I was the eyes for the blind and the feet for the lame.
I was a father to the poor, and whatever I did not know I searched out.
I broke the jaws of the wicked, and took the spoils from his teeth.
Then I said, 'I will die in my nest, and my days will multiply like the sand.
My root will spread through the waters, and the dew lay on my branches all night long.
My glory was always fresh in me, and the bow in my hand was always renewed.
Men were silent when I counseled them, they waited patiently and listened to me.
After they heard what I had to say they did not speak again, and my speech settled on them.
They waited for me to speak as if they were waiting for rain, they drank in my words as if they were the harvest rain.
If I laughed at them, they did not believe it, and they did not disregard the light from my face.
I chose their way out and I sat as their chief, and I lived like a king among his troops, and as one who comforted the mourners."
Then Job continued speaking to Bildad the Shuhite and said, "But now I am mocked by those younger than me, whose fathers I would not even have let sit with my dogs or flocks.
So how can the strength of their hands profit me, since they are now perishing in their old age?
Because of want and famine, they were solitary and fled into the wilderness in former times of desolation and waste.
They chop leaves from flowering bushes, and eat juniper roots for their meat.
They were driven away from men, and people shouted at them as if they were a thief.
They had to live in the valley cliffs, the earth's caves, and in the rocks.
They brayed like donkeys among the bushes, and they gathered together under the stinging nettles.
They were children of immoral, wicked, and foolish men, they were more repulsive than dirt.
Now I am a joke, and a perfect example for their song about fools.
They abhor me and flee far away from me, and they spit in my face.
Because God has cut my cord and afflicted me, and my enemies have loosened my bridle.
At my right hand, the youth raise up their destructive ways against me, and they push my feet away.
They ruin my path, without anyone else's help they plan disasters for me.
They come at me like wide breaking waves, with devastation that they themselves have rolled against me.
Terrors are released on me, they pursue my soul like the wind, and my welfare passes away like a cloud.
Now my soul is being poured out of me, and days of affliction have taken hold of me.
My bones are pierced within me in the middle of the night, and my sinews get no rest.
The great force of my disease ruins my clothing, the disease holds me by the collar of my coat.
God has throw me into the mud, and I have become like dust and ashes.
God, I cry out to you and you do not hear me, I stand up and you do not even notice me.
You have been cruel to me, you oppose me with your strong hand against me.
You lift me up to the wind and make me ride on it, and you dissolve my possessions.
Because I know you will bring me to death, and to the final home appointed for all living things.
However will he not stretch out his hand when he falls into the grave, even though he cries for help in his destruction.
Did I not weep for anyone who was in trouble, and was my soul not grieved for the poor?
When I looked for good, evil came to me. When I waited for light, darkness showed up.
My bowels boiled in agony, and the days of my affliction prevented me from resting.
I mourned outside in the sun, and I stood up and cried among the congregation.
I am a brother of dragons and a companion to owls.
My skin is blackened and my bones burn with fever.
My harp has turned to grief and mourning, and my organ sounds like those who weep."
Then Job continued speaking to Bildad the Shuhite and said, "I made a covenant with my eyes, why should I even think about a young woman?
What portion of God is there from above, and what inheritance from the Almighty comes from on high?
Is not destruction for the wicked, and strange punishments for the workers of immorality?
Does he not see my ways, and count all my steps?
If I have walked with vanity, or if my foot was hurried to deceive.
But let God weigh my honesty with an evenly balanced scale, and he will know my integrity.
If my steps have turned away from the true path, or my heart has followed my eyes, or if darkness has stained my hands.
Then let someone else eat what I have sown, and let my crops be rooted out.
If my heart has been deceived by a woman, or if I have laid in wait at my neighbor's door.
Then let my wife grind grain for others, and let other men lay down with her.
Because this is a heinous crime, and it is an immorality to be punished by judges.
Because it is a fire that consumes to destruction, and it would root out my entire harvest.
If I despised the cause of my male or female servants when they complained against me.
What will I do when God rises up when he visits me, and how will I answer him?
Did not he who made me in the womb also make them, and is he not the same one who formed us in the womb?
Have I withheld the desires of the poor, or have I caused the widow's eyes to fail?
Or have eaten my food alone without feeding the fatherless?
From my youth I brought him up with me as his father, and I have guided the widow from my mother's womb.
If I have seen anyone perish from lack of clothing, or if I have seen a poor person without a coat.
If his heart has not blessed me, or he was not warmed with the fleece from my sheep.
If I have lifted my hand up against the fatherless, when I saw I had help at the gate.
Then let my arm fall from my shoulder blade, and may the bone in my arm be broken.
Because destruction from God terrorized me, and I could not endure his judgements from high heaven.
If I have put my hope in or trusted my security to fine gold.
If I have rejoiced because I had great wealth and I had been given so much.
If I saw the sun when it shined, or the moon walking in bright light.
If my heart was secretly tempted and I blew a kiss with my hand.
This is also an immorality to be punished by the judge, because I would have denied my God above.
If I rejoice in the destruction of someone who hated me, or my spirit was lifted up when evil found him.
And I have not allowed my mouth to sin by cursing his soul.
There is no one from my tabernacle who can not say, 'We are so full, we have eaten more than enough of his food to be satisfied.
Strangers did not have to stay in the streets, because I opened my doors to travelers.
If I tried to conceal my sins like Adam, and I hid my immorality in my heart.
Did I fear crowds or the contempt of families, or was I so terrified that I stayed silent and went out the door?
Oh if only someone would hear me! Behold, my desire is that the Almighty would answer me, and that my accuser had written a book.
I would surely put it on my shoulders, and wear it like a crown on my head.
I would explain everything I have done to him, and approach him as if I were a prince.
If my land cries out against me, or the plowed furrows also complain.
If I have eaten its fruits without paying for it, or I have caused its owners to lose their life.
Then let weeds and thistles grow instead of wheat or barley." Job's words are ended.
So these three men stopped answering Job because he was righteous in his own sight.
Then Elihu's anger was kindled against Job because he justified himself rather than God. Elihu was Barachel the Buzite's son and they were related to Ram.
He was also angry with his three friends, because they had no answers, but they condemned Job anyway.
Now Elihu had waited until Job finished speaking, because they were older than him.
Elihu's anger was kindled against these three men when he realized that they had no answers.
So Barachel the Buzite's son Elihu answered and said, "I am young and you are very old, so I was afraid to speak and I did not dare to express my opinion.
I thought to myself, 'The old ones should speak, and their vast number of years should be able to teach wisdom.'
But there is a spirit in man, and the Almighty's inspiration gives them understanding.
Great men are not always wise, nor do the aged always understand God's judgments.
So I spoke up and said, 'Listen to me, I will also express my opinion.'
Behold, I waited for your words and listened to your reasons, as you searched for words.
Yes, I did pay attention when you spoke, and I realized that none of you convinced Job of his inequity or even had an answer for anything that he said.
Otherwise you would have said, 'We have found wisdom, let God not man push him down!'
But Job has not directed his words against me, and I will not answer him with your complaints."
They were amazed and speechless, and they could not answer.
So, I'm waiting for your answer, because you just stand there in silence saying nothing.
Now I will also give you my answer and my opinion.
Because I am so full of advice, but my restrains me from responding.
Behold, my stomach is like a new unvented wine bottle and it's ready to burst.
I must speak to be refreshed, so I will open my lips and answer.
I pray that I am not partial to anyone, and I am not going to flatter anyone with fancy titles.
Because if I flattered anyone, my maker would immediately remove me."
And Elihu continued speaking and said, "So Job, I pray you will listen to what I have to say.
Because now that I have opened my mouth and spoken out.
My words will come directly from my honest heart, and I will speak clearly with knowledge.
The spirit of God created me, and the Almighty's breath has given me life.
If you can answer me, then stand up and confront me if you can.
Behold, I am just like you since I am also formed from clay, and just like you I also wish to be in God's goodwill.
My terrors are not meant to make you afraid, nor will my hand be heavy on you.
Surely you have spoken and I have heard your voice.
And I heard you when you said, 'I am clean and without transgression, I am innocent and there is no immorality in me.
Behold, God looks for occasions to turn against me, and he counts me as his enemy.
He puts my feet in stocks and he watches my every move.'
Behold, this is what makes you unrighteous and my answer to you, is that God is greater than man.
Why do you struggle against him? Because he does not have to give you an accounting for anything that he has done.
Because when God speaks once or even twice, man still does not understand.
He speaks in a dream or a vision of the night, when deep sleep falls on men and they slumber in their bed.
Then he opens men's ears and makes sure they hear his instructions.
So that he may stop man's purpose, and prevent their pride.
He keeps man's soul from stumbling into the pit, and prevents him from perishing by the sword.
God chastens man with pain on his bed, and overwhelms his bones with throbbing distress.
So that he abhors his bread, and his soul detests his meat.
His flesh is consumed and disappears, and his previously unseen rib bones protrude.
Yes, his soul draws near the grave and his life succumbs to the destroyers.
If only there was a messenger or an interpreter with him, one among a thousand to answer him honestly.
To be gracious to him and say, 'Deliver him from going down to the pit, I have found a ransom for him.'
His flesh will be fresher than a child's, and he will return to the days of his youth.
He will pray to God and God will favor him. He will see God's face with joy because God will restore his righteousness.
He looks at men and if anyone says, 'I have sinned and perverted the righteous, and it did not profit me.
He will deliver his soul from the pit and his life will see the light.'
God often works all these things with man.
And brings his soul back from the pit, to be enlightened with the light of the living.
Mark my words Job and listen to me, hold your peace and let me speak.
If you have anything to say, speak up and answer me because it is my desire to justify you.
If not, listen to me and hold your peace, and I will teach you wisdom."
Furthermore Elihu answered and said.
And he said, "Hear my words and listen to me, O you wise and knowledgeable men.
Because the ears test words, like the mouth tastes meat.
So let us choose good judgment and righteousness for ourselves.
Because Job has said, 'I am righteous, but God has still taken away my judgment.
Should I lie about my righteousness? My wound is incurable, even though I am without transgression.'
Who is like Job and drinks scorn like water?
Who travels in the company of workers of immorality, and walks with wicked men.
Because he has said, 'It profits a man nothing to delight in God.'
So listen to me you men of understanding, far be it from Almighty God to do wickedness and commit immorality.
Because depending on the works of a man's hands, God will either reward him or bring him sorrow.
Yes it is true, God will not do anything wicked, nor will the Almighty pervert judgment.
Who put him charge of the earth, or appointed him to rule the whole world?
If he set his heart on man, and he returned his spirit and breath to himself.
All flesh would perish together and man would turn back to dust.
If you now have understanding, then listen to this and hear my words.
Will someone who hates righteous ever govern, and would you condemn God who is most righteous?
Is it fitting for God to say to a king, 'You are wicked!' Or to a prince say, 'You are ungodly!'
God does not accept princes above other people, nor does he regard the rich more than the poor, because he created all of them with his hands.
All people will die in an instance and pass away in the middle of the night, and the mighty will perish and be removed from power without the touch of a man's hand.
Because God's eyes are on the ways of man, and he sees everywhere men go.
There is no darkness nor shadow of death, where the workers of immorality can hide themselves.
Because God is righteous, and he does not need to add anything to a man when he enters into God's judgment.
He will break an endless number of mighty men into pieces, and put others in their place.
God knows their works, and he destroys and overthrows them in the middle of the night.
He strikes them down as wicked men in the wide open sight of others.
Because they turned away from him, and would not consider any of his ways.
Because they caused the cry of the poor to come to him, and he hears the cries of the afflicted.
When he gives them quiet rest who can make trouble? When he hides his face who can see him? Who can oppose him, whether he moves against a whole nation or just one man?
Hypocrites should not reign, or else the people will be trapped.
Surely it is meant to be said to God, 'I have accepted my punishment and I will not offend anymore.
Teach me the immorality I have done that I can not see, and I will not do it again.
Should God repay you for following your own ways after you have rejected his? So you must choose not me, tell me what you think?
I want the men of understanding to tell me, and the wise man to listen to me.
Job has spoken without knowledge, and his words are not wise.
My desire is for Job to be put on trial until the end, because he answers for wicked men.
Because he adds rebellion to his sins, he claps his hands at us, and makes multiple accusations against God."
And Elihu continued speaking.
And he said, "Do you think it's right for you to say, that I am more righteous than God?
Because you asked, 'What advantage is it to you, and what will it profit you if you are cleansed from your sin?'
So I will you answer and your companions.
Look up to the heavens and see the clouds high above you.
If you sin, what do you have against him, or if you commit many transgressions, what does it do to him?
If you are righteous, what do you give him, or what does he receive from your hand?
Your wickedness will only hurt a man like you, and your righteousness will profit the Son of Man.
Because of the multiple oppressions the mighty make against the oppressed, they cry out for relief from the arm of the mighty.
But no one says, 'Where is God my maker, who gives us songs in the night?
Who teaches us more than the beasts of the earth, and makes us wiser than the birds of heaven?
There they cry out, but no one answers because of the pride of evil men.
Surely God does not listen vain pleas, nor will the Almighty pay any attention to it.
Although you say you can not see him, still your judgment is before him and that's why you should trust in him.
But now, because it is not so he has visited you in his anger, even though he does not realize the full extent of it.
And that's why Job opens his mouth in vain, and multiplies his ignorant words."
Elihu also proceeded, and said.
And he said, "Bear with me a little longer, and I will show you that I have more to say on God's behalf.
I get my knowledge from far away, and I ascribe righteousness to my maker.
For truly I speak the truth, and the one with perfect knowledge is with you.
Behold, God is mighty and he does not despise anyone, he is mighty in strength and wisdom.
He does not protect the life of the wicked, but he gives righteousness to the poor.
He does not withdraw his eyes from the righteous, but they are on the throne with kings, and yes he does establish them forever, and they are glorified.
And if they are bound with chains, and caught in cords of affliction.
Then he shows them their work and transgressions that they have exceeded.
He also opens their ears to discipline, and commands them to return from immorality.
If they obey and serve him, they will spend their days and years in prosperity and pleasures.
But if they do not obey, they will perish by the sword and die without knowledge.
But the hypocrites in heart pile up anger, and they do not cry out when he binds them.
They die in their youth, and their life is surrounded by the unclean.
He delivers the poor from their afflictions, and opens their ears in oppression.
Even so, he would still have moved you from a straight place of hardship to a wide open space where there are no restrictions, and the rich food on your table would be plentiful.
But now, you have satisfied the judgment of the wicked, so judgment and justice have taken hold of you.
Beware for there is anger and he may strike you down, and then not even a great ransom could save you.
Will he be impressed with your riches? No, he will not be impressed with your gold or all the forces of your strength.
Do not desire the night, when people disappear from their place.
Take heed, do not turn to immorality because you have chosen it over affliction.
Behold, God's power glorifies and who else can teach like him?
Who has appointed God's way to him? And who can say to him, 'You have been immoral!'
Remember that you magnify his work, which men have seen.
Every man may see it, and even a man far away may behold it.
Behold, God is great and we do not know him, nor can the number of his years be counted.
Because he makes the small drops of water that pour down as rain, or they form the morning dew.
Which the clouds shower down abundantly on man.
Can anyone understand how the clouds spread across the sky, or the thundering noise of his tabernacle?
Behold, he scatters his lighting across it and covers the bottom of the sea.
Because by them he judges the people, and he gives them an abundance of meat.
He covers the lightening with clouds, and commands it not to strike through the clouds that come between them.
Its thunder announces his presence, and even the cattle know when a storm is coming."
Elihu continued to speak and said, "This also makes my heart tremble and it moves out of place.
Listen carefully to the sounds of God's thunderous voice when he speaks.
His thunder rumbles under the heavens as his lightning streaks across the skies to the ends of the earth.
After the thunder roars, God's majestic voice holds nothing back when his voice is heard.
When God's voice thunders we cannot comprehend the marvelously great things he has done.
Because God speaks to the snow and says, 'Fall and cover the earth.' His strength also tells the great and small rains when to pour out on the earth.
He seals every man's hand, so that all men will know his work.
Then all the animals go into their dens, and remain there.
The whirlwind comes from the south and the cold comes from the north.
The frost comes from the breath of God, and the entire width of the waters are frozen.
Watering the earth wearies the thick clouds, and he scatters his lightening through them.
And the clouds swirl all around by his counsel, and they do whatever he commands them to do on the face of the earth.
He causes the rains to come, whether it is for the correction of his land, or mercy.
O Job, listen to this and stand still, then consider God's wonderous works.
Do you know when God will send the clouds, or how he made his cloud's lighting flash?
Do you know how he balances the clouds, which are his wonderous works that come from perfect knowledge?
Or how your garments are warmed, when he quietens the earth by the south wind?
Can you spread out the skies like him to reflect the summer heat like a strong brass mirror?
Teach us what to say to him, because we cannot prepare our defense in the dark.
Will anyone tell him that I want to speak? And if a man speaks to him, he will surely be swallowed up.
And now men do not see the bright light in the clouds, but the wind passes by and cleanses them.
Fair weather comes from the north with God's majestic power.
We cannot find the Almighty by touching him, his power and judgments are excellent. Through his abundant mercy and justice, he will not afflict us.
And that's why men do fear him, and he does not respect any that are wise of heart.
Then the Lord answered Job from the whirlwind.
And the Lord said, "Who is this that darkens my counsel with words of ignorance?
Now cover yourself like a man because I will demand answers from you, and you will answer me!
Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth? Tell me now if you have any understanding.
Who laid it out and determined the earth's measurements? Speak now if you know who stretched the measuring line over it?
What was its foundation fastened to, or who laid its corner stone?
When did the morning stars sing together, and when did all the sons of God shout for joy?
Who enclosed the ocean's doors when it burst forth as if it had come from the womb,
when I made the cloud's garment and the thick darkness as a warm comfortable blanket for it,
when I broke up the oceans and decreed its boundaries and where to set its bars and doors,
and I declared, 'You may come this far, but no farther! And this is where your proud waves will stop.'
Since the beginning of your days, have you ever commanded the morning dawn and told the sun when to rise,
so that light spread to the ends of the earth, to shake the wicked from it?
The earth turns like clay under the seal, and the hills stand like a folded garment.
Light is withheld from the wicked, and their high and mighty arm will be broken.
Have you entered the deep ocean springs, or have you walked in the underwater rivers of the deep?
Have the gates of death been revealed to you, or have you seen the gates of the shadow of death?
Have you thought about the width of the earth? Tell me now if you know everything.
Which way is the way to where the light lives? Where is the home of darkness,
so you can return the darkness to it boundaries, do you know the path to its house?
Surely you know because you were born then and you have lived a great number of days, haven't you?
Have you entered the treasuries where the snow is stored, or have you seen the hail's treasuries?
Have you seen where I have reserved them for times of trouble, against the days of battle and war?
Which way is the light dispersed, or the direction that the east wind is scattered over the earth?
Who divided the channels for the flooding rivers, or cleared the way for lightning thunderbolts?
Who causes it to rain in the wilderness throughout the earth, where there are no men?
Who brought rain to satisfy the desolate wasteland, and made the bud of the tender herb bloom in the spring?
Does the rain have a father, and who is the father of the dew drops?
From whose womb does the ice come? And who gives birth to the grayish frost from heaven?
Who gives birth to the frozen waters that become hard as stone, when the face of the deep is frozen?
Can you bind the sweet influence of the Pleiades constellation, or loosen the grip of the Orion constellation?
Can you display the Mazzaroth constellation in its season, or guide the Arcturus constellation and his sons?
Do you know the legal decrees of heaven? Can you decree the laws of physics over the earth?
Can you lift up your voice to the clouds, and make the flood waters cover you?
Can you send the lightning, so that they will come to you and say, 'Here we are.'?
Who has put wisdom in the heart, or given knowledge and understanding to the mind?
Who has the wisdom to count and number the clouds, or who can plug the water bottles of heaven?
Who knows when the dust will turn into hard clods, and cling together?
Can you hunt the prey for the lion, or satisfy the appetite of the young lions.
Doyou know when they crouch in their dens, and lie in wait for you in their shelters?
Who provides food for the raven, when their young ones cry out to God as they wander around looking for meat?"
And the Lord continued speaking and said, "Do you know what time the wild mountain goats give birth, or do you know when the does have their calves?
Can you count the months they are pregnant, or do you know what time when they give birth?
They bow down to give birth to their young ones, and they release their sorrows.
Their young ones thrive and they grow up with the wheat in the field, then they leave and never return.
Who sets the wild donkeys free, or who turns groups of wild donkeys loose?
I made the wilderness the wild donkey's house, and the barren land his home.
He scorns the overpopulated city, and he never hears the team driver's shouts.
The mountain range is his pasture where he searches for anything green.
Will the wild ox be willing to serve you, or will he stay in your barn?
Can you force a wild ox to follow you, and plow the furrows and valleys in a field with a harness?
Do you trust its great strength enough to turn your hard labor over to it?
Do you believe it will bring your grain back to you to store in your barn?
Or who gave good wings and feathers to the peacock and ostrich?
Which leave their eggs in the earth, and warms them with dust.
And forgets that a foot could step on and crush them, or a wild beast may break them.
Her heart is hardened against her young ones, as though they were not even hers, her labor is in vain and fearless.
Because God has deprived her of wisdom and understanding.
When she lifts herself high up into the air, she laughs at the horse and its rider.
Have you given the horse its strength, or did you put the mane on his neck with thunder?
Can you make him as afraid as a grasshopper? His nostrils are glorious with a terrifying snort.
He paws the ground in the valley and rejoices in his strength, he charges into battle to meet armed men.
He mocks fear and is not frightened, nor does he turn back from the sword.
The quiver maracas against him, and the spear and shield glitter in the sunlight.
He devours the ground with rage and fierceness, and he charges at the sound of the trumpet.
He cheers when he hears the trumpets and the thunders and shouting of the captains, and he smells the battle from far away.
Does your wisdom teach the hawk how to fly or how to stretch out her wings toward the south?
Does the eagle fly at your command, and make her nest in high places?
She lives and endures in a strong nest in the craggy rocks.
From there she looks for her prey, and her eyes can see it from far away.
After she kills her prey and brings it to her young ones, they drink its blood."
Then the Lord spoke and further answered Job.
And he said, "Can anyone dealing with God blame the Almighty? If so then answer and instruct him."
Then Job answered the Lord, and said.
And he said, "Behold I am vile, so what kind of answer can I give you? I will cover my mouth with my hand.
I have spoken once and I have no answer, yes I have spoken twice but I have nothing further to say."
Then answered the Lord to Job out of the whirlwind, and said.
And he said, "Cover yourself like a man, I will demand an answer from you, and you will answer me.
Will you also question my judgment? Will you condemn me just to make yourself righteous?
Do you have an arm like God's, or can your voice thunder like his?
Then cover yourself with majesty and excellence, and show your glory and beauty.
