The wicked desire the plunder of evil men, but the righteous yield good fruit.
A wicked man is snared by his lip's transgressions, but the just will escape from trouble.
A man will be satisfied by the good speech of his mouth, and the works of a man's hands will be returned to him.
A fool is righteous in his own eyes, but a man that listens to the counsel of others is wise.
A fool's anger is instantly known, but a prudent man covers shame.
A man who speaks the truth shows righteousness, but a false witness speaks deceit.
A harsh man speaks like a piercing sword, but the tongue of the wise speaks good health.
The truthful lip will be established forever, but a lying tongue lasts just a moment.
A man who imagines evil has deceit in his hearts, but the counselors of peace have joy.
Nothing evil will happen to the righteous, but the wicked will be filled with mischief.
Lying lips are an abomination to the Lord, but those who deal honestly are his delight.
A prudent man conceals knowledge, but the fools heart proclaims foolishness.
The hand of the diligent will rule, but the dull and lazy end up in slavery.
A sad heart makes a man stoop over, but a good word makes it glad.
A righteous man makes friends cautiously, but the ways of the wicked seduces them.
The dull and lazy man does not roast his game from hunting, but a diligent man's prize is precious to him.
The way of the righteousness is life, and in the pathway of righteousness there is no death.
A wise son listens to his father's instructions, but a scorner does not hear rebuke.
A man eat good from the fruit of his mouth, but the soul of the transgressors will eat violence.
A man who holds his mouth protects his life, but a man who opens his lips will be destroyed.
The lazy soul desires much but has nothing, but the soul of the diligent will be satisfied.
A righteous man hates lying, but a wicked man is shameful and loathsome.
Righteousness protects an honest man, but wickedness overthrows the sinner.
A man that calls himself rich has nothing, but a man who says he is poor has great wealth.
A man's life may be ransomed by his riches, but a poor man hears no threat.
The light of the righteous rejoices, but the lamp of the wicked will be extinguished.
Disagreement comes only by pride, but a well advised man has wisdom.
Wealth gotten by vanity will dwindle away, but a man who earns through his labor will prosper.
Deferred hope makes a man's heart sick, but when his desire arrives, it is a tree of life.
Whoever despises the word will be destroyed, but a man who fears the commandments will be rewarded.
The law of the wise is a fountain of life, that turns one away from the snares of death.
Good understanding gives favor, but the way of transgressors is hard.
Every prudent man deals with knowledge, but a fool displays his foolishness.
A wicked messenger falls into mischief, but a faithful ambassador is healthy.
Anyone who refuses instruction will find poverty and shame, but a man who accepts blame will be honored.
Accomplished desires are sweet to the soul, but abandoning evil seems to be an abomination to fools.
A man that walks with wise men will be wise, but a companion of fools will be destroyed.
Evil pursues sinners, but the righteous will be repaid with goodwill.
A good man leaves an inheritance to his descendants, and the wealth of the sinner is stored up for the righteous.
Abundant food is in the worked land of the poor, but it is destroyed by lack of judgment.
The man who spares his staff hates his son, but the man that loves his son disciplines him ahead of time.
The righteous man eats to satisfy his soul, but the wicked man's stomach will hunger.
Every wise woman builds her own house, but the foolish woman tears it down with her hands.
The honest man fears the Lord, but the perverted man despises him.
The foolish man carries a staff of pride in his mouth, but the lips of the wise will protect them.
Where there are no oxen the crib is clean, but an abundant harvest comes through the strength of the ox.
A faithful witness will not lie, but a false witness will utter lies.
A scorner seeks wisdom and finds none, but knowledge is easy for anyone who understands.
Avoid a foolish man, because you will receive no knowledge from his lips.
The wisdom of a prudent man understands his ways, but the fools foolishness is his deceit.
Fools mock making the atonement of sin, but favor is found among the righteous.
A man's heart knows his own bitterness, and strangers do not meddle and interfere with his joy.
The house of the wicked will be overthrown, but the tabernacle of the honest will flourish.
There is a way which seems right to a man, but in the end it leads to death.
Even in laughter the heart is sorrowful, but in the end that cheerfulness is sadness.
The backslider in heart is filled with his own ways, but a good man will be satisfied with himself.
A simple man believes every word, but the prudent man looks carefully where he is headed.
A wise man fears evil and leaves it behind, but the confident fool rages.
A man that is quick to anger deals foolishly, and a man of wicked devices is hated.
A simple man inherits foolishness, but prudent men are crowned with knowledge.
The evil bow before the good, and the wicked at the gates of the righteous.
A poor man is even hated by his own neighbor, but a rich man has many friends.
A man that despises his neighbor sins, but a man that has mercy on the poor is happy.
Do not those who devise evil things make mistakes? But mercy and truth will belong to those who devise good things.
There is profit in all labor, but mere talk leads only to poverty.
The crown of the wise is their riches, but the foolishness of fools is foolishness.
A true witness delivers souls, but a deceitful witness speaks lies.
Fear of the Lord makes one strong in confidence, and his children will have a place of refuge.
The fear of the Lord is the fountain of life, that leads away from the snares of death.
A multitude of people are the king's honor, but a the lack of people leads to the destruction of the prince.
A man that is slow to anger has great understanding, but a man that has a hasty spirit glorifies foolishness.
A sound heart is the life of the flesh, but envy will decay the bones.
A man that oppresses the poor disapproves of his creator, but a man that honors him has mercy on the poor.
A wicked man is driven away by his wickedness, but the righteous man has hope in his death.
Wisdom rests in the heart of anyone with understanding, but those who are in the midst of fools are revealed.
Righteousness glorifies a nation, but sin is a disgrace to many people.
The king shows favor to a wise servant, but his anger is kindled against anyone that causes shame.
A kind answer turns anger away, but grievous words stir up anger.
A wise man uses knowledge correctly, but a fool's mouth pours out foolishness.
The Lord's eyes are everywhere, and he sees the good and the evil.
A wholesome tongue is a tree of life, but perverseness breaks the spirit's defenses.
A fool despises his father's instructions, but a man that accepts blame is prudent.
There is much treasure in the house of the righteous, but the revenue of the wicked generates trouble.
The wise man disperses knowledge, but the foolish heart does not.
The sacrifices of a wicked man are an abomination to the Lord, but the prayers of an honest man is his delight.
The way of the wicked is an abomination to the Lord, but he loves anyone that follows righteousness.
Correction is grievous to anyone that abandons the way, and the man who hates blame will die.
Hell and destruction are before the Lord, but the hearts of the children of men contains much more?
A scorner does not love someone who blames him, nor will he accept the wise.
A merry heart makes a cheerful appearance, but a sorrowful heart breaks the spirit.
The heart of anyone with understanding seeks knowledge, but the fool's mouth feeds on foolishness.
All the days of the afflicted are evil, but a man with a merry heart has a continuous feast.
It is better to have little and fear of the Lord, than it is to have great treasure full of trouble.
It is better to have a dinner of herbs where there is love, than to have a stalled ox full of hatred.
A wrathful man stirs up conflict, but a man that is slow to anger appeases conflict.
The way of a dull and lazy man is like a hedge of thorns, but the way of the righteous is clearly revealed.
A wise son makes a happy father, but a foolish man despises his mother.
Foolishness is joyous to anyone who is destitute of wisdom, but a man of understanding walks honestly.
Your purposes are disappointed without counsel, but with a multitude of counselors they are established.
A man has joy through his mouth's answers, and how good it is for te right word spoken at the right time!
The wise walk in the way of life to the above, so that he may leave the hell from beneath.
The Lord will destroy the house of the proud, but he will establish the widow's border.
The thoughts of the wicked are an abomination to the Lord, but the words of the pure are pleasant words.
A man that is greedy, gains troubles for his own house, but a man that hates gifts will live.
The righteous heart studies to answer, but the wicked mouth pours out evil things.
The Lord is far from the wicked, but he hears the prayers of the righteous.
The light of the eyes rejoices the heart, and a good report nourishes the bones.
The ear that listens to the blame of life endures among the wise.
A man that refuses instruction despises his own soul, but a man that hears blame gains understanding.
Fear of the Lord leads to wisdom, and humility comes before honor.
The preparations in a man's heart, and the tongue's answer comes from the Lord.
All of a man's ways are clean in his own eyes, but the Lord weighs the spirits.
Commit your works to the Lord, and your thoughts will be established.
The Lord has made all things for himself, including the wicked for the day of evil.
Everyone with a proud heart is an abomination to the Lord, even though he es hand in hand, he will not go unpunished.
Immorality is purged through mercy and truth, and men who fear the Lord leave evil behind.
When a man's ways please the Lord, he makes even his enemies to be at peace with him.
It is better to have little with righteousness, than great revenues without righteousness.
A man's heart devises his way, but the Lord directs his steps.
A king gives a divine sentence with his lips, but his mouth does not sin in judgment.
The Lord has only just weights and balances, all the weights in the bag are his concern.
It is an abomination to kings to commit wickedness, because the throne is established by righteousness.
Righteous lips are the delight of kings, and they love anyone who speaks the truth.
A king's anger is like a messenger of death, but a wise man will pacify it.
The light of the king's appearance is life, and his favor is like a cloud of the harvest rain.
It is much better to acquire wisdom than to receive gold! And to gain understanding is more valuable than choice silver!
The highway of the honest leaves evil behind, a man that keeps God's way protects his soul.
Pride goes before destruction, and an arrogant spirit precedes a fall.
It is better to have a lowly humble spirit, than to divide the spoils with the proud.
The man who handles things wisely will find good things, and whoever trusts the Lord is happy.
The wise at heart will be called prudent, and speaking with a sweet spirit increases learning.
Understanding is a wellspring of life to anyone that has it, but the instructions of a fool is foolishness.
A wise man's heart teaches his mouth truth, and adds learning to his lips.
Pleasant words are like a honeycomb, sweet to the soul and healthy to the bones.
There is a way that seems right to a man, but it ends up being the way to death.
A man that labors labors for himself, because his mouth craves food from him.
An ungodly man digs up evil, and his lips are like a burning fire.
A stubborn man sows conflict, and a mutterer separates best friends.
A violent man tempts his neighbor, and leads him into the way that is not good.
He shuts his eyes to devise stubborn things, and when he speaks he makes evil things happen.
The old gray head is a crown of glory, if it is found along the way of righteousness.
A man that is slow to anger is better than a mighty warrior, and a man who controls his angry spirit is greater than the warrior who captures a city.
A lot is cast into the lap, but every decision comes from the Lord.
A dry morsel and a quiet home, is better than a house full of conflict and sacrifices.
A wise servant will rule over a son who causes shame, and will share in the brothers inheritance.
The crucible is for refining silver and a furnace is for gold, but the Lord tests men's hearts.
Someone who does wicked things listens to false lips, and a liar listens to a naughty tongue.
Whoever mock the poor disapproves of his Maker, and a man who is glad at calamities will not go unpunished.
Descendants are an old man's crown, and the glory of children are their fathers.
Excellent speech is not becoming of a fool, how much less are lying lips to a prince.
A gift is like a precious stone in the eyes of anyone gives it, and it prospers wherever it turns.
The man who covers a transgression seeks love, but a man who repeats something separates friends.
Taking the blame cuts a wise man more deeply than a hundred stripes to a fool.
An evil man seeks only rebellion, and that's why a cruel messenger will be sent against him.
It is better to meet a bear robbed of her cubs, than a fool and his foolishness.
If a man who rewards evil for good, evil will not leave his house.
The beginning of conflict is like the beginning of a flood, so leave disagreement behind, before it meddles with your life.
A man that justifies the wicked, and a man that condemns the just, are both an abomination to the Lord.
So why should a fool have the price of wisdom in his hand, if he has no heart for it?
A friend always loves, but a brother is born for adversity.
A man without understanding shakes hands, and becomes the collateral of his friend.
A man that loves transgression also loves conflict, and a man that glorifies his gate seeks destruction.
A man with a stubborn heart finds nothing good, and a man with a perverse tongue falls into mischief.
A man who fathers a fool does so to his own sorrow, and the father of a fool has no joy.
A merry heart is like good medicine, but a broken spirit dries the bones.
A wicked man accepts a gift to pervert the ways of good judgment.
Wisdom comes before someone with understanding, but the fool's eyes wander to the ends of the earth.
A foolish son causes grief to his father, and bitterness to his mother.
It is not good to punish the righteous, nor attack a prince for justice.
A man with knowledge uses his words sparingly, and an man understanding has an excellent spirit.
Even a fool who holds his peace is thought to be wise, and a man that keeps his mouth shut is thought to be understanding.
A man who separates himself seeks selfish desire, and meddles and interferes with all wisdom.
A fool does not delight in understanding, but his heart is only interested in itself.
A wicked man comes with contempt, shame, and disrespect.
The words from a man's mouth are like deep waters, and the wellspring of wisdom is like a flowing brook.
It is not good to accept the wicked person to overthrow those with righteous judgment.
A fool's lips begin disagreement, and his mouth calls for beatings.
A fool's mouth is his destruction, and his lips are the snare of his soul.
The words of a gossiper are like wounds, and they cut deep into the stomach.
A man who is dull and lazy in his work, is the brother of one who causes great destruction.
The Lord's name is a strong defensive tower, and the righteous man runs to it for safety.
The rich man's wealth is his strength, which is like a high wall around his own conceit.
A man's heart is arrogant just before its destruction, and humility comes before honor.
A man that answers before he hears the question, brings shame and foolishness on himself.
A man's spirit will survive his infirmity, but who can bear a wounded spirit?
The heart of a prudent man gains knowledge, and the wise ear seeks knowledge.
A man's gift makes room for him, and brings him before great men.
A man who first states his own cause seems just, but his neighbor comes and questions him.
Casting lots ends disagreements, and separates mighty opponents.
An offended brother is harder win than a reinforced city, and their disagreements are like castle bars.
A man's stomach is satisfied by the fruit of his mouth, and by the harvest of his lips he will be satisfied.
Life and death are within the power of the tongue, and those who love it will eat its fruit.
Whoever finds a wife finds a good thing, and obtains the Lord's favor.
A poor man makes many pleas and requests, but a rich man answers harshly.
A man with friends must show always be friendly, but there is a friend who is closer than a brother.
A poor man who walks in his integrity, is better off than a fool with perverse lips.
A soul without knowledge is not good, and a man who is always in a hurry commits sin.
A man's foolishness perverts his way, and his heart worries about the Lord.
Wealth makes many friends, but a poor man is separated from his neighbor.
A false witness will not go unpunished, and a man who tells lies will not escape.
Many will plead for the prince's favor, and everyone is a friend of anyone who gives gifts.
A poor man's brothers all hate him, so how much more do his friends avoid him? He tries to pursue them with words, but they are nowhere to be found.
A man who receives wisdom loves his own soul, and those with understanding will find goodness.
A false witness will not go unpunished, and a man who tells lies will perish.
Delight is not suitable for a fool, much less for a servant to rule over princes.
A man's discretion defers his anger, and it is to his glory to overlook a transgression.
The king's anger is like a roaring lion, but his favor is like moist dew on the grass.
A foolish son is his father's disaster, and a quarrelsome wife is like a constant drip, drip, drip.
A house and riches are the fathers' inheritance, and a prudent wife is from the Lord.
Slothfulness throws a man into a deep sleep, and an idle soul will suffer hunger.
A man who keeps a commandment keeps his own soul, but a man with careless ways will die.
A man who has pity on the poor lends to the Lord, and those to whom he has given loans will repay him.
Chasten your son while there is hope, and do not let your soul despair over his crying.
An angry man will suffer punishment, because if you rescue him you must do it over and over again.
Listen to counsel and receive instruction, so that you may be wise in your latter days.
There are many devices in a man's heart, nevertheless the Lord's counsel will stand.
A man desires kindness, and a poor man is better off than a liar.
Fear of the Lord leads to life, and a man with life will endure and be satisfied, and he will not be visited by evil.
A dull and lazy man hides his hand, and he will not so much as bring it up to his mouth.
Defeat a scorner and the simple will beware, blame someone with understanding, and he will gain knowledge.
A man who assaults his father and chases his mother away, is a son who causes shame and brings disrespect.
My son, do not listen to instructions that causes one to ignore the words of knowledge.
An ungodly witness scorns justice, and the wicked mouth of consumes immorality.
Judgment is prepared for scorners, and beatings are for the fool's back.
Wine mocks, strong drink rages, and whoever is deceived that way is not wise.
Fear of a king is like a roaring lion, whoever provokes his anger sins against his own soul.
It is an honor for a man to not participate in conflict, but every fool will be meddling.
The sluggard does not plow because it is cold, so he will beg at harvest and have nothing.
Counsel from the heart of man is like deep water, but a man of understanding will draw it out.
Most men will proclaims his own goodness, but who can find a faithful man?
A just man walks in his integrity, and his children are blessed after him.
A king who sits on the judgment throne scatters all evil away with his eyes.
Who can say, "I have cleansed my heart, and I have been purified of my sins."
Unequal weights and measures, are both an abomination to the Lord.
Even a child is known by the things he does, whether his works are pure and upright.
The Lord has made both the hearing ear and the seeing eye.
Do not love sleep or you will become poor, open your eyes and you will have plenty of bread.
The buyer says it is worth nothing, but on his way out he boasts.
There is an abundance of gold and rubies, but the lips of knowledge are a precious jewel.
Take a man's garment as security for a stranger, and get collateral from him if it is for a foreign woman.
The bread of deceit is sweet to a man, but afterwards his mouth will be filled with gravel.
Everything is established by consultation, and only wage war with good advice.
A man who goes around gossiping reveals secrets, so do not mess with anyone who flatters with his lips.
Whoever curses his father or mother, will have his lamp put out in obscure darkness.
An inheritance may be received quickly in the beginning, but in the end it will not be blessed.
Do not say, "I will compensate evil," but wait on the Lord and he will save you.
Dishonest weights are an abomination to the Lord, and a false balance is not good.
A man's travels are of the Lord, so how can a man understand his own ways?
It is a snare for a man to dedicate something as holy, and after he makes his promise, he questions whether or not he must keep his word.
A wise king disperses the wicked, and rolls the threshing wheel over them.
The spirit of man is a lamp to the Lord, who searches his innermost heart.
Mercy and truth preserves the king, and his throne is upheld by mercy.
The glory of young men is their strength, and the beauty of an old man is his grey head.
The black and blue bruise cleanses away evil, and beating cleanses the innermost stomach.
A king's heart is like a river in the hands of the Lord, he directs it wherever he wants it to go.
The ways of every man is righteous in his own eyes, but the Lord ponders their hearts.
Justice and judgment is more acceptable to the Lord than sacrifice.
A haughty look, a proud heart, and the plowing of the wicked is sin.
The thoughts of the diligent lead only to abundance, but the hasty only want more.
The gathering of treasures by a lying tongue is a vanity of those who seek death.
The wicked men's robbery will destroy them, because they refuse to use good judgment.
The ways of man are stubborn and strange, but the work of the pure at heart is righteous.
It is better to live in a corner of the housetop, than with a brawling woman in a big house.
The soul of the wicked desires evil, his neighbor finds no favor in his eyes.
When the scorner is punished, the simple are made wise, and when the wise is instructed, he receives knowledge.
The righteous man wisely considers the house of the wicked, but God overthrows the wicked.
Whoever stops listening to the cries of the poor, will also cry and not be heard.
A secret gift pacifies anger, and a reward cools strong anger.
It is joy of the just is justice, but destruction goes to the workers of immorality.
The man who wanders away from understanding will remain in the congregation of the dead.
The man who loves pleasure will be a poor man, the man who loves wine and oil will not be rich.
The wicked will be ransom for the righteous, and the transgressor will be ransom for the honest.
It is better to live in the wilderness, than with an angry argumentative woman.
There is desirable treasure and oil in the home of the wise, but a foolish man spends everything.
The man who follows righteousness and mercy finds life, righteousness, and honor.
A wise man scales the city walls of the mighty, and throws down their confident strongholds.
Whoever holds his tongue keeps trouble away from his soul.
A man who deals in proud anger, will be called a proud and arrogant scorner.
The dull and lazy man's desires kills him, because his hands refuse to work.
The greedy covets all day long, but the righteous gives abundantly.
The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination, and even more so, when he brings it with a wicked mind?
A false witness will perish, but the man who hears speaks constantly.
A wicked man hardens his face, but an honest man directs his way.
There is no wisdom, understanding, or counsel that will prevail against the Lord.
The horse is prepared for the day of battle, but safety is of the Lord.
A good name is preferable to great riches, and loving care is favored more than silver and gold.
The rich and poor meet together, and the Lord made them all.
A prudent man foresees the evil and hides, but the simple keep going and are punished.
Humility and fear of the Lord brings riches, honor, and life.
Thorns and snares cover the path of the stubborn, but the man who keeps his soul will be far from them.
Train a child in the way he should go, and when he is old he will not depart from it.
The rich rules over the poor, and the borrower is a servant to the lender.
A man who sows immorality will reap vanity, and his anger's staff will fail.
A man with a bountiful eye will be blessed, because he gives part of his bread to the poor.
Throw out a scorner and disagreement will leave, and conflict and disrespect will cease to exist.
A man who loves a pure heart, will be the king's friend because of the grace of his lips.
The Lord's eyes preserve knowledge, and he overthrows the transgressor's words.
The dull and lazy man says, "There is a lion outside, and I will be killed in the streets."
The strange woman's mouth is a deep pit, and a man who is abhorred by the Lord will fall into it.
Foolishness is bound in a child's heart, but the staff of correction will drive it far away from him.
The man who oppresses the poor to increase his riches and gives to the rich, will surely come to want.
Bow your head and hear the words of the wise, and apply your heart to my knowledge.
For it is a pleasant thing to keep them inside of you, and they will be on your lips.
I have made this known to you today, so that your trust may be in the Lord.
Have I not written excellent things in counsels and knowledge to you?
So that I could make known to you the certainty of the words of truth, so that you might answer the words of truth to those who sent you?
Do not rob the poor man because he is poor, nor oppress the afflicted at the gate.
Because the Lord will plead their case, and spoil the soul of those who spoiled them.
Do not make friends with an angry man, and do not go with a furious man.
Or you will learn his ways, and your soul will be trapped.
Do not be one of those who shakes hands, or puts up collateral for debts.
If you have no debts to pay, who can take your bed from under you?
Do not remove the ancient landmark, which your fathers set.
Do you see diligent a man in his business? He will stand before kings, and he will not stand before mean men.
When you have dinner with a leader, carefully consider what is placed before you.
Put a knife to your throat, if you are a man with a huge appetite.
Do not desire his delicacies, because they are deceitful foods.
Do not labor to be rich, but be wise enough to restrain yourself.
Will you set your eyes on wealth that disappears? Because riches certainly make wings for themselves, and they fly away like an eagle toward heaven.
Do not eat the bread of someone with an evil eye, nor desire his deli meats.
Because in his heart he is counting everything you eat and drink and he says, "Eat and drink," but his heart is not with you.
Because you will vomit up what you have eaten, and lose your sweet words.
Do not even speak to a fool, because he will despise the wisdom of your words.
Do not remove the old markers that mark the borders of your land, and do not enter the fields of the fatherless.
Because their rescuer is mighty, he will plead their cause with you.
Apply your heart to learning, and listen to the words of knowledge.
Do not withhold the correction of a child, because if you beat him with a rod, he will not die.
You will beat him with the rod, and deliver his soul from hell.
My son, my heart will rejoice if your heart is wise.
Yes, my mind will rejoice when you speak of righteous things.
Do not let your heart envy sinners, but fear the Lord all day long.
For surely the end is coming, and your expectations will not be cut off.
My son, hear me and be wise and guide your heart in the righteous way.
Do not associate with drunkards, or piggish meat eaters.
Because drunkards and gluttony will lead to poverty, and drowsiness will clothe a man in rags.
Listen to your father who fathered you, and do not despise your mother when she is old.
Buy the truth, wisdom, instruction, and understanding and do not sell them.
The father of the righteous will greatly rejoice, and a man that fathers a wise child will rejoice in him.
Your father and mother will be glad, and the woman who gave birth to you will rejoice.
My son, give me your heart, and let your eyes observe my ways.
Because a whore is a deep ditch, and a foreign woman is a narrow pit.
She also lies in wait for her prey, and increases transgressors among men.
Who has sorrow, disagreements, babbling, red eyes, and unceasing wounds for no reason?
It is those who stay late drinking wine, and those who go seeking mixed wine.
Do not look you at the wine when it is red, when it gives his color in the cup, when it moves itself correctly.
Because in the end it bites like a serpent, and stings like an adder.
Your eyes will look at strange women, and your heart will utter perverse things.
Yes, you will be like a man who lies down in the middle of the sea, or a man that lies on the top of a mast.
And you will say, "They struck me and I was not sick, they beat me, and I felt no pain, when will I wake up? And I will look for it again."
Do not be envious of evil men, nor desire to be with them.
Because their heart studies destruction, and their lips speak of mischief.
Through wisdom a house is built, and it is established by understanding.
And its rooms will be filled with precious and pleasant riches by knowledge.
A wise man of knowledge is strong, and his strength only increases.
Because you will make war by wise counsel, and with a multitude of counselors there is safety.
Wisdom is too high for a fool; he does not open his mouth at the gate.
Men who scheme to do evil things will be called mischievous people.
The thought of foolishness is sin, and the scorner is an abomination to men.
If you faint on the day of adversity, your strength is small.
If you refrain from delivering those who are drawn into death, and those who are ready to be killed.

If you say, "Behold we did not know about it!" Does not God who ponders the heart consider it? And does not God who guards your soul know all about it? And will God not render unto each man according to his works?
My son, eat honey and the honeycomb because it is sweet and tastes good.
That's how the knowledge of wisdom will be to your soul. When you have found it, there will be a reward, and your expectations will not be cut off.
O wicked man, do not lay in wait for the righteous man's home, and do not spoil his resting place.
Because a just man falls seven times and rises up again, but the wicked man falls into mischief.
Do not rejoice when your enemy falls, and do not let your heart be glad when he stumbles.
Or else the Lord will be displeased when see it, and he will turn his anger away from him.
Do not worry about evil men, and do not envy the wicked.
Because there will be no reward for the evil man, and the candle of the wicked will be put out.
My son, fear the Lord and the king, and do not associate with the rebellious.
For their disaster will rise up suddenly, and who knows what the ruin of both of them will be?
The wise should also consider these things. Do not show partiality when you judge people.
The people curse the man and nations will abhor the man who says to the wicked, "You are righteous!"
But those who reprimand the wicked, will be delighted and blessed with good things.
An honest answer is like a kiss on his lips.
Prepare your work outside in the field and make sure it is satisfactory to you, then build your house afterwards.
Do not be a witness against your neighbor without cause, and do not deceive and lie to others.
Do not say, "I will do to him what he has done to me, I will repay the man in accordance with his work."
I went by the field of a dull and lazy man, and the vineyard of an ignorant man.
And, lo and behold, it was overgrown over with thorns, and nettles had covered its face, and its stone wall was broke down.
When I looked at and saw it, I received instruction and considered it well.
A little sleep, a little slumber, and a little folding of hands to rest.
That's how your poverty and want come upon you, like an armed man attacks one who travels.
Here are some more of Solomon's proverbs, which the men of King Hezekiah of Judah made copies of.
It is the glory of God to conceal something, and it is the honor of kings to search it out.
The heaven is for height, and the earth is for depth, but the heart of kings is unsearchable.
Skim the dross from the silver, and a bowl of refined silver will come from it.
Remove the wicked from the king's presence, and his throne will be established in righteousness.
Do not stand in the presence of the king, nor in the company of great men.
Because it is better that it is said to you, "Come up here," than it would be for you to be demoted by the prince, even if have seen it with your own eyes.
Do not rush into a struggle, or else you will not know how to end it, after your neighbor has put you to shame.
Debate your cause with your neighbor, without trying to discover each other's secrets.
Or else the one who hears it will put you to shame, and your infamy will never go away.
A superbly spoken word is like a gold apple in a silver setting.
A wise reprimand, is like a gold earring or a fine gold ornament to an obedient ear.
A faithful messenger is like a cold snow at the time of harvest to those who send him, because he refreshes the soul of his masters.
A man who boasts about himself and offers false gifts, is like the clouds and wind without rain.
Through patience a prince can be persuaded, and kind words break bones.
If you have found honey, only eat as much as you need to satisfy yourself, or else you will eat too much and vomit it up.
Leave your neighbor's house, before he grows weary of you and hates you.
A man who bears false witness against his neighbor is like a maul, a sword, or a sharp arrow.
Confidence in an unfaithful man in times of trouble is like a broken tooth, and a sprained foot.
A man who sings songs to a heavy heart, is like a man who removes his garment in cold weather, or like someone mixing vinegar and baking soda.
If your enemy is hungry, give him some bread to eat, and if he is thirsty, give him water to drink.
Because you will pile coals of fire on his head, and the Lord will reward you.
The north wind drives the rain away, so does an angry face and a backbiting tongue.
It is better to live in the corner of the housetop, than with a brawling woman and in a big house.
Good news from a distant country, is like cold water to a thirsty soul.
A righteous man kneeling before the wicked, is like a troubled fountain or a corrupt spring.
It is not good to eat too much honey, or for men to search for their own glory because it is not glory.
The man who has no control over his own spirit, is like a broken down city without walls.
Honor seems like snow in summer, or rain at harvest time to a fool.
Like a wandering bird or a flying swallow, an undeserved curse will never come to an end.
A whip for the horse, a bridle for the donkey, and a staff for the fool's back.
Do not answer a fool's foolishness, or else you will be just like him.
Answer a fool in accordance with his foolishness, or else he will think he is wise in his own conceit.
A man who sends messages through a fool, is like a man who cuts off his own feet and drinks violence.
A parable in a fool's mouth, is like lame legs of different lengths.
Honoring a fool, is like binding a stone in a sling.
A parable in the mouth of a fool, is like a thorn that falls into the hands of a drunkard.
The great God who formed everything, rewards both the fool and the transgressors.
A fool who returns to his foolishness, is like a dog that returns to his vomit.
There is more hope for a fool, than a man who is wise in his own conceit.
The dull and lazy man says, "There is a lion loose in the streets."
A dull and lazy man twists and turns on his bed, like a door that swings on its hinges.
A dull and lazy man conceals his hand, but it grieves him to bring it back to his mouth.
A dull and lazy man is wiser in his own conceit, than seven reasonable men.
A man who passes by, and interferes in someone else's conflict, is like someone who grabs a dog by the ears.
A mad man who throws burning spears, arrows, and death.
is like a man who deceives his neighbor and says, "I was just kidding."
Where there is no wood, the fire goes out, so where there is no gossiper, the conflict ceases.
An argumentative man who likes to kindle conflict, is like coal or wood to a burning fire.
The words of a gossiper are like wounds, and they cut deeply into the deepest parts of the stomach.
Burning lips and a wicked heart, are like a clay pot covered with silver dross.
A man who hates destroys with his lips, and stores deceit within himself.
When he speaks fairly, do not believe him, because there are seven abominations in his heart.
Those who cover hatred with deceit, will have their wickedness exposed before the whole congregation.
Whoever digs a pit will fall into it, and whoever rolls a stone will have it roll over him.
A lying tongue hates those who are afflicted by it, and a flattering mouth brings ruin.
Do no boast about tomorrow, because you do not know what the day may bring.
Do not praise yourself, but let someone else praise you.
A stone is heavy and a load of sand is a heavy burden, but a fool's anger is heavier than both of them.
Anger is cruel and outrageous, but who is able to stand before envy?
Open reprimand is better than secret love.
A friend's wounds are faithful, but an enemy's kisses are deceitful.
The full soul loathes a honeycomb, but to a hungry soul even bitter things taste sweet.
A man who wanders from his place, is like a bird that wanders away from her nest.
Ointment and perfume make the heart rejoice, and a man's loyal friendship counsels the heart.
Do not forsake your friend or your father's friend, and do not go to your brother's house on the day of your disaster, because a close neighbor is better than a distant brother.
My son, be wise and make my heart glad, so that I may answer anyone who disapproves of me.
A prudent man sees the evil coming and hides, but the simple man passes by unaware and is punished.
Take a garment as security for a stranger's debt, and get collateral if it is for a foreign woman.
If a man blesses his friend with a loud voice early in the morning, it will become a curse to him.
An argumentative woman, is like the continuous drip, drip, drip of a very rainy day.
Trying to hide her, is like trying to hide the wind or carry ointment in your right hand, it betrays itself.
Iron sharpens iron, like a man sharpens the appearance of his friend.
Whoever tends the fig tree will eat of its fruit, and a man who waits on his master will be honored.
The way water reflects the face, is like the true heart of a man which is reflected to another man.
Hell and destruction are never satisfied, nor are the eyes of man.
Like gold and silver are refined in the crucible and furnace, so is a man tested by his praise.
Even though you grind a fool with a mortar and pestle among the wheat, his foolishness will not leave him.
Diligently tend to the state of your flocks, and pay close attention to your herds.
Because riches do not last forever, nor does the crown last for every generation.
The hay appears, the tender grass grows, and the mountain herbs are harvested.
Lambs are for clothing, and the goats are the price of the field.
Then you and your household will have enough goats milk for food, and to take care of your young women.
The wicked flee when no one pursues them, but the righteous are as bold as a lion.
Because a land full of transgression has many princes, but an understanding and knowledgeable man will prolong a peaceful state.
A poor man who oppresses the poor is like a flooding rain which leaves no food.
Those who abandon the law praise the wicked, but those who keep the law resist them.
Evil men do not understand justice, but those who seek the Lord understand everything.
It is better to be poor and walk in his honesty, than to be rich and perverse in your ways.
Whoever keeps the law is a wise son, but a man who has unrighteous companions, shames his father.
A man who uses usury and deceitful schemes to increase his wealth, only gathers it for those who pity the poor.
A man who refuses to hear and listen to the law, even his prayers will be an abomination.
Whoever causes the righteous to go astray in an evil way, will fall into their own pit, but honest people will acquire and possess good things.
A rich man is wise in his own conceit, but the poor who understand searches him out.
When righteous men rejoice, there is great glory, but when the wicked rise, a good man hides.
A man who covers his sins will not prosper, but whoever confesses and abandons his sin will have mercy.
A happy man always fears, but a man who hardens his heart will fall into mischief.
A wicked ruler over the poor people, is like a roaring lion or a wandering bear.
A leader who lacks understanding is also a great oppressor, but a man who hates selfish desires will extend his days.
A man who does violence and takes the blood of another person will flee to the pit, and nobody will support him.
Whoever walks upright will be saved, but a man who does perverse things will immediately fall.
A man who tills his land will have plenty of bread, but whoever follows vain people will have more than enough poverty.
A faithful man will have abundant blessings, but a man in a hurry to be rich is not innocent.
To have respect of people is not good, because a man will do anything for a piece of bread.
The man who is in a hurry to be rich has an evil eye, and does not think he will be poor.
The man who reprimands someone will find more favor than one who flatters others.
Whoever robs his father or mother, and says it is not a sin, is the companion of a destroyer.
A man with a proud heart stirs up conflict, but a man who puts his trust in the Lord will be made fat.
A man who trusts own heart is a fool, but whoever walks wisely will be delivered.
A man who gives to the poor will lack nothing, but a man who hides his eyes will have many curses.
Men hide when the wicked rise, but when they perish the righteous increase.
A man who is often blamed becomes stubborn, and he will be destroyed suddenly beyond recovery.
The people rejoice when the righteous are in authority, but they mourn when the wicked rule.
Whoever loves wisdom rejoices over his father, but the man who keeps company with prostitutes wastes his wealth.
The king establishes the land with good judgment, but the man who accepts bribes destroys it.
A man who flatters his neighbor spreads a net to trap his feet.
There is a snare for an evil man in his transgressions, but the righteous sing and rejoice.
The righteous consider the cause of the poor, but the wicked have no regard for them.
Scornful men entrap a city with a snare, but wise men turn anger away.
A wise man has no rest, if he deals with a foolish man, whether he rages or laughs.
The bloodthirsty hate an honest man, but the righteous seek to comfort his soul.
A fool utters everything on his mind, but a wise man remains silent until later.
If a ruler listens to lies, all of his servants will be wicked.
When poor and deceitful men meet together, the Lord enlightens both of their eyes.
The king who faithfully judges the poor, will have his throne established forever.
The staff and blame give wisdom, but a child left to tend to himself shames his mother.
Transgressions increase when the wicked multiply, but the righteous will see their downfall.
If you correct your son, he will give you rest and be a delight to your soul.
People perish when there is no vision, but the man who keeps the law is happy.
A servant can not be corrected by words alone, because even though he understand he will not respond.
There is more hope for a fool, than there is for a man who is hasty with his words.
The man who delicately raises his servant from a child, in the end the servant will become his son.
An angry man stirs up conflict, and a furious man abounds in transgression.
A man's pride will bring him low, but honor will uphold the humble in spirit.
Whoever partners with a thief hates his own soul, he hears cursing and does not condemn it.
A man's fear attracts a snare, but whoever puts his trust in the Lord will be safe.
Many seek the ruler's favor, but the Lord judges everyone.
An unjust man is an abomination to the righteous, but an honest man is an abomination to the wicked.
These are the prophetic words of Jakeh's son Agur who spoke to Ithiel and Ucal.
And he said, "Surely I am more wicked and brutal than any other man, and I lack the understanding of a man.
I have no wisdom, nor do I know anything about the Holy One.

Who can ascend into heaven, or descend from heaven? Who gathers the wind in his fists? Who binds the waters in a garment? Who established all the ends of the earth? What is his name, and what is his son's name? Of course you know!
Every word of God is pure, he is a shield for those who put their trust in him.
Do not add to his words, or else he will blame you, and you will be found to be a liar.
I have required two things of you, do not deny them to me before I die.
Keep vanity and lies far away from me, give me neither poverty nor riches, feed me only with my fair share of food.
Or else I will have too much and deny you and say, 'Who is the Lord?' Or else I may become poor and steal, and take the name of my God in vain.
Do not accuse a servant before his master, or else he will curse you and you will be found guilty.
There is a generation that curses their father, and does not bless their mother.
There is a generation who are pure in their own eyes, and yet their filth remains unwashed.
There is a generation who are lofty in their own eyes! And their eyelids are lifted up.
There is a generation whose teeth are like swords, and their jaw teeth like knives, they devour the poor from the earth, and the needy from among men.
The parasitic leech has two daughters who cry, 'Give, give!' There are three things that are never satisfied, and four that say, 'It is not enough!'
The grave, the barren womb, the earth without water, and the fire that never says, 'It is enough!'
The ravens of the valley will peck out a man's eye who mocks his father and despises to obey his mother, and the young eagles will eat it.
There are three things which are too wonderful for me, and a fourth which I do not know.
The ways of an eagle soaring in the air, a serpent on a rock, a ship in the middle of the ocean, and a man with a maid.
Are the ways of an adulterous woman, who eats and wipes her mouth and says, 'I have done nothing wicked.'
Because three things disturb the earth, but the fourth it cannot withstand.
Because when a servant reigns, and a fool is filled with meat.
When a repulsive woman is married, and a housemaid who is heir to her mistress.
There are four things which are small on the earth, but they are exceedingly wise.
The ants are a weak people, yet they prepare and store their food in the summer.
The rabbits are just a feeble folk, yet make they their houses in the rocks.
The locusts have no king, yet they all swarm together.
The spider can be held in your hand, yet it is still found in kings' palaces.
There are three things which go well, and a fourth which is attractive as it passes by.
A lion is the strongest of the beasts, and does not retreat from anything.
A greyhound, a male goat, and an overpowering king against whom there is no rising up.
If you have foolishly lifted yourself up or thought evil things, put your hand over your mouth.
Surely when you churn milk it makes butter, and the wringing the nose draws blood, like the forced anger creates conflict."
These are words of King Lemuel, and the prophecy that his mother taught him.
And she said, "What must I say my son, what must I say to the son of my womb, and what must I say to the son of my promises?
Do not waste your strength on women, nor your time on things that destroy kings.
O Lemuel, it is not for kings to drink wine, nor for princes to drink strong drink.
Or else they will drink too much and forget the law, and pervert the judgment of anyone afflicted.
Give strong drink to anyone who is ready to perish, and wine to those with a heavy heart.
Let him drink to forget his poverty and his misery.
Open your mouth for the voiceless, and the cause of anyone appointed to destruction.
Open your mouth, judge righteously, and plead the cause of the poor and needy.
Who can find a virtuous woman? Because her price is far above rubies.
Her husband's heart can safely trust in her, and he will need for nothing.
She will do him good and not evil all the days of her life.
She seeks wool and flax, and willingly works with her hands.
She is like the merchant's ship, and she brings her food from far away.
She also rises while it is still night, and gives food to her household, plus a portion to her young women.
She appraises a field and buys it, and with the savings from her work, she plants a vineyard.
She clothes herself with strength, and strengthens her arms.
She knows that her merchandise is good, and her candle does not go out at night.
She puts her hands to the spindle, and her hands hold to the maternal.
She stretches her hand out to the poor, and reaches out to the needy.
She is not afraid for her household when it snows, because her entire household is clothed in scarlet.
She makes tapestry coverings for herself, and her clothing is made of purple silk.
Her husband is known at the city gates, when he sits among the elders of the land.
She makes fine linen and sells it, and delivers belts to the merchant.
Strength and honor are her clothing, and she will rejoice in the future.
She opens her mouth with wisdom, and she speaks of the law of kindness.
She watches over her household, and does not eat the bread of idleness.
Her children rise up and call her blessed, and so does her husband when he praises her.
And says, "Many daughters are virtuous, but you excel them all!"
Favor is deceitful and beauty is vain, but a woman who fears the Lord, will be praised.
Give her of the fruit of her hands, and let her own works praise her at the gates.
These are the teachings of King David's son, who was a wise man in Jerusalem.
The teacher declares, "Everything is meaningless and completely pointless vanity!"
What does a person truly gain from a lifetime of hard work?
Generations come and go, but the earth remains unchanged.
The sun rises and sets, then rushes back to rise again.
The wind blows south, then turns north, swirling endlessly and then returns to where it began.
Rivers flow into the sea, but the sea is never full. They return to where they came from and flow again.
Everything involves much labor, yet words cannot utter it. The eye is never satisfied, and the ear never hears enough.
Things that have happened will happen again, and what's been done will be done again. There's nothing truly new under the sun
Can we ever say, "Look, there is something new!" Because, everything has already existed long before us.
People do not remember the past, and future generations will not remember what happens to us today.
I am a teacher, but I was once the king of Israel in Jerusalem.
I have devoted my heart to seeking wisdom in order to understand everything that happens on earth, God has given this difficult task to humanity.
I have seen everything done under the sun, and they're all meaningless vanity and disheartening.
What is crooked can not be straightened, and anything missing can not be counted.
I have spoken with my own heart and said, "I have achieved greatness and gained more wisdom than anyone before me in Jerusalem. I have deep experience of knowledge and wisdom.
I have pursued wisdom, and also explored madness and foolishness, but I realized that even this is spiritual frustration.
Because the more wisdom you gain, the more grief you feel, and the more knowledge you have, only increases your sorrow."
In my heart I said, "Let me test joy and indulge in pleasure." But even that turned out to be meaningless vanity.
I said, "Laughter is madness, and what does pleasure really accomplish?"
I decided to enjoy wine while keeping wisdom in my heart, avoiding foolishness, to discover what is truly good for the sons of men to do during their lifetime.
I created great projects, I built houses and planted vineyards.
I created gardens and orchards, and I planted every kind of fruit tree.
I built ponds to irrigate the groves of growing trees.
I acquired servants and young women, and even had servants born in my house. I owned more livestock, both large and small, than anyone before me in Jerusalem.
I amassed gold and silver, and rare treasures from kings and provinces. I had male and female singers, plus other delights from the sons of men, and every kind of musical entertainment.
I became greater than anyone in Jerusalem before me, and my wisdom stayed with me.
I did not deny myself anything that my heart desired. I embraced every joy, because my heart rejoiced in all my work, and that was my reward.
But when I looked at everything I had accomplished, it all felt like meaningless vanity and spiritual frustration. Nothing is ever truly profitable under the sun.
I turned to consider wisdom, madness, and folly. What can anyone do who comes after the king? Only what's already been done.
I realized that wisdom is better than foolishness, just as light is better than darkness.
A wise man sees clearly, but a fool stumbles around in the dark. But then I saw that the same fate awaits both of them.
Then in my heart I said, "If the same thing happens to both the fool and me, what's the point of being wise?" That too felt like meaningless vanity.
Because the wise are remembered no more so than the fools. Everything will be forgotten, and the wise die just like the fool.
So I hated life, because everything done under the sun felt like a grievous burden, like my soul was chasing after the wind.
I even hated all the hard labor I had done under the sun, because I knew I would have to leave it to someone coming after me.
Who knows whether he will be a wise or foolish man? Yet he will control everything I worked for and achieved through wisdom. This is also meaningless vanity.
So my heart gave in to despair over all the work I had done under the sun.
Because a man may work with wisdom, knowledge, and skill, but in the end, he will leave everything to someone who didn't earn it. This too is meaningless vanity and extremely unfair.
So what does a man really gain from all the frustrations of his heart and hard work under the sun?
Because his days are filled with sorrow, and all his work brings pain and grief, and even at night his heart finds no rest. This too is meaningless vanity.
Nothing is better for a man than to eat, drink, and enjoy their work. This I realized is also a gift from God.
Because after all, who can truly enjoy life more than I did?

God gives wisdom, knowledge, and joy to those who please him. But he gives the sinner the task of gathering wealth, only to hand it over to those who please God. This too is meaningless vanity, like spiritual frustration.
There is a season for everything, and a time for every purpose under the heavens.
A time to be born, and a time to die, a time to plant, and a time to pick what has been planted.
A time to kill, and a time to heal, a time to tear down, and a time to build up.
A time to weep, and a time to laugh, a time to mourn, and a time to dance.
A time to throw away stones, and a time to gather stones together, a time to embrace, and a time to refrain from embracing.
A time to win, and a time to lose, a time to keep, and a time to throw away.
A time to tear, and a time to sew, a time to be silent, and a time to speak.
A time to love, and a time to hate, a time for war, and a time for peace.
What does it profit a man who labors in his work?
I have seen the labor, which God has laid upon the sons of men to keep them occupied.
He has made everything beautiful in his time, he has also placed the world in their hearts, so that none of them can understand the work that God has done from the beginning to the end.
I know that there is nothing better for them, than to rejoice and do good things in their life.
Everyone should eat, drink, and enjoy the results of their work, because it is God's gift.
Whatever God does lasts forever and nothing can be added to it or taken away from it. God does this so that people will respect him.
What has happened will happen again. What will happen has already happened, and God will restore what has happened in the past.
I have also seen corruption even in places of justice and righteousness.
I thought in my heart, "God will judge both the good and the bad, because there is a time for every action and purpose."
Then I said to myself, "God tests people so they can see that they are no better than animals."
People and animals share the same fate, they will all die. They breathe the same air and humans are not superior to the animals. Because everything is just meaningless vanity.
We all end up in the same place. We come from dust and we return to dust.
Who really knows if the human spirit rises and the animal spirit sinks into the earth?
That's why I have come to believe that the best thing is for people to enjoy their work, because that is their reward. Who can show them what comes after they are gone?

Then I returned and looked again and I saw all the oppression happening under the sun. I saw the tears of the oppressed, and there was no one to comfort them. Power was on the side of their oppressors, but the oppressed had no comforter.
So I praised the dead, who have already died, more than the living, who are still alive.
It is even better for the one who has not been born yet and who has not seen all the evil done under the sun.
I also noticed that all the hard work and skillful effort causes people to envy each other. This too is meaningless vanity and spiritual frustration.
Fools fold their hands and they consume themselves.
It is better to have one handful with peace, than to have two handfuls with hard work while spitirualy frustrated and chasing after the wind.
Then I looked again and saw more futility under the sun.

There is a lonely person all alone, childless, and with no siblings, yet they never stop working. They are never satisfied by wealth, and they never ask, Who am I working for? Why am I depriving myself of enjoyment? This too is just meaningless vanity and a miserable way to live.
Two people are better than one because they get more done working together.
If one falls, the other can help them up. But you should pity anyone who falls and has no one to help them.
Also, if two lie down together, they can stay warm. But how can one stay warm alone?
If someone is attacked, two can stand against them. A cord of three strands is not easily broken.
It is better to be a poor but wise child, rather than an old and foolish king who no longer listens to advice.
Someone may rise from prison to become king, while another born into royalty may end up poor.
I saw every living person under the sun follow the next young leader who comes to take the king's place.
There is no end to the people who came before, and those who come later will not be happy with him either. This too is meaningless vanity and spiritual frustration.
When you go to stand in God's house, be thoughtful and ready to listen rather than offer foolish sacrifices, because people often don't realize they're doing evil.
Don't be quick to speak or make impulsive promises to God, because God is in heaven and you're on earth, so speak sparingly.
Because dreams come from too much business, and foolishness is revealed through too many words.
If you make a promise to God, do not delay in fulfilling it. God does not delight in fools, so you must keep your word.
It is better to not make a promise than to make one and fail to keep it.
Do not let your words lead you into sin, and do not tell the angel that it was a mistake. Why provoke God's anger and risk having all your works destroyed?
Because too many dreams and words lead to many different meaningless vanities. Instead, you should fear God.
If you see injustice and oppression somewhere, do not be surprised, because those who are in power are watched by even higher powers.
The earth produces benefits for everyone, even the king depends on the land.
Those who love silver will never be satisfied with silver, and those who crave wealth will never have enough. This too is meaningless vanity.
As wealth grows, so do the number of people who consume it. So what does it benefit the owner except to watch it disappear?
A laborer sleeps peacefully whether he eats little or a lot, but the wealth of the rich keeps them awake.
I have seen a terrible evil under the sun, and wealth hoarded which caused harm to the owner's.
Sometimes wealth is lost through poor decisions, and when a son is born, there is nothing left to give.
Just as we entered the world naked, we leave it the same way, and we take nothing with us from all our hard work.
This too is the sad truth, we leave life just as we entered it. What do we gain from working so hard for nothing?
Throughout his life, a man lives in darkness, burdened by sorrow, frustration, and illness.
What I have found to be good is to eat, drink, and enjoy the fruits of your labor during the life God gives you, because that is your portion to share.
If God gives someone wealth and the ability to enjoy it, to accept their share, and find joy in their work, that is a gift from God.
Such a person will not dwell much on the days of their life, because God fills their heart with joy.
I have seen an evil under the sun, it is something many people experience.
A man may have wealth, riches, and honor from God, lacking nothing he desires, but God does not allow him to enjoy it, because someone else does. This is meaningless vanity and a tragic misfortune.
Even if a man has a hundred children and lives a long life, if his soul never experiences true happiness and he is not properly buried, I say an unborn child is better off than him.
That child enters life with vanity and departs in darkness, and his name will be forgotten in the darkness.
Because that child's soul has never seen the sun or known anything, but it finds more peace than the man.
Even if he lives two thousand years, without experiencing good, do we not all end up in the same place anyway?
People work hard to feed themselves, yet their hunger is never truly satisfied.
So what advantage does the wise man really have over the fool? What benefit does the poor man gain by knowing how to live with others?
It is better to enjoy what you can see than to chase endless desires. That too is meaningless vanity and spiritual frustration.
What exists has already been named, and it is known that man is limited. No one can deal with anyone stronger than themselves.
The more things there are, the more meaningless vanities there are. So what does it benefit anyone?
So who really knows what is good for a man during his short, vain and shadowy life? Who knows what will happen after he has disappeared from under the sun?
A good reputation is more valuable than a precious perfume, and the day of death is better than the day of one's birth.
It is better to visit a house of mourning than a house of feasting, because death is everyone's destiny, and the living should take it to heart.
Sorrow is better than laughter, because sadness can improve the heart.
The heart of the wise lives in the house of mourning, but fools seek only pleasure.
It is better to hear wise correction than to listen to the songs of fools.
The laughter of fools is like the crackling of thorns under a pot, and this too is just meaningless vanity.
Oppression drives the wise to madness, and bribes corrupt the heart.
The end of something is better than its beginning, and a patient spirit is better than pride.
Do not be quick to anger, because anger lives in the hearts of fools.
Do not ask why the days of the past were better than today, such questions are not wise.
Wisdom, combined with an inheritance, will profit those who see the sun.
Wisdom and money both offer protection, but wisdom gives life to those who possess it.
Consider God's work, who can straighten what he has made crooked?
Celebrate in times of prosperity, but reflect during adversity. God made both, so we can not predict what comes next.
In my vanity filled life, I have seen the righteous die despite their righteousness, and the wicked live a long life in spite of their wickedness.
Do not be excessively righteous or wise, why destroy yourself?
Do not be excessively wicked or foolish, why should you die before your time?
Hold onto both wisdom and caution, because those who fear God will avoid both extremes.
Wisdom makes one stronger than ten powerful leaders in the city.
There is no one on earth that does good, because everyone sins.
Do not pay attention to everything that people say, or you may hear your servant cursing you.
You know in your heart that you have also cursed others.
I tested all this with wisdom, saying, I will be wise, but true wisdom was far from me.
What is distant and exceedingly deep, who can find it?
I devoted myself to understanding wisdom and the reasons behind things, including the wickedness of foolishness, and the madness of man's behavior.
I found that a seductive woman is more bitter than death, her heart is a trap, her hands are chains. Those who please God escape from her, but she catches sinners.
Behold the teacher says, "This is what I have discovered, I have examined things one by one to understand.
I am still searching, but I have not found what I was seeking. I found one honest man among a thousand, but not one honest woman.
This is what I have concluded, God made people honest, but they have pursued many inventions."
Who is as wise as the one who deeply understands things? Wisdom brightens a person's face and softens their expression.
I advise you to obey the king's commands, in order to respect the oath you made before God.
Do not be hasty to walk away, and do not support wrongdoing, because the king does whatever he wants.
Where the king speaks, there is power and authority. Who can question him and say, What are you doing?
Those who keep the commandments will avoid trouble, and a wise man's heart recognizes both the right time and the right way to act.
Everything has a proper time and place, and that's why a man often suffers great misery.
Because no one knows what will happen next, and no one can tell them when it will happen.
No man has the power over the spirit to hold it back, nor can anyone avoid death. There is no escape from that battle, and wickedness will not save those who practice it.
I've seen all this and have thought deeply in my heart about everything that is done under the sun. Sometimes one man rules over another to his own harm.
So I saw wicked people buried, in the holy place where they were praised by the city where they had done wrong. This too is just meaningless vanity.
Because punishment for wrongdoing which is not carried out swiftly, is why men's hearts are fully set on doing evil.
Even if a sinner does evil a hundred times and lives a long life, I know things will go well for those who respect God and live in fear before him.
But things will not go well for the wicked. Their lives will be like shadows, and they will be short lived because they do not fear God.
There is a reality of vanity on earth, that good men sometimes suffer the fate of the wicked, and wicked people sometimes receive the rewards of the righteous. This too is just meaningless vanity!

So I praised joy, because there's nothing better for a man under the sun than to eat, drink, and be merry. Because these things stay with him through the hard work of his life that God gives him under the sun.
I focused my heart and mind on understanding wisdom and seeing all the business done on earth, even of those who never rest day or night.

Then I realized that not one can fully understand all of God's works. Even if a man works hard to try and figure it all out, he will not succeed. And even if a wise man claims to know, they still can not understand it.

I reflected on all of this and realized that the righteous and the wise, and their works are in God's hands. No one knows whether they will experience love or hate, and everything lies ahead of them is unknown.

Everything happens to everyone the same way. The same fate comes to the righteous and the wicked, the good and the bad, those who offer sacrifices and those who do not. The same applies to those who swear oaths and those who fear oaths.
This is an evil reality of everything done under the sun, the same fate comes to everyone. People's hearts are full of evil and madness while they live, and afterward, they join the dead.
Because for anyone still living there is still hope, and a living dog is better off than a dead lion.
The living know they will die, but the dead know nothing. They no longer receive rewards, and their memory is forgotten.
Their love, hate, and envy have also vanished. They no longer share in anything that is done under the sun.
Go your own way and eat your bread with joy and drink your wine with a cheerful heart, because God accepts your works.
Always wear white clothing, and never let your head go without oil.
Enjoy life with the wife you love all the days of your vanity filled life under the sun, that God has given you. Because that is life's portion of all your hard work under the sun.
Whatever your hands find to do, do it with all your strength. In the grave, where you're going, there is no work, planning, knowledge, or wisdom.

When I returned, I saw that under the sun, the race does not always go to the swift, nor the battle to the strong. Bread does not always go to the wise, nor wealth to the intelligent, nor favor to the skilled. But time and chance happens to everyone.
Because a man does not know when his time will come. Like fish caught in a cruel net or birds trapped in a snare, people are caught suddenly in evil times.
I also saw this wisdom under the sun, and I was impressed.
There was a small city with only a few men in it. A powerful king came against it and surrounded it, and built large siege works all around it.
There was a poor but wise man in that city, who saved it with his wisdom. But no one remembers that poor man.
So I said, "Wisdom is better than strength. But the poor man's wisdom is ignored, and his words go unheard.
The quiet words of the wise are better than the shouts of a ruler among fools.
Wisdom is better than weapons of war, but one sinner can destroy much good."
Just as dead flies make a pharmacist's ointment stink, a little foolishness can ruin someone known for wisdom and honor.
A wise man's heart leads him in the right direction, but a fool's heart leads them astray.
Even when a fool walks down the road, his lack of wisdom shows, and he lets everyone know he's a fool.
If a ruler becomes angry with you, do not abandon your post, because yielding will pacify serious offenses.
There is an evil thing I have seen under the sun, like an error that comes from a leader in power.
Foolishness is given great dignity, while the wealthy are placed in low positions.
I have seen servants riding horses and earthly princes walking like servants.
Whoever digs a pit may fall into it, and whoever breaks through a hedge may be bitten by a snake.
Those who move stones may get hurt, and those who chop wood may also be in danger.
If an axe is dull and it is not sharpened, more strength is needed to chop wood, but wisdom is profitable and helps get the job done.
Surely a serpent may bite before it is charmed, and a babbling fool is no better off.
A wise man's words are gracious, but a fool's speech leads to his own downfall.
A fool starts talking nonsense, and ends with mischievous madness.
A fool talks endlessly, no one can tell what he will say next, and no one can tell him what will come after he is gone.
Fools exhaust themselves with their efforts because they do not even know how to get to the city.
O land, woe unto you whose king is an immature child, whose leaders feast in the morning!
O land, blessed are you whose king comes from noble roots and whose leaders eat at the proper time for their strength, and not for drunkenness.
Slothful neglect causes buildings to decay, and laziness lets the houses leak.
Feasts bring laughter, wine brings joy, but money solves everything.
Do not curse the king, even in your thoughts, and do not curse the rich in your bedroom, because a bird might carry your words through the air, and something with wings could spread the news.
Throw your bread across the waters, because you will find it again after many days.
Share a portion with seven or even eight people, because you never know what disaster might strike the earth.
When the clouds are full, they empty their rain on the earth. If a tree falls toward the north or the south, it stays where it lands.
Those who watch the wind will never plant, and those who consider the clouds will never harvest.
Just as you do not understand how the spirit moves or how bones grow in a pregnant woman, you can not comprehend the works of God who makes everything.
Sow your seeds in the morning and keep working into the evening, because you do not know which efforts will succeed, or if they will both turn out well.
Truly, the light is sweet and it is a joy for the eyes to see the sun.
But, even if a man lives for many years and enjoys them all, he must remember that dark days will come, and there will be many of them. Everything that happens is just meaningless vanity.
O young man, celebrate your youth, and let your heart be glad while you are young. Follow your heart and your eyes, but remember, God will judge everything that you do.
So remove sorrow from your heart and avoid evil behavior, because youth and childhood are temporary vanities.
Remember your Creator while you are still young, before the difficult days come and the years arrive when you will say, "I find no pleasure in them."
Before the sun, light, moon, and stars are darkened, and the clouds do not return after the rain.
When the house keepers tremble, strong men stoop over, the people grinding the grain stop because they are so few of them, and those who look through windows see darkness.
When the doors to the street are shut, the sound of grinding grain fades, and people rise in the morning to the chirping of birds, even though all the daughters of music have grown faint.

When people fear heights and dangers along the road, the almond trees will blossom, the grasshopper drags itself along and desire fades, because we are headed to our eternal home, and mourners go about the streets.
Before the silver cord is snapped, the golden bowl is broken, the pitcher is shattered at the fountain, and the wheel is broken at the well.
Then the dust will return to the earth as it was, and the spirit returns to God who gave it.
And the teacher says, "Everything is meaningless vanity, this too is just completely meaningless vanity, like chasing the wind!"
The teacher was wise and taught the people knowledge. He carefully listened, studied, and arranged many proverbs.
He searched for just the right words, and every word he wrote was honest and true.
Wise words given by one shepherd, are as sharp as nails and a guiding light firmly fixed by skilled teachers.
Furthermore my child be warned, there is no end to the making of endless books, and too much study can wear you out.
Here is the conclusion of the whole matter, fear God and keep his commandments, this is man's whole duty.
Because God will judge every deed, whether they are good or evil, including everything that is hidden.
The Song of Songs, written by Solomon.
Let him kiss me with kisses from his lips, for your love intoxicates more than wine.
Your fragrant oils are rich and delightful, your name spills forth like perfume, no wonder women love you.
Draw me close to you, and we shall run together. The king has brought me into his chambers. We will rejoice in you, and delight in your love more than wine. Truly, you are loved.
O daughters of Jerusalem, I am dark-skinned but beautiful, like the tents of Kedar and Solomon's silken curtains.
Do not stare at me because of my sun-kissed skin. My mother's sons were angry with me, they made me tend their vineyards, while my own was neglected.
Tell me my heart's desire, where do you graze your flock and let them rest at noon. Why must I wander around like a stranger among your companions?
If you do not know, fairest of women, follow the tracks of the sheep and graze your young goats near the shepherds' tents.
My Love, I compare you to a graceful mare among Pharaoh's chariots.
Your cheeks shine with rows of jewels, your neck is adorned with golden chains.
We will make gold ornaments for you, inlaid with silver.
While the king relaxes at his table, my perfume releases its fragrance.
My beloved is like a sachet of myrrh resting between my breasts throughout the night.
My beloved is like a cluster of blossoms from the vineyards of En-Gedi.
My Love, how beautiful you are, your eyes are like doves.
My beloved, how handsome and delightful you are! Our bed is lush with green.
The beams of our house are cedar, and our rafters are made of fir.
I am the rose of Sharon and the lily of the valleys.
My love among the daughters is like a lily among thorns.
My beloved among the sons is like an apple tree among the forest. I sat in his shade with great joy and delight, and his fruit was sweet to my taste.
He brought me to the banquet hall, and he laid his banner of love over me.
Refresh me with jugs of wine and comfort me with apples, for I am lovesick.
His left hand is under my head, and his right hand embraces me.
O daughters of Jerusalem, I charge you by the gazelles and the does of the field, do not stir up nor awaken my love until it pleases you.
Listen! The voice of my beloved comes leaping over the mountains, and skipping across the hills.
My beloved is like a gazelle or a young deer. Behold, he stands behind our wall, gazing through the windows, peering through the lattice.
My beloved spoke to me and said, "Rise up, my love, my fair and beautiful one, and come away with me."
Since the winter has passed and the rain is over and finished.
The flowers appear on the earth, the season of singing birds has come, and the voice of the turtledove is heard in our land.
