The fig tree puts out its green fruit, and the tender grapevines blossom with fragrance. Arise, my love, beautiful and fair one, and come away with me.
O my dove, hiding in the clefts of the rock, in the secret places of the cliffs, let me see your face and hear your voice. For your voice is sweet, and the expression on your face is beautiful.
Catch the little foxes that ruin the vineyards for us, because our vineyards are in bloom.
My beloved is mine and I am his, and he feeds among the lilies.
Before the day breaks and the shadows flee, my beloved turns to me and becomes like a gazelle or a young stag on Mount Bether.
At night, I searched for the one my soul loves while lying in bed. I looked for him, but did not find him.
I will rise now and walk through the city streets and wide avenues, and I will seek the one that my soul loves. I searched for him, but could not find him.
The watchmen patrolling the city found me, and I asked them, "Have you seen the one whom my soul loves?"
Soon after I passed them, I found the one my soul loves. I held him and would not let him go until I brought him to my mother's house, into the room where she conceived me.
O daughters of Jerusalem, I charge you by the gazelles and the does of the field, do not awaken my love until he desires it.
Who is this coming from the wilderness like columns of smoke, perfumed with frankincense and myrrh, with all the fragrant powders of the merchant?
Look at Solomon's bed, it is surrounded by sixty courageous men, who are the mighty warriors of Israel.
They all carry swords and are well trained in warfare, they are ready for any danger at night with their swords at their sides.
King Solomon made himself a carriage with the wood from Lebanon.
He made its columns from silver and its base is gold, its seat is upholstered in purple, its interior lovingly crafted by the daughters of Jerusalem.
O daughters of Zion, go out and see King Solomon wearing the crown with which his mother crowned him with on the day of his wedding, on the day that his heart rejoiced.
Behold my love, you are fair and beautiful. Your eyes are like doves, and your hair is like a flock of sheep resting on Mount Gilead.
Your teeth are like freshly shorn sheep which are coming up from the washing, each one bearing twins and none of them are barren.
Your lips are like a scarlet thread, and your words are charming. Your temples resemble pieces of pomegranate behind your veil.
Your neck is like the Tower of David, built as an armory and adorned with a thousand shields, all belonging to mighty warriors.
Your breasts are like twin fawns, young gazelles which feed among the lilies.
Until the day breaks and shadows flee, I will go to the mountain of myrrh and the hill of frankincense.
My love, you are completely fair and beautiful and you have no flaws.
My bride, come with me from Lebanon, and we will look out from the lions' dens, the peaks of Mount Amana, Mount Shenir, Mount Hermon, and the leopard mountains.
You have captured my heart, my sister, my bride. You have ravished my heart with your eyes, with one chain around your neck I am undone.
How delightful is your love, my sister, my bride! Your love is better than wine, and your perfume is more fragrant than all the other spices!
O my spouse, honey drips from your lips. Milk and honey are under your tongue, and your clothes have the scent of Lebanon.
My sister, my bride, you are a locked garden, a sealed spring, and a hidden fountain.
Your garden is an orchard of pomegranates and delightful fruits, with henna and spikenard.
Spikenard and saffron, calamus and cinnamon, with all kinds of frankincense, myrrh, and aloes, along with all the finest spice.
You are a garden fountain, a well of fresh water, flowing streams from Lebanon.
O north wind, awaken! Come, south wind, and blow on my garden so that its fragrance may spread. Let my beloved come into his garden and enjoy his pleasant fruits.

I have entered my garden, my sister, my bride. I have gathered my myrrh with my spices, eaten my honeycomb with my honey, and I have drunk my wine with my milk. O friends, eat and drink deeply my beloved.

I was asleep, but my heart was awake. It was the voice of my beloved knocking, saying, "Open up to me my sister, my love, my dove, my flawless one. My head is drenched with dew, and my hair is damp from the dew of the night."
I have taken off my coat, how can I put it back on? I have washed my feet, so how could I dirty them again?
My beloved put his hand through the open the door, and my heart was stirred for him.
I rose to open for my beloved, and my hands and fingers dripped onto the handles of the lock with my fragrant sweet smelling myrrh.
I opened up for my beloved, but he turned away and was gone. My heart sank when he spoke. I searched for him but could not find him. I called out, but he did not answer.
The watchmen who patrolled the city found me. They struck me and wounded me. The guards at the wall stole my veil.
O daughters of Jerusalem, if you find my beloved, please tell him that I am lovesick.
What makes your beloved better than any other, you are most beautiful among women? What makes your beloved more special than another beloved, that you would ask us this?
My beloved is radiant white and ruddy, outstanding among ten thousand.
His head is purest gold, and his hair is wavy and black like a raven.
His eyes are like the doves beside streams of water, washed in milk and perfectly set.
His cheeks are like a bed of spices, like sweet smelling flowers. His lips are like lilies, dripping with sweet smelling myrrh.
His hands are like gold rings set with beryl jewels. His stomach is as polished as polished ivory adorned with sapphires.
His legs are like pillars of marble set on bases of fine gold. His appearance is as majestic as Lebanon, and as stately as cedars.
His mouth is most sweet, he is altogether lovely. O daughters of Jerusalem, this is my beloved and my friend.
O most fair and beautiful among women, where has your beloved gone? Which way did he turn so we can help you search for him?
My beloved has gone down to his garden, to the beds of spices, to feed in the gardens and gather lilies.
I belong to my beloved, and he belongs to me, he feeds among the lilies.
O my love, you are as beautiful as Tirzah, and as attractive and lovely as Jerusalem, like a majestic army with banners.
Turn your eyes away from me, because they overwhelm me. Your hair flows like a flock of goats descending from Mount Gilead.
Your teeth are like a flock of sheep coming up from the washing, each one bears twins, and there are none barren among them.
Your temples behind your veil are like a piece of pomegranate.
There are sixty queens, eighty concubines, and countless young virgin women.
But my dove, my one and only flawless one is her mother's only daughter, the favorite of the one who bore her. The daughters saw her and blessed her, and the queens and concubines praised her.
Who is this who shines like the morning dawn, as fair and beautiful as the moon, as radiant as the sun, and as majestic as an army with banners?
I went down to the garden of nut trees to see the fruits of the valley, and to see if the vine had budded and the pomegranates were blooming.
Before I realized it, my desires had made me like the royal chariots of Amminadab.
O Shulamite, return, return to me! Return so that we may gaze at you. What will you see in the Shulamite? It is as if she were a dance between two armies?
O prince's daughter, how beautiful are your feet in sandals! The curves of your thighs are like jewels, crafted by a master craftsman.
Your navel is like a rounded goblet that never lacks liquor. Your belly is like a mound of wheat surrounded by lilies.
Your breasts are like twin young gazelles that are perfectly matched.
Your neck is like a tower of ivory, and your eyes are like the pools in Heshbon by the gate of Bath-rabbim. Your nose is like the tower of Lebanon which overlooks Damascus.
Your head is like a crown on Mount Carmel, and your flowing hair is royal purple, and the king is captivated by its beauty.
O my love, how fair and pleasant you are with your charming delights!
Your figure is like a palm tree, and your breasts are like clusters of grapes.
I said, I will climb the palm tree and take hold of its branches. May your breasts be like grape clusters, and the scent of your breath like apples.
May your mouth taste like the finest wine, flowing smoothly to my beloved, gently making the lips of those sleep to speak.
I belong to my beloved, and his desire is for me.
Come my beloved, let us go out into the countryside and spend the night in the villages.
Let us rise up early and go to the vineyards to see if the vines are flourishing, or if the tender grapes have appeared, and the pomegranates are in bloom. That's where I will give you my love.
O my beloved, the mandrakes give off their fragrance, and I have saved all kinds of new and old delightful fruits at our doorway for you.
O if only you were like my brother, who nursed at my mother's breast! Then I could kiss you in public without shame.
I would lead you into my mother's house, and she would teach me. I would entice you spiced wine from my pomegranates.
His left hand is under my head, and his right hand embraces me.
O daughters of Jerusalem, I ask you not awaken or stir up love my until it is ready.
Who is this that is coming up from the wilderness, leaning on her beloved? I awakened you under the apple tree, where your mother gave birth to you, there where she brought you into the world.
Place me like a seal over your heart, like a seal on your arm. because love is as strong as death, and jealousy as cruele as the grave. The coals of its flames are fiery and intense.
Many waters cannot quench love, nor can floods drown it. If man gave all he owned for love, it would be completely rejected.
We have a little sister with no breasts. What should we do for her when she is spoken for?
If she is a wall, we will build a silver tower on her. If she is a door, we will enclose her with cedar panels.
I am a wall, and my breasts are like towers, then I became the one in whom his eyes found favor.
Solomon had a vineyard at Baal-hamon. He leased it to the vintners, and each was to bring a thousand pieces of silver for its fruit.
My vineyard is mine to tend. But you, Solomon, may have your thousand, and the two hundred who guard its fruit.
You who dwell in the gardens, your companions listen for your voice, so let me hear it also.
Come quickly, my beloved, like a gazelle or a young stag on the mountains of spices.
This is the vision of what Amoz's son Isaiah saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, all kings of Judah.
O heaven and earth, listen and pay attention because the Lord has spoken and this is what he said, "I have raised and cared for children, but they have rebelled against me.
The ox knows its owner, and the donkey knows its master's crib, but Israel does not know me, and my people do not understand."

O sinful nation! Your people are weighed down with immorality, your descendants are evildoers, with dishonest and corrupt children. They have abandoned and turned their backs on the Lord and provoked the Holy One of Israel!
Why should you continue to suffer? You rebel more and more, your whole head is sick, and your heart is weak.
From the soles of your feet to the top of your head, there is nothing substantial, there are only wounds and bruises. But there are open sores, uncleaned, unbandaged, and untreated with ointment.
Your land is desolate, your cities have been burned, and foreigners devour your fields in your presence. It has been overthrown by outsiders and it has become a desolate wasteland, .
The Daughter of Zion has been left like an abandoned cottage in a vineyard, like a deserted lodge in a garden of cucumbers, or a city under siege.
If the Lord of Hosts had not left us a very small remnant, we would have become just like Sodom and Gomorrah.
O rulers of Sodom and people of Gomorrah, listen and hear our Lord God's words and laws.
Our Lord God said, "Why are you making sacrifices to me?, I am overflowing with burnt offerings of rams and the fat from well fed animals. I do not delight in the blood of bulls, lambs, or goats.
When you come to appear before me, who has required you to come walking into my courts?
Stop bringing me vain and meaningless offerings. I detest the Sabbaths, incense, new moons, convocations, and I cannot endure your sinful assemblies.
My soul hates your new moon festivals and appointed feasts. They have become a burden to me. I am tired of carrying them.
When you lift up your hands in prayer, I will hide my eyes from you. Even if you offer many prayers, I will not listen because your hands are covered with blood.
Wash yourselves and be clean. Remove your evil deeds from my sight. Stop doing evil things.
Learn to do what is good. Seek justice, help the oppressed, defend the fatherless, and plead for the widows."

This is what the Lord says, "Let us come together now and be reasonable with each other! Even though your sins are like scarlet and they are as red as crimson, they will be made as white as snow, and they will be washed as white as wool.
If you are willing and obedient, you will eat from the good things of the land.
But if you refuse and rebel, you will be devoured by the sword, because the Lord has spoken.
How has this faithful city become such a prostitute! It was once full of justice, and righteousness lived there, but now it is filled with murderers.
Your silver has become worthless, and your wine is diluted with water.
Your leaders are rebels and the companions of thieves, they all love bribes and chase after rewards. They do not defend the fatherless, and the widow's cause never enters their thoughts.
Therefore, the Lord of Hosts, the Mighty One of Israel declares, 'Ah, I will ease my mind of my enemies, and I will avenge myself of them.
I will turn my hand against you and thoroughly purge your impurities, and I will remove all of your tin.
I will restore your judges and your counselors as they were in the beginning. Then you will be called the righteous and faithful city again.'
Zion will be rescued with justice, and her repentant converts will be saved with righteousness.
But rebels and sinners will all be altogether destroyed, and those who abandon the Lord will perish.
Because you will be ashamed of the sacred oaks that you desired, and confused because of the gardens you have chosen.
For you will be like an oak whose leaves wither, and a garden without water.
The strong will become as fragile as thread, their work will be the spark, and both of them will burn together, and no one will extinguish the fire."
This is the prophecy that Amoz's son Isaiah received about Judah and Jerusalem.
In the last days, the Lord's temple will be established at the highest point, exalted above all mountains, and all nations will flow to it.

Many people will say, "Come, let us go up into the Lord's mountain, to the house of the God of Jacob. He will teach us his ways, and we will follow him." For the law will come from Zion, and the Lord's word will come from Jerusalem.

He will judge between nations and settle disputes among many people. They will beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks. Nation will no longer rise up against nation, nor will they learn war anymore.
O House of Jacob, come and let us walk in the Lord's light.

O Lord God, you have abandoned your people, because they replenish themselves from the eastern countries, they are soothsayers like the Philistines, and they pleasure themselves with foreigner's children.
Their land is filled with gold and silver, and there is no end to their treasures. Their land is full of horses and they have countless chariots.
Their land is full of idols, and they worship what they have made with their own hands.
And mean men bow down and great men humble themselves, so do not forgive them.
Enter into the rock and hide in the dust, for the fear of the Lord and the glory of his majesty.
A prideful man will be humbled, arrogance will be brought down, and the Lord alone will be exalted on that day.
Because the Day of the Lord of Hosts will be for everyone who is proud and arrogant, and they will be brought down.
And it will be for all the tall cedars of Lebanon and the mighty oaks of Bashan.
And for all the high hills and mountains.
And for every high tower and fortified wall.
And for all the ships of Tarshish and every beautiful picture.
Man's pride will be humbled, their arrogance will be brought low, and the Lord alone will be exalted on that day.
The idols will be completely destroyed.
People will flee to caves in the rocks and holes in the ground, for fear of the Lord and the glory of his majesty, when he rises to shake the earth.
On that day, people will throw the gold and silver idols that they made to worship, into the caves with moles and bats.
They will hide in the rocky clefts and the ragged cliffs because of fear of the Lord and the glory of his majesty, when he rises to shake the earth.
Stop trusting men, who breathe through their nostrils, for how is he really held accountable?
Behold, the Lord of Hosts is removing every source of support, for both food and water from Jerusalem and Judah.
He is taking away the mighty men, the warriors, the judge, the prophet, the wise, and elderly.
Also the captain of fifty, the honorable man, the advisor, the skilled craftsman, and the eloquent speaker.
And God said, "I will appoint children as their leaders, and babies will rule over them."
And the people will oppress each other, everyone will turn against his neighbor. The youth will behave arrogantly toward the ancient ones, and the lowly will be against the honorable.
When a man grabs his brother in his father's house and says, "You have clothes, you be our leader, and take control of this ruined mess!"
But the brother will protest and say, "I am not a healer. I have no food or clothing in my house. Do not make me the people's leader."
Jerusalem is in ruins and Judah has fallen, because their words and actions defy the Lord, and provoke his glorious presence.
Their very appearance testifies against them. They openly declare their sin like Sodom, and they do not even try to hide it. Woe unto them, because they have rewarded themselves with evil!
Tell the righteous that all will go well for them, because they will enjoy the fruits of their actions.
But woe unto the wicked! Things will go badly for them, because their just rewards will be given to them.
My people are oppressed by children, and ruled by women. Oh my people, your leaders mislead you and destroy your paths.
The Lord stands up to plead his case, and he stands to judge his people.
The Lord will judge against the ancient ones, and the leaders of his people. Because you have devoured the vineyard, and the spoils of the poor is in your homes.
The Lord God of Hosts says, "What are you doing, why are you crushing my people and grinding the poor people's faces?"

Besides that the Lord says, "Because the daughters of Zion are arrogant, they walk with their heads held high, seducing men with their eyes, walking with dainty steps, and wearing tinkling bells on their feet."
That's why the Lord will afflict the heads of the daughters of Zion with scabs, and expose their secret parts.
In those days, the Lord will take away the bravery of their fine jewelry, the anklets, headbands, and crescent moon ornaments.
Their chains, bracelets, and veils.
Their bonnets, leg ornaments, headbands, tablets, and earrings.
Their rings and nose jewels.
Their changeable robes, cloaks, necklaces, and shawls.
Their mirrors, fine linen, hoods, and veils.

Instead of a sweet fragrance there will be a stench, instead of a belt there will be a a rope, instead of styled hair there will be a baldness, instead of fine clothing there will be a sackcloth and instead of beauty there will be burning.
Your men and mighty warriors, will fall in battle by the sword.
Her gates will mourn and grieve, and she will sit desolate on the ground.
In those days, seven women will approach one man and say, "We will provide our own food and clothing, if you will just let us use your name to remove our shame."
At that time, the Lord's branch will be beautiful and glorious, and the land's fruit will be excellent and appealing for the survivors in Israel.
And it will come to pass, that whoever remains in Zion or Jerusalem will be called holy, and everyone who is recorded among the living in Jerusalem.
When the Lord washes away the filth of the daughters of Zion, and purged Jerusalem's bloodstained hands from within by the spirit of judgment and burning fire.
Then the Lord will create a cloud of smoke by day and a glowing column of fire by night over every dwelling on Mount Zion, and over all her places of assembly. The Lord's glory will be their defense.
There will be a tabernacle to provide shade from the heat during the day, as a place of refuge and a safe haven from the storms and the rain.
Now I will sing a song for my beloved about his vineyard. My much loved one has a vineyard on a very fertile hill.
He fenced it in, cleared its stones, planted the finest vines in it, built a tower in the middle of it, and made a winepress. He thought it would produce good grapes, but it only yielded wild ones.
So now, people of Jerusalem and men of Judah, I pray you will judge between me and my vineyard.
What more could I have done, that I have not already done for my vineyard? Why then, when I thought it would produce good grapes, did it only produce wild grapes?
Now let me tell you what I am going do to my vineyard. I am going to remove its hedges, and it will be devoured, and I will break down its walls, and it will be trampled down.
I will lay waste to it. It will not be pruned or cultivated, briers and thorns will grow there, and I will command the clouds not to rain on it.

The vineyard of the Lord of Hosts is the House of Israel, and the people of Judah are his pleasant plants. He looked for justice, but saw oppression; he looked for righteousness, but only heard cries.
Woe unto those who join house to house and field to field until there is no room left, and they live alone in the land.
I heard the Lord of Hosts and he said, "Surely many houses will be desolate, even the large and beautiful ones will be unoccupied.
Ten acres of vineyard will only yield one bath of wine, and a homer of seed will produce just one ephah."
Woe unto those who rise early to chase strong drink and stay up late, until they are inflamed by wine.
They have harps, lyres, tambourines, flutes, and wine at their feasts, but they ignore the Lord's work and they do not consider the things he does.
Therefore, my people have gone into exile because they have no knowledge. Their honorable men are starving, and the masses are parched with thirst.
So hell has enlarged herself and opened her mouth wide, and their glory, the crowds, and those who rejoice will descend into it.
The mean man will be humbled, the mighty will be brought low, and the eyes of the proud will look down.
But the Lord of Hosts' judgement will be glorified, and the Holy God will be sanctified in righteousness.
Then lambs will graze as they please, and strangers will eat among the wasteland of the rich.
Woe unto those who drag immorality with ropes of vanity and sin as if they were pulling a cart.
They say, "Let him make haste and do his work, so that we can see it! Let the Holy One of Israel's plan come quickly, so that we may know what it is!"
Woe unto those who call evil good and good evil, who turn darkness into light and light into darkness, who make bitter taste sweet and sweet taste bitter.
Woe unto those who are wise in their own eyes and prudent in their own sight.
Woe unto those who are mighty wine drinkers, and strong men who mix strong drinks.
They justify the guilty for a bribe, and remove righteousness from the righteous.

Therefore, just as fire consumes straw and flames burn up the chaff, their roots will rot and their blossoms will blow away like dust, because they have rejected the Lord of Hosts' law, and despised the Holy One of Israel's word.

So the Lord's anger was kindled against his people. He has stretched out his hand against them and defeated them. The mountains trembled, and their corpses lay rotting in the streets. But his anger has not subsided, and his outstretched hand is still raised.
He will raise a flag for distant nations, and whistle for them from the ends of the earth. And they will come very swiftly.
No one will grow tired or stumble, and no one will sleep or slumber. Their belts will not loosen, and their shoe strings will not break.
Their arrows are sharp, and all their bows are ready. Their horses' hooves are like flint, and their chariot wheels are like a whirlwind.
They roar like young lions, seize their prey to carry it safely away, and no one can save it.
In those days, they will roar over it like the roaring ocean. If someone looks to the land, there will only be darkness and distress, even the light is darkened in the heavens.
In the year that King Uzziah died, I saw the Lord seated on a high exalted throne, and the train of his robe filled the temple.
The seraphim stood above the Lord's throne, and each one had six wings, they covered his face with two wings, they covered his feet with two wings, and he flew with two of them.
They called out to one another and said, "Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of Hosts, and the whole earth is filled with his glory."
The doorposts shook at the sound of their voices, and the temple was filled with smoke.
Then I said, "Woe unto me! I am ruined, because I am a man with unclean lips, and I live among people with unclean lips. My eyes have seen the king, the Lord of Hosts."
Then one of the seraphim flew up to me with a live coal in his hand, which he had taken from the altar with tongs.
He touched it to my mouth and said, "Look, this has touched your lips, your immorality is taken away, and your sins have been purged."
Then I heard the voice of the Lord say, "Who will I send, and who will go for us?" Then I said, "Here I am Lord, send me!"
He said, "Go to these people and say, 'You hear and see, but you do not understand what I want you to hear and see.'

Your words will harden their hearts, and they will not be able to see, hear, or understand what I want them to see, hear, and understand. If they could, they would understand with their hearts, then they would turn to me, and be healed.'"
Then I asked, "How long will it last Lord?" And he replied, "Until the cities are wasted and uninhabited, the houses are deserted, and the land becomes completely desolate."
The Lord will send people far away, and the land will be abandoned.

But a tenth of the population will remain, and it will be burned again, like a teil or an oak tree loose their leaves, and their stump is left in the ground after it is cut down. And the holy seed will be its stump.

During the days of Ahaz son of Jotham and grandson of King Uzziah of Judah, King Rezin of Syria, and King Pekah of Israel son of Remaliah, marched toward Jerusalem to wage war, but they failed to conquer it.
The house of David was informed and they said, "Syria has allied with Ephraim," and the people's hearts trembled like trees swaying in the wind.
Then the Lord said to Isaiah, "Take your son Shearjashub, and go meet Ahaz at the end of the aqueduct of the upper pool, on the road to the launderer's field."
Say to him, "Stay calm and do not fear or lose heart because of the fierce anger of Rezin, Syria, and the son of Remaliah, they are like smoldering sticks."
Because Syria, Ephraim, and Remaliah's son have plotted evil against you.
They are saying, "Let us attack Judah, break through its defenses, and appoint the son of Tabeal as king in its midst."
But this is what the Lord God says, "It will not succeed; it will not happen."
The capital of Syria is Damascus, and Damascus is led by Rezin. Within sixty-five years, Ephraim will be shattered and they will no longer be a people.
The capital of Ephraim is Samaria, and Samaria is led by Remaliah's son. If you do not stand firm and believe, then you will not stand at all.
The Lord spoke to Ahaz again and said,
"Ask your Lord God for a sign, whether from the depths below or the heights above."
But Ahaz replied, "I will not ask, nor will I test the Lord."
Then Isaiah said, "Listen now, O house of David! It is no small thing to try the patience of men, but must you also try the patience of my God?"
Therefore, the Lord himself will give you a sign, behold a virgin will conceive and give birth to a son, and they will call him Immanuel.
He will eat butter and honey so that he may learn to reject evil and choose good.
Before the boy knows how to reject evil and choose good, the land you dread will be deserted by both of its kings.
The Lord will bring down on you, your people, and your father's house a time unlike any since Ephraim separated from Judah, and even the king of Assyria.
In those days the Lord will summon flies from the furthest Egyptian rivers, and bees from the land of Assyria.
They will come and settle in the rock crevices of the desolate valleys, and on every thorn and all the bushes.
On that day, the Lord will use a razor, hired by the Assyrian king from beyond the river, to shave your head, feet, and even your beard.
And in those days a man will nourish a young cow and two sheep.
Because of the abundance of milk they produce, he will eat butter. Everyone left in the land will eat butter and honey.
And in those days every place which once had a thousand vines worth a thousand silver coins will be overrun with briers and thorns.
People will go there with bows and arrows because the land will be covered in briers and thorns.
And you will no longer go to the hills which were once cultivated with a hoe for the fear of the briers and thorns. Instead, they will be used for grazing oxen and sheep.
Then the Lord said to me, "Take a large scroll and write on it with a pen about Mahershalalhashbaz."
So I chose two faithful witnesses, Priest Uriah and Jeberechiah's son Zechariah to record it.
I went to the prophetess, and she conceived and gave birth to a son. Then the Lord said to me, "Name him Mahershalalhashbaz."
Before the child knows how to say, 'My father' or 'My mother', the wealth of Damascus and the spoils of Samaria will be carried off by the Assyrian king.
Then the Lord spoke to me again.
And he said, "Since these people reject the gentle waters of Shiloah and rejoice in Rezin and Remaliah's son.

Therefore, the Lord will bring the mighty floodwaters of the Euphrates River against the many strong, including the Assyrian king and all his glory. It will overflow its channels and flood its banks."
He will sweep through Judah, flooding everything, it will even reach up to their neck. His outstretched wings will cover your entire land, O Immanuel.
O you nations, you can join together, but you will be shattered. Listen, all you distant countries, you can prepare yourselves, but you will be broken into pieces.
You can plan your strategies together, but they will fail. Speak your words, but they will not stand, because God is with us.
For the Lord has spoken to me with a strong hand and warned me not to walk in the ways of these people.
Do not say "Everything is a conspiracy," like they do! And do not be afraid of the things that they fear.
But, sanctify the Lord of Hosts as holy, and let him be your fear and dread.
He will be a sanctuary, but also a stumbling stone and a rock of offense to both the houses of Israel, a trap and a snare to the people of Jerusalem.
Many among them will stumble and fall, and they will be broken, caught, and captured.
Preserve the testimony and seal the law among my disciples.
I will wait on the Lord, who hides his face from the house of Jacob, but I will still look for him.
Behold, me and the children that the Lord has given me, are signs and wonders in Israel from the Lord of Hosts, who lives on Mount Zion.

When people say to you, "Go consult with those who have familiar spirits, and wizards who whisper and mutter," you must remember that those people should be seeking their God! Should the living consult the dead?
Look to the law and the testimony. If their speech does not agree with these words, it is because there is no light in them.
They will wander through the land, distressed and hungry. And it will come to pass, that when they are hungry and worried, they will curse their king and their God and look upward.
Then, they will look to the earth and see only trouble, darkness, and gloomy anguish, and they will be driven into darkness.

Nevertheless, the gloomy dimness will not be like it was in her frustration, when he first humbled and afflicted the land of Zebulun and Naphtali. Or later when he brought deeper suffering to Galilee of the nations, in the region by the sea, beyond the Jordan River.
The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light, and those living in the land of the shadow of death, have had the light shined on them.
You have expanded the nation and you will increase its joy. They rejoice before you as people do at harvest time, like warriors do when they divide their spoils.
For you have broken the yoke that burdened them, the staff across their shoulders, and their oppressor's rod, just as you did on the day of Midian.
For every warrior is confused by noise in battle, but every bloodstained garment will be burned as fuel in the fire.
For a child is born to us, a son is given to us, and the government will rest on his shoulders. He will be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, and the Prince of Peace.

The growth of his government and peace will never end. He will reign on David's throne and over his kingdom, establishing it with justice and righteousness from now until forever. The zeal of the Lord of Hosts will accomplish this.
The Lord sent a prophetic message to Jacob, and it has fallen upon Israel.
And all the people will know, including Ephraim and the residents of Samaria, who speak with pride and arrogance.
When they say, "The bricks have fallen, but we will rebuild with carved stone. The sycamore trees were cut down, but we will replace them with cedars."
Therefore, the Lord will raise up Rezin's enemies against him and unite his foes.
The Syrians from the east and Philistines from the west will devour Israel with open mouths. Yet even then, his anger will not be turned away, and his outstretched hand is still raised.
But the people did not return to the one who defeated them, nor did they seek the Lord of Hosts.
So the Lord will cut Israel off from both head and tail, palm branch and reed, in one single day.
The ancient and honorable leaders are the head, and the prophets who teach lies are the tail.
For the leaders of these people will mislead them, and those who follow them will be destroyed.

That's why the Lord takes no joy in their young men and shows no mercy to their fatherless orphans and widows. Because everyone is a hypocrite and an evildoer, and every mouth speaks foolishness. Yet his anger is not turned away, and his outstretched hand is still raised.
Because wickedness burns like fire, and consumes briers and thorns, igniting the forest, which sends thick, dark, smoky clouds upward.
Through the wrath of the Lord of Hosts, the land is darkened. People are like fuel for the fire, no one spares even his brother.
They snatch food from the right hand but remain hungry;, and they eat from the left hand but they are still not satisfied. In the end, they will eat the flesh from their own arm.
Manasseh attacks Ephraim, Ephraim attacks Manasseh, and together they turn against Judah. Yet even then, his anger will not be turned away, but his outstretched hand is still raised.
Woe unto those who issue unrighteous decrees and prescribe oppressive and grievous written regulations.
They deny justice to the needy and take away the rights of the poor among my people, making widows their prey and they rob the fatherless orphans.
What will you do on the day the Lord visits, when destruction comes from afar? Where will you flee for help, and where will you leave your glorious pride?
Without me, they will bow down below the prisoners, and they fall among the slain. Yet even then, his anger will not not subside, but his outstretched hand remains raised up.
O Assyrian, you are the staff of my anger, and the staff in your hand is my indignant wrath.
I will send him against a hypocritical deceitful nation, against the people of my fury. I will command him to take the spoils, capture the prey, and trample them down like mud in the streets.
However, he does not intend to do this, nor does his heart think to plan it, but the goal of his heart is to destroy and eliminate many nations.
For he says, "Aren't all my princes kings?"
Is not Calno like Carchemish? Is not Hamath like Arpad? Is not Samaria like Damascus?
My hand has conquered kingdoms filled with idols, whose carved images surpassed those of Jerusalem and Samaria.
Should I not treat Jerusalem and her idols the same way I treated Samaria and her idols?
So, when the Lord finishes his work on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, he will punish the arrogant heart of the Assyrian king and his proud highfalutin looks.
For he says, "I did this with my own strength and wisdom, because I am clever. I removed national boundaries, looted their treasuries, and subdued their people like a mighty and courageous warrior."
My hand has found the people's riches like gathering eggs from a bird's nest. I gathered the whole earth like abandoned eggs, without one flapped wing, opened mouth, or bird peep.

Should the axe boast over the one who swings it, or will the saw magnify itself over the one who uses it? That would be like a staff lifting itself up against the one holding it, as if it is not just a piece of wood.
Therefore, the Lord of Hosts will send a wasting hunger disease among his well-fed fat ones, and under his glory he will kindle a burning fire like a consuming blaze.
The Light of Israel will become a fire, and his Holy One a flame. And it will burn and consume his thorns and briers in one single day.
His forests and fertile lands will be destroyed, both physically and spiritually, they will be like a defeated flag bearer collapsing in defeat.
The remaining trees in his forest will be so few that a child could count them.
In those days, Israel's survivors and those who escaped from Jacob's house will never again rely on the one who defeated them, but they will truly rely on the Lord, the Holy One of Israel.
Then the remnant of what remains of Jacob, will return to the mighty God.
Even though Israel's people are as numerous as the sands of the sea, only a small remnant will return. The destruction has been decreed and will overflow with righteousness.
For the Lord God of Hosts will carry out the destruction that he has determined throughout the land.
Therefore, this is what the Lord God of Hosts says: "O my people living in Zion, do not be afraid of the Assyrian, he will defeat you with a rod and lift his staff against you as Egypt did,
But soon, my indignation will end, and my anger will be directed toward their destruction."
The Lord of Hosts will raise a scourge against him, as he did when Midian was slaughtered at the rock of Oreb. And he will lift his staff over the sea, just as he did in Egypt.
And it will come to pass in those days, that his burden will be lifted from your shoulders, and his yoke will be taken from your neck. Then the yoke will be broken because of the anointing.
He has come to Aiath, passed through Migron, and stored his carriages and supplies in Michmash.
They have crossed the over the passage and camped at Geba. Ramah is afraid, and Gibeah of Saul has fled.
O daughter of Gallim, cry out, "Poor Anathoth," and let it be heard in Laish!
Madmenah has fled, and the people of Gebim are also fleeing.
On that day he will stop at Nob and shake his fist at Mount Zion, the hill of Jerusalem.
Behold, the Lord of Hosts will chop off the branches with terrifying power. The tall and the proud will be brought low, and the arrogant will be humbled.
He will cut down the forest thickets with an iron axe, and mighty Lebanon will fall.
A staff will grow out of a stem from Jesse's stump, and a branch will grow from his roots.
The Lord's Spirit will rest on him, a spirit of wisdom and understanding, a spirit of mighty counsel and strength, and a spirit of knowledge and reverence for the Lord.
He will be quick to understand the fear of the Lord. He will not judge by appearances, nor blame the accused based on hearsay.

Instead, he will judge the poor with righteousness, and blame with equality for the earth's meek and humble. He will strike the earth with the staff of his mouth, and destroy the wicked with the breath of his lips.
Righteousness will be the belt around his waist, and faithfulness will be the sash around his mind.
The wolf and the lamb will live together, the leopard will lie down with the kid goat, the calf, the lion, and the fattened animal will be together, and a little child will lead them.
The cow and the bear will graze side by side, their young ones will lie down together, and the lion will eat straw like the ox.
Infants will play near the asp's den, and toddlers will put his hand into a viper's nest without being harmed.
There will be no harm or destruction on my holy mountain, because the earth will be filled with the Lord's knowledge, like the waters that cover the oceans.
In those days, the root of Jesse will stand like a flag for the people. The Gentiles will seek him, and his resting place will be glorious.
Then once again, the Lord will reach out his hand to reclaim what is left of his people from Assyria, Egypt, Pathros, Cush, Elam, Shinar, Hamath, and the ocean's islands.
He will raise a flag for the nations and gather the outcasts of Israel. He will bring all the scattered people of Judah together from the four corners of the earth.
Ephraim's envy will end, and Judah's enemies will be cut off. Ephraim will not envy Judah, and Judah will not oppose Ephraim.
Together, they will swoop down on the Philistines to the west, plunder the people of the east, and take control of Edom and Moab. And the Ammonites will obey them.

The Lord will completely destroy and dry up the gulf of the Egyptian sea. With his mighty wind, he will shake his hand over the Euphrates River, and break it into seven streams, so people will be able to cross over on dry ground.
There will be a highway for what remains of his people from Assyria, just as there was for Israel when they came up from Egypt.
In those days you will say, "O Lord, I praise you! Even though you were angry with me, your anger has passed, and now you comfort me."
Behold! God is my salvation. I will trust and not be afraid, for the Lord God is my strength and my song, he has also become my salvation.
So, you will draw water from the wells of salvation with joy.
In those days you will say, "Praise the Lord! Call on his name. Declare what he has done among the people and proclaim that his name is glorified."
Sing to the Lord, for he has done glorious things, let this be known throughout all the earth.
O people of Zion, shout and cry out for joy, because the great and Holy One of Israel lives among you!
This is the prophetic burden of Babylon, which Amoz's son Isaiah saw.
Raise a banner high up on the mountain, shout loudly to them, wave your hand and shake your fist, so that they may enter the nobles' gates.
I have summoned my sanctified ones, and I have also called my mighty warriors to carry out my wrath, even those who rejoice in my greatness.

Listen to the noise of the crowds up on the mountains, it is like a vast number of people! It is a tumultuous noise of the kingdoms and nations gathering together, because the Lord of Hosts is preparing an army for the battle.
They come from distant lands, from the farthest reaches of the heavens. Even the Lord is there with his weapons of indignation, to destroy the entire land.
Cry out, because the Day of the Lord is here, and it will come as destruction from the Almighty.
Because of this, every man's hand will be weak, and every man's heart will melt.
They will be terrified, pain and anguish will grip them. They will writhe in pain like a woman in labor, they will stare at one another in shock, and their faces will be as red as a flame.
Behold, the Day of the Lord is coming, cruel with both harsh anger and fierce fury, and he will desolate the land to annihilate its sinners.
For the stars of heaven and its constellations will not shine, the sun will be darkened when it rises, and the moon will not give its light.
I will punish the world for its evil and the wicked for their sins. I will put an end to the arrogance of the proud, and humble the pride of the ruthlessly arrogant.
I will make a man more precious than pure gold, rarer than the gold of Ophir.
Therefore, I will shake the heavens, and the earth will tremble from her place at the wrath of the Lord of Hosts on the day of his fierce anger.
It will be like a hunted gazelle or sheep with no one to shepherd them. Each man will return to his own people and flee to his own land.
Whoever is found will be pierced through, and everyone with them will fall by the sword.
Their children will be smashed to pieces before their very eyes, their houses will be looted, and their wives ravished.
Behold, I will stir up the Medes against them, because they care nothing for silver and take no pleasure in gold.
Their bows will shatter the young men to pieces, and they will show no mercy to infants, nor will they spare the children.
Babylon, the glory of kingdoms, and the proud Chaldeans will be overthrown like God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah.
It will never be inhabited again, and no one will live there for generations. Arabs will not pitch tents there, and shepherds will not rest their flocks.
But wild animals will settle there, and its houses will be filled with howling creatures. Owls will dwell there, and serpents will dance there.
Wild beasts of the islands and dragons will howl in their desolate houses and her luxurious mansions. Her time is near, and her days will not be prolonged.
Because, the Lord will show mercy to Jacob and will once again choose Israel. He will settle them in their own land, and foreigners will join them and be loyal to the house of Jacob.

The people will welcome them and bring them home. The House of Israel will possess them in the Lord's land as servants and maids. They will take captive those who once held them captive and they will rule over their oppressors.
And it will come to pass on the day that the Lord gives you rest from your sorrows, your fear, and the harsh bondage you were forced to endure.
That you will recite this proverb against the king of Babylon and say, "How the oppressor and the golden city have ceased!
The Lord has broken the staff of the wicked and the rulers' scepter.
He struck down nations in anger with his constant pounding. He ruled the nations in anger, and no one stopped his persecution.
Now the whole earth is at rest with peace and quiet, and the people suddenly broke out into singing.
Even the fir trees and the cedars of Lebanon rejoice over you and say, 'Since you've been laid low, no one comes to cut us down.'
The underworld stirs beneath to greet you at your arrival. It awakens the dead, all the leaders of the earth, and raises the kings from their thrones.
They will all speak to you and say, 'Have you become weak like us? Are you like one of us now?'
Your pride is brought down to the grave, along with the sound of your harps. Maggots spread out beneath you, and worms cover you.
O Lucifer, son of the morning, how you have fallen from heaven! You who have weakened the nations has been cast down to the ground.
You said in your heart, 'I will ascend to heaven, I will raise my throne above the stars of God, and I will sit on the assembly mount in the far north.
I will climb above the clouds, and I will be like the Most High.'
But you will be brought down to the underworld, to the depths of the pit.
Those who see you will stare at you, ponder, and say, 'Is this the man who made the earth tremble and shook kingdoms?'
Who turned the world into a wasteland, destroyed its cities, and refused to release his prisoners?
All the kings of the nations lie in glory, each in his own house.

But you have been thrown out of your grave like a rejected branch, or like the clothing of those who were slain, pierced by the sword, and thrown down to the stones in the pit, like a trampled corpse.
You will not be buried with them, because you have destroyed your land and killed your people. The descendants of evildoers will never be honored.
Prepare to slaughter his children for the sins of their fathers, so that they do not rise, nor inherit the land or fill the world with cities."
For the Lord of Hosts declares, "I will rise against them, and wipe out Babylon's name, survivors, descendants, son and nephews."
And the Lord of Hosts says, "I will turn it into a place for owls and swamps, and I will sweep it with the broom of destruction,"
The Lord of Hosts has sworn and said, "It will be just as I have planned, and it will stand just as I have purposed it.
I will crush the Assyrians in my land and trample them on my mountains. Their yoke will be removed from my people, and their burden will be lifted from their shoulders.
This is the plan determined for the whole earth, and this is the hand stretched out over all nations."
The Lord of Hosts has planned it, so who can stop it? His hand is stretched out, and who can turn it back?
This prophetic message came in the year King Ahaz died.
O Philistine, do not rejoice because the rod that struck you is broken. Because the viper will come from the serpent's root, and its fruit will be a flying fiery serpent.
The poor will eat, and the needy will rest in safety. But I will kill your root with famine, and your survivors will be slain.
O gate and city, wail and cry out! All of Philistine has been dissolved. Smoke comes from the north, and no one is alone at their appointed time.
This is what the answer will be to the messengers of the nation? The Lord has established Zion, and his poor people will find refuge there.
This is the prophecy of Moab. At night Ar of Moab was destroyed and silenced, Kir of Moab was also devastated and silenced.
So he went up to the high places in Bajith and Dibon to mourn. Moab will cry over Nebo and Medeba, and they will all shave their heads, and every beard will be cut off.
They will wear sackcloth in the streets, and everyone will loudly cry out and weep deeply on the rooftops, and in the public squares.
Heshbon and Elealeh will cry out, their voices will be heard as far away as Jahaz. Because of this, Moab's warriors will cry out, and his life will be filled with sorrow.
My heart cries for Moab, its refugees will flee to Zoar. A three year old heifer weeps and climbs toward Luhith, while cries of destruction rise up from Horonaim.
Nimrim's waters will dry up, because the grass has died and withered away, and nothing green remains.
So the wealth they have gathered and stored will be carried away to the Brook of Willows.
The cries of Moab echo all around its borders, and the howling reaches Eglaim and Beerelim.
The waters of Dimon will be filled with blood, because I will bring even more disaster on Dimon, lions will attack those who escape from Moab and those who remain in the land.
Send the lamb to the ruler who rules from Sela to the wilderness to Mount Zion's daughter.
Because like a bird that is thrown out of its nest, the daughters of Moab will be stranded at the fjords of Arnon.
Offer advice, execute justice, make your shadow as dark as night at noon. Hide the outcasts, and do not expose those who wander.

Let my outcasts stay with you, Moab. Be a refuge for them and protect them from the destroyer. Because the extortionist is gone, the destruction has ended, and the invaders have been removed from the land.
A throne will be established through mercy, and he will sit on it faithfully in David's tabernacle, judging righteously, seeking justice, and hastily doing what is righteous.
We have heard of Moab's pride, how very proud and arrogant he is with his boasting, and his anger. But his lies will not stand.
Therefore, Moab will mourn for Moab. Everyone will grieve, because you will all weep for the foundations of Kirhareseth, because they have been struck down.

The Heshbon fields are withering, and Sibmah's vines are dying, because the heathen's rulers have destroyed its finest plants. They have reached all the way to Jazer, they wandered through the wilderness, and spread across the sea.
So I will weep for the Sibmah vines like Jazer does. I will drench Heshbon and Elealeh with my tears, because the joyful shouting over your summer fruits and harvest has ended.
Joy and happiness have left the fertile fields. No one sings or shouts in the vineyards. No one treads grapes in the winepresses, and I have silenced the harvest celebrations.
Therefore, my heart mourns for Moab like a harp, and my soul grieves for Kirharesh.
And it will come to pass, when Moab appears exhausted in the high places, he will go to its sanctuary to pray, but he will not succeed.
This is the word that the Lord spoke about Moab a long time ago.
But now the Lord says, "Within three years, like the term of a hired worker, Moab's glory will be condemned. Its great population will dwindle, and what remains will be small and feeble."
This prophecy is about the burden od Damascus. Behold, Damascus is no longer a city, it has become a pile of ruins.
The towns of Aroer are abandoned, they will be home to flocks that lie will down without fear.
"Ephraim's fortress will disappear, and Damascus will lose its kingdom. What is left of Syria will be like the fading glory of Israel," says the Lord of Hosts.
"In those days it will come to pass, that Jacob's glory will fade, and his body will grow thin.
It will be like a farmer harvesting the wheat, reaping wheat heads with his arm, like one collecting grain in the Valley of Rephaim."
Yet, a few grapes will be left for gleaning, like olives left after shaking the tree, two or three on the highest branches, and four or five on the outer limbs," says the Lord God of Israel.
On that day, a man will turn to his Creator and show respect to the Holy One of Israel.
He will not look to the altars he built or honor the things he has made, nor the Asherah poles. or the carved images.
In those days his strong cities will be like abandoned branches, left behind because of the Israelites, and there will be desolation.
Because you have forgotten the God who saves you, and ignored the rock who gives you strength. So you will plant beautiful gardens and fill them with strange seeds.
You will make your plants grow and your seeds flourish in the morning, but the harvest will pile of nothing on the day of grief and desperate sorrow.
Woe unto the crowds of many people, who roar like the sea, and to the rushing of nations, surging like mighty waters!
The nations will rush like rushing floodwaters, but God will rebuke them, and they will flee far away, blown like the mountain chaff, or rolling tumbleweeds before the wind.
And in the evening, there will be trouble, and before the morning comes, they will be gone. This is the fate of those who plunder and rob us.
Woe unto the land under the shadow of wings, located beyond the rivers of Ethiopia.

A nation that sends ambassadors across the ocean in boats made of woven reeds and says, "Go, swift messengers, to a nation scattered and stripped, to a people feared from ancient times until now, a nation measured and trampled down, whose land the rivers have spoiled."
All you worldly people who live on the earth, listen to him when he raises up a flag on the mountains and a trumpet is blown.
Because this is what the Lord said to me, "I will rest and ponder from my home, like the shimmering sunlit heat on the plants, or a cloud of dew in the heat of harvest."
For before the harvest, when the blossoms are perfect and the sour grapes are ripening, he will cut off the green shoots with pruning hooks and remove the branches.
They will all be left together for the mountain birds and wild animals of the earth. The birds will spend the summer on them, and the beasts will spend the winter there.

At that time, gifts will be brought to the Lord of Hosts from a people scattered and stripped, from a nation feared since ancient times, a people measured and oppressed, whose land the rivers have ruined, to a place named for the Lord of Hosts, Mount Zion.
This prophecy is about the burden of Egypt. Behold, the Lord will come to Egypt, riding a swift cloud, and the Egyptian idols will tremble before him, and the heart of Egypt will melt within them.
"And I will stir up Egyptians against each other. They will fight their own brothers, neighbor against neighbor, city against city, and kingdom against kingdom.
The spirit of Egypt will fail within its midst, and I will destroy its wise advice. They will turn to idols, sorcerers, mediums with familiar spirits, and wizards for answers.
I will hand the Egyptians over to a harsh master, and a fierce king will rule over them," says the Lord of Hosts.
And the oceans' waters will dry up, and the river will be parched and it will dry up.
They will divert the rivers to far away, the protective canals will dry up, and the reeds and rushes will wither.
The plants along the banks, by the mouth of the river, and everything sown by the waters will wither, dry up, be blown away, and disappear.
Fishermen will mourn, and all those who cast hooks into the river in the morning will mourn, and those who spread nets over the waters will waste away.
Besides that, those who work with fine flax and weave cloth will be confused.
All those who build dams and ponds for fish will be broken and lose hope.
The leaders of Zoan are fools. Pharaoh's wise advisers will become wicked and brutal and give foolish advice. How can you say to Pharaoh, "I am a son of the wise, and of ancient kings"?
Where are your wise men now? Let them tell you what the Lord of Hosts has planned for Egypt.
The leaders of Zoan are fools, and the leaders of Noph are deceived. They have seduced Egypt, even the cornerstones of its tribes.
The Lord has mixed a perverse spirit into the middle of Egypt. They have made Egypt stumble in everything it does, like a drunk man staggers in his own vomit.
There will be no work for Egypt, nothing that the head or tail, palm branch or rush, can do.
In those days, Egypt will be like frightened fearful women. They will tremble in fear, because of the Lord's hand which he will shake over them.
The land of Judah will terrify Egypt. Whenever anyone mentions it, they will be afraid because of what the Lord of Hosts has planned against them.
In those days, five Egyptian cities will speak the language of Canaan and swear allegiance to the Lord of Hosts. One of them will be called the City of Destruction.
In those days, there will be an altar to the Lord in the heart of Egypt, and a monument to the Lord at its border.
It will be a sign and a witness to the Lord of Hosts in Egypt. Because they will cry out to the Lord because of their oppression, and he will send them a savior, and a powerful one to rescue them.
In those days, the Lord will reveal himself to Egypt, and they will know the Lord. They will worship with sacrifices and donations. They will make a promise to the Lord and fulfill it.
The Lord will defeat Egypt, but he will also heal it. And they will turn to the Lord, and he will respond to their pleas and heal them.
In those days, there will be a highway from Egypt to Assyria. The Assyrians will come to Egypt, and the Egyptians will go to Assyria, and they will serve and worship together.
In those days, Israel will be a third partner with Egypt and Assyria, a blessing in the midst of the land.
The Lord of Hosts will bless them and say, "Blessed be my people of Egypt, Assyria the work of my hands, and Israel my inheritance."
The year that Tartan arrived in Ashdod, when he was sent by King Sargon of Assyria, he attacked the city and captured it.

At that same time, the Lord spoke through Amoz's son Isaiah and said, "Remove the sackcloth from your waist and take off your shoes." So Isaiah did as he was told, and he walked around naked and barefoot.
Then the Lord said, "Just as my servant Isaiah has walked naked and barefoot for three years as a sign and warning to Egypt and Ethiopia,
The Assyrian king will lead the young and old Egyptians and Ethiopians away as prisoners and captives, naked and barefoot with their buttocks exposed to shame all of Egypt.
The people will be afraid and ashamed because they trusted in Ethiopia and took pride in Egypt's glory.
And in those days, the people living on this island will say, 'Behold, this was our hope, where we fled for help to escape the king of Assyria. So how can we escape now?'"
This prophecy is about the burden of the desert by the sea. Just as southern whirlwinds sweep through, so it comes from the terrible desert land.
A disturbing vision has been revealed to me, the betrayer continues to deal treacherously, and the destroyers destroy. O Elam, go and lay siege! O Media, I will put an end to all the groaning.
I am filled with anguish, sharp pains hold to me like a woman in labor. I bowed over when I heard it, and I was stunned by what I saw.
My heart beats fast, and fear overwhelms me. My night of pleasure has turned into fear.
Prepare the table, stand watch at the watchtower, eat, drink, and rise up you leaders, and prepare your shields.
Because this is what the Lord said to me, "Appoint a watchman, and let him report what he sees."
What he saw was a chariot with a pair of horsemen, one with donkeys and another with camels. He listened carefully and paid close attention.
Then the watchman cried out, "My Lord, I see a lion!" I stand guard on the watchtower all day, and stay by my post all night.
Behold, a chariot with men and horsemen is coming. And he said, "Babylon has fallen! All her carved idols lay broken on the ground."
O my people, are crushed like grain on a threshing floor, and now I declare to you what I have heard from the Lord of Hosts, the God of Israel.
This a prophecy about the burden of Dumah. He calls out to me from Seir and says, "Watchman, what remains of the night and how much longer will it last?"
The watchman replied and said, "Morning is coming, but night will return. If you want answers, ask again, then come back."
This prophecy is about the burden of Arabia. You travelers from Dedanim will camp in the forests of Arabia.
The people of Tema brought water to the thirsty and offered bread to those who fled.
Because they fled from the drawn swords, the bent bow, and the horrors of war.
Because the Lord spoke to me about this and said, "Within a year, as it is counted by a hired servant, Kedar's glory will fail."
And there will be few of Kedar's skilled archers left, because the Lord God of Israel has spoken.
This is the prophecy about the Valley of Vision. What ails you now, that makes everyone rush up to the rooftops?
You were a chaotic city filled with joyous noise, and your people were not killed by the sword or in battle.
All your leaders fled together, and they were captured by archers. Everyone found were caught and taken prisoner, even those who fled far away.
So I said, "Leave me alone, and I will weep bitterly. Do not try to comfort me over the destruction of my people."
For the Lord God of Hosts declares it to be a day of trouble, confusion, and collapse in the Valley of Vision, a day of tearing down walls and crying out to the mountains.
Elam carried a quiver and came with chariots and horsemen, and Kir uncovered their shields.
And it will come to pass, that your best valleys will be filled with chariots, and horsemen will be arrayed at the gates.
And Judah's defenses were exposed, and you looked to the armor in the House of the Forest.
You saw the many breaches in the walls of the City of David and collected water from the lower pool.
You counted the houses of Jerusalem and tore some down to strengthen the wall.
You built a trench between the two walls for the water of the old pool, but you did not look to its maker nor consider the one who built it long ago.
In those days, the Lord God of Hosts called for weeping, mourning, shaving heads, and wearing sackcloth.
But instead, there was joy and celebration, slaughtering oxen and sheep, eating meat and drinking wine, saying, "Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die."
The Lord God of Hosts revealed this to me and said, "This sin will never be forgiven until you die!"
This is what the Lord God of Hosts says, "Go to Shebna, the palace treasurer, and speak to him.
And say to him, 'What are you doing here, and who gave you permission to carve a tomb high up into the rock for yourself here?'"
Behold, the Lord will take you away into harsh captivity, and he will completely surround you.
He will toss and turn you like a ball into a vast country. There you will die, and your splendid chariots will become a disgrace to your master's house.
I will drive you away from your position, and you will be brought down from your stately office.
And it will come to pass in those days, that I will summon my servant Eliakim son of Hilkiah.
And I will clothe him with your robe, strengthen him with your belt, and entrust your government with him. He will be like a father to the people of Jerusalem and Judah.
I will place the key of the house of David on his shoulder. So that what he opens, no one can shut, and what he shuts, no one can open.
I will fasten him like a nail in a secure place, and he will become a glorious throne for his father's house.
All the honor of his father's house will hang on him, including its descendants and all of its small vessels, from bowls to jars.
In those days the Lord of Hosts says, "The nail fastened in a secure place will be removed. It will break and fall, and its burden will be cut off." The Lord has spoken.

This prophecy is about the burden of Tyre, O ships of Tarshish, mourn because the city is destroyed, no homes remain, and there is no way to enter into it. News has reached them from the land of Cyprus.
Be still, all you people of the island, you who cross over the ocean and were enriched by the merchants of Sidon.
The Nile's waters brought seed from Egypt, and that harvest of the river was Tyre's income. She was a marketplace for many nations.
Sidon, you should be ashamed because the ocean speaks, and its mighty voice says, "I do not labor nor give birth to children. And I do not nurture young men nor raise young virgins."
When Egypt hears the report about Tyre, they will be very distressed.
Travel to Tarshish and cry out, you island dwellers.
Is this your once joyful city, whose history dates back to ancient times? Her own feet will carry her on a journey far away.
Who planned this downfall of Tyre, the crown city, whose merchants were like princes, and whose traders were honorable throughout the earth?
The Lord of Hosts planned it, to humble the pride of all glory, and to disgrace the honorable ones of the earth.
O daughter of Tarshish, roam through your land like a river, for your strength is gone.
God stretched out his hand over the ocean and shook the kingdoms. The Lord has commanded the destruction of the merchant city of Tyre's strongholds.
He said, "O oppressed virgin of Sidon, you will no longer rejoice. So go to Cyprus, but even there you will find no rest."
Behold the land of the Chaldeans, these people did not exist until the Assyrian built it for those living in the wilderness. They raised up its towers and palaces, then he brought it to ruin.
O ships of Tarshish, mourn because your fortress is destroyed.
In those days, Tyre will be forgotten for seventy years, the lifespan of one king. But after that, songs will be sung about Tyre, like those sung about Tyre the prostitute.
Pick up a harp and walk through the city, you forgotten prostitute. Play sweet music and sing many songs so that people will remember you.
And after seventy years, it will come to pass that the Lord will visit Tyre. And she will return to her trade and fornicate herself with all the kingdoms of the world.

Her profits and earnings will be dedicated to the Lord, and her treasure will not be stored or hoarded. Because her merchandise will be used by those who live for the Lord, for them to have sufficient food and durable clothing.
Behold, the Lord is making the earth empty and desolate. He turns it upside down and scatters its people abroad.
Everyone will be affected, people and priests, servants and masters, maids and mistresses, buyers and sellers, lenders and borrowers, those who charge interest and those who pay it.
The land will be completely emptied and ruined, because the Lord has spoken.
The earth mourns and fades away, the world languishes and wastes away. The arrogant people of the earth are languishing too.
The earth is polluted by its inhabitants, because they have broken the laws, changed the legal decrees, and violated the eternal everlasting covenant.
Therefore, a curse has consumed the earth, and its people are left desolate. The earth's inhabitants are burned, and only a few men remain.
The new wine dries up, the vine withers, and those who were joyful now sigh.
The merry sounds of tambourines has stopped, the celebration ends, and the harp's music is silenced.
People no longer sing while drinking wine. Strong drink tastes bitter to those who consume it.
The city of chaos is destroyed, every house is closed shut, and no one can enter.
People cry out for wine in the streets. Joy has darkened, and happiness across the land is gone.
Only devastation remains in the city, and the gate has collapsed in ruins.
This is how it will be among the people of the land, it will be like shaking an olive tree or picking the last grapes after the harvest.
They will raise their voices and sing for the Lord's majesty. They will shout it from across the oceans.
So glorify the Lord in the fires, and praise the name of the Lord God of Israel in the ocean's islands.

From the furthest parts of the earth we hear songs of praise and glory for the righteous. But I said, "I am wasting away! I am becoming lean! Treacherous traitors have betrayed, yes, they have dealt treacherous betrayal."
Fear, traps, and snares await you people of the earth.

And it will come to pass, that anyone who flees from the sound of fear will fall into the pit. If they climb out, they will be caught in a snare. Because the windows of heaven are open, and the earth's foundations are shaking.
The earth is completely shattered, dissolved, split apart, and violently shaken.
The earth staggers back and forth like a drunk and sways like a laborer's cottage in the wind. Its sin weighs heavily on it, and it will fall, never to rise again.
And in those days it will come to pass, that the Lord will punish the powerful ones in the heavens above, and the kings of the earth below.
They will be rounded up like prisoners in a pit, confined to prison, and after many days they will be visited.
The moon will be confused, and the sun will be ashamed, when the Lord of Hosts reigns gloriously before his ancient ones, in Jerusalem and on Mount Zion.
O Lord, you are my God. I will glorify you and praise your name, because you have done wonderful things. Your ancient counsel is faithful and true.
For you have turned a city into pile of rubble, a fortified city into ruins. The palace of strangers is no longer a city, and it will never be rebuilt.
Because of this, strong nations glorify you, and cities of terrible nations will fear you.

You have been strength for the poor, strength for the needy in their distress, a refuge from the storm, and shade from the heat when the fury of the ruthless ones is like a storm beating against a wall.
You silence the uproar of strangers like the heat in a dry land. Just as a cloud gives shade from the heat, you bring down the pride of ruthless people.
On this mountain, the Lord of Hosts will prepare a feast for all people, a feast of rich fat food full of marrow, and well-aged fine wines.
On this mountain, he will destroy the darkness that hides all people, and the veil which covers all nations.
He will victoriously swallow up death forever. The Lord God will wipe away every tear from every face, and remove his people's punishment from the earth, because the Lord has spoken.
And in those days it will be said, "Look! This is our God, we have waited for him, and he will save us. This is the Lord, we have trusted in him, and we will rejoice in his salvation."
Because the Lord's hand will rest on this mountain, and Moab will be crushed under him like straw is trampled in a manure pile.
He will stretch out his hands in their midst like a swimmer spreads his hands to swim, but the Lord will bring down their pride along with everything they have accomplished.
He will bring down their high fortified walls, lay them low and level them, like the dust on the ground.
In those days, this song will be sung in the land of Judah: "We have a strong city, God will appoint salvation for its walls and defenses.
Open the gates so that the righteous nation, which remains truthful may enter.
You will keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is steadfast, because he trusts in you.
Trust in the Lord forever, because the Lord God is a strong everlasting rock.
He brings down those who live in the proud lofty city, he lays it low, all the way to the ground, and reduces it to dust.
The poor and the needy will trample it underfoot.
The way of the righteous is honest, O you Most High, weigh the path of justice.
Yes, O Lord, we have waited for you, the desire of our soul longs for your name and remembrance.
With my soul I have desired you in the night, with my spirit within me I seek you early, because when your judgments are in the earth, the people of the world learn righteousness.
Even though grace is shown to the wicked, they do not learn righteousness. In a land of honesty, they will deal unjustly and fail to see the Lord's majesty.
Lord, when your hand is lifted up, they do not see it. But they will see and be ashamed of their envy toward your people, and the fire of your enemies will consume them.
Lord, you will establish peace for us, because everything we have accomplished was done by you.
O Lord our God, other masters besides you have ruled over us, but we will only honor your name alone.
They are dead and will never live, they are deceased and will not rise. So you have punished them, destroyed them, and erased all memory of them.
O Lord, you have increased the nation, and you are glorified. You have removed it far away to the ends of the earth.
Lord, in times of trouble they visited you, they poured out a prayer when you disciplined them.
We were like a pregnant woman nearly ready to give birth, who cried out in pain before you, O Lord.
We were pregnant, we writhed in pain, but we only gave birth to wind. We have not brought salvation to the earth, nor have the people of the world fallen.

Your dead will live, together with my dead body they will rise. Those of you who dwell in the dust, wake up and sing! Because your dew is like the morning dew, and the earth will bring forth her dead.
Come, my people, enter your rooms and shut the doors behind you. You must hide for a little while until the wrath has passed.
For behold, the Lord is coming out of his dwelling to punish the earth's inhabitants for their sins. The earth will reveal her bloodstained ground, and she will no longer conceal her slain."
In those days, the Lord will punish Leviathan the piercing serpent, and he will kill the sea great dragon with his powerful sword.
In those days, sing to her of a vineyard of red wine.
I, the Lord protect it. I water it constantly. I guard it day and night to prevent it from being hurt.
I am not angry. But if anyone were to challenge me with thorns and briers in battle, I would burn them all.
Let him take hold of my strength, so that he may make peace with me, and he will make peace with me.
Jacob's descendants will take root. Israel will blossom and flourish, and fill the world with fruit.
Has he defeated Israel, like those who defeated their oppressors? Were they killed like he killed their enemies?
When it shoots forth, you will debate it with measured force, as he calms his rough winds on the day of the east wind.
This is how Jacob's guilt will be removed. This is the result of removing his sin, when he turns all the altar stones into crushed chalk, and the Asherah poles and idols no longer stand.
The fortified city will be deserted. The homes abandoned and left like a wilderness. Calves will graze there, lie down, and eat its branches.
When its branches wither, they will be broken off. The women will come and burn them, because These people do not understand, so their creator will have no mercy, and he will show them no favor.
And in those days it will come to pass, that the Lord will collect his people, the children of Israel, one by one, from the Euphrates River to the stream of Egypt.
In those days, a great trumpet will sound. Those who were about to perish in Assyria and the outcasts in Egypt will come and worship the Lord on the holy mountain near Jerusalem.

Isaiah warned the proud drunken crown of Ephraim and said, "Woe unto the proud drunken crown of Ephraim, whose once glorious beauty is now a fading flower, who are at the head of the fertile valleys of those who are overcome by wine!
Behold, the Lord has one who is as strong and powerful as a violent destructive hailstorm and mighty flooding waters, and he will throw the proud crown of Ephraim's drunks down on the ground.
And the proud crown of Ephraim's drunks will be trampled underfoot.
The once glorious beauty at the head of the fertile valley will become a fading flower. But like the early fruit before summer, whoever sees it will immediately eat it.
In those days, the Lord of Hosts will be a crown of glory, and a beautiful jeweled crown for the remainder of his people.
He will be a spirit of justice to those who sit in judgement, and strength to those who defend the gates in battle.

But they have also gone astray because of wine and strong drink. The priests and prophets will be confused by alcohol, and they are overwhelmed by wine and misled by their drunken visions and judgments.
All their tables are covered in vomit and filth, and there is no clean place anywhere."

And the proud drunken leaders of Ephraim mocked Isaiah and said, "What can Isaiah teach anyone, and who can understand his gibberish? Does he think we are children just weaned from milk, or babies just off the breast?
Because Isaiah's way is line after line of rules, rules, rules, with a little gibberish here and a little gibberish there."
And Isaiah answered them and said, "So God will speak to these people in a foreign language with stammering lips.
To whom the Lord said, 'This is a refreshing restful place where the weary may find rest.' But they refused to listen.

So the Lord's word to them became: Line after line of rules, rules, rules, with a little gibberish here and a little gibberish there." So they would stumble backwards and be broken, trapped, and captured.
Therefore you arrogant men who rule the people in Jerusalem, listen to the Lord's word.
