Because you have said, 'We made a covenant with death and an agreement with hell. When the overwhelming scourge passes through, it will not touch us, because we have taken refuge in lies and hidden ourselves in falsehood.'

So this is what the Lord God says, 'Behold, I am laying a stone foundation in Zion, a tried and true stone, a precious cornerstone, and a firm foundation. Whoever believes in him will not be ashamed.'
I will use justice as a measuring line and righteousness as a level. Hail will sweep away your refuge of lies, and floodwaters will wash away your hiding place.
Your covenant with death will be canceled, and your agreement with hell will not stand. When the scourge passes through, you will be trampled by it.
Every time it comes, it will carry you away. It will sweep through morning after morning, day and night. It will frustrate your understanding of this message.
Because the bed is too short for a man to stretch out, and the blanket is too narrow to wrap around yourself.'
For the Lord will rise up like he did at Mount Perazim. God will be as angry as he was in the Valley of Gibeon, so he can do his strange work and perform his strange acts.
So do not be a mocker, or your chains will grow stronger, because I have heard of the destruction of the whole earth from the Lord God of Hosts.
Listen and hear my voice, pay attention and hear what I say.
Does the farmer plow all day to plant? Does he break and plow furrows in the soil?
Once he has leveled the surface, does he not scatter the cumin seed, plant wheat in rows, and plant barley and rye in its place?
For his God teaches and instructs him in his righteous ways.
Because caraway is not threshed with a threshing tool, and cumin is not crushed with a cart wheel. Caraway is beaten with a staff, and cumin with a rod.
Wheat for bread must be ground, but it is not endlessly threshed, and even though the cart wheels roll over it, the horses do not crush it.
For this also comes from the Lord of Hosts, who is wonderful in counsel and excellent in wisdom."
Woe unto the city of Ariel where David once lived! And let the sacrifices continue year after year.
But I will bring distress to Ariel, and there will be grief and sorrow, and it will still be called Ariel.
I will surround you with a mountain and lay siege against you, and I will build fortifications to defeat you.
You will be brought down, and speak from the ground, your voice will whisper like a ghost from the dust of the earth.
Besides that, your multitude of strangers will be like fine dust, and your ruthless enemies will suddenly and instantly blow away, like chaff in the wind.
The Lord of Hosts will visit you with thunder, earthquakes, loud noise, storms, and consuming fire.
All the nations that fight against Ariel and her defenses, will vanish like a dream in the night.

It will be like a hungry man dreaming of eating, but when he wakes up, he is still hungry, or a thirsty man who dreams of drinking, but when he wakes, he is faint and still thirsty. That's how it will be for all nations that fight against Mount Zion.
Pause and wonder, then shout and cry out, "They are drunk, but not from wine, they stagger, but not from alcohol.
Because the Lord has poured out a spirit of deep sleep and closed the eyes of your prophets and rulers, and he has covered the wise."
All visions have become like a sealed book, which is delivered to educated men and when they are asked to read it, they reply, "I cannot, because it is sealed."
Then the book is given to someone who is uneducated and they are asked to read it, and they reply, "I do not know how to read."
So the Lord says, "Because these people honor me with their words, but their hearts are far from me. Their fear is taught by man's rules.
Therefore, I will do something amazing among these people, a marvelous wonder. Because the wisdom of the wise will perish, and the understanding of the prudent will be hidden."
Woe unto those who try to hide their plans from the Lord, who do their deeds in darkness and say, "Who sees us, and who knows us?"

Surely you have turn upside down, and it is as if the clay is as respected as the potter! Can the clay say to the potter, "He did not make me!" Or should that which was created say to the creator, "You have no understanding?"
Soon, Lebanon will become a fertile field, and the fertile field will be considered a forest.
In those days, the deaf will hear the words of the book, and the blind will see from the obscurity of darkness and gloom.
The humble will rejoice in the Lord, and the poor among men will celebrate the Holy One of Israel.
For the terrible one will disappear, and the mockers will be consumed, and those who watch for immorality will be cut off.
Those who condemn others with a word, lay a trap for the innocent in the court, and deny justice to the righteous for no reason.
So the Lord, who redeemed Abraham, says this about Jacob, "Jacob will no longer be ashamed nor will his face grow pale."
But when he sees his children, the work of my hands, living among him, they will sanctify my name and the Holy One of Jacob, and they will fear the God of Israel.
Those who were confused will receive understanding, and those who murmured and complained will learn the true doctrine.
The Lord says this, "Woe unto the rebellious children, who seek advice but not from me, and who plan without my spirit, so that they add sin upon sin.
They walk down to Egypt without consulting me, seeking strength from Pharaoh and trusting in the shadow of Egypt's protection.
Therefore, Pharaoh's strength will bring you shame, and your trust in Egypt's shadow will lead to confusion.
Because his officials were in Zoan, and his ambassadors went to Hanes.
They were all ashamed of people who they could not profit from, neither helpful nor profitable, but only a source of shame and disappointment."

This is the burden of the beasts of the south, they will carry their wealth on donkeys and camels through a land of hardship and distress, inhabited by lions, vipers, and flying serpents, to a people who will not profit them.
Because the Egyptian's help is vain and pointless. That's why I cried out and said, "Their only strength is to sit still."
Now go, write this on a tablet and record it in a book, so it will stand as a witness forever.
These are rebellious people, deceitful children who refuse to listen to the Lord's law.
They speak to the wisemen and say, "Do not see," and they say to the prophets, "Do not tell us the truth, speak to us of pleasant things, and deceitful prophetic illusions.
Get out of our way, and turn away from the path, because and stop confronting us with the Holy One of Israel."
Therefore, the Holy One of Israel says, "Because you reject my word and trust, depend, and chase after oppression and deceit.
So this immorality will be like a broken defense which is ready to collapse, and it will suddenly break in an instant."
It will shatter like a potter's bowl, so completely broken that not even a sherd will be useful to scoop coals from a fire or draw water from the pit."
Because the Lord God, the Holy One of Israel said, "Your strength and salvation is found in quiet rest and trust, but you refused to listen."
But you said, "No! We will flee and ride on swift horses," so you will flee, but your pursuers will be faster.
A thousand will flee from the threat of only one, and five of you will flee, until only a flagpole on the mountain top is all that remains.

Yet the Lord will wait, so that he may be gracious to you, and that's why he will be glorified, because he wants to have mercy on you. For the Lord is a God of justice, blessed are those who wait for him.
For the people who live in Zion in Jerusalem, will no longer weep. He will be very gracious, and when he hears you cry out, he will answer you.
Even though the Lord gives you the bread of adversity and the water of affliction, your teachers will no longer hide from you, but you will see them.
And whether you turn to the left or to the right, your ears will hear a voice behind you saying, "This is the way, walk in it!"
You will discard your silver idols and worthless molten gold images. You will throw them away like a menstrual pad and say, "Get away from here!"
Then he will send rain for the seed you sow, and the land will produce abundant food, and in those days your livestock will graze in spacious pastures.
The Oxen and donkeys that work the soil will eat clean feed, which has been winnowed with a shovel and fork.
Streams and rivers will flow on every high mountain and hill on the day of great slaughter, when the towers fall.
Besides that, the moon will shine like the sun, and the sun will shine seven times brighter, like the light of seven days, when the Lord heals his people and repairs their wounds.
Behold, the Lord's name comes from afar, burning with anger and burdened by heavy judgment. His lips are full of fury, and his tongue is like a consuming fire.
His breath is like a flooding stream that reaches up to the neck. He will sift the nations with the sieve of vanity and place a bridle in the jaws of the people to lead them astray.
You will sing like on the night of a holy feast. Your heart will rejoice like one walking with music to the Lord's mountain, to the Mighty One of Israel.
The Lord will make his glorious voice heard and show his lightening descending down his arm, scattering everything with flames of consuming fire, cloudbursts, storms, and hailstones.
Because through the Lord's voice, the Assyrians will be struck down, and he will defeat them with his rod.
And the Lord's grounded staff will be accompanied by tambourines and harps everywhere that it goes. And he will fight them in battle with the shaking of his mighty arm.

For Tophet was ordained long ago, because its king is prepared. Its fire pit is deep and wide, with plenty of fire and wood. And the Lord's breath kindles the fire, like a stream of burning sulfur and brimstone.

Woe unto those who go down to Egypt for help, who rely on their horses, who trust in their numerous chariots, and in their powerful horsemen, but they do not look to the Holy One of Israel or seek the Lord!
Yet he is also wise and will bring evil, and he will not take back his words, but he will rise up against the house of evildoers and those who support the work of immorality.

The Egyptians are mere men, they are not God, and their horses are flesh, not spirit. When the Lord stretches out his hand, both the helper and the one helped will fall, and they will all fail together.

Because the Lord spoke to me like a roaring young lion attacking its prey. It is unafraid of the shepherds who gather against it, unmoved by their shouting. This is how the Lord of Hosts will come down to fight for Mount Zion and its hill.
Just like the birds flying overhead, so will be the Lord of Hosts when he comes to protect Jerusalem. He will defend and deliver it, and he will pass over and preserve it.
Return to him, you children of Israel who have deeply rebelled against him.
For in those days, every man will throw away their silver and gold idols, which their own hands made as sinful objects.
Then the Assyrians will fall, not by the sword of a mighty man, nor by the sword of a common man. He will flee from the sword, and his young men will be shamed.
And the Lord whose fire burns in Zion and whose furnace is in Jerusalem declares, "The Assyrian men will retreat to their stronghold out of fear, and their princes will fear their own flag."
Behold, there will be a king who rules with righteousness, and leaders will govern fairly.
A man will be like a shelter from the wind, a shelter from the violent storms, like streams in a dry land, and the shade of a massive rock in a weary land.
Those who see will have clear vision, and those who hear will truly listen.
The impulsive hearts will understand knowledge, and those who stammer will speak clearly.
The vile and wicked person will no longer be called noble, nor the will the stingy be described as generous.

Because the vile wicked person speaks foolishness, and their hearts plot immorality. He practices hypocrisy and speaks lies about the Lord, leaving the soul of the hungry empty, and denying a drink to the thirsty.
The tools of the stingy are evil, they devise cruel plans to deceive the poor with lies, even when the needy speak the truth.
But a noble man plans generous things, and he stands up for noble causes.
Wake up, you women who live in comfort, listen to me you careless daughters, and pay attention to what I say.
You careless women will face trouble and hardship for many days and years, because the harvest will fail and the gathering will not happen.
You women who are at ease, be troubled and shake with fear you careless ones, strip off your fine clothes, and wear sackcloth around your waist.
They will mourn for their breasts, over the loss of fertile fields and fruitful vines.
Thorns and briers will overrun the land of my people, even in the joyful homes of the joyous city.
Palaces will be abandoned, cities deserted, and strongholds will become animal dens forever, and a playground for wild donkeys and pastures for flocks.
This will last until the Spirit is poured out from above, and the wilderness becomes fertile, and the fertile land is seen as a forest.
Justice will live in the wilderness, and righteousness will remain in the fertile land.
The work of righteousness will bring peace, and its result will be righteous quietness and assurance forever.
My people will live in peaceful homes, secure dwellings, and quiet resting places.
Even when hail falls on the forest and the city is brought low, they will be safe.
Blessed are those who plant beside every stream and let their oxen and donkeys roam freely.
Woe unto you who destroy without being destroyed, and traitors who have not been betrayed! When you stop destroying, you will be destroyed, when you stop betraying, others will betray you.
O Lord, be gracious to us! We have waited for you, be our strength every morning and our salvation in times of trouble.
People fled at the sound of the tumult, when you rose up and scattered the nations.
Your plunder will be gathered like caterpillars swarming, and like locusts rushing in.
The Lord is glorified, because he lives on high. He has filled Zion with justice and righteousness.
Wisdom and knowledge will be the foundation of your times, and strength will bring salvation. Fear for the Lord is his treasure.
Behold, their brave ones cry out in the streets, and the ambassadors of peace will weep bitterly.
The highways are deserted, travelers have stopped. He has broken the covenant, despised the cities, and shows no regard for anyone.
The earth mourns and languishes. Lebanon is ashamed and withers, Sharon is like a wilderness, and Bashan and Carmel shed their fruits.
Now the Lord says, "Now I will rise and I will be glorified, now I will lift myself up.
You will conceive chaff and give birth to straw. Your breath is like a fire that will consume you.
The people will be burned like lime, like thorns cut down and thrown into the fire.
Listen to what I have done, you who are far away. And you who are near, acknowledge my power."
The sinners in Zion are terrified, fear surprises the hypocrites. Who among us can live with consuming fire? Who can dwell with everlasting flames?
Those who live righteously and speak truthfully, who reject unjust gain, refuse bribes, block their ears from hearing of bloodshed, and shut their eyes to evil.
They will dwell on high. Their refuge will be the fortress of rocks. Bread will be provided, and their water will be sure.
Your eyes will see the king in his beauty and they will see a land that stretches very far off.
Your heart will ponder terror. Where is the scribe? Where is the tax collector? Where is the one who counted the towers?
You will no longer see a fierce people, a nation with deeper speech than you can understand, with a stammering tongue which you cannot comprehend.

Look at Zion, our solemn city of festivals. Your eyes will see Jerusalem as a peaceful home, a tent that will never be taken down. Its stakes will never be removed, and none of its ropes will ever be broken.
But there the glorious Lord will be a place of wide streams and rivers for us, where no boat with oars will go, and no mighty ship will sail that way.
For the Lord is our judge, the Lord is our lawgiver, and our the Lord is our king. He will save us!
Your rigging is loose, they could not secure their mast or spread their sail. Then the prey of the great spoil will be divided, and even the lame will take part of the plunder.
No one living there will say, "I am sick." The people who live there will be forgiven their immorality.
All you nations and people, come near and listen, pay attention and let the earth and everything that comes from the world, hear this message.
The Lord is angry with all nations, and his fury is against their armies. He has completely destroyed them and handed them over for slaughter.
Their dead will be thrown out, their corpses will stink, and the mountains will melt from their blood.
And all the stars in heaven will dissolve, and the heavens will be rolled up like a scroll. Their stars will fall like leaves from a vine or figs from a fig tree.
Because my sword is bathed in the heavens! Behold, it will come down on Edom, and on the people I have cursed for judgment.

The Lord's sword is covered in blood, it is thick with fat, swollen with the blood from lambs and goats, and with fat from the kidneys of rams. Because the Lord has a sacrifice in Bozrah, and a great slaughter in Edom.
The wild oxen will fall with them, and bulls with other bulls. Their land will be soaked in blood, and the soil will be enriched with fat.
Because this is the Day of the Lord's vengeance, and the year of repayment for Zion's controversy.
And its streams will be turned into to pitch, and the dust from its soil will be turned into sulfur and brimstone, and its land will become burning pitch.
It will burn day and night, and its smoke will rise forever. From generation to generation it will lie in ruins, and no one will ever pass through it again.
But cormorants and bitterns will take possession of it, the owls and ravens will also live there. He will stretch out a measuring line of chaos and confusion, and the stones of emptiness over it.
They will summon its nobles to rule the kingdom, but they will not be there, and all her princes will vanish.
Thorns will grow in her palaces, nettles and brambles will grow in its fortresses. It will be a home for dragons and a court for owls.
The wild beasts of the desert, will meet with wild beasts of the island, and wild goats will cry to each other. The screech owl will rest there and find herself a place to rest.
The great owl will nest there, lay eggs and hatch them, and gather her young under her shadow. Vultures will also gather there, each with its own mate.
Seek out the Lord's book and read, not one of these will fail, no one will want her mate. Because God's mouth has commanded it, and his Spirit has gathered them together.
Because he has cast lots for them, and his hand has divided it among them by their heritage. They will possess it forever, and they will live there from generation to generation.
The wilderness and the lonely places will be glad for them, and the desert will rejoice and bloom like a rose.

It will bloom abundantly and rejoice with joy and singing. The glory of Lebanon will be given to it, along with the beauty of Carmel and Sharon. They will see the Lord's glory and the splendor of our God.
Strengthen the weak hands and support the feeble knees.
Say to those with fearful hearts, "Be strong, and do not be afraid, behold your God is coming with vengeance, and God will even compensate and save you."
Then the eyes of the blind will be opened, and the ears of the deaf will be cleared.
Then the lame will leap like a deer, and the dumb mute will sing, because the waters in the wilderness will burst forth, and streams will flow in the desert.
The dry ground will become a pool, and the thirsty land will be filled with springs. And in the place where dragons once lay, there will be tall grass with reeds and rushes.

And there will be a highway there, and it will be called the Way of Holiness. The unclean will not travel on it, because it will be for travelers who walk the straight path. Even fools will not go astray there.
There will be no lions there, and no dangerous beasts will travel on it. They will not be found there. But the rescued ones will walk there.
Those whom the Lord has ransomed will return, and come to Zion with songs and everlasting joy on their minds. They will receive joy and happiness, and sorrow and sighing will flee.
In the fourteenth year of the Israeli King Hezekiah's reign, King Sennacherib of Assyria, attacked all the fortified cities of Judah and captured them.
The king of Assyria sent Rabshakeh from Lachish to Jerusalem with a large army to meet King Hezekiah. He stood by the upper pool's conduit on the road near the launderer's field.
Then Hilkiah's son Eliakim, who was in charge of the palace, Shebna the scribe, and Joah son of Asaph the recorder, went out to meet him.
Then Rabshakeh said to them, "Tell Hezekiah, that this is what the great king of Assyria says, 'What is this confidence you rely on?
You say you have the knowledge and strength for war, but those are empty words. Who are your trusted counsellors that are advising you to rebel against me?
Look, you are trusting Egypt, the broken reed, that will break and pierce a man's hand if leans on it. That's what Pharaoh the king of Egypt is to anyone who trusts him.'

But if you say, 'We trust in our Lord God,' then do you not realize that he is the one whose altars and high places that Hezekiah removed, when he said to Judah and Jerusalem, 'You must worship before this altar'?
That's why I will make a pledge to my master, the Assyrian king, and I will give you 2,000 horses, if you can find riders that can ride them.
How will you repel even one officer from the least of my master's servants, relying on Egypt for chariots and horsemen?
Have I come against this land to destroy it without the Lord's approval? The Lord Himself told me, 'Go up against this land and destroy it.'"

Then Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah said to Rabshakeh, "Please speak to your servants in the Syrian language, because that's what we understand. Do not speak to us in Hebrew, which the Jews standing on the wall can hear and understand."

But Rabshakeh replied, "Has my master sent me to deliver this message only to you and your master? Has he not sent me to the people sitting on the wall, who will eat their own dung and drink their own piss with you?"
Then Rabshakeh stood and cried out loudly in the Jews' Hebrew language and said, "Hear the words of the great Assyrian king!
This is what the Assyrian king says, 'Do not let Hezekiah deceive you. He cannot save you.'
Do not let Hezekiah persuade you to trust in the Lord by saying, 'The Lord will surely deliver us, this city will not fall to the Assyrian king.'

Do not listen to Hezekiah. This is what the Assyrian king says, 'Make peace with me and come out to me. Then each of you will eat from your own vine and fig tree and drink water from your own cistern.
Until I come and take you to a land like your own, a land of grain and wine, bread and vineyards.'
Do not let Hezekiah mislead you by saying, 'The Lord will deliver us.' Have any of the gods of the nations rescued their lands from the king of Assyria?
Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim? Have they rescued Samaria from my hand?
Who among all the gods of these lands has rescued their land from my hand? So why should the Lord deliver Jerusalem from me?"
But the people remained silent and did not answer him, because the king had commanded and said, "Do not respond to him."
Then Eliakim son of Hilkiah, who was in charge of the palace, Shebna the scribe, and Joah son of Asaph the recorder, returned to Hezekiah with their clothes torn and reported Rabshakeh's words.
When King Hezekiah heard this, he tore his clothes, put on sackcloth, and went into the Lord's temple.
He sent Eliakim, who was in charge of the palace, Shebna the scribe, and the priest's elders to the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz all wearing sackcloth.
They said to him, "This is what Hezekiah says, 'Today is a day of distress, rebuke, and disgrace. Children are ready to be born, but there is no strength to deliver them.

Perhaps your Lord God will hear what Rabshakeh, the Assyrian king's servant, who was sent to insult the living God has said. And hopefully your Living God will rebuke him for what he has heard. Therefore, lift up your prayers for the Jewish survivors who still remain.'"
So King Hezekiah's servants went to Isaiah.
Isaiah said to them, "Tell your master, 'This is what the Lord says, "Do not be afraid of what you have heard, by which the servants of the king of Assyria have blasphemed me.
Behold, I will send a spirit to him so that he will hear a rumor, and return to his own land, where I will cause him to fall by the sword."'"
Then Rabshakeh returned and found the Assyrian king making war against Libnah, because he had heard that the king had left Lachish.
He heard the report about King Tirhakah of Ethiopia which said, "He has come out to make war with you." When he heard this, he sent messengers to King Hezekiah.
And he told the messengers to say, "King Hezekiah of Judah, do not let your God, whom you trust, deceive you by saying, 'Jerusalem will not be handed over to the king of Assyria.
Surely you have heard what the kings of Assyria have done to all the lands by destroying them completely. Do you think that you will be delivered?
Did the gods of the nations that my ancestors destroyed, like Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and the people of Eden in Telassar, deliver them?
Where are the kings of the cities of Hamath, Arpad, Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivah?'"
When Hezekiah received the letter from the messengers, he read it and went up to the Lord's temple, and spread it out before the Lord.
Then Hezekiah prayed to the Lord.
And he said, "Lord of Hosts, God of Israel, who lives on his throne between the cherubim, You alone are God over all the kingdoms of the earth. You made heaven and earth.
O Lord, listen, hear, and open your eyes and see. Hear the words that Sennacherib has sent to insult the living God.
The truth is Lord, that the kings of Assyria have laid waste to all the nations and their countries.
And they have thrown their gods into the fire, because they were not gods but the work of men's hands, wood and stone, and that's why they could be destroyed.
So now, O Lord our God, save us from his hand, so that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that you are the only Lord God."
Then Isaiah son of Amoz sent a message to Hezekiah and said, "This is what the Lord God of Israel says, 'Because you have prayed to me about King Sennacherib of Assyria.'
This is what the Lord has spoken against him and said, 'The Virgin Daughter of Zion despises you and mocks you. The Daughter of Jerusalem shakes her head as you flee.
Who have you insulted and blasphemed? Against whom have you raised your voice and lifted up your eyes in pride? You have insulted the Holy One of Israel.

You sent your servants to ridicule the Lord, and you said, "I have climbed the heights of the mountains, to the borders of Lebanon with many chariots. I will cut down its tallest cedars and its finest fir trees, and I will reach its highest peak, and the forests of Carmel.
I dug wells and drank their water, and I have dried up all the Egyptian rivers with the soles of my feet.
Have you not heard how I planned it long ago in ancient times. Now I have brought it to pass, so that you would lay waste to fortified cities and turned them into piles of rubble?

That's why, their inhabitants were drained of their power, and were dismayed and confused. They were like grass in the field, tender green shoots, like grass on rooftops, or wheat that was scorched before it grew.
But I know where you live, when you come and go, and how you rage against me.
And because you rage against me and your arrogance has reached my ears, I will put my hook in your nose and my bit in your mouth, and I will make you return by the way in which you came.

And this will be a sign for you O Hezekiah: This year you will eat what grows on its own, and the second year you will eat what springs from that. But in the third year, sow and reap, plant vineyards and eat its fruit."
And the survivors from the house of Judah will once again take root below and bear fruit above.
For the Lord of Hosts will help the protected ones to leave Jerusalem, and they will escape Mount Zion through his zeal.
Therefore, this is what the Lord says about the king of Assyria, 'He will not enter this city or shoot an arrow there. He will not come before it with a shield or build a siege ramp against it.
And he will return, the same way by which he came. He will not enter this city,' says the Lord.
'Because, I will defend this city and save it for my sake and for the sake of my servant David.'"
Then the angel of the Lord went out and struck down 145,000 in the Assyrian camp. When the people got up the next morning, they were surrounded by dead bodies.
So King Sennacherib of Assyria departed, returned home, and stayed in Nineveh.
While he was worshiping in the temple of his god Nisroch, his sons Adrammelech and Sharezer killed him with a sword and escaped to the land of Ararat. And his son Esarhaddon succeeded him as king.

In those days King Hezekiah became deathly ill. The prophet Isaiah the son of Amoz, came to him and said, "This is what the Lord says, 'Set your affairs in order, because you are going to die, and you will not recover.'"
Then Hezekiah turned his face toward the wall and prayed to the Lord.
And he said, "O Lord, please remember how I have walked faithfully before you with a sincere heart, and I have done that which is good in Your sight." And Hezekiah wept bitterly.
Then the Lord's word came to Isaiah:
And he said, "Go and tell Hezekiah, 'This is what the Lord God of your father David says, "I have heard your prayer and seen your tears. I will add fifteen years to your life.
And I will deliver you and this city from the hand of the king of Assyria, and I will defend this city.
This will be the sign to you from the Lord that he will do what he has promised.
Behold, I will cause the shadow on the sundial of Ahaz to go ten degrees backwards."'"So the sun moved backwards ten degrees on the dial, from where it had just been.
This is what King Hezekiah of Judah wrote after he had been sick and recovered.
So I said, "I am in the prime of my life, must I go to the gates of the grave, I have been deprived of my remaining years.
I will no longer see the Lord in the land of the living, and I will not look upon mankind with those who dwell on the earth.
My dwelling has been picked up and moved like a shepherd's tent. I have rolled up my life like a weaver, he cuts me off with debilitating sickness. And from day until night, you end my life.
I waited patiently and thought until morning, that he would break all my bones like a lion. And from day until night, you end my life.
I chattered like a swallow or a crane, I mourned like a dove. My eyes grew weak as I looked upward. O Lord, I am oppressed, please support me."
What can I say? He himself has spoken to me and done it. I will walk softly all of my years, because of the bitterness in my soul.
O Lord, men live because of these things, and my spirit finds life in them. So, will you restore my health and allow me to live.
Behold, because in peace I have had great bitterness. But in your love, you have delivered my soul from the pit of corruption, and thrown all of my sins behind Your back.
Because the grave cannot praise you, death cannot celebrate you, and those who go down to the pit cannot hope for your truth.
Only the living can praise you as I do today. Fathers will tell their children about your truth.
The Lord was ready to save me, so we will sing my songs with stringed instruments all the days of our lives in the Lord's house.
Because Isaiah has said, "Let them take a lump of figs and apply it like a poultice on the boil, and he will recover."
Hezekiah had also asked, "What will be the sign for me to know, when it's time for me to go up to the Lord's house?"
At that time Merodachbaladan, son of King Baladan of Babylon, sent letters and a gift to King Hezekiah, because he had heard that Hezekiah had been sick, but had recovered.

Hezekiah was pleased to see them, and showed them everything in his treasure house, including all the gold, silver, spices, precious ointments, the entire armory, and everything else that was stored in his vaults. There was nothing in his palace or throughout his kingdom, that Hezekiah did not show them.
Then the prophet Isaiah came to King Hezekiah and asked, "What did those men say, and where did they come from?" Hezekiah replied, "They came to visit me from a distant land called Babylon."
And Isaiah asked, "What have they seen in your palace?" Hezekiah answered, "They have seen everything in my palace. There is nothing among my treasures that I did not show them."
Then Isaiah said to Hezekiah, "Hear the word of the Lord of Hosts.
And the Lord says, 'Behold, the time will come when everything in your palace, and everything that your fathers have stored up until today, will be carried off to Babylon. There will be nothing left.
And some of your descendants, your own flesh and blood, will be taken away, to become eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon.'"
Then Hezekiah said to Isaiah, "The Lord's word which you have spoken is good." And he added, "At least there will be peace and truth in my lifetime."
Your God says, "O my people, I give you comfort!
Speak kindly to Jerusalem, and proclaim to her that her days of warfare are over, her immorality is forgiven, and she has received double from the Lord's hand for all of her sins."
A voice of one cries out in the wilderness, "Prepare and make straight the way of the Lord, make straight a highway in the desert for our God."
Every valley will be glorified, every mountain and hill made low, the crooked will be made straight, and the rough places will be made smooth.
Then the glory of the Lord will be revealed, and all people will see it together, because the Lord's mouth has spoken.
And the voice said, "Cry out!" And I asked, "What should I cry out?" And the voice said, "All people are like grass, and all their beauty is like the flowers of the field.
The grass withers and the flower fades when the breath of the Lord blows on it. Surely, all the people are grass.
The grass withers and the flower fades, but the word of our God stands forever."

You who bring good news to Zion, go up on a high mountains, and you who bring the good news to Jerusalem, lift up your voice with strength. Do not be afraid, and say to the cities of Judah, "Behold your God!"
For behold, the Lord God comes with a powerful hand, and his arm will rule for him. Because his reward is with him, and his works come with him.
He will feed his flock like a shepherd. He will gather the lambs in his arms, and carry them close to his heart, and gently lead those who are young.

Whose hand has measured the waters, or measured the heavens with the span of his fingers? Who counts and comprehends the earth's dust, and who has weighed the hills and mountains on his scales and balance?
Who has directed the Lord's spirit, or served as his counselor?
With whom did he consult, and who has instructed him and taught him in the path of justice and knowledge, or showed him the ways of understanding?
Behold, the nations are like a drop in a bucket, they are counted like dust on the scales. He lifts up the islands as if they were very small.
Lebanon is not sufficient for fuel, nor are its animals enough for a burnt offering.
All the nations are like nothing before him, they are regarded by him as worthless vanity and less than nothing.
To whom then will you compare God? What likeness will you set beside him?
A carved idol, cast by a workman? Which a goldsmith overlays with gold, and makes silver chains for it.
The poor, who cannot afford such offerings, choose wood from a tree that will not rot. They seek a skilled craftsman to prepare a carved idol, that will not moved.
Do you not know, have you not heard, have you not been told from the beginning, and have you not understood since the earth was founded?
That he sits enthroned above the circle of the earth, and its people are like grasshoppers. He stretches out the heavens like a curtain and spreads them out like a tent live in.
He brings princes to nothing and reduces the judges of the earth to empty vanity.
Yes, they will not be planted or sown, and no sooner do they take root in the ground, than he blows on them and they wither, and a whirlwind sweeps them away like straw.
"To whom will you compare me, or who is my equal?" says the Holy One.

Lift up your eyes and look up to the heavens, and behold the one who created all these? He brings out the stars and calls each one by name, and because of his great power and mighty strength, not one of them fails.
Why do you complain Jacob? And why do you say, O Israel, "My way is hidden from the Lord, and my judgement is ignored by my God"?
Do you not know? Have you not heard, that the Lord is the everlasting God, the Creator of the ends of the earth. He does not grow tired or weary, and his understanding is beyond measure.
He gives power to the weary, and he gives strength to the powerless.
Even the youth grow tired and weary, and young men will stumble and fall.
But those who wait on the Lord will renew their strength. They will soar on wings like eagles, they will run and not grow weary, and they will walk and not grow faint.
O islands, be silent before me and let the people renew their strength. Let them come near and speak, and let us meet together for judgment.

Who raised up the righteous man from the east, called him to his feet, gave nations into his hands, and made him rule over kings? He turned them into dust with his sword, and drove them away like straw with his bow.
He pursued them and passed safely, traveling a path that his feet had never walked.
Who has accomplished this work, calling on the descendants from the beginning? I the Lord, the first and the last, I am him.
The islands saw it and were afraid, the ends of the earth were afraid, but they drew near and came forward.
Everyone helped his neighbor, and said to his brother, "Be courageous."

The carpenter encouraged the goldsmith, and the one who smooths with the hammer inspired the one who strikes the anvil. They said, "It is ready for soldering," and he fastened it with nails, so that it would not fall apart.
But you, Israel, are my servant, Jacob, whom I have chosen, is the offspring of my friend Abraham.
You whom I brought from the ends of the earth, and I called you from its leaders, and I said to you, "You are my servant, I have chosen you and I will not throw you away."
Fear not, for I am with you. Do not be dismayed, because I am your God. I will strengthen you, I will help you, and I will uphold you with my righteous right hand.
Behold, all those who were angry with you will be ashamed and confused. They will be like nothing, and those who oppose you will perish.
You will search for them ,but you will not find them. Those who made war against you will be like nothing, and they will be completely gone.
For I your Lord God, will hold your right hand and say to you, "Fear not, because I will help you."
Because the Lord says, "Fear not Jacob you worm, and you men of Israel. I will help you! Your Redeemer is the Holy One of Israel.
Behold, I will make you into a sharp new threshing tool with teeth. You will thresh mountains and grind them down, and turn hills into chaff.
You will toss them in the air, and the wind will scatter them. Then you will rejoice in the Lord, and glory in the Holy One of Israel.
When the poor and needy search for water and find none, and their tongues are parched with thirst, I the Lord will hear them, and I the God of Israel, will not abandon them.
I will make rivers flow in high places and fountains appear in the valleys. I will turn the wilderness into a pool of water and dry land into springs.
I will plant cedar, acacia, myrtle, and olive trees in the wilderness. I will place fir, pine, and cypress trees together in the desert.
So that they may see, know, consider, and understand together that the hand of the Lord has done this, and the Holy One of Israel has created it."
The king and Lord God of Jacob says, "Present your case, and bring forth your strong arguments."
Let them bring their evidence and show us what will happen. Let them explain past events so we can consider and understand their outcome, or tell us what is to come.
Show us the things that are going to happen from now on, so that we will know you are gods. Yes, do something, good or evil, so that we can be amazed and watch together.
Behold, you are nothing, and your work is worthless, and whoever chooses you is an abomination.
I have raised up someone from the north, and he will come from the rising sun in the east, and he will call on my name. He will trample rulers like mortar, or like a potter treads clay.

Who has told us this from the beginning so that we could know? And who predicted it in the past so that we could say, "He is righteous"? Yes, no one told us, no one declared it, and no one heard your words.
The first one will say to Zion, "Behold, here they are!" And I will send a messenger to Jerusalem with good news.
Because I looked, but there was no man, and no counselor among them that could answer when I asked them.
Behold, they are all just empty vanity, their works are nothing, and their molten images are simply confused wind.
This is what the LORD God says, "Behold, here is my servant, whom I support, my chosen one in whom my soul delights. I have placed my spirit upon him, and he will bring justice to the Gentiles.
He will not cry or raise his voice, nor make it heard in the streets.
He will not break a bruised reed or extinguish a smoldering wick. He will faithfully bring justice.
He will not falter nor be discouraged until he establishes justice on earth. The islands will wait for his teachings."
The Lord God created the heavens and stretched them out, he spread out the earth and everything on it, he gives the breath of life to its people and spirit to those who walk on it.

Furthermore, the Lord God who created everything says this, "I, the Lord, have called you in righteousness. I will hold your hand, protect you, and appoint you as a covenant for the people and a light to the Gentiles.
I do this to open blind eyes, to free the prisoners and release those who sit in the darkness of the prison house.
I am the Lord, that is my name! I will not give my glory to another nor my praise to carved idols.
Behold, the former things have come to pass, and now I declare new things. Before they happen, I announce them to you."
Sing a new song to the Lord, and sing praises to him from the ends of the earth, you who go down to the sea, and everything in it, including the islands and everyone who lives there.
Let the wilderness and its cities lift up their voices. Let the villages where Kedar lives rejoice. Let the people of the rock sing and shout from the mountaintops.
Let them give glory to the Lord, and declare his praise in the islands.
The Lord will march out like a mighty warrior. He will stir up his jealousy like a man of war. He will shout, roar, and triumph over his enemies.
And the Lord roars, "I have held my peace for a long time. I have been quiet and restrained myself. But now I will cry out like a woman in labor, I will destroy and devour all at once.
I will lay waste to the hills and mountains, and dry up all their vegetation. I will make the rivers run dry, and drain the pools.

I will bring the blind along unfamiliar paths. I will guide them through unknown ways. I will turn darkness into light before them and make crooked things straight. I will do all these things and I will not abandon them.
Those who trust in idols and say to molten images, 'You are our gods,' will be turned back in shame.
Listen, you who are deaf, look, you who are blind, so that you may see.
Who is as blind as my servant, or as deaf as the messenger I sent? Who is as blind as the one who is perfect to me, and as blind as the Lord's servant?
You see many things, but you pay no attention. Your ears are open, but you do not hear."
The Lord was well pleased with his righteousness, he will magnify his law and make it honorable.

But these people have been robbed and plundered. They are all trapped in holes or hidden in prisons. They have become prey with no one to rescue them, and they were looted with no one to say, "Restore them!"
Who among you will pay attention to this? Who will listen and hear the future?
Who gave up Jacob for plunder and turned Israel over to the robbers? Was it not the Lord, against whom we have sinned? For they have refused to walk in his ways, nor did they obey his law.
So he poured out his fierce anger and the fury of battle. It engulfed them in flames, but they did not understand. It burned them, but they did not take it to heart.
But now, O Jacob and O Israel, this is what the Lord who created and formed you says, "Do not be afraid, for I have redeemed you. I have called you by name, and you are mine.
When you pass through the waters, I will be with you. When you cross rivers, they will not overwhelm you. When you walk through the fire, you will not be burned, nor will the flames consume you.
For I am the Lord your God, the Holy One of Israel, your savior. I gave Egypt to Ethiopia and Seba, as your ransom.
Because you were precious in my sight, you have been honorable, and I have loved you. Therefore, I will give men in exchange for you, and nations in exchange for your life.
Fear not, for I am with you. I will bring your descendants from the east and gather you from the west.
I will say to the north, 'Give them up!' and to the south, 'Do not hold them back!' Bring my sons from afar and my daughters from the ends of the earth.
Everyone who is called by my name, whom I have created for my glory, whom I have formed and made."
Bring out the blind who have eyes and the deaf who have ears.

Let all the nations gather together and let the people assemble. Who among them can declare this and show us former things? Let them present their witnesses to prove they are justified, or let them hear and say, "It is true."

And the Lord declares, "You are my witnesses and my servant whom I have chosen, so that you may know and believe me and understand that I am him. There were no gods formed before me, and there will be none after me.
Yes, I am the Lord, and apart from me there is no savior.
I have revealed, saved, and proclaimed, when there were no foreign gods among you. So you are my witnesses, that I am the Lord God."
Yes, before there was daylight I am him. No one can deliver anything from my hand. When I work, who can change it?
This is what your redeemer the Lord and the Holy One of Israel says, "For your sake I have attacked Babylon and brought down their nobles and the Chaldeans, whose cries echo in the ships.
I am the Lord, your Holy One, the Creator of Israel, and your King."
This is what the Lord says, who makes a way through the sea and a path through the mighty waters.
Who brings out the chariot and horse, the army and the power, they will lie down together and they not rise, they are extinct, and they are snuffed out like a wick.
He says, "Do not remember the former things nor dwell on the past.
Behold, I will do something new! Now it will spring up, and you will not recognize it? I will make a way in the wilderness and rivers in the desert.
The wild animals, the dragons, and the owls will honor me, because I provide water in the wilderness and rivers in the desert to give something to drink to my chosen people.
I have formed these people for myself, they will declare my praise.
But you have not called on me, O Jacob, and you have grown weary of me, O Israel.
You have not brought me sheep for your burnt offerings or honored me with your sacrifices. I have not burdened you with offerings nor wearied you with incense.
You have not bought me sweet cane with your money nor satisfied me with the fat of your sacrifices. But, you have burdened me with your sins and wearied me with your wickedness.
I am the one who wipes away your transgressions for my own sake, and I will not remember your sins.
Remind me and we can discuss things. Declare your case, so that you may be justified.
Your first father has sinned, and your teachers have rebelled against me.
So I disgraced the leaders of the sanctuary, and I handed Jacob over to the curse, and turned Israel over to disrespect."
Now Listen, O Jacob my servant and Israel, whom I have chosen.
This is what the Lord who made you and formed you in the womb, and who helps you says, "Do not be afraid, Jacob my servant and Jeshurun, whom I have chosen.
I will pour water on the thirsty and flood the dry ground. I will pour out my spirit on your descendants, and my blessings on your offspring.
They will grow like grass in a meadow, like willows by flowing streams.
One will say, 'I belong to the Lord,' another will call himself by the name of Jacob, and another will write on his hand, 'I am the Lord's,' and take the name of Israel for himself."
This is what the Lord, the king of Israel and the Lord of Hosts declares, "I am the first and the last, there are no other God but me.
Who is like me? Let him speak and declare it. Let him explain what has happened since I established the ancient people, and let them show it to us what is yet to come.
Do not fear nor be afraid! Have I not told you and declared it long ago? You are my witnesses. Is there any God besides me? No, there is no other God, I know of none."
Those who make carved idols are nothing but vanity, and the things they treasure are profitless. They are their own witnesses, they do not see nor understand, so that they are ashamed.
Who have formed a god or cast a carved idol that is profitable for nothing?
Behold, all his associates will be ashamed, and the workmen are only men. Let them all come together and take their stand, and they will fear and be ashamed together.
The blacksmith works with tools over the coals, shaping the idol with hammers and forging it with his strong arms. But he grows hungry and weak; he drinks no water and becomes faint.
The carpenter measures with his ruler to mark a line, planes it to fit, and lays it out with a compass. He makes it into a beautiful figure of a man, to live in a shrine.
He cuts down cedars and selects a cypress or an oak. He lets it grow strong among the trees of the forest. He plants an ash, and the rain nourishes it.
It becomes fuel for a man to burn, because he will use some of it to warm himself, kindle a fire, and bake bread. Then he makes a god and worships it, he makes an idol and bows down to it.
He burns part of it in the fire, roasts meat over it, and eats until he is satisfied. He warms himself and says, "Aha, I am warm, and I see the fire."
From the rest of it he makes a god, his carved idol. He bows down to it, worships it, prays to it, and says, "Save me, because you are my god."
They do not understand nor comprehend, because their eyes are shut so that they cannot see, and their hearts are closed so they cannot understand.

No one stops to think, no one has the knowledge nor understanding to say, "I burned part of it in the fire, baked bread on its coals, roasted meat and ate it. Should I make the rest of it into an abomination? Should I bow down to a tree trunk?"
He feeds on ashes, a deceived heart has misled him, so that he cannot save his soul nor say, "Is not this thing in my right hand a lie?"
Remember these things, O Jacob and Israel, for you are my servant. I formed you, you are my servant, O Israel, I will not forget you.
I have wiped away your sins like a thick cloud. Return to me, for I have rescued you.

Sing, O heavens, because the Lord has done it. Shout from depths of the earth. Let the mountains, forests, and every tree in them burst into song. Because the Lord has rescued Jacob and revealed his glory in Israel.
This is what the Lord your redeemer, who formed you in the womb says, "I am the Lord, who made all things, who stretches out the heavens alone, who spread the earth abroad by myself.
I frustrate the tokens of the liars, and make the diviners mad. I turn wise men backward and make their knowledge foolish.

I confirm the words of my servants and fulfill the plans of my messengers. I say of Jerusalem, 'You will be inhabited,' and of the towns of Judah, 'You will be rebuilt,' and I will raise up and restore their decayed ruins.
I say to the deep, 'Be dry,' and I will dry up your rivers.
And I say of Cyrus, 'He is my shepherd and will perform at my pleasure,' and I said to Jerusalem, 'You will be rebuilt,' and to the temple, 'Your foundation will be laid.'"
This is what the Lord says to Cyrus his anointed, whose right hand I have held to subdue nations before him. I will loosen the kings' belts and open doors before him, and the gates will not be shut.
And the Lord said, "I will go before you and make the crooked paths straight. I will shatter bronze gates and break iron bars.
I will give you the treasures of darkness and riches hidden in secret places, so that you may know that I am the Lord, who calls you by name, I am the God of Israel.
For the sake of my servant Jacob and Israel my chosen, I have called you by your name and given you a surname, even though you do not know me.
I am the Lord, and there is no other. There is no God besides me. I have equipped you, even though you do not know me.
So that the people from the rising of the sun of the east to the west may know, there is no one besides me. I am the Lord, and there is no other.
I form the light and create darkness. I make peace and create evil. I, the Lord, do all of these things.

I rain down from the heavens above, and let the skies pour out righteousness. Let the earth open up so that salvation may spring forth, and let righteousness grow together. I, the Lord, have created it.
Woe unto anyone who argues with their maker! Should clay struggle with the potter? Does the clay say, 'What are you making?' or 'Your work has no hands'?
Woe unto anyone who says to their father, 'What have you begotten?' or to their mother, 'What have you given birth to?'"
This is what the Lord and the Holy One of Israel, the Lord of Hosts, and your maker says, "Ask me about things that are to come for my children, and give me orders concerning the work of my hands.
I have made the earth and created mankind upon it. My own hands have stretched out the heavens, and I command all their hosts.
I have raised him up in righteousness, and I will guide all his ways. He will rebuild my city and set my exiles free, and not for payment nor reward."

This is what the Lord says, "The labor of Egypt, and the merchandise of Ethiopia, along with the Sabeans men of stature, will come to you and be yours. They will follow you in chains, bowing down to you and pleading, 'Surely God is with you, and there is no other God.'"
O God of Israel, you are truly a God who hides himself, you are the savior.
All idol makers will be ashamed and disgraced, they will go off together in confusion.
But Israel will be saved by the Lord with everlasting salvation. You will never be ashamed nor a confused world for all eternity.

This is the Lord who created the heavens, God Himself who formed and made the earth. He established it, and he did not create it in vain, but he formed it to be inhabited, and this is what he says, "I am the Lord, and there is no other.
I have not spoken in secret dark place of the earth. I did not say to Jacob's descendants, 'You seek me in vain.' I, the Lord, speak the righteous truth, and I declare what is right.
Assemble yourselves and come near together, you survivors who escaped from the nations. Those who carry carved wooden idols have no understanding, and they pray to gods that cannot save.

Declare and present your case, let them consult together. Who foretold this long ago, and who declared it from the distant past? Was it not I, the Lord? There is no other God besides me, a righteous God and a savior, there is no other God but me.
Turn to me and be saved, all the ends of the earth, for I am God, and there is no other.
I have sworn an oath by my name, and my righteous word has gone out and will not return, so that every knee will bow, and every tongue will swear allegiance to me.
Surely, one will say, 'In the Lord alone are righteousness and strength.'"All who rage against him will come to him and be put to shame.
In the Lord all the descendants of Israel will be justified and find glory.
Bel bows down, Nebo stoops low, their idols weigh down the beasts and the cattle. Your carts are weighed down, they are a burden to the weary beasts.
They all stoop and bow together. They could not carry the burden, and they themselves are taken into captivity.
Listen to me, O house of Jacob, everyone who remains from the House of Israel, those who I have carried since birth, which I have supported from the womb.
Even in your old age, I am him, and even when your hair turns gray I will carry you. I made you, and I will sustain you. I will carry and rescue you.
Who will you compare me to? Who is my equal? Who can you that we are alike?
They lavish gold from their bags and weigh silver on scales. Then they hire a goldsmith who makes it into a god. They bow down and worship it.
They carry it on their shoulders. They set it in its place, and there it stands, it does not move. People cry out to it, but it can not answer or save them from their troubles.
Remember this and act like men, think it over again, you who have transgressed.
Remember the things that happened long ago, for I am God, and there is no other. I am God, and there is no one like me.
I declare the end from the beginning, and from the ancient times things that are still to come. My plan will stand, and I will do what I desire.
I will call a ravenous bird from the east, the man who executes my plan from a distant land. Yes, I have spoken it, and I will also make it happen. I have planned it, and I will do it.
Listen to me, you brave and determined people who are far from righteousness.
I am bringing my righteousness closer, it will not be far away. My salvation will not be delayed. I will place salvation in Zion for Israel my glory.

Come down and sit in the dust, O virgin daughter of Babylon. Sit on the ground, there is no throne for you anymore, O daughter of the Chaldeans, because you will no longer be called tender and delicate.
Take the millstones and grind flour. Remove your veil, roll up your sleeves, bare your legs, and wade through the rivers.
Your nakedness will be exposed, and your shame will be revealed. I will take revenge, and I will not come to you as a man.
Our redeemer's name is the Lord of Hosts, the Holy One of Israel.
Be silent and retreat into darkness, O daughter of the Chaldeans. You will no longer be called the queen of kingdoms.
I was angry with my people, so I profaned my inheritance and handed them over to you. You showed them no mercy and placed a heavy burden on the ancient elderly ones.
You said, "I will be a lady forever," and you did not take these things to heart or consider how it would end.
So now listen, you who indulge in pleasure and live carelessly, saying in your heart, "I am, and there is no one else. I will never be a widow or lose my children."
But both these things will strike you in a single day, loss of children and widowhood. They will come upon you in full force because of your many sorceries and countless magic spells.
Because you have trusted in your wickedness and you said, "No one sees me." Your wisdom and knowledge has perverted you, and you have said in your heart, "I am, and there is no one else besides me."

That's why evil will come upon you, you will not know where it came from. Trouble will fall on you, and you will not be able to stop it. Devastation will come on you suddenly, and you will not see it coming.
Go ahead, stand there with your magic spells and your many sorceries, which you have practiced since youth. Maybe you will be able to profit, and maybe you will succeed.
You are exhausted from all the advice from your advisors. Let your astrologers, stargazers, and monthly fortune-tellers stand up and save you from what is to come.
Behold, they will be like straw, the fire will burn them. They will not be able to save themselves from the power of the flames. There will not be any coals to warm yourself or fire to sit beside.
That's what will happen to those you have worked with, your merchants since youth. They will wander off to their own place, and no one will save you.
Listen to this, O house of Jacob, you who are called Israel and come from the waters of Judah. You swear by the Lord's name and mention the God of Israel, but not truthfully nor righteously.
Because they claim to be from the Holy City, and rely on the God of Israel, whose name is the Lord of Hosts.
I have declared things from the past from the beginning, and they came from my mouth, I showed them, I did them suddenly, and they all happened.
I knew you were obstinate, your neck is like iron sinew, and your forehead is like brass.
That's why I told you from the beginning, before it happened, so you that would not say, "My idol did this, my carved and molten images commanded it."
You have heard and seen all this, and you will not admit it? Now I am revealing new things to you, hidden things you did not know about before.
They are being created now, and not from the beginning, even before the day before you heard about them, so you could not say, "I already knew that."
Yes, you had not heard or known, from the time that your ears were not opened. Because I knew that you would be deceitful, and you would deal treacherously, and you were called a rebel from birth.
For the sake of my name, I will withhold my anger, and for my praise I will restrain myself, so that I do not destroy you.
Behold, I have refined you, not with silver, but I have chosen you through the furnace of suffering.
For my own sake, yes, I will do this. I will not let my name be polluted or share my glory with another.
Listen to me, O Jacob and Israel, whom I have called, I am him, I am the first and the last.
My hand also laid the earth's foundation, and my right hand has spanned the heavens. When I summon them, they rise together.
All of you, gather together and listen, who among them has foretold these things? The Lord loves him, he will do as he pleases against Babylon, and his powerful arm will be against the Chaldeans.
I have spoken and called him. I have brought him, and he will succeed in his prosperity.
Come close and hear this. I have not spoken in secret from the beginning. From the time of the beginning, there I am. And now, the Lord God and his spirit has sent me.
The Lord says, "I am your redeemer, the Holy One of Israel, your God who teaches you what is best, and I guide you in the way you should go."
If only you had listened to my commandments! Then your peace would have flowed like a river, and your righteousness would be like ocean waves.
Your descendants would have been as countless as sand, and your children would be like its grains. His name would not have been cut off nor destroyed from before me.
Leave Babylon, flee from the Chaldeans, and sing with joy and declare the news to the ends of the earth and say, "The Lord has redeemed his servant Jacob."
They did not go thirsty when he led them through the deserts. He made water flow from the rock for them, he split the rock, and water gushed out.
And the Lord says, "There is no peace for the wicked."
O islands, listen to me and pay attention, you people from distant lands! The Lord called me before I was born, he mentioned my name while I was still in my mother's womb.
He has made my words as sharp as a sword. He protected me under the shadow of his hand and shaped me like a polished arrow, and he hid me in his quiver.
He said to me, "O Israel, you are my servant, and I will be glorified through you."
But I said, "I have labored in vain, and I have wasted my strength in vain, and for nothing. Yet surely my justice is with the Lord, and my work is with my God."

Now the Lord, who formed me in the womb to be his servant and bring Jacob back to him, even though Israel has not returned, says, that I will be glorious in the Lord's eyes, and my God will be my strength.

He said, "It is no small thing for you to lift up the tribes of Jacob and restore the protected survivors of Israel. I will also make you a light to the Gentiles so that my salvation reaches the ends of the earth."

This is what the Lord, the redeemer of Israel and his Holy One, says to the one who is despised and rejected by nations, and who is a servant of rulers, "Kings will stand up when they see you, and princes will bow down because of the faithful Lord, the Holy One of Israel, who has chosen you."

This is what the Lord says, "I heard you at the accepted time, and I helped you on the day of salvation. I will protect you and make a covenant with you for the people, to establish the earth, and to restore the inheritance of desolate heritages."
So that you will say to the prisoners, "Come out!" and to those in darkness, "Show yourselves!" They will find food along the road, and their pastures will be on every high hill.
They will not go hungry or thirsty, and the heat of the sun will not harm them. Because the One who has compassion on them will guide them and lead them to springs of water.
I will make roads through all my mountains, and my highways will be glorified.
Behold! They are coming from far away, from the north and the west, and even from the land of Sinim.
O heavens sing out, and O earth rejoice and be joyful! Let the mountains burst out singing! Because the Lord has comforted his people and will show mercy to those who are afflicted.
But Zion said, "The Lord has abandoned me, and my Lord has forgotten me."
So the Lord declares, "Can a mother forget her nursing child, or have no compassion for the child she gave birth to? She may forget, but I will never forget you.
Behold, I have engraved you on the palms of my hands, and your walls are always before me.
Your children will return quickly, and those who destroyed you will leave you.
Lift up your eyes and look around, everyone is gathering together to come to you. As surely as I live, you will wear them all as if they were jewelry, like a bride does.
Because your ruined and desolate lands, the land of your destruction, will soon be too crowded for your people, and those who devoured you will be far away.
The children born during your exile will say, 'This place is too small for us, you must give us more room to live!'

Then in your heart, you will ask yourself, 'Who gave me all these children? I was childless, bereaved, exiled, rejected, and wandering around all alone. So, who raised them, and where did they come from?'"
This is what the Lord God says, "I will raise my hand to the Gentiles and lift my banner to the people. They will bring your sons in their arms and carry your daughters on their shoulders.

Kings will be your caregiving fathers, and their queens will nurse you. They will face the ground and bow down to you, and they will lick the dust from your feet. Then you will know that I am the Lord, because those who wait for me will never be ashamed."
Can the strong be robbed of their prey, or lawful captives be set free?
But the Lord says, "Yes, even the captives will be taken away from the strong, and the prey of the ruthless will be rescued, because I will fight those who fight you, and I will save your children.

I will feed your oppressors their own flesh, and they will be drunk on their own blood, as if they were drinking wine. Then everyone will know that I, the Lord, am your savior and rescuer, the Mighty One of Jacob."

This is what the Lord says, "Where is your mother's divorce decree, the one I gave her when I sent her away, or to which of my creditors did I sell you? Behold, you have sold yourselves because of your own wickedness, and your mother was sent away because of your sins.

So, why was there no one there when I came? Why did no one answer when I called? Is my hand too weak to rescue you? Do I lack the strength or power to save? Behold, with my reprimand I dry up the oceans, and I turn the rivers into a wilderness. Their fish die of thirst, rot, and stink from lack of water.
I clothe the heavens with darkness, and I make sackcloth their covering."
The Lord God has given me wise speech, so I know how to encourage the weary. Morning by morning he awakens me, and opens my ears to listen like a student.
The Lord God has opened my ears, and I was not rebellious, nor did I turn back.
I offered my back to my attackers, and my cheeks to those who pulled out my hair. I did not hide my face from insults and spitting.
Because the Lord God will help me, so I will not be confused. That's why I have set my face like stone, and I know I that will not be ashamed.
The one who justifies me is near, so who will argue with me? Let my accuser and I face one another. Is he my accuser? Let him approach to me.
Behold, the Lord God will help me, so who will condemn me? They will all grow old like wornout clothes, and the moths will eat them up.
Who among you fears the Lord and obeys his servant's voice? Even if you walk in darkness and have no light, trust in the name of the Lord and rely on your God.

Behold, all of you who kindle your own fire and surround yourselves with sparks, walk in the light of your fire and the sparks you have ignited. This is what you will receive from me, you will lie down in sorrow.
Listen to me, you who pursue righteousness and seek the Lord. Look to the rock from which you were cut and to the quarry pit from which you were dug.
Look to Abraham, your father, and to Sarah who gave birth to you. I called him alone, blessed him, and made increased his descendants.

Because the Lord will comfort Zion, he will comfort all her ruined places. He will make her wilderness like Eden and her desert like the Lord's garden. Joy and happiness will be found there, with thanksgiving and songs of praise.
Listen to me, my people and nation. Because a law will come from me, and my justice will become a light to the nations.
My righteousness is near, my salvation has gone out, and my arms will judge the nations. The islands will wait for me, and they will trust in my strong arm.

Lift your eyes up to the heavens and look at the earth below. The heavens will vanish like smoke, and the earth will grow old like a worn garment. Its inhabitants will die the same way, but my salvation will last forever, and my righteousness will never be abolished.
Listen to me, you who know what is righteous, the people who carry my law in their hearts do not fear the disrespect of men, nor do they fear their insults.
Because moths will eat them like a garment, and worms will devour them like wool. But my righteousness will last forever, and my salvation will continue from one generation to the next.
Wake up, and put on strength, O arm of the Lord. Wake up as in the ancient days of the past, like the descendants of long ago. Was it not you Lord, who cut Rahab and wounded the dragon?
Was it not you Lord, who dried up the sea, the waters of the great deep, and made a path through the depths for the redeemed to cross over?

That's why the Lord's rescued people will return. They will be singing when they return to Zion, crowned with everlasting joy. They will obtain joy and happiness, and sorrow and mourning will flee away.
Yes, I the Lord am the one who comforts you. So why are you afraid of men who will die, and of the son of man who is made like grass?

You have forgotten the Lord your maker, who stretched out the heavens and laid the foundations of the earth. You live in constant fear every day because of the oppressor's fury, as if he were ready to destroy. But where is the oppressor's fury now?
The exiled captive is eager to be freed, so that he will not die in the pit nor go hungry.
But I am your Lord God, who divided the sea and its roaring waves, and his name is the Lord of Hosts.
I have put my words in your mouth and covered you with the shadow of my hand, so that I may plant the heavens, lay the foundations of the earth, and say to Zion, "You are my people."
Wake up O Jerusalem, and stand up! O Jerusalem, you who have drunk from the fury of the Lord's cup, you drank the dregs from the cup of trembling, and wrung them out.
There is no one to guide her among all the sons she bore, and no one to take her by the hand among all the children she has raised.
These two disasters have come upon you, who will mourn for you? Devastation and destruction, famine and the sword, who can I send to comfort you?
Your sons have collapsed, they lie at every street corner like a wild bull caught in a net. They are filled with the Lord's fury, and the reprimands of your God.
So listen to this now, you who are afflicted and drunk, but not with wine.

Your Lord God who defends his people has spoken, and this is what he has said, "Look, I have taken the cup of trembling from your hand, even the wrathful dregs of my cup of fury. You will never drink from it again.
Instead, I will give it to those who oppressed you, those who said to your soul, 'Bow down so we can walk all over you,' and you made your back like the ground, like a street for them to walk on."
Awake, awake, put on your strength, O Zion, put on your beautiful garments, O Jerusalem, the Holy city, because from now on there will no more come into you the uncircumcised and the unclean.
Shake yourself from the dust, rise, and sit down, O Jerusalem, loose yourself from the groups of your neck, O captive Daughter of Zion.
For in this says the Lord, you have sold yourselves for nothing, and you will be rescued without money.
For in this says the Lord God, my people went down previously into Egypt to travel there, and the Assyrian oppressed them without cause.
So what have I here, says the Lord, that my people are taken away for nothing? They that rule over them make them to howl, says the Lord, and my name is blasphemed continuously every day.
And for that reason my people will know my name, and for that reason they will know in those days that I am he that does speak, behold it is I.
How beautiful are the feet of those who preach peace and salvation on the mountains and bring good news of good will and says to Zion, "Your God reigns!"
Your watchmen will lift up the voice, with the voice together will they sing, because they will see eye to eye, when the Lord brings you back to Zion.
Suddenly burst out into joy, sing together, you waste places of Jerusalem, because the Lord has comforted his people, he has rescued Jerusalem.
The Lord has made bore his Holy arm in the eyes of all the nations, and all the ends of the earth will see the salvation of our God.
Come out from among them and separate yourself from them, do not touch anything unclean, and those who carry the Lord's vessels must be clean.
For you will not leave with haste, nor go by flight, because the Lord will go before you, and the God of Israel will be your rereward.
Behold, my servant will deal prudently, he will be glorified and extolled and be very high.
As many were astonished at you, his visage was so marred more than any man, and his form more than the sons of men.
So he will he sprinkle many nations, and kings will shut their mouths because of him. And those who were not told about him will see, and those who have not heard of him will understand.
Lord, who has believed our report? And to whom has the Lord's powerful arm been revealed?

For the Messiah will grow up before the Lord like a tender young plant, or a root from the dry ground. He has no royal form and he is not attractive. When we see him, his appearance has no beauty that would make us desire him.
He is a man of many sorrows, familiar with grief and he is despised and rejected by men. We despised him and turned our backs on him, and we did not respect him.
Surely he carried our grief and sorrows, but we thought he was stricken, defeated, and afflicted by God.
But he was wounded and bruised for our sin and wickedness. The punishment that brought us peace was upon him, and by his stripes we are healed.
We are all like sheep that have gone astray. Each of us has turned to our own ways, and the Lord has laid all of our immoralities on the Messiah.
He was oppressed and afflicted, but he did not open his mouth. He was led like a lamb to the slaughter, or a silent sheep standing before its shearers.
He was taken from prison and unjust judgment. Who can declare his descendants? For he was removed from the land of the living, and punished for the sins of my people.
He was put in the grave with the wicked and the rich when he died, even though he had committed no violence nor spoken any lies.

But it pleased the Lord to bruise him and cause him grief. When you make his life a sacrifice for sin, he will see his offspring and prolong his life, and the Lord's pleasure will prosper through him.
After his suffering for their wickedness, he will see the labor of his soul and he will be satisfied. Through his knowledge, my righteous servant will justify many, because he will carry their sins.

Therefore I will give him a portion with the great, and he will divide the plunder with the strong, because he has poured out his soul unto death, and he was numbered among the sinners, and he bore the sins of many, and he interceded for the transgressors.
"Rejoice, you childless woman who has never given birth or gone through labor. Sing loudly and rejoice, because the abandoned woman has more children than the married woman," says the Lord.
"Enlarge your tent and its surroundings. Stretch out the curtains of your homes, do not hold back. Lengthen your ropes and strengthen your stakes.
Because you will spread out to the left and to the right. Your descendants will inherit the Gentiles' possessions, and they will live in the deserted cities.

Fear not, because you will not be put to shame. Do not be confused, because you will not be disgraced. You will forget the shame of your youth, and you will no longer remember the sorrows of your widowhood.
For your creator is your husband, and the Lord of Hosts is his name. Your Redeemer is the Holy One of Israel, he will be called the God of the whole earth.
Because the Lord has called you back like an abandoned and heartbroken woman, like a wife who married young and was then rejected," says your God.
"For I abandoned you for a brief moment, but with great mercy I will bring you back.
In a surge of anger I hid my face from you for a moment, but with everlasting kindness I will show you mercy," says the Lord, your rescuer.
"Because this is like the days of Noah to me. For I have sworn that the waters of Noah would never again flood the earth, so I have sworn that I would not be angry with you nor rebuke you.
Even though the mountains may be removed and the hills may shake, my love will never leave you, and my covenant of peace will never be removed," says the Lord, who has mercy on you.
