"O you who are afflicted, uncomforted, and tossed about by violent storms, behold I will lay your stones with beautiful colors, and your foundations with sapphires.
I will make your windows from agates, your gates from sparkling jewels, and all your border walls from precious stones.
All your children will be taught by the Lord, and their peace will be great.
You will be established in righteousness, and you will be far from terror and oppression, because you will not fear and it will not come near you.
Look, people may gather unite you, but it will not be my doing. But whoever attacks you will fall because of you.
Behold, I created the blacksmith who fans the coals and forges weapons as his work. I also created the destroyer to bring ruin.
No weapon formed against you will succeed, and you will condemn every voice that accuses you. This is the heritage of the Lord's servants, and their righteousness comes from me," says the Lord.
Anyone who is thirsty, come to the water, even if you have no money, come, buy food, and eat. Yes, come and buy wine and milk without cost.
Why do you spend money on what is not food, and why do you work hard for that which does not satisfy? Listen closely to me, eat what is good, and let your soul delight in rich abundance.
Turn your ear to me then come and listen, and your soul will live. I will make you an everlasting promise which includes the faithful mercies that I promised David.
Behold, I have made him a witness to the people, and to be their leader and commander.
You will call out to a nation you do not know, and nations that do not know you will come running, because of your Lord God, the Holy One of Israel, because he has glorified you.
Seek the Lord while he can still be found, call on him while he is near.
Let the wicked abandon their ways, and the unrighteous man abandon his thoughts. Let them return to our Lord, who will have mercy on them, and they will return to our God, who forgives abundantly.
Because the Lord says, "My thoughts are not your thoughts, and my ways are not your ways.
Just as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways, and my thoughts are higher than your thoughts.
Just like the rain and the snow fall from heaven and do not return without watering the earth, making it sprout and grow, giving seed to the sower and bread to the eater.
So my word that leaves my mouth will be, and it will not return empty. But it will accomplish what I want it to accomplish, and it will prosper the purpose for which I sent it.
Because you will be led away with joy and in peace. The mountains and hills will sing before you, and all the trees will applaud.
Instead of thorns, fir trees will grow, instead of briers, myrtle trees will sprout. This will be an everlasting sign to honor the Lord, a sign that will never be erased."
This is what the Lord says: "Maintain your righteousness and do what is justice, because my salvation is nearly here, and my righteousness will be revealed soon.
Blessed is the man who does this, and the son of man who holds fast to it and keeps the Sabbath without polluting it, and refrains from doing evil.
Nor let the son of a foreigner who has joined himself to the Lord say, "The Lord has completely separated me from his people." And do not let a eunuch say, "Behold, I am just a dry tree."
For this is what the Lord says, "To the eunuchs who keep my Sabbaths, choose the things that please me, and hold fast to my covenant.
I will give them, in my house and within my walls, a memorial and a name better than sons or daughters. I will give them an everlasting name that will never be cut off.

Also to the foreigners who bind themselves to the Lord to serve him, to love the Lord's name, and to be his servants, and everyone who keeps the Sabbath without polluting it and who hold fast to my covenant.

I will even bring them to my holy mountain and give them joy in my house of prayer. Their burnt offerings and sacrifices will be accepted on my altar, for my house will be called a house of prayer for all people."
The Lord God, who gathers the Israelis exiles says, "I will gather still others to him, besides those I have already gathered to him."
All you beasts of the field, come and devour, all you beasts of the forest.
Israel's watchmen are blind, they are all ignorant. They are dumb dogs that cannot bark. They lie around sleeping and dreaming, yes, they love to sleep.
They are greedy dogs, which are never satisfied. They are shepherds who lack understanding, each one turns to his own way, each seeks his own gain.
And they all say, "Come, let's get some wine! Let's drink our fill of strong drink! And tomorrow will be just like today, only much more abundant!"
The righteous perish, and no one cares. Merciful people are taken away, and no one considers that the righteous are being spared from the evil to come.
He will enter into peace, they will rest in their beds, and each one walks in his honesty.
But come here, you sons of the sorceress, offspring of the adulterer and the whore.
Whom do you stand against? Against whom do you open your mouth wide and stick out your tongue? Are you not the children of rebellion, and the offspring of a lie?
You burn yourselves with idols under every green tree, slaughtering the children in the valleys beneath the cliffs of the rocks.
Your portion is among the smooth stones of the stream, they are your lot. You have poured out drink offerings to them and offered bread offerings. Should I be comforted by these?
You have placed your bed on a high and lofty mountain, where you went up to offer your sacrifices.

You have set up a memorial to yourself behind the doors and doorposts. Because you have uncovered yourself to someone other than me, you climbed up, and enlarged your bed and made a covenant with them. Because you loved their bed when you saw it.
You went to the king with ointment, increased your perfumes, sent your messengers far away, and you prostituted yourself even into hell.
You grew weary from your long journey, yet you never said, "There is no hope!" You found life in your own strength, so you were not grieved.
Who do you fear that made you lie and not remember me, and did not take it to heart? Have I not held my peace for a long time, and still you do not fear me?
I will expose your righteousness and your works, because they will not profit you.

When you cry out, your collection of idols will not save you. The wind will carry them all away, and your vanity will take them away. But whoever trusts in me will inherit the land and possess my holy mountain.
It will be said, "Build it up, and prepare the way! Remove every stumbling block from my people's path."

For the high and exalted One, who lives forever, whose name is Holy says this, "I dwell in a high and holy place, but also with the one who is remorseful and humble in spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble and to revive the heart of the remorseful.
I will not accuse you forever, nor will I always be angry, because the spirit and the souls which I have made would grow faint before me.
Because of his selfish immorality and greed, I was angry and I defeated him. I hid my face in anger, yet he stubbornly kept going in the way of his own heart.
I have seen his ways, and I will heal him. I will guide him and restore comfort to him and to those who mourn for him.
The Lord creates the fruit of the lips and he says, "Peace, to those far and near, and I will heal them.
But the wicked are like the stormy sea that cannot be stilled, and its waters churn up mud and dirt."
And my God says, "There is no peace for the wicked."
Cry out loudly and do not hold back, raise your voice like a trumpet. Show my people their transgressions and show the house of Jacob their sins.

They seek me every day and delight in learning my ways, as if they were a righteous nation that had not abandoned their God's laws. They ask me for just decisions and they take delight in approaching God.

That's why they say, "We have fasted, so why did you not notice? We have humbled our soul, so why have you not paid attention?" But on your fasting day, you still pursue your own pleasure, and demand hard labor from others.
Behold, you fast only to argue and debate, and to defeat others with wicked fists. You are not fasting today in a way that will make your voice heard in heaven.

Is this the kind of fast that I have chosen, or a day for a man to humble his soul? Is it just for him to bow his head like a reed and spread sackcloth and ashes underneath himself? Do you call that a fast, and an acceptable day to please the Lord?
Is not this the fast I have chosen? To break the chains of wickedness, to remove heavy burdens, to free the oppressed, and to shatter every yoke?
Is it not to share your food with the hungry and bring the homeless poor into your home? When you see someone without clothes, you clothe them, and do not turn away from your own flesh and blood?
Then your light will shine like the morning, and your healing will come quickly. Your righteousness will go before you, and the Lord's glory will protect you from behind.
Then you will call, and the Lord will answer. You will cry out, and he will say, "Here I am." If you remove the burdensome yoke from among you, stop pointing fingers, and speaking vanity.
If you offer your soul to the hungry and help those in need, then your light will shine in the obscurity, and your gloomy darkness will be like the day at noon.
The Lord will always guide you. He will satisfy your soul in droughts and fatten your bones. You will be like a well-watered garden, like a spring whose water never runs dry.

And your people with you will rebuild the ancient ruins. You will restore the foundations laid by many descendants long ago. You will be called the repairer of broken walls, the one who restores the streets to live on.

If you stop trampling the Sabbath and doing whatever you please on my holy day, and if you call the Sabbath a delight, the Lord's holy honorable day, and you honor him by not doing your own things, nor speaking your own words,
Then you will find joy in the Lord, and I will make you ride on the heights of the earth, and I will feed you with the inheritance of your father Jacob, because the Lord has spoken.
Behold, the Lord's arm is not too short to save, nor is his ear too dull to hear.
But your wickedness has created a separation between you and your God, and your sins have hidden his face from you, so he will not hear you.
Because your hands are stained with blood and your fingers are defiled with immorality, your lips have spoken lies, and your tongue has muttered perversity.
No one calls for justice or pleads for truth, they trust in vanity and speak lies. They conceive mischief and give birth to immorality.
They hatch viper eggs and weave spiderwebs. Whoever eats their eggs dies, and from a viper breaks out from a crushed egg.
Their webs will not become clothing, nor will they be able to cover themselves with their deeds. Their deeds are acts of immorality, and their hands are full of violence.
Their feet run toward evil, and they hurry to shed innocent blood. Their thoughts are immoral, and their paths are marked by ruin and destruction.
They do not know the way to peace, and there is no justice in their lives. They have made crooked paths for themselves, and whoever goes there will not know peace.
And that's why justice is so far from us, and righteousness does not reach us. Because we hope for brightness and wait for the light, but we only see obscure darkness, and we walk in gloomy darkness.
We grope for the wall like a blind person, and we stumble as if we had no eyes. We stumble at noon as if it were night, and we are like dead men in desolate places.
We all roar like bears and mourn bitterly like doves. We look for justice and salvation, but there is none, because it is far from us.
For our transgressions before you are many, and our sins testify against us. Because our transgressions are with us, and we know all about our wickedness.
We have transgressed and lied against the Lord, and we have turned away from our God, speaking of oppression and rebellion, and from our hearts we have conceived and uttered lies.
And so justice has turned back, and righteousness stands far away. For truth has fallen in the street, and fair equity cannot enter.
Yes, truth fails, and whoever tries to avoid evil is plundered. The Lord saw this, and he was displeased because there was no justice.
He saw that there was no man, and he was astonished that no one interceded. So his own arm brought him salvation, and his righteousness sustained him.
Because he put on righteousness like a high priest's jeweled vest and a helmet of salvation on his head. He put on garments of vengeance for clothing and wrapped himself in a zealous cloak.
He will repay them and the islands according to their deeds, he will send fury and retribution to his adversaries and enemies.
So they will fear the name of the Lord from the west and his glory from the rising of the sun. When the enemy comes in like a flood, the Lord's spirit will raise a standard against him.
And the Lord says, "The rescuer will come to Zion and to those in Jacob who turn from their transgressions."

Furthermore says the Lord, "As for me, this is my covenant with them. My Spirit that is upon you and my words which I have put in your mouth, will not depart from your mouth, nor from the mouth of your descendants, nor from the mouth of your descendants' descendants, from now on and forever."
Arise and shine, for your light has come, and the glory of the Lord has risen upon you.
For behold, deep darkness will cover the earth and the peoples, but the Lord will rise upon you, and his glory will be seen on you.
And the Gentiles will come to your light, and kings will be drawn to the brightness of your rising.
Lift up your eyes and look all around, they all gather together to come to you. Your sons will come from far away, and your daughters will be nursed by your side.
Then you will see and everything will flow together, your heart will fear and be enlarged, because the ocean's abundance will be brought to you, and the Gentiles' forces will come to you.
A multitude of camels from Midian and Ephah will cover you. Everyone from Sheba will come, bringing gold and incense, and they will proclaim the Lord's praises.

All the flocks of Kedar will be gathered to you, together with the rams of Nebaioth which will be brought to minister to you, as an acceptable sacrifice on my altar, and I will glorify my glorious home.
Who are these that fly like a cloud and like the doves to their windows?

Surely the islands will wait for me, and the ships of Tarshish will be the first to bring your sons from afar, along with their silver and gold, for the name of the Lord your God, and for the Holy One of Israel, because he has glorified you.
Foreigners will rebuild your walls, and their kings will serve you. Because in my anger I defeated you, but in my favor, I have had mercy on you.
Therefore, your gates will always be open, they will not be shut day or night, so that people may bring you the Gentiles' forces, so that their kings may be led in.
For the nations and kingdoms that will not serve you, will perish, and those nations will be utterly destroyed.
The glory of Lebanon will come to you, the fir tree, the pine tree, and the boxwood shrub all together, to beautify my sanctuary place, and I will make the place where I rest my feet glorious.

The sons of those who oppressed you will also come bowing down to you, and everyone who despised you will bow down at the soles of your feet. They will call you the City of the Lord, the Zion of the Holy One of Israel.
Even though you have been forsaken and hated, with no one passing through you, I will make you an eternal excellence, and a joy for many generations.
You will drink the Gentiles' milk and you will be nursed at the breasts of kings. Then you will know that I, the Lord, am your savior and your rescuer, the Mighty One of Jacob.

Instead of brass I will bring gold, and instead of iron I will bring silver. Instead of wood I will bring bronze, and instead of stones, I will bring iron. I will make your officers peace and I will make your tax collectors righteousness.
Violence will no longer be heard in your land, nor ruin or destruction within your borders. You will call your walls Salvation and your gates Praise.
The sun will no longer be your light by day, nor will the moon shine on you for brightness. Instead, the Lord will be your everlasting light, and your God will be your glory.
Your sun will never set again, and your moon will not wane, for the Lord will be your everlasting light, and the days of your sorrow will be ended.
All your people will be righteous, and they will inherit the land forever. They are the branch of my planting, the work of my hands, so that I may be glorified.
The least of you will become a thousand, and the smallest one a mighty nation. I, the Lord, will make it happen quickly in his time.

The Spirit of the Lord God is on me, because the Lord has anointed me to preach good news to the poor. He has sent me to comfort the broken hearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and freedom to those in prison.
To proclaim the year of the Lord's acceptance, and the day of our God's vengeance, in order to comfort all who mourn.

To provide for those who mourn in Zion, to give them a crown of beauty instead of ashes, the oil of joy instead of mourning, and a garment of praise instead of a spirit of sadness. They will be called the oaks of righteousness, a planting of the Lord, so that he might be glorified.
They will rebuild the ancient wasted ruins and restore the formerly devastated places, and they will rebuild the wasted cities that have been devastated for many generations.
Foreigners will stand and feed your flocks, and the sons of aliens will be your farmers and your vineyard managers.
But you will be called the Lord's priests, and men will call you our God's ministers. You will feed on the Gentiles' wealth, and you will boast in their riches.

Instead of your shame, you will receive a double portion, and instead of confusion, you will rejoice in your inheritance. And that's why they will possess a double portion in their own land, and everlasting joy will belong to them.
For I, the Lord, love justice, and I hate robbery as a burnt offering. I will direct their work in truth, and I will make an everlasting covenant with them.
Their descendants will be known among the Gentiles, and their offspring will be known among the people. Everyone who sees them will acknowledge that they are a people that the Lord has blessed.

I rejoice greatly in the Lord, my soul will be joyful in my God. For he has clothed me with salvation garments and covered me in his robe of righteousness, like a bridegroom wears ornaments on his head or a bride adorns herself with jewels.
For as the soil makes the sprout come up and a garden causes seeds to grow, so the Lord God will make righteousness and praise spring up before all nations.
For Zion's sake, I will not hold my peace, for Jerusalem's sake, I will not rest until its righteousness shines like the dawn, and its salvation is as bright as a burning lamp.
Then the Gentiles will see your righteousness, and all the kings will see your glory. You will be given a new name, one that the Lord's mouth will bestow upon you.
You will also be a crown of glory in the Lord's hand, a royal jeweled crown in your God's hand.

You will no longer be called forsaken, nor will your land be called desolate. Instead, you will be called Hephzibah, and your land will be called Beulah, because the Lord delights in you, and your land will be his bride.
Because as a young man marries a young woman, your sons will marry you. And just as a bridegroom rejoices over his bride, so your God will rejoice over you.
O Jerusalem, I have stationed watchmen on your walls, they will never hold their peace, day or night. You who remind the Lord of his promises, do not remain silent.
Give him no rest until he establishes Jerusalem and makes her the praise of the earth.

The Lord has sworn by his right hand and by the strength of his mighty arm and said, "I will no longer give your grain as food for your enemies, and foreigners will no longer drink your wine for which you have labored."
But instead, those who gather the harvest will eat it and praise the Lord. Those who gather the grapes will drink the wine in my holy courtyards.
Go through the gates, and prepare the way for the people. Build up the highway, clear the stones, and raise a banner for the people.
Behold, the Lord has proclaimed to the end of the earth and said, "Say to Daughter Zion, 'Look, your salvation is coming! Look, his reward is with him, and his work is before him.'"
They will be called, the Lord's redeemed by the holy people. And you will be called, sought after, and a city not forsaken.
Who is this coming from Edom, with dyed garments from Bozrah? Gloriously dressed, marching in the greatness of his strength? It is me, the one who speaks in righteousness and power to save.
Why are your clothes red, and your garments look like someone who has been treading in the winepress?
Because I have trodden the winepress alone with no one to help me. So I crushed them in my anger and trampled them in my fury. Their blood splattered on my garments, and I stained all my clothes.
Because the day of vengeance was in my heart, and the year of my redemption has come.
I looked, but there was no one to help, and I wondered why there was no one to support me. So my own arm brought salvation to me, and my fury upheld me.
I will trample the people in my anger, and make them drunk in my wrath, and I will bring down their strength out to the earth.

I will mention the Lord's loving kindnesses and praises, and everything that he has granted us, and the great goodness toward the House of Israel, which he has given them through his mercy and the abundance of his loving kindness.
Because he said, "Surely they are my people, children who will not lie." So he became their savior.
In all their suffering, he suffered too, and the angel of his presence saved them. In his love and compassion, he rescued them, and he and carried them all the days of his old age.
But they rebelled and frustrated the Lord's holy spirit. So he turned into their enemy, and he fought against them.
Then he remembered the days of old, the old days when he brought Moses, the shepherd of his flock and his people through the sea? Where is the one who put his holy spirit in them?
Who led them by the right hand of Moses, with his glorious arm, dividing the waters before them to make an everlasting name for himself?
Who led them through the depths like a horse in the wilderness, so that they would not stumble?
Like a beast descending into a valley, the spirit of the Lord gave him rest. So you led your people, to make a glorious name for yourself.

Look down on me from your holy and glorious home in heaven and see me. Where is your zeal and your strength, and the sound of your bowels and mercies toward me? Are your tender mercies withheld from me.
O Lord, there is no doubt that you are our father, even though Abraham is ignorant of us and Israel does not recognize us. O Lord, you are our father and our rescuer, your name is everlasting.
O Lord, why have you made us stray from your ways, and hardened our hearts from fear of you? Return for the sake of your servants, the tribes of your inheritance.
Your holy people possessed your sanctuary only for a little while, and our enemies have trampled it.
We are yours, and you never ruled over them, they were not called by your name.
O Lord, if only the heavens were torn open and brought down, so that the mountains would flow down in your presence.
Like a burning fire melts and boils water, to make your name known to your enemies, so that the nations would tremble in your presence!
When you did the terrible things we were not expecting, you came down and the mountains quaked in your presence.
For since the beginning of the world, men have not understood, ears have not heard, and eyes have not seen any other God. Behold what God has prepared for those who wait for him.
You come to the meet those who rejoice and do what is righteous, those who remember your ways. Because you were angry when we sinned, and those who continue in your ways will be saved.
But we have all become like one who is unclean, and all our righteousness is like filthy rags, and we all fade away like a leaf, and our wickedness blows us away like the wind.
No one calls on your name or makes an effort to take hold of you, because you have hidden your face from us, and you have given us over to our wickedness.
But now, O Lord, you are our father. We are the clay, you are the potter, and we are all the work of your hand.
Lord do not be angry or remember our immorality forever. Behold, we beg you to see us because we are all your people.
Your holy cities have become a wilderness, Zion is a wilderness, and Jerusalem is a place of desolate ruins.
Our beautiful and holy house, where our fathers praised you, has been burned with fire, and all of our pleasant things have been laid to waste.
O Lord, will you refrain yourself in the face of these things, and will you hold your peace and afflict us more than we can bear?
I was found by those who did not look for me, and I was made obvious to those who did not ask for me. So I said to a nation that was not called by my name, "Behold, I am here."
I have held out my hands all day long to a disobedient and rebellious people, who walk in a way that is not good and follows after their own thoughts.
These people constantly provoke me to anger to my face, who offer sacrifices in gardens and burn incense on brick altars.
They remain among the graves and spend their nights in tombs. They eat pig's meat, and they have the broth of abominable things in their bowls.
They say, "Stand by yourself and do not come near me, because I am holier than you!" They are smoke in my nostrils, and a fire that burns all day long.
Behold, it is written before me, I will not be silent but will compensate them in full.

For the Lord says, "Your sins and the sins of your ancestors, who have burned incense on the mountains and blasphemed me on the hills, so I will place a full measure of punishment for your former works into your embrace."

So this is what the Lord says, "Like when new wine is found in a cluster of grapes, the one says, 'Do not destroy it, for there is a blessing in it,' and for the sake of my servants, I will not destroy them all.
I will bring one of Jacob's descendants from Judah to inherit my mountains, and the ones I elect will inherit it, and my servants will live there.
Sharon will be a pasture for flocks, and the Valley of Achor will be a place for the herds to lie down, because of my people who have sought me.
But you are one of those who have abandoned the Lord, who forgot my holy mountain, who have prepared a table of chance and furnished their drink offering for those troops.

Therefore, I will add your number to the sword, and you will all bow down to be slaughtered. Because when I called, you did not answer, and when I spoke, you did not listen. But instead, you did evil before me and chose that in which I do not delight."

Therefore, this is what the Lord God says, "Behold, my servants will eat, but you will be hungry. Behold, my servants will drink, but you will be thirsty. Behold, my servants will rejoice, but you will be ashamed.
Behold, my servants will sing with a joyous heart, but you will cry out with a sorrow filled heart and wail in spiritual frustration.
You will leave your name as a curse for my chosen ones, because the Lord God will slay you and call his servants by another name.
Whoever blesses himself on earth will do so in the God of truth, and whoever swears an oath on earth will swear by the God of truth. Because the past troubles are forgotten and hidden from my eyes.
For behold, I am about to create new heavens and a new earth, and the former things will not be remembered or come to mind.
But be glad and rejoice forever in that which I will create. For behold, I will create a rejoicing Jerusalem for her people's joy.
I will rejoice in Jerusalem and take joy in my people, and the sound of weeping and crying will be heard there no more.
No longer will an infant live for only a few days, nor will an old man fail to live out their days. Because the child will live to be 100 years old, and the 100 year old sinner will be cursed.
They will build houses and live in them, and they will plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
They will not build, and another inhabit, they will not plant, and another eat, because like the days of a tree are the days of my people, and my elect will long enjoy the work of their hands.
They will not labor in vain, nor bring forth trouble, because they are the descendants of the Lord's blessed, and their offspring with them.
And before they call, I will answer, and while they are still speaking, I will hear.
The wolf and the lamb will feed together, the lion will eat straw with the bull, and dust will be the serpent's meat. They will not hurt nor destroy on my Holy mountain, says the Lord.
This is what the Lord says, "Heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool. So where is the house that you built for me, and where is my place of rest?
My own hands made all these things, and all of them came into being. But the one I will look to is the person who is poor and has a remorseful spirit, and trembles at my word.

The one who kills an ox is as if he killed a person, the one who sacrifices a lamb, as if he cut off a dog's neck, the one who offers a grain offering, as if he offered pig's blood, the one who burns incense, as if he blessed an idol. Indeed, they have chosen their own ways, and their souls delight in their abominations.

I will choose their punishments and bring their fears upon them, because when I called, no one answered. When I spoke, they did not listen. Instead, they did what was evil in my sight and chose that in which I do not delight."

You who tremble when you hear the Lord's word, hear what the Lord has to say, "Your brothers who hated you and threw you out for my name's sake and said, 'Let the Lord be glorified!' Because he will appear for your joy, and they will be ashamed.
A cities noise, a voice from the temple! It's the voice of the Lord, who gives compensation to his enemies.
Before she went into labor, she gave birth. Before her pain came, she gave birth to a baby boy.

Who has heard of such a thing? Who has seen such things? Can the earth be made to give birth in a single day? Or can a nation be born all at once? For as soon as Zion went into labor, she brought forth her children."
Your Lord God says, "Will I bring you to the point of birth and cause you not to give birth? Or will I cause you to give birth and then close the womb?
Rejoice with Jerusalem and be glad with her, all of you who love her. Rejoice with her for joy, all of you who mourn for her.
So that you may nurse and be satisfied from her comforting breasts, so that you may drink milk and be delighted with the abundance of her glory."

For this is what the Lord says, "I am going to extend peace to her like a river and the glory of the Gentiles will be like a flowing stream. Then you will nurse, you will be carried at her side, and you will be bounced on her knees.
Just as a mother comforts her son, so will I comfort you, and you will be comforted in Jerusalem.
When you see this, your heart will rejoice, and your bones will flourish like a plant. The hand of the Lord will be known to his servants, and his indignation will be known to his enemies.
For behold, the Lord will come with fire and chariots like a whirlwind, he will pour out his anger and he will rebuke with fury and flames of fire.
For the Lord will plead with all flesh with fire and his sword, and many will be slain by the Lord."
And the Lord says, "Those who sanctify and purify themselves in the gardens behind one tree in the middle, eating pig's flesh, and other abominable things, and the mouse, will be consumed together.
Because I know their works and their thoughts. The time will come when I will gather the nations of all languages, and they will come and see my glory.

I will set a sign among them and send some of their survivors to other nations, to Tarshish, Pul, and Lud, who are archers, to Tubal and Javan, to the distant islands that have not heard of my fame nor seen my glory. And they will declare my glory among the Gentiles."

And the Lord says, "They will bring all your brothers on horses, and in chariots, in litters, on mules, and on swift beasts, as an offering to the Lord from all the nations to my holy mountain in Jerusalem, the same way that the Israelis bring their grain offerings in a clean vessel into the Lord's house."
And the Lord says, "I will also choose some of them to be priests and Levites.
For just as the new heavens and the new earth that I will make will remain before me, so will your descendants and your name remain.
And it will come to pass that from one new moon to another, and from one Sabbath to another, all people will come to worship before me.

And they will go out and look upon the corpses of the people who have transgressed against me. For their worm will not die, nor will their fire be quenched, and they will be abhorred by all humanity."
These are the words of Hilkiah's son Jeremiah, who was one of the priests in Anathoth in the land of Benjamin.
The Lord's word came to Jeremiah in the thirteenth year of the reign of Josiah, the son of King Amon of Judah.

The Lord's word came to Jeremiah throughout the days of Jehoiakim, the son of King Josiah of Judah until the end of the eleventh year of Zedekiah, the son of King Josiah of Judah. And until the fifth month of the year that the people of Jerusalem were carried away as captives.
So the Lord's word came to me.
And the Lord said, "Jeremiah, before I formed you in your mother's womb, I knew you, and before you were born I sanctified you, and I ordained you as a prophet to the nations."
Then I said, "Alas, Lord God! I cannot speak, because I am only a child."
But the Lord said to me, "Do not say, 'I am only a child,' because you must go and speak to whoever I send you, and you will say whatever I command you to say.
Do not be afraid of them, because I am with you and I will deliver you!"
Then the Lord reached out his hand and touched my mouth and he said to me, "Behold, I have put my words in your mouth.
See, I have set you over the nations and kingdoms today, to uproot and tear down, to destroy and overthrow, to build and to plant."
Then the word of the Lord came to me again and said, "Jeremiah, what do you see?" And I replied, "I see a branch from an almond tree."
And the Lord said to me again and he said, "You have seen correctly, for I am watching to make sure that my word is hastily fulfilled."
And the word of the Lord came to me one more time again and said, "What do you see?" And I replied, "I see a boiling pot, and it is facing north."
Then the Lord finally said, "An evil will come suddenly and unexpectedly from the north, and it will break out upon all the inhabitants of the land.

Because I will summon all the families from the kingdoms of the north, and they will each come and set up their thrones at the entrance of the gates of Jerusalem. And they will attack her surrounding walls and all the cities of Judah.
And I will speak my judgments against them for all of their wickedness, because they have forsaken me, they have burned incense to other gods, and they have worshiped the works of their own hands.
As for you Jeremiah, prepare to stand up and speak to them about everything I will command you to say. Do not be dismayed by their faces, or I will confuse you before them.
For behold, today I have made you like a fortified city, an iron pillar, and bronze walls against the entire land, against the kings of Judah, its officials, its priests, and the people of the land.
They will fight against you, but they will not prevail, because I am with you and I will deliver you."
Furthermore, the word of the Lord came to me.

And the Lord said, "Go and cry out where Jerusalem can hear you and say, 'This is what the Lord says, "I remember the kindness of your youth, how you loved me like a bride, and you followed me through the wilderness, in a land that was not sown.
Israel was holy to the Lord, the first fruits of his harvest, and everyone who devoured him offended him, and evil will come upon them."'".
O house of Jacob, and all the families of the House of Israel, hear the Lord's word.
For this is what the Lord says, "What immorality did your fathers find in me, that they went so far away from me, and followed after vanity, and became worthless vanity?

Nor did they ask, 'Where is the Lord, who brought us up out of Egypt, who led us through the wilderness, through a land of deserts and ravines, through a land of drought and deep darkness, through a land where no man travels and no man lives?'
I brought you into a buontiful country, to eat its fruit and its good things. But when you entered, you defiled my land and made my inheritance an abomination.

The priests did not ask, 'Where is the Lord?' Those who handle the law did not know me. The pastors also transgressed against me, and the prophets prophesied by Baal and followed things that do not profit."
And the Lord declares, "Therefore, I will plead with you, and with your children's children.
Cross over to the islands of Cyprus and see, send word to Kedar and carefully consider if there has ever been such a thing.
Has a nation ever changed its gods, even though they are not gods? Yet my people have exchanged their glory for something that is worthless.
O you heavens, be astonishd and horribly afraid of this, and be very desolate.
For my people have committed two evils, they have forsaken me, the fountain of living water, and they have dug broken cisterns for themselves, that can't hold water.
Is Israel a servant? Was he born a slave? Why has he been plundered?
The young lions have roared and yelled at him. They have made his land a wasteland, and his cities are burned and uninhabitable.
The people of Noph and Tahpanhes have shaved the crown of your head.
You have brought this on yourself, by forsaking your Lord God when he led you along the way?
Now what will you gain by going to Egypt to drink the waters of the Nile? Or what will you gain by going to Assyria to drink the waters of the Euphrates?

Your own wickedness will correct you, and your backslidings will blame you. So, know and understand that it is an evil and bitter thing that you have forsaken your Lord God, and that you do not fear me.
Because long ago, I broke your yoke and your bonds, and you said, 'I will not transgress.' Yet on every high hill and under every green tree, you wandered about, acting like a prostitute.
But, I planted you as a noble vine, a completely righteous seed. How then did you turn into a strange and degenerate vine to me?
Even if you wash yourself with soda and lots of soap, your immorality is still marked before me."

And the Lord says, "How can you say, 'I am not polluted, and I have not gone after the Baalim?' See your way through the valley, and know what you have done. You are like a swift camel wandering about in her ways.

You are like a wild donkey used to the wilderness, that sniffs the wind at her pleasure, and when she is in heat, who can turn her away? Anyone who seeks her out will not become weary, and in her mating season, they will find her.
Keep your feet from becoming bare and your throat from thirst, but you said, 'There's no hope, because I have loved strangers, and I will chase after them.'
Like a thief who is ashamed when he is caught, so is the House of Israel ashamed, including themselves, their kings, their princes, their priests, and their prophets.

They speak to a block of wood and say, 'You are my father,' and to a stone, 'You gave birth to me.' Because they have turned their backs to me and not their faces, but in their time of trouble, they will say, 'Arise and save us!'
But O Judah, where are the gods you made for yourselves? Let them rise up if they can save you in your time of trouble, because you have as many gods as you have cities."
"So why do you still plead with me? You have all rebelled against me.
In vain, I have struck down your children, they received no correction, and your own sword has devoured your prophets like a destroying lion."

O vain generation, consider the word of the Lord! And hear what the Lord says, "Have I been a wilderness, or a land of darkness to Israel? That's why my people say, 'We are lords, so why should we come to you anymore?'
Can a young woman forget her jewelry, or a bride her wedding dress? Yet my people have forgotten me for countless days.
Why do you make your way so good at seeking love? This is why you have also taught the wicked ones your ways.
The blood of the souls of the poor innocents is found, even on your garments. I did not discover it through a secret search, but on every single one of them.
Yet you say, 'I am innocent, and surely his anger will turn away from me.' Behold, I will plead a case with you because you say, 'I have not sinned.'
Why do you ramble on so much about changing your way? You will be ashamed in Egypt, just as you were ashamed in Assyria.
You will leave there with your hands on your head, for the Lord has rejected those you trust, and you will not prosper with them."

The Lord says, "If a man divorces his wife, and she leaves him to become another man's wife, can he ever return to her? Or, would that land not be completely polluted? But you have played the whore with many lovers, and now you want to return to me, again.

Look up to the high places, and see if there is anyone with whom you have not laid. You have sat by the roadside waiting for your lovers, like an Arabian nomad in the wilderness. You have polluted the land with your whores and wickedness.
Therefore, the showers have been withheld, and there have been no spring rains. You have a whore's forehead, and you have refused to be ashamed.
Will you not from this time forward cry out to me and say, 'My father, you have guided me since my youth?
Will you be angry with me forever until the bitter end?' Behold, you have said these things, and still you have done as many evil things as you could."

The Lord also spoke to me in the days of King Josiah and asked, "Have you seen what that backsliding Israel has done? She went up on every high mountain and under every green tree, and played the whore.
And after she had done all these things, I thought that she would return to me. But she did not return, and her treacherous sister Judah saw it.

And I saw everything that caused Israel to backslide and commit adultery, and I gave her a certificate of divorce and sent her away, but her treacherous sister Judah had no fear and she went and played the whore as well.
Then through her indifference to her prostitution, Israel defiled the land, and committed adultery with stones and trees.
Yet, after all of this her treacherous sister Judah, has not returned to me with her whole heart, because she was only pretending!"
And the Lord spoke to me and said, "The backsliding Israel has shown herself to be more righteous than her treacherous sister Judah."

And the Lord said, "Go, and proclaim these words to the north and say, 'The Lord says, "Return, to me O Israel, and I will not allow my anger to fall upon you, because I am merciful!"'"Then the Lord said, "If you do, I will not be angry with you forever.

If you only acknowledge your immorality, and that you have transgressed against your Lord God. Because you have scattered your ways to strangers under every green tree, and you have not obeyed my voice."
And the Lord says, "Return, O backsliding children, because I am married to you, and I will take one of you from a city, and two of you from a family, and bring you to Zion.
Then I will give you pastors after my own heart, who will feed you knowledge and understanding.

And it will all come to pass, after you have multiplied and increased throughout the land"And the Lord says, "They will no longer discuss the Lord's Ark of the Covenant, they will not remember it, nor will it come to mind. They will not visit it, and they will never make another one.

At that time they will call Jerusalem the throne of the Lord, and all the nations will gather in Jerusalem, to honor the name of the Lord. And they will never walk after the evil imaginations of their evil heart anymore.
In those days the house of Judah will walk with the House of Israel, and they will come together from the land of the north to the land that I have given your fathers as an inheritance.
But I said, 'How can I put you among the children, and give you a pleasant land, a good heritage from all the nations!' And I thought, 'You will call me father, and never turn away from me.'
But just as a wife treacherously leaves her husband, you have betrayed me, O House of Israel."
And the Lord says, "A weeping voice and the pleas of the children of Israel was heard in the high places, because they have perverted their ways and forgotten their Lord God.
Return, you backsliding children, and I will heal your unfaithfulness." Behold, we come to you, because you are our Lord God.
Hoping for salvation from the many hills and mountains, is truly in vain, because Israel's salvation, is only in our Lord God.
Because from our youth, shame has devoured what our fathers have worked so hard for, including their flocks, their herds, their sons, and their daughters.
We lie down in our shame, and our confusion covers us, because we have sinned against our Lord God. And from our youth to this very day, we and our fathers have not obeyed the voice of our Lord God.
The Lord says, "O Israel, if you return to me, and abandon your abominations and put them out of my sight, then you will not be removed.
And if you swear, 'As the Lord lives in truth, judgment, and righteousness,' then the nations will be blessed by him, and they will glory in him."
Because this is what the Lord says to the men of Judah and Jerusalem, "Break up your fallow ground, and do not sow among thorns.

Circumcise yourselves to the Lord, and remove the foreskins of your heart, you men of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem. Or else my fury will come out like fire, and burn so intensely that no one can quench it, because of all your evil deeds."
Proclaim it in Judah and publish it in Jerusalem and say, "Blow the trumpet throughout the land. Cry out and say, 'Gather together and assemble yourselves, and let us flee into the fortified cities.'
Raise the standard flag toward Zion, retire and do not stay, because I will bring evil, and great destruction from the north.
The lion has come up from his thicket, and the destroyer of the Gentiles is on his way. He has left his lair to desolate your land, and your cities will be laid to waste, and become uninhabitable.
So, wear sackcloth, mourn, and wail because the fierce anger of the Lord has not been turned away from us."
And it will come to pass on that day, that the Lord will say, "The king's heart will perish, and the hearts of the princes and priests will be astonished, and the prophets will wonder."
Then I said, "Ah, Lord God! Surely you have completely deceived these people and Jerusalem by saying, 'You will have peace,' while in fact a sword reaches into our soul."
At that time it will be said to these people and to Jerusalem, "A dry wind from the high places in the wilderness blows toward the daughter of my people, but not to fan nor to cleanse.
A strong wind from those places will come to me, and then I will also sentence them."
Behold, he will come up like the clouds, his chariots will belike a whirlwind, and his horses are swifter than eagles. Woe unto us, because we are ruined.
O Jerusalem, wash the wickedness from your heart, so that you may be saved. How long will your vain thoughts remain within you?
For a voice from Dan, publishes and declares affliction from the hills of Mount Ephraim.
And the Lord says, "Behold, mention it to the nations, and publish it in Jerusalem, that spies have come from a distant country, and they raise their voices against the cities of Judah.
And like the keepers of a field, they have her completely surrounded, because she has rebelled against me.
Your ways and your deeds have procured these things for you, because your wickedness is bitter, and it reaches into your heart!"
Oh, my bowels! I have pain in my chest, my heart pounds loudly within me, and I cannot hold my peace. Because my soul has heard the sound of the trumpet, and the alarm of war.
Destruction after destruction cries out, because the whole land has been laid to waste. My tents and my curtains, are suddenly and instantly destroyed.
How long must I see the flag, and hear the sound of the war trumpets?
For my people are foolish, and they do not know me. They are like drunken children, and they have no understanding. They are wise in doing evil, but they have no idea how to do good things.
I looked at the earth, and it was void and formless. I saw the heavens, and they had no light.
I saw the mountains tremble, and all the hills lightly moved.
I looked and I saw that there were no men left, and all the birds of the air had also fled.
I saw that the fruitful land was a wilderness, and all of its cities were broken down before the Lord, by his fierce anger.
For this is what the Lord said, "The whole land will be desolated, yet I will not fully destroy it.
Therefore, the earth will mourn, and the heavens above will be black, Because I have spoken, I have planned it, and I will not repent, nor will I turn back from it.
The whole city will flee from the noise of the horsemen and the archers. They will enter the thickets, and climb up on the rocks, every city will be abandoned, and no one living will be left there.

Once you have been laid to waist, what will you do? Even though you clothe yourself in crimson, adorn yourself with gold jewelry, and paint your face in vain to make yourself beautiful, your lovers will despise you, and they will want to take your life.

For I have heard a voice like that of a woman in labor, and the anguish as if she were giving birth to her first child. The voice of the Daughter of Zion, that makes her wail and spread her hands and say, "Woe is me, for my soul is wearied because of the murderers!"
Run through the back streets and public squares of Jerusalem, and see if you can find a just, knowledgeable, and honest man, who seeks the truth, and if you do, I will pardon the city.
Even though they say, "As the Lord lives," they are lying.

O Lord, do your eyes not see the truth? You have stricken them, but they have not grieved. You have consumed them, but they have refused to accept correction. They have made their faces harder than stone, and they refuse to repent and return.
So I said, "Surely these are poor and foolish people, because they do not know the ways of the Lord, nor the judgments of their God.
I will go speak to the great and powerful men, because they know the ways of the Lord, and their God's judgments, but they too have broken the yoke, and smashed the chains.

Therefore a lion from the forest will kill them, and an evening wolf will lay them to waste. A leopard will prey on their cities, and everyone who goes out there will be torn in pieces. Because they have many transgressions, and their backsliding has increased."

And the Lord says, "How can I pardon you for this? Your children have forsaken me, and sworn by gods that are not gods. After I fully fed them, they committed adultery, and assembled their troops in the prostitute's houses.
They were like well fed horses in the morning, and everyone neighed after his neighbor's wife.
Should I not punish them for these things? And should I not avenge my soul on a nation such as this for these things?
Climb up on her walls and destroy her, do not completely ruin her, but remove her battlements, because they are not the Lord's.
For the House of Israel and the house of Judah have dealt very treacherously against me."
They have lied about the Lord and said, "He will not harm you and he will not let any evil come upon us, nor will we see the sword or famine.
And the prophets are just the blowing wind, and his word is not in them, so let them suffer from their own words."
Therefore, this is what the Lord God of Hosts says, "Because you have said these things, behold I will make my words a fire in your mouth, and these people will be the wood that the fire devours."
Behold O House of Israel, this is what the Lord says, "I will bring a nation against you from far away. It is an ancient but mighty nation, a nation whose language you do not know nor understand.
Their quiver is like a open tomb, and they are all mighty men.

They will devour your harvest and your bread, which should have been for your sons and daughters to eat. They will eat all of your flocks and herds, and they will feed on your vines and fig trees. They will attack your trusted and fortified cities with a sword. And your cities will be impoverished."
Yet the Lord says, "Nevertheless, in those days I will not completely put an end to you.

And when that time comes, you will say, 'Why has our Lord God done all of these things to us?' Then you will answer them and say, 'Since you have forsaken me, and served strange gods in your land, you will serve foreigners in a land that is not your own.'"
Declare this in the house of Jacob, and publish it in Judah.
And say this, "O you foolish and ignorant people, now hear this. You have eyes, but do not see, and you have ears, but do not hear.

Why do you not fear me? Do you not tremble in my presence, the one who placed the sand as a boundary for the sea through a never ending decree. A border that it cannot cross, and even though its waves toss themselves against it, they can not prevail. They roar, but can they not cross over it?
But these people have a rioting and rebellious heart, and they have rioted and left.
Nor have they said in their heart, 'Let us now fear our Lord God, who gives the rain, in its season of both the spring and fall, and he has reserved the weeks of harvest for us.'
Your wickedness have turned these things away, and your sins have deprived you of my good things.
For there are wicked men among my people who lay in wait, like someone who sets snares, they set traps to catch men.
Like a cage full of birds, their house is full of deceit, so they have become rich and powerful.
They have grown fat and shiny, and they have excelled in the deeds of the wicked. They have not judged the fatherless fairly, yet they prosper, and they have not judged the needy righteously."
For this is what the Lord says, "Should I not punish them for these things? Should not my soul be avenged on a nation such as this?
A wonderful and horrible thing has been committed in the land.
The prophets prophesy falsely, and the priests rule through their own means. My people love it that way so much, but what will you do when it all comes to an end?"
O children of Benjamin, gather together and flee from Jerusalem. Sound the trumpet in Tekoa, and set up a signal fire in Beth-Haccerem, because evil and great destruction appears from the north.
I have compared the Daughter of Zion to a beautiful and elegant woman.
The shepherds will come with their flocks to surround her and pitch their tents against her, and they will feed everyone in his place.
Prepare for war against her, rise up and let us attack at noon. Woe unto us, for the daylight is fading away, and the evening shadows grow longer.
Rise up, and let us attack at night, and destroy her palaces.
For this is what the Lord of Hosts says, "Cut down the trees, and raise a siege ramp against Jerusalem, this city needs to be overcome, because she is completely filled with oppression.
She pours out her wickedness, like water flows from a fountain. I constantly hear before me, the sounds of her violence, grief, wounds, and her spoils of war.
O Jerusalem, be forewarned, otherwise my soul will leave you, and I will make you desolate and uninhabited land."
This is what the Lord of Hosts says, "They will thoroughly glean the remnants of Israel as if it were a vine, like a grape harvester puts the grapes into a basket."
Who must I warn, and who will listen to me? Behold, their ear is uncircumcised, and they cannot hear. For behold, the Lord's word has been met with disapproval, and they do not delight in it.

So, I am full of the Lord's fury, and I am weary from holding it in. And this is what the Lord says, "I will pour out my wrath on both the children and the young men abroad. Because even the husband and his wife will be captured, and so will the old and the very old.
Their houses will be turned over to others, along with their fields and wives, because I will stretch out my hand against the inhabitants of the land."
Because the Lord says, "From the least to the greatest of them, everyone has given in to covetousness. And everyone from the prophet to the priest deals deceitfully.
They carelessly feign the healing of my people's wounds while saying, 'Peace, peace,' when there is no peace.

Were they ashamed of the abomination they have committed? No, they were not at all ashamed, nor could they even blush with embarrassment. So, they will fall among the fallen, and when I visit my wrath upon them they will collapse."

This is what the Lord says, "You stand at the crossroads and look, and you ask for the ancient paths and say, 'Where is the good way?' So, walk in the good ways, and you will find rest for your souls. But they said, 'We will not walk there!'
I appointed watchmen over you and said, 'Listen for the sound of the trumpet.' But they said, 'We will not listen!'
Therefore, O nations and congregations listen and learn what is going to happen to them.
O earth listen, and behold I will bring evil on these people, the fruit of their own thoughts, because they have not listened to me, but they have rejected my law.
What use to me, is incense from Sheba or sweet cane from a distant country? Your burnt offerings are unacceptable, and your sacrifices are not sweet to me."
So this what the Lord says, "Behold I will lay obstacles to understanding before these people, and the fathers and sons together will fall on them, friends and neighbors will perish."
And the LORD says, "Behold, people come from the north country, and a great nation will rise up from the ends of the earth.
O Daughter of Zion, they will lay hold of the bow and spear, they are cruel and merciless, their voice roars like the ocean, and they ride horses, arrayed like men ready for war against you."
We have heard the report, and our hands grow feeble. Anguish has taken hold of us with pain, like of a woman in labor.
Do not go out into the fields, nor walk by the road, because the enemy surrounds us with a sword and fear on every side.

O daughter of my people, clothe yourselves in sackcloth, and wallow in ashes. Mourn a most bitter lamentation, as if you were mourning for an only son, because the destroyer will come upon us suddenly.
Then the Lord said, "I have placed you among my people, as a tower and a fortress, so that you may know and try their ways.
They are all grievous rebels, they are as heartless as brass and iron, they slander, and they are all dishonest.
The bellows burn, the lead is consumed by fire, and the burning foundry refines in vain because the wicked have not been removed.
Men will call them rejected silver, because the Lord has rejected them."
This is the word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord.
And the Lord said, "Stand in the gateway of the Lord's house, and proclaim this message, 'Everyone in Judah who enters these gates to worship the Lord, hear the Lord's word.'
This is what the Lord God of Hosts of Israel says, 'Change your ways and your deeds, and I will allow you to live in this place.'
Do not trust in lying words and say, 'This is the temple of the Lord, the temple of the Lord, the temple of the Lord.'
Because, if you really change your ways and deeds, and you thoroughly show good judgement between a man and his neighbor.
If you do not oppress foreigners, the fatherless, or widows. And if you do not shed innocent blood in this place, and you do not walk after other gods at your own peril.
Then, I will allow you to live in this land that I gave to your fathers, forever and ever.
But behold, you continue to trust in lying words, that are not profitable.
Will you steal, murder, commit adultery, lie, burn incense to Baal, and walk after other gods whom you do not know.
And then you come and stand before me in this house which is named after me and say, 'We are delivered, so we can still do all these abominations'?
Has this house, which bears my name become a den of robbers in your eyes? Behold, even the Lord says, 'I have seen it.'
But go now to my place where I first put my name in Shiloh, and see what I did to it because of the wickedness of my people Israel.
And now the Lord says, 'Because you have done all these things that I have spoken to you about over and over again, but you did not listen, and I called you but you did not answer.
Therefore, what I have done to Shiloh, I will also do to this house that bears my name. I will do this to the house in which you trust, the place that I gave to you and your fathers.
And I will throw you out of my sight, as I have thrown out all your brothers, all of Ephraim's descendants.'
So, do not pray for these people, and do not cry or plead for them. Do not intercede with me on their behalf, because I will not hear you.
Do you not see what they are doing in the cities of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem?
The children gather wood, the fathers kindle the fire, and the women knead their dough to make cakes for the queen of heaven. They pour out drink offerings to other gods, to provoke my anger.
And the Lord says, 'Do they provoke my anger, or do they only provoke themselves in their own confusion?'

So the Lord God says, 'Behold my anger and my fury will be poured out on this place, on man, on beast, on the trees of the field, and on the fruit of the ground, and it will burn and it will not be quenched.'
The Lord God of Hosts of Israel says, 'Add your burnt offerings to your other sacrifices, and eat the meat yourselves!'
Because, I did not speak to your fathers nor did I give them commandments about burnt offerings or sacrifices, on the day that I brought them out of the land of Egypt.

But what I commanded them and said was this, 'Obey my voice, and I will be your God, you will be my people and walk in all the ways that I have commanded you, so that everything will be well with you.'
But they did not listen, they listened to the counsel and imaginations of their own evil hearts and went backwards, not forward.
Since the day that your fathers left the land of Egypt until today, I have sent all my servants the prophets to you, over and over again.
Yet they did not listen to me, but stiffened their stubborn neck, and they did worse than their fathers.
So, you must tell them all of these things, but they will not listen, and you will call to them, but they will not answer you.
But you must say to them, 'This is a nation that does not obey their Lord God's voice, nor accept his correction. So, truth has perished, and is not found in their mouths.
O Jerusalem, cut off your hair and throw it away, and mourn in high places, because the Lord has rejected and forsaken the generation of his anger.'
For the Lord says, 'The children of Judah have done evil in my sight, they have set their abominations in the house named after me, and polluted it.

They have built an altar in the high places of Tophet, which is in the Valley of Hinnom, to burn their sons and their daughters in the fire, which is something I never commanded them to do, nor did the thought ever enter my heart.'

So, behold the Lord says, 'The days will come when this place will no longer be called Tophet nor the Valley of Hinnom, but it will be called the valley of slaughter, because they will bury the dead in Tophet, until there is no place left.
And these people's corpses will be meat for the birds of the heaven and for the beasts of the earth, and no one will chase them away.
Then I will remove the sounds of joy and happiness, and the voices of the bride and bridegroom, from the cities of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem, because the land will become a desolation."
And the Lord of Hosts says, "At that time, they will bring the bones of Judah's kings, his princes, the priests, the prophets, and the bones of the inhabitants of Jerusalem, out of their graves.

They will spread their bones before the sun and moon, and all the stars in heaven whom they have loved, served, followed, sought, and worshipped. Their bones will not be gathered nor buried, but they will become dung lying on the ground.
Whoever remains of this evil family will choose death over life, no matter where I have driven them."
Besides that, tell them that this is what the Lord says, "Will a man fall, and not rise up again? Will he turn away and not return?
Why then do the people of Jerusalem always backslide into never ending backsliding? They hold fast to deceit, and they refuse to return to me.

I listened to them and heard, but they did not speak the truth. No man repents of his wickedness and says, 'What have I done?' Everyone has turned to his own devices, like a horse charges into battle.
Yes, even the stork soaring through the heavens knows her appointed seasons. The turtledove, the crane, and the swallow observe their time of migration, but my people do not know the Lord's judgment.
How can you ask, 'Are we not wise, because the Lord's Law is with us?' Since the scribes pen has certainly written in vain.
Because the wise men have rejected the Lord's word, they have been dismayed, trapped, and shamed, so what wisdom do they really possess?

Therefore, I will give their wives and their fields to others. Because from the least of them to the greatest, they all covet the wealth of others, and from the prophet to the priest they all deal dishonestly.
For they have carelessly healed the wounds of my people's daughter and said, 'Peace, peace,' when there is no peace.

Were they ashamed after they committed an abomination? No, they were not at all ashamed, nor could they even blush from embarrassment. So they will fall among the fallen, and when I visit them, they will be thrown down."

And this is what the Lord says, "Therefore, I will surely consume them! There will be no grapes on the vine, nor figs on the fig tree, and the leaves will fall away, and the things that I have given them will pass away from them.

Because the people have said, 'So, why are we just sitting here? Let us flee in silence to the defended cities, because our Lord God has silenced us. He has given us poison water to drink, because we have sinned against the Lord.
We looked for peace and good health, but we have found nothing good, and we have seen nothing but trouble!

The whole land trembles, as the sound of the enemies mighty snorting horses was heard from Dan, because they have come and devoured the land and everything in it, including the city and everyone living there.'"
For the Lord has said, "Behold I will send serpents and vipers among you, which cannot be charmed, and they will bite you.
When I try to comfort my sorrow, my heart is faint within me.

Listen to the crying voice of my people's daughter from a country far away that says, 'Is the Lord no longer in Zion? Has her king left her?' Why have they provoked me to anger with their carved images, and strange vanities?
And the crying voice of my people's daughter said, 'The harvest has passed, the summer has ended, and we have not been saved.'"
For the Lord has said, "Because of the wounds of my people's daughter I have been hurt, and I have become black and astonished.
Is there no balm in Gilead? Are there no physicians there? Why then has the health of my people's daughter not been restored?"
Oh, if only my head were water, and my eyes were a fountain of tears, so that I might weep day and night for my people's slain daughter!
Oh, if only I had a traveling man's place to live in the wilderness, so that I could depart and leave my people! For they are all adulterers, and an assembly of treacherous men.

Then the Lord answered and said, "They bend their tongues like bows to spread lies, but they do not courageously speak the truth on earth. For they proceed from one evil to the next, and they do not know me.
Everyone take heed of your neighbor, and do not trust your brothers, for every brother will completely overthrow you, and every neighbor will spread slander.
And they will each deceive their neighbor, and will not speak the truth, they have taught their tongue to speak lies, and wear themselves out committing immorality.
You live in the midst of deceit, and they refuse to know me through their deceit."
Therefore this is what the Lord of Hosts says, "Behold, I will melt them and try them, because what else can I do for my people's daughter?
Their tongues are like deadly arrows that speak deception. A man speaks of peace to his neighbor, but in his heart he lays in wait to trap him.
Should I not punish them for these things, when I visit them? Should my soul not take vengeance on a nation such as this?

For I will be weeping and wailing for the mountains, and lament over the wilderness homes, because they have scorched so that no one can pass through them. Men will no longer hear the voice of the grazing cattle, and both the birds of the air and the beasts have fled, and they are all gone.
I will make Jerusalem a pile of rubble and a den of dragons. Then I will desolate Judah's cities and leave them uninhabitable.
Which man is wise enough to understand these things? Who has the Lord spoken to and taught how to explain them? Why does the land perish, and burn up like a desert, making it impassable for anyone?"
Then the Lord answered and said, "It is because they have forsaken my law which I set before them. They have not walked in my law, nor have they obeyed my voice.
But they have chased after the imaginations of their own heart, and they have done what their fathers taught them, and followed the teachings of the Baalim false gods."
So this is what the Lord God of Hosts of Israel says, "Behold I will feed wormwood to these people, and give them poison water to drink.
I will also scatter them among the heathen, whom they nor their fathers have known, and I will send a sword after them, until I have consumed them."
And the Lord of Hosts says, "Consider the skilled women in mourning and send for them, so that they may come.
Let them hurry here and wail for us, so that our eyes may overflow with tears, and our eyelids will gush with water.
For the sound of wailing will be heard from Zion that says, 'Oh, how we are destroyed! We are greatly confused, for we have abandoned the land because our homes have been torn down.'"
Now you women must hear the Lord's word! Open your ears to receive the word from his mouth. Teach your daughters to wail, and every one of her neighbors to lament.
For death has climbed up into our windows, and it has entered into our palaces to cut off the children from streets, and the young men from the public squares.

Speak up and say, "This is what the Lord says, 'Men's corpses will fall like dung on the open field, or like a handful of grain that falls during the harvest, and after the harvester finishes no one will pick them up.'"
This is what the Lord says, "Do not let the wise men glory in their wisdom, nor the mighty men in their strength, nor the rich man in his riches.
But let anyone who glories in these things understand and know that I am the Lord who exercises loving kindness, justice, and righteousness on the earth, for I delight in these things."
So this is what the Lord says, "Behold, the days are coming when I will punish all of them whether they are circumcised or uncircumcised.

Egypt, Judah, Edom, Ammon, Moab, and all of those who live in the farthest corners of the wilderness. For all these nations are uncircumcised, and the entire House of Israel is uncircumcised at heart."
O House of Israel, the Lord speaks, so hear his word.
And this is what the Lord says, "Do not learn the ways of the heathen, and do not be shocked by the signs of heaven, because the heathen are shocked by them.
For the people's customs are vain, because one cuts a tree from the forest with an axe, then a craftsman works it and shapes it with his hands.
They inlay it with gold and silver, then fasten it with hammers and nails, so that it cannot move.
They are as honest as a palm tree, but they do not speak, they must be carried, because they cannot walk. Do not be afraid of them, because they can do no evil, nor can they do good."
O Lord, there is no one like you. You are great, and your name is great and mighty.
O King of nations, for if it pertains to you, who would not fear you, because among all the wise men of the nations, and in all their kingdoms, there is no one else like you.
But they are completely wicked, brutal, and foolish and their stock in trade is a doctrine of vanities.

Silver hammered into plates is brought from Tarshish, and gold from Uphaz, the work from a craftsman and the hands of the goldsmith. Their clothes are blue and purple, all the work of skilled workers.
But the Lord is the true God, he is the living God, and an everlasting king. The earth trembles at his anger, and the nations cannot endure his indignation.
And this is what you must say to them, "The gods who have not made the heavens nor the earth, will perish from the earth and from under these heavens."
The Lord made the earth with his power, he established the world through his wisdom, and he has stretched out the heavens to his liking.
When his voice thunders, there is a rush of water in the heavens, and he causes the clouds to ascend from the ends of the earth, he makes lightning with rain, and brings the wind from his treasuries.
Every man is wicked, brutal, and without God's knowledge. Every goldsmith is confused by their carved images, because their molten images are a lie, and there is no breath of life in them.
They are worthless vanity, and the work of errors. In the time of their visitation and punishment, they will perish.
The portion of Jacob is not like them, because God is the maker of all things. Israel is the staff of his inheritance, and his name is the Lord of Hosts.
So, you inhabitants of the fortress, collect all your belongings from the land.
For this is what the Lord says, "Behold, at this time I will sling the inhabitants out of the land and cause them distress, so that they may be captured."
Woe is me, because my painful wound is very grievous! But I said, "This truly is my grief, and I must bear it."
My tabernacle has been destroyed, and all my ropes have been severed. My children have all left me, and they are not here. There is no longer anyone left to pitch my tent or set up my curtains.
For the pastors have become wicked and brutal, and they have not sought the Lord. Therefore they will not prosper, and all their flocks will be scattered.
Behold, the noise of rumors is heard and a great disturbance comes from the north country. And the cities of Judah will be desolated, because it is a den of dragons.
O Lord, I know that a man's ways are not his own, and it is not within any man who walks to direct his own steps.
O Lord, correct me with justice, but not in anger, or else you will bring me to nothing.
Pour out your fury on the heathen who do not know you, and on the families who do not call on your name, because they have devoured and consumed Jacob, and they have desolated his home.
This word came to Jeremiah from the Lord.
And the Lord said, "Hear the words of this covenant, and speak to the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
And say to them, 'This is what the Lord God of Israel says, "Cursed is the man who does not obey the words of this covenant."

I gave your fathers this command when I brought them out the iron foundries of Egypt and I said, "Listen to me and obey my voice, and do everything the way I command you, so that you will be my people, and I will be your God."
So that I may establish the oath which I swore to your fathers, to give them a land flowing with milk and honey, as it is to this day." Then I answered and said, "O Lord, so be it."
Then the Lord said to me, "Proclaim all these words in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem and say, 'Hear the words of the Lord's covenant, and obey them.'
For from the time that I brought them out of the land of Egypt to this very day, I earnestly protested to your fathers over and over again and said, 'Obey my voice!'

But they did not obey me, nor did they listen to me, but they all walked in the imaginations of their evil hearts, and that's why I brought down on them all the words of this covenant, which I commanded them to do, but they did not keep them."
And the Lord said to me, "There is a conspiracy among the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.

They have turned back to the wickedness of their forefathers, who refused to hear my words. And they have followed and served other gods. The House of Israel and the house of Judah have broken the covenant that I made with their fathers.
So this is what the Lord says, 'Behold I will bring evil upon them that they cannot escape, and even though they will cry out to me, I will not listen to them.
Then the cities of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem will go and cry to the gods to whom they offer incense, but those gods will not save them in the time of their trouble.

Because O Judah, your gods are as numerous as your cities. And the shameful altars to shameful things, and the altars you have built to burn incense to Baal, are as numerous as the people in the streets of Jerusalem.'
So do not pray for these people, and do not cry out and lament for them, because I will not hear them when they call out to me in their times of trouble.
What right does my beloved have to cry out to me in my house, since she has been involved with so much obscenity with so many. Can the holy meat save you when you do evil, and then rejoice in it?
The Lord once called you a beautiful green olive tree, with good fruit. But with a great tumultuous noise he will kindle a fire on it, and its branches will be broken.

For the Lord of Hosts, who planted you, has pronounced evil against you, because of the evil that the House of Israel and the house of Judah have brought against themselves, and they have provoked my anger by offering incense to Baal."
And the Lord gave me knowledge and showed me their evil deeds, so then I knew.

But I was like a lamb or an ox that is led to slaughter, and I did not know that they had plotted against me and said, "Let us destroy the tree with its fruit, and we will cut him off from the land of the living, so that his name may is no longer remembered."
O Lord of Hosts, who judges righteously and tries the heart, mind, and soul, let me see your vengeance upon them, because I have revealed my cause to you.
Therefore this is what the Lord says about the men of Anathoth who seek to take your life, "Do not prophesy in the name of the Lord, or you will die by our hand."
