So this is what the Lord of Hosts says, "Behold I will punish them. Their young men will die by the sword, and their sons and daughters will die by famine.
And there will be no survivors, "Because I will bring evil on the men of Anathoth, in the year of their punishment."

O Lord, you are righteous when I plead with you, but let me ask you about your judgments, for what reason do the ways of the wicked prosper? As for those who deal treacherously with others, why are they allowed to be happy?
You have planted them, and they have taken root and they grow and bear fruit, you are close to them in their mouth, but far from their heart, mind, and soul.
But O Lord, you know me, you have seen me, and you have tested my heart toward you. Pull the wicked out like sheep for the slaughter, and prepare them for the day of slaughter.

How long must the land mourn and the grass of every field wither? Because of the wickedness of those who live there, all the birds and beasts have been consumed. And the wicked have said, "For he cannot see when our last day is coming."

And the Lord said, "If you have exhausted yourself trying to run with the footmen, then how can you compete with horses? And if they have worn you out in peaceful land that you have trusted, then how will you do in the Jordan River's flooding?
For if even your brothers from your father's house have dealt treacherously with you, and cried out to the multitude around you. Do not believe them, even though they speak good things about you.
I have forsaken my house and left my heritage, I have turned my soul's dearly beloved over to the hand of her enemies.
My heritage is like a lion in the forest to me and it cries out against me, so I have hated it.
My heritage is like a speckled bird of prey surrounding her with other birds of prey circling against her to me. Gather all the beasts of the field to come and devour her.
Many pastors have destroyed my vineyard, and they have trampled my plot of land under foot. They have turned my pleasant piece of land into a desolate wilderness.
They have desolated it, and since it has been desolated it mourns to me. The whole land has been made a desolation, because no man takes it to heart.
The spoilers have come to all the high places throughout the wilderness, because the Lord's sword will devour the land from one end of it to the other, and no flesh will have peace.
They have sown wheat but harvested thorns, they have felt the pain but they will not profit from it. And they will be ashamed of your revenues because of the Lord's fierce anger."

This is what the Lord says, "All my evil neighbors who attack the inheritance which I have given to my people of Israel as an inheritance, behold I will uproot them from their land, and uproot the house of Judah from among them.
After I have removed them, I will return again and have compassion on them, and return every man to his own heritage and his own land.

And if they diligently learn the ways of my people and swear by my name and say, 'As the Lord lives, just as they taught my people to swear by Baal, then they will be rebuilt in the midst of my people.
But if they will not obey, I will completely uproot and destroy that nation."
This is what the Lord said to me, "Jeremiah, go and get a linen belt and put it around your waist, but do not put it in water."
So I got a belt as the Lord told me, and put it around my waist.
Then the Lord's word came to me a second time.
And the Lord said, "Take the belt the you have around your waist, and take it to the Euphrates River. Hide it there in a crevice in the rocks."
So I went and hid it near the Euphrates River, as the Lord had commanded me.
Many days later the Lord spoke to me and said, "Rise up and go to the Euphrates River, and take the belt from there that I commanded you to hide.
So I went to the Euphrates River, and dug the belt out of the place where I had hidden it, and behold the belt was damaged, and it was completely worthless.
Then the Lord's word came to me again.
And this is what the Lord said, "This is how I will ruin the pride of Judah and the great pride of Jerusalem.

These evil people, who refuse to hear my words, who walk in the imaginations of their own heart, who walk after, serve, and worship other gods. They will be like this worthless belt, which is good for nothing.

For just like that belt clings to a man's waist, I have made the whole House of Israel and the whole house of Judah cling to me. This is so that they might be my people, for my namesake, for my praise, and for my glory, but they would not listen to me.

So speak to them about this and tell them that this is what the Lord God of Israel says, 'Every bottle will be filled with wine,' and when they say to you, 'Do we not certainly know, that every bottle will be filled with wine?

Then you will reply to them and say, 'This is what the Lord says, "Behold I will fill all the inhabitants of this land, even the kings that sit on David's throne, the priests, the prophets, and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem with drunkenness.
And I will dash them against one another, including the fathers and the sons, and I will not pity them, spare them, nor have mercy on them, but I will destroy them."'
Listen and pay attention, and do not be proud because the Lord has spoken.

Give glory to your Lord God, before he causes darkness, and your feet stumble on the dark mountains. And while you look for light, he will turn it into the shadow of death, and make it a gross darkness.
But if you will not listen, my soul will weep in secret places for your pride, and my eyes will overflow with tears, because the Lord's flock will be carried away as captives.
So speak to the king and queen and say, 'Humble yourselves and sit down, because your nations will come down and so will your crown of glory.'
The cities of the south will be closed shut and no one can open them, all of Judah will be completely carried away as captives.
Lift up your eyes and see those who come from the north. Where are the beautiful flocks that you were given?
What will you say when he punishes you? Because, you will be ruled over by those whom you have taught to be captains and leaders. Will your sorrows not overtake you like a woman in labor?
And if you say in your heart, 'Why have these things have happened to me?' It is because of your great immorality that your veil has been stripped away, and your body has been exposed.
An Ethiopian cannot change his skin color, nor can a leopard change his spots? Nor can those of you who are used to doing evil, do good things.
So I will scatter them like the straw is blown away by the wind in the wilderness!
Then the Lord said, 'This is your lot, your portion and measure from me, because you have forgotten me and you trusted in a lie.
So I will expose the veil over your face, so that your shame may be seen.
I have seen your adulterous nature, the obscenity of your prostitution, and your abominations on the hills in the fields. O Jerusalem, woe unto you! When will you ever be made clean?'"
These is the Lord's word that came to Jeremiah concerning the drought.
And the Lord said, "Judah mourns and its gates languish, and a cry goes up from Jerusalem because the ground is blackened.

The nobles sent their children for water, but when they went to the wells they found no water. So they returned with empty vessels, and they covered their heads because they were ashamed and confused.
The ground was cracked because there has been no rain on the earth, the farmers were ashamed and they covered their heads.
Yes, the doe also abandoned its calf in the field, because there was no grass.
And the wild donkeys stood in the high places, they sniffed the wind like dragons, and their eyes failed because there was no grass.
O Lord, even though our wickedness testifies against us, please do something for your name's sake, because we have sinned against you with our many backslidings.
O savior of Israel, in whom we hope in times of trouble, why should you be like a stranger in the land, or a traveling man who only stays for the night?
O Lord, why should you be like an astonished man or a mighty man who cannot save us? Yet you are in our midst and we are called by your name, so please do not abandon us.

This what the Lord says about these people, "These people loved to wander, they have not restrained their feet, so the Lord does not accept them, so now he will remember their immorality and visit their sins."
Then the Lord said to me, "Do noy pray for the well-being of these people.
When they fast, I will not hear their cry, and when they offer burnt offerings and donations, I will not accept them, but I will consume them by the sword, famine, and pestilence."

Then I said, "Ah, Lord God! Behold, the prophets tell these people and say, 'You will not see the sword, nor will you experience famine,' and they were assured that you will give them peace in this place."

Then the Lord said to me, "The prophets speak lies to you in my name, I did not send them, nor have I spoken to them or commanded them. But they prophesy a false vision and worthless divination, and the nothingness and deceit of their own heart."

So, this is what the Lord says concerning the prophets who prophesy in my name, "I did not send the prophets who say to them, 'The sword and famine will not be seen in this land,' and those prophets will be consumed by the sword and famine.

And the people they prophesy to, will be thrown out into the streets of Jerusalem because of the sword and famine. They will have no one to bury them and their wives, nor their sons or daughters, because I will pour their wickedness all over them.
So, this is what you must say to them, "My eyes overflow with unceasing tears night and day, because the virgin daughter of my people has been broken by a very grievous attack.

If I go out into the field, I see those killed with the sword! And if I enter the city, then I seed those who are sick with famine! Because both the prophet and the priest travel to an unknown land that they do not know."

Have you completely rejected Judah? Has your soul loathed Zion? Why have you defeated us, and why is there no healing for us? We looked for peace, and there was nothing good. We hoped for a time of healing, and saw nothing but trouble!
O Lord, we acknowledge our wickedness and our fathers' immorality, because we have sinned against you.
For your name's sake, do not abhor us nor disgrace the throne of your glory, please remember your covenant with us and do not break it.

Is there anyone among the Gentiles' vanities who can make it rain, or can the heavens give showers by themselves? O Lord our God, are you not you not the one we wait on, because you have made all these things.
Then the Lord said to me, "Even though Moses and Samuel stood before me, my mind will not favor these people. Throw them out of my sight, and let them go.

If they ask you, 'Where can we go?' Then tell them that this is what the Lord says, 'Those who are destined for death, go to death, and those who are destined for the sword, go to the sword, and those who are destined for famine, go to famine, and those who are destined for captivity, go to captivity.'"
Furthermore the Lord says this, "I will appoint four kinds of destroyers over them, the sword to kill, the dogs to tear, the birds of the heavens, and the beasts of the earth to devour and destroy.
And I will scatter them throughout all kingdoms of the earth, because of what Manasseh son of King Hezekiah of Judah did in Jerusalem.
O Jerusalem, who will have pity on you, mourn over you, or even ask about how you are doing?"
For the Lord says, "You have forsaken me and gone backwards, so I will stretch out my hand against you and destroy you, because I am weary of repenting.
I will toss them into the air and scatter them at the gates of the land. I will bereave them of their children and destroy my people since they did not return from their ways.

Their widows are more numerous to me than the sand of the seas. I have brought a destroyer against the mothers of the young men at noon, and I have caused the destroyer and terrors to suddenly fall on the city.

The mother of seven languishes and she has given up the ghost. Her sun has gone down while it was still day, she will be ashamed and confused. And the rest of them I will deliver to their enemies to be put to the sword.

Woe is me, and to my mother who gave birth to me, I am a man of conflict and disagreement to the whole earth! I have never lent on usury, but men have lent to me on usury, and every one of them curses me."
Then the Lord said, "Truly it will all go well with what remains of you, because I will make the enemy treat you well in the time of evil and affliction.
Can anyone break the iron or steel from the north?
Your wealth and treasures I will surrender as plunder without price for all your sins within all your borders.
And I will send you into your enemies land, a land that you do not know, because my anger has been kindled like a fire which will burn against you."
O Lord, you understand me, so remember me and visit me. Avenge me against my persecutors, and do not take me away for your long suffering. Know that for your sake, I have suffered rebuke.
Your words were found and I ate them. Your words became my joy and made my heart rejoice. Because I am called by your name, O Lord God of Hosts.
I did not sit in the assembly of mockers, nor did I rejoice with them. I sat alone because your hand was upon me, for you have filled me with indignation.
Why does my pain never end, why is my wound incurable, and why does it refuse to be healed? Will you always appear to be an illusion to me, like water that never comes?

Therefore this is what the LORD says, "If you return, then I will restore you and you will stand before me. And if you save the precious words from the vile, you will speak for me. So, let them return to you, but do not return to them.
And I will make you a fortified brass wall to these people, and they will fight against you, but they will not prevail against you, because I am with you to save you and to deliver you.
I will deliver you from the hands of the wicked, and rescue you from the ruthless."
Then the Lord's word came to me again.
And the Lord said, "You must not marry a wife, nor have sons or daughters in this place."
Because, this is what the Lord says about having sons and daughters born in this place, and about their mothers who gave birth to them, and their fathers who fathered them in this land.

And the Lord says, "They will die grievous deaths, they will not be mourned, they will not be buried, but they will be like dung laying on the ground. They will be consumed by the sword and famine, and their corpses will be meat for the birds of the air, and the beasts of the earth."

Because this is what the Lord says about this, "Do not go to mourn them, and do not enter the house of mourning for them, because I have taken my peace, my loving kindness, and my mercies away from these people.
Both the great and the small will die in this land and they will not be buried. Men will not mourn them, they will not cut themselves, nor will they shave their head for them.
Men will not tear their clothes in mourning for them, nor comfort those who mourn for the dead. Men will not even give them a cup of consolation for the loss of their father or mother.
You must not enter a house of feasting, and sit with them to eat and drink."

Because this is what the Lord God of Hosts of Israel says, "Behold, I will remove from this place right before your eyes while you still live, the sounds of joy and happiness, and the voices of the bride and bridegroom.

And it will come to pass, when you tell these people all these things, they will ask you, 'Why has the Lord pronounced all of this great evil against us? What immorality or sin have we committed against our Lord God?'"

Then you will answer them and say, "Because the Lord says that your fathers have forsaken me, and they followed other gods. For they have forsaken me, served other gods, worshipped them, and they have not kept my laws.
And you have done worse than your fathers, because every one of you walk after the stubborn imaginations of your evil heart, instead of listening to me.
So I will throw you out of this land into a land that you nor your fathers have known. There you will serve other gods day and night, because I will show you no favor."
So that's why the Lord says this, "Behold, the days are coming when it will no longer be said, 'As the Lord lives, who brought Israelites up out of the land of Egypt.'

But, instead they will say, 'As the Lord lives who brought the Israelites up from the land of the north, and from all the lands where he had driven them.' Then I will once again bring them back into the land that I gave to their fathers."

Therefore, this is what the Lord says, "I will send for many fishermen to catch them. After that I will send for many hunters, and they will hunt them from every hill, mountain, and all the clefts in the rocks.
For my eyes see all of their ways, they are not hidden from my face, nor is their immorality hidden from my eyes.
And first I will compensate them double for their immorality and sin, because they have defiled my land and filled my inheritance with the carcass of their detestable abominations."

O Lord, my strength, my fortress, and my refuge on the day of affliction, the Gentiles will come to you from the ends of the earth, and they will say, "Surely our fathers have inherited lies, vanity, and things in which there is no profit."
And the Lord said, "Can a man make gods for himself? No, there are no such gods!
Therefore, I will this once let them know, and I will make them know the power and might of my hand, and they will know that my name is The Lord."
The Lord says, "The sin of Judah is written with a diamond pointed iron pen. It is carved on the tablet of their heart and on the horns of your altars.
While their children remember their altars and their Asherah poles by the green trees high up on the hills.
O my mountain in the field, I will give your wealth and treasures from your high places as spoils of war, because of the sin throughout your entire land.

And even yourself, will abandon the heritage that I gave you, and I will make you serve your enemies in a land which you do not know, because you have kindled a fire in my anger, which will burn forever."
This is what the Lord says, "Cursed is the man who trusts in men, and makes flesh his strength, and whose heart abandons the Lord.
For he will be like the shrub in the desert, and he will not see when good comes. But he will inhabit the dried places in the desert, in an uninhabited land of salt.
Blessed is the man who trusts the Lord, and who puts his hope in the Lord.

For he will be like a tree planted near the water that spreads its roots by the river. It does not see when the heat comes, but its leaves will always be green. It does not need to be careful in a year of drought, nor does it cease to produce fruit.
The heart is deceitful and desperately wicked above everything else, who can understand it?
I, the Lord, search the heart and examine the soul to reward every man according to his ways and everything he deserves.
A man who unrighteously receives riches, is like a partridge that sits on eggs that do not hatch. His riches will abandon him in the middle of his days, and in the end he will be the fool."
A glorious throne, exalted from the beginning is our place of sanctuary.
O Lord, the hope of Israel, all who abandon you will be ashamed. Those who turn away from you will be written in the dust because they have forsaken the Lord, the fountain of living water.
O Lord, heal me and I will be healed, save me and I will be saved, because you are my praise.
Behold, they say to me, "Where is the word of the Lord? Let it come now!"
But, I have not turned away from being your pastor to follow you. I have not desired that miserable day. And you know what you heard that my lips spoke before you.
Do not terrorize me, you are my hope on the day of evil.
Let those who persecute me be confused, but do not let me be confused, let them be dismayed, but do not let me be dismayed, bring the day of evil upon them, and destroy them with double destruction.
This is what the Lord said to me, "Go and stand at the people's gate through which the kings of Judah come and go, and all the other gates of Jerusalem.
And say to them, 'Kings of Judah, and all the inhabitants of Judah and Jerusalem, who enter through these gates, hear the Lord's word.
The Lord says to take heed for yourselves, and do not carry a load nor bring it through the gates of Jerusalem, on the Sabbath.
Do not carry a load out of your houses nor do any work on the Sabbath, but keep the Sabbath day holy, as I commanded your fathers.'"
And the Lord says, "But they did not listen nor obey, because they were stubborn and refused to listen or receive my instruction.
So it will come to pass, that if you diligently listen to me, and you do not bring a load through the city gates nor do any work on the Sabbath, but you keep the Sabbath day holy.

Then kings and princes will enter through the gates of this city. They will sit on the throne of David, riding in chariots and on horses, with their officials, along with the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and this city will remain inhabited forever.

And they will come from all around the cities of Judah and Jerusalem, and from Benjamin, the plains, the mountains, and the south. And they will bring into the Lord's house burnt offerings, sacrifices, bread offerings, incense, and praise sacrifices.

But if you do not listen to me and keep the Sabbath day holy, and not carry loads in through the gates of Jerusalem on the Sabbath, then I will kindle an unquenchable fire in its gates, and it will devour all the palaces of Jerusalem."
This is the word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord.
And the Lord said, "Get up and go down to the potter's house, where I will make you hear my words."
Then I went down to the potter's house, and he was working on the potter's wheel.
But the clay bowl that he was making was flawed by the potter's hand, and it seemed best to him to start over on another bowl, so he did.
Then the word of the Lord came to me.
And the Lord said, "O House of Israel, can I not do with you as this potter does with this clay? Because in my hand, you are like the clay in the potter's hand."
And the Lord said, "At any time I can speak about a nation or a kingdom, and it will be uprooted, pulled down, and destroyed.
But if that nation which I have warned, turns from their evil, then I will repent of the evil that I had planned for them.
And at any time I can speak about a nation or a kingdom, to build it up and establish it.
But if it continues to do evil in my sight and does not obey my voice, then I will repent of the good that I had planned for them.

Now therefore, go and speak to the people of Judah and Jerusalem and say, 'This is what the Lord says, "Behold I planning to do evil against you, and I am devising a device against you! Every one of you return from your evil ways, and change your ways and deeds back to good."'
And they said, 'There is no hope, so we will walk after our own devices, and everyone will do the imaginations of his evil heart.'"
So this is what the Lord said, "Speak to the heathen and ask them, 'Who has ever heard of such things? The virgin of Israel has done a very horrible thing.
Can a man trek through the snow of Lebanon which covers the field rocks, or will the cold flowing waters that come from another place be forsaken?

Because my people have forgotten me, they have burned incense to vain worthless idols, and they stumble in the ancient paths from their ways, to walk in pathways that have not been thrown by the potter.
They make their land desolate with never ending hissing, everyone who passes by will be astonished, and they will shake their head.
I will scatter them like an east wind before the enemy. I will turn my back to them, and I will not show them my face on the day of their disaster."

Then they said, "Let's plan some devices against Jeremiah, because the law will never leave the priest, nor counsel from the wise, nor the word from the prophet. Come, let us denounce him and ignore his words."
O Lord, listen and pay attention to those who deal with me.
Should evil be compensated with good? For they have dug a pit for my soul. Remember how I stood before you to speak good of them, to turn your anger away from them.

Therefore, deliver their children over to famine, and pour out their blood by the force of the sword. Let their wives become childless widows, let their men be put to death, and let their young men be killed by the sword in battle.
Let a cry be heard from their houses, when you suddenly bring troop against them, because they have dug a pit to capture me, and they have hidden snares for my feet.

Yet O Lord, you know all about their plans to kill me. Do not forgive their immorality, nor erase their sin from your sight. But let them be overthrown before you, and deal with them in this way in your time of anger.
This is what the Lord says, "Go and get a potter's clay bottle, and take from the ancient people and priests.
And go out to the Valley of Hinnom's son, which is near the entry of the east gate, and proclaim what I will tell you to say there.

And say, 'O kings of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem, hear the Lord's word, this is what the Lord God of Hosts of Israel says, "Behold I will bring evil upon this place, and whoever hears this, his ears will tingle."

Because they have forsaken me, and made this place a strange place. They have burned incense to other gods here, gods whom neither they nor their fathers nor the kings of Judah have known, and they have filled this place with the blood of innocents.
They have also built altars in high places to Baal, where they burn their sons as burnt offerings to Baal, which I did not command, nor speak, nor did it ever come into my mind.'"
Therefore the Lord says, "Behold the days have come, that this place will no longer be called Tophet, nor the Valley of Hinnom's son, but it will be known as the Valley of Slaughter.

And I will void the counsel of Judah and Jerusalem in this place, and I will make them fall by the sword before their enemies, and by the hands of those who seek their lives, and I will give their corpses as meat to eat for the birds of the air, and the beasts of the earth.
And I will make this place a desolate hissing city, and everyone who passes by will be astonished and they will hiss, because of all the plagues there.

And I will make them eat the flesh of their own sons and daughters, and everyone will eat the flesh of their friend in the siege and straightness. Because, their enemies and those who seek their lives, will straighten them out.
Then you will break the clay bottle in sight of the men who travel with you.

And you will say to them, 'This is what the Lord of Hosts says, "Even so I will break these people and this city, like a broken potter's bowl, that cannot be repaired. And they will bury them in Tophet, until there is no place left to bury them."'"
And the Lord says, "As a result of this I will make this place and its inhabitants like the city of Tophet.

The houses of Jerusalem and palaces of Judah's kings, will be defiled like Tophet, because they have burned incense to all the stars of heaven on the rooftops of all the houses there, and poured out drink offerings to other gods."
Then Jeremiah came from Tophet, where the Lord sent him to prophesy, and he stood in the court of the Lord's house, and spoke to all the people.

And Jeremiah said, "This is what the Lord God of Hosts of Israel says, 'Behold I will bring all the evil on this city and her towns that I have pronounced against it, because they have stiffened their stubborn necks, so they could not hear my words.'"
Now priest Immer's son Pashur and chief official in the Lord's house, heard that Jeremiah had prophesied these things.
Then Pashur had Jeremiah the prophet beaten and put into stocks at the high gate of Benjamin near the Lord's temple.
The next day, when Pashur released Jeremiah from the stocks, Jeremiah said to him, "The Lord does not call you Pashur, but he calls you Magormissabib.

For this is what the Lord says, 'Behold I will make you a terror to yourself and all your friends, and they will fall by their enemies' sword, and your eyes will see it, and I will han Judah over the hands of the king of Babylon, and he will kill them with the sword, and carry the survivors to Babylon as captives.

Besides that, I will give all this city's wealth, all of its works, all of its precious things, and all of the treasures of the kings of Judah to their enemies, who will plunder them, capture them and carry them to Babylon.

And you, Pashur and everyone who lives in your house will go into captivity, and you will be carried to Babylon. And you, and all of your friends, to whom you have prophesied lies will die and you will be buried there.'"
O Lord, you have deceived me and I was deceived and you are stronger than me. You have prevailed and overcome me, and everyone mocks me every day.
For since I spoke and cried out, I cried violence and destruction, because the word of the Lord was become a reproach and a mockery to me every day.

Then I said, "I will not mention his name, nor speak in his name anymore." But his word was like a burning fire confined to my bones in my heart. And I was weary from forgiving, and I could not remain.

For I heard the defamation of many, with fear on every side. And they say, "We will report him." And all my friends watch for my failure and say, "Perhaps he will be tempted, and we will prevail and take our revenge against him."

But the Lord is with me like a mighty and terrible warrior! Therefore, my persecutors will stumble, and they will not prevail. They will be greatly ashamed, because they will not prosper, and their everlasting confusion will never be forgotten.
O Lord of Hosts, who examines the righteous, who sees the heart, mind, and soul, let me see your vengeance on them, because I have committed my cause to you.
Praise the Lord, and sing to the Lord! Because he has delivered the soul of the poor from the hands of evildoers.
Curse the day I was born, and do not bless the day my mother gave birth to me.
Curse the man who brought the news to my father and said, "A son has been born to you," making him very happy.
May that man be like the cities which the Lord did not repent of overthrowing, and let him hear the cries in the morning, and the shouting at the noon tide.
Because he did not kill me in the womb, so that my mother might have been my grave, and her womb would be always full of me.
Why did I come out of the womb only to see labor and sorrow, so that my days would be consumed with shame?
This is the Lord's word which came to Jeremiah, when King Zedekiah sent Melchiah's son Pashur, and priest Maaseiah's son Zephaniah to him.

And they said, "I pray you will inquire of the Lord for us, because King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon is waging war against us. Please ask the Lord if he will deal with us as he has with all of his past wonderous works, so that King Nebuchadnezzar will leave us."
Then Jeremiah answered them and said, "Go back to Zedekiah.

And tell him, 'This is what the Lord God of Israel says, "Behold I will turn your own weapons of war against you! And I will bring the king of Babylon and the Chaldeans who lay siege against you outside the walls into the middle of this city.
And with anger, fury, and great wrath I myself will fight against you with an outstretched hand and a mighty arm.
And I will defeat the inhabitants of this city, both man and beast, they will die of a great pestilence."'"

And this is what the Lord also said, "Afterwards I will deliver King Zedekiah of Judah, his servants, the people, and whoever else survives the pestilence, the sword, and the famine in this city into the hands of King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon, their enemies, and those who seek to take their life. And he will defeat them with the edge of the sword and he will not spare them, pity them, nor have mercy on them.
Then speak to these people and say, 'This is what the Lord says, "Behold I place before you the way of life, and the way of death.
Whoever endures in this city will die by the sword, famine, and pestilence, but whoever goes out and surrenders to the Chaldeans will live, and his life will be spared as plunder."'"
Because the Lord says, "I have decided to bring evil and not good against this city, and it will be placed into the hands of the king of Babylon, and he will burn it with fire.
Therefore, go and tell the house of the king of Judah to hear the Lord's word."

O house of David, this is what the Lord says, "Execute justice in the morning, and deliver the victim from the hand of the oppressor, or else my fury leave and burn like fire, that no one can extinguish, because of your evil deeds."
And the Lord says, "Behold, I am against those who inhabit the valley above the rocky plain, who say, 'Who can come against us and enter our homes?"
Because the Lord says, "I will punish you in accordance with what your deeds deserve, and I will kindle a fire in your forests, and it will devour everything around you."
This is what the Lord says, "Go down to the house of the king of Judah.
And speak to them and say, 'O King of Judah, who sits on the throne of David, your servants, and your people who enter through these gates, hear the Lord's word.'"

The Lord also says this, "Execute justice and righteousness, and deliver the victim from the hands of the oppressor! Do not wrong or inflict violence on strangers, the fatherless, widows, and do not shed innocent blood in this place!
For if you do as I command, then the kings sitting on King David's throne will enter through the palace gates riding in chariots and on horses with his servants, and his people."
Furthermore the Lord says, "But, if you refuse to hear these words, I swear by myself, that this house will be devastated."
Because this is what the Lord says about the king of Judah's palace, "You are like Gilead to me or the summit of Lebanon, but I will surely turn you into a wilderness and uninhabited cities.
I will prepare destroyers against you and anyone with weapons, and they will cut down your choicest cedars, and throw them into the fire.
Many nations will pass by this city and they will ask their neighbors, 'Why has the Lord done this to such a great city?'
Then they will answer each other and say, 'It is because they have forsaken their Lord God's covenant, and they have worshipped and served other gods.'
So do not weep nor for mourn the dead, but weep bitterly for anyone who goes away, because they will never return to see their native country."
Because Shallum the son of King Josiah of Judah, reigned in his father's place. And this is what the Lord said about Shallum, "Shallum left this place, and he will never return.
But he will die in the place where they have taken him captive, and he will never see this land again.
Woe unto anyone who builds his house through unrighteousness and wrong doing, or uses his neighbor's service without wages, and gives him nothing in return for his work.
Woe unto anyone who says, 'I will build a wide house with spacious rooms,' and he cuts out windows, panels it with cedar, and paints it with vermilion.
Do you reign as king, because you enclose yourself in cedar? Did your father not eat and drink, and administer justice and righteousness, and then everything went well for him?
He judged the cause of the poor and needy, then all was well with him, was this not what it is like to know me?
But your eyes and heart are set only on your own covetousness, shedding innocent blood, oppression, and doing violence."

Therefore this is what the Lord says about Jehoiakim the son of King Josiah of Judah, "They will not mourn for him and say, 'Alas my brother or sister!' They will not mourn for him and say, 'Alas the Lord and his glory!'
He will be buried like a donkey, dragged away and thrown outside the gates of Jerusalem.
Go up to Lebanon, cry out and lift up your voice in Bashan, and cry out from the passages, because all of your lovers have been destroyed.
I spoke to you in your prosperity, but you said, 'I will not listen.' This has your way since you were a youth, and you have not obeyed my voice.
The wind will eat up all your pastors, and your lovers will go into captivity, surely then you will be ashamed and confused for all of your wickedness.
O inhabitants of Lebanon, who make your nest in the cedars, how gracious you will be when pain comes to you, the pain like that of a woman in labor!"
And the Lord says, "As I live, even if you, Coniah the son of King Jehoiakim of Judah were a signet ring on my right hand, I would pull you off my finger.
I will hand you over to the hands of those, whom you fear and who want to take your life. I will place you into the hands of the Babylonian King Nebuchadnezzar and the Chaldeans.
And I will throw you and your mother who gave birth to you, into another country, to die where you were not born.
But they will never return, to the place they desire to return."
Is this man Coniah a despised and broken idol? Is he a bowl that no one wants or desires? Why have he and his descendants been thrown into a land that they do not know?
O earth, earth, earth, hear the Lord's word.

Because, this is what the Lord says, "Write this down you childless man, a man who will not prosper in his lifetime. A man whose descendants will not prosper, nor sit on the throne of David and rule Judah ever again."
This is what the Lord says, "Woe unto the pastors who destroy and scatter the sheep from my pasture!

Therefore, the Lord God of Israel spoke against the pastors who feed my people and said, "You have scattered my flock and driven them away, and you have not visited them. So I will visit your evil doings on you.
I will gather what is left of my flock from all the countries where I have driven them, and bring them back to their pastures, where they will be fruitful and multiply.
I will establish shepherds to watch over and feed them, they will no longer fear nor be dismayed, and they will no longer be missing."
Behold the Lord says, "The days are coming when I will raise up a righteous branch for David, and a king will reign and prosper, and wisely execute justice and righteousness on the earth.
In his days Judah will be saved and Israel will live safely. This is the name by which he will be called, 'The Lord Our Righteousness.'"
Therefore the Lord says, "Behold the days are coming when they will no longer say, 'As sure as the Lord lives, who brought the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt.

But, instead they will say,'As sure as the Lord lives, who led the descendants of the House of Israel out of the north country, and from all the countries where I had driven them,' and they will live in their own land."
My heart is broken because of the prophets, all my bones shake, I have become like a drunkard or a man overcome by wine, because of the Lord and his holy words.
For the land is full of adulterers, because of swearing the land mourns and the pleasant wilderness places have dried up, and their path is evil, and their power is not righteous.
For the Lord says, "Both the prophet and priest are profane, and I have found their wickedness in my house."

Therefore the Lord says, "That's why their ways will be as slippery to them as the darkness that they will be driven to, where they will fall, because I will bring evil on them, even in the year of their visitation.
And I have seen foolishness in the Samaritan prophets, they prophesied in Baal's name, and caused my people Israel to go astray.

I have also seen in the prophets of Jerusalem a horrible thing, they commit adultery and walk in lies. They also strengthen the hands of evildoers, so that no one returns from their wickedness, they are all like the inhabitants of Sodom and Gomorrah to me."

So this is what the Lord of Hosts says about the prophets, "Behold I will feed them wormwood, and make them drink poisoned water, because the unfaithfulness of Jerusalem's prophets has spread throughout the land."
Furthermore the Lord of Hosts says, "Do not listen to the prophets who prophesy to you, because they make you vain and they speak of visions from their own heart, not from the Lord's mouth.
They still say to those who despise me, 'The Lord says you will have peace!' And they speak to whoever walks after the imaginations of their own heart and say, 'No evil will come upon you!'
But which of them has stood in the counsel of the Lord, and heard and understood his word? Who has heard and obeyed his word?
Behold, a furious and grievous whirlwind from the Lord has gone out, it will fall grievously on the heads of the wicked.
The Lord's anger will not return until he has executed and performed the thoughts of his heart, and in the latter days you will understand it perfectly.
I did not send these prophets, but they ran, and I have not spoken to them, but they prophesied.
But if they had stood in my counsel, and made my people hear my words, then they would have turned them from their evil ways and their evil deeds."
This is what the Lord says, "Am I just a God close at hand, and not a God far away?
Can anyone hide in secret places where I will not see them? Do I not fill the heaven and earth?
I have heard what the prophets said, who prophesy lies in my name when they said, 'I had a dream, I had a dream.'
How long will these lies be in the heart of the prophets who prophesy lies? Yes, they are prophets of the deceit of their own heart.
They think they can make my people forget my name through their dreams, which every man tells his neighbor, just like their fathers forgot my name for Baal.
Let the prophet who has a dream, tell his dream, and let him who has my word speak faithfully. What is chaff compared to the wheat?"
For the Lord says, "Is not my word like a fire or a hammer that breaks the rock into pieces?"
So the Lord says, "Behold I am against the prophets, who steal my words from everyone and his neighbor."
Because the Lord says, "Behold, I am against the prophets, who wag their tongues and say, 'This is what God says!'"

And the Lord says, "Behold, I am against those who prophesy and tell false dreams to my people, which causes them to err because of the light heartedness of their lies. But I did not send them nor commanded them, so they will not profit these people at all."
And when these people, the prophet, or a priest questions you and says, "What is the Lord's burden? Then you must say to them, 'What burden? For I will even forsake you!'
As for the prophet, the priest, and the people who say, 'This is the Lord's burden, not mine!' I will even punish that man and his house."
This is what you must say to everyone including their neighbor, and their brother, 'What has the Lord answered and said to you?'
You must not mention the Lord's burden anymore, because every man's word will be his burden, for you have perverted the words of our living Lord God of Hosts.
This is what you must say to the prophet, 'What has the Lord answered and said to you?'
But since you say, 'This is the Lord's burden!' Then this is what the Lord says, 'Because you say 'This word is the Lord's burden,' and I sent you and told you not say, 'This is the Lord's burden!'
Therefore, I will even completely forget you and forsake you, and the city that I gave you and your fathers. And I will throw you out of my presence.
Then I will bring everlasting disrespect and never ending shame upon you, which will not be forgotten."

Behold, after King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon captured and carried Jeconiah the son of King Jehoiakim of Judah and Judah's princes, along with Jerusalem's carpenters and smiths away to Babylon, the Lord showed me two baskets full of figs in front of the Lord's temple.
One basket had very good figs, like the first ripened figs, and the other basket had very naughty figs, which were so bad they could not be eaten.
Then said the Lord to me, "What do you see you Jeremiah?" And I said, "I see figs, the good figs are very good, and the evil figs are so evil that they cannot be eaten."
Again the word of the Lord came to me.

And this is what the Lord, the God of Israel said, "Like these good figs, is how I will acknowledge the captives from Judah, whom I have sent from this place into the land of the Chaldeans for their good.
For I will set my eyes on them for good, and I will return them to this land. I will build them up and not pull them down, I will plant them, and not uproot them.
I will give them a heart to know me, and that I am the Lord. They will be my people, and I will be their God, because they will return to me with their whole heart."

And this is what the Lord says, "As surely as the evil figs are so evil they cannot be eaten, so are King Zedekiah of Judah, his princes, the remnants of Jerusalem, those remaining in this land, and those who live in the land of Egypt. So, I will deal with them as you deal with rotten figs.
I will deliver them into the hands of all the kingdoms of the earth to be removed, to be hurt, to be a disgrace, a proverb, a taunt, and a curse wherever I drive them away into captivity.
And I will send the sword, the famine, and the pestilence among them until they have been consumed and removed from the land, that I have given to them and their fathers."
This is the word that came to Jeremiah about all the people of Judah in the fourth year of Jehoiakim the son of King Josiah of Judah, which was the first year of King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon.
Which Jeremiah the prophet spoke to all the people of Judah and Jerusalem.
And Jeremiah said, "God's word came to me thirteen years ago when Josiah was still king of Judah. And I have been telling you what he says every morning since then, but you never listen to me.
And the Lord has sent all his servants the prophets to you over and over again, but you have not listened nor inclined your ear to hear.
The prophets spoke to you and said, 'All of you, turn away from your evil ways and deeds, and you can live in the land that the Lord has given to you and your fathers forever and ever.
And do not chase after, serve, or worship other gods, and do not provoke my anger with things you make with your hands, and I will do you no harm.'
Therefore this is what the Lord says, 'But you have not listened to me, and you have provoked my anger with the things you make with your hands, to your own harm.'
So this is what the Lord of Hosts says, 'Because you have not heard my words.

Behold, I will send for all the northern families, and I will send for my servant King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon, and I will bring them against this land, its inhabitants, and against all the surrounding nations. And I will completely destroy them, and make them a hissing astonishment, and a never ending devastation.
Besides that, I will remove the sounds of joy and happiness, the voices of the bride and bridegroom, the sound of the millstones, and the light of the lamp.
And this whole land will become a devastated astonishment, and these nations will serve the king of Babylon for seventy years.
But after seventy years have passed, and because of their immorality, I will punish the king of Babylon, that nation, and the land of the Chaldeans, and I will make it never ending devastation.
I will bring against that land every word which I have pronounced against it, even everything that is written in this book, which Jeremiah has prophesied against all the nations.
Because many nations and great kings will enslave them, and I will compensate them according to their deeds, and the works of their own hands.'"
For this is what the Lord God of Israel said to me, "Take this furious cup of wine from my hand, and make all the nations to whom I send you drink from it.
And they will drink and they will be moved, and they will go mad, because of the sword that I will send among them."
Then took I the cup from the Lord's hand, and made all the nations, to whom the Lord sent me drink from it.
To make Jerusalem, the cities of Judah, its kings, and its princes a hissing, devastated, and cursed astonishment, as it is to this very day.
Pharaoh king of Egypt, his servants, his princes, and all of his people.
All the mixed tribes, all the kings of Uz, all the Philistine kings, Ashkelon, Gaza, Ekron, and all that remains of Ashdod.
Edom, Moab, and the Ammonites.
All the kings of Tyre, Sidon, and the islands which are across the sea.
Dedan, Tema, Buz, and all those in the farthest corners of the world.
All the kings of Arabia and the mixed people who live in the desert.
All the kings of Zimri and Elam, and Medes.
All the kings of the north both near and far. And one after another all the world's kingdoms on the face of the earth, and the king of Sheshach will drink from this furious cup of wine after them.

Then God told me to speak to them and say, "This is what the Lord God of Hosts of Israel says, 'Drink up, get drunk, and vomit. Then fall over and never get up again, because of the sword I will send among you.'"
So the Lord of Hosts says, "If they refuse to take the cup from your hand and drink, then say to them, 'The Lord of host says, "You will drink.'"

For behold, I will begin to bring evil on the city that is named after me, so how could you go completely unpunished? You will not be unpunished, because I will call for a sword to come against all the inhabitants of the earth."'"

So the Lord said, "Prophesy all of this against them and say, 'The Lord will roar from on high, and raise his voice from his holy home. He will roar loudly over his home, like those who tread grapes, and he will give a great shout against all the earth's inhabitants.
A noise will come even to the ends of the earth, because the Lord has a controversy with the nations, he will judge all flesh, and he will put those who are wicked to the sword."
This is what the Lord of Hosts says, "Behold evil will move from nation to nation, and a great whirlwind will be raised up from the shores of the earth's coasts."
And on that day those killed by the Lord will be scattered from one end of the earth to the other, they will not be mourned, nor gathered, nor buried, and they will be like dung lying on the ground.
O you shepherds, howl and cry and wallow around in the ashes, you leaders of the flock. Because the days of your slaughter have come, and you will fall and be dispersed like a shattered bowl.
Neither the shepherds nor the leaders of the flock will have anywhere to flee to escape.
The cries of the shepherds and howling of the leaders of the flock will be heard, because the Lord has destroyed their pasture.
And their peaceful homes in the meadows have been torn down because of the Lord's fierce anger.
He has abandoned his shelter like a lion, because their land has become desolate because of the fierce oppressor, and the Lord's fierce anger.
This word came to Jeremiah from the Lord at the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim the son of King Josiah of Judah.

And this is what the Lord said, "Stand in the court of the Lord's house, and speak to all the cities of Judah, which come to worship in the Lord's house. Tell them every word that I command you to speak, and do not omit one word.
If they will listen, and turn from their evil ways, so that I may repent from the evil, which I purpose to do to them because of their evil deeds.
And when you speak to them tell them that the Lord says, 'If you do not listen to me and walk in my law, which I have set before you.
And if you do not listen to my servants the prophets, whom I have sent to you over and over again, but you still did not listen.
Then I will make this house like Shiloh, and I will make this city a curse to all the nations of the earth.'"
So all the priests, the prophets, and the people heard Jeremiah speaking these words in the Lord's house.
Now when Jeremiah finished saying everything that the Lord had commanded him to say, then all the people, the priests, and the prophets said, "You will surely die."
Why did you prophesy in the Lord name and say, "This house will be like Shiloh, and this city will be desolate and deserted!" And all the people assembled against Jeremiah in the Lord's temple.
When Judah's princes heard these things, they came from the king's palace to the Lord's temple, and sat down at the entrance of the new gate of the Lord's house.

Then the priests and the prophets spoke to the princes and all the people and said, "This man is worthy of death, because he has prophesied against this city, and you have all heard it with your own ears!"
Then Jeremiah spoke to the princes and all the people and said, "The Lord sent me to prophesy every word that you have heard against this house and this city.
So now, it is up to you to amend your ways and your deeds, and obey the voice of your Lord God. If you do the Lord will repent of the evil that he has planned against you.
As for me, behold I am here in your hands, do with me whatever seems good and righteous to you.

But know this for certain, that if you put me to death, you will surely bring innocent blood upon yourselves, this city, and its inhabitants, because the truth is the Lord sent me to speak every one of these words for you to hear."
Then the princes and all the people said to the priests and the prophets, "This man is not worthy of death, because he has spoken to us in the name of our Lord God!"
Then some of the elders of the land got up and spoke to the whole the assembly of the people.

And they said, "Micah the Morasthite prophesied in the days of King Hezekiah of Judah when he spoke to all the people of Judah and said, 'This is what the Lord of Hosts said, "Zion will be plowed like a field, Jerusalem will become a pile of rubble, and the temple mount will be overgrown like the high places in a forest."'

Did King Hezekiah of Judah and the people of Judah put him to death? Did Hezekiah not fear the Lord, and implore of the Lord, and did the Lord not repent of the evil which he had planned against them? But we are about to procure a great evil against our very own souls."
Now there was another man who prophesied in the Lord's name, Urijah son of Shemaiah from Kiriath-Jearim. He prophesied against this city and this land everything that Jeremiah just said.
And when King Jehoiakim and all his mighty men and the princes heard his words, the king sought to put him to death.But when Urijah heard about it, he fled in fear and went to Egypt.
Then King Jehoiakim sent some men including Elnathan son of Achbor to Egypt.
And they fetched Urijah from Egypt, and brought him to King Jehoiakim, who killed him with the sword and threw his dead body into the graves of the common people.
Nevertheless the hand of Ahikam the son of Shaphan was with Jeremiah, so he was not handed over to the people to be put to death.
At the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim son of King Josiah of Judah, this word came to Jeremiah from the Lord.
And Jeremiah said this is what the Lord said to me, "Make a yoke and put it around your neck.
And send word to the kings of Edom, Moab, Ammon, Tyre, and Sidon, to be delivered by the messengers who came to Jerusalem with King Zedekiah of Judah.
Give them a message from the Lord God of Hosts of Israel to deliver to their masters.
And tell them this is what the Lord says, "I made the earth, the men, and the beasts of the land with my great power and outstretched arm, and have given it to whoever I wanted.
And now have I turned all of these lands over to the hands of my servant King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon, and I have also given him the beasts of the field to serve him.
All nations will serve him, his son, and his grandson until the time comes for his own land, and then many nations and great kings will enslave him.

But it will come to pass, when a nation or kingdom does not serve King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon, and refuses to put their neck under his yoke, then I will punish that nation with the sword, famine, and pestilence, until I have consumed them by his hand."
So do not listen to your prophets, diviners, dreamers, wizards, nor sorcerers who spoke to you and said, "You must not serve the king of Babylon."
For their prophesy is a lie that will remove you far from your land, because the Lord says, "I will drive you out, and you will perish."
But to the nations that surrender their neck to the yoke of the king of Babylon and serve him, the Lord says, "I will let them remain there and they can live in their own land."
I also spoke all of these words to King Zedekiah of Judah and said, "Surrender your necks under the yoke of the king of Babylon, and serve him and his people, and live.
Why must you and your people die by the sword, famine, or pestilence since the Lord has spoken against the nation that will not serve the king of Babylon?
So do not listen to the prophets who speak to you and say, "You will not serve the king of Babylon!" Because they prophesy a lie to you.
For the Lord says, "I have not sent them but they prophesy a lie in my name, so that you and the prophets themselves I will be forced to drive out, and you will perish."

I also spoke to the priests and all these people and said, "This is what the Lord says, 'Do not listen to your prophets who prophesied to you and said, "Behold the bowls from the Lord's house will shortly be brought from Babylon," because they prophesy a lie to you.'
Do not listen to them, but serve the king of Babylon and live, why should this city be laid waste?

But if they are prophets, and if the word of the Lord is with them, let them now make intercession to the Lord of Hosts, so that the bowls which are left in the Lord's temple and in the house of the king of Judah, and in Jerusalem do not go to Babylon.
Because this is what the Lord of Hosts says about the columns, the sea, the foundations, and the rest of the bowls that remain in this city.

Which King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon did not take when he captured Jeconiah the son of King Jehoiakim of Judah, and carried him away along with all the nobles of Judah and Jerusalem from Jerusalem to Babylon.
Yes, this is what the Lord God of Hosts of Israel says, about the bowls that remain in the Lord's temple, and in the house of the king of Judah and of Jerusalem.
And the Lord says, 'They will be carried to Babylon, where they will remain until the day that I visit them, then I will bring them back and restore them to this place.'"

That same year, at the beginning of the reign of King Zedekiah of Judah, in fifth month of the fourth year, that the prophet Azur's son Hananiah from Gibeon, spoke to me in the Lord's house in the presence of the all priests and the people.
And Hananiah said, "The Lord God of Hosts of Israel spoke and said, 'I have broken the yoke of the king of Babylon.
And within two years, I will restore this place and return all the bowls of the Lord's house, that King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon removed and carried away to Babylon.

And I will return this place to Jeconiah the son of King Jehoiakim of Judah, along with all the captives from Judah who went to Babylon.' And the Lord also said, 'I will break the yoke of the king of Babylon.'"
Then the prophet Jeremiah spoke to the prophet Hananiah, in the presence of the priests and everyone who stood in the Lord's temple.

And Jeremiah said, "Amen, may the Lord do so! May the Lord do what you have prophesied, and return to this place, all the bowls of the Lord's house and everyone who is carried away as captives to Babylon.
Nevertheless, listen now this word that I speak into your ears, and the ears of all the people.
The ancient prophets who came before me and you, who prophesied of war, evil, and pestilence against many countries and great kingdoms.
As for the prophets who prophecies peace, when the word of those prophets comes to pass, then that prophet will be known as one who was truly sent by the Lord."
Then Hananiah the prophet grabbed the yoke from the prophet Jeremiah's neck, and broke it.

And Hananiah spoke in the presence of all the people and said, "This is what the Lord says, 'Even so I will break the yoke of King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon from the neck of all nations within two full years!" So the prophet Jeremiah left and went his own way.
Then the Lord's word came to Jeremiah the prophet, after Hananiah the prophet had broken the yoke he took from the prophet Jeremiah's neck.
And the Lord said to Jeremiah, "Go and tell this to Hananiah and say, 'This is what the Lord says, "You have broken a wooden yoke, but you have made an iron yoke for them in its place."'

For this says the Lord God of Hosts of Israel says about that, 'I have put an iron yoke around the neck of all these nations, and I have also given him the beasts of the field, so that they may serve King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon, and they will serve him!'"
Then the prophet Jeremiah said to Hananiah the prophet, "Now hear this Hananiah, the Lord has not sent you, but you make these people trust in a lie.
So this is what the Lord says, "Behold I will remove you and throw from the face of the earth, you will die this year because you have taught rebellion against the Lord."
So Hananiah the prophet died in the seventh month of that same year.

Now this is what was written a letter that the prophet Jeremiah sent from Jerusalem to the surviving elders, the priests, the prophets, and all the people whom Nebuchadnezzar had carried away as captives from Jerusalem to Babylon.
After king Jeconiah, the queen, the eunuchs, the carpenters, the smiths, and the princes of Judah and Jerusalem were captured in Jerusalem.
The letter was given to Elasah son of Shaphan and Gemariah son of Hilkiah, whom King Zedekiah of Judah sent to King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon.
And it stated, "This is what the Lord God of Hosts of Israel says to everyone who was captured and carried away from Jerusalem to Babylon, at God's command.
The Lord says, "Build houses and live in them, plant gardens and eat its fruit.

Get married and father sons and daughters, and find wives for your sons, and husbands for your daughters, so that they may bear sons and daughters, so that you may multiply there, and you will not decrease.
Seek peace for the city where I have sent you as captives, and pray to the Lord for it, because if it has peace you will have peace."
For this is what the Lord God of Hosts of Israel says, "Do not let the prophets and diviners, in your midst deceive you, nor listen to the dreams they give you.
For they falsely prophesy to you in my name, and I have not sent them!"
For this is what the Lord says, "A"fter seventy years in Babylon I will visit you, and confirm my promise to return you to this place.
For I know the plans that I have planned for you, thoughts of peace and not of evil, to give you an expected future.
Then you will call on me and come and pray to me, and I will listen to you.
You will seek me and find me, when you search for me with all your heart.

You will find me, and I will turn away your captivity, and I will gather you from all the nations and places where I have driven you. I will bring you back to the place from which you were carried away into captivity."
Since you have said, "The Lord has raised up prophets for us in Babylon."
Know that this is what the Lord says about the king who sits on David's throne, all the people who live in this city, and your brothers who were not sent away with you into captivity.
This is what the Lord of Hosts says, "Behold I will the sword, the famine, and the pestilence against them. And they are so evil that I will make them like vile figs, that cannot be eaten.

I will persecute them with the sword, famine, and pestilence. And I will deliver them up to be removed and sent to all the kingdoms of the earth as a curse, an astonishment, a hissing, and a condemnation among all the nations where I have driven them."
And the Lord says, "Because you would not listen to me when I sent my servants the prophets to you over and over again, but you would not Listen.
Therefore hear what the Lord has to say to all of you who were sent from Jerusalem to Babylon in captivity."

As far as Ahab son of Kolaiah and Zedekiah son of Maaseiah who prophesy lies to you in my name are concerned, this is what the Lord God of Hosts of Israel says, "Behold I will deliver them into the hands of King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon, and he will kill them right before your very eyes.
Because of them all the people from Judah in captivityin Babylon will curse and say, 'May the Lord make you like Zedekiah and Ahab, whom the king of Babylon roasted in the fire!'

Because they have committed vile acts in Israel by committing adultery with their neighbors' wives, and they have told lies in my name, which I did not commanded. Because the Lord says, 'I know for I am the witness.'"
You must also speak to Shemaiah the Nehelamite.

And you must say, "The Lord God of Hosts of Israel says, 'Because you have sent letters in your name to all the people who are in Jerusalem, to the priest Maaseiah's son Zephaniah, and to all the priests.

And the letter stated, "The Lord has made you priest instead of priest Jehoiada, so that you would be officers in the Lord's house, because everyone who is mad and makes himself a prophet, should put in prison and in stocks."'
So now, why have you not blamed Jeremiah of Anathoth, who makes himself a prophet to you?
For he sent a message to us in Babylon that said, 'This captivity will be long, build houses and live in them, plant gardens and eat its fruit.'"
And priest Zephaniah read this letter to the prophet Jeremiah.
Then the Lord's word came to Jeremiah.

And the Lord said, "Send a message to everyone in captivity and say, 'This is what the Lord says about Shemaiah the Nehelamite, because he has prophesied to you, and I did not send, and he made you trust in a lie.'

That's why the Lord says, 'Behold I will punish Shemaiah the Nehelamite and his descendants. He will have no one left among these people, nor will he see the good things that I will do for my people, because he has taught rebellion against the Lord.'"
These words came to Jeremiah from the Lord.
And the Lord God of Israel spoke and said, "Write down everything I have said to you in a book.
For the days are coming when I will bring my people of Israel and Judah out of captivity, and return them to the land that I gave to their fathers, and they will possess it."
And this is what the Lord said about Israel and Judah.
For this what the Lord says, "We have heard a trembling fearful voice, and not a voice of peace.
Ask now and see, can a man can give birth to a child? If not, then why do I see all the men with pale faces and their hands on their stomach, like a woman in labor?
Alas, how awful that day will be! None will be like it, for it is the time of Jacob's trouble, but he will be saved from it."
For the Lord of Hosts says, "In those days I will break the yoke from your neck, and I will rip off your bonds, and strangers will no longer enslave them.
But they will serve their Lord God, and King David, whom I will raise up for them.

So, O my servant Jacob the Lord says to you, 'Do not fear nor be dismayed O Israel,' because I will save you from far away, and your descendants from the land of their captivity! Jacob will return to rest and quiet, and no one will make him afraid."

For the Lord says, "I am with you to save you. Even though I will completely put an end to all of the nations where I have scattered you. But I will not put a complete end to you, but I will justly correct you, and I will not leave you altogether unpunished."
For this is what the Lord says, "Your injury is incurable, and your wound is grievous.
There is no one to plead your cause, there is nothing to prevent your imprisonment, and you have no healing medicines.
All your lovers have forgotten you, they do not look for you, because I have wounded you like an enemy, with the chastisement of someone cruel, because your many immoralities and sins have increased.
Why do you cry out for your affliction? Your sorrow is incurable. And I have done these things to you, because of your many immoralities and increased sins.

Nevertheless, those who devour you will be devoured, and every one of your adversaries, will be captured and exiled. And those who plunder you will be plundered, and all those who prey on you will become prey.
For I will restore your health to, and I will heal your wounds, because they called you an outcast and said, 'This is Zion, whom no one cares about.'"

This is what the Lord says, "Behold I will return Jacob's tents from captivity, and I will have mercy on his homes. And the city will be rebuilt from her own ruins, and the palace will remain where it was ordered.
And sounds of thanksgiving and celebration will be heard there. I will multiply them and they will not be decreased, I will also glorify them, and they will not be ridiculed.
Their children will also be as they were before, and their congregation will be established before me, and I will punish all their oppressors.
And their nobles will be one of their own, and their governor will rise from their midst, and I will make him draw near, and approach to me, because who would engage his heart to approach to me?
And you will be my people, and I will be your God."
Behold, the Lord's furious never ending whirlwind has gone out, to fall painfully on the heads of the wicked.
The fierce anger of the Lord will not turn back until he has completely achieved the full intent of his heart. And in the latter days you will understand this.
The Lord says, "At the same time, I will be the God of every Israelite family, and they will be my people."
So this is what the Lord said, "The people who survived the sword found grace in the wilderness, even when I went with Israel to find rest."
The Lord appeared to me from the past and said, "Yes, I have loved you with an everlasting love, so I have drawn you to me with loving kindness.
O virgin of Israel, I will rebuild you again and you will once again take your tambourines, and go out dancing joyously in the streets.
You will plant vineyards on the mountains of Samaria again, and they will be planted and eaten as common fruit.
For a day will come when the watchmen on Mount Ephraim will cry, 'Rise up, and let us go to our Lord God in Zion.'"
For this is what the Lord says, "Sing with joy for Jacob, and shout among the leaders of the nations! Publish this with praise and say, 'O Lord, save what remains of your people of Israel!'

Behold, I will bring them from the north country, and gather them from the furthest corners of the earth, including the blind, lame, pregnant women, and women in labor. A great company will return from that place.

They will come with weeping and pleas, and I will lead them. I will make them walk beside the rivers of water, on a straight path where they will not stumble. Because I am Israel's father and Ephraim is my firstborn."
O you nations, hear the Lord's word and declare it in the islands far away and say, "The One who scattered Israel will gather them and keep them as a shepherd keeps his flock.
For the Lord has rescued and ransomed Jacob from the hands of anyone who was stronger than him.

Therefore, they will come and sing on the heights of Zion, and they will flow together over the Lord's goodness. Because of the bountiful wheat, wine, oil, the young flock and herds, and their soul will be like a well-watered garden, and they will not know sorrow anymore.
Then young the virgins will rejoice in dance with both young and old men. Because I will turn their mourning into joy, and I will comfort them, and make them rejoice for their sorrow."
And this is what the Lord says, "I will satisfy the priests' souls with riches, and I will fill my people with my goodness."
And this is what the Lord says, "A voice of lamentation and bitter weeping was heard in Ramah, it was Rachel weeping for her children and she refused to be comforted, because they were gone."
And this is what the Lord says, "Refrain from weeping, crying, and tears, because your work will be rewarded. Then your children will return from the enemies land."
And this is what the Lord says, "So there is hope for your future, and your children will return to their own land.
I have surely heard Ephraim's mourning and crying, "You have severely chastised me, like a bull unaccustomed to the yoke. Return to me and I will be returned, because you are my Lord God.
Surely after I returned, I repented, and after that I was instructed and I struck my thigh, because I was ashamed and confused and I carried the disgrace of my youth."

And this is what the Lord says, "Is not Ephraim my dear son and a pleasant child? For since I spoke against him, I still earnestly remember him. Therefore my bowels are troubled for him, and I will surely have mercy on him.
Set up road marks, make high heaps, and set your heart toward the highway on which you traveled before. O virgin of Israel, return to your cities.
O you backsliding daughter, how long will you wander around? For the Lord has created a new thing on the earth, and a woman will surround a man."

The Lord God of Hosts of Israel has said, "When I restore them from captivity, They will again use words in the land of Judah and its cities and say, 'Let the Lord bless you, O home of justice and O holy mountain.'
For Judah and in all its cities will all live together in the land, including the farmers, and those who go with flocks.
For I have satisfied the weary soul, and I have replenished every sorrow filled soul."
This woke me up and I looked, and I saw that my sleep had been sweet to me.
And this is what the Lord says, "Behold, the days are coming when I will sow the houses of Israel and Judah, with the seed of man and beast."

And this is what the Lord says, "And it will come to pass, that just as I watched over them to uproot, tear down, throw down, destroy, and afflict, is the same way I will watch over them to build and plant.
In those days they will no longer say, the fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children's teeth are set on edge.
But everyone will die for their own immorality, and every man who eats sour grapes, will have his teeth set on edge."
And the Lord says, "Behold, the days are coming that I will make a new covenant with the houses of Israel and Judah."

And the Lord says, "It will not be like the covenant that I made with their fathers on the day that I took them by the hand and led them out of Egypt. And they broke my covenant even though I had been a husband to them."

And the Lord says, "But this will be a new covenant that I will make with the House of Israel after those days. I will put my law within them and write it in their hearts. And I will be their God, and they will be my people."

And the Lord says, "No longer will each man teach his neighbor or brother and say, 'Know the Lord,' because they will all know me, from the least to the greatest of them. Because I will forgive their immorality, and I will no longer remember their sin."

And this is what the Lord says, "Who gives light from the sun by day, and who makes the legal decrees for the moon and the stars to give light by night? Who divided the sea when its waves roar? The Lord of Hosts is his name!"
And the Lord says, "Therefore, only if this legal decree departs from my presence, will Israel's descendants also cease to exist as a nation before me forever."

And this is what the Lord says, "If the heavens above could be measured, and the earth's foundations could be searched below, would I also reject all of Israel's descendants for everything that they have done."
And the Lord says, "Behold, the days are coming when this city will be rebuilt for the Lord from the Hananeel tower to the corner gate.
The measuring line will stretch straight out to the hill of Gareb, and it will surround Goath.

The whole valley of the dead bodies and ashes, and all the fields all the way to the Brook of Kidron, to the corner of the horse gate to the east, will be holy to the Lord. It will never be uprooted nor thrown down ever again.
This is the word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord in the tenth year of King Zedekiah of Judah's reign, which was the eighteenth year of King Nebuchadnezzar's reign.
When the Babylonian king's army laid siege to Jerusalem, and Jeremiah the prophet was confined in the court's prison, which was in the king of Judah's house.

For King Zedekiah of Judah had imprisoned him and said, "Why do you prophesy this way and say, 'This is what the Lord says, "Behold I will allow the king of Babylon to capture this city, and I will turn it over to him.

King Zedekiah of Judah will not escape from the hands of the Chaldeans, but he will surely be delivered into the hands of the king of Babylon. He will meet with him face to face and they will speak eye to eye."'"
And the Lord says, "Nebuchadnezzar will lead Zedekiah to Babylon, where he will stay until I visit him, and even though you fight the Chaldeans, you will not prosper."
And Jeremiah said, "The Lord's word came to me.
And he said, 'Behold, Hanameel the son of your uncle Shallum will come to you and say, "Buy my field in Anathoth, because it is your right of redemption to buy it."'

So my cousin Hanameel came to see me in the court's prison as the Lord said he would, and Hanameel said to me, 'I pray that you will buy my field in Anathoth in the land of Benjamin, since it is your right of inheritance and redemption.' Then I knew that this was the Lord's word."
So I bought the field in Anathoth from my cousin Hanameel, and I weighed out seventeen silver shekels to pay him.
I signed and sealed the contract and took the money to the witnesses, and weighed it out on the balance scales.
Then I took the legally sealed deed, as well as the open copy.

And I gave a copy of the purchase agreement to Baruch son of Neriah and grandson of Maaseiah, in the presence of my cousin Hanameel and the witnesses who signed the purchase agreement, before all the Jews who sat in the court's prison.
And I spoke to Baruch before them.
And I said, "This is what the Lord God of Hosts of Israel says, 'Take these sealed and open purchase agreement documents, and put them in a clay bowl to preserve them for a long time.'"
For this is what the Lord God of Hosts of Israel says, "Houses, fields, and vineyards will once again be possessed in this land."
Now after I delivered the purchase agreement to Baruch son of Neriah, I prayed to the Lord.
And I said, "Ah Lord God! Behold, you made the heaven and the earth with your great power and out stretched arm, and nothing is too difficult for you.
You show loving kindness to thousands, and compensate the children for the immorality of their fathers after them, and the Great and Mighty Lord God of Hosts is your name.

You are the one whose advice and works are great and mighty, because your eyes are open to the sons of men and all of their ways. And you reward each one according to their ways and the fruit of their deeds.
You have sent signs and wonders into the land of Egypt, Israel, and among other men even to this day. You have made a name for yourself, that has lasted to this very day.
You brought your people Israel out of the land of Egypt with signs and wonders. You rescued them with great terror, a strong hand, and an out stretched arm.
You gave them this land, which you swore to give to their fathers, a land flowing with milk and honey.
