And they entered the land and took possession of it. But they did not obey your voice, nor would they walk in your law, they have done nothing that you have commanded them to do, so you made all of this evil to come upon them.

Behold the mountains have come to capture the city. And the city has fallen into the hands of the Chaldeans who fight against it by sword, famine, and pestilence. Because what you have spoken has come to pass, as it can now be seen."
O Lord God, you have said to me, 'Buy the field before witnesses, because the city has been given into the hand of the Chaldeans.'"
Then the Lord's word came to Jeremiah.
And the Lord said, "Behold, I am the Lord, the God of all flesh. Is there anything too difficult for me?"
So this is what the Lord says, "Behold I will give this city into the hand of the Chaldeans and King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon, and he will capture it.

And the Chaldeans who fight against this city, will come and set fire to this city. They will burn it along with the houses where they offered incense to Baal on the rooftops, and where they poured out drink offerings to other gods, to provoke my anger."
For the Lord says, "Because the children of Israel and Judah have only done evil before me since their youth, and they have only provoked my anger with the works of their hands.
For this city has provoked my anger and my fury from the day that they built it, even to this very day, and I should remove it from before my face.

Because the children of Israel and Judah, have provoked my anger with all of the evil which they, their kings, their princes, their priests, their prophets, the men of Judah, and all the other inhabitants of Jerusalem have done.
They have turned their back to me, and they do not face me, even though I have taught them over and over again, but they have not listened nor received my instructions.
But they have defiled my house named after me, and they have put their abominations in it.

And they built altars in high places to Baal in the valley of the son of Hinnom, and burned their sons and daughters in the fire to Molech, which I commanded them not to do. It had never even come into my mind, that they should commit this abomination, to cause Judah to sin."
Therefore, about this city of which you say, "It will be delivered into the hand of the Babylonian king by the sword, famine, and pestilence."

The Lord God of Israel has spoken and said, "Behold, I will gather them from all the countries where I have drove them in my anger, fury, and wrath and I will bring them back to this place, and I will make them live safely.
And they will be my people, and I will be their God.
And I will give them one heart and one way, so that they may fear me forever, for their own good, and the good of their children after them.
And I will make an everlasting covenant with them, that I will not turn away from doing good for them, but I will put my fear in their hearts, so that they will never leave me.
Yes, I will rejoice in doing good for them, and I will faithfully plant them in this land with my whole heart and soul."
For this is what the Lord says, "Just as I have brought all this great evil upon these people, so will I bring on them all the good things I have promised them.
And fields will be bought in this land, of which you say, 'It is desolate and uninhabited by man or beast, and it has been delivered into the hands of the Chaldeans.'

Men will buy fields for money, and deeds will be signed, papers will be sealed and witnessed in the land of Benjamin, Jerusalem, the cities of Judah, the cities of the mountains, the cities of the valley, and in the cities of the south, because I will return them from their captivity."
while Jeremiah was still confined to the court's prison, the Lord's word came to him a second time.
And the Lord said, "This is what the Lord who made and formed the earth, to establish it, and the Lord is his name."
And the Lord said, "Call to me, and I will answer and show you great and mighty things, which you do not know."
For this is what the Lord God of Israel says about the houses of this city, and the palaces of the kings of Judah that were crushed by the mountains, and defeated by the sword.
The Chaldeans come to fight and fill those cities with men's dead bodies whom I have killed in my furious anger. For I have hidden my face from this city because of all its wickedness.
Nevertheless, I will bring it health and healing, and I will cure its people and reveal the abundance of peace and truth to them.
I will restore Judah and Israel from captivity and return them and I will rebuild them, as they were in the beginning.
I will cleanse them from all the immorality they have committed against me, and I will forgive them for all the wickedness they have committed against me.

And this city will be a joyous name to me, a praise, and an honor before all the nations of the earth, who will hear of all the good that I do for them. Then they will fear and tremble in awe of all the goodness and prosperity that I will procure for it."

This is what the Lord says, "In this place, that you say will be a desolation and without man nor beast, even in the cities of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem, that are deserted and uninhabited by man nor beast, there will once again be heard.

The sounds of joy and happiness, the voices of the bride and bridegroom, the voices of those who bring the sacrifice of praise into the Lord's temple, and the voices of those who say, 'Praise the Lord of Hosts, because the Lord is good and his mercy endures forever!'"For the Lord says, "I will return the captives from the land of captivity, as it was in the beginning."
This is what the Lord of Hosts says, "This desolate place and all of its cities, which are uninhabited by man and beast, will once again be a home of shepherds where they can rest their flocks."

The Lord says, "In the mountain and valley cities, the southern cities in the land of Benjamin, and all the cities and places around Jerusalem and Judah, the flocks will once again pass through under control of the one who counts them."
The Lord says, "Behold, the days are coming when I will fulfill the good promises I have made to the houses of Israel and Judah.
In those days and at that time, I will cause the branch of righteousness to grow for David, and he will administer justice and righteousness in the land.
In those days Judah will be saved, and Jerusalem will live safely, and the name that will cause this to happen is, 'Our Lord of Righteousness'."
For this is what the Lord says, "There will never come a time when David will not have a descendant to sit on the throne of the House of Israel.
Nor will there ever come a time when the Levite priests will not have a descendant to come before me to offer burnt offerings, kindle bread offerings, and make continuous sacrifices."
And the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah.
And this is what the Lord said, "If you can break my covenant with the day and the night, so that they cease to occur at their appointed time.
Then my covenant with my servant David may also be broken, so that he would not have a descendant to reign on his throne. And this will also be true of my ministers the Levite priests.
Just as the stars of the heavens cannot be counted, nor the sand of the sea can be measured, so I will multiply the descendants of my servant David, and the Levites who minister to me."
Furthermore, the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah again.

And the Lord said, "Have you do not noticed what these people have said, because they ask, 'Has the Lord abandoned and thrown away the two families which he has chosen?' It is obvious, that they despise my people, and they no longer consider them to be a nation."
So this is what the Lord says, "If I had not established my covenant with the day and the night, and I had not appointed the legal decrees of heaven and earth.

Then I would abandon Jacob and my servant David's descendants, and I would not allow his descendants to rule over Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob's descendants. Because I will return them from their captivity, and I will have mercy on them."

This is the Lord's word that came to Jeremiah when King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon, his army, all the earthly kingdoms he ruled over, and all the other people fought against Jerusalem and all of its cities.

And this is what the Lord God of Israel said, "Go and speak to King Zedekiah of Judah and tell him, 'This is what the Lord says, "Behold I will turn this city over to the hands of the Babylonian king, and he will burn it with fire.
And you will not escape from his hands, but you will surely be captured and delivered to him. You will see the Babylonian king face to face and eye to eye, and you will be carried to Babylon.'"
But O King Zedekiah of Judah, hear what the Lord has to say about you, "You will not die by the sword.

But you will die in peace, and the people will burn incense in your honor as they did for your fathers, and the former kings who came before you. And they will mourn for you and say, 'Ah Lord!' For I the Lord have proclaimed this."
Then Jeremiah the prophet spoke to King Zedekiah of Judah in Jerusalem and told him all of these things.
While at the same time, the Babylonian king's army fought against Jerusalem, and the two remaining cities of Judah, Lachish, and Azekah. Because they were Judah's only remaining defended cities.
After King Zedekiah made a covenant with all the people of Jerusalem to proclaim liberty, the Lord's word came to Jeremiah.
And the Lord said, "Each man should free all his male Hebrew servants, and no one is allowed to force a Jewish brother to serve them."
When all the princes and all the people, who entered into the covenant, heard that everyone should free their servants, so that they would not have to serve them anymore, they obeyed and let them go.
But later they changed their minds and made their freed servants and housemaids return to slavery. And they brought them back into bondage as servants and housemaids.
So the Lord's word came to Jeremiah again.
And this is what the Lord God of Israel said, "I made a covenant with your fathers on the day that I brought them out of the land of Egypt, and from the house of slavery.

And I said, 'At the end of every seven years, you must free your Hebrew brothers, who have been sold to you. They may serve you for six years, but after that you must let him go free.' But your fathers did not incline their ear to listen to me.
And now you have returned to me and done the right thing in my sight, and proclaimed liberty for your neighbor, and you made a covenant before me in the house that is named after me.

But then you changed your mind and polluted my name. And each of you have forced your freed servants to return, who had been allowed to go wherever they pleased, and you brought them back into bondage as your servants and housemaids."

Therefore, this is what the Lord says, "You have not listened to me, and proclaimed liberty for your brother and neighbor. So behold I will proclaim liberty for you, and grant you the freedom to fall by the sword, pestilence, and famine, and I will exile you to all the kingdoms of the earth.
And I will treat those who have transgressed against my covenant and not fulfilled the terms of the covenant they made before me, like the calf they cut in half in order to pass between its pieces.
And all the princes of Judah and Jerusalem, the priests, and all the people of the land who passed between the calves halves.
I will deliver into the hands of their enemies who seek to take their lives. And their corpses will be food for the birds of the air and the beasts of the earth.
I will deliver King Zedekiah of Judah and his princes into the hands of their enemies who seek to take their lives, and to the army of the Babylonian king who had left you alone.

And the Lord says, "Behold, I will command your enemies to return to this city, and they will return and fight against it. And they will capture it, and burn it with fire, and I will make the cities of Judah an uninhabited devastation."
This is the word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord in the days of Jehoiakim the son of King Josiah of Judah.
And the Lord said, "Go to the house of the Rechabites, and speak to them, and bring them into one of the chambers in the Lord's temple, and give them wine to drink."
So I took Jaazaniah son of Jeremiah, the son of Habaziniah, his brothers, all his sons, and everyone else in the house of the Rechabites.

And I brought them into the Lord's temple, into a chamber occupied by the sons of Hanan the son of Igdaliah, a man of God. This chamber was near the princes' chamber, which was above the chamber of Maaseiah the son of Shallum the door keeper.
Then I set cups and a pitcher full of wine before the sons of the house of the Rechabites, and I said to them, "Drink some wine."
But they said, "We do not drink wine, because our father Jonadab son of Rechab commanded us and said, "You nor your descendants must ever drink any wine.

Nor are you ever allowed to build a house, sow seed, or plant vineyard, because none of those things are for you. But you will live in tents all the days of your lives, so that you may live a long time in a land where you are strangers.
We have obeyed everything that Jonadab the son of Rechab our father commanded us. So we have not drunk wine for all the days of our lives, nor do our wives, our sons, nor our daughters.
Nor have we built houses to live in, nor have we owned vineyards, fields, or seed.
But we have lived in tents and obeyed everything exactly as our forefather Jonadab commanded us.
But when King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon marched into the land we said, 'Let us go to Jerusalem to escape the Chaldean and Syrian armies.' So we live in Jerusalem."
Then the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah.
And this is what the Lord God of Hosts of Israel said, "Go and tell the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem that the Lord says, 'Will you not accept my instruction and listen to my words?'

Jonadab the son of Rechab commanded his sons not to drink wine, and they did as he commanded them, because to this very day they have drank no wine. They continue to obey their father's commandment, but even though I have spoken to you over aqnd over again, you have not listened to me!

I have also sent my servants the prophets to you over and over again and they have said, 'All of you turn away from your evil ways, and amend your deeds. Do not chase after and serve other gods, and you will live in the land which I have given to you and your fathers, but you did not incline your ear to listen to me.
Yes, the sons of Jonadab the son of Rechab have obeyed their father's commandment, but these people have not listened to me.'

Therefore, this is what the Lord God of Hosts of Israel says, 'Behold I will bring on Judah and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem all the evil that I have pronounced against them. Because I have spoken to them, but they did not listen and I have called to them but they did not answer.'"

And Jeremiah said to the house of the Rechabites, "This is what the Lord God of Hosts of Israel says, 'Because you have obeyed your father Jonadab's commandment, stood by all of his principals, and done everything that he told you to do.
This is what the Lord God of Hosts of Israel says, 'Jonadab son of Rechab will never fail to have a man to stand before me.'"
In the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of King Josiah of Judah, this word came to Jeremiah from the Lord.
And the Lord said, "Write down everything on a scroll that I spoke to you against Israel, Judah, and all the nations during the reign of King Josiah, from that first day to this very day,.
Perhaps, if the house of Judah hears about all the evil which I plan to do to them, that each of them may turn from their evil ways, so that I can forgive their immoral sins."
Then Jeremiah called Baruch son of Neriah, and as Jeremiah spoke, Baruch wrote down everything that the Lord spoke to Jeremiah in a scroll.
And Jeremiah commanded Baruch and said, "I am quarantined and I cannot enter the Lord's temple.

So you must go to the Lord's house on the fasting day, and read the Lord's words which you have written in the scroll as I spoke, where the people can hear you. Read them where all the people of Judah who come out from their cities can hear you.
Maybe they will present their plea before the Lord, and each one will return from their evil ways, because the anger and fury that the Lord has pronounced against these people is great."
So Neriah's son Baruch did everything that the prophet Jeremiah told him to do, and he read everything in the Lord's book in the Lord's house.

And in the ninth month of the fifth year of Jehoiakim the son of King Josiah of Judah, they proclaimed a fast before the Lord to all the people in Jerusalem, and to all those who came to Jerusalem from Judah.

Then in the higher court of the Lord's temple at the entrance of the new gate of the Lord's house from the chamber of Gemariah son of Shaphan the scribe, Baruch read Jeremiah's words from the scroll where everyone could hear him.
When Micaiah son of Gemariah son of Shaphan, heard all of the Lord's words from the scroll.

He went down to the scribe's chamber in the king's palace, where all the princes sat, including Elishama the scribe, Delaiah the son of Shemaiah, Elnathan the son of Achbor, Gemariah the son of Shaphan, Zedekiah the son of Hananiah, and all the princes.
Then Micaiah declared to them, everything that he had heard when Baruch read the scroll where everyone could hear.

So all the princes sent Jehudi son of Nethaniah, son of Shelemiah, son of Cushi to Baruch with a message and said, "Come here and bring the scroll which you read in public to the people." So Baruch the son of Neriah took the scroll and went to meet them.
And they said to him, "Sit down, and read so we can hear it." So Baruch read it to them.
When they had heard what was written in the scroll, they were all afraid, and they turned to Baruch and said, "We will surely tell the king all of this."
And they spoke to Baruch and asked, "Tell us now, how did you come to write all of this? Did all of it come from Jeremiah's mouth?"
Then Baruch answered and said, "He spoke all of this to me, and I wrote it all in the scroll in ink."
Then the princes said to Baruch, "You and Jeremiah must go and hide, and do not tell anyone where you are."
So they went to the king in the court, but they stored the scroll in the chamber of Elishama the scribe, and reported everything to the king.
So the king sent Jehudi to fetch the scroll, and he took it from Elishama the scribe's chamber, and Jehudi read it to the king and all the princes who stood beside him.
Now it was the ninth month and the king sat in his winter quarters, and there was a fire burning on the hearth before him.
After Jehudi read three or four pages, the king would cut it off with a knife, and throw it in the fire, until the entire scroll was consumed by the fire.
Yet after the king and all of his servants heard everything that was written in the scroll, they were not frightened nor did they tear their garments.
Nevertheless Elnathan, Delaiah, and Gemariah urged the king not to burn the scroll, but he would not listen to them.
But the king commanded Jerahmeel son of Hammelech, and Seraiah son of Azriel, and Shelemiah son of Abdeel to take Baruch the scribe and Jeremiah the prophet, but the Lord had hidden them.
After the king had burned the scroll that Baruch had written with Jeremiah's words, the Lord's word came to Jeremiah again.
And the Lord said, "Take another scroll and write down everything that was in the first scroll that King Jehoiakim of Judah burned."

And say to King Jehoiakim of Judah, "This is what the Lord says, 'You burned the first scroll and said, "Why have you written that the king of Babylon will certainly come and destroy this land, and make it uninhabitable by man and beast?"'"

So this is what the Lord says about King Jehoiakim of Judah, "He will have no one to sit on David's throne, and his dead body will be thrown out into the heat of the day, and exposed to the frost at night.

And I will punish him, his descendants, and his servants for their immorality. I will bring on them, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and the men of Judah all of the evil that I warned them about, but they did not listen."

Then Jeremiah gave another scroll to Baruch the scribe son of Neriah, who had written everything that Jeremiah told him in the first scroll that King Jehoiakim of Judah burned in the fire. And many other similar words were added to it.
King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon made Zedekiah son of Josiah the king of Judah, who ruled instead of Coniah son of Jehoiakim.
But neither he, his servants, nor the people of the land would listen to the Lord's words, which Jeremiah the prophet spoke.
King Zedekiah sent Shelemiah's son Jehucal and priest Maaseiah's son Zephaniah to the prophet Jeremiah with a message that said, "Pray to our Lord God for us."
Now Jeremiah was free to come and go among the people, because they had not yet put him in prison.
Then Pharaoh's army left Egypt, and when the Chaldeans who had besieged Jerusalem heard the news, they left Jerusalem.
Then the Lord's word came to the prophet Jeremiah.
And this what the Lord God of Israel said, "Go to the king of Judah who sent you to me and say, 'Behold Pharaoh's army, which has come out to help you, will return to their own land in Egypt.
And the Chaldeans will come back, and fight against this city, and they will capture it and burn it.'"
And this is what the Lord says, "Do not deceive yourselves and say, 'The Chaldeans will surely leave us alone,' because they will not leave.
Even if you defeated the whole Chaldean army, and only wounded men remained in their tents, they would still rise up and burn this city to the ground."
When the Chaldean army broke camp and left Jerusalem for fear of Pharaoh's army.
Jeremiah left Jerusalem to go to the land of Benjamin, to claim his share in the midst of the people.

And when Jeremiah the prophet reached the gate of Benjamin, a captain of the guard was there, whose name was Irijah son of Shelemiah, the son of Hananiah, and he took him and said, "You are taking sides with the Chaldeans."
Then said Jeremiah, "This is a false accusation, I am not joining the Chaldeans." But Irijah did not listen to him, and he took Jeremiah to the princes.
So the princes were angry with Jeremiah and had beaten, and imprisoned in Jonathan the scribe's house, because it had been made into a prison.
When Jeremiah entered the dungeon, he went to his cell where he remained for many days.

Then King Zedekiah sent for him, and had him secretly brought to the king's palace, where he asked him, "Is there any word from the Lord?" And Jeremiah said, "There is, and he has said that you will be delivered into the hands of the Babylonian king."
Then Jeremiah asked King Zedekiah, "What have I done to offend you, your servants, or these people, that caused you to have me put in prison?
Where are your prophets now who prophesied to you and said, "The king of Babylon will not attack you nor this land.'?
So, O my Lord the king, I pray that you will now hear and accept my plea, and I pray you will not return me to prison in Jonathan the scribe's house, or I will die there."
Then King Zedekiah commanded that they send Jeremiah to the from of the street bakers, until all the bread in the city was gone. So Jeremiah remained in the court's prison.
Then Shephatiah son of Mattan, Gedaliah son of Pashur, Jucal son of Shelemiah, and Pashur son of Malchiah, heard everything that Jeremiah had said to all the people.

And Jeremiah said, "This is what the Lord says, 'Whoever remains in this city will die by the sword, famine, and pestilence. But whoever surrenders to the Chaldeans will live, because their life will be like the spoils of war, and they will live.'
And the Lord also says this, 'This city will surely be given into the hands of the Babylonian king's army, who will capture it.'"

Therefore the princes reported to the king and said, "We beg you to put this man to death, because he weakens the hands of the warriors and all the people, who remain in this city, by saying such things to them, because this man does not seek to help these people, but he wants to harm them.
Then King Zedekiah said, "Behold he is in your hands, because there is nothing I can do to stop you."

Then took they Jeremiah, and threw him into Malchiah son of Hammelech's dungeon, which was in the court's prison. They lowered Jeremiah down into the dungeon with ropes, where there was only mud and no water, and Jeremiah sunk into the mud.
Now Ebedmelech the Ethiopian, one of the eunuchs in the king's palace, heard that they had put Jeremiah in the dungeon, while the king was sitting in the Gate of Benjamin.
Ebedmelech left the king's palace, and he went to speak to the king.

And Ebedmelech said, "My Lord the king, these men have done an evil thing to Jeremiah the prophet, whom they have thrown into the dungeon. For he will likely die from hunger in that place, because there is no more bread in the city.
Then the king commanded Ebedmelech the Ethiopian and said, "Take thirty men with you, and pull Jeremiah the prophet out of the dungeon before he dies."
So Ebedmelech took the men with him, and went to the king's palace under the treasury. And they took old clothes and worn out rags, and lowered them down into the dungeon with ropes to Jeremiah.
Then Ebedmelech the Ethiopian said to Jeremiah, "Put these old clothes and worn out rags under your armpits to pad the ropes." And Jeremiah did so.
So they pulled Jeremiah up out of the dungeon with ropes, and Jeremiah remained in the court's prison.

Then Zedekiah the king sent for Jeremiah the prophet, and had him brought to the third entrance of the Lord's temple. And the king said to Jeremiah, "I want to ask you something, and do not hide anything from me."
Then Jeremiah said to Zedekiah, "If I tell you, you will surely put me to death. And if I give you advice, will you even listen to me?"
So King Zedekiah secretly swore to Jeremiah and said, "As"the Lord lives that made this soul, I will not put you to death, nor will I hand you over to the men who seek to take your life."

Then Jeremiah said to Zedekiah, "This is what the Lord God of Hosts of Israel says, 'If you surrender to the Babylonian king's princes, then your soul will live, and this city will not be burned, and you and your household will live.
But if you do not surrender to the Babylonian king's princes, this city will be handed over to the Chaldeans, and they will burn it, and you will not escape them.'"
And Zedekiah the king said to Jeremiah, "I am afraid of the Jews who have deserted to the Chaldeans, because they might hand me over to them to mock me."
But Jeremiah said, "They will not deliver you to the Jews. And I beg you to obey the Lord's word which I speak to you, so it will all go well for you, and your soul will live.
But if you refuse to surrender, this is the Lord's word has shown me.

All the women who are left in the king of Judah's palace will be brought to the Babylonian king's princes, and those women will say, 'Your friends have turned on you, and they have prevailed against you. Because your feet sank in the mud, and they turned their backs to you.'
So they will bring all your wives and children to the Chaldeans, and you will not escape them, but you will be taken by the Babylonian the king, and this city will be burned."
Then Zedekiah said to Jeremiah, "Do not tell these things to anyone else, or you will die.
But if the princes hear that I have spoken with you, and they come to you and say, 'Tell us everything that you have said to the king, and do not hide anything from us, or we will put you to death.'
Then say to them, 'I presented my plea to the king, so that he would not send me back to die in Jonathan's house.'"

Then all the princes came to Jeremiah and asked him what the king had said, and he told them everything that the king commanded him to say. So they believed him and left, because none of them had heard the king's orders with their own ears.
So Jeremiah lived in the court's prison until the day that Jerusalem was captured.
In the tenth month of the ninth year of King Zedekiah of Judah, King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon came and besieged and attacked Jerusalem with his entire army.
And on the ninth day, of the fourth month, of the eleventh year of Zedekiah, the city defenses were broken.

And all the Babylonian king's princescame in and sat in the middle gate including Nergal-Sharezer, Samgar-Nebo, Sarsechim, Rab-Saris, Nergal-Sharezer, Rab-Mag, along with the rest of the Babylonian king's princes.
When King Zedekiah of Judah and all his warriors saw them, they fled and left the city at night, through the king's garden, near the gate between the two walls, and they fled through the plains.

But the Chaldean army pursued them, and overtook on the plains of Jericho. After they captured him, they brought him to King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon, who was in Riblah in the land of Hamath, where Nebuchadnezzar passed judgment on Zedekiah.
Then the Babylonian king killed Zedekiah's sons in Riblah before his very eyes, and the Babylonian king also killed all of Judah's nobles.
Besides that, he had Zedekiah's eyes put out, then bound him in chains and carried him to Babylon.
And the Chaldeans burned the king's palace, and the people's houses and tore down the walls of Jerusalem.
Then Nebuzaradan captain of the guard carried away the remaining people in the city as captives to Babylon, as well as the deserters who had joined him.
But Nebuzaradan captain of the guard left the poor people, who had nothing in Judah at that time, and gave them vineyards and fields.
Now King of Babylon gave orders about Jeremiah to Nebuzaradan captain of the guard.
And Nebuchadnezzar said, "Take him and look after him, do not harm him, but do for him whatever he asks of you."
So Nebuzaradan captain of the guard, Nebushasban, Rab-Saris, Nergal-Sharezer, Rab-Mag, and all of the Babylonian king's princes.
Sent for Jeremiah and had him brought out of the court's prison, and turned him over to Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan, who carried him home, so he lived among his own people.
Now the Lord's word had come to Jeremiah, while he had been confined to the court's' prison.

And the Lord said, "Go and speak to Ebedmelech the Ethiopian and say, 'This is what the Lord God of Hosts of Israel says, "Behold I will bring my words against this city for evil and not for good, and on that day they will be fulfilled before your very eyes."'"
But on that day the Lord says, "I will deliver you, and you will not be turned over to the men you fear.
Because I will surely deliver you, and you will not fall by the sword. But your life will be like the spoils of war to you, because you have trusted me."

This word came from the Lord to Jeremiah after Nebuzaradan captain of the guard released Jeremiah from his chains and left him in Ramah, after he removed him from all the captives of Jerusalem and Judah who were being carried away to Babylon.
And the captain of the guard found Jeremiah and said to him, "Your Lord God has pronounced this evil on this place.
Now the Lord has fulfilled his word, and he has done everything he said he would do. For all of this has happened to your people because they have sinned against the Lord, and they did not obey him.

But now, behold I am releasing you from the chains around your wrists. If it seem good to you to come with me to Babylon, then come and I will look after you. But if it seems wrong to you to come with me to Babylon, then stay here. Behold, the entire land lies before you, so wherever it seems good and convenient for you to go, then go to there."

Before Jeremiah left to return, Nebuzaradan came to him and said, "Return to Gedaliah son of Ahikam and Shaphan's grandson, whom the king of Babylon has made governor over the cities of Judah, and live with him among the people, or you can go wherever it seems right to you." So then the captain of the guard gave him some rations and a gift, and turned him loose.
Then Jeremiah went to Gedaliah son of Ahikam in Mizpah, and lived with him among the people who were left in the land.

When all the army captains that were in the fields and their men, heard that the Babylonian king had made Gedaliah son of Ahikam the governor of the land, and had appointed him to govern over the men, women, children, the poor of the land, and all the others who were not carried away as captives to Babylon.

Then Ishmael son of Nethaniah, Johanan and Jonathan sons of Kareah, Seraiah son of Tanhumeth, Ephai the Netophathite's sons, Jezaniah the son of a Maachathite, and all their men went to Gedaliah in Mizpah.

And Gedaliah son of Ahikam and Shaphan's grandson swore an oath to them and their men and said, "Do not fear to serve the Chaldeans, live in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and all will go well for you.

As for me, I will live in Mizpah and serve the Chaldeans who come to us. As for you, gather grapes for your wine, summer fruits, and oil and put them in your storage jars, and live in the cities you have taken."

When all the Jews in Moab, Ammon, Edom, and all the other countries, heard that the Babylonian king had left a remnant of the people in Judah, and that he had appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam and Shaphan's grandson over them.
All the Jews returned to Gedaliah in Mizpah in the land of Judah from all the places where they had been driven, and they gathered an abundance of wine and summer fruits.
At the same time, Johanan son of Kareah and all the armies captains who were in the fields went to see Gedaliah in Mizpah.
And they asked, "Did you know that King Baalis of Ammon has sent Nethaniah's son Ishmael to kill you?" But Gedaliah son of Ahikam did not believe them.

Then Johanan son of Kareah spoke to Gedaliah in Mizpah in secret and said, "I beg you to let me go and kill Nethaniah's son Ishmael and nobody will know anything about it, Why should he be allowed to kill you, so that all the Jews who have gathered around you are scattered, and whoever remains in Judah will perish?
But Gedaliah son of Ahikam answered Johanan son of Kareah and said, "Do not do this, because what you are lying about Ishmael."

In the seventh month of the year, Ishmael son of Nethaniah and Elishama's grandson, who was a member of the royal family and one of the king's princes, came with ten men to Gedaliah son of Ahikam of Mizpah, and they all ate bread together in Mizpah.

Then Ishmael son of Nethaniah and the ten men with him got up and struck Gedaliah son of Ahikam and Shaphan's grandson with a sword, and killed the one whom the Babylonian king had appointed as governor over the land.
Ishmael also killed all the Jews, the Chaldeans, and the warriors who were with Gedaliah in Mizpah.
The day after he killed Gedaliah, and before anyone else knew about it.
Eighty men from Shechem, Shiloh, and Samaria cut themselves, shaved their beards, and tore their clothing then came to Mizpah carrying offerings and incense for the Lord's temple.
Ishmael son of Nethaniah left Mizpah and went to meet them weeping all the way, and when he met them he spoke to them and said, "Come to meet Gedaliah son of Ahikam."
And when they came into the middle of the city, Ishmael son of Nethaniah and the men with him killed them, and threw them into the pit.
But ten men with them pleaded with Ishmael and said, "Please do not kill us, because we have treasures of wheat, barley, oil, and honey out in the field." So he did not kill them with their brothers.

Now the pit in which Ishmael had thrown all the men's dead bodies along with Gedaliah, was a pit that King Asa had built out of fear of King Baasha of Israel. But, Ishmael son of Nethaniah filled it with all those he had killed.

Then Ishmael carried away all the inhabitants of Mizpah as captives including the king's daughters and everyone else who remained in Mizpah. Ishmael son of Nethaniah also carried away those whom Nebuzaradan captain of the guard had committed to Gedaliah son of Ahikam, and fled to the Ammonites.
But when Johanan son of Kareah, and all the armies captains with him, heard of all the evil things that Ishmael son of Nethaniah had done.
They took all of their men and went to attack Ishmael son of Nethaniah, and they found him near Gibeon's great waters.
When all the people who were with Ishmael saw Johanan son of Kareah, and all the armies captains who were with him, they were glad.
So all the captive people that Ishmael had carried away from Mizpah turned and went to join Johanan son of Kareah.
But Ishmael son of Nethaniah escaped from Johanan with eight men, and went to the Ammonites.

Then Johanan son of Kareah, and all the captains of the armies that were with him took the what remained of the people from Mizpah whom he had saved from Ishmael son of Nethaniah, after Ishmael had killed Gedaliah son of Ahikam, including the warriors, the women, the children, and the eunuchs whom he had brought back from Gibeon.
And they left and went to live in Chimham, which is near Bethlehem, before they went to Egypt.
They left to escape the Chaldeans, because they were afraid of them, because Ishmael son of Nethaniah had killed Gedaliah son of Ahikam, whom the Babylonian king had appointed governor over the land.
Then all the army captains, including Johanan son of Kareah, Jezaniah son of Hoshaiah, and all the people both great and small approached Jeremiah.
They spoke to Jeremiah the prophet and said, "We beg you to accept our plea, and pray to your Lord God for us, because there are but a few of us left from many, as you can see with your own eyes.
Pray that your Lord God will show us the way in which we must walk, and the thing that we must do."
Then the prophet Jeremiah said, "I have heard you, and behold I will pray to your Lord God as you have asked, I will keep nothing from you, and I will tell you whatever he says."
And they said to Jeremiah, "May the Lord be a true and faithful witness against us, if we do not do everything which your Lord God tells you to tell us to do.
Whether it is good or evil, we will obey the voice of our Lord God to who we send you, so that things will go well for us, when we obey our Lord God!"
Then ten days later, the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah.
So Jeremiah summoned Johanan son of Kareah, and all the captains of the forces who were with him, and all the people both great and small.
And he said to them, "This is what the Lord God of Israel says, to whom you sent me to present your plea before him.
And the Lord said, 'If you stay in this land, then I will build you up and not pull you down. I will plant you and I will not uproot you, because I will repent of all the evil I have done to you.'
And the Lord says, 'Do not be afraid of the king of Babylon whom you fear because I am with you, to save you and to deliver you from his hand.
And I will show mercy to you, so that he will have mercy on you, and allow you to return to your own land.'
But if you say, 'We will not live in this land,' nor obey the voice of your Lord God.
And you say, 'No, we will go live in the land of Egypt, where we will see no war, nor hear the sound of the battle trumpets, nor hunger for bread.'

So those of you who remain of Judah, listen and hear the Lord's word, because this is what the Lord God of Hosts of Israel says, 'If you are completely determined to go and live in Egypt, and you go there.
Then the sword that you fear, will overtake you in the land of Egypt, and the famine which you fear, will closely follow after you in Egypt, and you will die there.
So all of those who are determined to go to Egypt will die there by the sword, famine, and pestilence, and none of them will survive or escape the evil that I will bring upon them.'

For this is what the Lord God of Hosts of Israel says, 'Just as my anger and fury has been poured out on the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so will my fury be poured out on you. When you enter Egypt, you will become a disgraceful curse and a disrespected astonishment, and you will never see this place again.'
O remnants of Judah, the Lord has said this about you, 'Do not go to Egypt!' But know this for sure, I have warned you today.
Because you have deceived your hearts, when you sent me to your Lord God saying, 'Pray to our Lord God for us, and we will do whatever our Lord God says to do.'
And now, I have told you this today, but you have not obeyed the voice of your Lord God, nor anything which he sent me to tell you.
Therefore, know this for sure, you will die by the sword, famine, and pestilence where you desire to go and live."
After Jeremiah had finished speaking to all of the people and telling them everything that their Lord God had sent him to them to say.
Then Azariah son of Hoshaiah, Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the proud men spoke to Jeremiah and said, "You are lying, our Lord God has not sent you to tell us not to go to Egypt.
But Baruch son of Neriah has sent you against us, to deliver us into the hand of the Chaldeans, so that they might put us to death, and carry us away as captives to Babylon."
So Johanan son of Kareah, all the army captains, and all the people did not obey the Lord's command to stay and live in the land of Judah.
But Johanan son of Kareah, and all the army captains took the remaining survivors of Judah, who had returned to live in the land of Judah from all nations where they had been driven.

Including the men, women, children, the king's daughters, and everyone whom Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard had left with Gedaliah son of Ahikam and Shaphan's grandson, as well as Jeremiah the prophet and Baruch son of Neriah.
So they went to the land of Egypt because they did not obey the voice of the Lord, and they even went as far as Tahpanhes.
Then the Lord's word came to Jeremiah in Tahpanhes.
And the Lord said, "Take some large stones, and hide them in the clay of the brick kiln, at the entrance of Pharaoh's house in Tahpanhes, where the men of Judah can see you.

And tell them that this is what the Lord God of Hosts of Israel says, 'Behold I will send my servant King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon here, and I will set up his throne on these stones that I have hidden, and he will spread his royal pavilion over them.
When he comes, he will defeat Egypt, and he will deliver death to those destined for death, and captivity to those destined for captivity, and the sword for those destined for the sword.

And I will kindle a fire in the temples of the Egyptian gods, and Nebuchadnezzar will burn their temples, and carry their gods away as captives. He will wrap himself with the land of Egypt, as a shepherd puts on his garment, and he will leave there in peace.
He will also demolish the images of Beth-Shemesh, throughout the land of Egypt, and he will burn the temples of the Egyptian gods.'"
This is the word that came to Jeremiah about all the Jews who live in the land of Egypt, Migdol, Tahpanhes, Noph, and in the country of Pathros.

And this is what the Lord God of Hosts of Israel said, "You have seen all the evil that I brought upon Jerusalem and all the cities of Judah, and behold to this day they are a devastation, and no one lives there.
It is because of the wickedness that they committed to provoke my anger, by burning incense to and serving other gods, whom you, nor they, nor your fathers know.
However I sent all my servants the prophets to you, over and over again and they said, 'Oh you people, do not this abominable thing that I hate.'
But they did not incline their ear to hear or listen to me, nor did they turn from their wickedness, but they continued to burn incense to other gods.
So my fury and anger was poured out and kindled in the cities of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem, and to this very day they have been laid to waste and desolated."

Therefore, this is what the Lord God of Hosts of Israel says now, 'Because you have committed this great evil against your own souls, for you have cut off from Judah every man, woman, child, and nursing infant, leaving you with no survivors.

Why do you provoke me to anger with the works of your hands, burning incense to other gods in the land of Egypt, where you have gone to live. You have cut yourselves off, and you are a disrespected curse among all the nations of the earth?

Have you forgotten the wickedness of your fathers, your own wickedness, the wickedness of your wives, the wickedness of the kings of Judah and their wives, which they have committed in the land of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem?
To this day they are not humble, nor do they fear and walk in the laws that I have set before you and your fathers."
So this is what the Lord God of Hosts of Israel said, "Behold I will set my face against you for evil, and I will cut off all of Judah.

And I will take those who survived from Judah who are determined to go to Egypt where they will die. Everyone both great and small will fall and die by the sword or they will be consumed by famine. And they will become a loathsome curse, an astonishment, and repulsively dispised.
Because I will punish those who live in Egypt, just as I have punished Jerusalem by sword, famine, and pestilence.

So that no one from Judah, who have gone to live in Egypt, will escape or survive to return to the land of Judah, where they desire to return and live, because no one will return but a few people who escape."

Then all the men who knew that their wives had burned incense to other gods, and all the women standing there which was a vast number, along with all the people who lived in Egypt and Pathros, answered Jeremiah.
And they said, "As for everything you have said to us in the Lord's name, we will not listen to you.

But we will do whatever we want to do. We will burn incense to the queen of heaven and pour out drink offerings to her as we have been doing just as our fathers, our kings, and our princes have done in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem. Because in those days, we had we plenty of food stored, we were well, and we saw no evil.
But ever since we stopped burning incense to the queen of heaven and pouring out drink offerings to her, we have wanted for everything, and we have been consumed by the sword or famine."

And the women also said, "When we burned incense to the queen of heaven and poured out drink offerings to her, did our men not know that we made cakes to offer her in worship, and poured out drink offerings to her?"
Then Jeremiah spoke to all the people who had spoken, including the men, women, and anyone else who had answered him before.

And Jeremiah said, "The incense that you, your fathers, your kings, your princes, and all the people of the land burned in the cities of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem, did the Lord not remember them, and did it not come into his mind?

So, the Lord can no longer bear the evil deeds and abominations which you have committed! And this is the reason that your land has become a devastation, an astonishment, and an uninhabited curse to this very day!

Because you have burned incense and sinned against the Lord, and you have not obeyed the Lord's voice, nor walked in his laws and testimonies, so all this evil has happened to you, which continues to this day."
Then Jeremiah spoke to all the people including all the women and he said, "All of you from Judah who live in the land of Egypt, hear the Lord's word.

This is what the Lord God of Hosts of Israel said, 'You and your wives have said that you will fulfill with your hands, and you will surely do whatever you want to do. And you will burn incense to the queen of heaven, and pour out drink offerings to her. So, do what you have promised, and keep your vows!'"

But first, all of you from Judah, who live in the land of Egypt hear the Lord's word, because this is what the Lord says, "Behold I have sworn by my great name that never again will any man from Judah living in Egypt use my name and say, 'As surely as the Lord God lives.'
Behold, I will watch over them for evil and not for good! And all of the men of Judah who are living in Egypt will die by the sword or they will be consumed by famine, until none of them are left.

But a small number of them will escape the sword and they will return to Judah from Egypt. And, in the end all of those from Judah who went to live in Egypt and survived, will know whose word will stand, theirs or mine!"
And the Lord said, "Let this will be a sign to you, I will punish you in Egypt, so that you will know that my words will surely stand against you for evil."

For this is what the Lord says, "Behold I will turn Pharaoh Hophra king of Egypt over to his enemies, and into the hands of those who seek to take his life, just as I delivered King Zedekiah of Judah over his enemy King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon, and into the hands of the one who sought to take his life."
This is the word that Jeremiah the prophet spoke to Baruch son of Neriah when he wrote them in a book as they were dictated to him in the fourth year of Jehoiakim the son of King Josiah of Judah.
And this is what Jeremiah said, "O Baruch, this is what the Lord God of Israel says to you.
You said, 'Woe' is me! Because the Lord has added grief to my sorrow, I am exhausted from my sighing, and I can find no rest.'"

Therefore this is what Jeremiah was to say to Baruch, "This is what the Lord says about that, 'Behold, I will tear down whatever I have built, and I will uproot everything I have planted throughout the land.'
And the Lord says, 'Do you seek great things for yourself? Do not seek them, because I will bring evil on all flesh, but I will give your life to you as a spoil of war wherever you go.'"
This is the Lord's word which came to the prophet Jeremiah against the Gentiles.

And against Egypt and the army of Pharaoh Necho king of Egypt near the Euphrates river in Carchemish, who King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon defeated in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of King Josiah of Judah.
And the Lord said, "Deploy your shields, and prepare for battle!
Harness the horses, and horsemen take your positions with your helmets, sharpen the spears, and put on your armor!"
And the Lord says, "Why have I seen them dismayed and turned back? Why are their warriors beaten down so swiftly as they flee without looking back? Because fear was all around them!
Do not let the swift flee away, nor the warriors escape! North of the Euphrates river they will stumble and fall.
Who is this that rises like a flood, whose waters move like the rivers?
Egypt rises like a flood, his waters move like the rivers and he says, 'I will rise up and cover the earth, and I will destroy the city and its inhabitants.'
Rise up you horses and rage with your chariots! Let the warriors who handle the shield come forth from Ethiopia and Libya, and the archers from Lydia who handle and draw their bow.

For this day belongs to the Lord God of Hosts, a day of vengeance against his adversaries! The sword will devour until it is satisfied and made drunk with their blood. Because the Lord God of Hosts has a sacrifice in the north country near the Euphrates river.
O virgin daughter of Egypt, go to Gilead for balm, for you will use many medicines in vain, because you will not be cured.
The nations have heard of your shame, and your outcry has filled the land, because warriors stumble over warriors, and they have both fallen together."
This is the word that the Lord spoke to the prophet Jeremiah, about the coming of King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon to defeat the land of Egypt.
And the Lord said, "Declare it in Egypt, and publish it in Migdol, Noph and Tahpanhes and say, 'Stand fast and prepare yourselves, because the sword will devour all of those around you.'
Why have your warriors been swept away? They cannot stand because the Lord drove them down.
He made many stumble and fall over one another. Then they said, 'Rise up, let us return to our own people in the land where we were born, where we can escape the oppressor's sword.'
Where they cried out, 'Pharaoh king of Egypt is nothing but noise, and his appointed time has passed.'"
And the king whose name is the Lord of Hosts says, "As surely as I live, someone will come who is like Mount Tabor among the mountains and like Carmel by the sea.
O daughter living in Egypt, prepare yourself for captivity, because Noph will be laid waste and become an uninhabited desolation.
Egypt is like a beautiful heifer, but destruction will come against it from the north.

Even the mercenaries among her are like fat bulls. Because they have also turned back and they fled together, they will not stand their ground, because their day of disaster had come upon them, and the time of their visitation had come.
Egypt will flee like a serpent, because their army will march against her with axes, like woodsmen chopping wood."
And the Lord says, "They will cut down her forests, even though it cannot be searched, because they are more endless than grasshoppers.
The daughter of Egypt will be confused, she will be delivered into the hand of the people of the north."
The Lord God of Hosts of Israel says, "Behold I will punish the people of Noph, Pharaoh, all of Egypt along with their gods, and their kings even all of those that trust in Pharaoh.
And I will deliver them into the hand of those who seek to take their lives, including King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon and his servants, and afterward it will be inhabited, as it was in the old days.

But you, O my servant Jacob do not fear, and do not be dismayed, O Israel. Because I will save you and your descendants from the far away land of their captivity! Jacob will return, to rest easy and no one will make him afraid."

And the Lord says, "O my servant Jacob, fear not because I am with you, because I will completely destroy all of the nations where I have driven you, but I will not completely destroy you. But I will correct you justly, and I will not allow you to go completely unpunished."
The word of the Lord that came to Jeremiah the prophet against the Philistines, before Pharaoh had defeated Gaza.

And this is what the Lord said, "Behold waters rise up from the north like an overflowing flood, and it will overflow the land, and everything in it, including the city and everyone living there. Then the men there will cry, and all the inhabitants of the land will howl.
At the sound of his strong horses stampeding hoofs, rushing chariots, and rumbling wheels. The fathers will not look back for their children because of their feeble hands.
For the day has come to destroy all the Philistines, and to cut off every remaining ally from Tyre and Sidon. Because the Lord will destroy the Philistines and what remains of the country of Caphtor.
Baldness has overcome Gaza, Ashkelon will be cut off, how long will those who remain of their valley cut themselves?
O sword of the Lord, how long will it be before you are quiet? Put your sword back into your sheath, rest and be still.
How can it be quiet when the Lord has commanded a charge against Ashkelon, and against the shores of its coasts? That's where he has appointed it.
The Lord God of Hosts of Israel spoke against Moab and said, "Woe unto Nebo, for it will be spoiled! Kiriathaim will be confused and captured, and Misgab is confused and dismayed.

There will be no more praise of Moab, because Heshbon has devised evil against them and said, 'Come, let us stop it from becoming a nation.' O Madmen, you will also be cut down, and the sword will pursue you.
A crying voice is heard from Horonaim that says, 'Devastation and great destruction!'
Moab will be destroyed, and her crying children will be heard.
Because they weep bitterly as they ascend to Luhith, and as they descend to Horonaim the enemies have heard a cry of destruction.
And they cry out, 'Flee, run for your lives, and be like the brush in the wilderness.'
Because you have trusted in your own works and treasures, you will also be captured. Chemosh, his priests, and his princes will all go into captivity together.
The destroyer will come over every city, and no city will escape, the valley will also perish and the plain will be destroyed, just as the Lord has said.
Give wings to Moab, so that it may flee and escape, because its cities will become desolate and uninhabited.
Cursed is the man who does the Lord's work deceitfully, and cursed is he who withholds his sword from bloodshed.

Moab has been at ease since his youth, and settled like wine sediments at the bottom of the barrel. And the barrel has not been emptied nor poured from vessel to vessel. Nor has Moab gone into captivity, so its flavor has remained with him, and its scent has not changed."
Therefore the Lord says, "The days are coming when I will send wanderers to him, who will cause him to wander. They will empty his bowls, and break their bottles.
And Moab will be ashamed of Chemosh, just as the House of Israel was ashamed when they put their trust in Bethel.
How can you say, 'We are mighty warriors ready for war'?"
The king whose name is the Lord of Hosts says, "Moab has been destroyed and her cities have been invaded, and his best young men have gone down to the slaughter.
The disaster of Moab is nearly here, and his affliction comes quickly.
All of you who surround him, mourn him. And everyone who knows his name speak up and say, 'How the strong staff and beautiful rod have been broken!'
O daughter living in Dibon, come down from your glory and sit in the thirsty desert, because Moab's destroyer will come on you, and destroy your strongholds.
O inhabitant of Aroer, stand by the roadside and see! Ask this of anyone who flees and the woman who escapes, 'What has happened?'
Moab is confused, for it has been broken down. Howl and cry and tell it in Arnon, that Moab has been destroyed.
And judgment has come on the high plains countries of Holon, Jahaz, and Mephaath.
And on Dibon, Nebo, and Bethdiblathaim.
And on Kiriathaim, Bethgamul, and Bethmeon.
And on Kerioth, Bozrah, and on all the cities of the land of Moab, both near and far.
The horn of Moab has been cut off, and his arm is broken."
And the Lord says, "Make him drunk, because he has magnified himself against the Lord. So Moab will also wallow in his vomit, and become a mockery and a joke.
For was not Israel a joke and a mockery to you? Was he ever found among thieves? For every time you speak of him, you laugh.
O people of Moab, leave the cities and live in the rocks. Be like a dove that makes her nest in the sides of the cave's mouth.
We have heard of the pride of Moab, he is exceedingly proud and conceited. He has an arrogant and proud heart."
And the Lord says, "I know his anger, but it is futile, and his lies will have no effect whatsoever.
Therefore, I will howl and cry out for all of Moab, and my heart will mourn for the men of Kirheres.
O vine of Sibmah, I will weep for you as I wept for Jazer. Your plants have grown to the sea, they even reach to the sea of Jazer. The destroyer has fallen on your summer fruits and grape harvest.

Joy and happiness have been removed from the abundant fields of Moab, and I have made the wine to stop flowing from the winepresses. None of the treaders will shout for joy, their shouts are not happy.

There is a cry from Heshbon all the way to Elealeh, and even as far away as Jahaz, they have raised their voice like a three year old heifer. And from Zoar to Horonaim the waters of Nimrim have also dried up."
Besides that the Lord says, "I will cause anyone in high places in Moab, who makes offers to or burns incense to false gods to cease to exist.
So that my heart sounds like a like pipe organ as it sobs for Moab and the men of Kirheres, because their wealth will have perished.
For every head and beard will be clipped, bald, and shaved. Every hand will be cut, and everyone will be clothed in sackcloth.
In the streets and on all the rooftops of Moab, there will be lamenting and mourning, because I have broken Moab like a bowl in which there is no pleasure."
For the Lord says, "They will howl and say, 'How broken down it is! How Moab has turned its back in shame!' Since Moab has become a mockery and a dismay to all of those around him."
For this is what the Lord says, "Behold he will fly like a eagle, and spread his wings over Moab.
Kerioth and its strongholds were surprised and captured. On that day the hearts of the mighty warriors of Moab will be like the heart of a woman in the pains of labor.
Moab will simply be destroyed as a people, because he has magnified himself against the Lord.
O inhabitants of Moab, you have fear and the pit and the snare against you."

For the Lord says, "The man who flees from fear will fall into the pit, and the one who climbs out of the pit will be caught by the snare, because I will even bring it all on Moab, in the year of their visitation.

Those who fled were forced to stand helpless under the shadow of Heshbon. But a fiery flame will come from Heshbon and the midst of Sihon, and devour the corner of Moab, and the crown of the head of the thundering ones.
O Moab, woe unto you! The people of Chemosh have perished, because your sons and daughters have been captured."
But the Lord declares, "I will restore Moab from its captivity in the latter days. This is how far the judgment of Moab has come."
This is what the Lord says about the Ammonites, "Has Israel no sons nor heirs? Why then has the Ammonite king inherited Gad, and why do his people live in Israel's cities?"

Therefore the Lord says, "Behold the days are coming when I will sound the alarm of war against Rabbah of the Ammonites! It will become a desolate pile of rubble, and her daughters will be burned, then Israel will be the heir to those who were his heirs.

O Heshbon, howl because Ai has been spoiled. O daughters of Rabbah, cry and clothe yourselves with sackcloth. Mourn and run back and forth within the hedges, because your king, his priests and his princes, will all go into captivity together.
O backsliding daughter, why do you glory in your flowing valleys? You trusted in her treasures and said, 'Who can come against me?'"
The Lord God of Hosts says, "Behold, I will bring fear against you from everyone around you. Each one of you will be driven right out, and no one will gather up the surviving wanderers."
And the Lord says, "Afterwards, I will return Ammon's captive children."
The Lord of Hosts says this about Edom, "Is there no longer any wisdom in Teman? Has counsel perished from the prudent? Has their wisdom vanished?
O inhabitants of Dedan, flee, turn back, and lie low because I will bring disaster on Esau when I visit him.
If grape harvesters come to you, would they not leave some grapes for gleaning? If thieves come in the night, will they not steal until they have enough?

But I have stripped Esau bare, I have uncovered his secret places, and he will not be able to hide himself. His descendants will be destroyed along with his brothers and his neighbors. And he will no longer exist.
Leave your fatherless orphans and I will preserve their lives. Let your widows trust in me."

Because this is what the Lord says, "Behold, if those who do not deserve to drink from this cup will assuredly drink from it, are you the one who will go completely unpunished? You will not go unpunished, but you will surely drink from it."
And the Lord says, "For I have sworn by myself, that Bozrah will become a devastation, a disgrace, a waste, and a curse, and all of its cities will become a never ending wasteland."
I have heard a rumor from the Lord, that an ambassador was sent to the heathen with a message that said, "Gather together and march against her, and rise up for battle!
For, I will make you small among the heathen, and despised among men.

Your terror and your proud heart has deceived you. O you who live in the clefts of the rock and hold to the mountain heights, even though you make your nest as high as the eagle, I will bring you down from there.
Edom will also become a devastation, everyone that goes near it will be astonished, and they will all hiss at all of its plagues."
And the Lord says, "As it was in the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah and its neighboring cities, no son of man will live nor abide there.

Behold, he will rise up like a lion from the swollen Jordan RIver and attack the home of the strong. But I will suddenly make him run from her, and who is this chosen man I will appoint over her? For who is like me, and who can appoint me at that time, and who is the shepherd that can stand before me?"

Therefore hear the Lord's counsel and the plans he has devised against Edom. Hear the strategies he has prepared against the inhabitants of Teman that say. "Surely the least of the flock will be drawn out, and he will make their homes desolate and empty.
The earth will quake at the sound of their fall, their cry will be heard all the way to the Red Sea.
Behold, he will soar and fly like an eagle, and spread his wings over Bozrah. On that day the heart of Edom's mighty warriors will be like the heart of a woman with labor pains."
This is what the Lord says about Damascus. "Hamath and Arpad are confused because they have heard evil things. They are fainthearted, and there is sorrow over the sea that cannot be calmed.
Damascus has grown feeble and she has turned to flee. Her fear has seized her, anguish and sorrow have overtaken her like a woman in labor.
How is the city of praise not abandoned, the city of my joy!
Thererfore, her young men will fall in her streets, and all their warriors will be cut off in those days.
And I will kindle a fire within the walls of Damascus, and it will consume Ben-Hadad's palaces."
This what the Lord says about Kedar and the kingdoms of Hazor which King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon will defeat, "Rise up and go to Kedar, and destroy the people of the east.
They will take away all their tents, flocks, curtains, bowls, and camels. And they will cry out to them, 'Fear is on every side!'"
For the Lord says, "O inhabitants of Hazor, flee, run far away, and lie low because King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon has prepared a plan and strategy against you."
And the Lord says, "Rise up, and attack the wealthy nation that lives carefree. They live alone and they have no defensive gates or bars."

And the Lord says, "Their camels will be booty, and their abundant cattle will be a spoil of war, and I will scatter all those who live in the farthest corners there into wind, and I will bring disaster upon them from all sides.
Hazor will become a home for dragons and a devastation forever. No men will endure there nor will any son of man live there."
This is the Lord's word that came to the prophet Jeremiah against Elam at the beginning of the reign of King Zedekiah of Judah.
And this is what the Lord of Hosts says, "Behold I will break Elam's bow, which is their main source of power.
I will bring the four winds from the four corners of heaven against Elam, and I will scatter them throughout those winds. There will be no nation where the outcasts of Elam will not be forced to go."

For the Lord says, "I will make Elam dismayed before their enemies and those who seek to take their life. In my fierce anger, I will bring evil upon them, and I will even send the sword after them, until I have consumed them."
The Lord says, "I will set my throne in Elam, and I will destroy their king and their princes."
And the Lord declares, "But in the last days, I will return Elam from captivity."
This is the word that the Lord spoke against Babylon and the Chaldeans through the prophet Jeremiah.

And the Lord said, "Declare and publish this among the nations, raise a flag, conceal nothing and say, 'Babylon has been captured, Bel is confused, Merodach and her images are broken to pieces, and her idols are confused.'
For a nation from the north has come against her, which will desolate her land. No one will live there, both man and beast will flee."
In those days and at that time the Lord says, "Israel and Judah's descendants will come together, weeping as they come seeking their Lord God.
They will ask the way to Zion with their faces turned that way. They will say, 'Come, let us join together with the Lord in a never ending covenant that will never be forgotten.'
My people have been lost sheep, and their shepherds have led them astray, and turned them away on the mountains. They have wandered from mountain to hill, and forgotten their resting place.
Whoever found them, devoured them and their enemies said, 'We have not offended, because they have sinned against the Lord, who is their home of justice, and the hope of their fathers.'
Flee from the midst of Babylon, and leave the land of the Chaldeans, and be like the male goats who lead the flocks.

For I will raise up an assembly of great nations from the north country against Babylon, and they will array their armies against her, and she will be captured. Their arrows will be like those of a mighty and skilled warrior, and none will return without plunder."
And the Lord says, "Chaldea will be plundered, all those who spoil her will be satisfied.
O destroyers of my heritage, because you were happy and rejoiced, and you have grown fat like a heifer eating grass, and you bellow like a bull.
Your mother will be greatly confused and ashamed. Behold she will be among the least of the nations, a wilderness, a dry land, and a desert.
Because of the Lord's anger, Babylon will not be inhabited, but it will be completely desolate. Everyone who goes near Babylon will be astonished, and they will hiss at all of her plagues.
All you who draw the bow, array your armies and surround Babylon. Shoot at her and spare no arrows, because she has sinned against the Lord.
Shout against her from all sides, she has surrendered, her foundations and walls have collapsed. This is the Lord's vengeance, therefore what she has done to others, do the same to her.
Cut off the sower and the harvester from Babylon. For fear of the oppressor's sword they will all return to their own people, and flee everyone to their own land.
Israel is a scattered flock of sheep, chased away by lions. First the king of Assyria devoured him, then King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon broke his bones."
Therefore, this is what the Lord God of Hosts of Israel says, "Behold I will punish the king of Babylon and his land, as I have punished the king of Assyria.
I will bring Israel back home, and he will feed on Carmel and Bashan, and his soul will be satisfied on Mount Ephraim and Mount Gilead."
In those days, and at that time the Lord says, "Israel and Judah's sins and immorality will be searched out, but they will not be found because I will pardon those whom I choose to preserve."
And the Lord says, "Go up against the land of Merathaim and the people of Pekod. Completely waste and destroy them, and do everything that I have commanded you.
A sound of battle and great destruction is in the land.
How the hammer of the whole earth is split and broken! How Babylon has become a such devastation among the nations!
O Babylon, I laid a snare for you and you were taken before you even knew it. You were also found and captured, because you have struggled against the Lord.
The Lord has opened his armory, and brought out his weapons of indignation, for this is the work of the Lord God of Hosts in the land of the Chaldeans.
Come against her from the farthest border. Break open her storehouses and pile her up like grain, completely destroy her and let there be nothing left of her.
Kill all her bulls and send them down to the slaughter. Woe unto them! For their day has come, the time of their visitation.
Hear the voice of those who flee and escape from the land of Babylon, who declare in Zion the vengeance of our Lord God, and the vengeance of his temple.

Assemble the archers who draw the bow against Babylon, surround her and do not let anyone escape. Repay her equally for all her work, and do to her as she has done to others. Because she has stood proud against the Lord, the Holy One of Israel."
Therefore the Lord says, "Her young men will fall in the streets, and all her warriors will be cut off in those days.
And the Lord God of Hosts says, "O you most proud Babylon, behold I am against you, for your day and the time of my visit has come.
The most proud will stumble and fall, and no one will raise him up. And I will kindle a fire in his cities to devour everyone around him."
This is what the Lord of Hosts says, "Israel and Judah's descendants were oppressed together, and everyone who took them captive held them fast, and refused to let them go.
But their rescuer is strong, and his name is the Lord of Hosts. He will thoroughly plead their case, so that he may give rest to the land, but he will disturb those who live in Babylon."
And the Lord says, "A sword is against the Chaldeans, the inhabitants of Babylon, her princes, and her wise men.
A sword is against the liars and they will become foolish. A sword is against her mighty warriors, and they will be surprised.
A sword is against their horses, their chariots, and all the mixed people who are in her midst, and they will become like women. A sword is against her treasures, and they will be robbed.
A drought is over her waters, and they will be dried up. For it is a land of carved images, and they are mad over their idols.

So the wild desert animals, the wild island beasts, and the owls will live in there. And for all time, it will never again be inhabited, nor will it ever again be lived in from generation to generation."
And the Lord says, "As God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah along with their neighbors, so there will be no one to endure there, nor will any son of man live there.
Behold, an army and a great nation will come from the north, and many kings will be raised up from the ends of the earth.

O daughter of Babylon, they will carry bows and lances, they are cruel and merciless. Their voice will roar like the sea, and they array and ride their horses in formation ready for battle against you.
When the king of Babylon has heard the report of them his hands grew feeble. He was overwhelmed by anguish and pain like that of a woman in labor.

Behold, he will come up like a lion from the swollen Jordan River to the home of the strong. But I will make them suddenly run away from her. Who is this chosen one, that I will appoint over her? For who is like me, and who can appoint me at that time? What shepherd can stand against me?"
So hear the Lord's plans and strategies that he has planned against Babylon and the Chaldeans. Surely the least of the flock will draw them out, and he will surely desolate them and their home.
At the sound of Babylon's capture the earth will quake, and the cry will be heard among the nations.
This is what the Lord says, "Behold I will raise up a destroying wind against Babylon and those who live in her midst who rebel against me.
I will send armies to winnow Babylon and empty her land, because on the day of trouble they will attack her from all sides.
They will attack her archers and anyone who lifts up his armor. They will not spare her young men, and they will completely destroy all of her armies.
In the land of the Chaldeans they will all be pierced through and killed, and they will all fall in her streets.
For Israel and Judah have not been forsaken by their Lord God of Hosts, even though their land was filled with sin against the Holy One of Israel."
And the Lord said, "Flee from the midst of Babylon, and escape with your soul! Do not be cut off by her immorality, because this is the time of the Lord's vengeance, and he will compensate her.
Babylon was a gold cup in the Lord's hand, that made the whole earth drunk. All nations have drunk her wine, so the nations have all gone mad.
Babylon has fallen suddenly and been destroyed. Howl for her, take balm for her pain, perhaps she can be healed.
We would have healed Babylon, but she can not healed. Abandon her, and let each of us go to our own country, because her judgment reaches to heaven, and is even lifted up to the skies.
The Lord has brought forth our righteousness! So come, let us declare in Zion the work of our Lord God."

Sharpen the arrows and gather the shields! The Lord has aroused the spirit of the kings of the Medes, because he has devised a plan to destroy Babylon, because it is the Lord's vengeance for his temple.
Set up a flag on the walls of Babylon, strengthen the watchmen, and prepare the ambushes, because the Lord has devised and done what he said he would do against the Babylonians.
O you who live by many waters with abundant treasures, your end has come, and your selfish desires have been measured.
The Lord of Hosts has sworn by himself and said, "Surely I will fill you with men as with locusts, and they will shout against you."
He made the earth with his power, he established the world by his wisdom, and stretched out the heavens by his understanding.
When his voice thunders, the waters in the heavens roar, and he makes the clouds rise from one end of the earth to the other. He makes lightning with rain and brings the wind from his treasures.
Every man becomes wicked and brutal by his own knowledge, every goldsmith is confused by his carved image, because his molten image is a lie, and there is no breath in them.
They are all vanity and the work of errors, in the time of their visitation they will perish.
Jacob's portion is not like them, because God is the maker of all things, and Israel is his staff of inheritance, and the Lord of Hosts is his name.
And the Lord says, "You are my battle axe and weapons of war, because I will break all the nations to pieces with you, and I will destroy kingdoms with you.
I will break the horse and his rider and the chariot and his rider into pieces with you.
I will also break both young and old men and women into pieces with you. And I will break the young man and the maiden into pieces with you.
I will also break the shepherd and his flock, the rancher and his oxen, and the captains and rulers into pieces with you."
And the Lord says, "Before your very eyes I will repay Babylon and all the people who live in Chaldea for all the evil they have done in Zion."

And the Lord says, "O mountain of destruction, you who destroy the whole earth, I am against you. I will stretch out my hand against you, and roll you down from the rocks, and make you a burnt mountain."
And the Lord says, "They will not take one cornerstone nor a foundation stone from you, but you will be forever desolate.

Raise a flag in the land, blow the trumpet among the nations, prepare the nations to go to war against her. Assemble the kingdoms of Ararat, Minni, and Ashchenaz against her. Appoint a captain to attack her, and bring the horses up like a swarm of locusts.
Prepare the nations against her with the kings of the Medes, its captains, all of its rulers, and all the lands under their authority.
And the land will tremble with sorrow, because every one of the Lord's plans will be used against Babylon, to devastate the land of Babylon and leave it uninhabited.

The mighty warriors of Babylon have abandoned the fight, they remained in their strongholds. Their strength has failed, they have become like women, they burned her homes, and the defensive bars of her gates are broken.
One courier runs to meet another, and messenger after messenger goes to show the king of Babylon that his city has been captured at one end.
The passages have been blocked, the marshes have been burned, and the soldiers are frightened."
