For this is what the Lord God of Hosts of Israel says, "The daughter of Babylon is like a threshing room floor at the time of threshing. But it is just a little while longer until the time of her harvest comes."

And the people of Zion will say, "King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon has devoured me, he has crushed me and made me an empty bowl. He has swallowed me up like a dragon, and he has filled his stomach with my delicacies and vomited me out.
May the violence done to me and my flesh be on Babylon, and may my blood be on the people of Chaldea."
Therefore this is what the Lord says, "Behold I will plead your case and take vengeance for you. I will dry up her sea and her springs.
Babylon will become a pile of rubble and a home for dragons, and an uninhabited astonishment and hissing.
They will roar together like lions, they will growl like lion cubs."
And the Lord says, "In the heat I will make them a feast, and I will make them drunk so that they may rejoice. Then they will fall into a never ending sleep, and never wake up.
I will bring them down like lambs to the slaughter, like rams with male goats.
How Sheshach has been captured! And how the praise of the whole earth has been lost to the surprise attack! How Babylon has become an astonishment among the nations!
The sea has overcome Babylon, she is covered with its flood of waves.
Her cities have become a devastation, a dry land, a wilderness, a land in where no one lives, nor does any son of man pass by.
I will punish Bel in Babylon! I will bring from his mouth that which he has swallowed up. The nations will no longer flow to him, and the walls of Babylon will fall.
My people, leave her! Save your souls from the Lord's fierce anger!
Do not let your heart grow weak, and do not fear the rumors heard in the land. For rumors will both come year after year of violence in the land, and of ruler against ruler.
Therefore the days are coming, when I will judge the carved images of Babylon. Her whole land will be confused, and all of her slain will lie fallen in her midst."
And the Lord says, "Then heaven and earth and all that is in them, will sing for joy over Babylon because her destroyers will come against her from the north.
And as Babylon has slain the fallen Israelis, so will Babylon's killed fall to the earth.
You who have escaped the sword, leave and do not stand around, remember the Lord far from here, and let Jerusalem come into your mind.
We are confused, because we have heard disrespect, and shame has covered our faces, because strangers have entered the sanctuaries of the Lord's house."
So the Lord says, "Behold the days are coming when I will judge her carved images, and the wounded will groan throughout her land."
And the Lord says, "Even if Babylon could soar up to heaven, and she fortified and strengthened her walls, I would still send destroyers to lay waste to her.
A sound of a crying and great destruction comes from Babylon and the land of the Chaldeans.
Because the Lord has destroyed Babylon and silenced her great voice, When her waves roar like great waters, the noise of their voice is heard.
Because the destroyer has come against Babylon, and her mighty warriors will be captured, all of their bows will be broken, because the Lord God of retribution will surely repay in full.
And the king, whose name is the Lord of Hosts says, "I will make her princes, wise men, captains, rulers, and her mighty warriors drunk. They will sleep a never ending sleep, and never wake up."

This is what the Lord of Hosts says, "Babylon's thick walls will be completely torn down, her high gates will be burned. The people will labor in vain, and the nations will exhaust themselves fueling the fames.
This is what the prophet Jeremiah told the quiet prince Seraiah son of Neriah and Maaseiah's grandson, when he went with King Zedekiah of Judah into Babylon in the fourth year of his reign.
So Jeremiah had written all these words of evil against Babylon in a book that detailed all the destruction of Babylon.
And Jeremiah said to Seraiah, "When you go to Babylon see that you read all of these words.
Then you will say, 'O Lord, you have spoken against this place and promised to cut it off, so that no one will remain in it, neither man nor beast, and it will be desolate forever.'
When you have finished reading this book, tie a stone to it, and throw it into the middle of the Euphrates River.

Then you will say, 'This is how Babylon will sink, and never rise again, because of the evil that I will bring upon her. And her people will be weary.'"This is how far the words of Jeremiah have come.
Zedekiah was twenty one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned for eleven years in Jerusalem, and his mother's name was Hamutal of Libnah, who was Jeremiah's daughter.
Zedekiah did evil things in the Lord's sight, just as Jehoiakim had done.
It was because of the Lord's anger that all of these things happened in Jerusalem and Judah, until he finally threw them from his presence. Zedekiah also rebelled against the king of Babylon.

Then on the tenth day of the tenth month in the ninth year of his reign, King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon attacked Jerusalem with his entire army. They encamped outside the city and built forts all around it.
So Jerusalem was under siege until King Zedekiah's eleventh year.
On the ninth day of the fourth month, the famine in the city was so severe that the people of the land had no bread.

Then the city walls were breached, and all the soldiers fled the city by night through the gate between the two walls near the king's garden. Now the Chaldeans had surrounded the city, so they fled through the plains.
But the Chaldean army pursued King Zedekiah and overtook him on the plains of Jericho, his army panicked and was routed.
The Chaldeans captured the King Zedekiah, and carried him to the Babylonian king up in Riblah in the land of Hamath, where King Nebuchadnezzar pronounced judgment over him.
And the Babylonian king killed Zedekiah's sons right before his eyes, he also killed all of Judah's princes in Riblah.
Then the Babylonian king put out Zedekiah's eyes and bound him in chains. He carried him to Babylon, and put him in prison, where he remained until the day he died.
On the tenth day of the fifth month, in the nineteenth year of King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon, Nebuzaradan captain of the guard, who served the Babylonian king, entered Jerusalem.
Nebuzaradan burned the Lord's temple to the ground, along with the king's palace, all the houses in Jerusalem, and all the great men's historical houses.
Then the entire Chaldean army that accompanied Nebuzaradan, demolished all of the defensive walls that surrounded Jerusalem.
Then Nebuzaradan carried away some of the poorest people and others who remained in the city as captives, along with those who had joined the Babylonian king and the rest of the defeated army.
But Nebuzaradan left some of the poorest of the land to tend the vineyards and fields.
They also tore down the brass columns, brass foundations, and the brass sea that were in the Lord's temple, and carried all of the brass to Babylon.
They also carried away the brass caldrons, shovels, candle snuffers, bowls, and spoons which were used to minister in the Lord's temple.
And Nebuzaradan captain of the guard also carried away all the sinks, firepans, bowls, caldrons, lampstands, spoons, and cups that were made of pure gold or fine silver.
The amount of brass taken from the two columns, the one sea, and the brass bulls from under the foundations, which King Solomon had made in the Lord's temple, was beyond measure.
Each hollow column was four fingers thick, eighteen cubits high, and twelve cubits around its circumference.

Each column had a brass ornamental capital on top of it, and each capital was five cubits high, with a network of brass pomegranates all around it. The second column with its pomegranates was the same.
Each capital had ninety-six pomegranates on its sides, and there was a total of one-hundred pomegranates above the surrounding network.
And Nebuzaradan captain of the guard also took the chief priest Seraiah, and Zephaniah the second priest, and the three doorkeepers.

He also took a eunuch from Jerusalem, who had led King Zedekiah's warriors, as well as seven of the king's trusted advisers. He also took the army's principal scribe, who who had enlisted the people of the land, and sixty men who were found in the middle of the city.
So Nebuzaradan took them to the Babylonian king in Riblah.
And the Babylonian king struck them down and put them to death in Riblah in the land of Hamath. And this is how Judah was carried away as a captive from his own land.
In the seventh year of King Nebuchadnezzar's reign, he captured 3,023 Jews and carried them away.
In the eighteenth year of King Nebuchadnezzar's reign, he attacked Jerusalem and captured 832 people and carried them away.
In the 23rd year of Nebuchadnezzar, Nebuzaradan his captain of the guard carried away 745 Jewish captives, for a total of 4,600 people.

On the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month of the thirty-seventh year after the Babylonians exiled King Jehoiachin of Judah, the new King Evil-Merodach of Babylon decided to be kind to Jehoiachin, and set him free.
And he spoke kindly to Jehoiachin, and set his throne above the throne of the other kings who were with him in Babylon.
So Jehoiachin changed from his prison clothes, and he dined regularly at the king's table for the rest of his life.
And the Babylonian king supplied Jehoiachin with food every day for the rest of his life until the day that he died.
How lonely is the city that was once so full of people! How she has become like a widow! She was once great among the nations, and a princess among the provinces, but now she pays taxes!
She weeps bitterly at night, with tears rolling down her cheeks. Even with many lovers she has no one to comfort her, all her friends have betrayed her and become her enemies.
Judah has gone into exile, and she is afflicted with great servitude. She lives among the heathen but she finds no rest. All her persecutors overtook her between the straits.
The roads to Zion mourn, because no one comes to her solemn feasts. Her gates are deserted, her priests sigh, her virgins are afflicted, and she is overcome with bitterness.

Her adversaries have become her masters, and her enemies prosper. For the Lord has afflicted her with grief for her many transgressions, her children were captured and carried away into captivity by the enemy.
The Daughter of Zion has lost her beauty, her princes have become like deer who find nowhere to pasture. They have lost all their strength before their pursuer.

In the days of her affliction and miseries, Jerusalem remembers all her pleasant things that she had back in the old days. When her people fell into the enemies hands, no one helped her. Her enemies saw her and they mocked her Sabbaths.
Jerusalem has sinned grievously, therefore she has been removed, and everyone that honored her, now despises her. Because they have seen her nakedness, so she sighs and turns away backward.

The filthiness underneath, stains her skirts, and she does not remember how her came end in the last days. So her downfall came wonderfully, and she had no comforter. O Lord, behold my affliction, because the enemy has magnified himself.
The adversary has spread out his hand over all her pleasant things. Because she has seen the heathen enter her sanctuaries, whom you had forbidden to enter your congregation.
All her people sigh as they search for bread. They have traded their pleasant things for meat to save their soul. O Lord, look, see, and consider, because I have become vile.
Is this nothing to all of you who pass by? Look and see if there is any other sorrow like mine, which was done to me. See how the Lord has afflicted me on the day of his fierce anger.
The Lord has sent fire into my bones from above, which has overcome them. He has spread a net for my feet which has turned me back, and he has made me desolate and faint all day long.

He has bound my transgressions like a yoke around my neck with his hand, they are wrapped around me, he has made my strength disappear. The Lord has delivered me into the hands of those whom I am unable to withstand.

The Lord has trampled all of my mighty warriors under foot, he has assembled a great army against me to crush my young men. The Lord has trampled the virgin daughter of Judah, like grapes in a winepress.

For all these things I weep, and the tears flow from my eyes and run down my cheek, because there is no comforter near my soul to comfort me. My children are destitute, because the enemy has prevailed.

Zion spreads out her hands, and there is no one to comfort her. The Lord has spoken about Jacob and commanded, that his adversaries would completely surround him. Jerusalem has become like an unclean menstruous woman among them.
The Lord is righteous, because I have rebelled against his commands. So I pray all you people will listen, and see my sorrow. Because all my virgins and young men have gone into captivity.
I called for my lovers, but they deceived me. My priests and elders gave up the ghost in the city, while they searched for meat to relieve their souls.
O Lord, see how distressed I am, my bowels are troubled and my heart is pounding, because I have grievously rebelled. Outside the sword bereaves! At home there is death!

They have heard me sigh, but there is no one to comfort me. All my enemies have heard of my troubles, and they are glad you have done this to me. But you will bring the day that you announced, and they will be just like me.
Let all of their wickedness come before you, and do to them, as you have done to me for all my transgressions. Because my sighs are many, and my heart is faint.
O how the Lord has covered the Daughter of Zion with a cloud in his anger! He has thrown the beauty of Israel down from heaven to earth. He does not remember his footstool on the day of his anger!

With no pity, the Lord has swallowed up all of Jacob's homes. He has demolished all of the daughter of Judah's strongholds in his anger. He has brought them to the ground and polluted the kingdom and its princes.

He has cut off the entire horn of Israel in his fierce anger. He has drawn back his right fist as the enemy approaches, and his anger has burned against Jacob like a flaming fire that devours everything around it.

He bent his bow like an enemy, and he stands firm with his right hand. Like an adversary he has killed everyone who were pleasant for the eye to see. He has poured out his fury like fire in the Daughter of Zion's tabernacle.
The Lord was like an enemy as he swallowed up Israel. He swallowed all of her palaces, and destroyed her strongholds. He has increased the mourning and lamentation of the daughter of Judah.

And he has violently removed his tabernacle, as if it were a plowed garden, and he has destroyed his meeting places! The Lord made Zion forget her appointed solemn feasts and Sabbaths. He has despised both the king and priest in his great indignation and anger.

The Lord has abandoned his altar as he abhorred his sanctuary. He has surrendered her defensive walls and palaces to the hands of the enemy. They have made a great noise in the Lord's temple as if it were the day of a solemn feast.

The Lord's purpose was to destroy the Daughter of Zion's defensive walls. So he stretched out a measuring line that he has not withdrawn his hand from destroying. He made the ramparts and walls mourn and languish together.

Her gates have sunk into the ground, and he has destroyed and broken her entrance gate bars. Her king and princes have been exiled among the Gentiles! The law no longer exists, and her prophets no longer receive visions from the Lord.
The Daughter of Zion's elders sit on the ground and remain silent. They have thrown dust on their heads and they wear sackcloth. Jerusalem's virgins hang their heads toward the ground.
My eyes fail with tears, and my bowels are troubled. My liver pours out on the ground over the destruction of my people's daughter, because the children and infants pass out in the city streets.
They ask their mothers, "Where is the wheat and wine?" When they passed out like the wounded in the city streets, their soul was poured out into their mother's embrace.

O Daughter of Jerusalem, how can I testify as a witness for you? What can I compare and liken you to? O Virgin Daughter of Zion, how can I comfort you? For your broken defenses are as great as the sea, so who can heal you?
Your prophets have seen vain and foolish things for you, and they did not exposed your immorality to prevent your captivity. But they have seen false burdens and causes of banishment for you.

Everyone who passes by claps their hands at you. They hiss and shake their head at the Daughter of Jerusalem and say, "Is this the city that men call the perfection of beauty, the joy of the whole earth?"
All your enemies speak out against you, they hiss and grind their teeth and say, "We have swallowed her up, and we have found the day that we waited for and we have seen it with our own eyes!"

The Lord has done everything that he devised to satisfy his commandments from the old days. He has destroyed without pity, and he has allowed your enemies to rejoice over you. He has exalted your enemies battle horn.

The people's hearts cried to the Lord and said, "O wall of the Daughter of Zion, let your tears run down like a river day and night. Give yourself no rest, and do not allow the apple of your eye cease to exist.

Rise up and cry out from the first watch of the night, and pour out your heart like water in front of the Lord. Lift your hands up to him and beg for your young children's lives who faint from hunger at the top of every street.
O Lord, look and consider to whom you have done this. Should the women eat their offspring and the infants they have nursed? Should the priests and prophets be killed in the Lord's sanctuary?
The young and the old lie on the ground and in the streets. My virgins and young men have fallen by the sword, you have killed them all on the day of your anger. You have killed them without pity.

You summoned and surrounded me with all of my terrors like a solemn day of feasting. On the Day of the Lord's anger no one escaped nor survived! Everyone I ever held dear and comforted in a warm blanket was destroyed by my enemy.
I am the man who has seen the affliction from the staff of God's anger.
He has not led me into light, but into darkness.
Surely, God has turned his hand against me all day long.
He has made my flesh and skin old, and he has broken my bones.
He has built against me and surrounded me with bitter labor.
He sent me into dark places, like those who have been dead for a long time.
He has built hedges around me, so that I cannot escape, and he has weighed me down with heavy chains.
Even when I cry and shout in pain, he shuts out my prayers.
He has barred my way with carved headstones, and he has made my paths crooked.
He was like a bear, or a lion hiding in its secret places waiting to ambush me.
He turned me away from my ways, and tore me to pieces, and he has left me a deserted.
He drew his bow, and set me up as a target for his arrow.
He made the arrows in his quiver pierce my heart, mind, and soul.
I was mocked by all of my people, and their song all day long.
He has filled me with bitterness, and made me drunk with wormwood.
He has also broken my teeth with gravel, and covered me with ashes.
My soul has been removed from all peace, and I have forgotten prosperity.
And I said, "My strength and hope have perished from the Lord."
I remember my affliction, misery, wormwood, and bitterness.
My soul still remembers and is humbled.
Then my mind remembers and I have hope.
It is because of the Lord's mercies that we have not been consumed, for his compassion never fails.
They are renewed every morning, for great is your faithfulness!
My soul says, "The Lord is my portion, so I will hope in him."
The Lord is good to those who wait for him, and the soul who seeks him.
It is good for a man to both quietly wait and hope for the Lord's salvation.
It is good for a man to bear his yoke while he is still young.
He sits alone in silence, because God has let him carry his yoke.
He buries his mouth in the dust, so perhaps there is still hope.
He turns the other cheek to anyone who attacks him, and he is filled with disrespect.
For the Lord will not abandon me forever.
But even though he causes grief, he will still have compassion from the abundance of his mercies.
For he does not willingly afflict nor grieve the sons of men.
To crush under his feet all the prisoners of the earth.
To deny a man's righteousness in front of the Most High.
The Lord does not approve of subverting a man's cause.
Who spoke and made it happen without the Lord's command?
Do not both evil and good proceed from the mouth of the Most High?
Why should any living man complain about the punishment of his sins?
Let us examine and test our ways, and turn back to the Lord.
Let us say, "We lift up our heart with our hands to God in heaven."
We have transgressed and rebelled, and you have not pardoned.
You have covered yourself with anger and persecuted us. You have killed us without pity.
You have covered yourself with a cloud, so that our prayers cannot pass through.
You have made us like scum and garbage among the people.
All our enemies have opened their mouths against us.
A fearful trap has come upon us, and brought devastation and destruction.
My eyes overflows with rivers of tears for the destruction of my people's daughter.
Tears unceasingly trickle down from my eyes with no intermission.
Until the Lord looks down from heaven and sees.
The things I see with my eyes grieve my heart because of all the daughters of my city.
My enemies bitterly chased me like a bird, without cause.
They dropped my life into a dungeon, and threw stones at me.
Water flowed over my head and I said, "I am dead."
O Lord, I called on your name from the depths of the dungeon.
You have heard my plea as I cried, "Please do not ignore my breathing as I cry."
You moved closer on that day when I called on you and you said, "Do not be afraid!"
O Lord, you defended my soul's cause and you redeemed my life.
O Lord, you have seen the wrong done to me, and you judged my cause.
You have seen all their vengeance and schemes against me.
O Lord, you have heard their disrespect and schemes against me.
The rumors of those who rose up against me, and their devices against me all day long.
Behold, I am their music whether they are sitting down or standing up.
O Lord, compensate them with the work of their own hands.
Give them a sorrowful heart, as your curse to them.
Persecute, destroy, and remove them from under the Lord's heavens in your anger.
O how the gold has become dim! How the most fine gold has changed! The sanctuary stones have been poured out on top of every street.
The precious sons of Zion, once compared to fine gold, are now only as valuable as clay pitchers from the potter's hands!
Even the sea monsters offer their breast to nurse their young. My people's daughters have become as cruel as ostriches in the wilderness.
The nursing child's tongue sticks to the roof of his mouth from thirst. The young children ask for bread and no one shares with them.
Those who ate delicacies are homeless in the streets, those who were brought up wearing crimson robes, embrace dunghills.
For the punishment of my people's daughter for her immorality is greater than the punishment of the sins of Sodom, that was instantly overthrown, and no one turned a hand to help her.
Her Nazarites were purer than snow and whiter than milk, their bodies were more ruddy than rubies polished like sapphires.
Now their appearance is blacker than coal, they are not recognized in the streets. Their skin has withered and sticks to their bones like a stick.
Those killed with the sword are better off than those who die from hunger and waste away from hunger pains for a lack of fruit in the field.
The hands of the pitiful women have cooked their own children, who were their meat in the destruction my people's daughter.
The Lord has accomplished his fury as he poured out his fierce anger. He has kindled a fire in Zion, and it has consumed its foundations.
The earth's kings nor the world's inhabitants believed that the adversary and enemy could have entered Jerusalem's gates.
For the sins of her prophets, and the wickedness of her priests, that have shed the blood of the just in the middle of her.
They wandered around like blind men in the streets, and they polluted themselves with blood, so that men could not even touch their garments.
They cried out to them and said, "You are unclean, so leave and do not touch us!" Then they fled and wandered away, and the heathens said, "They can no longer stay here."
The Lord's anger has divided them, he no longer respects them nor the priests, and he no longer favors the people's elders.
As for us, our eyes failed as we searched in vain for help, and we looked for a nation that could not save us.
They hunt our every step, so that we cannot go out in our own streets. Our end is near, our days are finished, for our end has come.
Our persecutors are swifter than the eagles of heaven. They pursued us on the mountains, and laid in wait for us in the wilderness.
The Lord's anointed and the breath from our nostrils was captured in their pits. For we had said of him, "We will live among the nations heathen, under his shadow."
O Daughter of Edom, rejoice and be happy that you live in the land of Uz. But this cup will also pass to you, and you will get drunk and expose your nakedness.
O Daughter of Zion, the punishment for your immorality is finshed, and he will no longer carry you away as captives. O Daughter of Edom, he will visit your immoralities and discover your sins.
O Lord, remember what has happened to us. Look and consider our disgrace!
Our inheritance has been turned over to strangers, and our houses have been given to aliens.
We are fatherless orphans and our mothers are like widows.
We must buy the water we drink for money, and our wood is sold to us.
Our necks are under the yoke of persecution, and we labor without rest.
We are subjected to the hands of the Egyptians and the Assyrians, to satisfy our need for bread.
Our fathers have sinned, and they are no longer with us. We carry the burden of their wickedness.
Servants rule over us, and there is no one to deliver us from their hands.
We get our bread at the risk of our lives because of the sword in the wilderness.
Our skin was black like an oven because of the terrible famine.
They ravished the women in Zion, and the maids in Judah's cities.
Princes were hanged by their hand, the elders' faces were not honored.
They took the young men to grind grain at the millstone, and the children fell under the loads of wood.
The elders have left the city gate, and the young men stopped making their music.
The joys of our hearts have left, our dancing has turned into mourning.
Woe unto us, the crown is fallen from our head because we have sinned!
For this our hearts have grown faint, because of these things our eyes have grown dim.
Because of Mount Zion, which lies desolate with foxes walking on it.
O Lord, you and your throne remain forever from generation to generation.
So Lord, why have you forsaken us for such a long time, and will you forget us forever?
O Lord, turn back to us and we will turn back to you to renew ourselves, like we did in the old days.
But you have completely rejected us, because you are very angry with us.
On the fifth day, of the fourth month, of my thirtieth year while I, Ezekiel was among the captives near the Kebar River, the heavens opened up and I saw visions of God.
On the fifth day of the month of the fifth year of King Jehoiachin's exile.
In the land of the Chaldeans near the Kebar River, the Lord's word came directly to me, Buzi's son Ezekiel the priest, and the Lord's hand was upon me.

I looked and I saw a whirlwind coming from the north, a great cloud with fiery lightning flashing across itself, surrounded by brilliant white light. In the midst of the fiery display, the fire glowed like amber.
Then from the midst of the cloud, the likeness of four living creatures that appeared to be human came forth.
Each one had four faces and four wings.
They had straight legs, and the soles of their feet were like calves hooves, and they shined like polished brass.
They had human hands under their wings on each of their four sides, and all four living creatures had faces and wings.
Their wings touched each other, they did not turn when they moved, and they all moved straight forward.
All four of them had a man's face on one side, a lion's face on the right side, an ox's face on the left side, and lastly an eagle's face.
That was how their faces appeared, and their wings stretched upward. Each one had two wings touching the wings of the creature next to them on each side, and two wings covered their bodies.
They each went straight forward, and wherever the spirit went, they would go without turning.
The living creatures likenesses, appeared to be like fiery burning coals or lamps. A very bright fire would flow down between the living creatures flashing like lightning.
And the living creatures ran back and forth like flashing lightning.
Now as I looked at the living creatures, I saw a wheel on the ground next to each of the living creatures with its four faces.
The wheels were crafted to look like gleaming beryl, and all four looked just alike. They appeared to be one wheel in the middle of another wheel.
They moved in all four directions, but they did not turn as they went.
Their rings were so high that they were dreadful, and all four rings were full of eyes all around them.
When the living creatures moved, the wheels moved with them. When the creatures rose up from the earth, the wheels rose up with them.
Wherever the spirit went, they also went, and the wheels would rise up beside them, because the spirit of the living creatures was in the wheels.
When the creatures moved, the wheels moved. When the creatures stood, the wheels stood. And when the creatures rose, the wheels rose, because the spirit of the living creatures was in the wheels.
Stretched out above the heads of the living creatures was what appeared to be a firmament that glowed like a majestic crystal.
Under the firmament, their wings stretched straight out toward one another, each one also had two wings which covered their bodies.
When they moved, their wings sounded like great roaring waters, or the voice of the Almighty speaking, or like the noise of a great marching army. When they stood, they lowered their wings.
A voice came from the firmament above their heads as they stood, and lowered their wings.
Above the firmament that was over their heads there appeared to be a throne that looked like a sapphire, and attached to what appeared to be the throne was the likeness of a man high above.

And from what looked like his waist up, I saw the gleaming amber color and what appeared to be fire all around its inside. And from what looked like his waist downward, I saw what appeared to be fire, and brilliant light surrounding him.

The appearance of the brilliant light surrounding him was like a rainbow in a cloud on a rain day. This was how the Lord's glory appeared to me, and when I saw it, I fell facedown, and I heard the voice of the one speaking.
The one spoke to me, Ezekiel and said, "Son of man, stand on your feet, and I will speak to you."
As he spoke to me the spirit entered me and stood me on my feet, and I heard the one speaking to me.
And he said to me, "Son of man, I am sending you to the Israelis, a rebellious nation that has rebelled against me. They and their fathers have rebelled against me to this very day.
For they are disrespectful and stubborn children. But I am sending you to them, because I want you to speak to them and say, 'This is what the Lord God says.'
Because they are a rebellious house, and whether they listen or not, they will know that a prophet has been among them.

But you, son of man, do not be afraid of them or their words. Even though they are a rebellious house and you are surrounded by briers, thorns, and scorpions, do not fear their words or be dismayed by the expressions on their faces.
But you must speak my words to them, whether they listen or not, because they are most rebellious.
But you, son of man, hear what I say to you and do not be rebellious like that rebellious house. Open your mouth, and eat what I give you."
Then I looked up, and I saw a hand reaching out to me with a book in it.
And he spread it out before me, and there were lamentations, mourning, and sorrows written within it and on its cover.
Furthermore he spoke to me, Ezekiel and said "Son of man, eat what you find here. Eat what is in this book, then go and speak to the House of Israel."
So I opened my mouth, and he made me eat the book.
And he said to me, "Son of man, fill your stomach and bowels and eat what is in this book that I have given you." Then I ate it, and it tasted as sweet as honey in my mouth.
And he said to me, "Son of man, go to the House of Israel, and speak my words to them.
For you are not being sent to a people of strange speech or a difficult language, but to the House of Israel.
But surely, if I had sent you to many other people of strange speech or a difficult language whose words you do not understand, they would have listened to you.
But the House of Israel will not listen to you, because they will not listen to me. For the entire House of Israel is disrespectful and hardhearted.
Behold, I have made your face as strong as their faces, and your forehead as strong as their foreheads.
I have made your forehead like a diamond and harder than flint. Do not fear them or be dismayed by their looks, even though they are rebellious."
Furthermore he said to me, "Son of man, listen carefully and store all the words that I speak to you in your heart.
And go to your people and their descendants in captivity, and whether or not they will listen, speak to them and say, 'This is what the Lord God says!'"
Then the spirit lifted me up, and I heard the voice of a great rushing wind behind me that said, "Blessed be the glory of the Lord from his place."
I also heard the noise of the living creatures wings as they touched each other, and the sound of the wheels next to them, a great rushing noise.
So the spirit lifted me up and took me away, and I left with bitterness and anger in my spirit, but the strong hand of the Lord was upon me.
Then I came to the exiles in Telabib, who lived near the Kebar River, and for seven days I sat there among them, completely astonished.
After seven days the Lord's word came to me.
And he said, "Son of man, I have made you a watchman over the House of Israel, so hear my words and warn them for me.

When I say to the wicked, 'You will surely die!' And you do not speak out and warn him about his wicked ways to save his life, that wicked man will die in his immorality, but I will hold you responsible for his blood.
But if you warn the wicked man, and he does not turn from his wickedness and his wicked ways, he will die in his immorality, but you will have saved your soul.

Again, when a righteous man turns away from his righteousness and commits immorality, and I lay a stumbling block before him, he will die. If you did not warn him, he will die in his sin, and the righteous things he has done will not be remembered. But I will hold you responsible for his blood.
But if you warn the righteous man, and that righteous man does not sin, he will surely live, because he was warned, and you have also saved your soul."
And the Lord's hand was upon me there and he said, "Rise up, go out into the plains, and I will talk with you there."
Then I got up, and went out into the plains, and behold the Lord's glory stood there, like the glory which I had seen near the Kebar River, and I fell facedown.
Then the spirit entered me, set me up on my feet, and spoke to me and said, "Go, and shut yourself inside your house.
But you son of man, will be bound with ropes, and you will be unable to go out among the people.
I will make your tongue stick to the roof of your mouth, you will be silenced, and you will be unable to rebuke them, because they are a rebellious house.

But after I speak with you, I will open your mouth, and you will say to them, 'This is what the Lord God says, "Whoever listens, let him hear, and whoever refuses to listen, let him refuse, because they are a rebellious house."'"
He also spoke to me, Ezekiel and said, "Son of man, you must also lay a clay tablet before you, and draw the city of Jerusalem on it.
Then lay siege against it, build a fort and a mountain ramp, and set up camps against it, then surround it with battering rams.

Use an iron pan to build an iron wall between you and the city. When you turn your face against it, you will lay siege against it, and it will be under siege. This will be a sign to the House of Israel.
Then lie down on your left side, and lay the immorality of the House of Israel upon yourself. And you will bear Israel's immorality for the number of days that you lie on your side.
For I have assigned 390 days for you to bear the House of Israel's immorality, which is equal to their 390 years of immorality.
After 390 days, lie on your right side and you will bear the house of Judah's immorality for forty more days, for I have appointed you one day for each year.
Then turn your face toward the siege of Jerusalem, and prophesy against it with your uncovered arm.
And behold, I will bind you with ropes, so that you cannot turn from one side to the other, until you have finished all the days of your siege.
Take enough wheat, barley, beans, lentils, grain, and cumin to make enough bread for yourself to eat for the entire 390 days that you lie on your side.
You must ration the meat that you eat, and measure out about 6 1/2 ounces a day to eat each day at meal time.
You must also measure out about one-sixth of a gallon of water to drink at certain times of the day.
And you will eat this food as you would eat barley cakes, after you bake it with human dung as the people are watching."
And the Lord said, "This is how the children of Israel will eat their defiled bread among the Gentiles, where I will drive them."

Then I said, "Ah Lord God! Behold, from my youth to this very day, my soul has never been polluted, and I have not eaten anything that has died of natural causes, or has been torn to pieces by wild animals. No abominable meat has ever entered my mouth."
Then he said to me, "Very well, I will let you use cow dung instead of human dung to bake your bread."
He also said to me, "Son of man, behold I intend to break the staff of bread in Jerusalem, and they will eat bread rationed by weight, and they will carefully drink measured water with astonishment.
They will suffer and want for bread and water, and they will be astonished as they watch each other waste away in their immorality."
And he spoke to me, Ezekiel and said, "Son of man, use a sharp knife like a barber's razor, and shave your head and beard. Then weigh out and divide the hair on a set of scales.

After the days of the siege have ended, burn one third of it in a fire in the middle of the city. Then take a third of it and slash it with a knife, and scatter a third of it in the wind. And I will draw a sword behind them.
Keep a few strands of hair and bind them to the seams of your garment.
Then take a few more strands of hair, and throw them into the fire and burn them, because from that a fire will spread throughout the entire House of Israel."
This is what the Lord God says, "This is Jerusalem, which I have set at the center of all the nations and countries around her.
She has turned my laws and judgments into wickedness more so than any of the other nations or countries around her, because they have refused to obey and walk in my laws and judgments."

Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says, "Because you have rebelled more than all the other nations around you, and you have not obeyed nor walked in my laws and judgments, nor have you kept all the judgments of the other nations around you."
Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says, "Behold, I am against you, and I will execute my judgments in your midst where all the nations can see it.
And because of all of your abominations, I will do to you something that I have never done before and will never do again.
That's why the fathers will eat their sons, and the sons will eat their fathers. I will execute judgments against you, and I will scatter whatever remains of you in the wind.

Therefore the Lord God says, "As surely as I live, and because you have defiled my sanctuary with all your detestable things and abominations, you will be diminished in my eyes, and I will not spare you nor will I have any pity.

A third you will die from pestilences and famine will consume them in your midst. A third of them will fall by the sword all around you, and I will scatter a third of them into the wind, and draw out a sword behind them.
This will ease my anger after it has been accomplished, my fury will rest on them and I will be comforted, and they will know that in my zeal, I the Lord have spoken and my wrath has been soothed.
I will also make you a waste and dispised among all the nations around you, and in the sight of whoever passes by you.

So you will be disapproved, taunted, a warning and an astonishment to all the nations around you, when I execute my judgments against you in anger, fury and furious rebukes. For I the Lord have spoken.
When I send the evil arrows of famine to you to destroy you, I will increase your famine, and break the staff of bread you depend on.
So I will send famine and evil beasts against you, and they will bereave you. Pestilence and blood will pass through you, and I will bring the sword against you. For I the Lord have spoken."
And the Lord's word came to me, Ezekiel again.
And he said, "Son of man, turn your face toward Israel's mountains and prophesy against them.

And say, 'O Mountains of Israel, hear the Lord God's word! This is what the Lord God says to the mountains, hills, rivers, and valleys, "Behold I will send a sword against you and destroy your high places.
Your altars will be demolished and your images will be broken. I will throw your killed men before your idols.
I will lay the Israelites dead corpses before their idols and scatter your bones all around your altars.

The cities, their high places, and your altars will be laid waste, decimated, and demolished wherever you live. Your idols will be broken and cease to exist, your images will be cut down, and your works will be wiped out.
Your dead will fall in your midst and you will know that I am the Lord.
But I will leave a few survivors, so that some will escape the sword and be scattered among the nations throughout the land.

And those of you who escape will remember me among the nations wherever you are carried away as captives. Because I have broken the whorish hearts of those who left me, and those who go whoring after their idols with their eyes. They will loathe themselves for the evil they have committed with their abominations.
And they will know that I am the Lord, and that I did not say in vain that I would do this evil to them."'"
This is what the Lord says, "Clap your hands and stomp your feet and say, 'Alas!' Because of the all evil abominations of the House of Israel, they will fall by the sword, famine, and pestilence.
The one far away will die of the pestilence, the one nearby will fall by the sword, the one who remains will die by the famine, and this is how I will relieve my fury against them.

Then you will know that I am the Lord, when their dead men lie among their idols and altars on every high hill and mountain top, under every green tree and every thick oak, in the place where they offered sweet savory offerings to their idols.
So wherever they live, I will stretch out my hand against them, and make their land desolate, more desolate than the wilderness toward Diblath, and they will know that I am the Lord."
Furthermore the Lord's word came to me, Ezekiel.
And he said, "Son of Man, this is what the Lord God of Israel says, 'The end! The end has come for the four corners of the land.
Now the end has also come for you, and I will send my anger against you. I will judge you for your ways, and I will repay you for all of your abominations.

I will see you, but I will not spare you nor will I have pity on you. But I will repay you for your ways and the abominations that you have allowed within your midst. Then you will know that I am the Lord.'"
This is what the Lord God says, "Behold evil, and only evil has come!
The end has come! The end has come! And, it has come looking for you!
Those of you who live in the land, now is the time, for morning has come to you. The day of trouble is near, and once again, the sounds of joy are not on the mountains.
Soon, I will pour out my fierce anger upon you. I will judge you for your ways and repay you for all of your abominations.

I will see you and I will not spare you nor have pity, and I will repay you for your ways and the abominations which you have allowed within your midst. Then you will know that I am the Lord who destroys.
Behold the day has come! Mourning has gone out, the staff has budded, and pride has bloomed.
Violence has grown into a staff of wickedness! None of them will remain, none of their people, none of their wealth, and there will be no cries or tears for them.
The time has come and the day draws near that the buyer will not rejoice, nor will the seller mourn, because God's anger is upon all of its people.

For the seller has not redeemed those whom he has sold even though they are still alive. Because the vision of the entire population will not be repealed, nor will anyone be allowed to strengthen themselves with the immoralities of their own life.
They have blown the trumpet and prepared for battle, but no one goes to war, because my anger is upon all of their armies.
The sword is outside the gates, but pestilence and famine are within. Those out in the field will die by the sword, and those in the city will be devoured by famine and pestilence.
But the survivors will escape to the mountains, mourning like valley doves for their immoralities.
Every hand will be feeble, and every knee will be as weak as water.
They will also wear sackcloth, and horror will overcome them. Shame will cover their faces, and they will all shave their heads.

They will throw their silver in the streets, and their gold will be removed. Their gold and silver will be unable to deliver them from the Lord's day of anger. They will be unable to satisfy their souls or fill their stomachs, because their wealth has become the stumbling block of their own immorality.
The majestic and beautiful ornaments in his temple, have been transformed into their images of abominations and detestable things. So I have removed them far away from them.
I will hand these things over to strangers as loot and plunder to the earth's wicked people as spoils of war, who will pollute them.
I will also turn my face from them, and they will pollute my secret place because the robbers will defile it.
Forge the chain, because the land is full of bloody crimes, and the city is full of violence.
Therefore I will bring the worst heathen to take possession of their houses. I will also make the strong and pompous cease to exist, and their holy places will be defiled.
Destruction comes! They will seek peace, but they will not find it.
Mischief will overtake the mischievous, and rumor after rumor will be heard. Then they will seek a prophet's vision, but the law from the priest will perish, so will the counsel of the elders.

The king will mourn, princes will be clothed in desperation, and the hands of the people of the land will tremble. I will treat them the way they have treated others, and I will judge them with their own values. Then they will know that I am the Lord."
On the fifth day, of the sixth year, of the sixth month, as I, Ezekiel sat in my house with Judah's elders, the Lord God's hand fell upon me.
Then I looked and saw what appeared to be a man with fire from his waist down, and from his waist upward he appeared to be the color of brilliantly glowing amber.

He put out what looked like a hand, and took me by the hair of my head. Then the spirit lifted me up between heaven and earth, and brought me in visions of God to the northern door of the inner gate in Jerusalem, where the image that provokes jealousy was seated.
And behold, I saw the glory of the God of Israel there, just like the vision that I saw out on the plains.
Then God spoke to me, Ezekiel and said, "Son of man, look up toward the north." So I looked up toward the north, and I saw this image of jealousy in the entrance of the northern altar gate.

Furthermore he said to me, "Son of man, do you see what they are doing? Do you see the great abominations that the House of Israel has committed here, that has driven me far away from my sanctuary? But, you will see eve greater abominations when you turn around."
Then God brought me to the courtyard door, and when I looked, I saw a hole in the wall.
Then he spoke to me, Ezekiel and said, "Son of man, dig through the wall." So I dug through the wall, and I found a doorway on the other side.
Then he spoke to me, Ezekiel and said, "Go in and see the wicked abominations that they are doing here."
So I went in and I saw every form of creeping thing, reptile, abominable beast, and all the other idols of the House of Israel drawn on all over their walls.
And I stood before seventy elders from the House of Israel, and Shaphan's son Jaazaniah stood among them. Each man had a thick cloud of incense rising from the censer he had in his hand.

Then God said to me, "Son of man, have you seen what the elders of the House of Israel do in the dark, in the chambers of their own images? For they say, 'The Lord has not seen us, because he has forsaken the earth.'"
Then God spoke to me, Ezekiel and said, "Turn around again, and you will see them committing even greater abominations.
Then he brought me to the door of the northern gate of the Lord's house, and I saw women weeping for Tammuz the Mesopotamian fertility god.
Then he said to me, "O Son of Man, do you see this? Turn around again, and you will see even greater abominations than these."

Then God brought me into the inner court of the Lord's house, and between the entrance hall and the altar at the door of the Lord's temple, I saw about twenty-five men, facing east, with their backs turned to the Lord's temple, and they were worshipping the eastern sun.

Then he said to me, O Son of Man, have you seen this? Is it not enough that the house of Judah commits all the abominations that they have committed here? But they have filled the land with violence to constantly provoke my anger? And look at them, they even put the branch to their nose.
Therefore, I will also deal with them in my fury. I will see them, but I will not spare them, nor will I have pity. And even though they cry out to me with a loud voice, I will not hear them.
Then God also cried out to me, Ezekiel with a loud voice and said, "Draw near, all of you who have taken over the city, even all of you destroyers armed with weapons."

And, behold six men came from the higher northern gate, one carrying a weapon of slaughter in his hand. There was one man among them clothed in linen who had a writing kit next to him. And they went in and stood beside the brass altar.
Then the God of Israel's glory rose up from the cherub where he had been, and moved to the temple's threshold, and he called out to the man clothed in linen, who had the writing kit next to him.
And the Lord said to him, "Go throughout the city of Jerusalem, and mark the foreheads of the men who sigh and cry for all the abominations done in city's midst."
And as I, Ezekiel was listening he said to the others, "Follow him throughout the city, killing everyone, do not spare nor have pity on anyone.

Completely slaughter both young and old, men and women, virgins, children, and infants, but do not go near any man who has the mark, and begin at my sanctuary." Then they began with the elders who were in front of the temple.
Then the Lord spoke to them and said, "Defile the house, and fill the courtyards with the dead, now go!" And they left, and killed throughout the city.
While they were killing them, I was left alone, and I fell facedown and cried out and said, "Oh Lord God! When you pour out your fury on Jerusalem, are you going to destroy all of Israel's survivors?

Then the Lord spoke to me, Ezekiel and said, "Israel and Judah's immorality is exceedingly great, the land is full of blood, and the city is full of perversions. Because they say, 'The Lord has forsaken the earth, and he does not see us.'
But as for me, I will see them, but I will not spare them, nor will I have pity on them, but I will repay them and bring their ways down on their own heads."
Then the man with the writing kit who was clothed in linen reported to the Lord and said, "I have done as you commanded!"
Then I, Ezekiel looked up and, in the firmament above the cherubims head, there appeared to be a sapphire throne.

And the Lord spoke to the man clothed in linen and said, "Go between the wheels under the cherub, and take the burning coals from between the cherubims with your hands, and scatter them over the city!" And I watched as he went in.
Now when the man went in, the cherubims stood on the temple's right side, and a cloud filled the inner court.
Then the Lord's glory left the cherub, and stood over the temple's threshold, the cloud filled the temple, and the courtyard was filled with Lord's glorious brilliance.
The sound of the cherubims wings could be heard all the way out to the outer courtyard, and it sounded like the voice of God Almighty when he speaks.
Then the lord commanded the man clothed in linen and said, "Take the fire from the wheels between the cherubims," so he went and stood beside the wheels.
Then one cherub stretched out his hand and took some of the fire that was between the cherubims, and put it into the hands of the man clothed in linen, who took it and left.
The cherubim appeared to have what looked like human hands under their wings.
When I looked, I saw the four wheels beside the cherubim, one wheel beside each cherub, and the wheels appeared to be the color of a beryl gemstone.
As for their appearance, all four looked alike, and they appeared to be a wheel within a wheel.
When they moved, they could go in four different directions, but they did not turn as they went. They would go in whatever direction the head looked, but they did not turn as they went.
Their whole body, including their backs, hands, and wings were full of and surrounded by eyes, and so were the wheels.
I heard them crying out to the wheels and saying, "O wheels."
Each one had four faces, the first face was a cherub's face, and the second face was a man's face, and the third face was a lion's face, and the fourth face was an eagle's face.
Then the cherubims rose upward. These were the living creature that I saw near the Kebar River.
When the cherubims moved, the wheels moved beside them, and when the cherubims lifted their wings to fly from the ground to the mountain, the wheels did not leave their side.
When they stood, the wheels also stood, and when they flew up, the wheels also flew with them, because the spirit of the living creatures was in them.
Then the Lord's glory left the temple's threshold, and stood over the cherubims.

And as I, Ezekiel watched, the cherubims raised their wings, and flew up from the earth, and the wheels beside them also left when they left. They all stopped at the entrance of the east gate of the Lord's temple, and the God of Israel's glory was above them.
These are the descriptions of the living creatures that I saw under the God of Israel near the Kebar River, and I knew that they were cherubims.
Each one had four faces and four wings, and what looked like human hands under their wings.
Their faces were the same faces I saw near the Kebar River, and they all moved straight forward.

Then the spirit also lifted me up and brought me to the east gate of the Lord's house. And I saw twenty-five men at the gate's doorway, along with Prince Jaazaniah son of Azur, and Prince Pelatiah son of Benaiah, both leaders of the people.
Then the Lord spoke to me, Ezekiel and said, "Son of man, these are the men who devise mischief, and advise this city wickedly.
They say, 'Is it not the time to build houses? This city is a caldron, and we be the meat in the stew.'
Therefore O son of man, prophesy against them!"
And the Spirit of the Lord fell on me and told me to speak and this is what the Lord says, "O House of Israel, this is what you think, and I know everything that comes into your minds.
You have multiplied those you killed in this city, and you have filled its streets with the dead."
Therefore this is what the Lord God says, "The people you have killed and laid in the middle of this city will be the meat, and this city is the caldron, but I will bring you out of it."
And the Lord God says, "You fear the sword, so I will bring a sword against you."
I will bring you out of the city and deliver you into the hands of strangers, and I will execute my judgments against you.
You will fall by the sword, and I will judge you all the way to the borders of Israel, and you will know that I am the Lord.
This city will not be your caldron, nor you will be the meat in the stew, but I will judge you all the way to the borders of Israel.
And you will know that I am the Lord! For you have not walked in my laws nor executed my judgments, but you have obeyed the heathen orders of the nations are all around you."
While I prophesied, Benaiah's son Pelatiah died. Then I fell facedown, and cried out in a loud voice and said, "Oh Lord God! Will you totally end what remains of Israel?"
Then the Lord's word came to me again.

And the Lord God said, "Son of man, even your brothers, relatives, and the entire House of Israel are the people from Jerusalem who have said, 'We are far from the Lord, and this land has been given to us as a possession.'"

Therefore this is what the Lord God says, "Even though I have thrown them far away among the heathen and scattered them among the countries, I will still be like a little sanctuary to them in the countries where they have gone."
Furthermore this is what the Lord God says, "I will gather you from the people, and assemble you from the countries where you have been scattered, and I will give you the land of Israel.
When they return to that place, they will remove all the detestable things and all the abominations there.
And I will give them a united heart, and I will put a new spirit in them, and I will remove their heart of stone and I will give them a heart of flesh.
So that they may walk in my laws, keep my legal decrees, and practice them. Then they will be my people, and I will be their God."
But as for those whose hearts chase after the detestable things and abominations, this is what the Lord God says, 'I will repay them in their own ways, on their own heads.'"
Then the cherubims lifted up their wings and the wheels beside them, and the God of Israel's glory shown above them.
And the Lord's glory rose up from the middle of the city, and stood on the mountain east of the city.
Afterwards, in a vision from the Spirit of God, the spirit picked me up, and brought me back to the captives in Chaldea. After the vision that I had seen left me.
I spoke to the exiles in captivity, and told them everything that the Lord had shown me.
Then the word of the Lord came to me, Ezekiel.
And the Lord said, "Son of man, you live in a rebellious house, whose people have eyes but do not to see, they have ears but do not hear, because they are a rebellious house.

Therefore son of man, prepare to remove your stuff into exile. You will move from your place to another place, during the day as they are watching. So that they may understand, even though they are rebellious.
Then bring out the stuff that you prepared for exile during the day as they are watching. And in the evening you will leave while they are watching, as one that goes into captivity.
Dig through the wall while they are watching, and carry your stuff out through the wall.
While they are watching, carry your stuff on your shoulders out into the twilight. Cover your face, so that you cannot see the ground, because I have made you a sign to the House of Israel."

And I did as I was commanded, I brought my stuff prepared for exile out during the day, and in the evening I dug through the wall with my hands. Then I carried my stuff on my shoulder, and walked out into the twilight, as they all watched.
In the morning the Lord's word came to me, Ezekiel.
And the Lord said, "Son of man, has not the rebellious House of Israel said to you, 'What are you doing?'
Tell them, this is what the Lord God says, 'This burden concerns the prince and the entire House of Israel in Jerusalem.'
Then say, 'I am your sign.' Just as I have done, so will it be done to them, they will removed and carried into captivity.

And in the twilight, the prince among them will carry his stuff out on his shoulder, and dig through the wall to carry his stuff out through the wall. And he will cover his face, so that he cannot see the ground.
I will also spread my net over him, and he will be caught in my snare. I will bring him to Babylon in the land of the Chaldeans, but will he not see it, even though he will die there.
And I will scatter him, his officers, and troops to all the winds, and I will draw the sword to chase after them.
And they will know that I am the Lord, when I scatter them among the nations, and disperse them throughout the countries.

But I will save a few of their men from the sword, famine, and pestilence, so that they may declare all of their abominations among the heathen where they are exiled. Then they will know that I am the Lord."
Moreover the Lord's word came to me, Ezekiel.
And the Lord said, "Son of Man, carefully eat your bread and drink your water with trembling fear.

Speak to the people of the land and say, "This is what the Lord God says about those living in the land of Israel, 'They will carefully and fearfully eat their bread and drink their water. Her land be made desolate and stripped of everything there, because of all the violence of those who live there.
And the inhabited cities will be laid waste, and the land will become desolate. Then you will know that I am the Lord.'"
And the word of the Lord came to me, Ezekiel.
And the Lord said, "Son of man, what is the proverb that you have in the land of Israel that says, 'The days are prolonged, and every vision fails!'?

Therefore tell them this is what the Lord God says, 'I will end this proverb, and they will no longer use it as a proverb in Israel.' But say to them, 'The days are here, and the effects of every vision will be seen.
For there will be no longer be any empty visions or flattering divinations within the House of Israel.'"

And the Lord God said, "O rebellious house, I am the Lord and when I speak, whatever I speak will come to pass! My words will no longer be prolonged, because in your lifetime I will say the word, and it will happen."
Again the word of the Lord came to me, Ezekiel.
And the Lord God said, "Son of Man, behold those from the House of Israel say, 'The vision that he sees is for the distant future, and he prophecies of times that are far from now.'"
Therefore the Lord God says, "Tell them that the Lord God has spoken and said, 'My words will be delayed no longer, but the words which I have spoken will be done.'"
And the word of the Lord came to me, Ezekiel.
And the Lord said, "Son of Man, prophesy against the prophets of Israel who prophesy from their own hearts and say to them, 'Hear the Lord's word!
For this is what the Lord God says, "Woe is the foolish prophet who follow their own spirit, and have seen nothing!"'
O Israel, your prophets are like foxes in the deserts.
You have not gone up into the gaps nor restored the hedge, so that the House of Israel could stand in the battle on the Lord's day.
They have seen empty visions and lying divinations and said, 'The Lord says,' but the Lord has not sent them, and they have made others hope that they would confirm their words.
Have you not seen empty visions, and have you not spoken a lying divination, when you in fact say, 'The Lord has said it,' even though I have not spoken?"
Therefore this is what the Lord God says, "Because you have spoken vain words and seen lies, I am against you."

My hand will be against the prophets who see empty visions, and those who divine lies. They will not be part of my people's assembly. They will not be written in the register of the House of Israel, nor will they enter into the land of Israel! Then you will know that I am the Lord God.
Because, they have seduced my people and said, 'Peace!' But there was no peace, and they built a wall, and others plastered it with weak mortar.
Tell those who plastered it with weak mortar, that it will fall. An overflowing shower of great hailstones will fall on it and a stormy wind will tear it down.
After the wall has fallen, they will not ask you, 'Where is the plaster that you used to plaster the wall?'"
Therefore this is what the Lord God says, "In my furious anger I will tear it down with a stormy wind and an overflowing shower of great hailstones to consume it.

I will tear down to the ground the wall that you have plastered with weak mortar, so that its foundation is exposed. And the city will fall, and you will be consumed in its midst. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
After this I will turn my anger against the wall and those who plastered it with weak mortar. Then I will say to you, 'The wall is gone, and so are those who plastered it.'
In other words, I will turn my anger against the prophets of Israel who prophesy about Jerusalem, and see visions of peace for her, when there is no peace."
And the Lord God says, "Son of Man prophesy against, and turn your face against your people's daughters who prophesy from their own heart.

And say, 'This is what the Lord God says, "Woe is the women who sew magic bracelets for their wrists, and make scarfs for the heads of every height to hunt their souls! Will you hunt the souls of my people, but save your own soul?

Will you pollute me among my own people for a handful of barley or a piece of bread? Will you kill the souls that should not die, and save the souls of those who should not live, by lying to my people who hear your lies?"'"

Therefore this is what the Lord God says, "Behold I am against your magic bracelets, that you use to hunt the souls to make them fly like birds, and I will tear them from your arms. So I will set those souls free, even the souls that you hunt the souls to make them fly like birds.
I will also tear your scarfs, and deliver my people from your hands, and they will be no longer be hunted by you. Then you will know that I am the Lord.

Because you have made the righteous hearts sad with your lies, even though I have not made them sad. You have also strengthened the hands of the wicked and promised them life, so that they would not turn from their wicked ways.
Therefore you will see no longer see empty visions or divine lies, because I will deliver my people from your clutches. Then you will know that I am the Lord."
Then some of Israel's elders came and sat before me, Ezekiel.
And the Lord's word of came to me.
And the Lord said, "Son of man, these men have set up idols in their hearts, and put their immoral stumbling blocks before themselves, should I speak to all of them anyway?

So speak to them and tell them this is what the Lord God says, 'Anyone from the House of Israel who sets up idols in his heart, and puts their immoral stumbling block before themselves, then comes to the prophet, I the Lord will answer them with the advice of their multitude of idols.
So that I may keep the people's hearts of the House of Israel, for they are all estranged from me because of their idols.'
Therefore tell the House of Israel that this is what the Lord God says, 'Repent and turn away from your idols and abominations.

For everyone of the House of Israel or foreigners living in Israel who separates himself from me, and sets up idols in his heart, and puts his immoral stumbling block before himself, and comes to ask a prophet about me, I the Lord will answer him myself.
And I will set my face against that man and will make him a sign and a proverb, and I will cut him off from among my people. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
But if a prophet is deceived and speaks a false a message, then I the Lord have deceived him, and I will stretch out my hand against him, and destroy him from among my people Israel.
Then they will bear the punishment of their immorality, and the prophet will be punished just like anyone who seeks his advice.
So that the House of Israel no longer goes astray from me, and no longer pollute themselves with all their transgressions. Then they will be my people, and I will be their God.'"
Again the word of the Lord came to me, Ezekiel.

And the Lord said, "Son of man, when the land sins against me by trespassing grievously, then I will stretch out my hand against it, and break its staff of bread and send famine against it, and I will cut off both man and beast from it."
And the Lord said, "Even though these three men Noah, Daniel, and Job were in the land, their righteousness could only deliver their own souls.
If I send foul smelling beasts throughout the land to spoil it, so that it is left desolate, then no man will pass through it for fear of the beasts."
And the Lord said, "As I live, even though these three men were in the land, they could not deliver their own sons or daughters. They can only deliver themselves, but the land will be desolate.
Or if I bring a sword against that land and say, 'Sword, go throughout the land,' so that I cut off both man and beast from it."
Then the Lord God said, "As I live, even though these three men were in the land, they could not deliver their own sons or daughters, but they themselves will be the only ones delivered.
Or if I send a pestilence into that land, and pour out my fierce anger on it with bloodshed, and cut it off from both man and beast."

And the Lord God says, "As I live, even though Noah, Daniel, and Job were in the land, they could not deliver their sons or daughters, but their souls were the only ones that could be delivered by their righteousness.

For this is what the Lord God says, "How much worse will it be when I send my four bitter judgments against Jerusalem including the sword, famine, foul smelling beasts, and pestilence to cut it off from both man and beast?

But there will be some survivors left, both sons and daughters who will be brought out. And behold they will come to you, and you will see their ways and their deeds, and you will be comforted for all of the evil that I have brought upon Jerusalem."
And the Lord God says, "They will comfort you, when you see their ways and their deeds, and you will know that everything I have done, I have not done without cause."
Then the word of the Lord came to me, Ezekiel.
And the Lord said, "Son of man, why is the vine better than any tree, or a branch from any tree of the forest?
Can wood be taken from it to do any kind of work, or can men make a peg to hang a bowl on from of its wood?
No, it is thrown into the fire for fuel, the fire devours and burns both its ends and the middle. Is it good for anything?
Even when it was whole, it was not meant for useful work. How much less useful will it be for any work, after the fire has devoured and burned it up?"
Therefore this is what the Lord God says, "Like the vine among the trees of the forest, which I have given to the fire for fuel, so I will give up the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
I will turn my face against them, and they will go from one fire to another, and it will devour them. And when I turn my face against them, you will know that I am the Lord."
And the Lord God says, "Because, I will make the land desolate, for they have trespassed against me."
Again the word of the Lord came to me, Ezekiel.
And the Lord said, "Son of Man, confront Jerusalem about her abominations.
And tell her that this is what the Lord God says, 'O Jerusalem, you were born and you are native to the land of Canaan, your father was an Amorite and your mother was a Hittite.
On the day you were born your umbilical cord was not cut, you were not washed and cleansed in water, you were not rubbed with salt, nor were you held and comforted in warm blankets.
No one pitied you enough to do any of these for you, or have compassion for you. But on the day you was born you were thrown out into the open field, to be loathed.
When I passed by, I saw that you were wallowing in your own blood. When I saw you lying in your own blood I said, "Live!" Yes, when I saw you lying in your own blood I said, "Live!"
I made you multiply like the plants in the field. You have increased and grown great, and become beautiful ornaments. You were naked and bare, but your breasts have formed, and your hair has grown.'"

Then the Lord God said, "I passed by and saw that your time for love was here. So I spread my robe over you and covered your nakedness. Yes, I swore an oath and entered into a covenant with you, and you became mine.
Then I thoroughly washed your blood away with water, and I anointed you with oil.
I also clothed you in fine linen embroidered with silk, and I covered your feet with leather sandals.
I adorned you with jewelry and put bracelets on your wrists, and a chain around your neck.
I put a jewel on your forehead, and earrings in your ears, and a beautiful crown on your head.

So you were adorned with gold and silver, and your clothes were made of fine embroidered linen and silk. You ate fine flour, honey, and oil. You were extremely beautiful, and you prospered into a kingdom."
And the Lord God said, "Your fame spread among the heathen because of your beauty, for the beauty which I put on you was perfect.
But you trusted in your own beauty, and played the whore because of your fame. You poured out your fornications on anyone who passed by, and it was theirs for the asking.
You took your garments and covered your high places with many different colors, and then played the prostitute. These things should never have happened!
You also took my fine gold and silver jewels, which I had given to you, and made images of men for yourself, and committed prostitution with them.
You used your embroidered garments to cover them, and you placed my oil and incense before them."
And the Lord God said, "You also took my meat, fine flour, oil, and honey, which I gave you to feed you, and placed it before them as a sweet savor, and that is what happened.
You have also taken your sons and your daughters, whom you bore to me, and sacrificed them to be devoured by your idols. Was your whoring just a small matter to you?
You have killed my children, and delivered them through the fire for your idols?
And in all of your abominations and whores you did not remember the days of your youth when you were naked and bare, wallowing in your own blood."
And the Lord God said, "Woe, woe to you! And after all of your wickedness.
You have also built a prestigious shrine to yourself in every high place on every street.
You built your high places at the head of every street, and made your beauty abhorrent. You have multiplied your whoring and spread your legs to everyone who passed by.
You also committed fornication with your Egyptian neighbors. And great of flesh you have increased your whoring, to provoke my anger.
Therefore I have stretched out my hand over you, and reduced your daily food. I have delivered you over to those who hate you, the daughters of the Philistines, who are ashamed of your obscene ways.
You have also played the whore with the Assyrians, because you were insatiable. Yes, you have played the whore with them and still you were never satisfied.
You have also multiplied your fornication in the land from Canaan to Chaldea, and yet you were never satisfied there either."
And the Lord God says, "How weak is your heart, you do all of these things, which are the work of an overbearing whorish woman.
But when you built your prestigious shrines at the head of every street, and made your high places in every street, you did not act like a prostitute, because you refused to be hired.
But you are like an adulterous wife who commits adultery, and takes strangers instead of her husband!
They give gifts to all their whores, but you give gifts to all of your lovers. You hire them, so that they may come to you from every direction for your prostitution.
So your prostitution is contrary from other women, in fact no one comes to you looking for whores, and you give a reward instead of receiving a reward, so you are very contrary."
So you whore, listen and hear the Lord's word.

This is what the Lord God says, "Because your filth was poured out, and your nakedness discovered through your whores and lovers, and all your idols of abomination, and because of the blood of your children, which you gave them.

That's why I will gather all of your lovers with whom you have taken pleasure, and all of those whom you have loved, along with all of those you have hated. I will gather them against you from all around, and expose your nakedness to them, so that everyone will see all of your nakedness.
And I will judge you, as women who commit adultery and shed blood are judged, and I will give you the fury of your bloodshed and jealousy.
Then I will hand you over to them, and they will tear down your prestigious shrines and high places, they will strip off your clothes, take your fine jewels, and leave you naked and bare.
They will also bring a gang against you, and they will stone you, and thrust you through with their swords.
They will burn your houses, and execute judgments against you in sight of many women, and I will make you stop playing the whore, and you will never be hired again.
So I will rest my fury toward you, my jealousy will leave you, then I will be quiet, and I will no longer be angry."

And the Lord God says, "Because you did not remember the days of your youth, but you have worried me with all these things, I will repay you and bring your ways down on your own head. And you will no longer commit this obscenity above all your other abominations.
Behold, everyone who uses proverbs will use this proverb against you and say, 'Like mother, like daughter.'

You are your mother's daughter, who loathes her husband and her children. You are your sister's sister, who loathed their husbands and their children. Your mother was a Hittite, and your father was an Amorite.
Your oldest sister was Samaria, she and her daughters live north of you, and your younger sister was Sodom, who lives with her daughters south of you.
But you did not walk in their ways, nor practice their abominations. And since you felt that it was a very small thing, you were soon even more corrupt than them in every way."
And the Lord God says, "As I live, your sister Sodom nor her daughters have done what you and your daughters have done.
