Behold, this was your sister Sodom and her daughter's immoralities. They were prideful and gluttonous, with an abundance of idleness, and she did not help the poor and needy.
They were arrogant, and committed abominations before me, so I took them away and then I saw good.
Furthermore Samaria has not committed half of your sins, but you have multiplied your abominations more than they have. You have justified your sisters by all the abominations you have committed.

You who have also judged your sisters, bear the shame for your own sins, and you have committed more abominable things than they have. They are more righteous than you, and you are also confused, and you bear your shame since you have justified your sisters.
When I bring Sodom, Samaria, and their daughters back from their captivity, I will bring you and your captives back to be among them.
So that you may bear your own shame and confusion from everything that you did to comfort them.
When your sisters, Sodom, Samaria, and their daughters return to their former estates, then you and your daughters will return to your former estate.
For you did not mention your sister Sodom on the day of your pride.
Before your wickedness was discovered, when you were disrespected by the Philistines and Syria's daughters, and everyone all around you who despise you."
And the Lord said, "You have carried your obscenity and abominations."
Therefore this is what the Lord God says, "I will deal with you as you have dealt with others who have despised the oath and broken the covenant.
Nevertheless, I will remember my covenant with you in the days of your youth, and I will establish an everlasting covenant with you.
Then you will remember your ways and be ashamed when you receive your younger and older sisters. I will give them to you as daughters, but not because of my covenant with you.
And I will establish my covenant with you. Then you will know that I am the Lord."

And the Lord God says, "So that you can remember and be confused, and you will never again open your mouth because of your shame. For all my anger toward you has been pacified, because of everything you have done."
And the word of the Lord came to me, Ezekiel.
And the Lord said, "Son of Man, speak and submit a riddle and a parable to the House of Israel.
Tell them that this is what the Lord God says, 'A great eagle with great and long wings, full of feathers of diverse colors came to Lebanon, and took the highest cedar branch.
He cropped its topmost young twigs, and carried them into a land of traders and planted them in a city of merchants.
He also took the seed of the land, and planted it in a fertile field like a willow tree, beside great abundant waters.
It grew and became a low spreading vine, whose branches turned toward him. Its roots grew under it and it became a vine, its branches grew and sent out sprigs.

But there was also another great eagle with great wings and many feathers. And behold, this vine bent her roots toward him, and shot out her branches toward him, so that he might water it by the furrows where she was planted.
It was planted in a good soil by great abundant waters, so that it might be a good vine and bring out branches and bear fruit.'

So tell them that this is what the Lord says, 'Will it prosper? Will he not pull it out by its roots, and cut off its fruit, so that it withers? All of her leaves will wither in the spring, and it will not take many great or powerful people to pluck it out by its roots.
Yes, even if it is planted, will it prosper? Will it not completely wither when the east wind blows across it? It will wither in the furrows where it grew.'"
Then, once again the Lord's word came to me, Ezekiel.

And the Lord said, "Now, speak to this rebellious house and say, 'Do you not know what these things mean?' Tell them, 'Behold the king of Babylon has come to Jerusalem, and captured its king and its princes, and he led them back to Babylon.
He has captured the king's descendant and swore an oath and made a covenant with him, he has also taken the land's mighty men.
So that the kingdom's stature would be laid low, unable to lift itself up, but it could only stand by keeping his covenant.

But the king rebelled against Babylon by sending his ambassadors to Egypt, to ask for horses and an army. Will he prosper? Will he escape when he does such things, or will he break the covenant, and be delivered?'"
And the Lord God says, "As surely as I live, he will die in Babylon in the land where the king enthroned him, whose oath he despised and whose covenant he broke.
Pharaoh with his mighty army and great forces will be no help for him in the war, by building mountains and forts to attack many people.
He despised the oath by breaking the covenant. After he offered his hand to seal the covenant, he broke his promise and he has done all of these things, and he will not escape."
Therefore this is what the Lord God says, "As surely as I live, I will repay him on his own head for my oath that he despised when he broke my covenant.
I will spread my net over him and catch him in my snare, and I will bring him to Babylon. Then I will prosecute him there for his trespasses against me.
And all his fugitives and groups will fall by the sword, and those who survive will be scattered toward all the winds. Then you will know that I the Lord have spoken."

This is what the Lord God said, "I will take the highest branch from the top of the cedar, and set it on the earth. I will crop one tender branch from the top of its young twigs, and plant it on a famous high mountain.
I will plant it on a mountain the height of Israel, and its boughs will sprout, and bear fruit and become a good cedar. Every kind of winged bird will live under it, in the shadow of its branches.

Then all the trees of the field will know that I am the Lord! For I have brought down the high tree, glorified the lowly tree, dried up the green tree, and made the withered tree flourish. I the Lord have spoken this and I have done it.
The word of the Lord came to me, Ezekiel.
And the Lord said, "What do you mean, when you use this proverb about the land of Israel and say, 'The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children's teeth are set on edge'?"
Then the Lord God said, "As surely as I live, you will never have an occasion to use this proverb in Israel again.
Behold, every soul is mine, including the souls of both the father and son, but the soul that sins will die.
But if a man is just and righteous, and he does that which is lawful.
And he has not eaten on the mountains or looked up to the idols in the House of Israel. And he has not defiled his neighbor's wife, nor approached a woman during her period.

And he has not oppressed anyone, but has repaid the debtor and paid what he promised. And he has not inflicted violence on anyone, and he has given his bread to the hungry, and he has covered the naked with a garment.
He does not engage in usury and loan money to charge interest. But he has abandoned his immorality, and executed true judgment between men.
He has obeyed my laws, kept my judgments and dealt honestly, therefore he is a just man and he will surely live."
And the Lord God said, "If that man fathers a violent son who sheds blood or is a thief, and he does any of these things.
Even though the father has not done any of them, and the son has eaten on the mountains, and defiled his neighbor's wife.
He has oppressed the poor and needy, and violently robbed people, and does not repay his debts. And he looks up to the idols, then he has committed abominations.

And he has loaned money for usury and collected interest. Will he be allowed to live? He will not live, and because he has done all of these abominations, he will surely die, and his blood will be on his own hands.
Now, if a son sees all of his father's sins and considers them, and does not do likewise.
And he does not eat on the mountains, or look up to the House of Israel's idols, and he has not defiled his neighbor's wife.
And he has not oppressed anyone, he has not failed to repay his debts, nor violently robbed people. But he has given his bread to the hungry, and covered the naked with a garment.

And he has withheld from harming the poor, and he has received no interest or usury. But if he has executed my judgments, and walked in my laws, he will not die for his father's immorality, and he will surely live.
As for his father, because he cruelly oppressed people, violently robbed his brother, and did things which were not good among his people, he will die in his own immorality.
But, you ask why? Does not the son bear the father's immorality? When the son has done everything that is lawful and righteous, and he has kept and obeyed all of my laws, he will surely live.

The soul that sins will die. The son will not bear the father's immorality, nor will the father bear the son's immorality. The righteousness of the righteous man will be on him, and the wicked will fall from their own wickedness.
But if the wicked man turns away from all the sins that he has committed, and he keeps and obeys all of my laws, and he does lawful and righteous things, he will surely live and he will not die.
All the transgressions he has committed, will not be held against him. And because of all the righteousness he has done, he will live."
And the Lord God said, "I take no pleasure when the wicked die? I prefer that he would turn from his wicked ways and live?

But if a righteous man turns away from his righteousness, and commits immorality and every other abominable thing that the wicked man does, should he live? All the righteousness he has done will not be remembered, and he will die in all of the trespasses and sins he has committed.
But you say, 'The Lord's way is not fair.' So hear now, O House of Israel, 'Is it my ways that are unfair? Or is it not your ways that are unfair?'
When a righteous man turns away from his righteousness, and commits immorality and dies in his sin, he will die because of the immoralities that he has committed.
But I say again, 'When a wicked man turns away from his wickedness, and he does that which is lawful and righteous, he will save his soul and live.'
It is because he thinks about and turns away from all of the transgressions he has committed, that he will surely live and he will not die.
But the House of Israel says, 'The Lord's ways are not fair.' O House of Israel, are not my ways fair? And are not your ways unfair?"
So the Lord God said, "O House of Israel, I will judge each one you with your own ways. Repent, and turn from all of your sins, so that your immorality does not bring you to ruin.
Throw all of your transgressions away from you, that have made you sin. And make yourself a new heart and spirit. O House of Israel, why should you die?"
For the Lord God says, "I take no pleasure in anyone's death, so repent from your sin and live!"
And the Lord spoke to me Ezekiel and said, "Lament for Israel's princes.
And say, 'Was your mother a lioness who laid down with lions? And she nourished her cubs among the young lions.
She raised one of her cubs, and it became a young lion. It learned to catch its prey, and it devoured men.
When the nations heard of him, they trapped him in their pit, and they brought him in chains to the land of Egypt.
Now when she saw that she had waited in vain, and her hope was lost, she taught another of her cubs to be a young lion.
And he went and down among the lions and became a young lion. He learned to catch the prey, and he devoured men.
He knew of their desolate palaces, and he laid waste their cities, and decimated the land, and everything in it was shaken by the noise of his roaring.
Then the nations attacked him from the provinces on every side, they spread their net over him and he was trapped in their pit.
They put him in chains and brought him to the king of Babylon. They brought him into their strongholds, and he was no longer heard roaring on Israel's mountains.
Your mother was like a vine planted in your blood near the water. She was fruitful and full of branches because of the abundant water.
She had strong limbs, fit for the scepters of those who carried the burden of ruling. Her stature was glorified among the thick branches, and she towered high above her branches.
But she was furiously uprooted and thrown down to the ground. The east wind dried up her fruit, her strong limbs were broken and they withered, and the fire consumed them.
Now she is planted in the wilderness, in a dry and thirsty land.
And fire has burned through her limbs and branches, and devoured her fruit, so that she has no strong limbs to be a rulers scepter.' This lament will be used for a lamentation."
On the tenth day of the fifth month of the seventh year, some of Israel's elders came to ask the Lord, and they sat down before me.
Then came the word of the Lord to me, Ezekiel.

And the Lord said, "Son of Man, speak to Israel's elders, and say tell them this is what the Lord God says, 'Have you come to question me?' Because the Lord God says, 'As surely as I live, I will not be questioned by you.'
O Son of Man, will you judge them and confront them with the abominations of their fathers?"

Tell them that this is what the Lord God says, "On the day that I chose Israel, and lifted up my hand to the house of Jacob's descendants. When I made myself known to them in the land of Egypt and I lifted up my hand and said, 'I am your Lord God.'

On that day I lifted up my hand to them, and swore to bring them out of the land of Egypt into a land that I had found for them. A land flowing with milk and honey, more glorious than all of the other lands.
Then I said to them, 'Every one of you throw away every one of your abominations, and do not defile yourselves with Egypt's idols, for I am your Lord God.'

But they rebelled against me, and they would not listen to me. They did not throw away their abominations, nor did they forsake Egypt's idols! Then I said, 'I will pour out my furious anger on them, in the middle of Egypt.'
But I acted for my name's sake, so that my name would not be polluted before the heathen where they were living, to whom I had revealed myself to in Israel, by bringing them out of the land of Egypt.
So I brought them out of the land of Egypt into the wilderness.
I gave them my laws, and showed them my judgments, for a man to do these things and live by them.
Furthermore I also gave them my Sabbaths as a sign between me and them, so that they might know that I am the Lord who sanctifies them."

And the Lord said, "But the House of Israel rebelled against me in the wilderness, they did not walk in my laws and they despised my judgments. These laws and judgments were designed for a man to live by, but they greatly polluted my Sabbaths. Then I said, 'I will pour out my furious anger on them in the wilderness and consume them.'
But I acted on behalf of my own name's sake, so that my name would not be polluted before the heathen, and I brought my people out as the heathen watched.

But I also lifted up my hand, and swore to them in the wilderness that I would not bring them into the land flowing with milk and honey which I had given them, which was more glorious than all of the other lands.
Because they despised my judgments, and refused to walk in my laws. And they polluted my Sabbaths, because their hearts followed their idols."
And the Lord said, "Nevertheless I pitied them which kept me from destroying them, and I did not put an end to them in the wilderness.
But I spoke to their children in the wilderness and said, 'Do not walk in the laws of your fathers, nor observe their judgments and defile yourselves with their idols.
I am your Lord God, so walk in my laws, and keep and obey my judgments.
My holy Sabbaths are a sign between me and you, so that you will know that I am your Lord God."

And the Lord said, "Even though the children have rebelled against me, and they did not walk in my laws, nor did they keep and obey my judgments, which were designed for a man to live by. But they polluted my Sabbaths therefore I said, 'I will pour out my furious anger on them, to satisfy my anger against them in the wilderness.'
But I withdrew my hand, and acted for my own name's sake, so that my name would not be polluted in the presence of the heathen who were watching as I brought them out.
However, I lifted up my hand to them in the wilderness, and promised that I would scatter them among the heathen, and disperse them through the countries.
But because they despised my laws and they did not execute my judgments, and they polluted my Sabbaths chasing after their fathers' idols.
So in return, I gave them laws and judgments that were not good, by which they should not live.
So in order to decimate them, I polluted them with their own unclean gifts, and made them sacrifice everything that was born from the womb through the fire. Then they would know that I am the Lord."
And the Lord said, "Therefore son of man, speak to the House of Israel and tell them that this is what the Lord God says, 'Just as your fathers blasphemed me and trespassed against me.

And I brought them into the land, which I lifted up my hand and promised to give to them. There they saw every high hill and all the thick trees, and every sacrifice they offered there, provoked my anger, including their sweet savory offerings and the drink offerings they poured out there.
Then I said to them, 'Where is this high place to which you go?' And it is still named Bamah to this very today.'"
Therefore, tell the House of Israel that this is what the Lord God says, "Will you pollute yourselves just as your fathers did, and prostitute yourselves with their abominations?

For when you offer gifts and make your sons to pass through the fire, you pollute yourselves with all your idols to this day. O House of Israel, should I be questioned by you? For as surely as I live, I will not be questioned by you!
And what you have in mind will never happen when you say, 'We will be like the heathen and the families of the other countries, and serve wood and stone.'"
And the Lord God says, "As surely as I live, and with a mighty hand and an out stretched arm, I will pour out my furious anger and rule over you.
And with a strong mighty hand and an out stretched arm, I will bring you out from the people and gather you from all the countries where you were scattered, when my fury poured out.
And I will bring you into the wilderness of the people, I will plead your cause face to face with you.
I will plead with you, just like I pleaded with your fathers in the wilderness of the land of Egypt.
And I will make you to pass under the rod and bring you into the bond of the covenant.

I will purge the rebels and those who transgress against me from among you. I will bring them out of the country where they live, and they will not enter into the land of Israel. Then you will know that I am the Lord."

And this is what the Lord God says, "As for you, O House of Israel, everyone of you go and serve your idols. But from now on, if you will not listen to me, but you will no longer pollute my holy name with your gifts and idols.

And the Lord God says, "For on my holy mountain, the high mountain of Israel, where the entire House of Israel will serve me in the land. I will accept them there and require your offerings and the first fruits of your gifts, along with all your holy things.

I will accept you with your sweet savory offering, when I seperate you from the people, and gather you from all the countries where you have been scattered. And I will be sanctified through you before the heathen.
When I will bring you into the land of Israel, the country which I lifted up my hand and promised to give to your fathers. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
There you will remember and loathe yourselves, for all the evil ways and deeds in which you have defiled yourselves."
And the Lord God says, "O House of Israel, you will know that I am the Lord when I treat you mercifully for your wicked ways and corrupt deeds for my own name's sake."
Furthermore the Lord's word of came to me, Ezekiel.
And the Lord said, "Son of man, face the south and preach against it, and prophesy against the forest of the south field.

And tell the southern forest to hear what the Lord God says, 'Behold I will kindle a fire in you, and it will devour every green and dry tree in you, the fiery flame will not be quenched, and every face from north to south will be burned.
Then all flesh will see that I the Lord have kindled this fire, and it cannot be quenched.'"
Then I Ezekiel said, "Oh my Lord God! These people are saying that I am just speaking in parables!'"
And the word of the Lord came to me, Ezekiel.
And the Lord said, "Son of man, look toward Jerusalem, then deliver this prophetic message and preach against the holy places, and prophesy against the land of Israel."
And the Lord said to tell the land of Israel that this is what the Lord says, "Behold I am against you, and I will draw my sword from its sheath, and cut you off from the righteous and the wicked.
I will cut you off from the righteous and the wicked, and unsheathe my sword against all flesh from the south to the north.
Then all flesh will know that I the Lord have drawn my sword out of its sheath, and I will not return it to its sheath ever again.
Thererfore son of man, grieve before their very eyes for your broken waist and bitter grief."

And the Lord says, "When they ask you, 'Why are you grieving?' Then you must answer them and say, 'Because news is coming that will melt every heart. Everyone's hands will be feeble, every spirit will faint, and all knees will be as weak as water because it is coming.'"
Again the word of the Lord came to me, Ezekiel.
And the Lord said, "Son of man, prophesy and tell them that this is what the Lord says, 'A sword has been sharpened and hardened.
It has been sharpened for a bitter slaughter, it has been hardened until it glows. Should we rejoice? For it despises my son's staff, as it does every tree.
And he has given this sword to be sharpened and hardened, so that it may be handled by the hand of the killer.'
O son of man, cry and howl because this sword will be against my people and all the princes of Israel. Terrors from the sword will be against my people, therefore beat your thigh."
And the Lord God says, "Because the sword is a trial, and what if the sword has contempt for the ruler's staff? It will no longer exist.
Therefore son of man, prophesy and clap your hands. Swing the killing sword two or three times. It is the sword which enters the private chambers of the great who are killed.
I have pointed the sword against all of their gates, so that their hearts would fail and their ruins would be multiplied. Ah, the sword is bright and wrapped up reday for the slaughter.
Go one way or the other, either to the right or the left, or whatever direction you face.
I will also clap my hands and my fury will rest. I the Lord have spoken."
Again the word of the Lord came to me, Ezekiel.

And the Lord said, "Son of man, appoint two different directions from which the Babylonian king's sword may come, and both will come from one land. Choose a place at the head of the roadway that points to the city.
Choose a way for the sword to come against Rabbath of the Ammonites, and another against Judah into the defended Jerusalem.
For the Babylonian king stood at the parting of the way, at the junction of two roads. He used divination to harden his arrows and make them bright, he consulted with images and examined the liver.

At his right hand was the divine inspiration for Jerusalem to appoint captains, to open the mouth for the slaughter, to shout, to send battering rams against the gates, to build a ramp, and to construct a fort.
It will appear to be a false divine inspiration to his loyal people who are watching and have sworn oaths to him. But he will recall and remember their immorality, so that they may be captured."

Therefore this is what the Lord God says, "Because you have remembered your immorality, and your transgressions have been discovered, so that all of your sins have been revealed. And because I say, 'I remember you, and you will be taken with the hand.
And you, profane and wicked prince of Israel, the day has come when your immorality will end.'"
This is what the Lord God says, "Remove the crown, things will no longer be the same, glorify the lowly and humiliate anyone high up.
I will overturn, overturn, and overturn and it will no longer exist until the one comes whose right it is to own, and I will give it to him."

And you Ezekiel, son of man prophesy and tell them that this is what the Lord God says about the Ammonites disrespect, "The sword has been drawn for the slaughter, and it was hardened until it glows to consume.
While they see vanity and divine lies about you, to bring you down on the necks of the wicked who are killed, whose day has come for their immorality to end.
Will I make it return to its sheath? I will judge you in the place where you were created, in your native land.
And I will pour out my indignation upon you, I will blow my fiery anger against you. I will deliver you into the hands of wicked and brutal men, who skillfully destroy.
You will be used for fuel to the fire, and your blood will flow in the middle of the land. You will no longer be remembered, because I the Lord have spoken."
Again the word of the Lord came to me, Ezekiel.
And the Lord said, "Now son of man, will you judge the bloody city? Yes, you will show her all of her abominations.
Then you tell them that this is what the Lord God says, 'This city sheds its own blood in the middle of its streets. Her time has come for the idols she makes to defile herself, to be exposed.

You are guilty of shedding your own blood, and you have defiled yourself the idols which you have made. You have made your days draw near to the end of your years, so I have made the heathen to be disgusted by you, and you are a mockery to all countries.
Those near and far from you, will mock your infamous and much frustrated people.
Behold, the princes of Israel have used their power over everyone to shed their blood.
You treat your father and mother with contempt and ridicule them. In your midst you have oppressed strangers, and you have ignored the fatherless and the widows.
You have despised my holy things, and you have profaned my Sabbaths.
There are men within your borders who spread tales of bloodshed, and in your midst are those who eat on the mountain shrines and commit obscenity.
In your midst have they have seen the nakedness of their fathers, in you have they been with the women who were set apart during their menstrual cycle.
And one has committed abomination with his neighbor's wife, another has lewdly defiled his daughter-in-law, and another has humbled his sister, his own father's daughter.'"
And the Lord God says, "In your midst they take gifts to shed blood. You use usury to charge excess interest and extort money from your neighbors, and you have forgotten me.
Therefore I have slapped my hand against your dishonest gain, and against the bloodshed in your midst.
Can your heart endure, or will your hands be strong on the days that I deal with you? I the Lord have spoken and I will act.
I will scatter you among the heathen and disperse you throughout the countries, and I will purge your filth from you.
And you will receive your inheritance in full view of the heathen. Then you will know that I am the Lord."
And the word of the Lord came to me, Ezekiel.

And the lord said, "Son of Man, the House of Israel will become trash to me. They have become brass, tin, iron, and lead in the middle of the furnace, and they are nothing but impurities in the silver."
Therefore this is what the Lord says, "Because you have all become trash, I will gather you into the middle of Jerusalem.

As they gather silver, brass, iron, lead, and tin into the middle of the furnace, to blow the fire on it and melt it, so will I gather you in my furious anger, and I will leave you there until you melt.
Yes, I will gather you and blow the fire of my fierce anger on you, and you will melt in the middle of the furnace.
And just like silver is melted in the middle of the furnace, you will also be melted in the furnace, and you will know that I the Lord have poured out my fury on you."
And the word of the Lord came to me, Ezekiel.
And the Lord said, "Son of Man, say to her, 'You are an unclean land, upon which no rain has fallen.'

There is a conspiracy among the prophets in the middle of Jerusalem, like a roaring lion ravaging its prey. They have devoured souls, and they have taken her treasures and precious things. They have made many widows in the middle of the city.

Her priests have violated my laws, and profaned my holy things. They see no difference between the holy and the profane, nor have they shown the difference between the unclean and the clean. They have hidden their eyes from my Sabbaths, and my name is profaned among them.
Her princes in the middle of Jerusalem are like wolves ravaging their prey, shedding blood, and destroying souls for dishonest gain.
Jerusalem's prophets have plastered them with watered down mortar. They see visions of vanity, and divine lies to them and say, 'This is what the Lord God says,' when the Lord has not spoken."
And the Lord God said, "The people of the land have used oppression and robbery to take advantage of the poor and needy. Yes, they have wrongfully oppressed strangers.
And I searched for a man among them, who would repair the hedge, and stand in the breach before me for the land, so that I would not destroy it. But I found no one!
Therefore I poured out my indignation on them, and consumed them with my fiery anger. I have repaid them in their own way, and I brought down their own judgements on their own heads."
The Lord's word came again to me, Ezekiel.
And the Lord said, "Son of man, there were two women, both were the daughters of one mother.
And they were whores since their youth in Egypt, their virgin breasts were touched there.
The oldest was Aholah and her sister was Aholibah. They were mine and they gave birth to sons and daughters. Aholah is Samaria, and Aholibah is Jerusalem.
Aholah played the whore while she was still mine, and she lusted after her lovers, who were her Assyrian neighbors.
The Assyrian captains and rulers were clothed in blue, and all of them were handsome young horsemen, riding their horses.
She was a whore with all of the elite men of Assyria, and she defiled herself with all of her lovers and their idols.
She did not abandon her whoring when she left Egypt. She began whoring in her youth and slept with strange men. They touched her virgin breasts, and poured their prostitution all over her.
Therefore I have delivered her into the hands of her Assyrian lovers, whom she lusted after.
They exposed her nakedness, and took her sons and daughters, and killed her with the sword. She became famous among women, because they judged her.
When her sister Aholibah saw this, she was more corrupt in her whoring than her sister.
She lusted after her handsome young Assyrian captains and ruling neighbors, who were the most beautifully clothed horsemen riding on their horses.
When I saw that they were defiled, and they had both chosen the same path."
And the Lord said, "But Oholibah whored even more, because when she saw the men portrayed on the wall, and the images of the Chaldeans engraved in vermilion.
Wearing belts around their waists, with extravagantly dyed attire on their heads, all of them looked like Babylonian princes from Chaldea, where they were born.
As soon as she saw them, she lusted for them and sent messengers to them in Chaldea.
When the Babylonians came to her love bed, they defiled her with their prostitution. She was polluted along with them, and her mind turned away from them in disgust.
So she exposed her whoring and her nakedness, then my mind turned away from her and her sister in disgust.
But she multiplied her prostitution, and remembered the days of her youth when she played the whore in Egypt.
For she lusted after their lovers, who were like donkey flesh, and whose discharge was like that of horses.
So you remembered the obscenity of your youth, and the Egyptians who touched your young breasts."

Therefore this is what the Lord God says, "O Aholibah, behold I will raise up your disgusting lovers against you. You have turned your mind away thembut I will bring them against you from every direction.

The Babylonians, Chaldeans, Pekod, Shoa, Koa, and all of the Assyrians with them, and all of their desirable young captains and rulers, their great and renowned lords, all of whom are riding on horses.

And they will attack you with an army of people, chariots, wagons, and weapons. They will march against you and surround you with shields and helmets, and I will make them judge you by their own standards.

And I will turn my jealousy against you, and they will deal furiously with you. They will remove your noses and ears, and your survivors will fall by the sword. They will take your sons and your daughters, and the rest of you will be devoured by fire.
They will also strip off your clothes, and take your fine jewelry.
I will make sure your obscenity ceases to exist, and put an end to your prostitution that you brought from the land of Egypt. And you will no longer look up to Egypt nor remember them anymore."
For this is what the Lord God says, "Behold I will deliver you into the hands of the people you hate, from whom turned your mind away from in disgust.
And they will hatefully deal with you, and take away all that you have labored over. They will leave you naked and bare, and the nakedness and obscenity of you and your whores will be exposed.
I will do all these things to you, because you have gone chasing after heathen whores, because you have been polluted by their idols.
You have walked in the ways of your sister, so I will put her cup into your hand."
And this is what the Lord God says, "You will drink from your sister's large deep cup. It contains so much filth that you will be mocked as a laughing stock.
Your sister Samaria's cup of confusion and devastation will fill you with drunkenness and grief."
And the Lord God says, "You will drink from it, and break it into sherds of pottery, and tear off your own breasts. For I the Lord have spoken."
Therefore this is what the Lord says, "Because you have forgotten me, and pushed me behind your back, so you will also bear your own obscenity and whores."
Besides the Lord spoke to me Ezekiel and said, "Son of man, will you judge Aholah and Aholibah? Yes, declare their abominations to them.

For they have committed adultery, and blood is on their hands. They have committed adultery with their idols, and so have their sons, whom they bore to me. They passed them through the fire, to sacrifice and devour them.
They have done this to me, on the same day that they defiled my sanctuary and profaned my Sabbaths.
For on the same day they killed their children and sacrificed them to their idols, they came into my sanctuary to profane it, and they did all of this in the middle of my house.
Furthermore, you sisters have sent messengers to summon men to come to you from far, and they came. Because you washed yourself for them, painted your eyes, and adorned yourself with jewelry.
You sat on a stately bed with a table prepared before it, on which you placed my incense and oil.
A voice of a multitude was at ease with her, and the common men of the Sabeans were brought in from the wilderness, who put bracelets on their hands and beautiful crowns on their heads.
Then I spoke to her who had grown old in adulteries and said, 'Now will they commit prostitution with her, and she with them?'
But they slept with the obscene women, Aholah and Aholibaher like the whores that they were.
And the righteous men will judge them as as if they were adulteresses or women who had shed blood. Because they are adulteresses, and blood is on their hands."
For this is what the Lord God says, "I will bring a company of men against them, and I will allow them to be removed and plundered.
And the company of men will stone them, and slash them with their swords. They will kill their sons and daughters, and burn their houses with fire.
So I will make obscenity cease to exist in the land, so that all women will be taught not to imitate your obscenity.
They will repay you for your obscenity, and you will bear the sins of your idolatry. Then you will know that I am the Lord God."
Again on the tenth day, of the tenth month, of the ninth year the word of the Lord came to me, Ezekiel.
And the Lord said, "Son of man, record the name of the day and the date that the king of Babylon attacked Jerusalem.
Speak to the rebellious house, and tell them a parable and tell them that this is what the Lord God says, 'Fill a pot with water and set it on the fire.
Put the good pieces of meat into it including the thigh, the shoulder, and the choicest bones.
Burn the other bones from the choicest of the flock under the pot to boil the choicest bones.'"
Therefore this is what the Lord God says, "Woe unto the bloody city, to the scum filled pot, and whose scum has not left it! Empty it piece by piece, and do not cast lots for it.
For her bloodshed is within her, she poured it out on a rock, and she did not pour it out on the ground to cover it with dust.
So that it would cause fury and vengeance, I have placed her blood on top of a rock, so that it would not be covered."
Therefore this is what the Lord God says, "Woe unto the bloody city! And I will even pile up the kindling for a fire great.
Pile on wood, kindle the fire, cook the meat and spices together, and burn the bones.
Then set the empty pot on its coals, so that its brass is very hot, and burn its filthy scum until it melts and consumes the scum.
She has exhausted herself with lies, and her great filthy scum did not leave her, so her scum will be left in the fire.
I have tried to purge you because of your filthy obscenity, but you were not purged. Your filth will not be purged again until my furious anger rests on you."

And the Lord God says, "I, the Lord have spoken, and the time is coming when I will act and not refrain, nor will I spare you nor repent. I will judge you and they will judge you by your own ways and deeds."
Again the word of the Lord came to me, Ezekiel.
And the Lord said, "Son of man, behold I take away your desires in a single stroke, but you must not mourn or weep, nor let your tears run down your face.
Refrain from crying, do not mourn for the dead, cover your head, and put your shoes on your feet. Do not cover your lips or eat the bread of men.
So I spoke to the people in the morning, and in the evening my wife died, and the next morning I did as I was commanded.
Then the people spoke to me and asked, 'Will you not tell us why you are doing these things and what they mean to us?'"
Then the word of the Lord came to me Ezekiel, and I answered them.

So I spoke to the House of Israel and told them that this is what the Lord God says, "Behold I will profane my sanctuary, the source of your excellent strength, the desire of your eyes, and that which your soul pities. And your sons and daughters whom you have left behind will fall by the sword.
Then you will do as I have done, and you will not cover your lips nor eat the bread of men.
And you will keep your heads covered, and keep your shoes on your feet. You will not mourn nor weep, but you will waste away for your wickedness, and mourn one another.
Ezekiel will be a sign to you, and you will do everything that he has done. When this happens, you will know that I am the Lord God.
Son of man, you will know on the day that I take away their strength, the joy of their glory, the desire of their eyes which they have set their minds to, and their sons and daughters.
So that those who escape in those days will come to you, and report to you so that you hear it with your own ears.
In those days your mouth will be opened to those who have escaped. Then you will speak and be no longer be mute, and you will be a sign to them. Then they will know that I am the Lord."
The word of the Lord came again to me, Ezekiel.
And the Lord said, "Son of Man, turn your face against the Ammonites, and prophesy against them."

Speak to the Ammonites and tell them that this is what the Lord God says, "Because you said, 'Aha!' Against my sanctuary, when it was profaned, when the land of Israel was desolated, and the house of Judah went into captivity.
Therefore I will deliver you to the men of the east as their possession. They will set up their palaces and build homes in you, and they will eat your fruit and drink your milk.
I will make Rabbah a camel stable, and the Ammonites a resting place for sheep. Then you will know that I am the Lord."
For this is what the Lord God says, "Because you have clapped your hands, stamped your feet, and rejoiced with all your heart of spite against the land of Israel.

So I will stretch out my hand against you, and deliver you as plunder to the heathen. I will cut you off from the people, and make you perish from among the countries, and I will destroy you. Then you will know that I am the Lord."
This is what the Lord God says, "Because Moab and Seir have said, 'Behold the house of Judah is just like to all the other heathen.'
Therefore I will expose Moab's flanks from its central cities to its frontier cities, and the glory of the country Beth-Jeshimoth, Baalmeon, and Kiriathaim.
And I will give them along with the Ammonites to the men of the east as their possession, so that the Ammonites will no longer be remembered among the nations.
And I will execute my judgments against Moab, and they will know that I am the Lord."
This is what the Lord God says, "Because Edom has dealt with vengeance against the house of Judah, and they have greatly offended and revenged themselves."

Therefore this is what the Lord God says, "I will also stretch out my hand against Edom and cut it off every man and beast. I will lay waste to it from Teman to Dedan, and they will fall by the sword.
And the Lord God says, "My vengeance will fall on Edom by the hand of my people Israel, and they will treat Edom with my fury and anger, and they will know my vengeance."
And this is what the Lord says, "Because the Philistines have dealt with a malicious heart, and they have taken revenge to destroy Judah because of an old hatred."
Therefore this is what the Lord God says, "Behold I will stretch out my hand against the Philistines, and I will cut off the Cherethims, and destroy what remains of them along the coast.
And I will execute great vengeance against them with furious rebukes. Then, when I lay my vengeance on them they will know that I am the Lord."
Then on the first day, of the eleventh month, of the twelfth year the Lord's word came to me.

And the Lord said, "Son of Man, because Tyre has spoken against Jerusalem and said, 'Aha! The people's gates are broken, and she is turned to me, now I will be replenished, and she will be laid waste.'"
Therefore this is what the Lord God says, "O Tyre, I am against you, and I will make many nations come against you, like the ocean waves crash against the shore.
They will destroy the walls of Tyre and tear down her towers. I will also scrape the dust from her and make her like a barren rock."
And the Lord God says, "She will become a place to spreading nets in the middle of the sea. For I have spoken, and she will become plunder for the nations.
Her daughters out in the field will be killed by the sword. Then they will know that I am the Lord."
For this is what the Lord God says, "Behold I will bring King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon, a king of kings, from the north, with horses, chariots, horsemen, companies, and many men against Tyre.
He will kill your daughters out in the field with the sword. He will build a fort against you, then he will throw a mountain of siege works and raise a shield against you.
He will set battering rams against your walls, and cut down your towers with his axes.
His massive army of horses will cover you with their dust. Your walls will shake from the noise of their horsemen, wheels, and chariots when he and his men enter your broken city gates and defenses.
His horses' hooves will trample down all of your streets. He will kill your people with the sword, and your strong garrisons will fall to the ground.
They will plunder all of your riches, and prey on your merchandise. They will break down your walls, and destroy your pleasant homes. They will throw your stones, timber, and dirt into the water.
I will make the noise of your singing cease to exist, and the music from your harps will no longer be heard."
And the Lord God says, "I will make you like the top of a barren rock, you will become a place to spread fishing nets. You will never be rebuilt ever again, because I the Lord have spoken."
This is what the Lord God says to Tyre, "Will not the islands shake from the sound of your fall, when the wounded cry and the people are slaughtered in your midst?

Then all the princes of the sea will come down from their thrones. They will lay down their robes, and remove their embroidered garments. They will clothe themselves with trembling fear and sit on the ground. They will tremble every moment and they will be astonished by you.

They will lament for you and say, 'O you who had been inhabited of seafaring men, how you have been destroyed. That renowned city, which was strong on the sea, both she and her people, who imposed their terror to haunt all people has been destroyed!
Now the islands tremble on the day of your downfall, the islands that are in the sea will be troubled by your departure.'"
For this is what the Lord God says, "When I make you a desolate city, like the uninhabited cities, when I will raise up the deep against you, and great waters will cover you.

When I bring you down with those who descend into the pit, with the ancient people from the old days. I will set you in the low parts of the earth, in desolate places from the old days, with those who go down to the pit, so that you no longer inhabit, or sit in glory in the land of the living."
And the Lord God says, "I will make you a terror, and you will be no longer exist, even though they search for you, you will never be found."
Then the Lord's word came again to me, Ezekiel.
And the Lord said, "Son of Man, lament now for Tyre."
And tell Tyre that this is what the Lord God says, "O you who are located at an ocean port, a merchant of the people for many islands. O Tyre, you have said, 'I am of perfect beauty.'
Your borders are in the middle of the sea, and your builders have perfected your beauty.
They have made all of your ship's boards of Senir's fir trees, and they have taken cedars from Lebanon to make your masts.
They made your oars from the oaks of Bashan, a company from the Ashurites made your benches out of ivory brought from the Cyprus islands.
Your sails which you spread out were made from fine linen with embroidered work from Egypt, with blue and purple coverings from the islands of Elishah.
O Tyre, the inhabitants of Sidon and Arvad were your mariners, your wise men, and your pilots.
The elders of Gebal and its wise men were your calkers. All the ships of the sea with their mariners were there to trade for your merchandise.
The men of Persia, Lud, and Phut the men of war in your army, they hung their shield and helmet on you, and they displayed your beauty.
The men of Arvad with your army manned your walls all around, and the Gammadims manned your towers. They hung their shields all around your walls, they made your beauty perfect.
Tarshish was your merchant because of all your riches of silver, iron, tin, and lead that they traded with you.
Javan, Tubal, and Meshech were your merchants. They traded slaves and brass bowls in your market.
The house of Togarmah traded in your markets with horses, horsemen, and mules.
The men of Dedan were your merchants, many islands were markets, they traded with you for ivory and ebony horns.
Syria was your merchant because of the abundant merchandise you produced. They traded emeralds, purple, embroidered work, fine linen, coral, and agate in your markets.
Judah and the land of Israel were your merchants. They traded wheat from Minnith and Pannag plus honey, oil, and balm in your markets.
Damascus was your merchant because of the abundant merchandise you produced and all of your other riches including the wine of Helbon, and white wool.
Dan and Javan traveled back and forth from your city to trade bright iron, cassia, and calamus in your markets.
Dedan was your merchants who traded wearing precious clothes for chariots.
Arabia and all the princes of Kedar were your merchants, and they traded lambs, rams, and goats with you.
The merchants of Sheba and Raamah were your merchants, and they traded all kinds of spices, precious stones, and gold in your markets.
Haran, Canneh, Eden, the merchants of Sheba, Assyria, and Chilmad were your merchants.
These were your merchants in all sorts of merchandise including blue clothes, embroidered work, and cedar chests bound with cords for rich apparel.
The ships of Tarshish sang of you in your markets, and you were replenished and made very glorious in the middle of the sea.
Your rowers brought you into great waters, but the east wind has broken you in the middle of the sea.

Your riches, markets, merchandise, mariners, pilots, calkers, the merchants who trade your merchandise, all your men of war, and all the companies which are in your midst, will fall into the sea on the day of your ruin.
The fields and pastures will quake at the sound of your crying pilots.
Anyone who handles the oar, the mariners, and all the pilots of the sea will come down from their ships and stand on dry land.
They will make their voices heard against you, and they will cry bitterly. They will throw dust on their heads, and wallow in the ashes.
They will make shave their bald heads for you, and clothe themselves in sackcloth, and they will weep for you with a bitter wailing heart.
In their wailing they will lament and mourn over you and say, 'What city is like Tyre which was destroyed in the middle of the sea?
When your merchandise traveled over the seas, you filled many people. You enriched the kings of the earth with your abundant riches and merchandise.
At the time that you are broken by the deep sea, your merchandise and all of your companies will fall with you.
All the inhabitants of the islands will be astonished at r collapse. Their kings will be extremely frightened, and they will appear to be very troubled.
The merchants among the people will hiss at you, and you will come to a terrible end, and you will be gone never to exist again.'"
The word of the Lord came again to me, Ezekiel.

And the Lord said, "Son of man tell the prince of Tyre that this is what the Lord God says, "Because of your proud heart and you have said, 'I am a God, I sit in God's seat in the middle of the sea!' But you are not God, you are a man, even though you believe in your heart that your heart is like that of God's.
Behold, you are wiser than Daniel and no secret can hide from you.
You have acquired riches and stored gold and silver in your treasuries, with your wisdom and understanding.
You have used your great wisdom and trading practices to increase your riches, but your heart has become proud because of your riches."
Therefore this is what the Lord God says, "Because you think your heart is like the heart of God.
Behold, I will bring strangers against you, and the terrible nations will draw their swords against the beauty of your wisdom, and they will defile your brilliance.
They will bring you down to the pit, and you will die the death of those who are killed in the middle of the sea.
But will you still say, 'I am God,' before someone who is killing you? You are not God, but you are only a man to those who want to kill you."
And the Lord God says, "You will die the death of the uncircumcised at the hands of strangers, because I have spoken."
Then the Lord's word came to me, Ezekiel.
And the Lord said, "Son of man, lament for the king of Tyre and tell him that this the Lord God says, 'Seal the sum total, full of wisdom and in perfect beauty.

You have been in God's garden of Eden. You were adorned with every kind of precious stone including the sardius, topaz, diamond, beryl, onyx, jasper, sapphire, emerald, carbuncle, and gold. The craftmanship of your tambourines and flutes were prepared for you on the day that you were created.
I ordained you as a guardian cherub to cover and protect. You were on God's holy mountain, and you walked up and down among the fiery stones.
From the day that you were created you were perfect in your ways, until immorality was found within you.

By your abundant merchandise they have filled your midst with violence, and you sinned. Therefore O guardian cherub, from among the fiery stones I will throw you like profanity out of God's mountain and destroy you.
Your heart became proud because of your beauty, your wisdom has been corrupted because of your brilliance. So I will throw you to the ground before kings, so that they may see you.

You have defiled your sanctuaries with your massive wickedness, and the immorality of your trades. So I will bring out a fire from your midst, and it will devour you. I will turn you into ashes on the earth in view of all everyone who sees you.
Everyone among the people who know you will be astonished, and you will come to a terrible end, and you will no longer exist."
Again the word of the Lord came to me, Ezekiel.
And the Lord said, "Son of Man, turn your face against Sidon, and prophesy against it.

Tell them that this is what the Lord God says, 'O Sidon look and see that I am against you, and I will be glorified in your midst. Then after I have executed my judgments and I have been sanctified in her, they will know that I am the Lord.
For I will send pestilence and blood into her streets, and the wounded will be judged by the sword from every side in her midst. Then they will know that I am the Lord.
And there will no longer be a brier nor a grieving thorn to prick the House of Israel, from everyone around them who despised them. Then they will know that I am the Lord God.'"

This is what the Lord God says, "After I have gathered the House of Israel from among the people where they were scattered, I will be sanctified in them in clear view of the heathen. Then they will live in their land which I have given to my servant Jacob.

They will live safely there and build houses and plant vineyards. Yes, they will live with confidence, after I have executed judgments against those all around them who despise them. Then they will know that I am their Lord God."
On the twelfth day, of the tenth month, of the tenth year the Lord's word came to me, Ezekiel.
And the Lord said, "Son of man, turn your face against Pharaoh king of Egypt, and prophesy against him and Egypt."

Speak to them and tell them that this is what the Lord God says, "Behold Pharaoh king of Egypt. I am against you the great dragon that lies in the middle of its rivers, which has said, 'My river belongs to me, and I made it just for myself.'

But I will put hooks in your jaws, and I will make the fish in your rivers stick to your scales. I will bring you up from the middle of your rivers, and all the fish in your rivers will stick to your scales.

I will throw you out into the wilderness and leave you, and all the fish in your rivers there. You will fall in the open fields, and you will not be brought together nor gathered for burial. I have given you as meat to the beasts of the field and the birds of the air.
And all of Egypt's inhabitants will know that I am the Lord, for they have only been a staff of reeds to the House of Israel.
When they took hold of your hand, you broke and tore their shoulders. When they leaned on Egypt, you broke your promise and their backs were wrenched so they could not stand."
Therefore this is what the Lord God says, "Behold I will bring a sword against you, and cut off both man and beast from you.
It is because Egypt has said, 'The river is mine, because I have made it,' that the land of Egypt will be left desolate and laid waste. Then they will know that I am the Lord.
Therefore I am against you and your rivers. I will completely lay waste to the land of Egypt and leave it desolate from the tower of Syene, all the way to the border of Ethiopia.
The foot of both man and beast will no longer pass through it, nor will it be inhabited forty years.

And I will make the land of Egypt a desolation in the midst of desolate countries. And her cities among the cities that are laid waste will be left desolate for forty years. I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations, and disperse them throughout the countries."
But this is what the Lord God says, "After forty years I will gather the Egyptians from the other people where they were scattered.
I will return the Egypt from captivity, and bring them back to the land of Pathros, which is their home land. There they will become a low class kingdom.

Egypt will become the most immoral and wicked kingdom, and it will never glorify itself above other nations ever again. Because I will diminish them, so that they will no longer rule over the nations.
And the House of Israel will no longer put their confidence in Egypt, because they will be reminded of their immoralities when they turned to Egypt. Then they will know that I am the Lord God."
On the first day of the first month of the twenty-seventh year the Lord's word came to me, Ezekiel.

And the Lord said, "Son of man, King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon sent his army to serve a great service against Tyre. Every head was made bald, and every shoulder was made raw. But he and his army were paid no wages for the services that they had served against Tyre."
Therefore this is what the Lord God says, "Behold I will give the land of Egypt to King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon, and he will take her army, her spoils, and her prey as the wages for his army.
And the Lord God says, "I have given him the land of Egypt for his labor and services he has served against it, because they worked for me!
In those days I will make the horn bud out from the House of Israel, and I will open your mouth in their midst. Then they will know that I am the Lord."
The Lord's word came again to me, Ezekiel.
And the Lord said, "Son of man, prophesy and tell them that this is what the Lord God says, 'Howl, for the day is worthy of sorrow!
Because the cloudy Day of the Lord is near, and it will become the heathen's time.
A sword will come against Egypt, and there will be great pain in Ethiopia when the slain fall in Egypt. They will capture her armies, and her foundations will be destroyed.
Ethiopia, Libya, Lydia, Chub, all of the mixed race people, and the men of the land who are in league with them will fall by the sword.'"
And this is what the Lord says, "Egypt's allies will fall, and her proud power will collapse." For the Lord says, "They will fall from the tower of Syene by the sword.
And they will be left desolate in the midst of the desolate countries, and her cities will lie among the wasted cities.
Then they will know that I am the Lord, after I have set a fire in Egypt, and all her helpers are destroyed.
In those days messengers will go out from God in ships to frighten the careless Ethiopians, and great pain will come upon them on the day of Egypt's destruction, for it is coming."
This is what the Lord God says, "I will also make the Egyptian army cease to exist at the hand of King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon.
The king and his people are the most terrible of the nations, and they will be brought to destroy the land. They will draw their swords against Egypt, and fill the land with the killed.
I will make the rivers run dry, and sell the land to the wicked, and I will lay waste to the land, and everything in it by the hand of strangers. For I the Lord have spoken."
This is what the Lord God says, "I will also destroy their idols, and make their images cease to exist in Noph. There will no longer be princes in Egypt, and I will put fear in the land of Egypt.
I will leave Pathros desolate, set fire to Zoan, and I will execute my judgments against the city of No.
I will pour out my fury on the city of Sin, which is the strength of Egypt, and I will cut off the armies of the city of No.
I will set fire to Egypt, and the city of Sin will suffer in great pain. The city of No will be torn apart, and Noph will suffer distress every day.
The young men of Aven and Pibeseth will fall by the sword, and those cities will go into captivity.
The day will also be darkened in Tehaphnehes, when I break the yokes of Egypt there. Her pompous strength will cease to exist, and a cloud will cover her, and her daughters will go into captivity.
As a result of all this, I will execute my judgments in Egypt. Then they will know that I am the Lord."
On the seventh day, of the first month, of the eleventh year the Lord's word came to me, Ezekiel.
And the Lord said, "Son of man, I have broken Pharaoh king of Egypt's arm. It will not be bandaged or put in a cast for healing, to make it strong enough to hold a sword."
Therefore this is what the Lord God says, "Behold I am against Pharaoh king of Egypt. I will break his arms, both his strong arm and his broken arm, and I will make the sword fall out of his hand.
I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations, and disperse them throughout the countries.
I will strengthen the Babylonian king's arms, and put my sword in his hand. But I will break Pharaoh's arms, and he will groan before the Babylonian king like a man with lethal wounds.

But I will strengthen the Babylonian king's arms, and Pharaoh's arms will collapse. I will put my sword into the Babylonian king's hands, and he will stretch it over the land of Egypt. Then they will know that I am the Lord.
I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations, and disperse them throughout the countries. Then they will know that I am the Lord."
On the first day, of the third month, of the eleventh year the Lord's word came to me, Ezekiel.
And the Lord said, "Son of man, speak to Pharaoh king of Egypt, and to his people and say, 'Who is like you in your greatness?'
Behold, the Assyrian was a cedar in Lebanon with beautiful branches and a shaded forrest. His high stature towered above all, and his top was among the thick boughs.
The Assyrian's waters made him great, and the deep springs made him tall. Her rivers ran all around his plants, and sent her small rivers to all the trees of the field.
Therefore his height was glorified above all the other trees of the field. His branches multiplied and grew long as he spread out because of the abundant waters.
All the birds of air made their nests in his branches. All the field beasts gave birth to their young, and all the great nations lived under his canopy.
He was beautiful in his greatness, and the length of his branches grew, because his roots were near the abundant waters.

The cedars in the garden of God could not hide him, the fir trees were not like his boughs, and the chestnut trees were not like his branches, nor any tree in the garden of God was like to him in his beauty.
I made him beautiful with his many branches, so that all the trees of God's Garden of Eden envied him."
Therefore this is what the Lord God says, "Because he has lifted himself up in height, and shot to the top among the thick boughs, and his heart has grown proud of his height.
So I have delivered him into the hands of the mighty one among the heathen. The mighty one will surely deal with him, because I have driven him out for his wickedness.

Foreigners, and the most terrible nation have cut him off, and left him behind. His branches have fallen on the mountains and in all the valleys. His boughs are broken in all of the rivers of the land. And all the people of the earth have left him and his shadow behind.
All the birds of the air remain nested among his ruins, and all the field beasts will live among his branches.

To that end, none of the trees left by the waters would glorify themselves because of their height. Their shoots will not reach their top among the thick boughs, nor will their well-watered trees stand among their height. Because they have all been delivered unto death, to the lower parts of the earth, among the children of men who descend to the pit."

This is what the Lord God says, "On the day he went down to the grave, I caused mourning. I covered the deep for him, and I restrained the floods from him. His great waters were restrained, and I made Lebanon mourn for him, and all the trees of the field fainted because of him.

I made the nations quake at the sound of his downfall, when I threw him down to hell with those who descend into the pit. All of Eden's trees, the choicest and best of Lebanon that the drink water, will be comforted on the earth below.
They also descended with him into hell along with those who are killed by the sword, and those who were his allies, that lived under his shadow among the heathen."

And the Lord God says, "Who else is like you in this glory and greatness among all the trees of Eden? But you will be brought down along with the trees of Eden to the lower parts of the earth. And you will lie in the middle of the uncircumcised with those who are killed by the sword. This is about Pharaoh and all his people."
On the first day, of the twelfth month, of the twelfth year the Lord's word came to me, Ezekiel.

And the Lord said, "Son of man, lament for Pharaoh king of Egypt and say to him, 'You are like a young lion among the nations, and you are like a whale in the sea. You walked out with your rivers and troubled waters, and fouled their rivers.'"
This is what the Lord God says, "Therefore I spread my net over you with a company of many people, and they will pull you up in my net.
Then will I leave you on the land, and throw you out in the open field. I will make all the birds of the air remain on you, and all the beasts of the whole earth wiill eat their fill of you.
I will lay your flesh on the mountains, and fill the valleys with your blood.
I will also use your blood to water the land in which you swim, even the mountains and rivers will be full of you.
When I put you out, I will cover the heavens and darken the stars. I will cover the sun with a cloud, and the moon will not give its light."
And the Lord God says, "I will darken all the bright lights of heaven above you, and set darkness over your land.
I will frustrate the hearts of many people, when I bring about your destruction among the nations, in countries you do not know.

Yes, I will make many people amazed by you, and their kings will be horribly afraid of you, when I brandish my sword before them. And on the day of your downfall each of them will tremble every moment in fear of his own life."
For this is what the Lord God says, "The Babylonian king's sword will come against you!
I will make all of your armies fall by the sword of the mighty and most terrible of the nations. They will plunder Egypt's pompous and proud, and all of its armies will be destroyed.
I will also destroy all of its beasts beside the great waters. No man's foot will trouble them ever again, nor will the hooves of the beasts trouble them."
And the Lord God says, "Then I will make their waters run deep, and their rivers will run like oil.
When I defeat all of those who live there, I will leave the land of Egypt desolate, and the country destitute of everything that filled it. Then they will know that I am the Lord."
And the Lord God says, "This is how everyone will mourn and lament for her, when the daughters of the nations mourn her. They will mourn for her, her people, and even for Egypt."
On the fifteenth day of the month, of the twelfth year the Lord's word came to me, Ezekiel.
And the Lord said, "Son of man, wail for the people of Egypt, and throw the daughters of the famous nations down to the lower parts of the earth, along with those who go down to the pit.
Who do you surpass in beauty? Go down among the uncircumcised.
They will fall in the midst of those who are killed by the sword, for she has been delivered to the sword. Draw a sword against her and all of her armies.
The strongest among the mighty will speak to Egypt and her allies from the midst of hell. They have gone down and lie among the uncircumcised, with those killed by the sword.
Assyria is there along with her entire company, his graves are all around him. All of them have been killed, and they have fallen by the sword.
Her graves are set in the depths of the pit, and her company is all around her grave. All of those who caused terror in the land of the living have been killed, and they have fallen by the sword.

Elam and all of her people are all around her grave. All of them have been killed, and they have fallen by the sword. And all of those who caused terror in the land of the living have all gone down uncircumcised into the lower parts of the earth. They carried their shame with them down to the pit.

They have made her bed in the midst of all her uncircumcised dead who were killed by the sword, and she is surrounded by her graves. They caused terror in the land of the living, but they carried their shame with them down to the pit. Egypt has been placed among those who have been killed.
Meshech, Tubal, and all her uncircumcised armies were killed by the sword and surrounded by her graves, because they spread their terror throughout the land of the living.

They will not lie with the uncircumcised mighty who have fallen and gone down to hell with their weapons of war. They have laid their swords under their heads, but their wickedness rests on their bones. Even though they were once the terror of the mighty in the land of the living.
Yes, you too will be broken and lie in the midst of the uncircumcised, along with those who are killed by the sword.

Edom is there, along with her kings and her princes, who even with their might are laid next to those who were killed by the sword. They will lie with the uncircumcised and those who go down to the pit.

All the princes of the north and all the Sidonians went down with the killed, ashamed of their terror and their might, and they lie uncircumcised along with those who are killed by the sword, and bear their shame along with those who go down to the pit."
And the Lord God says, "Pharaoh will see them, and he will be comforted over all his armies. Pharaoh and all his army will be killed by the sword."

And the Lord God says, "For I have sent my terror throughout the land of the living, and he will be laid among the uncircumcised along with those killed with the sword, including Pharaoh and all of his armies."
Again the Lord's word came to me, Ezekiel.
And the Lord said, "Son of man, speak to your people's children and say to them, 'When I bring the sword against a land, if the people of the land choose a man from among them as their watchman.
And he sees a sword coming against the land, and he blows the trumpet to warn the people.
Then whoever hears the trumpet and does not take warning, if the sword comes and takes him away, his blood will be on his own head.
Since he heard the sound of the trumpet, but failed to heed the warning, his blood is on him. But he that heeds the warning will save his soul.

But if the watchman sees the sword coming, and he does not blow the trumpet to warn the people, And if the sword comes against them and takes a person's life, that person will be taken away in his immorality, but his blood will be on the watchman's hands.
So I have made you son of man, a watchman to the House of Israel, therefore you will hear the word from my mouth, and give them my warnings.
When I say to the wicked, 'O wicked man, you will surely die!' If you do not speak to warn the wicked man about his ways, and that wicked man dies in his immorality, his blood will be on your hands.
Nevertheless, if you warn the wicked man to turn away from his ways, and he does not turn from his ways, he will die in his immorality, but you will have saved your soul.
Therefore son of man, speak to the House of Israel and say, 'If our transgressions and sins are on us, and we pine away in them, then how should we live?'

Say to them the Lord God says, 'As surely as I live, I take no pleasure in the death of the wicked, but the wicked must turn away from his wicked ways to live. So O House of Israel, turn from your evil ways, because why should you die?

Therefore son of man speak your people's children and say, 'The righteousness of the righteous man cannot deliver him on the day of his transgression. As for the wickedness of the wicked, he will not fall on the day that he turns from his wickedness. But the righteous will be unable to live because of his righteousness on the day that he sins.

When I tell the righteous that he will surely live, but if he trusts in his own righteousness, and commits immorality, none of his righteousness will remembered, but he will die for the immorality that he has committed.
Again, when I say to the wicked, 'You will surely die!' If he turns from his sin, and does that which is lawful and righteous.
If the wicked restores the pledge, and makes restitution for what he has stolen and walks in the laws of life, without committing immorality, he will surely live and he will not die.
None of the sins he has committed will be mentioned to him. For he has done that which is required by the law and what is righteous, and he will surely live.
Yet your people's children say, 'The ways of the Lord is not fair!' But it is really their way that is not fair.
When the righteous man turns from his righteousness and commits immorality, he will die because of it.
But if the wicked man turns from his wickedness, and does that which is lawful and righteous, he will live.
But you say, 'The Lord's way is not fair!' O House of Israel, I will judge every one of you for your ways."
On the fifth day, of the tenth month, of the twelfth year of our captivity, someone who had escaped from Jerusalem came to me, Ezekiel and said, "The city has been defeated."
Now the evening before the escapee came to me, the Lord's hand was upon me. And before the man came to me the next morning, the Lord opened my mouth. So my mouth was opened, and I was no longer mute.
Then the word of the Lord came to me, Ezekiel.

And the Lord said, "Son of man, those who inhabit the waste lands of Israel spoke and said, 'Abraham was only one man, and he inherited the land, but we are many and the land has been given to us as an inheritance.'"
Therefore tell them this is what the Lord God says, 'You eat meat with the blood in it, you look up to your idols and shed blood. Should you possess the land?
You stand on your sword, you commit abominations, and every one of you defiles his neighbor's wife. Should you possess the land?'

So Ezekiel, speak to them and tell them that this is what the Lord God says, 'As surely as I live, those who live in the waste lands will fall by the sword, and I will give anyone who lives in the open field to the beasts to be devoured, and those who live in the forts and caves will die from the pestilence.
For I will leave the land most desolate, and the pompous pride of her strength will cease to exist. Israel's mountains will be left desolate, so that no one will be able to pass through them.
Then they will know that I am the Lord, after I have laid waste to the land and left it most desolate, because of all of the abominations they have committed.

Also son of man, your people's children are still talking against you near the walls and in the doorways of their houses. Everyone and his brother speaks to each other and say, 'I pray you will come and hear the Lord's word!'

And they come to you as people do, and they sit before you as my people to hear your words, but they will not practice them. Because they show much love with their mouth, but their hearts chase after their selfish desires.
And you are like a lovely song to them sung with a pleasant voice, and a well played instrument, because they hear your words, but they do not practice them.
And when this comes to pass, and it will come! Then they will know that a prophet has been among them."
And the Lord's word came to me, Ezekiel.

And the Lord said, "Son of man, prophesy against the shepherds of Israel and tell them that this is what the Lord God says to the shepherds, "Woe unto the shepherds of Israel who only feed themselves! Should not the shepherds feed their flocks?
You eat the fat, clothe yourselves in wool, and kill the fatted sheep, but you do not feed the flock.

You have not strengthened the diseased, nor have you healed the sick. You have not bandaged the injured, nor have you searched for those who were driven away. And you have not searched for the lost, but you rule over them with force and cruelty.
They were scattered because there was no shepherd. And they became meat for all the field beasts after they were scattered.
My sheep wandered throughout all of the high hills and mountains. My flock was scattered throughout the earth, and no one searched for them.
Therefore hear the Lord's word shepherds.

And the Lord God says, "As surely as I live, because there was no shepherd my flock has become prey and meat for every field beast. And because my shepherds did not search for or feed my lost flock, but they only fed themselves."
Therefore hear the Lord's word shepherds.

This is what the Lord God says, "Behold I am against the shepherds, and I will remove my flock from their care, and make them stop feeding my flock, so the shepherds will no longer be able to feed themselves. For I will deliver my flock from their mouths, so that they no longer be meat for them."
For this is what the Lord God says, "Behold I the Lord will both search for and seek out my sheep.
As a shepherd looks for his flock when he is among his scattered sheep, so I will look for my sheep. I will rescue them from all the places where they were scattered on that dark and cloudy day.

And I will bring them out from the other people and gather them from the countries. I will return them to their own land, and feed them by the rivers on Israel's mountains, and in all the inhabited places of the country.
I will feed them in a good pasture, and on Israel's high mountains where their shed will be. They will lie down in a good pastures, and they will they feed in rich pastures on Israel's mountains."
And the Lord God says, "I will feed my flock and make them lie down.
I will seek the lost, and return those who were driven away. I will bandage the broken and strengthen the sick. But I will destroy the fat and strong, and feed them with my judgment."
And this is what the Lord God says, "As for you my flock behold I will judge between sheep and cattle, between rams and goats.

Does it seem to be a small thing to you that you have eaten up all the good pasture? But must you also trample down the rest of your pastures with your feet? You have drunk from the deep waters, but must you foul the rest of them with your feet?
As for my flock, they eat that which your feet you have trampled down, and they drink the water which you have fouled with your feet."
Therefore this is what the Lord God says, "Behold I will even judge between the fatted calf and the lean calf.
Because you have pushed them with side and shoulder, and pushed the diseased ones away with your horns, until you scattered them abroad.
