I will save my flock, they will no longer be your prey, and I will judge between the calves.
I will set one shepherd over them, and my servant David will even feed them. He will feed them and he will be their shepherd.
And I will be their Lord God, and my servant David will be a prince among them. For I the Lord have spoken."
And the Lord said, "I will make a covenant of peace with them, and I will make the evil beasts cease to exist in the land. Then they will live safely in the wilderness, and sleep in the woods.
I will make them and the all places around my hill to be a blessing. I will make the showers come down in their seasons, and they will be showers of blessing.

The field trees will yield her fruit, and the earth will yield her produce. They will live safely in their land, and they will know that I am the Lord, when I have broken the grips of their yoke, and delivered them from the hand of those who enslaved them.
And they will no longer be prey for the heathen, and the beast of the land will not devour them. But they will live safely, and no one will make them afraid.
And I will raise them up as a renowned plant, and they will no longer be consumed by hunger in the land, nor will they bear the heathen's shame anymore."
And the Lord God says, "This is how they will know that I am their Lord God, and that I am with them. Then they will know that the people of the House of Israel are my people.
And the Lord God says, "The flocks of my pasture are men, you are my flock and I am your God."
Then the Lord's word came to me, Ezekiel.
And the Lord said, "Son of man, turn your face against Mount Seir, and prophesy against it.
And tell it that this is what the Lord God says, "O Mount Seir, behold I am against you, and I will stretch out my hand against you to make you most desolate.
I will lay waste to your cities, and you will be left desolate. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
Because you harbor a never ending hatred, and shed the blood of Israel's children by force with the sword in their time of disaster, at the time that their immorality was finally ended."
Therefore this is what the Lord God says, "As surely as I live, I will prepare you for bloodshed and it will pursue you. Since you did not hate bloodshed, bloodshed will pursue you.
Thus I will leave Mount Seir most desolate, and cut it off from those who pass through it or return from it.
I will fill his mountains with his dead men. Those killed with the sword will fall on your hills, in your valleys, and in your rivers.
I will make you a never ending devastation, and your cities will not return. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
Because you have said, 'These two nations and countries will be ours, and we will possess them,' when they were in fact the Lord's."
And the Lord God says, "As surely as I live, I will treat you with your own anger and envy which you showed in your hatred against them. And I will make myself known to them when I judge you.

And you will know that I am the Lord, and that I have heard all of the blasphemies which you have spoken against Israel's mountains when you said, 'They are desolate, and they have been given us to consume!'
You boasted against me and multiplied your words against me, and I have heard them."
This is what the Lord God says, "When the whole earth rejoices, I will make you desolate.

Just as you rejoiced when the inheritance of Israel's house became desolate, I will do the same to you. O Mount Seir, you will be left desolate, along with all of Edom. Then they will know that I am the Lord."
Also, Ezekiel you son of man, prophesy to Israel's mountains and say, "O"mountains of Israel, hear the Lord's word."
For this is what the Lord God says, "Because the enemy has spoken against you and said, 'Aha! Even the ancient high places are our possessions.'"

Therefore prophesy and tell them that this is what the Lord God says, "Because they have made you desolate and swallowed you up on every side, so that you might become a possession to the rest of the heathen. Furthermore you were slandered by the lips of talkers, and became an infamous people.

So, you mountains of Israel, hear what the Lord God has to say to the mountains, hills, rivers, valleys, desolate waste lands, and abandoned cities which have become prey and a mockery to the rest of the heathen all around you.

Therefore this is what the Lord God says, "Surely in my fiery jealousy I have spoken against the rest of the heathen, and against all of Edom. They took my land as their own possession with whole hearted joy and spiteful minds, then plundered it as prey.

So prophesy about the land of Israel, and tell the mountains, hills, rivers, and valleys that this is what the Lord God says, 'Behold I have spoken in my jealous fury because you have carried the heathen's shame.'"
Therefore this is what the Lord God says, "I have raised my hand, and the heathen all around you will surely bear their own shame.
But you, O mountains of Israel, grow your branches and produce fruit for my people of Israel, because they are ready to come home.
For behold, I am for you, I will turn to you and you will be tilled and sown.
I will multiply the people and the entire House of Israel upon you. The cities will be reinhabited and the waste lands will be rebuilt.

I will multiply both man and beast upon you, and they will increase and bear fruit. I will settle you as your old estates were once settled, and you will do better than you did in the beginning. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
Yes, I will make men walk on you, including my people of Israel. They will possess you, and you will be their inheritance, then you will no longer be deprived of men."
This is what the Lord God says, "Because they say to you, 'Your land devours men, and has deprived your nations of children.'"
Therefore the Lord God says, "You will no longer devour men, nor deprive your nations of children."
And the Lord God says, "I will not let men hear of your shame from the heathen, nor allow you to bear the rebuke of the other people, nor will I cause your nation to fall."
Then the Lord's word came to me, Ezekiel.

And the Lord said, "Son of man, when the people of Israel lived in their own land, they defiled it by walking in their own ways and deeds. Their ways before me were like the uncleanliness of a woman during her menstrual cycle.
Therefore I poured out my fury on them for the blood they had shed upon the land, and because they had polluted it with their idols.
I scattered them among the heathen and dispersed them throughout the countries, and I judged them by their own ways and deeds.
When they entered the heathen's land, they profaned my holy name, when the heathen said to them, 'These are the Lord's people, who had to leave his land.'
But I had pity for my holy name, which the House of Israel had profaned among the heathen, where they went."

Therefore speak to the House of Israel and tell them that this is what the Lord God says, "O House of Israel, I do not do this for your sakes, but for the sake of my holy name, which you profaned among the heathen, where you went."

And the Lord God says, "I will sanctify my great name, which was profaned in the midst of the heathen. Then the heathen will know that I am the Lord, after I am sanctified in you before their very eyes.
For I will take you from among the heathen and all the other countries, and return you to your own land.
Then will I sprinkle clean water on you, and your filth will be cleansed from you, and I will cleanse you of all your idols.
I will also give you a new heart, and I will put a new spirit inside you. I will take the stony heart from your body, and I will give you a new heart of flesh.
I will put my spirit inside of you, and make you walk in my laws, and you will keep and perform my judgments.
You will live in the land that I gave to your fathers. Then you will be my people and I will be your God.
I will also save you from all of your uncleanliness, and I will call for the wheat to increase, and bring no famine against you.
I will multiply the fruit of the trees, and the increase the crops of the field, so that you will no longer bear the rebuke of famine among the heathen.
Then you will remember that your own evil ways and deeds were not good. Then you will loathe yourselves for your wickedness and abominations."
And the Lord God says, "O House of Israel, let it be known to you, that I do not do this for your own sakes, so be ashamed and confused because of your own ways."
This is what the Lord God says, "In the days when I have cleansed you from all of your wickedness, I will also cause you to live in the cities, and the waste lands will be rebuilt.
And the desolate land will be tilled, instead of allowing it to lay desolate in sight of all who passed by.
And they will say, 'This land that was desolate has become like the Garden of Eden, and the wasted, desolated, and ruined cities have been fenced and inhabited.'
Then the heathen who are left all around you will know that I the Lord rebuilt the ruined places, and planted the desolate. I the Lord have spoken, and I will do it!"
This is what the Lord God says, "I will once again be asked by the House of Israel, to provide for them, and I will increase their people like a flock.
Like the holy flock of Jerusalem during her solemn feasts, so that the wasted cities will be filled with flocks of people. Then they will know that I am the Lord."
The hand of the Lord was upon me, Ezekiel. And he carried me out in the Lord's spirit, and set me down in the middle of a valley full of bones.
The Lord made me pass them by and all around, and behold there were a great many very dry bones in the open valley.
And the Lord said to me, "Son of man, can these bones live?" And I answered, "O Lord God, only you know."
Again the Lord spoke to me, Ezekiel and said, "Prophesy about these bones, and tell them, 'O you dry bones, hear the Lord's word.'"
This is what the Lord God says to these bones, "Behold I will cause the breath of life to enter you, and you will live.
I will lay sinews on you, and cover you with flesh and skin, and I will put breath in you, and you will live. Then you will know that I am the Lord."
So I prophesied as I was commanded and as I prophesied, there was noise and shaking, and bone after bone came together.
I saw the sinews and flesh grow on them, and the skin covered them, but there was no breath in them.

Then the Lord spoke to me, Ezekiel and said, "Son of man, prophesy to the wind and say this is what the Lord God says, 'O breath, come from the four winds and breathe on these dead, so that they may live.'"
So I prophesied as he commanded me, and the breath came into them, and they lived. And an exceedingly great army stood up on their feet.
Then the Lord spoke to me, Ezekiel and said, "Son of man, these bones are the whole House of Israel. Behold they say, "Our bones are dried up, our hope is lost, and we are cut off for our parts.'"

Therefore prophesy to them and tell them that this is what the Lord God says, "O my people, behold I will open your graves and cause you to come up out of your graves, and bring you to the land of Israel.
O my people, you will know that I am the Lord after I have opened your graves, and brought you up out of your graves."
And the Lord said, "I will put my spirit in you and you will live. I will place you in your own land, then you will know that I the Lord have spoken and it was done."
The word of the Lord came again to me, Ezekiel.

And the Lord said, "Furthermore son of man, take a stick and write on it, 'For Judah and his companions the children of Israel.' Then write on another stick, 'For Joseph, the stick of Ephraim and for all his companions the House of Israel.'
Then join the two sticks together, and they will become one in your hand.
When the children of your people speak to you and say, 'Will you now show us what you mean by these sticks?'"

Tell them this is what the Lord God says, "Behold I will take Joseph's stick, which is in Ephraim's hand, along with his tribes of Israel, and put them together with Judah's stick to make one stick from both, and they will be one in my hand.
When the sticks on which you have written are in your, and in full view of all the people."

Then tell them that this is what the Lord God says, "Behold I will take the children of Israel from the heathen where they have gone, and will gather them from every side, and return them to their own land.

I will make them one nation in the land of Israel's mountains, and there will be one king over all of them, and they will no longer be two nations And they will never be divided into two kingdoms ever again.

They will never defile themselves with their idols, their detestable things, or their transgressions ever again. But I will save them from their homes, in which they have sinned. I will cleanse them, so that they will be my people and I will be their God.
And my servant David will be their king, and they will all have one shepherd. But they will walk in my judgments, and observe and keep my laws.

And they will live in the land that I have given to my servant Jacob, where your fathers have lived. They will live there with their children, and their children's children forever. And my servant David will be their prince forever.
In addition, I will make a peace covenant with them, and it will be an everlasting covenant with them. I will place them and multiply them, and I will set my sanctuary in the middle of them forever.
My tabernacle will be with them. And I will be their God and they will be my people.
And the heathen will know that I the Lord have sanctified Israel, and my sanctuary will be in the middle of them forever."
And the word of the Lord came to me, Ezekiel.
And the Lord said, "Son of man, turn your face against Gog of the land of Magog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal. And prophesy against him.
And tell him that this is what the Lord God says, 'O Gog chief prince of Meshech and Tubal, I am against you.
I will push you back, put hooks in your jaws, and I will bring you out with your entire army including your horses and horsemen, a great company with all sorts of armor, shields, and swords.
Persia, Ethiopia, and Libya will accompany them with shields and helmets.
Gomer and all of his troops, the house of Togarmah from the north and all of his troops, and many other people with you.
Be prepared to be their guard, and prepare your companies who are assembled with you.

After many days you will be visited. In the latter years you will return to the land after it has recovered from the sword. A land whose people were gathered to Israel's mountains, which had always been a waste land. But they will have been brought back from the nations, where they will all live safely.
You, all your troops, and many people with you will ascend and come like a storm, and you will cover the land like a cloud.'"
This is what the Lord God says, "Then evil thoughts will come into your mind, and you will plan evil things.
And you will say, 'I will go up into the land of unwalled villages where the people are at rest and they all live safely, in homes without defensive walls, bars, or gates.

To plunder, take prey and turn your hand against the desolate inhabited places, and against the people gathered from the nations, who live in the middle of the land, and who have acquired cattle and goods.'

Sheba, Dedan, and the merchants of Tarshish with all its young lions, will say to you, 'Have you come to plunder? Have you gathered your company to take prey and carry away gold and silver, to take our cattle and goods as the spoils of war?'
Therefore son of man, prophesy and tell Gog that this is what the Lord God says, "In the days that my people of Israel live securely, will you not know it?
Then you and many people with you, will come from your place in the north, a great company and mighty army, all riding horses.

And you will attack my people of Israel like a cloud that covers the land. O Gog, In the latter days I will bring you against my land, so that the heathen will know me, when I am sanctified in you before their very eyes."

This is what the Lord GOD says, "Are you the one of whom I spoke of in the old day through my servants the prophets of Israel, who prophesied in those days for many years that I would bring you against them?"
And the Lord God says, "At the time when Gog comes against the land of Israel, my fury will show in my face.
For in my fierce jealous rage and fiery anger I have spoken, surely in those days the land of Israel will quake.

So that the fish of the sea, birds of the air, field beasts, every creature that creeps on the earth, and all the men who are on the face of the earth will shake in my presence. The mountains will be thrown down, the steep cliffs will fall, and every wall will collapse to the ground."
And the Lord God says, "I will summon a sword against Gog throughout all my mountains, and every man will turn his sword against his own brother.
I will plead against him with pestilence and bloodshed. I will rain flooding rains, great hailstones, fire, and brimstone down on him, his troops, and the many people with him.
As a result of all this I will magnify and sanctify myself, and I will reveal myself before the eyes of many nations! Then they will know that I am the Lord."
Therefore Ezekiel son of man, prophesy against Gog and tell him that this is what the Lord God says, "Behold I am against you, O Gog chief prince of Meshech and Tubal.
I will turn you back, and leave only one sixth of you, and I will make you come up from the north, and bring you against Israel's mountains.
I will defeat the bow in your left hand, and make the arrows fall out of your right hand.
You, your troops, and all the people with you will fall on Israel's mountains. And I will give you to every kind of ravenous bird and the field beasts to be devoured."
And the Lord God says, "You will fall in the open field, because I have spoken.
I will send fire against Magog, and those who live carefree in the islands. Then they will know that I am the Lord.
So I will make my holy name known in the midst of my people of Israel. I will not let them pollute my holy name anymore, and the heathen will know that I am the Lord, the Holy One in Israel."
Behold the Lord God says, "The time has come and it is done, for this is the day of which I have spoken.
And those who live in Israel's cities will go out, and set fire to and burn the weapons, shields, swords, bows, arrows, clubs, and spears which will burn in the fire for seven years."

And the Lord God says, "They will have to harvest no wood from the field, nor cut down any trees from the forests, because they will burn the weapons for fuel, and plunder those who plundered them, and rob those who robbed them.

In those days I will give Gog a burial place in Israel, in the Valley of Passengers east of the sea. The stench will clog the noses of the passengers, because they bury will Gog and all of his troops there, and they will call it the Valley of Hamongog.
It will take the House of Israel seven months to bury them and cleanse the land."
And the Lord God says, "Yes, all the people of the land will bury them, and it will become a day to remember when I the Lord am glorified.
After seven months, they will employ men to regularly go throughout the land to bury the remaining passenger's dead bodies to cleanse the earth.
When the passengers who pass through the land see a man's bones, they must erect a sign next to it, until the gravediggers bury it in the Valley of Hamongog.
The city will be named Hamonah, and this is how they will cleanse the land."

And this is what the Lord God says, "Ezekiel son of man, speak to every bird and field beast and say, 'Assemble yourselves together from every side to my sacrifice that I make for you. A great sacrifice on Israel's mountains, so that you may eat flesh and drink blood.
You will eat the flesh of the mighty, and drink the blood of the princes of the earth and rams, lambs, goats, and bulls all of which were fattened up in Bashan.
You will eat fat until you are full, and drink blood until you are drunk from the sacrifices which I have sacrificed for you."
And the Lord God says, "You will fill yourselves at my table with horses, chariots, mighty men, and all the other men of war.
I will set my glory among the heathen and they will all see the judgments I have executed, and that I have laid my hand on them.
So the House of Israel will know that I am their Lord God from that day forward.

Then the heathen will know that the House of Israel went into captivity for their immorality, because they trespassed against me, therefore I hid my face from them, and put them into the hands of their enemies, so that they all fell by the sword.
I have done things to them equal to their own uncleanliness and transgressions, and I have hidden my face from them."
Therefore this is what the Lord God says, "Now I will return Jacob from the captivity and have mercy on the whole House of Israel, and I will be jealous for my holy name.
After they have carried their shame and all of their trespasses against me, when they lived safely in their land and no one frightened them.
When I have brought them back from the people, and gathered them from the lands of their enemies, I will be sanctified in them in sight of many nations.
Then they will know that I am their Lord God, who caused them to be led into captivity among the heathen. For now I have returned them to their own land, and I have left none of them behind."
And the Lord God says, "I will no longer hide my face from them, because I have poured out my spirit on the House of Israel."

At the beginning of the twenty-fifth year of our captivity, on the tenth day of the month, in the fourteenth year after the city was defeated, the Lord's hand was on me and he brought me to that place.
In visions from God, he brought me into the land of Israel and set me to the south side of a very high mountain, where there was what looked like the framework of a city.
He brought me to that place, and I saw a man who appeared to be made of brass. He stood in the gates with a linen line and a measuring rod in his hand.

And the man said to me, "Son of man, look with your eyes, and hear with your ears, and open your heart to everything that I show you. Because you were brought here so that I might show them to you, so you can declare everything that you see to the House of Israel."
And I saw a wall surrounding the outside of the house, and in the man's hand a measuring rod six hand width cubits long, and he measured the building to be one rod wide and one rod high.
Then he came to the eastern gate, and climbed its stairs, and measured the gate's threshold to be one rod deep, and the other gate's threshold to be one rod deep.
Every little chamber was one rod long and one rod deep, and the little chambers were five cubits apart, and the gate's threshold by the inner entrance hall was one rod.
He also measured the inside of the gate's entrance hall to be one rod.
Then he measured the gate's entrance hall to be eight cubits, and its posts were two cubits, and the inner gate's entrance hall faced inward.
And there were three little chambers on each side of the eastern gate, and each one was the same size, and the posts on each side were the same size.
He measured the entry gate and it was ten cubits wide and thirteen cubits long.
The space also before the little chambers was one cubit on this side, and the space was one cubit on that side, and the little chambers were six cubits on this side, and six cubits on that side.
Then he measured the gate's distance between the roof of one little chamber to the next, and from door to door it was twenty-five cubits.
He also measured all the posts around the courtyard gate to be sixty cubits high.
And it was fifty cubits from the entrance of the gate to the other end of the entrance hall.
There were narrow inset windows in the little chambers. And there were posts with carved palm trees, and arches all around the inside of the gate.
Then he brought me into the outer courtyard, and there were thirty chambers all around the courtyard, and the walkway was paved all around the courtyard.
And the pavement beside the gates length was the same as the gates lower pavement.
Then he measured the width from the front of the lower gate to the front of the outside of the inner courtyard to be one hundred cubits eastward and northward.
And he measured the length and width of the gate's northern outer courtyard.
Its three little chambers on each side, and its posts and arches had the same measurements as the first gate, which was fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
Their windows, arches, and palm trees measured the same as the eastern gate. There were seven steps that went up to its arches which were before them.
There was an inner courtyard gate next to the northern gate, and also one near the eastern gate, and the distance from gate to gate measured one hundred cubits.
After that he brought me south and I saw a gate there. Then he measured its posts and arches, and they had the same dimensions as the others.
It had windows in it and arches all around it, like the other windows. It was fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
It had seven steps leading up to its arches, and there were palm trees on each side of its posts.
There was a gate in the inner southern courtyard, and from southern gate to southern gate, it measured one hundred cubits.
And he brought me into the southern courtyard gate, and he measured the south gate and it had the same dimensions as the others.
Its gate chambers, posts, and arches had the same dimensions as the others, and there were windows and arches all the way around it. It was fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
Its arches all around were twenty-five cubits long, and five cubits deep.
Its arches faced the outer courtyard, and its posts were decorated with palm trees, with eight steps leading up to its arches.
And he brought me into the eastern inner court, and he measured the gate and it had the same dimensions as the others.
Its gate chambers, posts, and arches measured the same as the others, and there were windows and arches all around it. It was fifty cubits long, and twenty-five cubits wide.
And its arches faced the outer courtyard, and its posts were decorated with palm trees on each side, and it had eight steps leading up to its arches.
Then he brought me to the north gate, and its dimensions were the same as the others.
Its little chambers had posts, arches, and windows all around it. It was fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
Its posts faced the outer courtyard, and each post was decorated with palm trees on each side, and it had eight steps leading up to it.
Its chambers and entrances were next to the gate posts, where they washed the burnt offerings.
The gate's entrance hall had two tables on each side, where the burnt offerings, sin offerings, and trespass offerings were killed.
Outside, there were two tables on each side as one goes up to the northern gate entrance, and on each side of the gate's entrance hall there were two more tables.
There were four tables on each side of the gate, eight tables in all where they killed their sacrifices.

And the four tables were made of carved stone for the burnt offering. It was a cubit and a half long, and a cubit and a half wide, and one cubit high. Where they also laid the instruments they used to kill the burnt offerings and sacrifices.
There were hooks, each a hand wide, fastened all around inside the room, and the offering's flesh was laid on its tables.
Outside the inner gate were the inner courtyard chambers beside the northern gate facing south for the singers. And another beside the eastern gate having facing the north.
And he said to me, "This south facing chamber is for the priests, who are responsible for taking care of the house.
And the north facing chamber is for the priests who maintain the altar. But Zadok's sons are the only Levites who are allowed to come near the Lord to minister to him."
So he measured the courtyard, and it was one hundred cubits long and one hundred cubits wide square. The altar that was in front of the house.
And he brought me to the house entrance hall, and measured each post of the entrance hall. Each post measured five cubits wide on each side, and the gate measured three cubits wide on each side.
The entrance hall measured twenty cubits long and eleven cubits wide. Then he brought me next to the steps leading up to it, and there were columns next to each side of it.
Afterward he brought me to the temple and measured the posts, each post measured six cubits wide on each side, which was the width of the tabernacle.
The entrance was ten cubits wide, and each door was five cubits wide. The outer sanctuary was forty cubits long and twenty cubits wide.
Then went he into the inner sanctuary and the entrance door post was two cubits wide, and the door was six cubits long and seven cubits wide.
Then he measured the room in the front of the temple, and it was twenty cubits long and twenty cubits wide. And the man said to me, Ezekiel, "This is the Most Holy Place."
Then he measured the temple walls, and each wall was six cubits thick, and each side chamber around the temple was four cubits wide.

There were three levels of side chambers one above the other, with thirty chambers on each level. There were ledges all around the temple walls to support the side chambers, but the ledges were not attached to the temple walls.

The winding staircase that led to the side chambers wound around and widened as they ascended upward through the temple. So the width of the staircases increased from the lowest chamber to the highest chamber in the middle of the temple.
I also saw that the temple's foundation height all around the side chambers was a full six cubit rod long.
The outer wall of the side chamber was five cubits thick, and the space that was left was for the side chambers that were inside.
The distance between the chambers was twenty cubits wide on each side of the temple.
The side chamber doors faced the open area, one door faced north and the other door faced south, and the area that was left was five cubits wide all the way around.
Now the building that faced the west end of the temple courtyard was seventy cubits wide, and the building wall was five cubits thick all the way around, and it was ninety cubits long.
Then he measured the temple, and it was one hundred cubits long, and the temple courtyard and the building along with its walls were one hundred cubits long.
The east temple courtyard and the temple wall measured one hundred cubits wide.
And he measured the building next to the temple courtyard behind it, and its galleries on each side along with the inner temple and the courtyard entrance halls was one hundred cubits long.
The door posts, narrow windows, and the galleries on all three levels next to the door had wooden ceilings. The walls from the ground up to the windows, and the windows were covered with wood.
The space above the outside door and the inner temple walls both inside and out were measured.
And the space was decorated with cherubims and palm trees, with a carved palm tree between each cherub, and every cherub had two faces.
There was a face of a man facing the palm tree on one side, and the face of a young lion facing the palm tree on the other side. They were made throughout the temple all the way around.
The cherubims and palm trees were made, and they covered the temple wall from the ground to above the door all the way around the temple.
The temple posts were square, and the sanctuary facade appeared the be similar.

The wooden altar was three cubits high and two cubits long, and its corners and the length of its walls were made of wood. And the man said to me, Ezekiel, "This is the table that is before the Lord."
Both the temple and the sanctuary had two doors.
Each door had two swinging panels that opened and closed.
Each temple door had cherubims and palm trees carved on them, like the ones on the walls, and there were thick wooden planks covering the face of the outside entrance hall.
There were narrow windows and palm trees on each side of the entrance hall. And the temple's side chamber walls were also covered with thick wooden planks.
Then the man brought me, Ezekiel into the outer courtyard through the north hall, and he brought me into the chamber next to the temple courtyard before the north side of the building.
The building with the north door was one hundred cubits long and fifty cubits wide.
There were three stories of galleries facing each other next to the twenty cubit long inner courtyard opposite of the outer courtyard pavement.
There was a ten cubit wide inner walkway before the chambers that was one hundred cubits long, and the chamber doors faced north.
Now the upper chambers were shorter because the galleries were higher than the lower chambers in the middle of the building.
For they were three stories high, but they did not have columns like the courtyards. So the upper building was straightened more than the middle and lower ground floor levels.
The outer wall in front of the chambers next to the outer courtyard was fifty cubits long.
For the chambers in the outer courtyard were fifty cubits long, and those facing the temple were a hundred cubits long.
Below these chambers was the east side entrance that could be entered from the outer courtyard.
The chambers were built in the thickest part of the eastern courtyard wall next to the temple courtyard beside the building.
The walkway before them appeared to be similar to the northern chambers, and they seemed to be the same length and width, with similar windows, doors, and dimensions.
There was a door on the front walkway directly in front of the eastern wall entrance similar to the south facing chamber doors.

Then the man said to me, Ezekiel, "The north and south chambers before the temple courtyard, are the holy chambers, where the priests who are allowed to approach the Lord will eat the most holy things. They will lay the most holy things and the bread offering, sin offering, and trespass offering there, because it is a holy place.

When the priests enter, they may not leave the holy place and go into the outer courtyard, but they must change the garments they use to minister there and leave the holy garments there because they are holy. They must wear other garments to approach those things which are for the people."
When the man finished measuring the inner house, he brought me out by the eastern gate, and measured everything all around it.
He measured the east side with the measuring rod, and it was 500 cubits long.
He measured the north side with the measuring rod, and it was 500 cubits long.
He measured the south with the measuring rod, and it was 500 cubits long.
He turned around and measured the west side with the measuring rod, and it was 500 cubits long.
He measured the walls on all four sides. And the walls to separate the sanctuary from the profane place were 500 cubits long and 500 cubits wide.
Afterward the man brought me Ezekiel back to the gate facing east.
And, behold the glory of the God of Israel came from the east, and his voice made a noise that sounded like many waters, and the earth glowed with his glory.
In this vision I saw the same thing that I saw in the vision I had when the Lord came to destroy the city. These visions were like the one I had near the Kebar River, when I fell facedown.
The Lord's glory entered the temple through the east facing gate.
So the spirit took me up to the inner courtyard, and behold the glory of the Lord filled the temple.
While the man stood next to me, I heard the Lord speaking to me from the temple.

And the Lord said to me, Ezekiel, "Son of man, this is a place for my throne and the soles of my feet, where I will live among the children of Israel forever. The House of Israel and their kings will no longer defile my holy name, by putting their corpses in the high places or committing prostitution.

By setting their threshold next my thresholds, and their posts next to my posts with kust a wall between me and them, they defiled my holy name by the abominations that they committed. Therefore I have consumed them with my anger.
Now let them remove their prostitution and their kings corpses far away from me, and I will live in their midst forever.
As for you son of man, show the temple plans to the House of Israel, so that they may be ashamed of their wickedness, and let them measure the plans.

And if they are ashamed of what they have done, show them the temple design, and the fashion of its entrances and exits. Show them all of its designs, legal decrees, and laws. And while they are watching write it down, so that they may keep its complete designs, and all of its legal decrees, and do them.
This is the temple law, and the top of the mountain and the area surrounding it will be most holy. Behold, this is the law of the temple.

These are the altar's measurements in long cubits, which is a cubit and a hand width. Its foundation will be one cubit deep and one cubit wide. Its border around its edge will be one span wide, and this will be the highest point of the altar.

From its foundation on the ground to the lower ledge will be two cubits and it will be one cubit wide. From the smaller ledge to the larger ledge will be four cubits, and the ledge will be one cubit wide.
So the altar will be four cubits high, and four horns will point upward from the altar.
The square altar will be twelve cubits long and twelve cubits wide.

The square ledge will be fourteen cubits long and fourteen cubits wide, and the border around it will be half a cubit wide, and its foundation will be one cubit wide. And its stairs will face eastward."

And the Lord said to me, Ezekiel, "Son of man, this is what the Lord God says, 'These are the altar's legal decrees for the day that they build it, to be kept when they offer burnt offerings and to sprinkle blood on it after that.'"
The Lord God says, "You must give a young bull as a sin offering to the Levite priests, the descendants of Zadok, who are allowed to approach me to minister to me.
You must put its blood on the altar's four horns, and on the four corners of the ledge, and all around its border. This is how you will cleanse and purge the altar.
You must take the bull as the sin offering, and he will burn it in the temple's appointed place outside of the sanctuary.
And on the second day you will offer a kid of the goats without blemish for a sin offering, and they will cleanse the altar, as they did cleanse it with the bull.
When you have finished cleansing it, you will offer a young unblemished bull, and an unblemished ram from the flock.
Offer them before the Lord, and the priests will throw salt on them to offer them up as a burnt offering to the Lord.
You will prepare a goat as a sin offering for seven days, they must also prepare an unblemished young bull and ram from the flock.
They will purge and purify the altar for seven days, and this is how they will consecrate themselves."

The Lord God says, "On the eighth day after the seven days of consecration are over, the priests must continue to make peace offerings and burnt offerings on the altar, then I will forgive your sins."
Then the man brought me back to the gate of the outer sanctuary that faced east, but it was shut.

Then said the Lord to me, Ezekiel, "This gate will be shut, and it will not be opened. No man will be allowed to enter through it, because the Lord God of Israel, has entered through it. Therefore it will be kept shut.
It is only for the prince himself to sit within this gate to eat bread before the Lord. He will enter the entrance hall through that gate, and will leave the same way."
Then the man brought me through the north gate to the front of the temple. I looked, and behold the Lord's glory filled the Lord's temple, and I fell facedown.

And the Lord said to me, Ezekiel, "Son of man, pay close attention, and see and hear everything that I say to you about all the laws and legal decrees of the Lord's temple. Pay particularly close attention when you enter and exit the temple and its sanctuary."
Tell the rebellious people even those in the temple of Israel that this is what the Lord God says, "O temple of Israel, suffice it to say that all of your abominations must end.

You have brought strangers and uncircumcised of heart and flesh into my sanctuary. You even pollute my temple, when you offer my bread, the fat, and the blood. They have broken my covenant because of all of your abominations.
You have not kept control of my holy things, but you have put others to take charge of my sanctuary and do your work for you."
This is what the Lord God says, "No stranger uncircumcised at heart or flesh will enter my sanctuary, not even a stranger who lives among the children of Israel.
Even the Levites who moved far away from me when Israel went astray, who left to chase after their idols, will bear the consequences of their immorality.

But they will be ministers in my sanctuary, and take charge of the temple gates and minister to the temple. They will kill the burnt offering and the sacrifices for the people, and they will stand before them to minister to them."

And the Lord God says, "Because they ministered to them before their idols and caused the temple of Israel to fall into immorality, therefore I have lifted up my hand against them, and they will bear their immorality.

And they will not come near me, to perform the duties of the priest's office for me, nor are they to come near any of my holy things in the Most Holy Place, but they will bear the shame of the abominations they have committed.
But I will put them in charge of the temple, because of all of the temple's required service, and everything that must be done there."

The Lord God says, "But the Levite priests Zadok's descendants, who kept charge of my sanctuary when the Israelis went astray from me, can come near me to minister to me, and they will stand before me to offer me the fat and blood.
They will be allowed to enter my sanctuary, and come close to my table to minister to me, and they will keep my charge.

When they enter at the gates of the inner courtyard, they must wear linen garments, and they are not allowed to wear anything made of wool while they minister at the gates of the inner courtyard or inside the temple.
They must wear linen hats on their heads and linen pants around their waist, they must not wear anything that makes them sweat.

When they go into the outer courtyard to the people, they will take off their garments for ministering, and lay them in the holy chambers. Then they will put on other garments, so that they do not sanctify the people with their garments.
They must not shave their heads, nor let their hair grow long, but they will neatly trim their hair.
No priests are allowed to drink wine when they enter the inner courtyard.
No priests are allowed to marry a widow or a divorced woman, but they must marry a young women of the descendants of the temple of Israel, or a dead priest's widow.
And they will teach my people the difference between the holy and the profane, and make them recognize the difference between the unclean and the clean.
And they will stand in judgment of all controversies, and judged according to my judgments, and they will keep my laws and my assemblies laws, and keep my Sabbaths holy.
A priest must not come close to a dead person and defile themselves. Unless they are a father, mother, son, or daughter, brother, or unmarried sister of the deceased, then they may defile themselves.
After he is cleansed, the priest must calculate seven days."
And the Lord God says, "Then on the day that the priest returns to the inner courtyard of the sanctuary to minister, he will offer his sin offering.
As for their inheritance, I am their inheritance, and you will give them no possession in Israel, because I am their possession.
They will eat the bread, sin, and trespass offerings, and every dedicated thing in Israel will be theirs.

The best of the first fruits of everything and every donation of every sort of contribution will belong to the priests You will also give the priest the first batch of your dough, so that the blessing may rest upon your home.
The priests are not allowed to eat anything that died of natural causes or is torn apart by birds or beasts."

And the Lord God spoke to me, Ezekiel and said, "When you cast lots and divide the land for an inheritance, you will offer a donation to the Lord, a holy portion of the land. It will measure 25,000 cubits long, and 10,000 cubits wide. And all of the land within its borders will be holy.

Within this area there will be a square piece of land that measures 500 cubits long and 500 cubits wide for the sanctuary. And the sanctuary will be surrounded by a strip of land 50 cubits wide for its fields and pastures.
So the land for the sanctuary and the Most Holy Place will measure 25,000 cubits long and 10,000 cubits wide.

This holy portion of land will be for the priests who minister in the sanctuary, who are allowed to come near and minister to the Lord. It will be a place for their houses, and a holy place for the sanctuary.

Another section of land 25,000 cubits long and 10,000 cubits wide will also be reserved next to the holy piece of land for the Levites who minister in the temple. And the Levites will also have 20 chambers as a possession for themselves.
You will assign a piece of land 5,000 cubits wide and 25,000 cubits long as a possession to the city, next to the donated holy portion of land, and it will belong to the whole House of Israel.

A portion of land will be reserved for the prince on each side of the donated holy portion of land, which lies before the donated holy portion and the city's possession as the city's possession. It will be located from the west side westward and from the east side eastward, and it will extend the length of one of the portions, from the western border to the eastern border.
This land will be his possession in Israel. And my princes will no longer oppress my people, but they give the rest of the land to the House of Israel assigned by tribe.

This is what the Lord God says, "O princes of Israel, be satisfied and put an end to your violence and plunder, and execute good judgment and justice." Because the Lord God says, "Stop demanding payments from my people.
You must use honest scales, an honest ephah, and an honest bath.

The ephah and the bath will be the same quantity, and a bath will contain a one-tenth part of a homer, and an ephah will contain a one-tenth part of a homer, and both will be based on the standard measure of the homer.
The shekel will be equal to twenty gerahs. Twenty shekels plus twenty-five shekels plus fifteen shekels will equal one maneh.
And you will offer as your donation, one-sixth of an ephah from each homer of wheat, and one-sixth of an ephah from each homer of barley.
The legally required oil donation will be based on the bath. You must offer one-tenth of a bath from each cor, and a cor is equal to one homer or ten baths, because ten baths equal one homer."

And the Lord God says, "One lamb from a flock of 200 must be offered from the lush pastures of Israel. These are for a bread offering, a burnt offering, and a peace offerings, to make atonement for the people.
All the people of the land will give this donation for the prince in Israel.

And it will be the prince's responsibility to give burnt offerings, bread offerings, and drink offerings for the feasts, new moons, Sabbaths, and for all of the solemn affairs of the House of Israel. So he will prepare the sin offerings, bread offerings, burnt offerings, and peace offerings to make atonement for the House of Israel."
This is what the Lord God says, "On the first day, of the first month, you must take a young unblemished bull and cleanse the sanctuary.
The priest will take some blood from the sin offering and put it on the temple doorposts, on the four corners of the altar's ledge, and on the gateposts of the inner courtyard.
And you will do this on the seventh day of the month for anyone who errs or anyone who is simpleminded. And this is how you will make an atonement for the temple.
On the fourteenth day, of the first month, you will hold the Passover's seven days of feasting, during which time unleavened bread will be eaten.
On that day the prince will prepare a bull as a sin offering for himself and for all the people of the land.
Each of the seven days of the feast, he will prepare a burnt offering, seven unblemished bulls and rams, and a kid goat as a sin offering to the Lord.
And the priest will prepare a one ephah bread offering for each bull, and an ephah for each ram, and a hin of oil for each ephah of bread.
On the fifteenth day of the seventh month, during the seven days of feast, the priest must make the same preparations for the sin offering, burnt offering, bread offering, and the oil offering."

The Lord God spoke to me Ezekiel and this is what he said, "The gate of the inner courtyard that faces east will be kept shut during the six working days, but on the Sabbath and the day of the new moon it will be opened.

The prince will enter through the entrance hall of the outer east gate and stand by the gatepost, as the priests prepare his burnt offerings and peace offerings. He will worship at the threshold of the gate and then he will leave, but the gate will not be shut until evening.
The people of the land will also worship before the Lord at this gateway on the Sabbaths and the new moons.
The burnt offerings that the prince offers to the Lord on the Sabbath day will be six unblemished lambs and an unblemished ram.
There will be a one ephah bread offering for each ram, and the bread offering for each lamb will be as much as he can afford to give, along with a hin of oil for each one ephah bread offering.
And on the day of the new moon the sacrifice will require an unblemished young bull and ram, six unblemished lambs, and an unblemished ram.

And the priest will prepare a one ephah bread offering for a bull, and a one ephah bread offering for a ram, and whatever his hand can measure for the lambs, plus a hin of oil for each one ephah bread offering.
When the prince enters, he will enter through the entrance of that gateway, and he will leave the same way."

And the Lord said, "When the people of the land come before the Lord on the solemn feasts, whoever enters to worship through the north gate must leave by the south gate, and whoever enters through the south gate must leave by the north gate. No one will return through the same gate by which they entered, but they must leave by the opposite gate.
And the prince will enter with the people when they go in, and when they leave, he will leave with them.

At the feasts and at the solemn affairs, there will be a one ephah bread offering per bull, a one ephah bread offering per ram, and as much as he can afford to give for the lambs, and a hin of oil per ephah of bread offering."

And the Lord said, "When the prince voluntary prepares a burnt offering or peace offering to the Lord, the east facing gate will be opened for him. He must prepare his burnt offerings and peace offerings as he does on the Sabbath day. Then he will leave, and the gate will be shut after he has gone.
You will prepare a daily burnt offering to the Lord of a year-old unblemished lamb every morning.

You must prepare a one-sixth ephah bread offering every morning, along with a third of a hin of oil to moisten the fine flour, as a continuous bread offering to the Lord. This shall be a never ending legal decree.
And this is how they must they prepare the lamb, bread offering, and oil every morning as a continuous burnt offering."
This is what the Lord God says, "If the prince give a gift to any of his sons as an inheritance, it will be passed down to his son's descendants. And it will become their property by inheritance.

But if he gives a gift of his inheritance to one of his servants, then it will belong to him until the year of liberty. Afterward it will return to the prince. Because his inheritance is only for his son's to inherit.

The prince must not take from the people's inheritance by oppressing them or evicting them from their own property. But he will give his sons an inheritance from his own property, so that my people are not scattered from their own property."
Then the man brought me through the entrance at the side gate, into the holy priest's chambers which looked northward, and he showed me a place on the two western sides.

Then the man said to me, "This is the place where the priests will boil the trespass and sin offerings, and bake the bread offering, so that they do not bring them into the outer courtyard and sanctify the people."
Then the man brought me into the outer courtyard, and made me pass by the four courtyard corners, and I saw another courtyard in every corner of the courtyard.
The four corners of the courtyard there had other courtyards joined to it that were forty cubits long and thirty cubits wide. Each of these four corners had the same dimensions.
There was a row of buildings all around all four of them, and each one had boiling places built under and all around its rows.
Then the man said to me, "These are the places where those who minister in the temple will boil the sacrifices offered by the people."

Afterwards the man brought me, Ezekiel back to the door of the temple, and I saw water coming from under the east temple threshold, because the front of the temple faced east. And the water flowed from under from the south side of the temple, south of the altar.
Then brought he me through the north gate, and led me around the outside to the outer gate facing east, and there I saw running water coming out of the right side.
When the man with the measuring line in his hand left and headed eastward, he measured a thousand cubits and brought me through ankle deep water.
Then he measured another thousand cubits and brought me through knee-deep water. Then he measured another thousand cubits again and brought me through waist-deep water.

Afterward he measured another thousand cubits over a river that I could not cross, because the river's water had risen to a height that was deep enough to swim in, but it could not be crossed on foot.
And the man said to me, Ezekiel, "Son of man, have you seen this? Then he brought me back to the river bank.
When I returned, I saw many trees along both sides of the river banks.
Then the man said to me, "These waters flow toward the east country and down into the desert, then out to the sea. When the water empties into the sea, the waters will be healed.

Then every living thing that moves, will go wherever the rivers flow and live, and there will be a vast number of fish. Because these waters will flow to the place where they will be healed, and everything will live wherever the river flows.
Fishermen will stand by the shore from En-Gedi all the way to En-Eglaim, and they will spread their nets and catch an abundance of many different types fish from the Mediterranean Sea.
But its swamps and marshes will not be healed, they will be made salty.

A fruit trees will grow along both sides of the river bank. Its leaves will not wither and it will produce a never ending supply of fruit. It will bring forth new fruit every month because the sanctuary waters will flow to them. Its fruit will be eaten for food and its leaves will be used for medicine."
This is what Lord God says, "This is how you will divide up the borders of the land which you will inherit among the twelve tribes of Israel. Joseph will receive two portions.
Each of them will inherit an equal portion. Because I lifted up my hand and promised to give it to your fathers, and this land will fall to you as an inheritance.
And this land will border the land toward the north side from the Mediterranean Sea, by the way of Hethlon to Zedad.
On the way to Hamath, Berothah, Sibraim, which is between the borders of Damascus, Hamath, Hazar-Hatticon near the coast of Hauran.
The border from the sea will go to Hazar-Enan, along the northern border of Damascus, and the northern border of Hamath. And this will be the northern border.
The eastern border will be measured from Hauran, Damascus, Gilead, and the land of Israel by the Jordan River from the border to the eastern. And this will be the eastern border.
The south side will run southward from Tamar all the way to the waters of conflict in Kadesh, and along the river to the Mediterranean Sea. This will be the southern border.
On the west side the Mediterranean Sea will be the border until a man comes to the border of Hamath. This will be the western border.
And you must divide this land equally among the tribes of Israel.

After you divide this land by lot as an inheritance for you and the foreigners who travel and father children among you. You must treat these foreigners as if they were born among the children of Israel, and they will share an inheritance with you among the tribes of Israel."
And the Lord God says, "And in whatever tribe the foreigner travels, you will give him his inheritance there."

And the Lord God spoke to me, Ezekiel and said, "Now these are the names of the tribes. And Dan will have one portion from the north end to the coast along the road to Hethlon, Hamath, and Hazar-Enan, on the northern border of Damascus, to the coast of Hamath, because these are his borders from the east to the west.
Along the border of Dan, from the east side to the west side, will be a portion for Asher.
Along the border of Asher, from the east side to the west side, will be a portion for Naphtali.
Along the border of Naphtali, from the east side to the west side, will be a portion for Manasseh.
Along the border of Manasseh, from the east side to the west side, will be a portion for Ephraim.
Along the border of Ephraim, from the east side to the west side, will be a portion for Reuben.
Along the border of Reuben, from the east side to the west side, will be a portion for Judah."

And the Lord God spoke to me, Ezekiel and said, "Along the border of Judah, from the east side to the west side will be the offering you are to offer. It will measure 25,000 cubits wide, and it will be the same length as one of the other parts from the east side to the west side. And the sanctuary will be centered in its middle.
The donation you must offer to the Lord will be 25,000 cubits long and 10,000 cubits wide.

This holy donation will be for the priests. It will measure 25,000 cubits long on the north side, 10,000 cubits wide on the west side, 10,000 cubits wide on the east side, and 25,000 cubits long on the south side, and the Lord's sanctuary will be centered in its middle.
It will be for the sanctified priests from Zadok's descendants, who kept my charge and did not go astray like the Levites did when the Israelis went astray.
And this donation of land is offered to them as a thing most holy next to the border of the Levites.

Next to the border of the priests, the Levites will have a piece of land 25,000 cubits long and 10,000 cubits wide. The entire length of the land will be 25,000 cubits, and its total width will be 10,000 cubits.
They will not sell it, exchange it, nor transfer the best parts of the land, because it is holy to the Lord."

And the Lord God spoke to me, Ezekiel and said, "And the remaining 5,000 cubit width and 25,000 cubit length, will be a profane place for the city, housing, fields, and pastures. And the city will be in the middle of it.
And each side measures 4,500 cubits on the north, south, east, and west sides.
And each side of the city's fields and pastures measures 250 cubits toward the north, south, east, and west sides.
The remaining length of the donated holy portion of land will be 10,000 cubits on the east side and 10,000 cubits on the west side. And its abundant produce will feed those who serve the city.
And those who serve the city will come from all the tribes of Israel.
The entire holy donation you must offer will be 25,000 cubits by 25,000 cubits square, along with the city's property."
And the Lord God spoke to me, Ezekiel and said, "The rest of the land on each side of the holy portion including the city will be for the prince.
So the Levitical possession and the city possession, will be in the center of the land which belongs to the prince, between the borders of Judah and Benjamin.
As for the rest of the tribes, Benjamin will have a portion from the east side to the west side.
And Benjamin's land will border Simeon's portion, from the east side to the west side.
And Simeon's land will border Issachar's portion, from the east side to the west side.
And Issachar's land will border Zebulun's portion, from the east side to the west side.
And Zebulun's land will border Gad's portion, from the east side to the west side.
The southern border of Gad will stretch from Tamar all the way the waters of conflict in Kadesh, then on to the river toward the Mediterranean Sea."
And the Lord God spoke to me, Ezekiel and said, "This is the land which you will divide by lot to the tribes of Israel for their inheritance, and these are their portions.
And the city exits on the north side of the city will be 4,500 cubits long.

And the city gates will be named after the tribes of Israel. There will be three gates on the north side of the city and they will be named the gate of Reuben, the gate of Judah, and the gate of Levi.
And the three exit gates on the east side of the city will be 4,500 cubits long, and they will be named the gate of Joseph, the gate of Benjamin, and the gate of Dan.
And the three exit gates on the south side of the city will be 4,500 cubits long, and they will be named the gate of Simeon, the gate of Issachar, and the gate of Zebulun.
And the three exit gates on the west side of the city will be 4,500 cubits long, and they will be named the gate of Gad, the gate of Asher, and the gate of Naphtali.
The perimeter all around the city measured 18,000 cubits, and from that day forward the name of the city will be, 'The Lord is there.'"
In the third year of the reign of King Jehoiakim of Judah King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon came to Jerusalem and besieged it.

And the Lord put King Jehoiakim of Judah into Nebuchadnezzar's hand, along with some of the vessels from the house of God. He carried these vessels into the land of Shinar to the house of his own god, and he put them in his god's treasury.
Then the king told Ashpenaz the master of his eunuchs, to bring certain descendants of the Israelis king and princes.

Unblemished and attractive young men, skilled in all wisdom, knowledge, understanding, and science, and as such have the ability to stand in the king's palace to teach them the language and knowledge of the Chaldeans.
The king appointed them a daily provision from the king's food and wine. So after he nourished them for three years they would be allowed to stand before the king.
Now among those chosen to serve the king were descendants of Judah, Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah.
The master of the eunuchs renamed them, and he gave Daniel the name of Belteshazzar and he renamed Hananiah to Shadrach, Mishael to Meshach, and Azariah to Abednego.
But Daniel decided in his heart that he would not defile himself with the king's food or wine. So he asked the prince of eunuchs if he might not have to defile himself.
Now God gave Daniel favor, care, and compassion from the prince of eunuchs.

And the prince of eunuchs said to Daniel, "My Lord I fear the king, who has appointed your food and drink. Why should he see your faces looking worse than all the other young men like you? You will make me endanger my head to the king."
Then Daniel spoke to Melzar, whom the prince of the eunuchs had set over Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah.
And I Daniel said, "I beg you to test your servants for ten days, and let them give us vegetables to eat and water to drink.
Then compare our appearance to the appearance of those who eat from the king's food, then deal with your servants as you see fit."
So he consented to test them this way for ten days.
And after ten days they appeared healthier and fatter than all those who ate their portion from the king's food.
So Melzar stopped feeding the king's food and wine, and gave them beans and water instead.
And God gave these four young men skillful knowledge, learning, and wisdom. And Daniel was given the understanding of all visions and dreams.
Now after the three years that the king ordered that they should be taught, the prince of eunuchs brought them before King Nebuchadnezzar.
And the king spoke with them, and among all of them none of them were like Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah. So they stood before the king.
And in all matters of wisdom and understanding about which the king enquired of them, he found them to be ten times better than all the sorcerers and astrologers within his entire realm.
And Daniel continued to serve until the first year of King Cyrus.
And in the second year of King Nebuchadnezzar's reign, the king had dreams that troubled his spirit and interfered with his sleep.
So the king summoned his sorcerers, astrologers, magicians, and the Chaldeans to interpret the king's dreams. When they came and stood before the king.
Then the king said to them, "I had a dream, and my troubled spirit wants to know what this dream means."
Then the Chaldeans spoke to the king in Aramaic and said, "O king, may you live forever! Tell us your dream and we will interpret it."

King Nebuchadnezzar answered the Chaldeans and said, "I have forgotten the dream, if you cannot tell me about the dream and its interpretation, I will have you cut into pieces and your houses will be laid waste.
But if you tell me about the dream and its interpretation, you will receive gifts, rewards, and great honor from me. So tell me about the dream and its interpretation."
They answered the king again and said, "O king, please tell us your dream, and we will interpret it for you."
And the King answered them and said, "I know you are just stalling for time, because you know that I have forgotten the dream.

But if you cannot tell me about the dream, there is just one decree for you. Because I know you have prepared lying and corrupt words to speak before me, hoping to delay things until something changes. So tell me about the dream and I will know that you can truthfully interpret it for me."

Then the Chaldeans answered the king and said, "No man on the earth can tell the king his dream. Furthermore no king, lord, or ruler has ever asked such a thing from any magician, astrologer, or Chaldean.
What the king requires is something very rare, and there are no others who can tell the king about his dream, except the gods whose homes are not in the flesh."
This made the king furiously angry, and he commanded that all of Babylon's wise men were to be destroyed.
The decree went out to kill all the wise men, and they went to find Daniel and his friends to kill them.
Then Arioch the king's captain of the guard, went out to kill the wise men of Babylon, but Daniel answered him with wise counsel.
Daniel spoke to Arioch the king's captain and asked, "Why is the king being so hasty with his decree?" Then Arioch told Daniel about the king's dream.
So Daniel went and asked the king to give him more time, and told the king that he would interpret the his dream.
Then Daniel went home and told his companions Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah what was happening.
Daniel asked them to plead for mercy from the God of heaven about this secret dream, so that Daniel and his friends would not perish with the rest of Babylon's wise men.
Then the secret dream was revealed to Daniel in a night vision. And Daniel blessed the God of heaven.
Daniel blessed God and said, "Blessed be the name of God forever and ever, because wisdom and power belong to him.
He changes the times and seasons, he adds and removes kings. He gives wisdom to the wise, and knowledge to those who know and understand.
God reveals the deep and secret things, he knows what lies in the darkness and in the light that lives within him.
O God of my fathers, I thank you and praise you. You have given me wisdom and power, and now made known to me what we asked of you, because you have revealed the king's dream to us."

Daniel went to see Arioch, whom the king had ordered to destroy all of Babylon's wise men. And Daniel spoke to Arioch and said, "Do not destroy Babylon's wise men, take me to the king and I will interpret the king's dream."
Then Arioch hastily brought Daniel to the king and said, "I have found one of the captives of Judah, who can interpret the king's dream."
So the king spoke to Daniel whose name he had changed to Belteshazzar and asked, "Can you explain my dream and tell me what I have seen?"
Daniel answered the king and said, "No wise men, astrologers, sorcerers, or prophets can explain the secret dream which the king has demanded of them.

But there is a God in heaven who reveals secrets, and he has revealed to King Nebuchadnezzar what will happen in the latter days. And these are your dream and the visions which you saw in your head as you lay on your bed.
As for you, O king, the thoughts that came into your mind as you lay on your bed are about the future. And God who reveals secrets has made known to you what will happen.
But this secret was not revealed to me because I am wiser than any other living man, but for their sake the Lord will interpret the king's dream, so that you can understand your heart's thoughts.
O king, you saw the great, brilliant, and terrible solid form of this dazzling statue as it stood before you.
This statue's head was made of fine gold, his breast and arms were made of silver, and his stomach and thighs were made of brass.
His legs were made of iron, and his feet were made of part iron and part clay.
You watched as a stone was cut without human hands. It struck the statue on his iron and clay feet and broke them to pieces.

Then the iron, clay, brass, silver, and gold were all broken into pieces, and became like chaff on the summer threshing room floor. The wind carried them away, so that no trace of them could be found. But the stone that destroyed the statue became a great mountain and it filled the whole earth.
This is the king's dream, and now we will tell the king what all this means.
O king, you are a king of kings, because the God of heaven has given you a kingdom, power, strength, and glory.
God has placed in your hands every place that the sons of men, field beasts, or birds of the air live, and he has made you the ruler over all of them. You are this head of gold.
After you, another kingdom will rise that is inferior to you. Then a third kingdom of brass will rise to power and rule over all the earth.
Finally a fourth kingdom will rise that is as strong as iron, because iron breaks, subdues, and bruises all things. And like iron this kingdom will break all other kingdoms into pieces.

The fact that you saw the feet and toes were made of part potters clay and part iron, means this kingdom will be divided. But some of the strength of the iron will remain within it, because as you saw the iron was mixed with clay.
And like the toes of the feet were made partly of iron and partly of clay, so the kingdom will be partly strong and partly broken.
The fact that you saw the iron mixed with clay, shows that even though the seed of men will be mixed together, the races will not be loyal to one another, just as iron cannot be mixed with clay.

And in the days of these kings our heavenly God will set up a kingdom, which will never be destroyed and the kingdom will not be left to another people. But it will break all of these kingdoms into pieces and consume them, and it will stand forever.

Therefore just as you saw that the stone was cut from the mountain without human hands and it broke the iron, brass, clay, silver, and gold into pieces. So has our great God shown the king what is going to happen from now on. This dream is certain to be fulfilled and its interpretation can be trusted."
Then king Nebuchadnezzar fell facedown and worshipped Daniel, and ordered a donation of sweet incense to be offered to him.
The king spoke to Daniel and said, "This is the truth, the fact that you could reveal this secret dream to me, shows that your God is the God of gods, a Lord over kings and a revealer of secrets."
Then the king made Daniel a great man, and gave him many generous gifts. He made him ruler over the entire province of Babylon and chief governor over all of Babylon's wise men.
Then Daniel made a request of the king, and he assigned Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego to manage the affairs of the province of Babylon, but Daniel sat in the king's courtyard.
King Nebuchadnezzar made a golden image that was sixty cubits high and six cubits wide, and he set it up on the plains of Dura in the Babylonian province.

Then King Nebuchadnezzar summoned the princes, governors, captains, judges, treasurers, counselors, sheriffs, and all the rulers of the provinces. They were summoned to come to the dedication of the image which King Nebuchadnezzar had set up.

Then the princes, governors, captains, judges, treasurers, counselors, sheriffs, and all the rulers of the provinces gathered together to dedicate the image that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up. And they came and stood before the image that Nebuchadnezzar had set up.
Then a herald cried aloud, "O people of the nations and languages, you are commanded.

At the time that you hear the sound of the maraca, flute, harp, sliding trumpet, psaltery, dulcimer, and all kinds of music, you must fall down and worship the golden image that King Nebuchadnezzar has set up.
Whoever does not fall down and worship will be thrown into a blazing fiery furnace that same hour."

Therefore as soon as all the people heard the sound of the maraca, flute, harp, sliding trumpet, psaltery, and all kinds of music, all the people, nations, and languages fell down and worshipped the golden image that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up.
Then some of the Chaldeans came to accuse the Jews.
They spoke to King Nebuchadnezzar and said, "O king, may you live forever!
O king, you made a decree, that every man who hears the sound of the maraca, flute, harp, sliding trumpet, psaltery, dulcimer, and all kinds of music will fall down and worship the golden image.
And whoever does not fall down and worship would be thrown into a blazing fiery furnace.

There are certain Jews that you appointed to manage the affairs of the province of Babylon, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego who have ignored you. O king, they do not serve your gods nor do they worship the golden image which you have set up.
Then Nebuchadnezzar in his rage and fury commanded them to bring Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. Then they brought these men before the king.
Nebuchadnezzar spoke to them and said, O Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego is it true that do you not serve my gods nor worship the golden image which I have set up?

Now if you are ready, when you hear the sound of the maraca, flute, harp, sliding trumpet, psaltery, and dulcimer, and all kinds of music you must fall down and worship the image which I have made. But if you refuse to worship, you will immediately be thrown into the blazing fiery furnace. So then who is this god that will deliver you from my hands?
Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego answered the king and said, "O Nebuchadnezzar, we are not afraid to answer your question.
O king, if our God whom we serve exists, then he can deliver us from the blazing fiery furnace, and he will deliver us from your hand.
But O king if he does not deliver us, then let it be known to you, that we will not serve your gods, nor worship the golden image which you have set up!"

Then Nebuchadnezzar was full of fury, and the expression on his face changed toward Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. Then he spoke, and commanded the furnace to be heated seven times more than it was usually be heated.
And the king commanded the most powerful men in his army to bind Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego and throw them into the blazing fiery furnace.
Then these men were bound in their coats, pants, hats, and their other garments, and thrown into the blazing fiery furnace.
The king's commandment was so urgent, and the furnace was so hot that the fiery flames killed the men who took Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego up to the furnace.
So Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego fell into the blazing fiery furnace.
Then King Nebuchadnezzar was astonished, and rose up in haste and spoke to his counselors and said, "Did we not throw three men bound into the fire?" They answered the king and said, "Yes O king."
The king responded and said, "I see four men walking around in the middle of the fire, and they are not hurt, and the fourth one looks like the Son of God!"

Then Nebuchadnezzar came close to the mouth of the blazing fiery furnace and said, "Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego you are servants of the most high God, come out and come here." Then Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego came out the fire.

The princes, governors, captains, and the king's counselors gathered together and looked these men over, and they saw that the fire had no power over their bodies. The hair on their head was not singed, their coats were not burned, nor did they have the smell of fire on them.

Then Nebuchadnezzar spoke and said, "Blessed be the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego who has sent his angel to save his servants who trusted in him. They have ignored the king's word and risked their bodies by refusing to serve or worship any god but their own true God.

Therefore I decree that the people of all nations or languages, who speak inappropriately against the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego will be cut into pieces, and their houses will be laid waste. Because there is no other God that can do this sort of thing.
Then the king promoted Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego in the province of Babylon.
King Nebuchadnezzar sends greetings of peace to all people, nations, and languages across the earth.
I thought it would be good to share the signs and wonders the Most High God has performed for me.
His signs are incredible, and his wonders are powerful! His kingdom will last forever, and his rule will continue through every generation.
I, Nebuchadnezzar, was relaxing at my home and prospering in my palace.
I had a dream that frightened me, and the thoughts and visions I had while lying in my bed disturbed me.
So I issued a decree to summon all the wise men of Babylon to interpret the dream for me.
Then all the sorcerers, astrologers, prophets, and Chaldeans came to me, and I told them about the dream, but no one could interpret it.
Then Daniel finally came to me and I shared my dream with him. I had Daniel's name changed to Belteshazzar, after my god because he is filled with the spirit of the holy gods.
So I said, "O Belteshazzar, master of the sorcerers, I know the spirit of the holy gods is in you and that no secret escapes you, so tell me how I should interpret my dream.
These are the visions I saw while lying in bed, I saw a tree standing in the center of the earth, and it was very tall.
The tree grew strong and tall, and it reached high into the sky and it was visible from every part of the earth.
