Its leaves were beautiful, and it bore abundant fruit, providing food for everyone. Animals rested beneath it, and birds nested in its branches. Every creature was nourished by it.
In my vision, I saw a watcher and a holy one descending from heaven.
The holy one shouted, 'Cut down the tree! Trim its branches, strip its leaves, and scatter its fruit. Let the animals flee from beneath it and the birds flee from its branches.
But leave the stump and roots in the ground, bind it with iron and bronze, and surround it with grass. Let it be drenched with dew from heaven and share the grassy field with the animals.
Let his heart be changed from human to animal, and let him live this way for seven time years.

This message is a decree from the watchers, declared by the holy ones, so that the living may know that the Most High rules over human kingdoms. He gives them to whoever he chooses, even the most immoral and wicked men.'
Now Belteshazzar, this is the dream that I King Nebuchadnezzar had, so explain it to me. None of my wise men can interpret it, but you can, because the spirit of the holy gods is in you."

Then Daniel, also called Belteshazzar, was astonished for a while, and his thoughts troubled him. The king said, "Do not let the dream or its meaning upset you." And Belteshazzar replied, "My lord, this dream applies to your enemies, and it was meant for those who oppose you.
The tree you saw, which grew strong and tall, reached the sky and it was visible across the whole earth.
With its beautiful leaves and abundant fruit, it provided food for all, it sheltered animals beneath it, and hosted birds in its branches.
O king, that tree represents you. You have grown powerful, and your greatness reaches the heavens. Your rule extends across the earth.

You saw a watcher, a holy one descend from heaven and say, 'Cut down the tree and destroy it, but leave the stump and roots in the ground, and bind it with iron and bronze in the grass. Let it be soaked with dew and live among the animals until seven years pass.'
O king, this is the interpretation, it is the decree of the Most High concerning you.

You will be driven away from people and live with wild animals. You will eat grass like an ox and be drenched with dew. This will last for seven time years until you recognize that the Most High rules over human kingdoms and gives them to whomever He chooses.
The command to leave the stump and roots means your kingdom will be restored once you acknowledge that heaven rules.
So, O king, please accept my advice, turn away from your sins, be righteous, and show mercy to the poor. Perhaps then your prosperity will continue."
And every bit of this happened to King Nebuchadnezzar.
Twelve months later, he was walking on the roof of the royal palace in Babylon.
The king said, Is this not the great Babylon that I built as my royal residence, by my mighty power and for my glorious majesty?
And while he was still speaking, a voice came from heaven and said, "King Nebuchadnezzar, this message is for you, your kingdom is taken from you.

You will be driven away from people and live with wild animals. You will eat grass like an ox, and seven time years will pass until you understand that the Most High rules over human kingdoms and gives them to whomever he chooses."

Immediately, the prophecy was fulfilled. Nebuchadnezzar was driven away from people, he ate grass like an ox, and was soaked with dew. His hair grew like eagle feathers, and his nails looked like bird's claws.

At the end of the allotted time, I, Nebuchadnezzar, looked up to heaven, and my sanity returned. I praised the Most High and honored the Most High One who lives forever. His kingdom is eternal, and his rule lasts through all generations.
All people on earth are insignificant compared to him. He does whatever he pleases in heaven and on earth. No one can stop him or question his actions.
At that moment, my sanity returned, and my honor and splendor were restored. My advisors and nobles found me, and I was reinstated as king. Even greater majesty was added to me.
Now I, Nebuchadnezzar, praise, exalt, and honor the King of Heaven. All his works are true, and his ways are just. He can humble those who walk in pride.
King Belshazzar held a grand feast for a thousand of his nobles and drank wine in their presence.

While enjoying the wine, Belshazzar ordered that the gold and silver vessels taken from the temple in Jerusalem by his father Nebuchadnezzar be brought to him so that he, his nobles, wives, and concubines could drink from them.
So they brought the gold vessels taken from God's temple in Jerusalem, and the king, his nobles, wives, and concubines drank from them.
They drank wine and praised the gods made of gold, silver, bronze, iron, wood, and stone.
At that moment, a hand appeared and wrote with its finger on the plaster wall near the lampstand in the king's palace. And the king saw the hand as it was writing.
The king's facial expression changed, and his thoughts troubled him so much that his legs gave way, and his knees knocked together.

The king shouted for the astrologers, Chaldeans, and diviners to be brought in. The king spoke to the wise men of Babylon and said, "Whoever can read what is written here and explain it to me will be clothed in scarlet, have a gold chain placed around his neck, and be made third in command of the kingdom."
Then all the king's wise men came in, but none of them could read the writing or explain its meaning to the king.
King Belshazzar became even more troubled, his face grew pale, and his nobles were stunned.

The queen heard the king and the nobles talking, so she entered the banquet hall and said, "O king, may you live forever! Do not let your thoughts trouble you, and do not let the expression on your face show fear.

There is a man in your kingdom who has the spirit of the holy gods. In your father's time, it was known that his insight, understanding, and wisdom was like that of the gods. King Nebuchadnezzar, your father, appointed him master of the sorcerers, astrologers, Chaldeans, and the diviners.

Because Daniel, whom the king named Belteshazzar, has an exceptional spirit of knowledge and understanding. He can interpret dreams, solve difficult problems, and dissolve doubts. So you should send for Daniel, and he will interpret the writing."
Then Daniel was brought before the king, and the king spoke to him and said, "Are you Daniel, one of the exiles from Judah whom my father brought here from Jerusalem?
I have heard that the spirit of the gods is in you, and that light, understanding, and extraordinary wisdom is found within you.
The wise men and astrologers were brought before me to read this message and explain it, but they could not explain it.

But I have heard that you can interpret things and dissolve doubts. If you can read what is written here and explain it, you will be clothed in scarlet, have a gold chain placed around your neck, and you will be made third in command of the kingdom."
Daniel replied back to him and said,, "You can keep your gifts or give them to someone else, but I will still read the writing and explain it to the king.
O king, the Most High God gave your father Nebuchadnezzar a kingdom, greatness, glory, and honor.
Because of the majesty he gave him, people of all nations and languages feared him. He killed or spared whomever he wished, and he promoted or humbled whomever he chose.
But when his heart became proud and his mind was hardened with pride, he was removed from his royal throne and stripped of his glory.

He was driven away from the sons of men, his heart became like that of an animal, and he lived with wild donkeys. They fed him with grass like an ox, and his body was drenched with dew from heaven until he knew that the Most High God rules over the kingdoms of men, and appoints rulers as he pleases.
But you, Belshazzar, his son, have not humbled your heart, even though you knew all this.

Instead, you have exalted yourself against the Lord of heaven. You brought the sacred vessels from his temple, and you, your nobles, wives, and concubines drank wine from them. You praised the gods of silver, gold, bronze, iron, wood, and stone, which do not see, hear, or understand. And you did not glorify the God who gave you life and controls your destiny.
Therefore, he sent the hand that wrote this message.
This is what was written MENE, MENE, TEKEL, UPHARSIN.
And this is what it means, MENE - God has numbered your kingdom and brought it to an end.
TEKEL - You have been weighed on the scales and found lacking.
UPHARSIN - Your kingdom is divided and given to the Medes and Persians."
Then Belshazzar ordered Daniel to be dressed in scarlet and given a gold chain, then he declared him to be third in command of the kingdom.
That very night, Belshazzar, king of the Chaldeans, was killed.
And Darius the Mede took control of the kingdom at the age of sixty-two.
It pleased King Darius to appoint 120 princes to rule over the entire kingdom.
He also appointed three presidents over these princes including Daniel who was first. The princes were to report to them, so that the king would suffer no damage.
Daniel possessed an excellent spirit and he was the most respected of the presidents and princes, so the king decided to place him over the entire realm.

Then the presidents and princes tried to find something to use against Daniel concerning the kingdom. But they could not find anything to use against him, because he was faithful and there was no error or corruption found in him.
Then these men said, "We will never find anything to use against Daniel, unless we find something in the law of his God we can use against him."
So the presidents and princes went together to speak to the king and said to him, "King Darius, may you live forever!

And all the presidents, governors, princes, counselors, and captains of the kingdom have decided together to establish a royal decree for the king to sign into law. And this law will state that anyone who petitions or asks anything of a god or a man for the next thirty days except for the you, O king, would be thrown into the lions den.
Now O king, establish the law and sign the decree, so that it cannot be changed, as a law of the Medes and the Persians, which cannot be altered."
So King Darius signed the written decree into law.

When Daniel learned that the decree had been signed, he went into his house and opened the windows in his chamber facing Jerusalem, and he knelt down and prayed three times a day. And he gave thanks his God, just as he had always done.
Then the men got together and went and found Daniel praying and pleading with his God.

Then they immediately went to see the king about his decree and they asked, "O king, did you sign a decree, that states that if anyone prays to a god or another man, except for you within the next thirty days, they will be thrown into the lions den?" The King answered and said, "Yes, it is recorded according to the law of the Medes and Persians, and it cannot be altered."
Then they replied to the king and said, "Daniel, one of the captives from Judah, does not respect you nor the decree you have signed O king. He still makes his petition three times a day."
When the king heard this, he was extremely displeased with himself, and he set his heart on delivering Daniel, and he labored until sundown trying to figure out how to deliver him.
Then the men approached the king again and said, "O king, remember that any law of the Medes and Persians established by the king cannot be changed."
Then the king gave the order and they brought Daniel and threw him into the lions den. Now the king spoke to Daniel and said, "Your God whom you continuously serve will deliver you."
A stone was brought and placed over the mouth of the den, and the king sealed it with his own signet ring and the signet rings of his lords, so that nothing could be changed about Daniel's situation.
Then the king went to his palace and spent the night fasting. No musical instruments were brought before him, and he could not sleep all night.
The king rose very early the next morning, and went hastily to the lions den.

When the king arrived at the den, he cried out with a very sad voice and spoke to Daniel and said, "O Daniel, servant of the living God whom you continuously serve, was your God able to deliver you from the lions?"
Then Daniel said to the king, "O king, may you live forever!
My God has sent his angel, and has shut the lions' mouths, that they have not hurt me, because I have been found innocent before him and also before you, and I have done no harm to you, O king."
Then the king was extremely happy for him, and commanded them to remove Daniel from the lions den. So Daniel was lifted up out of the den, and he had no wounds, because he believed in his God.

Then the king commanded them to bring the men to him who had accused Daniel. So they were brought and thrown into the lions den along with their children and their wives. And before they reached the bottom of the lions den, the lions broke their bones and tore them to pieces
Then King Darius wrote to all the people, nations, and languages that live on the earth and said, "May abundant peace be with you.

I decree, that in every domain of my kingdom that men must tremble and fear the God of Daniel, for he is the living God who stands fast forever, his kingdom will never be destroyed, and his authority will never end.
He delivers and rescues, he works signs and wonders in heaven and on earth, and he has delivered Daniel from the power of the lions.
So Daniel prospered during the reigns of both King Darius and King Cyrus the Persian.
In the first year of the reign of King Belshazzar of Babylon, Daniel had a dream and visions in his head as he lay on his bed. Then he wrote down the dream, and this is a sumMary of his statement.
Daniel spoke and said, "In my night vision, I saw the four winds of heaven struggling against the Mediterranean Sea.
Then I saw four great beasts come up out of the sea, and each one was different than the others.
The first one looked like a lion with eagle's wings, and its wings were torn off as it lifted up from the earth, and it was made to stand on its feet like a man, and it was given a man's heart.
I saw a second beast that looked like a bear. It raised itself up on one side and it had three ribs between the teeth in its mouth. Then they said to it, "Get up and devour much flesh!"
Then I saw another beast that looked like a leopard with four bird wings on its back, and the beast also had four heads, and it was given dominion and authority.

After this in my night visions I saw a fourth beast that was dreadful, terrible, and extremely strong. It had great iron teeth that it used to devour, break into pieces, and then stomp whatever was left with its feet. It was different from all the other beasts and it had ten horns.
As I thought about the horns, another little horn came up among them and three of the first horns were torn out by the roots. This horn had eyes like a man's eyes and a mouth that spoke great things.

I watched until the thrones were thrown down, and the Ancient of Days stook his seat. His garments were as white as snow, and the hair on his head was like pure wool. His throne was like a fiery flame, and his wheels were like a burning fire.
A fiery river flowed out from before him. Millions ministered to him, and 100,000,000 stood before him. The judgment was established and the books were opened."

And Daniel spoke and said, "Then I continued to watch because of the great words which the horn was speaking. I watched until the beast was killed, his body was destroyed and thrown into the burning flame.
As for the rest of the beasts, they had their authority taken away, but their lives were prolonged for a season and a time.
As my night visions continued, I saw one who looked like the Son of Man coming with the clouds of heaven. He came toward the Ancient of Days, and they brought him into his presence.

The Son of Man was given authority, glory, and a kingdom so that the people of all nations and languages could serve him. His authority is an everlasting authority that will not pass away, and his kingdom is a kingdom which will never be destroyed.
I Daniel was grieved in my spirit and body, and the visions in my head troubled me.
So I approached one of those who stood there, and I asked him the truth about all of this. So he told me all about all of these things.
And the one I approached said, 'These four great beasts are four kings, who will rise up from the earth.
But the saints of the Most High will take possession of the kingdom for forever and ever.'"

And Daniel spoke and said, "Then I wanted to know the truth about the fourth beast, which was different from all the others. It was extremely dreadful, with iron teeth and brass nails which devoured, broke into pieces, and stomped with its feet everything that was left.

So I asked about the ten horns on its head and the other horn that came up which caused three other horns to fall. The horn that had eyes and a mouth that spoke very great things, and looked more stout than his friends.
I saw this same horn making war against the saints and it prevailed against them.
Until the Ancient of Days arrived and judged in favor of the saints of the Most High, and the time came for the saints to take possession of the kingdom.

And this is what the one I approached said, 'The fourth beast will be the fourth kingdom on earth, which will be different from all the other kingdoms, and it will devour the whole earth, trample it down, and break it into pieces.
And the ten horns are ten kings that will rise from this kingdom. Then another king will rise after them, and he will be different from the first, and he will subdue three kings.

He will speak great words against the Most High and weary the saints of the Most High. He will try to change the times and laws, and the saints will be given into his hand until a time, times, and half a time.
But the judge will be seated, and the king's authority will be taken away, consumed, and destroyed until the end.

Then the kingdom, authority, and the great kingdoms under the entire heavens will be given to the people of the saints of the Most High. And the kingdom of the Most High will be an everlasting kingdom, and all authorities will serve and obey him.'
This is the end of the matter. As for me Daniel, my thoughts troubled me and my demeanor changed, but I kept these things in my heart."
In the third year of the reign of King Belshazzar a second vision appeared to Daniel after his first vision.
And I Daniel said, "In the vision I saw that I was in the Shushan palace, which is in the province of Elam. And I also saw that I was standing beside the Ulai River in the vision.
Then I looked up and saw a ram with two horns standing before the river. Its two horns were long, but one was longer than the other, and the longer one grew last.
I saw the ram pushing toward the west, north, and south. No beasts could stand before him, nor could any be delivered from his grip. He did whatever he wanted and became great.
As I was thinking about all this, I saw a male goat coming from the western face of the whole earth without touching the ground. And the goat had a significant horn between his eyes.
He came to the ram with two horns I had seen standing beside the river, and ran to him with his furious power.

He was full of resentment as I saw him approach the other ram. He defeated the ram and broke his two horns, and the broken ram was powerless to stand before him. But the goat threw him down to the ground and stomped him, and there was no one who could deliver the ram from his hand."

And I Daniel said, "Therefore the male goat grew very great, and when he was at his strongest, the great horn was broken, and four notable horns grew in its place, pointing toward the four winds of heaven.
From one of these horns a little horn emerged and grew exceedingly great, toward the south and east, and toward the pleasant land.
And goat grew great all the way to the hosts of heaven, and it threw down some of the hosts and stars of heaven to the ground, and stomped on them.
So the goat magnified himself, even to the prince of the host, and he removed God's daily sacrifice, and the place of God's sanctuary was thrown down.
Because of transgression an army and the daily sacrifice were given to the goat, and it threw the truth to the ground, and whatever it did prospered."

And I Daniel said, "Then I heard a saint speaking, and another saint said to the saint who was speaking, 'How long will it be before the vision is fulfilled about the daily sacrifice, the transgression of devastation, the surrender of the sanctuary, and the host is trampled under foot?
And he said to me, 'It will be 2,300 days until the sanctuary is cleansed.'
After I Daniel, had seen the vision and tried to understand what it meant, one stood before me that looked like a man.
And I heard a man's voice calling from between the banks of the Ulai River which said, 'Gabriel, make this man understand the vision.'
So he came near where I stood, but I was afraid and I fell facedown as he said to me, 'O Son of Man, understand the vision because it is about the time of the end.'"
And I Daniel said, "Now as Gabriel was speaking to me, I was in a deep sleep facedown on the ground. Then he touched me, and helped me stand upright.
And Gabriel said, 'Behold I will help you understand what will happen in the time of the last end of indignation, because at the appointed time the end will come.
The ram which you saw with two horns are the kings of Media and Persia.
And the rough goat is the king of Greece, and the great horn between his eyes is the first king.
Now the broken horn which was replaced by the four horns stands for four kingdoms will rise up from that nation, but not with his power.
In the latter days of their kingdom, when the transgressors have come into full power, a king with a fierce demeanor, who understands dark sentences will stand up.
His power will be mighty, but it will not be his own power. He will cause terrible destruction and prosper in whatever he practices. He will destroy the mighty and the holy people.

Through his policies he will also cause deceit to prosper in his hand, and he will magnify himself in his own heart. And he will destroy many in peaceful times, he will also stand up against the Prince of princes. And he will be broken, but not by human hands.
And the vision of the evenings and mornings which was told is true. Therefore you must seal up the vision, because it is about the future.'
Then I Daniel fainted, and was sick for days. Afterward I got up, and attended to the king's business, and I was astonished by the vision, but I did not understand it."
In the first year of the reign of King Darius the Mede, son of Ahasuerus, king over the realm of the Chaldeans.

In the first year of the reign of King Darius, I Daniel understood from what was written in the books, that the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah the prophet, who said that the devastation of Jerusalem would last for seventy years.
So I turned my attention to the Lord God, to seek him with prayer, pleas, fasting, sackcloth, and ashes.
Then I Daniel, prayed to my Lord God and confessed and said, "O Lord, the great and dreadful God, who keeps the covenant of mercy for those who love him, and to those who keep his commandments.
We have sinned and committed immorality, we have done wicked things and rebelled, we have even departed from your commandments and judgments.
We did not listen to your servants the prophets, who spoke in your name to our kings, our princes, our fathers, and all of the people of the land.

O Lord, you are righteousness, but today we are all confused including the men of Judah, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and all of the people of Israel who are near and far away throughout all the countries where you have driven them, because we have trespassed against you.
O Lord, all of us deserve to be confused including our kings, princes, and fathers because we have sinned against you.
Mercy and forgiveness belongs to our Lord God, even though we have rebelled against him.
Nor have we obeyed the voice of our Lord God, to walk in his laws, which he sent to us through his servants the prophets.

Yes, all of Israel has transgressed against your law and left, so that they would not have to obey your voice. So the promised curse that is written in the Law of Moses the servant of God has been poured out on us, because we have sinned against you.

You have confirmed your words, which you have spoken against us and the judges who judged us, by bringing a great evil upon us, because under the entire heaven nothing has ever been done the way it has been done to Jerusalem.

Just like it is written in the Law of Moses, all of this evil has come upon us, but we still have not prayed to our Lord God, so that we might find the strength to turn from our wickedness and understand your truth.
Therefore the Lord kept watch over the evil and brought it upon us, because our Lord God is righteous in everything he does, and we did not obey his voice."

Furthermore I Daniel, prayed to my Lord God and confessed and said, "O Lord our God, now you have brought your people out of the land of Egypt with a mighty hand. You have made you name renowned for your sake to this very day, but we have sinned and done wicked things.

O Lord, in accordance with all your righteousness, I beg you to let your anger and fury be turned away from your city Jerusalem, your Holy mountain, because of our sins, and the wickedness of our fathers, Jerusalem and your people have become a disappointment to everyone around us.
Therefore O our God, hear the prayers and pleas of your servant, and for the Lord's sake shine your face on your desolated sanctuary.

O my God, listen and hear, then open your eyes and see the devastation of our city named after you. Because we do not present our pleas before you because of our righteousness, but only because we seek your great mercies.
O Lord, hear! O Lord, forgive! O Lord, listen and do something for your own sake. O my God, do not delay because your city and your people are named for you."
While I Daniel was speaking, praying, and confessing my sin and the sin of my people of Israel, and I presented my plea before my Lord God for his holy mountain.
As I was still speaking and praying, Gabriel, the man I had seen in the earlier vision, flew swiftly to me and touched me at about the same time as the evening sacrifice.
He spoke to me to inform and said, "O Daniel, I have now come to give you expertise and understanding.
When you began your pleas the commandment went out for me to come and show you the truth, because you are greatly loved. So consider and understand the vision's meaning.

It has been decided that there will be seventy weeks for your people and your holy city, to put an end to your transgressions and sins. Then you must make atonement for your immorality, to bring in everlasting righteousness, to seal up the vision and prophecy, and to anoint the Most Holy Place.

Therefore know and understand this, from the time that the commandment went out to restore and rebuild Jerusalem there will be seven weeks and sixty-two weeks until the Messiah the Prince. But it will be rebuilt with streets and walls, even in times of trouble.

After sixty-two weeks the Messiah will be cut off, but not for his sins. Then the people of the prince who is to come will destroy the city and the sanctuary. Then it has been decided that the end will come like a flood, and there will be war and devastation until the end.

And he will confirm a covenant with many for one week, but in the middle of the week he will put an end to sacrifice and donations. And for spreading their abominations, he will desolate the temple until the determined consumption is poured out on the desolation.

In the third year of the reign of King Cyrus of Persia a message was revealed to Daniel, whose name had been changed to Belteshazzar. The message was true, but the appointed time was a long time away. And he understood the message because of the vision he had.
In those days I, Daniel had been mourning for three full weeks.
I ate no good bread, and I put no meat or wine in my mouth, and I did not anoint myself with oil until the end of the three whole weeks.
On the twenty-fourth day of the first month, I was standing next to the great Hiddekel River.
Then I looked up and saw a man clothed in linen, whose waist was covered with fine gold from Uphaz.

His body was like beryl, his face looked like lightning, his eyes looked like fiery lamps, his arms and feet looked like they were the color of polished brass, and his voice sounded like the voice of an army.
And I Daniel was the only one who saw the vision, because the men there with me could not see it, but a great quaking fell on them, and they fled to hide themselves.
Therefore I was left alone when I saw this great vision. No strength remained in me because my looks corrupted me, and I had no strength.
But I heard his voice and his words, and as I heard his words, I fell into a deep sleep facedown on the ground.
Then a hand touched me, and set me up on my hands and knees.

And the man said to me, "O Daniel, you are a greatly loved man, understand what I say to you and stand upright, for I have now been sent to you." After he spoke these word to me, I stood up trembling.

Then the man said to me, "Daniel, fear not because from the first day that you decided to understand in your heart, and chasten yourself before your God, your words were heard, and I have come because of your words.
But the prince of the kingdom of Persia opposed me for twenty-one days. But Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help me, and I remained there with the kings of Persia.
Now I have come to make you understand what will happen to your people in the latter days, because the vision is for the future."
After he had spoken to me, I turned my face to the ground, and I was speechless.

And, behold the one who resembled one of the sons of men touched my lips, then I opened my mouth and spoke. And I said to the one who stood before me, "O my Lord, because of the vision, my sorrows have turned against me, and I have no strength.
How can I, the servant my Lord talk with you my Lord? For I have no strength left in me, and I have no breath left."
And again the one who looked like a man touched me and he strengthened me.
And the man said to me, "O greatly beloved man, fear not, peace be unto you and be strong." As he spoke to me, I was strengthened and I said, "Speak my Lord because you have strengthened me."
Then the man said, "Do you know why I have come to you? I must return to fight against the prince of Persia, but after I have left, the prince of Greece will come.
But first I will show you what is written in the Scriptures of Truth. For there is no one who can stand with me against these things, except for Michael your prince."
And the man said, "In the first year of King Darius the Mede, I stood up to confirm and strengthen him.

And now I will show you the truth. Behold, there will be three kings in Persia yet to rise up, and then a fourth who will be far richer than all the others. Through the strength of his wealth he will stir up everyone against the kingdom of Greece.
And a mighty king will rise up, one who will rule with great authority, and he will do whatever he wants.

When he stands up, his kingdom will be broken up, divided, and scattered to four winds of heaven. It will not be given to his descendants, nor will his authority with which he ruled, because his kingdom will be uprooted, and given to others besides them.
The king of the south will be strong, but one of his princes will be stronger than him, and he will rule his kingdom with great authority.

After a few years they will join together, because the daughter of the king of the south will go to the king of the north to forge an alliance. But she will not retain her power nor will he rise up in strength. But she will be given up along with those who brought her, her fathered, and the one who strengthened her in those times."
And the man said, "But from her roots one will come who stands up in his place and marches his army, and enters the fortress of the king of the north. And he will fight against them and prevail.
He will carry their gods as captives into Egypt, along with their princes, and their precious gold and silver bowls. And he will reign for more years than the king of the north.
So the king of the south will become part of his kingdom, and then he will return to his own land.
But his sons will be stirred up and they will assemble a vast army. Then they will march through like a flood and he will return, but he will remain stirred up all the way back to his fortress.
But the king of the south will become very resentful, and he will march out and fight with the king of the north, who will raise a great army, but his army will be handed over to his enemy."
And the man said, "After the army has been carried away, his heart will be lifted up, and he will throw down tens of thousands, but he will not be strengthened.
For the king of the north will return, and he will raise an army greater than the first one, and after a certain number of years he will attack with a great army funded by much wealth.
In those times many will rise up against the king of the south, and your people's thieves will glorify themselves to fulfill the vision, but they will fall.

So the king of the north will come, and build a siege mountain, and capture the most fortified cities. The armed defenders of the south will not be able to withstand the attack, nor will his elite troops have the strength to withstand the onslaught.
But whoever attacks him will be able to do whatever he wants, and no one will be able to stand before him. And he will stand in the glorious land, which will be consumed in his hand.

He will march with the strength of his entire kingdom along with his honest ones. And he will give the king of the south one of his daughters in marriage and corrupt her, but she will not stand on her father's side or help him."

And the man said, "After this he will turn his interest to the islands and capture many of them. But a prince will attack on his own behalf and make the king of the north's criticism cease to exist, and the prince will turn his own criticism against him.
Then the king of the north will turn back the fortress of his own land, but he will stumble and fall, never to be found again.
Then one will rise up in his place who will raise taxes for the glory of the kingdom, but within a few days he will be destroyed, but not from anger nor in battle.
And a vile person will rise up in his place, to whom they will not give the honor of the kingdom, but he will come offering peace and take the kingdom with flattery.
Then a flood of troops will be broken and disappear right in front of him, including the prince of the covenant.
After a treaty is made with him he will work deceitfully, because he will rise to power and become strong with a small number of people.

He will enter peacefully in the richest places of the province, and he will do things that his fathers or forefathers have never done. He will scatter prey, plunder, and riches among his people and he will devise schemes and devices against the strongholds, but only for a short time.

He will stir up his power and courage against the king of the south with a great army. Then the king of the south will stir up a very great and mighty army prepared for battle. But he will not withstand the schemes and devices they devised against him.
Yes, those who feed from his provisions and meat will destroy him, and his army will be overthrown and many will be killed."
And the man said, "Both of these kings will have hearts of mischief, and they will speak lies at the same table, but they will not prosper because the end will come at the appointed time.
Then he will return to his own land with great riches, and his heart will be against the holy covenant, so he will return and exploit the people in his own land.
At the time appointed he will return and march toward the south, but it will not be like the it was the first time.
For the ships of Cyprus will come against him and he will be grieved. Then he will resent the holy covenant and return, and he will focus on those who have forsaken the holy covenant.
His armed troops will rise up on his behalf, and they will pollute the sanctuary of strength. They will end the daily sacrifice and set up the abomination of desolation.
He will corrupt those who do wicked things against the covenant with flattery, but those who know their God will be strong and exploit his weaknesses.
And those who understand among the people will instruct many, but for many days they will fall by the sword or flame. They will also be captured and plundered.
When they fall, they will be given a little help, but many will cling loyally to the flatterers.
Some of those who understand will fall, to be tried and purged to make them white until the time of the end, because it is not yet the appointed time."

And the man said, "And the king will do everything in his power to glorify himself and magnify himself above every god. He will speak marvelous things against the God of gods, and he will prosper until the indignation is completed, because what has been decided will be done.
He will have no regard for the God of his fathers, nor the one desired by women, nor any other God, because he will magnify himself above them all.
But in their place he will honor the god of war, and he will honor a god his fathers did not know with gold, silver, precious stones, and pleasant things.

He will attack the strongest strongholds with a strange god, and he will glorify those who acknowledge him, and he will make them rulers over many, and they will divide up the land for their own personal gain.

And at the end time the king of the south will push against him, and the king of the north will attack him like a whirlwind with chariots, horsemen, and many ships. Then he will invade many countries and overthrow them.
He will also invade the glorious land and many countries will be overthrown, but some will escape from his hand including Edom, Moab, and the Ammonite chiefs.
He will stretch out his hand against many countries, and the land of Egypt will not escape.
But he will have power over the treasuries of gold and silver, and all the precious things of Egypt. The Libyans and Ethiopians will be at his steps.
But reports from the east and the north will disturb him, so much so that he will rush out with great fury to completely destroy many.
And he will plant the tabernacles of his palace on the glorious holy mountain between the oceans, but he will come to his end and no one will help him."

And the man said, "At that time Michael, the great prince who watches over your people will stand up, and a time of trouble will come the likes of which have never been seen since the beginnings of nations to this very day. But at that time your people and everyone whose name is found written in the book will be delivered.
Many of those who sleep in the earth's dust will awaken, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.
The wise will shine like the brilliant stars, and those who lead many to righteousness will shine like the stars forever and ever.
But you Daniel, close and seal up the words in this book until the time of the end. Many will run back and forth, and knowledge will be increased.
Then I Daniel looked up, and I saw two others standing there, one on this side of the river bank, and one on the other side of the river bank.
One of them spoke to the man clothed in linen, who was above the river waters and said, "How long will it be until the end of these wonders?"

Then I heard the man clothed in linen, who was above the river waters as he spoke and held up his right hand and left hand toward heaven. He swore by the one who lives forever and he said, "It will be for a time, times, and half a time. When he has finally managed to scatter the power of the holy people, then all these things will be accomplished."
I heard all this, but I did not understand and I asked, "O my Lord, what will be the outcome of all these things?"
And the Lord said, "Go your way Daniel, because the words are closed and sealed until the time of the end.
Many will be purified, made white, and tested, but the wicked will act wickedly. None of the wicked will understand, but the wise will understand.
And from the time that the daily sacrifice is removed, and the abomination of desolation is set up, there will be 1,290 days.
Blessed is he who waits until the end of the 1,335 days.
But you go your way Daniel until the end, because you will rest, and stand in your lot at the end of the days."
This is the word of the Lord that came to Hosea son of Beeri in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, and Jeroboam son of Joash, king of Israel.
When the Lord's word first came to Hosea the Lord said, "Go and take a whore for a wife and have children with a whore, because this land has committed great prostitution by leaving the Lord."
So Hosea married Gomer the daughter of Diblaim, who conceived and gave birth to a son.
And the Lord said to Hosea, "Name him Jezreel, because in a little while I will avenge the blood of Jezreel upon the house of Jehu, and I will make the kingdom of the House of Israel cease to exist.
On that day I will break the bow of Israel in the Valley of Jezreel."

Then Gomer conceived again and gave birth to a daughter, and God said to Hosea, "Name her Loruhamah (Not Loved), because I will no longer have mercy on the House of Israel, but I will completely remove them.
However I will have mercy on the house of Judah, and I will save them, but not by bow, sword, battle, horses, nor horsemen. But they will be saved by their Lord God!"
After she weaned Loruhamah, she conceived again and gave birth to a son.
Then God said, "Name him Loammi (Not my people), because you are not my people, and I will not be your God.

But the number of Israel's children will be like the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor counted. Then in the place where it was said to them, 'You are not my people!' It will be said to them, 'You are the sons of the living God.'
Then the children of Judah and Israel will be gathered together, and appoint one leader for themselves, and they will come up out of the land, because it will be a great day for Jezreel."
And the Lord spoke to Hosea and said, "Tell your brothers, 'Ammi (My people)' and tell your sisters, 'Ruhamah. (My loved One)'

Plead with your mother Israel because she is not my wife, nor am I her husband. Therefore tell her to remove her whores and put them out of her sight, and remove her adulteries from between her breasts.
Or else I will strip her naked and reveal her as she was on the day that she was born. And I will make her like the wilderness in a dry land, and kill her with thirst.
And I will have no mercy on her children, because they are the children of whores.
Because their mother who conceived them has shamefully played the whore said, 'I will chase after my lovers, who give me my bread, water, wool, flax, oil, and drink.'"
And the Lord spoke to Hosea and said, "So, I will grow a hedge with thorns and build a wall along Israel's path, so she cannot find her way.

And she will follow after her lovers but never overtake them. She will look for them but never find them. Then she will say, 'I will return to my first husband, because it was better with me then than it is now.'
For she did not know that I gave her all her wheat, wine, and oil and I multiplied her silver and gold, which they prepared for Baal.
Therefore I will return and take away my wheat at harvest time, and my wine in its season. I will recover my wool and flax that I gave her to cover her nakedness."
And the Lord spoke to Hosea and said, "And now I will expose her obscenity in front of her lovers, and no one will deliver her from my hand.
I will also make her joy cease to exist including her feasts, new moons, Sabbaths, and all her solemn feasts.
I will destroy her vines and fig trees, of which she has said, 'These are rewards from my lovers, and I will make a forest out of them, and the field beasts will eat them.'
I will visit her during the days of the Baals when she burns incense to them, on the days that she adorns herself with earrings and jewelry. When she followed her lovers and forgot me.
Therefore I will lure her into the wilderness, and speak gently to her.

I will give her vineyards from back to her, and I will give her the Valley of Achor as a gateway to hope. There she will sing, as she did in the days of her youth, and as she did in the days when she left the land of Egypt."
And the Lord spoke to Hosea and said, "And on that day Israel will call me Ishi (My Husband), and she will no longer call me Baali. (Master)
For I will remove the names of the Baals from her mouth, and they will no longer be remembered by their name.

In those days I will make a covenant for them with the field beasts, the birds of the air, and the reptiles that crawl on the ground. I will break the bow and the sword, and remove the battle from the earth, and I will make them lie down in safety.
And I will betroth you to me forever. Yes, I will betroth you to me in righteousness, good judgment, loving kindness, and mercies.
I will even betroth you to me in faithfulness, and you will know the Lord."
And the Lord spoke to Hosea and said, "In those days, I will hear and respond to the heavens, and they will hear the earth.
Then the earth will hear the wheat, wine, and oil, then they will hear Jezreel.

I will sow her as my own on the earth, and I will have mercy on her even though she does not deserve mercy. And I will say to those who were not my people, 'You are my people!' And they will say, 'You are my God!'"

Then the Lord spoke to me, Hosea and said, "Go and love love your wife again, even though she is with another and she is an adulteress. Love her as the Lord loves the Israelis, who look to other gods and love jugs of wine."
So I bought her for fifteen silver shekels, and a homer and a half of barley.
Then I said to her, "You must live with me for me many days, you will not play the whore, and you will not belong to another man, and I will also belong to you."
And the Lord said, "For the children of Israel will live without a king, a prince, a sacrifice, an image, a robe, or a teraphim for many days.
Afterward the Israelis will return, and seek the Lord their God, and their king David, and they will fear the Lord and his goodness in the latter days."
O children of Israel, hear the Lord's word, because the Lord has a dispute with the people of the land and he says, "There is no truth, mercy, nor knowledge of God in the land!
Swearing, lying, killing, stealing, and adultery has broken out throughout the land, and one bloodshed leads to another.
Therefore the land mourns, and everyone who lives on it will languish along with the field beasts, the birds of the air, and even the fish of the sea will be removed.
But let no man struggle nor blame another, because your people are like those who struggle with the priest.
Therefore you will fall by day, and the prophet will fall with you in the night, and I will destroy your mother."

And the Lord said, "My people have been destroyed for lack of knowledge. And because you have rejected knowledge, I will also reject you as my priest. I see that you have forgotten your God's law, so I will also forget your children.
As the people increased, so did their sin against me, therefore I will turn their glory into shame.
They feed on my people's sin, and they set their hearts on their immorality.
The people and priests are just alike, so I will punish them for their ways, and reward them for their deeds.
They will eat, but not have enough. They will commit prostitution, but they will not increase, because they have refused to obey the Lord.
Prostitution, wine, and new wine breaks the heart.
My people ask counsel of their stocks, and their staff informs them, because the spirit of whores has made them err, and they have gone a whoring against their God.

They sacrifice on the mountaintops, and burn incense on the hills under the oaks, poplars, and elms because of the good shade there. So then your daughters commit prostitution and your spouses commit adultery."

And the Lord said, "But I will not punish your daughters when they commit prostitution, nor your spouses when they commit adultery. Because the men themselves go out and offer sacrifices with whores. Therefore the people who do not understand will fall.
Even though Israel plays the whore, Judah does not yet offend. So do not go to Gilgal nor Bethaven, and do not swear and say, 'As surely as the Lord lives!'
For Israel backslides like a backsliding heifer, so now the Lord will feed them like a lamb in a large pasture.
Ephraim is joined to idols, leave him alone!
Their leader's drink sour drinks, and they continuously commit prostitution, and they love shame.
The wind has bound her up in her wings, and they will be ashamed because of their sacrifices."

And the Lord spoke to me Hosea and said, "O priests, House of Israel, and house of the king hear this and listen because this judgment is against you, since you have been a snare at Mizpah, and a net spread over Tabor.
The rebels are profound at making slaughter, even though I have rebuked them all.
I know about Ephraim, and Israel is not hidden from me. For now, O Ephraim, you have committed prostitution and Israel is defiled.
They will not be allowed to return to their God because of their deeds. For the spirit of whores is in their midst, and they do not know the Lord.
Israel's pride testifies against them to his face. Therefore Israel, Ephraim, and Judah will all fall in their immorality.
They will go with their flocks and herds to seek the Lord, but they will not find him, because he has withdrawn from them.
They have dealt treacherously against the Lord, because they have fathered illegitimate children. Now they will be devoured along with their land in a month.
O Benjamin, blow the cornet in Gibeah and the trumpet in Ramah, and shout the battle cry in Bethaven.
Ephraim will be laid to waste on the day of rebuke. Among the tribes of Israel I have declared that which will surely happen.
The princes of Judah are like those who remove the boundary stones, therefore I will pour out my anger against them like water.
Ephraim is oppressed and broken in judgment, because he willingly walked after the commandment.
Therefore I will be like a moth to Ephraim, and like something rotten to Judah's house.
When Ephraim saw his sickness and Judah saw his wound, then Ephraim went to the Assyrian King Jareb, but he could not cure you, nor heal your wound.
For I will be like a lion to Ephraim and a young lion to Judah's house. I will even tear them to pieces and then leave, and I will carry them away where no one can rescue them.
Then I will return to my place, until they acknowledge their offense and look for me. In their affliction they will seek me early on."
And Hosea spoke for the House of Israel and said, "Come, and let us return to the Lord, because he has torn us to pieces, and he will heal us. He has defeated us, and he will bind up our wounds.
After two days he will revive us, on the third day he will raise us up, so that we can live in his presence.
Then will we know, if we follow him in order to know the Lord, as he rises like the morning sun, he will come to us like the spring rains that water the earth."
And the Lord said, "O Ephraim and Judah, what will I do with you? For your goodness is like a morning cloud and the early dew that evaporates.
Therefore I have carved them with prophets, I have killed them with the words of my mouth, and your judgments flash like lightning that goes forth.
For I desire mercy, not sacrifice, and I desire the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings.
But they, like men, have transgressed the covenant. There they have dealt treacherously against me.
Gilead is a city of those who do immoral things, and pollute it with blood.
A company of priests who consent to murder, are like a gang of thieves lying in wait for a man along the way, because they commit obscenity.
I have seen a horrible thing in the House of Israel, for there is Ephraim's prostitution, and Israel is defiled.
O Judah, he has also made a harvest for you, when I return my people from captivity."

And the Lord spoke to Hosea and said, "After I have healed Israel, Ephraim's immorality and Samaria's wickedness will be discovered. Because they tell lies and thieves break in, and gangs of robbers steal everything.
But they do not consider in their hearts that I remember all of their wickedness. Now their own deeds have surrounded them, and they are staring me in my face.
They make the king and princes rejoice in their wickedness and lies.
They are all adulterers, like an oven heated by the baker who does not have to feed the fire until he has kneaded and leavened the dough.
On the day of our king, the princes make him sick with their wine, so he shakes hands with those who scorn him.
For they have inflamed their heart like an oven while they lie in wait. Their baker sleeps all night, but in the morning their anger burns like a flaming fire.
They are all as hot as an oven, and they devour their judges. All their kings have fallen, and there is no one among them who calls out to me.
Ephraim has mixed himself among the people. Ephraim is a cake baked in the oven unturned.
Strangers have devoured his strength and he does not know it. Yes, his hair has gray streaks here and there, but he does not know it.
And the pride of Israel testifies to his face, but after all this they still do not return to nor seek their Lord God.
Ephraim is also like a silly heartless dove, they call out to Egypt and go to Assyria.
When they go, I will spread my net over them and I will bring them down like the birds of the air. So I will chastise them, as their congregation has never heard before.
Woe unto them, for they have fled from me! Destruction to them, for they have transgressed against me! Even though I would have rescued them, they still speak lies against me.
They did not cry out to me in their hearts when they howled on their beds. They assemble together for wheat and wine, and they rebel against me.
Although I have bound and strengthened their arms, they still imagine mischief against me.
They return, but not to the Most High. They are like a deceitful bow, their princes fall by the sword for the rage of their tongue. For all of this they will be ridiculed in the land of Egypt."

And the Lord spoke to Hosea and said, "Put the trumpet to your mouth! He will come like an eagle against the Lord's temple, because they have transgressed against my covenant and trespassed against my law.
Israel will cry out to me and say, 'My God, we know you!'
But Israel has rejected everything that is good, and the enemy will pursue him.
They have set up kings without me. They make princes without my knowledge. They make idols with their silver and gold, so that they are cut off.
O Samaria, your golden calf has cast you aside. My anger has been kindled against them, how long will it be before they attain innocence?
For the workman from Israel made this abomination, therefore it is not God, but the Samarian calf will be broken into pieces.
For they have sown the wind, and they will reap the whirlwind. It has no stalk, and its grain will yield no flour, even if it does produce, the strangers will swallow it up.
Israel is swallowed up! Now they will be among the Gentiles like a bowl full of displeasure.
For they have gone to Assyria like a wild donkey by itself. And Ephraim has hired lovers.
Yes, even though they hire from among the nations, I will now gather them, and they will shrink a little from the burden of the king of princes.
Because Ephraim has made many altars to sin, the altars will be his sin.
I have written to him with the great things of my law, but they thought it was a strange thing.
They sacrifice flesh for my sacrificial offerings, and eat it, but the Lord does not accept them. Now he will remember their immorality and visit their sins. Then they will return to Egypt.
For Israel has forgotten their Maker and they build temples, and Judah has multiplied its fortified cities. But I will send a fire upon their cities, and the fire will devour its palaces."
And the Lord God spoke to Hosea and said, "O Israel, do not rejoice like other people, because you have gone a whoring from your God. You have made love for money on every threshing room floor.
The threshing floor and the winepress will not feed them, and the new wine will fail her.
They will not live in the Lord's land, but Ephraim will return to Egypt, and they will eat unclean things in Assyria.

They will not offer wine offerings to the Lord, and their sacrifices will not be pleasing to him, but they will be like the bread of mourners to them, and all who eat it will be polluted. For their bread will be for their own soul, and it will not be allowed to enter the Lord's temple.
What will you do on the solemn day, and on the Day of the Lord's feast?

Because, even if they flee the destruction, Egypt will gather them up and Memphis will bury them. The pleasant places for their silver will be overgrown with nettles, and thorns will grow in their tabernacles.

The days of the visitation have come, and the days of compensation have arrived, so let Israel know. The prophet is called a fool and the spiritual man is called insane, because of your abundant immorality and great hatred."
And the Lord God said, "The watchman of Ephraim was with my God, but the fowler's snare lies hidden in the prophet's path, and hatred is in his God's house!
They have deeply corrupted themselves, just like it was in the days of Gibeah, so God will remember their immorality and he will visit their sins.

I found Israel to be like grapes in the wilderness. I saw your fathers as the fig tree's first ripened fruit. But they went to Baal-Peor, and separated themselves to that shame, and their abominations were as detestable as the ways they loved."
And the Lord God said, "As for Ephraim, their glory will fly away like a bird from the birth, the womb, and the conception.
Although they raise their children, I will bereave them and there will be no men left. Yes, woe unto them when I leave them!
And I saw Ephraim like Tyre planted in a pleasant place, but Ephraim will bring his children to the murderer.
O Lord, what will you give them? Give them wombs that miscarry and dry breasts.

All their wickedness is in Gilgal, because I hated them there! I will drive them out of my house because of their wickedness and their deeds. And I will no longer love them, and all of their princes are rebellious.
Ephraim is defeated, their roots are withered and they will bear no fruit. Yes, even though they bear children, I will kill the beloved fruit of their wombs.
My God will throw them away, because they did not listen to him, and they will be wanderers among the nations."

And Hosea said, "Israel is an empty vine, because he brings forth fruit only for himself. As the abundance of his fruit increased his altars also increased. The more goodness his land produced, the more he made their sacred images.
Their heart is divided and they will be found faulty. The Lord will break down their altars, and he will spoil their images.
For now they will say, "We have no king, because we do not fear the Lord, so what can a king do for us?"
They have spoken words, and sworn a false covenant. So this judgment springs up like poisonous hemlock in the furrows of a field.
The inhabitants of Samaria will fear because of Bethaven's calf idols, because the people and the priests who rejoiced in its glory, will mourn over it because it has been taken from them.
It will also be carried to Assyria for a present to King Jareb, Ephraim will receive shame, and Israel will be ashamed of his own counsel.
As for Samaria and her king, they will be cut off like the foam on the water.
The high places of Aven will be destroyed because it is the sin of Israel. Thorns and thistle grow on their altars, and they will say to the hills and mountains, 'Cover us and, fall on us.'"
And the Lord God spoke to Hosea and said, "O Israel, you have sinned since the days of Gibeah and there you stand. The battle in Gibeah against the children of immorality did not overthrow them.
It is my desire to chastise them, and the people will be gathered against them, when they put them in bondage or their two sins.
And Ephraim is like a heifer that is taught to love threshing wheat, but I placed a yoke on her fair neck. I will make Ephraim ride. Judah will plow, and Jacob will break his clods.
Sow righteousness for yourselves, reap in mercy and break up your fallow ground. Because it is time to seek the Lord, until he comes and rains righteousness upon you.
You have plowed wickedness and reaped immorality, you have eaten the fruit of lies, because you trusted in your own way and in your army of mighty men.

So a tumult will rise among your people, and all your fortresses will be demolished the same way Shalman destroyed Betharbel on the day of battle, when mothers were dashed into pieces along with their children.
O Bethel, this is how it will be for you because of your great wickedness, on a morning when the king of Israel is completely cut off."
And the Lord God spoke to Hosea and said, "When Israel was a child, I loved him, and I called my son out of Egypt.
But as the Balls called them they left, and they sacrificed to the Baals and burned incense to carved images.
I also taught Ephraim how to walk, taking them by their arms, but they did not know that it was I who healed them.
I led them with cords of a man with groups of love, and I removed the yoke from their jaws, and I gave them meat to eat.
He will not return to the land of Egypt, and the Assyrian will become his king, because they refused to return.
And the sword will endure in his cities, and it will consume his branches and devour them with their own plans.
And my people are bent to backsliding from me, even though they were called to the Most High, no one would glorify him.

O Ephraim, how will I give you up? O Israel how will I deliver you? How will I make you like Admah? How will I treat you like Zeboim? My heart is turned inside of me, my repentances have been kindled together.
I will not execute my fiercest anger, I will not return to destroy Ephraim. For I am God and not man, I am the Holy One in your midst, and I will not enter into the city.
They will walk after the Lord, and he will roar like a lion. When he roars, the children from the west will tremble.
They will tremble like a bird from Egypt or a dove from Assyria, and I will place them in their houses.
Ephraim surrounds me with lies, and the House of Israel with deceit. But Judah still rules with God and is faithful with the saints."

And the Lord God spoke to Hosea and said, "Ephraim feeds on wind and chases after the east wind, every day he increases his lies and devastation, and they make a covenant with the Assyrians and carry oil into Egypt.
The Lord also holds this against Judah. He will punish Jacob with Jacob's own ways, and he will be repaid everything that he deserves for his deeds.
Jacob grabbed his brother's heel in the womb, and through his dependance on God's strength, Jacob had power.
Yes, Jacob had power over the angel and prevailed, he wept and pleaded with God through the angel. He later found God in Bethel, where Jacob spoke with Israel.
The Lord God of Hosts is his name and his name is the Lord's eternal memorial.
So Israel, return to your God, keep mercy and justice and continue to wait on your God.
A merchant weighs his deceit in the balance scales in his own hand, and he loves to oppress.
And Ephraim said, 'But I have become rich, and I have found my own wealth. In all my labors, they will find no sinful immorality within me.'"
And the Lord God spoke to Hosea and said, "I have been your Lord God since you were in the land of Egypt. And I will make you live in tabernacles again, like it was in the days of the solemn feast.
I have also spoken through the prophets, and I have multiplied their visions. And I have used parables to minister through the prophets.
Is there immorality in Gilead? Truly they are just worthless vanity. Do they sacrifice bulls in Gilgal? Yes, their altars are like stones piled up in a field's furrows.
Jacob fled to the country of Syria, and Israel worked and tended sheep to support a wife.
The Lord brought Israel out of Egypt led by a prophet, and Israel was protected by a prophet.
Ephraim has provoked God's anger most bitterly, therefore the blood on Ephraim's hands will be left on him, and his Lord's disapproval will return to him."
And the Lord God spoke to Hosea and said, "Ephraim trembled when he spoke, and he exalted himself in Israel, but when he offended through Baal, he died.
Now they sin even more, and their craftsmen make molten silver images and idols from their own understanding. And they say about them, 'Let the men who sacrifice kiss the calves!'
Therefore they will be like the morning clouds and early dew that passes away, like the chaff blown from the threshing room floor by the whirlwind, or blown away like the smoke from a chimney.
But I am your Lord God from the land of Egypt, and you will know no other God but me, because there is no savior besides me.
I knew you in the wilderness, in the land of great drought.
They were filled from their pastures and their hearts were glorified, so they have forgotten me.
Therefore I will attack them like a lion, or I will observe them along the road like a leopard.
I will meet them like a bear that has lost her cubs, and I will tear open their hearts. I will devour them there like a lion, and the wild beast will tear them apart."
And the Lord God said, "O Israel, you have destroyed yourself, but your help is in me.
I will be your king. Where is there any other king that can save you in all your cities, or your judges of whom you said, 'Give me a king and princes'?
I gave Israel a king in my anger, and took him away in my anger.
The immorality of Ephraim is bound up, and his sins are hidden.
The pain and sorrows of a pregnant woman will come on him because he is an unwise son. He cannot stay long in the place where children are given birth.
I will ransom Israel from the power of the grave and rescue them from death! O death, I will be your plagues! O grave, I will be your destruction! Your repentance will be hidden from my eyes.

Even though Ephraim is fruitful among his brothers, an east wind from the wilderness will come from the Lord. His springs will run dry, and his fountain will dry up, the enemy invader will plunder the treasuries of all their precious bowls.
Samaria will become desolate, because she has rebelled against her God, they will fall by the sword, their infants will be dashed to pieces, and their pregnant women will be ripped apart."
And the Lord God spoke to Hosea and said, "O Israel, return to your Lord God, because you have fallen by your immorality.
Take your words with you and return to the Lord. Then say to him, 'Remove all of our immorality and receive us graciously, so that we may offer you the calves of our lips.
Assyria cannot save us and we will not ride on horses. We will never again say about the work of our hands, "You are our gods." For in Israel's Lord God the fatherless find mercy.'
Then I will heal their backsliding and I will love them freely, because my anger will be turned away from Israel.
I will be like the dew to Israel, Ephraim will grow like a lily, and Israel will take root like the cedars of Lebanon.
Israel's branches will spread, and his beauty will be like an olive tree, and his scent will smell like the cedars of Lebanon.
Those who live under God's shadow will return, they will grow like the wheat or the vine. His scent will be like Lebanon's wine.
Ephraim will say, 'What do I have to do with idols anymore?' Because the Lord has heard and observed Israel, and I am like the green fir tree in which your fruit is found.

Whoever is wise enough will understand these things. Whoever is prudent enough will know them? For the ways of the Lord are righteous, and the just will walk in them, but the transgressors will fall because of them."
The Lord's word came to Joel son of Pethuel.
And the Lord said, "Hear and listen to this all you old men who live in the land. Has this ever happened in your days, or even in the days of your fathers?
Tell your children about it, and tell your children to tell their children to tell the next generations on down.
What the caterpillar left behind, the locust has eaten, and what the locust left behind, the inchworm has eaten, and what the inchworm left behind, the caterpillar has eaten.
Wake up you drunkards, weep and howl all you who drink wine, because of the new wine has been cut off from your mouth.
For a strong nation of locusts with armies too vast to count has come upon my land. Their teeth are like lion's teeth, and they have fangs like a great lion.
The locusts have laid waste to my vines, and barked at my fig tree, he stripped it clean and bare, then he threw it away and its branches have turned white.
Mourn like a virgin covered in sackcloth morning for her youthful husband."
And the Lord said, "The bread and drink offerings have been cut off from the Lord's house, even the Lord's priests and ministers mourn.
The field has been laid to waste and the land mourns, because the wheat has been consumed, the new wine has dried up, and the oil rots.
Be ashamed you ranchers and vineyard because the wheat, barley, and the field's harvest has perished.
The vine has dried up and the fig tree, pomegranate tree, palm tree, apple tree, and all the trees in the field languish and have withered. For all the joy from the sons of men has withered away."

The Lord's word came to Joel and said, "All you priests and altar ministers of my God, clothe yourselves in sackcloth, mourn and howl, then come and spend the night. Because the bread and drink offering has been withheld from your God's house.
Call for and sanctify a fast, summon a solemn assembly, gather the elders and all the inhabitants of the land into your Lord God's house, and cry out to the Lord.
For alas the Day of the Lord is here! And the Day of the Lord will come as destruction from the Almighty.
Has not meat, joy, and happiness been cut off from our God's house before our very eyes?
The seed is rotten under the dirt clods, the gardeners have been decimated, and the barns are broken down because the wheat has withered.
How the beasts do groan! The cattle herds are baffled, because they have no pasture, even the sheep flocks are made desolate."
And Joel said, "O Lord, I will cry out to you, because fire has devoured the wilderness pastures, and flames have burned all the trees in the field.
The field beasts also cry out to you, because the river waters have all dried up, and fire has devoured the wilderness pastures."
And the Lord spoke to Joel and said, "Blow the trumpet in Zion, and sound an alarm on my holy mountain. let all the inhabitants of the land tremble, because the Day of the Lord has come.

A day of darkness and gloom, and a day of clouds and thick darkness. Like the morning dew covers the mountains, a great and strong army appears, the likes of which has never been seen before, and will never be seen again, not even to many generations afterwards.
A fire devours before them and a flame burns behind them. The land is like the Garden of Eden before them, and a desolate wilderness behind them, and nothing will escape them.
They look like horsemen riding galloping horses.
They leap over the mountaintops in chariots, sounding like crackling fire that devours straw, like a powerful army arrayed for battle.
And as they advance the people will be subjected to much pain, and every face will be covered in black soot."
And the Lord spoke to Joel and said, "They will attack like mighty warriors and climb the wall like men of war. Each one will march in formation, and they will not break their ranks.
They will not impale one another, and each will walk in his assigned route. But when they fall on the sword, they will not be wounded.
They will invade the city, and they will run along the top of the wall. They will climb up on the houses, and enter through the windows like a thief.
The earth will quake before them, the heavens will tremble, the sun and the moon will be darkened, and the stars will not shine.
The Lord will speak before his army. His camp is vast, because whoever executes his word is powerful. For the Day of the Lord is very great and terrible, and who can endure it?"
Therefore the Lord now also says, "Return to me with all your heart, and with fasting, weeping, and mourning.
Tear your heart, not your garments and return to your Lord God, because he is gracious, merciful, slow to anger, and of great kindness, then he will repent of this evil.
Who knows if he will return and repent, and leave a blessing behind him? Maybe even a bread and drink offering to your Lord God.
Blow the trumpet in Zion, sanctify a fast, and summon a solemn assembly.
Gather the people, sanctify the congregation, assemble the elders, gather the children, and those who are nursing children. Let the bridegroom leave his chamber, and the bride leave her closet.

Let the priests who are the Lord ministers, weep between the entrance hall and the altar. Let them say, 'O Lord, spare your people and do not hand your heritage over to be despised, or let the heathen rule over them. So that the heathen among the people would say, 'Where is their God?'
Then the Lord will be jealous for his land, and pity his people."
Yes, the Lord will answer his people and say, "Behold I will send you wheat, wine, and oil and you will be satisfied. Then I will no longer make you despised among the heathen.

But I will remove the northern army far away from you, and drive him into a barren and desolate lands facing the eastern sea and his rear flanks will face the farthest sea. His stink will rise and his foul stench will ascend. For the Lord has done great things.
O land, do not fear, be glad and rejoice, because the Lord will do great things.
O field beasts, do not be afraid, because the wilderness pastures sprout, the tree bears her fruit, the fig tree and vine yield their strength."

And the Lord spoke to Joel and said, "O children of Zion, be happy and rejoice in your Lord God, because he has given you the spring rains moderately. He will make the spring and the harvest rain come down for you as it did in the first month.
The threshing floors will be full of wheat, and the vats will overflow with wine and oil.
I will restore your crops to you for the years that the locust, inchworm, and caterpillar, which my great army that I sent among you has eaten.
You will eat plenty and be satisfied, then you will praise the name of your Lord God, who has dealt wondrously with you, and my people will never again be ashamed.
Then you will know that I am in Israel, and that I am your Lord God, and there is no one else. And my people will never again be ashamed."

And the Lord spoke to Joel and said, "Afterward, I will pour out my spirit on all flesh, and your sons and daughters will prophesy, your young men will see visions, and your old men will dream dreams.
I will also pour out my spirit on your maids and servants in those days, and they will prophesy.
I will show wonders in the heavens above and on the earth below of blood, fire, and columns of smoke.
The sun will be darkened, and the moon will be turned blood red, before the great and terrible Day of the Lord comes."
And as the Lord has said, "Whoever calls on the name of the Lord will be saved. Because on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, the survivors will be called by the Lord and saved."
And the Lord spoke to Joel and said, "For in those days and at that time, when I bring the captives of Judah and Jerusalem back again.

I will also gather all nations and bring them down into the Valley of Jehoshaphat. Where I and will plead with them for my people and my heritage Israel, whom they have scattered among the nations, and divided my land.
They cast lots for my people, traded a boy as a prostitute, and sold a girl for wine to drink.
O Tyre, Sidon, and all the coasts of Palestine, what have you to do with me? Will you repay me, and if you repay me, I will swiftly and speedily return your vengeance back upon your own head.
For you have taken my silver and gold, and carried my good and pleasant things into your temples.
You have also sold the children of Judah and Jerusalem to the Greeks, so that you could remove them far from their borders."
Behold, I will raise them from the place where you sold them, and I will return your vengeance back upon your own head.
I will sell your sons and daughters into the hands of the children of Judah, and they will sell them to the Sabeans, a people far off, for I the Lord have spoken."
And the Lord said, "Proclaim this among the Gentiles, 'Prepare for war, wake the mighty men, let all the warriors assemble and march.
Beat your plowshares into swords and your pruning hooks into spears, let the weak say, "I am strong!"
All you heathen, assemble together and surround that place. O Lord, make your mighty ones come down.
Awaken the heathen, and march to the Valley of Jehoshaphat, because I will sit there to judge all the surrounding heathen.
Use the sickle to harvest your ripe crops, then come to the winepress for the vats are full and overflowing because of their great wickedness.'"
And the Lord said, "Millions and millions are in the valley of decision, for the Day of the Lord in the valley of decision is near.
The sun and the moon will be darkened, and the stars will no longer shine.
The Lord will also roar out of Zion, and his voice will be heard from Jerusalem. Heaven and earth will shake, but the Lord will be the hope of his people, and the strength of the children of Israel.
Then you will know that I am your Lord God who lives on my holy Mount Zion. Because Jerusalem will be made holy, and she will never be conquered by strangers ever again.

In those days, the mountains will drip new wine, and the hills will flow with milk. All the rivers of Judah will flow with water, and water will flow from a fountain in the Lord's temple to water the Valley of Shittim.
Egypt will be decimated, and Edom will become a deserted wilderness, because of the violence done against the children of Judah in their own land. For they have shed innocent blood.
But Judah will live forever, and Jerusalem will survive from generation to generation.
For I will cleanse their blood that I have not yet cleansed, because I the Lord live in Zion."

These are the words of Amos, who was with the herdsmen of Tekoa, when he had a vision about Israel in the days of King Uzziah of Judah and Jeroboam the son of King Joash of Israel, and what he saw two years before the earthquake.

Amos spoke and said that this is what the Lord says, "The Lord will roar from Zion, and his voice will be heard from Jerusalem, the shepherds will mourn from their homes, and the top of Mount Carmel will wither."
