Amos spoke and said that this is what the Lord says, "For three or even four transgressions of Damascus, I the Lord will not remove its punishment, because they have thrashed the land of Gilead with iron threshing tools.
But I will set fire to the house of Hazael, which will devour Ben-Hadad's palaces.

For the Lord says, "I will destroy the gates of Damascus, and I will also cut off the inhabitants of the plains of Aven, and the one who holds the scepter from the house of Eden. And the people of Syria will be captured and carried to Kir."

Amos spoke and said that this is what the Lord says, "For three or four transgressions of Gaza, I the Lord will not remove its punishment, because they carried away the entire population into captive captivity, and deliver them to Edom.
But I will set fire to the walls of Gaza, which will devour its palaces."

For the Lord God says, "I the Lord will cut off the inhabitants from Ashdod, and the one who holds the scepter from Ashkelon. I will turn my hand against Ekron, and the surviving Philistines will perish."

And this is what the Lord says, "For three or four transgressions of Tyre, I the Lord will not remove its punishment, because they delivered the entire population to Edom in captivity, and did not remember covenant of brotherhood.
But I will set fire to the walls of Tyre, which will devour its palaces."

Then Amos spoke again and said that this is what the Lord says, "For three or four transgressions of Edom, I the Lord will not remove its punishment, because he pursued his brother with the sword and showed no mercy. His anger raged constantly, and he stayed angry forever.
But I will set fire to Teman, which will devour the palaces of Bozrah."

And Amos spoke and said that this is what the Lord says, "For three or four transgressions of the children of Ammon, I the Lord will not remove its punishment, because they have ripped up the pregnant women of the land of Gilead, just to enlarge their borders.
But I will set fire to the walls of Rabbah, which will devour its palaces with a violent firestorm on the day of battle, as the warriors scream and shout."
And the Lord says, "Their king will be captured, then he and his princes will be carried away together."

Amos spoke and said that this is what the Lord says, "For three or four transgressions of Moab I will not remove its punishment, because he burned the king of Edom's bones until they turned into lime.
But I the Lord will set fire against Moab, which will devour Kirioth's palaces, and Moab will die in the tumult, in the midst of shouting and the sound of the trumpet."
And the Lord says, "And I the Lord will remove its judge from its midst, and kill all of its princes with him."

Then Amos spoke and said that this is what the Lord says, "For three or four transgressions of Judah, I will not remove its punishment, because they have despised the Lord's Law and they did not kept his commandments. Their lies in which their fathers have walked have caused them to err.
But I will set fire against Judah, which will devour Jerusalem's palaces."

Amos spoke and said that this is what the Lord says, "For three or four transgressions of Israel, I will not remove its punishment, because they sold their righteousness for silver and their poor for a pair of shoes.
They slobber on the heads of the poor like they were the dust of the earth. They turn away the meek, and a man and his father will chase the same young women to profane my holy name.
They lay down beside any altar wearing pledged clothing, and they drink the wine of the condemned in the house of their God.
But it was I the Lord who destroyed the Amorite before them, even though they were as tall as cedar trees and as strong as the oaks. And I destroyed his fruit above and his roots below.
I also brought you out of the land of Egypt, and led you for forty years through the wilderness, to possess the Amorite's land."
And the Lord said, "I raised up your sons to be prophets, and your young men to be Nazarites. O children of Israel, do you not even believe that this true?
But you gave wine to the Nazarites to drink, and commanded the prophets not to prophesy.
Behold, I am as depressed under you as a cart full of pressed sheaves or grain.
Therefore the swift will not flee, but they will perish, and the strong will not reinforce his forces, nor will the mighty be able to save himself.
And he who handles the bow will not stand, and he that is swift of foot will not deliver himself, nor will the horse rider deliver himself."
And the Lord says, "Then the courageous among the mighty will flee completely naked in those days."
Then Amos spoke to the Israelis and said, "O children of Israel, hear what the Lord has spoken against you and the whole family which I brought up from the land of Egypt."
And the Lord said through Amos, "I have known only you from among all the families of the earth. Therefore I will punish you for all your wickedness.
Can two walk together, if they do not agree on their destination?
Does a lion roar in the forest, when he has no prey? Does a young lion cry out of his den, if he has taken nothing?
Can a bird fall in a snare on the earth, where there is no snare? Can anything on earth be removed from a snare, that has caught nothing at all?
When a war trumpet is blown in the city, do not the people tremble in fear? If there is evil in a city, has it not been caused by the Lord?
Surely the Lord God will do nothing, without revealing his secret to his servants the prophets.
The lion has roared, who will not fear? The Lord God has spoken, who will not prophesy?
Publish these words in the palaces of Ashdod and the palaces of Egypt and say, 'Assemble together on the mountains of Samaria, and see the great unrest and oppression in its midst.'"
And the Lord said through Amos, "For they do not know how to do the right thing, and they store up violence and robbery in their palaces."
Therefore the Lord God said this through Amos, "An adversary will even surround the land, he will destroy your strength, and your palaces will be plundered.
Just like a shepherd snatches two legs or a piece of an ear from the mouth of the lion, so the Israelis who live on the corner of a bed in Samaria, or a couch in Damascus, will be rescued.
Hear and testify in the house of Jacob, and tell them what the I Lord God of Hosts said.
Tell them that on the day that I visit Israel for their transgressions, I will also visit the altars of Bethel, then the altar horns will be cut off and thrown on the ground."
And the Lord said, "I will defeat the winter and summer houses, the ivory houses will perish, and the great houses will come to an end."

Amos spoke to the wealthy selfish women in Samaria and said, "Hear this, you Bashan cows who live on Mount Samaria, who oppress the poor and crush the needy, who say to your masters, 'Bring us something to drink.'"
The Lord God swore by his holiness through Amos and said, "Behold the days are coming when you will be taken away with hooks, and your posterity will be caught with fishhooks.
You will leave at the broken defenses, every cow at that which is before her, and you will throw them into the palace.
Come to Bethel and Gilgal and transgress even more. Bring your sacrifices every morning and your tithes every three years.
O you children of Israel, offer a thanksgiving sacrifice with leavening. Publicly proclaim and publish your free offerings, because that's what you like to do.
I have also afflicted your cities with cleanness of teeth, and a lack of bread everywhere. But I the Lord say, 'You still have not returned to me.'"

And the Lord God spoke through Amos and said, "I withheld the rain from you for three months before the harvest. I made it rain in one city but withheld it from another. One city was given rain, but the city that got no rain withered.
So people from two or three cities wandered from one city to the next to drink water and they were not satisfied. But I the Lord say, 'You still have not returned to me.'
I defeated you with blight and mildew, when your gardens, vineyards, fig trees, and olive trees increased, the caterpillar devoured them. But I the Lord say, 'You still have not returned to me.'

I sent the pestilence among you like the ones in Egypt, I killed your young men with the sword, I took your horses away, and I made the stench of your camps come into your nostrils. But I the Lord say, 'You still have not returned to me.'
I overthrew some of you, as God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah, and you were like a radical troublemaker saved from the fire. But I the Lord say, 'You still have not returned to me.'"
And the Lord God spoke through Amos and said, "Therefore O Israel. I will do all of this to you, and because I do all this to you, O Israel, prepare to meet your God!

Because, he is the one who forms the mountains, creates the wind, and declares his thoughts to man. He is the one who makes the morning turn to darkness, and walks on the earth's high places. Because I the Lord God say, 'The Lord God of Hosts is his name.'"
Amos spoke for the Lord God and said, "O House of Israel, hear my lament and what I have against you.
The virgin of Israel has fallen, she will no longer rise, she has been abandoned on her land, and there is no one to raise her up."

Then Amos spoke for the Lord God again and told the Israelis that this is what the Lord God said, "The city that marches out a thousand troops will only have a hundred survive. And the city that marches out a hundred will only have ten survive in the House of Israel."
For the Lord says to the House of Israel, "Seek me, and you will live!
But do not seek Bethel nor enter Gilgal, and do not pass through Beersheba, because Gilgal will surely be captured, and Bethel will come to nothing.
Seek the Lord, and you will live, or else he will break out like fire in the house of Joseph, and devour it, and no one in Bethel will be able to quench it.
You who turn good judgment into wormwood, and leave righteousness lying on the earth.

Seek the one who made the seven stars and Orion, and turns the shadow of death into the morning dawn. The one who darkens the day with night, and summons the ocean waters, and pours them out on the face of the earth, for his name is the Lord.
The one who strengthens the plundered against the strong, so that the plundered come against the fortress."
For the Lord says to the House of Israel, "Those who hate the one who reprimands in the gate and abhors the one who speaks honestly.

Therefore, because you walk all over the poor, burden them with taxes on their wheat, even though you have built houses of carved stone, you will not live in them, and even though you have planted bountiful vineyards, you will not drink wine from them.
For I know your many transgressions and your mighty sins. You afflict the just and take bribes, and turn the poor away from justice at the gate.
So the prudent will remain silent at that time, because it will be an evil time.
Seek good and not evil, so that you may live, and so the Lord God of Hosts, will be with you, as the House of Israel has said.
Hate evil and love good, and establish good judgment at the gate, then perhaps the Lord God of Hosts will be gracious to what remains of Joseph."

Therefore the Lord God of Hosts says, "There will be wailing in all streets, and they will say on all the highways, 'Alas! Alas!' They will call the rancher to mourn, and they will summon the skillful mourners to lament and wail.
There will be wailing in all vineyards, because the Lord says, 'I will pass through you.'
Woe unto you who desire the Day of the Lord! What will the Day of the Lord mean for you? The Day of the Lord will be darkness and not light.
It will be like a man who flees from a lion, only to be met by a bear, or a man who went into his house and leaned against the wall, and was bitten by a serpent.
Will not the Day of the Lord be darkness and not light, with no brightness at all?"
And the Lord God of Hosts says, "I hate and despise your feast days, and I cannot stand the smell of your solemn assemblies.
Even though you offer me burnt offerings and bread offerings, I will not accept them, nor will I respect your peace offerings from your fattened beasts.
Take the noise of your songs away from me, because I will not listen the melodies of your instruments.
But let judgment run down like water, and righteousness like a mighty stream.
O House of Israel, why have you offered me sacrifices and offerings in the wilderness for forty years?
You have carried your Moloch tabernacle and the star of your God Chiun images, which you made for yourselves."
So the Lord, whose name is the God of Hosts says, "I will send you into captivity beyond Damascus."
Amos spoke for the Lord God and said, "Woe unto those who are at ease in Zion and trust in Mount Samaria, and to those who lead the nations, and to whom the House of Israel goes!

Go to Calneh and see, then go from there to the great Hamath, then go down to Gath of the Philistines. Are they any better than the kingdoms of Israel and Judah, or are their borders greater than your borders?
You believe that the evil day is far away, but you bring the reign of violence closer.
You lie on ivory beds and stretch out on your couches. You eat lambs from the flock and calves from the stall.
You chant to the sound of harps, and invent your own musical instruments like David.
You drink wine in bowls, and anoint yourselves with the best ointments, but you are not grieved over Joseph's affliction.
Therefore they will now go as captives with the first who were exiled, your banquets and your stretching out on your couches will end."

The Lord God has sworn by himself, and this is what the Lord God of Hosts says through Amos, "I hate Jacob's superior opinion of himself, and I hate his palaces. Therefore I will deliver up the city along with everything in it.
Then if ten men remain in one house there, they will also die.

And when a man's uncle takes his body and removes his bones from the house to be burned, he will speak to whoever is in the house say, 'Is anyone else in the house with you?' Then the one in the house will say, 'There is no one else.' Then the uncle will say, 'Be quiet, because we must not mention the name of the Lord.'"
For the Lord commands, "He will destroy the great house and break its defenses, and the little house will be crushed.
Can horses run across rocky cliffs or can one plow there with oxen? For you have turned judgment into poison, and its righteous fruit into hemlock.
You who rejoice in absolutely nothing and say, 'We have captured their battle horns with our own strength?'"
But the Lord God of Hosts says, "Behold O House of Israel, I will raise up a nation against you, and they will attack you from the entrance of Hamath to the wilderness river."
This is what the Lord God has shown me, "I Amos saw the swarms of grasshoppers he formed after the king's harvest, as the late crops began to grow.
Then after they had eaten the land's grass, I said, 'Lord God, I beg you to forgive us! For how can Jacob survive since he is so small?'
Then the Lord repented from his plan and said, 'It will not happen.'"
This is what the Lord God has shown me, "I Amos saw the Lord God summon a fire to deal with his judgment, and it devoured the great deep and consumed the land.
Then I said, 'Lord God, I beg you to stop! For how can Jacob survive since he is so small?'
Then the Lord repented from his plan and said, 'This too will not happen.'"
This is what the Lord God has shown me, "And I Amos saw the Lord standing on a level wall made plumb by the plumbline in his hand.
And the Lord said to me, 'Amos, what do you see you?' And I said, 'A plumbline.' Then the Lord said, 'Behold I will set a plumbline in the middle of my people Israel, and I will no longer save them.
Isaac's high places will be decimated, and Israel's sanctuaries will be laid to waste, and I will rise up against the house of Jeroboam with the sword.'"

Then priest Amaziah of Bethel sent a message to King Jeroboam about Israel and said, "Amos has conspired against you in the midst of the House of Israel, and the land is unable to bear all of his words.
For this is what Amos has said, 'Jeroboam will die by the sword, and Israel will surely be led away as captives from their own land.'"
Amaziah also said to Amos, "O you prophet, go away and flee to the land of Judah, and eat bread and prophesy there.
But do not prophesy in Bethel anymore, because it is the king's chapel and the king's court."
Then Amos answered Amaziah and said, "I was no prophet, nor was I a prophet's son, but I was a herdsman and a gatherer of sycamore fruit.
And the Lord took me as I followed my flock and told me to go and prophesy to my people Israel.
Therefore, hear the Lord's word, 'You say, "Do not prophesy against Israel, and do not preach against the house of Isaac."'

So this is what the Lord says, 'Your wife will be a prostitute in the city, and your sons and daughters will fall by the sword. Your land will be divided with a measuring line, and you will die in a polluted land. Then Israel will surely be carried into captivity away from this land.'"
This is what the Lord God has shown me, "I Amos saw a basket of summer fruit.
And the Lord asked, 'Amos, what do you see?' And I said, 'A basket of summer fruit.' Then the Lord said to me, 'The end has come for my people of Israel, and I will no longer save them.'
And the Lord God said, 'The temple songs will turn to howling in those days. And there will be many dead bodies thrown out in silence everywhere.'
Hear this, those of you who devour the poor and needy, and make them fail.

And you ask, 'When will the new moon and Sabbath be gone, so that we may market and sell our wheat? Let us shrink the ephah, and increase the value of the shekel, and deceitfully cheat the poor with dishonest scales.
So that we may buy the poor slaves for silver, and the needy for a pair of shoes, and sell the waste from the wheat.'"
The Lord has sworn by Jacob's superior opinion of himself and said, "Surely I will never forget any of their works.
Will not the land tremble for this, and will not everyone who lives there mourn? And it will rise up like a flood, and the land will be thrown out and drowned, like the Nile River floods in Egypt."
And the Lord God said, "In those days, I will cause the sun to go down at noon, and I will darken the earth on a clear day.

I will turn your feasts into mourning, and all your songs into lamentation. I will make everyone wear sackcloth and shave every head. And I will make it like mourning an only son, and its end will be like a bitter day."
And the Lord God said, "Behold, the days are coming, when I will send a famine against the land, not a famine of bread nor a thirst for water, but a famine of hearing the Lord's words.
They will wander from sea to sea and from north to east, and they will run back and forth seeking the Lord's word, but they will not find it.
In those days the fair virgins and the young men will faint from thirst.
Those who swear by the sin of Samaria and say, 'O Dan, your God and the ways of Beersheba lives!' Even they will fall and never rise again."

I, Amos, saw the Lord standing on the altar and he said, "Strike the door lintel so that the posts shake. Cut them down on all the people's heads, and I will kill the last of them with the sword. Those who flee will not get away, and those who escape will not be delivered.
Even though they dig down into hell, my hand will take them. And even though they climb up to heaven, I will bring them down from there.

Even though they hide on top of Mount Carmel, I will search them out and take them from there. And even though they hide from me on the bottom of the sea, I will command the serpent there, and he will bite them.
Even though they are driven into captivity by their enemies, I will command the sword there and it will kill them. Then I will set my eyes on them for evil, and not for good."
The Lord God of Hosts is the one who touches the land and it melts, and everyone who lives there will mourn. The land will rise up like the Nile River floods in Egypt, and it will be drowned.

He is the one who builds his many stories in the heavens, and establishes his troops on the earth. He summons the waters of the sea, and pours them out over the face of the earth. And the Lord is his name.
And the Lord said, "O children of Israel, are you not like the Ethiopian children to me? Did I not bring Israel out of the land of Egypt, the Philistines from Caphtor, and the Syrians from Kir?"

And the Lord said, "Behold, the Lord God's eyes are on the sinful kingdom, and I will destroy it and remove it from the face of the earth, But I will save and not completely destroy the house of Jacob.
For I will give the command, and I will sift the House of Israel among all nations like wheat is sifted in a sieve, but not even the least of the grain will fall to the earth.
All of my people's sinners will die by the sword, and all those who say, 'Evil will not overtake us nor prevent us.'
In those days I will return, and rebuild David's tabernacle which has fallen down, and I will rebuild its ruins and restore it as it was before.
And the Lord who will do this says, 'Those who possess the remains of Edom and of all the heathen will be called by my name.'"
The Lord says, "Behold, the days are coming when the plowman will overtake the reaper, the grape crushers, and whoever sows seed. Sweet wine will fall from the mountains, and all the hills will melt.

And I will once again bring my people of Israel out of their captivity, and they will and inhabit the wasted cities. They will plant vineyards, and drink its wine. They will also plant gardens and eat their fruit."
And your Lord God says, "I will plant them in their land, and they will no longer be uprooted from the land which I have given them."

This is the vision that God sent to Obadiah, and this is what the Lord God says through Obadiah about Edom, "We have heard a rumor from the Lord, and an ambassador has been sent among the heathen to say, 'Rise up, and let us go attack Edom in battle!'
Behold, I have made you small among the heathen, and you are greatly despised.
Your heart's pride has deceived you, you who live in the clefts of the rocks, whose home is high, who say in your heart, 'Who will bring me down to the ground?'
Even though you glorify yourself like an eagle, and you build your nest among the stars, I will bring you down from there.

If thieves or robbers come to you in the night, O how you would be cut off! Would they not steal until they had enough? If the grape harvesters came to you, would they not leave some grapes for the gleaners?
How are Esau's things discovered! How are his hidden things found!

All of the men of your confederacy have brought you to the border, even the men who were at peace with you have deceived and prevailed against you. Those who eat your bread have laid a wound under you, because there is no understanding in him."
And the Lord said through Obadiah, "In those days, I will even destroy Edom's wise men and the wisdom that comes from Esau's mountain!
O Teman's mighty men of war you will be dismayed, and everyone from Esau's mountain will be slaughtered and cut off.
Because of your violence against your brother Jacob, your shame will cover you and you will be cut off forever.
On the day that you stood on the other side and the strangers carried his forces away as captives, and foreigners entered his gates and cast lots for Jerusalem, you were even just like one of them.

But you should not just looked on, the day that your brother became a stranger. You should not have rejoiced over the children of Judah on the day of their destruction, and you should not have spoken proudly on their day of distress.

You should not have entered my people's gate on the day of their disaster. You should not have just stood by and watched their affliction on the day of their disaster, and you should not have stolen their wealth on the day of their disaster.
Nor should you have stood at the crossroads to cut off those who were able to escape, and you should not have delivered up those who survived on the day of distress."
And the Lord said through Obadiah, "For the Day of the Lord is near for all the heathen. What you have done, will be done to you, and your reward will be returned to you on your own head.
For as you have been drinking on my holy mountain, so will all the heathen go on drinking continuously. Yes, they will drink and swallow it down, and they will be as if they had never existed.
But there will be deliverance and holiness on Mount Zion, and Jacob's house will take possession of their inheritance.

Jacob's house will be set ablaze, and Joseph's house will be engulfed in flames. Esau's house will be the straw to kindle the fire and devour them. There will be no survivors in the house of Esau, because the Lord has spoken.
Those of the south will take possession of Esau's mountain, the Philistines from the plains will take possession of Ephraim's and Samaria's fields, and Benjamin will take possession of Mount Gilead.

And this multitude of captives from the children of Israel will possess the land of the Canaanites, all the way to Zarephath. The captives of Jerusalem who are in Sepharad will possess the cities of the south.
And saviors will come to Mount Zion to judge Esau's mountain, and it will be the Lord's kingdom."
Now the word of the Lord came to Jonah son of Amittai.
And the Lord said to Jonah, "Get up and go to that great city Nineveh and cry out against it, because their wickedness has come up before me."

But Jonah got up and fled to Tarshish and away from the Lord's presence. He went down to Joppa and found a ship bound for Tarshish. So he paid the fare and went down into the ship to go to Tarshish away from the Lord's presence.
But the Lord sent a great wind across the sea, and a mighty violent storm rose up upon the sea, and the ship was being broken apart.

Then the mariners were afraid, and every man cried out to his God, and to lighten the ship they threw its cargo into the sea. But Jonah had gone down into the ship's hold, where he laid down and was fast asleep.
So the ship's captain went to him and said, "O sleeper, what are you doing? Get up and call on your God, perhaps your God will think of us and save us."
And the each of sailors said to their shipmates, "Come, and let us cast lots, to determine who brought this evil upon us. So they cast lots, and the lot fell on Jonah."
Then they asked Jonah, "Please tell us what have you done to cause this evil to fall upon us? What is your occupation, what country and what people do you come from?"
And he said to them, "I am a Hebrew and I fear the Lord God of heaven, who made the sea and the dry land."
Then the men were extremely frightened and they said to him, 'Why have you done this?' Because he had told them, and they knew that he had fled from the Lord's presence.
Then because the sea was raging and was churned up they asked him, "What can we do with you to calm the sea for us?".
And he said to them, "Throw me into the sea, so that it will be calmed down for you, because I know that it is my fault that this great violent storm has come upon you."
But the men rowed harder trying to bring the ship back to land, but they could not make it, because the sea was so churned up and it raged against them.
Therefore they cried out to the Lord and said, "O Lord, we beg you not to let us perish for this man's life, and do not lay innocent blood on us. For you, O Lord, have done as you pleased."
So they picked Jonah up and threw him into the sea, and the ocean's raging ceased.
Then the men were extremely fearful of the Lord, and they made promises and offered a sacrifice to the Lord.
Now the Lord had prepared a great fish to swallow Jonah, and Jonah was in the belly of the fish for three days and three nights.
Then Jonah prayed to his Lord God from inside the fish.
And he prayed and said, "Because of my affliction I cried out to the Lord from the belly of hell, and you heard my voice.
For you have thrown me into the middle of the deep sea, the swells surrounded me, and all of your clouds and waves covered me.
Then I said, 'I have been thrown out of your sight, but I will still look toward your holy temple.'
The waters surrounded me all the way to my soul, the depth closed in all around me, and the seaweed wrapped around my head.
O Lord my God, I sank down to the bottom of the mountains, the earth closed in around me forever, but you brought my life up from the corruption.
As my inner soul fainted I remembered the Lord, and my prayer went up to you in your holy temple.
Those who observe lying selfishness forsake their own mercy.
But I will sacrifice to you with thanksgiving, and I will pay everything that I have promised to pay. Salvation is of the Lord.
Then the Lord spoke to the fish, and it vomited Jonah out on dry land.
Then the word of the Lord came to Jonah a second time.
And the Lord said, "Get up and go to the great city of Nineveh, and preach to them what I told you to preach.
So Jonah got up and went to Nineveh, as the Lord commanded. Now Nineveh was a great city and it took three days to get there.
And the first day that Jonah entered the city after his journey, he began to preach and said, "Only forty days left until Nineveh is overthrown!"
So the people of Nineveh believed God, they proclaimed a fast and wore sackcloth, from the greatest to the least of them.
When word came to the king of Nineveh, he got up from his throne, took off his robe, clothed himself in sackcloth, and sat on ashes.
Then the king and his nobles published a proclamation throughout Nineveh that said, "No man or beast, herd or flock may eat anything. They must not eat or drink anything.
But let man and beast be covered with sackcloth, and cry out mightily to God. Yes, let everyone turn from his evil ways and abandon the violence in their hands.
Who knows if God will turn and repent, and turn back from his fierce anger, so that we do not perish."
And God saw what they were doing, and that they had turned from their evil ways. Then God repented from the evil that he had planned to do to them, and he did not do it.
But Jonah was extremely displeased, and he became very angry.

And he prayed to the Lord and said, "O Lord, I pray was this not what I said while I was still in my country? So I fled toward Tarshish, because I knew that you were a gracious, merciful, and slow to anger God of great kindness, who repents of doing evil.
Therefore O Lord, I beg you to take my life from me, because it is better for me to die than it is to live.
Then the Lord said, "Do you have a reason to be angry?"
So Jonah left the city and sat on its east side, where he built a booth to sit under in the shade, so he could see what would happen to the city.
And the Lord God prepared a gourd, and made it grow over Jonah's head to provide shade for him and to ease his grief. And Jonah was extremely happy to have the gourd.
But God prepared a worm when the dawn broke the next day, and it attacked the gourd and it withered.
When the sun rose, God prepared a forceful east wind, and the sun beat on Jonah's head so hard that he fainted and wished he could die and said, "It is better for me to die than it is to live."
And God answered Jonah and asked, "Do you have any reason to be angry about the gourd?" And Jonah said, "I do have a reason to be angry enough to die."
Then the Lord said, "You mourn over a gourd, which you did not tend nor did you make it grow. It came up one night and it perished one night.
Should I not spare the great city of Nineveh, in which there are more than 120,000 people who do not know the difference between their left and right hands, and it also has many cattle?"
This is the Lord's word about Samaria and Jerusalem, that Micah the Morasthite saw during the days of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah who were the kings of Judah.
And this is what the Lord said through Micah, "Listen and hear all you people of the earth and everything else on it! Let the Lord God be a witness against you from his holy temple.
For behold, the Lord will come down from his holy place, and walk on the high places of the earth.
The mountains will melt beneath his feet, and the valleys will be torn apart, like wax melts before the fire, and water rushes down a steep slope."

And the Lord spoke through Micah and said, "All of this is for Jacob's transgression and the sins of the House of Israel. What is Jacob's transgression? Is it not Samaria? And what are the high places of Judah? Are they not Jerusalem?
Therefore I will make Samaria like a pile of rocks in the field, and a place to plant a vineyard. Then I will pour its stones down into the valley and uncover its foundations.

All of its carved images will be beaten to pieces, and all of its treasures offered to idols will be burned. I will lay waste and desolate all of its idols, because she collected it by hiring herself out as a whore, and they will be returned as the price of a whore."
And the Lord spoke through Micah and said, "Therefore I will wail and howl, I will walk stripped naked, I will wail like the dragons, and mourn like the owls.
For her wounds are incurable because it has reached Judah, and he has even come to my people's gate in Jerusalem.
Do not declare it in Gath and do not weep at all. But, roll around in the dust in the House of Aphrah.
You inhabitants of Saphir leave with your naked shame, and you inhabitants of Zaanan do not come out mourning over Bethezel, for Bethezel's protection will be removed.
For the inhabitants of Maroth waited for good, but evil came down from the Lord, even to the gates of Jerusalem.
O you inhabitants of Lachish, hitch your chariots to your swiftest horses. You were the beginning of the Daughter of Zion's sins, because Israel's transgressions were found in you.
Therefore, you will give presents to Moresheth-Gath, and the houses of Achzib will prove to be a lie to the kings of Israel.
But I will bring a conqueror to the inhabitants of Mareshah, and Israel's glorious leaders will go to Adullam.
Cut your hair and shave your head bald, and mourn for your delicate children. Make yourselves as bald as an eagle, for they have left you and gone into captivity."
Woe unto those who devise immorality, and work evil in their beds! They practice immorality in the morning light, because it is in the power of their hands.
They covet fields and houses, and take them away by violence. They oppress a man and his household, they even deprive him of his heritage.
Therefore this is what the Lord said to me, Micah, "Behold I will devise evil against this family, from which you cannot free your necks, nor will you be so proud, for this will be a time of evil.

In those days they will use one parable against you, and mourn with a bitter lament and say, 'We are completely ruined, and he has changed my people's portion. O how he has removed it from me! He has divided our fields and turned them away from us.'
Therefore you will have no one left in the Lord's congregation to cast lots by cord for the land.
They say do not prophesy to those who prophesy, so they will not prophesy, and their shame will overtake them.
O house of Jacob, has the Lord's spirit been limited? Are these his doings? Do not my words do good for anyone who walks righteously?"
And this is what the Lord said to me, Micah, "But lately my people have risen up against me like a enemy. You pull off the robes and undergarments from those passing by like men returning from war.
You have thrown my people's women out of their pleasant homes, and you have removed my glory from their children forever.
So get up and leave, because this is not your place of rest, because it is polluted and it will destroy you with a bitter destruction.
If a man walking in the spirit of lies told a lie and said, 'I will prophesy to you of wine and of strong drink,' then he will be the prophet that these people deserve.

O Jacob, I will surely assemble all of you, and I will surely gather Israel's survivors. I will put them together like the sheep of Bozrah or a flock in the middle of their fold. And they will make a great noise because there are so many men.
The breaker will come up before them, and they will break through the gate and leave. Their king will pass through before them, and the Lord will lead the way."
Then Micah said, "O heads of Jacob and princes of the House of Israel, I pray you will listen and hear. Is it not for you to know true justice?
But you hate good and love evil. You have torn their skin from them, and taken the flesh from their bones.
You also eat the my people's flesh, and strip their skin from them and break their bones. You chop them into pieces as if you were preparing to cook them in a pot, like meat in the caldron.
Then they will cry out to the Lord, but he will not hear them. He will even hide his face from them at that time, since they have behaved with ill will in everything they do.
This is what the Lord says, 'As for the prophets who make my people err, who clench their teeth and proclaim peace, as they prepare for war against anyone who does not put food in their mouths.

That's why the night will come to you and you will have no visions. It will be dark, but you will have no divine inspiration. The sun will go down over the prophets, and the day will turn dark over them.
Then all the wise men will be ashamed, and the diviners will be confused. Yes, they will all cover their lips, because there is no answer from God.'"
Then Micah said, "But I am truly full of the power of the Lord's spirit of justice and courage to declare to Jacob his transgressions and Israel's sins.
I pray you will hear this, O leaders and princes of the houses of Jacob and Israel, you who despise justice and pervert all equality.
You build up Zion with bloodshed and Jerusalem with immorality.

Your leaders judge for bribes, your priests are hired with money to teach, and your prophets divine for money. But they lean on the Lord and say, 'Is not the Lord among us? So no evil can come against us.
Therefore because of you, Zion will be plowed like a field, and Jerusalem will become heaps of broken walls, and the temple mount will become the overgrown forests of the high places."

Then Micah spoke for the Lord God of Hosts and said, "In the last days, the mountain for the Lord's house will be established on top of the mountains, and it will be glorified above all other hills, and people from all over will come there.

Many nations will come and say: 'Come, let us go up to the house of Jacob's God on the Lord's mountain. He will teach us his ways, and how to walk in his paths.' For the law will go forth from Zion and the Lord's word will come from Jerusalem.

He will judge between many people and reprimand strong nations from far away, and they will beat their swords into plow shares, and their spears into pruning hooks. Then nation will not lift up sword against nation, nor will they learn war ever again.
But each man will sit under his own vine and his own fig tree, and no one will make them afraid. For the Lord of Hosts has spoken.
For all people will walk in the name of their Lord God for forever and ever."
And the Lord spoke through Micah and said, "In those days I will assemble her lame, and gather her outcasts who were driven out, and those whom I have afflicted.
And I will make those who remain and those who were forced to leave into a strong nation. Then the Lord will reign over them on Mount Zion from that day until forever.
And you, O guardian of the flock, the stronghold of the Daughter of Zion, your first authority will be restored to you, and the kingdom will return to the Daughter of Jerusalem."
And the Lord spoke through Micah and said, "Why do you cry out aloud? Do you have no king among you? Has your counsellor perished, and have the pains of a woman in labor taken hold of you?

O Daughter of Zion, you will be in labor pains like a woman in labor, because you will now leave the city and live out in the field. You will go to Babylon, where you will be delivered, and the Lord will rescue you from the hands of your enemies!
Now many nations have also gathered against you who say, 'Let her be defiled and let us turn our eye to Zion.'
But they do not know the Lord's thoughts, nor do they understand his counsel, for he will gather them like sheaves on a threshing room floor.

O Daughter of Zion, rise up and thresh the harvest, for I will make you iron horns and brass hooves to beat many nations into pieces. Then you will consecrate their gains and wealth to the Lord of all the earth."

Then Micah spoke for the Lord God of Hosts and said, "Now, O daughter of troops, gather your troops because Assyria has laid siege against us. They will defeat the judge of Israel with a staff to the cheek.
But you, Bethlehem Ephratah, even though you are small among the thousands of Judah, a savior will come from me that will be a ruler in Israel, one who is from the everlasting eternal days of old.
Therefore the savior will give them up, until she who is in labor has brought forth a nation of Israel, then his surviving brothers will return to the children of Israel.
He will stand and feed God's flock with the strength of the Lord, in the majesty of the name of his Lord God. And they will endure, because his greatness will last until the ends of the earth.
This man will be the peace, when the Assyrians invade our land and march all over our palaces. Then we will raise against them seven shepherds, and eight leaders of men.

They will lay waste to the land of Assyria, and the entrances of the land of Nimrod with the sword. Thus the savior will deliver us from the Assyrians when they invade our land and march within our borders."

And Micah spoke for the Lord and said, "Jacob's survivors will be in the midst of many people like dew from the Lord or rain showers on the grass, that does not delay for man or waits for the sons of men.

And Jacob's survivors will be among the Gentiles in the midst of many people like a lion among the beasts of the forest, or a young lion among the flocks of sheep, who both tramples down and tears to pieces, and no one can deliver them.
Your hand will be lifted up over your adversaries, and all your enemies will be cut off."
For the Lord said, "In those days I will remove your horses from your midst, and I will destroy your chariots.
I will remove the cities of your land and tear down all of your strongholds.
I will remove your witchcraft from your hand, and you will have no more prophets.
I will also remove your carved images and statues from your midst, and you will no longer worship the works of your hands.
I will pluck your Asherah poles from your midst, and destroy your cities.
I will execute my furious anger and vengeance on those who have not obeyed me, like nothing they have ever heard of before."
Then Micah spoke and said, "Stand and plead your case before the mountains, and let the hills hear your voice.
Now, O mountains and the everlasting foundations of the earth, hear the Lord's judgements, because the Lord has a dispute with his people, and he will plead with Israel."
And the Lord said, "O my people, testify against me and tell me, what have I done to you and how have I wearied you?
For I brought you up from the land of Egypt, and rescued you from the house of slavery, and I sent Moses, Aaron, and Miriam to you.
O my people, remember what King Balak of Moab counseled and what Balaam son of Beor answered. Remember your journey from Shittim to Gilgal, so that you may know of the Lord's righteousness."
And the people of Israel spoke and said, "Why should I come before the Lord, and bow myself before the high God? Should I come before him with burnt offerings of year old calves?
Will the Lord be pleased with 1,000's of rams or 10,000 rivers of oil? Should I give my firstborn child for my sin, or the child of my body for my soul's sin?"
Then Micah responded and said, "O man, has he not shown you what is good? What does the Lord require of you but to act justly and love mercy, and to walk humbly with your God?"
Then the Lord's voice cried out to the city of Jerusalem and said, "The man of wisdom will see your name, so hear the rod and know who has appointed it.
Are there still wicked treasures and the abominable deceitful measurements in the house of the wicked?
Can I count those with wicked balance scales and a bag of deceitful weights, among the pure at heart?
For the rich men are full of violence, and its inhabitants have spoken lies, and the tongue in their mouth speaks deceitful lies.
Therefore I will also make you sick when I smite you and make you desolate because of your sins.
You will eat, but you will not be satisfied and your vomiting will remain in your midst. You will hold on but you will not be delivered, and what you save I will give up to the sword.
You will sow, but you will not reap. You will press olives, but you will not anoint yourselves with oil. And you will make sweet wine, but you will not drink it.

For you have kept Omri's laws and all the works of Ahab's house, and you have accepted their counsels. I should make you a desolation and let its inhabitants hiss at you, therefore you will bear my people's disrespect."

And Micah said, "Woe is me! For I am like those who harvest the summer fruit and glean the prime grapes from the vineyard. But there are no grape clusters to eat, and no first ripe fruit that my soul desired.
The good man has perished from the earth, and there is no one honest among men. They all lie in wait for blood, and every man hunts his brother with a net.
They earnestly do evil with both hands, the prince and judge both ask for gifts. When the great man utters his mischievous desires, they wrap up the deal.
The best of them is like a brier, the most honest is sharper than a thorn hedge. The day of your watchmen and your visitation comes, and now is their time of confusion.
You cannot trust your friend, do not put your confidence in a guide. Seal the doors of your mouth from her who lies in your embrace.
For the son dishonors the father, the daughter rises up against her mother, the daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law, a man's enemies are members of his own house."
And Micah said, "Therefore I will look to the Lord, I will wait for the God of my salvation, and my God will hear me.
O my enemy, do not rejoice against me when I fall, for I will rise again. And when I sit in the dark, the Lord will be my light.
I will bear the Lord's indignation because I have sinned against him, until he pleads my case and execute justice for me, he will bring me out to the light, and I will behold his righteousness.
Then she who is my enemy will see it, and shame will cover her who said to me, 'Where is your Lord God?' My eyes will see her as she is trampled like mud in the streets.
On the day that your walls are to be rebuilt, then the decree will be far removed.

In those days the people will come to trade in Israel from the fortified cities of Assyria and Egypt, from their fortresses all the way to the Euphrates River, from sea to sea and mountain to mountain.
Despite all that, the land will become desolate because of the fruit of the deeds of those who live there."

And Micah prayed to the Lord and said, "Feed your people with your rod, the flock of your heritage. They live alone in the woods in the midst of Carmel. Let them feed in Bashan and Gilead, as it was in the days of old.
As it was in the days when you left Egypt and said, 'I will show my marvelous things.
The nations will see and be confused of all their might. They will lay their hands over their mouths, and their ears will become deaf.
They will lick the dust like a serpent, and they will crawl out of their holes like earthworms.' They will be afraid of our Lord God, and they will fear because of you.
Who is a God like to you, that pardons immorality, and passes by the transgressions of the remains of his heritage? Our God who does not retain his anger forever, because he delights in mercy.
He will return to us and have compassion for us again, he will subdue our wickedness. You will throw all of their sins into the depths of the sea.
You will show truth to Jacob and mercy to Abraham, as you have sworn to our fathers since the days of old."
The burden of Nineveh, and the book about Nahum the Elkoshite's vision.

And Nahum prophesied and said, "The Lord God is jealous and takes revenge. The Lord takes revenge with furious anger. The Lord will take vengeance on his adversaries, and he reserves his anger for his enemies.
The Lord is slow to anger and great in power. The Lord will not acquit the wicked at all. The Lord's path is in the whirlwind and the storm, and the clouds are the dust on his feet.
He reprimands the sea and makes it dry, and he dries up all the rivers. Bashan, Carmel, and the flower of Lebanon languish and wilt.
The mountains quake, the hills melt, and the earth is burned in his presence, including the whole world and everyone living there.
Who can stand before his indignation and who can endure his fierce anger? His fury is poured out like fire, and he throws the rocks thrown down.
The Lord is good, a stronghold on the day of trouble, and he knows those who trust in him.
But he will put an end to Nineveh with an overwhelming flood, and he will pursue his enemies into darkness."
What do you imagine against the Lord? Whatever it is he will put an end to it, and affliction will not rise up a second time.
For while they are as tangled together as thorns, and they are as drunk as drunkards, they will be devoured like fully dry straw.
There is one who comes from Nineveh, a wicked counsellor who imagines evil against the Lord."
And this is what the Lord says, "Even though they are quiet and many others are quiet, they will be cut down when he passes through. Though I have afflicted you, I will no longer afflict you.
For now I will break his yoke and take it from you, and I will break your shackles and split them apart."

And the Lord has given a commandment about Nineveh and said, "There will no longer descendants to sow your name. I will cut off your carved and molten images from the house of your gods. I will make your grave, because you are vile."

Then Nahum said, "Behold O Judah, a messenger is coming over the mountains who proclaims peace and brings you good news! The message is to keep your solemn feasts and your promises, because the wicked will never pass through your borders again, and they have been completely cut off."
And Nahum said, "O Nineveh, the one who breaks to pieces has come up against you, so guard the fortress, watch the roadway, reinforce your defenses, and fortify your mighty power.
For the Lord has turned away Jacob's excellence just like Israel's excellence, because the plunderers have emptied them out, and scarred their vine's branches.

The shields of the foes of Nineveh are made red, the courageous men are dressed in scarlet. Their chariots will be fitted with flaming torches on the day they have prepared, and the fir trees will be terribly shaken.
The chariots will rage in the streets and justle against one another in the broad streets. They will look like torches and they will run like lightning.
Nineveh will recount their worthy troops, and they will stumble as they march. They will rush to defend its wall, and their defenses will be prepared.
The river gates will be opened and the palace will collapse."
And Nahum said, "It has been decreed that the city will be led away captive, and her young maids will lead her with the voice of doves beating their breasts.
But Nineveh is like an old a pool of water, but now they will flee away. And they will cry out, 'Stand, stand and fight!' But no one will look back.
Take your silver and gold plunder, because there is no end to the stored glory of all the pleasant furniture.
Nineveh has been emptied, left void, and laid to waste. Hearts melt, knees knock together, bodies feel much pain, and their faces are all covered in black soot.
Where is the home and the place to feed the young lions. Where even the old lions walked with the lion's cub, and no one made them afraid?
The lion tore enough pieces for his cubs, and strangled prey for his lioness. He filled his dens with prey and plunder."

And the Lord of Hosts said, "Behold, I am against you and I will burn her chariots up in smoke, and the sword will devour your young lions. I will cut off your prey from the earth, and your messengers will no longer be heard."
And Nahum said, "Woe unto the bloody city of Nineveh! It is full of lies, robbery, and plunder.
The noise of a whip, the rattling wheels, the prancing horses, and the jumping chariots.
The horseman lifts up both the bright sword and the glittering spear, and many are killed. Nineveh is full of a great number of dead bodies, and there is no end to the corpses that they stumble over.
All because of the sins of the whores and the mistress of witchcraft, who sells nations and families through her prostitution and witchcraft."
The Lord of Hosts says, "Behold I am against you and I will lift your skirts above your face, and I will show the nations and kingdoms your nakedness and shame.
I will throw your abominable filth on you and make you vile, and I will make a spectacle of you."
And Nahum said, "Then those who see you will flee from you and say, 'Nineveh has been laid to waste, but who will mourn her? Where will I find comforters for you?
Are you better than Thebes, which was situated among the rivers with water all around it, whose rampart and wall was the sea?
Ethiopia and Egypt were her infinite strength, Put and Lubim were her helpers.

But she was carried away, she went into captivity, her young children were also dashed to pieces at the top of every street. They cast lots for her honorable men, and all her great men were bound in chains.
You too will become drunk, then you will go into hiding and seek strength because of the enemy.
All of your strongholds will be like fig trees with the first ripe figs, if they are shaken, they will fall into the mouth of the eater.
Behold, the people in your midst are women. The gates of your land will be left wide open to your enemies, and fire will devour your gate's bars.
Draw your water for the siege, fortify your strongholds, work the clay, and tread the morter, and strengthen the brick kiln."
And Nahum said, "Fire will devour you, the sword will cut you off, it will consume you like the locusts. So increase your numbers like the locust, and make yourself like many locusts.
You have multiplied your merchants more than the stars of heaven, and the locust spoils the land and flees away.
Your royalty are like locusts, and your captains are like the swarms of locusts who camp in the hedges on a cold day, but when the sun rises they flee, and no one knows where they went.
O King of Assyria, your shepherds slumber, your nobles live in the dust, your people are scattered over the mountains, and nobody unites them.
Your wound are grievous, and there is no healing for your bruises, whoever hears the rumors about you will clap their hands, for has anyone ever escaped your constant wickedness?"
This is the burden which Habakkuk the prophet saw in a vision.
And Habakkuk said, "O Lord, how long must I cry, but you will not hear? I even cry out to you about violence, but you will not save!
Why do you show me immorality, and make me see grievances? For destruction and violence are before me. And there are those who stir up conflict and disagreement.
Therefore the law is slack and justice is nonexistent. For the wicked surround the righteous, so wrong judgments proceed.
Look you heathen, wonder about marvelous things! Because I will do a work in your days which you would never believe, even if someone told you about it.
For I will raise up the bitter and hasty Chaldeans. And that nation will march through the entire land, to seize homes that are not their own.
They are terrible and dreadful, their judgment and dignity proceeds only from themselves.

Their horses are swifter than leopards, and more fierce than the evening wolves. Their horsemen will spread out as they charge, and they will come from far away. They fly like an eagle that dives down to eat.
All of them will come for violence, they will advance like the east wind, and they will gather prisoners like sand.
They will scoff at the kings and scorn the princes, they will humiliate every stronghold, because they will pile up dust to build siege ramps, and capture it.
Then he will change his mind, and he will pass through and offend God, and he will impute that his power comes from his god."

And Habakkuk prayed, "O my Lord God, my Holy One, are you not from everlasting? We will not die. O Lord, you have ordained them to execute your judgment. O mighty God, you have established them for correction.

Your eyes are too pure to see evil, you cannot look at immorality. So why do you look at those who deal treacherously, and hold your tongue when a wicked man devours a man more righteous than himself?
Why have you made men like the fish of the sea, or the creeping things, and the reptiles that have no ruler?
The angler pulls all of them up with his hook, they catch them in their nets, and gather them with their dragnets, then they happily rejoice.
Therefore they sacrifice to their nets, and burn incense to their dragnets. Because these things have provided them with abundant riches and plenty of meat.
So will they not spare the nations, and continue to empty their nets forever, unmercifully killing all the nations?"
And Habakkuk said, "I will stand guard at my post along the watchtower, to see what God has to say to me, and ponder how I should answer him when I am blamed."
And the Lord answered me and said, "Write the vision plainly and clearly on tablets, so that a herald may read it to Babylon.
For this vision is for a future appointed time, but in the end, it will speak, and it does not lie. Even though it may take some time, wait for it, because it will surely come without delay.
Behold, the Chaldean's proud soul is not honest with him, but the righteous will live by faith.

Yes also, because the Chaldean transgresses by wine, he is a proud man, who never stays home and enlarges his desires like hell and death, which cannot be satisfied. But he gathers all nations and piles up all people to himself.

Will not all of these people take up a parable and a taunting proverb against him and say, 'Woe unto anyone who increases himself with that which is not his! How long will he overload himself with thick clay!'
Will they not rise up suddenly to bite you, and awaken those who will frustrate you, and you will be their plunder?
Because you have plundered many nations, all the surviving people will plunder you, because of your bloodshed against men and your violence against the land, the city, and all of its inhabitants.
Woe unto anyone who covets an evil selfish desire for his own house, so that he may set his nest on high, so that he may be delivered from the power of evil!
You have brought shame to your house by cutting off many people, and you have sinned against your own soul.
For the stone will cry out from the wall, and the beam will cry out from the timber to answer it.
Sorrow will come to anyone who builds a town with bloodshed, and establishes a city by immorality!
Behold, is it not from the Lord of Hosts that the people who labor in the fire only weary themselves in vain?
For the earth will be filled with the knowledge of the Lord's glory like the waters cover the sea.
Sorrow will come to anyone who gives his neighbor a drink from his bottle to make him drunk, so he can look at their nakedness!

You are filled with shame not glory. So you must also drink, and expose your uncircumcised foreskin. The cup from the Lord's right hand will be turned on you, and shame will be spewed all over your glory.
For the violence of Lebanon will overcome you, and the slaughter of beasts made them afraid, because of men's bloodshed and the violence against the land, the city, and all the inhabitants there.
What does it profit the man who made carved or molten images and teaches lies? Because its maker trusts his own work to make silent idols?
Sorrow will come to anyone who says to the wood, 'Wake up!' Or to the silent stone, 'Rise up!' Can it teach anything! Behold, it is overlaid with gold and silver, and it has no breath at all in it."
And Habakkuk said, "But the Lord is in his holy temple, so let all the earth be silent before him."
This is a prayer of Habakkuk the prophet in the style of Shigionoth.
And Habakkuk prayed, "O Lord, I have heard you and I was afraid. O Lord, revive your work in the middle years. Then make your works known in the middle years. In your anger, please remember mercy!
Praise the Lord God from Teman, and the Holy One from Mount Paran. His glory covered the heavens, and the earth was filled with his praise.
His brilliance shone like sunlight, he had horns coming out of his hand, where his power was hidden.
Pestilence went out before him, and burning coals went forth at his feet.
He stood and measured the earth, he saw the nations and drove them apart, the everlasting mountains were scattered, and the never ending hills collapsed. But his ways are everlasting.
I saw the affliction in tents of Cushan, and the curtains of Midian trembled.
O Lord, were you displeased with the rivers? Were you so angry with the rivers and the sea, that you rode your horses and chariots of salvation?
Your bow was made quite naked by your word and the oaths of the tribes. Praise the Lord! You split the earth with rivers.
The mountains saw you and trembled, the waters overflowed and swept everything away, the deep called out and lifted its waves up on high.
The sun and moon stood still in their homes, at the flash of your lightning arrows and shiny glittering spear they went forth.
You marched through the land with indignation, and you threshed the heathen in anger.
You went forth for the salvation of your people, and to save your anointed ones. You wounded the head from the house of the wicked, by uncovering their foundation to the neck. Praise the Lord!
You used his own spears to strike the head of his villages. They came out like a whirlwind to scatter me, and they were rejoicing to secretly devour the poor.
You walked through the sea and the swells of the great waters with your horses.

When I heard, my body trembled, my lips quivered at the voice, and decay entered my bones. I trembled within myself, so that I could rest until the day of trouble, when Babylon comes to attack and invade the people with his troops.

Even though the fig trees do not blossom, the vines yield no fruit, the labor to press the olive oil will fail, the fields will yield no crops, the flocks will be cut off from the fold, and there will be no cattle in the stalls.
I will still rejoice in the Lord, and I will find happiness in the God of my salvation.
The Lord God is my strength, and he makes my feet like the deer. He makes me walk upon my high places, for the lead singer with my stringed instruments."
This is the Lord's word which came to Zephaniah son of Cushi, son of Gedaliah, son of Amariah, and son of Hizkiah in the days of King Josiah son of King Amon of Judah.
And the Lord said, "I will completely consume everything on the land."
I will consume man and beast, the birds of the heavens, fish of the sea, and the wicked people's obstacles to understanding. And I will cut off mankind from the land.
I will also stretch out my hand against Judah and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem. I will cut off what remains of Baal from this place, and the names of the Chemarim priests.
I will cut off those who worship the stars of heaven on the housetops. And I will cut off those who worship and swear by the Lord, who also swear by Malcham.
I will cut off those who turned away from the Lord. I will cut off those who have neither sought nor asked for the Lord.
Hold your peace in the presence of your Lord God, because the Day of the Lord is here, for the Lord has prepared a sacrifice and he has prepared his guests.
I will punish the princes, the king's children, and everyone clothed in strange apparel on the Day of the Lord's sacrifice.
On that same day I will also punish all those who leap over the threshold, and fill their masters' houses with violence and deceit."
And the Lord says, "The noise of crying will come from the fish gate, and howling from the second area, and a great crashing sound will come from the hills.
O inhabitants of Maktesh, howl because all the merchant people will be cut down, and everyone carrying silver will be cut off.
Then I will search Jerusalem with candles, and I will punish the men who have settled on false security. I will punish those who say in their heart, 'The Lord will do no good or evil.'

That's why their goods will become plunder, and their houses will e devastated. They will also build houses, but they will not inhabit them. They will plant vineyards, but they will not drink its wine.
The great Day of the Lord is coming closer and closer, quicker and quicker. When the voice of the Day of the Lord is heard, even the mighty men will cry bitterly.
That day is a day of anger, a day of trouble and distress, a day of waste and devastation, a day of darkness and gloom, a day of clouds and thick darkness.
A day of trumpets and alarm against the fortified cities, and against the high towers.
I will bring distress against men, that will make them walk like blind men, because they have sinned against the Lord. Their blood will be poured out like dust and their flesh like dung.

Neither their silver nor their gold will be able to deliver them on the Day of the Lord's anger. The whole land will be devoured by his fires of jealousy, because he will bring a sudden good riddance to all of those who live on the land."
And Zephaniah said, "O despised nation, gather yourselves together.
Before the decree comes, and before the day passes like chaff, before the Lord's fierce anger comes against you, and before the Day of the Lord's anger come against you.
Seek the Lord, all you meek of the earth who have worked for his justice. Seek righteousness, seek meekness and maybe you will be hidden on the Day of the Lord's anger.
For Gaza will be abandoned, and Ashkelon will be devastated. Ashdod will be driven out at noon, and Ekron will be uprooted.

Sorrow will come to the coastal inhabitants, O nation of the Cherethites! O Canaan land of the Philistines the Lord's word is against you which says, 'I will destroy you, and there will be no inhabitants left.'
The coast will be for homes of shepherds and laborer's cottages, and sheds for flocks.

The coast will be for the survivors of the house of Judah. They will feed their flocks there, and they will lie down in the houses of Ashkelon in the evening, for their Lord God will visit them, and return them from captivity.
I have heard the disrespect from Moab, and the insults from the Ammonites, who disrespect my people and threatened their borders."

Therefore the Lord God of Hosts of Israel says, "As surely as I live, Moab will be like Sodom and the Ammonites will be like Gomorrah. A place that breeds nettles and salt pits, and a never ending devastation. The rest of my people will plunder them, and the survivors of my people will control them.
This will they have because of their pride, because they have disrespected and magnified themselves against the people of the Lord of Hosts.
The Lord will be terrible to them when he starves all the gods of the earth. Then men from every shore will worship him, even on all the heathen's islands.
The Ethiopians will also be killed by my sword.
He will stretch out his hand against the north, and destroy Assyria. He will devastate Nineveh, and dry it out like a wilderness.

Flocks and beasts of all the nations will lie down in her midst. Both the cormorant and bittern will roost in her upper lintels, and they will sing in the windows. Devastation will be against the thresholds, because God will uncover the cedar work.

This is the rejoicing city that lived carelessly and thought in her heart, 'I am the only one that matters, and there is no one besides me.' O how she has become a devastation, a place for beasts to lie down! And passers by will hiss and point their finger."
And Zephaniah said, "Woe unto the oppressing city that is filthy and polluted!
She did not obey the voice, she refused correction, she did not trust in the Lord, she did not draw near to her God.
Her princes are roaring lions and her judges are evening wolves, they gnaw the bones and leave nothing for tomorrow.
Her prophets are reckless and treacherous people, her priests have polluted the sanctuary, and they do violence to the law.
The just and righteous Lord is within her, he will do no immorality. Every morning he bring his judgments to light, he does not fail, but the unjust know no shame."

And the Lord said, "I have cut off the nations, their towers are decimated, I laid waste to their streets and no one passes by. Their cities have been destroyed, so that there are no men nor inhabitants.
So I said, 'Surely you will fear me and receive my instructions.' Then their homes would not be cut off, but no matter how I punished them, they got up early and corrupted all their deeds."

Therefore the Lord says, "Wait on me, until the day that I rise up against the prey, because I am determined to gather the nations, so that I may assemble the kingdoms, to pour out my indignation and fierce anger against them. Because the entire earth will be devoured by my jealous fire.
For then I will return a pure truthful language to the people, so that they may all call on the name of the Lord, to serve and consent to him as one.
From beyond the rivers of Ethiopia my petitioners, even the daughters of my scattered people, will bring me an offering.

In those days you will not be ashamed of the things that you have done against me. Because at that time, I will remove from your midst, those who rejoice in your pride, and you will no longer be arrogant on my holy mountain.
I will also leave an afflicted and poor people in your midst, and they will trust in the name of the Lord.
Then the survivors of Israel will do no immorality nor speak lies. No deceit will be found in their mouths, because they will feed and lie down, and no one will make them afraid."
And Zephaniah said, "O Daughter of Zion, sing and shout! O Israel, be happy and rejoice with all your heart, O Daughter of Jerusalem!
The Lord has taken away your judgments, he has thrown out your enemy. Israel's king the Lord, is in your midst, and you will see no more evil.
In those days they will say to Jerusalem, 'Fear not, O Zion, do not let your hands be slack.
The Lord God in your midst is mighty, he will save you and he will rejoice over you with happiness, he will rest his love on you, and he will rejoice over you with singing.'"
And the Lord said, "I will gather those who are full of sorrow for the solemn assembly, and those among you to whom its disgrace was a burden.

Behold, at that time I will undo everything that afflicts you, and I will save her lame, and I will gather those who were driven out. I will give them praise and fame in every land where they have been put to shame.

At that time I will bring you in and I will gather you together. Because I will make your name praised among all people of the earth, when I return your captives before your very eyes." The Lord has spoken.

On the first day, of the sixth month, of the second year of the reign of King Darius the Lord's word came through Haggai the prophet to Zerubbabel son of governor Shealtiel of Judah, and to Joshua son of the high priest Josedech.
And this is what Haggai said that the Lord of Hosts said, "These people say, 'The time has not come to rebuild the Lord's house.'"
Then the Lord's word came through Haggai the prophet.
This is what Haggai said that the Lord of Hosts said, "Is it time for you to live in your paneled houses, while this house lies in ruins?"
Therefore this is what the Lord of Hosts says, "Consider your ways.

You have sown much but harvested little, you eat but you never have not enough, you drink but you are still thirsty, you clothe yourself but you are never warm. You earn wages but you put them into a bag full of holes."
Furthermore the Lord of Hosts says, "Consider your ways.
Go, and bring some wood up to the mountain and build a house, and I will take pleasure in it and be glorified.

You looked for much but collected little. When you brought it home I blew on it, and the Lord of Hosts said, 'Why? I tell you that it is because my house still lies in ruins, and each one of you men run your own house.'
Therefore, because of you the heavens above you withheld their dew, and the earth has withheld her fruit.
Then I sent a drought throughout the land, mountains, wheat, new wine, oil, men, cattle, everything that grows on the ground, and everything produced by your laboring hands."

Then Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Joshua son of high priest Josedech, along with all the surviving people, obeyed the voice of their Lord God, and the words of Haggai the prophet, whom their Lord God had sent to the people, then they feared the Lord.
Then the Lord's messenger Haggai spoke the Lord's message to the people and said, "The Lord says, 'I am with you!'"

And the Lord stirred up the spirits of Zerubbabel son of governor Shealtiel of Judah, Joshua son of the high priest Josedech, and all the surviving people. Then they all came and worked on the temple of the Lord of Hosts of Israel, who is their God.
On the twenty-fourth day of the sixth month of the second year of the reign of King Darius.
On the twenty-first day, of the seventh month, the LORD's word came through Haggai the prophet.
And Haggai said that this is what the Lord said. "Speak to Zerubbabel son of governor Shealtiel of Judah, and Joshua son of the high priest Josedech, and the rest of the people.
And say this, 'Who is left among you who saw this house in her first glory, and how do you see it now? Does this version not look like there is no comparison to it at all?'
And the Lord says, 'But be strong and work, O Zerubbabel, O Joshua son of the high priest Josedech, and all you people of the land. Because the Lord of Hosts says, 'I am with you.
I made this promise to you when you left Egypt. And my spirit remains among you, second do not fear.'"
For this is what the Lord of Hosts said through Haggai, "Once again, in a little while I will shake the heavens, the earth, the sea, and the dry land.
I will shake all nations, and all nations will come with their desires, and I will fill this house with glory, says the Lord of Hosts.
The silver and gold is mine, says the Lord of Hosts.
The glory of this latter house will be greater than the former house, and I will give peace to this place, says the Lord of Hosts."
On the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month of the second year of King Darius' reign, Haggai the prophet received God's word from the Lord.
And Haggai said to the priests, "This is what the Lord of Hosts asks about the law.
'If a man carries holy meat in his garment, and it touches the bread, stew, wine, oil, or any meat, will it still be holy?' And the priests answered and said, 'No.'"
Then Haggai said, "If someone has become unclean by touching a dead body or any of these other things, is it unclean?" And the priests answered and said, "Yes, it will be unclean."
Then Haggai answered and said, "Therefore the Lord says, 'So it is with these people, and this nation before me, and all the works of their hands. Everything they offer from there is unclean.'
And now, I pray you will consider from this day forward, before one stone is laid on top another stone in the Lord's temple.
Since those days, when one came expecting a pile of twenty measures, but there were only ten, when one came to the winepress to draw out fifty bottles from the press, but there were only twenty.
So the Lord says to you, 'I defeated you and all the labors of your hands with blight, mildew, and hail but you still did not return to me.
So consider this carefully from this day forward, the twenty-fourth day, of the ninth month, the day that the foundation of the Lord's temple was laid.
Is there still seed in the barn? Yes, but the vine, the fig tree, the pomegranate, and the olive tree have produced fruit. But from this day forward I will bless you.'"
Once again the word of the Lord came to Haggai on the twenty-fourth day of the month.
And the Lord said through Haggai, "Speak to governor Zerubbabel of Judah and say, 'I will shake the heavens and the earth.

And I will overthrow thrones and kingdoms, and I will destroy the strength of the heathen's kingdoms. I will overthrow chariots and their riders, the horses and their riders will fall, each by his brother's sword.'

In those days the Lord of Hosts says, 'I will take you, O Zerubbabel my servant and son of Shealtiel.' And the Lord says, 'I will make you like a signet ring, because I have chosen you.' And the Lord of Hosts has spoken."
In the eighth month, of the second year of the reign of King Darius, the Lord's word came to the prophet Zechariah son of Berechiah, Iddo's grandson.
And the Lord said through Zechariah, "The Lord has been bitterly displeased with your fathers.
Therefore I want you you say to them this is what the Lord of Hosts says, 'Return to me, says the Lord of Hosts, and I will return to you, says the Lord of Hosts.'

Do not be like your fathers, to whom the former prophets cried out and said this is what the Lord of Hosts says, 'Return from your evil ways and your evil doings now!' But they did not listen to me, says the Lord.'
Where are your fathers and the prophets now, do they live forever?

But my words and laws, which I commanded through my servants the prophets, overtook your fathers and they returned to me and said, 'Just as the Lord of Hosts thought to do to us, for our ways of doing things, is how he has dealt with us.'"
On the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month, which is the month of Sebat, the word of the Lord came to the prophet Zechariah son of Berechiah, Iddo's grandson.
And Zechariah said, "One night I saw a man riding a red horse, and he stood among the myrtle trees in the bottom lands, and behind him were red, speckled, and white horses.
Then I asked, 'What are these my Lord?' And the angel spoke to me and said, 'I will show you what they are.'
And the man who stood among the myrtle trees answered and said, 'They are the ones the Lord has sent to walk back and forth throughout the earth.'
And they answered the Lord's angel who stood among the myrtle trees and said, 'We have walked back and forth throughout the earth, and behold the whole earth sits tranquilly at rest.'
Then the angel of the Lord spoke and said, 'O Lord of Hosts, how long will you have no mercy on Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, with whom you have been very angry these last seventy years?'
And the Lord answered the angel who spoke to me with good and comforting words.
So the angel who spoke with me said, 'Cry out and say that this is what the Lord of Hosts says, "I am very jealous for Jerusalem and Zion.
But I am bitterly displeased with the heathen who are at ease. Because I was just a little displeased, but they helped add to the affliction."'
Therefore this is what the Lord says, 'I have returned to Jerusalem with mercy, where my house will be rebuilt, says the Lord of Hosts, and a measuring line will be stretched out over Jerusalem.'
