So cry out again that this is what the Lord of Hosts says, 'My cities will once again spread prosperity abroad, and the Lord will comfort Zion again and choose Jerusalem.'"
Then lifted I up my eyes and saw four horns.
I asked the angel who spoke to me and said, "What are these?" And he answered me, "These are the horns that have scattered Judah, Israel, and Jerusalem."
And the Lord showed me four carpenters.

Then I said, "What have they come to do?" And he spoke and said, "These horns have scattered Judah, so that no man could raise his head. But these carpenters have come to fight the Gentiles and throw out their horns. Because they have raised their horns over Judah and scattered it."
Then I Zechariah, looked up again and saw a man with a measuring line in his hand.
Then I Zechariah said, "Where are you going?" And he said to me, "To measure the length and width of Jerusalem."
And, behold the angel who had spoken to me left, and another angel went out to meet the first angel.
And the angel said to him, "Run out, and say to this young man, 'Jerusalem will be inhabited like a town without walls to protect the multitude of men and cattle within it.
For the Lord says, 'I will be her surrounding wall of fire, and I will be the glory in her midst.'"
And the Lord says, "Hurry, get up and flee from the land of the north, because I have spread you abroad like the four winds of heaven.
O Zion, escape and save yourselves all you who live with the daughter of Babylon!"
For this is what the Lord of Hosts says, "After the Lord's glory sent me to the nations who plundered you, because whoever touches you touches the apple of his eye.
I will shake my fist against them, and they will be like plunder for their servants. Then you will know that the Lord of Hosts has sent me."
And the Lord says, "O Daughter of Zion, sing and rejoice because I will come and live in your midst.
In those days, many nations will be joined to the Lord, and they will be my people, and I will live in your midst. Then you will know that the Lord of Hosts has sent me to you.
And the Lord will inherit Judah as his portion in the Holy Land, and the Lord will once again choose Jerusalem.
So all people will be silent before the Lord, because he has raised himself up from his holy home."
Then the angel stood before me, Zecahariah, and he showed me the high priest Joshua standing before the Lord's angel, and Satan stood at his right hand to resist him.
And the Lord said to Satan, "O Satan, the Lord that has chosen Jerusalem reprimands you! Is not this man the fiery advocate that I saved from the fire?"
Now Joshua was wearing filthy garments as he stood before the angel.
So the angel spoke to those who stood before him and said, "Remove his filthy garments." And he said to Joshua, "Behold I have removed your immorality, and I will clothe you with clean clothing."
Then I Zecahariah said, "Let them put a clean turban on his head." So they put a clean turban on his head, and clothed him with clean garments, as the Lord's angel stood nearby.
Then the angel of the Lord protested to Joshua.

And the angel told Joshua that this is what the Lord of Hosts says, "If you walk in my ways and you keep my teachings, then you will also judge my house and control my courts. Then I will give you a place to walk among these who stand nearby.
O high priest Joshua, now you and your friends who sit before you hear this, for they are men who people marvel. For behold, I will bring out my servant the Branch.

Look at the stone that I have laid before Joshua, on that one stone there will be seven eyes. Behold I will engrave an inscription on it, says the Lord of Hosts, and I will remove the immorality of this land in a single day.
In those days, the Lord of Hosts says, 'You will invite every neighbor to come and sit under your own vine and fig tree with you.'"
And the angel who spoke to me returned and woke me up again, like a man being awakened from his sleep.
And he asked me, "Zechariah, what do you see?" And I said, "I see a solid gold lampstand, with a bowl and seven lamps on top of it, with seven pipes attached to the lamps on top.
It has two olive trees beside it, one on the right side of the bowl and one on its left side."
Then I asked the angel, "My Lord, what are these?"
Then the angel answered me and said, "Zecahriah, do you not know what these are?" And I said, "No, my Lord."
Then he answered me and said, "Zecahriah, this is the Lord's word to Zerubbabel when the Lord of Hosts said, 'Not by might nor by power, but by my spirit.
Who are you, O great mountain? You will be leveled and become a plain before Zerubbabel, and he will bring forth its headstone, with shouts and cries of, 'Grace and goodwill be to it!'"
Then the word of the Lord came to me again.
And the Lord said, "Zecahriah, Zerubbabel hands have laid the foundation of this house and his hands will also finish it. Then you will know that the Lord of Hosts has sent me to you.
For who has despised the day of insignificant things? For the Lord's seven eyes that see everything throughout the entire earth, will rejoice when they see the plumb line in the hands of Zerubbabel."
Then I responded to the angel and asked, "What are these two olive trees on the left and right side of the lampstand?"
I responded to him again and asked, "What are the two olive branches beside the two gold pipes through which the golden oil pours out?"
The angel answered me and asked, "Do you not know what these are?" And I said, "No, my Lord."
Then he said, "Zecahriah, these are the two anointed ones, who stand beside the Lord of the whole earth."
Then I turned and looked up and I saw a flying scroll.
And the angel asked me, "Zechariah, what do you see?" And I answered and said, "I see a flying scroll that is twenty cubits long and ten cubits wide."

Then the angel said, "Zechariah, this is the curse that goes out and covers the face of the whole earth. On one side of the scroll it is written, 'Whoever steals will be removed!' And on the other side it is written, 'Whoever perjures themself will be removed!'

For the Lord of Hosts says, 'I will bring this scroll into the thief's house, and into the house of anyone who swears falsely by my name. And it will remain in his house and consume all of it including its timber and stones."
Then the angel who had been speaking to me moved forward and said, "Zechariah, look up and see what is coming."
And I asked, "What is it?" And the angel said, "This is a measuring basket that goes forth. Furthermore, it represents their immorality throughout the whole earth."
And behold, I saw a lead talent rise up from the basket, and there was a woman sitting within it.
And the angel said, "This is wickedness!" And he threw the woman into the basket, and he threw the lead talent over the mouth of the basket.
Then I looked up, and I saw two women coming out with the wind in their wings. They had wings like those of a stork, and they lifted up the basket between the heaven and earth.
Then I spoke to the angel and asked, "Where are they taking the basket?"
And the angel said, "Zechariah, they are going to build a house in Shinar, and when it is established, the basket will be set there on her own base."
I turned and looked up, and I saw four chariots coming out from between two brass mountains.
The first chariot had red horses, and the second chariot had black horses.
The third chariot had white horses, and the fourth chariot had dapple-gray and bay horses.
Then I spoke to the angel with me and asked, "My Lord, what are these?"
And the angel answered me and said, "Zechariah, these are the four spirits of heaven, who go forth from standing before the Lord over all the earth.
The black horses are going to the north country, and the white horses are going out after them, and the dapple-gray is going toward the south country."

And the bay horse left to walk back and forth throughout the earth. And the Lord said, "Go out and walk back and forth throughout the earth." So they left and walked back and forth throughout the earth.
Then the Lord cried out and spoke to me and said, "Zechariah, look at those going toward the north country, they have quieted my spirit in the north country.
And the word of the Lord came to me.
And the Lord said, "Zechariah, take up an offering from the captives from Heldai, Tobijah, and Jedaiah, who have come from Babylon. And on the same day go to the house of Josiah son of Zephaniah.
Then take the silver and gold and make a crown. Then set it on the head of the high priest Joshua son of Josedech.
And tell him that this is what the Lord of Hosts said, 'Behold this is the man whose name is the Branch, and he will branch out of his place, and he will build the Lord's temple.
He will build the Lord's temple, he will be clothed in glory and sit and rule on his throne. He will be a priest on his throne, and the counsel of peace will be between both of them.'
The crown will be a memorial in the Lord's temple to Helem, Tobijah, Jedaiah, and Hen son of Zephaniah.

Even those who are far away will come and help build the Lord's temple. Then you will know that the Lord of Hosts has sent me to you. And all this will happen, if you diligently obey the voice of your Lord God."
On the fourth day, of the ninth month which was the month of Chislev, in the fourth year of the reign of King Darius, the word of the Lord came to Zechariah.
When the people of Bethel had sent Sherezer and Regemmelech and their men to the house of God, to pray before the Lord.

And also to speak to the priests and the prophets who were in the temple of the Lord of Hosts, and they asked, "Should I weep, fast, and separate myself in the fifth month, as I have done these many years?"
Then came the word of the Lord of Hosts to me.

And the Lord said, "Zechariah, speak to the priests and all the people of the land and say, 'When you fasted and mourned in the fifth and seventh month for those seventy years, did you even fast to me at all?
And when you ate and drank, did not you eat and drink for yourselves?

Should you not hear the words which the Lord has cried through the former prophets, when Jerusalem and the cities all around her were inhabited and prosperous, when the south and the plains were inhabited?'"
And the word of the Lord came to Zechariah.
And the Lord told Zechariah to tell them that this is what the Lord of Hosts said, "Execute true justice, and show mercy and compassion to every man and his brother.
Do not oppress the widow, the fatherless, the stranger, nor the poor. And do not imagine evil against one another in your hearts."
But they refused to listen, and turned their stubborn shoulder to him. Then they plugged their ears, so that they could not hear.

Yes, they made their hearts as hard as stone, and they would not hear the law, or the words which the Lord of Hosts had sent from his spirit through the former prophets. So a great anger came from the Lord of Hosts.
And the Lord of Hosts said, "Therefore, just as the Lord cried and they refused to hear, so when they cried, I refused to hear them.

But I scattered them with a whirlwind among all the nations whom they did not know. And the land was left desolate after them, and no man could come or go through the land, because they had laid waste to the pleasant land and left it desolate."
Again the word of the Lord of Hosts came to me.
And this is what the Lord of Hosts said to me, "Zechariah, I was greatly and furiously jealous for Zion."
This is what the Lord says, "I have returned to Zion, and I will live in Jerusalem. For Jerusalem will be called a city of truth, and it will be the holy mountain of the Lord of Hosts."
This is what the Lord of Hosts says, "Once again old men and old women will live on the streets of Jerusalem, and each man will have a staff in his hand because of old age.
And the city streets will be full of boys and girls playing in the streets."
This is what the Lord of Hosts said, "If it is impossible in the eyes of what remains of these people in these days, should it also be impossible in my eyes?"
This is what the Lord of Hosts says, "Behold I will save my people from the east countries and the west countries.
I will bring them back to live in Jerusalem. Then they will be my people, and I will be their truthful and righteous God."

This is what the Lord of Hosts says, "Let your hands be strong, you who now hear these words of the prophets, who were present when the foundation of the temple of the Lord of Hosts was laid, so it could be rebuilt.
For before those days neither man nor beast were hired for wages. There was no peace for anyone who came or went because of the affliction I had set between every man and his neighbor."
And the Lord of Hosts says, "But now I will not treat the rest of these people as I did in the former days.

For the seed will be prosperous, the vine will give her fruit, the ground will increase her crops, and the heavens will give their dew. And I will give all these things to what remains of these people as an inheritance.
O houses of Judah and Israel, since you were a curse among the heathen, I will save you, and you will be a blessing. Fear not, but let your hands be strong."
For this is what the Lord of Hosts says, "Just as I thought to punish you when your fathers provoked me to anger, and I did not repent.
So I have again thought in these days to do good to Jerusalem and the house of Judah. So do not fear.
These are the things that you must do, each man must speak the truth to his neighbor, and execute the judgment of truth and peace in your gates.
Do not imagine evil in your hearts against your neighbor, and love no false oath, because the Lord says, 'I hate all of these things.'"
And the word of the Lord of Hosts came to me.

And this is what the Lord of Hosts said, "Zechariah, the fasts of the fourth, fifth, seventh, and tenth months will become a time of joy, happiness, and cheerful feasts to the house of Judah. So love truth and peace."
This is what the Lord of Hosts says, "Someday it will happen, that the inhabitants of many cities will come.
And the inhabitants of one city will move to another city and say, 'Let us go at once to seek and pray before the Lord of Hosts.' I am also going.
Yes, many people and strong nations will come to seek the Lord of Hosts in Jerusalem, and to pray before the Lord."

And this is what the Lord of Hosts says, "In those days it will happen, that ten men from many nations and languages will take hold of the skirt of any Jewish person and say, 'We will go with you, because we have heard that God is with you.'"
This is the burden of the Lord's word that came to Zechariah against the land of Hadrach and its place of rest Damascus, when the eyes of man and all the tribes of Israel, will be upon the Lord.
And also against Hamath on its border, along with Tyre and Sidon, even though they are very wise.
Tyre built herself a stronghold, and heaped up silver like dust, and fine gold like it was mud on the streets.
Behold, the Lord will throw her out, and defeat her with the power of the sea, and she will be devoured by fire.

Ashkelon will see it and fear. Gaza also will see it, and she will be filled with sorrow. Ekron will be ashamed, because her expectations will wither. Gaza's king will perish, and Ashkelon will be left uninhabited.
A mixed race bastard will live in Ashdod, and I will cut off the pride of the Philistines.

And I the Lord will remove his blood from his mouth, and his abominations from between his teeth, but even the survivors will be for our God. And he will be like a governor in Judah, and Ekron will be like the Jebusites.

And I the Lord will camp around my house because of the army, the passers by, and those who return. And never again will an oppressor ever pass through them again, for now I have seen it with my own eyes.
O Daughter of Zion, rejoice greatly! O Daughter of Jerusalem, shout! Behold your king is coming and he is just and humble salvation. He will come riding on a donkey colt, the foal of a donkey.

And I the Lord will cut off Ephraim's chariot and Jerusalem's horse, and the battle bow of war will be cut off. Then he will speak peace to the heathen, and his authority will be from sea to sea, and from the Euphrates river all the way to the ends of the earth.
As for you, by the blood of your covenant, I the Lord have also released your prisoners from the waterless pit.
O prisoners of hope, return to your stronghold, today I the Lord will declare that I will even give you double.
When I the Lord have bent my bow for Judah, and filled the bow with Ephraim. And I have raised up your sons, O Zion, against the sons of Greece, and made you like the sword of a mighty man.
Then the Lord will be seen above them, his arrows will flash like lightning, the Lord God will blow the trumpet, and he will move in whirlwinds of the south.

The Lord of Hosts will defend them, and they will devour, and subdue with sling stones. They will drink and make a rowdy noise through the wine, and they will be filled like bowls, and drenched like the altar's corners.
And their Lord God will save them in those days like the flock of his people. Because they will be like the jewels in a crown, and lifted up like a flag over his land.
How great is his goodness and his beauty! Wheat will make the young men cheerful, and new wine will make the young women happy.
And Zechariah said, "Ask the Lord for spring rains, so that the Lord will make storm clouds, and give everyone rain and grass in the fields.

For the idols have spoken vanity, and the diviners see lies, and tell false dreams, and offer comfort in vain. Therefore the people wandered away like a flock of sheep, and they were troubled because there was no shepherd."

And the Lord spoke through Zechariah and said, "My anger was kindled against the shepherds, and I punished the goats. For the Lord of Hosts has visited his flock the house of Judah. He has made them like his good brave horse in the battle.
The cornerstone, the nail, the battle bow, and every oppressor will all come from Judah together.
And they will be like mighty men, who trample down their enemies like mud in the streets. They will fight in the battle, because the Lord is with them, and those riding on horses will be confused."

And the Lord said, "I will strengthen the house of Judah and save the house of Joseph. I will bring them back to their place, because I will have mercy on them, and they will be as though I had not abandoned them, because I am their Lord God, and I will hear them.
Ephraim will be like a mighty man, and their hearts will rejoice as if they were drinking wine. Yes, their children will see it and be happy, and their hearts will rejoice in the Lord.
I will whistle for them and gather them together, for I have rescued them, and they will be as numerous as they were before.
I will sow them among the people, and they will remember me in distant countries. They will live with their children and return again.
I will also bring them out of the land of Egypt again, and gather them from Assyria. Then I will bring them into the land of Gilead and Lebanon, until there is no place left for them to go.

They will pass through the sea of affliction, and I the Lord will defeat the waves in the sea. All the deep rivers will dry up, and the pride of Assyria will be brought down, and the scepter of Egypt will leave and go away.
I will strengthen them in the Lord, and they will walk up and down in his name."
And the Lord spoke to Zechariah and said, "O Lebanon, Open your doors, so that the fire may devour your cedars.
O fir tree, howl because the cedar has fallen and the mighty have been plundered! O Bashan oaks, howl because the ancient forest has come down!
The shepherds are howling because their glory has been plundered, and the young lions are roaring because Jordan's pride has been plundered."
This is what my Lord God says, "Zechariah, feed the flock for the slaughter.
The flock's purchasers slaughter them, and believe themselves to be not guilty. And those who sell them say, 'Blessed be the Lord, because I am rich.' Even their own shepherds do not pity them."

For the Lord says, "I will no longer have pity on the inhabitants of the land, but I will deliver each man into his neighbor's hand, and into the hand of his king. They will defeat the land, and I will not deliver them from their neighbor nor their king.
So, I will feed the flock for the slaughter, even the poor of the flock. Then I took two poles and I called one Grace, and the other one I called Unity, and I fed the flock.
I also cut off three shepherds in one month, and my soul loathed the flock, and their soul also despised me."
Then I Zechariah said, "I will not feed you. Let the dying die, and let those who are to be cut off, be cut off, and let the survivors eat each other's flesh.
I took my staff called Grace and cut it apart, so that I could break my covenant which I had made with all the people.
And it was broken in those days, so that the poor of the flock who waited on me knew that it was the Lord's word.
And I said to them, 'If you think it is a good price, then give me my price, and if not, then do not pay it.' So they weighed out my price of thirty pieces of silver."

And the Lord said to me, "Throw it to the potter, he has appraised them for a good price." And I Zechariah said, "So I took the thirty pieces of silver, and threw them to the potter in the Lord's temple.
Then I cut my other staff named Grace apart, so that I could break the brotherhood between Judah and Israel."
And the Lord said to me, "Zechariah, take the instruments of a foolish shepherd once again.

For I will raise up a shepherd in the land, who will not visit those who are lost, nor will he seek the young, nor heal the broken, nor feed those who are still standing. But he will eat the flesh of the fat sheep, and tear their hooves to pieces.
Woe unto the lazy shepherd who abandons the flock! The sword will be against his arm and his right eye. His arm will be completely dried up, and his right eye will be completely blinded."
This is the burden of the Lord's word about Israel. The Lord who stretches out the heavens, lays the earth's foundation, and forms the spirit of man within him.
And this is what the Lord said, "Behold Zechariah, I will make Jerusalem a trembling cup to all the people around them. When both Judah and Jerusalem will be besieged.

In those days, when all the people of the earth gather together against her, I will make Jerusalem a burdensome stone for all people. And all those who burden themselves with it will be cut to pieces."

And the Lord says, "In those days Zechariah, I will defeat every horse with astonishment, and his rider with madness. I will open my eyes to the house of Judah, and I will defeat all the people's horses with blindness.
Then the governors of Judah will say in their hearts, 'The inhabitants of Jerusalem will be my strength, for the Lord of Hosts is their God.'

In those days I will make the governors of Judah like a wood fire on the hearth or a fiery torch among the sheaves. They will devour all the people around them on the right and on the left. And the inhabitants of Jerusalem will have her own place again.
The Lord will also save Judah's tents first, so that the glory of David's house and the glory of Jerusalem's inhabitants do not magnify themselves against Judah.
In those days the Lord will defend Jerusalem's inhabitants, so that the most feeble among them will be like David, and the house of David will be like God, or like the angel of the Lord before them.
And in those days, I will seek to destroy all the nations that come against Jerusalem.

And I will pour out the spirit of grace and goodwill on the house of David and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and they will look upon the one they have pierced. They will mourn for him, as one who mourns and grieves bitterly for his only son, or one grieves bitterly for his firstborn son.
In those days there will be great mourning in Jerusalem, like the mourning of Hadad-Rimmon in the Valley of Megiddo.
And each family will all mourn separately on their own land, including the family of David's house and their wives, and the family of Nathan's house and their wives.
The family of Levi's house and their wives, and Shimei's family and their wives.
Plus all the remaining families and their wives."
And the Lord said, "In those days a fountain will be opened to David's house and the inhabitants of Jerusalem to cleanse them of their unclean sins."

And the Lord of Hosts says, "In those days I will cut off the names of the idols from the land, and they will no longer be remembered. I will also remove the prophets and the unclean spirits from the land.

Then if anyone still prophecies, his father and mother will say to him, 'You will not continue to live, because you speak lies in the name of the Lord.' And his father and mother will impale him when he prophecies.
In those days, all the prophets will be ashamed of their visions, and they will wear rough garments to deceive.
But he will say, 'I am not a prophet, I am a rancher, because I was taught to herd cattle since I was young.'
When someone asks him, 'What are these wounds on your hands?' Then he will answer, 'I got these wounds in my friend's house.'"
And the Lord of Hosts says, "O sword, awaken against my shepherd and my fellow man and defeat the shepherd. Then the sheep will be scattered, and I will turn my hand against the children."
And the Lord says, "In all the land, two-thirds will be cut off and die, but a third will be left there.

And I will bring one-third through the fire, and refine them as silver is refined, and I will test them as gold is tested. Then they will call on my name and I will hear them and I will say, 'These are my people!' And they will say, 'The Lord is my God.'"
And the word of the Lord came to Zechariah and said, "Behold, the Day of the Lord is coming, and your plunder will be divided in your midst.

For I will gather all nations to do battle against Jerusalem, and the city will be captured, the houses will rifled, and the women will be ravished. Half of the city will go into captivity, but the rest of the people will not be removed from the city."
Then the Lord will go out and fight against those nations, as he fought them on the day of battle.

In those days he will stand on Mount Olive, which stands east of Jerusalem. And Mount Olive will be split down the middle from east to west, forming a very great valley. Half of the mountain will be moved north and the other half will be moved south.

You will flee to the mountain valleys, because the valleys will reach all the way to Azal. Yes, you will flee, like you fled the earthquake in the days of King Uzziah of Judah, and my Lord God will come to you with all his saints.
And in those days, the light will not be clear nor dark.
But it will be a day which is only known to the Lord, with no day or night, but in the evening there will be light.
In those days, living waters will leave Jerusalem, half of them will flow into the former sea, and half of them will flow into the hinder sea, in summer as well as in winter.
And in those days, the Lord will be king over all the earth, and there will be only one Lord, and his name will be the One True God.

All the land from Geba to Rimmon south of Jerusalem will be turned into plains. But Jerusalem will be lifted up and she will continue to be inhabited, from Benjamin's gate to the place of the first gate, to the corner gate, and from the tower of Hananeel to the king's winepresses.
And men will live there, and there will be no more utter destruction, but Jerusalem will be safely inhabited.

And this plague from the Lord will defeat all the people who have fought against Jerusalem. Their flesh will be consumed as they stand on their feet, their eyes will be consumed in their sockets, and their tongues will be consumed in their mouth.
And in those days, a great panic from the Lord will be among them. Each man will seize his neighbor's hand, and they will all rise up against their neighbors.
Judah will also fight at Jerusalem, and the great abundance of wealth of all the heathen surrounding them will be collected including their gold, silver, and apparel.
And similar plague will affect the horses, mules, camels, donkeys, and all of the other beasts in their tents.
Then every surviving nation that attacked Jerusalem will go every year to worship the king, the Lord of Hosts, and to keep the Feast of Tabernacles.
But there will be no rain for whoever does not come up from all the families of the earth to Jerusalem to worship the king, the Lord of Hosts.
And if a family from Egypt that has no rain does not go up to keep the Feast of Tabernacles, then the Lord will defeat the heathen there with the plague.
This will be Egypt's punishment, and the punishment of all the nations that do not go to keep the Feast of Tabernacles.
In those days will there be inscribed on the bells of the horses, "Holiness to the Lord!" And the cooking pots in the Lord's house will be like the bowls before the altar.

Yes, every pot in Jerusalem and Judah will be holy to the Lord of Hosts. And all those who come to sacrifice will take some pots and cook in them. And in those days there will no longer be a Canaanite in the temple of the Lord of Hosts.
This is the burden of the Lord's word to Israel through Malachi.
And the Lord said, "I have loved you." But you say, "How have you loved us?" And the Lord said, "Was not Esau Jacob's brother? But I loved Jacob.
I hated Esau, so I laid waste to his mountains, and gave his heritage to the dragons of the wilderness."

In fact Edom says, "We are impoverished, but we will return and rebuild the desolate places." This is what the Lord of Hosts says, "They will build, but I will destroy. They will be called the border of wickedness, and a people whom the Lord will have indignation against forever.
You will see this with your own eyes and say, 'The Lord will be magnified beyond the border of Israel.'"

And the Lord of Hosts says, "A son honors his father and a servant his master. But if I am a father, where is my honor, and if I am a master, where is my fear? O priests, who despise my name and say, 'How have we despised your name?'
You offer polluted bread on my altar and say, 'How have we polluted you?' It is because you say, 'The Lord's table is hateful.'"

And the Lord of Hosts says, "If you offer blind animals for sacrifice, is it not evil? And if you offer lame and sick animals, is it not evil? If you offer it to your governor, will he be pleased with you or even accept you?"
And the Lord of Hosts says, "But now, I pray you will beg God to be gracious to us. Since this has been your offerings, will he regard your people?"

And the Lord of Hosts says, "Who is there among you who would shut the temple doors for no pay? Nor do you kindle fire on my altar for no pay. I take no pleasure in you, nor will I accept an offering from your hand."
And the Lord of Hosts says, "For from sunrise until the sun goes down, and everywhere a pure incense offering is offered in my name, my name will be great among the Gentiles.
But you have profaned my name and said, 'The table of the Lord is polluted, and its fruit and meat are hateful.'"
And the Lord of Hosts says, "You also said, 'Behold how weary it is! Then you have sniffed it and brought the torn, lame, and the sick as an offering! So should I accept this from your hand?

But cursed is the deceiver who has a male in his flock, and promises to make a corrupt sacrifice to the Lord, because the Lord of Hosts says, 'I am a great king, and my name is dreaded among the heathen.'"
The Lord of Hosts spoke through the prophet Malachi and said, "O priests, now this commandment is for you."

And the Lord of Hosts says, "If you will not listen and take my word to heart, and give glory to my name, then I will send a curse against you, and I will even curse your blessings. Yes, I have already cursed them, because you do not take my word to heart.
Therefore, I will corrupt your descendants and spread the dung from your solemn feasts on your faces, and you will be taken away with it."
And the Lord of Hosts says, "Then you will know that I have sent this commandment to you, so that my covenant with Levi might be kept.
My covenant with Levi was one of life and peace, and I gave them to him for the fear with which he feared me, and he was afraid before my name.
The law of truth was in his mouth, and no immorality was found in his speech, he walked with me in peace and equity, and he turned many away from immorality.
For the priests should keep and preach knowledge, and they should seek the law from his mouth, because he is the messenger of the Lord of Hosts."
And the Lord of Hosts says, "But you have left the true way, and your law has caused many to stumble! And you have corrupted Levi's covenant.
So I have made you despised and humiliated before all the people, because you have not kept my ways, and you have shown partiality through the law.
Do we not all have only one father? Has not the One True God created us all? Why does each man deal treacherously against his brother, by profaning the covenant of our fathers?
Judah has dealt treacherously, and abominations have been committed in Israel and Jerusalem. For Judah has profaned the Lord's much loved holiness, and he has married the daughter of a strange god.
The Lord will cut off any man who does this from Jacob's tabernacles including the master and the scholar, even if he brings an offering to the Lord of Hosts.
And you have done this again, by covering the Lord's altar with tears, weeping, and groaning, because the Lord no longer regards or accepts the offerings from your hands with goodwill.

But you ask, 'Why?' It is because the Lord has been a witness between you and the wife of your youth, against whom you have dealt treacherously, even though she is your companion and your wife of the covenant.

And did the Lord not make you both one? Yet had he the rest of the spirit, so why one? Because he seeks a Godly descendant, so listen to your spirit, and do not deal treacherously with the wife of your youth."
For the Lord God of Israel says, "I hate divorce, because the one who divorces his wife covers his garments with violence. Therefore, Listen to your spirit, so that you do not deal treacherously.

You have wearied the Lord with your words. But you say, 'How have we wearied him?' It is because you say, 'Everyone who does evil is good in the Lord's sight, and he delights in them.' Or when you say, 'Where is the God of justice?'"

And the Lord spoke through Malachi the prophet and said, "Behold, I will send my messenger and he will prepare the way before me! And the Lord you are seeking will suddenly come to his temple." For the Lord of Hosts says, "Behold the messenger of the covenant, in whom you delight will come.
But who can endure the day of his coming, and who can stand when he appears? For he is like a refiner's fire or a launderer's soap.
And he will sit as a refiner and purifier of silver. He will purify the sons of Levi, and purge them like gold and silver. So that they may offer a righteous offering to the Lord.
Then the offerings of Judah and Jerusalem will be pleasant to the Lord, as they were in the days of old in the years of the past."

And the Lord of Hosts says, "I will come near to you for judgment. And I will be a swift witness against the sorcerers, the adulterers the widow, the fatherless, those who swear false witness, those who oppress the worker hired for wages, and those who turn away the stranger from justice, and those who do not fear me.
For I am the Lord and I do not change! Therefore you sons of Jacob have not been consumed."

And the Lord of Hosts says, "Even from the days of your fathers you have strayed from my legal decrees, and you have not kept them. Return to me, and I will return to you. But you said, 'How can we return?'
Will a man rob God? But you have robbed me. But you say, 'How have we robbed you?' You have robbed my tithes and offerings.
And this whole nation is cursed because you have robbed me.

Therefore, bring all the tithes into the storehouse, so that there is meat in my house." And the Lord of Hosts says, "So test me in this here and now. Then see if I do not open the windows of heaven, and pour out a blessing on you. And there will not be enough room to receive it all!

And the Lord of Hosts says, "I will reprimand the consumer for your sakes and he will not destroy the fruits of your ground. Nor will the vine in your field fail to produce her fruit at the time of harvest."
And the Lord of Hosts says, "All nations will call you blessed, because you will be known as a delightful land.
And the Lord says, "Your words have been stout against me. But you say, 'How have we spoken so much against you?'
You have said, 'It is vain to serve God? How does it profit us to keep his legal decrees and walk mournfully before the Lord of Hosts?
So now we call the proud happy. Yes, those who work wickedness are prosperous and those who tempt God are even delivered.'"

At that time, those who feared the LORD spoke often to each other, and the Lord listened. He heard what was said, and the Book of Remembrance was written before the Lord for those who feared the Lord and studied his name.
And the Lord of Hosts says, "In those days they will be mine when I prepare my jewels. Then I will spare them, as a man spares his own son who serves him.
Then you will return, and you will recognize the difference between the righteous and the wicked. Furthermore, you will know who serves God and who does not."

And the Lord of Hosts spoke through Malachi the prophet and said, "Behold, a day is coming that will burn like an oven, and all the proud and those who do wicked things will be like straw. And the straw will burn up on that day and leave them with no root or branch.
But for those who fear my name, the Son of Righteousness will rise with healing in his wings, and you will go forth and mature like calves in the stall."
And the Lord of Hosts says, "You will trample down the wicked, because they will be ashes under the soles of your feet on the day that I do this.
Remember the law of my servant Moses, who I commanded to give my laws and judgments to all of Israel in Horeb.
Behold, I will send Elijah the prophet to you before the great and dreadful Day of the Lord comes.
And he will turn the heart of the fathers to the children, and the heart of the children to their fathers. Otherwise, I will come and defeat the earth with a curse."
The history of Jesus Christ's family can be traced back to his ancestors, Abraham and David.
Abraham was Isaac's father, Isaac was Jacob's father, and Jacob was Judah and his brothers' father.
Judah had two sons with Tamar, Phares and Zara. Phares had a son named Esrom, and Esrom had a son named Aram.
Aram was Aminadab's father, Aminadab was Naason's father, and Naasson was Salmon's father.
Salmon and Rachab were Booz's parents, Booz and Ruth were Obed's parents, and Obed was Jesse's father.
Jesse was King David's father, King David was Solomon's father, and Solomon's mother was Urias' widow.
Solomon was Roboam's father, Roboam was Abia's father, and Abia was Asa's father.
Asa was Josaphat's father, Jehoshaphat was Joram's father, and Joram was Ozias' father.
Ozias was Joatham's father, Joatham was Achaz's father, and Achaz was Ezekias' father.
Ezekias was Manasses' father, Manasses was Amon's father, and Amon was Josias' father.
Josiah was the father of Jechoniah and his brothers, and they were all taken to Babylon at about the same time.
After they were carried away to Babylon, Jechoniah had a son named Salathiel, and Salathiel had a son named Zorobabel.
Zorobabel was Abiud's father, Abiud was Eliakim's father, and Eliakim was Azor's father.
Azor was Sadoc's father, Sadoc was Achim's father, and Achim was Eliud's father.
Eliud was Eleazar's father, Eleazar was Matthan's fathered, and Matthan was Jacob's fathered.
Jacob was the father of Joseph, Joseph was married to Mary, Mary was the mother of Jesus. Jesus is also known as the Christ.
So, there were 14 generations from Abraham to David, 14 generations from David to the Josias' sons exile to Babylon, and 14 generations from the Babylonian exile to the birth of Jesus Christ.

This is the story of Jesus Christ's birth. Mary was his mother, and she was engaged to Joseph. Before they were married, while she was still a virgin, she found out that she was pregnant by the Holy Spirit.
Mary's husband, Joseph, was a compassionate man, and he did not want to humiliate Mary in public, so he thought about having their engagement quietly annulled.

While Joseph was considering what to do, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream and said, "Joseph, son of David, do not be afraid to take Mary as your wife, because the child that she is carrying comes from the Holy Spirit.
Mary is going to give birth to a son, and you will name him Jesus because he will save his people from their sins.
This will fulfill all of God's word that the prophets spoke about the Lord.
When they said, 'A virgin will give birth to a son, and they will call him Emmanuel.' Which means, 'God is with us'."
When Joseph woke up, he did what the Lord's angel told him to do, and he took Mary to be his wife.
Mary was a virgin when she married Joseph, and they never had sexual relations until after she gave birth to their firstborn son, Jesus.
Jesus was born in the city of Bethlehem which is in Judea during the reign of King Herod. When he was born, wise men came to Jerusalem from the east.
They said they had come to worship the newborn king of the Jews because they had seen his star rising in the east, and they knew that he had been born.
King Herod and all of Jerusalem were very troubled when they heard this.
So Herod gathered his chief priests and scribes together and demanded that they tell him where the Christ child was to be born.
And they said to him, "The prophet said that he would be born in Bethlehem, which is in Judah.
Bethlehem is not the least of the cities of Judah, because a governor will come from Judah to rule over the Israelis."
Then Herod secretly summoned the wise men and asked them when and where they had seen the star.
He sent the wise men to Bethlehem and told them to find the child. He told them to send word back to him after they had found him, so he could also go and worship the Christ child.
After they heard what the king said, they left and the eastern star led them directly to the Christ child.
When they saw the star, they were filled with great joy.

As they entered the house, they saw Mary and her baby son, and they knelt down and worshipped him. They opened their treasure chests and presented the young child with gifts of gold, frankincense, and myrrh.
God warned the wise men in a dream not to return to Herod, so they took a different route back to their own country.

After the wise men left, an angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream and said, "Get up, take the child and his mother to Egypt, and stay there until I tell you to return. Herod is going to try to kill the child."
Joseph got out of bed in the middle of the night and took Mary and the baby to Egypt.
They stayed in Egypt until Herod died, fulfilling the prophecy of the Lord's prophet who said, "I have called my son out of Egypt."

Herod was furious when he realized that the wise men had tricked him. He ordered his soldiers to kill all the male children in Bethlehem who were two years old or younger, based on the time the wise men told him that the star had first appeared. So, the soldiers went and killed all the boys under the age of two in Bethlehem, from the Mediterranean Sea to the Dead Sea.
This fulfilled the prophecy of the prophet Jeremiah.
Because Jeremiah said, "There was weeping, lamentation, and mourning in Ramah, because Rachel was weeping for her missing children, and she could not be comforted."
After Herod died, an angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream while he and Mary were still in Egypt.
The angel said, "Get up, take the child and his mother back to Israel, because those who were trying to kill the child are dead."
So Joseph obeyed the angel's command and took the child and his mother back to Israel.
When Joseph heard that Herod's son Archelaus was ruling Judea, he was afraid to go there, because he had been warned in a dream not to go to Judea, so he turned and went to Galilee instead.
They settled in the town of Nazareth to fulfill the prophecy that the prophets had made about Jesus being called a Nazarene.
One day John the Baptist came out of the Judean wilderness and began preaching.
And he said, "Repent, because the Kingdom of Heaven is here.

Because I am the one that the prophet Isaiah spoke of when he said, 'The voice of one crying in the wilderness came out of the woods and said, prepare the way of the Lord and make his paths straight.'"
John wore clothes made of camel's hair, he had a leather belt around his waist, and he ate locusts and wild honey.
Many people from Jerusalem, Judea, and the whole region around the Jordan came to hear him preach.
He baptized them in the Jordan River, and they confessed their sins.
But when he saw the Pharisees and Sadducees coming to be baptized, he said to them, "You are a generation of vipers, who told you that you could escape God's wrath?
Your behavior will be proof of your repentance.
Do not think that just because Abraham is your father that you do not have to repent, because I am telling you God can turn any of these stones into Abraham's children.
Now the axe is laying at the tree's roots, and every tree that does not produce good fruit will be cut down and thrown into the fire.

I will baptize you with water as a symbol of your repentance, but the one coming after me is mightier than me, and I am not even worthy to carry his shoes. He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire.
He will separate the wheat from the chaff, then he will store the wheat in the barn and burn the chaff in an unquenchable fire."
Then Jesus came from Galilee to be baptized by John in the Jordan River.
But John did not want to baptize Jesus and he said, "Why have you come to me, I should be baptized by you."
Jesus answered him and said, "`We must do this because God's righteousness must be satisfied,´" then John Baptized him.
Jesus came out of the water after he was baptized. The sky opened up and Jesus saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove from heaven, and it landed on him.
A voice came from heaven and said, "This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased."
The spirit led Jesus out into the wilderness to be tempted by Satan.
After he had fasted forty days and forty nights, he was very hungry.
That's when Satan came to tempt him and said, "If you are the Son of God, command these stones to turn into bread."
But Jesus answered them and said, "`It is written that man does not live by bread alone, but by every word that comes from the mouth of God.´ (Deuteronomy 8:3)"
Then Satan took Jesus to Jerusalem and set him on top of the temple's roof.
Satan told Jesus to jump off the roof and said, "Because it is written, that God will send his angels to protect you and lift you up so that not even your foot will be dashed against a rock."
Jesus responded to Satan and said, "`It is also written that you must not tempt your Lord God.´ (Deuteronomy 6:16)"
Satan took him up on top of a high mountain and showed him the world's kingdoms in all their glory.
And Satan said to him, "I will give you all of these things if you get down on your knees and worship me."
Then Jesus said to him, "`Get out of here Satan because it is written that you must worship your Lord God and serve nobody but him.´ (Deuteronomy 6:13)"
Then Satan left him, and the angels came and ministered to him.
When Jesus heard that John had been thrown into prison, he went to Galilee.
He left Nazareth and moved to the coast of Capernaum, between Zebulon and Nephthalim.
This fulfilled the prophet Isaiah's prophecies.
When Isaiah said." In the coastal lands of Zebulon and Nephthalim, which are beyond the Jordan River in Galilee where the Gentiles live.
Where the people who sat in darkness saw a great light, and for those who lived in the land of the shadow of death, a light sprang up."
From that time on Jesus began preaching and said, "`Repent because the Kingdom of Heaven is here.´"
When Jesus was walking by the Sea of Galilee, he saw two brothers, Simon (also called Peter) and Andrew, who were fishermen casting their nets into the sea.
And Jesus said to them, "`Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men.´"
They immediately left their nets and followed him.
After leaving there, Jesus saw two other brothers, James and John, the sons of Zebedee. They were in a fishing boat with their father, mending their nets and Jesus called out to them.
They immediately left their father and his fishing boat and followed Jesus.
Jesus traveled all over Galilee, teaching in the synagogues, preaching the good news of the Kingdom of God, and healing all kinds of disease and sickness.

His fame spread throughout Syria, and the people brought him all their sick people. They had many different diseases and he healed them all, including those who were possessed by demons, those who were insane, and those who were paralyzed.
Large crowds of people followed him from Galilee, Decapolis, Jerusalem, Judea, and from places beyond the Jordan River.
When Jesus saw the huge crowds, he went up into the mountains, and when he was ready, he sent for his disciples, and they came to him.
He began teaching them, as if he were preaching a great sermon to the crowds.
And Jesus said, "`Blessed are the poor in spirit because the Kingdom of Heaven is theirs.´
`Blessed are those who mourn because they will be comforted.´
`Blessed are the meek because they will inherit the earth.´
`Blessed are those who hunger and thirst to be righteous, because they will be completely fulfilled.´
`Blessed are the merciful because they will be shown mercy.´
`Blessed are the pure in heart because they will see God.´
`Blessed are the peacemakers because they will be called the children of God.´
`Blessed are those who are persecuted for being righteous, because the Kingdom of Heaven is theirs.´
`Blessed are those who are reviled, persecuted, falsely accused, and have evil things said about them because of me.´
`The prophets who lived before you were also treated this way, and you should rejoice and be very glad, happy, and excited because you will be given a great reward in heaven.´
`You are the salt of the earth, but if salt loses its flavor, how can it be made salty again? It is no longer good for anything, except to be thrown out and trampled underfoot.´
`You are the light of the world. A city that is the light of the world cannot be hidden, and it is seen by everyone.´
`People do not light candles and hide them under baskets, but they put them on lampstands so they can shine for everyone in the house.´
`So let your light shine before everyone, so they can see your good works and glorify your heavenly father.´
`Do not think that I have come to destroy the law or the prophets, I have not come to destroy, but to fulfill.´
`For Truly, I say to you, not one detail of God's law will pass away until heaven and earth disappear, and everything is accomplished.´

`That's why anyone who breaks one of the least of his commandments and teaches other men to break them, will be called the least in the Kingdom of Heaven, but whoever keeps God's commandments and teaches them to other men, will be called great in the Kingdom of Heaven.´
`That's why I say to you, unless your righteousness exceeds the righteousness of the scribes and Pharisees, you will not enter into the Kingdom of Heaven.´
`You have heard what the ancient people were told, do not kill, and whoever kills will be in danger of judgment.´

`That's why I tell you, if you are angry with someone for no reason, you will be judged! If you insult someone and call them stupid or worthless, you will be brought before the supreme court, and if you call someone a fool, you will be in danger of the fires of hell.´
`And if you bring your gift to the altar and remember that your brother or sister has something against you.´
`Leave your gift at the altar, go and be reconciled with your brother or sister, and then come back and offer your gift.´
`Try to make amends with your accuser before you go to court, or they could take you to the judge, who will then hand you over to the officer, who will then send you to jail.´
`Truly I tell you; you will not be released from jail until you have paid every last penny that you owe.´
`Moses said to the ancient people, 'Do not commit adultery.'´
`But I tell you, if you look at a woman with lustful intent, you have already committed adultery with her in your heart.´
`If your right eye causes you to sin, gouge it out and throw it away, because it is better for you to lose one part of your body than to have your whole body thrown into hell.´
`And if your right hand causes you to sin, cut it off and throw it away, because it is better for you than finding yourself in hell.´
`Moses said, 'Whoever wants to divorce his wife, must just give her divorce papers.'´
`But I tell you, if a man divorces his wife for any reason other than sexual immorality, he is causing her to commit adultery, and if he marries a divorced woman, he is also committing adultery.´
`The ancient people said, you should never break a promise that you have made to the Lord.´
`But I tell you not to make any promises at all, and do not swear by heaven either, because it is God's throne.´
`Do not swear by the earth because the earth is his footstool, or by Jerusalem because it is the city of the great king.´
`Do not swear by your head because you cannot make one hair on your head turn black or white.´
`All you have to say is yes or no, because anything more than that comes from the evil one.´
`You have heard it said, an eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth.´
`But I say to you, 'Do not resist evil,' but if someone slaps you on your right cheek, turn the other cheek so they can slap the other cheek too.'
`If someone takes you to court and sues you for your coat, let them have your robe too.´
`If someone forces you to walk a mile, then walk two miles with them.´
`Do not turn anyone away who wants to borrow from you but give to whoever asks.´
`You have heard it said, 'You must love your neighbor and hate your enemy.'´
`But I tell you to love your enemies, bless those who curse you, do good to those who hate you, and pray for those who use you and persecute you.´
`Because you are the children of your heavenly father, who makes his sun rise on the evil as well as the good, and he makes it rain on the just and the unjust.´
`But if you only love the people who love you, where is the reward in that? Even tax collectors do that.´
`If you only greet your own brothers, are you doing anything more than the others? Even tax collectors do that.´
`That's why you should strive to be as perfect as your heavenly father.´"
And Jesus said, "`Do not donate your money just for other people to see how good you are, because if you do, you will have no reward in heaven from your heavenly father.´

`When you give to charity, you should not publicly announce it in the streets and synagogues like the hypocrites do because they are only seeking to be glorified by others. Truly I tell you the truth when I say, 'They have already received their reward.'´
`When you give to charity, do not let anyone know about it, not even your own left hand.´
`Your charitable giving should be done in secret, and your heavenly father, who sees everything will reward you publicly.´
`When you pray, do not be like the hypocrites who pray in public places to be seen by other people. For truly I tell you the truth when I say, they have already received their reward.´
`When you pray, go somewhere private and shut the door. Pray to your father who sees everything done in secret, and your father will reward you openly.´
`Do not just repeat the same things in your prayers over and over again, like the unbelieving heathens because they think God will hear them if they just keep talking.´
`That's why you are not like them because your heavenly father knows what you need even before you ask him.´
`This is how you should pray to your heavenly father, 'Our father who is in heaven, hallowed be your name;´
`Your kingdom come, your will be done on earth, as it is in heaven.´
`Give us this day our daily bread.´
`And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.´
`Lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil, for yours is the kingdom, the power, and the glory for ever and ever. Amen.'´
`This is because if you forgive others when they trespass against you, your heavenly father will forgive you.´
`But if you do not forgive them, your heavenly father will not forgive you either.´

`When you fast, do not act like the hypocrites, they make themselves look sad on purpose to make it look like they are fasting. Truly I tell you the truth when I say, they have already received their entire reward.´
`But when you fast, do not neglect your appearance, so take a bath, wash your face, and brush your hair.´

`When you fast, do not do it to show off to others. Do it for your heavenly father, who sees everything that you do when no one is watching, and your father will reward you openly for your good deeds.´
`Do not store your treasures on earth, where moths and rust can destroy them, and thieves can break in and steal them.´
`Instead, store your treasures in heaven, where moths and rust can't destroy them, and thieves cannot break in and steal them.´
`Because wherever you store your treasures, is where your heart will be.´
`The eye is the light of the body, if your eye is healthy, your whole body will be full of light.´
`But if your eye is evil, your whole body will be full of darkness, and if the light within you is darkness, then that darkness will be great!´
`No one can serve two masters, because they will love one and hate the other, or they will be devoted to one and despise the other. You cannot serve God and money.´
`That's why I tell you not to worry about your life, or what to eat or drink, or what you will wear on your body. Is life not more than just food and clothing?´
`Look at the birds in the air. They do not sow or reap or store grain in barns, but your heavenly father feeds them, are you not worth more to him than the birds?´
`Can anyone add an inch to their height by worrying?´
`Why do you worry about your clothes? Consider the field lilies, they grow and they do not work or spin threads.´
`Even Solomon, who was wise, wealthy, and powerful, was not as beautifully dressed as the field lilies.´
`That's why, if God clothes the field grass, which is alive today but thrown into the fire tomorrow, will the Lord not clothe you even better than the grass, O you of little faith?´
`You should never worry about what to eat or drink, or what you should wear.´
`Because the Gentiles chase after these things, but your heavenly father already knows that you need them.´
But you should seek God and his righteous kingdom, and he will give you all of these things.
Do not worry about tomorrow, but let tomorrow worry about tomorrow, because each day has enough troubles all of its own."
And Jesus said, "`Do not judge others, or you will be judged.´
`Because you will be judged in the same way that you judge others, and you will be treated the same way that you treat others.´
`How is it that you can see a splinter in your brother's eye, but you do not see the plank in your own eye?´
`Or how can you tell your brother that you will pull the splinter out of his eye, when you have a plank in your own eye?´
`Hypocrites, you must remove the plank from your own eye first, then you will be able to see clearly enough to remove the splinter from your brother's eye.´

`Do not give your holy things to dogs, do not throw your pearls to the pigs, or share your valuable insights with people who do not listen. Because they will ignore you and twist everything you say against you.´
`Ask, and it will be given to you, seek, and it will be found for you, knock, and it will be opened to you.´
`For whoever asks for something, will receive it. Whoever looks for something, will find it, and whoever knocks will find that the door is open.´
`If your son asks you for bread, would you give him a stone instead?´
`If he asked you for a fish, would you give him a snake?´
`If you are a sinner, do you still not love your children and want to give them good things? So, how much more does our father in heaven who loves us, want to give us good things if we ask?´
`That's why you should treat others, the same way you want them to treat you, because this is the prophet's law.´
`You must enter through the narrow gate, because the gate that leads to ruin is wide, its path is easy and many people take the easy path to ruin.´
`Because the road to life is straight and narrow, and only a few people will find the road that leads to the Kingdom of Heaven.´
`Beware of false prophets who are disguised in sheep's clothing, they may look like good, honest, and harmless sheep, but they are actually cruel and greedy wolves.´
`You will know them by their fruits, because good people do not gather their grapes from thorns, nor their figs from thistles.´
`Good trees produce good fruit, but a corrupt tree produces evil fruit.´
`A good tree cannot produce evil fruit, and a corrupt tree cannot produce good fruit.´
`Every tree that produces bad fruit, is cut down and thrown into the fire.'
`That's why you will know them by their fruits.´
`It is not enough that you call me your Lord, you must also do the will of my father, who is in heaven, because that is the only way you will enter heaven.´
`In those last days, many people will say to me, 'Lord, we have prophesied and cast out demons and done many other wonderful works in your name.'´
`And then I will say, 'Away from me, for I never knew you and you do works of iniquity.'´
`Therefore, whoever hears what I say and does what I tell them to do, then I will see them as a wise man, who built his house on a rock.´
`Because the rain will fall, the floods will come, the winds will blow, and they will beat against that house, but it will not fall because it was built upon a rock.´
`Whoever hears what I say and does not do what I tell them to do is like a foolish man, who built his house upon the sand.´
`Because the rains will descend, the floods will come, the winds will blow and beat against that house, and it will fall with a great roar.´"
When Jesus finished talking, the people were astonished by his teachings.
Because he taught them like he had real authority, not the way the scribes had been teaching them.
When Jesus came down from the mountain, tremendous crowds followed him.
A leper came to worship him and said, "Lord, if you want to, you can heal me and make me clean."
And Jesus reached out and he touched him and said, "`I do want to heal you, and now you are clean.´" Immediately the man was healed and his leprosy was gone.
And Jesus said to him, "`Make sure you do not tell anyone about this, go and show yourself to the priest, and offer the gift that Moses commanded you to offer, as your testimony to them.´"
As Jesus entered Capernaum, a Roman centurion came up to him and begged him to come to his house.
And he said, "Lord, my servant at home is sick with the palsy, and he's grievously tormented."
Then Jesus said to him, "`I will come and heal him.´"
The centurion said, "Lord, I am not worthy for you to come to my house, because all you have to do is say the words, and my servant will be healed.
I know, because I am a man who commands soldiers, and if I tell them to go, they go. If I tell them to come, they come, and if I tell my servant to do something, he does it."
When Jesus heard this, he was astonished, then he said to his followers, "`Truly I tell you; I have never seen faith this great, not even in Israel.´
`Many will come from the east and west, and they will sit in the Kingdom of Heaven with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.´
`But the kingdom's children will be thrown into the outer darkness, and there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.´"
And Jesus said to the centurion, "`Go home, because since you have believed me, your request has been granted,´" and his servant was immediately healed.
When Jesus entered Peter's house, he saw that Peter's mother-in-law was sick in bed with a fever.
So Jesus touched her hand, and her fever broke, then she got up, and served them.
In the evening, they brought many people to Jesus who were demon possessed, so he cast out the evil spirits and healed the sick with his words.
This fulfilled what the prophet Isaiah meant when he said, "He took our sickness and infirmities away with him."
When Jesus saw that he was surrounded by a massive crowd of people, he told them to go to the other side of the Sea of Galilee.
One of the scribes came to him and said, "Teacher, I will follow you wherever you go."
And Jesus said to him, "`Foxes have holes, birds have nests, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head.´"
Another one of his disciples said to him, "Lord, can I go and bury my father first?"
But Jesus said to him, "`Follow me, and let the dead bury their own dead.´"
Then Jesus boarded a ship, and his disciples followed him.
Suddenly a great, violent storm rose up, and the waves covered the ship, but Jesus was asleep.
So the disciples woke him up and said, "Lord, save us, we are going to die."
And Jesus said to them, "`O you of little faith, why are you fearful?´" Then he got up and reprimanded the winds and the sea. Immediately the storm subsided and the water was calm.
They were surprised again and said, "What kind of man is this, because even the winds and the seas obey him!"

When they got to the other side they arrived in the country of the Gergesenes, where Jesus met two demon possessed men coming out of the tombs. They were very fierce, and nobody wanted to go anywhere near them.
And the demon possessed men cried out and said, "Why are you here, Jesus, Son of God? Have you come to torment us before the appointed time?"
Nearby, there was a large herd of pigs eating.
So the demon possessed men begged him to send them away and into the herd of pigs.

And Jesus said to them, "`Go!´" Then the demons left the demon possessed men and entered the herd of pigs. The whole herd of pigs ran violently down a steep slope; they fell into the sea and perished.
Then the men who were no longer possessed fled to the city. When they got there, they told everyone how Jesus had saved them from the demons that had possessed them.
After that the whole city went out to meet Jesus, and they begged him to go away.
Jesus boarded a passing ship and returned to his hometown.
The local people brought him a man lying on a bed who was sick with palsy. Jesus saw their faith, and he said to the sick man, "`Cheer up son, your sins are forgiven.´"
Some of the scribes were talking to themselves and they thought that Jesus was blasphemous.
But Jesus knew their thoughts and he said, "`You have evil thoughts in your hearts?´
`And that's why I ask you if it easier to say, 'Your sins are forgiven,' or would you rather I say, 'Get up and walk'?´
`So in order for you to know that the Son of Man truly does have the power to forgive sins on earth, I say to the sick, 'Get up, take your bed and go home.'´"
And the man got up and went home.
But when the massive crowds saw what had happened, they were astonished and they glorified God, who had given such power to men.
When Jesus left that place, he saw Matthew sitting in the tax collector's booth and he said to him, "`Follow me!´" So, he got up and followed him.
Jesus was sitting in a house where he and his disciples had gathered, and there were many tax collectors and sinners sitting with them.
When the Pharisees saw this, they said to his disciples, "Why does your master eat with tax collectors and sinners?"
Jesus heard them and he said, "`People who are not sick do not need a physician, but sick people do.´
`So go and figure out what it means when I say, 'I desire mercy, not sacrifice.' I have not come for the righteous, but I have come to call the sinners to repentance.´"
Then John the Baptist's disciples came to Jesus and asked, "Why do we fast with Pharisees so often, but your disciples do not fast at all?"

And Jesus replied to them and said, "`Do the bridesmaid's' children mourn the bridegroom in the wedding chamber as long as he is with them? But the days will come, when the bridegroom will be taken away from them, then they will fast.´
`Nobody mends an old garment with a new cloth patch, because when the new patch shrinks, the hole in the old garment will be torn and made worse.´

`Nobody puts new wine into old wineskins either, because the old wineskins will burst, and the wine will spill out. Instead, they put new wine into new wineskins, that way both the new wine and the new wineskin will be preserved.´"
While Jesus was talking to John's disciples, a church official came to him and said, "My daughter just died, but if you come and lay your hand on her, she will come back to life."
So, Jesus and his disciples got up and followed him.
A woman who had been bleeding menstrual blood for twelve years, pushed her way through the crowd and she came up behind him, and touched the hem of his garment.
Because she had thought to herself, if she could just touch his garment, she would be healed.
But Jesus felt her touch his robe and he turned around and said, "`Daughter, your faith has healed you!´" And she was immediately healed.
When Jesus entered the official's house, he saw that the people and musicians were making sad and mournful music.
Jesus said to them, "`Get out of the way because this girl is not dead, she is only sleeping!´" Then they laughed at and scorned him.
When the people moved out of the way, Jesus went in and took her by the hand, and she got up.
This immediately made the name of Jesus famous throughout the land.
When Jesus left the church official's house, two blind men who were crying followed him and they said, "Son of David, have mercy on us."

When Jesus entered another house, the blind men followed him in, and Jesus said to them, "`Do you believe that I can heal you and give your sight back to you?´" And they said, "Yes Lord, we believe that you can."
Jesus touched their eyes and said, "`Then your faith will make it so.´"
Their eyes were opened, and Jesus spoke to them sternly and said, "`Do not tell anybody about this!´"
But when they left, they went out and told everyone what Jesus had done.
After the blind men left, Jesus' followers brought a mute to him that was possessed by a demon.
After Jesus cast out the demon, the mute man spoke and the people were astonished and they said, "Nothing like this has ever been seen in Israel."
But the Pharisees said, "He casts out demons through Satan, the prince of the devils."
Jesus traveled to all the cities and villages, where he taught in their synagogues and preached the gospel of the Kingdom of Heaven. Everywhere he went, he healed the people's sicknesses and diseases
But when Jesus saw the crowds, he was moved with compassion for them, because they were lost and weak. They were like sheep without a shepherd.
Then Jesus said to his disciples, "`The harvest truly is plentiful here, but there are not enough laborers in the field.´
`That's why the harvest Lord will send more laborers out into the field to gather his harvest.´"
Jesus gathered his twelve disciples together and gave them the power to cast out unclean demons, heal the sick, and cure all types of disease.
These are the names of Jesus' twelve apostles. The first one is Simon who is called Peter, and his brother Andrew. Then there is James who is Zebedee's son, and his brother John.
Then there is Philip, Bartholomew, Thomas, Matthew the tax collector, James the son of Alphaeus and Lebbaeus, whose surname was Thaddaeus.
Then Simon the Canaanite, and lastly Judas Iscariot who was the one who betrayed Jesus.
When Jesus sent these twelve apostles out, he said, "`Do not go near the Gentile cities, or enter any of the Samaritan cities.´
`But go and find the lost sheep from the House of Israel.´
`As you travel and preach, tell the people that the Kingdom of Heaven is here.´
`Heal the sick, cleanse the lepers, raise the dead, cast out demons. And you have received freely, so give freely.´
`Do not take any gold, silver, or brass money with you.´
`Do not bring any money, extra clothes or shoes, or even a walking stick when you travel, because you deserve to be fed and cared for when you are teaching.´
`When you go somewhere new, find a good person and stay there with them until you leave.´
`When you enter someone's home, be gracious and greet them politely.´
`If the people welcome you, share your peace with them, but if they do not welcome you, take your peace with you and leave their house.´
`If anyone does not receive you or listen to you, then shake the dust off your feet as you are leaving.´
`Truly I tell you; it will be better for the land of Sodom and Gomorrah on the day of judgment, than it will be for that city.´
`Beware, because I have sent you out as sheep among wolves, so you must be as wise as wisemen, and as harmless as doves.´
`Because they will turn you over to the courts and ridicule you in their churches.´
`You will be brought before governors and kings because of me; this is so you can witness to them and the Gentiles.´
`When they deliver you up for judgement, do not worry about what to say, because when that hour comes, I will give you the words to speak.´
`Because it will not be you speaking, but it will be your father's spirit speaking through you.´
`People will betray their own families, brothers will kill their brother, and children will turn against their parents and have them killed.´
`Everyone will hate you because of me, but whoever endures to the end will be saved.´
`If people in one city persecute you, simply flee to another. Because truly I tell you, you will not go through all the cities of Israel before the Son of Man returns.´
`The disciple cannot expect to be elevated above their teacher, and the servant cannot expect to be above their master.´

`Disciples must not expect to be treated better than their teacher or their Lord. If they insult your teacher and call him one of Beelzebub's demons, what do you think they will say about you and the others who work with your Lord?´
`That's why you should not fear them, because there is nothing they can cover up that will not be revealed, and there is nothing hidden that will not become known.´
`Whatever I teach you in the dark, you must tell everyone in the light, and whatever is whispered in your ear preach from the housetops.´
`Do not fear those who can kill the body but cannot kill the soul, instead fear the one who can destroy both the body and soul in hell.´
`Two sparrows are sold for a penny, but not one of them will fall to the ground without your father in heaven knowing it.´
`Every hair on your head is numbered.´
`So do not fear, because you are of more value to your father in Heaven than many sparrows.´
`That's why if anyone testifies for me before men, then I will testify for them before my father in heaven.´
`But anyone who denies me before men, then I will also deny them before my father in heaven.´
`Do not think that I have come to bring peace on earth, because I did not come to bring peace, I have come to bring a sword.´
`Because I have come to set father against son, daughter against mother, and daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law.´
`A man's enemies will be within his own household.´
`Anyone who loves their father or mother more than they love me is not worthy of me, and anyone who loves their son or daughter more than they love me, is not worthy of me.´
`Anyone who does not pick up their own cross and follow me, is not worthy of me.´
`Anyone who finds their own life will lose it, and anyone who loses their life for my sake will find it.´
`Anyone who receives you also receives me, and anyone who receives me receives the one who sent me.´
`If you welcome a prophet who speaks for God, you will receive a prophet's reward. And if you welcome someone who does good things, then you will receive the same blessings as they.´
`If you help any one of these children by giving them even a glass of water because they are my followers, truly I tell you, you will never lose your reward.´"
When Jesus finished instructing his disciples, he left to teach and preach in the cities.
When John the Baptist was in prison he heard about everything Jesus had been doing, and he sent two of his disciples to see him.
When they found him, they asked him, "Are you the one who is supposed to come, or should we keep looking for someone else?"
Jesus answered them and said, "`Go and tell John everything you have seen and heard.´
`The blind receive their sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf can hear, the dead are raised up, and the poor have the gospel preached to them.´
`And blessed is he, who is not offended by me.´"
As they were leaving, Jesus spoke to the multitudes about John and said, "`What did you go out into the wilderness to see? Did you go out to see a reed shaken by the wind?´
`Did you go out to see a man dressed in fancy clothes? Because, you know that people who wear fancy clothes live in the king's houses.´
`Instead you went out to see prophet. But truly I tell you, you have seen much more than just a prophet.´
`Because this is the one that the prophets wrote about when they said, 'I will send my messenger out ahead, to prepare the way for you.'´
`And I tell you this, no one ever born is greater than John the Baptist, but even the least in God's kingdom are greater than him.´
`Ever since John the Baptist started preaching, the Kingdom of Heaven has suffered much violence, and the violent ones are trying to take control.´
`Up until John came, the prophets have been preaching about God's laws and rules.´
`But if you are willing to accept it, this is the Elijah who is supposed to come.´
`Anyone who has ears to hear, let them hear.´
`How can I describe the people of this generation? They are like children sitting in the marketplace shouting at their friends.´
`We played the flute for you, but you would not dance, we tried to share your grief, but you did not grieve.´
`People said that John was demon possessed because he did not eat or drink.´
`The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and they said I was a greedy drunkard, and a friend of tax collectors and sinners. But wisdom is justified by her children.´"
Then Jesus renounced the cities where most of his miracles had been performed, because they refused to repent.

And Jesus said, "`Woe unto Chorazin and Bethsaida! Because if the miracles that happened there had happened in Tyre and Sidon, they would havve repented a long time ago, and they would be wearing sackcloth and ashes.´
`But I say to you, on judgement day things will be better for Tyre and Sidon, than it will be for you.´
`Capernaum, you are glorified in heaven, but you will be brought down to hell. Because if the miracles that happened there had happened in Sodom, Sodom would still be standing today.´
`But I tell you, it will be more tolerable for Sodom on the day of judgment, than it will be for you.´"
Then Jesus said, "`Thank you, father, Lord of heaven and earth, for hiding these things from the wise and learned, and revealing them to little children.´
