`Because it seemed good to you father.´
`My father has given me authority, but no one knows the son except the father. No one knows the father except the son and those to whom the son chooses to reveal himself.´
`Come unto me, all you who labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.´
`Take my yoke, and learn about me, because I am meek and lowly in heart, and your souls will find rest in me.´
`Because my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.´"
On the Sabbath, Jesus was walking through a wheat field with his disciples and they were hungry, so they began to pick the wheat heads and eat them.
When the Pharisees saw this, they said to him, "Your disciples are breaking the Sabbath law."
But he said to them, "`Did you not read what David, and his followers did when they were hungry?´
`How they went into God's house and took the priest's bread, which was only for the priests, and it was unlawful for David and his companions to eat it?´
`Have you not read the laws that say when the temple priests break the Sabbath laws, they are not guilty?´
`But I tell you, there is one right here who is greater than the temple.´
`But if you understood what I meant when I said, 'I ask for mercy, and not sacrifice!' Then you would not have condemned the innocent.´
`Because the Son of Man is Lord even of the Sabbath day.´"
When he left, he went into their synagogue.

There was a man there with a crippled hand, and they asked him if it was lawful to heal on the Sabbath? They asked him this because they were trying to make him say something that they could use against him.
And he said to them, "`If one of you had a sheep, and it fell into a pit on the Sabbath day, would you not reach down into the pit and pull it out?´
`How much more valuable is a man than a sheep? That's why it is lawful to do good things on the Sabbath.´"
Then Jesus said to the man, "`Stretch out your hand,´" so he stretched out his hand, and it was healed.
Then the Pharisees left, and they met to scheme and plot and make a plan to destroy Jesus.
But Jesus knew what they were up to and he left, but the crowds followed him, and he healed them all.
And told them all that he did not want them to tell people what he had done.
This was to fulfill what the prophet Isaiah was talking about.
When Isaiah said, "This is my servant, the one I love and the one I have chosen. I am well pleased with him, and I will put my Spirit on him, and he will judge the Gentiles.
He will not fight or shout, and no one will hear his voice in the streets.
He will not break a bruised reed, or snuff out a smoldering wick, until he sends judgement to victory.
And the Gentiles will trust in his name."
Then they brought him a demon possessed man who was blind and dumb, Jesus healed him, and the man could both speak and see.
The people were amazed and they said, "Is this the son of David?"
But when the Pharisees heard this, they said, "This man uses the power of Beelzebub, the prince of demons to cast out demons."
But Jesus knew what they were thinking and he said to them, "`A kingdom divided against itself is brought to destruction, and house divided against itself cannot stand.´
`If Satan casts out Satan, he is divided against himself, so how can his kingdom stand?´
`And if I use Beelzebub to cast out demons, who do your children use to cast them out, and that's why they will be your judges.´
`But if I use God's Spirit to cast out demons, then the Kingdom of God has come to you.´
`How can someone break into a strong man's house, and destroy his stuff, without tying him up first.´
`If you are not with me, then you are against me, and if you do not help me gather, then you scatter abroad.´
`That's why I say, 'All sin and blasphemy will be forgiven, but blasphemy against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven.´
`Anyone who speaks against the Son of Man will be forgiven, but whoever speaks against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven, not in this world nor the world to come.'´
`Either make the tree and its fruit good, or make the tree and its fruit corrupt, because the tree is known by its fruit.´
`O you wicked vipers! How can you be evil and say good things? Because the mouth says what the heart is full of.´
`A good man with good treasure in his heart produces good things, and an evil man with evil treasure in his heart produces evil things.´
`But I tell you, on the day of judgment, every man will give an accounting of every idle word that they have spoken.´
`Because you will either be vindicated or condemned by your words.´"
Then some of the Pharisee scribes said, "Master, show us a sign."
But he answered them and said, "`An evil and adulterous generation seeks a sign, and no sign will be given to them, except for a sign from the prophet Jonah.´
`Because in the same way that Jonah spent three days and three nights in the belly of the whale, the Son of Man will be in the heart of the earth for three days and three nights.´
`One day the people of Nineveh will stand up and judge this generation, and they will condemn it. Because they repented when Jonah preached to them, and now someone greater than Jonah is here!´

`The queen of the south will rise up and judge with this generation and condemn it. Because she came from the farthest parts of the earth to hear Solomon's wisdom, and now someone greater than Solomon is here.´
`When an unclean demon leaves a man, it walks through dry places seeking rest and it finds none.´
`Then it returns to the house where it came out of the person, and it finds the place empty, swept clean, and decorated.´
`Then the demon brings seven more demons even more evil than itself. They enter the person, and they become worse off than they were before. That's how it will be for this wicked generation.´"
While he was talking to the people, his mother and brothers stood outside, asking to speak with him.
Then someone said to him, "Your mother and brothers are outside, and they want to talk to you."
But he answered them and said, "`Who is my mother, and who are my brothers?´"
And he stretched out his hand and pointed toward his disciples and said, "`Behold these are my mother and my brothers!´
`Because whoever does my heavenly father's will, are my brother, sister, and mother.´"
That day Jesus left the house to go and sit by the seashore.
Great crowds of people began to gather around him, so he went and sat in a fishing boat, and they stood on the shore before him.
Then he spoke to them in parables about many things and said, "`Listen carefully, a farmer went out to sow his seed.´
`As he sowed, some of the seed fell along the path and the birds came and devoured them.´
`Some fell on stony ground where there was not much topsoil, but because there was not much topsoil they immediately sprouted.´
`But when the sun rose, they were scorched, and because they had no root they withered away.´
`Some fell among the thorns, and the thorns grew and choked them out.´
`Other seeds fell on good ground and produced grain, some a hundredfold, some sixtyfold, and some thirtyfold.´
`Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear.´"
And the disciples came to him and asked, "Why do you speak to the people in parables?"
Jesus answered them and said, "`You have been given the knowledge of the mysteries of the Kingdom of Heaven, but they have not been given this knowledge.´
`Because whoever has much will be given even more abundance, but whoever does not have much, will have what they do have taken away from them.´
`So I speak to them in parables, because even though they have their sight, they do not see, and even though they listen, they do not hear, nor do they understand.´
`This satisfies Isaiah's prophecy which says, 'Even though you hear, you will not understand, and even though you see, you will not perceive.'´

`Because these people's hearts have grown callous, they barely hear with their ears, and their eyes are closed. Otherwise, they would see with their eyes and hear with their ears. Then they would understand with their heart and turn to me, so I could heal them.´
`But blessed are your eyes and ears, because you see and hear.´

`For I truly say to you, 'Many prophets and righteous men have desired to see the things which you have seen, but they have not seen them. And they desire to hear the things which you have heard, but they have not heard them.'´"
And Jesus said, "`So, listen carefully, and I will explain the parable of the farmer.´
`When someone hears the message of the kingdom but does not understand it, the wicked one will come and snatch away what was sown in his heart. This is the seed that was sown along the path.´
`But the seed that was sown in rocky ground, is the one who hears the word and immediately receives it with great joy.´
`But the word does not take root in him, and it only endures for a little while, and when tribulation or persecution comes because of the word, he is offended and gives up.´
`He is also the one who received the seed sown among the thorns. He hears the word, but he cares more for this world and the deceitfulness of riches, so it chokes the word and he becomes unfruitful.´
`But the one who receives the seed sown on good ground is the one who hears the word, who understands and it bears fruit and produces crops, some a hundredfold, some sixtyfold, and some thirtyfold.´"
And Jesus told them another parable and said, "`The Kingdom of Heaven is like a man who sowed good seed in his field.´
`But while he slept, his enemy came and sowed weeds among the wheat and ran away.´
`When the wheat sprouted, it grew and produced grain, but the weeds also appeared.´
`So the household servants came to him and said, 'Sir, we sowed good seed in your field, so where did all these weeds come from?´'
`He answered them and said, 'An enemy has done this to me.' And the servants said to him, 'Do you want us to go and pull the weeds from the field?'´
`But he answered them and said, 'No, because when you pull the weeds, you will disturb the wheat's roots.'´
`Let them grow together until harvest time, then I will tell the harvesters to gather and bundle the weeds first to be burned, then harvest the wheat to put in the barn.'´"
Then he told them another parable and said, "`The Kingdom of Heaven is like a mustard seed that a man sows in his field.´
`The mustard seed is the smallest of all the seeds, but when it grows it becomes the greatest of plants and grows into a tree, and the birds come and live in its branches.´"
Once again he told them another parable and said, "`The Kingdom of Heaven is like a woman who put some yeast into three measures of flour to make her bread rise.´"
Jesus always used parables to teach the people, and he spoke to the crowds of people about all of these things in parables.
He did this to fulfill the prophecy that the prophet spoke of when he said, "I will speak in parables and say things that have been kept secret since the world's foundation was laid."
When Jesus sent the crowds away and went into the house, his disciples came to him and said, "Please explain the parable of the weeds in the field to us."
He answered them and said, "`The Son of Man is the one who sows the good seed.´
`The field is the world, and the good seed are the children of the kingdom, but the weeds are the children of the wicked one.´
`The enemy who sowed the weeds is the devil, the harvest is the end of the world, and the harvesters are the angels.´
`As the weeds are bundled together and burned in the fire, that's how it will be at the end of this world.´
`The Son of Man will send angels into his kingdom to gather up all of the immoral and offensive weeds.´
`Then he will throw them into a fiery furnace, and there will be much weeping and gnashing of teeth.´
`The righteous will shine like the sun in their father's kingdom. Whoever has ears to hear, let them hear.´
`Again, the Kingdom of Heaven is like a treasure hidden in a field. When a man finds it, he hides it, and joyfully goes to sell everything that he owns, and when he returns, he buys the field.´
`Again, the Kingdom of Heaven is like a merchant looking for good pearls.´
`When he finds a pearl of great value, he sells everything that he owns and goes and buys it.´
`Again, the Kingdom of Heaven is like a net thrown into the sea, that gathers every kind of fish.´
`When it was full they pulled it to shore and sat down, and they put the good fish in their barrels, but they threw the bad fish away.´
`That's the way it will be at the end of the world; the angels will come and separate the wicked from the just.´
`They will throw the wicked into the fiery furnace, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.´"
Then Jesus asked his disciples, "`Do you understood everything I have told you?´" And they said, "Yes Lord."
And he spoke to them again and said, "`Every disciple who has been taught about the Kingdom of Heaven is like a homeowner, who brings new and old treasures from his storeroom.´"
When Jesus finished telling them all of these parables he left them.
When he arrived back in his own country, he taught the people in their synagogues. They were astonished and they asked, "Where did this man get his wisdom and such miraculous powers?
Is he not Mary and Joseph the carpenter's son? Are not his brothers named James, Joseph, Simon, and Judas?
Are not all of his sisters with us? Where then did this man get all of this knowledge?"
They were offended by Jesus, but he said to them, "`A prophet is only without honor in his own home and his own country.´"
And because of their disbelief, he did not perform many miracles there.
At that time Governor Herod heard about Jesus.
Herod spoke to his servants and said, "This Jesus must be John the Baptist risen from the dead, because these miraculous works reveal themselves through him.
Herod said this because he had ordered John the Baptist to be put in shackles, arrested, and imprisoned to make his wife Queen Herodias happy. Herodias was Herod's dead brother Philip's widow.
Herodias had done this because John the Baptist had said to Herod, "It is unlawful for you to be with your dead brother's wife."
Herod would have put him to death, but he was afraid of the people because they believed John the Baptist was a prophet.
But when they celebrated Herod's birthday, Herodias had her daughter dance for the guests, which pleased Herod.
Herod was so pleased that he swore an oath and promised to give her anything she asked for.
Herodias had instructed her daughter and told her what to say to Herod beforehand, and her daughter answered Herod and said, "Bring me John Baptist's head on a platter."
The king was very grieved, but he had sworn an oath in front of his guests, so he ordered his servants to fulfill her request.
So the king sent word to the prison to have John the Baptist beheaded.
Then they brought John's head to her on a platter, and she gave it to her mother.
Then John's disciples buried his body, and they went to tell Jesus what had happened to John.
When Jesus heard the news, he took a ship to a private solitary place. When the people heard that Jesus had left, they followed him on foot from the cities.
As Jesus left the ship, he saw the large crowd coming toward him, and he felt compassion for them and healed their sick.
In the evening, his disciples came to him and said, "This is such a desolate place, and it is getting late. Send the crowd away, so they can go into the villages and buy themselves some food."
But Jesus said, "`They do not need to leave, you can give them something to eat.´"
They replied to him and said, "We have nothing here but five loaves of bread and two fish."
And Jesus said, "`Bring them to me.´"

Then he told the crowd to sit on the grass, and he took the five loaves and the two fish, and he looked up to heaven. He blessed and broke the loaves of bread and gave them to his disciples who distributed it to the crowd.
After everyone ate, they picked up the leftovers which filled twelve baskets full of food.
They fed about 5,000 men, women, and children that day.
Shortly afterwards, Jesus made his disciples take a boat to the other side of the sea ahead of him, as he sent the crowds away.
After Jesus sent the crowds away, he went up into the mountains all by himself to pray, and when evening came, he was alone.
By that time, the boat was in the middle of the sea, and it was being tossed around by the waves, because the wind blew against it.
During the fourth watch of the night Jesus came toward them, walking on the water.
When the disciples saw him walking on the water, they were terrified and said, "It is a ghost!" And they cried out in fear.
But immediately Jesus spoke up and said, "`Cheer up it's only me, do not be afraid.´"
Peter answered him and said, "Lord, if it is you, command me to walk to you on the water."
And Jesus said, "`Peter come to me!´" When he stepped out of the boat, he walked toward Jesus on the water.
But the wind blew violently and he was afraid and began to sink, so he cried out to Jesus and said, "Lord, save me!"
And immediately Jesus reached out his hand and caught him and said, "`O you of little faith, why did you doubt?´"
Then as they stepped into the boat, the wind ceased.
Then everyone in the boat worshipped him and said, "It is true! You are the Son of God."
After they crossed the sea, they arrived in the land of Gennesaret.
When the men there realized who Jesus was, they sent word to everyone throughout the land, and the people brought all of their sick and diseased to him.
And they all begged him to just let them touch the hem of his garment, and anyone who touched him was healed.
Then the scribes and Pharisees from Jerusalem came to Jesus.
And they said, "Why do your disciples break the traditions of the elders? They do not even wash their hands when they eat."
But Jesus answered them and said, "`Why do you also transgress against God's commandments with your traditions?´
`For God said, 'Honor your father and mother, and whoever curses their father or mother, must be put to death.'´
`But you say, 'Whoever says to his father or mother, "If you receive a gift from me, it will be profited to me by God."'´
`Then you say that he does not need to honor his father or mother, and he will be set free because of his gift. This is how you have made God's commandment ineffective by your traditions.´
`You hypocrites, Isaiah prophesied well about you.´
`When he said, 'These people draw near to me with their mouth, and honor me with their lips, but their heart is far from me.'´
`But they worship me in vain, teaching the commandments of men as their doctrines.´"
Then Jesus summoned the crowd to him and he said, `"Hear this and understand.´
`It is not what goes into a man's mouth that defiles a man, but it is what comes out of his mouth that defiles a man.´"
Then his disciples came to him and said, "Do you not understand that the Pharisees were offended, when they heard what you said?"
But Jesus them answered and said, `"Any plant that my heavenly father did not plant, will be uprooted and discarded.´
`So leave them alone, for they are the blind leading the blind, and if the blind lead the blind, both will fall into the ditch.´"
Then Peter said to Jesus, "Explain this parable to us."
And Jesus said, "`Do you still not understand what this means?´
`Do you not know that whatever enters through the mouth goes into the stomach, and is thrown down the drain?´
`But the things which proceed from the mouth come from the heart, and it is those things that defile a man.´
`Therefore, evil thoughts such as murders, adulteries, fornications, thefts, false witness, and blasphemies proceed from the heart.´
`And these are the things which defile a man, but eating with unwashed hands does not defile a man.´"
Then Jesus left there and journeyed to the coasts of Tyre and Sidon.
And, behold a Canaanite woman from that area came to him and cried out, "O Lord son of David, have mercy on me, my daughter is grievously possessed by a demon."
But he did not answer her, and his disciples came to him and said, "Send her away, because she keeps crying to us."
But Jesus answered them and said, "`I have not been sent just to find the lost sheep of the House of Israel.´"
Then she came and worshipped him and said, "Lord, help me."
But Jesus answered her and said, "`It is not right to take the children's bread and throw it to the dogs.´"
And she said, "Yes that is true Lord, but even the dogs eat the crumbs that fall from their master's table."
Then Jesus answered her and said, "`O woman, your faith is great, so let your will be done.´" And her daughter was healed that very hour.
Then Jesus left and passed by the Sea of Galilee, and he went up into the mountains and sat down.
And a great crowd came to him with their lame, blind, mute, maimed, crippled, and many other problems, and they laid them at the feet of Jesus, and he healed them.
The crowd was amazed when they saw the mute speak, the maimed and crippled made whole, the lame walk, and the blind made to see. And they glorified the God of Israel.

Then Jesus summoned his disciples and said, "`I have compassion for this crowd, because they have been with me for three days with nothing to eat. And I will not send them away hungry, or they may faint on their way home.´"
And his disciples spoke to him and said, "Where can we find enough bread in the wilderness to feed such a large crowd?
And Jesus answered them and said, "`How many loaves do you have?´" And they said, "Seven, and a few little fish."
Then Jesus commanded the crowd to sit down on the ground.
He took the seven loaves and the fish and gave thanks, and broke them up, and gave the pieces to his disciples, and the disciples gave it to the crowd.
They all ate and were filled, and the disciples collected seven baskets full of meat and bread from what was left over.
4,000 men, plus all the women and children were fed.
When Jesus sent the crowd away, and he took a ship to the coast of Magdala.
The Pharisees and Sadducees came and tempted Jesus, because they wanted to see a heavenly sign from him.
But he answered them and said, "`When the evening comes you say, 'The weather will be fair, because the sky is red.'´

`And in the morning you say, 'There will be foul weather today, because the sky is red and overcast.' O you hypocrites, you recognize the signs of the sky, but do you not recognize the signs of the times.´
`A wicked and adulterous generation looks for a sign, but there will be no sign, except for the sign of the prophet Jonah.´" Then Jesus left them and went away.
When his disciples came to him on the other side, they had forgotten to bring bread.
Then Jesus spoke to them said, "`Take heed and beware of the leavening of the Pharisees and Sadducees.´"
And they reasoned among themselves and asked, "Is this because we have brought no bread?"
When Jesus heard them talking, he said, "`O you of little faith, why do you question yourselves because you have brought no bread?´
`Do you still not understand, and do you not remember the five loaves that fed 5,000 people, and how many baskets of leftovers you picked up afterwards?´
`Do you not remember the seven loaves of bread that fed 4,000 people, and how many baskets of leftovers you picked up afterwards?´
`How do you not understand that I was not speaking to you about bread, when I told you to beware of the leavening of the Pharisees and Sadducees?´"
Then they understood that Jesus was not telling them to beware of the leavening of bread, but he was warning them about the teachings of the Pharisees and Sadducees.
When Jesus arrived at the coast of Caesarea Philippi, he questioned his disciples and asked, "`Who do men say that the Son of Man is?´"
And they said, "Some say you are John the Baptist, some say Elijah, and others say you are Jeremiah or one of the other prophets."
Then Jesus asked them, "`But who do you say that I am?´"
Simon Peter answered and said, "You are the Christ, the Son of the living God."
And Jesus answered him and said, "`Blessed are you, Simon son of Jonah! For this has not been revealed to you by flesh and blood, it has been revealed to you by my father in heaven.´
`And I also say that you are Peter, and upon this rock, I will build my church, and the gates of hell will not prevail against it.´
`Therefore, I will give you the keys to the Kingdom of Heaven, and whatever you bind here on earth will be bound in heaven, and whatever you set loose here on earth will be released in heaven.´"
Then Jesus charged his disciples and told them not to tell any man that he was the Christ.

From that day forward Jesus began to show his disciples that he must go to Jerusalem and suffer many things at the hands of the elders, chief priests, and scribes. And that he would be killed and raised to life again on the third day.
Then Peter took him aside and began to reprimand him and said, "Far be it from you, Lord, this will not happen to you."
But Jesus turned to Peter and said, "`Get behind me Satan, you are offensive to me because you do not think of the things of God, but you are only concerned of the things of men.´"
Then Jesus spoke to his disciples and said, "`If a man wants to follow me, he must deny himself and take up his cross and follow me.´
`For whoever desires to save his own life will lose it, and whoever loses his life for my sake will find it.´
`For what does it profit a man if he gains the whole world, and loses his own soul, or what will a man give in exchange for his soul?´
`Because the Son of Man will come in his father's glory with his angels, and he will reward each person for the things that they have done.´
`Truly I tell you; there are those standing here who will not taste death until they see the Son of Man coming in his kingdom.´"
After six days Jesus took Peter, James, and his brother John up into the high mountains with him.
Then Jesus was transfigured before them. His face shone like the sun, and his clothes were as brilliant white as the light.
Suddenly, Moses and Elijah appeared and they were speaking with Jesus.
Then Peter spoke to Jesus and asked, "Lord, it is good that we are here. If you want, we will make three tabernacles, one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah."
As Peter spoke, behold a bright cloud overshadowed them, and a voice came from the cloud which said, "This is my beloved son, in whom I am well pleased. Listen to him!"
And when the disciples heard this, they fell facedown, and they were extremely frightened.
Then Jesus came and touched them and said, "`Get up and do not be afraid.´"
When they looked up, they saw no one except for Jesus.
As they came down from the mountain, Jesus spoke to them and said, "`Do not tell anyone about the vision, until the Son of Man has risen from the dead.´"
Then his disciples spoke to him and asked, "Why do the scribes say that Elijah must first come?"
So Jesus answered them and said, "`Elijah will truly come and restore all things first.´
`But I say to you, that Elijah has already come, and they did not know him, but they have done to him whatever they wished. This is the same way that the Son of Man will suffer from them.´"
Then the disciples understood that Jesus was speaking to them about John the Baptist.
When they came to the crowd, a man came to Jesus and knelt down to him.
Then the man said, "Lord, have mercy on my son, because he is lunatic who suffers from seizures, and he often falls into the fire or the water.
So I brought him to your disciples, but they could not cure him."
Then Jesus answered the man and said, "`O faithless and perverse generation, how long must I remain with you? How long can I tolerate you? Bring the boy to me.´"
And Jesus reprimanded the demon, and the demon left the boy, and the child was cured from that very hour.
Then the disciples came to Jesus privately and asked, "Why could we not cast out this demon?"

And Jesus answered them and said, "`It is because you have so little faith. For truly I tell you, if you have faith the size of a mustard seed, and you say to this mountain, 'Move from here to there!' It will move, and nothing will be impossible for you.´
`However this kind of demon will only leave through prayer and fasting.´"
While they were living in Galilee, Jesus said to them, "`The Son of Man will be betrayed into the hands of men.´
`And they will kill him, but on the third day he will be raised to life again!´" And they were extremely grieved.
When they arrived in Capernaum, the tax collectors came to Peter and asked, "Does your master not pay tribute taxes?"

Peter answered them and said, "Yes he does." When Peter entered the house, Jesus stopped him and said, "`What do you think Simon? Who do the kings of the earth collect their customs or tribute taxes from? Do they collect taxes from their own children, or from strangers?´"
Peter answered him and said, "They collect taxes from strangers." So, Jesus said, "`So are the children free of taxes?´

`Therefore, just so we do not offend them, go to the sea and throw out a hook. Then take the first fish you catch, open his mouth and you will find a piece of money, take it and give to the tax collectors for me and you.´"
At the same time the disciples came to Jesus and asked, "Who is the greatest in the Kingdom of Heaven?"
Jesus called a little child to come to him and set him in the middle of the group.
And Jesus said, "Truly I tell you; unless you are converted and become like little children, you will not enter into the Kingdom of Heaven.
Therefore, whoever humbles himself like this little child, will be the greatest in the Kingdom of Heaven.
Whoever welcomes anyone like this little child in my name, welcomes me.
But whoever causes one of these children who believe in me to sin, would be better off to have a millstone hung around his neck, then drowned at the bottom of the sea.
Woe unto the world because of sin! For sin must come, but woe unto the man through which the sin comes!

Furthermore, if your hand or foot causes you to sin, cut it off and throw it away. It is better to enter life maimed or crippled than to have both hands and both feet and be thrown into the everlasting fire.
If your eye causes you to sin, pluck it out and throw it away, it is better for you to enter life with one eye, rather than keep both eyes and be thrown into hell fire.
Make sure that you do not despise any of these little children, because I am telling you that their angels in heaven always see the face of my father in heaven.
For the Son of Man has come to save that which was lost."
And Jesus said, "What do you think? If a man has a hundred sheep and one of them has gone astray, does he not leave the ninety-nine, and go up into the mountains to look for the one that is lost?
Truly I tell you; if he finds that lost sheep he will rejoice more over it, than any of the other ninety-nine that did not go astray.
Even so, it is not the will of your father in heaven, that any of these children should perish.
Furthermore, if your brother trespasses against you, go and confront him alone and in private, if he listens to you, you have found your brother.
But if he will not listen to you, then take one or two others with you, so that every fact can be established with the testimony of two or three witnesses.
If he refuses to listen to them, then tell the church. But if he refuses to listen to the church, then you have lost your brother, and he will be like a heathen or a publican to you.
Truly I tell you; whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven, and whatever you let loose on earth will be turned loose in heaven.
Again I tell you, if two of you agree on earth about anything and ask for it, then my father in heaven will do what you ask.
For wherever two or three or more are gathered together in my name, there I will be also."
Then Peter spoke to Jesus and asked, "Lord, how often should I forgive my brother who has sinned against me, should I forgive him seven times?"
Jesus answered him and said, "I tell you, not just seven times, but seventy-seven times!
Because, the Kingdom of Heaven is like a king, who wanted to settle his accounts with his servants.
When he started calculating, one of them owed him 10,000 talents.
But because he did not have the money to pay, the king ordered him to be sold to pay the debt, along with his wife and children and everything that he owned.
Then the servant fell on his knees before the king and said, 'Lord, have patience with me, and I will repay you everything that I owe.'
The servant's king was moved with compassion, then had him released and forgave his debt.
But that same servant left, and went to find one of his fellow servants, who owed him a hundred pence. He grabbed him by the throat and said, 'Pay me what you owe me.'
His fellow servant fell down at his knees and implored him and said, 'Please have patience with me, and I will pay you everything I owe you.'
But he refused to wait, so he went and had him thrown into debtors prison, until he could pay the debt.
So when his fellow servants saw what happened, they were very upset and they went and told the king what had happened.
After the king heard this, he summoned his servant and said, 'O you wicked servant, I forgave you of all your debt, because you begged me.
You should have also had compassion for your fellow servant, like the mercy that I had for you!
And the king was angry and turned him over to the jailers to be tortured, until he could pay what he owed.
This is how my heavenly father will treat you, unless you forgive your brothers for their sins from your hearts."
After Jesus finished saying these things, he left Galilee and went to the coasts of Judea beyond the Jordan River.
A laege crowd followed him, and he healed them there.
The Pharisees also came to test him and they asked, "Is it legal for a man to divorce his wife for any reason?"
And Jesus answered them and said, "`Have you not read, that the one who made them in the beginning, made them both male and female?`
`This is why a man will leave his father and mother, and hold loyally to his wife, and the two will become one flesh?´
`Therefore they are no longer two, but one flesh. So whatever God has joined together, let no man pull apart.´"
Then they asked him, "Why then, did Moses command a man to give his wife a written divorce paper and send her away?"
Jesus answered them and said, "`Moses allowed this because your rock-hard hearts caused you to divorce your wives, but it was not this way in the beginning.'

`But I tell you, that whoever divorces his wife unless it is because of fornication, and marries another woman, commits adultery, and whoever marries this man's wife after she is divorced, commits adultery.´"
Then the disciples said to Jesus, "If this is the case with a man and his wife, then it best not to marry."
But Jesus said to them, "`Not all men can accept this, except for those to whom it is intended.´

`For some eunuchs were born that way, and some eunuchs were made that way by men. Then there are eunuchs, who live that way for the sake of the Kingdom of Heaven. So let the man who is able to accept this, do so.´"
Then they brought little children to him, so that he could lay his hands on them and pray, and the disciples reprimanded them.
But Jesus said, "`Do not forbid the little children to come to me, but let them come, because the Kingdom of Heaven belongs to those such as these.´"
Then he laid his hands on them and left.
A young man came to Jesus and asked, "Good Master, what good thing can I do to have eternal life?"
And Jesus answered him and said, "`Why do you call me good? There is no one good except for the One True God, but if you want to enter into eternal life, keep the commandments.'"
Then the young man asked him, "Which commandments?" Jesus answered him and said, "`Do not commit murder, do not commit adultery, do not steal, do not bear false witness.´
`Honor your father and your mother and love your neighbor as you love yourself.´"
And the young man said, "I have kept all of these commandments since I was young, is there anything else I need to do?"
Jesus said to him, "`If you want to be perfect, go and sell everything that you own, give the money to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. Then come and follow me.´"
But when the young man heard this, he went away very sad because he was very wealthy.
Then Jesus spoke to his disciples and said, "`Truly I tell you; it is very difficult for a rich man to enter the Kingdom of Heaven.´
`And again I tell you, it is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle, than it is for a rich man to enter into the Kingdom of God.´
When his disciples heard this, they were extremely amazed and asked, "Then who can be saved?"
But Jesus looked at them and said, "`With men salvation is impossible, but with God all things are possible.´"
Then Peter answered Jesus and said, "Behold we have forsaken everything to follow you, what will we receive in return?"

And Jesus said, "`Truly I tell you; when all things are renewed and the Son of Man sits on his throne of glory, those of you who have followed me will also sit on twelve thrones and judge the twelve tribes of Israel.´
`Anyone who has forsaken houses, brothers, sisters, fathers, mothers, a wife, children, or lands for my name's sake, will receive a hundred times more, and inherit everlasting life.´
`But many who are first will be last, and those who are last will be first.´"
And Jesus said, "`For the Kingdom of Heaven is like a vineyard owner, who left early in the morning to hire workers for his vineyard.´
`After he agreed to hire the workers for a penny a day, he sent them out to his vineyard.´
`At about the third hour he left and went to the marketplace, where he saw others idly standing around.'
`And the vineyard owner said to them, 'If you want to work in the vineyard, I will pay you whatever is right,' so they went to work.´
`Then he left the vineyard again at about the sixth and ninth hours and did the same thing.´
`At about the eleventh hour he left, and found others standing around idle and he spoke to them and asked, 'Why are you just standing around?'´
`And they answered him and said, 'Because no one has hired us.' So, he said to them, 'If you go out and work in the vineyard, I will also pay you whatever is right.'´
`So when evening came, the vineyard owner said to his manager, 'Call the workers and give them their pay, and pay the last hired first, then pay the first hired.'´"
And Jesus said, "`So, when those who were hired at about the eleventh hour came, each man was paid a penny.´
`But when those who were hired first came, they thought they should be paid more, but they were each paid one penny.´
`After they received their pay, they grumbled about the vineyard owner.´
`And the first hired men said, 'These people that you hired last have only worked one hour, and you paid them the same as us. But we carried the full burden and worked through heat of the day.´
`But the vineyard owner answered them and said, 'Friend, I have done you no wrong, did you not agree to work for me for one penny?´
`So take what is yours and go. Because I decided to pay the last man hired the same amount that I paid you.´
`Is it unlawful for me to do whatever I want with my own money? Are you jealous because I am generous?´
`So last will be first, and first will be last, because many will be called, but few will be chosen.´"
Jesus was going to Jerusalem with his twelve disciples, and he continued to speak to them along the way.
And he said, "`Behold, we are going to Jerusalem, where the Son of Man will be betrayed to the chief priests and scribes. And they will condemn him to death.´
`They will deliver him to the Gentiles to be mocked, flogged, and crucified. But on the third day he will be resurrected.´"
Then the mother of Zebedee's sons came to Jesus with her sons, because they wanted to worship and request something from him.
And Jesus asked her, "`What do you want?´" She replied to him and said, "Please let my two sons sit beside you in your kingdom, one on your right and the other on your left."

But Jesus answered her and said, "`You do not understand what you are asking. Can you drink from the cup that I must drink from, and are you baptized with the baptism with which I am baptized?´" They answered and said, "Yes."

Jesus responded to them and said, "`You will indeed drink from my cup, and you will be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with. But who will sit at my right or left hand, is not my decision to make, but it is for my father to decide, and he will give it to those for whom he prepared it.´"
When the ten other disciples heard this, they were upset and indignant with the two brothers.
But Jesus took them aside and said, "`You know that the Gentile princes exercise authority over the people, and their superiors exercise authority over them.´
`But it will not be this way among you. For whoever wants to be great among you must be your minister.´
`And whoever wants to be first among you must be your servant.´
`Because the Son of Man did not come to be ministered to, but he came to minister to others and to give his life as a ransom for many souls.´"
As they left Jericho, a massive crowd followed Jesus.
And behold, there were two blind men sitting alongside of the road. When they heard Jesus passing by, they cried out and said, "O Lord, son of David, have mercy on us."
And the crowd reprimanded them and told them to hold their peace, but they cried out even louder and said, "O Lord, son of David, have mercy on us."
Then Jesus stopped and called out to them and said, "`What do you want me to do for you?´"
Then they said to him, "Lord, please open our eyes."
So Jesus had compassion on them and he touched their eyes, and they immediately received their sight and they followed him.
As Jesus and the disciples approached Jerusalem, after they went to Bethphage on Mount Olive, Jesus sent two disciples on a mission.
Jesus instructed them and said, "`Go to the village next door where you will find a donkey and her colt tied. Untie them and bring them to me.´
`If anyone asks what you are doing, tell them that the Lord needs them, and they will send them with you away.´
`This will be done to satisfy what was prophesied.´
`When the prophet said, 'Tell Sion's daughter, behold your meek and gentle king comes to you riding on a donkey colt, the foal of a donkey.´"
So the disciples went to do what Jesus had commanded them.
They brought the donkey and the colt, and laid their cloaks on them, and Jesus sat on them.
Then a huge crowd spread their garments along the way, others cut branches from the trees and spread them on the road.
The crowd that went before Jesus, and those who followed him cried out and said, "Hosanna to the son of David, blessed is he that comes in the name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest!"
When Jesus entered Jerusalem, the entire city was excited and asked, "Who is this man?"
And the crowd said, "This is Jesus the prophet from Nazareth of Galilee."
Then Jesus went into God's temple and drove out all the merchants. He overturned all the tables and chairs of the money changers and dove sellers.
And Jesus said to them, "`It is written that my house will be called a house of prayer, but you have made it a den of thieves.´"
Then the blind and lame came to Jesus in the temple, and he healed them.
The chief priests and scribes were very upset when they saw the wonderous things Jesus had done, and heard the children in the temple shouting, "Hosanna to the son of David!"
So they asked Jesus, "Do you hear what they are saying?" And Jesus answered them and said, "`Have you never read, 'From the mouth of babes and infants God has perfected praise'?´"
Then Jesus left the city and went to stay in Bethany.
In the morning Jesus was hungry as he returned to the city.
And Jesus saw a fig tree along the way, but he found nothing on it but leaves. And he said to it, "`No fruit will ever grow on you again from now on and forever.´" Immediately the fig tree withered.
When the disciples saw this, they were amazed and said, "Why did this fig tree wither so fast!"

Jesus answered them and said, "`Truly I say to you, if you have faith and do not doubt, you will not only be able to do what has been done to the fig tree, but if you say to this mountain, 'Be gone from here and be thrown into the sea,' it will be done.´
`As with all things, if you believe, you will receive whatever you ask for in prayer.´"
When Jesus arrived at the temple, the people's chief priests and elders came to him as he was teaching and asked, "By what authority do you do these things, and who gave you this authority?"
And Jesus answered them and said, "`I would also like to ask you one thing, and if you answer me, I will likewise tell you by what authority I do these things.´
`Where did the baptism of John come from? Was it from heaven or from men?´" And they talked among themselves and said, "If we say it is from heaven, he will say, 'Then why did you not believe him?'
But if we say, 'It is from men,' then the people may attack us, because they believe John is a prophet."
So they answered Jesus and said, "We cannot say." And he said to them, "`Then I will not tell you by what authority I do these things.´"
And Jesus said, "`So, what do you think? There was a man who had two sons, and he came to the first one and said, 'Son, go out and work in my vineyard today.'´
`But the son answered him and said, 'No, I will not go,' but afterward he changed his mind and went to work.´
`Then he went to the second son and said the same thing, and the second son answered and said, 'Yes sir, I will go,' but he did not go.´

`Which of the two did the will of his father?´" They said to him, "The first son." Then Jesus said to them, "`Truly I tell you; tax collectors and prostitutes will enter the Kingdom of God before you do.´
`Because John came to you in righteousness, and you did not believe him, but the tax collectors and prostitutes believed him. And even after you saw the truth, you did not repent and believe him.´"

And Jesus said, "`Hear another parable, there was a landowner who planted a vineyard. He planted a hedge all around it, dug a winepress, and built a tower. Then he rented it out to some farmers, and he went away to a far distant country.´
`At harvest time he sent his servants to collect his share of the fruit from the farmers as payment.´
`But the farmers killed one of his servants, then beat one and stoned another.´
`Then the owner sent more servants than he did the first time, and they treated them the same way.´
`But last of all he sent his son to them because he thought they would respect his son.´
`But when the farmers saw the son, they plotted among themselves and said, 'This is the heir, if we kill him, we can seize his inheritance for ourselves.'´
`So they trapped him and threw him out of the vineyard and killed him.´
`So when the vineyard owner returns, what will he do to those farmers?´"
Then they said to him, "He will destroy those miserably wicked men, and lease his vineyard to other farmers, who will give him his share of the fruit when it is in season."

So Jesus answered them and said, "`Have you never read the scriptures that said, 'The stone that the builders rejected, is the stone that will become the cornerstone. This is from the Lord, and it is marvelous in our eyes'?´
`Therefore I say to you, the Kingdom of God will be taken from you, and given to a nation that will produce its fruits.´
`And whoever falls on this stone will be broken, but whoever it falls upon, will be ground to powder.´"
When the chief priests and Pharisees heard his parables, they figured out that Jesus was talking about them.
But they were afraid to seize Jesus, because the crowd thought of him as a prophet and they feared the people.
Jesus spoke to them in parables again.
And Jesus said, "`The Kingdom of Heaven is like a king, who arranged a marriage for his son.´
`He sent his servants to call on those who were invited to the wedding, but they would not come.´

`Again, he sent other servants and said, 'Tell those who are invited, that I have prepared my son's wedding. My fat oxen and cattle have been killed, and everything is ready, so please come to the wedding.'´
`But they made light of it, and went their own ways, one to his farm, another to his merchandise.´
`The rest of the attacked the king's servants and spitefully mistreated them, then killed them.´
`But when the king heard about it, he was angry, so he sent his armies to destroy the murderers, and burned up their city.´
`Then he said to his servants, 'The wedding has been prepared, but those I invited were not worthy.´
`Therefore, go out to the highways and invite as many people as you can find to the marriage.'´
`So those servants went out to the highways, and invited as many people as they could find, both good and bad, and the wedding hall was filled with guests.´
`When the king went to greet his guests, he saw a man there who was not dressed for a wedding.´
`And he said to him, 'Friend, how did you get in here without being dressed for a wedding?' But the man was speechless.´
`Then the king said to the servants, tie him up and take him and throw him out into the darkness, where there will be much weeping and gnashing of teeth.´
`For many are called, but few are chosen.´"
Then the Pharisees left and went to have a meeting about how they could trap Jesus with his own words.

They sent their disciples to Jesus along with the Herodians and said, "Master, we know that you are true, so teach us the ways of God's truth. We know you do not care about worldly things, because you do not regard the earthly person of men.
So tell us what you think? Is it lawful to pay taxes to Caesar or not?"
But Jesus understood their wicked intent and said, "`Why do you hypocrites test me?´
`Show me the tax money.´" And they brought him a penny.
And Jesus said to them, "`Whose image and inscription is on this coin?´"
And they said to him, "Caesar's." Then Jesus said to them, "`So, render unto Caesar that which belongs to Caesar and give to God that which belongs to God.´"
When they heard this, they were astonished, so they left him and went their own way.
That same day the Sadducees, who say that there is no resurrection came to see Jesus.
They spoke to Jesus and asked, "Master, Moses said that if a man dies without children, his brother must marry the widow and raise children for his brother.
Now there were seven brothers among us, and the first one married a wife and died with no children. So, he left his wife to his brother.
The same was true for the second, the third, and all the way to the seventh brother.
Then last of all the woman also died.
So in the resurrection, whose wife will she be from among the seven brothers, because they had all been married to her."
Jesus answered them and said, "`You are in error, you do not know the scriptures or the power of God.´
`For in the resurrection there will be no marriage, nor will they be given in marriage, but they will be like God's angels in heaven.´
`But about the resurrection, have you not read what God told you about life.´
`When God said, "I am the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob"? God is not the God of the dead, but of the living.´"
When the crowd heard this, they were astonished by his doctrine.
But when the Pharisees heard that he had silenced the Sadducees, they gathered together.
Then one of them who was a lawyer, tried to test Jesus with a question.
And the lawyer asked Jesus, "Master, what is the law's greatest commandment?"
Jesus said to him, "`'Love your Lord God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind.'´
`This is the first and greatest commandment.´
`And the second is like it, 'You must love your neighbor as you love yourself.'´
`These two commandments are the foundation of all the laws and the prophets.´"
Then Jesus continued to speak to the Pharisees while they were gathered together.
And he asked them, "`What do you think of Christ? Whose son do you think he is?´" And they said to him, "He is David's son."
So Jesus said to them, "`How then does David in the spirit call him Lord.´
`For David said, 'The Lord said to my Lord, sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies your footstool.'?´
`If David called him Lord, how can he be his son?´"
No one was able to answer him, and from that day forward they did not dare to ask him any more questions.
Then spoke Jesus to the crowds and his disciples.
And Jesus said, "`The scribes and Pharisees sit in Moses' seat.´
`Therefore observe and do whatever they tell you, but do not do the things that they do, because they do not practice what they teach.´
`For they lay heavy burdens and grievous loads to be carried on men's shoulders, but they themselves will not lift one little finger to help anyone.´
`But everything they do is just to be seen by other men, they broaden their amulets and enlarge their garment's borders.´
`They love the upper rooms at feasts, and the front seats in the synagogues.´
`They love being greeted in the markets and being called rabbi by men.´
`But do not let men call you 'Rabbi,' because Christ is your teacher, and you are all brothers.´
`Do not call anyone on earth your father, because you have one father, who is in heaven.´
`Do not let anyone call you master, because Christ is your teacher.´"
And Jesus said, "`But whoever is greatest among you will be your servant.´
`And whoever glorifies himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be glorified.´

`But woe unto you scribes and Pharisees, you are hypocrites! You close the Kingdom of Heaven to men, because you neither enter the kingdom yourselves, nor do you allow those who want to enter to go in.´
`Woe unto you hypocritical scribes and Pharisees! Because you devour widows' houses and pretend to make long prayers, so you will receive the greatest damnation.´
`Woe unto you hypocritical scribes and Pharisees! Because you surround sea and land to convert one believer, then you make him twice as much a son of hell as yourselves.´
`Woe unto you blind guides who say, 'It means nothing to swear by the temple, but whoever swears by the temple gold is a indebted!'´
`You blind men, which is greater, the gold, or the temple that sanctifies the gold?´
`And you say, 'It means nothing to swear by the altar, but whoever swears by the gift that is on the altar is guilty.'´
`You blind men, which is greater, the gift, or the altar that sanctifies the gift?´
`Therefore whoever swears by the altar, swears by it and everything that is on it.´"
And Jesus said, "`Whoever swears by the temple, swears by it, and him who lives there.´
`And whoever swears by heaven, swears by the throne of God, and by him who sits there.´

`Woe unto you hypocritical scribes and Pharisees! Because you pay tithes of mint, anise, and cummin, but you have omitted the important matters of law, judgment, mercy, and faith. You should have done these things, as well as the other things.´
`You blind guides who strain out a gnat but swallow a camel.´
`Woe unto you hypocritical scribes and Pharisees! Because you clean the outside of a cup and platter but leave the inside full of extortion and excess.´
`You blind Pharisee! First, cleanse the inside of the cup and platter, then clean the outside of them also.´
`Woe unto you hypocritical scribes and Pharisees! Because you are like white tombs, that appear beautiful outside, but you are full of dead men's bones and uncleanliness.´
`Even so, outwardly you appear righteous to men, but inside you are full of hypocrisy and immorality.´
`Woe unto you hypocritical scribes and Pharisees! Because you build tombs for the prophets and adorn the tombs of the righteous.´
`Then you say, 'If we had lived in the days of our fathers, we would not have joined with them to take the blood of the prophets.´
`So you witness against yourselves, that you are the children of those who killed the prophets.´"
And Jesus said, "`So, fill yourselves with the full measure of your father's sins.´
`You serpents are a generation of vipers, how can you escape the damnation of hell?´
`Therefore, I will send prophets, wise men, and scribes to you, and you will kill and crucify some of them, and you will scourge some of them in your synagogues and persecute them from city to city.´
`So that all the righteous bloodshed on the earth may come upon you, from the blood of righteous Abel to Zacharias son of Barachias, whom you killed between the temple and the altar.´
`Truly I tell you; all of these things will come down on this generation.´

`O Jerusalem, you who kill the prophets and stone those who are sent to you, how often I have wanted to gather your children together, like a hen protects her chicks under her wings, and you would not listen!´
`Behold, your house will be left desolate.´
`For I tell you, you will not see me again until you say, 'Blessed is he that comes in the name of the Lord.'´"
As Jesus left the temple, his disciples came to show him around the temple buildings.
And Jesus said to them, "`Do you see everything here? Truly I say to you, not one stone will be left standing on top of another because they will all be thrown to the ground.´"
As he sat on Mount Olive, the disciples privately came to him and said, "Tell us, when will all these things happen, and what will be the sign of your return and the end of the age?"
And Jesus answered them and said, "`Watch carefully, and make sure that no one deceives you.´
`Because many will come in my name and say, 'I am the Christ!' And they will deceive many.´
`You will hear of wars and rumors of wars, but do not let your heart be troubled, because all these things must come to pass, but the end has not yet come.´
`Because nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom. And there will be famines, pestilences, floods, and earthquakes in different places.´
`All these things are the beginning of sorrows
`Then they will deliver you up to be persecuted and killed, and all nations will hate you for my namesake.´
`Many will be offended, and they will hate and betray each other.´
`Many false prophets will rise and deceive many people.´
`Because of the abundance of immorality, the love of many will grow cold.´
`But those who endure until the end, will be saved.´
`And the gospel of the kingdom will be preached all over the world as a witness to all nations, and then the end will come.´
`So when you see all the abominations of devastation, which were spoken of by the prophet Daniel, go stand in the Most Holy Place, so that whoever can read will understand.´
`Then let those living in Judea flee into the mountains.´
`Anyone on their housetop, must not come down to remove anything from their house.´
`Those out in the field, must not return home to get their clothes.´
`Those who are pregnant or nursing a child in those days, will suffer much sorrow!´
`But pray that your time to flee is not in winter or on the Sabbath day.´
`Because at that time, there will be great tribulation which has not been seen since the beginning of the world until now, and it will never be seen again.´
`And if those days are not shortened, no flesh will be saved, but for the sake of the elected those days will be shortened.´
`Then if someone says to you, 'Look here is the Christ, or look there is the Christ,' do not believe it.´
`Because false Christs and false prophets will rise and perform great signs and wonders, so much so, that it would even deceive the elected if that were possible.´
`Behold, I have told you all this before it happens.´
`So, if they say to you, 'Behold he is in the desert!' Do not go out there, or if they say, 'Behold he is in a secret room!' Do not believe it.´
`Because, just as lightning comes from the east and flashes to the far west, the coming of the Son of Man will also be seen this way.´
`Because wherever there is a dead carcass, the eagles will gather.´
`Immediately after the tribulation of those days: The sun will be darkened, the moon will not give its light, the stars will fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken.´
`Then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in heaven, and all the tribes on earth will mourn, and they will see the Son of Man coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.´
`He will send his angels with the sound of great trumpets, and they will gather his elected together from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.´
`Now learn this parable of the fig tree; When its branches are tender and its leaves sprout, you know that summer is near.´
`So, when you see all these things happening, you will know that he is near and maybe even at the door.´
`Truly I tell you; this generation will not pass away until all these things have happened.´
`Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will never pass away.´
`No one knows the day or hour that these things will happen, not even the angels in Heaven, because my father in Heaven is the only one who knows these things.´
`But just as the time of the flood was in the days of Noah, is also the sudden way that the coming of the Son of Man will be.´
`Because just as it was in the days before the flood they were eating and drinking, marrying and becoming engaged, until the day that Noah entered the ark.´
`They did not know the time of the flood until it came and carried them all away, that is also how it will be for the coming of the Son of Man.´
`At that time two people will be out in the field, and one will be taken and the other will be left behind.´
`Two women will be grinding grain in the mill, and one will be taken and the other will be left behind.´
`So keep watch faithfully, because you do not know when your Lord will come.´
`But remember this, if the homeowner had known what time the thief would come, he would have kept watch, and he would not have allowed his house to be robbed.´
`So you must always be ready, because the Son of Man will come when you least expect him.´
`Who then is wise and faithful enough for his Lord to appoint him a supervisor over his household, to provide meat for them at the proper time?´
`Blessed is the servant, whose Lord finds him doing his Job when he comes.´
`Truly I tell you; he will put that man over all of his possessions.´
`But, what if that evil servant says in his heart, 'My Lord will be away for a long time.'´
`And he begins to beat his fellow servants and eat and drink with drunkards.´
`And the Lord returns to that servant at a time that he is not expected.´
`He will remove him, and put him in his place with the hypocrites, and there will be much weeping and gnashing of teeth.´"
Then Jesus said, "`The Kingdom of Heaven will be like ten virgins, who took their lamps and went to meet the bridegroom.´
`Five of them were wise and five of them were foolish.´
`The foolish ones took their lamps with them, but they took no oil.´
`The wise ones filled their lamps with oil before they left.´
`As the bridegroom lingered, they all slept.´
`At midnight someone shouted, 'The bridegroom is coming, go out and meet him.'´
`Then all the virgins got up and trimmed their lamps.´
`And the foolish ones said to the wise, 'Give us some of your oil, because our lamps have gone out.'´
`But the wise ones answered and said, 'No, otherwise there will not be enough for us, you should go to the oil sellers and buy some oil for yourselves.'´
`When they went to buy oil, the bridegroom came and those who were ready went with him to the marriage feast, and the door was shut.´
`Afterwards the foolish virgins arrived and said, 'Lord, open the door and let us in.'´
`But he answered and said, 'Truly I tell you; I do not know you.'´
`Therefore pay attention and keep watch, because you will never know the hour or the day when the son of man will return.´"

And Jesus said, "`The Kingdom of Heaven is like the man who was planning a trip to a far distant country. He called his servants to a meeting and gave them the responsibility of overseeing his possessions while he was gone.´
`He gave five talents to one servant, two talents to another, and one talent to another, each man was rewarded based on his own abilities. Then he left and went on his trip.´
`The one who received the five talents went and traded with them and made five more talents with them.´
`And the one who received two talents, he also made two more talents with them.´
`But the one who received only one talent went and dug a hole and hid his lord's money.´
`After a long time the lord of those servants returned to settle up with them.´
`And the one who received five talents brought him five additional talents and said, 'Lord, you gave me five talents, behold I have added five more talents to them.'´
`His lord said to him, 'Well done good and faithful servant, you have been faithful over a few things, so I will put you in charge of many things. Enter into the joy of your lord.'´
`The one who received two talents also came to him and said, 'Lord, you gave me two talents, behold I have added two more talents to them.'´
`Then his lord said to him, 'Well done, good and faithful servant, you have been faithful over a few things, so I will put you in charge of many things. Enter into the joy of your lord.'´
`Then the one who had received the one talent came and said, 'Lord, I knew that you were a hard man, and you reap where you have not sown, and you gather where you have not thrown seed.´
`So I was afraid and I went and buried your talent in the ground, so here is what is yours.'´
`His lord answered him and said, 'You wicked, dull, and lazy servant, you knew that I reap where I have not sowed and gather where I have not thrown seed.´
`So you should have invested my money with the money changers, and I would have at least earned some interest on my money.´
`Therefore he took the talent from him and give it to the one who had ten talents.´
`For whoever has much will be given more, and he will have an abundance. But whoever has little, will have what little he does have taken away from him.´
`And he threw the unprofitable servant out into the outer darkness, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.´"
And Jesus said, "`When the son of man returns in his glory, with all his holy angels he will sit on his throne of glory.´
`And all the nations will be gathered before him, and he will separate them one from another, like a shepherd divides his sheep from the goats.´
`And he will put the sheep at his right hand, but he will put the goats on his left.´
`Then the King of Heaven will say to those at his right, 'Come, you who are blessed by my father, inherit the kingdom which was prepared for you since the foundation of the world.´
`For I was hungry and you gave me something to eat, I was thirsty and you gave me something to drink, I was a stranger and you took me in.´
`I was naked and you clothed me, I was sick and you visited me, I was in prison and you came to minister to me.´

`Then the righteous will answer him and say, 'Lord, when did we see you when you were hungry and give you something to eat? And when did we see you when you were thirsty and give you something to drink?'´
`When did we see you as a stranger and take you in, or when did we see you naked and clothe you?´
`Or when did we see you were sick or in prison, and came to you?'´
`And the King of Heaven will answer them and say, 'Truly I tell you; 'Whatever you have done for one of the least of my brothers, you have also done for me.'´
`Then the King of Heaven will also say to those at his left, 'Leave me, for you are cursed into the everlasting fire, which was prepared for the devil and his angels.´
`For I was hungry and you gave me nothing to eat, and I was thirsty, but you gave me nothing to drink.´
`I was a stranger and you did not take me in, I was naked and you did not clothe me, I was sick and you did not visit me, and I was in prison but you did not minister to me.'´
`Then they will also answer him and say, 'Lord, when did we see that you were a stranger, hungry, thirsty, naked, sick, or in prison and we did nothing for you?'´
`Then he will answer them and say, 'Truly I tell you; since you did nothing for one of the least of these, then you did nothing for me.'´
`And they will be sent away to everlasting punishment, but the righteous will enter into eternal life.´"
When Jesus finished saying all these things, he spoke to his disciples.
And Jesus said, "`You know that the Passover feast is only two days away, when the Son of Man will be betrayed and crucified.´"
At that time the chief priests, scribes, and the people's elders assembled together at the palace of Caiaphas the high priest.
Where they conspired together about how to quietly arrest and kill Jesus.
But they said, "We cannot arrest him on the feast day, or there may be an uproar among the people."
While Jesus was at Simon the leper's house in Bethany.
A woman came to him with an alabaster box filled with a very precious perfume and poured it on his head as he was sitting at the table.
But when his disciples saw it, they were indignant and said, "What is the purpose of this waste?"
This perfume could have been sold for a lot of money, and it could have been given to the poor.
Jesus was aware of what they were saying and he said to them, "`Why are you troubling this woman? For she has done a good thing for me.´
`For you will always have the poor with you, but you will not always have me.´
`For she has poured this perfume on my body to prepare it for my burial.´
`Truly I tell you; wherever this gospel is preached throughout all the world, what this woman has done for me will also be told as her memorial.´"
Then Judas Iscariot who was one of the twelve disciples went to the chief priests.
And Judas said to them, "What will you give me to deliver Jesus to you?" And they made a contract with him for thirty pieces of silver.
And from that time forward, Judas looked for an opportunity to betray Jesus.
Now on the first day of the Feast of Unleavened Bread, the disciples came to Jesus and said, "Where do you want us to prepare a place for you to eat the Passover Feast?"
And Jesus said, "`Go to a man in the city and tell him that the teacher says, 'My time has come, so I will keep the Passover at your house with my disciples.'´"
So the disciples did as Jesus had told them and they prepared the Passover.
Now when the evening came, he sat down with the twelve disciples.
As they ate Jesus said, "`Truly I tell you that one of you will betray me.´"
And they were extremely upset and they all began to ask him, "Lord, am I the betrayer?"
And he answered them and said, "`The one who dips his hand in the dish with me, is the one who will betray me.´
`The Son of Man will go just as it is written of him, but woe unto the man who betrays the Son of Man! It would have been better for that man if he had never been born.´"
Then Judas, the one who had betrayed him answered and said, "Teacher am I the betrayer?" Jesus answered him and said, "`You have said it yourself.´"
As they were eating, Jesus took a piece of bread and blessed it, he broke it into pieces, and gave it to his disciples and said, "`Take this and eat, for this is my body.´"
Then he took the cup and gave thanks to God and gave it to them and said, "`All of you drink this.´
`For this is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many for the forgiveness of sins.´
`But I tell you, I will not drink from this fruit of the vine from now on until that day when I drink a new drink with you in my father's kingdom.´"
After they sang a hymn, they went up into Mount Olive.
Then Jesus said to them, "`Because of me, all of you will abandon me tonight. For it is written, 'I will defeat the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will be scattered abroad.'`
`But after I have risen, I will lead you into Galilee.´"
Peter answered him and said, "Even if everyone else abandons you, I will never be desert you."
But Jesus said to him, "`Honestly Peter, I tell you this, before the cock crows tonight, you will deny me three times.´"
Peter said to him, "Even if I have to die with you, I will not deny you." All the other disciples agreed and said the same thing.
Then Jesus went with them to a place called Gethsemane, and he said to the disciples, "`Sit here, while I go and pray over there.´"
Jesus took Peter and the two sons of Zebedee with him, and he was filled with sorrow and grief.
Then Jesus said to them, "`My soul is filled with extreme sorrow to the point of death. So, stay here and keep watch with me.´"
Jesus went a little farther and fell facedown and prayed and said, "`O my father, if it is possible let this cup pass from me, nevertheless not my will, but your will be done.´"
Jesus returned to the disciples and he found them asleep, and he said to Peter, "`What is this, you could not keep watch with me for one hour?´
`Watch and pray that you do not enter into temptation, for the spirit is indeed willing, but the flesh is weak.´"
Then Jesus went away a second time and he prayed and said, "`O my father, if this cup cannot pass away, unless I drink from it, then your will be done.´"
When Jesus returned, he found them asleep again, because their eyes were very heavy.
So he left and went away once again and prayed a third time and said the same words.
Then Jesus returned to his disciples and he said to them, "`Go ahead and sleep now, because the hour is here, and the Son of Man has been betrayed into the hands of sinners.´
`Rise up and let us go, for behold the one who betrays me is here!´"
While Jesus was speaking, Judas one of the twelve came toward him with a small army armed with swords and spears, sent from the chief priests and the people's elders.
Now the betrayer gave the soldiers a sign and said, "The one I kiss will be Jesus, and you can arrest him."
Judas immediately approached Jesus and said, "Hello teacher," and he kissed him.
And Jesus said to him, "`Friend, do what you have come to do.´" Then the soldiers grabbed Jesus and arrested him.
Then one of the disciples with Jesus drew his sword and struck one of the high priest's servants and cut off his ear.
But Jesus said to him, "`Put your sword away, because whoever draws the sword will die by the sword.´
`Do you think that I cannot pray to my father right now, and he will immediately give me more than twelve legions of angels?´
`But if I do that, how can the scriptures be satisfied, that say it must be this way?´"
That same hour Jesus said to the soldiers, "`Why have you come with swords and spears to arrest me like I was a thief? I sat with you teaching in the temple for days, but you did not arrest me.´
`All of this must be done this way, in order for the prophets' scriptures to be fulfilled.´" Then all the disciples abandoned him and fled.
Those who had arrested Jesus led him away and brought him to the high priest Caiaphas, where the scribes and elders were assembled.
But Peter followed him at a distance to the high priest's palace, and he went in and sat with the servants to see the final outcome.
Now the chief priests, elders, and the entire council were looking for false testimony against Jesus, so they could put him to death.
But they found no evidence, even though many false witnesses had come out. Finally, two false witnesses came forward.
And one of the false witnesses said, "This fellow said, 'I can destroy God's temple, and rebuild it in three days.'"
Then the high priest got up and said to Jesus, "Do you have nothing to say about what these witnesses have accused you of?"

But Jesus held his peace and remained silent, and the high priest Caiaphas spoke to him and said, "I ask you to swear under oath by the living God, that you tell us whether you are the Christ, the Son of God."
Jesus answered him and said, "`It is as you have said, nevertheless I say to you, from now on you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of power and coming in the clouds of heaven.´"
Then Caiaphas tore his clothes and said, "Jesus has committed blasphemy! We have no further need of witnesses, because you have now heard his blasphemy.
So what do you think?" They answered Caiaphas and said, "He is guilty, and should be put to death."
Then they spit in his face, and some beat him, others slapped him with their hands.
As they were saying, "Prophesy to us Christ, who just hit you?"
Now Peter was sitting outside the palace, and a girl approached him and said, "You were with Jesus of Galilee."
But Peter denied it before everybody and said, "I do not know what you are talking about."
When he left, he went out through the entrance hall where another young woman saw him and said to everyone there, "This man was also with Jesus of Nazareth."
But he denied it again and swore an oath and said, "I do not know the man."
After a while those standing around came and said to Peter, "You are also one of the followers of Jesus, because your speech betrays you."
Then Peter began to curse and swear and he said, "I do not know the man!" And immediately the cock crowed.
Then Peter remembered what Jesus had said to him earlier when he said, "Before the cock crows, you will deny me three times!" And Peter wept bitterly as he left.
The next morning, all the chief priests and the people's elders conspired to put Jesus to death.
They had him bound him and led away, and they delivered him to Governor Pontius Pilate.
When Judas the betrayer saw that Jesus had been condemned, he repented and brought the thirty pieces of silver back to the chief priests and elders.
And Judas said, "I have sinned and betrayed innocent blood!" And they said, "So what, you did it."
Then he threw the pieces of silver into the temple and left, then he went and hanged himself.
The chief priests took the silver pieces and said, "It is not lawful for us to put them into the treasury, because it is blood money."
After they discussed it, they used the money to buy the potter's field, to be used as a place to bury strangers.
Therefore that field is called the Field of Blood to this very day.
Then the scripture was satisfied that Jeremiah the prophet had spoken which said, "They took the thirty pieces of silver which was the value placed on him by the children of Israel.
They paid for the potter's field with the silver, as the Lord commanded me."
As Jesus stood before the governor, the governor asked him, "Are you the king of the Jews?" And Jesus said to him, "`You have said it.´"
But when he was accused by the chief priests and elders, he said nothing.
Then Pilate asked him, "Do you hear all the accusations they are making against you?"
But Jesus never answered or said a word, which surprised the governor.
Now it was the governor's custom to release a prisoner chosen by the people at that feast.
And they had a notorious prisoner called Barabbas in custody.
So when the people gathered together, Pilate asked them, "Who do you want me to release to you? Barabbas, or Jesus who is called Christ?"
Because Pilate knew that they had delivered Jesus to him out of envy.

When Pilate sat down at the judgment seat his wife sent him a message that said, "You must have nothing to do with that righteous man, because I have suffered many things today from a dream that I had about him."
But the chief priests and elders had persuaded the crowds that they should ask for the release of Barabbas, and have Jesus destroyed.
The governor answered them and asked, "Which of these two men do you want me to release to you? They said, "Barabbas."
Then Pilate asked them, "What do you want me to do with Jesus who is called Christ?" They all answered him and said, "Crucify him!"
But the governor asked, "Why, what evil has he done?" But they cried out even louder and said, "Crucify him!"
