When Pilate realized that he could not reason with the crowd, and they were growing violent and restless, he took some water and washed his hands before the crowds and said, "I am innocent of this righteous man's blood, therefore his blood is on you."
Then all the people answered him and said, "So let his blood be on us and our children."
Then Pilate released Barabbas to them, and after he had Jesus flogged, he delivered him over to be crucified.
Then the governor's soldiers took Jesus to the common hall and gathered the whole company of soldiers around him.
They stripped him and put a scarlet robe on him.
After they weaved a crown of thorns, they put it on his head. They put a staff in his right hand, then they knelt down before him and mocked him and said, "Hail, to the king of the Jews!"
They spit on him and beat his head with the staff.
After that they mocked him some more, then they removed his robe and put his own clothes back on him and led him away to be crucified.
As they came out, they forced a man from Cyrene named Simon to carry his cross.
When they arrived at a place called Golgotha, also known as the place of the skull.
They gave him some vinegar mixed with bitter herbs to drink, but after he tasted it, he would not drink it.

They crucified him and divided his garments among themselves by casting lots. This was to satisfy the words spoken by the prophet who said, "They divided my garments among themselves and cast lots for my clothes."
After sitting down they kept watch over him there.
They hung a sign of accusation over his head on which was written, "This is Jesus the king of the Jews."
Two thieves were crucified with him, one on his right side and another on the left.
Everyone who passed by him, shook their head and condemned him.
And they said, "If you are the Son of God, and you can destroy the temple and rebuild it in three days, save yourself and come down from that cross."
The chief priests along with the scribes and elders also mocked him.
And they said, "He saved others, but he cannot save himself. If he is the King of Israel, let him come down from that cross and we will believe him."
He trusts God, so let God deliver him if God wants him, all because Jesus said, "I am the Son of God."
The thieves who were also crucified with him, cast the same insults at him from their teeth.
Suddenly, starting from the sixth hour until the ninth hour a darkness covered the entire land.
At about the ninth hour Jesus cried in a loud voice and said, "`Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani?´" Or in other words, "`My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?'´"
When some of those standing there heard that, they said, "This man calls out for Elijah."
Immediately one of them ran and filled a sponge with vinegar and put it on a staff to give him drink.
The rest of them said, "Leave him alone",let us see if Elijah comes to save him."
Then Jesus cried out again in a loud voice, and he gave up the ghost.
Immediately the temple veil was torn in half from top to bottom, there was an earthquake and the rocks split.
Graves were opened, and many bodies of the sleeping saints were raised up.
After the resurrection of Jesus, the saints who had come out of the graves went into the holy city and appeared to many people.
When the centurion and the other guards watching Jesus with him, saw the earthquake and all the other things happening, they were terrified and said, "This was truly the Son of God."
And many women who had followed Jesus from Galilee to minister to him, were watching from far away.
Among them was Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James and Joseph, and the mother of Zebedee's children.
Then in the evening, a rich man named Joseph of Arimathea who was also a disciple of Jesus came.
And Joseph went to Pilate and begged for the body of Jesus. Pilate commanded the body to be delivered Joseph.
When Joseph took the body, he wrapped it in a clean linen cloth.
And laid it in his own new tomb, which he had carved out of the rock. Then he rolled a great stone across the door of the tomb and left.
Mary Magdalene and the other Mary were sitting next to the tomb.
Now the next day, which was the day after the preparation, the chief priests and Pharisees all went to see Pilate.
And they said, "Sir, we remember what the deceiver taught while he was still alive when he said, "`After three days I will rise again!´"

Therefore you must command the tomb to be secured until the third day, or his disciples will come at night and steal his body. Then they will tell the people that he has risen from the dead, and their last lie will be worse than the first."
Pilate said to them, "You have guards, so go and make sure the tomb is as secure as you can make it."
So they went and made the tomb secure, they sealed the stone and posted a guard to keep watch.
At the end of the Sabbath, at dawn on the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary came to visit the tomb.
Suddenly there was a great earthquake, as the angel of the Lord descended from heaven to roll the stone away from the door, and he sat on it.
He looked like lightning, and his clothes were as white as snow.
And the guards shook in fear of him and became like dead men.
And the angel spoke and said to the women, "Fear not, because I know that you are looking for Jesus who was crucified.
He is not here, because he has risen as he said he would! Come and see the place where the Lord lay.
Then go quickly and tell his disciples that he has risen from the dead, and behold he goes before you into Galilee. There you will see him, just as I have told you."
So they quickly left the tomb trembling with fear and great joy and ran to tell his disciples what the angel had said.
As they went to tell his disciples, Jesus met them along the way and said, "`Greetings!´" And they came and worshipped at his feet.
Then Jesus said to them, "`Do not be afraid, but go and tell my brothers to go to Galilee, and they will see me there.´"
Now as the women were leaving, some of the watch guards came into the city to tell the chief priests what had happened.
When they assembled the elders and discussed the situation, they gave the soldiers a large sum of money.
And they told them to say, "'Jesus' disciples came at night and stole his body while we were sleeping.'
If the governor hears about this, we will persuade him not to discipline you and we will protect you."
So they took the money and did as they were told. And this story has been reported among the Jews to this very day.
Then the eleven disciples went to Galilee, to the mountain where Jesus had told them to go.
When they saw him, they worshipped him, but some still doubted.
So Jesus came and spoke to them and said, "`All power has been given to me in heaven and on earth.
Therefore go and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the father, and of the son, and of the holy spirit.
Teach them to observe everything I have commanded you, and remember I am always with you, even until the end of the world. Amen!´"
This is beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God.
This is what was written by the prophets when they said, "Behold I am sending my messenger ahead of you to prepare the way for you.
There is a voice crying out in the wilderness that says, 'Prepare a way for the Lord, and make his paths straight!'"
John baptized people in the wilderness, as he was preaching that baptism was a sign of repentance and forgiveness of sins.
People from all over Judea and Jerusalem came to confess their sins, and to be baptized by John in the Jordan River.
John wore a camel hair garment, with a leather belt around his waist, and he ate locusts with wild honey.
When John preached, he said, "There is one who is greater than me coming, and I am not even worthy to untie the straps of his sandals.
I have baptized you with water, but Jesus will baptize you with the Holy Spirit."
During those days, Jesus came from Nazareth in Galilee and was baptized by John in the Jordan River.
As soon as he came out of the water, John saw the sky open and the Spirit of God descending on him like a dove.
Then a voice came from heaven and said, "You are my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased."
Immediately after that, the Holy Spirit led him out into the wilderness.
He stayed out in the wilderness with wild animals for forty days, and he was tempted by Satan, but the angels ministered to him.
After John the Baptist was imprisoned, Jesus went to Galilee and began to preach the good news of God's kingdom.
And he said, "`The time has come and the Kingdom of God is here, so repent from your sins and believe the gospels.´"
As Jesus was walking along shores of the Sea of Galilee, he saw two fishermen Simon and his brother Andrew casting a net into the sea.
Jesus said to them, "`Come and follow me, and I will make you fishers of men.´"
So they immediately left their nets and followed him.
As he walked a little further, he saw James and his brother John, who were Zebedee's sons. They were on a boat, mending their fishing nets.
He immediately called out to them, and they left their father Zebedee on the boat with the workers and went with him.
They went to Capernaum, and on the Sabbath day he went to the synagogue and taught.
They were amazed by his teachings, because he taught them like someone who had authority and power, not like scribes.
There was a man in the synagogue who was possessed by an unclean spirit.
The man cried out, "Leave us alone Jesus of Nazareth. What do you want from us, have you come to destroy us? I know who you are, you are the Holy One of God."
Jesus rebuked the demons within him and said, "`Hold your peace, and come out of him.´"
The evil spirit injured the man, then it shouted with a loud voice and left him.
Jesus amazed them all, so much so, that they all asked each other, what kind of new teaching is this? Because this man commands evil spirits with authority, and they obey him.
Right away his reputation spread throughout the whole region of Galilee.
They immediately left the synagogue, along with James and John, and went to Simon and Andrew's home.
But Simon's mother-in-law was in bed sick with a fever, and they told Jesus about her.
Jesus lifted her up and took her hand, immediately the fever left her, and she got up and served them.
In the evening, after the sun set, they brought all the sick people and people possessed by evil spirits to Jesus.
The whole city gathered around them at the front door.
He healed many sick people with various diseases, and drove out many evil spirits, but he did not let the evil spirits speak because they knew who he was.
In the early morning before dawn, he got up and left and went to a place where he could be alone to pray.
Simon and those with him followed Jesus.
When they found Jesus, they said to him, "Everyone is looking for you."
Then Jesus said to them, "`We must go to the nearby towns, because I came here to preach to them.´"
So, Jesus preached in synagogues all over Galilee and drove out evil spirits.
One day a man who was infected with leprosy approached Jesus and asked him for help. So, Jesus knelt down to him, and the infected man said, "You have the power to heal me if you want to."
Jesus was moved with compassion, and he laid his hand on the man and said, "`I want to, you are now clean.´"
As soon as Jesus spoke, the leprosy left the man and he was healed.
Jesus gave strict orders to the man and told him to leave quickly.
Jesus spoke to the man and said, "`Do not tell anyone about this, but go and show yourself to the priest to prove to them that you are healed. Then make the offerings that Moses told you to make.´"

But when the man left, he started to spread the story everywhere. Everyone heard about it, and Jesus could no longer publicly enter the city. He was all alone and he had to stay outside the city, but people still came to him from all over.
After a few days Jesus went back to Capernaum, and the people had heard that he was in the house.
Soon, there were so many people gathered around the house, that there was no room left inside or even outside near the door, and Jesus preached to them anyway.
Four people came to see Jesus, and they were carrying a paralyzed man on a stretcher.
The crowd was so large that they could not get close to Jesus, so they cut a hole in the roof of the house and lowered the paralyzed man down to him on his mat.
When Jesus saw their faith, he said to the crippled man, "`Son your sins are forgiven.´"
But some of the scribes who were sitting there were thinking in their heart.
Why is this man speaking such blasphemies, only God can forgive sins.
Jesus' spirit knew immediately what they were thinking, and he said to them, "`Why are you thinking such things in your heart?´
`Is it easier to say to a crippled man, 'Son, your sins are forgiven,' or to say to him, 'Get up, pick up your bed and walk'?´
`But, just so you know that the Son of Man has the power to forgive sin here on earth, I say to this crippled man.´
`Get up, pick up your mat, and go home.´"

Immediately the man got up, picked up his mat, and walked out the front door for everyone to see. Everyone who saw this was amazed, then they praised God and said, "We have never seen anything like this before."
Jesus left and went out by the seashore, where the crowds followed him and he taught them.
Jesus saw Levi, son of Alphaeus sitting in the tax booth and he spoke to him and said, "`Come with me,´" and he got up and followed him.
While Jesus was eating dinner at Levi's house, many tax collectors and other sinners came and sat with him and his disciples, because there were so many of them following Jesus.
When the scribes and Pharisees saw him eating with sinners and tax collectors, they said to his disciples, "Why is he eating and drinking with tax collectors and sinners?"
When Jesus heard them, he said, "`Healthy people do not need a physician, but sick people do. I did not come to teach the righteous, but I came to call the sinners to repentance.´"
John the Baptist's disciples and the Pharisees often fasted, but Jesus and his disciples did not, and the Pharisees came to Jesus and asked, "Why do you and your disciples not fast?"
Jesus said to them, `"My disciples are like the children of the bride's friends at her wedding. They ca not fast while the bridegroom is with them.´
`But the day will come when the groom is taken away from them, and that is when they will fast.´
`Nobody patches old clothing with new cloth, because it will shrink and pull away, and make the tear worse.´

`New wine cannot be stored in old wineskins because the new wine will expand and burst the old wineskins, spill the wine and ruin the wineskins. New wine must be stored in new wineskins because they can expand as the new wine expands.´"
One Sabbath day, Jesus was walking through a wheat field with his disciples. As they walked, his disciples began to pick and eat the wheat.
And the Pharisees asked him, "Why are they breaking the laws of the Sabbath day?"
Jesus answered them and said, "`Do you not know the story about David, when he and his friends were hungry and needed food?´
`And how he went into God's house when Abiathar was the high priest, and ate the priest's bread offering, and shared it with his friends.´"
And Jesus said to them, "`The Sabbath was made for man, man was not made for the Sabbath.´
`And that's why the Son of Man is also the Lord of the Sabbath.´"
Jesus went back to the synagogue, and a man there had a crippled hand.
The Pharisees were waiting to see if Jesus would heal the man on the Sabbath, so they could accuse him of breaking the Sabbath law.
And Jesus spoke to the man with the crippled hand and said, "`Come here.´"

Then Jesus asked them, "`What is more lawful, to do good on the Sabbath, or to do evil on the Sabbath, to save someone's life, or to kill someone?´" But the Pharisees remained silent and said nothing.
Jesus was angry because he saw that their hearts were so hardened. So, he said to the sick man, "`Hold out your hand,´" he did, and they all saw that his hand had been healed.
The Pharisees left and immediately met with the Herodians to plot against Jesus, and they started planning how to kill him.
Jesus and his disciples went out to the sea to be alone, but large crowds from Galilee and Judea followed them.

Large crowds came to see Jesus from Jerusalem, Edom, the region beyond the Jordan River, and the area around Tyre and Sidon. They had heard about the great things he was doing and wanted to see him for themselves.
Jesus told his disciples to get a boat ready, because the crowd was so large, that he thought they would be overrun.
Because he had healed so many people that the sick people were crowding in to touch him.
When the unclean spirits saw Jesus, they bowed down before him and cried out, "You are the Son of God!"
And he gave them a stern warning and told them not to reveal who he was.
Jesus left and went up into the mountains, and he asked his apostles to come with him, and they left and went with him.
Jesus ordained twelve men to be his apostles, and he sent them out to preach the gospel.
He gave them the power to heal the sick and to cast out demons.
And he changed Simon's name to Peter.
James and John, the sons of Zebedee, were given the name Boanerges, which means "Sons of Thunder."
And the other apostles were Andrew, Philip, Bartholomew, Matthew, Thomas, James the son of Alphaeus, Thaddaeus, and Simon the Canaanite.
And everyone went into a house with Jesus, including Judas Iscariot, who would later betray him.
The crowd gathered again, and there were so many people that they could not even eat their meal.
When his friends heard about it, they went to stop Jesus because they thought that he had lost his mind.
The scribes from Jerusalem said that Jesus was possessed by Beelzebub the prince of demons, and he was using Satan's powers to cast out demons.
Jesus spoke to the scribes in parables and he asked them, "`How can Satan cast out Satan?´
`If a kingdom is divided against itself, it cannot stand.´
`If a house is divided against itself, it cannot stand.´
`Satan would destroy himself, if he turned against himself and became divided.´
`When a strong person is overpowered and bound up, their house can be robbed, the same way that Satan must be bound up before his demons can be cast out.´
`Truly I tell you; all the sins and any blasphemies uttered against anyone cursed by the sons of men will be forgiven.´
`But anyone who blasphemes the Holy Spirit will never be forgiven, and they will be in danger of eternal damnation.´"
Someone said that Jesus had an unclean spirit.
His mother and brothers came to see him, but they stood outside and sent someone in to tell him that they were there.
While the crowds were sitting around him, someone told him that his mother and brothers were outside looking for him.
And he answered them and said, "`Who is my mother, and who are my brothers?´"
And he looked around at everyone sitting with him and said, "`Look, these are my mother and my brothers!´
`Because anyone who does God's will is my brother, sister, and mother.´'
Jesus started teaching by the seashore, and the crowds gathered around him, so he got into a boat and sat out in the water, and all the people stayed behind on the beach.
He used parables to explain his teachings to them about many things.
And Jesus said, "`Listen, a farmer went out to plant his fields.´
`As the farmer was sowing his seed, some of the seed fell by the side of the road and the birds ate them.´
`Some of the seed fell on rocky ground, where there was very little soil, so they quickly sprouted but the roots were not very deep.´
`And those plants wilted and died when the sun rose, because the roots were too shallow.´
`Some of the seed fell among the thorns, when the thorns grew, they choked those plants and they produced no fruit.´
`The other seed fell on good soil and produced fruit which grew and grew, some seed produced a harvest of thirtyfold, some sixtyfold, and some a hundredfold."´
`Those of you with ears, listen to what I have to say and understand.´"
Later when Jesus was alone, the twelve disciples and the others around him, asked him to explain the parable.

Jesus said to his disciples, "`You have been given the gift of knowing the mysteries of God's kingdom. But those who are not part of God's kingdom will not understand the things I say to them in parables.´
`Even though they see they do not perceive, and they may hear but they do not understand. Because if they understood, they would believe and their sins would be forgiven.´"
`If you do not understand this parable, then how can you understand any of the parables?´
`The farmer sows the word.´
`Some people are like the seed sown by the side of the road where they hear the word. But as soon as they hear it, Satan immediately comes and steals the word that was sown in their heart.´
`Some are like the seed sown on stony ground, they hear the word and immediately receive it with happiness.´
`But it does not take root in them, and it only endures for a short time. Later, when affliction or persecution rises up because of the word, they are immediately offended and give up.´
`Some are like the seed sown among thorns, who hear the word.´
`But the cares of this world, the deceitfulness of riches, and the lusts of other things interfere and choke the word, and it becomes unfruitful.´
`But some are like the seed sown on good ground, they hear and receive the word, and it produces fruit, some thirtyfold, some sixtyfold, and some a hundredfold.´"
And Jesus said, "`Is a candle brought out just to be put under a basket or a bed? Is it not placed on a lampstand instead?´
`For nothing is hidden that will not be seen, nor can anything be kept secret that will not be revealed in the light.´
`If you have ears to hear, then hear.´"
`Pay attention to what you hear. For how you measure, is how it will be measured back to you, and to you who hear even more will be given.´
`For the one who has much, more will be given to him, and the one who has nothing, will have what he does have taken away.´"
`So the Kingdom of God, is like a man who threw seed on the ground.´
`Night and day the man sleeps and gets up, and the seed springs up and grows, but he does not understand how.´
`For the earth produces fruit from herself, first the leaves sprout then the kernel, and finally the full head of wheat grows.´
`But when the fruit is ripe, immediately the farmer brings the sickle because harvest time has come.´"
And Jesus said, "`To what can we compare the Kingdom of God, or to which parable should we compare it?´
`It is like a mustard seed, which is one of smallest seeds sown on the earth.´
`But when it is sown, it grows and becomes greater than all the other herbs. It shoots out great branches, so that the birds of the air may live under its shade.´"
And Jesus spoke of many such parables to the people, some of whom heard and understood.
Jesus did not speak to the crowds publicly without speaking in parables. But when he was alone with his disciples, he explained everything to them.
That evening Jesus said to his disciples, "`Let's cross over to the other side.´"
After they sent the crowds away, Jesus was already in the boat and they left with him, along with some other small boats around him.
A great windstorm arose and the waves began to beat against the boat, which was now filling with water.
Jesus was in the stern of the boat, asleep on a pillow, so the disciples woke him and said, "Teacher, do you not care if we die?"
So Jesus got up, reprimanded the wind and said to the sea, "`Peace, be still!´" And the wind ceased, and a great calm was restored.
Then Jesus said to his disciples, "`How can you be so fearful? Why is it that you have no faith?´"
After that, they were extremely fearful and they said to one another, "What kind of man is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?"
When they arrived at the other side of the sea in the country of the Gadarenes.
After Jesus left the boat, a man with an unclean spirit immediately came out of the tombs to meet him.
This man lived alone among the tombs, because no one had the strength to bind him, not even with chains.
And nobody could tame him, even though he had often been bound in chains and shackles, but he broke the shackles and tore the chains apart.
He was always in the mountain tombs, and he cried and cut himself with stones every day and night.
But when he saw Jesus from far away, he ran to worship him.
Then he cried out with a loud voice and said, "What do you want with me Jesus, son of the Most High God? I beg you not to torment me before God."
For Jesus had already said to him, "`Come out of that man, you unclean spirit.´"
And Jesus asked him, "`What is your name?´" And the demons answered and said, "My name is Legion, because there are many of us."
And the demons implored him not to send them far away outside the country.
There was a large herd of pigs feeding there near the mountains.
So all the demons begged Jesus to send them into the pigs.

Jesus told them to leave, and the unclean spirits immediately left the man. There was about 2,000 of them, and they entered the herd of pigs and ran violently down the hill, where they fell off the cliff into the sea and they all drowned.
The people who fed the pigs fled and went to tell the story in the city and countryside, and the people there went out to see what was going on.
When they saw Jesus and the man who had been possessed by a legion of the devil's demons sitting there fully clothed, and in his right mind, they were very afraid.
And those who saw what had happened told the others about the demon possessed man, and also about the pigs.
And they begged Jesus to leave their area.
When Jesus got back into the boat, the demon possessed man begged Jesus to let him go with him.
However Jesus would not let him go, but he said to the man, "`Go home to your friends, and tell them what great things the Lord has done for you, and the compassion he has had for you.´"
Then the man left and began to proclaim throughout Decapolis what great things Jesus had done for him, and everyone marveled.
When Jesus crossed back over to the other side by boat, many people gathered around him near the sea.
Suddenly a synagogue ruler named Jairus arrived, and when he saw Jesus, he fell at his feet.
Jairus begged Jesus to come with him and he said, "My little daughter is near the point of death. I pray you will come and lay hands on her, so that she may be healed and live."
So Jesus went with him, and many people followed and crowded around him.
There was a woman in the crowd, who had been plagued with menstrual bleeding for twelve years.
This woman had suffered many things, and she had spent all her money on physicians, but her condition had only gotten worse.
When she heard about Jesus, she squeezed through the crowd and came up behind him and touched his garment.
For she had said to herself, "If I can just touch his clothes, I will be healed."
Right away the blood flowing from her dried up, and she felt in her body that she had been healed of her affliction.
Jesus immediately knew within himself that something good had left him, so he turned around and said, "`Who touched my clothes?´"
And his disciples said to him, "Do you see this crowd around you, how can you ask, 'Who touched me?'"
Jesus looked all around to see who had touched him.
The woman was trembling and afraid, but she also knew what had been done within her, so she came and fell down before him and told him the truth.
Then Jesus said to her, "`Daughter, your faith has made you whole, therefore go in peace because your plague has been healed.´"
While Jesus was still speaking, messengers came from Jairus the synagogue ruler's house who said, "Your daughter is dead, there is no need to trouble the teacher any further?"
As soon as Jesus heard what was said, he said to Jairus, "`Do not be afraid, just believe.´"
Then Jesus allowed no one to follow him except for Peter, James, and John the brother of James.
When Jesus arrived at the house of Jairus the synagogue ruler, he saw the commotion and all the loudly weeping people standing around.
Then Jesus entered the house and said, "`Why are you making such a fuss with all this weeping? The girl is not dead; she is only asleep.´"
And they laughed and made fun of him. But after he had put them all out, he took the girl's father and mother and the others with him, into the room where the girl was lying.
Jesus took the girl by the hand and said to her, "`Talitha koum! Which means, 'Little girl get up!'´"
Right away the girl got up and walked around, because she was only twelve years old, and they were greatly astonished.
Then Jesus gave them strict orders to tell no one about what had happened, and he told them to give her something to eat.
Jesus left the country of the Gadarenes with his disciples and went home.

Then on the Sabbath day, he began to teach in the synagogue. Many of those who heard him were astonished and said, "Where does this man get these thoughts, and what kind of wisdom has he been given? How does he perform such works and miracles?
Is he not the carpenter, the son of Mary and brother of James, Joses, Juda, and Simon? Are not his sisters also here with us?" And they were offended by Jesus.
Then Jesus said to them, "`A prophet is not without honor except in his own country, among his own family in his own home.´"
So he could not perform any miracles there, except for a few sick people that he laid hands on and healed.
Jesus was amazed at their disbelief, but he went all around the different villages teaching the people.
Jesus summoned the twelve disciples to him, then he began to send them out on missions two by two, and he gave them power over unclean spirits.
Jesus told them to take nothing with them on their journey except a staff. He told them to take no luggage, no bread, and no money in their purse.
But he told them to just wear sandals, and not to take two coats with them.
And Jesus said to them, "`Wherever you enter a house, stay there until you leave that place.´

`If the people there do not receive you or listen to you, simply shake the dust off your feet as a testimony against them when you leave. Truly I tell you; it will be more tolerable for Sodom and Gomorrah on the day of judgment, than it will be for that city.´"
So they left and preached that men should repent.
They threw out many demons, and anointed many sick people with oil, and healed them.

King Herod had heard of Jesus, because his famous name had spread far and wide and the king said, "John the Baptist has risen from the dead, that's why these miraculous works reveal themselves through him."
Others said, "This is Elijah." Still others said, "He is a prophet, like one of the ancient prophets."
But when Herod heard this, he said, "No, it is John who I beheaded, he has risen from the dead."
For Herod had given the order himself to have John arrested and imprisoned for the sake of Herodias. Because she was his dead brother Philip's wife, but he had married her.
And John had confronted Herod and said, "It is unlawful for you to marry your brother's wife.
So Herodias held a grudge against John, and she would have had him killed, but she could not.
But Herod feared John, because he knew that John was a just and holy man. When Herod heard John speaking about many things, he listened gladly.
Then on Herod's birthday, the king had a feast prepared for his lords, high captains, and Galilee's prominent citizens.
When the daughter of Herodias came in, she danced for King Herod and the others with him. The king was so pleased that he said to the girl, "Ask whatever you want from me, and I will give it you."
And the king swore to her and said, "Whatever you ask of me, I will give you, even up to half my kingdom."
Then she went to her mother and asked, "What should I ask for?" And her mother said, "Ask for the head of John the Baptist!"
So right away she hastily returned to the king and said, "I ask that you bring me the head of John the Baptist on a platter."
The king was filled with extreme sorrow, but for the sake of his oath that he had made in front of all those around him, he could not reject her.
So the king immediately sent an executioner with orders to bring John the Baptist's head to her, and the executioner went and beheaded him in the prison.
The executioner brought John's head to the girl on a platter, and she gave it to her mother.
When John's disciples heard this, they went and retrieved his corpse and laid it in a tomb.
At the same time the apostles gathered around Jesus and told him about everything they had done and taught on their mission.

And Jesus said to them, "`Come with me to a place in the desert, where we can be alone and rest for a while.´" For so many people were coming and going, that they did not even have enough leisure time to eat.
So they left and went to a place in the desert by boat where they could be alone.
But many people recognized Jesus when they saw the group departing, and they ran on foot from all the cities to the place where they were headed and they arrived there before Jesus.
When Jesus came out, he saw the large crowds, and he was moved with compassion for them. Because he knew that they were like sheep without a shepherd, and he began to teach them many things.
But it was near the end of the day, so his disciples came to him and said, "This place is out in the desert, and it is already late in the day.
Send the crowd away, so they can go into the countryside and the villages to buy some bread, because they have nothing to eat."
Then Jesus answered them and said, "`Well give them something to eat!´" And they answered him and said, "Should we go and buy three or four shekels worth of bread to feed all of these people?"
So Jesus said, "`Go and see how many loaves you have?´" After they counted them, they said, "We have five loaves and two fish."
Then Jesus told them to make all the people sit down in groups on the green grass.
They all sat down in groups of hundreds and fifties.

Then Jesus took the five loaves and the two fish, and he looked up to heaven. He blessed and broke the five loaves and divided the two fish. Then he gave them to his disciples to distribute among all the people.
And they all ate and were filled.
After the people ate, they collected twelve baskets full of leftover bread and fish.
So they fed about 5,000 men, women, and children from those loaves of bread.
Right away Jesus made his disciples get into the boat, and go to the other side of Bethsaida, while he sent the people away.
After he sent them away, Jesus left and went up on the mountain to pray.
In the evening, the boat was in the middle of the sea and Jesus was alone on the land.

Jesus saw them struggling to row the boat, because the wind was blowing against them. Then at about the fourth watch of the night, Jesus came walking toward them on the water and he would have walked past them.
Except when they saw him walking on the water, they thought it was a ghost and they cried out in fear.
For they had all seen him and they were terrified, but Jesus immediately began to talk to them and he said, "`Cheer up, it is only me, do not be afraid.´"
Then he climbed into the boat with them and the wind stopped blowing. They were all absolutely amazed beyond measure and filled with wonder.
For they did not understand the miracle of the loaves, because their hearts had been hardened.
After they crossed the sea and arrived in the land of Gennesaret, they rowed to shore.
When they climbed out of the boat, the people recognized Jesus right away.
And the whole region around them began to run and carry the beds of those who were sick to Jesus wherever they heard he was.

And wherever he went whether it was the villages, cities, or countryside, they laid the sick in the streets and begged Jesus to let them just touch the hem of his garment. And everyone who touched him was healed and made whole.
Then some of the scribes and Pharisees from Jerusalem got together and went to see Jesus.
When they saw some of his disciples eating bread with dirty unwashed hands, they found fault with them.
Because the Pharisees and all the Jews do not eat unless they wash their hands often, which was one of the traditions of the elders.
When they return from the market the Jews and Pharisees do not eat unless they wash first. They also observed and held many other traditions, like washing the cups, pots, brass bowls, and tables.
Then the Pharisees and scribes asked Jesus, "Why do your disciples not walk in the ways of the elder's traditions, why do they eat with unwashed hands?"
Jesus answered them and said, "`Well, it is as Isaiah prophesied about you hypocrites, in which it was written, 'These people honor me with their lips, but their hearts are far from me.´
`However, they worship me in vain because they teach the doctrines of men as God's commandments.'´
`For you set aside the commandments of God, but you hold to the traditions of men such as washing pots, cups, and many other such things that you do.´"
Jesus also said to them, "`You know full well that you reject God's commandments because you only want to keep your own traditions.´
`For Moses said, 'Honor your father and your mother, and whoever curses their father or mother, let them die the death.'´
`But you say, 'If a man says to his father or mother, "Whatever you have profited from me is Corban (a gift to God), and he will be set free."'´
`And you no longer require him to do more for his father or mother.´
`You make the word of God ineffective through your traditions and many other similar things you do, which you have delivered to the people instead of God's word.´"
Jesus summoned all the people to him and said, "`Every one of you listen to me and understand.´
`Nothing that enters a man from outside can defile him, but the things which come out of a man are the things that defile him.´
`If a man has ears to hear, let him hear.´"
When Jesus left the crowd and entered the house, his disciples asked him about the parable.
So, Jesus explained it to them and said, "`Are you also without understanding? Do you not understand that whatever enters a man from outside cannot defile him?´
`Because it does not enter his heart, it enters his stomach where it is digested and purged, then it goes down the drain.´"
And Jesus said, "`It is what comes out of a man that defiles a man.´
`For from within the hearts of men comes evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, and murders.´
`Plus thefts, covetousness, wickedness, deceitfulness, lasciviousness, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, and foolishness.´
`All of these evil things come from within a man and defile him.´"
Then Jesus got up and went to the region of Tyre and Sidon, where he entered a house. He wanted to be where no one could find him, but he could find no place to hide.
Becasue a woman whose young daughter had an unclean spirit, heard about Jesus and she went to him and knelt down at his feet.
She was a Greek woman of Roman Phoenician descent, and she begged Jesus to throw the demon out of her daughter.
But Jesus said to her, "`First let the children eat, because it is not right to throw the children's bread to dogs.´"
And she answered him and said, "Yes Lord, but even the dogs under the table are allowed to eat the children's crumbs."
Then Jesus answered her and said, "`Because you have said this, the demon has left your daughter, and you can go home.´"
When she got home, she found that the demon had left her daughter and the girl was laying on her bed.
Once again, Jesus left the region of Tyre and Sidon and traveled through Decapolis to the Sea of Galilee.
The people brought a deaf man with a speech impediment to Jesus, and they begged him to lay hands on the man.
So Jesus took the man out of sight of the crowd, and put his fingers in the man's ears, then he spit and touched his tongue.
Jesus looked up to heaven, then he sighed and said to the man, "`Ephphatha! (which means be opened)´"
Immediately the man's ears were opened, and the strings holding his tongue were loosened, and he began to speak plainly.
Then he told those who had seen what happened not to tell anyone about it. But the more he told them not to tell anyone, the more they made a big deal out of it and proclaimed it everywhere.
The people were astonished beyond measure and said, "Jesus makes all things well! He makes both the deaf hear and the dumb speak."
In those days the massive crowds grew and grew, but the people had nothing to eat, so Jesus called his disciples to him.
And Jesus said, "`I feel compassion for these crowds because they have been with me for three days now, and they have nothing to eat.´
`But if I send them away to their own homes hungry, they may faint along the way, because some of them come from different places far away.´"
His disciples answered him and said, "Where can we find enough bread in this wilderness to satisfy all these people?"
Jesus asked them, "`How many loaves of bread do you have?´" And they said, "We have seven loaves."

Then Jesus commanded the people to sit down on the ground, and he took the seven loaves of bread and gave thanks to God. He broke the bread and gave it to his disciples to be distributed among the people, and they did.
They also had a few small fish, and Jesus blessed them and told the disciples to also distribute the fish among the people.
So the people ate their fill, and the disciples picked up seven baskets full of leftover pieces of broken bread and fish.
About 5,000 men, women, and children were fed that day then Jesus sent them away.
Almost immediately Jesus got into a boat with his disciples and went to the region of Dalmanutha.
But there the Pharisees came out and began to question Jesus, they were testing him and asking for a heavenly sign from him.
And he sighed deeply in his spirit and said, "`Why is this generation always looking for a sign? Truly I tell you; no sign will be given to this generation.´"
Then Jesus left them and got back into the boat and went to the other side.
Now the disciples had forgotten to take bread, and there was only one loaf of bread on the boat with them.
And Jesus warned them and said, "`Be careful, and do not trust the leavening of the Pharisees or Herod.´"
The disciples discussed it among themselves and said, "`Jesus said this because we have no bread.´"
When Jesus became aware of their conversation he said, "`Why are you talking about having no bread? Do you still not understand? Are your hearts still that hard?´
`Do you have eyes and still not see? Do you have ears and still not hear? And do you not remember what happened?´
`When I broke the five loaves of bread and fed 5,000 people, how many baskets full of leftovers did you pick up?´" And they told him that they had picked up twelve full baskets of leftovers.
Then Jesus asked them, "`When I fed 4,000 people with two fish, how many baskets full of leftovers did you pick up?´" And they told him they had picked up seven full baskets of leftovers.
And Jesus said to them, "`So, how is it that you do not understand?´"
When they arrived in Bethsaida, the people brought a blind man to Jesus and begged him to touch the man.
Jesus took the blind man by the hand and led him out of town. Then he spit on the blind man's eyes, and laid his hands on him and asked, "`Can you see?´"
And the man looked up and said, "I see men who look like trees walking around."
After that Jesus put his hands on the man's eyes again and made him look up. Then the man's sight was restored, and he saw everyone very clearly.
Jesus sent the man away back to his home and said, "`Do not go into town, or tell anyone in town what has happened.´"
Jesus and his disciples left and went to the towns around Caesarea Philippi. Along the way there, Jesus spoke to his disciples and asked, "`Who do men say that I am?´"
And they answered him and said, "`Some say you are John the Baptist, but some say you are Elijah, and others say you are one of the ancient prophets.´"
And Jesus said to them, "`But who do you say that I am?´" And Peter answered him and said, "You are the Christ!"
And Jesus told the disciples not to tell anyone about him.
Then Jesus began teaching them that the Son of Man must suffer many things and be rejected by the elders, chief priests, and scribes. And he would be killed, but after three days he would rise again.
Jesus spoke this message openly, but Peter took him aside and began to reprimand him.

But Jesus turned around and looked at his disciples and he reprimanded Peter and said, "`Get behind me Satan! You do not respect the things of God, because you are only interested in the things of men.´"
Then Jesus called the people to him along with his disciples and said, "`Whoever wants to come after me must deny himself and take up his cross and follow me.´
`For whoever wants to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life for my sake and for the sake of the gospels will save it.´
`For what does it profit a man to gain the whole world, and lose his own soul?´
`Or what will a man give in exchange for his soul?´
`So whoever is ashamed of me and my words in this adulterous and sinful generation, then the Son of Man will also be ashamed of him when he comes with the holy angels in his father's glory.´"
And Jesus said to them, "`Truly I tell you; some of you standing here will not taste death, until you have seen the Kingdom of God coming with power.´"
After six days Jesus led Peter, James, and John high up on a mountain where they could be by themselves and he was transfigured before them.
His clothes began to shine as brilliantly white as snow, it was so bright that no fuller (textile worker) on earth could have whitened them.
Then Elijah and Moses appeared and they were talking with Jesus.
Peter spoke to Jesus and said, "Teacher, it is good that we are here because we can make three tabernacles, one for you, and one each for Moses and Elijah."
Peter did not know what else to say because they were all extremely frightened.
Then a cloud appeared and overshadowed them, and a voice came out of the cloud that said, "This is my beloved son, listen to him!"
Suddenly they all looked around, and there was no one there with them except for Jesus.
As they descended from the mountain, Jesus ordered them not to tell anyone about the things they had seen until the Son of Man had risen from the dead.
So they kept secret what they had seen, but just between themselves they questioned each other about what rising from the dead meant.
They spoke to Jesus and asked, "Why do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?"
Jesus answered them and said, "`Truly Elijah does come first and restore all things. So why is it written that the Son of Man must suffer many things, and be seen as nothing?´
`I can tell you that Elijah has indeed come, and as it is written they treated him however they wanted.´"
When Jesus came to his disciples, he saw a huge crowd around them, and the scribes were questioning them.
As soon as the people saw Jesus, they were totally amazed and they ran to greet him.
And Jesus asked the scribes, "`Why are you questioning them?´"
Someone in the crowd answered him and said, "Teacher, I have brought my son who is possessed by a dumb spirit to you.
Whenever it attacks him it tears him up and makes him foam at the mouth, grind his teeth, and waste away. I spoke to your disciples, and they tried to throw him out, but they could not."
Jesus answered him and said, "`O faithless generation, how long will I be with you? How long will I suffer you? Bring him to me.´"
So the disciples brought the man's son to Jesus, but when the spirit saw him, it immediately threw him into convulsions, and he fell on the ground wallowing around foaming at the mouth.
Jesus asked his father, "`How long has this demon been with him?´" The man answered him and said, "He has been this way since he was a child."
It has thrown him into the fire and into the water to destroy him quite often. If there is anything you can do, have compassion on us and help us."
Jesus said to the man, "`If you can believe, all things are possible for anyone who believes.´"
Immediately the father cried out with tears and said, "Lord, I believe you can help me with my disbelief."
When Jesus saw the people running towards them, he rebuked the foul spirit and said to the demon, "`You deaf and dumb spirit, I order you to come out of him and never enter him again.´"
The demon cried out, then tore him violently and left the man. The man looked like he was dead and many people said, "He is dead!"
But Jesus took him by the hand and helped him stand up.
When Jesus went into the house with his disciples, they asked him privately, "Why could we not throw this demon out?"
And Jesus answered them and said, "`This kind of demon can only be expelled through prayer and fasting.´"
They left there and passed through Galilee, but Jesus did not want anyone to know they were there.

Jesus wanted to spend some time teaching his disciples and he said, "`The Son of Man will be delivered into the hands of men, and they will kill him. But after they kill him, he will rise again on the third day.´"
The disciples did not understand what he was saying, and they were afraid to ask.
After they arrived in Capernaum, Jesus was into the house with the disciples and he asked them, "`What were all of you arguing about on the way here?´"
But they held their peace and remained silent, because they had been arguing over which one of them was the greatest among them.
When Jesus sat down, he called the twelve and said, "`If a man wants to be first, he must be the last and the servant of all.´"
Then Jesus took a child and sat him down in the middle of them and took the child by his arms.
And Jesus said, "`Whoever receives one such as this child in my name, receives me, and whoever receives me, not only receives me but they receive the one who sent me.´"
John answered Jesus and said, "Teacher, we saw someone who was not one of our followers casting out demons in your name. We forbid him to do that because he does not follow us."
But Jesus said, "`Do not forbid him, because no one who performs a miracle in my name can casually speak evil of me.´
`For whoever is not against us is with us.´
`Because if anyone gives you a cup of water in my name because you belong to Christ, truly I tell you, they will not lose their reward.´
`But whoever offends one of these children who believe in me, would be better off if they had a millstone hung around their neck, and then thrown into the sea.´

`Therefore, if your hand offends and causes you to sin, cut it off. Because it would be better for you to enter life maimed, than it would be to have both hands and go to hell, where the never-ending fire is unquenchable.´
`A place where their worm does not die, and the fire is unquenchable.´

`And if your foot offends and causes you to sin, cut it off. Because it would be better for you to enter life crippled, than it would be to have both feet and go to hell, where the never-ending fire is unquenchable.´
`A place where their worm does not die, and the fire is unquenchable.´
`And if your eye offends and causes you to sin, pluck it out. Because it would be better for you to enter life with just one eye, than it would be to have two eyes and be thrown into hell.´
`Where their worm does not die, and the fire is not quenched.´
`For everyone will be salted with fire, and every sacrifice will be sealed with salt.´
`Salt is good, but if the salt loses its saltness, how will you season it? So, keep your salt among you, and have peace with one another.´"
Then Jesus got up and went to the coasts of Judea by the farthest side of Jordan. The people turned to him and as it had become accustomed, he taught them again.
And the Pharisees came to Jesus to test him and asked, "Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife?"
Jesus answered them and asked, "`What did Moses command you?´"
And they said, "Moses allowed them to write a divorce order to put her away."
So Jesus answered them and said, "`Moses wrote this law for you because your hearts were so hard.´
`But from the very beginning of the creation God made them male and female.´
`For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and hold loyally to his wife.´
`And the two will be as one flesh, so they are no longer two, but they become as one flesh.´
`Therefore, what God has joined together, let no man pull apart.´"
When his disciples returned to the house with Jesus, they asked him the same question again.
And Jesus answered them and said, "`Whoever divorces his wife, and marries another woman, commits adultery against her.´
`And if a woman divorces her husband, and marries another man, she also commits adultery.´"
The people began to bring young children to Jesus so he could touch them, and his disciples reprimanded the people who brought them.
When Jesus saw this, he was very displeased and said to them, "`Allow the little children to come to me, and do not forbid them, for the Kingdom of God is made up of those such as these.´
`Truly I tell you; whoever does not receive the Kingdom of God like a little child will not enter the kingdom.´"
Then he picked them up in his arms and put his hands on them and blessed them.
After Jesus left and went on his way, someone came running toward him and knelt down to him and said, "Good teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?"
Jesus answered him and said, "`Why do you call me good? No one is good except the One True God!´
`You know the commandments, do not commit adultery, do not kill, do not steal, do not bear false witness, do not defraud others, honor your father and mother.´"
And the man answered him and said, "Teacher, I have observed all these things since my youth."

Then Jesus looked at him and loved him and said, "`There is only one thing that you lack, go and sell whatever you have and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. So come, take up the cross and follow me.´"
The man went away sad and grieved when he heard that, because he possessed great wealth.
Then Jesus looked around at all his disciples and said, "`O how hard it is for those with riches to enter the Kingdom of God!´"
The disciples were astonished at what Jesus had just said. But Jesus spoke to them again and said, "`Children, how hard it is for those who trust in riches to enter the Kingdom of God!´
`It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle, than it is for a rich man to enter the Kingdom of God.´"
They were astonished beyond belief and spoke among themselves and said, "Then who can be saved?"
Jesus looking at them said, "`With men it is impossible, but not with God, because with God all things are possible.´"
Then Peter began to say to him, "Behold, we have left everything to follow you."
And Jesus answered him and said, "`Truly I tell you; there is no man who leaves his house, brothers, sisters, father, mother, wife, children, or lands for my sake and the sake of the gospels.´
`Who will not receive a hundredfold more now in this time, houses, brothers, sisters, mothers, children, and lands but with persecutions and eternal life in the world to come.´
`But many who are first will be last, and those who are last will be first.´"
They were on the way to Jerusalem and Jesus went before them. The disciples were amazed as they followed, but the twelve were afraid because Jesus began to tell them what was going to happen to him.
And Jesus said to them, "`Behold we are going to Jerusalem, where the Son of Man will be delivered to the chief priests and scribes. They will condemn him to death and deliver him to the Gentiles.´
`They will mock him, scourge him, spit on him, and kill him, but on the third day he will rise again.´"
One day James and John the sons of Zebedee came to him and said, "Teacher, we would like to ask you to do something for us that we desire."
Jesus answered them and asked, "`What would you like me to do for you?´"
They said to him, "Let us sit by your side in your glory, one on your right hand and the other on your left."
But Jesus said to them, "`You do not know what you are asking. Can you drink from the cup that I drink from, and be baptized with the same baptism that I am baptized with?´"
And they said to him, "We can!" And Jesus said, "`You will indeed drink from the cup that I drink from, and you will be baptized with the same baptism by which I am baptized.´
`But who will sit at my right hand or my left is not my decision to make, but it will be given to those for whom it is prepared.´"
When the other ten disciples heard this, they began to be very displeased with James and John.
But Jesus called them to himself and said, "`You know those who are appointed to rule over the Gentiles exercise lordship over them, and their great ones exercise authority over them.´
`But it will not be this way among you, for whoever wants to be great among you, will be your minister.´
`Whoever among you who wants to be the chief, will be the servant of all.´
`For even the Son of Man did not come to be ministered to, but to minister and give his life as a ransom for many.´"
And they arrived in Jericho, and as Jesus left Jericho with his disciples and a great number of people, blind Bartimaeus son of Timaeus sat by the roadside begging.
When he heard it was Jesus of Nazareth passing by, he began to cry out and say, "Jesus, son of David, have mercy on me!"
Many people told him to hold his peace and be quiet, but he cried out even more and made a great deal of it and said, "Son of David, have mercy on me!"
And Jesus stopped and stood still and told them to bring the blind man to him, and they called the blind man and said to him, "`Be comforted and get up, for he calls for you.´"
So the blind man cast away his garment and got up and went to Jesus.
Jesus spoke to the blindman and said, "`What would you have me do for you?´" The blind man said to him, "Lord, I ask that I might receive my sight."
And Jesus said to him, "`Go your way, because your faith has made you whole.´" Then the blind man immediately received his sight and began to follow Jesus.
When they approached Jerusalem, on the way to Bethphage and Bethany at Mount Olive, Jesus sent out two of his disciples.
And Jesus said to them, "`Make your way to the village nearby. As soon as you enter the village you will find a colt tied there which no one has ever man ridden, untie him and bring him here.´
`If a man asks you, 'What are you doing?' Tell him that the Lord needs him and the man will immediately send the colt here.´"
So they left and found the colt tied beside the door, outside at the intersection of two roads and they untied him.
Some of those who stood nearby asked them, "Why are you untying that colt?"
And they told them what Jesus had told them to say, and they let them go.
They brought the colt to Jesus; they threw their garments on the colt and Jesus sat on him.
Many people spread out their garments and others cut down tree branches and strew them along the way.
Those who went before them and those who followed cried out and said, "Hosanna! Blessed is he that comes in the name of the Lord.
Blessed is the kingdom of our father David, who comes in the name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest!"
Then Jesus entered Jerusalem and went into the temple. After he looked all around at everything and since it was already evening, he left Bethany with the twelve disciples.
The next day, as they were coming from Bethany, Jesus was hungry.
He saw a fig tree with leaves from a distance. But when he got there, he found nothing but leaves, because the fig season had not yet arrived.
Then Jesus spoke to the tree and said, "`No man will ever eat your fruit again, from now until forever!´" And his disciples heard him.
When they arrived in Jerusalem, Jesus went into the temple and began throwing out all the merchants. He turned over all the tables and chairs of the money changers and dove sellers.
Jesus would not even allow a merchant to carry a bowl through the temple.
Then Jesus taught them and said, "`Is it not written, 'My house will be called a house of prayer for all nations?' But you have made it into a den of thieves.´"
When the scribes and chief priests heard all the commotion, they looked for a way destroy him because they feared him. But all the people were astonished by his doctrine.
When evening came, Jesus left the city.
The next morning as they were passing by, the disciples saw that the fig tree had withered from its roots.
Then Peter remembered the day before and said to Jesus, "Teacher, look the fig tree that you cursed has withered away."
Jesus answered him and said, "`Have faith in God!´

`For truly I tell you, whoever says to this mountain, 'Be gone and be thrown into the sea!' And they do not doubt in their heart, but if they have faith in their heart that whatever they say, will happen, then it will happen.´
`Therefore I tell you, whatever you desire and ask for in prayer, if you believe that you have received it, then it will be given to you.´
`When you stand praying, if you remember that you have something against anyone, then you must forgive them, so that your father who is in heaven will also forgive you of your trespasses.´
`But if you do not forgive them, then your father who is in heaven will not forgive you of your trespasses.´"
After they returned to Jerusalem, Jesus was walking in the temple when the chief priests, scribes, and elders all came to him.
And they said to Jesus, "By what authority do you do these things, and who gave you the authority to do these things?"
Jesus answered them and said, "`I will also ask one question of you, and if you answer me, I will tell you by what authority I do these things.´
`Answer me this, was the baptism of John the Baptist from heaven or from men?´"
They discussed it among themselves and said to each other, "If we say, 'It was from heaven.' He will say, 'So, why did you not believe him?'"
But they were afraid to say, "It is from men." Because the people believed that John was indeed a prophet.
So, they answered Jesus and said, "We do not know." And Jesus answered them and said, "`Then I cannot tell you by what authority I do these things.´"

Jesus began to speak to them by parables and said, "`A man planted a vineyard, and built a hedge around it. Then he dug a place for the wine vat, and built a tower, and rented it out to some farmers and went on a trip to a distant country.´
`In the harvest season, he sent a servant to the farmers to collect his share of the vineyard fruit from the ranchers.´
`But they beat him and sent him away empty handed.`
`So the man sent another servant to them, and they threw stones at him and wounded his head, and they treated him shamefully and sent him away.´
`He sent another servant and him they killed, and he sent many others, but they beat some and killed some.´
`He had a much-loved only son, and he sent him to them last and he thought, 'They will respect my son.'´
`But the farmers schemed among themselves and said, 'This is the heir, let's kill him and take his inheritance.'´
`So they killed him and threw his body out of the vineyard.´
`So what will the vineyard owner do? He will come and destroy the farmers and give the vineyard to others.´
`Have you not read the scripture that says, 'The stone that the builders rejected has become the head cornerstone.'´
`The Lord has done this, and it is marvelous in our eyes.'?´"
After this the leaders sought to stop him, but they feared the people, because they knew that Jesus had spoken this parable against them, and they left him, and went their way.
Then they sent some Pharisees and Herodians to trick him into saying something they could use against him.

When they arrived, they said to him, "Teacher, we know that you are truthful and you do not show favoritism to anyone, because you are impartial to all men, and you teach God's way in truth. So, tell us truthfully is it lawful to pay tribute taxes to Caesar, or not?
Should we pay them, or not pay them?" But Jesus saw right through their hypocrisy and he said to them, "`Why do you test me? Bring me a penny.´"
They brought it and he asked them, "`Whose image and inscription are these?´" And they said to him, "It is Caesar's."
Then Jesus answered them and said, "`Give to Caesar the things that belong to Caesar and give to God the things that are God's.´" And the Pharisees and Herodians were completely dumbfounded.
Then the Sadducees who do not believe in the resurrection came to see him.

And they said, "Master, Moses wrote to us, 'If a man's brother dies and leaves his wife behind, and leaves no children. Then the man's brother should marry his brother's widow and raise children for his brother.
Now there were seven brothers, and the first one married a wife but died childless.
And the second brother married her and he died childless, and the third brother did likewise.
Finally the seventh brother married her and died childless, lastly the woman also died.
So in the resurrection after they rise, since all seven of them had been married to her, whose wife will she be?
And Jesus answered them and said, "`Do you not know that you are in error because you do not know the scriptures, nor do you know the power of God?´
`For when they rise from the dead, they will neither marry nor be given in marriage, but they will be like the angels who are in heaven.´
`But about the dead who will rise, have you not read in the Book of Moses, how God spoke to him from the burning bush and said, 'I am the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob?´
`He is not the God of the dead, but the God of the living, therefore you err greatly.´"
One of the scribes that came there had heard them debating. And he had seen how well Jesus answered their questions and he asked him, "Which is the most important commandment of them all?"
Jesus answered him and said, "`O Israel hear this, the most important commandment of our Lord God, the Lord who is one.´
`And the first commandment is, you will love your Lord God with all your heart, mind, soul, and with all your strength.´
`And the second commandment is like the first, you will love your neighbor as you love yourself. There are no other commandments greater than these.´"
And the scribe said to him, "Well said teacher, you have told the truth, because there is only one God, and there are no others but him.

And to love him with all your heart, all your understanding, all your soul, and all your strength, and to love your neighbor as yourself, is more important than all the burnt offerings and sacrifices."
When Jesus saw that he answered shrewdly he said to him, "`You are not far from the Kingdom of God.´" And no one dared to ask him another question after that.
While Jesus taught in the temple he asked, "`How can the scribes say that Christ is the son of David?´
`For David himself said that the Holy Spirit spoke through him and said, 'The Lord said to my Lord, sit on my right hand, until I make your enemies your footstool.'´
`Therefore David himself calls him Lord, so then how can he be David's son?´" And the common people listened to him joyfully.
Jesus taught them his doctrine and said, "`Beware of the scribes, who love to go around in long clothing, and they love to be greeted in the marketplaces.´
`And they want to have the chief seats in the synagogues, and the rooms of honor at the feasts.´
`They devour widows' houses, and they make long prayers with false claims, and these people will receive the greater damnation.´"
Then Jesus sat next to the treasury and saw the people throwing money into the treasury, and many who were rich threw in much.
A poor widow came and threw in two small copper coins, which is equal to a denarius.
Jesus called his disciples to him and said, "`Truly I tell you; this poor widow has thrown more into the treasury than all the others put together.´"
`For the others contributed from their abundance, but she is poor and she threw in everything that she had to live on.´"
As Jesus left the temple, one of his disciples said to him, "Teacher, look at the beautiful stone buildings here!"
Jesus answered him and said, "`Do you see these great buildings? There will not be one stone left standing on top of another, that will not be torn down.´"
As Jesus sat next to the temple on Mount Olive, Peter, James, John, and Andrew spoke to him privately.
And they asked him, "Tell us, when will all these things happen, and what will be the sign just before they happen?"
Jesus answered them and said, "`Pay attention and make sure that no one deceives you.´
`For many will come in my name and say, 'I am Christ,' and deceive many people.´
`And when you hear of wars and rumors of wars, do not be troubled, because these things must happen, but it will not yet be the end.´

`For nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom, and there will be earthquakes in different places, and there will be famine and trouble, but these things are just the beginnings of sorrows.´

`So pay attention, because they will deliver you up to councils and the synagogues where you will be beaten. You will be brought before kings and rulers for my sake, because I am a testimony against them.´
`The gospel must first be published among all nations.´

`But when they lead you and deliver you up to persecution, do not think or plan ahead of time what you will say. But whatever you must say will be given to you in the hour that you speak, because it will not be you speaking, for it will be the Holy Spirit.´
`Brother will betray brother to death and fathers will betray their sons. Children will rise up against their parents and cause them to be put to death.´
`You will be hated by all men for my name's sake, but the one who endures until the end will be saved.´

`But when you see the abomination of devastation standing where it should not be, that the prophet Daniel spoke of. Then the reader will understand, and those who are in Judea will flee to the mountains.´ (Daniel 9:27)
`Then no one on the rooftops must go down and enter into the house to take anything from his home.´
`And anyone who is in the field must not turn back to retrieve his garment´
`But woe unto those who are with child, and those nursing children in those days!´
`Pray that your time to flee is not in the winter.´
`For in those days there will be such affliction, that has not been seen since the beginning of God's creation until now, nor will be seen in the future.´
`And unless the Lord shortens those days, no one could be saved. But for the sake of his chosen elect, he has shortened those days.´
`So in those days if a man says to you, 'Look, here is the Christ, or he is over there, do not believe him.'´
`For false Christs and false prophets will rise up and show signs and wonders, to seduce even the elect if it were possible.´
`But pay attention because I have foretold all these things to you.´
`But in the days after the tribulation, the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give her light.´
`The stars of heaven will fall, and the heavenly powers in heaven will be shaken.´
`Then they will see the Son of Man coming in the clouds with great power and glory.´
`He will send his angels and gather his elect together from the four winds, from the farthest parts of the earth to the farthest parts of heaven.´
`Now learn the parable of the fig tree, when her branches are still tender and puts out leaves, you know that summer is near.´
`So it will be when you see these things happening, then you will know that the Lord is near, even at the door.´
`Truly I tell you; this generation will not pass until all these things have happened.´
`Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will never pass away.´
`But no one knows the day or the hour when these things will happen. No man, not the angels in heaven, not even the son, for only the father knows.´
`So pay attention, watch, and pray because you do not know when the time will come.´
`Because the Son of Man is like a man going on a distant journey, who left his house and gave authority to his servants. He assigned work to every man and told the gatekeeper to keep watch.´
`So watch because you do not know when the master of the house will return, whether it is in the evening, at midnight, when the cock crows, or in the morning.´
`Or else he will return suddenly and find you sleeping.´
`And what I say to you I say to everyone: Keep Watch!´"
It was two days before the Passover Feast of Unleavened Bread, and the chief priests and scribes were looking for a crafty way to arrest Jesus and put him to death.
But they said, "We cannot do it on the feast day because the people may riot."
At that time Jesus was in Bethany sitting at the table of Simon the leper's house, where a woman with an alabaster jar of very precious spikenard perfume opened the jar and poured it on his head.
Some people were indignant because of this and they said, "Why did she waste this expensive perfume?
Because it could have been sold for more than 50 shekels, and the money could have been given to the poor!" And they murmured against her.
And Jesus said, "`Leave her alone, why are you troubling her? She has done a good thing for me.´
`For you will always have the poor with you, and you may do good things for them whenever you want, but you will not always have me.´
`She has done what she could to anoint my body ahead of time in preparation of my burial.´
`Truly I tell you; wherever this gospel is preached throughout the whole world, what she has done will also be spoken of as a memorial to her.´"
Then Judas Iscariot one of the twelve disciples left to betray Jesus.
The chief priests were very happy to hear this, and they promised to give him money. Then Judas looked for a convenient opportunity to betray Jesus.

On the first day of the Feast of Unleavened Bread, at the time they killed the Passover sacrifice, Jesus' disciples asked him, "Where do you want us to go to prepare a place for you to eat the Passover?"
So Jesus sent two of his disciples into the city and he said, "`Go into the city, and you will see a man carrying a pitcher of water, follow him.´
`And speak to the owner of the house that he enters and say, 'The teacher asks, "Where are the guest chambers, where I can eat the Passover with my disciples?"'´
`And he will take you to a large upper room furnished and prepared for us. That's where you can prepare the feast.´"
Then his disciples left and went into the city, and they found everything just as Jesus had told them it would be, and they prepared for the Passover.
In the evening Jesus came with the twelve disciples.
As they sat and ate Jesus said, "`Truly I tell you; one of you eating here with me will betray me.´"
All the disciples began to be filled with sorrow, and each one spoke to Jesus and asked, "Am I the one?" And another one asked, "Is it me?"
Jesus answered them and said, "`It is one of the twelve who is dipping his bread in the dish with me.´
`The Son of Man will indeed go as it is written about him, but woe unto the man who betrays the Son of Man! It would have been better for that man if he had never been born.´"
As they ate, Jesus took some bread and blessed it, broke it and gave a piece to each one of his disciples and said, "`Take this and eat it, it is my body.´"
Then Jesus took the cup and after he had given thanks, he gave it to them, and they all drank from it.
Then Jesus said to them, "`This is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many.´
`Truly I tell you; I will drink no more from the fruit of the vine, until the day that I drink the new wine in the Kingdom of God.´"
After they sang a hymn, they left and went up into Mount Olive.
Jesus spoke to them and said, "`You will all be offended because of me tonight for it is written, 'I will kill the shepherd, and the sheep will scatter.'´
`But after that I will rise again and go before you into Galilee.´"
Then Peter said to Jesus, "All the others may be offended, but I will not."
Jesus answered Peter and said, "`Truly I tell you; this very night before the cock crows twice, you will deny me three times.´"
But Peter spoke more vehemently and said, "If I have to die with you, I will not deny you in any way." All the others agreed with Peter and said the same thing.
When they arrived at a place named Gethsemane, Jesus said to his disciples, "`Sit here while I go pray.´"
Then Jesus took Peter, James, and John with him who began to be very alarmed and deeply troubled.
Jesus said to them, "`My soul is extremely sorrowful to the point of death, stay here and keep watch.´"
Jesus went a little further and fell on the ground and prayed and said, "`If it is possible let this hour pass from me.´"
And Jesus also said to God, "`Abba (father) all things are possible with you, please take this cup from me. Nevertheless, not my will, but your will be done.´"
Jesus returned and found the disciples sleeping, and he said to Peter, "`Simon, are you asleep? Could you not keep watch for just one hour?´
`Watch and pray, or you may enter into temptation. For the spirit truly is willing, but the flesh is weak.´"
Again Jesus went away and prayed the same words.
But when he returned, he found them asleep again, because their eyes were heavy. And they did not know how to answer him.
Jesus returned to them a third time and said, "`Go ahead, sleep and get your rest. That is enough, the hour has come, behold the Son of Man has been betrayed into the hands of sinners.´
`Get up, let us go, look my betrayer is here.´"
Immediately, as Jesus was still speaking, Judas Iscariot one of the twelve arrived with many guards armed with swords and spears, who were sent by the chief priests, scribes, and elders.
The betrayer gave the guards a signal and said, "Whoever I kiss will be Jesus, arrest him and lead him away safely."
As soon as he arrived, Judas went straight to Jesus and said, "Master, Master," then he kissed him.
The guards grabbed Jesus and arrested him.
One of the bystanders drew a sword and struck one of the high priest's servants and cut his ear off.
And Jesus spoke up immediately and said to them, "`Have you come with swords and spears to arrest me as if I were a thief?´
`I was in the temple teaching you every day, and you did not arrest me, but the scriptures must be fulfilled.´"
Then everyone abandoned Jesus and fled.
A young man following Jesus was wearing a linen cloth thrown around his naked body. And the guards grabbed the young man.
He struggled free of the linen cloth and fled naked from them.
They led Jesus to the high priest, who had all the chief priests, elders, and scribes assembled together.
And Peter followed Jesus from a distance to the high priest's palace. He sat with the servants and warmed himself by the fire.
The chief priests and the whole council looked for a witness against Jesus to put him to death, but they found none.
Many people testified a false witness against Jesus, but none of their testimonies agreed with each other.
Then some came and testified a false witness against him.
And they said, "We heard him say, I will destroy this temple made with hands, and within three days I will build another made without hands."
But their testimonies did not agree with each other either.
The high priest stood up in the middle of them and asked Jesus, "Why do you say nothing about these people witnessing against you?"
But Jesus held his peace and said nothing. So, the high priest questioned Jesus again and asked, "Are you the Christ, the Son of the Blessed?"
And Jesus said, "`I am, and you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of power and coming in the clouds from heaven.´"
Then the high priest tore his clothes and said, "We have no need for any further witnesses?
