You have heard the blasphemy, so what do you think?" They all condemned him and declared that he was guilty and he deserved to die.
Some began to spit on him, they covered his face and blindfolded him. Then they beat him and said, "Prophesy!" And the servants slapped him with the palms of their hands.
Peter was beneath the palace, and one of the high priest's maids came down.
When she saw Peter warming himself, she looked at him and said, "You were with Jesus of Nazareth!"
But Peter denied it and said, "I do not know or understand what you are talking about!" And he left through the entrance hall and then the cock crowed.
Another maid saw him and began to say to those standing around, "This is also one of them!"
Peter denied it again and a little later, those standing around said to Peter one more time, "You are surely one of them, because you are a Galilean, and your accent gives you away."
But Peter began to curse and swear and he said, "I do not know the man you are talking about."
Then the cock crowed a second time, and Peter remembered that Jesus had said to him, "`Before the cock crows twice, you will deny me three times,´" and he began to weep.
The first thing in the morning the chief priests consulted with the elders, scribes, and the entire council. Then they had Jesus bound and carried to Pilate.
And Pilate asked him, "Are you the king of the Jews?" And Jesus answered him and said, "`You have said it.´"
The chief priests accused him of many things, but he refused to answer them.
Pilate spoke to him again and said, "Do you have no answer? Look at how many things they are accusing you of."
But Jesus still would not answer them, and Pilate was astounded.
Now at the feast it was Pilate's custom to pardon and release any prisoner that the people asked for.
There was a prisoner named Barabbas, who had committed murder in an insurrection who was bound with Jesus and the others.
And the crowds began crying out for Pilate to do what he had always done and release a prisoner.
But Pilate answered them and said, "Do you want me to release the king of the Jews to you?"
Pilate did this because he knew that the chief priests had only brought Jesus to him because they envied Jesus.
But the chief priests had convinced the people to ask Pilate to release Barabbas instead of Jesus.
So Pilate spoke to them again and said, "Well then, what do you want me to do with this Jesus whom you call the king of the Jews?"
And they cried out again, "Crucify him!"
Then Pilate said to them, "Why, what evil has he done?" And they cried out even more loudly, "Crucify him!"
Pilate wanted to placate the crowds, so he released Barabbas. Then he had Jesus flogged and delivered to the soldiers to be crucified.
The soldiers led Jesus to the hall called the Praetorium (Roman Governor's Residence), and they called all the other soldiers together.
They dressed Jesus in a purple robe, then they made a crown of thorns and placed it on his head.
They began to salute Jesus and shouted, "Hail, king of the Jews!"
And they beat his head with a stick, then they spit on him and knelt down and worshipped him.
After they mocked Jesus they removed the purple robe, and put his clothes back on him, and led him out to be crucified.
They forced a passerby named Simon a Cyrenian who was coming from the country to carry the cross for Jesus. Simon was the father of Alexander and Rufus.
They brought Jesus to the place known as Golgotha. (Place of a Skull)
Then they gave Jesus a drink of wine mixed with myrrh, but he refused it.
After they crucified Jesus, the soldiers divided his garments and cast lots to decide which man got each garment.
It was the third hour when they crucified Jesus.
They wrote an inscription with the accusations against Jesus on a board and hung it over his head that said, "THE KING OF THE JEWS!"
They crucified two thieves with Jesus, one on his right hand and the other on his left.
And the scripture was fulfilled which says, "He was counted among the transgressors."
People passing by screamed at him, shook their heads and said, "You were going to destroy the temple, and rebuild it in three days.
So save yourself and come down from the cross."
The chief priests and scribes also mocked Jesus and laughed among themselves and said, "He saved others, but he cannot save himself.
So let Christ the king of Israel descend from the cross, then we will see and believe." And those who were crucified with him also reviled him.
When the sixth hour came, darkness covered the whole land until the ninth hour.
At the ninth hour Jesus cried out with a loud voice and said, "`Eloi, Eloi, lama sabachthani?´" Which means "My God, My God, why have you forsaken me?"
Some of those standing nearby heard it and said, "Look he's calling for Elijah."
One of them ran and filled a sponge full of vinegar and put it on a stick, then gave Jesus a drink and said, "Leave him alone, let's see if Elijah comes and takes him down."
Then Jesus cried out with a loud voice, and he gave up the ghost.
That moment the temple veil was torn in half from top to bottom.
When the centurion standing next to him saw that Jesus had cried out so loudly and gave up the ghost, he said, "Truly this man was the Son of God!"
There were also some women looking on from a distance, including Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of James the less, Joses, and Salome.
Other women also followed Jesus and ministered to him when he was in Galilee. And they were accompanied by many other women who had come up to Jerusalem with Jesus.
When the evening came, because it was the preparation day which was the day before the Sabbath.
Joseph of Arimathea an honorable counsellor, who also waited for the Kingdom of God, came and boldly went to Pilate and begged for the body of Jesus.
Pilate was surprised that Jesus was already dead and summoned the centurion and asked him if Jesus had been dead for a while.
When he spoke to the centurion, he knew for sure that Jesus was dead and he gave the body to Joseph.
Joseph bought some fine linen, then took the body of Jesus down and wrapped him in linen and laid him in a tomb which was carved out of a rock and rolled a stone over the tomb's door.
Mary Magdalene and Mary, the mother of Joses saw this and they knew where Jesus was laid.
When the Sabbath was over, Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of James and Salome, bought some sweet spices and went to anoint the body of Jesus.
Very early in the morning at sunrise on the first day of the week, they went to the tomb.
They discussed it among themselves and said, "Who can we get to roll away the stone from the tomb's door?"
But when they looked, they saw that the stone had already been rolled away, even though it was very large.
Upon entering the tomb, they saw a young man sitting on the right side of the tomb. He was clothed in a long white robe, and they were frightened.
And he said to them, "Do not be afraid, you are looking for Jesus of Nazareth who was crucified. But he has risen and he is not here, look this is where they laid him.
Go tell Peter and his disciples that Jesus has gone ahead of you to Galilee, he told you that you would see him there."
Then they quickly fled the tomb, because they were trembling and amazed, but they said nothing to anyone because they were afraid.
Jesus had risen early on the first day of the week, and the first to see him was Mary Magdalene, from whom he had expelled seven demons.
Mary went to those who had been with Jesus, and she told them what she had seen as they mourned and wept.
When they heard that Jesus was alive and she had seen him, they did not believe it.
After that Jesus appeared to two other disciples in another form, as they were walking out in the country.
They went and told the rest of the disciples about it, but they did not believe them either.

Afterward Jesus appeared to the eleven as they sat eating. Then he severely criticized them because of their hard-hearted disbelief, and they did not believe those who had seen him after he had risen.
Then Jesus said to them, "`Go into all the world, and preach the gospel to every creature.´
`Whoever believes and is baptized will be saved, but those who do not believe will be damned.´
`These signs will follow those who believe in my name, they will cast out demons and speak in new tongues.´
`They will pick up serpents, and if they drink anything deadly, it will not hurt them, they will lay hands on the sick and they will recover.´"
After the Lord Jesus finished speaking to them, he was taken up into heaven, where he sat at the right hand of God.
So they left and obeyed the Lord's command. They went and preached everywhere, and the Lord was working within them, and God confirmed their word with signs. Amen.
I Luke write this, because many have set out to document the things which are most surely believed among us.
Even as they delivered the testimonies to us from eyewitnesses and ministers of the word from the beginning.
Therefore most excellent Theophilus, having a perfect understanding of all things from the very first, it also seemed like a good idea to me to write an orderly account for you.
So that you might know the certainty of those things, in which you have been instructed.
There was in the days of King Herod of Judea, a priest named Zacharias from the priest's division of Abia, whose wife Elizabeth was a daughter of Aaron.
Zacharias and Elizabeth were both righteous before God, walking blamelessly in all the laws and commandments of the Lord.
They had no children because Elizabeth was barren, and they were both well advanced in years.
One day while Zacharias was performing the duties of the priest's office before God in the order of his division.
It was the custom of the priest's office to cast lots to choose who would burn incense before the Lord, and Zacharias was chosen to burn incense when he entered the Lord's temple.
And the whole congregation was praying outside at the time of the incense offering.
Then an angel of the Lord appeared to Zacharias in the temple standing on the right side of the incense altar.
When Zacharias saw him, he was troubled and fearful.
But the angel said to him, "Fear not Zacharias because your prayer has been heard. Your wife Elizabeth will bear a son for you, and you will call him John.
You will have joy and happiness, and many will rejoice at his birth.
For he will be great in the Lord's sight, and he will not drink wine nor strong drink, and even from his birth he will be filled with the Holy Spirit.
Many of the children of Israel will return to their Lord God because of him.

And he will go before the Messiah in the spirit and power of Elijah. He will turn the hearts of the fathers to the children, and the disobedient to the wisdom of the righteous, to prepare the people for the Lord's coming."
And Zacharias said to the angel, "How will I know this? For I am an old man, and my wife is well advanced in years?"
The angel answered him and said, "I am Gabriel who stands in the presence of God, and I have been sent to speak to you and show you these glad tidings.
Behold you will be silenced and unable to speak until the day that these things happen, because you do not believe my words which will be fulfilled at the proper time."
The people waited for Zacharias, and they wondered why he stayed in the temple so long.
When Zacharias came out, he could not speak and they thought that he had seen a vision in the temple, because he motioned to them but he remained speechless.
When his days of service in the temple were complete, he went back to his own home.
After Zacharias returned from the temple his wife Elizabeth conceived, but she hid her pregnancy from others for five months.
Then she said, "The Lord has looked at me and dealt favorably with me, and he has taken away my disgrace among men."
In the sixth month of her pregnancy God sent the angel Gabriel to a city in Galilee named Nazareth.
God sent the angel Gabriel to a virgin named Mary who was promised in marriage to a man named Joseph from the house of David.
The angel went to Mary and said, "Hail to you Mary who are highly favored, for the Lord is with you and you are blessed among all women.
When she saw him, she was troubled by what he was saying, and she wondered why he had greeted her this way.
And the angel said to her, "Fear not Mary, because you have found favor with God.
Behold you will conceive a son, and you will name him Jesus.
He will be great, and he will be called the Son of the Highest, and the Lord God will give him his father David's throne.
And he will reign over the house of Jacob forever, and there will be no end to his kingdom."
Then Mary said to the angel, "How can this be, I have never been with a man?"

And the angel answered her and said, "The Holy Spirit will come to you, and the power of the Highest will overshadow you. That is also why this holy thing which will be born from you will be called the Son of God.
Behold your cousin Elizabeth who was called barren, has also conceived a son in her old age and she is in her sixth month of pregnancy.
For with God nothing is impossible."
And Mary said, "Behold I am the Lord's housemaid, may it be as you have said." And the angel left her.
In those days Mary got up and hurried into the hill country to a city in Juda.
Where Mary entered the house of Zacharias and greeted Elizabeth.
When Elizabeth heard Mary, the baby jumped in her womb, and Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit.
Then Elizabeth spoke out with a loud voice and said, "Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb!
Why does the mother of my Lord come to me?
For as soon as I heard the sound of your voice, the baby leaped for joy in my womb.
And blessed is she who believed the things would be fulfilled which were foretold to her from the Lord."
And Mary said, "My soul magnifies the Lord.
And my spirit has rejoiced in God my savior.
For he has regarded the low estate of his handmaiden, because from now on all descendants will call me blessed.
For the Mighty One has done great things for me, and holy is his name.
His mercy is on those who fear him from generation to generation.
He has shown strength with his arm; he has scattered the proud in the imaginations of their hearts.
He has brought down the mighty from their seats and glorified the humble.
He has filled the hungry with good things and sent the rich away empty handed.
He has helped his servant Israel and remembered his mercy.
As he told our fathers, Abraham, and his descendants forever."
Mary lived with Elizabeth for about three months, then returned to her own home.
Then Elizabeth's time to deliver arrived, and she gave birth to a son.
Elizabeth's neighbors and her cousins heard how the Lord had shown great mercy to her, and they rejoiced with her.
On the eighth day they came to circumcise the child, and they named him Zacharias after his father.
But his mother spoke up and said, "No, he must be called John."
And they said to her, "But none of your relatives are named John."
So they made signs to his father to find out what he wanted to name him.
Zacharias asked for a writing tablet and wrote, "His name is John!" And they were all astonished.
Immediately Zacharias opened his mouth, and his tongue was loosened, and he spoke and praised God.
Everyone around him was overcome with fear, and people throughout the hill country of Judea were talking about what had happened.
Everyone who heard about them were wondering in their hearts and asked, "What kind of child will this be?" And the hand of the Lord was with Zacharias.
John's father Zacharias was filled with the Holy Spirit and he prophesied.
And Zacharias said, "Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, because he has visited and rescued his people.
He has raised up a horn of salvation for us in the house of his servant David.
The Lord has spoken through his holy prophets, who have been with us since the world began.
So that we would be saved from the hands of our enemies and everyone that hates us.
The Lord has shown us the mercy that he promised our fathers, and he has remembered his holy covenant.
The Lord has kept the oath which he swore to our father Abraham.
And he has delivered us from the hands of our enemies, so that we might serve him without fear.
So we can serve the Lord in holiness and righteousness all the days of our life.
And you child, will be called John the prophet of the highest, because you will go before the Lord to prepare his way.
You will give the knowledge of salvation to his people through the remission of their sins.
You will teach about the tender mercy of our God, by which the day will spring forth and be visited on us from on high.
And you John will give light to those who sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, to guide our feet into the way of peace."
And the child grew strong in spirit in the deserts until the day he appeared to Israel.
In those days, Caesar Augustus proclaimed a decree that the whole world should be taxed.
This first tax was made when Cyrenius was governor of Syria.
Everyone went into their own city to pay the tax.
Joseph also left the city of Nazareth in Galilee and went to Judea to the city of David called Bethlehem, because he was from the house and lineage of David.
So Joseph went to pay his taxes with Mary who he was engaged to marry, who was also expecting a child.
While they were there, Mary's nine-month pregnancy was up and her time to give birth had come.
So Mary gave birth to her firstborn son and wrapped him in warm swaddling clothing and laid him in a manger, because there was no room for them in the inn.
While they were in that country, there were shepherds living in the fields nearby, keeping watch over their flock by night.
Lo and behold, an angel of the Lord came to the shepherds, and the Lord's glory shone all around them, and they were extremely frightened.
And the angel said to them, "Fear not, for I bring you good news of great joy for all people.
For unto you on this day in the city of David a savior is born, who is Christ the Lord.
And this will be a sign to you; you will find a baby wrapped in warm swaddling clothing lying in a manger.
Suddenly a multitude of heavenly hosts praising God appeared with the angel.
And they were saying, "Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace and goodwill toward men!"
Then as the angels left them and went back to heaven, the shepherds said to each other, "Let's go to Bethlehem and see that which the Lord has made known to us."
And they hastily went to Bethlehem where they found Mary, Joseph, and the baby lying in a manger.
After they saw this, they spread the word everywhere about what they were told about this child.
Everyone who heard it wondered about the things that the shepherds were telling them.
But Mary kept all these things in her heart and pondered them.
When the shepherds returned, they glorified and praised God, for they had seen and heard everything that the angel had told them.
After the eight days were up that Joseph and Mary were required to wait before circumcising the child Jesus, which was the name that the angel had given him before he was conceived.
And after the days of Mary's purification required by the Law of Moses were finished, Joseph and Mary brought Jesus to Jerusalem, to present him to the Lord.
Because, as it is written in the Law of the Lord, "Every firstborn male child who opens the womb will be consecrated to the Lord."
And the Law of the Lord also required them to offer a sacrifice of a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons.
There was a man named Simeon in Jerusalem who was righteous and devout. He was waiting for the consolation of Israel, and the Holy Spirit was upon him.
The Holy Spirit had revealed to Simeon, that he would not die before he had seen the Lord's Christ.
Simeon was led by the spirit into the temple, where Joseph and Mary had brought baby Jesus to do what the law required.
Then Simeon picked Jesus up in his arms and blessed God.
And Simeon said, "Lord, let your servant leave this world in peace now as you have said.
For my eyes have seen your salvation.
Which you have prepared in front of all people.
A light to enlighten the Gentiles, and for the glory of your people of Israel."
Joseph and Mary marveled at the things which were spoken about Jesus.

Then Simeon blessed them and said to Mary mother of Jesus, "Behold this child is appointed to cause the fall and rising up again of many people in Israel, and to be a sign which many will speak against.
Yes, a sword will also pierce you through your own soul, to reveal the thoughts of many hearts."
There was a very old prophetess named Anna daughter of Phanuel, from the tribe of Aser. Anna had been a virgin when she married her husband who she lived with for only seven years before he died.
Anna had been a widow for about eighty-four years, and she had not left the temple, but she had served God with fasting and prayers night and day.
Anna had also come at that moment to give thanks to the Lord, and she spoke of Jesus to whoever had come looking for redemption in Jerusalem.
After Joseph and Mary did everything required by the Law of the Lord, they returned to their own city of Nazareth in Galilee.
The child Jesus grew and grew strong in spirit, he was filled with wisdom, and the grace of God was upon him.
Now his parents went to Jerusalem every year for the Passover feast.
When Jesus was twelve years old, they went to Jerusalem since it was the custom for the Passover feast.
After they had been there for the appropriate number of days, Joseph and Mary returned home, but Jesus had stayed behind in Jerusalem which they did not know.
They thought Jesus with them, but after they had been travelling for a full day, they went to look for him among their family and friends.
When they could not find him, they returned to Jerusalem looking for him.
After three days of looking, they found Jesus in the temple sitting among the doctors, both listening to them and asking them questions.
Anyone who heard him was astonished by his answers and understanding.
When Joseph and Mary saw him, they were amazed and his mother said to him, "Son, why have you done this to us? Behold, your father and I have been worried looking for you."
And Jesus said to them, "`Why were you looking for me? Did you not know that I must be doing my father's business?´"
And they did not understand what Jesus had said to them.
Then Jesus went back down with them to Nazareth and he obeyed them, but his mother kept all these things in her heart.
And the wisdom and stature of Jesus increased, both in God's favor and with man.

In the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar, while Pontius Pilate was governor of Judea, Herod was the tetrarch (governor of one-fourth of a domain or kingdom) of Galilee. Herod's brother Philip was the tetrarch of Ituraea and of the region of Trachonitis, and Lysanias was the tetrarch of Abilene.
Annas and Caiaphas were the high priests, but the word of God came to John the son of Zacharias in the wilderness.
And John went throughout the countryside around the Jordan River, preaching the baptism of repentance for the remission of sins.
The coming of John is written about in the book of Isaiah the prophet who said, "The voice of one crying out in the wilderness, will prepare the way of the Lord, and make his paths straight.
Every valley will be filled, every mountain and hill will be brought low, the crooked will be made straight, and the rough ways will be made smooth.
And all living flesh will see God's salvation."
Then John preached to the crowds that came to be baptized by him and said, "O generation of vipers, I have warned you to flee from the anger to come?
Therefore, you must produce fruit worthy of repentance, and do not begin to say to yourselves, 'Abraham is our father!' For I tell you, God can raise up Abraham's children from these stones.
Now the axe is ready at the root of the trees, and every tree that does not produce good fruit will be cut down and thrown into the fire."
And the people asked him, "Well then, what can we do?"
John answered them and said, "Whoever has two coats, give one to someone who has none, and whoever has meat must do likewise."
Then the tax collectors also came to be baptized and asked John, "Master, what can we do?"
John answered them and said, "Collect no more tax than you are required by law to collect."

Some soldiers also demanded answers from John and asked, "What can we do?" And he answered them and said, "Commit no violence against anyone, do not make false accusations, and be content with your wages."
The people were waiting expectantly and they all pondered in their hearts, whether or not John was the Christ.

John answered them all and said, "I have indeed baptized you with water, but one mightier than I am is coming. For I am unworthy to untie his shoelaces, but he will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire.

The Lord's flail (tool for separating wheat from chaff) is in his hand to thoroughly purge his threshing room floor, and he will gather his wheat into his barn, but he will burn the chaff with unquenchable fire."
And John preached these and many other encouraging things to the people.
But John blamed Herod the tetrarch for marrying his brother Philip's wife Herodias, and for all the other evils which Herod had committed.
But Herod added this above all his other evil deeds, and he put John in prison for speaking out.
Now while all the people were being baptized, Jesus also wanted to be baptized. And as he was praying the heavens opened up.
Then the Holy Spirit descended in the bodily shape of a dove and landed on him, and a voice came from heaven which said, "You are my beloved son, in whom I am well pleased."
Jesus was about thirty years old when he began to teach, and the people thought that he was just the son of Joseph who was the son of Heli.
Who was the son of Matthat, son of Levi, son of Melchi, son of Janna, who was the son of Joseph.
Who was the son of Mattathias, son of Amos, son of Naum, son of Esli, who was the son of Nagge.
Who was the son of Maath, son of Mattathias, son of Semei, son of Joseph, who was the son of Juda.
Who was the son of Joanna, son of Rhesa, son of Zorobabel, son of Salathiel, who was the son of Neri.
Who was the son of Melchi, son of Addi, son of Cosam, son of Elmodam, who was the son of Er.
Who was the son of Jose, son of Eliezer, son of Jorim, son of Matthat, who was the son of Levi.
Who was the son of Simeon, son of Juda, son of Joseph, son of Jonan, who was the son of Eliakim.
Who was the son of Melea, son of Menan, son of Mattatha, son of Nathan, who was the son of David.
Who was the son of Jesse, son of Obed, son of Booz, son of Salmon, who was the son of Naasson.
Who was the son of Aminadab, son of Aram, son of Esrom, son of Phares, who was the son of Juda.
Who was the son of Jacob, son of Isaac, son of Abraham, son of Thara, who was the son of Nachor.
Who was the son of Saruch, son of Ragau, son of Phalec, son of Heber, who was the son of Sala.
Who was the son of Cainan, son of Arphaxad, son of Sem, son of Noah, who was the son of Lamech.
Who was the son of Methuselah, son of Enoch, son of Jared, son of Maleleel, who was the son of Cainan.
Who was the son of Enos, son of Seth, son of Adam, who was the son of God.
Then Jesus was full of the Holy Spirit as he returned from the Jordan River, and he was led by the spirit out into the wilderness.
Where he was tempted by the devil for forty days, during which time he ate nothing. Jesus was very hungry after those forty days ended.
And the devil said to him, "If you are the Son of God, turn this stone into bread."
Jesus answered him and said, "`It is written, 'Man does not live by bread alone, but by every word of God.'´"
Then the devil took him up into the high mountains and showed him all the world's kingdoms in a moment of time.
And the devil said to him, "I will give you all this power and the glory of these kingdoms, because it has been delivered to me and I can give it to whoever I want.
Therefore if you will only worship me, it will all be yours."
But Jesus answered him and said, "`Get behind me Satan, because it is written, 'You will worship your Lord God and only serve him.'´"
Then Satan brought him to Jerusalem and set him on top of the temple pinnacle and said to him, "If you are the Son of God, throw yourself down from here.
For it is written, he will command his angels to keep you and protect you.
And at any time they can lift you up in their hands to prevent you from dashing your foot against a stone."
So Jesus answered him and said, "`It is said, that you must not tempt your Lord God.´"
When the devil was finished trying to lure Jesus into temptation, he left him for a while.
Jesus returned to Galilee filled with the power of the spirit, and his fame began to spread throughout the entire region.
Jesus taught in their synagogues, and he was glorified by everyone.
When Jesus arrived in Nazareth where he had been raised, as was his custom he went to the synagogue on the Sabbath day, and he stood up to read the scriptures.
They gave the book of the prophet Isaiah to Jesus, and he opened the book and found a certain place in the book.

And Jesus read aloud what was written in the book where it said, "`The Spirit of the Lord is upon me because he has anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor. God has sent me to heal the broken hearted, to preach deliverance of the captives, to recover the sight of the blind, to liberate those who are bruised.´
`And to preach the acceptable year of the Lord.´"
Then Jesus closed the book and gave it back to the minister and sat down, and everyone in the synagogue was staring at him.
Jesus began to teach them and said, "`Today the scripture you have just heard, has been fulfilled.´"
And they all wondered about Jesus and his gracious words and they asked each other, "Is this not Joseph the carpenter's son?"

Jesus spoke to them and said, "`Today you will surely quote this proverb to me and say, 'Physician, heal yourself! Do for us here in your own country, everything that we have heard that you did in Capernaum.'´"
And Jesus said, "`Truly I tell you; no prophet is accepted in his own country.´
`But I tell you the truth, many widows were in Israel in the days of Elijah, when the heavens were closed shut for three years and six months, when there was a great famine throughout the land.´
`But no one was sent by Elijah, except the one that he sent to a widowed woman in Sarepta a city in Sidon.´
`Many lepers were in Israel during the time of Eliseus the prophet, and none of them were cleansed except Naaman the Syrian.´"
When the people in the synagogue heard these things, they were all filled with anger.
They all got up and threw him out of the city, and they led him to the top of the hill on which their city was built, so they could throw him off the cliff headfirst.
But he walked through the middle of the crowd and left.
Jesus went down to Capernaum a city in Galilee, where he taught them on the Sabbath days.
The people were astonished by the doctrine of Jesus, because his words were so powerful.
In the synagogue a man who was possessed by the spirit of an unclean demon, cried out with a loud voice.
The man's demons said, "Leave us alone, what do we have to do with you, Jesus of Nazareth? Have you come to destroy us? I know you and I know who you are, you are the Holy One of God."
Then Jesus reprimanded him and said, "`Quiet, hold your peace, and come out of him!´" The demon threw the man down in the middle of them all and it came out of him, and it did not hurt him.
Everyone was amazed and discussed it among themselves and said, "What kind of word is this! For he commands the unclean spirits with authority and power, and they come out!"
And the fame of Jesus spread throughout the province of every country around them.
Jesus got up and left the synagogue. He went to Simon's house, where he discovered that Simon's mother-in-law was sick with a terrible fever, and they begged Jesus to help her.
So Jesus stood over her and reprimanded the fever, it left her and she immediately got up and began to minister to them.
When the sun was setting, everyone who was sick with different diseases was brought to Jesus, and he laid his hands on each one of them and healed them.
He also drove out many demons from many people who cried out and said, "You are Christ the Son of God!" And he rebuked them told them not to speak, because the demons knew that he was Christ.
The next morning, Jesus left and went out into the desert, and the people went looking for him. They found Jesus and tried to keep him from leaving.
But Jesus said to them, "`I must preach the Kingdom of God to other cities, because I was sent for that reason.´"
And Jesus preached in the synagogues of Galilee.
Once as Jesus stood by the lake of Gennesaret, the people pressed him to hear the word of God.
Jesus saw two boats sitting along the lakeshore, but the fishermen had gone to wash their nets.
Jesus climbed into a boat that belonged to Simon and asked him to push away from land a little bit, and he sat down and taught the people from the boat.
After he finished speaking Jesus spoke to Simon and said, "`Push out into the deep water and lower your fishing nets to catch some fish.´"
Simon answered him and said, "Master, we have worked all the night and we have caught nothing, but I will lower the net for you."
After they had this done, they caught a huge number of fish and their net broke.
So they called out to their partners in the other boat and asked them to come and help them. They came and filled both boats so full that they began to sink.
When Simon Peter saw this, he knelt down in front of Jesus and said, "O Lord, leave me because I am a sinful man."
Because Simon Peter and everyone with him were astonished how many fish they had caught.
So were James and John the sons of Zebedee, who were partners with Simon. Then Jesus said to Simon, "`Fear not, from now on you will catch men.´"
After they brought their boats back to land, they abandoned everything and followed Jesus.
While Jesus was in one of the cities, a man with leprosy came and knelt down before him and begged for help and said, "Lord, if you are willing, you can make me clean."
Then Jesus put out his hand and touched the man and said, "`I am willing, be clean!´" Immediately his leprosy left him.
Jesus told the man not to tell anyone and he said, "`Go, and show yourself to the priest, and give him the offering that Moses commanded for your cleansing, as a testimony to them.´"
But word of Jesus spread abroad even more, and great crowds came to hear him and to be healed of their diseases.
So he frequently withdrew to the wilderness to pray.

One day, as he was teaching, there were Pharisees and doctors of the law sitting nearby, who had come from every town around Galilee, Judea, and Jerusalem. And the power of the Lord was present with Jesus to heal the sick.
Some men brought a bedridden man who was paralyzed, and they tried to find a way bring him in to lay him before Jesus.
When they could not find a way in through the crowds, they climbed up on the housetop and lowered him and his couch down through the roof into the middle of the crowd before Jesus.
When Jesus saw their faith he said to the crippled man, "`Your sins are forgiven.´"
The scribes and Pharisees began talking among themselves and said, "Who is this man who speaks blasphemies? Who can forgive sins but God alone?"
But Jesus knew what they were thinking, so he spoke up and said, "`Why are you allowing these thoughts in your hearts?´
`Is it easier to say, 'Your sins are forgiven, or to say, 'Get' up and walk'?´
`But just so you know that the Son of Man has power on earth to forgive sins.´" Then he turned to the crippled man and said, "`I say to you, get up and pick up your couch and go home.´"
Immediately the crippled man got up in front of them, and took his couch and went home, glorifying God.
They were all amazed and they glorified God, but they were filled with fear and said, "We have seen strange things today."
After all this Jesus left. As Jesus was leaving, he saw a tax collector named Levi sitting at the collection booth and he said, "`Follow me.´"
So Levi got up and followed Jesus.
Levi prepared a great feast for Jesus in his own house, and there were a lot of tax collectors and others who sat with them.
But the scribes and Pharisees murmured against his disciples and said, "Why do you eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?"
Jesus answered them and said, "`Those who are whole do not need a physician, but the sick do.´
`I did not come to call the righteous, but I came to call the sinners to repentance.´"
And they asked Jesus, "Why do John's disciples often fast and pray like the disciples of the Pharisees, but you just keep on eating and drinking?"
Jesus answered them and said, "`Can you make the children of the bridal chamber fast, while the bridegroom is still with them?´
`But the day is coming when the bridegroom will be taken away from them, and then will they fast.´"

Then Jesus spoke a parable to them and said, "`No one repairs an old garment with a piece of cloth from a new garment. if they did then both the new garment will be torn, and the piece taken from the new garment will noy match the old garment.´
`No one puts new wine into old wineskins, otherwise the new wine would burst the wineskins, and it will be spilled, and the wineskins will be ruined.´
`But new wine must be put into new wineskins, and both will be protected.´
`No one wants new wine after drinking old wine, because the old wine is better.´"
On the second Sabbath after the first of the month, Jesus was walking through the wheat fields, and his disciples were picking the ripe wheat heads, then rubbing them in their hands and eating them.
One of the Pharisees asked them, "Why are you breaking the law on the Sabbath?"
Jesus answered him and said, "`Have you not read of what David and his friends did when they were hungry?´
`About how David and the others went into God's house and ate the priests bread offering, which was only lawful for the priests to eat?´"
Furthermore Jesus said, "`The Son of Man is also the Lord of the Sabbath.´"
On another Sabbath, Jesus was teaching in the synagogue where a man with a withered right hand was sitting.
The scribes and Pharisees were watching to see if Jesus would heal on the Sabbath day, they were trying to find something to use against him and make accusations against him.
But Jesus knew what they were thinking, and he said to the man with the withered hand, "`Get up, and stand out in the middle of the sanctuary.´" So, he got up and stood there.
Then Jesus said to them, "`I will ask you one thing, is it lawful to do good or evil on the Sabbath day? To save life, or to destroy it?´"
After looking around at all of them he said to the man, "`Stretch out your hand.´" When he did, his hand was completely restored like the other one.
The scribes and Pharisees were filled with anger, and they asked each other what they should do about Jesus.
In those days, Jesus went up into a mountain to pray, and he prayed to God all night long.
When daylight came, he called his disciples to him and he chose twelve of them, whom he also appointed as apostles.
Simon, whom he had named Peter and his brother Andrew, plus James, John, Philip, and Bartholomew.
And Matthew, Thomas, James the son of Alphaeus, and Simon the Zealot.
And Judas the brother of James, and Judas Iscariot who was also the traitor.

Then Jesus went with them and they all stood out in the plains. Where a large number of his disciples, and a massive crowd of people from all over Judea, Jerusalem, and the coasts of Tyre and Sidon had come to hear him and to be healed of their diseases.
And they were healed, and so were those who were tormented by unclean spirits.
Everyone in the crowd tried to touch Jesus, because goodness was coming from him and he healed them all.
Jesus looked up at his disciples and said, "`Blessed are the poor, for yours is the Kingdom of God.´
`Blessed are you who hunger now, for you will be filled. Blessed are you who weep now, for you will laugh.´
`Blessed are you when people hate you, when they drive you away and despise you and renounce your name as evil, because of the Son of Man.´
`Rejoice and leap for joy in those days, because your reward in heaven is great. Because their fathers treated the prophets the same way.´
`But woe unto you who are rich! For you have received your reward.´
`Woe unto you who have been fed! For you will hunger. Woe unto you who laugh now! For you will mourn and weep.´
`Woe unto you when everyone speaks well of you! For their fathers spoke of the false prophets the same way.´
`But I say to you who are listening, love your enemies and do good for those who hate you.´
`Bless those who curse you and pray for those who maliciously use you.´"
`Furthermore Jesus said, "`Whoever strikes you on the cheek, then offer them the other cheek also. And whoever takes your cloak, offer them your coat as well.´
`Give to anyone who asks you, and if anyone takes anything you own, do not ask them to give it back.´
`Do unto others as you would have them do unto you.´
`For if you only love those who love you, what appreciation will you be given? For sinners also love those who love them.´
`And if you only do good for those who do good to you, what appreciation will you be given? For even the sinners do that.´
`And if you only lend to those whom you hope will repay you, what appreciation will you be given? For even sinners lend to sinners, to be repaid in full.´

`But love your enemies and do good and lend to them hoping for nothing in return. Then your reward will be great, and you will be the children of the Most High, for he is kind to the unthankful and the evil.´
`Therefore be merciful, just as your father also is merciful.´
`Judge not, and you will not be judged. Do not condemn, and you will not be condemned. Forgive, and you will be forgiven.´

`Give, and it will be given to you in good measure, pressed down, shaken together, and running over men will give for you to embrace. For with the same measure that you use it will be measured back to you.´"
Then Jesus spoke a parable to them and said, "`Can the blind lead the blind? Will they not both fall into the ditch?´
`A disciple is not above his teacher, but one who is perfect will be his teacher.´
`Why do you see the speck that is in your brother's eye, but you do not even notice the beam that is in your own eye?´

`How can you say to your brother, 'Brother, let me pull that speck out of your eye,' when you yourself do not see the beam that is in your own eye? You hypocrite, first throw the beam out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly enough to pull the speck out of your brother's eye.´
`For a good tree does not produce corrupt fruit, nor does a corrupt tree produce good fruit.´
`For every tree is known by its own fruit. For men do not collect figs from a thorn bush, nor do they harvest grapes from a bramble bush.´
`For a good man brings good treasures from his good heart, and an evil man brings evil treasure from his evil heart, because his mouth speaks from the abundance of his heart.´
`Why do you call me 'Lord, Lord,' but you do not do what I say?´
`This is what the one who comes to me and hears what I say and does them is like.´

`He is like a man who built a house and dug a deep foundation and laid it on a rock. When the stream rose and flooded, and beat vehemently against that house, it could not be shaken because it was built on a rock.´

`But the one who hears and does nothing, is like a man who built a house on the ground without a foundation. When the stream vehemently beat against that house, it immediately fell and its ruins were great.´"
After Jesus finished speaking to the audience, he went to Capernaum.
One of the centurions there had a sick servant who was very dear to him and near death.
When he heard about Jesus, he sent some Jewish elders to Jesus to beg him to come and heal his servant.
When they reached Jesus, they immediately begged him and said, "This centurion is worthy for you to come and heal his servant.
For he loves our nation, and he has built a synagogue for us".
Then Jesus went with them but before they reached the house, the centurion sent friends to Jesus who said, "Lord, do not trouble yourself, because I am not worthy to have you under my roof.
Nor do I consider myself worthy to come to you, but just say the word and my servant will be healed.

Because I am also a man with authority, and I have soldiers under me, and I say to one, 'Go,' and he goes. And I say to another, 'Come,' and he comes. And I tell my servant to do something and he does it."
When Jesus heard these things, he was astonished, and he turned around and said to the people following him, "`I tell you, I have not found such great faith, not even in Israel.´"
When those who were sent returned to the house, they found that the sick servant had been healed.
The day after that, Jesus went to a city called Nain, and his disciples went with him, along with many other people.
When Jesus approached the city gate, he saw a a dead man being carried out. He was his mother's only son and she was a widow, and many people from the city were with her.
When the Lord saw her, he had compassion for her and he said to her, "`Do not weep.´"
Jesus went and touched the open coffin, and the ones carrying it stood still and he said, "`Young man, I tell you to rise.´"
And the dead man sat up and began to speak, and Jesus returned him to his mother.
And fear overcame everyone, and they glorified God and said, "A great prophet has risen up among us!" And they said, "God has visited his people!"
This rumor spread throughout all of Judea, and throughout all the surrounding regions.
Then John the Baptist's disciples told John about all these things.
So John sent two of his disciples to find Jesus and he told them to ask him, "Are you the one who is to come, or should we look for someone else?"
When the men found Jesus they said, "John the Baptist has sent us to you and he asks, "Are you the one who is to come, or should we look for someone else?"
During that same hour Jesus cured many people of their infirmities and plagues. And he drove out evil spirits and gave sight to many who were blind.

Then Jesus answered them and said, "`Go and tell John what you have seen and heard. Tell him that the blind see, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the gospel is preached to the poor.´
`Blessed is he, who is not offended because of me.´"
When John's messengers left, Jesus began to speak to the people about John and said, "`What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaking in the wind?´
`Did you go out to see a man dressed in fine clothing? Behold, those who are so gorgeously dressed, and live in luxury are found in king's courts.´
`But what did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell you, and much more than a prophet.´
`John is the one about whom it is written, 'Behold I will send my messenger before you, who will prepare your way before you.´
`For I say to you, among those who are born of women there is no greater prophet than John the Baptist, but he who is least in the Kingdom of God is greater than John.´
All the people who heard Jesus, including the tax collectors praised God's justice, because they had been baptized by John.
But the Pharisees and lawyers rejected God's counsel against themselves, because they had not been baptized by John.
And the Lord said, "`To whom should I liken the men of this generation, and what are they like?´
`They are like children sitting in the marketplace calling out to one another and saying, 'We played the pipes for you, and you did not dance, we sang a dirge for you, and you did not weep.'´
`For John the Baptist came neither eating bread nor drinking wine and you said, 'He has demon!'´
`The Son of Man comes eating and drinking and you say, 'He is a gluttonous man, a drunkard, and a friend of tax collectors and sinners!'´
`But wisdom is justified by all her children.´"
Then one of the Pharisees invited Jesus to come eat with him, and he went to the Pharisee's house, and sat down at his table.
And behold a woman in the city who was a sinner found out that Jesus was eating at the Pharisee's house, and she brought an alabaster jar of perfume.
Then she stood at his feet behind him weeping and began to wash his feet with tears. She wiped them with her hair, and kissed his feet, and anointed them with the perfume.

When the Pharisee who had invited him, saw this, he thought to himself and said, "If this man were a prophet, he would have known who touched him and what type of woman she was because she was a sinner."
Jesus answered him and said, "`Simon, I have something to say to you.´" And Simon said, "Speak up teacher."
And Jesus said, "`There was a banker who had two debtors, one owed him five hundred denarius, and the other one owed him fifty.´
`When they were unable to pay, he quite frankly forgave both of them. So, tell me, which one will love him more?´
Simon answered Jesus and said, "I suppose it is the one who he has forgiven the largest debt." And Jesus said to him, "`You have judged correctly.´"

Then Jesus turned to the woman and said to Simon, "`Do you see this woman? I entered your house, and you gave me no water to wash my feet, but she has washed my feet with tears and wiped them with her hair.´
`You gave me no kiss, but this woman has not stopped kissing my feet since I came in.´
`You did not anoint my head with oil, but this woman has anointed my feet with perfume.´
`Therefore I tell you, her many sins have been forgiven, because she has loved much, but the one who has been forgiven little, also loves little.´"
And Jesus said to her, "`Your sins are forgiven.´"
And those who were eating with him began to think to themselves, "Who is this that can also forgive sins?"
Then Jesus said to the woman, "`Your faith has saved you, go in peace.´"
Afterwards, Jesus and the twelve disciples went throughout every city and village, preaching and teaching the good news of the Kingdom of God.
There were some women with Jesus who had been healed of evil spirits and infirmities including Mary Magdalene, from whom he had cast out seven demons.
Joanna the wife of Herod's manager Chuza, Susanna, and many others who ministered to him from their own resources.
When a large crowd gathered together, and people were coming to Jesus from every city, he told them a parable.
And Jesus said, "`A farmer went out to sow his seed, and as he sowed, some seed fell by the roadside, and it was trampled, and the birds of the air devoured it.´
`Some seed fell on rocky ground, and as soon as it sprouted, the seedlings withered, because they lacked moisture.´
`Some seed fell among thorns, and the thorns sprouted with it, and choked the seedlings.´
`Other seed fell on good ground, and sprouted, and produced fruit a hundredfold.´" After he had said these things, he called out and said, "`Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear.´"
Then Jesus disciples questioned him and asked, "What does this parable mean?"

And Jesus said, "`The knowledge of the mysteries of the Kingdom of God has been given to you, but I speak to others in parables, so that even though they see, they still do not see, and even though they hear, they do not understand.´
`This is what the parable means, the seed is the word of God.´
`The seed sown by the roadside are those who hear God's word, and the devil immediately comes and takes it from their hearts, otherwise they would believe and be saved.´
`The seed sown on rocky ground are those who hear God's word and they receive it with joy, but the word does not take root. So they believe for a while, but when temptation comes, they fall away.´
`The seed which fell among thorns are those who hear and go out, but they are choked with cares, riches, and pleasures of this life, and they produce no ripe fruit.´
`But the seed that is sown on the good ground are those with an honest and good heart, who after hearing the word, keep it and patiently produce good fruit.´
`No one lights a candle and covers it with a bowl or puts it under a bed, but they set it on a lampstand, so that those who enter may see the light.´
`For there is nothing done in secret that will not be revealed, nor is there anything hidden that will not be made known and seen in the light.´
`Therefore take heed to how you listen, for whoever has will be given more, and whoever has not, will have even that which he seems to have taken away.´"
Then the mother and brothers of Jesus came to see him, but they could not get near him because of the crowds.
Someone in the crowd spoke to Jesus and said, "Your mother and brothers are standing outside wanting to see you."
Jesus answered and said, "`My mother and brothers are those who hear the word of God and do what he says.´"
One day Jesus climbed aboard a boat with his disciples and he said, "`Let's go over to the other side of the lake,´" and they launched the boat.
But as they sailed Jesus fell asleep, and a violent windstorm blew against the boat as they crossed the lake. The boat began to fill with water and they were in jeopardy.

The disciples went to Jesus and woke him up and said, "Teacher, Teacher, we are perishing!" Then he got up and reprimanded the wind and the raging water, immediately the storm stopped and the lake was calm.
But Jesus said to them, "`Where is your faith?´" They were afraid and they wondered and said one to another, "What kind of man is this! For he commands even the winds and water, and they obey him."
Then they arrived in the country of the Gadarenes, which is near Galilee.
When Jesus left the boat, he was met by a demon possessed man from the city. He had neither worn clothes nor lived in a house for a long time, but he lived among the tombs.
When the man saw Jesus, he cried out and fell down before him, and with a loud voice he said, "What Do I have to do with you, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I beg you, do not torment me."

For Jesus had commanded the unclean spirit to come out of the man. Because many times it had seized him, and he was kept bound in chains and shackles, but he broke the chains, and he was driven by the demon into the wilderness.
Then Jesus questioned him and asked, "`What is your name?´" And he answered and said, "Legion." Because he was possessed by many demons.
And the demons begged Jesus not to command them to leave and go into the deep.
So there was a herd of pigs feeding on the side of the mountain, and the demons asked him to let them go into the pigs, and he let them.
Then the demons left the man and entered the pigs, and the herd ran violently down a steep slope and fell into the lake, and they were drowned.
When those who were feeding the pigs saw what happened, they fled into the city and the countryside and told everyone what had happened.

Then the people went out to see what was happening. When they found Jesus and the man whom the demons had left, he was sitting at the feet of Jesus, fully clothed, and in his right mind. And they were afraid.
And the people who saw what happened told them how the demon possessed man was healed.
Then all the people from the whole country surrounding the Gadarenes begged Jesus to leave, because they were terrified, so he got into the boat and headed back.
Now the man whom the demons had left begged Jesus to let him go with him, but Jesus sent him away.

And Jesus said to him, "`Return to your own home, and show people what great things God has done for you.´" So, he left and told everyone throughout the whole city what great things Jesus had done for him.
After Jesus returned, the people gladly received him because they were all waiting for him.
A synagogue leader named Jairus came to him and knelt down at Jesus' feet and begged him to come to his house.
For Jairus only had one twelve-year-old daughter and she was dying. But as Jesus went with him the people crowded around him.
And there was a woman who had been plagued with a bleeding problem for twelve years, and she had spent everything she had on physicians, who could not heal her.
She came up behind Jesus, and touched the hem of his robe, and immediately she was healed of her bleeding problem.
Suddenly Jesus stopped and said, "`Who touched me?´" When everyone denied it, Peter and those with him said, "Teacher, there is a massive crowd around you and you ask, "Who touched me?"
Jesus answered them and said, "`Someone has touched me, because I felt the power leave me.´"

Then the woman realized that she could not remain hidden, so she came forth trembling. She knelt down before him and declared to him and all the people why she had touched him, and how she had been immediately healed.
And Jesus said to her, "`Daughter, your faith has healed you, go in peace.´"
While Jesus was still speaking, someone came from the synagogue leader's house and said to him, "Your daughter is dead, do not trouble the Teacher anymore."
But when Jesus heard this, he spoke up and said, "`Fear not, just believe and she will be made whole.´"
And when Jesus entered the house, he would not let anyone go in with him except for Peter, James, John, and the father and mother of the young woman.
Everyone wept and wailed for her, but Jesus said, "`Do not weep, for she is not dead, she is just asleep.´"
Then they all laughed and scorned him, because they knew that she was dead.
Jesus put them all out of the house, and he took her by the hand and said, "`Little girl, get up´".
And her spirit returned, and she got up right away, then Jesus told them to give her something to eat.
Her parents were astonished, but Jesus told them not to tell anyone what had happened.
Then Jesus called his twelve disciples together, and he gave them power and authority over all demons, and the power to cure diseases.
And he sent them out to preach the Kingdom of God, and to heal the sick.
And Jesus said to them, "`Take nothing for your journey, no staff, no luggage, no bread, no money, nor an extra coat.´
`Whatever house you enter, stay there until you leave the area.´
`If anyone does not accept you, shake the dust from your feet when you leave that city, as a testimony against them.´"
So they left and went through the towns, preaching the gospel and healing everywhere they went.
Now Herod the tetrarch (Roman governor of one fourth of a kingdom or domain) heard everything that Jesus had done, and he was confused. Because some were saying that John had risen from the dead.
And some were saying that Elijah had reappeared, and others said that one of the old prophets had risen again.
And Herod said, "I have beheaded John, but who is this that I hear such things about?" And he wanted to see Jesus.
When the apostles returned, they told Jesus everything that they had done. Then Jesus took them away to a private place in the desert near a city called Bethsaida.
When the people discovered that Jesus was nearby, they followed him and he received them. And Jesus spoke to them of the Kingdom of God and healed those who needed healing.

Toward the end of the day the twelve disciples came to Jesus and said, "Send the crowds away, so they can go into the towns and the countryside to find somewhere to stay, and get some food. Because we are in a desolate place here."
But Jesus said to them, "`You give them something to eat!´" And they said, "But we only have five loaves of bread and two fish, unless we go and buy some food for all these people."
For there were about 5,000 men and Jesus said to his disciples, "`Make them sit down in groups of fifty.´"
And they made them all sit down.
Then Jesus took the five loaves of bread and two fish, and he looked up to heaven and blessed them. Then he broke them and gave them to the disciples to distribute among the crowd.
And they ate until they were all filled, and they picked up twelve baskets full of leftover fish and bread.
One day as Jesus was praying alone with his disciples he asked them, "`Who do the people say that I am?´"
They answered him and said, "Some say John the Baptist, but some say Elijah, and others say that you are one of the old prophets who has risen from the dead."
Jesus said to them, "`But who do you say that I am?´" Peter answered and said, "The Christ of God."
And Jesus strictly warned them and told them not to tell anyone.
Then Jesus said to them all, "`The Son of Man must suffer many things, and be rejected by the elders, chief priests, scribes, and he will be killed then raised up on the third day.´"
`If a man wants to come after me, let him deny himself and take up his cross daily, and follow me.´
`For whoever wants to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life for my sake will save it.´
`For what does it profit a man, if he gains the whole world, but loses himself or is thrown away?´
`For whoever is ashamed of me and my words, the Son of Man will also be ashamed of him when he comes in his own glory, his father's glory, and the glory of the holy angels.´
`But I tell you the truth, there are some standing here who will not taste death, before they see the Kingdom of God.´
About eight days after he said these things, he took Peter, John, and James and went up on a mountain to pray.
As he prayed, his appearance was altered and his clothes glowed brilliantly white.
And, behold two men Moses and Elijah were talking with him.
They appeared in glory and spoke of his death which he would accomplish in Jerusalem.
Peter and those with him were very sleepy, but when they awoke, they saw his glory and the two men standing with him.

As Moses and Elijah left, Peter said to Jesus, "Teacher, it is a good thing we are here. Let us make three tabernacles, one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah." Because he did not know what else to say.
While Peter spoke, a cloud came and overshadowed them, and they were afraid as they entered the cloud.
A voice came from the cloud and said, "This is my beloved Son, listen to him!"
When the voice finished speaking, they found Jesus alone, and they kept it secret and told no one about any of the things which they had seen in those days.
The next day, after they had come down from the hill, many people came out to meet Jesus.
But a man from the crowd cried out and said, "Teacher, I beg you to look at my son because he is my only child.
A spirit seizes him and he suddenly cries out. It tears him and he foams at the mouth over and over again. It keeps bruising him and it hardly ever leaves him.
I begged your disciples to cast him out, but they could not."
And Jesus answered him and said, "`O faithless and perverse generation, how long must I be with you and put up with you? Bring your son here.´"
As he was coming toward Jesus, the demon threw the young man down and tore him. Jesus reprimanded the unclean spirit and healed the child, then returned him to his father.
And they were all amazed at the mighty power of God. But while everyone wondered about all the things which Jesus had done, he spoke to his disciples.
And Jesus said, "`Listen closely to what I say, because the Son of Man will be delivered into the hands of men.´"
But they did not understand this, and its meaning was hidden from them, they did not perceive it, and they were afraid to ask him what it meant.
Then they were discussing among themselves, which one of them would be the greatest.
But Jesus knew what they were thinking in their hearts, and he placed a child beside him.

And Jesus spoke to them and said, "`Whoever receives this child in my name receives me, and whoever receives me receives the one who sent me, because whoever is least among you all, will be the greatest.´"
And John answered him and said, "Teacher, we saw someone casting out demons in your name, and we made him stop, because he does not follow us."
But Jesus said, "`Do not forbid him, because whoever is not against us is for us.´"
As the time approached for Jesus to ascend into heaven, he was determined to go to Jerusalem.
He sent messengers ahead of him to a Samaritan village to prepare for his visit.
But they did not welcome him, because he was going to Jerusalem.
When his disciples James and John saw this, they said, "Lord, why do you not command fire to come down from heaven and consume them, the way Elijah did?"
But Jesus turned to them and reprimanded them and said, "`You do not understand the spirit you are speaking of.´
`For the Son of Man has not come to destroy men's lives, but to save them!´" And they went to another village.
As they were walking along the way, someone said to Jesus, "Lord, I will follow you wherever you go."
And Jesus said to him, "`Foxes have holes and birds of the air have nests, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head.´"
And Jesus said to another man, "`Follow me.´" But he said, "Lord, I must first go and bury my father."
Jesus said to him, "`Let the dead bury their dead, but you go and preach the Kingdom of God.´"
Another also said, "Lord, I will follow you but let me first go and tell my family at home farewell."
And Jesus said to him, "`No man who puts his hand to the plough and looks back, is fit for the Kingdom of God.´"
After all these things happened, the Lord Jesus appointed another seventy apostles and sent them out two by two before his face arrived in every city and place that he intended to visit.
So before they, left Jesus told them, "`The harvest truly is great, but the laborers are few. Therefore, pray that the Lord of the harvest will send laborers into his harvest.´
`So go but beware, for I am sending you out like lambs among wolves.´
`Carry no purse, luggage, or shoes with you and salute no one along the way.´
`And whatever house you enter into first say, 'Peace to this house.'´
`If a son of peace is there, your peace will rest on that house, if not it will return to you.´
`Remain in that house, eating and drinking whatever they serve, because the laborer is worthy of his wages. Do not move from house to house.´
`If you enter a city and they accept you, eat whatever they set before you.´
`Heal the sick there and tell them, 'The Kingdom of God has come near you.'´
`But if you enter a city and they do not accept you, go out into the streets of that city.´
`And tell that city, 'We even wipe the dust of your city from our feet as a testimony against you. But you can be sure of this, the Kingdom of God has come near you today.'´
`But I tell you, it will be more tolerable for Sodom in those days than it will be for that city.´

`Woe unto you, Chorazin! Woe unto you Bethsaida! For if the mighty works performed in you had been performed in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented a long time ago, sitting in sackcloth and ashes.´
`But it will be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon at the judgment than it will be for you.´
`You, Capernaum have been glorified to heaven, but you will be thrown down into hell.´
`Whoever hears you hears me, and whoever despises you despises me, and whoever despises me despises the one who sent me.´"
The seventy apostles returned with joy and said, "Lord, even the demons are subject to us through the power of your name."
So Jesus told them, "`I saw Satan fall like lightning from heaven.´
`Behold, I have given you the power to tread on serpents and scorpions, and to overpower the enemy, and nothing will hurt you.´
`But do not rejoice because the spirits are subject to you, rejoice instead that your names are written in heaven.´"

Then Jesus rejoiced in spirit and said, "`O father Lord of heaven and earth, I thank you for hiding these things from the wise and prudent, but you have revealed them to children. Yes, father because even this seemed good in your sight.´
`Everything has been given to me by my father. No one knows who the son is except the father, and no one knows who the father is except the son and whoever the son chooses to reveal him.´"
Jesus turned to his disciples and spoke to them privately and said, "`Blessed are the eyes which have seen the things that you have seen.´
`For I tell you, that many prophets and kings have desired to see and hear the things which you have seen and heard, but they have not seen nor heard them.´
One day a lawyer stood up to test Jesus and asked, "Master, what must I do to inherit eternal life?"
Jesus answered him and said, "`Do what is written in the law! Have you not read it?´"
The lawyer answered him and said, "You must love your Lord God with all your heart, all your soul, all your strength, and with all your mind, and you must love your neighbor as you love yourself."
Jesus said to him, "`You have answered correctly. Do this and you will live.´"
But the lawyer wanted to justify himself to Jesus and he asked, "And who is my neighbor?"
Jesus answered and said, "`A man went down from Jerusalem to Jericho when he was attacked by thieves, who stripped him of his clothes and wounded him, and they left him lying there half dead.´
`By chance a priest came walking by, but when he saw the wounded man, he crossed over to the other side of the road to pass by.´
`A Levite did the same thing, even though he saw the wounded man, he ignored him and passed by on the other side of the road.´
`But a Samaritan was traveling through the area, and when he saw the wounded man, he had compassion for him.´
`So the good Samaritan went to him and poured oil and wine on his wounds and bandaged them. Then put him on his own animal and brought him to a nearby inn and took care of him.´
`The next day he left, and he gave two denarii to the innkeeper and said to him, 'Take care of him, and if you have to spend more on him, I will repay you when I return.'´
`So which one of these three men, do you think was a neighbor to the one who was attacked by thieves?´"
And the lawyer said, "It was the one who showed mercy for him." Then Jesus said to him, "`Go, and do likewise.´"
As they were traveling, Jesus entered a village where a woman named Martha welcomed him into her home.
Martha had a sister named Mary, who sat at the feet of Jesus listening to his words.
But Martha was encumbered by all the work needed to serve everyone, and she came to Jesus and said, "Lord, do you not care that my sister has left me to serve everyone alone? Tell her to help me!"
And Jesus answered her and said, "`Martha, Martha, you are careful and worried about many things.´
`But only one thing is needed. Mary has chosen the good path, which will not be taken away from her.´"
One day as Jesus finished praying one of his disciples spoke to him and said, "Lord, teach us to pray the way John taught his disciples to pray."
Then Jesus said to them, "`Say this when you pray, 'Our father who is in heaven, hallowed be your name. Your kingdom come, your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven.´
`Give us this day our daily bread.´
`And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who are indebted to us, and lead us not into temptation but deliver us from evil.´"
And Jesus said to them, "`Suppose you have a friend that you go to in the middle of the night and say, 'Friend, loan me three loaves of bread.´
`For I have a friend coming to visit me, and I have nothing to serve him?´
`And your friend answers you and says, 'Do not bother me, my door is already locked and my children and I are in bed. I cannot get up and get anything for you.'´
`I tell you, even though his friend will not get up and give to him out of friendship, he will get up and give to him because of the man's persistence´
`So I say to you, 'Ask, and it will be given you, seek, and you will find, knock, and it will be opened for you.'´
`For everyone who asks receives, and whoever seeks will find, and to anyone who knocks it will be opened.´
`If a son asks his father for bread, will he give him a stone, or if he asks his father for a fish, will he give him a serpent?´
`Or if he asks his father for an egg, will he give him a scorpion?´
`If you who are evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your heavenly father give you the Holy Spirit if you ask?´"
One day Jesus was casting out a demon from a dumb mute man, and when the demon left the man who had been a dumb mute, he spoke and the people were amazed.
But some of them said, "Jesus uses the chief devil Beelzebub to cast out demons."
Still others tested Jesus by demanding that he show them a sign from heaven.
But Jesus knew what they were thinking and he said to them, "`Every kingdom divided against itself will be destroyed, and a house divided against itself cannot stand.´
`If Satan is divided against himself, how can his kingdom stand? How can I cast out demons through Beelzebub if it is as you say it is.´
`And if I use Beelzebub to cast out demons, who do your sons use to cast out demons, because they are the ones who will be your judges.´
`But if I cast out demons with the finger of God, then the Kingdom of God has no doubt come upon you.´
`When a strong man armed with weapons guards his palace, his property is secure.´
`But when a man stronger than him comes against him, and overcomes him, he will take all of the weaker man's armor in which he trusted and divide up his plunder.´
`Whoever is not with me is against me, and whoever does not gather with me scatters.´
`When an unclean spirit leaves a man, it walks through dry places looking for rest and does not find it. Then it says, 'I will return to the house that I left.'´
`When it returns, it finds the house swept clean and organized.´
`Then it goes and brings seven other spirits more wicked than itself, and they enter and live there. And the final plight of that man is worse than it was at the first.´"
As Jesus was speaking about these things, a woman in the crowd spoke up and said to him, "Blessed is the womb that gave birth to you, and the breasts that nursed you!"
But Jesus said, "`Yes, but blessed are those who hear the word of God and keep it.´"

The people continued to gather together, and as the crowd increased Jesus began to say, "`This is an evil generation, they seek a sign, but no sign will be given to them, except the sign of Jonah the prophet.´
`For just as Jonah was a sign to the Ninevites, so the Son of Man will also be to this generation.´

`The queen of the south will rise up in judgment with the men of this generation and condemn them. Because she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon and behold someone greater than Solomon is here.´
`The men of Nineveh will rise up in judgment with this generation and condemn it, for they repented at the preaching of Jonah, and behold one greater than Jonah is now here.´
`No one lights a candle, and hides it in a secret place, nor does he put it under a basket, but he puts it on a lampstand, so that those who come in may see the light.´
`The light of your body is the eye, therefore when your eye is good, your whole body is full of light. But when your eye is evil, your body is also full of darkness.´
`Therefore, be careful and make sure the light within you is not darkness.´
`So if your whole body is full of light, and has no part of the darkness, the whole body will be full of light, as when a bright shining candle gives you light.´"
As Jesus was speaking, a Pharisee begged him to come dine with him, so he went and sat down at his table.
But the Pharisee was surprised to see that Jesus did not first wash before dinner.
And the Lord Jesus said to him, "`Now you Pharisees clean the outside of a cup and platter, but your inner heart is full of ravenous wickedness.´
`You fools, did not the one who made the outside, also make that which is inside?´
`But rather give as alms your inner things and behold everything will be clean for you.´
`But woe unto you Pharisees! For you tithe mint, rue, and all kinds of herbs, but you ignore justice and the love of God. You should have done these things, and not left the other things undone.´
`Woe unto you Pharisees! For you love the most prominent seats in the synagogues, and to be greeted in the marketplace.´
`Woe unto you scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! For you are like unmarked graves which do not appear, and the men who walk over them are not even aware that they are there.´"
Then one of the lawyers spoke up and said to Jesus, "Master, when you say these things, you also show your disapproval of us."
And Jesus answered him and said, "`Woe unto you lawyers as well! For you burden men with grievous loads to carry, but you yourselves do not lift a finger to lighten their load.´
`Woe unto you! For you build tombs for the prophets who your fathers killed.´
`Truly you bear witness that you will allow the deeds of your fathers to stand, because they did indeed kill the prophets, but you build their tombs.´
`Therefore the wisdom of God also said, 'I will send them prophets and apostles, and they will kill and persecute some of them.'´
`So that the blood of all the prophets, which was shed from the very foundation of the world, may be required from this generation.´
`From the blood of Abel to the blood of Zacharias who was killed between the altar and the temple. Truly I tell you; it will be required of this generation.´
`Woe unto you lawyers! For you have taken away the key to knowledge. You refused to enter into knowledge yourselves, and you hinder those who were trying to enter.´"
As Jesus spoke to the scribes and Pharisees, they began to vehemently urge and provoke him into saying many things.
For they were trying to trick him into say something that they could use against him.

In the meantime, such an endless number of people gathered together that they were bumping into each other. Then Jesus began to speak first to his disciples and he said, "`Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.´
`For there is nothing concealed that will not be revealed, and there is nothing hidden that will not be made known.´
`That's why whatever you said in darkness will be heard in the light, and whatever you whispered in closets will be proclaimed from the rooftops.´
`So I tell those of you who are my friends, 'Do not be afraid of those who can kill the body, but they can do nothing else after that.´
`But I am warning you about who to fear ahead of time, fear the one who has the power to throw you into hell after he has killed you! Yes, I tell you to fear God.'´
`Are not five sparrows sold for two pennies? And not one of them is forgotten by God?´
`But even the hairs on your head are all numbered. So do not fear, because you are more valuable than many sparrows.´
`I also tell you this, whoever confesses me before men, the Son of Man will also confess before the angels of God.´
`But whoever denies me before men will be denied before the angels of God.´
`Anyone who speaks against the Son of Man will be forgiven, but anyone who blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven.´
`When they bring you to the synagogues, magistrates, and other powers do not worry about what to say or how to answer.´
`For the Holy Spirit will teach you what to say at the right time.´"
Someone in the crowd spoke out and said to Jesus, "Teacher, talk to my brother and tell him to share his inheritance with me."
But Jesus replied to him and said, "`Man, who made me your judge or estate executor?´"
And Jesus addressed the crowd and said, "`Take heed and do not covet things, because a man's life does not consist of the abundance of things that he owns.´"
Then Jesus told the crowd a parable and said, "`Some land owned by a rich man produced an over abundant harvest.´
`The rich man thought to himself and said, 'What can I do, I have nowhere to store all my crops?'´
`And the rich man said, 'I know what to do, I will tear down my barns and build bigger barns to store all my goods and crops.´
