`And I will tell my soul, "Soul, you have stored enough good things to last for many years. So, relax, eat, drink, and be merry."'´
`But God said to the rich man, 'You fool, tonight your soul will be required of you, then who will own everything that you have stored up?'´
`So someone who stores up earthly treasures for themselves is not rich toward God.´"
Jesus continued speaking to his disciples and said, "`Therefore I tell you, 'Do not worry about your life or what you will eat, nor your body or what you will wear.'´
`Life is much more than meat, and the body is more than just clothes.´
`Consider the ravens, they neither sow nor reap and they have no storehouse or barn, but God still feeds them. How much more valuable are you than the birds?´
`Which one of you can add one cubit to your height by worrying about it?´
`So if you are unable to do such a small thing, why worry about the rest?´
`Consider how the lilies grow, they do not toil and they do not spin thread. But I tell you that Solomon in all his glory was not as well adorned as one of these lilies.´
`O you of little faith, if God clothed the field grass which is thrown in the oven tomorrow, how much more will he clothe you?´
`So do not worry about what to eat or drink, and do not allow your mind to doubt.´
`For all the nations of the world seek these things, and your father knows that you need all of them.´
`But seek first the Kingdom of God, and all of these things will be added to you.´
`So fear not little flock, because it gives your father great pleasure to give you the kingdom.´

`Sell what you have and give to the poor, which will provide a purse for yourselves that does not grow old. It is a treasure in heaven that will not fail, where no thief dares to approach and no moths corrupt.´
`For wherever your treasure is stored, there your heart will be also.´
`Keep your belt around your waist and keep your lights burning.´
`Then you will be like men who wait for their Lord to return from the wedding. When he knocks on the door, they will immediately open it for him.´

`Blessed are the servants who the Lord finds keeping watch when he returns. Truly I tell you; the Lord will dress himself to serve and he will make his servants sit down to eat, and he will serve them.´
`And if he comes during the second or third watch, blessed are the servants who stay alert.´
`But understand this, if the homeowner knew when the thief was coming, he would have kept watch, and his house would not have been broken into.´
`That's why you must be ready, because the Son of Man will come when you least expect it.´"
Then Peter asked Jesus, "Lord, are you telling this parable just for us, or is it for everyone else as well?"
Jesus answered him and said, "`Who is the faithful and wise manager, whose Lord let him manage his household and gives him his fair share when the time comes?´
`Blessed is the servant, whose Lord finds him alert when he returns.´
`For I tell you the truth, he will make this servant ruler over everything that he has.´
`But if that servant says in his heart, 'My Lord is not returning any time soon!' And he begins to beat the other servants, and he starts eating and getting drunk.´
`The Lord of that servant will come when he is least expected at an hour when he is not anticipated. Then he will cut his servant out and place him among the unbelievers.´
`And the servant who knows what his Lord requires and does not prepare for or do the things that his Lord asked, will be beaten with many stripes.´

`But the one who unknowingly does things worthy of punishment will be beaten with fewer stripes. For to whoever much has been given, much will be required. And from men who have contributed much, even more will be asked of them.´
`I have come to set a fire on the earth, if only it were already kindled!´
`But I have to be baptized with an awful baptism, and I will be under stress until it is finished!´
`Do you suppose that I have come to give peace on earth? I tell you I have not, I have come to create division.´
`From now on there will be five divided people in one household, three against two and two against three.´

`Father will be divided against son and son against father, mother will be divided against daughter and daughter against mother, mother-in-law will be divided against daughter-in-law and daughter-in-law against mother-in-law.´"
Jesus also said to the people, "`When you see a cloud rising from the west, right away you say, 'A shower is coming.' And it does.´
`When you see the south wind blowing, you say, 'It will be a hot day.' And it is.´
`You hypocrites! You know how to interpret the signs of the sky and the earth. Why do you not recognize the signs of the time?´
`Why do you not even know how to judge for yourselves what is right?´

`When you go to the magistrate try to reconcile with your adversary on the way, otherwise he will hand you over to the judge, the judge will deliver you to the officer, and the officer will throw you into prison.´
`I tell you, you will not leave that prison until you have paid every last penny.´"
At that time some of the people there told Jesus about the Galileans whose blood Pilate had mixed with their sacrifices.
Jesus responded to them and said, "`Do you suppose that these Galileans were worse sinners than all the other Galileans, because they suffered such things?´
`I tell you they were not. But unless you repent, all of you will also perish.´
`Or those eighteen who were in the tower Siloam when it fell and killed them. Do you think they were worse sinners than all the other men who lived in Jerusalem?´
`I tell you they were not. But unless you repent, all of you will also perish.´"
Jesus also told them this parable, "`A man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard, and when he went to harvest the fruit, he found none.´
`Then he said to his vineyard manager, 'Behold I have come looking for fruit on this fig tree for three years in a row, and found none. So cut it down! Why should I let this space be wasted?'´
`But his manager responded to him and said, 'Lord, leave it for one more year and I will cultivate and fertilize it.'´
`If it bears fruit then all is well, if after that it does not, then I will cut it down.´"
Later Jesus was teaching in one of the synagogues on the Sabbath.
There was a woman there who had been tormented by a disabling spirit for eighteen years. She was bent over and she could not stand up by herself.
When Jesus saw her, he asked her to come to him and he said, "`Woman, you are released from your disability.´"
Jesus laid his hands on her, and she immediately straightened up and glorified God.

The synagogue leader was indignant because Jesus had healed someone on the Sabbath day and he said to the people, "There are six days for men to work, so come and be healed on those days but not on the Sabbath day."
Then Jesus answered him and said, "`You hypocrite! Do not every one of you untie your ox or donkey and lead them to water?´
`Should this woman a daughter of Abraham, not be released from this bondage on the Sabbath day? Satan has kept her bound up for the last eighteen years.´"
After Jesus said these things, all of his adversaries were ashamed and everyone else rejoiced over all the glorious things Jesus had done.
Then Jesus said, "`To what can I compare the Kingdom of God, and what is it like?´
`It is like a tiny mustard seed, which a man threw into his garden. It grew and grew and became a great tree, and the birds of the air lived in its branches.´"
Again Jesus said, "`To what can I compare the Kingdom of God?´
`It is like leavening, which a woman added to three measures of flour until all of it was leavened.´"
Then Jesus traveled through the cities and villages, teaching on his way to Jerusalem.
Along the way someone asked Jesus, "Lord, will only a few of us be saved?".
And Jesus answered and said, "`Struggle to enter through the straight gate. Because I tell you, many will try to enter but they will be unable to enter.´

`After the homeowner gets up and shuts the door, and you are left standing outside knocking on the door and saying, 'Lord, Lord, open up for us!' But he will answer you and say, 'I do not know where you are from.'´
`Then you will say, 'But we ate and drank in your presence, and you taught in our streets.'´
`But the homeowner will say, 'I tell you, I do not know where you are from. All of you immoral people must depart from me.'´
`There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth when you see Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and all the other prophets in the Kingdom of God, when you yourselves are thrown out.´
`They will come from the east, west, north, and south to sit down in the Kingdom of God.´
`And behold, those who are last will be first, and those who are first will be last.´"
That same day some Pharisees came to Jesus and said, "Get out, leave this place because Herod wants to kill you."
Jesus spoke to the Pharisees and said, "`Go and tell that sly old fox, 'Behold I will cast out demons and cure people today and tomorrow, and on the third day I will be perfected.'´
`Nevertheless I must walk today, tomorrow, and the following day because it is not acceptable for a prophet to perish outside of Jerusalem.´

`O Jerusalem, who kills the prophets and stones those who are sent to you. How often I would have gathered your children together, like a hen gathers her brood under her wings but you would not come!´
`Behold, your house has been left desolate. Truly I tell you; you will not see me again until the time comes for you to say, 'Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord.'´"
One Sabbath as Jesus went to eat bread at the home of one of the chief Pharisees, they were watching him.
And a man with a swollen body sat before Jesus.
Jesus spoke to the lawyers and Pharisees and asked, "`Is it legal to heal on the Sabbath day?´"
But they did not answer, so Jesus healed him and the man left.
Then Jesus spoke to them and said, "`Which of you have ever had a donkey or an ox fall into a pit on the Sabbath, that you did not immediately go and pull him out?´"
And they could not answer him about these things.
Jesus noticed that the invited guests had chosen the most prominent places in the room to sit, so he told them a parable.
And Jesus said, "`When you are invited to a wedding, do not sit in the most prominent place because someone more honorable than you may have also been invited.´
`And the one who invited you may come to you and say, 'Give this man your place.' Then you will be humiliated, and you will have to take the lowest seat.´

`But when you are invited, go and sit in the lowest place, so that when the one who invited you comes, he will say to you, 'Friend, move to a better place.' Then you will not be embarrassed before those at the table with you.´
`For whoever glorifies himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be glorified.´"

Then Jesus also spoke to the one who invited him and said, "`When you prepare a dinner or a supper, do not invite your friends, brothers, family, nor your rich neighbors. Otherwise, they may invite you just to compensate you.´
`But when you prepare a feast, invite the poor, the crippled, the maimed, the lame, and the blind.´
`Then you will be blessed, because they cannot compensate you, and you will be compensated at the resurrection of the righteous.´"
When one of the men sitting at the table with Jesus heard these things he said, "Blessed is the one who will eat bread in the Kingdom of God."
Then Jesus said to him, "`A man prepared a great feast and invited many people.´
`Then the man sent his servant at supper time to tell those who were invited to come, because everything was now ready.´
`But they all began to make excuses. The first one said, 'I bought a piece of land, and I must go and see it. I pray you will excuse me.'´
`Another said, 'I bought five yoke of oxen, and I must go to inspect them. I pray you will excuse me.'´
`And another said, 'My wife and I just got married, so I cannot come.'´

`So that servant returned and told his Lord about these things. Then the homeowner was very angry and he spoke to his servant and said, 'Go out into the city streets and invite the poor, the crippled, the maimed, the lame, and the blind.'´
`And the servant said, 'Lord, it has been done as you have asked, but there is still room for more.'´
`And the homeowner said to the servant, 'Go out into the highways and hedges and invite them to come, so that my house is filled with guests.´
`For I tell you, none of those men who I invited will ever taste my feast.'´"
Then Jesus turned to face the vast crowd following him.
As Jesus looked out at them he said, "`If anyone comes to me who does not hate his own father, mother, wife, children, brothers, sisters, and even his own life cannot be my disciple.´
`Whoever does not carry his own cross and follow me, cannot be my disciple.´
`For which one of you who plans to build a tower, does not first sit down and calculate the cost, in order to make sure he has sufficient funds to finish it?´
`Otherwise, after he lays the foundation and he is unable to finish it, everyone who sees it will begin to make fun of him.´
`And they will say, 'This man was unable to finish what he began.'´
`Or what king going to war against another king does not first sit down and consult with his generals, to determine whether he can defend his kingdom with 10,000 men against his enemy's 20,000 men?´
`If he cannot, he will send an ambassador to the other king while he is still far away and ask for his terms of surrender´
`So, if any one of you cannot surrender everything that you have, then you cannot be my disciple.´
`Salt is good but if salt loses its saltiness, how can it season anything?´
`It is neither fit for the land or the manure pile, and men will throw it away. He who has ears to hear, let him hear.´"
Then all the tax collectors and sinners moved closer to Jesus so they could hear him.
But the scribes and Pharisees whispered to each other and said, "This man accepts sinners and he eats with them!"
Then Jesus told them this parable.
And Jesus said, "`Which one of you, who has a hundred sheep and loses one, does not leave the other ninety-nine in the wilderness, then goes and looks for the lost one until you find it?´
`And when you find it, you lay it on your shoulders and rejoice.´
`And when you return home, you call your friends and neighbors together and say to them, 'Rejoice with me, because I have found my lost sheep.'´
`I tell you, this same joy is felt in heaven over one sinner who repents, even more so than all the other ninety-nine righteous people who do not need to repent.´
`Or consider the woman who has ten pieces of silver, if she loses one does she not light a candle and sweep the house, and diligently look for it until she finds it?´
`After she finds it, she calls her friends and neighbors together and says, 'Rejoice with me, because I have found my lost piece of silver.'´
`I tell you the truth, that same joy is felt in the presence of God's angels over one sinner who repents.´"
Jesus continued speaking and said, "`A man had two sons.´
`The youngest son said to his father, 'Father, give me my share of the inheritance.' So the father divided his wealth between them.´
`Not long after that the youngest son gathered his inheritance together, and journeyed to a far distant country where he wasted it all living the wild life.´
`After he spent everything he had, a terrible famine devastated the land and he began to starve.´
`So he hired himself out to a citizen of that country, who sent him into his fields to feed the pigs.´
`He was so hungry that he wanted to eat the husks that the pigs were eating, but no one would give him any to eat.´
`When he finally came to his senses he said, 'How many of my father's hired servants have more than enough bread to eat, and I am dying of hunger!´
`I am leaving this place to return to my father and I will say to him, 'Father, I have sinned against heaven before you.´
`I am no longer worthy to be called your son, so make me one of your hired servants.'´
`So he returned to his father. But when he was still a long way away, his father saw him coming and he was filled with compassion for him. Then he ran and hugged his neck and kissed him.´
`And the son said to his father, 'Father, I have sinned against heaven before you. I am no longer worthy to be called your son.'´
`But the father said to his servants, 'Bring the best robe and put it on him, then put a ring on his hand and shoes on his feet.´
`Then bring the fatted calf and kill it, and we will eat and be merry.´
`For this is my son who was dead but he is now alive, he was lost but now he is found, and they began to celebrate.´
`Now his oldest son was in the field, and as he approached the house, he heard music and dancing.´
`So he called out to one of the servants and he asked what was going on.´
`And the servant said to him, 'Your brother has come home, and your father has killed the fatted calf, because his son has returned safe and sound.'´
`The oldest son was angry and he would not go in the house, so his father came out and pleaded with him to come in.´

`But the oldest son answered his father said, 'I have served you for all these years, I have not transgressed against you and I am at your command at any time. But you have never even given me a kid goat, so that I could make merry with my friends.´
`But as soon as your other son shows up after wasting all your wealth on whores, you killed the fatted calf for him.´
`And the father said to his son, 'You are always with me, and everything that I have is yours.´
`But we should be happy and celebrate, because your brother was dead and now he is alive, and he was lost but now he has been found.'´"
Jesus also said to his disciples, "`There was a rich man, who had a manager that was accused of wasting the rich man's resources.´
`The rich man summoned him and said, 'Why do I hear these things about you? Give me an account of your management because you may no longer be my manager.'´
`Then the manager thought to himself, 'What can I do if my Lord takes away my management job? I cannot dig ditches and I am too ashamed to beg.´
`I know what I can do before I lose my job, so that people will welcome me into their homes.´
`So the manager called all of the rich man's debtors and he said, 'How much do you owe to my Lord?'´
`The first debtor said, 'A hundred measures of oil.' And the manager replied, 'Take your bill, sit down and quickly write fifty.'´
`Then the manager said to another debtor, 'How much do you owe?' And the debtor answered, 'A hundred measures of wheat.' And the manager said, 'Take your bill, and write eighty.'´
`Then the rich man commended the deceitful manager because he had dealt shrewdly. Because this generation of the world's children deal more shrewdly with their own kind than the children of light.´
`So I tell you, make friends with the unrighteous greedy, so that when you fail, they will receive you into everlasting homes.´
`Whoever is faithful with the least, is also faithful with much more, but whoever is dishonest with the least is also dishonest with much more.´
`Therefore if you have not been faithful with the unrighteous greedy, who will commit true riches into your trust?´
`If you have been unfaithful with another man's finances, who will trust you with your own finances?´
`No servant can serve two masters, because either he will hate one and love the other, or he will be loyal to one and despise the other. You cannot serve God and greed.´"
When the covetous Pharisees also heard all of these things, they mocked Jesus.
Then Jesus said to them, "`You only justify yourselves before men, but God knows what is in your hearts, because that which is highly esteemed among men is an abomination in God's sight.´
`The law and the prophets were preached until John arrived. Since then, the Kingdom of God has been preached, and everyone is trying to force their way in.´
`It is easier for heaven and earth to pass away, than it is for one scrap of the law to fail.´
`Whoever divorces his wife and marries another woman commits adultery. Whoever marries a woman who is divorced from her husband commits adultery.´"
And Jesus said to them, "`There was a rich man clothed in fine purple linen, who ate sumptuously every day.´
`And a beggar named Lazarus laid at the rich man's gate covered with sores.´
`Lazarus begged to be fed with the crumbs from the rich man's table, and the dogs came and licked his sores.´
`When Lazarus the beggar died, he was carried by angels into Abraham's embrace. The rich man also died and was buried.´
`The rich man found himself being tormented in hell and he looked up and saw Abraham embracing Lazarus from a distance.´
`The rich man cried out and said, 'Father Abraham, have mercy on me. Please send Lazarus to dip his finger in water and cool my tongue, because I am being tormented in this flame.'´
`But Abraham said, 'Son, remember you received many good things in your lifetime and Lazarus received evil things, but now he is being comforted and you are being tormented.´
`Besides that, there is a great fixed gulf between you and us, so that no one can pass from here over to you, nor can anyone cross over to us from there.'´
`Then the dead rich man said, 'Father Abraham, I pray you will please send Lazarus to my father's house.´
`Because I have five brothers that he must testify to, otherwise they will also end up in this place of torment.'´
`But Abraham answered him and said, 'They have Moses and the prophets, they can listen to them.'´
`And the dead rich man said, 'Father Abraham, they will not listen, but if someone rises from the dead and goes and testifies to them, they will repent.'´
`Then Abraham said to him, 'If they do not listen to Moses and the prophets, they will not be persuaded even if someone rises from the dead and goes to them.'´"
Then Jesus said to the disciples, "`It is impossible to prevent temptations when they come, but woe unto him through whom they come!´
`It would be better if a millstone were hung around his neck and he was thrown into the sea, than it will be for anyone who causes one of these little children to sin.´
`Be cautious if your brother trespasses against you. If he does reprimand him but forgive him if he repents.´
`If your brother trespasses against you seven times in a day, and he returns to you seven times in a day and says, 'I repent, please forgive me.' Then forgive him.´
And the apostles said to Jesus, "Please increase our faith!"

Jesus responded to them and said, "`If you only had faith no larger than a tiny mustard seed, then you could say to this sycamore tree, 'Uproot yourself and go plant yourself in the sea!' And it will obey you.´
`Which of you whose servant plows your fields and feeds your cattle, will immediately say to him when he comes in from the field, 'Go and sit down at the table.'?´
`But would you not really say to him, 'Go and make my supper, then get dressed and serve me. After I eat and drink you can eat and drink?´
`Do you thank your servant because he did what he was told to do? I think not.´
`So it is for you also, when you do everything that you are told to do, you should say, 'We are just unprofitable servants, we have only done our duty.'´"
Later Jesus passed through Samaria and Galilee on his way to Jerusalem.
As Jesus entered a certain village he was met by ten lepers, who stood back from him at a distance.
They all spoke to him and said, "Jesus, please have mercy on us."
When Jesus saw them, he said, "`Go and show yourselves to the priests.´" On the way there the lepers were cleansed.
One of them realized that he was healed, so he turned back and glorified God with a loud voice.
The healed man was a Samaritan, and he knelt down at the feet of Jesus to give thanks.
Then Jesus said, "`Were not ten lepers cleansed? So where are other the nine?´
`Not one has returned to give glory to God, except this foreigner.´"
Then Jesus said to him, "`Get up and go your way, your faith has made you whole.´
When the Pharisees demanded to know when the Kingdom of God would come, Jesus answered them and said, "`The signs of the coming Kingdom of God cannot be seen.´
`Nor will they say, 'Look here or look there!' For, behold the Kingdom of God is within you.´"
Then Jesus said to the disciples, "`The day will come when you long to see one of the days of the Son of Man, but you will not see it.´
`People will tell you, 'Look here or look there!' Do not chase after or follow them.´
`For like lightning flashes and lights up the heavens from one end to the other, so will it be when the Son of Man comes in his day.´
`But first he must suffer many things and be rejected by this generation.´
`As it was in the days of Noah, so will it also be in the days of the Son of Man.´
`They ate, they drank, they married, and they were given in marriage until the day that Noah entered the ark. Then the flood came and destroyed them all.´
`Just as it was in the days of Lot, they ate, they drank, they bought, they sold, they planted, and they built.´
`But the day that Lot left Sodom, fire and brimstone rained down from heaven and destroyed them all.´
`It will also be this way for them on the day the Son of Man is revealed.´
`In those days, do not let whoever is up on the rooftop come down to get his stuff from the house. And do not let whoever is in the field return for anything he left behind.´
`Remember Lot's wife.´
`Whoever tries to save his life will lose it, and whoever loses his life will preserve it.´
`I tell you on that night two men will be in one bed, and one will be taken, but the other will be left behind.´
`Two women will be grinding grain together; one will be taken and the other will be left behind.´
`Two men will be in the field, and one will be taken, but the other will be left behind.´"
And the disciples asked Jesus, "Where teacher?" Jesus answered them and said, "`Wherever a dead body lies the eagles will gather.´"
Then Jesus told them a parable about why men should always pray and they should not lose heart.
And Jesus said, "`There was a judge in a city who did not fear God nor respect man.´
`And in that city there was a widow who came to him and said, 'Avenge me against my adversary.'´
`For a while he refused but then he thought to himself, 'Even though I do not fear God nor respect men.'´
`This widow keeps bothering me and she is wearing me out by constantly coming here, so I will give her what she wants.'´"
And Jesus said, "`Listen to what the unjust judge said.´
`Will not God give justice his own elect, who cry day and night to him, even though he suffers along with them?´
`I tell you that he will quickly give them justice. Nevertheless, will the Son of Man find any faith left on earth when he comes?´"
Then Jesus told another parable to some people who thought they were righteous, but they despised other people.
And Jesus said, "`A Pharisee and a publican (Roman tax collector) went into the temple to pray.´
`The Pharisee stood and prayed to himself and said, 'God, I thank you that I am not like other men who are extortioners, unjust, adulterers, or even publicans.´
`I fast twice a week and I tithe everything that I possess.'´
`But the publican stood back and would not even look up to heaven, and he beat his chest and said, 'God be merciful to me for I am a sinner!'´
`I tell you; the publican went home justified but not the Pharisee, because whoever glorifies himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be glorified.´"
The people also brought some infants for Jesus to touch, but when his disciples saw this, they reprimanded them.
But Jesus called the children to him and said, "`Let the little children come to me and do not forbid them, because the Kingdom of God belongs to those such as these.´
`Truly I tell you; whoever does not receive the Kingdom of God like a little child will not enter the kingdom.´
Then one of the rulers asked him, "Good teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?"
Jesus replied to him and said, "`Why do you call me good? No one is good except the One True God.´
`You know the commandments, do not commit adultery, do not kill, do not steal, do not bear false witness, honor your father and mother.´
And the ruler said, "I have kept all of these from my youth."
When Jesus heard this, he said, "`You only lack one thing, go and sell everything that you own and give it to the poor, then you will have treasure in heaven. After that come and follow me.´"
When the ruler heard this, he was very sorrowful because he was quite rich.
Jesus realized how very sorrowful the ruler was and he said, "`How hard it is for those who have riches to enter into the Kingdom of God!´
`Because it is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle, than it is for a rich man to enter the Kingdom of God.´"
Everyone who heard that asked, "Then who can be saved?"
But Jesus said, "`What is impossible for man is possible with God.´"
Then Peter said, "We have left everything to follow you."
Jesus said to them, "`Truly I tell you; whoever has left his home, parents, brothers, wife, or children for the sake of the Kingdom of God.´
`Will receive much more in return now, and in the world to come with everlasting life.´"
Then Jesus spoke to the twelve disciples privately and said, "`Behold we are going to Jerusalem, where all things written by the prophets about the Son of Man will be fulfilled.´
`For the Son of Man will be delivered to the Gentiles, and he will be mocked, treated spitefully, and spit on.´
`Then they will scourge him, put him to death, but he will rise again on the third day.´"
The disciples did not understand any of these things. The meaning of the things that Jesus was telling them was kept hidden, and they did not know what he was talking about.
As they approached Jericho, a blind man was sitting by the roadside begging.
When he heard the crowd passing by, he asked them what was happening.
And they told him that Jesus of Nazareth was passing by.
And the blind man cried out and said, "Jesus, son of David, have mercy on me!"
The people walking ahead of Jesus reprimanded him and told the blind man to be quiet, but he cried out even louder and said, "Son of David, have mercy on me!"
Jesus stopped and told them to bring the blind man to him, so they brought him.
Then Jesus asked, "`What do you want me to do for you?´" And the blind man said, "Lord, I wish to receive my sight."
Jesus granted his request and said, "`Then receive your sight, for your faith has saved you.´"
The man immediately received his sight, and he glorified God as he followed Jesus. Everyone else who saw it also praised God.
Then Jesus entered and passed through Jericho.
There was a rich man named Zacchaeus in Jericho, who was a chief tax collector.
He was trying to see Jesus, but he could not see over the crowd because he was short.
So Zacchaeus ran ahead of the crowd and climbed up into a sycamore tree, because Jesus was about to pass by that way.
When Jesus was near the tree, he looked up and saw Zacchaeus and he said, "`Zacchaeus, hurry down from that tree because I want to visit you at your house today.´"
Zacchaeus quickly climbed down and joyfully received Jesus.
When the people saw this, they all whispered to each other and said, "Jesus has gone to be the guest of a sinner."
But Zacchaeus stood up and said to Jesus, "Look teacher, I give half of everything I own to the poor, and if I have taken anything from anyone under false pretenses, I will repay it fourfold."
Jesus said to Zacchaeus, "`This day salvation has come to this house because Zacchaeus is also a son of Abraham.´
`For the Son of Man has come to find and save that which was lost.´"
As the crowd heard these things Jesus told them a parable, because he was near Jerusalem and the people thought that the Kingdom of God was going to immediately appear.
So Jesus said, "`A nobleman traveled to a far country to claim a kingdom for himself, then returned home.´
`Before he left, the nobleman summoned his ten servants, and gave them ten minas and said to them, 'Use this to keep the business going while I am gone.'´
`But some of the citizens of the kingdom the nobleman was going to claim hated him, so they sent a messenger to him who said, "We do not want you to be our ruler.'´
`After the nobleman returned from claiming his kingdom, he ordered the servants to whom he had given the money to come to see him. He wanted to find out how much profit each man had made.´
`The first man came to him and said, 'Lord, your mina has gained ten minas.'´
`The nobleman said to him, 'Well done good servant, you have been faithful with very little, so you now have authority over ten cities.´
`And the second man came to him and said, 'Lord, your mina has gained five minas.'´
`So the nobleman said to him, 'You will also be over five cities.'´
`And the third man came to him and said, 'Lord, here is your mina, which I kept protected for you in a napkin.'´
`I was afraid because you are a demanding man, for you take what you did not make, and you reap what you did not sow.´

`So the nobleman said to him, 'You wicked servant, I will judge you by the words from your own mouth. You knew that I was a demanding man, because I take what I did not make, and I reap what I did not sow.´
`Why did you not give my money to the bank, so that when I returned, I could have at least collected some interest?'´
`Then the nobleman said to those who stood nearby, 'Take the mina from this man, and give it to the one who has ten minas.'´
`And they said to him, 'But Lord, he already has ten minas.'´
`So the nobleman said, 'I tell you this, whoever has much will be given more, and whoever does not have much, will have even what he does have taken away from him.´
`But as far as my enemies who do not want me to rule over them are concerned, bring them here and kill them before me.'´"
After Jesus said all this, he went on ahead to Jerusalem.
When Jesus was near Bethany and Bethphage at Mount Olive, he sent two of his disciples out.
And Jesus said to them, "`Go to the nearest village, and you will find an unbroken never ridden colt tied up near the entrance, untie him and bring him here.´
`If anyone asks you, 'Why are you untying him?' Tell them, 'Because the teacher needs him.'´"
So they went and found the colt just as Jesus had told them.
As they were untying the colt, its owners asked them, "Why are you untying our colt?"
And the disciples said, "Because the teacher needs him."
When they brought the colt to Jesus, they threw their garments on the colt then Jesus sat on him.
As Jesus rode the colt toward Jerusalem, the people spread their cloaks along the road.
When Jesus reached the foot of Mount Olive, all of the disciples began to loudly rejoice and praise God, because of all the mighty works that they had seen.
And they were all saying, "Blessed is the king who comes in the name of the Lord! Peace in heaven and glory to God in the highest!"
Some of the Pharisees among the crowd said to him, "Master, you need to reprimand your disciples!"
But Jesus answered them and said, "`I tell you, if these people were to remain silent even the stones would immediately cry out.´"
Jesus wept when he first saw Jerusalem.
Then Jesus began to prophesy and he said, "`O Jerusalem, if only you had known what would have brought you peace on this day! But now those things are all hidden from your eyes.´
`For the days are coming when your enemies will dig a trench to surround and trap you on every side.´
`They will level you and your children to the ground. They will not leave one stone within your borders standing, because you did not know your time of visitation from God.´"
Then Jesus went into the temple, and he began to throw out the merchants who were buying and selling there.
Jesus said to them, "`It is written, that my house is a house of prayer, but you have made it into a den of thieves.´"
Jesus taught in the temple daily. But the chief priests, scribes, and the people's leaders wanted to destroy him.
But they could not figure out a way to kill him, because all the people wanted to hear anything Jesus had to say.
One day, when Jesus was teaching the people in the temple and preaching the gospel the chief priests, scribes, and elders came to see him.
They spoke to Jesus and said, "Tell us, by what authority do you do these things, and who gave you this authority?"
Jesus answered them and said, "`First, I would like you to answer one question for me.´
`Was the baptism of John from heaven, or was it from men?´"
The priests, scribes, and elders discussed it among themselves and said, "If we say it was from heaven, he will say, 'Then why did you not believe him?'
But if we say it was from men, all the people will stone us, because they are convinced that John was a prophet."
So they all answered him and said, "We do not know where it was from."
Jesus replied to them and said, "`Then I cannot tell you by what authority I do these things.´"
Then Jesus began to tell the people this parable, "`A man planted a vineyard, and leased it to some farmers and he went to a distant country for a long time.´
`At the harvest season he sent a servant to the farmers, to collect his share of the fruit from the vineyard, but the farmers beat him and sent him away empty handed.´
`So the owner sent another servant, and they beat him too, treated him shamefully, and sent him away empty handed.´
`The owner sent a third servant, and they wounded him and threw him out.´
`Then the vineyard owner said, 'What can I do about this? I know, I will send my beloved son, maybe they will respect him when he gets there.'´
`But when the farmers saw him, they thought about it and said, 'This is the owner's heir, let us kill him and we can take his inheritance for ourselves.'´
`So they threw the son out of the vineyard and killed him. So, what should the vineyard owner do to them?´
`I tell you this; the owner will come and destroy those farmers and give the vineyard to others.´" When the people heard this, they said, "God forbid that this should ever happen."
But Jesus looked at them and said, "`So, what is the meaning of the written statement that says, 'The stone that the builders rejected, will become the head cornerstone?´
`Whoever falls on that stone will be broken, but whoever it falls on will be ground into powder.'´"
When the chief priests and scribes realized that this parable was about them, they wanted to arrest Jesus right then, but they were afraid of the people.

So they watched him and sent spies to him pretending to be righteous men. They were looking for anything he was saying that they could use against him to deliver him to the power and authority of the governor.
The spies asked him, "Master, we know that you are a righteous teacher, and you are not impressed by a person's position, but you truly teach the way of God.
So is it lawful for us to pay taxes to Caesar, or not?"
But Jesus recognized their viper craftiness and said to them, "`Why are you testing me?´
`Show me a penny. Whose image and inscription is on this penny?´" They answered and said, 'Caesar's.'´
Then Jesus said to them, "`So, give to Caesar the things which belong to Caesar and give to God the things which belong to God.´"
And they were disappointed that they could not trap Jesus with his own words in front of the people. And they were so astonished by his answer that they remained silent.
Then some of the Sadducees who deny that there is a resurrection came to question Jesus.
And they said, "Master, Moses wrote that if a man's married brother dies without children, his surviving brother must marry his wife and raise children for his brother.
So there were seven brothers, and the first brother married a wife and died childless.
The second brother married the dead brother's wife, and he died childless.
The third brother married the dead brother's wife, and he died childless. And the same thing happened for all seven brothers.
Last of all the woman also died.
So in the resurrection whose wife will she be? Because all seven of them had been married to her."
And Jesus answered them and said, "`The children of this world marry and are given in marriage.´
`But those who are found to be worthy of being resurrected from the dead in the world to come, will neither marry nor be given in marriage.´
`Nor will they die anymore because they will be equal to the angels. For they are the children of the resurrection which will make them the children of God.´
`Even Moses showed that the dead are raised at the burning bush, when he calls the Lord, 'The God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.'´
`For he is not a God of the dead, but he is the God of the living because to him all are alive.´"
Then some of the scribes answered Jesus and said, "Master, you have answered well."
After that they did not dare ask Jesus any more questions.
Then Jesus said, "`How can they say that Christ is David's son?´
`When David himself says in the book of Psalms, 'The Lord said to my Lord, "I want you to sit at my right hand.´
`Until I make your enemies your footstool."'´
`So if David calls him Lord, how can he then be his son?'"´
Then Jesus spoke to his disciples in front of the large audience.

And Jesus said, "`Beware of the scribes, who desire to walk in long robes. They love to be greeted in the markets; they love the highest seats in the synagogues and the most prominent room at the feasts.´
`They also devour widows' houses and make long prayers just to put on a show. And they will receive the greater damnation.´"
Jesus looked up and he saw the rich men putting their gifts into the temple treasury.
And he also saw a poor widow giving two small copper coins.
So Jesus said, "`Truly I tell you; that this poor widow has thrown in more than everyone else.´
`For all the others have given to God from their abundance, but this poor widow has given everything that she had to live on.´"
Some people were talking about the beautiful temple stonework and the gifts in the treasury.
So Jesus said, "`As for these things which you are looking at, there will come a time when not one of these stones will be left standing on another, for they will all be thrown down.´"
And they asked Jesus, "Master, when will these things happen, and what will be the sign that these things are about to happen?"
And Jesus said, "`Pay attention and do not be deceived because many will come in my name and say, 'I am Christ, and the end of time is near.' Do not follow them.´
`But when you hear of wars and other distractions, do not be terrified, because all these things must happen first, but the end is not near.´"
Then Jesus said to them, "`Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom.´
`There will be great earthquakes in different places and famines, pestilences, and fearful sights, and there will be great signs from heaven.´

`But before all these things happen, they will arrest you and persecute you. They will bring you before kings and rulers to be thrown into prisons, and they will deliver you up to the synagogues. All of this will be for my name's sake.´
`And it will turn into a testimony for you.´"
And Jesus continued speaking and said, "`Therefore, settle your hearts and do not meditate or worry about how you will answer.´
`For I will give you wisdom and a wise mouth, which all of your adversaries will be unable to deny nor resist.´
`You will also be betrayed by parents, brothers, family, and friends and some of you will be put to death because of them.´
`You will be hated by all men for my name's sake.´
`But not one hair on your head will perish.´
`Your patient endurance will help you take possession of your souls.´
`But when you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, then will know that her devastation is near.´
`Then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains and let those in the middle of the city leave, and do not let those living in the country enter the city.´
`For these will be the days of vengeance, so that everything that is written can be fulfilled.´
`But woe unto those who are pregnant or nursing children in those days! For there will be great distress in the land and anger against these people.´
`They will fall by the sword and led away as captives into all nations. Jerusalem will be trampled down by the Gentiles until the times of the Gentiles are fulfilled.´
`There will be signs in the sun, the moon, and the stars. And on earth the nations will be distressed and confused by the roaring waves of the sea.´
`Men's hearts will fail from fear after seeing all those things happening on the earth, because the powers of heaven will be shaken.´
`And then they will see the Son of Man coming in a cloud with power and great glory.´
`When these things begin to happen, lift up your heads and look up because your redemption draws near.´"
Then Jesus told them a parable and said, "`Look at all the trees including the fig tree.´
`When they sprout, you can see and know for yourselves that summer is near.´
`So when you see all these things happening, you will also know that the Kingdom of God is near.´
`Truly I tell you; this generation will not pass away until all of these things have happened.´
`Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will never pass away.´
`Pay attention to yourselves, otherwise your hearts could be overcome by gluttony, drunkenness, and the cares of this life when you least expect it.´
`For a snare of sin will come against everyone who lives on the face of the earth.´
`So keep watch, and always pray that you will be counted among the worthy to escape the things that are going to happen when you stand before the Son of Man.´"
Jesus taught in the temple every day, and at night he went up into Mount Olive to rest.
And the people came to the temple to see and hear him early in the morning.
Now the Passover Feast of Unleavened Bread drew near.
And the chief priests and scribes met to discuss how they could kill Jesus, because they feared the people.
Then Satan entered into Judas Iscariot, who was one of Jesus' twelve disciples.
Judas slipped away from the other disciples and went to talk to the chief priests and captains about betraying Jesus to them.
The chief priests and captains were very happy, and they made a contract to give Judas money for his betrayal.
And Judas promised to find them an opportune time to betray Jesus when there were no crowds around.
Then the day of unleavened bread came, when the Passover lamb must be killed.
So Jesus sent Peter and John to find a place to go for the Passover Feast and he said, "`Go and prepare a place for us to eat and celebrate the Passover.´"
Peter and John asked him, "Where do you want us to prepare everything?"
Jesus responded to them and said, "`When you enter the city, you will see a man carrying a pitcher of water, follow him to his house.´
`Then speak to the homeowner and say, 'The teacher wants us to ask you, "Where are the guest chambers where I can eat the Passover with my disciples?"'´
`He will show you a large furnished upper room where you must prepare for the Passover.´"
Peter and John went and found the man that Jesus told them about, and they prepared for the Passover.
When the Passover hour arrived Jesus sat down with his twelve apostles.
Then Jesus said to them, "`I have patiently desired to eat this Passover with you before I must suffer.´
`For I tell you, I will not eat it again until it is fulfilled in the Kingdom of God.´"
Jesus picked up his cup and gave thanks to God and said, "`Divide this among yourselves.´
`For I tell you, I will not drink from the fruit of the vine again, until the Kingdom of God comes.´"

Then Jesus took a piece of bread and gave thanks to God, and broke it into pieces and gave it to them and said, "`This is my body which I have given for you, so do this when you want to remember me.´"
After supper Jesus picked up the cup and in the same way he said, "`This cup is the new testament in my blood, which is shed for you.´
`For behold, the hand of my betrayer is sitting with me at the table.´
`Truly the Son of Man will go just as it has been decided, but woe unto the man who betrays him!´"
Then the disciples began talking among themselves about which one of them was going to betray Jesus.
And they were also arguing about which one of them would be considered the greatest.
So Jesus said to them, "`The Gentile kings lord over the Gentiles, and those with authority over them are called benefactors.´
`But you will not be like them, the one who is the greatest among you will be like the youngest among you, and the one who leads will be the one who serves the others.´
`For who is greater, the one who sits and eats at table or the one who serves? In this world is it not the one who sits and eats at table? But I am among you as one who serves.´
`You are the ones who have been with me during my temptations.´
`And I will appoint a kingdom to you, just as my father has appointed mine.´
`This will be so that you can eat and drink at my table in my kingdom, and sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel.´"
Then Jesus said, "`Look Simon, Satan has asked God to sift all of you like wheat.´
`But I have prayed for your faith not to fail, then after you are converted you will strengthen your brothers.´"
And Peter said to him, "Teacher, I am ready to go to prison and die with you."
But Jesus said, "`I tell you Peter, the cock will not crow today before you deny knowing me three times.´"
Jesus spoke to his disciples again and said, "`When I sent you out with no purse, no luggage, and no shoes did you need anything?´" And they said, "Nothing."
Then Jesus said to them, "`But now let whoever has a purse or luggage take it with them. And let whoever has no sword sell his garments and buy one.´
`For I tell you, this written Scripture which says, 'And he was counted among the transgressors,' must be accomplished in me because the things written about me have an ending.´"
And the disciples said, "Teacher, we have two swords." And Jesus said to them, "`It is more than enough.´"
As was his custom, Jesus left and his disciples followed him to Mount Olive.
When he came to his chosen place he said, "`Pray that you do not enter into temptation.´"
Then he withdrew about a stone's throw away from them and knelt down and prayed.
Jesus prayed and said, "`Father if you are willing, I ask that you remove this cup from me, nevertheless not my will be done, but your will be done.´"
An angel from heaven appeared to Jesus and strengthened him.
And since Jesus was in agony he prayed even more earnestly, and sweat fell like drops of blood on the ground.
When Jesus got up from praying, he returned to his disciples and found them sleeping, for they were exhausted from sorrow.
And Jesus said to them, "`Why are you sleeping? Get up and pray, otherwise you may enter into temptation.´"
While Jesus was still speaking, he saw a small army coming toward him led by Judas, who was one of the twelve disciples. And Judas moved closer to Jesus kissed him.
But Jesus said to him, "`Judas why are you betraying the Son of Man with a kiss?´"
When those around Jesus saw what was about to happen they said, "Lord, should we fight with the sword?"
Then one of them struck the high priest's servant and cut off his right ear.
Jesus spoke out and said, "`That is enough!´" Then he touched the servant's ear and healed him.
Then Jesus spoke to the chief priests, the temple captains, and the elders who had come for him and said, "`Have you come to arrest me with swords and spears like I was a thief?´
`I was with you in the temple every day and you did not try to arrest me, but this hour belongs to you and the power of darkness.´"
Then they led him away and brought him to the high priest's house, and Peter followed them from a distance.
They kindled a fire in the middle of the courtyard and they all sat together, and Peter sat among them.
But a servant girl saw Peter sitting by the fire, and she looked straight at him and said, "This man was also with Jesus!"
Peter denied knowing Jesus and said, "Woman, I do not know him!"
After a while someone else saw Peter and said, "You are also one of them!" And Peter said, "Man, I am not with them!"
After about an hour someone else confidently confirmed her story and said, "The truth is this fellow was also with Jesus, because he is a Galilean!"
And Peter said, "Man, I do not know what you are talking about!" And immediately as he was still speaking, the cock crowed.
Then Jesus turned and looked at Peter and he remembered that Jesus had said, "`Before the cock crows, you will deny me three times.´"
Then Peter left weeping bitterly.
The men who held Jesus mocked and beat him.
After they blindfolded him they struck Jesus on the face and said, "Can you prophesy to us and tell us who just hit you?"
And they said many other things blasphemous things against him.
At daybreak, the people's elders, chief priests, and scribes got together and led him to their council chambers.
And they said to Jesus, "Tell us, are you the Christ?" And Jesus said to them, "`If I tell you the truth, you will not believe me.´
`And if I also ask you a question, you will not answer me nor will you let me go.´
`From now on the Son of Man will sit at God's right hand.´"
Then they all said, "Are you the Son of God?" And Jesus said to them, "`You say that I am.´"
And they said, "Why do we need more witnesses? We have heard it for ourselves straight from his own mouth."
Then the whole council of chief priests got up and led Jesus to Pilate.

As they stood before Pilate, they began to make accusations against Jesus and they said, "We found this man perverting our nation. He has forbidden the payment of taxes to Caesar, and he said that he is Christ the king."
Pilate spoke to Jesus and asked, "Are you the king of the Jews?" And Jesus answered him and said, "`You have said it.´"
Then Pilate spoke to the chief priests and the people and said, "I find no fault in this man."
Then they spoke more forcefully and said, "But he stirs up the people with all his teachings from here to Galilee and throughout all of Israel."
When Pilate heard about Galilee, he asked if the man was a Galilean.
As soon as Pilate realized that Jesus was from Herod's jurisdiction, he sent Jesus to Herod who just happened to be in Jerusalem at that time.
When Herod saw Jesus, he was extremely happy because he had been wanting to see him for a long time. Herod had heard many things about Jesus, and he was hoping to see one of his miracles.
Then Herod asked Jesus many questions, but Jesus refused to answer.
But the chief priests and scribes continued to vehemently accuse Jesus.
Then Herod and his soldiers thought that Jesus was a big nothing and they mocked him. They dressed him in a gorgeous robe and sent him back to Pilate.
That day Pilate and Herod became friends, because before this there had been much hostility between the two.
Then Pilate summoned the chief priests, the rulers, and the people together.

And Pilate spoke to them and said, "You have brought this man to me as someone who perverts the people. But I have cross examined him before you, and I have found no fault in him. Jesus is not guilty of the things that you accuse him of.
Even Herod has found him not guilty, because I sent Jesus to Herod, and he says that Jesus has done nothing to deserve the death penalty.
Therefore I will punish Jesus and release him.
For we must release one of the prisoners to the people at the feast."
All at once the crowd cried out and said, "Take Jesus away and release Barabbas!"
Barabbas had been thrown into prison for murder and sedition in the city.
But Pilate wanted to release Jesus instead of Barabbas, so he spoke to the crowd again.
Then they all cried out again and said, "Crucify Jesus, crucify him!"
And Pilate spoke to the crowd a third time and said, "Why, what evil has Jesus done? I have found no reason to put him to death, so I am going to punish him and let him go."
Instantly the crowd shouted very loudly demanding that Pilate crucify Jesus. So, the unruly crowd and the chief priests prevailed.
Then Pilate pronounced a sentence that met their demands.
Pilate released Barabbas who was thrown into prison for sedition and murder because he was the one they wanted, but he condemned Jesus to placate the crowd.
As the soldiers led Jesus away, they grabbed a Cyrenian man named Simon coming from the country and forced him to carry the cross for Jesus.
A huge crowd of people followed Jesus, including some women who wept and mourned for him.
But Jesus turned to them and said, "`Daughters of Jerusalem, do not weep for me, weep for yourselves and your children.´
`For the days are coming when they will say, 'Blessed are the barren wombs that have never given birth, and the breasts which have never nursed children.´
`Then they will begin to say to the hills and mountains, 'Fall on us and cover us!'´
`For if they do these things while the tree is green, what will they do when it is old and dried out?´"
There were two other criminals being led away with Jesus to be put to death.
When they came to the place called Calvary, they crucified Jesus and the two criminals one on his right side and the other to his left.
Then Jesus said, "`Father, forgive them for they do not know what they are doing!´" Then the soldiers removed his clothing and cast lots for it.
As the people and the rulers stood nearby watching, the rulers derided Jesus and said, "Jesus saved others, so if he is Christ let the chosen son of God save himself!"
And the soldiers also mocked Jesus and offered him vinegar to drink.
Then the soldiers said, "If you are the king of the Jews, save yourself!"
The soldiers wrote an inscription on a plank in Greek, Latin, and Hebrew and hung over his head that said, "THIS IS THE KING OF THE JEWS!"
One of the criminals who was crucified with Jesus screamed at him and said, "If you are Christ, save yourself and us!"
But the other one reprimanded him and said, "Do you not fear God, because you are under the same condemnation?
For we have been justly sentenced for our deeds, and we have received our just rewards, but Jesus has done nothing wrong."
And he said to Jesus, "Jesus, remember me when you come into your kingdom!"
And Jesus said to him, "`Truly I tell you; today you will be with me in paradise.´"
At about the sixth hour, darkness covered the entire earth until the ninth hour.
The sun was darkened, and the temple veil was torn in half.
Then Jesus cried out with a loud voice and said, "`Father, I commend my spirit into your hands!´" After saying this, Jesus gave up the ghost.
When the centurion saw what happened, he glorified God and said, "Truly this was a righteous man."
When all the people who had come together at that place saw everything that happened, they beat their chests and returned home.
But everyone who knew Jesus including the women who had followed him from Galilee, stood back at a distance watching everything that was happening.
There was a councilman named Joseph who was a good and just man.
Joseph, who also waited for the Kingdom of God was from the Jewish city of Arimathea, and he did not agree with the council's decisions.
Joseph went to Pilate and begged for the body of Jesus.
He took the body down, wrapped it in linen, and laid it in a tomb of carved stone where no one had ever been buried before.
That day was preparation day and the beginning of the Sabbath.
And the women who had followed Jesus from Galilee saw the tomb and where his body had been laid.
So the women returned to prepare the spices and perfumes for the burial, but they rested on the Sabbath day as it was commanded.
Very early in the morning on the first day of the week, the women went to the tomb with the spices and other items they had prepared for the burial.
But they found the stone had been rolled away from the tomb.
They entered the tomb, but they could not find the body of Jesus.
And they were baffled over the whereabouts of the body, suddenly there were two men standing beside them wearing shining garments.
The women were afraid and they bowed facedown to the ground, and the men wearing the shiny garments spoke to the women and said, "Why are you looking for the living among the dead?
He has risen and he is not here! Remember what he told you when he was still in Galilee.
For Jesus had said, "`The Son of Man must be delivered into the hands of sinful men to be crucified, but on the third day he will rise again.´"
And they remembered his words.
The women returned from the tomb, and told everything to everyone including the eleven disciples.
Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Mary the mother of James, and a few other women with them told the apostles everything.
But the women's words words seemed like idle tales to the apostles, and they did not believe them.
Then Peter got up and ran to the tomb and looked in and saw the empty tomb with the linen clothes laying there. Then Peter left as he wondered to himself about what had just happened.
Two of the followers of Jesus left that day and went to a village called Emmaus, which was about sixty furlongs( 7.5 miles) from Jerusalem.
And they discussed everything that had happened.
As they were talking together, Jesus himself moved closer and walked with them.
But their eyes were prevented from recognizing him.
And Jesus said to them, "`What are you two talking about? Why are you walking along so sadly?´"
The one name Cleopas answered him and asked, "Are you the only stranger in Jerusalem who does not know what has been happening there these last few days?"

And Jesus asked them, "`What things?´" And they answered him and said, "The things that happened to Jesus of Nazareth! He was a prophet who spoke powerful words and performed mighty miracles before God and all the people.
The chief priests and rulers condemned Jesus to death and delivered him over to be crucified.
But we trusted that Jesus would be the one who would save Israel. And besides that, today is the third day since all these things happened.
Some of the women from our group astonished us, because they went to the tomb early this morning.
But they could not find his body and they came and told us that they had seen a vision of angels, who said that Jesus was alive.
Some of those with us went to the tomb and found it just as the women had said, but they did not see him.
Then Jesus said to them, "`O foolish ones, you are so slow to believe in your hearts everything that the prophets wrote.´
`Should the Christ not have suffered all these things to enter into his glory?´
Along the way, Jesus explained everything written in the scriptures about himself, beginning with Moses and all the prophets.
As they approached the village where they were going, Jesus seemed like he wanted to go a little further.
But they begged him to stay and said, "Stay with us, because it is nearly evening and the day is almost over." So Jesus stayed with them.
As he sat at the table with them, he took some bread, blessed it and broke it into pieces and gave it to them.
Suddenly their eyes were opened, they knew who he was and he vanished from their sight.
And they said to each other, "Did not our hearts burn within us, as he talked to us by the road side when he opened the scriptures for us?"
Right then they got up and returned to Jerusalem, where they found the eleven disciples and those with them all gathered together.
And they said, "Jesus has indeed risen from the dead and he has appeared to Simon.
And they told them about everything that had happened on the road, and how they recognized Jesus after he broke the bread.
As they were speaking, Jesus appeared in their midst and he spoke to them and said, "`Peace be with you!´"
But they were frightened and terrified, and they thought that they were seeing a spirit.
So Jesus said to them, "`Why are you troubled, and why do doubts rise in your hearts?´
`Look at my hands and feet and you will see that it is me. Touch me and see, because a spirit does not have flesh and bones and you can clearly see that I do.´
After he had spoken, he showed them his hands and feet.
While they still astonished with disbelief they were joyously overcome with wonder. And Jesus said to them, "`Do you have anything to eat here?´"
So they gave him a piece of a broiled fish, and piece of a honeycomb.
And he ate it before them.

Then Jesus said to them, "`This is what I was talking about while I was still with you. I told you that everything written about me in the Law of Moses, and by the prophets, and in the psalms must all be fulfilled.´"
And Jesus opened their understanding of the scriptures.
And Jesus said to them, "`It is written that the Christ will suffer and rise from the dead on the third day.´
`And that repentance and remission of sins would be preached in his name among all nations, beginning in Jerusalem.´
`You are witnesses of all these things.´
`And behold, I am sending you the promise of my father. But you must stay in the city of Jerusalem, until you are clothed with power from on high.´"
Then Jesus led them out as far as Bethany, and he lifted up his hands and blessed them.
As he blessed them, he departed from them and he was carried up into heaven.
They worshipped Jesus, and returned to Jerusalem with great joy.
After that they were constantly praising and blessing God in the temple. Amen.
In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
That's the same way it was with God in the beginning.
Everything was made by him, and nothing was made without him.
In him there was life, and life was the light of men.
And light shines in the darkness, but the darkness does not understand it.
Then God sent a man named John into the world.
John came to bear witness of the Light, so that all men through him could believe.
He was not the Light, but he was sent to testify and bear witness of the Light.
The light, which is true Light, who gives light to everyone that comes into the world.
The one who made the world was in the world, but the world did not know him.
He came to his own people, but they did not recognize him.
But he gave power to all of those who received him, and those who believed in his name would become the sons of God.
And they were reborn, not reborn from the will of man or of flesh and blood, but they were reborn through the spirit of God.
The Word became flesh and lived among us, and we have seen his glory, which is the glory of the only begotten son of the father, full of truth and grace.
John cried out and testified about him and said, "This is the man of whom I spoke, he is the one who was to come after me, he is preferred above me because he came before me."
From his fullness we have all received grace for grace.
Because the law was given by Moses, but truth and grace come from Jesus Christ.
No man has ever seen God, except his only Son, who God has proclaimed is held in his father's embrace.
And this was John's response when the Jews sent priests and Levites from Jerusalem to see him and they asked, "Who are you?"
But he did not deny it and he confessed and said, "I am not the Christ!"
And they asked him, "Then what are you, are you Elijah?" And he said, "I am not." Then they asked, "Are you the prophet?" And he answered, "No."
Then they asked him, "Who are you? So that we can give those who sent us an answer. What do you say about yourself?"
He answered them and said, "I am the voice of the one crying out in the wilderness saying, 'Make straight the way of the Lord,' just as the prophet Isaiah predicted."
Then the Pharisees who were sent to see him.
Asked him, "Then why are you baptizing if you are not the Christ, Elijah, or the prophet?"
John answered them and said, "I baptize with water, but there is one standing among you, whom you do not know.
He is the one coming after me who is preferred before me, whose shoelaces I am unworthy to untie."
All this happened in Bethabara beyond the Jordan river, where John was baptizing.
The next day John saw Jesus coming his way and he said, "Behold the lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world.
This is the one of whom I said, 'There is a man coming after me who is preferred before me, for he was before me.'
I did not know him, but he is the reason that I have come baptizing with water, so that he could reveal himself to Israel."
And John testified and said, "I saw the Spirit descending from heaven like a dove, and it landed on his shoulder.

And I did not know him, but the one who sent me to baptize with water said to me, 'The one on whom you see the Spirit descending, and resting on his shoulder is the same one who will baptize with the Holy Spirit.'
And I saw and testified that he was the Son of God."
The next day John was there again with two of his disciples.
And when he saw Jesus as he was walking their way he said, "Behold the lamb of God!"
When John's two disciples heard this, they followed Jesus.
When Jesus saw them following him, he said to them, "`What are you looking for?´" They replied to him and said, "Rabbi (Teacher), where do you live?"
He replied to them and said, "`Come and see.´" So, they went to see where he lived, and they stayed with him that day because it was about ten o'clock.
One of the two men who had heard John speak and then followed Jesus was Simon Peter's brother Andrew.
But first Andrew went and found his brother Simon and said, "We have found our Messiah the Christ."
Andrew brought him to Jesus, who saw him and said, "`You are Simon the son of John, you will be called Cephas, which means rock.´"
The following day Jesus went to Galilee and found Philip and said to him, "`Follow me.´"
Now Philip was from Bethsaida, the same city as Andrew and Peter.
Philip found Nathanael and said to him, "We have found the one who Moses wrote about in the law, and the one the prophets predicted, he is Joseph's son Jesus of Nazareth."
And Nathanael said to him, "Can anything good ever come from Nazareth?" And Philip said, "Come and see."
Jesus saw Nathanael coming his way and said, "`Behold a true Israelite indeed, in whom there is no deceit!´"
Nathanael said to him, "Where do you know me from?" Jesus answered him and said, "`Before Philip called you, I saw you under the fig tree.´"
Nathanael answered him and said, "Rabbi, you are the Son of God and the king of Israel."
Jesus answered him and said, "`Do you believe in me because I said I saw you under the fig tree? Because you will see greater things than this.´"
And Jesus said to Nathanael, "`Truly, truly I say to you; from now on you will see heaven open and the angels of God ascending and descending on the Son of Man.´"
On the third day the mother of Jesus was at a wedding in Cana of Galilee.
Jesus and his disciples had also been invited to the wedding.
When they ran out of wine, Jesus' mother spoke to him and said, "They have no wine."
But Jesus said to his mother, "`Woman, what does this have to do with us? My hour has not yet come.´"
The Jesus' mother spoke to the servants and said, "Do whatever Jesus tells you to do."
So they had six stone jars that were used by the Jews for purification, and each one could hold about twenty to thirty gallons of wine.
And Jesus spoke to them and said, "`Fill these jars with water.´" So, they filled them to the brim.
Then Jesus said, "`Pour some in a cup and take it to the banquet manager.´" So, they took some to the manager.

The banquet manager did not know that the water had been turned into wine, but the servants who had brought the water to Jesus knew. When the banquet manager tasted the wine, he pulled the bridegroom aside.

And the banquet manager said to him, "Everyone serves the best wine at the beginning of the feast, and when the people are drunk, they bring out the cheap wine. But you have saved the best wine for last!"
Then the glory of Jesus was obvious after he performed his first miracle in Cana of Galilee, after this his disciples believed in him.
Later Jesus went down to Capernaum with his mother, brothers, and disciples but they did not stay there for very long.
The Jewish Passover was getting close, so Jesus went to Jerusalem.
Jesus found the merchants in the temple selling oxen, sheep, and doves and the money changers were also sitting there.
So Jesus made a whip out of small ropes and drove them all out of the temple with their sheep and oxen. Then he dumped the money changers' coins on the ground and turned over their tables.
And Jesus spoke to the dove sellers and said, "`Take these things out of here, and do not make my father's house a house of merchandise.´"
Then Jesus' disciples remembered that it was written, "Zeal for my father's house has eaten me up."
Then the Jews responded to Jesus and asked, "Can you show us a sign that proves where your authority to do these things come from?
Jesus answered them and said, "`If you destroy this temple I will raise it up in three days.´"
Then the Jews said, "It has taken forty-six years to build this temple, and you can raise it up in three days?"
But the Jews did not know that Jesus was talking about the temple of his body.
After Jesus had risen from the dead, his disciples remembered when he had told them this. So, they believed the scriptures and the words that Jesus had spoken.
While Jesus was in Jerusalem on the Passover Feast Day, many people believed in him when they saw the miracles he had done.
But Jesus did not commit himself to them because he knew them all.
And Jesus needed no testimony about man because he already knew everything that was in man.
There was a Pharisee and Jewish leader named Nicodemus.
Nicodemus came to Jesus one night and said, "Rabbi, we know that you are a teacher from God, because no man can do the miracles that you do unless God is with him."
Jesus answered him and said, "`Truly, truly I say to you; unless a man is born again, he cannot see the Kingdom of God.´"
And Nicodemus asked, "How can a man be born when he is old? Can he reenter his mother's womb a second time to be reborn?
Jesus answered him and said, "`Truly, truly I say to you; unless you are reborn of water and the Spirit, you cannot enter the Kingdom of God.´
`That which is born of the flesh is flesh, and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit.´
`Do not wonder why I told you, that you must be born again.´
`When the wind blows it goes wherever it wants and you hear its sound, but you cannot tell where it came from or where it is going. This is how it is with everyone born of the Spirit.´"
Nicodemus did not understand Jesus and he asked, "How can this be?"
Jesus answered him and said, "`How can you be Israel's teacher and not know these things?´
`Truly, truly I say to you; we talk about the things we know about, and we testify about what we have seen, but you do not accept our testimony.´
`If I tell you about earthly things and you do not believe me, how can you believe me if I tell you about heavenly things?´
`No man can ascend up to heaven, unless the Son of Man who is in heaven comes down from heaven.´
`Just as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, the Son of Man must be lifted up in the same way.´
`So that whoever believes in him does not perish but will have eternal life.´
`For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, so that whoever believes in him will not perish but have everlasting life.´
`Because God did not send his only son into the world to condemn it, but he sent his son to save the world through him.´
`For whoever believes in him is not condemned, but anyone that does not believe in him is already condemned because they do not believe in the name of God's only begotten son.´
`And this is the condemnation, 'Light has come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than the light, because their deeds were evil.'´
`Everyone who does evil hates the light and does not come into the light because his deeds will be exposed.´
`But the one who is truthful comes into the light, to make it obvious that his deeds are accomplished in God.´"
After these things Jesus and his disciples went to the land of Judea, where he stayed with them and they baptized.
John was also baptizing in Aenon near Salim, because there was a lot of water there, and people came to be baptized.
For John had not yet been thrown into prison.
Then some of the Jews questioned John's disciples about their purification and washing practices.
John's disciples came to him and said, "Rabbi, the one you testified about who was with you beyond the Jordan River, is baptizing the same way and everyone is going to him."
John answered them and said, "A man can receive nothing unless it is given to him from heaven.
You yourselves can testify that I said, 'I am not the Christ, but I am the one who was sent before him.'
The bridegroom has the bride, but the bridegroom's friend who stands and listens for him rejoices greatly when he hears his voice. Therefore, this is my joy, and it is now finished.
Jesus must increase, but I must decrease.
The one who comes from above is above all. The one who is from the earth is earthly and speaks of the earth, The one who comes from heaven is above all.
The one who comes from heaven testifies about what he has seen and heard, and no one believes his testimony.
The one who believed his testimony has sealed his testimony that said God is true.
For the one whom God has sent, speaks the words of God because God gives him the immeasurable Spirit.
The father loves the son, and the father has put all things into his son's hand.
Whoever believes in the son has everlasting life. Whoever does not believe in the son will not see life, but God's anger remains on him."
When Jesus realized the Pharisees had heard that he had made and baptized more disciples than John the Baptist.
Even though Jesus himself did not baptize, but his disciples did.
Jesus left Judea and returned to Galilee.
But he had to go through Samaria.
Then he came to a city in Samaria named Sychar, near the parcel of land that Jacob had given his son Joseph.
Jacob's well was there and Jesus was weary from his journey, so he sat down on the well at about the sixth hour.
Then a Samaritan woman came to draw water, and Jesus spoke to her and asked, "`Can I have a drink?´"
Because his disciples had gone into the city to buy something to eat.
Then the Samaritan woman said to him, "You are a Jew and I am a Samaritan woman, so why are you asking me for drink? Jews usually have no dealings with Samaritans.
Jesus answered her and said, "`If you only knew the gift of God who is asking you for a drink, you would be asking him for a drink, and he would have given you living water.´"
The woman replied to him and said, "Sir, you have nothing to draw water with and the well is deep, where will you get that living water from?
Are you greater than our father Jacob who gave us this well and drank from it himself, as well as his children and his cattle?"
Jesus answered her and said, "`Whoever drinks this water will thirst again.´
`But whoever drinks the water that I give him will never be thirsty again. But the water that I give him will be a well that springs up into everlasting life within him.´"
Then the woman said to him, "Sir, give me this water, so that I will never be thirsty again and I will never have to come back here to draw water.
Jesus said to her, "`Go and call your husband and bring him back here.´"
The woman answered him and said, "I have no husband." And Jesus answered her and said, "`You have told the truth, for you do not have a husband.´
`But you have had five husbands, and the man you are with now is not your husband. You have spoken truthfully.´"
Then the woman said to him, "Sir, I think you must be a prophet.
Our fathers worshipped on this mountain, but you Jews say that Jerusalem is the only place where people must go to worship."
