Jesus replied to her and said, "`Believe me woman, the hour is coming when you will not worship the father on this mountain nor in Jerusalem.´
`You worship what you do not know, we Jews know what we worship, because salvation is from the Jews.´
`But the hour is coming and is now here, when the true worshippers will worship the father in spirit and in truth, because the father seeks those such as these to worship him.´
`God is a Spirit, and those who worship him must worship him in spirit and in truth.´
The woman said to him, "I know that a coming Messiah will be called Christ and when he comes, he will tell us everything."
Jesus said to her, "`I tell you that I am him.´"
After this his disciples arrived and they were surprised that Jesus was talking with a woman. But none of them asked, "What do you want with her, or why are you talking to her?"
Then the woman left her water bucket and went back to the city.
And she said to the men, "Come and see a man who told me everything I have ever done. Do you think this could be the Christ?"
Then they left the city and went to see Jesus.
Meanwhile Jesus' disciples prayed with him and said, "Teacher, eat something."
But Jesus answered them and said, "`I have meat to eat that you know nothing about.´"
So the disciples spoke to each other and asked, "Did someone bring him something to eat?"
Then Jesus answered them and said, "`My meat is to do the will of the one who sent me, and to finish his work.´
`Do not say, 'There is still four months until the harvest? Behold, I tell you to look out into the fields because they are white and ready for harvest.´
`The reaper is ready to collect his wages and gather the fruit to eternal life, so that both the sower and the reaper can rejoice together.´
`Because this old saying, 'One sows and another reaps,' is true.´
`I sent you to reap where you did not labor, for other men have done the work and you have reaped their labor.´"
Many of the Samaritans of that city believed in Jesus because of the woman's testimony when she said, "He told me everything that ever I did."
So when the Samaritans came to him, they implored him to stay with them, and he stayed there for two days.
And many more believed because of his message.
Then they said to the woman, "Now we believe, not because of what you said, but because we have heard him for ourselves. We now know that this is indeed the Christ, the savior of the world."
After two days there Jesus left and went to Galilee.
Jesus himself had testified, that a prophet has no honor in his own country.
When Jesus arrived in Galilee, the Galileans welcomed him. They had seen everything he had done in Jerusalem at the feast, because they had also been at the feast.
So Jesus returned to Cana of Galilee, where he had turned the water into wine. But there was a nobleman there with a sick son in Capernaum.
When he heard that Jesus had come to Galilee from Judea, he went to implore Jesus to come and heal his son because he was near death.
Then Jesus said to him, "`Unless you people see signs and wonders, you will never believe.´"
The nobleman said to Jesus, "Sir, please come before my child dies."
Jesus said to him, "`Go home because your son will live.´" And the man believed what Jesus told him, so he went home.
On his way home the nobleman's servants came to meet him with news and said, "Your son is alive and he is recovering."
Then the nobleman asked them when his son began to recover, and they said to him, "The fever left him yesterday at the seventh hour."
So the father knew that it was at the same time that Jesus had said, "`Your son will live.´" Then the nobleman and his whole house believed.
This was the second miracle that Jesus performed when he went to Galilee from Judea.
After this there was a Jewish feast and Jesus went to Jerusalem.
Near Jerusalem beside the sheep market there was a pool with five entrance halls, which in Hebrew is called Bethesda.
In that area, there was a huge crowd of impotent folks who were blind, sick, and paralyzed waiting for the water fountain to erupt.

For an angel descended to the pool at certain times and stirred the water. Then whoever was first to step into the water after it was stirred up was made whole and cured of whatever health problems they suffered.
There was a crippled man there who had been plagued with an infirmity for thirty-eight years.
When Jesus saw him, he knew that the man had been plagued for a long time. So, Jesus asked him, "`Do you want to be healed and made whole?´"
The impotent man answered him and said, "Sir, I have no one to help put me into the pool when the water is stirred up, and when I try to get to the water, someone steps down ahead of me."
Then Jesus said to him, "`Get up and pick up your bed and walk.´"
Immediately the man was healed, so he picked up his bed and walked. And this happened on the Sabbath.
The Jews approached the man who was cured and said, "It is the Sabbath, and it is unlawful for you to carry your bed."
The healed man answered them and said, "The man who healed me said to me, '`Pick up your bed and walk.´'"
Then the Jews asked him, "Who told you to pick up your bed and walk?"
The healed man did not know because there was a large crowd by the pool and Jesus had not told him his name, and he had already left.
Afterward Jesus found the healed man in the temple and said to him, "`Behold you have been made whole, go and sin no more otherwise something worse may happen to you.´"
Then the man went and told the Jews that it was Jesus who had healed him.
After that the Jews began to persecute Jesus and they tried to find a way to kill him, because he had done these things on the Sabbath.
But Jesus answered them and said, "`My father has been working until now, and I am also at work.´"
And the Jews were even more intent on killing him after that, because he had not only broken the Sabbath, but he had also said that God was his father, making himself equal with God.
Then Jesus answered them and said, "`Truly, truly I say to you; the son can do nothing by himself except what he has seen the father doing. For whatever the father does, the son also does.´
`For the father loves the son and he shows the son everything that he himself has done. And to your amazement, the father will show him even greater works than these.´
`For just as the father quickly raises up the dead and gives them life, so will the son also give life to whomever he chooses.´
`For the father judges no one, but he has committed all judgment to the son.´
`So that all men will honor the son just as they honor the father. For whoever does not honor the son, does not honor the father who sent him.´
`Truly, truly I say to you; whoever hears my words and believes in the one who sent me, will have everlasting life and they will not be condemned, but they will pass from death into life.´
`Truly, truly I say to you; the hour is coming and is indeed here now for the dead to hear the Son of God's voice, and those who hear him will live.´
`For just as the father has life in himself, he has also given the son to have life in himself.´
`The father has also given the son authority to execute judgment, because he is the Son of Man.´
`Do not marvel over this, because the hour is coming when everyone who is in the grave will hear his voice.´
`And those who have done good will come out to the resurrection of life, and those who have done evil will come out to the resurrection of damnation.´
`I can do nothing by myself, I judge as I hear and my judgment is just because I do not seek to do my own will, but I seek only to do the will of my father who sent me.´
`If I witness about myself, then my witness is not true.´
`There is another who testifies about me, and I know that his testimony about me is true.´
`John was sent to you and he told you the truth.´
`I do not accept testimony from man, but I tell you these things, so that you can be saved.´
`John was a burning shining light, and you were willing to rejoice in his light for a season.´

`But I have come with a greater witness than John's. Because the works which my father has given me to finish, are the same works that I am doing. This testimony about me is that the father has sent me.´
`And the father himself who sent me has carried a testimony about me. But not at any time have you heard his voice, nor have you seen his shape.´
`And you do not have his word abiding within you, because you do not believe the one that he sent.´
`You search the scriptures, because you think you have eternal life in them. But the scriptures are the words which testify about me.´
`And you will not come to me, so that you can have life.´
`For I receive no honor from men.´
`But I do know that you do not have the love of God in you.´
`I have come in my father's name, and you will not accept me, but you will accept someone else if he comes in his own name.´
`How can you believe if you accept honor from each other, but you do not seek the honor that comes only from God?´
`Do not think that I will be the one to accuse you before the father. But it is Moses whom you trust who will be your accuser.´
`For if you had believed Moses, you would have believed me because he wrote about me.´
`But if you do not believe the writings of Moses, then how can you believe my words?´"
After this Jesus crossed over the Sea of Galilee (aka. Sea of Tiberias).
A large crowd followed him because they had seen the miracles he had performed for the sick.
Jesus went up on a mountain and sat down with his disciples.
And it was nearly time for the Jewish Feast of the Passover.
When Jesus looked up, he saw a large crowd coming toward him and he said to Philip, "`Where can we buy some bread for these people to eat?´"
Jesus was just asking Phillip this question to test him, because he already knew what he was going to do.
Philip answered him and said, "We only have two hundred denarii, and that will not buy enough bread for each of them to even have a little piece of bread."
One of Jesus' disciples, Simon Peter's brother Andrew spoke up.
And Andrew said, "There is a boy here with five barley loaves and two small fish, but that is not enough for so many!"
And Jesus said, "`Make the men sit down.´" There was plenty of grass in that place, so the men who numbered about 5,000, sat down.
Then Jesus took the loaves and fish, and after he gave thanks to God, and he distributed it to the disciples. They gave it to the people sitting down, and everyone had as much as they wanted to eat.
When they were full, Jesus said to his disciples, "`Gather up the leftover pieces, so that nothing is wasted.´"
So they picked up twelve baskets full of leftovers from the five barley loaves, which remained after everyone had eaten.
Then the men who had seen the miracle that Jesus done they said, "This is the truth, a prophet has come into the world."
When Jesus realized that they were planning to take him by force and make him a king, he departed and went up into the mountains by himself.
When evening came, his disciples went down to the sea.
The disciples boarded a boat and crossed the sea heading toward Capernaum. It was dark, but Jesus had not yet come to them.
A strong wind started blowing which caused the seas to violently rise up.
So after they had rowed about 25 or 30 furlongs (about 3 1/2 miles), they saw Jesus walking on the water toward the boat and they were afraid.
But Jesus said to them, "`It is me, do not be afraid!´"
Then they willingly brought him into the boat, and immediately the boat arrived at the shores of their destination.

The following day, the people who remained on the other side of the sea saw that there were no other boats, they realized that his disciples had left alone in the only boat there, and Jesus had not gone with them.
However other boats had come from Tiberias to the place where the 5,000 had eaten the bread for which Jesus had given thanks to God.
When those people realized that neither Jesus nor his disciples were there, they took their boats to Capernaum to find Jesus.
When they found Jesus on the other side of the sea they asked him, "Rabbi, when did you come here?"
Jesus answered them and said, "`Truly, truly I say to you; you do not look for me because you saw miracles, you only search for me because you ate the loaves of bread until you were full.´

`Do not labor for meat that perishes, but for meat which will be given to you by the Son of Man that will last until everlasting life. Because God the father has placed his seal of approval on the son.´"
Then they asked Jesus, "What must we do, so that we can do the works of God?"
Jesus answered them and said, "`This is the work of God, believe in the one whom God has sent!´"
So they asked him, "What sign can you show us, so that we can see it and believe in you? What miracle can you do?
Our fathers ate manna in the desert because it is written, 'God gave them bread from heaven to eat.'"
Then Jesus said to them, "`Truly, truly I say to you; Moses did not give you bread from heaven. My father is the one who gives you the true bread from heaven.´
`For the bread of God is the one who comes down from heaven and gives life to the world.´"
Then they said to him, "Lord, give us this bread forever."
And Jesus said to them, "`I am the bread of life, whoever comes to me will never hunger, and whoever believes in me will never thirst.´
`It is just as I have told you, you have seen me, but you still do not believe.´
`Everything that my father gives me will come to me, and I will not throw out anyone who comes to me.´
`For I did not come down from heaven to do my own will, but I came to do the will of my father who sent me.´
`And it is the will of my father who sent me that I should lose nothing he has given me, but I will raise them up again at the last day.´
`It is the will of my father who sent me that whoever sees the son and believes in him, will have everlasting life and I will raise them up at the last day.´"
Then the Jews whispered about Jesus because he said, "`I am the bread which came down from heaven.´"
And they said, "Is this not Jesus the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know? How can he say, 'I came down from heaven?'"
So Jesus answered them and said, "`Do not gossip among yourselves.´
`No man can come to me, unless the father who sent me accepts him, and I will raise him up at the last day.´
`Because it is written by the prophets, 'And they will all be taught by God.' Everyone who has heard the father and learned from him comes to me.´
`No man has seen the father except the one who is from God, for he has seen the father.´
`Truly, truly I say to you; whoever believes in me has everlasting life.´
`I am the bread of life.´
`Your fathers ate manna in the wilderness, and they are dead.´
`This is the bread which comes down from heaven, so that anyone who eats of it will not die.´
`I am the living bread which came down from heaven. If anyone eats this bread, they will live forever. The bread that I give is my flesh, which I will give to save the life of the world.´"
When the Jews heard this, they struggled amongst themselves and said, "How can this man give us his flesh to eat?"
Then Jesus said to them, "`Truly, truly I say to you; unless you eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink his blood, you will have no life within you.´
`Whoever eats my flesh and drinks my blood, has eternal life, and I will raise them up at the last day.´
`For my flesh is indeed meat, and my blood is indeed drink.´
`Whoever eats my flesh and drinks my blood, lives in me and I live in him.´
`Just as the living father has sent me, and I live because of the father. So will the one who eats my flesh and lives because of me.´
`This is the bread which came down from heaven, not like the mana that your dead fathers ate because whoever eats this bread will live forever.´"
Jesus said all of these things in the synagogue as he taught in Capernaum.
When many of his disciples heard this, they said, "This is a hard lesson, who can listen to it?
When Jesus realized that his own disciples whispered about it, he said, "`Does this offend you?´
`What will you do if you see the Son of Man ascend up to where he was before?´
`It is the spirit that gives life because the flesh profits nothing. The words I have spoken to you are spirit and they are life.´
`But there are some of you who do not believe!´" Jesus had known since the beginning who would not believe and who would betray him.
And Jesus said, "`So that's why I told you, no one can come to me, unless my father gave them to me.´"
After Jesus said this many of his disciples left and no longer walked with him.
Then Jesus said to the twelve disciples, "`Will you also go away?´
Then Simon Peter answered him and said, "Teacher, to whom can we go? You have the words of eternal life.
We believe and know for sure that you are the Christ, and the Son of the living God."
Jesus answered them and said, "`I have chosen all twelve of you, but one of you is a devil!´"
Jesus was talking about Judas Iscariot son of Simon, because Judas was the one of the twelve who would betray him.
After all this Jesus traveled throughout Galilee, because he did not want to go to Judea where the Jews wanted to kill him.
Now it was nearly time for the Jewish Feast of Tabernacles.
So Jesus' brothers said to him, "You should leave and go to Judea, then your disciples can also see all of your miracles.
Nobody does things in secret if they want to be famous. And since you are doing these things, you should go and show yourself to the world."
Jesus' brothers said this because they did not believe him either.
Then Jesus said to them, "`My time has not yet come, but your time is always here.´
`The world cannot hate you, but it does hate me because I testify that its works are evil.´
`So you can go to this feast, but I am not going there because my time has not yet fully come.´"
Jesus told them this and he stayed in Galilee.
After his brothers left, Jesus went to the feast in secret.
But the Jews looked for him at the feast and asked, "Where is he?"
All the people were gossiping among themselves about Jesus because some said, "He is a good man." But others said, "No he is not, he deceives the people."
However no one spoke openly about him because they feared the Jews.
But about halfway through the feast Jesus went into the temple and taught.
The Jews were amazed and they said, "How does this man know so much? He is not a man of letters, and he has never been taught!"
Jesus answered them and said, "`My doctrine is not my own, but it is from the one who sent me.´
`If a man does God's will, he will understand the doctrine, and he will know whether it is from God or not, or if I am only speaking of myself.´
`Whoever speaks only of himself seeks his own glory, but whoever seeks the glory of the one who sent him is truthful, and there is no unrighteousness in him.´
`Moses gave you the law, but none of you keep the law! So why do you want to kill me?´"
The people answered him and said, "You have a demon!" Then they asked, "Who wants to kill you?"
Jesus answered them and said, "`I performed one miracle and you were all amazed.´
`But Moses gave you circumcision, not because it is of Moses but because it is of the fathers, and you circumcise men on the Sabbath day.´
`You circumcise men on the Sabbath day, and you say that the Law of Moses has not been broken. So why are you angry with me because I have healed a man on the Sabbath day?´
`Do not judge people by their appearance but judge them righteously.´"
Then some of the people from Jerusalem said, "Is this not the man they want to kill?
But, lo and behold he speaks boldly and they say nothing to him. Do you think the rulers really know he is the Christ?
However we know where this man comes from. But when Christ comes no one will know where he comes from."

Then Jesus cried out in the temple as he was teaching and said, "`You know me and you know where I am from. I have not come for myself, but I have come for the one who sent me who is true. And you do not know him.´
`But I know him because I am from him, and he has sent me.´
Then they tried to arrest him, but no one laid a hand on him because his hour had not yet come.
Many of the people believed in Jesus and said, "When Christ comes, will he perform more miracles than this man?"
The Pharisees heard the people discussing such things about him. So, the Pharisees and chief priests sent officers to arrest him.
Then Jesus said, "`I will be with you for just a little while longer, and then I will return to the one who sent me.´
`You will look for me, but you will not find me, and you cannot come to where I am.´"
Then the Jews discussed it among themselves and said, "Where can he go, that we cannot find him? Will he teach the Gentiles where the Jews are dispersed among the Gentiles?
What did he mean when he said, 'You will look for me, but you will not find me, and you cannot come to where I am'?"
On the last and greatest day of the feast, Jesus stood in the temple and cried out and said, "`If a man is thirsty, let him come to me and drink.´
`For the scriptures have spoken about people who believe in me where it is written, 'Rivers of living water will flow to them from within him.'´"
But Jesus was speaking about the spirit that would be given to those who believe in him. For the Holy Spirit had not yet been given because Jesus had not yet been glorified.
Therefore many of the people who heard this said, "The truth is that Jesus is the prophet."
Others said, "Jesus is the Christ." But some said, "Do you really think Christ will come from Galilee?
Does not the scripture say that Christ is a descendant of David and he comes from Bethlehem where David lived?"
So the people were divided because of Jesus.
Some of the officers wanted to arrest Jesus, but no one laid a hand on him.
Then the officers returned to the chief priests and Pharisees who asked the officers, "Why have you not arrested him?"
The officers answered them and said, "No man has ever spoken like this man."
Then the Pharisees asked them, "Have you also been deceived?
Do any of the rulers or Pharisees believe in him?
But these people who do not know the law are cursed."
Then Nicodemus who had visited Jesus at night spoke up.
And Nicodemus asked, "Do our laws judge a man before hearing his version of what he has done?"
The Pharisees answered him and said, "Are you not also from Galilee? Check into it yourself because no prophets rise up from Galilee."
Then they all went to their own homes.
Jesus went to Mount Olive.
Then he went into the temple early in the morning, and all the people came and sat down and he taught them.
The scribes and Pharisees brought a woman to Jesus who was caught in adultery, and they put her in the middle of the crowd.
Then they said to Jesus, "Master, this woman was caught in the very act of adultery.
The law of Moses commands us to stone her, so what do you say?"
They said this to test Jesus so that they could make accusations against him. But Jesus stooped down and wrote on the ground with his finger as if he had not heard them.
So they continued questioning Jesus and he stood up and said, "`Let anyone among you who is without sin throw the first stone.´"
Then Jesus stooped down and wrote with his finger on the ground again.
Everyone who heard Jesus say this felt convicted by their own conscience. So, beginning with the oldest, they left one by one until Jesus was the only one left standing beside the woman.
When Jesus stood up, he saw that there was no one there except for the woman and he said to her, "`Woman, where are your accusers? Has no one condemned you?´"
She answered Jesus and said, "No one, Lord." And Jesus said to her, "`Nor do I condemn you. Go and sin no more!´"
At a later time Jesus spoke to the people again and said, "`I am the light of the world, whoever follows me will not walk in darkness, but they will have the light of life!´"
So the Pharisees said to him, "You testify only about yourself, and your testimony is not true."

Then Jesus answered them and said, "`Even though I testify about myself, my testimony is truthful, because I know where I came from and I know where I am going. But you do not know where I came from, nor do you know where I am going.´"
`You judge by the flesh, but I judge no one.´
`But even if I do judge, my judgment is true because I am not alone, for I have been sent by the father who is within me.´
`It is also written in your law, that the testimony of two witnesses reveals the truth.´
`So I testify about myself, and the father who sent me also testifies about me.´"
Then the Pharisees said to him, "Where is your father?" And Jesus answered them and said, "`You neither know me nor my father, for if you knew me, you would have also known my father.´"
Jesus spoke these words in the treasury as he taught in the temple, and no one laid a hand on him because his time had not yet come.
Then Jesus spoke to them again and said, "`I will go away and you will look for me, but you will die in your sins because you cannot go where I am going.´"
Then the Jews said, "Is Jesus going to kill himself? Because he said, `'You cannot go where I am going.'´"
And Jesus said to them, "`You are from below and I am from above, you are from this world, but I am not from this world.´
`That's why I say that you will die in your sins if you do not believe I am who I say I am.´
So they asked him, "Who are you?" And Jesus replied to them and said, "`I am the one I have told you about since the beginning.´
`I have many things to say about you and to judge, but the one who sent me is true, and I tell the world that everything I have heard comes from him.´"
But they did not understand that Jesus was speaking to them about the father.

Then Jesus said to them, "`After you have lifted up the Son of Man, you will know who I am and that I can do nothing on my own. But I can only speak about and do the things that my father has taught me.´
`For the one who sent me is with me and the father has not left me, because I always do what pleases him.´"
And as Jesus spoke many people believed in him.
Then Jesus said to the Jews who believed in him, "`If you continue in my word, then you are indeed my disciples.´
`And you will know the truth, and the truth will set you free.´"
Then the Jews spoke up and said, "We are Abraham's descendants and we have never been enslaved by anyone, how can you say that we will be made free?"
Jesus answered them and said, "`Truly, truly I say to you; whoever commits a sin is a servant of sin.´
`And the servant does not endure in the house forever, but the son endures forever.´
`Therefore if the son sets you free, you will indeed be free.´
`I know that you are Abraham's descendants, but you want to kill me because my word has no place in you.´
`I speak about what I have seen with my father, and you do what you have seen from your father.´"
Then the Jews answered Jesus and said, "But Abraham is our father!" So Jesus responded to them and said, "`If you were Abraham's children, you would do the works of Abraham.´
`But now you want to kill me, a man who has told you the truth which I have heard directly from God. Abraham did not do this!´
`But you do the deeds of your father.´" Then they said to him, "We were not born from adulterous fornication, and God is our one and only father."
Jesus spoke to the Jews again and said, "`If God were your father, you would love me, because I was sent here from God and I have not come here for myself. For God has sent me.´
`So why do you not understand anything that I say? It is because you cannot hear my message?´

`You come from your father the devil, and you do the lusts of your father. The devil was a murderer from the beginning, and he did not live in the truth because there is no truth in him. When he lies, he speaks only about what he knows, because he is a liar and the father of all lies.´
`You do not believe me because I tell you the truth .´
`Which one of you can convict me of sin, and why do you not believe me if I tell you the truth?´
`Whoever is from God hears God's words, but you cannot hear his word because you are not from God.´"
Then the Jews answered Jesus and said, "Are we not correct to say that you are a Samaritan and you have a demon?"
Jesus answered the Jews and said, "`No, I do not have a demon, but I do honor my father, and you dishonor me.´
`I do not seek my own glory, but there is one who seeks my glory and he judges.´
`Truly, truly I say to you; if you keep my word, you will never see death.´"
So the Jews said to Jesus, "Now we know for sure that you have a demon. Abraham and the prophets are dead, and you say, `'If you keep my word, you will never taste of death.'´
Are you greater than our dead father Abraham and the dead prophets; who do you claim to be?"
Jesus answered the Jews and said, "`Your God is my father, and he is the one who honors me, and if I honor myself, my honor is worth nothing.´
`You do not know him, but I do know him. And if I were to say that I do not know him, then I would be a liar like you, but I do know him and I keep his word.´
`Your father Abraham rejoiced to see my day. And when he saw it, he was glad.´"
Then the Jews scoffed at Jesus and said, "You are not even fifty years old, yet you have seen Abraham?"
Jesus taught them and said, "`Truly, truly I say to you; before Abraham, I am.´
Then they picked up stones to throw at him, but Jesus hid and he passed right through their midst and left the temple.
As Jesus was passing by, he saw a man who had been blind since birth.
Jesus' disciples questioned him and asked, "Teacher, did this man's sin cause him to be born blind, or was it his parent's sins?"
Jesus answered them and said, "`It was neither this man nor his parent's sin, but this has happened so that the works of God could be seen in him.´
`I must do the works of the one who sent me, while it is still day. Because the night is coming, when no one will be able to work.´
`As long as I am in the world, I am the light of the world.´"
After Jesus said this, he spit on the ground and made some clay from the spit and dirt, and he rubbed the clay on the blind man's the eyes.
Then Jesus spoke to the blind man and said, "`Go and wash in the pool of Siloam.´" So, he went where he was sent and washed, then he could see.
The neighbors who had seen him before and knew that he was blind said, "Is this not the blind man who sat and begged?"
Some said, "This is him," Others said, "This man just looks like him." But the formerly blind man said, "I am him."
So they asked him, "How were your eyes opened?"

The formerly blind man answered them and said, "A man named Jesus made some clay and rubbed it on my eyes and said to me, `'Go and wash in the pool of Siloam.'´ So, I went and washed and I could see."
Then they asked him, "Where is he now?" And he said, "I do not know."
Then they brought the formerly blind man to the Pharisees.
Because Jesus had made the clay and opened his eyes on the Sabbath day.
The Pharisees asked him again how he had received his sight. He said to them, "He put clay on my eyes, I washed and now I can see."

That's why some of the Pharisees said, "This man is not from God because he does not keep the Sabbath day." Others said, "How can a man who is a sinner do such miracles." And the Jews were divided against each other.
They spoke to the blind man again and said, "What do you say about Jesus, since he has opened your eyes?" The blind man said, "He is a prophet."
But the Jews did not believe that he had been blind, or that his sight had been restored, until they summoned the formerly blind man's parents.
The Jews spoke to the man's parents and asked, "Is this your son, who you say was born blind? If so, why can he now see?"
His parents answered them and said, "We know that this is our son who was born blind.
We do not know why or how he can now see, and we do not know who opened his eyes. But he is an adult, so ask him, because he can speak for himself.
The formerly blind man's parents said this, because they were afraid of the Jews. Because the Jews had agreed earlier that anyone who confessed to being the Christ would be put out of the synagogue.
So his parents said, "He is an adult, ask him."
Then they called the formerly blind man again and said, "Give God the praise! We know that this man is a sinner."
The formerly blind man answered and said, "Whether or not he is a sinner, I do not know. The one thing I do know, is that I was in fact blind, but now I see."
Then they asked him again, "What did he do to you? How did he open your eyes?"
He answered them and said, "I have already told you, and you refused to listen, so why do you want to hear it again? Do you also want to become his disciples?"
Then they condemned him and said, "You are his disciple, but we are Moses' disciples.
We know that God spoke to Moses, but we do not know where this fellow comes from."
The formerly blind man answered them and said, "Well it is absolutely amazing that you do not know where he is from, and yet he has restored my sight.
We know that God does not hear sinners, but if a man worships God and he does God's will, God will hear him.
Since the beginning of the world, it has never been heard that a man born blind could have his sight restored.
If this man were not from God, he could have done nothing."
The Jews answered him and said, "You were born in absolute sin, and you dare to teach us?" Then they threw him out.
Jesus heard that they had thrown the formerly blind man out and after he found the man he asked, "`Do you believe in the Son of God?´"
The formerly blind man answered and said, "Lord, who is the Son of God, so I can believe in him?"
And Jesus said to him, "`You have both seen him, and you are talking to him right now.´"
And the formerly blind man said, "Lord, I believe." And he worshipped Jesus.
And Jesus said, "`I have come into this world for judgment, so that those who do not see can see, and those who see may be made blind.´"
Some of the Pharisees who were with him heard him say this and they asked, "Are we blind too?"
Jesus answered them and said, "`If you were blind, you would have no sin. But your sin remains because you say you can see.´"
And Jesus said, "`Truly, truly I say to you; whoever does not enter the sheep pen through the door, but climbs in some other way, is a thief and a robber.´
`But whoever enters through the door is the shepherd of the sheep.´
`The gatekeeper opens the gates to the shepherd, and the sheep hear the shepherd's voice, and he calls his own sheep by name and leads them out.´
`When the shepherd leads his own sheep out, they follow him because they know his voice.´
`The sheep do not know the stranger's voice, and they will not follow him, but they will flee from him.´"
When Jesus told them this parable, they did not understand what he was saying.
Then Jesus spoke to them again and said, "`Truly, truly I say to you; I am the doorway to the sheep pen.´
`Everyone who came before me were thieves and robbers, but the sheep did not listen to them.´
`I am the door. If anyone enters through me, they will be saved, and they will come in and go out and find pasture.´
`Thieves come only to steal, kill, and destroy. I have come so that they might have life, and to have it more abundantly.´
`I am the good shepherd, and the good shepherd gives his life for his sheep.´

`But a hired hand is not the good shepherd, and they are not his own sheep. When the hired hand sees the wolf coming, he leaves the sheep and flees. Then the wolf catches them and scatters the sheep.´
`The hired hand flees because he is a hired hand, and he does not care for the sheep.´
`I am the good shepherd, and I know my sheep and my sheep know me.´
`Just as the father knows me, I know the father and I lay down my life for my sheep.´
`I have other sheep who are not part of this flock. I must also bring them in, and they will listen to my voice, and there will be one flock and one shepherd.´
`That's why my father loves me, because I lay down my life for my flock only to pick it up again.´
`No one takes my life from me, but I lay it down voluntarily. I have the power to lay it down and I have the power to pick it back up again. For I have received this commandment from my father.´
Once again, there was a division among the Jews after they heard these things.
Many of them said, "Jesus has a demon and he is insane, why would anyone listen to him?"
Others said, "These are not the words of someone who is demon possessed. Can a demon open the eyes of the blind?"
This happened in Jerusalem at the Feast of Dedication in the winter.
One day Jesus walked into the temple in Solomon's entrance hall.
Then all the Jews came and swarmed around him and said, "How long will you continue to make us doubt? If you are the Christ, tell us plainly."
Jesus answered them and said, "`I told you before and you did not believe me, the works that I do in my father's name testify about me.´
`But you do not believe me because it is as I told you before, you are not my sheep.´
`My sheep hear my voice and I know them, and they follow me.´
`I give them eternal life, and they will never perish nor can anyone pluck them out of my hand.´
`My father who gave them to me is greater than all. Therefore, no one can pluck them out of my father's hand.´
`I and my father are one.´"
Then the Jews picked up stones to stone Jesus again.
But Jesus spoke out and said, "`I have shown you many good works from my father, which of those works makes you want to stone me?´"
The Jews answered Jesus and said, "We do not want to stone you for your good works but for your blasphemy. Because you are just a man and you make yourself out to be God."
So Jesus answered them and said, "`Is it not written in your laws, 'I have said, you are gods, and you are all children of the Most High God.?´ (Psalms 82:6)'
`If he called them gods to whom the word of God came, and the scripture cannot be broken.´
`Then how can you say that the one whom the father has sanctified and sent into the world commits blasphemy, because I said, 'I am the Son of God'?´
`If I am not doing the works of my father, then do not believe me.´
`But if I am doing the works of my father, even though you do not believe me, believe the works. Then you will know and believe, that the father is in me and I am in the father.´
After that, they tried to arrest Jesus again, but he escaped.
Then Jesus crossed the Jordan River again and went to the place where John had first baptized, and he lived there.
Many people turned to Jesus and said, "John did no miracles at all, but everything that he has said about this man is true."
And many people there believed in Jesus.
A man named Lazarus was sick. He lived in the town of Bethany where Mary and her sister Martha lived.
It was Mary's brother Lazarus who was sick, she was the one who had anointed Jesus with perfume and wiped his feet with her hair.
So Lazarus' sisters sent a message to Jesus that said, "Lord, someone you love is sick."
When Jesus heard this, he said, "`This sickness will not cause death, it is meant for the glory of God, in order for the Son of God to be glorified by this.´"
Now Jesus loved Martha, her sister, and Lazarus.
That's why, when Jesus heard that Lazarus was sick, he stayed where he was for two more days.
Then Jesus said to his disciples, "`Let us go back to Judea.´"
But his disciples replied to him and said, "Teacher, the Jews there tried to stone you, are you sure you want to go back there?"
Jesus answered them and said, "`Are there not twelve hours in a day? If a man walks during the day, he does not stumble because he sees by the light of this world.´
`But if he walks at night, he stumbles because there is no light in him.´"
After Jesus said these things to them, he said, "`Our friend Lazarus is asleep, but I am going to wake him up.´"
Then his disciples said, "Lord, if he is asleep, he is doing well."
The disciples thought that Jesus was saying that Lazarus was just sleeping, however he was actually talking about Lazarus being dead.
Then Jesus spoke to them plainly and said, "`Lazarus is dead.´
`For your sake I am glad that I was not there, because my intentions are for you to believe. So let us go to him.´"
Thomas who is also called Didymus spoke to his fellow disciples and said, "We must go too, so we can die with Jesus."
When Jesus arrived, he discovered that Lazarus had been lying in the grave for four days.
Bethany was near Jerusalem, which was only about two miles away.
Many of the Jews had come to comfort Martha and Mary about their brother.
As soon as Martha heard that Jesus was coming, she went and met him, but Mary stayed in the house.
Then Martha spoke to Jesus and said, "Lord, if only you had been here, my brother would not have died.
But even now I know that whatever you ask from God, he will give it you."
Then Jesus answered Martha and said, "`Your brother will rise again.´"
Martha responded to him and said, "I know he will rise again on the resurrection at the last day."
But Jesus said to Martha, "`I am the resurrection and the life, whoever believes in me will live, even if they were dead.´
`Whoever lives and believes in me will never die. Do you believe this?´"
Martha answered Jesus and said, "Yes Lord, I believe that you are the Christ, the Son of God who has come into the world."
After Martha said this, she left and secretly went to her sister Mary and said, "The teacher has come, and he is asking for you."
As soon as Mary heard this, she quickly got up and went to Jesus.
Jesus had not yet entered the town, but he waited at the place where Martha had met him.
When the Jews who were comforting Mary in the house saw how quickly she had gotten up and left, they followed her and said, "She must be going to mourn and weep at the grave."
When Mary arrived and saw Jesus, she fell down at his feet and said, "Teacher, if only you had been here, my brother would not have died."
When Jesus saw Mary and the Jews with her weeping, his spirit groaned and it was troubled.
And Jesus asked, "`Where have you laid him?´" They answered him and said, "Lord, come and see."
And Jesus wept.
Then the Jews said, "See how Jesus loved him!"
And some of them said, "Could this man who opened the eyes of the blind have prevented Lazarus from dying?"
So once again, Jesus groaned to himself as he walked to the grave, which was a cave with a stone laid across its entrance
Then Jesus said, "`Remove the stone.´" But Martha, the sister of the dead man, spoke to him and said, "Teacher, he must stink by now because he has been dead for four days."
Jesus looked at her and said, "`Did I not tell you, that you will see the glory of God if you believe?´"
So they removed the stone from the dead man's grave, and Jesus looked up to heaven and said, "`Father, I am thankful that you have heard me.´
`I knew that you always hear me, but I only said this for the people standing here, so that they will believe that you sent me.´"
After Jesus said this, he cried out with a loud voice and said, "`Lazarus, come out!´"
The dead man came out bound hand and foot in grave clothes, and his face was covered with a scarf. Then Jesus said to them, "`Unwrap him and let him go.´"
Many of the Jews who had come with Mary saw everything that Jesus had done, and they believed in him.
But some of them went to the Pharisees and told them what Jesus had done.
Then the chief priests and Pharisees convened the council and said, "What can we do? This man is performing many miracles.
If we ignore him, everyone will believe in him, and the Romans will come and take away both our place and our nation."
But that year's high priest a man named Caiaphas spoke to them and said, "You know nothing at all!
Do you not realize that it will be better for us for one man to die for the people, so that the whole nation does not perish?"
This thought did not come from Caiaphas himself, but since he was the high priest that year, he was prophesying from God that Jesus would die for their nation.
And not just for the nation, but also to unite God's scattered children and gather them together in one place.
Then from that day forward, they met together to scheme and plot the death of Jesus.
So Jesus no longer walked openly among the Jews, but he went to a city named Ephraim near the wilderness, where he stayed with his disciples.
The time for the Jewish Passover was near, and many people left the country and went to Jerusalem to purify themselves before the Passover.
The people looked for Jesus as they stood in the temple and they kept asking each other, "What do you think? Will he come to the feast or not?"
Both the chief priests and Pharisees had given orders that anyone who knew where Jesus was must report it, so they could arrest him.
Then six days before the Passover, Jesus went to Bethany where he raised Lazarus from the dead.
They prepared a supper for Jesus, where Martha served but Lazarus was seated at the table with him
Then Mary took a pound of very costly spikenard perfume and anointed Jesus' feet, then wiped it off with her hair. The house was filled with the perfume's scent.
Then one of Jesus' disciples Judas Iscariot the son of Simon, who would later betray him spoke.
And Judas said, "Why was this perfume not sold for 300 denarii so the money could be given to the poor?
Judas did not say this because he concerned about the poor, but because he was a thief, and he carried the money bag where the money was kept.
Then Jesus said, "`Leave her alone, she has kept this perfume to prepare for the day of my burial.´
`For the poor will always be with you, but you will not always have me.´"
Many Jewish people learned that Jesus was there, and they came not only to see him, but they also wanted to see Lazarus who had been raised from the dead.
But the chief priests decided that they would also put Lazarus to death.
Because many of the Jews were leaving the chief priests and they were believing in Jesus.
The next day many people came to the feast after they heard that Jesus was coming to Jerusalem.
They took palm tree branches and left to meet Jesus and they shouted, "Hosanna, blessed is the king of Israel who comes in the name of the Lord."
Because Jesus had found a young donkey that he sat on as he rode into Jerusalem.
For it is written, "Fear not daughter of Zion, behold your king comes riding on a donkey colt, the foal of a donkey. (Zechariah 9:9)"
At first, Jesus' disciples did not understand these things, but after Jesus was glorified, they remembered that these things were written about him, and that the people had done these things to him.
Then many people who were with Jesus when he raised Lazarus from the dead and called him from his grave, testified about him.
That's why so many people went meet Jesus, because they had also heard that he had performed this miracle.
Then the Pharisees said to each other, "Do you see how this is going to come to nothing? Behold, the whole world is chasing after Jesus."
There were some Greeks among those who came up to worship at the feast.
Some of the Greeks came to see Philip who was from Bethsaida in Galilee, and they spoke to him and said, "Sir, we would like to see Jesus."
Philip went and told Andrew, then both Andrew and Philip went to tell Jesus.
Jesus answered them and said, "`The hour has come for the Son of Man to be glorified.´
`Truly, truly I say to you; unless a kernel of wheat falls to the ground and dies, it is just a seed. But if it dies, it will produce much fruit.´
`Whoever loves his life will lose it, and whoever hates his life in this world will keep it for eternal life.´
`If a man serves me let him follow me, and wherever I am my servant will also be there, and if a man serves me, my father will honor him.´
`Now my soul is troubled so what should I say, 'Father, save me from this hour'? No, for this is the very reason that I have now come.´
`Father, glorify your name!´" Then they heard a voice from heaven that said, "I have both glorified it, and I will glorify it again."
So when the people who stood nearby heard this voice, they said that it thundered, others said that an angel had spoken to them.
Then Jesus spoke to them about the voice and said, "`This voice did not come because of me, but it came for your sake.´
`Now the judgment of this world has come, and the prince of this world will be thrown out.´
`And if I am lifted up from the earth, all men will be drawn to me.´"
When Jesus said this he was talking about what kind of death he would die.
The people questioned Jesus and asked, "We have heard from the law that Christ lives forever. Why are you saying, the Son of Man must be lifted up? Who is this Son of Man?"

Then Jesus said to them, "`The light will be with you for just a little while longer. Walk while you have the light, otherwise darkness will come upon you, because whoever walks in the darkness does not know where he is going.´
`While you have light, believe in the light, so that you may be the children of light.´" After Jesus said these things, he left and hid from the people.
Because even though he had done so many miracles before them, they still did not believe in him.
This was to satisfy what Isaiah the prophet had spoken of when he said, 'Who believed our report, and to whom has the Lord's powerful arm been revealed?' (Isaiah 53:1)
Therefore they could not believe, because Isaiah had said again.

"Your words will harden their hearts, and they will not be able to see, hear, or understand what I want them to see, hear, and understand. If they could, they would understand with their hearts, then they would turn to me, and be healed."
Isaiah said these things because he had seen the glory of Jesus, and he spoke about him.
Nevertheless, many of the chief rulers also believed in Jesus, but they did not confess their belief in Jesus because of the Pharisees. They were afraid they would be put out of the synagogue.
Because they loved the praise of men more than the praise of God.
So Jesus cried out and said, "`Whoever believes in me, does not just believe in me, but they also believe in the one who sent me.´
`Whoever sees me also sees the one who sent me.´
`I have come as a light into the world, so that whoever believes in me will not remain in darkness.´
`If anyone hears my words and does not believe, I do not judge them, because I have not come to judge the world but I have come to save the world.´
`Whoever rejects me and does not receive my words, has one who will judge him on the last day by the words that I have spoken.´
`For I have not spoken about myself, but I have spoken about my father who sent me. My father gave me a commandment about what I should say and how I should say it.´
`And I know that his commandment is everlasting life! Therefore, I say exactly what the father told me to say, exactly the way he told me to say it.´"
It was now just before the Passover Feast, and Jesus knew the hour had come for him to leave this world and return to the father. And to the very end he loved his own people who were in the world.
As the last supper ended, the devil had now put the idea to betray Jesus into the heart of Simon's son Judas Iscariot.
Jesus knew that the father had placed all things in his hands, and that he had come from God and he would return to God.
Jesus got up from the supper table, then he laid his garments aside and wrapped himself in a towel.
After that Jesus poured water into a sink, and began to wash the disciples' feet, then he dried them with a towel.
When he got to Simon Peter, Peter objected and said, "Lord, are you going to wash my feet?"
Jesus answered him and said, "`You do not understand what I am doing now, but you will understand later.´"
Peter replied to him and said, "You will never wash my feet." But Jesus answered him and said, "`If I do not wash your feet now, you will have no part with me.´"
Simon Peter responded to Jesus and said, "Lord, do not just wash my feet, but wash my head and hands too."
Jesus answered him and said, "`Whoever has already been washed does not need to wash anything except his feet to be completely clean, and you are already clean but not all of you are clean.´"
Jesus knew who would betray him, so he said, "`Not all of you are clean.´"
So after Jesus washed their feet, he put his garments back on and sat down again and said, "`Do you know what I have done for you?´
`You call me teacher and Lord, and you speak truthfully because I am.´
`If I am your Lord and teacher and I have washed your feet, then you should also wash one another's feet.´
`For what I have done for you is an example of what you should do for others.´
`Truly, truly I say to you; the servant is not greater than his Lord, nor is the one who was sent greater than the one who sent him.´
`If you know these things and do them, you will be happy.´

`I am not speaking about all of you, for I know who I have chosen. But the scripture must be fulfilled where it is written, `'The one who ate bread with me, has lifted up his heel against me.'´ (Psalm 41:9)
`I am telling you this now beforehand, so that when it happens you will believe that I am the one God sent.´
`Truly, truly I say to you; whoever receives those I send also receives me. And whoever receives me receives the one who sent me.´"
After Jesus said this, his spirit was troubled and he testified to them and said, "`Truly, truly I say to you; one of you will betray me.´"
Then the disciples looked at each other, they were worried that they might be the one Jesus was talking about.
Now one of Jesus' disciples whom he loved was leaning against and embracing Jesus.
So Simon Peter signaled to him, to ask Jesus who he was talking about.
The one embracing Jesus asked him, "Teacher, who is the betrayer?"
Jesus answered him and said, "`He is the one I will hand this bread to after I dip it.´" Then he gave the bread to Judas Iscariot, the son of Simon.
After the bread was dipped Satan entered Judas Iscariot. Then Jesus said to him, "`What you are about to do, do it quickly.´"
But no one at the table knew why Jesus said this to Judas.

Some of them thought Jesus had said this to Judas because he carried the money bag. They thought he was telling Judas to buy what was needed for the feast, or that he should give something to the poor.
After Judas received the dipped bread, he immediately left and went out into the night.
When Judas left, Jesus said, "`Now the Son of Man is glorified, and God is glorified in him.´
`If God is glorified in the son, then God will also glorify the son in himself, and he will glorify him right away.´
`So now I tell you little children, I will only be with you for a little while longer. You will look for me, but as I told the Jews, where I am go going, you cannot come.´
`So I give to you a new commandment, 'You must love one another. And as I have loved you, you must also love one another.'´
`Everyone will know that you are my disciples, if you love one another.´
Then Simon Peter asked Jesus, "Teacher, where are you going?" Jesus answered him and said, "`Where I go, you cannot follow me now, but you will follow me afterwards.´"
Then Peter asked him, "Teacher, why can I not follow you now? I will lay down my life for you."
Jesus answered him and said, "`Will you lay down your life for me Peter? Truly, truly I say to you; the cock will not crow until you have denied me three times.´"
And Jesus said, "`Do not let your hearts be troubled, if you believe in God then believe in me as well.´
`In my father's house there are many mansions, if this were not true, I would have told you. But I must go to prepare a place for you.´
`And if I go and prepare a place for you, I will return then you will also be where I am.´
`You know where I am going and you know the way there.´"
Then Thomas asked Jesus, "Teacher, we do not know where you are going, so how can we know the way there?"
Jesus answered him and said, "`I am the way, the truth, and the life and no one may come unto the father except through me.´
`If you had known me, you would have also known my father, so from now on you will know the father because you have seen him.´"
Then Philip said to Jesus, "Teacher, show us the father and we will be satisfied."
Jesus answered him and said, "`Philip, have I been with you for this long and you still do not know me? For whoever has seen me has seen the father, so why do you say, 'Show us the father'?´

`Do you not believe that I am in the father, and the father is in me? When I spoke to you earlier, I was not speaking about myself, I was speaking about the father who lives within me, and he is the one who performs the miracles.´
`Believe me when I say that I am in the father and the father is in me or simply believe me for the sake of those very miracles.´
`Truly, truly I say to you; whoever believes in me, will also do these and even greater miracles than I do because I am going to my father.´
`And whatever you ask in my name, I will do, so that the father may be glorified in the son.´
`If you ask anything in my name, I will do it.´
`If you love me, you will keep my commandments.´
`And I will pray to the father, and he will give you another comforter, so that he may live with you forever.´
`But the world cannot receive the spirit of truth, because it does not see him, nor does it know him. But you do know him because he lives with you, and he will be in you.´
`And I will not leave you as an uncomforted mourner, and I will come to you.´
`But in a little while, the world will no longer see me, but you will see me. This is because I live so that you may also live.´
`On that day you will know that I am in my father, and you are in me, and I am in you.´
`Whoever has my commandments and keeps them, is the one who loves me, and the one who loves me will be loved by my father, and I will love him, and I will reveal myself to him.´"
Then Judas (Not Iscariot) asked Jesus, "Lord, how will you reveal yourself to us, but not to the world?"
Jesus answered him and said, "`Whoever keeps my words loves me and my father will love them, and we will come and make our home with them.´
`Whoever does not love me, will not keep my word. The words you have heard from me are not my words, but they are the words of the father who sent me.´
`I have spoken all these things to you while I am still with you.´
`But my father will send the comforter to you in my name. The Holy Spirit is the comforter who will teach you all things and remind you of everything I have told you.´
`Peace I leave with you; my peace I give to you. I do not give to you as the world gives. So do not let your heart be troubled and do not be afraid.´
`You have heard me say, 'I am going away, but I will come back to you.' So, if you love me, you will rejoice that I am going to the father because my father is greater than me.´
`I have told you about all of this before it happens, so that when it does happen, you will believe.´
`So from now on I will not talk with you very much, because the prince of this world who has nothing against me is coming.´
`But, so that the world will know that I love the father, and because the father has given me a commandment, I will do as he asks. So, get up, and let's leave this place.´"
And Jesus said, "`I am the true vine, and my father is the farmer.´
`My father takes away every branch in me that does not produce fruit, and he prunes every branch that produces fruit, so it will produce more fruit.´
`Now you are clean because of the word which I have spoken to you.´
`Live in me, and I will live in you. Just as a branch cannot bear fruit by itself, unless it lives in the vine, nor can you produce fruit, unless you live in me.´
`I am the vine and you are the branches, whoever lives in me, and I live in them will produce much fruit, because without me you can do nothing.´
`If someone does not live in me, they are thrown out like a withered branch, then they are collected and thrown into the fire and burned.´
`If you live in me, and my words live in you, whatever you ask will be done for you.´
`This is how my father is glorified, so that you may produce much fruit as my disciples.´
`As the father has loved me, so have I loved you. Continue in my love.´
`If you keep my commandments, you will live in my love, even as I have kept my father's commandments, and I live in his love.´
`I have told you these things, so that my joy might remain in you and your joy will be complete.´
`This is my commandment, 'Love one another as I have loved you.'´
`No man has a greater love than this, that he will lay down his life for his friends.´
`You are my friends if you do what I command you.´

`From now on I will not call you servants, because the servant does not understand what his lord is doing, but I have called you my friends, because I have told you everything that I have heard from my father.´
`You have not chosen me, but I have chosen and ordained you, so that you will go and produce fruit and your fruit will remain, so that whatever you ask of the father in my name, he will give you.´
`This is my commandment to you, 'Love one another.'´
`If the world hates you, you know that it hated me before it hated you.´
`If you were of the world, the world would love you as one of its own, but because you are not of the world and I have chosen you from the world, is why the world hates you.´
`Remember what I have told you, 'The servant is not greater than his Lord.' If they have persecuted me, they will also persecute you, if they have kept my teachings, they will also keep yours.´
`But they will do all of these things to you for my name's sake, because they do not know the one who sent me.´
`If I had not come and spoken to them, they would not have been guilty of sin, but now they have nothing to hide their sin.´
`Whoever hates me also hates my father.´
`If I had not done all the miracles for them that no one else could do, they would not be guilty of sin, but now they have seen and hated both me and my father.´
`This is to fulfill the word that is written in their law, 'They hated me without cause.'´ (Psalm 35:19 and Psalm 69:4)
`But when I send the comforter to you that comes from the father, then the spirit of truth that comes from the father will testify about me.´
`And you will also testify, because you have been with me from the beginning.´"
And Jesus said, "`I have told you these things, so that you will not be offended.´
`They will put you out of the synagogues, and the time is coming when whoever kills you will think they are serving God.´
`They will do these things to you, because they do not know me or the father.´
`But I have told you these things, so that you will remember them when the time comes. And I did not tell you about these things in the beginning, because I was with you.´
`But now I am going back to the one who sent me, and no one even asks me, 'Where are you going?'´
`But because I have said these things, your hearts are filled with grief and sorrow.´
`Nevertheless I tell you the truth, it is to your advantage that I go away because if I do not go away, the comforter will not come to you, but I will send him to you when I leave.´
`When the comforter comes, he will blame the world for its sin, righteousness, and judgment.´
`Of its sin, because they do not believe in me.´
`Of its righteousness, because I am going to my father, and you will no longer see me.´
`Of its judgment, because the prince of this world has been judged.´
`I still have many things to say to you, but you cannot stand to hear them right now.´
`However when the spirit of truth comes, he will guide you into all truth. Because he will not speak of himself, but he will speak of what he hears, and he will show you things to come.´
`He will glorify me, because he will receive what is mine and he will show it to you.´
`Everything that my father has is mine, so I said that he will take from what is mine and show it to you.´
`In a little while you will no longer see me, then a little while later you will see me again, because I am going to the father.´"

Then some of his disciples discussed this among themselves and wondered what he was talking about when he said, "`In a little while you will no longer see me, then a little while later you will see me again, because I am going to the father.´"
They kept asking each other, "Why does he keep saying, `'In a little while?'´ We do not understand what he is saying."
Jesus knew they were confused and he said, "`Are you confused about what I mean when I say, 'In a little while you will no longer see me, then a little while later you will see me again'?´
`Truly, truly I say to you; that you will weep and mourn but the world will rejoice. You will be sorrowful, but your sorrow will be turned to joy.´

`When a woman is in labor, she feels pain and sorrow, because her time to give birth has come. But as soon as she gives birth to her child, she no longer remembers the pain and anguish, because she is overjoyed that a child has been born into the world.´
`That's why you will have sorrow, but I will see you again, and your hearts will rejoice and no one will take your joy from you.´
`In those days you will ask me nothing. Truly, truly I say to you; whatever you ask of the father in my name, he will give you.´
`Until now, you have asked for nothing in my name. Ask and you will receive, so that your joy may be full.´
`I have told you about these things in proverbs, but the time is coming when I will no longer speak to you in proverbs, but I will show you the plain truth from the father.´
`In those days you will ask in my name. But I am not saying that I will pray to the father for you.´
`For the father himself loves you, because you have loved me and you have believed that I came from God.´
`I came into the world from the father. But I must leave the world and return to the father.´"
Then Jesus' disciples spoke to him and said, "Lo and behold, now you are speaking plainly without proverbs.
Now we are sure that you know everything, and you do not need anyone to question you. This is why we believe that you came from God."
Jesus answered them and said, "`Do you believe me now?´
`Behold, the hour has now come when each one of you will be scattered to your own place, and you will leave me alone. But I am not alone because the father is with me.´
`I have told you these things, so that in me you will have peace. In the world you will have tribulation, but you can cheer up because I have overcome the world.´"
After Jesus said these things he looked up to heaven and said, "`Father, the hour has come to glorify your son, so that your son may also glorify you.´
`For you have given him power over all flesh, so that he could give eternal life to all of those you have given him.´
`And this is eternal life, so that they may know you and Jesus Christ whom you have sent, and that you are the only true God.´
`I have glorified you on earth, I have finished the work you have given me to do.´
`And now O father, I ask you to glorify me with yourself with the glory which I had with you before the world was created.´
`I have revealed your name to those you have given me from the world. They were yours and you gave them to me, and they have kept your word.´
`Now they know that everything you have given me is from you.´
`For I have given them the words which you gave me, and they have received them. And now they surely know that I came from you, and they believe that you sent me.´
`I pray for them, and I do not pray for the world, but I pray for those you have given me because they are yours.´
`All that I have is yours, and all that you have is mine, and I am glorified in them.´

`And now I am no longer in the world, but they are in the world, and I am coming to you. Holy father, protect those you have given me through your own name, so that they may be one just as we are one.´

`While I was with them in the world, I protected them in your name. I have protected those you have given me, and none have been lost, except the son of perdition in order to fulfill the scripture.´ (John 6:39)
`And now I am coming to you, but I am saying these things while I am in the world, so that they will have my joy fulfilled within themselves.´
`I have given them your word, and the world has hated them because they are not of the world, just as I am not of the world.´
`I do not pray that you take them out of the world, but I ask that you protect them from the evil one.´
`For they are not of the world, just as I am not of the world.´
`Sanctify them through your truth because your word is truth.´
`Just as you sent me into the world, I have also sent them into the world.´
`For their sake I sanctify myself, so that they may also be sanctified through the truth.´
`I do not pray for them alone, but also for those who will believe in me through their word.´
`So that they may all be one, just as you father are in me and I am in you. So that they may also be one in us, and the world can believe that you sent me.´
`And the glory you have given me I have given them, so that they may be one, just as we are one.´
`I am in them and you are in me, so that they may be made perfect in one, and the world will know that you have sent me, and you have loved them, just as you have loved me.´
`Father, it is also my will that those you have given me, be with me wherever I am. So that they may see my glory, which you have given me because you loved me before the foundation of the world.´
`O righteous father, the world has not known you, but I have known you, and they know that you have sent me.´
`And I have declared your name to them, and I will continue to declare it, so that the love you have shown me may also be in them, and I will be in them.´"
After Jesus said all this, he left with his disciples and crossed the Brook of Cedron, where they entered a garden.
Jesus' betrayer Judas also knew the place, because Jesus had often visited there with his disciples.
Then Judas brought a band of soldiers and officers from the chief priests and Pharisees there with lanterns, torches, and weapons.
Jesus knew everything that would happen to him, so he went to meet them and asked, "`Who are you looking for?´"
They answered him and said, "Jesus of Nazareth." Jesus replied to them and said, "`I am him.´" And his betrayer Judas also stood there with them.
As soon as Jesus said, "`I am him,´" they backed up and fell to the ground.
Then Jesus asked them again, "`Who are you looking for?´" And they said, "Jesus of Nazareth."
Jesus answered them and said, "`I have already told you that I am him, so if you are looking for me, let the others go.´"
Jesus said this to satisfy the statement he had made earlier when he said, "`I have protected those you have given me, and none of them have been lost.´"(John 6:39, 17:12)
Simon Peter drew his sword and used it to cut off the high priest servant's right ear. The servant's name was Malchus.
And Jesus said to Peter, "`Sheath your sword, should I not drink from the cup that my father has given me?´"
Then the soldiers, the captain, and the Jewish officers cuffed and arrested Jesus
First they led Jesus to Annas the father-in-law of Caiaphas, because Caiaphas was the high priest that year.
Caiaphas was the one who had advised the Jews that it would be better for them if one man were to die for the people.
Simon Peter and another disciple followed Jesus. The high priest knew this other disciple, so that disciple went into the high priest's palace with Jesus.
But Peter stood outside beside the door. Then the disciple who the high priest knew went and spoke to the girl attending the door, and brought Peter inside.
Then the girl attending the door said to Peter, "Are you not also one of this man's disciples?" Peter said, "I am not!"
The servants and officers standing there made a fire to warm themselves because it was cold, and they stood there with Peter as he also warmed himself.
Then the high priest asked Jesus about his disciples and his doctrine.
Jesus answered him and said, "`I spoke openly to the world, I taught in the synagogue and temple where the Jews always go, and I have said nothing in secret.´
`Why are you asking me? Go and ask those who heard me because they know what I said.´"
After Jesus spoke, one of the officers standing nearby slapped him with the palm of his hand and said, "Is this how you answer the high priest?"
Jesus answered him and said, "`If I said something evil testify about the evil, but if spoke the truth why did you hit me?´"
Then Annas sent Jesus, still cuffed to Caiaphas the high priest.
Simon Peter stood nearby warming himself, and someone asked him, "Are you not also one of Jesus' disciples?" Peter denied it and said, "I am not!"
One of the high priest's servants who was related to the one whose ear Peter had cut off said, "Did I not see you in the garden with Jesus?"
Peter denied it again and immediately the cock crowed.

Then they led Jesus from Caiaphas to the judgment hall, and it was early so they did not go into the judgment hall. If they had gone in they would be defiled, and they would not have been able to eat the Passover.
Then Pilate went to them and said, "What are you accusing this man of?"
They answered Pilate and said, "If he were not a criminal, we would not have brought him to you."
Then Pilate spoke to them and said, "Take him, and judge him by your own laws." So, the Jews said to Pilate, "It is illegal for us to put a man to death."
When they said this it fulfilled what Jesus had said when he spoke about the kind of death he would die.
Then Pilate went back in the judgment hall and summoned Jesus and asked him, "Are you the king of the Jews?"
Jesus answered him and said, "`Did you say this yourself or have others told you about me?´"
Pilate answered Jesus and said, "Am I a Jew? Your own nation and the chief priests have brought you to me, what have you done?"

Jesus answered Pilate and said, "`My kingdom is not of this world, if my kingdom were of this world, then my servants would fight to keep the Jews from arresting me. But my kingdom is not from here.´"

So Pilate said to Jesus, "So, are you a king?" Jesus answered him and said, "`You say that I am a king. But the reason I was born and the reason I have come into the world, is to testify about the truth. Everyone who is from the truth hears my voice.´"
Then Pilate said to Jesus, "What is truth!" After Pilate said this, he went back to the Jews and said to them, "I find no fault in him at all.
But you have a custom that I release one prisoner to you at the Passover, so do you want me to release the king of the Jews to you?"
Then the crowd cried out and said, "Do not release this man, but release Barabbas!" Now Barabbas was a robber.
Then Pilate had Jesus flogged.
The soldiers wove a crown of thorns and put it on Jesus' head, then they put him in a purple robe.
They all said, "Hail, king of the Jews!" And they beat him with their fists.
After that Pilate went back out and spoke to the Jews again and said, "Behold, I am bringing Jesus out to let you know that I have found no fault in him."
Then Jesus came out, wearing a crown of thorns and the purple robe and Pilate said to them, "Look at this man!"

When the chief priests and officers saw Jesus, they cried out and said, "Crucify him, crucify him!" Pilate replied to them and said, "You take him and crucify him, because I have found no fault in him."
The Jews answered him and said, "We have laws, and by our law he should die, because he has made himself the Son of God."
After Pilate heard what they were saying, he was even more afraid.
He went back into the judgment hall and asked Jesus, "Where are you from?" But Jesus would not answer him.
Then Pilate said to him, "Will you not speak to me? Do you not know that I have power to either crucify you or to release you?"
Jesus answered Pilate and said, "`You would have no power over me at all, if it had not been given to you from above. So, the one who has handed me over to you has committed a greater sin.´"
After that Pilate tried to release Jesus, but the Jews cried out and said, "If you let this man go, you are not Caesar's friend, whoever makes himself a king defies Caesar."
When Pilate heard them saying that, he brought Jesus out and sat in the judgment seat in a place called the Pavement, which in Hebrew is Gabbatha.
It was about the sixth hour on the day of preparation for the Passover, and Pilate said to the Jews, "Behold your king!"
But they cried out, "Away with him, take him away and crucify him!" Pilate responded to them and said, "Should I crucify your king?" The chief priests answered and said, "We have no king but Caesar."
Then Pilate handed Jesus over to them to be crucified, and they led Jesus away.
Jesus left carrying his cross and went to a place called The Place of the Skull, which in Hebrew is called Golgotha.
This was where they crucified Jesus in between two others, one on each side of him.
Pilate wrote a sign on a piece of wood that said, "JESUS OF NAZARETH, THE KING OF THE JEWS," and hung it on the cross over his head.
This sign was read by many Jews, because the place where Jesus was crucified was near the city, and it was written in Hebrew, Greek, and Latin.
Then the chief priests of the Jews said to Pilate, "Do not write, 'The king of the Jews,' but write, 'He said he was the king of the Jews.'"
But Pilate answered, "I have written what I have written."
After the soldiers crucified Jesus, they took his garments and divided them into four parts, and each soldier got one part. And they also had his seamless coat which was woven from top to bottom.

So they said among themselves, "Do not tear it, but let us cast lots to see who gets it. The soldiers did these things to fulfill the scripture in which it is written, "They divide my garments among them and cast lots for my clothes."(Psalms 22:18)
Jesus' mother and her sister, as well as Cleophas' wife Mary, and Mary Magdalene stood near the cross.
So when Jesus saw his mother and the disciple whom he loved standing nearby, he said to his mother, "`Woman, see your son!´"
Then Jesus said to his disciple, "`Behold your mother!´" After that hour, Jesus' disciple took his mother Mary into his own home.
After this, Jesus knew that everything had now been accomplished, and to fulfill the scripture, Jesus said, "`I am thirsty.´"(Psalm 69:21)
There was a bowl full of vinegar sitting there, so they soaked a sponge with vinegar and put it on a hyssop stalk and lifted it up to his mouth.
After Jesus received the vinegar, he said, "`It is finished!´" Then he bowed his head and gave up the ghost.

It was the day of Preparation, the next day was the High Sabbath, and the Jews did not want the bodies hanging on the cross on the Sabbath day. So, they implored Pilate to break their legs and have the bodies taken away.
Then the soldiers came and broke the legs of the two men who were crucified with Jesus.
But when they came to Jesus, they saw that he was already dead, so they did not break his legs.
But one of the soldiers had a spear and he pierced Jesus in his side, and immediately blood and water came gushing out.
The one who saw it testified to this for the record and his record is true. And he knows that he is telling the truth, so that you will believe.
For these things were done to fulfill the scripture where it is written, "Not one of his bones will be broken."(Psalms 34:20)
And another scripture that says, "They will look upon the one they have pierced."(Zechariah 12:10)

After this, Joseph of Arimathea who was secretly a disciple of Jesus because he feared the Jews, went and implored Pilate to let him take the body of Jesus for burial. Pilate gave him permission, so he went and took the body of Jesus.
And Nicodemus who had come earlier to visit Jesus at night, also came and brought a mixture of about seventy-five pounds of myrrh and aloes.
