Then they anointed Jesus' body with spices and wrapped it in linen clothing, which is how the Jews bury someone.
There was a new tomb where no one had ever been buried before, in a garden near where Jesus was crucified.
So they laid Jesus' body there because it was the Jewish preparation day, and the tomb was close by.
The first day of the week early one morning while it was still dark, Mary Magdalene went to the tomb and saw that the stone had been rolled away from the tomb entrance.
Then she ran to tell Simon Peter and the other disciple whom Jesus loved and she said, "They have taken Jesus out of the tomb, and we do not know where they have laid him."
So Peter and the other disciple left and went to the tomb.
They both ran to the tomb, but the other disciple outran Peter, and he was the first one to arrive.
The other disciple stooped down and looked in the tomb, and he saw the linen clothes lying there but he did not go in.
When Simon Peter arrived, he entered the tomb and saw the linen clothes lying there.
The cloth used to wrap around Jesus' head was not lying with his linen clothes, but it had been folded and placed in a spot all by itself.
Then the other disciple who was the first to arrive, also entered the tomb and he saw and believed.
For they still did not understand that the scripture said that Jesus must rise from the dead.
Then the disciples went back to their own home.
But Mary Magdalene remained outside the tomb weeping and as she wept, she stooped down and looked into the tomb.
Mary saw two angels dressed in white sitting where the body of Jesus had lain, one sat by the head and the other by the feet.
The angels asked Mary, "Woman, why are you weeping?" And Mary replied to them and said, "Because they have taken Jesus away, and I do not know where they have taken him."
After Mary said this, she turned around and saw Jesus standing there, but she did not know it was Jesus.

Jesus spoke to her and said, "`Woman, why are you weeping, and who you looking for?´" Mary Magdalene thought Jesus was the gardener and she said, "Sir, if you have carried him away, tell me where he is and I will go get him."
Then Jesus called her by name and said, "`Mary Magdalene.´" She turned around and said to him, "Rabboni!"(which means Teacher)

Jesus said to her, "`Do not touch me, because I have not yet ascended to my father, but I am going to my brothers to tell them that I am ascending to my father and your father, and to my God and your God.´"
After this, Mary Magdalene went and told the disciples that she had seen Jesus, and she told them what Jesus had said.

That evening, which was the first day of the week, the disciples were huddled together behind locked doors because they were afraid of the Jews. Jesus came and stood in their midst and he said to them, "`Peace be with you.´"
After Jesus said this, he showed them his hands and his side. The disciples were very happy when they saw Jesus.
Then Jesus spoke to them again and said, "`Peace be with you, just as my father has sent me, I am also sending you.´"
After Jesus said this, he breathed on them and said, "`Receive the Holy Spirit.´"
`Those whose sins of any kind that you forgive will be forgiven, and those whose sins of any kind you do not forgive, then forgiveness will be withheld from them.´"
But Thomas also known as Didymus, one of the twelve disciples was not with them when Jesus came.

The other disciples told Thomas what they had seen and they said, "We have seen the Lord!" But Thomas did not believe them and he said, "Unless I see the nail holes in his hands and put my finger in them, and I put my hand in the wound in his side, I will not believe.
Eight days later Jesus' disciples along with Thomas were sitting inside behind locked doors, when Jesus came again and stood in their midst and said, "`Peace be with you.´"
Then Jesus said to Thomas, "`Look here, and put your finger in my hands and your hand in the wound in my side. Stop doubting and believe.´"
And Thomas answered Jesus and said, "My Lord and my God."
Jesus said to him, "`Thomas, you believe in me because you have seen me, but blessed are those who have not seen and yet they still believe.´"
Jesus truly did many other amazing signs in the presence of his disciples, which are not written in this book.
But these are written down so that you can believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and that by believing in him you can have life in his name.
Later Jesus appeared to the disciples again by the sea of Tiberias, and this is how he revealed himself.
Simon Peter, Thomas also known as Didymus, Nathanael from Cana in Galilee, Zebedee's sons, and two other disciples were all together there.
And Simon Peter said to them, "I am going fishing." They all said, "We will go with you." So, they immediately climbed into a boat and left, but they caught nothing that night.
That morning, Jesus stood along the shoreline, but the disciples did not realize it was him.
Then Jesus said to them, "`Children, do you have any fish?´" They answered him and said, "`No.´"
And Jesus said to them, "`Throw the net out on the right side of the boat, and you will find some.´" So, they threw the net, and they could not haul it in because they had caught so many fish.
So the disciple whom Jesus loved said to Peter, "It is the Lord!" When Simon Peter heard that it was the Lord, he put on the fisherman's coat he had removed and jumped into the sea.
The other disciples rowed the boat ashore dragging the net full of fish, because they were only about 200 cubits from land.
As soon as they got back to dry land, they saw some fish roasting over a fire and some bread.
Then Jesus said to them, "`Bring some of the fish you caught.´"
So Simon Peter went and pulled the net full of fish ashore. And they counted 153 large fish in all, but the net had not torn.
Jesus said to them, "`Come and dine with me,´" but none of the disciples would dare ask him, "Who are you?" Because they knew that it was Jesus.
Then Jesus came and gave them some bread and fish.
This was the third time since Jesus had risen from the dead, that he had revealed himself to his disciples.

When they finished eating, Jesus spoke to Simon Peter and said, "`Simon son of Jonas, do you love you me more than the others?´" And Peter answered him and said, "Yes Lord, you know I love you." And Jesus said, "`Feed my sheep.´"
Jesus spoke to Simon Peter a second time and said, "`Simon son of Jonas, do love you me?´" Peter answered him and said, "Yes Lord, you know I love you." Then Jesus said to him, "`Feed my sheep.´"

And Jesus spoke to Simon Peter a third time and said, "`Simon son of Jonas, do you love me?´" Peter was grieved when Jesus asked him a third time, "`Do you love me,´" so Peter responded and said, "Lord, you know everything and you know that I love you." So, Jesus said to him, "`Feed my sheep.´

`Truly, truly I say to you; when you were young, you dressed yourself and walked wherever you wanted to go. But when you are old, you will stretch out your hands and someone else will dress you and carry you where you do not want to go.´"
Jesus said this to signify what type of death Peter would die to glorify God. After Jesus said this, he said to Peter, "`Follow me!´"
Then Peter turned around and saw the disciple whom Jesus loved following them. He was also the one who leaned against Jesus at the last supper who had asked, "Lord, who will betray you?"
Peter saw the other disciple and he asked Jesus, "Lord, what do you want this man to do?"
Jesus answered him and said, "`If it is my will that he remains until I return, what is that to you? I want you to follow me!´"

Then a rumor spread among the brothers that this disciple would not die, but Jesus had not said that he would not die. But Jesus had actually said, "`If it is my will that he remains until I return, what is that to you?´"
This is the disciple who testified and wrote of these things, and we know that his testimony is true.
Jesus also did many other amazing things. And if all of these things were written down by everyone, I suppose that not even the world itself could contain all the books that would be written. Amen!
Greetings Theophilus, in my first written report I wrote about everything that Jesus began to do and teach.
Things that continued until the day that he was taken up to heaven, after he had given his instructions through the Holy Spirit to his chosen apostles.

He had also shown himself to his disciples after his passionate suffering with infallible proof that he was alive. They saw him alive for forty days after his crucifixion, as he spoke to them about the Kingdom of God.
While they were assembled together, Jesus spoke to the disciples and said, "`Do not leave Jerusalem, but wait for the gift promised by the father that you have heard me talk about.´
`For John truly baptized with water, but in a few days, you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit.´"
So when the disciples were together, they spoke to Jesus and asked, "Lord, will you now restore the kingdom of Israel?"
And Jesus said to them, "`It is not for you to know the times or the seasons that the father has put under his own power.´
`But you will receive power after the Holy Spirit has come upon you, and you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem, throughout Judea, Samaria, and to the ends of the earth.´"
After Jesus said these things, the disciples watched as Jesus ascended, and a cloud covered him so that they could no longer see him.
They gazed intently toward heaven as Jesus left, when suddenly two men dressed in white apparel appeared beside them.
The men in white said, "Men of Galilee, why are you standing here looking up into heaven? Jesus, who has been taken from you, will also return the same way you have seen him go up into heaven."
Then the disciples returned to Jerusalem from Mount Olive, which is about a Sabbath day's walk from Jerusalem.

When they arrived, they went to an upper room where the other disciples lived including Peter, James, John, Andrew, Philip, Thomas, Bartholomew, Matthew, James the son of Alphaeus, Simon the Zealot, and Judas brother of James.
They all continued to pray and plea as one, along with Mary the mother of Jesus, the other women, and Jesus' brothers.
In those days Peter stood among about 120 disciples.
As Peter stood there, he spoke to them and said, "Brothers, the scripture had to be fulfilled, in which the Holy Spirit spoke through King David about Judas, who guided the officers to arrest Jesus.
Because Judas was one of us and he was part of this ministry."
People knew that Judas had purchased a field with the money from his immoral reward. But Judas had fallen headfirst in this field, his stomach burst open and his bowels came gushing out.
This field became known to everyone in Jerusalem, where in their own language they called that field Aceldama. (The field of blood)
Then Peter said, "It is written in the book of Psalms, 'Let his home be desolate and uninhabited, and let someone else take his place' (Psalm 69:25 and Psalm 109:8)
So, we must choose another disciple from one of these men who have accompanied us for the entire time that Jesus moved among us.

Beginning with John's baptism, until the day that Jesus was taken from us and he ascended up into heaven. For one of those veteran disciples must be ordained as a witness along with us of his resurrection."
So they proposed two candidates, Joseph (aka. Barsabas or Justus) and Matthias.
Then they prayed and said, "Lord, you know the hearts of all men, show us which one of these two men you have chosen.
So that the one you have chosen may become a part of this ministry and an apostle. For Judas fell from his transgressions, and he must go to his own place."
Then they cast lots and Matthias was chosen, and he was added to the eleven apostles.
When the day of Pentecost arrived, all of the disciples were together in one place.
Suddenly the sound of a rushing mighty wind came from heaven and filled the whole house where they were sitting.
Then split tongues that looked like fire appeared to them and came to rest on each one of them.
They were all filled with the Holy Spirit, and began to speak in other tongues, as the Spirit gave them the words.
And devout Jews from every nation under heaven lived in Jerusalem.
When this noise was heard outside, a confused crowd gathered together, because they had each heard the disciples speaking in their own language.
And they were all amazed and astonished and they asked one another, "Do not all of these men who are speaking come from Galilea?
How can we hear them talking in our own native language?
For we are Parthians, Medes, Elamites, and people from Mesopotamia, Judea, Cappadocia, Pontus, and Asia.
Phrygia, Pamphylia, Egypt, and parts of Libya near Cyrene, visitors from Rome, Jews and Jewish converts.
Cretes and Arabians, we all hear them speaking about the wonderful works of God in our own tongues!"
They were all confused and amazed and they said one to another, "What does this mean?
Others mockingly said, "These men are drunk on new wine."
But Peter stood up with the eleven disciples and raised his voice and said, "Men of Judea and all of you who live in Jerusalem, know this and listen to my words.
For these men are not drunk like you think, because it is just the third hour of the day!
But this is what the prophet Joel predicted.
When Joel said, 'And God says, "Afterward, I will pour out my spirit on all flesh, and your sons and daughters will prophesy, your young men will see visions, and your old men will dream dreams.
I will also pour out my spirit on your maids and servants in those days, and they will prophesy
I will show wonders in the heavens above and on the earth below of blood, fire, and columns of smoke.
The sun will be darkened, and the moon will be turned blood red, before the great and terrible Day of the Lord has come.
And it will come to pass, that whoever calls on the name of the Lord will be saved."'"(Joel 2:28-32)

Then Peter continued speaking and said, "Men of Israel hear these words, Jesus of Nazareth was a man approved by God who came among you. And as you also know, Jesus showed you many miracles, signs, and wonders which were performed by God in your midst.
Jesus was delivered by God's determined counsel, and through his prior knowledge he knew that those of you who have wicked hands would take him, crucify him, and kill him
But God has raised Jesus up and released him from the pains of death, because it was impossible for death to hold him in its clutches.
For David spoke about Jesus when he said, 'I always put the Lord before me, because he is at my right hand and I will not be moved.
So my heart is glad, my glory rejoices, and my flesh also rests in hope.
Because you will not leave my soul in hell, nor will you let your Holy One see decay.
You will show me the path to life, you will fill me with joy in your presence, and there are eternal pleasures at your right hand.'"(Psalm 16:8-11)
And Peter continued speaking and said, "Brothers, let me speak freely to you and tell you that the patriarch David died and was buried, and his tomb is still with us to this very today.
But David was a prophet, and he knew that God had sworn an oath to him and promised that he would raise up Christ as one of his descendants to sit on his throne.
David saw this beforehand and spoke of the resurrection of Christ, and he said that Christ's soul would not be left in hell, nor would his flesh see decay.
God has raised up this Jesus to life, of which we all are witnesses.
Therefore Jesus was glorified by the right hand of God, and he has received the promised Holy Spirit from the father, and he has poured out what you now see and hear.
For David did not ascend into the heavens, but he himself said, 'The Lord said to my Lord, "Sit at my right hand.
Until I make your enemies your footstool."' (Psalm 110:1)
So let the whole House of Israel know for sure, that God made this Jesus that you have crucified, both Lord and Christ."
When the people heard this, their hearts were pained and they said to Peter and the rest of the apostles, "Brothers, what can we do?"
Then Peter spoke to them and said, "Every one of you must repent and be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins, and you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit.
For this promise is for you and your children, and everyone else far away from God, it is even for as many as our Lord God decides to call."
Peter testified with many other encouraging words and said, "Save yourselves from this perverse generation."
Then those who gladly received this message were baptized, and about 3,000 believing souls were added to the church that day.
They continued devoutly in the apostles' doctrine and fellowship, and in the breaking of bread and in prayers.
Fear came over every soul, and many signs and wonders were performed by the apostles.
All who believed were together as one and they had everything in common
They sold their possessions and goods and shared them with whoever was in need.
And they continued to meet daily as one in the temple, and they broke bread from house to house, sharing their meals with happiness and a sincere heart.
Praising God and having the favor of all the people, and every day the Lord added those who were saved to the church.
One day at about the ninth hour which was prayer hour, Peter and John went into the temple.
A man who was born lame was carried daily to the temple gate called Beautiful, where he was laid to ask for money from those who entered the temple.
When he saw Peter and John about to enter the temple he asked them for money.
Peter and John looked directly at him and said, "Look at us!"
And he turned his attention to them, expecting to receive something from them.
Then Peter said, "Silver and gold I do not have, but what I have I give to you, in the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth get up and walk."
Peter took the man's right hand and helped him stand up, and immediately his feet and ankle bones were strengthened.
Then he leaped up and began walking. Then he walked into the temple with them leaping and praising God.
Everybody there saw him walking and praising God.
And they knew that he had been begging for alms at the temple gate called Beautiful, and they were all shocked and amazed by what had happened to him.
As the lame man who had been healed clung to Peter and John, all the people were amazed, and they ran to them in the entrance called Solomon's hall.
When Peter saw this, he spoke to the people and said, "Men of Israel, why does this surprise you? Why are you staring so intently at us, as if we had made this man walk by our own power or holiness?
The God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob who is the God of our fathers, has glorified his son Jesus. You handed Jesus over and denied him before Pilate, who was determined to release him.
But you denied the holy and righteous one and asked for a murderer to be released to you instead.
You killed Jesus the creator of life, and we are witnesses of the one whom God has raised from the dead.
And faith in the name of Jesus has strengthened this man whom you see and know. Yes, it is faith in the name of Jesus that has given this man perfect healing in your presence.
And now brothers, I know that you killed Jesus through your ignorance, as did your rulers.
But the prophecies that God had foretold through the mouth of his prophets, that said Christ would suffer have now been fulfilled.
Therefore repent and be converted, so that your sins may be erased, when the times of refreshing come from the presence of the Lord.
And God will send Jesus Christ, who was previously preached to you.
But Jesus, whom heaven must receive until the time comes for the restitution of all things, has been announced by God through his holy prophets ever since the world began.
For Moses truly said to the fathers, 'Your Lord God will raise up a prophet like me from among your brothers, and you must listen to everything he says to you. (Deuteronomy 18:15)
And I will deal sternly with anyone who does not listen to what I tell the prophet to say in my name.' (Deuteronomy 18:19)
Yes, and many prophets from Samuel to those who followed after him, have also spoken and foretold these days.

You are the children of the prophets, and the covenant that God made with our fathers when he spoke to Abraham and said, 'Through your descendants all the families of the earth will be blessed.' (Genesis 12:3)
And you are the children of God who first raised up his son Jesus for you and sent him to bless you by turning every one of you away from your wickedness."
As Peter and John spoke to the people they were approached by the priests, the temple guard captain, and the Sadducees.
They were grieved that Peter and John were teaching the people and preaching about resurrection from the dead through Jesus.
So they arrested Peter and John and held them in custody until the next day because it was evening.
However many people who heard the word believed, and there were about 5,000 men listening.
The next day their rulers, elders, and scribes.
Annas the high priest, Caiaphas, John, Alexander, and many others who were relatives of the high priest all gathered together in Jerusalem.
And they had Peter and John brought before them and they asked them, "By what power or what name, have you done this?"
Then Peter was filled with the Holy Spirit and he said to them, "Rulers and elders of the people of Israel!
If we must be interrogated today to discover how we have done a good deed for this crippled man who was healed.

Then let it be known to all of you and the people of Israel! This miracle was done through the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, whom you crucified, and God raised from the dead. That is how this man was healed and why he stands before you today.
Jesus is the stone that was rejected by the builders, who has become the head cornerstone.
And salvation does not come through anyone else, because there is no other name under heaven given to men by which we can be saved."
The council was surprised when they saw the boldness of Peter and John, because they thought they were both ignorant and uneducated. Then they realized that they had both been with Jesus.
When they saw the healed man standing with them, there was nothing they could say.
But after the council ordered Peter and John removed from their presence, the council discussed it among themselves.
As the council talked it over, they said, "What can we do with these men? For they have indeed performed a notable miracle which we cannot deny, because it is obvious to everyone in Jerusalem.
But to keep it from spreading any further, we simply must threaten them and tell them that from now on, they must not speak the name of Jesus to anyone."
Then the council brought Peter and John back in and ordered them not to speak the name of Jesus nor teach in his name again.
But Peter and John answered the council and said, "Judge for yourselves, whether it is more righteous in the sight of God for us to listen to you or to God.
For we can only speak of the things which we have seen and heard."
So the council threatened them even more and then released them. The council tried but they could find no reason to punish them because all the people glorified God for the miracle that was done.
For the man who was healed by this miracle was over forty years old.
When Peter and John returned to their own people, they reported everything the chief priests and elders had said to them.
After their people heard this, they lifted up their voices to God as one voice and said, "Lord, you are our God who made the heavens, the earth, the sea, and everything in them.
You are our God who has spoken through the mouth of his servant David and said, 'Why do the heathen rage, and the people imagine vain things?
The kings of the earth and the world rulers conspire together against the Lord and his Christ.' (Psalms 2:1-2)
For the truth is this, Herod and Pontius Pilate along with the Gentiles and the people of Israel all gathered together against your holy child Jesus whom you have anointed.
For they did what your hand and your counsel determined beforehand needed to be done.
And now Lord, look at their threats and grant your servants all the boldness they need to speak your word.
And stretch out your hand to heal Lord, so that signs and wonders may be done through the name of your holy child Jesus."
After they prayed, their meeting place was shaken. They were all filled with the Holy Spirit, and they boldly spoke the word of God.
And the crowds of people who believed were of one heart and one soul. No one claimed that the things they owned were their own possessions, but they all shared everything.
The apostles gave a powerful witness about the resurrection of the Lord Jesus, and they all shared an abundance of grace.
No one among them lacked for anything, because those who owned lands or houses sold them, and brought the money for the things that were sold.
They laid the money down at the apostles' feet, who distributed it among everyone based on their needs.
Joseph, who the apostles called Barnabas (Son of Consolation) was a Levite from Cyprus.
One day Joseph sold some land he owned and brought the money and laid it at the apostles' feet.
But a man named Ananias and his wife Sapphira, sold some property.
Ananias and his wife brought part of the proceeds and laid them at the apostles' feet.
But Peter said, "Ananias, how has Satan managed to fill your heart with lies to the Holy Spirit, and why have you withheld some of the proceeds from the sale of your land?

When you owned the property was it not your own, and after you sold it, was it not within your power to spend the proceeds as you please? Why did you conceive this thing in your heart? You have not just lied to men, but you have lied to God."
After Ananias heard these words he collapsed and died, and everyone who heard about it was overcome with great fear.
So some young men got up and wrapped his body and carried him out and buried him.
Ananias' wife Sapphira showed up about three hours later, but she did not know what had happened to her husband.
Peter spoke to Sapphira and asked, "Did you and your husband sell your land for this amount?" And she said, "Yes, that is how much it was sold for."
Then Peter spoke to Sapphira and said, "Why did both of you decide to tempt the Lord's Spirit? Behold, the men who buried your husband are at the door, and they will carry you out too."
Then Sapphira immediately collapsed at his feet and died. When the young men came in, she was dead, so they carried her out and buried her next to her husband.
Everyone in the church who heard about this was overcome with great fear.
The apostles performed many signs and wonders among the people, and the believers all gathered together as one in the entrance to Solomon's hall.
The people acknowledged and honored the apostles, but many people were afraid and did not dare join them.
But large crowds of both men and women believers continued to be brought to the Lord.
People brought the sick into the streets and laid them on beds and couches, hoping that Peter's shadow would at least fall on some of them as he was passing by.
There was also a crowd of people who came from the cities all around to Jerusalem. They brought their sick folks and those who were tormented by unclean spirits, and they were all healed.
Then the high priest and all his subordinates from a local Sadducee sect were filled with indignation, so they went to see the disciples.
When they got there, they arrested the apostles and put them in the common prison.
But the Lord's angel went at night and opened the prison doors and released them.
And the angel said, "Go and speak to the people in the temple and tell them everything about this new life."

After the apostles heard what the angel had to say, they entered the temple to teach early in the morning. But the high priest and his subordinates assembled the full council and senate of the children of Israel. Then the high priest sent officers to the prison to have the apostles brought to them.
But when the officers could not find them in the prison, they returned to the council.
And the officers said, "We truly found the prison shut and securely locked with the guards standing outside the doors, but when we opened the cell, we found no one inside."
When the high priest, the temple captain, and the chief priests heard this, they doubted the officers' report, and they knew this story would grow.
Then someone came to the high priest and his subordinates and said, "Behold the men you put in prison are standing and teaching the people in the temple."
Then the temple captain went with the officers, and they nonviolently brought the apostles to the temple because they were afraid the people would stone them.
When they returned, they brought the apostles before the council and the high priest.

And the high priest interrogated them and said, "Did we not give you strict orders not to teach in the name of Jesus? Now you have filled Jerusalem with your doctrine, and you intend to blame us for this man's blood."
Then Peter and the other apostles answered and said, "Should we obey men rather than God?
The God of our fathers raised up Jesus, whom you killed and hung on a tree.
God has glorified Jesus with his right hand and made him a prince and a savior, and he came to bring repentance and forgiveness of sins to Israel.
We are witnesses about these things for Jesus and so is the Holy Spirit, whom God has given to those who obey him."
When the council heard this, they were enraged and they discussed killing the apostles.

Then there was a Pharisee named Gamaliel who was a doctor of the law with a good reputation among the people. And Gamaliel stood up in the council and ordered the officers to put the apostles outside for a little while.
And Gamaliel said to the council, "Men of Israel, consider carefully what you intend to do with these men.
In the past a man named Theudas rose up, boasting about being special and about four hundred men joined him. He was killed, and all of his followers were scattered and brought to nothing.
After this, Judas of Galilee also rose up in the days of the census taxes and attracted many people to him. He also perished and all of his followers were dispersed.
And now I say to you, refrain from doing anything to these men and leave them alone, because if this teaching or these miracles are from men, it will all come to nothing.
But if by chance this is from God, you cannot overthrow it and you will find yourselves fighting against God."
The entire council agreed with him, and they summoned the apostles and had them beaten. Then they ordered them not speak in the name of Jesus, and they let them go.
So the apostles left the council's presence, rejoicing that they were found worthy enough to suffer shame in the name of Jesus.
After that, the apostles went every day from house to house and to the temple where they taught and preached in the name of Jesus Christ.

In those days, the number of disciples was increasing, and the Greek followers began complaining against the Hebrew followers, because their widows were being neglected in the daily food distributions.
Then the twelve apostles summoned all of the disciples together and said, "We must not abandon the word of God to wait on tables.
Therefore brothers, select seven wise honest men full of the Holy Spirit from among you, and give them the responsibility of distributing resources.
Because we must devote ourselves to constant prayer and the ministry of the word."
This proposal pleased everyone, and they chose Stephen a man full of faith and filled with the Holy Spirit plus Philip, Prochorus, Nicanor, Timon, Parmenas, and Nicolas a Jewish convert from Antioch.
They brought these men to the apostles and after they prayed, the twelve apostles laid hands on them.
So the word of God continued to grow, and the number of disciples in Jerusalem greatly increased, and a great number of priests obeyed the faith.
Stephen was full of faith and power, and he did great wonders and miracles among the people.
Then some people from the Synagogue of the Libertines including the Cyrenians, Alexandrians, and men from Cilicia and Asia began arguing with Stephen.
But they were unable to resist his wisdom and the spirit by which he spoke.
So they bribed some men to say, "We have heard Stephen speak blasphemous words against Moses and God."
This stirred up the people, the elders, and the scribes. So, they went to him, arrested him and brought him before the council.
They testified falsely against Stephen and said, "This man speaks blasphemous words nonstop against this Holy Place and the law.
For we have heard him say, that this Jesus of Nazareth will destroy this place and change the customs which Moses has given us."
But everyone on the council could not stop staring at Stephen, because his face looked like an angel's face to them.
Then the high priest asked Stephen, "Are these things true?"
And Stephen said, "Men, brothers, and fathers listen to me! The God of glory appeared to our father Abraham when he was in Mesopotamia, before he lived in Haran.
And God said to Abraham, 'Leave your country and your relatives, and go to the land I will show you.'
Then Abraham left the land of the Chaldeans and lived in Haran. After Abraham's father died, God moved him away from there into this land where you now live.

God gave Abraham no inheritance here, not even a foot of land. But even while Abraham still had no children, God promised that he would give this land to Abraham and his descendants as their possession.
And God told Abraham that his descendants would travel to a strange land, where they would be enslaved and terribly mistreated for 400 years.
And God said, 'I will judge the nation that enslaves them, and afterwards they will come and serve me here.'
Then God gave Abraham the covenant of circumcision, and Abraham fathered Isaac and circumcised him eight days after he was born, and Isaac fathered Jacob, and Jacob fathered the twelve patriarchs.
And the patriarchs were envious of Joseph, so they sold him as a slave into Egypt. But God was with him.
God saved Joseph from all his afflictions and gave him favor and wisdom in the sight of Pharaoh King of Egypt, who appointed Joseph as governor over all of Egypt and his household.
Then famine and great suffering covered the land of Egypt and Canaan, and our fathers could find no food.
But when Jacob heard that there was wheat in Egypt, he sent our fathers there for the first time.
The second time they went to Egypt, Joseph told his brothers who he was, and he told Pharaoh they were his relatives.
Then Joseph sent for his father Jacob to come to him with all his relatives, which totaled about seventy-five souls altogether."
And Stephen said, "So Jacob went down to Egypt, where he and our fathers died.
They were carried back to Shechem and laid in the tomb that Abraham had bought from the sons of Hamor in Shechem.
But when the time to fulfill the promise that God had sworn to Abraham drew near, our people grew and multiplied in Egypt.
Until another king rose who did not know Joseph.
The new king dealt deviously with our relatives, and oppressed our fathers, and forced them to throw out their young children to die.
Moses was born at that time and he was beautiful, but he was only nourished in his father's house for three months.
When he was thrown out, Pharaoh's daughter found him and nourished him and raised him as her own son.
Moses was taught all the wisdom of the Egyptians, and he spoke powerful words and performed mighty deeds."
And Stephen said, "When Moses was forty years old, he felt a need in his heart to visit his Israelis brothers.
Moses saw an Egyptian mistreating an Israelis, and he defended and avenged the oppressed one and killed the Egyptian.
He thought his Israelis brothers would understand that God was saving them through his intervention, but they did not understand.
The next day Moses found two Israelis fighting, and he tried to intervene again and said, 'Sirs, you are brothers, why are you treating each other this way?'
But the man who wronged his neighbor pushed him away and said, 'Who made you a ruler and a judge over us?
Will you kill me, the way you did the Egyptian yesterday?'
When Moses heard this, he fled, and he lived as a foreigner in the land of Midian, where he fathered two sons.
Forty years later, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a burning bush, in the wilderness of Mount Sinai.
When Moses saw the burning bush, he was amazed at how it appeared, and as he moved closer to see it, he heard the voice of the Lord.
And the Lord said, 'I am the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.' Then Moses began trembling and he did not dare look.
Then the Lord spoke to him and said, 'Remove the shoes from your feet, because you are standing on holy ground.
For I have seen the affliction of my people in Egypt, I have heard their groaning, and I have come down to deliver them. So now, I am sending you back to Egypt.'

This was the Moses, whom they rejected and said, 'Who made you a ruler and a judge over us?' This was the same Moses that God sent to be their ruler and rescuer through the angel who appeared to him in the burning bush.
This Moses led them out of Egypt after he had shown many signs and wonders in the land, in the Red Sea, and in the wilderness for forty years.
This is the Moses who said to the Israelis, 'Your Lord God will raise up a prophet for you from among your brothers like me. Listen to him!'
Moses was in the wilderness church with the angel who spoke to him on Mount Sinai. Moses gave our fathers the living words he received from God to pass on to us."
And Stephen said, "But our fathers would not obey God, and they pushed him away. In their hearts they had turned back to Egypt.
And they said to Aaron, 'Make gods to go before us! For we do not know what has become of this Moses, who brought us out of Egypt.'
In those days they made a calf and offered sacrifices to an idol and rejoiced in the works of their own hands.

Then God turned away from them, and gave them up to worship the stars of heaven, as it is written in the book of the prophets, 'O House of Israel, why have you offered me sacrifices and offerings in the wilderness for forty years?
Yes, you have carried your Molech tabernacle and the star of your god Rephan, which you made for yourselves to worship. Therefore, I will carry you away beyond Babylon.'
Our fathers had the Tabernacle of Witness in the wilderness. It was constructed just as God had told Moses to make it from the plans he had seen.
Our fathers carried the tabernacle into the Promised Land under Joshua, as God drove out the nations before them, and the tabernacle remained in use until the time of King David.
King David found favor before God, and he wanted to build a tabernacle for the God of Jacob.
But it was Solomon who built a house for God.
However, according to the prophet, the Most High does not live in temples made with hands.
The prophet said this is what the Lord says, 'Heaven is my throne and the earth is my footstool, what kind of house will you build me? Or where will be place of my rest?
Has not my hand made all these things?'
You are stubborn people with uncircumcised hearts and ears! You always resist the Holy Spirit, and you do just as your fathers did.
Which prophets did your fathers not persecute? They even killed those who predicted the coming of the righteous one. Whom you have now betrayed and murdered.
And you have received the law ordained by the angels, which you have not kept."
When the council heard these things, they were enraged and they snarled at him gnashing their teeth.
But Stephen was full of the Holy Spirit, and he looked intently up into heaven and saw the glory of God, and Jesus standing at the right hand of God.
Then Stephen said, "Behold I see the heavens opened up, and the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God."
Then the council cried out with a loud voice and covered their ears, and they ran toward him.
Then they threw Stephen out of the city and stoned him. At the same time the witnesses laid their clothes down at the feet of a young man named Saul.
As they stoned Stephen, he was calling on God and saying, "Lord Jesus, receive my spirit."
And he knelt down and cried with a loud voice, "Lord, do not hold this sin against them!" Then he fell asleep after he said this.

Saul was also in Jerusalem, and he approved of Stephen's death. At that time a great persecution broke out against the church in Jerusalem. All the followers except the apostles were scattered throughout the regions of Judea and Samaria.
But some devout followers lamented greatly and carried Stephen away and buried him.
Saul created havoc throughout the church, and he went from house to house arresting men and women and putting them in prison.
This caused the church to be scattered abroad, and the followers went everywhere preaching the word.
Then Philip went down to the city of Samaria and preached to them about Christ.
The people there paid close attention to Philip's message, and they believed as one when they heard and saw the miracles that Phillip performed.
For many unclean spirits came screaming loudly out of those who were demon possessed, and many paralyzed and lame people were healed.
And there was great joy in that city.
But there was a man in the city there named Simon who practiced sorcery. Simon claimed to be some sort of great power and he had bewitched the people of Samaria.
All the people from the least to the greatest listened to Simon because they said, "This man's great power comes from God!"
The people in Samaria had respected Simon for a long time because he had bewitched them with his sorcery.
But when they believed what Philip was preaching about the Kingdom of God and the name of Jesus Christ, both men and women were baptized.
Simon also began to believe, so after he was baptized, he continued to follow Philip. Simon was astonished to see all the signs and miracles that Phillip was doing.
When the apostles in Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of God, they sent Peter and John to see them.
When Peter and John arrived in Samaria, they prayed for the people to receive the Holy Spirit.
For they had not yet received the Holy Spirit, because they had only been baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.
Then Peter and John laid their hands on the people, and they received the Holy Spirit.
When Simon saw that the people received the Holy Spirit when the apostles laid their hands on them, he offered them money.
And Simon said to Peter, "Can you also give me this power, so that whoever I lay hands on may receive the Holy Spirit."
But Peter responded to him and said, "May your money perish with you, because you think that God's gift can be purchased with money.
You have no place in God's ministry, because your heart is not righteous in the sight of God.
Therefore you must repent of your wickedness and pray to God, perhaps he will forgive you for the thoughts of your heart.
Because I can see that you are trapped in the gall of bitterness and bound by immorality."
Then Simon answered him and said, "Pray to the Lord for me, so that none of the things you have said will happen to me."
After Peter and John testified and preached the Lord's word there, they returned to Jerusalem and preached the gospel in many Samaritan villages on the way back.
One day an angel of the Lord spoke to Philip and said, "Get up and go south toward the desert road that goes down from Jerusalem to Gaza."

So Philip got up and left, and along the way he met an Ethiopian man, who was a eunuch of great authority under Queen Candace of Ethiopia. He was in charge of all of her treasure, and he had been to Jerusalem to worship.
As the eunuch was returning, he was sitting in his chariot reading Isaiah the prophet.
Then the Holy Spirit spoke to Philip and said, "Go and stay near this chariot."
So Philip ran over to him, where he heard the man reading the prophet Isaiah and Phillip asked him, "Do you understand what you are reading?"
And the eunuch said, "How can I understand without someone to guide me?" Then the man asked Philip to come and sit with him.

The scripture the man was reading was the one that said, "He was oppressed and afflicted, but he did not open his mouth. He was led like a lamb to the slaughter, or a silent sheep standing before its shearers. (Isaiah 53:7)
He was taken from prison and unjust judgment. Who can declare his descendants? For he was removed from the land of the living and punished for the sins of my people."(Isaiah 53:8)
And the eunuch asked Philip, "So tell me, is this prophet talking about himself or someone else?"
Then Philip opened his mouth and began with this scripture and preached to him about Jesus.
As they traveled, they came to a pool of water and the eunuch said, "Look here is some water, is there anything that prevents me from being baptized?"
And Philip said, "You can be baptized if you believe with all your heart." And the eunuch answered and said, "I believe that Jesus Christ is the Son of God."
Then the eunuch ordered the chariot to stop, and Philip and the eunuch both went down to the water, and Phillip baptized him.
When they came up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord transported Philip away, and the eunuch no longer saw him, but he went on his way rejoicing.
But Philip appeared in Azotus, and as he passed through the area he preached in all the cities until he arrived in Caesarea.
Saul was still threatening to slaughter the Lord's disciples, when he went to the high priest.
Saul requested letters he could give to the synagogues in Damascus, that stated if he found any men or women who belonged to way, he could arrest them and bring them back to Jerusalem.
As Saul got near Damascus, suddenly there was a light from heaven shining all around him.
And as he fell to the ground, he heard a voice saying to him, "`Saul, why are you persecuting me?´"
And Saul asked, "Who are you, Lord?" And the Lord said, "`I am Jesus whom you persecute, your pain is same as that of an ox that rebels against the rancher's pricks.´"(Stick for leading oxen)
Saul was trembling and astonished and he said, "Lord, what do you want me to do?" And the Lord said to him, "`Get up, and go into the city, where you will be told what you must do.´"
When the men traveling with Saul heard the voice, they were speechless because they saw no one there.
Saul stood up, but when he opened his eyes, he was blind, and they had to lead him by the hand to Damascus.
Saul was blind for three days and he would not eat nor drink.
There was a disciple in Damascus named Ananias, and the Lord spoke to him in a vision and said, "`Ananias.´" And Ananias answered, "I am here, Lord."
And the Lord said to him, "`Get up and go to the house of Judas on Straight Street where the one called Saul of Tarsus is praying.´
`Saul has seen a vision of a man named Ananias coming and laying hands on him to restore his sight.´"
Then Ananias answered and said, "Lord, I have heard from many people about all the evil Saul has done to your saints in Jerusalem.
And he has come here with the authority from the chief priests to arrest everyone who calls on your name."
But the Lord said to Ananias, "`Go there anyway, because Saul is my chosen vessel to carry my name before the Gentiles, kings, and the children of Israel.´
`And I will show him the many great things he must suffer for my name's sake.´"

So Ananias went to the house and laid his hands on Saul and said, "Brother Saul, the Lord Jesus who appeared to you along the road here has sent me to restore your sight, so that you may be filled with the Holy Spirit."
Immediately the scales that covered Saul's eyes fell, and his sight was restored, then he got up and was baptized.
After Saul had eaten and regained his strength, he spent a few days with the disciples in Damascus.
But right away Saul began preaching in the synagogues that Christ is the Son of God.

Everyone who heard him was amazed and said, "Is this not the same man who killed everyone in Jerusalem who preached in the name of Jesus? And did he not come here intending to arrest them and bring them back to the chief priests?"
But the strength of Saul's spirit increased even more, which confused the Jews who lived in Damascus, proving that Jesus is the Christ.
After a few days, the Jews met and decided to kill him.
But Saul knew they were laying a trap to kill him, and he also knew they were watching the gates day and night to catch him.
Then one night the disciples lowered him down the outer wall in a basket.
When Saul returned to Jerusalem, he tried to join the disciples, but they were all afraid of him and they did not believe that he was a disciple.

But Barnabas brought Saul to the apostles and told them how Saul had seen the Lord on the road, and that Jesus had spoken to him. And since then, he had preached boldly in Damascus in the name of Jesus.
So Saul stayed with them, and he came and went as he pleased throughout Jerusalem.
Saul argued boldly with the Greek Jews in the name of the Lord Jesus, but they tried to kill him.
When the brothers found out, they took Saul to Caesarea and sent him to Tarsus.
Then the churches throughout Judea, Galilee, and Samaria were at rest, and they grew and were instructed in how to walk in the fear of the Lord, with the Holy Spirit's comfort.
As Peter traveled throughout the area, he also went down to visit the saints who lived in Lydda.
Where he met a man named Aeneas, who had been paralyzed and bedridden for eight years.
And Peter said to him, "Aeneas, Jesus Christ makes you whole, so get up and make your bed." And he immediately got up.
When everyone who lived in Lydda and Saron saw Aeneas they turned to the Lord.
There was a disciple in Joppa named Tabitha (interpreted as Dorcas), and this woman was full of good works, charity, and kindness.
Then she got sick and died, and after they washed her corpse, they laid her in an upper chamber.
Since Lydda was near Joppa, and the disciples heard that Peter was there, they sent two men to ask if he would come quickly to them.

Then Peter got up and went with them, and when he arrived, they brought him to the upper chamber. All the widows stood around Peter weeping, and they showed him all the coats and garments Dorcas had made while she was still with them.
But Peter sent them all out of the room and he knelt down and prayed. Then Peter turned to the body said, "Tabitha, get up." Then she opened her eyes and when she saw Peter, she sat up.
Peter gave her his hand and helped her stand up, then he summoned the saints and widows and showed them that she was alive.
And it became known throughout all of Joppa, and many believed in the Lord.
Then Peter stayed a while in Joppa with a tanner named Simon.
There was a centurion named Cornelius in Caesarea, who was in the Italian garrison.
Cornelius was a devout man who feared God as did his entire household, and he had given generously to the people, and he prayed to God all the time.
Evidently, Cornelius had a vision one day at about the ninth hour when he saw God's angel coming to him who said, "Cornelius."
Cornelius was afraid when he looked at the man and he said, "What is it Lord?" And the angel said to him, "Your prayers and generous gifts have not gone unnoticed by God.
So send some men to Joppa to find Simon (Surnamed Peter).
He stays with a tanner also named Simon in a house near the sea, and he will tell you what you must do."
When the angel finished speaking to Cornelius he left, then Cornelius summoned two of his household servants and a devout soldier from his garrison.
After Cornelius told them everything, he sent them to Joppa.
The next day at about the sixth hour, Peter went up on the rooftop to pray as the travelers approached the city.
Peter was very hungry and he would have eaten, but he fell into a trance as they prepared the meal.
Then Peter saw heaven open up, and a vessel was descending down to earth toward him that looked like a great sheet knit together at the four corners.
In this vessel were all kinds of four footed earthly beasts including wild beasts, reptiles, and birds of the air.
And a voice came to Peter that said, "Get up Peter, kill and eat!"
But Peter said, "No Lord, I have never eaten anything common or unclean."
The voice spoke to Peter a second time and said, "Whatever God has cleansed do not call common."
Then Peter heard this voice a third time, and the vessel returned to heaven.
As Peter wondered to himself what this vision meant, the men from Cornelius had enquired about Simon's house, and they were standing at his gate.
They asked if Simon (Surnamed Peter) was staying there.
As Peter thought about the vision the Holy Spirit said to him, "Look, there are three men looking for you.
So get up and go with them without hesitation because I have sent them."
Then Peter went down to meet the men whom Cornelius had sent to him and said, "Behold I am the one you are looking for, why have you come?"

And they said, "Centurion Cornelius is a righteous man who fears God, and he has a good reputation among the entire Jewish nation. A holy angel was sent from God to Cornelius who told him to invite you to his house, so he can hear your words.
So Peter invited them in and they stayed until the next day. Then Peter went with them accompanied by some of the brothers from Joppa.
The next day they entered Caesarea where Cornelius was waiting for them, and he had summoned his family and close friends.
And as Peter was entering the house, Cornelius met him and fell down at his feet to worship him.
But Peter lifted him up and said, "Stand up, I myself am also a man."
As the two talked they went in, and Peter found that many people had come together.
And Peter said to them, "You know that it is unlawful for a Jewish man to associate with people from other nations. But God has shown me that I should not call anyone common or unclean.
That's why I did not deny your request to come, and I came as soon as you sent for me. So I ask you, why you have sent for me?"
And Cornelius said, "Four days ago at about the ninth hour I was fasting as I prayed in my house, and I saw a man standing before me in brilliant clothing.
And the man said, 'Cornelius, your prayers and generous gifts have not gone unnoticed by God.
So send for Simon (Surnamed Peter) in Joppa, and invite him here. He is staying with a tanner named Simon in a house near the sea, and he will tell you what you must do.'
Then I immediately sent for you, and you were good enough to come. Therefore, we are all present here before God to hear everything that God has commanded you to tell us."
Then Peter opened his mouth and said, "The truth is, I truly understand that God does not favor one person over another.
But God accepts people from every nation who fear him and work righteously.
God has sent word to the children of Israel preaching peace through Jesus Christ, who is Lord of all.
That word I tell you, which you already know was published throughout Judea beginning in Galilee, after the baptism that John preached.
Of how God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Spirit and power. Jesus went around doing good and healing all who were oppressed by the devil, because God was with him.
We are witnesses of everything that Jesus did both in the land of the Jews and in Jerusalem. But they killed Jesus and hung him on a tree.
And God publicly raised Jesus up from the dead on the third day.
But Jesus was not seen by everyone, he was seen by witnesses chosen by God, who ate and drink with him after he rose from the dead.
And he commanded us to preach to the people and testify that it is Jesus who was ordained by God to be the judge of the quick and the dead.
And all the prophets witness and testify, that through the name of Jesus whoever believes in him will receive forgiveness of sins."
As Peter spoke these words, the Holy Spirit fell on everyone who heard the word.
And all the circumcised believers who had come with Peter were astonished, because the gift of the Holy Spirit had also been poured out on the Gentiles.
For they heard the Gentiles speaking in tongues and magnifying God. Then Peter spoke.
And Peter said, "Can anyone forbid the water to baptize these Gentiles, who have received the same Holy Spirit that we have?"
Then Peter ordered them to be baptized in the name of the Lord. So, they begged him to stay a few more days.
The apostles and brothers in Judea heard that the Gentiles had also received the word of God.
So when Peter arrived in Jerusalem, the circumcised believers began to chastise him.
And the circumcised believers said, "You went and ate with uncircumcised men!"
But Peter had been rehearsing his answer, and he explained his response to them from the beginning.

And Peter said, "I was in the city of Joppa praying, when I fell into a trance and I saw a vision of a vessel descending from heaven that looked like a great sheet, being lowered by its four corners coming to me.
As I stared at it, I saw the four-footed beasts of the earth and the wild beasts, the reptiles, and the birds of the air.
And I heard a voice saying to me, 'Get up Peter, kill and eat!'
But I said, 'No Lord, I have never eaten anything common or unclean.'
But the voice from heaven answered me again and said, 'Do not call anything common that God has cleansed.'
And I heard this three times, then everything was drawn back up into heaven.
Then three men from Caesarea had already come to the house where I was staying.
The Holy Spirit told me to get up and go with them without hesitation. So, I went with six brothers who accompanied me, and we entered the man's house.
The man explained to us how he had seen an angel in his house, who spoke to him and said, "Send some men to Joppa to find Simon (Surnamed Peter).
Simon Peter will tell you, how you and all your household can be saved.
As I began to speak, the Holy Spirit fell on them just as it did on us in the beginning.
Then I remembered that the Lord had said, '`John indeed baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit.´'
So then, if God has given them the same gift he has given to those of us who believed in the Lord Jesus Christ, who am I to stand against God?"
When they heard this, they held their peace and glorified God and said, "Then God has also granted the Gentiles repentance unto life."
Now those who were scattered abroad by the persecution that arose after Stephen, traveled as far as Phoenicia, Cyprus, and Antioch preaching the word to no one but the Jews.
But some of them were men from Cyprus and Cyrene, who went to Antioch and spoke to the Greeks and preached the good news of the Lord Jesus.
The Lord's hand was with them, and a great number of people believed and turned to the Lord.
Then news about all these things reached the church in Jerusalem, and they sent Barnabas all the way to Antioch.
When Barnabas arrived, he saw the grace of God within them and he was glad, so he encouraged them all to keep and hold the Lord's purpose loyally in their hearts.
Barnabas was a good man full of faith and the Holy Spirit, and many people followed the Lord.
Then Barnabas went to Tarsus to find Saul.
When Barnabas found Saul, he brought him to Antioch, and that whole year they assembled in the church and taught many people. Antioch is where the disciples were first called Christians.
And in those days prophets went to Antioch from Jerusalem.
One of the prophets, a man named Agabus stood up and declared through the Holy Spirit that there would be a great famine throughout the whole world, which happened under Claudius Caesar.
But the disciples were determined to help the brothers in Judea to the best of their ability.
So they sent help and gifts to the elders through Barnabas and Saul.
Around that time King Herod decided to attack some of those who belonged to the church.
And he killed John's brother James with the sword.
Herod he saw that it pleased the Jews, so he proceeded to arrest Peter during the Feast of Unleavened Bread.
After Herod arrested Peter and put him in prison, he assigned four squads of soldiers to guard him, and he intended to bring Peter to face the people after Easter.
So Peter was held in prison, but the church prayed nonstop on his behalf to God.
So the night before Herod planned to bring him out, Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, bound with chains and the guards were standing by the prison doors.

Suddenly, an angel of the Lord came to Peter and a light shined in the prison. The angel tapped Peter on the side and helped him up and said, "Get up quickly." Then Peter's chains fell off of his hands.
And the angel said to Peter, "Get dressed and tie your sandals." So, he did and the angel said, "Wrap your garment around you and follow me."
So Peter followed him, but he did not think what the angel was doing was really happening, because he thought he was seeing a vision.

When they passed the first and second guards, they came to the iron gate that leads to the city. The gate opened for them by itself and they left, then as they passed through one street the angel immediately left Peter.
When Peter came to himself, he said, "Now I know for sure; the Lord sent his angel to deliver me from the hands of Herod and from everything the Jews were expecting.
After thinking about it, Peter went to the house of Mary the mother of John (Surnamed Mark), where many were gathered together praying.
As Peter knocked at the gate, a girl named Rhoda answered the door.
When Rhoda recognized Peter's voice, she was overjoyed and she did not open the gate, but she ran and told everyone that Peter was standing at the front gate.
And they responded to her and asked, "Are you mad?" But she continued to insist that it was true. Then they said, "It must be his angel."
But Peter continued knocking, and after they opened the door and saw him, they were astonished.

But he held up his hand motioning for them to be quiet, then he told them how the Lord had brought him out of the prison, and he said, "Go and tell James and the brothers about this." Then Peter left and went somewhere else.
But at the break of dawn, there was no small commotion among the soldiers about what had become of Peter.
When Herod looked for Peter, he could not find him. So, he interrogated the guards and ordered them to be put to death. Then Herod left Judea and went down to live in Caesarea.

Herod was extremely displeased with the people of Tyre and Sidon. But they had befriended the king's eunuch Blastus, and they went to Herod asking for peace, because their food came from the king's country.
And on the day of their appointment with Herod, he sat before them on his throne wearing his royal apparel, and he made a speech to them.
And the people shouted and said, "This is the voice of a God, not a man!"
Then Herod was immediately struck down by the Lord's angel, and he was eaten by worms, then he gave up the ghost and died, because he did not give glory to God.
But the word of God grew and multiplied.
Then Barnabas and Saul returned from Jerusalem and brought John (Surnamed Mark) with them, after they fulfilled their ministry.
The church at Antioch had a few prophets and teachers such as Barnabas, Simeon (aka. Niger), Lucius of Cyrene, Saul (aka. Paul), and Manaen (who had been raised with Herod the tetrarch).
As they ministered to the Lord and fasted, the Holy Spirit said, "Separate Saul and Barnabas to do the work for me which I have called them to do."
After they fasted and prayed and laid hands on them, they sent Saul and Barnabas away.
So the Holy Spirit sent them out, and they left Seleucia and sailed to Cyprus.
When they arrived in Salamis with John, they preached the word of God in the Jewish synagogues.
As they traveled throughout the island on the way to Paphos, they found a Jew named Bar-Jesus (aka. Elymas) who was a sorcerer and a false prophet.
Sergius Paulus who was with the deputy of the country and a prudent man, summoned Saul and Barnabas because he wanted to hear the word of God.
But Elymas (aka. Bar-Jesus) the sorcerer opposed them and tried to keep the deputy away from the faith.
Then Saul (aka. Paul), was filled with the Holy Spirit and he stared directly at Elymas.
And Paul said, "You are full of deceit and mischief, because you are a child of the devil and an enemy of all righteousness. Will you never stop perverting the righteous ways of the Lord?

And now, the hand of the Lord is upon you, and you will be blinded. You will not see the sun for an entire season, and immediately a mist and darkness fell over him, and he left trying to find someone who would lead him by the hand.
When the deputy saw what happened he was astonished, and he believed in the Lord's doctrine.
When Paul and his associates left Paphos, they went to Perga in Pamphylia where John left them and returned to Jerusalem.
But when they left Perga, they went to Antioch in Pisidia and entered the synagogue on the Sabbath and sat down.

After the synagogue leaders finished reading the law and the prophets, they sent word to Saul and Barnabas and said, "Brothers, if you have any words of encouragement for the people, please speak up."
Then Paul stood up and motioned with his hand and said, "Men of Israel, and those of you who fear God, listen to me!
The God of the people of Israel chose our fathers. Then God glorified the Israelis when they lived as foreigners in the land of Egypt, and with an uplifted arm he brought them out of bondage.
And God suffered the behavior of his people for about forty years as they wandered in the wilderness.
After God destroyed seven nations in the land of Canaan, he divided up their land by lot and gave it to his people.
After that, God gave them judges for a period of about 450 years until the time of Samuel the prophet.
Afterward they wanted a king, and God gave them a king for forty years named Saul son of Kish from the tribe of Benjamin.

After God removed King Saul, he raised up David as their king, and God testified about David and said, 'I have found David the son of Jesse, to be a man after my own heart, he will completely fulfill my will.'
And God has brought one of this man's descendants to Israel, a man named Jesus as his promised savior.
Before Jesus came, John preached a baptism of repentance to all the people of Israel.
As John completed his work he said, 'Who do you think that I am? I am not the savior, but there is one coming after me, whose shoes I am not even worthy to untie.'
Brothers, children of Abraham, and everyone among you who fears God, this word of salvation is sent to you.
For the people in Jerusalem and their rulers did not recognize Jesus, but by condemning him they fulfilled what the prophets had written which they had read every Sabbath.
Even though they found no reason to condemn him to death, they still asked Pilate to kill him.
After they fulfilled everything that was written about Jesus, they took him down from the tree and laid him in a tomb.
But God raised him from the dead.
And Jesus was seen alive for many days by those who came with him from Galilee to Jerusalem, and they are his witnesses to the people.
And we declare the good news to you of the promise that was made to our fathers.

And how God has fulfilled this promise for us their children, by raising up Jesus from the dead, as it is also written in the second Psalm, 'You are my son, and today I have become your father.' (Psalm 2:7)
God raised Jesus up from the dead and he never saw decay since God said, 'I will make you an everlasting promise which includes the faithful mercies that I promised David.' (Isaiah 55:3)
Therefore God also said in another Psalm, 'Nor will you let your Holy One see decay.' (Psalm 16:10)
Because after David served his own generation and did the will of God, he fell asleep and was laid to rest with his fathers and he saw decay.
But the one whom God raised from the dead, saw no decay.
Therefore brothers, let it be known that through this man Jesus is preached the forgiveness of sins.
And through him everyone who believes is justified from all things, which before could not be justified through the Law of Moses.
So beware, or the things that were spoken of by the prophets may come upon you.

When the prophet said, 'Look you heathen, wonder about marvelous things and perish! Because I will do a work in your days which you would never believe, even if someone told you about it.'"(Habakkuk 1:5)
After the Jews left the synagogue, the Gentiles implored Paul and Barnabas to preach this message to them on the next Sabbath.
When the congregation broke up, many of the Jews and devout converts followed Paul and Barnabas. So, they both spoke to the people and persuaded them to continue in the grace of God.
The next Sabbath day almost the whole city came to hear God's word.
But when the Jews saw the large crowds, they were very envious. So, they spoke against Paul and blasphemously contradicted him.

Then Paul and Barnabas grew bold and said, "It was necessary for us to first speak the word of God to the Jews. But since you reject it and you see yourselves as unworthy of everlasting life, then we will turn to the Gentiles.
For the Lord has given us a command and he said, 'I will also make you a light to the Gentiles so that my salvation reaches the ends of the earth.'"(Isaiah 49:6)
When the Gentiles heard this, they rejoiced and glorified the Lord's word, and everyone who was ordained for eternal life believed.
And the Lord's word was proclaimed throughout the region.
But the Jews incited the prominent religious women and leading men of the city. Then they stirred up persecution against Paul and Barnabas and drove them out of their area.
So they shook the dust off of their feet in protest and went to Iconium.
But the disciples were filled with joy and the Holy Spirit.
In Iconium, Paul and Barnabas both went into the Jewish synagogue to speak, and a great number of Jews and Greeks believed.
But the unbelieving Jews stirred up the Gentiles and turned their minds to evil against the brothers.
So Paul and Barnabas spent a long time speaking boldly and testifying for the Lord about the grace of God, who allowed them to perform signs and wonders.
But the people of the city were divided, and some believed the Jews, but some believed the apostles.
But then both the Gentiles and the Jews, along with their rulers decided to maliciously assault and stone them.
But Paul and Barnabas became aware of their threat, and they fled to the Lycaonian cities of Lystra and Derbe and the surrounding region.
Where they preached the gospel.
There was a man in Lystra with crippled feet, who had never walked and he had been crippled since he was born.
When this man heard Paul speak, he stared intently at him, and Paul saw that the man had the faith to be healed.
Then Paul said with a loud voice, "Stand up!" And the man jumped up and walked.
When the people saw what Paul had done, they raised up their voices and said in the Lycaonian language, "The gods have come down to us looking like men!"
And they called Barnabas, Jupiter. Then they called Paul, Mercurius because he was the main speaker.
Then Jupiter's priest who was just outside their city, brought oxen and garlands to the gates, and he would have made sacrifices with the people.
But when the apostles Paul and Barnabas heard about this, they cried and tore their clothes, and they ran in among the people.

And Paul and Barnabas said, "Sirs, why are you doing this? We are also just passionate men like you, but we are preaching that you should turn to the living God and away from these vanities. For God made the heaven, the earth, the sea, and everything in them.
But in the past, God has suffered and allowed all nations to walk in their own ways.

Nevertheless, God did not leave himself without a witness to testify that it was God, who has given us the good rains from heaven, fruitful seasons, and he has filled our hearts with food and happiness.'
But even after they said this, they could barely restrain the people from making sacrifices to them.
Then some Jews from Antioch and Iconium came there and persuaded the people to stone Paul. Afterwards, they dragged Paul out of the city thinking he was dead.
However, as the disciples stood around him, Paul got up and went into the city, and the next day he left with Barnabas and went to Derbe.
After Paul and Barnabas had preached the gospel to that city and taught many, they returned to Lystra, Iconium, and Antioch.
Then Paul and Barnabas taught the new souls of the disciples and encouraged them to continue in the faith and said, "We must suffer much tribulation to enter into the Kingdom of God."
Paul and Barnabas ordained elders in every church with praying and fasting, and they entrusted them to the Lord in whom they believed.
Paul and Barnabas passed through Pisidia, then they went to Pamphylia.
Then they preached the word in Perga, and they went down to Attalia.
From Attalia they sailed to Antioch, where they had been recommended by the grace of God for the work they had completed.
When they arrived in Antioch, they gathered the church together and told them about everything that God had done with them, and how he had opened the door of faith to the Gentiles.
And Paul and Barnabas lived there with the disciples for a long time.
Some men came down from Judea to teach the brothers and they said, "Unless you are circumcised as Moses ordered, you cannot be saved."

There was no doubt that Paul and Barnabas fervently disagreed with them. So, they decided that Paul and Barnabas, and some other believers would go ask the apostles and elders in Jerusalem about this.
So the church let them go, and they passed through Phoenicia and Samaria telling everyone about the Gentiles' conversion, and this brought great joy to all the brothers.
When Paul and Barnabas arrived in Jerusalem, they were received by the church and the apostles and elders, and they told them everything that God had done with them.
But a sect of the Pharisees who believed stood up and said, "The Gentiles must be circumcised, and they must obey the law of Moses."
So the apostles and elders met together to debate this matter.
After much arguing, Peter stood up and said, "Brothers, you know that a good while back, God made us choose the Gentiles to hear the gospel from me and believe.
And God who knows people's hearts, witnessed to them by giving them the same Holy Spirit that he had given us.
Because God did not care whether it was us or them who was saved, and he purified their hearts by faith.
So why do you tempt God, and put a yoke on the neck of his disciples, which neither we nor our fathers could bear?
But we believe that through the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ we will be saved, just as they are."
Then all the people remained silent and listened to Barnabas and Paul, as they declared all the miracles and wonders God had worked among the Gentiles through them.
After Paul and Barnabas had been quiet for a while, James spoke up and said, "Brothers, listen to me!
Simon Peter has told us how God first visited the Gentiles to take from them a people for his own name.
And the prophets' words agree with him.
Because the prophets wrote, 'In those days I will return, and rebuild David's tabernacle which has fallen down, and I will rebuild its ruins and restore it as it was before.'
And the Lord who will do this says, 'So that the surviving men and Gentiles who call on my name may seek the Lord.
For God knows all of his works from the beginning of the world.'
Therefore it is my judgement, that we should not trouble the Gentiles who have turned to God.
But we must write to them to tell them, that they must abstain from the pollution of idols, fornication, eating strangled things, and consuming blood.
For Moses has been preached in every city and read in the synagogues on every Sabbath since the days of old."

Then the apostles, elders, and the whole church decided to choose men from their own congregation to send to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas. They chose Judas (surnamed Barsabas) and Silas, who were leading men among the brothers.
And they wrote letters to send with them that said, "The apostles, elders, and brothers send greetings to our Gentile brothers in Antioch, Syria, and Cilicia.
Because we have heard that some men who came from us have upset you and said, 'You must be circumcised and keep the law.' We did not say this.
It seemed like a good idea to us to choose some men to send to you along with our beloved Paul and Barnabas.
Men who have jeopardized their own lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.
Therefore, we have sent Judas and Silas to tell you the same things in person.
For it seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us, to lay no greater burden on you than these necessary things.
You must abstain from meats offered to idols, fornication, eating strangled things, and consuming blood. You would do well to avoid these things. So, farewell."
When Judas and Silas were dismissed, they went to Antioch where they gathered the whole church together, and they delivered the letter.
After they read the letter, the entire church rejoiced for the consolation.
Judas and Silas were also prophets, and they said many things to encourage and strengthen the brothers.
After they had been there a while, the church brothers let them go in peace back to the apostles.
But Silas decided to stay longer.
Paul and Barnabas also decided to stay in Antioch along with many others, teaching and preaching the Lord's word.
After a while Paul spoke to Barnabas and said, "Let us go back and visit our brothers in every city where we have preached the Lord's word, to see how they are doing."
Barnabas was determined to take John (aka. Mark) with them.
But Paul did not think it was a good idea to take John with them, because he had left them in Pamphylia and had not helped them with the work there.
Their disagreement was so sharp that they each went their own way. So, Barnabas took Mark and sailed to Cyprus.
Paul chose Silas and left, and the brothers recommended them to the grace of God.
And Paul went through Syria and Cilicia strengthening the churches.
Paul went to Derbe then on to Lystra, where he found a disciple named Timothy, the son of a Jewish woman who believed and a Greek father.
The brothers in Lystra and Iconium had spoken well of Timothy.
So Paul wanted Timothy to go with him, and he took him to be circumcised because all of the Jews there knew that Timothy's father was Greek.
As they traveled throughout the cities, they delivered the decisions that were ordained by the apostles and elders in Jerusalem that the Gentiles were required to keep.
So the churches were established in the faith and their numbers increased daily.
After they traveled throughout Phrygia and Galatia, Paul and Timothy were forbidden by the Holy Spirit to preach the word in Asia.
When they arrived in Mysia, they tried to enter Bithynia, but the Spirit suffered and they could not go there.
So they passed by Mysia and went down to Troas.
Paul had a vision one night of a man standing in Macedonia, and the man pleaded with him and said, "Come to Macedonia and help us!"
After Paul had seen the vision, we immediately left for Macedonia because we were convinced that the Lord wanted us to preach the gospel there.
So we left Troas and set sail for Samothracia and sailed to Neapolis the next day.
From there we went to Philippi, which is the main city and a colony of that part of Macedonia, and we were there for a few days.
