On the Sabbath we left Philippi and went to the nearby riverside, where people usually prayed. We sat down and spoke to the women we met there.
A woman named Lydia from the city of Thyatira who worshipped God and sold purple cloth, heard us, and the Lord opened her heart, and she accepted everything Paul said.
After she and her household were baptized, she implored us to stay in her house and said, "If you have judged me to be faithful to the Lord, come and stay in my home." And she convinced us to stay.
Then as we went to prayer, we met a girl possessed by a spirit of divination who earned a lot of money for her masters, by fortune telling.
The girl followed Paul and the rest of us, and she cried out and said, "These men are the servants of the Most High God, who are showing us the way to salvation!"
She kept this up for many days, which grieved Paul so much that he turned to the spirit and said, "I command you in the name of Jesus Christ to come out of her!" And the spirit immediately left her.
When her masters realized that their plans to use her to make money was gone, they grabbed Paul and Silas, and drug them to the marketplace rulers.
They brought them to the magistrates and said, "These men are Jews who are causing a lot of trouble in our city.
They are teaching customs which are unlawful for us as Romans to receive or observe."
The crowds rose up against Paul and Silas, and the magistrates ordered their clothes torn off and had them beaten.
After they were beaten with whips many times and thrown into prison, the jailor was ordered to keep them secured.
When the jailer received this order, he threw them into the inner prison and fastened their feet in the stocks.
At midnight as Paul and Silas prayed and sang praises to God, the other prisoners heard them.
And suddenly there was a great earthquake that shook the foundations of the prison, and immediately all the doors flew open and everyone's chains came loose.
The jailer was awakened from his sleep, and when he saw the prison doors open, he drew his sword and would have killed himself, because he thought that the prisoners had fled.
But Paul cried with a loud voice and said, "Do not harm yourself because we are all here."
The jailer called for a light and he went in trembling and fell down before Paul and Silas.
Then the jailer brought them out and asked, "Sirs, what must I do to be saved?"
Paul and Silas said, "Believe in the Lord Jesus Christ, and you and your house will be saved."
Then Paul and Silas spoke the Lord's word to him and to everyone in his house.
That night the jailer took Paul and Silas and washed their stripes. Then right away he and his entire household and were baptized.
After he brought them into his home, he set a meal before them. And everyone in his household rejoiced because they had begun to believe in God.
At sunrise the magistrates sent the sergeants to the jailer and they said, "Let those men go."
Then the jailer spoke to Paul and said, "The magistrates have sent word to release you, so you may leave and go in peace."

But Paul answered the sergeants and said, "They have beaten us without a trial and thrown us into prison even though we are Roman citizens, and now they want to secretly remove us? So, honesty I say, you can tell them to come and remove us themselves."
When the sergeants told the magistrates this, they were afraid after they heard that Paul and Silas were Romans.
So the magistrates came and begged them to leave the city, and they brought Paul and Silas out of prison.
Then Paul and Silas left the prison went to Lydia's house. After they entered and saw the brothers, they comforted them and left.
After they passed through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they arrived in Thessalonica, where there was a Jewish synagogue.
And Paul went to them as he usually did, and he discussed the scriptures with them on three Sabbath days.
Paul opened and alleged, that Christ had to suffer and be raised from the dead, and he said, "This Jesus, whom I preach to you about, is the Christ."
Some of the people believed and joined Paul and Silas, along with a huge number of devout Greeks, and more than a few of the leading women there.

However, the Jews who did not believe Paul were envious, and they took some obscene fellows of the baser sort to gather a large crowd, and they had the whole the city in an uproar. They assaulted the house of Jason and looking for Paul and Silas to bring them out to the people.

But when they could not find them, they brought Jason and some of the other brothers to the city rulers and accused them and said, "These men who have turned the whole world upside down, have also come here.
And Jason welcomed them into his home, and contrary to the decrees of Caesar, they have said that there is another king named Jesus."
When the people and the city rulers heard these things, they were very upset.
But after the rulers had taken secure bond payments from Jason and the others, they let them go.
Then the brothers immediately sent Paul and Silas away to Berea at night, and when they arrived there, they went into the Jewish synagogue.

These people were more noble than those in Thessalonica, because they received the word with completely open minds, and they searched the scriptures daily, to determine if the things that were said were true.
Therefore, many of them believed, so did many of the honorable Greek women, and more than a few of the men.
But when the Jews of Thessalonica heard that Paul was preaching God's word in Berea, they went there to stir up the people.
Then the brothers immediately sent Paul away by sea, but Silas and Timothy stayed there.
When the people who directed Paul brought him to Athens, they returned with Paul's request to Silas and Timothy to come to him as quickly as possible.
While Paul waited for them in Athens, his inner spirit was stirred up, when he saw that the city was completely given over to idolatry.
So, every day he argued with the Jews and the devout people in the synagogue, and also with the people he met in the market.

Then some of the Epicurean and Stoick philosophers encountered Paul, and some said, "What is this man babbling about?" Other said, "He seems to be a speaking about strange gods." Because he preached to them about Jesus and the resurrection.
And they brought him to Areopagus and said, "What is this new doctrine you are teaching?
For you bring strange things to our ears, so we want to know what these things mean."
For all the Athenians and strangers there, spent their time doing nothing but telling or listening to some new ideas.
Then Paul stood in the middle of Mars' Hill and said, "Men of Athens, I see that you are too superstitious about everything.
For as I passed by and saw your devotions, I even found an altar with this inscription, 'To the unknown God.' Therefore, you ignorantly worship some unknown thing, but now I declare this to you.
The God who made the world and everything in it, is Lord of heaven and earth, and he does not live in temples made with men's hands.
Nor is he worshipped with men's hands, as if there were anything that he needed, since he is the one who gives life and breath to everyone, and all living things.
God has made all nations from one man, and a place for everyone on the face of the earth to live. And God has determined their appointed times and the boundaries of their homelands.
But God wanted them to seek the Lord, and if by chance they might find him, even though he is not far from any one of us.
For as some of your own poets have said, 'In him we live and move and have our being because we are all his offspring.'
Therefore, since we are all God's offspring, we should not think that the Godhead is like gold, silver, stone, or a carved image made by man's own devices.
And at times God has winked at this ignorance but now he commands all men everywhere to repent.

Because he has appointed a day, in which he will judge the world in righteousness by that man whom he has ordained, of which he has given assurance to all men, in that he has raised him from the dead."
When they heard about the resurrection of the dead, some people mocked Paul, but others said, "We want to hear more from you about this."
So Paul left the Areopagus.
However, some men joined him and believed, among whom was Dionysius the Areopagite and a woman named Damaris, along with others who were with them.
After all this Paul left Athens and went to Corinth.

Where he found a Jew, who was born in Pontus named Aquila and his wife Priscilla. They had recently left Italy because Emperor Claudius had ordered all the Jews to leave Rome, so Paul went to visit them.
Since they all practiced the same craft, Paul lived and worked with them because by occupation they were all tentmakers.
Paul reasoned with the people in the synagogue every Sabbath persuading the Jews and the Greeks.
When Silas and Timothy arrived from Macedonia, Paul was pressed by the spirit, and he testified to the Jews that Jesus was Christ.
When they opposed Paul and blasphemed, he shook his clothes and said to them, "Your blood is on your own heads! My conscience is clean! From now on I will go preach to the Gentiles."
So, Paul left and went next door to the synagogue and entered the house of a man named Justus, who worshipped God.
Crispus was the leader of the synagogue, and he believed in the Lord along with everyone in his house, and many of the Corinthians who heard the word believed and were baptized.
Then the Lord spoke to Paul in a vision one night and said, "`Paul, do not be afraid, but continue to speak out, and do not hold your peace.´
`For I am with you, and no man will hurt you, because I have many people in this city.´"
So Paul stayed for another year and a half, teaching the word of God among the Corinthians.
When Gallio was the deputy of Achaia, the Jews attacked Paul and brought him to the judgment seat.
And they said, "This fellow persuades men to worship God in ways that are contrary to the law."
When Paul was about to open his mouth, Gallio said to the Jews, "O you Jews, if this were about some wrong or wicked obscenity, I would reasonably listen to you.
But since it is a question about words and names and your own law, look to it yourselves, because I will not judge such matters."
Then he drove them away from the judgment seat.
After that all the Greeks beat Sosthenes the synagogue leader before the judgment seat. Which Gallio was not the least bit interested in at all.
Paul stayed there for a while before he left the brothers and sailed to Syria with, after he shaved his head in Cenchrea to keep a vow he had made.
When Paul arrived in Ephesus, he left Priscilla and Aquila, and he went to the synagogue, where he reasoned with the Jews.
When they asked him to stay longer with them, he declined the offer.
But Paul bid them farewell and said, "I must be in Jerusalem for this coming feast, but if God is willing, I will return. And he sailed from Ephesus.
When Paul landed in Caesarea, he went to offer salutations to the church, then he went down to Antioch.
After Paul had spent some time Antioch, he systematically traveled over all the country of Galatia and Phrygia, strengthening all the disciples.
A Jew named Apollos who was born in Alexandria, came to Ephesus. He was an eloquent man, well versed and mighty in the scriptures.
Apollos was instructed in the ways of the Lord, and he had a fervent spirit. He spoke and taught diligently about the things of the Lord, but he only knew about the baptism of John.
Apollos began to speak boldly in the synagogue, and when Aquila and Priscilla heard him, they took him under their wing and explained the ways of God to him more perfectly.

When Apollos decided to go to Achaia, the brothers encouraged him and wrote the disciples in Achaia and asked them to welcome him. Upon the arrival of Apollos, he was a big help to those who had believed through grace.
For he powerfully and publicly convinced the Jews, proving by the scriptures that Jesus is the Christ.
While Apollos was in Corinth, Paul traveled through the upper coasts and went to Ephesus where he found certain disciples.
And Paul spoke to the disciples and asked them, "Have you received the Holy Spirit since you began to believe?" And they said to him, "We have not even heard of the Holy Spirit."
Then Paul asked them, "How were you baptized?" And they replied, "We have received John's baptism."

So Paul replied to them and said, "John truly baptized with the baptism of repentance that he preached to the people, so that they would believe in the one who would come after him, who is Jesus Christ."
When they heard this, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.
Paul laid his hands on them, then the Holy Spirit came upon them and they spoke in tongues and prophesied.
There were about twelve men there altogether.
Then Paul went into the synagogue where he spoke boldly for about three months. He argued and persuaded the people about the things of the Kingdom of God.

But different people hardened themselves against these teachings, and they refused to believe and spoke evil of that way before the people. So Paul left and took the disciples to the school of Tyrannus, where they continued to argue and discuss things daily.
And this continued for about two years, so that everyone who lived in Asia heard the word of the Lord Jesus, both Jews and Greeks.
And God worked special miracles through the hands of Paul.
So that even handkerchiefs or aprons that were touched by Paul's body were brought to the sick, and the diseases and evil spirits left them.
Then some vagabond Jewish exorcists, took it upon themselves to invoke the name of the Lord Jesus over those who had evil spirits and they would say, "We adjure you by Jesus of whom Paul preaches."
And the chief Jewish priests Sceva had seven sons who did this.
But the evil spirit answered them and said, "I know Jesus and Paul, but who are you?"
And the possessed man with the evil spirit leaped on them and attacked them and overcame them. So they fled from that house naked and wounded.
All the Jews and Greeks who lived in Ephesus knew about this, and fear overcame all of them, and the name of the Lord Jesus was magnified.
And many who believed came and confessed their deeds.
Many of them who practiced mystical arts brought their books together, and burned them before everyone. And some people calculated the price of those books to be about 50,000 pieces of silver.
So the word of God grew mightily and prevailed.
After all these things happened, Paul's spirit was steadfast as he had passed through Macedonia and Achaia on the way to Jerusalem and he said, "After I go to Jerusalem, I must also see Rome."
So Paul sent Timothy and Erastus who ministered to him on to Macedonia, but Paul himself stayed in Asia for a season.
At the same time there arose a great disturbance about the way.
For a silversmith named Demetrius who made silver shrines for Diana, brought great profits to the craftsmen.
Then Demetrius summoned all the workmen of similar occupations together and said, "Sirs, you know that our wealth comes to us through this craft of ours.
Besides that you can see and hear that it is not just in Ephesus but almost throughout all of Asia, Paul has persuaded and turned away many people when he said, 'Gods made with hands are not gods!'

So, not only is our craft in danger of becoming worthless, but the temple of the great goddess Diana whom all of Asia and the world worships, is becoming despised and her magnificence is being destroyed.
When the craftsmen heard this, they were full of anger and they cried out and said, "Great is the Diana of the Ephesians!"
Then the whole city was filled with confusion, and the crowd caught Paul's two traveling companions the Macedonians, Gaius and Aristarchus, and they rushed them into the theatre.
Paul wanted to confront the people, but the disciples would not let him go.
Some of the Asian chiefs who were Paul's friends, sent word to him, begging him not to venture into the theatre.
Therefore the assembly was confused because some of the people cried one thing and some another, and most of them did not even know why they had come together.
Some Jews pulled Alexander out of the crowd and pushed him out front, and Alexander raised his hand to quiet the people and defend himself.
But when the people discovered that Alexander was a Jew, then for about two hours nonstop they all cried out with one voice, "Great is Diana of the Ephesians!"

After the town clerk appeased the people he said, "You men of Ephesus, who among you does not know that the city of the Ephesians is a worshipper of the great goddess Diana, and the image which fell down from Jupiter?
Since these things cannot be denied, you should be quiet and do nothing hastily.
For you have brought these men here, who are neither robbers of churches nor blasphemers of your goddess.
Therefore, if Demetrius and the craftsmen with him have something against someone, the law is open and there are deputies, so let them accuse one another.
But if you are asking anything about other matters, it must be determined by a lawful assembly.
For we are in danger of being called into question for today's uproar, and we may have to give a legal accounting of this meeting."
When the town clerk finished speaking, he dismissed the assembly.
When the uproar ceased, Paul summoned the disciples and embraced them, then he left and went to Macedonia.
After Paul traveled through those areas and gave them much encouragement, he went to Greece.
Paul stayed in Greece for three months, but when the Jews began to lay a trap for him as he was about to set sail for Syria, he decided to return through Macedonia.
Paul was accompanied by Asia Sopater of Berea, Aristarchus and Secundus the Thessalonians, Gaius of Derbe, Timothy, and Tychicus and Trophimus of Asia.
Then they went on ahead of us and waited for us in Troas.
After the Feast of Unleavened Bread, we sailed from Philippi and met them in Troas five days later, where we stayed for seven days.
On the first day of the week, the disciples came together to break bread. Paul was prepared to leave the next day, so he stayed up late and preached to them until midnight.
There were many lights in the upper chamber where they were gathered together.

A young man named Eutychus sat on a window sill, and he fell into a deep sleep as Paul was preaching. Eutychus was sound asleep when he fell from the window on the third floor, and he was dead when they picked him up.
But Paul went down and embraced Eutychus and said, "Do not be troubled because he is still alive!"
Then Paul went back upstairs, broke bread, and ate, then he continued talking until daybreak and left.
And the people were more than a little comforted when they brought the young Eutychus home alive.
We went on before Paul to the ship and sailed to Assos, where we had planned to meet Paul because he went there on foot.
When Paul met us in Assos, we took him aboard the ship and sailed to Mitylene.
We sailed from there and arrived in Chios the next day. The following day we arrived in Samos where we stayed a while in Trogyllium, and the next day we arrived in Miletus.
For Paul was determined to sail past Ephesus because he did not want to spend time in Asia. Paul hurried because he wanted to be in Jerusalem on the day of Pentecost if possible.
From Miletus Paul sent for the church elders in Ephesus.
When the church elders from Ephesus arrived, Paul spoke to them and said, "You know how I behaved the whole time that I lived among you, since the very first day that I arrived in Asia.
How I served the Lord with a humble mind, with many tears and temptations which befell me, when the Jews were lying in wait to trap me.
And how I withheld nothing profitable from you, but I have shown you and taught you the truth both publicly, and from house to house.
Testifying both to the Jews and the Greeks, teaching repentance toward God and faith toward our Lord Jesus Christ.
And now, behold I am going to Jerusalem bound in the spirit and not knowing what will happen to me there.
Except that the Holy Spirit warns me in every city that I go, that chains and afflictions await me.

But none of these things matter to me, nor do I count my life dear to me. So I can finish my course and the ministry which I have received from the Lord Jesus, to testify the gospel of the grace of God with joy.
For behold, now I know that all of you to whom I have been preaching the Kingdom of God, will no longer see my face.
Therefore I ask you to record this today, that I am innocent of the blood of all men.
For I have not refused to declare the counsel of God to all of you.
Therefore beware, and keep watch over the entire flock which the Holy Spirit has made you overseers. You must feed God's church which he has purchased with his own blood.
For this I know, after I depart grievous wolves will enter in among you and they will not spare the flock.
Men will also rise up from among your own ranks, speaking perverse things to draw disciples to themselves and away from you.
So keep watch and remember, for about three years I did not cease warning everyone night and day with tears.
Now brothers, I commend you to God and to the word of his grace, which is able to build you up and give you an inheritance among all of those who are sanctified.
For I have coveted no one's silver, gold, or apparel.
You yourselves know that my hands, have ministered to my necessities and to those who were with me.
I have shown you all things, and how we should labor to support the weak, and remember the words of our Lord Jesus when he said, '`It is more blessed to give than to receive.´'"
After Paul said all this, he knelt down and prayed with all of them.
And they all wept as they hugged Paul's neck and kissed him.
They were all filled with sorrow, mostly because Paul said that they would no longer see his face, and they accompanied him to the ship.
After we had gotten away from them, we sailed straight to Coos, and the following day we went on to Rhodes and from there to Patara.
We found a ship sailing to Phenicia, so we climbed aboard and set sail.
After we sighted Cyprus, we sailed left of it to Syria and landed in Tyre, because that's where the ship was supposed to unload her cargo.
We stayed for seven days with the disciples we found there, who told Paul through the spirit, that he should not go up to Jerusalem.

After we had been there for seven days, we left and on went our way. The disciples all followed us out of the city and they brought their wives and children with them, then we all knelt down on the beach and prayed.
When we finally left them, we boarded a ship and they returned home.
When we arrived in Ptolemais from Tyre, we greeted the brothers there and stayed with them for one day.
The next day all of us in Paul's company, left and went to Caesarea. Upon arrival we stayed at Philip the evangelist's home, who was one of the seven. (Acts 6:1-6)
Philip had four virgin daughters who prophesied.
After we had been there for several days, a prophet named Agabus came down from Judea.

When Agabus arrived, he bound his own hands and feet with Paul's belt and said, "The Holy Spirit says, 'This is how the Jews in Jerusalem will bind the man who owns this belt and deliver him into the hands of the Gentiles.'"
After we heard these things, everyone there including us implored Paul not to go up to Jerusalem.
Then Paul answered, "Are you weeping to break my heart? For I am not only ready to be bound, but also to die in Jerusalem in the name of the Lord Jesus."
When we failed to persuade Paul, we stopped trying and said, "The will of the Lord be done."
After that we boarded our carriages and went to Jerusalem.
Some of the disciples also went with us to Caesarea, and they brought us to the home of an old disciple named Mnason of Cyprus, with whom we stayed.
When we arrived in Jerusalem, the brothers there gladly received us.
The day following Paul went with us to visit James, and all the elders were present.
After Paul greeted them, he meticulously declared everything God had done among the Gentiles through his ministry.
When they had heard it all, they glorified the Lord. Then they said to Paul, "You see brother, there are thousands of Jews there who believe, and they are all zealous for the law.
But the people there were told that you teach the Jews who live among the Gentiles to forsake Moses. They were also told that you teach them not to circumcise their children nor observe our customs.
So what should we do? The multitude will come together because they will hear that you have come.
So this is what we must say to you, we have four men who have made promises.

Go and purify yourself along with these men and pay their expenses, so that they may shave their heads. Then everyone will know that everything they were told about you is not true, but that you also walk in obedience to the law.
As for the Gentile believers, we have concluded and written that they are only required to refrain from eating things offered to idols, eating blood, eating meat that was strangled, and fornication."

So the next day Paul and the men purified themselves. Then they all entered the temple to inform them that when their days of purification were finished, every one of them would be making an offering.
After the seven days were almost up, the Jews from Asia saw Paul in the temple, so they stirred up all the people and grabbed him.

And they cried out, "Men of Israel, help us! This is the man, who teaches everyone everywhere against our people, the law, and this place. Furthermore he has also brought Greeks into the temple, and polluted this holy place."
For they had previously seen Paul in the city with Trophimus an Ephesian, whom they thought Paul had brought into the temple.
The entire city was agitated and the people rushed together. Then they seized Paul and drug him out of the temple, and immediately shut the doors.
As they were about to kill him, the chief captain of the Roman guard received the news that all of Jerusalem was in an uproar.
The chief captain immediately rushed down to the mob with soldiers and centurions. When they saw the chief captain and the soldiers, they stopped beating of Paul.
Then the chief captain seized Paul and ordered him to be bound with two chains, then he demanded to know who Paul was and what he had done.

Some people among the mob shouted one thing and some shouted another. When the captain realized that he could not know for certain what caused the tumult, he ordered Paul to be carried back to the castle.
When Paul got to the stairs, the soldiers had to carry him because of the people's violence.
Because the mob who followed them shouted, "Away with him!"
As Paul was to be led into the castle, he spoke to the chief captain and asked, "May I speak to you?" The captain said, "Can you speak Greek?
Are you not that Egyptian, who recently stirred up an insurrection and led 4,000 murderers out into the wilderness?"
But Paul said, "I am a Jew from Tarsus in Cilicia, a citizen of no ordinary city and I beg you to allow me to speak to the people."

After the chief captain gave Paul permission to speak to the people, Paul stood on the stairs and signaled the people with his hand, and the crowd was immediately silent. So Paul spoke to them in the Hebrew tongue.
And Paul said, "Men, brothers, and fathers hear my defense which I make to you now."
When they heard Paul speaking to them in the Hebrew, they remained silent.

And Paul said, "Truly I am a Jew, and I was born in Tarsus of Cilicia. Yet I was brought up in this city at the feet of Gamaliel. I was taught the strict laws of our fathers, and I am just as zealous toward our God as any of you who are here today.
I persecuted the followers of this way to death, binding and delivering both men and women into prisons.

As the high priest and all of the elders can also bear witness of me, of whom I also received letters for the brothers. And I went to Damascus to arrest and bring those people to Jerusalem to be punished.
Along the way to Damascus at about noon, a great light from heaven suddenly shone all around me.
And I fell to the ground, and heard a voice saying to me, '`Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me?´'
And I answered, "Who are you, Lord?" And he said to me, '`I am Jesus of Nazareth, whom you persecute.´'
And those who were with me also saw the light and they were afraid, but they did not hear the voice that spoke to me.
And I said, 'What can I do Lord?' And the Lord said to me, '`Rise up and go to Damascus, where you will be told of all the things which are appointed for you to do.´'
When I was blinded by the glory of that light, I was led by the hand by those who were with me to Damascus.
A devout man named Ananias who observes and obeys the law, who has the highest reputation among the Jews living there.
Came and stood before me and said, 'Brother Saul, receive your sight,' and at the same time I looked up and saw him.
And Ananias said, 'The God of our fathers has chosen you to know his will, and to see that Just One and hear the voice of his mouth.
For you will be his witness to all men of what you have seen and heard.
So now why do you delay? Rise up and be baptized, wash away your sins by calling on the name of the Lord.'
When I returned to Jerusalem, I was in a trance as I prayed in the temple.
And I saw Jesus saying to me, '`Hurry, and leave Jerusalem quickly because they will not receive your testimony about me.´'
And I said, 'Lord, they know that I imprisoned and beat those who believed in you in every synagogue.
When your martyr Stephen's blood was shed, I was also standing there consenting to his death, and I kept watch over the clothes of those who killed him.'
And Jesus said to me, '`Leave, because I am sending you far away from here to the Gentiles.´'"
They were listening to Paul until they heard this, then they began shouting and said, 'Remove this fellow from the earth, because he is not fit to live.'
As they cried out, they tore off their clothes and threw dust into the air.
The chief captain ordered Paul to be brought to the castle and cross examined by scourging, in order to find out why they cried out against him.
As they bound him with straps, Paul said to the centurion standing near him, "Is it lawful for you to scourge a Roman citizen without a trial?"
When the centurion heard this, he went to the chief captain and said, "Be careful of what you do next because this man is a Roman citizen."
Then the chief captain went to Paul and asked, "Are you a Roman citizen?" And Paul said, "Yes."
And the chief captain answered, "I paid a great sum to obtain the freedom of citizenship." And Paul said, "But I was born a free Roman."
Then those who would have examined him immediately left, and the chief captain was also afraid when he discovered that Paul was a Roman because he had arrested him.

The next day, because he wanted to know for certain why Paul was accused by the Jews. So, he turned him loose from his chains and ordered the chief priests and their council to appear. Then he brought Paul down and sat him before them.
Paul earnestly addressed the council and said, "Men and brothers, I have lived before God with a clear conscience to this day."
Then the high priest Ananias ordered those who stood near Paul to punch him in the mouth.
Then Paul said to Ananias, "God will destroy you, you whitewashed wall! You sit to judge me by the law, and order me to be beaten which is contrary to the law?"
And those who stood nearby said, "Do you revile God's high priest?"
Then Paul said, "Brothers, I did not know that he was the high priest for it is written, 'You must not speak evil of your people's rulers.'"

But when Paul realized that some of them were Sadducees and some were Pharisees, he cried out in the council and said, "Men and brothers, I am a Pharisee and the son of a Pharisee. It is because I hope for the resurrection of the dead that I am being called into question."
When Paul said this, an argument broke out between the Pharisees and the Sadducees and the crowd was divided.
For the Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, no angels, and no spirit but the Pharisees confess both.

Then there arose a great outcry among the council, and the Pharisee scribes struggled to get up and speak and they said, "We find no evil in this man, but if a spirit or an angel has spoken to him, let us not fight against God.

Then a great uproar arose, and the Roman chief captain was afraid that Paul would be pulled to pieces. So, he ordered his soldiers to go down and take him from the people by force and bring him into the castle.
The following night the Lord stood beside Paul and said, "`Cheer up Paul, because you have testified about me in Jerusalem, so you must also bear witness of me in Rome.´"
The next day, some of the Jews banded together and bound themselves under a curse and said, "We will not eat or drink until we have killed Paul!"
And there were more than forty men involved in this conspiracy.
The conspirators went to the chief priests and elders and said, "We have bound ourselves under a great curse, and we will not eat or drink until we have killed Paul.

So you and the council must ask the Roman chief captain to bring Paul down to you tomorrow. Tell him that you must further interrogate Paul, and we or whoever he stands close to will be ready to kill him.
When Paul's sister's son heard of their deceitful plan, he went to the castle and told Paul.
Then Paul summoned one of the centurions to him and said, "Bring this young man to the chief captain, because he has something to tell him.
So the centurion took him to the chief captain and said, "Paul the prisoner summoned me and asked me to bring this young man to you to tell you something."
Then the chief captain took the young man's hand and brought him into his private office and asked, "What do you want to tell me?"
And the young man said, "The Jews are planning to ask you to bring Paul down to the council tomorrow, under the pretense that they want to interrogate him further.

But you must not listen to them, because there are more than forty men planning to ambush him. They have all bound themselves with an oath, and they all said they will not eat or drink until they have killed Paul. And now they are ready to keep this promise if you send Paul to them."
Then the chief captain responded to the young man and let him leave and said, "Do not tell anyone else what you have told me!"
The chief captain summoned two centurions and said, "Prepare 200 soldiers, 70 cavalry, and 200 soldiers to go to Caesarea in the third hour of the night.
Provide animals for Paul to ride and escort him safely to Felix the governor."
And the chief captain wrote a letter to send with them.
And the letter stated, "Claudius Lysias sends greetings to the most excellent governor Felix.
I took an army to rescue Paul from the Jews when I discovered that he was a Roman citizen, because they would have killed him.
I tried to find out what they had accused Paul of, so I brought him to their council.
I realized Paul was accused over questions about their own law, but he was not charged with anything worthy of death or chains.
When I was told that the Jews planned to ambush Paul, I immediately sent him to you and ordered his accusers to repeat their accusations against him to you. Farewell."
Then the soldiers did as they were ordered and took Paul to Antipatris at night.
The next day they left him with the horsemen and returned to the castle.
When they arrived in Caesarea, they delivered the letter to the governor and also presented Paul to him.
After the governor read the letter, he asked Paul what province he was from, and the governor discovered that Paul was from Cilicia.
And the governor said, "I will hear your case when your accusers get here." So, the governor ordered Paul to be held in Herod's judgment hall.
Five days later, Ananias the high priest descended with the elders and a speaker named Tertullus, who informed Governor Felix of their charges against Paul.

When Paul was brought to court, Tertullus began accusing him and said, "Most noble Felix, since you arrived, we have enjoyed a great peace, and very worthy deeds have been done for this nation by your providence.
We have always gratefully accepted this everywhere most noble Felix.
But, even though I do not want to further burden you with tedious details, I pray you will mercifully hear a few words from us.
For we have found this man Paul to be a pestilence, who stirs up sedition among all the Jews throughout the world, and a ringleader of the Nazarene sect.
Paul tried to profane the temple, so we seized him and we would have judged him in accordance with our law.
But the chief captain Lysias came to us, and with great violence took him from our hands.
Lysias ordered Paul's accusers to come to you, so that by examining him yourself you may know everything that we have accused him of."
The other Jews also asserted and testified that these things were all true.

Then the governor motioned to Paul and asked him to speak, so Paul answered him and said, "Since I know that you have been a judge over this nation for many years, I will most cheerfully answer for myself.
In order for you to understand, I want you to know that it has only been twelve days since I went to Jerusalem to worship.
These people did not find me in the temple arguing with anyone, nor was I stirring up the people in the synagogues or the city.
Nor can they prove any of the things they are accusing me of.
But this I confess to you; I do worship the God of my fathers in a way which they call heresy. I believe in everything written in the law and in the prophets.
And I have the same faith toward God, which they themselves also have, and I believe that there will be a resurrection of the dead, both for the righteous and the unrighteous.
And I always try to maintain a clear conscience toward God and men.
Now after many years I have come to bring alms and offerings to my nation.
When some Jews from Asia found me in the temple after my purification, I was not stirring up the people nor creating an uproar.
If any of these men had any objections against me, they themselves should have brought me here before you.
So, let them now state what evil they found in me as I stood before their council.
Except for this one thing that I cried out about the resurrection of the dead, and that's why I have been called into question before you today."
Governor Felix had a good understanding of the way before he heard this, so he postponed the proceedings and said, "When Lysias the chief captain comes down, I will investigate your case further."
So Felix ordered a centurion to hold Paul but told him to allow him some liberty and to allow his acquaintances to visit and minister to him.
A few days later, Governor Felix and his Jewish wife Drusilla sent for Paul to hear about his faith in Christ.
As Paul spoke of righteousness, temperance, and the judgment to come, Felix trembled and answered him and said, "You may go now, but I will summon you later when the time is right."
Felix had also hoped that Paul would give him some money to set him free, so he sent for him quite often and spoke with him.
But after two years Porcius Festus replaced Felix as governor, and Felix wanted to curry favor with the Jews, so he left Paul in prison.
Three days after Governor Festus arrived in the province, he ascended from Caesarea to Jerusalem.
The high priest and the Jewish chief informed Festus about Paul and pressured him.
Because they wanted Festus to send Paul to Jerusalem, where they were planning to ambush and kill him.
But Festus answered them and said, "Paul should be kept in Caesarea, and I myself will be leaving to go there shortly.
So, which one of you is willing to go down there with me to accuse this man of any wickedness he may be guilty of."
After Governor Festus had been there for ten more days, he went down to Caesarea. The next day he sat on the judgment seat and ordered Paul to be brought in.
When Paul was brought in, the Jews who came down from Jerusalem stood all around him, and they made many unproven grievous complaints against him.
Paul answered for himself and said, "I have broken no Jewish laws, no temple laws, none of Caesar's laws, nor any other laws at all."
But Festus wanted to please the Jews and he answered Paul and asked, "Are you willing go up to Jerusalem to be judged for these things before me?"
Then said Paul, "I stand at Caesar's judgment seat where I should be judged, and as you very well know, I have done no wrong to the Jews.

For if I am an offender or I have committed anything worthy of death, I do not refuse to die. But if I have done none of these things they accuse me of, then no one can deliver me over to them. So, I appeal to Caesar."
Once Festus discussed this with the council, he answered Paul and said, "You have appealed to Caesar, so you will go to Caesar."
After a few days King Agrippa and Bernice came to Caesarea to greet Festus.
After they had been there a few days, Festus discussed Paul's cause with the king and said, "There is a man that Felix left here in prison.
About whom the chief priests and the Jewish elders informed me when I was in Jerusalem, and they want me to enter a judgment against him.

But I told them, it is not the Roman custom to execute a man, before he has faced his accusers and their charges face to face. Paul has the right to defend himself against the crimes he is accused of.
So the day after they got here, I sat on the judgment seat without delay and ordered Paul to be brought in.
When the accusers stood up, they made no legally criminal accusations against Paul that I thought they would accuse him of.
They merely questioned him about their own superstitions, and a dead man named Jesus whom Paul said was still alive.
And because I doubted the severity of such questions, I asked Paul if he would go to Jerusalem to be judged there about these things.
But Paul appealed his case to Caesar Augustus for a private hearing, so I ordered him to be held until I could send him to Caesar."
Then King Agrippa said to Governor Festus, "I would like to hear this man myself." And Festus said, "Then you will hear him tomorrow."
The next day, after Agrippa and Bernice arrived with great pomp, they entered the court room along with the chief captains and principal men of the city, and Festus ordered Paul to be brought in.

Then Festus said, "King Agrippa, and all the men who are present here with us, look at this man. The entire Jewish assembly has asked me, both here and in Jerusalem that I not allow Paul to live any longer.
But when I discovered that Paul had done nothing worthy of death, and that he himself has appealed to Caesar Augustus, I have decided to send him to Caesar.

But, I have nothing criminal to write to my Lord about. So, I have brought him before you, and especially before you O King Agrippa, so that after examination I would have something to write to Caesar about.
For it seems unreasonable to me, to send a prisoner to Caesar with no proof of the crimes laid out against him."
Then King Agrippa said to Paul, "You are permitted to speak for yourself." Then Paul stretched out his hand and answered for himself.
And Paul said, "King Agrippa, I will be happy to answer for myself before you today, I will touch on everything that the Jews have accused me of.
Especially since I know that you are an expert in all the questions about the Jewish customs, so I beg you to listen to me patiently.
All the Jews know that I have lived among my own nation in Jerusalem since I was a child.
Those who have known me from the beginning could testify if they wanted to, that I have lived as a Pharisee in the strictest sect of our religion.
Now I stand before you to be judged for my hope of the promise made to our fathers by God.
The same promise that all of our twelve tribes hope in is coming, as they intently serve God, day and night. King Agrippa, it is because of this hope, that the Jews have made accusations against me.
Why would you think that it is an incredible thing, that God could raise the dead?
I also honestly thought to myself at that time, that I should do everything I could to oppose the name of Jesus of Nazareth.
Which I also did in Jerusalem, when I confined many of the saints to prison after I received the authority from the chief priests. After they were put to death, I still spoke out against them.
I often punished them in every synagogue and forced them to blaspheme. I was so extremely angry with them, that I persecuted them even in strange cities.
But one day as I was on my way to Damascus with the full authority and commission from the chief priests.
At midday, O king, as I was on the way, I saw a light from heaven brighter than the sun, shining all around me and those who traveled with me.
When we all fell to the ground, I heard a voice speaking to me in Hebrew that said, '`Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me? It is hard for you to kick against the pricks!´'
And I said, 'Lord, who are you?' And he said, '`I am Jesus whom you persecute.´
`Get up and stand on your feet, because I have appeared to you to make you a minister and a witness of the things which you have already seen, and of the things which I will show you later.´
`I will deliver you from the people and from the Gentiles, to whom I now send you.´

`I am sending you to open their eyes, so that they may turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God. So that they may receive forgiveness for their sins, and an inheritance among those who are sanctified by their faith in me.´'
So, O King Agrippa, I was not disobedient to the heavenly vision.
But I first preached to those in Damascus and Jerusalem, then throughout all of Judea, and finally to the Gentiles, so they would repent and turn to God and do works worthy of repentance.
That's why the Jews seized me in the temple and tried to kill me.
So after I obtained help from God, I have continued to this day to witness to both small and great. And I have said nothing more than what the prophets and Moses said would happen.
For they said Christ would suffer, and he would be the first to rise from the dead, and he would show his light to the Jewish people and the Gentiles."
As Paul spoke for himself, Festus interrupted him and spoke out loudly and said, "Paul, you are beside yourself, too much learning has driven you mad."
But Paul answered Festus and said, "Most noble Festus, I am not mad and I speak sober and truthful words.
For I know that the king knows all about these things, and I can speak freely before him. I also know that none of these things are hidden from the king, because this was not done in a corner.
King Agrippa, do you believe in the prophets? For I know that you believe."
Then Agrippa said to Paul, "You have almost persuaded me to become a Christian."
And Paul said, "I would only ask God, that not only you but also everyone who hears me today would become what I am, except for these chains."
After Paul finished speaking, the king, the governor, Bernice, and everyone who sat with them got up.
When they left, they all talked among themselves and said, "This man has done nothing worthy of death or prison."
Then King Agrippa spoke to Festus and said, "Paul could have been set free if he had not appealed to Caesar."
After they decided that we should sail to Italy, they delivered Paul and some of the other prisoners to a centurion named Julius, who belonged to Augustus' garrison.
We boarded an Adramyttium ship bound for the coasts of Asia, and a Macedonian man Aristarchus of Thessalonica was with us.
The next day we landed at Sidon, where Julius treated Paul courteously and allowed him to go visit his friends to refresh himself.
When we left Sidon, we sailed below Cyprus because the winds blew against us.
After we sailed across the sea of Cilicia and Pamphylia, we arrived in the Lycian city of Myra.
Where the centurion found an Alexandrian ship sailing for Italy that he had us board.
After we sailed slowly for many days, we arrived off the coast of Cnidus. The scarce winds had slowed us down, so we sailed below the island of Crete near Salmone.
We had barely passed the coast, when we came to a place called the Fair Havens near the city of Lasea.
By now so much time had passed, that sailing had become dangerous because the fast was over and the stormy season had come, so Paul warned them.
Paul spoke to them and said, "Sirs, I can see that this voyage will suffer much damage and destruction, not only to the ship but also to our lives."
Nevertheless, the centurion believed the owner and master of the ship more than he believed Paul.

And because the harbor was unsuitable to winter over, most of the passengers decided go on because they thought they could make it to Phoenix for the winter. Phoenix was a harbor in Crete facing both southwest and northwest.
When the south winds began to blow softly, they thought their chance had come so they weighed anchor and sailed close to the coast of Crete.
But not long after they set sail, a tempestuous wind called a typhoon rose up against them.
When the ship was caught up by the wind it could not withstand it, so we let the storm drive it along.
We were running below an island named Cauda, and it took a lot of work just to secure the lifeboat.
After we hauled up the lifeboat, we used chains to reinforce the underside of the ship and fearing that we would run aground on the sandbars, we dropped our sails and were driven along.
We were being wildly tossed around by an extremely violent storm, so the next day we lightened the ship.
On the third day we threw out the ship's tackle with our own hands.
When neither the sun nor the stars appeared for many days, and we were being tossed around by this violent storm, we lost all hope that we would be saved.

But after they had all fasted for quite a while, Paul stood out in the middle of them and said, "Sirs, you should have listened to me when I said we must not leave Crete, and you would have avoided all this harm and loss.
And now I encourage you to cheer up, because none of you will lose your life, but the ship will be lost.
Because last night the angel of God to whom I belong and whom I serve, stood before me.
And the angel said, "Fear not Paul, you must be brought before Caesar. And look, God has given you the lives of everyone who sails with you.
So cheer up sirs, because I believe God and I believe what he has told me, will happen.
But, we will be stranded on some island."
On the fourteenth night we were still being driven up and down across the Adriatic Sea, and at about midnight the sailors decided that they were moving closer to land.
So they took soundings and found the water to be twenty fathoms deep. After they had gone a little further, they took soundings again and found it to be fifteen fathoms deep.
Then fearing that we would crash into the rocks, they threw out four anchors from the stern and prayed for daylight.
As the sailors prepared to flee the ship, they had lowered the lifeboat into the sea while pretending to throw out anchors from the bow of the ship.
But Paul spoke to the centurion and the soldiers and said, "Unless these men stay in the ship, you cannot be saved."
Then the soldiers cut the ropes to the lifeboat and set her adrift.
As daylight approached, Paul implored them all to eat and said, "This is the fourteenth day that you have fasted and eaten nothing.
So for the sake of your health, I beg you to eat because none of you will lose a single hair from your head."
After Paul spoke, he took some bread and gave thanks to God and broke it in the presence of them all, and he began to eat.
They were all cheerful after this, so they also began to eat.
And there was a total of 276 souls onboard that ship.
After they finished eating, they lightened the ship some more and threw some wheat out into the ocean.
At daybreak, even though they did not recognize the land they found a harbor with a beach, so they decided to run the ship aground if possible.
They pulled up the anchors and cut them loose and dropped them into the water, then they loosened the ropes that held the rudder. Finally, they hoisted the mainsail and made for the beach.
They struck a sandbar where the two seas met before they got to the beach and the ship ran aground. The bow was stuck fast and was unmovable, but the stern was broken apart by the violent waves.
The soldiers decided to kill the prisoners to keep them from swimming away and escaping.
But the centurion wanted to save Paul, so he stopped them and ordered those who could swim to jump into the water first and swim ashore.
And the rest took some boards and broken pieces of the ship as floats to swim ashore, and they all safely escaped to land.
After they escaped, they learned that the island was named Melita.
The barbaric people living there treated us kindly, and they built a fire and sheltered all of us since it was cold and raining.
When Paul gathered a bundle of sticks and laid them on the fire, a viper crawled out of the heat and fastened itself to his hand.

When the barbarians saw the venomous snake hanging on Paul's hand, they said among themselves, "There is no doubt that this man is a murderer, even though he has escaped the storm, vengeance will not allow him to live."
But Paul shook the snake into the fire and he felt no pain.

However when they looked at Paul's hand, it should have been swollen and he should have fallen down dead. But after they watched him for a long time, they saw that no harm had come to him, so they changed their minds and said that he was a God.
Publius the island's chief official received us at his estate nearby, where we were courteously allowed to stay for three days.
Then the father of Publius lay sick with a fever and a bloody stomach infection, so Paul entered and prayed over him, and laid his hands on him and he was healed.
After this, others on the island who had diseases also came to Paul and were healed.
These people also honored us with many honors, and they loaded us down with everything we needed when we left.
After three months we left on an Alexandrian ship, which had wintered over on the island, whose sign was Castor and Pollux (Greek and Roman half-brother gods).
We landed in Syracuse and stayed there for three days.
From there we weighed anchor and went to Rhegium, after we had been there for one day the south winds began to blow and the next day, we sailed to Puteoli.
Where we found some brothers who asked us to stay with them for seven days, and then we went to Rome.
When the brothers there heard about us, they came to meet us from as far away as the Appii Forum and the Three Taverns. When Paul saw them, he thanked God and he was encouraged.
When we arrived in Rome, the centurion delivered the prisoners to the captain of the guard, but Paul was allowed to live by himself with a Roman soldier to guard him.

Three days later, Paul called the chief Jews together, after they had come together, he said to them, "Men and brothers, even though I have committed no crime against the people or our fathers' customs, I was brought here as a prisoner from Jerusalem and delivered into the hands of the Romans.
Who, after they had examined me, would have let me go because they found no reason to put me to death.
But the Jews spoke against it, and I was forced to appeal to Caesar even though I had no accusations to make against my nation.
That's why I have asked to speak with you, it is because of the hope of Israel that I am bound with this chain.
And they said to him, "We have received no letters from Judea about you, nor have any of the brothers come to show or speak any harm about you.
But we do want to hear what you think about this sect, because we do know that it is spoken against everywhere."

After they picked a day, they made an appointment with him, and many came to visit him in his lodging from morning until evening. Where he explained and testified about the Kingdom of God, persuading them about Jesus, both from the Law of Moses and from the prophets.
And some believed what Paul said but some did not.
When they could not agree among themselves, they began to leave after Paul had spoken his final word and said, "The Holy Spirit spoke well to our fathers through Isaiah the prophet.
When he said, 'Go to these people and say, "You will hear and not understand, and you will see and not perceive."

For these people's hearts have grown callous, their ears can barely hear and their eyes are closed, otherwise they would see with their eyes and hear with their ears. Then they would understand with their heart and be converted and I would heal them.'
So let it be known that the salvation of God is sent to the Gentiles and they will hear it.
Then the Jews left after he said this, because they had a lot to discuss among themselves.
Paul lived in his own rented house for two whole years, and he received everyone who came to him.
Paul confidently preached to them about the Kingdom of God and taught them everything he knew about the Lord Jesus Christ, and no one forbid him to speak.
Paul was a servant of Jesus Christ, and he was called to be an apostle and separated by God to teach the gospel. While he was in Corinth he dictated a letter to the Christians in Rome.
And Paul's letter said, "God had previously promised this through his prophets in the holy scriptures.
In which it is written about God's son and our Lord Jesus Christ, who was one of David's descendants in the flesh.
Jesus was declared to be the powerful son of God in the Holy Spirit, by his resurrection from the dead.
And we have received the grace and apostleship from our Lord Jesus Christ to be faithfully obedient to our God among all the nations in his name.
Among which nations you are also called by our Lord Jesus Christ.
This invitation to be saints is extended to everyone in Rome who is loved by God. So I offer you grace and peace from God our father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
First, I must thank my God through Jesus Christ for all of you, so that people throughout the whole world will speak of your faith.
For God is my witness, whom I serve with my spirit by preaching the gospel of his son Jesus Christ, so that I may unceasingly mention you in my prayers.
By making a request in one way or another through God's will, for a prosperous journey to come visit you.
For I do long to see you, and impart some spiritual gift to you, so that you may be established.
In order for both you and I to be comforted together by our mutual faith.

And since I did not want you to be ignorant brothers, I have often planned to come visit you, but it has not been possible until now. And I hope to harvest the same fruit among you that I have harvested among the other Gentiles.
I am also indebted both to the Greeks and the Barbarians, and also to the wise and the unwise.
So, as much as my abilities allow, I am ready to preach the gospel to those of you who are in Rome.
For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ, because it is within God's power to give his salvation to everyone who believes, first to the Jews then also to the Greeks.
For the righteousness of God is revealed from beginning to end, for just as it is written, 'The righteous will live by faith.'
For God's anger is revealed from heaven against all men, whose ungodly failure to adhere to moral principles and their unrighteous rejection of the truth.
For that which may be known about God is obvious to them, because God has shown it to them.

For the invisible things of God since the creation of the world are clearly seen. And understanding by seeing the things that have been made through his eternal power and Godhead, so that they have no excuse.
Because even though they knew God, they did not glorify him as God, nor were they thankful and they became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened.
Even though they claimed to be wise, they became fools.
And they changed the glory of the incorruptible God into an image made to resemble a corruptible man, birds, four footed animals, and reptiles.
Therefore, God also gave them up to uncleanliness through the lusts of their own hearts, to dishonor their own bodies with one another.
Men who changed God's truth into a lie and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is forever blessed. Amen.
Because of this, God gave them up to vile affections, because even their women changed the natural things into unnatural things.
Men abandoned their natural relationships with women, and their lust burned toward one another. Men lusting for men which is unnatural, and they received what they deserved for their error.
And since they did not want to retain the knowledge of God in their mind, God gave them over to a depraved mind, to do those things which should not be done.
They were filled with all unrighteousness, fornication, wickedness, covetousness, spitefulness, and they were full of envy, murder, strife, and deceit. They are malignant gossiping whisperers.
They are backbiters, God haters, malicious, and arrogant boasters, and they invent all kinds of evil things and disobey their parents.
They are without understanding and they are promise breakers, without natural affection, implacable, and unmerciful.
They know that God's judgment says that those who do such things are worthy of death. For they not only do these things, but they also take pleasure in seeing others do these things."

And Paul continued dictating his letter which said, "Therefore it is inexcusable for whoever you are to judge others, because you condemn yourself by the way you judge others, because you do the same things as those you judge.
But we are sure that God's judgment is truthful and against those who do such things.
And will those of you who do such things, then judge those who do the same things, escape God's judgment?
Or do you despise the riches of God's goodness, tolerance, and long suffering, not knowing that the goodness of God leads you to repentance?
But because of your hard and unrepentant heart you store up anger for yourself for the day of anger and the revelation of God's righteous judgment.
God will give to every man in accordance with his deeds.
And God will give eternal life to those who patiently continue to do well and seek glory, honor, and immortality.
But those who are argumentative and obey unrighteousness instead of the truth, will receive indignation and anger.
Tribulation and anguish will be on every man's soul who does evil, first for the Jews and also for the Gentiles.
But glory, honor, and peace will be for every man who does good works, first for the Jews and also for the Gentiles.
God shows favoritism to no one.
For those who have sinned without the law will also perish without the law, and those who have sinned under the law will be judged by the law.
Because it is not those who just hear the law who are righteous before God, but it is those who do not break the law who will be justified.
For when the Gentiles, who do not have the law, do by their very nature the things contained in the law, are a law unto themselves even though they do not have the law.
So they show that the work of the law is written in their hearts, for their conscience also bears witness to this, and their thoughts either accuse or excuse each other.
On the day that God judges the secrets of men through Jesus Christ as I proclaim with my gospel.
Behold, you who are called a Jew, who also rest in the law and boast in God.
And those who know God's will and approve of his more excellent things, and those who are instructed by the law.
And those of you who confidently guide the blind and are a light for those who are in darkness.
You instruct the foolish and teach ignorant babes, and you have in the law a form of knowledge and truth.
So you who teach others, do you not also teach yourself? You preach that a man should not steal, so do you steal?
You teach that a man should not commit adultery, so do you commit adultery? You who abhor idols, do you commit sacrilege?
You who boast in the law, do you dishonor God by breaking the law?
For it is written, 'The name of God is blasphemed among the Gentiles because of you.'
For circumcision is honestly profitable if you keep the law, but if you break the law your circumcision is turned into uncircumcision.
So if the uncircumcised keep the law's righteousness, will his uncircumcision not be counted as circumcision?
And will not the uncircumcised who by his very nature satisfies the law, judge those of you who have the written law and are circumcised but you transgress against the law?
For a man's outwardly appearance does not make him a Jew, nor is the circumcision only outward and physical in the flesh.
But a man is a Jew, if he is inwardly circumcised in his heart and spirit and not by the written law, and his praise comes from God not men."
And Paul continued dictating his letter which said, "What advantages do the Jews have, or why is circumcision valuable?
They have many advantages in every way, mainly because God committed them to his inner sanctuaries.
So what if some of them did not believe? Will their disbelief make God's faithfulness ineffective and worthless?
God forbid: No! But yes, for God is true, every man is a liar, and it is written, 'So that God may be justified in every word that he speaks and overcome when he judges.'
But if our unrighteousness praises God's righteousness, what can we say? That God is unrighteous when he takes vengeance on us? Because I am speaking as a man.
God forbid, because how then would God judge the world?
But if God's truth and glory thrive more abundantly through my lie, why am I still judged as a sinner?
So why not say, as some have slanderously reported and said that we say, 'Let us do evil, so that good may come from it?' Then whose damnation is justified.
What then? Are we better than them? No, not in any way, because we have already proven that both the Jews and Gentiles are all under sin.
For it is written, 'No one is righteous, no, not even one.
No one who seeks God understands.
For together they have all gone out of their way to become unprofitable. There are none who do good, no, not even one.
Their throat is an open tomb. They use their tongues to deceive, and the poison of asps is under their lips.
Their mouth is full of cursing and bitterness.
Their feet are swift to shed blood.
They leave destruction and misery in their path.
And they do not know the ways of peace.
There is no fear of God before their eyes.'
Now we know that whatever the law says, it says to those who are under the law, so that every mouth may be silenced and the whole world may answer to God.
Therefore, no one will be justified in God's sight through the deeds of the law, because the knowledge of sin comes through the law.
But now God's righteousness outside of the law has been revealed through the witness of the law and the prophets.
Even the righteousness of God comes through faith in Jesus Christ to all of those who believe, for there is no difference between the two.
For all have sinned and come short of the glory of God.
We are freely justified by God's grace through the redemption in Christ Jesus.
God has sent his son Jesus Christ to appease his wrath and declare his righteousness through faith in the blood of Jesus, for the remission of past sins through God's tolerance.
And I say that God has declared his righteousness at this time, so that he may be just and to justify those who believe in Jesus.
So where then is boasting? By what law or works is it excluded? It is not excluded by law or by works, but by the law of our faith in Jesus Christ.
Therefore we can conclude that a man is justified through his faith outside of the deeds of the law.
Is God only the God of the Jews? Or is he not also the God of the Gentiles? Yes, he is also the God of the Gentiles.
Since there is only one God, who will justify the circumcised and the uncircumcised through their faith in Jesus Christ.
Do we then void the law through our faith? God forbid: No! But yes, we establish the law through our faith."
And Paul continued dictating his letter which said, "What can we say about our father Abraham who found his truth with God before the flesh?
For if Abraham was justified by his works, he would have been glorified, but not before God.
For what does the scripture say? Abraham believed God and he was found to be righteous.
Now for those who do the works the reward is not grace, but it is debt.
But anyone who does no works, but believes in the one who justifies the ungodly, his faith is counted as righteousness.
David also describes God's righteous blessings for those who do no works.
For David said, 'Blessed are those whose sins and wickedness are forgiven and covered.
And blessed is the man whom the Lord does not make accusations of sin.'
Is this blessing only for the circumcised, or is it also for the uncircumcised? For we say that faith was believed to be righteousness by Abraham.
So how then did God credit righteousness to Abraham, was it before or after his circumcision? It was before his circumcision not after.

And he received the sign of circumcision as a seal of the righteousness of faith which he had before he was circumcised, so that he could be the father of everyone who believes. And even though they are not circumcised, they may still be given righteousness.
For Abraham is not only the father of those who are circumcised, but he is also the father of those who walk in the faith, that our father Abraham had before he was circumcised.
For the promise that Abraham would become the heir of the world, did not come to Abraham or his descendants through the law, but through the righteousness of faith.
For if those who are of the law are the only heirs, then faith is made void and the promise is ineffective.
For the law brings anger because where there is no law, there is no transgression.

So the promise comes by faith, and it is through grace that the promise can be guaranteed to all descendants. This promise is not just for those who are of the law, but also for those who have the faith of Abraham, who is the father of us all.

For it is written, 'I have made you a father of many nations.' Because Abraham believed God who gives life to the dead, and calls into existence those things which do not already exist as if they were already there.
When all hope was lost, Abraham believed in the hope that he would become the father of many nations, according to what God had spoken and said, 'So shall your descendants be.'
Abraham was not weak in faith, and he considered his own body to be as good as dead when he was about a hundred years old, and he believed his wife Sarah's womb to be lifeless.
He did not stagger from disbelief of God's promise, but he was strong in faith, and he gave the glory to God.
Abraham was fully persuaded of everything that God had promised, which he was also able to perform.
Therefore, he was considered righteous.
Now it was not written, 'Righteousness was credited to Abraham,' just for the sake of Abraham alone.
But righteousness is also to be credited to us, if we believe in the one who raised our Lord Jesus Christ from the dead.
For Jesus was delivered over to death for our sins and was then raised up again for our justification."
And Paul continued dictating his letter which said, "So when we are justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ.
Through Christ we also have access by faith into this grace in which we stand and rejoice in the hope of God's glory.
And not only that, but we also glory in suffering, because we know that suffering brings patience.
Patience brings experience, and experience brings hope.
And hope makes us unashamed, because God's love is poured into our hearts by God's gift of the Holy Spirit.
For when we were still without strength, Christ died for the ungodly at just the right time.
For scarcely will someone die for a righteous man, but perhaps some may have the courage to die for a good man.
But God showed us his love, in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.
But much more than that, since we are now justified by his blood, we will be saved from God's anger through Christ.

For if we were God's enemies, and we were reconciled to God by the death of his son Jesus Christ. And since we are now reconciled to God, how much more will we be saved through the life of Jesus Christ!
And not only that, but we also rejoice in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom we have now received the atonement.
So sin and death entered the world because of one man, and death was then passed on to all men because all have sinned.
For sin was in the world before the law, but sin is not alleged when there is no law.
Nevertheless death reigned from Adam to Moses, even over those whose sin did not resemble Adam's transgression. For Adam is the figure of the one who was to come.

But the free gift from God is not like the offense. For if many died because of the sin of one man, how much more did God's grace and his gift which comes through one man, Jesus Christ who has generously his given life to many.
And not only is this gift nothing at all like the one who sinned, because the judgment that followed one sin brought condemnation, but this free gift is given to justify the sins of many.
For if by one man's offense death reigned through that one man, how much more will those who receive an abundance of grace and righteousness reign in life through this one man, Jesus Christ!
Therefore since one man's offense brought judgment and condemnation to all men, so will the righteousness of one man give the free righteous gift of life to all men.
For just as one man's disobedience made many into sinners, so will the obedience of one man make many righteous.
Besides that, the law entered to increase the offense. But where sin increased, grace increased much more abundantly.
So that just as sin has reigned until death, so also will grace reign through righteousness to secure eternal life through our Lord Jesus Christ."
And Paul continued dictating his letter which said, "Well then what can we say? Should we continue in sin, so that grace may abound?
God forbid: No! How can we who are dead to sin, live in sin any longer?
Do you not know that those of us who were baptized into Jesus Christ were also baptized into his death?
Therefore we are buried with him by baptism into death, so that just as Christ was raised up from the dead by the glory of the father, we may also walk in this new life.
For if we have been united together with Jesus in his death, we will also be united with him in his resurrection.
We know that our old self was crucified with Christ, so that the body of sin was destroyed and that from now on we will not serve sin.
For the dead are freed from sin.
Now if we are dead with Christ, we believe that we will also live with him.
Knowing that Christ was raised from the dead and can no longer die, because death has no authority over him.
For since he died, he died to sin once and for all, but since he lives, he lives for God.
Likewise you may also count yourselves as indeed dead to sin, but alive to God through our Lord Jesus Christ.
So do not let sin reign in your mortal body, that makes you obey its lusts.

Do not surrender parts of your body as unrighteousness instruments of sin but yield to God just as those who are brought from death to life and surrender your body parts as instruments of righteousness to God.
For sin will have no authority over you, because you are not under the law, you are instead under grace.
What then? Shall we sin because we are under grace but not under the law? God forbid: No!

Do you not know that whoever you offer yourselves to as obedient servants, you are a servant to the one you obey, whether you are a servant of sin which leads to death, or a servant of obedience which leads to righteousness?
But thank God, that even though you were once the servants of sin, you have wholeheartedly obeyed the new form of doctrine which you were given.
Since then you were freed from sin, and you have become the servants of righteousness.

I speak as a man because I understand the weakness of your flesh. For just as you offered the parts of your body as servants to uncleanliness and from one immorality to another, you should now offer the parts of your body as servants to righteousness which leads to holiness.
For when you were the servants of sin, you were free from righteousness.
What fruit did you harvest from those things which you are now ashamed of? For the final end of those things is death.
But now that you are free from sin, and have become God's servants, your fruit is holiness, and the final outcome is everlasting life.
For the wages of sin is death, but God's free gift is eternal life through our Lord Jesus Christ."
And Paul continued dictating his letter which said, "Brothers who know the law, do you not know that the law only has authority over a man as long as he is alive?
For a woman's husband is only bound by the law to be her husband as long as he is alive, but she is by law released from her husband if he dies.

So then, if while her husband is still alive she marries another man, she will be called an adulteress. But if her husband dies, she is free from that law and she is not an adulteress even though she has married another man.

Therefore my brothers, you have also become dead to the law through the body of Christ, so that you could be married to the one who is raised from the dead, so that we could bring forth fruit for God.
For when we lived in the flesh, the motions of our sins in the law worked in our bodies to bring forth fruit for death.
But now since we have died to what held us we have been delivered from the law, so that we could serve in a new spirit, and not in the old letter of the law.
What then can we say? Is the law sin? God forbid: No! I did not know about sin except through the law, because I would not have known about lust except through the law that said, 'Do not covet.'
But sin, worked all types of lust in me through the commandment. For without the law sin is dead.
For I was alive without the law once, but when the commandments came, sin revived and I died.
And the commandment which I thought was meant to ordain life actually brought death.
For sin deceived me through the commandment, and it killed me.
Therefore the law is holy and the commandment is holy, just, and good.

So was that which is good then made to be death to me? God forbid: No! But sin, so that it might be exposed as sin, produced death in me through that which is good, so that through the commandment sin might become extremely sinful.
For we know that the law is spiritual, but I am carnal and I was sold under sin.
For I do that which I do not allow, because what I want to do I do not do, but what I do is what I hate.
If then I do what I do not want to do, I consent that the law is good.
So it is no longer me who does it, but it is the sin living within me that does it.
For I know that nothing good lives within my flesh, because I have the will present within me to do that which is good, but I cannot.
For the good that I want do, I do not do, but the evil which I do not want to do, is what I do.
Now if I do what I do not want to do, it is no longer me who does it, but the sin that lives within me that does it.
So I found that in the law, when I want to do good that evil is present within me.
For the inner man within me delights in the law of God.
