But I see another law in my body at war with the law of my mind, and bringing me into captivity to the law of sin which is in my body.
O I am a wretched man! Who will deliver me from the body of this death?
I thank God through our Lord Jesus Christ. So then with my mind I serve the law of God, but with my flesh I serve the law of sin."
And Paul continued dictating his letter which said, "Therefore, there is no condemnation of those who walk in the spirit with Jesus Christ, and those who are not in the flesh.
For the law of the spirit of life in Jesus Christ has made me free from the law of sin and death.

For what the law could not do because it was weak through the flesh, God sent his own son Jesus Christ to atone for the sin in the likeness of sinful flesh, and Jesus was condemned for the sin of the flesh.
So that the righteousness of the law can be satisfied in those of us who walk in the spirit and not in the flesh.
For those who chase after the flesh think about the things of the flesh, but those who chase after the spirit think about the things of the spirit.
For to be carnally minded is death, but to be spiritually minded is life and peace.
Because the carnal mind is hostile to God, for the carnal mind is not subject to the laws of God, nor can it be.
So then, those who are in the flesh cannot please God.
But you are not in the flesh for you are in the spirit, so the spirit of God lives in you. For if a man does not have the spirit of Christ, he does not belong to Christ.
And if Christ is in you, the body is dead because of sin, but the spirit is life because of righteousness.

But if the spirit of the one who raised Jesus Christ from the dead is alive in you, then the one who raised Jesus from the dead will also give life to your mortal bodies through his spirit that lives in you.
Therefore brothers, we are not indebted to the flesh, and we are not required to live according to the flesh.
For you must die if you live according to the flesh, but if you allow the deeds of the body to die through the spirit, you will live.
For those who are led by the spirit of God, are the sons of God.
So you have not received the spirit of bondage that returns you to fear, but you have received the spirit of adoption, by which we cry, 'Abba! Father!'
The spirit itself testifies with our spirit that we are God's children.
And if we are his children, then we are God's heirs and joint heirs with Christ. So, if we suffer with him, we may also be glorified together with him.
For I estimate that our present sufferings, are incomparable to the glory which will be revealed in us.
For the worldly creature waits in earnest expectation for what materializes from the sons of God.
The worldly creature was made subject to vanity, not willingly but because of the one who subjugated it in hope.
Because the creature itself will also be delivered from the bondage of corruption into the glorious liberty of the children of God.
For we know that the whole creation groans and labors in pain together until now.
And it is not just them, but it is us as well who have the first fruits of the spirit, we even groan inside of ourselves waiting for the adoption, in other words, the redemption of our body.
For we are saved by hope, but hope that is seen is not hope, because why would a man hope for what he has already seen?
But if we hope for what we do not see, then we wait patiently for it.
Likewise the spirit also helps us with our weaknesses, because we do not know what we should pray for, so the spirit himself intercedes on our behalf with groans too deep for words.
And the one who searches hearts knows what is in the mind of the spirit, for the spirit himself intercedes on our behalf according to the will of God.
And we know that all things work together for the good of those who love God, and those who are called in accordance with God's purpose.
For those whom God knew beforehand were also predestined to be conformed to the image of his son Jesus, so that he would be the firstborn of many brothers.
Besides that, those whom God predestined to be his children, he also justified, and those whom he justified, he also glorified.
What then can we say about these things? And If God is for us, then who can be against us?
God did not spare his own son, but he delivered him up for all of us, so how can he not also freely give us all things through Jesus?
Who can charge anything against God's elect? For it is God who justifies.
Who can condemn us? It is Christ who died and was raised from the dead, and he is at the right hand of God making intercession for us.
Who will separate us from the love of Christ? Will tribulation, distress, persecution, famine, nakedness, peril, or the sword separate us from the love of Christ?
For it is written, 'But for your sake we face death all day long, and we are just sheep for the slaughter. (Psalms 44:22)'
No, in all of these things we are more than conquerors through Jesus who loved us.
For I am convinced that neither death, life, angels, nations, powers, present things, nor things to come.
Nor height, nor depth, nor any other worldly creature will be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in our Lord Jesus Christ."
And Paul continued dictating his letter which said, "I speak the truth in Christ, I do not lie, my conscience also bears my witness in the Holy Spirit.
For I have great sadness and continuous sorrow in my heart.
Because I could wish that I myself were cursed and cut off from Christ for the sake of my brothers, my family, and my own flesh and blood.
Who are the Israelis to whom the adoption, glory, covenants, the giving of the law, the service of God, and the promises pertain.
They are the fathers from whom Christ descended, and Christ is God overall and blessed forever. Amen!
It is not as if God's word has had no effect. For not all of Israel's descendants are Israel.
Nor is it because they are descendants of Abraham that are they all God's children: 'because Isaac and his descendants will be called to build a great nation.' (Genesis 21:12)
That is to say, those who are the children of the flesh are not God's children, but it is the children of the promise who are counted as the descendants.
For this is what the promise says, 'I will return in the spring, and your wife Sarah will give you a son.' (Genesis 18:10)
It is not only this, but Rebecca's children who were also conceived by one man, our father Isaac.
But it is for the unborn children who have done no good or evil, so that God's plan of election might stand, not from works but from the one who calls.
It was said to Rebekah, 'And the eldest son will serve the younger one.' (Genesis 25:23)
For it is written, 'I have loved Jacob, but I have hated Esau.' (Malachi 1:2-3)
What then can we say? Is there unrighteousness with God? God forbid: No!
For God said to Moses, 'I will have mercy for those to whom I will have mercy, and I will have compassion for those to whom I will have compassion.' (Exodus 33:19)
So then it does not depend on what a man wants or does, but on God who shows mercy.
For the scriptures say to Pharaoh, 'But I have allowed you to stay, in order to show you my power, so that my name can be proclaimed everywhere on earth.' (Exodus 9:16)
Therefore God has mercy for whoever he wants to have mercy, and he hardens whoever he wants to harden.
Then one of you will ask me, 'So why does God still find fault? For who can resist his will?'
No O man, for who are you to speak against God? Will the thing that was formed say to the one who formed it, 'Why have you made me this way?'
Does the potter not have the power over a lump clay, to make one a bowl to honor and another a bowl to dishonor?
What if God were willing to show his anger and make his power known, after enduring much suffering for a long time with the bowls of anger fitted for destruction.
So that God might make known the riches of his glory on the bowls of mercy, which he had previously prepared for glory.
Including those of us whom he has called, not only from the Jews but also from the Gentiles?
But as God also said in Hosea, 'I will have mercy on her even though she does not deserve mercy. And I will say to those who were not my people, you are my people!' (Hosea 2:23)
And someday in the place where it was said to them, 'You are not my people,' is where they will be called the children of the living God.
For Isaiah also cries out about Israel, 'Even though Israel's people are as numerous as the sands on the beach, only a small remnant will return.' (Isaiah 10:20-23)
For God will finish the work in righteousness, because the Lord will make short work of his fulfillment of the scriptures on the earth.
And as Isaiah said before, 'If the Lord of Hosts had not left us a very small remnant, we would have become just like Sodom and Gomorrah.' (Isaiah 1:9)
What then can we say? That the Gentiles who did not pursue righteousness, have even attained the righteousness of faith.
But Israel, which followed after the law of righteousness, has not attained the law of righteousness.
Why? Because they did not seek righteousness by faith, but they believed it came through the works of the law. For they stumbled over a stumbling block.
For it is written, 'Behold I have laid a stumbling block and a rock of offense in Zion, and whoever believes in Jesus Christ will not be ashamed.'"
And Paul continued dictating his letter which said, "Brothers, my heart's desire and my prayer to God is for Israel to be saved.
For I testify for those who have a zeal for God, but their zeal is not based on knowledge.
For they are ignorant of God's righteousness, and they go around trying to establish their own righteousness, for they did not submit themselves to God's righteousness.
For Christ is the end of the law of righteousness for everyone who believes.
For Moses describes the law's righteousness when he wrote, 'You must live by and obey my laws and judgments because I am the Lord.' (Leviticus 18:5)

But the righteousness which comes through faith speaks to the wise and says, 'Do not say in your heart, "Who will ascend into heaven and retrieve it for us?"' (Deuteronomy 30:12) For you do not need to bring Christ down from above.
Or do not say, 'Who will sail across the sea and retrieve it for us?' (Deuteronomy 30:13) For you do not need to raise up Christ from the dead again.
But what does it say? 'The word is very near to you; it is in your mouth and in your heart. (Deuteronomy 30:14) For this is the word of faith which we preach.
That if you confess the Lord Jesus with your mouth and believe in your heart that God has raised him from the dead, you will be saved.
For you believe with your heart and you are made righteous, and you confess with your mouth, and you are saved.
For the scripture says, 'Whoever believes in him will not be ashamed!' (Isaiah 28:16)
For there is no difference between the Jews and the Greeks because the same Lord is the Lord over everyone, and he gives richly to those who call on him.
For whoever calls on the name of the Lord will be saved.
So how can they call on Jesus if they do not believe in him? And how can they believe in Jesus if they have not heard of him? And how will they hear of Jesus without a preacher?
And how can they preach if they are not sent? For it is written, 'How beautiful are the feet of those who preach peace and salvation on the mountains and bring good news of good will!' (Isaiah 52:7)
But they have not all obeyed the gospel. For Isaiah says, 'Lord, who believed our report?' (Isaiah 53:1)
So then faith comes by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.
But I ask, 'Have they not heard?' Yes, they honestly did hear, they were heard throughout all the earth, and their words went the ends of the world.
So I ask, 'Did Israel not understand?' First Moses says, 'I will make them jealous with people who are not a nation, and I will provoke them to anger with a foolish nation.' (Deuteronomy 32:21)
But Isaiah is very bold and says, I was found by those who did not look for me, and I was made obvious to those who did not ask for me.
And Isaiah spoke of Israel and said, 'I have held out my hands all day long to a disobedient and rebellious people.'"(Isaiah 65:2)

And Paul continued dictating his letter which said, "So I ask you, 'Has God thrown away his people?' God forbid: No! For I am also an Israelite and a descendant of Abraham, from the tribe of Benjamin.
God has not thrown away his people whom he knew beforehand. Do you not remember what the scriptures say about Elijah? How he spoke to God against Israel and said,
'Lord, the Israelis have forsaken your covenant, torn down your altars and killed your prophets. Now I am the only one left, and they want to take my life away as well. (1 Kings 19:10)'
But what was God's answer to Elijah? God said, 'But I have 7,000 people left in Israel who have not bowed to Baal or kissed him with their lips. (1 Kings 19:18)'
So even back then there was also a remnant who were chosen by grace.

And if they were chosen by grace, then is it no longer because of their works, otherwise grace is no longer grace. But if they were chosen by works, then it is no longer grace, otherwise work is no longer work.
What then? Israel has failed to obtain that which he was seeking, but the elect have obtained it and the rest were blinded.
For this is the way it is written, 'God has given them a sleepy spirit, they have eyes that could not see, and ears that would not hear to this very day. (Isaiah 29:10) and (Deuteronomy 29:4)'
And David says, 'Let their table become a snare before them, and let what should have been for their benefit become a trap.
Let their eyes be darkened, so that they cannot see, and make their body shake continuously. (Psalm 69:22-23)'
So then I Paul ask, 'Has Israel stumbled and fallen beyond redemption?' God forbid: No! But rather salvation has come to the Gentiles through their fall, to provoke Israel's jealousy.
Now if Israel's fall means riches for the world, and their diminishing means riches for the Gentiles, how much greater will Israel's fullness bring?
For I Paul speak to you Gentiles since I am the Apostle of the Gentiles, and I magnify my office.
And it is my hope that if I can provoke my own people's jealousy, that some of them might be saved.
For if they cast away their reconciliation with the world, what will they receive from Israel but life from the dead?
For if the first fruit is holy, the rest is also holy, and if the root is holy, so are the branches.
And if some of the branches are broken off, and you who are a branch of a wild olive tree were grafted in among them, then you will share in the nourishment of the root and fatness of the olive tree.
So do not boast against the branches. But if you do boast, remember you do not feed the root, the root feeds you.
Then you will say, 'The branches were broken off, so that I could be grafted in.'
Well, they were broken off because of disbelief, but you stand by faith. So do not be proud and conceited, but fear God.
For if God did not spare the natural branches, be warned, he will not spare you either.
Therefore behold, the goodness and severity of God is on those who fell, but his goodness will be toward you, if you continue in his goodness. Otherwise, you also will be cut off.
And if they do not continue to endure in disbelief, they will be grafted back in because God can graft them back in again if he wants.

For if you were cut out of the olive tree which is wild by nature, and unnaturally grafted into a good olive tree, how much more will those who are the natural branches, be grafted into their own olive tree?

So brothers, I would not want you to be ignorant of this mystery, otherwise you might be taken in by your own conceit. Because the blindness has in part happened to Israel, so that the fullness of the Gentiles can come in.
So that all of Israel can be saved, for it is written, 'A deliverer will come from Zion and turn away the ungodliness from Jacob.
For this is my covenant with them, when I take away their sins. (Isaiah 59:20-21) and (Isaiah 27:9)'
And regarding the gospel, they are enemies for your sakes, but as for the election, they are beloved for the sake of the fathers.
For God does not regret his gifts and callings.
For even though in times past you did not believe God, you have still obtained mercy even during your disbelief.
Even so the Israelis and the Gentiles at times also did not believe, so that they may obtain God's mercy just like you.
For God has concluded that they are all in disbelief, so that he can have mercy on everyone.
O the depth of the richness of both God's wisdom and his knowledge! How unsearchable are God's judgments, and his past ways are undiscoverable!
For who knows the mind of the Lord, or who has been his counsellor?
Or who has given to God first, so that God must repay him?
For all things are of him, through him, and to him and God's glory lasts forever! Amen!"

And Paul continued dictating his letter which said, "Therefore brothers, I beg you because of God's mercies, that you present your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and acceptable to God, which is your reasonable service.
Do not conform to this world but be transformed by renewing your mind. So that you may prove what is the good, acceptable, and perfect will of God.
For by the grace given to me, I say to every man among you, 'Do not think more highly of yourself than you should, but think soberly about how God has given every man a measure of his faith.'
For as we have many members in one body, and all members do not have the same office.
So we who are many, are one in the body of Christ, and every one of us are members of each other.
We all have different gifts, which were given to us through grace, and if it is prophecy, let us prophesy in proportion to our faith.
Or if it is ministry let us minister, or if we are teachers let us teach.
Or if it is encouragement let us encourage, or if it is giving let us give with simplicity, or if it is leadership let us rule with diligence, or if it is mercy let us show mercy with cheerfulness.
Let love be without deceit. Abhor that which is evil and hold loyally to that which is good.
Be kind and affectionate toward one another with brotherly love and prefer honoring one another.
Do not be dull and lazy in business but serve the Lord with a fervent spirit.
Rejoice in hope, be patient in tribulation, and instantly continue in prayer.
Distribute the necessities to the saints and be hospitable.
Bless those who persecute you, bless others and do not curse.
Rejoice with those who rejoice, and weep with those who weep.
Be of the same mind toward one another. Do not think of proudful high things but spend your time with men who are low in stature, your conceit does not make you wise.
Do not repay a man evil for evil. Provide honest things in sight of all men.
If it is possible, as much as it in you, live peaceably with all men.
Dearly beloved, do not avenge yourselves, but rather give God's anger a place, because it is written, 'The Lord says, "Vengeance and repayment is mine. (Deuteronomy 32:35)"'
Therefore, if your enemy is hungry, feed him. If he is thirsty, give him something to drink, because doing this will pile coals of fire on his head.
Do not be overcome by evil but overcome evil with good."
And Paul continued dictating his letter which said, "Let every soul be subject to the higher powers. For there is no power except that which comes from God, the powers that exist are ordained by God.
Therefore whoever resists the powers, resists the legal decree of God, and those who resist will receive their own damnation.
For rulers are not a terror to good works, but to the evil. Do you not want to be unafraid of those in power? Then do what is good, and you will have praise from the powers that be.

For the one in power is God's minister to you for your good. But if you do that which is evil, be afraid because he does not bear the sword in vain, because he is God's minister, he is a revenger to execute anger against whoever does evil.
Therefore you must submit to authority, not only for anger, but also for the sake of your conscience.
Because you must also pay tribute, for they are God's ministers and they continuously attend to this very thing.

So give to all that which they are due, give tribute to those to whom tribute is due, give payment to those to whom payment is due, give fear to those to whom fear is due, and give honor to those to whom honor is due.
Owe nothing to anyone but love one another because whoever loves others has satisfied the law.

For the commandments say, 'Do not commit adultery! Do not kill! Do not steal! Do not bear false witness! Do not covet! (Exodus 20:13-17) and (Deuteronomy 5:17-21)' And if there were just one other commandment, it would be briefly understood by this saying, 'You must love your neighbor as yourself! (Leviticus 19:18)'
Love works no ill will toward his neighbor, and that's why love satisfies the law.
And since you know that the time is now, then you know that it is high time for you to awaken from your sleep, because our salvation is now nearer than it was when we first believed.
The night is nearly over and the day is here, so let us throw off the works of darkness and put on the armor of light.
Let us walk honestly as in the day, not in rioting and drunkenness, not in whoring and promiscuity, and not in conflict and envy.
But put on the armor of the Lord Jesus Christ and make no provision for the flesh or satisfy its lusts."
And Paul continued dictating his letter which said, "Receive those who are weak in faith without doubtful disputes.
For one who is weak in faith may believe that he can eat anything, and another who is weak may eat only herbs.
Do not let those who eat despise those who do not eat, and do not let those who do not eat judge those who eat, because God has received him.
Who are you to judge another man's servant? To his own master he stands or falls. Yes, he will be upheld because God can make him stand.
One man regards a certain day above the others, while another man considers every day to be alike. Each man must be fully convinced in his own mind.

Whoever regards a day as special does so to the Lord, and whoever does not regard the day does so to the Lord. Whoever eats does so to the Lord and gives thanks to God, and whoever abstains from eating does so to the Lord and gives thanks to God.
For none of us live just for ourselves, and no one dies by themselves.
For if we live, we live for the Lord, and if we die, we die for the Lord, so whether we live or die we belong to the Lord.
For to this end, Christ both died and rose from the grave and was revived, so that he might be Lord of both the dead and the living.
So why do you judge your brother, or why do you think of your brother as nothing? For we will all stand before the judgment seat of Christ.
For it is written, 'The Lord says, "As I live, every knee will bow, and every tongue will swear allegiance to me. (Isaiah 45:23)"
So then each one of us will give an accounting of ourselves to God.
Therefore, let us no longer judge one another, but rather judge this way, let no man put an obstacle to understanding or a reason to fall in his brother's way.
I am completely convinced by the Lord Jesus, that nothing is unclean in itself. But if anyone thinks anything is unclean to him, then it is unclean to him.
If your brother is grieved by what you eat, you are no longer acting charitably. So do not destroy those for whom Christ died with your food.
Do not let what you consider good to be spoken of as evil.
For the Kingdom of God is not meat and drink, but it is righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit.
For whoever serves Christ in this way is acceptable to God, and approved of by men.
Therefore, let us pursue the things which make for peace, and the things which allow us to instruct one another.
Do not destroy the work of God simply for food. All food is indeed pure, but it is evil for a man who eats to become a stumbling block to others.
It is not good to eat meat, drink wine, nor do anything else which makes your brother stumble, or offends or makes him weak.
Do you have faith? Then have it privately before God. Happy are those who do not condemn themselves for the things which they allow.
But those who doubt are condemned if they eat, because they do not eat from faith and whatever is not from faith is sin."
And Paul continued dictating his letter which said, "We who are strong should bear the infirmities of the weak, but not to please ourselves.
Let each one of us please our neighbor for his good and his own welfare.
For even Christ did not please himself, but as it is written, 'The disrespect of those who despise you has fallen on me. (Psalm 69:9)'
For whatever was written in the past was written for our instruction, so that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.
Now may the God of patience and consolation grant you the peace to be in harmony with one another in Jesus Christ.
So that all of you may with one mind and one mouth glorify God the father of our Lord Jesus Christ.
Therefore receive one another, as Christ also received us for the glory of God.
Now I tell you that Jesus Christ became a minister of the circumcised for God's truth, to confirm the promises made to the fathers.

So that the Gentiles could glorify God for his mercy. For it is written, 'O Lord, that's why I will give thanks to you among the heathen and sing praises to your name. (Psalm 18:49) and (2 Samuel 22:50)'
And again it is written, 'O nations rejoice with his people. (Deuteronomy 32:43)'
And again it is written, 'Praise the Lord, all you Gentiles, and all you people, applaud him. (Psalm 117:1)'
And again Isaiah says, 'The root of Jesse will stand like a flag for the people. The Gentiles will seek him, and his resting place will be glorious. (Isaiah 11:10)'
Now may the God of hope fill you with pure joy and peace in believing, so that you may abound in hope through the power of the Holy Spirit.
And now my brothers, I myself am also convinced that you are also full of goodness, filled with knowledge, and you are also able to reprimand one another.
However brothers, I have written more boldly to you on some issues to remind you, because of the grace that God has given me.
So that I could be the minister of Jesus Christ to teach the gospel of God to the Gentiles, so that the Gentiles could become an acceptable offering to God, sanctified by the Holy Spirit.
So that I may glory through Jesus Christ in those things which pertain to God.
For I do not have the courage to speak of anything which Christ has not worked through me, leading the Gentiles to obedience, by word and deed.
Through mighty signs and wonders, by the power of the of God's Spirit, so that from Jerusalem, and all the way around to Illyricum, I have fully preached the gospel of Christ.
Yes, I have struggled to preach the gospel where Christ was unknown, otherwise I would be building on another man's foundation.
But it is written, 'And those who were not told about him will see, and those who have not heard of him will understand. (Isaiah 52:15)'
That's why I have often been hindered from coming to you.
But now there is no other unvisited place for me around here, and I have had a great desire for many years to come visit you.
So when I travel to Spain, I will come visit you, because I trust that after I have been in your company for a while, that will you see to my needs and help me with my journey.
But right now I am going to Jerusalem to minister to the saints.
For the people of Macedonia and Achaia, were pleased to contribute to the poor saints in Jerusalem.
It honestly pleased them and they owed it to them, for if the Gentiles share in their spiritual things, then it is also their duty to help minister to them with material things.
Therefore after I have done this and delivered this fruit to them, I will come visit you on my way to Spain.
And I am sure that when I come, I will come with the full blessing of the gospel of Jesus Christ.
Now brothers, I beg you for the sake of the Lord Jesus Christ and the love of the Holy Spirit, that you join in my struggle by praying to God for me.
So that I may be delivered from those who do not believe in Judea, and that my service in Jerusalem may be accepted by the saints there.
So that by God's will, I may come to you with joy, and we may all be refreshed together.
Now may the God of peace be with you all. Amen."
And Paul finished dictating his letter which said, "I commend to you our sister Phebe, a servant of the church in Cenchrea.
Please receive her in the Lord in a manner worthy of the saints, and assist her with whatever she needs from you, because she has helped many, including myself.
Greetings to Priscilla and Aquila my helpers in Christ Jesus.
Who have risked their own necks to save my life, and I give thanks not only to them, but also to all Gentile churches.
Likewise I greet the churches who meet in their houses. I send salutations to my well beloved Epaenetus, who was the first convert to Christ in Achaia.
Greetings to Mary, who has worked hard for us.
Salutations to Andronicus and Junia, my next of kin and my fellow prisoners, who are notable among the apostles, who were also in Christ before me.
Greetings to Amplias my beloved in the Lord.
Salutations to Urbane, our helper in Christ, and my beloved Stachys.
Salutations to Apelles approved in Christ. Salutations to those who are of Aristobulus' household.
Salutations to my Herodion family. Greetings to those who are of the household of Narcissus who are in the Lord.
Salutations to Tryphena and Tryphosa, who labor in the Lord. Salutations to the beloved Persis, who has labored much in the Lord.
Salutations to Rufus chosen in the Lord, and his mother who has also been a mother to me.
Salutations to Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermas, Patrobas, Hermes, and the brothers who are with them.
Salutations to Philologus, Julia, Nereus and his sister, and Olympas and all the saints who are with them.
Salutations to all of you with a holy kiss. Salutations to the churches of Christ.
Now I beg you brothers, watch out for those who cause divisions and offenses contrary to the doctrine which you have learned, and avoid them.
For those people do not serve our Lord Jesus Christ, but their own stomach, and they use good words and fair speeches to deceive the hearts of the simple.
And everyone abroad has heard of your obedience, so I am glad for you. But I want you to be wise about what is good, and innocent about what is evil.
And the God of peace will soon bruise Satan under your feet. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you. Amen.
Salutations to Timothy my fellow worker, and Lucius, Jason, and my next of kin Sosipater.
And I Tertius, who wrote Paul's words in this letter, also send my salutations to you in the Lord.
Salutations to Gaius who hosted me and the whole church. Salutations to Erastus the eunuch of the city and Quartus a brother.
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.
Now to the one with the power to establish you in accordance with my gospels, and Jesus Christ's preaching, and the revelation of the mysteries, which have been kept secret since the world began.

But now it has become obvious through the prophets' scriptures by the commandments of the everlasting God, who has made it known to all nations that his commandments are for the obedient and faithful.
Let there be glory to the only wise God, through Jesus Christ forever. Amen."
Paul who was called to be an apostle of Jesus Christ through the will of God, and Sosthenes our brother.

Wrote this letter to the church of God in Corinth, and those who are called to be saints and are sanctified in Christ Jesus, together with all those everywhere who call on the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, who is both their Lord and ours.
And the letter said, "Grace and peace be to you, from God our father and our Lord Jesus Christ.
I always thank my God for you because of the grace of God which he has given you through Jesus Christ.
So that you are enriched by God in every way, in all speech and knowledge.
Because our testimony of Christ has been confirmed in you.
So that you lack no spiritual gift, waiting for the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ.
Jesus will also confirm you until the end, so that you may be held blameless on the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.
God is faithful, for you were called into the friendship of God's own son our Lord Jesus Christ.

Now brothers I beg you in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ to agree on the same things, so that there are no divisions among you. Then you will be perfectly joined together in the same mind and judgment.
My brothers I have been told by those who are from the house of Chloe, that there are disagreements among you.
Now this is what I mean, some of the people among you are saying, 'I follow Paul,' and some are saying, 'I follow Apollos,' or 'I follow Cephas,' or 'I follow Christ.'
So I ask you, 'Is Christ a divided soul? Was Paul crucified for you, or were you baptized in the name of Paul?'
I thank God that I did not baptize any of you except Crispus and Gaius.
Otherwise some would say that I baptized you in my own name.
And yes, I did also baptize the household of Stephanas, but other than that I do not remember baptizing anyone else.
Christ did not send me to baptize, he sent me to preach the gospel, but not with words of wisdom, otherwise the cross of Christ would become ineffective.
For the preaching of the cross is foolishness to those who are dying, but to us who are saved the cross is the power of God.
For it is written, 'Because the wisdom of the wise will perish, and the understanding of the prudent will be hidden. (Isaiah 29:14)'
Where are the wise? Where is the scribe? Where is the philosopher who disputes this world? Has God not made the wisdom of this world foolish?
Because God in his wisdom saw that the world through its wisdom did not know God, for God was pleased by the foolishness of those who were preaching to save those who believe.
For the Jews require a sign, and the Greeks look for wisdom.
But we preach the crucifixion of Christ, which is an obstacle to understanding to the Jews, and it sounds foolish to the Greeks.
But to those who are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ is God's power and his wisdom.
Because God's foolishness is wiser than men and God's weakness is stronger than men.
So brothers when you were called, not many of you were wise by the worldly standards of the flesh, and not many mighty or noble men are called.
But God has chosen the foolish things of the world to confound the wise, and God has chosen the weak things of the world to confound the things which are mighty.
God has chosen these base and despised things of the world, and he has chosen the things that are not base and despised to bring down the things that are.
So that no flesh will be glorified in his presence.
But because of him you are in Christ Jesus, whom God has made wise, righteous, sanctified, and redemptive to us.
So that just as it was written, 'Let anyone who glories in these things understand and know that I am the Lord. (Jeremiah 9:23-24)'"
And Paul continued writing his letter to the church of God in Corinth and said, "Brothers, when I came to you, I did not come with eloquent speech or wisdom as I declared God's testimony to you.
For I decided to not teach anything among you, except that Jesus Christ was crucified.
And I was trembling, weak, and fearful with you.
My speech and preaching was not enticing words of a man's wisdom, but it was a demonstration of the Holy Spirit and his power.
So that your faith did not stand in the wisdom of men, but in the power of God.
However among those who are mature in spirit we speak wisdom, but it is not the wisdom of this world, nor the wisdom of this world's princes which always comes to nothing.
But we speak of the mystery of God's hidden wisdom, which God ordained for our glory before the world began.
Which none of the princes of this world knew because had if they had known, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory.

But it is written, 'For since the beginning of the world, men have not understood, ears have not heard, and eyes have not seen any other God. Behold what God has prepared for those who wait for him. (Isaiah 64:4)'
But God has revealed them to us through his Holy Spirit, because the Holy Spirit searches all of God's deep things.
For no one knows a man's inner thoughts except the man's own spirit within him? And no one knows God's inner thoughts except the Spirit of God.
So we have not received the spirit of this world, but we have received the spirit of God, so that we could know the things which God has freely given to us.
These are the things we are speaking about, not in words which teach man's wisdom, but that which the Holy Spirit teaches, comparing spiritual things with spiritual words.
But the natural man does not receive the things of God's Spirit because they are foolishness to him, nor can the natural man know them because they are only understood by the spirit.
So the spiritual man judges all things, but he himself is not judged by anyone.
For it is written, 'Who can understand the Lord's mind in order to instruct God? But we have been given the mind of Christ. (Isaiah 40:13)'"
And Paul continued writing this letter to the church in Corinth and said, "Brothers, I could not speak to you as I speak to the spiritual, but I speak to you as worldly babes in Christ.
For I have fed you with milk and not meat, because until now you were unable to bear it but now you can.
For you are still worldly, because there is in fact still envy among you, conflict, and divisions. So, are you still not walking in the world as men?
For when one of you says, 'I follow Paul,' and another says, 'I follow Apollos,' are you not carnal?
Who then is Paul, and who is Apollos? Are they not the ministers who helped you believe? For the Lord has given each man his place.
I planted and Apollos watered, but God made it grow.
So then neither the one who plants nor the one who waters is anything, for only God can make it grow.
Now he that plants and he that waters are one, and every man will receive his own reward in accordance with his own labor.
For we labor together with God, you are God's husbandry and you are God's building.
By God's grace which he has given me as his wise master builder, I have laid the foundation, and another will build after that. But each man must be careful about how he builds afterwards.
For no man can lay a foundation other than that which was laid by Jesus Christ.
If a man builds on this foundation using gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, and straw.
His work will become obvious, because it will be declared in the light of day. For it will be revealed by fire, and the fire will test the quality of each man's work.
If what a man has built after the foundation was laid by Jesus Christ endures, he will receive a reward.
If a man's work is burned up, he will suffer loss but he himself will be saved by fire.
Do you not know that you are the temple of God, and that the Spirit of God lives within you?
If a man defiles God's temple, God will destroy him because the temple of God is holy, for you are that temple.
Let no man deceive himself. If any man among you seems to be wise in this world, let him become a fool so that he may become wise.
For the wisdom of this world is foolishness with God. For it is written, 'He captures the wise in their own craftiness. (Job 5:13)'
And again it is written, 'The Lord knows that the thoughts of man are just vanity. (Psalm 94:11)'
Therefore do not glory in worldly men. For all things are yours.
Whether it is Paul, Apollos, Cephas, the world, life, death, things in the present, or things to come; all things are yours.
For you belong to Christ, and Christ is God's."
And Paul continued writing this letter to the church in Corinth and said, "So let men think of us as the ministers of Christ, and stewards of God's mysteries.
Now stewards are required to be faithful.
It is insignificant to me whether you or anyone else judges me. For I do not even judge my own self.
For I know nothing by myself but that does not justify me, because it is the Lord who judges me.

Therefore judge nothing before its time but wait until the Lord comes. For the Lord will bring to light the things hidden in darkness, and expose the motives of men's hearts, and then every man will praise God.

And brothers, I have transferred these things to myself and Apollos for your sakes, so you could learn from us. Because you should not think more of men than that which is written. Then you will not accept the pride of one man over another.
For who makes you different from one another, and what do you have that you were not given? Now if you did receive it, why do you glory as if it was not given to you?
Now you are full and rich, and you have reigned as kings without us. I wish to God that you did reign, so that we could also reign with you.
I think that we who are God's apostles have been placed last by God, as if we were appointed to death. For we have become a spectacle to the world and the angels as well as men.
We are fools for Christ's sake, but you are wise in Christ! We are weak but you are strong! You are honorable but we are despised.
Even to this very hour we are both hungry, thirsty, naked, brutalized, and we are homeless.
We labor and work with our own hands. When we are reviled, we bless. When we are persecuted, we suffer through it.
When we are defamed, we plead kindly. The world makes us its filth and the scum of the earth to this day.
I Do not write these things to shame you, but as my beloved sons I write to warn you.
For even though you have 10,000 instructors in Christ, you do not have many fathers, for in Christ Jesus I have become your father through the gospel.
Therefore I beg you to become followers of me.
Because I have sent Timothy to you, who is my beloved son and faithful in the Lord. Timothy will remind you of my ways which are in Christ, and which I teach everywhere in every church.
Now some of you are egotistical, as though I were not coming to you.
But I will come to you soon, if it is the Lord's will. Then I will know what these egotistical people are saying, and what power they have.
For the Kingdom of God is not just in words, but it is in power.
So which would you prefer? That I come to you with a rod, or in love, and in the spirit of meekness?"

And Paul continued writing this letter to the church in Corinth and said, "It is being reported that there is a type of fornication happening among you that is not even acceptable among the Gentiles, which is for a man to fornicate with his father's wife.
And you are proud! But you should have mourned and remove the one doing this from among you.
For truly I say, even though I am absent in the body, I am present in spirit, and I have already judged the one who has done this as if I were there.
When you are gathered together in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, I am also there with you in spirit through the power of our Lord Jesus Christ.
To deliver this man over to Satan for the destruction of the flesh, so that his spirit may be saved on the day of our Lord Jesus.
Your glorifying is not good. Do you not know that a little leavening works its way through the whole batch of dough?
Therefore, purge the old leavening so that you may become a new batch of unleavened dough. For Christ was our Passover sacrifice who was sacrificed for us.
So let us not keep the feast with the old leavening, nor with the leavening of malice and wickedness, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.
I wrote you a letter telling you not to keep company with adulterers.
But I was not including the unbelieving fornicators, covetous, extortioners, or idolaters of this world. Because if that were true, you would have to leave this world altogether.

But now I am writing to you telling you not to keep company with a man who says he is a brother in Christ, but he is an adulterer, covetous, idolater, screamer, drunkard, or an extortioner. You must not eat with someone like this.
For why should I have to judge those who are outside the church? Are you not to judge those inside the church?
But God judges those outside the church, so remove those wicked people from among your people."

And Paul continued writing this letter to the church in Corinth and said, "If you are courageous and you have something against someone, why do you go before the law of the unjust and not before the saints?
Do you not know that the saints will judge the world, and if you can judge the world, are you unworthy to judge even the smallest matters?
Do you not know that we will judge angels? How much more will we judge the things of this life?
So then, if you must judge the things pertaining to this life, do you set those who are the least esteemed in the church to judge them?
Therefore, I speak to your shame. Is there not one wise man among you? No? Is there not one of you who is able to judge righteously between your brothers?
But brother goes against brother before the law of the unbelievers.
Therefore, there is complete fault among you because you go to the law against one another. Why do you not accept the wrong? Why do you not suffer the fraud among yourselves?
No? Instead you do wrong and defraud even your own brothers.

Do you not know that the unrighteous will not inherit the Kingdom of God? Do not be deceived, do not be a fornicator, nor an idolater, nor an adulterer! And do not be effeminate nor abuse yourselves by homosexual acts.
Because neither thieves, nor the covetous, nor drunkards, nor revilers, nor extortioners will inherit the Kingdom of God.
And some of you were this way, but you have been washed, sanctified, and justified in the name of our Lord Jesus and by the spirit of our God.
Everything is lawful to me, but not all things are beneficial! Everything is lawful for me, but I will not be enslaved under the power of anything!
Meat is for the stomach, and the stomach is for meat, but God will destroy both of them. Now the body is not for fornication, but it is for the Lord and the Lord is for the body.
God has raised up the Lord and he will also raise us up with his power.
Do you not know that your bodies are part of the body of Christ? Do you think that I will take members from the body of Christ, and turn them into prostitutes? God forbid: No!
What then? Do you not know that whoever has joined with the body of a whore is of one body? Because God says, 'The two shall become as one flesh.'
But whoever is joined to the Lord is one spirit.
Flee fornication! Every sin that a man commits is outside the body, but whoever commits fornication sins against his own body.
What then? Do you not know that your body is the temple of the Holy Spirit which is within you, whom you have received from God? For you are not your own?
For you were bought for a price, therefore glorify God in your body and spirit, which both belong to God."
And Paul continued writing this letter to the church in Corinth and said, "Now about those things which you wrote to me and asked, 'Is it good for a man not to touch a woman?'
So in order to avoid fornication, each man should have his own wife and every woman should have her own husband.
The husband must give due benevolence to his wife, and the wife must do the same for her husband.
The wife no longer has power over her own body because the husband does, and the husband has no power over his own body because the wife does.

Do not deny each other except by mutual consent for a short time, so that you may devote yourselves to fasting and prayer. Then come together again, so that Satan cannot tempt you through your failure to resist.
But I speak of this by permission, and not a commandment.

Because I wish everyone were like me, and I wish they could get along without getting married. But we are not all the same and God gives some the gift of a husband or wife, and he gives the gift of being happily unmarried to others.
So I say to the unmarried and the widowers, it is best to be like me and stay unmarried if you can.
But if you cannot control yourself, go ahead and get married because it is better to marry than to burn with lust.
And to the married I give this command from the Lord, 'The wife must not leave her husband.
But and if she leaves, she must remain unmarried or reconcile with her husband. And the husband must not divorce his wife.'
But to the rest of you I not the Lord speak and I say, 'If a brother is married to a wife who does not believe, and she is happy living with him, then he must not divorce her.
Or if a woman has a husband who does not believe, and he is happy living with her, then she must not divorce him.
For the unbelieving husband is sanctified by the wife, and the unbelieving wife is sanctified by the husband. Otherwise your children would be unclean, but now they are holy.
But if the unbelieving spouse leaves, let them leave. A brother or a sister is not under bondage in such cases, but God has called us to peace.
For how does the wife know, whether or not she will save her husband, or how does the man know, whether or not he will save his wife?
But no matter what God has given to each man or what the Lord has asked of him, let him walk the path, and this is what I have ordained for all churches.
For if any man is called to be circumcised, let him not become uncircumcised. And if any man is called to be uncircumcised, let him not become circumcised.
Circumcision and uncircumcision are both nothing, but the keeping of God's commandments is something.
So let every man endure the calling for which he was called.
Were you a servant when you were called? Do not worry about it, but if you are made free then take advantage of it.
For whoever is called to be a servant in the Lord, is the Lord's freeman, likewise whoever was free when he was called, is Christ's servant.
You were bought with a price, and you are not the servants of men.
Brothers, let every man who is called endure with God.
Now I have no commandments from the Lord concerning virgins. But I offer my judgment as one who has obtained mercy from the Lord to be faithful.
Therefore, I suppose that it is good for a man to remain this way because of today's present distress.
Are you bound to a wife? Do not get divorced. Are you divorced from a wife? Do not look for a wife.
But if you do marry, you have not sinned, and if you marry a virgin, she has not sinned. But those who do marry will have trouble in this world, and I want to spare you of this trouble.
But brothers I say this to you, 'The time is short and it remains so, and those who have wives should live as if they had none.
And those who weep should live as if they do not weep, and those who rejoice should live as if they do not rejoice, and those who buy should live as if they possess nothing.
And those who use this world live as if they are not abusing it, because this current world is passing away.'
But I would have you live carefree. The unmarried man cares for the things that belong to the Lord, so how can he please the Lord.
But the married man cares for the things that are of this world, so how can he please his wife.

There is also difference a between a wife and a virgin. The unmarried woman cares for the things of the Lord, so that she may be holy both in body and in spirit. But the married woman cares for the things of this world, so how can she please her husband.
And I am saying this for your own benefit, not to ensnare you, but I am saying this to help you to show attractive and undistracted attention to the Lord.
But if a man thinks he is behaving improperly toward his virgin, and she has passed the flower of her age and they should marry. Then let him do as he will because he does not sin, so let them marry.

But the man who is steadfast in his heart and does not think marriage is necessary, and he has control over his own will, and he has decided in his own heart that he will not marry, then he does well.
So the man who marries does well, but the man who does not marry does better.
The wife is bound by the law as long as her husband lives, but if her husband dies, she is at liberty to marry whoever she wants, but only if he belongs to the Lord.
But in my judgment she would be happier if she endured unmarried, and I also think that I have the Spirit of God within me."

And Paul continued writing this letter to the church in Corinth and said, "Now as for touching things which were offered to idols, we all know that we all have knowledge. Knowledge scoffs at flattery but charity instructs.
A man thinks he knows something, but he also knows that he does not know what he should know.
But if a man loves God, then God loves that man.
As for eating those things that are offered to idols, we know that an idol is nothing in this world. And we also know that there is only one God and there are no others.
For even though they are called gods in heaven and on earth, there are many so-called gods and lords.
But we know that there is only one God, who is the father from whom all things come and we are in him. And there is only one Lord Jesus Christ through whom all things come, and we live through him.
However not all men have this knowledge, because some have the conscience of an idol to this day. They eat things that are offered to an idol because their conscience is weak and defiled.
But meat does not bring us closer to God, because we are neither better off nor worse off whether we eat or we do not eat.
But take heed, otherwise your liberty may become an obstacle to understanding for those who are weak.
For if a man sees those of you who have this knowledge siting and eating in the idol's temple, those with a weak conscience may be emboldened to eat those things which are offered to idols.
nd through your knowledge, will not the weaker brother for whom Christ died, also perish?
But when you sin this way against your brothers and you wound their weak conscience, you also sin against Christ.
Therefore, if meat makes my brother offend, I will eat no meat while the world still stands, otherwise I may cause my brother to offend."
And Paul continued writing this letter to the church in Corinth and said, "Am I not an apostle? Am I not free? Have I not seen our Lord Jesus Christ? Are you not my work in the Lord?
Even if I am not an apostle to others, I am without a doubt an apostle to you, for you are the seal of my apostleship in the Lord.
My answer to those who cross examine me is this.
Do we not have the power to eat and drink?
Do we not have the power to lead a sister or a wife, as do the other apostles and brothers in the Lord and Cephas?
Or are Barnabas and I the only ones who do not have the power to endure working?
Who goes to war at his own expense? Who plants a vineyard and does not eat its fruit, or who feeds a flock and does not eat the flock's milk?
I say these things as a man, but does the law not also say the same things?
For it is written in the Law of Moses, 'You must not muzzle an ox while it is treading the wheat. (Deuteronomy 25:4)' Does God care for the oxen?

Or does God not speak altogether for our sake? It is no doubt for our sake that this is written, so that the one who plows and the one who thrashes, both do so in the hope that they would share in the harvest.
If we have sown spiritual things to you, is it such a great thing for us to reap from your carnal things?
If others partake of this power over you, should we not also? But we have not used this power, and we have suffered through all things, otherwise we would hinder the gospel of Christ.
Do you not know that those who minister about holy things live from the things of the temple, and those who wait at the altar share with the altar?
Even so the Lord has ordained that those who preach the gospel should live by the gospel.
But I have used none of these things, nor have I written asking for these things for myself, because I would rather die, than let any man void my glory.
For even though I preach the gospel, I have no reason to glory, because necessity and sorrow are laid upon me, if I do not preach the gospel!
For if I do this thing willingly, I have a reward. But if I do this against my will, the teaching of the gospel is still committed to me.
So what then is my reward? Honestly, when I preach the gospel, I preach the gospel of Christ free of charge, so that I do not abuse my power in the gospel.
For even though I am free from all men, I have still made myself a servant to all, so that I might gain more.
And to the Jews I became like a Jew, so that I might win over the Jews. And to those who are under the law, I became like those under the law, so that I might win over those who are under the law.

To those who are without the law, I became like those without the law, even though I am not outside the law of God, but I am under the law to Christ, so that I might win over those who are without the law.
To the weak I became like those who are weak, so that I might win over the weak. I am like all things to all men, so that I might save some through any means necessary.
I do this for the gospel's sake, so that I might partake of the gospel with you.
Do you not know that those who run a race must all run, but only one receives the prize? So run to win.
For everyone who struggles to master all things are temperate in all things. For they do so to obtain a corruptible crown, but we are incorruptible.
Therefore I do not run under uncertainty, and I do not fight as one who beats the air.
But I keep my body under subjugation by any means necessary when I have preached to others, so that I myself would be as a castaway."

And Paul continued writing this letter to the church in Corinth and said, "Besides that brothers, I do not want you to be ignorant of how our fathers were under the cloud when they walked through the Red Sea.
And they were all baptized to Moses in the cloud and in the sea.
And we all ate the same spiritual meat.
And we all drank the same spiritual drink, because they drank from the spiritual rock that followed them and that rock was Christ.
But God was not well pleased with many of them because they were weak in the wilderness.
Now these things were examples to teach us not to lust after evil things like they also lusted.
You must not be idolaters as were some of them, for it is written, 'Then the people sat down to eat and drink and began playing around. (Exodus 32:6)'
Nor should we commit fornication as some of them committed, when 23,000 fell in one day. (Numbers 25:1-9)
Nor should we tempt Christ as some of them also tempted him, and they were destroyed by serpents. (Numbers 21:5-6)
Nor should you murmur as some of them also murmured, and they were destroyed by the destroyer. (Numbers 16:41-50)
Now all of these things happened to them as examples, and they are all written down for our retribution, for the ends of the world have come upon us.
Therefore let anyone who thinks he stands take heed otherwise he will fall.

No temptation has taken hold of you except those which are common to man. But God is faithful, and he will not allow you to suffer temptation above that which you can withstand. But God will also make a way for you to escape temptation, so that you may be able to bear it.
Therefore my dearly beloved, flee from idolatry.
For I speak as I would speak to wise men, so judge what I say.
Does not the cup of blessing from which we bless, not come from the communion of the blood of Christ? The bread which we break, is it not the communion of the body of Christ?
For we are many parts of one bread and one body because we all partake of that one bread.
Behold the people of Israel, do not those who eat from the sacrifices also partake of the altar?
What then am I saying? Am I saying that an idol has any value, or what is offered in sacrifice to idols has any value?
No, I am saying that the things which the Gentiles sacrifice, they sacrifice to demons and not to God. And I would not want you to be friends with demons.
You cannot drink from the Lord's cup and the cup of demons, and you cannot partake of the Lord's table and the table of demons.
Should we provoke the Lord to jealousy? Are we stronger than God?
All things are lawful for me but not all things are beneficial, all things are lawful for me but not all things are instructive.
Therefore no man should seek his own wealth, but he should seek the good for every other man.
Eat whatever is sold in the markets, that asks no questions for the sake of their conscience.
For the earth and its fullness belongs to the Lord.
If any of those who do not believe ask you to attend a feast and you decide to go. Eat whatever is set before you and ask no questions for the sake of their conscience.
But if a man says to you, 'This was offered in sacrifice to idols,' do not eat it for his sake or for the sake of his conscience. Because the earth and its fullness belongs to the Lord.
I say, do not do this for the sake of your own conscience, but for the sake of the other. For why should my liberty be judged by another man's conscience?
For if by grace I am a partaker of that for which I give thanks, why should I be spoken evil of?
Therefore whether you eat or drink or do anything else, do it all to the glory of God.
Do not offend anyone including the Jews, nor the Gentiles, nor the church of God.
Even as I try to please all men in all things, I am not seeking my own profit, but I seek the profit of many, so that they may be saved."
And Paul continued writing this letter to the church in Corinth and said, "Be my followers, just as I am a follower of Christ.
Now I praise you brothers, and I ask that you always remember me and keep the legal decrees that I have delivered to you.
But I want you to know, that the head of every man is Christ and the head of every woman is a man, and the head of Christ is God.
Every man who prays or prophesies with a covered head, dishonors his head.
But every woman who prays or prophecies with her head uncovered dishonors her head, because it is as if she had shaved her head.
For if a woman's head is not covered then she must shave her head, but if it is shameful for a woman to shave her head, she should cover her head.
For a man should not cover his head, because man is made in the image and glory of God, but woman is made in the glory of man.
For a man is not of a woman, but the woman is of a man.
Nor was man created for woman, but woman was created for man.
Because of this, a woman should have power over her own head, because of the angels.
But in the Lord, the man is not outside of the woman nor is the woman outside of the man.
All things are from God, for just as woman is part of man, so man is also born of woman.
So judge for yourselves, is it attractive for a woman to pray to God with an uncovered head?
Does not even nature itself teach you that if a man has long hair, it is shameful to him?
But if a woman has long hair, it is a glory to her, because her hair is given to her as a covering for her head.
But if a man disagrees with this, we have no other custom nor do God's churches.
Now this is what must I declare to you, because I cannot praise you, for you do not come together for what is best but for what is worse.
For first of all, when you come together in the church, I hear that there are divisions among you and I partially believe it.
For there must be doctrinal heresy among you, so that you will recognize those among you who are approved by God.
Therefore when you come together in one place, it is not to eat the Lord's supper.
For everyone eats their own supper before each other, and one goes hungry but another is drunk.

So what am I saying? Do you not have houses where you can eat and drink? Or do you despise the church of God, and shame those who have nothing? What can I say to you? Will I praise you in this? I do not praise you for this.
For everything I have received from the Lord I have also delivered to you. The Lord Jesus took some bread on the same night that he was betrayed.
Then after Jesus gave thanks to God, he broke the bread and said, '`Take this and eat it, for it is my body which is broken for you, do this and remember me.´'
The same way he also took the cup after his supper and said, '`This cup is the new testament in my blood, drink this and remember me whenever you drink it.´'
For as often as you eat this bread and drink from this cup, you proclaim the Lord's death until he returns.
Therefore anyone unworthy who eats this bread and drinks from the Lord's cup, will be guilty of sinning against the body and blood of the Lord.
But each person must examine themselves and decide if they should eat that bread and drink from that cup.
For anyone unworthy who does not recognize the Lord's body condemns themselves, because they eat and drink from this cup anyway.
For this is why many among you are weak, sickly, or asleep.
For if we would truthfully judge ourselves, we would not be judged.
But when we are judged by the Lord we are chastened, so that we will not be condemned along with the world.
Therefore my brothers, when you come together to eat wait on one another.
If a man is hungry, let him eat at home, so that you do not come together in condemnation, and I will explain the rest when I arrive."
And Paul continued writing this letter to the church in Corinth and said, "Now brothers, I do not want you to be ignorant of the spiritual gifts.
For you know that when you were Gentiles, you were led astray and carried away by those dumb idols.
Therefore I give you this understanding, no man speaking from the Spirit of God can curse Jesus. And no one can say, 'Jesus is the Lord,' except through the Holy Spirit.
Now there are different gifts, but we all have the same Holy Spirit.
And there are diverse administrations, but we all have the same Lord.
And there are diverse operations, but it is the same God who works in all people.
But the materialization of the Holy Spirit is given to profit every man.
For one person the word of wisdom is given through the Holy Spirit, but another is given the word of knowledge by the same Holy Spirit.
To another faith is given by the same Holy Spirit, but to another the gifts of healing is given by the same Holy Spirit.

To another is given the gift of working of miracles, but to another the gift of prophecy is given. To another the gift of recognizing spirits is given. To another the gift of speaking different languages is given, but to another the gift of interpreting other languages is given.
But all of these works are of one and the same Holy Spirit, who divides gifts to each man however he wants.
For as the body is one and it has many parts, and all of the parts of that one body are one body in Christ.
For by one Holy Spirit we are all baptized into one body, whether we are Jews or Gentiles, whether we are bound or free, and we have all been made to drink into one Holy Spirit.
For the body is not one part, but many.
So if the foot says, 'Since I am not the hand, I am not part of the body.' Does that statement make it not part of the body?
And if the ear says, 'Since I am not the eye, I am not part of the body.' Does that statement make it not part of the body?
If the whole body were an eye, how could we hear? And if the whole body were an ear, how could we smell?
But God has set every part of the body however it pleased him.
And if they were all one part, where would the body be?
But now there are many parts, but still only one body.
And the eye cannot say to the hand, 'I do not need you,' nor can the head say to the feet, 'I do not need you.'
No, those parts of the body which seem to be the most feeble, are necessary.

And those parts of the body which we think are less honorable, we bestow with honor even more abundantly. And those parts of the body which we think are less attractive are treated as the most attractive.
For our attractive parts have no such need, but God has tempered the body together, and given more abundant honor to the part which is lacking.
So that there would be no spirit of division in the body, but that the parts would have the same care one for another.
And if one part suffers, then all the parts suffer with it, or if one part is honored, then all the parts rejoice with it.
Now each one of you are a particular part of the body of Christ.

And God has appointed some in the church as first apostles, second as prophets, third as teachers, and fourth as miracle workers. Then come the gifts of healings, spiritual helpers, governments, and those who speak in different languages.
Are all apostles? Are all prophets? Are all teachers? Are all miracle workers?
Do all have the gifts of healing? Do all speak in different tongues? Do all interpret different languages?
But earnestly covet the best gifts, and now I will show you a more excellent way."
And Paul continued writing this letter to the church in Corinth and said, "If I speak in the tongues of men and angels but I have no charity, I only sound like a brass horn or a tinkling cymbal.
If I have the gift of prophecy and I understand all mysteries and I possess all knowledge and I have enough faith to move mountains, but I do not have charity, I am nothing.
And if I give everything I own to feed the poor and I give my body to be burned but I have no charity, it profits me nothing.
Charity is long suffering and is kind, charity does not envy, charity does not boast about itself, and charity is not conceited.
Charity does not behave improperly, charity does not seek her own way, charity is not easily provoked, and charity thinks no evil.
Charity does not rejoice in immorality, but charity rejoices in the truth.
Charity bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, and endures all things.
Charity never fails, but where there are prophecies, they will fail, and where there are tongues, they will cease, and where there is knowledge, it will vanish away.
For we only know part of God's spirit, and we can only prophesy part of God's spirit.
But when that which is perfect has come, then that which is only a part will be done away with.
When I was a child, I spoke as a child, I understood as a child, and I thought as a child. But when I became a man, I put away my childish things.
For now we see through a glass darkly, but then we will see God face to face. Now I only know a part of God's spirit, but then I will know God as I am also known by him.
And now these three endure: faith, hope, and charity but the greatest of these is charity."
And Paul continued writing this letter to the church in Corinth and said, "Pursue charity and desire spiritual gifts, but especially pursue the gift of prophecy.
For the one who speaks in unknown tongues does not speak to men, but to God, because no one understands him, but he speaks the mysteries of the spirit.
But the one who prophesies speaks to men to educate, improve, encourage, and comfort them.
For the one who speaks in an unknown tongue instructs himself, but the one who prophecies also instructs the church.

I would prefer that all of you who speak in tongues could prophesy, because the one who prophecies, is greater than the one who speaks in tongues, unless he interprets so that the church may receive instruction.
Now brothers, if I come to you speaking in tongues, how can I profit you unless I speak to you either through revelation, knowledge, doctrine, or by prophesying?
Even things without life giving sound such as the flute or the harp, unless each instrument makes a distinct sound, how will anyone know what notes the flute or harp are playing?
For if the trumpet makes an uncertain sound, who will prepare themselves for battle?
So likewise, unless you speak in tongues that others can understand, how will anyone know what was said? For you will just be speaking to the air.
There are so many different kinds of languages in the world, and none of them are insignificant.
Therefore if I do not understand the language, I will be a barbarian to the one speaking, and the one speaking will be a barbarian to me.
But since you are zealous of spiritual gifts, strive to excel in instructing the church.
Therefore pray that anyone who speaks in an unknown tongue may also interpret what is said.
For if I pray in an unknown tongue, my spirit prays but my mind does not understand.
What then should I do? I will pray with the spirit, and I will also pray with my mind. I will sing with the spirit, and I will also sing with understanding.
Otherwise when you bless with the spirit, how can someone who does not understand say, 'Amen,' when you give thanks, since they do not understand what you are saying?
For you honestly give thanks, but the others do not learn or understand.
I thank my God that I speak in tongues more than all of you.
But in the church, I would rather speak five comprehensible words to teach others, than 10,000 words in an unknown tongue.
Brothers, stop thinking like children and be mature in your understanding, but be like children in malice.
In the law it is written: 'For God will speak to these people in a foreign language with stammering lips, but they refused to listen. (Isaiah 28:11-12)'
Therefore speaking in tongues is not a sign for those who believe, but for those who do not believe. But prophesy is for those who believe, and it does not serve those who do not believe.
So if the whole church comes together in one place, and they all speak in tongues, then those who do not understand or they are unbelievers will say that you are crazy.
But if they all prophesy, then one who does not believe or understand will become convinced and he will be judged by all.
The secrets of his heart will be revealed to all, and he will bow facedown and worship God, and report the truth that God is truly among you.
So then brothers, how is it that when you come together every one of you has a psalm, a doctrine, a tongue, a revelation, or an interpretation? Let instructions be given for everything.
If a man speaks in an unknown tongue, let it be at most two or three people who speak one at a time, and let one interpret.
But if there is no interpreter, let him remain silent in church and speak only to himself and God.
Let two or three prophets speak and let the other judge.
If anything is revealed to someone siting nearby, let the first speaker hold his peace.
For you may all prophesy one at a time, so that all may learn and all may be comforted.
And the spirits of the prophets are subject to the prophets.
For God is not the author of confusion but of peace, as he is in all the churches of the saints.
Let your women remain silent in church, because they are not permitted to speak but they are commanded by the law to be obedient.
And if they want to learn something, they can ask their husbands at home, for it is shameful for women to speak in the church.
What? Did God's word come from you, or did it come for you and no one else?
If a man thinks of himself as a prophet or a spiritual man, let him acknowledge the things I write to you about are the Lord's commandments.
But if a man is ignorant, let him be ignorant.
Therefore brothers, covet the gift of prophesy, and do not forbid anyone to speak in tongues.
Let all things be done decently and orderly."

And Paul continued writing this letter to the church in Corinth and said, "Besides that brothers, I declare that the gospel which I have preached to you, which you have also received, and in which you stand.
By which you are also saved, and I ask you to remember what I have preached to you. Otherwise, you have believed in vain.
For I have given you the first fruit of everything that God has given me, which is that Christ died for our sin as it is written in the scriptures. (Isaiah 53:5–6 and Isaiah 53:12)
And Christ was buried, so that he could rise again on the third day as the scriptures stated. (Hosea 6:2)
And Jesus was seen by Cephas, then by the twelve disciples.
After that, he was seen by more than 500 brothers at one time, most of whom are still living to this day, but some have fallen asleep.
After that, he was seen by James, then by all of the other apostles.
And last of all he was also seen by me, since I am one who was born just in time.
For I am the least of the apostles, and I am not worthy to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the church of God.

But by the grace of God I am what I am, and God's grace was not bestowed upon me in vain. But I have labored more abundantly than all the others. Yet it was not me, but the grace of God which was with me.
Therefore, whether it was me or them, we preached and you believed.
If we preached that Christ rose from the dead, then how can some of you now say that there is no resurrection of the dead?
But if there is no resurrection of the dead, then Christ has not risen.
And if Christ has not been raised from the dead, then our preaching is in vain, and your faith is also in vain.

Yes, others have found us to be false witnesses of God, because we have testified that God has raised Christ from the dead, but they say that Jesus has not been raised from the dead. But if that is so, then the dead have not been raised up.
For if the dead do not rise, then Christ has not been raised up.
And if Christ was not raised, your faith is in vain, and you remain in your sins.
Then those who have fallen asleep in Christ have also perished.
If we only have our hope in Christ in this life, then we are the most miserable of all men.
But now, Christ has risen from the dead and become the first fruits of those who slept.
For since death came by man, then the resurrection of the dead has also come by man.
For just as Adam died, we will all die, but in Christ we will all be made alive.
But each one in his own time, Christ was the first fruits, but afterward those who belong to Christ will rise when he returns.
Then the end will come, when Jesus delivers the kingdom to God the father, after he has put down all rulers, authority, and power.
For Jesus must reign, until he has put all of his enemies under his feet.
The last enemy to be destroyed is death.
For God has put all things under his feet. (Psalm 8:6) But when he says all things have been put under God, it is obvious that Jesus is the exception, for he is the one who put all things under God.
And when all things are subdued by him, then the son himself will also be made subject to the One True God who put all things under God, so that God may be all in all.
Otherwise, what will those who are baptized for the dead do? If the dead do not rise at all, then why are they baptized for the dead?
And why do we stand in jeopardy every hour?
I protest death by your rejoicing in our Lord Jesus Christ, for I die daily.
I have fought with beasts in Ephesus, as if it had been ordered by men. And if the dead do not rise, what advantage has it given me? So let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die.
Do not be deceived, evil communications corrupt good manners.
Awaken to righteousness and do not sin, because some of you have no knowledge of God, and I say this to your shame.
But some will ask, 'How can the dead be raised up, and what kind of body will they have?
You fool! That which you sow is not harvested, unless it first dies.
And what you sow now, is not for the body that will be, but it is just a seed, and by chance it will become wheat or some other type of grain.
But God gives that seed a body that pleases God, and every seed has its own body.
All flesh is not the same as other flesh, men have one kind of flesh, the beasts have a different kind of flesh, and so do the fish and the birds.
