There are also celestial and terrestrial bodies, but the glory of the celestial is one type of glory, and the glory of the terrestrial is another type.
The sun has one type of glory, and the moon has another type of glory, and the stars have a completely different type of glory, because one star's glory differs from the glory of other stars.
It is also this way for the resurrection of the dead. It is sown in corruption; but it is raised in incorruption.
It is sown in dishonor; but it is raised in glory. It is sown in weakness; but it is raised in power.
It is sown as a natural body; but it is raised as a spiritual body. For there is a natural body, and there is a spiritual body.
And so it is written; 'The first man to be made a living soul was Adam, the last Adam was made a living spirit. (Genesis 2:7)
However, the spiritual did not come first, the natural came first, but afterward the spiritual came.
The first man came from the dust of the earth and was earthly, but the second man is the Lord from heaven.
As it is with the earthly, so it is for those who are also earthly, and as it is for the heavenly, so it is for those who are also heavenly.
And just as we have carried the image of the earthly, we shall also bear the image of the heavenly.
Now brothers, I say that flesh and blood cannot inherit the Kingdom of God, nor does corruption inherit incorruption.
Behold, now I will show you a mystery; we will not all sleep, but we will all be changed.
In a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the sound of the last trumpet. For the trumpet will sound, and the dead will be raised incorruptible, and we will be changed.
For the corruptible must put on incorruption, and the mortal must put on immortality.
So, when the corruptible have put on incorruption, and the mortal have put on immortality, then what was written will come to pass; 'Death has been swallowed up in victory. (Isaiah 25:8)'
O death, where is your sting? O grave, where is your victory? (Hosea 13:14)
The sting of death is sin, and the strength of sin is the law.
But thanks be to God, who gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.
Therefore, my beloved brothers, be steadfast, unmovable, and remain abundant in the Lord's work, because just as you already know, your labor in the Lord is not in vain."
And Paul finished writing this letter to the church in Corinth and said, "Now about the collections for the saints, I have given orders to the churches of Galatia for you to follow.
On the first day of the week each one of you should set aside and save some, in accordance with how God has prospered you, so that no collections will be needed when I come.
And when I come, I will send whoever you approve by your letters, to bring your liberal offerings to Jerusalem.
And if it is wise for me to also go there, then they may go with me.
Now I will come to you after I pass through Macedonia, because I must pass through Macedonia.
And it may be that I will stay with you through winter, so that you may help me on my journey wherever I go.
For I do not want to just see you while passing through, but I trust I will be able to stay with you for a while, if the Lord permits.
But I will stay in Ephesus until Pentecost.
For a great door for success has opened up for me, even though there are many adversaries.
Now if Timothy comes, see that he stays with you without fear, because he does the Lord's work, just as I also do.
Therefore, do not let anyone despise him, but send him out in peace, so that he may come to me, because I look forward to seeing him along with the brothers.
Now about our brother Apollos, I greatly desire for him to come to you with the brothers. But he decided not to come at this time, so he will come at his convenience.
Keep watch, and stand fast in the faith, be strong and brave like men.
Let everything you do be done with charity.
I know that you brothers also know that the house of Stephanas was the first fruits of Achaia, and they have addicted themselves to the ministry of the saints. So, I beg you to
submit yourselves to those such as these and to everyone who labors and helps us.
I am glad that Stephanas, Fortunatus, and Achaicus have arrived, because they have supplied what was lacking on your part.
For they have refreshed your spirit and mine, so I ask that you acknowledge such men as these.
The churches of Asia salute you. Aquila and Priscilla offer many salutations to you in the Lord, along with the church that meets in their house.
All the brothers greet you. So, greet one another with a holy kiss.
I Paul, send this salutation to you from my own hand.
If anyone does not love the Lord Jesus Christ, let them be an Anathema Maranatha (Which means: Cursed is the one who does not love the Lord Jesus Christ).
May the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you.
And my love will be with you all in Jesus Christ. Amen!"
Paul, an Apostle of Jesus Christ by God's will and our brother Timothy, wrote a letter to the church of God in Corinth and all the saints throughout Achaia which said,
"Grace be to you and peace from God our father, and from the Lord Jesus Christ.
Blessed be God the father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the father of mercies and the God of all comfort.
Our God who comforts us in all our tribulation, so that we may comfort those who are in any kind of trouble, with the comfort by which we ourselves are comforted by God.
For just as Christ 's sufferings abound within us, so does our consolation which also abounds through Christ.
And if we are afflicted, it is for your consolation and salvation, and if we are comforted, it is for your consolation and salvation. For we also suffer and endure the same sufferings as you.
And our hope for you is steadfast, for we know that as you share in our sufferings, so also will you share in our consolation.

For we would not want our brothers to be ignorant of the trouble we encountered in Asia. We were burdened beyond our own strength and above our ability to endure, so much so that we even despaired our own life.
But we had the sentence of death within ourselves, so that we did not trust in ourselves, but we had to trust in God who raises the dead.
The God who delivered us from such a great death, and who still delivers us, and in whom we trust that he will deliver us yet again.
You also help us with your prayers, for the gift that is bestowed upon us by the many people who give thanks to God on our behalf.

For we rejoice in this; the simple testimony of our conscience is in Godly sincerity, not with fleshly wisdom. But by the grace of God, we have had our conversation with the world, and more abundantly toward you.
For we write nothing more to you, than what you have read or acknowledged, which I trust you will continue to acknowledge to the very end.
Since you have also partially acknowledged us and you rejoice in us, just as we will also rejoice in you on the Day of the Lord Jesus.
Being confident of this, I decided to come visit you before, so that you might receive a second benefit.
And to pass by you on my way to Macedonia, and to return to you on my way back from Macedonia, so that you may help me on my way to Judea.
Therefore, when I thought about this, did I plan carelessly? Or do I propose these things in accordance with the flesh, so that I say, 'Yes, yes,' when I meant to say, 'No, no'?
But since God is true, our word toward you was not 'Yes and no.'
For Jesus Christ the son of God, who was preached about to you by Silvanus, Timothy, and me, was not, 'Yes and no,' but in Christ it was always, 'yes.'
For all of God's promises through Christ are always, 'Yes,' and in him we say, 'Amen,' to the glory of God.
Now God establishes both us and you in Christ, for God has anointed us.
For God has also placed his seal on us and given our hearts an earnest spirit.
Furthermore, I call on God's record for my soul to spare you, since I had not yet come to Corinth.
Not that we have authority over your faith, but we are your helpers for your joy, because you stand by your faith."
And Paul continued writing this letter to the church of God in Corinth which said, "But I decided that I would not return to you in sadness.
For if I make you sorry, who is left to make me happy, except those whom I have made sorry?

And I have written this to you, so that when I return, I will not have sorrow from those with whom I should rejoice. For I have confidence in you all, so that my joy is the joy that I share with you all.
For out of much affliction and anguish of heart, I wrote to you with many tears. Not to grieve you, but to show you the abundant love which I have for you.
But if anyone has caused grief, he has not grieved me, but I say this in part, so that I do not overwhelm you all.
Suffice it to say, that this punishment is sufficient for such a man as one who was afflicted by so many.
So to the contrary, you should forgive and comfort him, otherwise such a man may perhaps be swallowed up and overcome by so much sorrow.
Therefore I beg you to confirm your love toward him.
For this is why I am writing, so that I might know that your test would prove, whether or not you are obedient in all things.
If you forgive someone of anything, then I also forgive them. For if I forgave anyone of anything, it is for your sakes that I forgave it through the person of Christ.
Otherwise Satan would gain an advantage over us, for we are not ignorant of his devices.
Furthermore, when I came to Troas to preach Christ's gospel, the Lord opened a door for me.
I had no rest in my spirit, because I did not find my brother Titus there, so I left them and went to Macedonia.
Now thanks be to God, who always causes us to triumph in Christ, and manifests the aroma of his knowledge through us everywhere.
For we are the sweet smell of Christ to God among those who are saved, and for those who are perishing.
To one we are the smell of death unto death, and to the other the smell of life unto life. And who is sufficient to teach these things?
For we are not like so many others, who corrupt God's word. But we speak of Christ in the sight of God out of God's sincerity."

And Paul continued writing this letter to the church of God in Corinth which said, "Do we need to begin again to commend ourselves as some others do? Do we need letters of commendation to you or from you?
You are our letter written in our hearts, known and read by all men.

For you are obviously declared to be the letter from Christ, since you were ministered to by us, not written with ink. But you were written with the spirit of the living God, not in stone tablets, but in fleshly tablets of the heart.
And we have such trust towards God through Jesus Christ.
Not that we have sufficient confidence in ourselves to think that anything is from ourselves, but our sufficiency is from God.
For God has made us competent ministers of the new testament, not of the letter but of the spirit, because the letter kills but the spirit gives life.

But if the ministry of death which was written and engraved on stones was so glorious, that the children of Israel could not safely look upon the face of Moses because of the fading glory of his appearance.
How then can the ministry of the spirit not be rather glorious?
For if the ministry of condemnation is glory, how much more does the ministry of righteousness exceed in glory.
For in this respect, even then that which was made glorious had no glory, because of the glory that excels beyond it.
For if that which was done away was glorious, how much more glorious is that which remains.
Therefore, since we have such a hope, we speak very plainly.
Not like Moses who put a vail over his face, so that the children of Israel could not see the end of that which was abolished.
But their minds were blinded, because until today that same vail remains unremoved in the reading of the Old Testament, because only in Christ is that vail taken away.
But even today, when Moses is read, that vail covers their heart.
Nevertheless, when anyone turns to the Lord, the vail will be taken away.
Now the Lord is that spirit, and where the Lord's spirit is, there is liberty.
But we all, with an open unveiled face see the reflection of the glory of the Lord, and we are all changed into his image from one glory to the next, through the Lord's spirit."
And Paul continued writing this letter to the church of God in Corinth which said, "Therefore, since we have had this ministry, we have received mercy, and we do not faint.

But we have renounced the hidden dishonest thing, we do not walk in craftiness, nor do we handle God's word deceitfully, but by the materialization of the truth, we commend ourselves to every man's conscience in the sight of God.
But if our gospel is hidden, it is hidden to those who are lost.
It is hidden by the God of this world, who has blinded the minds of those who do not believe, otherwise the light of the glorious gospel of Jesus Christ, who is the image of God, would shine in them.
For we do not preach about ourselves, we preach about the Lord Jesus Christ, and about ourselves as your servants for Jesus' sake.
For God, who commanded the light to shine out of the darkness, has shined in our hearts and given us the light of the knowledge of God's glory in the face of Jesus Christ.
But we have this treasure in earthen vessels, so that the excellency of this power may be from God, and not from us.
We are troubled on every side, but we are not distressed, and we are baffled, but we do not despair.
We are persecuted, but not forsaken, and we are thrown down, but not destroyed.
We always carry the death of our Lord Jesus within our body, so that the life of Jesus may also be manifested in our body.
For those of us who live are always delivered over to death for the sake of Jesus, so that the life of Jesus may also be manifested in our mortal flesh.
So then death works in us, so that life may work in you.
We have the same spirit of faith, in accordance with what is written where it says: 'I believed, therefore I have spoken, (Psalm 116:10)' so we also believe and we speak.
Knowing that God who raised up the Lord Jesus, will also raise us up through Jesus and present us along with you.
For all things are for your sake, so that the abundant grace might through the thanksgiving of many redound to the glory of God.
Because we do not faint for this cause, but even though our outward man perishes, still our inner man is renewed day by day.
For our light and momentary affliction works much more for us and exceeds the eternal weight of glory.
We do not look at the external things which are seen, but we look at the things which are not seen. For the things which are seen are temporary, but the things which are not seen are eternal."

And Paul continued writing this letter to the church of God in Corinth which said, "For we know that if our earthly tabernacle home were dissolved, we have a building from God, an eternal house in heaven, not built with human hands.
For we groan and we earnestly desire to be clothed in our heavenly home.
So that if we are clothed, we will not be found naked.
For those of us who are in this tabernacle must groan under our burdens. Because it is not that we want to be unclothed but we desire to be clothed, so that mortality may be swallowed up by life.
Now God has worked in us and given us this very same thing, which is an earnest Holy Spirit.
Therefore, we are always confident, and we know that while we are at home in the body, we are also absent from the Lord.
For we walk by faith, not by sight.
And I say that we are confident, and rather willing to be absent from the body so we can be present with the Lord.
So we labor, whether we are present or absent from this body, so that we may be accepted by the Lord.
For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ, so that each one may receive their reward for the things done in the body, whether it was good or bad.
Therefore, since we know the terror of the Lord, we try to persuade other men. But we have become obvious to God, and I also trust we have made ourselves obvious in your consciences.
For we do not commend ourselves to you again. But we are giving you an occasion to glory on our behalf, so that you may answer those who glory in their appearance, but not in their heart.
For even if we are crazy and beside ourselves it is for God, but we remain sober for your cause.
For Christ's love constrains us, because in our judgement, Jesus died for all of us, and then all were dead.
Jesus died for all, so that those who live would not live only for themselves from now on, but for the one who died for them and rose again.
So, from now on know this, we regard no man by the flesh. Even though we once knew Christ in the flesh, we no longer know him this way.
Therefore, if a man is in Christ, he is a new creature, old things have passed away and behold all things have become new again.
And all things are from God, who has reconciled himself to us through Jesus Christ, and he has given us the ministry of reconciliation.
That is to say, that God was reconciling the world to himself in Christ, by not imputing their trespasses against them. And God has committed this word of reconciliation to us.
Therefore, we are now ambassadors for Christ, and it is as if God has begged you through us. So, we pray on behalf of Christ, that you will be reconciled to God.
For God made the one who knew no sin to be sin for us, so that we could become the righteousness of God in him."
And Paul continued writing this letter to the church of God in Corinth which said, "We are workers together with God, and we beg you not to receive the grace of God in vain.
For God says, 'I heard you at the accepted time, and I helped you on the day of salvation (Isaiah 49:8). Behold the accepted time is now, and the day of salvation is now.
We offer no offense against anything, so that the ministry is not blamed.
But we prove ourselves to be ministers of God in all things, with much patience, in afflictions, necessities, and distresses.
In stripes, imprisonments, tumults, labors, in watching, and in fasting.
Through purity, knowledge, long suffering, kindness, and through the Holy Spirit and true love.
By the truthful word, and by the power of God, and by the armor of righteousness on the right and the left hand.
By honor and dishonor, by evil reports and good reports, we are seen as deceivers, and yet we are true.
We are seen as unknown, and yet we are well known, we are seen as dying, but we live, and we are chastened but we are not killed.
We are seen as sorrowful, yet we are always rejoicing, we are seen as poor, yet we are making many rich, we are seen as having nothing and yet we possess everything.
O you Corinthians, we have spoken openly to you, and our heartshave been enlarged.
You are not restrained by us, but you are restrained by your own hearts.
So now as an equal compensation, I will speak to you as if you were my children and say, 'May your heart also be enlarged.'
Do not be unequally yoked to unbelievers, for what fellowship can righteousness have with unrighteousness, and what communion can the light have with darkness?
And what harmony can Christ have with Belial? Or what does a believer have in common with an infidel?

And what agreement can the temple of God have with idols? For you are the temple of the living God, and it is just as God has said, 'I will live in them, and walk in them, and I will be their God, and they will be my people. (Leviticus 26:11–12)'
For the Lord says, 'Come out from among them, and separate yourselves from them, touch nothing unclean (Isaiah 52:11), and I will receive you.'
And I will be your father, and you will be my sons and daughters. (2 Samuel 7:14)' Thus says the Lord Almighty."

And Paul continued writing this letter to the church of God in Corinth which said, "Therefore dearly beloved, we have these promises, so let us cleanse ourselves from all the filth in the flesh and spirit, and perfect our holiness in the fear of God.
So accept us, for we have wronged no one, we have corrupted no one, and we have defrauded no one.
I do not say this to condemn you, for I have previously said that you are in our hearts, and we live and die with you.
My speech has been very bold toward you, and I have greatly glorified you; I am filled with comfort, and I have been exceedingly joyful in all of our tribulations.
For, when we came to Macedonia, our bodies had not rested, and we were troubled on every side. We were fighting on the outside, but we were fearful on the inside.
Nevertheless God, comforts those who are thrown down, and he comforted us by sending Titus.
And not only by the arrival of Titus, but also by how Titus was comforted by you. For he told us of your earnest desire, your mourning, and your fervent mind toward me, so that I rejoiced even more.
For even though I caused you sorrow with my letter, I do not regret it. I did regret it at the time, because I thought that the letter had caused you sorrow, but only for a short time.
Now I rejoice, not because you were made sorrowful, but because your sorrow led to your repentance, because you sorrow was for a Godly reason, and you were not damaged by us in any way.
For Godly sorrow works repentance that leads to salvation with no regrets, but worldly sorrow brings only death.

For you can now see what this Godly sorrow has given you, and what careful clearing of yourselves it has worked in you to see what indignation, fear, vehement desires, zeal, and what revenge it has removed! You have proven yourselves to be clear about all things concerning this matter.
So even though I wrote to you, I did not write because someone had done wrong, nor because someone had suffered a wrong, but so that our care for you in God's sight might appear to you.
Therefore, we were comforted in your comfort, and we were exceedingly more joyful for the joy of Titus, for his spirit was refreshed by you all.
For I am not ashamed of anything I have boasted to him about you, but everything we said to you was the truth, and so was our boasting to Titus about you.
And his inner affection toward you is even more abundant, when he remembers your obedience as you received him with fear and trembling.
Therefore, I rejoice and I have confidence in you in all things."
And Paul continued writing this letter to the church of God in Corinth which said, "Furthermore brothers, we want to witness to you about the grace that God has bestowed on the churches of Macedonia.
How in their great trial of affliction, that their abundant joy and deep poverty abounded into rich generosity.
For I bear witness to their power and beyond, how willing they were to give of themselves.
Earnestly pleading with us that we would accept their gift and allow them to take on the fellowship of ministering to the saints.
And they did, but not as we had expected, but they first gave themselves to the Lord, and then to us because it was God's will.
So, we desired that Titus would finish what he had begun, in the same grace he had with you.
Therefore, since you abound in everything, including faith, speech, knowledge, diligence, and in your love to us, make sure that you also abound in this grace.
I am not demanding this, but I am saying this to compare your boldness to that of others, and to prove the sincerity of your love.
For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that even though he was rich, he became poor for your sake, so that through his poverty you might become rich.
So I give you my advice, for this is expedient for you, last year you began before others, not only to do God's will, but you were also straightforward about it.
Therefore keep doing it, so that you may continue to perform as you have been with a readiness of will to serve.
Because a willing mind is accepted according to what a man has, and not according to what he does not have.
For I do not mean that other men should have it easy, and you should be burdened.
But so that there is equality, at this time your abundance may be able to supply their needs, so that later on their abundance may also supply your needs.
For as it is written; 'Those who gathered much had nothing left over, and those who gathered little lacked nothing. (Exodus 16:18)'
But thanks be to God, who put the same earnest care for you into the heart of Titus.
For he did indeed accept the encouragement, but since he was more outgoing, he went to you on his own accord.
And we have sent a brother with him, who is praised throughout all the churches for his work in the gospel.
And not only that, this brother who was also chosen by the churches to travel with us with this grace to help us administer to the glory of the Lord and to declare your willing mind.
We hope to avoid being blamed for the way this abundance is administered by us.
For we not only try to provide for honest things in the Lord's sight, but also in the sight of men.
And we have sent our brother with them, whom we have often proven diligent in many things, but now even more so in the great confidence which I have in you.
If anyone wants to inquire about Titus, he is my partner and fellow helper among you. And if anyone asks about our brothers, they are the messengers of the churches and the glory of Christ.
Therefore, show the churches proof of your love and the reason for our boasting on your behalf."
And Paul continued writing this letter to the church of God in Corinth which said, "Now it is wasteful for me to write to you about this subject of ministering to the saints.
For I know your eager mind, and I have boasted of you to the Macedonians that since last year Achaia was ready, and your zeal has provoked many others.
But I have sent the brothers, otherwise our boasting of you would have been in vain, but that just as I said, you may be ready.
Otherwise, if by chance any Macedonians come with me and find you unprepared, and we say nothing, then you would be ashamed of this same confident boasting.

Therefore, I thought it was necessary to encourage the brothers to go before you, to prepare ahead of time for your bounty, which you had given notice of earlier. So that it may be prepared from your bounty, and not as something of selfish desire.
But this I say, "Whoever sows sparingly will also reap sparingly, and whoever sows bountifully will also reap bountifully.
Let each man give in accordance with whatever is in his heart and not grudgingly or because it is required, for God loves a cheerful giver.
And God is also able to make grace abound toward you, so that you always have sufficiency in all things, and you will abound in every good work.
For as it is written; 'God has dispersed his gifts to the poor, his righteousness endures forever. (Psalm 112:9)'
Now those who minister seed to the sower, minister both bread for your food, and they multiply the seed you have sown, and increase the fruits of your righteousness.
You will be bountifully enriched in everything through us, and that which causes us to give thanksgiving to God.
For the administration of this service for the saints, not only supplies what the saints are lacking, but is also abundant in many giving thanks to God.
While through the experiment of this ministry they glorify God for your professed confession of the gospel of Christ, and for your liberal giving to them, and to all men.
And their prayers for you, by those who long to offer you the exceeding grace that God has given you.
Thanks be to God for his unspeakable gift!"

And Paul continued writing this letter to the church of God in Corinth which said, "Now I beg you by the meekness and gentleness of Christ. For I am humble when I am with you, but when I am not there in person, I am bold toward you.
But I beg that when I am present with you, I do not need to be that bold and confident against those among you who think that we should walk according to the flesh.
For though we walk in the flesh, we do not wage war according to the flesh.
For our weapons of warfare are not carnal, but through God they have the mighty power to destroy strongholds.
We tear down imaginations and every high thing that glorifies itself against the knowledge of God, and we capture every thought to make it obedient to Christ.
And we are ready to take revenge against all disobedience, when your obedience is fulfilled.
Do you look at the outward appearance of things? If a man trusts within himself that he is Christ's, let him remind himself that just as he belongs to Christ, so do we.
For even though I did somewhat boast about our authority the Lord has given us for your moral instruction, and not for your destruction, I will not be ashamed.
I do not want to seem to be trying to frighten you with my letters.
For they say, 'Paul's letters carry a heavy and powerful burden, but his body is weak and his speech is hateful.'
So let those such as this know, that the words we use in our letters when we are absent, we will indeed use when we are present.

For we do not dare to make ourselves part of or compare ourselves with some of those who commend themselves. They measure themselves by themselves, and compare themselves with themselves, and prove that they are not wise.
But we will not unceasingly boast of things beyond measure, but only within the measure of the rule which God has given us, a measure that will reach even you.
For we do not stretch ourselves beyond our measure, as if we had not reached out to you. For we have also come this far to preach the gospel of Christ to you.
We do not boast of things beyond our measure of other men's labors. But we hope that as your faith increases, we will be abundantly enlarged by you in accordance with our rule.
So that we can preach the gospel in the regions beyond you. Then we will not boast in another man's line of things made ready by our hand.
But let those who glorify, glorify in the Lord.
For it is not those who commend themselves who are approved, but it is those whom the Lord commends that areapproved."
And Paul continued writing this letter to the church of God in Corinth which said, "I pray to God that you will bear with me for a little of my foolishness, and you do indeed bear with me.
For I am jealous of you with a Godly jealousy, for I have promised you to one husband, so that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ.
But I fear, that just as the serpent deceived Eve through his subtle deceit, that your minds will be corrupted from the simplicity that is in Christ.

For if someone comes and preaches to you about a different Jesus than the one we have preached, or you receive a spirit different than the one you have received from us, or a gospel different than the one you accepted, you might accept him too easily.
For I do not think of myself as one tiny bit inferior to the most chief apostles.
But even though I use rude speech, I am not lacking in knowledge, and we have made ourselves thoroughly obvious to you in all things.
Have I committed an offense by abasing myself so that you might be glorified, because I have freely preached the gospel of God to you?
I robbed other churches by taking wages from them, so that I could be of service to you.

And while I was in need when I was with you, I was a burden to no one, because whatever I was lacking, the brothers from Macedonia supplied. For I have prevented myself from being a burden to you in all things, and I will continue to take care of myself.
As surely as the truth of Christ is in me, no one will stop me from boasting of this throughout the regions of Achaia.
Why is that? Is it because I do not love you? God knows that I do!
I will continue to do what I do, so that I may cut off those who desire an opportunity to glorify themselves in an attempt to convince people they are like us.
For such men are false apostles, deceitful workers, pretending to be the apostles of Christ.
And it is no wonder, because Satan himself pretends to be an angel of light.
Therefore, it is no surprise that if Satan's ministers pretend to be like the ministers of righteousness, their end will come according to their works.
I say again, 'Let no one think of me as a fool, otherwise, you will receive me as a fool, which may also cause me to boast about myself a little.
So, I do not speak as the Lord, but I confidently speak as a boasting foolish fool.
Since many glorify the flesh, I will also glorify the flesh.
For you gladly suffer fools, since you are so wise.
You even allow men to enslave you, devour you, and take from you. You even allow a man to glorify himself and strike you on the face.
I speak about disapproval, as though we had been weak. However, whenever anyone is bold, I also speak foolishly, for I am also bold.
Are they Hebrews? So am I. Are they Israelis? So am I. Are they Abraham's descendants? So am I.
Are they ministers of Christ? I speak as a fool, but I am much more: For I am more abundant in labor, I am beaten with stripes beyond measure, I am more frequently in prison, and more often in death.
I have received 39 stripes five different times from the Jews.
Three times was I beaten with rods, once was I stoned, three times I have suffered through a shipwreck. And I spent one night and one day in the deep blue sea.

When I travel, I am often in the peril of the waters and robbers, and I am often in peril of my own countrymen and the heathen. I am also often in peril in the city, the wilderness, the sea, and among false brothers.
In weary and pain, I often in keep watch at night without sleep, and I am often fasting, hungry, and thirsty while cold and naked.
Besides those things that I do without every day, the daily care of all the churches comes to me.
Care for those who are weak, for I am not weak? Care for those who are offended, and I do not burn?
If I must glorify, I will glorify the things which concern my infirmities.
The God and father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who is blessed forever, knows that I do not lie.
In Damascus, the governor under King Aretas surrounded the city with a garrison of men, just to apprehend me.
But I was lowered down from the wall through a window in a basket and I escaped."

And Paul continued writing this letter to the church of God in Corinth which said, "It is not expedient for me to glorify myself. For there is no doubt that I will go on receiving visions and revelations from the Lord.
I knew a man in Christ about fourteen years ago who was brought up to the third heaven, whether in the body or not, I could not tell. And only God knows.
And I knew that this man, whether it was in the body or out of the body, I could not tell, but God knows.
I knew this man was brought up into paradise, and he heard unspeakable words which are not lawful for a man to speak.
I will glorify such a man, but I will not glorify myself, except in my infirmities.

For even if I did glorify myself, I would not be a fool, because I would still be speaking the truth. But now I restrain myself, otherwise men would think more of me than what they see or hear from me.

And to prevent me from being glorified beyond measure through the abundance of the revelations, I was given a thorn in the flesh. Satan's messenger uses this thorn to torment me and prevent me from being glorified beyond measure.
For I have begged the Lord to let this thing leave me three different times.

But the Lord spoke to me and said, 'My grace is sufficient for you, because my strength is made perfect in weakness.' Therefore, I most happily glory in my infirmities, so that the power of Christ may rest on me.
Therefore, I take pleasure in infirmities, disrespect, persecutions, distresses, and a lack of necessities for Christ's sake, because I am strongest when I am weak.
I have become a fool in glorifying myself, but you pushed me into it. Because you should have commended me, since I am in no way inferior to the most chief apostles, even though I am nothing.
Truly the signs of an apostle were worked among you in patience, signs, wonders, and mighty deeds.
For how were you treated inferior to other churches, except that I was not a burden to you? Forgive me of this wrong!

Behold, I am now ready to come to you for the third time, and I will not be a burden to you. I do not seek your possessions, I seek only you, because the children should not save for their parent's future, but the parents should save for their children's future.
For I will very gladly spend my money and myself for you, even though the more abundantly I love you, the less I am loved.
And even though I did not burden you, I was very crafty, and I caught you with deceit.
But did anyone I sent to you, ever exploit you in any way?
I asked Titus to visit you along with our brother. Did Titus exploit you? Did we not walk in the same spirit and in the same steps?
Again, do you think we are making excuses about ourselves to you? Dearly beloved, we speak and do all things before God in Christ, simply for your instruction.

For I fear that when I come, I will not find you to be as I would like, and you may not find me to be as you like. But I fear there will be debates, envy, wrath, strife, backbiting, whispering, swelling, and tumults.
And I fear that when I return, my God will humble me among you, and I will be forced to grieve for many who have sinned and not repented of their uncleanliness, fornication, and lasciviousness."
And Paul continued writing this letter to the church of God in Corinth which said, "This is the third time I am coming to you. Every word must be established by the mouth of two or three witnesses.
I previously warned you the second time I was with you. Since I am now absent, I am writing to those who sinned earlier and to all the others, and I will spare no one if I return.
Since you seek proof that Christ speaks through me. Christ is not weak, but he is mighty toward you.
For even though he was crucified through weakness, he lives by the power of God. For we are also weak in him, but we will live with him by the power of God to serve you.
Examine yourselves to see if you are in the faith. Can you not see for yourselves that Jesus Christ lives within you, you cannot if you are a scoundrel?
But I trust that you will know that we are not scoundrels.
Now I pray to God that you do no evil, not so we would appear to be approved, but so that you would do what is honest, even if we appear to be scoundrels.
For we can do nothing against the truth, but only for the truth.
For we rejoice when we are weak, but you are strong, and we also wish for your perfection.
So I write these things while I am absent, otherwise when I am present, I would use sharp powerful words that the Lord has given me for your education and not for your destruction.
Finally brothers, farewell. Be perfect, be of good cheer, be of one mind, live in peace, and may the God of love and peace will be with you.
Greet one another with a holy kiss.
All the saints send you their salutations.
May the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, the love of God, and the communion of the Holy Spirit, be with you all. Amen!"
I Paul, am not an apostle of men nor by man, but by Jesus Christ and God the father, who raised Jesus from the dead.
And all the brothers with me, wrote this letter to the churches of Galatia which said,
"May you have the grace and peace from God the father, and from our Lord Jesus Christ.
Jesus gave himself for our sins, so that he could deliver us from this present evil world, which is the will of God our heavenly father.
And glory belongs to God forever and ever. Amen.
I marvel at how quickly you abandoned the teachings of the one who called you to the grace of Jesus Christ and turned to another gospel.
Which is not really another gospel, but something else being taught by those who would trouble you and pervert the gospel of Christ.
But cursed be the man, even if it was us or an angel from heaven, who preached any other gospel to you than that which we have preached.
As we have said before, and I now repeat, cursed be the man who preaches any other gospel to you than that which you have already received from us.
And do I now seek to please men, or am I trying to persuade men for God? For if I were still trying to please men, I would not be the servant of Christ.
But brothers, I certify to you that the gospel which was preached by me does not come from man.
For I neither received it from man, nor was I taught it, but it came as a revelation from Jesus Christ.
For you have heard of my past conversations in the Jewish religion, and how I persecuted and wasted the church of God beyond measure.
And how I profited much more than many of my equals in the Jewish religion in my own nation, and how I was extremely zealous for the traditions of my fathers.
But when it pleased God, who separated me from my mother's womb, he called me by his grace.
To reveal his son in me, so that I could preach about him among the heathen, and immediately I did not consult with flesh and blood.
Nor did I go to those who were apostles before me in Jerusalem, but I went to Arabia and later returned to Damascus.
Then after three years I went to Jerusalem to see Peter and lived with him for fifteen days.
But I saw no other apostles, except for the Lord's brother James.
Now behold, I say to you before God that I do not lie to you about the things I am writing.
Afterwards I went to the regions of Syria and Cilicia.
But at that time, I was still unknown to the churches of Judea which were in Christ.
For they had only heard that the man who had persecuted them in the past, was now preaching the faith which he once tried to destroy.
And they glorified God in me."
And Paul continued this letter to the churches of Galatia which said, "Then fourteen years later, I returned to Jerusalem with Barnabas and Titus.

I went to teach them about a revelation I had about the gospel that I had preached to the Gentiles. But I spoke privately to those who had the reputation there as leaders, otherwise I felt like I would have run, or had already run to them in vain.
But not even Titus, who went with me, had been compelled to be circumcised even though he was Greek.
Because some false brothers caught us unaware, for they had come into our midst to secretly spy on our liberty in Jesus Christ, in an attempt to enslave us.
We did not allow them to control us, not even for a minute, so that the truth of the gospel could continue in you.

But those who thought of themselves as somewhat superior, or whatever they thought they were, it makes no difference to me. For God favors no man above another, and those who seemed to concur with each other, added nothing to me.
On the contrary, they saw that teaching the gospel to the uncircumcised had been committed to me, just as Peter had been committed to the gospel of the circumcised.
For the same one who worked successfully in Peter's apostleship to the circumcised, is the one who did the mighty works in me toward the Gentiles.

But when James, Cephas, and John, who seemed to be pillars of the faith, saw the grace that was given to me, they gave Barnabas and the right hand of friendship to me. So that we could go to the heathen, and they could go to the circumcised.
The pillars of the faith only asked us to remember the poor, which is what I also want.
When Peter came to Antioch, I confronted him to his face, because he was to blame.

Because James used to eat with the Gentiles before he was confronted by some men about the circumcision. And when they showed up, James withdrew and separated himself from the Gentiles because he was afraid of the men who preached circumcision.
And other Jews also pretended to agree with James, so much so that Barnabas was also carried away by their deceit.

But when I saw that they did not walk upright with the truth of the gospel, I said to Peter before all of them, 'If you as a Jew, live as if you are a Gentile, and not like a Jew; why do you compel the Gentiles to live like a Jew?'
For we who are Jews by nature, are not Gentile sinners.

We also know that a man is not justified by works of the law, but by the faith of Jesus Christ. We believe in Jesus Christ, so that we can be justified through our faith in Christ, not by works of the law. Because no flesh can be justified by works of the law.
But if we seek to be justified by Christ, and we also find that we ourselves are sinners, does that make Christ the minister of sin? God forbid: No!
Therefore, if I rebuild the sinful things that I destroyed, then I turn myself into a transgressor.
For through the law, I am dead to the law, so that I might live to God.

For I have been crucified with Christ. Nevertheless, I live, but it is not me, it is Christ who lives in me. And the life which I now live in the flesh, I live by the faith of God's son, who loved me and gave his life for me.
And I do not want to frustrate the grace of God, because if righteousness comes through the law, then Christ died in vain."

And Paul continued this letter to the churches of Galatia which said, "O foolish Galatians! Who has bewitched you? So that you cannot obey the truth, for it has been preached before your very own eyes that Jesus Christ was crucified?
I would just like to learn this from you. Did you receive the spirit by works of the law, or by hearing in faith?
Are you so foolish? You began in the spirit, and are you now made perfect by the flesh?
Have you suffered so many things in vain? If it was in vain.
Does God minister to your spirit and work miracles among you by works of the law, or by hearing in faith?
Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness.
Therefore, you must understand that those who have faith, are also the children of Abraham.
The scripture foresaw that God would justify the heathen through faith, for the gospel was preached to Abraham beforehand and said, 'All nations will be blessed through you. (Genesis 22:18)'
So then those who are of the faith are blessed along with faithful Abraham.
For those who rely on the works of the law are under the curse, for it is written, 'Cursed is he who does not continue to do all things written in the Book of the Law. (Deuteronomy 27:26)'
But no man can be justified by the law in God's sight, for it is evident: 'The righteous will live by faith. (Habakkuk 2:4)'
And the law is not based on faith but: 'Those who do these things will live by them (Leviticus 18:5).'
Christ has rescued us from the law's curse since he was made a curse for us, for it is written: 'Anyone hanged on a tree is cursed by God! (Deuteronomy 21:23)'
So that the blessing promised to Abraham would come to the Gentiles through Jesus Christ, in order for us to receive the promise of the spirit through faith.
Brothers, I am speaking as a man, even if a covenant is made and confirmed by just men, no man can annul it or add to it.
Now these promises were made to Abraham and his descendants. God did not promise this to the descendants of many, but to the descendants of one, and that one is Christ.
And I say that the covenant was previously confirmed before God in Christ. And the law that came 430 years later, cannot annul nor make the promise ineffective.
For if the inheritance comes from the law, it is no longer a promise, but God gave it to Abraham as a promise.
Then why do we serve the law? The law was added because of transgressions, until the descendant came to whom the promise was made, and it was ordained by angels in the hand of a mediator.
Now a mediator is not needed for just one, but God is one.
Is the law against the promises of God? God forbid: No! For if there had been a law given which could have given life, in all honesty righteousness would have come from the law.
But the scripture concludes all things are under sin, so that by faith in Jesus Christ the promise might be given to those who believe.
But before faith came, we were kept locked under the law, until the faith could be revealed afterwards.
Therefore the law was our schoolmaster to bring us to Christ, so that we might be justified by faith.
But after faith has come, we are no longer under a schoolmaster.
For you are all the children of God by faith in Jesus Christ.
For as many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on the armor of Christ.
There is neither Jew nor Greek, slave nor free, male nor female: for you are all one in Jesus Christ.
And if you belong to Christ, then you are Abraham's descendant and an heir according to the promise."
And Paul continued this letter to the churches of Galatia which said, "So what I am saying, is that as long as the heir is a child, he is no different than a servant, even though he owns everything.
But he is under tutors and governors until the time appointed by his father.
So even when we were children, we were enslaved under the elements of the world.
But when the right time came, God sent his son Jesus, born from a woman, and born under the law.
To rescue those who were under the law, so that we could receive our adoption as sons.
And because you are sons, God sent his son's spirit into your hearts, crying out, 'Abba, father!'
Therefore, you are no longer a servant, but a son, and if you are a son, then you are an heir of God through Christ.
However, when you did not know God, you served those who by nature are not gods.
But now that you know God, or rather God knows you, how can you return to the weak and beggarly principles? Do you want to be in bondage again?
You observe days, months, times, and years.
And I am afraid for you, for I fear that I have bestowed labor upon you in vain.
Brothers, I beg you to be like me, because I am just like you, and you have not injured me at all.
For you know that at first, I preached the gospel to you through an infirmity in the flesh.
And you did not despise nor reject me because of the temptations which were in my flesh, but you received me like an angel of God, or even as Jesus Christ.
Where then is the blessedness you spoke of? For I can testify, that at one time if it had been possible, you would have taken out your own eyes and given them to me.
So have I now become your enemy, because I tell you the truth?
For the deceitful workers disguised as apostles of Christ zealously affect you, but not in a good way. They want to exclude you, so that your zealousness benefits them.
But it is always good to be zealously affected by a good thing, and not only when I am with you.
My little children, for whom I labor in birth pains again until Christ is formed in you.
I wish I could be present with you now, and I wish I could change the tone of my voice, but I do have my doubts about you.
Tell me, those of you who desire to be under the law, do you not understand the law?
For it is written, 'Abraham had two sons, one by a slave woman, the other by a free woman. (Genesis 16:15) and (Genesis 21:1-2)'
The son who was born to the slave woman was born from the flesh, but the son born to the free woman was born from God's promise.
Because this is the comparison, these two women represent two covenants. The covenant that comes from Hagar is Mount Sinai, and she gives birth to slave children.
Because Hagar represents Mount Sinai in Arabia, she answers to Jerusalem because she and her children are slaves.
But the Jerusalem which is above her is free, and she is the mother of us all.

For it is written; 'Rejoice, you childless woman who has never given birth or gone through labor. Sing loudly and rejoice, because the abandoned woman has more children than the married woman. (Isaiah 54:1)
Now brothers, we are like Isaac, for we are the children of promise.
But back then just as it is now, the son who was born of the flesh, persecutes the son who was born of the spirit.
Nevertheless, what does the scripture say? 'Throw out the slave woman and her son, because the son of the free woman will not share his inheritance with the son of the slave woman. (Genesis 21:10)'
So then brothers, we are not the children of the slave woman, we are the children of the free woman."

And Paul continued this letter to the churches of Galatia which said, "Therefore, stand fast in the liberty by which Christ has made us free, and do not allow yourselves to be entangled in the yoke of bondage again.
Behold, I Paul say to every man who is circumcised, Christ will profit you nothing.
For I testify once again to every man who is circumcised, you are indebted to obey the whole law.
Christ has become ineffectual to whoever among you are trying to be justified by the law, for you have fallen from grace.
For by faith through the spirit, we wait for the hope of righteousness.
For in Jesus Christ neither circumcision nor uncircumcision profits us anything, but faith works through love.
You ran well at first, so who hindered you and caused you not to obey the truth?
This persuasion does not come from the one who calls you.
For a little leavening will leaven the whole lump of dough.
I have confidence that through the Lord, you will be no other than wise minded. But the one who troubles you will bear God's judgment, whoever he may be.
And brothers, if I am still preaching circumcision, why do I still suffer from persecution? If the law is the answer, then the offense of the cross has ceased.
I even wish that those who trouble you would be cut off.
For you brothers, have been called to liberty, so do not use your liberty as an occasion for the flesh, but serve one another through love.
For even in this, the whole law is satisfied in just one statement, 'You must love your neighbor as you love yourself.'
But if you bite and devour one another, be careful that you do not consume each other.
This then is what I say, 'Walk in the spirit, and you will not gratify the lust of the flesh.
For the flesh lusts against the spirit, and the spirit lusts against the flesh. For they are contrary to each other, which prevents you from doing whatever you want.'
But if you are led by the spirit, you are not under the law.
Now the works of the flesh are obvious such as adultery, fornication, uncleanliness, debauchery,
idolatry, witchcraft, hatred, division, jealousy, anger, conflict, sedition, heresy,

envy, murder, drunkenness, reveling, and other things such as this which I have warned you about before. And just as I have told you in the past, those who do such things will not inherit the Kingdom of God.
But the fruit of the spirit is love, joy, peace, long suffering, gentleness, goodness, faith,
meekness, and temperance. For there is no law against such things.
And those who belong to Christ have crucified the flesh with its affections and lusts.
If we live in the spirit, let us also walk in the spirit.
Let us not desire vain glory, nor envy and provoke one another."

And Paul finished this letter to the churches of Galatia which said, "Brothers, if a man is overtaken by sin, you who are spiritual, restore one such as this in the spirit of meekness. But you yourself must think, otherwise you may also be tempted.
Bear one another's burdens to fulfill the law of Christ.
For if a man thinks he is something when he is nothing, he deceives himself.
But let every man test his own work, then he will rejoice in himself alone, and not in another.
For every man will bear his own burden.
Let the one who is taught in the word, communicate all good things to his teacher.
Do not be deceived, for God will not be mocked. For whatever a man sows, that he shall also reap.
For the one who sows to his flesh will reap from the flesh of corruption, but the one who sows to the spirit, will reap everlasting life from the spirit.
And let us not grow weary of well doing, because in due season we will reap, if we do not give up.
Therefore, if we have the opportunity, let us do good to all men, especially to those who are of the household of faith.
Do you see what a large letter I have written to you with my own hand.
Those who desire to impress you in the flesh, try to force you to be circumcised. Otherwise, they would suffer persecution for the cross of Christ.
For those who are circumcised do not keep the law, but they desire to have you circumcised, so they can glory in your flesh.
But God forbid that I should glory, except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, by whom the world is crucified to me, and I am crucified to the world.
For in Jesus Christ neither circumcision nor uncircumcision profits anything, except a new creature.
And as many as walk according to this rule, peace and mercy be on them, and on the God of Israel.
From now on let no man trouble me, because I bear the marks of the Lord Jesus on my body.
Brothers, may the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen!"
Paul an Apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, wrote a letter to the faithful saints of Jesus Christ in Ephesus.
And in this letter to the Ephesians, Paul wrote, "Grace and peace be to you from God our father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
Blessed be the God and father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us with all spiritual blessings in heavenly places in Christ.
Because he chose us to be in him before the foundation of the world, to be holy and without blame before him in love.
He has predestined us for adoption as his children through Jesus Christ, according to the good pleasure of his will.
To praise his glory and grace, in which he has made us acceptable to his beloved son.
In whom we have been redeemed through his blood and the forgiveness of sins, in accordance with the riches of his grace.
In which he has given us an abundance of wisdom and prudence.
God has made known to us the mystery of his will, in accordance with his good pleasure and the purpose which he has in himself.
So that as the fullness of times are dispensed, God can bring together all things, including both those things which are in heaven and those which are on earth, as one in Christ.
Through Christ we have also obtained an inheritance, since we were predestined according to God's purpose who works all things through the counsel of his own will.
So that we, who first trusted in Christ would be the first to praise his glory.
Christ in whom you also trusted, after you heard the true word of the gospel of your salvation. And in whom you also believed afterwards that you were sealed with the promised Holy Spirit.
Christ who is the earnest promise of our inheritance until the redemption of the purchased possession, to the praise of his glory.
Therefore, after I also I heard of your faith in the Lord Jesus, and your love to all the saints.
I do not cease to give thanks for you, by mentioning you in my prayers.
So that the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the father of glory, may give you the spirit of wisdom and revelation in the knowledge of him.
May your eyes be enlightened with understanding, so that you may know what the hope of the Lord's calling is, and what the richness of his glorious inheritance is in the saints.
And what God's extremely great power is toward those of us who believe, according to the mighty power of his works.
Which God worked in Christ, when he raised him from the dead, and set him at his own right hand in the heavenly places.
Far above all nations, power, might, authority, and every name that is named, not only in this world, but also in the world to come.
For God has put all things under Christ's feet and made Jesus the head over all things of the church.
Which is Christ's body, and the fullness of the one who fulfills everything in all things."
And Paul continued writing his letter to the faithful saints of Jesus Christ in Ephesus which said, "And God has hastened you who were dead in your sin and trespasses.
In times past you followed the course of this world, and the prince of the power of the air which is the spirit that now works in the children of disobedience.

Among whom we also had our conversations in times past in the lusts of our flesh. Fulfilling the desires of the flesh and of the mind, and we were by nature the children of wrath, just like the others.
But because of God's great love for us, he is rich in mercy.
Even when we were dead in our sins, God has hastened us together with Christ, and by grace you are saved.
And God has raised us up together and made us sit together in heavenly places in Christ Jesus.
So that in the ages to come, God might show the extremely abundant riches of his grace in his kindness toward us through Jesus Christ.
For by grace are you saved through faith, and it does not come from yourself, but it is the gift of God.
Not by works, otherwise all men would boast.
For we are God's workmanship, created in Jesus Christ to do good works, which God has ordained for us in advance so that we would walk in them.
So remember, that in the past you were Gentiles in the flesh. And you were called uncircumcised by those who were called to the circumcision in the flesh made by hands.
So that at that time you were without Christ, you were aliens from the commonwealth of Israel, and strangers from the covenants of promise. Hopeless, and without God in the world.
But now in Jesus Christ you who sometimes were far away are brought close by the blood of Christ.
For Jesus is our peace; he has made both one and torn down the dividing partition wall between us.
Christ has abolished the hostility, legal decrees, and the law of commandments in his flesh, in order to make within himself from two, one new man, thereby making peace.
So that Christ could reconcile both of them to God in one body by killing their hostility on the cross.
And Jesus came and preached peace to those of you who were far away, and to those who were close.
For through him we both have access to the father through one spirit.
Therefore you are no longer strangers and foreigners, but you are fellow citizens with the saints, and members of God household.
You are built on the foundation of the apostles and prophets; Jesus Christ himself is the chief corner stone.
In Jesus the entire building is fitted together and framed and grows into a holy temple in the Lord.
In Jesus you are also built together as a home for God through the Lord's spirit."
And Paul continued writing his letter to the faithful saints of Jesus Christ in Ephesus which said, "For this reason I Paul, the prisoner of Jesus Christ for you Gentiles.
If you have heard of the plan of God's grace which was given to me for you.
How God made known the mystery to me through revelation, which I have briefly written to you about before.
And when you read this, you may understand my understanding of the mystery of Christ
Which was not made known the sons of men in other generations as it has now been revealed through the Holy Spirit to God's holy apostles and prophets.
So that through the gospel the Gentiles could be fellow heirs, and of the same body, and partake of God's promise in Christ.
I became a minister of the gospel through the gift of God's grace that was given to me by the successful working of his power.
Even though I am less than the least of all saints, this grace was given to me, to preach among the Gentiles of the unsearchable riches of Christ.
And to make all men see the fellowship of the mystery, which has been hidden in God who created all things through Jesus Christ since the beginning of the world.
God's intent is to now make known to the nations and powers in heavenly places through the church the many wisdoms of God.
According to the eternal purpose which God accomplished in our Lord Christ Jesus.
In whom we have the boldness to confidently access God through our faith in Jesus.
Therefore, I ask you not to be frightened by my tribulations on your behalf, which is your glory.
For this reason I bow to the father of our Lord Jesus Christ.
After whom the whole family in heaven and on earth has been named.
So that he may grant you from the riches of his glory, the strength through his mighty Holy Spirit to your inner man.
So that Christ may live in your hearts through faith, and you may be rooted and grounded in love.
To be able to comprehend with all saints the width, length, depth, and height of God's love.
And know the love of Christ, who surpasses all knowledge, so that you may be filled with all the fullness of God.
Now to God, who can do everything much more abundantly above whatever we ask or think, according to the power at work within us.
And to God be the glory in the church through Jesus Christ throughout all generations of the world without end. Amen!"
Therefore, I am the prisoner of the Lord, and I beg you to walk worthy of the vocation to which you are called.
With gentle, humble, and long-suffering forgiveness for one another in love.
Endeavoring to keep the unity of the spirit in the bond of peace.
There is one body and one spirit, just as you were called in one hope when you were called.
One Lord, one faith, and one baptism.
One God and father of all, who is above all, through all, and in all of you.
But God's grace has been given to every one of us according to the measure of the gift of Christ.
Therefore David said, 'When the Lord ascended on high, he led the captives away and gave gifts to men. (Psalm 68:18)'
Now that Jesus has ascended, what does this mean, except that he also first descended into the lower parts of the earth?
The Christ that descended is the same one who also ascended far above all heavens, so that he may fulfill all things.
In order to prepare the saints for the work of the ministry, and for the moral support of the body of Christ.
For the perfecting of the saints, because the work of the ministry, because the instructing of the body of Christ.
Until we all come in the unity of faith and in the knowledge of God's son, as we mature to the full measure of the stature of a perfect man in Christ.
So from now on we will no longer be children, tossed around and carried away by every wind of doctrine, the tricks of men, or the skillful craftiness by which they lie in wait to deceive us.
But by speaking the truth in love, we may grow up into Christ in all things, who is the head.

From whom the whole body is fitted and joined and pressed together by every supporting joint. With the moral support that the body needs to work together according to the successful work of each individual part, which makes the body grow in love.
Therefore this is what I say and testify in the Lord, that from now on you must not walk as other Gentiles walk, in the vanity of their mind.
Their understanding has been darkened and alienated from the life of God by their ignorance, because of the blindness of their heart.
They have lost their morality and given themselves over to lustful, unclean work, and greed.
But this is not how you have come to learn of Christ.
If that is so, then you have heard him, and you have been taught by him, and the truth is in Jesus Christ.
So that you may cast off the former conversation of the old man, which has been corrupted through its deceitful lusts.
And be renewed in the spirit of your mind.
Then you will put on the new man, who is created in righteousness to be like God, true and holy.
Therefore each of you must put away lying, and speak truthfully with your neighbor, for we are all members of one another.
Be angry, but do not sin, and do not let the sun go down on your anger.
Do not give the devil a place at the table.
Let anyone who stole, steal no more but rather let him labor and work with his hands for all things which are good, so that he may have something to give to anyone in need.
Let no corrupt communication come from your mouth but speak only that which is good as moral support to minister grace to the listeners.
And do not grieve God's Holy Spirit, by which you are sealed until the day of redemption.
Remove all bitterness, rage, anger, clamor, evil speaking, and malice from you.
Be kind and tenderhearted to one another, forgiving each other, just as God for Christ's sake, has forgiven you."
Therefore as followers of God, be like dear children.
Walk in love, just as Christ who has also loved us and given himself for us as a fragrant sacrificial offering to God.
But become like saints, and do not allow fornication nor any unclean or covetous behavior be named even once among you.
Nor any filthy foolish talk, nor crude jokes which are inappropriate, but rather offer thanksgiving.
For this you know; no whoremonger, unclean person, covetous man, nor any idolaters will have any inheritance in the kingdom of Christ and God.
Let no man deceive you with vain words, because the anger of God comes on the children of disobedience from these things.
Therefore, do not partake in their sins with them.
For you were sometimes in darkness, but now you are in the Lord's light, so walk as children of light.
For the fruit of the spirit is in all goodness and righteous truth.
Proving what is acceptable to the Lord.
And have no fellowship with the unfruitful works of darkness but rather reprimand them.
For it is shameful to even speak of those things which they do in secret.
But all things that are reprimanded are manifested by the light, because whatever is manifested is a light.
So Isaiah says, 'Awaken you who sleep, and rise from the dead, and Christ will shine his light on you. (Isaiah 60:1)'
See that you walk in cautious wisdom, and not as fools.
Redeeming the time, because the days are evil.
Therefore, do not be unwise but understand the Lord's will.
And do not drink wine excessively and get drunk but be filled with the spirit.
Speak to yourselves in psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs. Sing and make music in your heart to the Lord.
Always give thanks to God the father in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ for all things.
Submit yourselves to one another in the fear of God.
Wives, submit yourselves to your own husbands as to the Lord.
For the husband is the head of the wife, just as Christ is the head of his church body, and he is the savior of the body.
So, just as the church is subject to Christ, the wives are also subject to their own husbands in everything.
Husbands, love your wives, just as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it.
So that he could sanctify and cleanse it, by washing it with the water of the word.
In order to present it to himself as a glorious, spotless, unwrinkled church and not blemished by any other such thing, so that it could be holy.
So, men should love their wives as they love their own bodies. For whoever loves his wife loves himself.
For no man ever hated his own flesh, but he nourishes and cherishes it, just as the Lord loves the church.
For we are members of the body of Christ, his flesh, and his bones.
That's why a man will leave his father and mother, and be joined to his wife, and the two will become one flesh.
This is a profound mystery, but I am speaking about Christ and the church.
Nevertheless, each one of you must love your own wife as you love yourself, and the wife must respect her husband.
Furthermore Paul's letter to the Ephesians said, "Children, obey your parents in the Lord for it is the right thing to do.
Honor your father and mother, which is the first commandment with a promise.
This promise states, 'So that everything goes well for you and you can live a long life on earth. (Deuteronomy 5:16)'
Fathers, do not provoke your children to anger, but nurture them and bring them up in the Lord's discipline.
Servants, obey your fleshly managers with fearful trembling and a faithful heart, just as you obey Christ.
Not just working when you are being watched like those who only want to please men, but as servants of Christ who do the will of God from their hearts.
Serve men with goodwill, as you would serve the Lord.
Because whether you are free or you are a servant, you will know that the good you do for others will be returned to you from the Lord.
And managers, treat your servants with this same goodwill and do not threaten them, because you know that both your God and theirs is in heaven, and he shows no favoritism.
Finally my brothers, be strong in the Lord and his mighty power.
Put on the full armor of God, so that you can withstand the devil's tricks.
For we do not wrestle against flesh and blood, but against the rulers of this world's darkness, nations, powers, and spiritual wickedness in high places.
Therefore pick up the full armor of God, so that when the day of evil comes you will be able to stand up and withstand the evil.
So stand up with truth strapped to your waist wearing God's armored vest of righteousness.
And prepare your feet with the gospel of peace.
Above all, pick up the shield of faith that you will use to quench all the fiery darts of the wicked.
Take the helmet of salvation and the sword of the spirit, which is the word of God.
Always praying in the spirit with every kind of prayer and plea, persevering and keeping watch, and making pleas for all saints.
As for me, pray that I may boldly open my mouth and speak every word given to me by the spirit, to make known the mystery of the gospel.
Because I am an ambassador in chains, so pray that in chains I may speak as boldly as I should.
But I am sending Tychicus to you, a beloved brother and faithful minister in the Lord who will tell you everything, and you will also know everything about me and how I am doing.
For I have sent him to you in order for you to know everything about us and he will comfort your hearts.
May there be peace from God the father and the Lord Jesus Christ to all the brothers with love and faith.
Grace to everyone who sincerely loves our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen!"
Paul and Timothy, the servants of Jesus Christ, wrote this letter to all the saints, bishops, and deacons who are part of the body of Jesus Christ in Philippi which said,
I thank my God every time I remember you.
I thank my God on every remember of you.
I always pray with joy every time I pray and make a request for you all.
For your fellowship in the gospel from the very first day until now.
And I am very confident of this, the good work which Jesus Christ began in you will continue until the day that he returns.

It is even correct for me to think of all of you this way because I have you in my heart. For both in my bondage and in defense of and confirmation of the gospel, you all partake of the grace with me.
For as God is my witness, how greatly I long for all of you from the bowels of Jesus Christ.
And I pray; that your love will be more and more abundant in knowledge and judgment.
So that you may approve of the excellent things, so that you will not be offensive, but you will be sincere until the day that Jesus Christ returns.
And that you are filled with the fruits of righteousness, which are to God's glory and praise through Jesus Christ.
But brothers, I want you to understand that all of the things that have happened to me, have instead advanced the gospel even further.
For my bondage in Christ has become obvious to everyone in the palace, and everywhere else.
And many of the brothers in the Lord, grow more confident by my bondage and they fearlessly speak the word much more boldly.
Some do indeed preach Christ out of envy and strife, but others preach from their goodwill.
The ones who preach the Christ of contention, do not do so sincerely but they think it will add affliction to my bondage.
But others preach out of love, knowing that I am prepared to defend the gospel.
So what? I only care that Christ is preached in every way, whether it is in dishonesty or truth. I still rejoice, and yes, I will continue to rejoice.
For I know that through your prayers this will only add to my salvation, and the spirit of Jesus Christ will provide.

Christ will provide everything according to my earnest expectation and hope, so that I will not be ashamed. But I will always be bold, so that Christ will now also be magnified in my body, whether it is by life or by death.
For to me, Christ is life and death is gain.
But if I continue to live in the flesh, teaching Christ is the fruit of my labor, but I do not know which I should choose.
For I am torn between the two, because I desire to leave to be with Christ; which is a far better place.
Nevertheless, I must remain and endure in the flesh for the benefit of all.
And I am confident; that I will endure and continue with you all to further advance your joyous faith.
So that your rejoicing for me may be more abundant in Jesus Christ when I return to you.

But make sure all of your conversations are worthy of the gospel of Christ. Then whether or not I come to see you or I am absent and I only hear of your affairs, make sure that you stand fast in one spirit, with one mind striving together for the faith of the gospel.
That way nothing your adversaries do will terrify you, which to them is an evident token of damnation, but to you it is your salvation from God.
For it has been given to you on behalf of Jesus Christ, to not only believe in him, but to also suffer for his sake.
Since you now suffer some of the same conflicts within you which you saw in me, and you now hear that I still have within me."

Paul and Timothy continued this letter to all the saints, bishops, and deacons in Philippi which said, "Therefore if there is any consolation, comfort of love, fellowship of the spirit, or affections and mercies in Christ.
Then fulfill my joy in you, so that you and I are likeminded in the same love, and also of one accord and one mind.
Do nothing through strife or vain glory but with a humble mind, hold each other in higher esteem than you hold yourselves.
Do not just look to your own things but look also to the concerns of others.
But let this mind, which was also in Jesus Christ be in you.
Jesus who was in the form of God, did not think it was robbery to be equal with God.
But Jesus reduced his reputation to nothing, and took upon himself the form of a servant, and was made into the likeness of men.
And being found to be in the appearance as a man, he humbled himself and became obedient even until his death on the cross.
Therefore God also has highly glorified him and given him a name which is high above every other name.
So that the knee of everything in heaven, on earth, and under the earth will bow to the name of Jesus.
And every tongue will confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the father.
Therefore, my beloved, since you have always obeyed, not just in my presence, but also much more in my absence, you will work out your own salvation with fear and trembling.
For it is God who works in you both to your goodwill and to do on behalf of God's good pleasure.
Do everything without complaints and arguments.
So that you may be the unpunished, blameless, and harmless sons of God, in the middle of a crooked and perverse nation, among which you shine as lights in the world.
As you hold out the word of life, so that I may rejoice on the day of Christ because I did not run nor labor in vain.
Yes, even if I am offered as the sacrifice and service of your faith, I will happily rejoice with you all.
And for this same cause you also happily rejoice with me.
But I trust in the Lord Jesus to send Timothy to you soon, so that I may also be of good cheer, when I find out how you are doing.
For I have no other likeminded man who will naturally care for your state of mind.
For all the others look after their own interests, not those of Jesus Christ.
But you know that Timothy has proven himself, in that he has been like a son with the father, since he has served with me in the gospel.
Therefore, I hope to send Timothy as soon as I see how things how things are going for me.
But I trust in the Lord that I myself may also soon come to you.
But I thought it was necessary to send Epaphroditus, my brother, companion in labor, and fellow soldier back to you. For even though he has been ministering to my wants, he is also your messenger.
For Epaphroditus has longed to see you all, and he was filled with sorrow because you heard that he had been sick.
