For Epaphroditus was indeed sick and near to death, but God had mercy on him. For God not only had mercy on Epaphroditus, but he also had mercy on me, otherwise I would have nothing but sorrow piled upon sorrow.
Therefore, I am carefully sending Epaphroditus back to you, so that when you see him again, you can rejoice and I may be less sorrowful.
So receive him in the Lord with joy and happiness and hold such men as this in high regard.
Because Epaphroditus nearly died for the work of Christ, and he risked his life to supply your lack of service to me."

Paul and Timothy continued this letter to all the saints, bishops, and deacons in Philippi which said, "Finally my brothers, I rejoice in the Lord to write the same things to you, which to me indeed is not grievous, but it is for your safety.
Beware of dogs, evil workers, and the concision.
For we are the circumcision who worship God in the spirit and rejoice in Jesus Christ, and we have no confidence in the flesh.
Even though I may also have confidence in the flesh. If any other man thinks that he might have trust in the flesh, I have more.
Circumcised on the eighth day of the stock of Israel in the tribe of Benjamin, and a Hebrew of Hebrews as a Pharisee stirring up the law.
And as for zeal, I persecuted the church, stirring up the righteousness which is blameless in the law.
But whatever was gain to me, I counted as loss for Christ.

And undoubtably, I count all things as loss except for the excellence of knowing my Lord Jesus Christ. For I have suffered the loss of everything for Jesus, but I count it all as nothing but dung, so that I may win Christ.
And to be found in Christ, since I do not have my own righteousness through the law, except for that which is through faith in Christ and the righteousness from God by faith.
So that I may know Christ and the power of his resurrection and the fellowship of his sufferings, willingly conformed to his death.
So that I may somehow attain the resurrection from the dead.
It is not as if I have already attained this nor am I already perfect, but I follow Christ so that I may apprehend that for which I have also been apprehended by Jesus Christ.
Brothers, I do not consider myself to have already apprehended this. But I do this one thing; I forget those things which are behind me, and I reach out to those things which are ahead.
I press on toward the goal of winning the prize of God's heavenly calling in Jesus Christ.
Therefore, let all of us who are mature minded think this way, and if you think otherwise about anything, God will also reveal this to you.
Nevertheless, we must walk by the same rules which we have already attained, and we must think the same thing.
Brothers, join together and follow me, and watch those who walk as the example we have set for you.
For I have often told you and now I tell you once again as I weep, that there are many who are enemies of the cross of Christ.
Who end in destruction, whose God is their stomach, who glory is in their shame and think only of earthly things.
For our conversation is in heaven, where we also look for our savior the Lord Jesus Christ.
Who will change our vile body and fashion it to be just as his glorious body, with the power which enables him to subdue all things to himself."

Paul and Timothy continued this letter to all the saints, bishops, and deacons in Philippi which said, "Therefore, my dearly beloved brothers for whom I have longed, I offer my joy and crown, so stand fast in the Lord my dearly beloved.
I beg Euodias and Syntyche to be of the same mind as the Lord.

And I also plead with you, my true friend and I ask you to help those women who have labored with me in the gospel, along with Clement and my other fellow laborers, whose names are in the Book of Life.
Always rejoice in the Lord, and again I say, rejoice.
Let your moderation be known to all men. The Lord is here.
Be careful of nothing but let your requests be made known to God in everything through prayer and plea with thanksgiving.
And the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding will keep your hearts and minds through Jesus Christ.
Finally brothers, whatever is true, honest, just, pure, lovely, or it deserves respect or praise, then think of these things if something has any goodness at all.
And do those things, which you have learned, received, heard, and seen in me, and the God of peace will be with you.
But I greatly rejoiced in the Lord, now that you have at the last increased your care of me again, in which you were so careful, but you lacked the opportunity.
Not that I speak from want or need, because I have learned to be content in whatever state I find myself in.
For I know both how to be humble, and I know how to abound. And in all things everywhere, I have been instructed in both how to be full or hungry, and both how to abound or suffer in need.
I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me.
Nevertheless, you have done well and communicated with me about my affliction.
Now you Philippians also know, that in the beginning of the gospel when I left Macedonia, no other churches communicated with me about giving and receiving except you.
For even in Thessalonica you once again sent help for my necessities.
Not because I desire a gift, but I desire fruit that may abound to your account.

But I now have everything that I need and I am full, after I received the things which you sent from Epaphroditus. For they are a fragrant and acceptable sacrificial offering and well pleasing to God.
But my God will supply all of your needs according to his glorious riches in Jesus Christ.
Now glory be to God our father forever and ever. Amen!
Greetings to every saint in Jesus Christ. The brothers who are with me greet you.
All the saints salute you, especially those who are from Caesar's household.
May the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen!"
Paul, an Apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, and Timothy our brother.
Wrote this letter to the saints and faithful brothers in Christ who are in Colosse which said, "Grace and peace be to you from God our father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
We always thank God the father of our Lord Jesus Christ for you when we pray.
Since we first heard of your faith in Jesus Christ, and the love which you have to all the saints.
And for the hope, which is laid up for you in heaven, which you have already heard in the word of the truth of the gospel.
This gospel which has come to you that brings forth fruit all over the world. Just as it has done in you, since the day you heard it and knew the grace of God in truth.
And as you have also learned, our dear fellow servant Epaphras, who is a faithful minister of Christ for you.
Who also declared your love in the spirit to us.

Therefore, since the day we heard of you, we do not cease praying for you, so that you may have the desire to be filled with the spiritual understanding, knowledge, and wisdom of God's will in all things.
So that you may walk worthy of the Lord to please him and be fruitful in every good work and increase your knowledge of God.
Strengthened with his glorious might and power so that you may have joyful patience and long suffering.
Giving thanks to God the father, who has brought us together to take part in the inheritance of the saints in the light.
For God has delivered us from the power of darkness and has transported us into the kingdom of his dear son Jesus.
In whom we even have redemption and forgiveness of sins through his blood.
Jesus is the image of the invisible God, and the firstborn of every creature.
For all things in heaven and on earth, including the visible and invisible were created by God, whether they are thrones, authorities, nations, or powers. All things were created by God for God.
God comes before all things, and all things consist of him.
And God is the head of the body of the church. God is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead, so that he may have preeminence in all things.
For it pleased God the father to have all of his fullness live in Jesus.
And God made peace through the blood of the cross of Jesus Christ. So I say, 'By Jesus God has reconciled all things to himself whether they are things on earth, or things in heaven.'
And you who were sometimes alienated from God and enemies in your mind and you did wicked works, yet God has now reconciled himself to you.
In the body of his flesh through the death of Jesus Christ, to present you as holy, unblemished, and blameless in his sight.

If you continue and remain grounded and settled in the faith and you are not moved from the hope of the gospel, which you have heard. For this hope of which I Paul have been made a minister, was preached to every creature under heaven.
And I now rejoice in my sufferings for you, and I fill up my flesh with that which is behind the afflictions of Christ for his body's sake, which is the church.
Of which I have been made a minister, according to God's exemption which is given to me for you, to fulfill God's word.
Even the mystery which has been hidden from the generations and the descendants but is now revealed to his saints.
To whom God would make known the glorious riches his mystery among the Gentiles, which is Christ in you and the hope of glory.
We preach and proclaim Jesus, we warn and teach every man in all wisdom, so that we may present every man as perfect in Jesus Christ.
To which I also labor, striving to do God's work, which works mightily within me."

Paul and Timothy continued writing this letter to the saints and brothers in Christ in Colosse which said, "For I want you to know what a great conflict I have in my soul for you, and for those in Laodicea, and for all who have not met me face to face in the flesh.
So that their hearts can be comforted, knit together in love, and filled with the riches of the full assurance of understanding, so they can acknowledge the mystery of God the father, and Christ.
In whom are hidden all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge.
And I say this, 'Otherwise a man would be able to deceive you with enticing words.'
For even though I am absent in the flesh, I am still with you in the spirit, rejoicing to see your orderly and steadfast faith in Christ.
Therefore, since you have received the Lord Jesus Christ, you must walk in him.
Rooted and built up in him and established in the faith just as you have been taught, overflowing with thanksgiving.
Beware otherwise any man could spoil you through philosophy and vain deceit, based on the traditions of men and the most basic principles of the world, and not based on Christ.
For all the fullness of the Godhead bodily lives in Jesus.
And you are complete in him, for Christ is the head of all nations and power.
In whom you are also circumcised with the circumcision made without hands, by removing the bodily sins of the flesh by the circumcision of Jesus Christ.
You are buried with Christ in baptism, in whom you have also risen through faith in God's operation, who has raised Jesus from the dead.
And you were dead in your sins and the uncircumcision of your flesh, but God has hastened together with Jesus, who has forgiven all of your trespasses.
For Jesus has erased the handwritten legal decrees that are against us, which were contrary to us, and took it out of our way and nailed it to his cross.
And Jesus has disarmed the nations and powers, he made a public show of them, triumphing over them in his cross.
Therefore, let no man judge what you eat or drink, or your respect of a holy day, the new moon, or the Sabbath.
Which are only shadow of things to come, but the body belongs to Christ.
Let no man deceive you about your reward using voluntary humility and worshipping of angels, by intruding into those things which he has not seen. For he is vainly puffed up by his fleshly mind.
And he does not have the head, from which the whole body is knit together by joints and parts that nourish, minister, and grow with the increase of God.
Therefore, if you have died with Christ from the basic principles of the world, why do you live as though you were still living in the world, and still subject to its laws.
Do not touch, do not taste, and do not handle.
Which will all perish with use, which are all based on the commandments and doctrines of men!
Such things do indeed have the appearance of wisdom, in worship, humility, and neglect of the body, but these things do not in any way give honor through satisfaction of the flesh."

Paul and Timothy continued writing this letter to the saints and brothers in Christ in Colosse which said, "If you have then risen with Christ, seek those things which are from above, where Christ sits at the right hand of God.
Set your affection on things from above, not on earthly things.
For you are dead, and your life is now hidden with Christ in God.
When Christ, who is our life reappears, then you will also appear with him in glory.

Therefore, mortify (which means: embarrass, humiliate, shame) your members who are of the earth through: fornication, uncleanliness, inordinate affection, evil concupiscence (which means: lust, lechery, carnality), and greed which is idolatry.
For these things cause God's wrath to come upon the children of disobedience.
And when you lived among them, you also walked in these ways for some time.
But now you must remove all of these things from your mouth: anger, rage, malice, blasphemy, and filthy language.
Do not lie one to another, since you have removed the old self along with his deeds.
For you have put on the new self, which is being renewed in the knowledge and the image of his creator.
Where there is neither Greek, Jew, circumcision, uncircumcision, barbarian, Scythian, slave, nor free, but Christ is all and is in all.
Therefore, as the elect of God, clothe yourselves with mercy, kindness, humility, gentleness, and long suffering patience.
You must restrain and forgive one another, even if you have a disagreement with someone else. Forgive one another just as Christ has forgiven you.
And above all of these things put on the cloak of charity, which is the bond of perfection.
And let the peace of God rule in your hearts, to whom you are also called in one body. And be thankful!
Let the word of Christ live richly within you in all wisdom, as you teach and reprimand one another singing psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs, with grace to the Lord in your hearts.
And whatever you do in words or deeds, do it all in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, and give thanks to God the father through him.
Wives, submit yourselves to your husbands, since it is fitting in the Lord.
Husbands, love your wives, and do not be bitter against them.
Children, obey your parents in all things, for this well pleases the Lord.
Fathers, do not provoke your children to anger, otherwise they will be discouraged.
Servants, obey your masters in everything fleshly, not only when they are watching you, like those who only want to please men, but with a sincere heart and the fear of God.
And whatever you do, do it whole heartedly, as if you were doing it for the Lord and not for men.
For you know that you will receive the reward of an inheritance from the Lord, because you serve the Lord Jesus Christ.
But whoever does wrong will be paid for his wrong doings, and God shows no favoritism to any person."

Paul and Timothy finished writing this letter to the saints and brothers in Christ in Colosse which said, "Masters, give your servants whatever is just and fair, since you also know that you have a master in heaven.
Continue praying and be watchful and thankful.
And as you pray, also pray for us, so that God will open a door to us to speak the word of the mystery of Christ, for which I am also in bondage.
So that I may manifest it as I should when I speak.
Walk in wisdom toward those who are outside the word and redeem the time.
Let your speech always be with grace and seasoned with salt, so that you may know how to answer every man.
Tychicus will tell you everything about my state of mind. He is a beloved brother, faithful minister, and fellow servant in the Lord Jesus Christ.
I have sent him to you to discover the condition of your heart, and to comfort you.
Along with Onesimus, a faithful and beloved brother, who is one of you. They will tell you how we do everything here.
Aristarchus my fellow prisoner sends his salutations, and so does Barnabas' sister's son Marcus, from whom you have already received instructions. And if he comes back to you, welcome him.
And Jesus, who we call Justus, also sends his greetings. These are my only fellow workers for the Kingdom of God who have comforted me and are also of the circumcision.

Epaphras, who is also one of you and a servant of Jesus Christ, sends his salutations to you. He is always laboring passionately for you in prayers, so that you may stand perfect and complete in all of God's will.
For I can testify that Epaphras has a great zeal for you, as well as those in Laodicea and Hierapolis.
Luke, the beloved physician, and Demas also send their greetings to you.
Greet the brothers in Laodicea and send greetings to Nymphas who hosts the church in his house.
And when this letter is read among you, make sure that it is also read in the church of the Laodiceans, and that you likewise read the letter sent from Laodicea.
And say to Archippus, 'Make sure that you fulfill the ministry which you have received in the Lord.'
I Paul, send this salutation written with my own hand. Remember my bondage. Grace be with you. Amen!"

Paul, Silvanus, and Timothy, wrote this letter to the Thessalonian church which is in God the father and in the Lord Jesus Christ which said, "Grace and peace be to you, from God our father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
We always give thanks to God for all of you and mention you in our prayers.
We unceasingly remember your work of faith, labor of love, and patient hope in our Lord Jesus Christ before God our father.
Knowing that you are beloved brothers, chosen by God.
For our gospel did not come to you in word only, but also in power through the Holy Spirit, and with much assurance. Just so you would know what type of men lived among you for own your salvation.
And you became our followers and followers of the Lord, when you received the word with the joy of the Holy Spirit, even though you suffered much affliction at that time.
So that you would become an example to all who believe in Macedonia and Achaia.
For not only was the Lord's word heard from you in Macedonia and Achaia, but also in every other place where your faith towards God has spread abroad, so that we no longer need to say anything else.
For they themselves show of us what kind of welcome we had from you, and how you turned from idols to serve the true and living God.
To wait for God's son Jesus Christ to return from heaven, whom God raised from the dead, who has even delivered us from the wrath to come."
Paul, Silvanus, and Timothy, continued writing this letter to the Thessalonian church which said, "For you yourselves brothers know that you did not accept us in vain.

But you also know how shamefully we were previously treated and how we suffered in Philippi. But we were bold in our God and spoke the gospel of God to you, even though there was much heated discussion.
For our encouragement was not from deceit, uncleanliness, nor deceitful.
But we were allowed by God to be entrusted with the gospel, so we do not speak to please men, but we speak to please God, who tries our hearts.
For as you know, we have not at any time used flattering words, nor put on a cloak to hide greed. God is our witness!
For we have not sought glory from men, from you, nor from any others, when we as the apostles of Christ could have become burdensome to you.
But we were gentle among you, like a nurse who cherishes her children.
We cared so affectionately for you, that we were not only willing to give you the gospel of God, but we also offered you our own souls, because you were so dear to us.
But brothers, surely you remember our labor and work. For we labored both night and day, because we did not want to owe any one of you, but we preached the gospel of God to you.
You are witnesses and so is God, of how holy, justly, and blamelessly we behaved among those of you who believe.
As you know we encouraged, comforted, and treated each one of you as a father treats his own children.
So that you could walk in a manner worthy of God, who has called you into his kingdom and glory.

For this reason, we also unceasingly thank God, because when you received the word of God which you heard from us, you did not receive it as the word of men, but as the true word of God, which also works successfully in you who believe.
For you brothers, became followers of the churches of God in Judea which are in Jesus Christ. For you have also suffered from your own countrymen, just as the Jews have suffered.
Who both killed the Lord Jesus Christ and their own prophets, but have also persecuted us, and they do not please God, and they are behave contrary to all men.
Forbidding us to speak to the Gentiles to tell them how they can be saved. So the Gentiles always continue to pile up their sins until the maximum anger comes upon them.
But brothers, even though we were removed from your physical presence for a short time, we were not removed in heart. For we have endeavored and desired even more abundantly to see your face.
Therefore, we would have come to you earlier, and I Paul, even tried over and over again, but Satan hindered us.
For who is our hope, our joy, and our crown of rejoicing? If it is not you, in the presence of our Lord Jesus Christ at his coming?
For you are our joy, hope, and glory."

Paul, Silvanus, and Timothy, continued writing this letter to the Thessalonians which said, "Therefore when we could no longer restrain ourselves, we thought it would be a good idea to be left alone in Athens.
And we sent our brother Timothy, God's minister and our fellow laborer in the gospel of Christ, to establish you and comfort your concerns about your faith.
So that no man could be moved by these afflictions, for you yourselves know that we have been appointed to this ministry.
For truly, when we were with you, we warned you beforehand that we would suffer tribulation, and as you know it has happened.

Therefore, when I could no longer restrain myself, I contacted you to find out how your faith was holding up, just in case the tempter had tempted you by some means, and our labor would have been in vain.

But now Timothy has returned to us and brought us good news of your faith and charity and told us that you have always had fond memories of us. Timothy also tells us that you greatly desire to see us, just as we also desire to see you.
Therefore brothers, even in all of our affliction and distress, we have been comforted about you, because of your faith.
For now we live, if you stand fast in the Lord.
How much more can we thank God for you, for all of the joy that we enjoy before our God for your sakes.
Night and day we earnestly pray that we will see you face to face again, to help perfect that which is lacking in your faith.
Now it seems that God our father himself and our Lord Jesus Christ, are directing our way back to you.
And may the Lord increase your abundant love toward one another and everyone else, just like our abundant love toward you.
So to that end may the Lord establish your hearts as blameless and holy before God our father, at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ with all of his saints."

Paul, Silvanus, and Timothy, continued writing this letter to the Thessalonians which said, "Furthermore brothers, we ask and encourage you to live and walk in the Lord Jesus Christ to please God, in the way that you have learned to walk from us, so that you may do so more and more abundantly.
For you know the commandments that we have given you from the Lord Jesus.
For this is God's will, that since your sanctification, you should abstain from fornication.
And each one of you should know how to own his own body in sanctification and honor.
Not in the lust of passion, like the Gentiles who do not know God.
So that no man goes beyond his boundaries and defrauds his brother in this way, because the Lord is the avenger of such things, just as we have forewarned you and testified about.
For God has not called us to uncleanliness, but to holiness.
Therefore, the man who does such things, does not despise man, he despises God, who has also given us his Holy Spirit.
But you do not need me to write to you about brotherly love, for you yourselves have been taught by God how to love one another.
And indeed, you do show this love to all the brothers throughout Macedonia, but we beg you brothers to continue to increase more and more.
And we ask that you quietly study how to attend to your own business and work with your own hands, as we commanded you.
So that you may walk honestly among those who are without faith, and so that you may lack nothing.
But brothers, I would not want you to be ignorant about those who are asleep, so that you do not grieve as those who have no hope.
For since we believe that Jesus died and rose again, we also know that those who are asleep in Jesus, God will bring with him.
For this is what we say to you about the Lord's word, we who are alive and remain until the Lord comes, will not prevent those who are asleep.
For the Lord himself will descend from heaven with a shout and the voice of an archangel, and with the trumpet of God, and the dead in Christ will be the first to rise.
Then we who are alive and remain will be caught up together with them in the clouds to meet the Lord in the air. And so, we will be forever with the Lord.
Therefore, comfort one another with these words."
Paul, Silvanus, and Timothy, finished writing this letter to the Thessalonians which said, "But about the times and seasons, brothers, you now have no need for me to write to you.
For you yourselves perfectly know that the Day of the Lord will come like a thief in the night.
For when they say, 'Peace and safety!" That's when sudden destruction will come upon them, just as labor comes upon a pregnant woman, and they will not escape.
But you, brothers, are not in darkness, so that day should not overtake you like a thief.
You are all the children of light and of the day; we are not children of the night nor of darkness.
Therefore let us not sleep like the others but let us watch and stay sober.
For those who sleep, sleep at night, and the drunks are drunk at night.
But let those of us who are of the day, stay sober and put on the breastplate of faith and love, and wear the hope of salvation as a helmet.
For God has not appointed us to wrath, but to obtain salvation through our Lord Jesus Christ.
Jesus died for us, so that we could live together with him whether we are awake or asleep.
Why not get together to comfort yourselves and teach one another, just as you already do.
And brothers, we ask you to understand those who labor among you, who lead you and warn you in the Lord.
And to very highly esteem them in love for the sake of their work and be at peace among yourselves.
Now brothers, we urge you to: warn those who are unruly, comfort the feebleminded, support the weak, and be patient toward all men.
See that no one renders evil for evil to anyone; but forever follow that which is good, both for yourselves and for all men.
Rejoice forever.
Pray without ceasing.
Give thanks in everything, for this is God's will for you in Jesus Christ.
Do not quench the spirit.
Do not despise prophecies.
Test all things and hold fast to that which is good.
Abstain from all appearances of evil.
And may the very God of peace completely sanctify you; and I pray to God that your whole spirit, soul, and body will be preserved and held blameless when our Lord Jesus Christ returns.
Faithful is the one who calls you, who will also do these things.
Brothers, please pray for us.
Greet all the brothers with a holy kiss.
I charge you before the Lord to read this letter to all of the holy brothers.
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you. Amen!"
Paul, Silvanus, and Timothy, wrote this letter to the church of Thessalonians in God our father and the Lord Jesus Christ which said,
"Grace and peace to you, from God our father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
Brothers, since it is appropriate we are always bound to thank God for you, because your faith grows exponentially, and the charity of every one of you toward each other thrives.
So that we ourselves glorify you in God's churches for your patience and faith during all the persecutions and tribulations that you have endured.
Which is an obvious sign of God's righteous judgment, so that you may be counted as worthy of the Kingdom of God, for which you also suffer.
Since it is a righteous thing for God to compensate those who trouble you with tribulation.
And those of you who are troubled come and rest with us, when the Lord Jesus is revealed from heaven with his mighty angels.
In flaming fire taking vengeance on those who do not know God, and those who do not obey the gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ.
For they will be punished with everlasting destruction, separated from the Lord's presence and the glory of his power.
When the Lord comes, he will be glorified in his saints and admired by all of those who believe, because you believed our testimony in those days.
Therefore, we also always pray for you, so that our God would count you as worthy of this calling and powerfully fulfill all the good pleasure of his goodness and works of the faith.
So that the name of our Lord Jesus Christ may be glorified in you, and you in him from the grace of our God and the Lord Jesus Christ."
Paul, Silvanus, and Timothy, continued writing this letter to the Thessalonians which said, "Now brothers, since the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, and our gathering together in him, we ask you.
Do not be shaken or troubled so soon in your mind, by any spirit, word, or letter that seems to come from us, announcing that the day of Christ has come.
Let no man deceive you in any way, because that day will not come until the falling away first comes, and the man of sin, the son of perdition is revealed.
Who opposes and glorifies himself above everything that is called or worshipped as a god, and he will sit in God's temple as God and proclaim himself to be God.
Do you not remember that I told you these things, when I was still with you?
And now you know what holds him back, so that he might be revealed in his own time.
For the mystery of wickedness is already at work, but only the one who now allows will continue to allow, until the obstacle is removed from the way.
And then the wicked one will be revealed, whom the Lord will consume with the spirit of his mouth, and destroy with his brilliant return.
The coming of the lawless one will come along with the works of Satan with all kinds of power, signs, and lying wonders.
And the lawless one will come with delusion of unrighteousness in those who perish, because they did not receive the love of the truth that would have saved them.
Therefore God will send them a strong delusion, so that they will believe a lie.
So that those who did not believe the truth but took pleasure in unrighteousness, may all be condemned.

But we are always bound to give thanks to God for you beloved brothers of the Lord. Because God has chosen you from the beginning to receive salvation through sanctification of the spirit and belief in the truth.
To which God called you through our gospel, to the obtain from the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ.
Therefore brothers, stand fast and hold to the traditions which you have been taught, whether by word or our letter.
Now our Lord Jesus Christ himself and God our father, who has loved us, and forever consoled us with good hope through grace.
So comfort your hearts and establish yourselves in every good word and work."

Paul, Silvanus, and Timothy, finished this letter to the Thessalonians which said, "Finally brothers, pray for us, so that the word of the Lord may spread freely and be glorified, just as it has with you.
And that we may be delivered from unreasonable and wicked men, because not all men have faith.
But the Lord who will establish you and keep you from evil is faithful.
And we have confidence in the Lord that you both do and you will continue doing the things that we commanded you.
May the Lord direct your hearts into God's love and to patiently wait for Christ.
Now we command you brothers in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, to withdraw yourselves from every brother who walks disorderly, and not in the tradition which he received from us.
For you yourselves know how you ought to follow us, because we ourselves did not behave disorderly among you.
Nor did we eat any man's bread for nothing, but we worked and labored day and night, so that we would not owe anything to any of you.
Not because we have no power, but to make ourselves an example for you to follow.
For even when we were with you, we told you this, 'If anyone will not work, they should not eat.'
For we hear that there are some who among you are disorderly busybodies, and they do not work at all.
Now we command and encourage such people through our Lord Jesus Christ, to quietly work, and eat their own bread.
But you brothers, do not grow weary in well doing.
If a man does not obey our word in this letter, take note of that man, and do not keep company with him, so that he may be ashamed.
But do not count him as an enemy but reprimand him as a brother.
Now by all means, may the Lord of peace himself always give you peace. The Lord be with you all.
This salutation comes from Paul, and it is written with my own hand. This is a sign of every letter that I write.
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen!"
Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the command of God our savior and the Lord Jesus Christ, who is our hope.
Wrote this letter to my own son in the faith Timothy which said, "Grace, mercy, and peace, from God our father and our Lord Jesus Christ.
As I asked you to continue to endure in Ephesus, when I went to Macedonia, so that you could urge some not to teach other doctrines.
Nor listen to fables and endless genealogies, which minister and question the faith rather than Godly instruction.
Now the end of this commandment is charity from a pure heart, a good conscience, and a sincere faith.
For some have swerved and turned away to vain talking.
They desire to be teachers of the law, but they do not understand what they say nor what they affirm.
But we know that the law is good, if a man uses it lawfully.

We know that the law was not made for a righteous man, but it was made for the lawless, the disobedient, the ungodly, the sinners, the unholy, the profane, the killers of fathers and mothers, and murderers.
It was made for whoremongers, homosexuals, enslavers, liars, perjured people, and for any other thing that is contrary to sound doctrine.
According to the glorious gospel of the blessed God, which has been committed into my trust.
And I thank our Lord Jesus Christ, who has enabled me and counted me as faithful, by putting me into the ministry.
For I was previously a blasphemer, a persecutor, and injurious, but I obtained mercy because had I acted in ignorant disbelief.
And our Lord's grace was exceedingly abundant with faith and love which is in Jesus Christ.
This is a faithful saying, which is worthy of acceptance by all, 'Jesus Christ came into the world to save all sinners.' Of whom I am the worst.

However, for this reason I obtained mercy, so that first in me Jesus Christ can reveal all his long suffering patience, as an example to those who should from now on believe in him for life everlasting.
May the eternal, immortal, invisible king, and the only wise God have honor and glory forever and ever. Amen.
Now Timothy my son, I commit to you, according to the previous prophecies which went before you, that you might use them to war the good warfare.
Holding to your faith and a good conscience, which some have rejected and shipwrecked their faith.
Among whom is Hymenaeus and Alexander, whom I have delivered to Satan, so that they may learn not to blaspheme."
Paul continued writing this letter to his faithful son in the faith Timothy which said, "Therefore, I first of all encourage you to make pleas, prayers, intercessions, and give thanks for all men.
Then pray for kings and those who are in authority, so that we may lead a quiet and peaceful life in all Godliness and honesty.
For this is good and acceptable in the sight of our God and savior.
Our God who would have all men saved and come to the knowledge of the truth.
For there is only one God and one mediator between God and men, and that man is Jesus Christ.
Who gave himself as a ransom for everyone, which will be testified just in time.
To whose purpose I was ordained as a preacher and an apostle. For I speak the truth in Christ, and I do not lie, and I teach the Gentiles in faith and truth.
Therefore I would have men everywhere pray and lift up holy hands, without anger or doubt.
Likewise, I would have women adorn themselves in modest apparel, with modesty and sobriety, not with braided hair, gold, pearls, or expensive clothes.
But with that which becomes a woman who professes Godliness and good works.
Let a woman quietly learn in silence and submission.
But I do not believe a woman should teach nor to take authority over a man, but she must remain silent.
For Adam was formed first, then Eve.
And Adam was not deceived, but the woman was deceived into transgression.
But she will be saved through childbearing, if her children continue in faith, charity, holiness, and sobriety."
Paul continued writing this letter to his faithful son in the faith Timothy which said, "This is a true saying, if a man desires the office of a bishop, he desires a good work.
A bishop must be blameless and married to only one wife, he must be vigilant, sober, behave properly, hospitable, and inclined to teach.
He must be patient and not be given to wine, violence, or fighting, and he must not be greedy for dirty money nor covetous.
He must rule his own house well and seriously control his children with dignity.
For if a man does not know how to rule his own house, how can he care for God's church?
He must not be a novice, otherwise his pride may lift up his ego, and he will fall into the same condemnation as the devil.
Furthermore, a bishop must have a good reputation from those who are without, otherwise he may fall into the devil's spiteful snare.
Likewise deacons must be serious, and they must not be twofaced nor given to much wine, nor greedy for dirty money.
They must hold to the mystery of the faith with a pure conscience.
They must also first be tested, then let them use the office of a deacon after being found blameless.
And their wives must also be serious, sober, and faithful in all things, but they must not be gossipers.
The deacons must also be married to only one wife and rule their children and their homes well.
For those who have served the deacon's office well, will acquire for themselves a good degree and great boldness in the faith that is in Jesus Christ.
I write these things to you, hoping to come see you soon.
But if I stay too long, so that you may know how you should behave yourself in God's house, which is the church of the living God and the pillar and foundation of the truth.

And the great mystery of Godliness was revealed without controversy when God was manifested in the flesh, justified in the Holy Spirit, seen by the angels, preached to the Gentiles, believed in by the world, and taken up into glory."

Paul continued writing this letter to his faithful son in the faith Timothy which said, "Now the Holy Spirit expressly states, that in the latter times some will abandon the faith, by paying attention to seducing spirits and the doctrines of devils.
They will tell hypocritical lies, with a conscience seared by a hot iron.
They will forbid marriage, and command others to abstain from eating meat, which God has created to be received with thanksgiving by those who believe and know the truth.
For every one of God's creatures is good, and nothing that is received with thanksgiving should be refused.
For it is sanctified by the word of God and prayer.
If you remind the brothers of these things, you will be a good minister of Jesus Christ, nourished by words of the faith with the good doctrine you have attained.
But refuse profane old wives' tales and train yourself for Godliness instead.
For bodily exercise is of little value, but Godliness is profitable in all things, having the promise of the life that is now, and the life that is to come.
This is a faithful saying and worthy of acceptance by all.
Therefore we both labor and suffer disrespect, because we trust in the living God, who is the savior of all men, especially of those who believe.
So command and teach these things.
Let no man despise your youth but be an example for the believers in your word, your conversation, your charity, your spirit, your faith, and your purity.
Until I come, attend to reading, encouragement, and to doctrine.
Do not neglect the gift that is in you, which was given to you through prophecy, and with the laying on of hands by the elders.
Meditate on these things and devote yourself to them completely, so that your gain is obvious to everyone.
Pay close attention to yourself and your doctrine. Continue in your doctrine, because doing so, you will both save yourself and those who hear you."
Paul continued writing this letter to his faithful son in the faith Timothy which said, "Do not reprimand an elder, but pray for him as a father, and pray for the younger men as brothers.
Pray for the elder women as mothers and the younger as sisters with absolute purity.
Honor the widows who are indeed widows.
But if a widow has children or nephews, let them learn first learn to show devotion at home, and repay their parents, for this is good and acceptable before God.
Now the woman who is indeed a desolate widow, but she trusts God and continues to plea and pray night and day.
But the woman who lives for pleasure is dead even if she is still alive.
And give these instructions to the believers, so that they may be held blameless.
But if anyone does not provide for his own, especially his own household, he has denied the faith and is worse than an infidel.
Do not let a widow who was married to only one man, and she is less than 60 years old, be supported by the congregation.
Well known for good works, such as raising children, helping strangers, washing the saints' feet, relieved the afflicted, and diligently devoted herself to every good work.
But refuse to support the younger widows, for when they have begun to grow promiscuous against Christ, they will remarry.
Incurring damnation, because they have cast off their first faith.
And they will learn to be idle, wandering around from house to house. They will not only be idle, but also tattletales and busybodies, gossiping about things which they should not talk about.
Therefore, I say that the younger women should remarry, bear children, guide their household, and do not give the adversary an occasion to speak critically.
For some have already turned away to follow Satan.
If a man or woman who believes has dependent widows, they must help them, so that the church is not burdened, so that it may help those who are indeed widows.
Let the elders who rule well, be counted as worthy of double the honor, especially those who labor in the word and doctrine.
For the scripture says, 'You must not muzzle an ox while it is treading the wheat, (Deuteronomy 25:4) and you deserve to be fed and cared for when you are teaching. (Matthew 1010)'
Do not accept an accusation against an elder unless there are two or three witnesses.
Reprimand those who sin before everyone, so that others may also fear.
I charge you before God, the Lord Jesus Christ, and the elect angels; observe these things and show no favor or partiality to one above another.
Do not suddenly lay hands on a man, nor share in other men's sins, but keep yourself pure.
Do not drink just water but use a little wine for the sake of your stomach and your frequent ailments.
Some men's sins are exposed beforehand, going before them to judgment; but some men's sins are exposed later.
Likewise, the good works of some are obvious, but those that are not obvious cannot be hidden."

Paul continued writing this letter to his faithful son in the faith Timothy which said, "Let all those who are under the yoke of servitude regard their own masters as worthy of honor, so that God's name and his doctrine is not blasphemed.

Those who have believing master's should not despise them because they are brothers. But rather they should serve them faithfully, because those who partake of their benefits are faithful and beloved. So teach and encourage these things.
If a man teaches otherwise and does not consent to the wholesome words of our Lord Jesus Christ, and his doctrine which is Godly.
Then he is proud and knows nothing, but he dotes on questions and the strife of words, from which comes envy, conflict, screams, and evil conjecture.
And perverse arguments between men with corrupt minds, who are destitute of the truth, thinking that enriching themselves is Godliness. So withdraw yourself from those such as these.
But Godliness with contentment is great gain.
For we brought nothing into this world, and it is certain we will carry nothing out of it.
But we will be content just having food and clothes.
But those who want to be rich will fall into temptation and a snare, and into many foolish and hurtful lusts, which drown men in destruction and perdition.
For the love of money is the root of all evil! Some have coveted money, and they have erred from the faith and pierced their hearts with many sorrows.
But you, O man of God, flee these things, and follow righteousness, godliness, faith, love, patience, and meekness.
Fight the good fight of faith! Take hold of eternal life to which you have been called, and to which you have also professed and made a good confession before many witnesses.
I charge you in the sight of God who breathes life into all things and before Jesus Christ, who witnessed and made a good confession before Pontius Pilate.
I charge you to keep this commandment spotless and blameless, until our Lord Jesus Christ reappears.
Which he will show in his own times, who is the blessed and only sovereign king of kings, and Lord of lords.
Who is the only immortal, at home in the light which no man can approach, whom no man has ever seen nor can see, to whom everlasting honor and power belong. Amen!
Teach those who are rich in this world, so that they are not high minded and trust in uncertain riches. But teach them to trust in the living God, who richly gives us all things to enjoy.
Teach them too do good, so that they are rich in good works, ready to distribute, and willing to communicate.
Laying up and storing for themselves a good foundation against the future, so that they may take hold of eternal life.
O Timothy, keep that which has been committed to your trust, avoid profane and vain babblings, and the false oppositions of so called science.
Which some have professed and erred away from the faith. Grace be with you. Amen!"
I Paul, an Apostle of Jesus Christ by God's will along with the promise of life which is in Jesus Christ.
Wrote this letter to Timothy my dearly beloved son which said, "Grace, mercy, and peace, from God the father and our Lord Jesus Christ.
I thank God, whom I serve with a pure conscience as did my forefathers. that I have unceasingly remembered you in my prayers both night and day.
For I greatly desire to see you when I think of your tears, so that I may be filled with joy.
When I recall the sincere faith that is in you, which first lived in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice, and I am persuaded that this faith is also in you.
For this reason, I remind you to stir up God's gift which is in you since my laying on of hands.
For God has not given us the spirit of fear, but he has given us the spirit of power, love, and sound mind.
So, do not be ashamed of me or of our Lord's testimony, for I am his prisoner, so that we could take part in the afflictions of the gospel by the power of God.
For God saved us, and called us with a holy calling, not because of our own works, but for his purpose and grace, which was given to us in Jesus Christ before the world began.
Because it is now obvious since the appearance of our savior Jesus Christ, that he has abolished death, and brought life and immortality to light through the gospel.
To which I have been appointed as a preacher, an apostle, and a teacher to the Gentiles.
That's why I also suffer these things, nevertheless I am not ashamed because I know whom I have believed and am persuaded that he can keep what I have committed to him against the day of judgement.
Hold fast to the form of sound words, which you have heard from me, in the faith and love that is in Jesus Christ.
And the good thing which was committed for to you keep through the Holy Spirit which lives in us.
You know that everyone in Asia has turned away from me, including Phygellus and Hermogenes.
May the Lord have mercy on the house of Onesiphorus, because he has often refreshed me and he was not ashamed of my chains.
But when he was in Rome, he very diligently sought me out and found me.
May the Lord grant Onesiphorus the Lord's mercy in those days. And you know very well, how much he ministered to me in Ephesus."
Then I Paul continued writing this letter to Timothy my dearly beloved son which said, "Therefore my son, be strong in the grace that is in Christ Jesus.
And commit the things that you have heard from me among many witnesses, to faithful men who will also be able to teach others.
Therefore endure the hard life of a good soldier in Jesus Christ.
No man of war entangles himself in the affairs of this life, in order to please the one who has chosen him to be a soldier.
And a man is not crowned as master, unless he struggles lawfully.
The rancher who labors must be the first to partake of the fruits.
Consider what I am saying, and the Lord will give you understanding of all things.
Remember that Jesus Christ is a descendant of David who was raised from the dead as I have proclaimed with my gospel.
For which I have suffered trouble and bondage like an evildoer, but God's word is never bound up.
Therefore, I endure all of these things for the sake of the elect, so that they may also obtain the salvation which is in Jesus Christ with eternal glory.
And this faithful saying states, 'Because if we be died with him, we will also live with him.
If we suffer, we will also reign with him; if we deny him, he also will deny us.
If we do not believe, he remains faithful, for he cannot deny himself.
Remember these things and teach them to those who are before the Lord, so that they do not struggle over words that profit nothing, except to subvert the listeners.
Study to show yourself to be approved by God and a workman who does not need to be ashamed, righteously distributing the word of truth.
But shun profane and vain babblings, because they will increase ungodliness even more.
And the words of people like Hymenaeus and Philetus will gnaw at your soul like a canker sore.
For they have erred concerning the truth, and they have said that the resurrection has already happened and they destroy the faith of some.
Nevertheless, the sure foundation of God stands and displays this seal; 'The Lord knows those who belong to him. And everyone who calls on the name of Jesus Christ will depart from immorality.'
But a great house contains not only gold and silver vessels, but also those made of wood and clay. Some are dedicated to honor, but some are dedicated to dishonor.
Therefore, if a man purges these things from himself, he will be a vessel for honor: sanctified for the master's use and prepared for every good work.
Flee from youthful lusts, but pursue righteousness, faith, charity, and peace with those who call on the Lord from a pure heart.
But avoid foolish and ignorant questions, for you know that they only engender strife.
And the Lord's servant must not argue, but he must be patient and kind to all men and prepared to teach.
And if the Lord's servant most humbly instructs those who oppose him; God may perhaps give them repentance that leads to their acknowledgment of the truth.
Then they may recover from the devil's snare, who has made them captives of his evil will."
Then I Paul continued writing this letter to Timothy my dearly beloved son which said, "You must also know this, in the last days perilous times will come.
For men will be lovers of their own selves, masturbators, boasters, blasphemers, disobedient to parents, covetous, proud, unthankful, and unholy.
Without natural affection, homosexual, truce breakers, false accusers, incontinent, fierce, and despisers of those who are good.
Traitors, strong willed, high minded, lovers of pleasures more than lovers of God.
They will have a form of Godliness, but they will deny its power. So you must turn away from such things.
For this sort of man will creep into houses, and lead silly women loaded with sins and diverse lusts away as captives.
They are forever learning, but never able to know the truth.
Now just as Jannes and Jambres opposed Moses, so do those who resist the truth. Men with corrupt minds, and who are unprincipled in the faith.
But they will proceed no further, for their foolishness will become as obvious to everyone as it was for Jannes and Jambres.
But you have fully seen my doctrine and my life's conduct, purpose, faith, long suffering, charity, and patience.
And my persecutions and afflictions, which came upon me in Antioch, Iconium, and Lystra. What persecutions I have endured! But the Lord delivered me from them all.
Yes, and all who live Godly in Jesus Christ will be mocked and persecuted!
But evil men and seducers will go from bad to worse, they will deceive and they will be deceived.
But as for you, continue in the things which you have learned and been assured of, for you know from whom you have learned them.
And since you were a child you have known the holy scriptures, which will make you wise for salvation through faith in Jesus Christ.
All scripture comes from God's inspiration, and is a profitable doctrine for rebuke, correction, and instruction in righteousness.
So that the man of God may be made perfect, thoroughly equipped for all good works."

Then I Paul finished writing this letter to Timothy my dearly beloved son which said, "Therefore, I inform you before God and the Lord Jesus Christ, who will judge the quick and the dead when he and his kingdom appear.
Preach the word, be instantly prepared in season and out of season; blame, reprimand, and encourage with every type of long suffering patience and doctrine.
For the time will come when they will not accept sound doctrine, but with itching ears they will pile up teachers who have the same lusts as themselves.
And they will turn their ears away from the truth and turn to fables.
But watch out for all things, endure afflictions, do the work of an evangelist, fulfill and prove your ministry.
For I am now ready to be offered, and the time of my departure is here.
I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, and I have kept the faith.
From now on I have a crown of righteousness laid up for me, which the righteous Lord will judge and give to me on that day. And not only for me, but also for all of those who love it when he appears.
Do your best to come see me soon.
For Demas has forsaken me because he loves this present world, and he has gone to Thessalonica. Crescens went to Galatia, and Titus went to Dalmatia.
Luke is the only one left with me. Bring Mark with you, for he helps me in the ministry.
And I have sent Tychicus to Ephesus.
When you come, please bring the cloak, the books, and especially the parchments with you that I left in Troas with Carpus.
Alexander the coppersmith did much evil to me. And the Lord will reward him according to his own works.
You must also be wary of Alexander, because he has greatly opposed our words.
At my first trial no man stood with me, everyone abandoned me, and I pray to God that it will not be held against them.
But the Lord stood with me and strengthened me, so that through my preaching God's word may be fully known and that all of the Gentiles would hear. Then I was delivered from the mouth of the lion.
And the Lord will deliver me from every evil work and bring me to his heavenly kingdom. For the glory belongs to the Lord forever and ever. Amen!
Greet Prisca and Aquila, and the household of Onesiphorus.
Erastus stayed in Corinth, but I left Trophimus in Miletum because he was sick.
Do your best to come before winter. Eubulus sends his greetings, and so do Pudens, Linus, Claudia, and all the brothers.
The Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Grace be with you all. Amen!"
I Paul, am a servant of God and an Apostle of Jesus Christ, according to the faith of God's elect, acknowledge the truth which comes from Godliness.
In hope of eternal life, which God, who cannot lie promised before the world began.
Which God has in due time made obvious through preaching God's word, that has been committed to me by God our savior.
Wrote this letter to Titus, my own son through the common faith, grace, mercy, and peace from God the father and the Lord Jesus Christ our savior which said,
I left you in Crete, so that you could organize the things that are wanting, and ordain elders in every city, just as I had appointed you.
Elders must be blameless and the husband of one wife, with faithful children who are not wild or unruly.
For a bishop must be a blameless steward of God; not stubborn, not quick to anger, not given to wine, nonviolent, and not greedy for dirty money.
But he must love hospitality and good men, and he must be sober, just, holy, and temperate.
He must hold fast to the faithful word as he was taught, so that he may be able to both encourage and convince deniers through sound doctrine.
For there are many unruly and vain talkers and deceivers, especially those who are circumcised.
Whose mouths must be stopped, because they subvert whole houses and teach things which they should not, just for the sake of dirty money.
One of their own Cretian prophets once said, 'The Cretians are always liars and evil beasts with slow bellies (lazy gluttons).'
This witness is true. Therefore, reprimand them sharply, so that they may be sound in the faith.
Do not listen to Jewish fables and the commandments of men, who turn from the truth.
To the pure all things are pure, but nothing is pure to those who are defiled and unbelieving, even their mind and conscience is defiled.
They profess that they know God, but they deny him through their works. They are abominable, disobedient, and unprincipled in every good work."
I Paul, continued writing this letter to Titus which said, "But speak of the things which become sound doctrine.
So that the old men may be sober, grave, temperate, and sound in faith, charity, and patience.
And may the old women be likewise, so that their behavior becomes like holiness and teachers of good things, not false accusers nor given to much wine.
So that they may teach the young women to be sober, and to love their husbands and children.
And to also be discreet, chaste, good, homemakers, obedient to their own husbands, so that God's word is not blasphemed.
They should also encourage the young men to be sober minded.
Make an example of yourself in all things by showing a pattern of good works with gravity, sincerity, and an incorruptible doctrine.
With sound speech that cannot be condemned, so that the one who is contrary to you may be ashamed and have nothing evil to say about you.
Encourage servants to be obedient to their own masters, and to well please them in all things without arguing.
Encourage them to not steal, but remain faithful, so that they may adorn the doctrine of our God and savior in all things.
For the grace of God that brings salvation has appeared to all men.
Teaching us that, we must deny unGodliness and worldly lusts, and we should live soberly, righteously, and Godly in this present world.
Looking for that blessed hope, and the glorious appearance of our great God and savior Jesus Christ.
Who gave himself for us, so that he could rescue us from all immorality, and to purify a peculiar people for himself, who are zealous for good works.
Speak and encourage these things and reprimand with all authority. Let no man despise you."
I Paul, finished writing this letter to Titus which said, "Remind the believers to submit to nations and powers, to obey the magistrates, and to be ready for every good work.
To speak evil of no one, and do not be brawlers but be gentle and humble to all men.
For we ourselves were also sometimes foolish, disobedient, and deceived. For we served various lusts and pleasures, living with malice, hate, and envy toward one another.
But after that, the love and kindness of God our savior toward man appeared.
He did not save us by our works of righteousness, but he saved us with his mercy, through his regenerative washing and by renewing the Holy Spirit.
For which God abundantly shed his blood on us through our savior Jesus Christ.
So that we have been justified by his grace, in order to be made heirs through the hope of eternal life.

This is a faithful saying, and it is my wish that you constantly affirm these things, so that those who have believed in God will carefully maintain good works. These things are good and profitable for men.
But avoid foolish questions, genealogies, disagreements, and quarrels about the law because they are unprofitable and in vain.
Reject any man who is a heretic after the first or second reprimand.
Knowing that a man such as this is subverted, and sinful, and he has condemned himself.
When I send Artemas or Tychicus to you, be diligent and come to me in Nicopolis because I have decided to winter over there.
Plan their journey diligently when you bring Zenas the lawyer and Apollos, so that they need nothing.
And our people must learn to do the good works for necessary purposes, so that they will not be unfruitful.
All who are with me send you their greetings. Greet those who love us in the faith. Grace be with you all. Amen!"
I Paul, a prisoner of Jesus Christ and our brother Timothy, wrote this letter to our dearly beloved and fellow laborer Philemon.
This letter is also addressed to our beloved Apphia, and our fellow soldier Archippus and the church that meets in your home which said,
"Grace and peace to you from God our father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
I thank my God for you, and I always mention you in my prayers.
For I have heard of the love and faith you have toward the Lord Jesus and all of the saints.
So that your communication of faith may become successful as you acknowledge every good thing which is in you through Jesus Christ.
For we take great joy and consolation in your love, because you brother, have refreshed the hearts of the saints.
Therefore, even though I may be bold enough in Christ to encourage you to do that which is appropriate.
But I, Paul prefer to beg you for love's sake since I am now old and also a prisoner of Jesus Christ.
I beg you for my son Onesimus, whom I fathered in chains.
Which was unprofitable to you in the past, but now he has profitable to you and to me.
Whom I have sent back to you again, so please receive him for he is my heart.
I would have kept him with me, so that instead of you he could have ministered to me in the bonds of the gospel.
But I would do nothing without your approval, so that your benefit would not be out of necessity, but willingly.
For perhaps he had to leave for a season, so that you could receive him forever.
No longer a servant but above a servant, he is an especially beloved brother to me, but even more so to you, both in the flesh and in the Lord?
So if you think of me as a partner, receive him as if her were me.
But if he has wronged you or owes you anything put it on my account.
I Paul have written this letter with my own hand, I will repay it, but besides that I did not want to say that you yourself even owe me.
Therefore brother, let me have the joy of the Lord from you to refresh my heart.
For I am confident of your obedience so I wrote to you, knowing that you will also do more than I ask.
But I also ask that you prepare a lodging for me, because I trust that through your prayers I will be given back to you.
Therefore, Epaphras my fellow prisoner in Jesus Christ salutes you.
My fellow laborers Marcus, Aristarchus, Demas, and Lucas also salute you.
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen!"
God, who at different times and in different ways has in the past spoken to the fathers through the prophets.
Has in these last days spoken to us through his son, whom he has appointed as the heir of everything, and through whom he also made the worlds.

The son who shines as brilliantly as God's glory, and in the exact image of his person, and upholds everything by the word of his power, when he all by himself has purged us of our sins, sat down at the right hand of the majestic God on high.
For God's son was made so much better than the angels, and he has inherited a much more excellent name than them.
For which one of the angels did God ever say at any time, "You are my son, for today I have become your father," or did he say again, "I will be his father, and he will be my son"?
And again, when God brought his firstborn into the world, he said, "Let all of God's angels worship him."
And God spoke of the angels and said, "God makes his angels spirits, and he makes his ministers a fiery flame.
But to God's son he says, "O God, your throne will last forever and ever, and righteousness is the scepter of your kingdom.
You have loved righteousness and hated immorality, therefore your God, has anointed you with the oil of happiness above your friends.
And you Lord, laid the earth's foundation in the beginning, and the heavens were created by the works of your hands.
They will perish but you will remain, and they all will grow old just like a garment.
And just like clothes you will fold them up, and they will be changed, but you remain the same forever, and your years will never fail.
But to which of the angels did God ever say at any time, "Sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies your footstool"?
Are not all of the angels ministering spirits, sent out to minister for those who will inherit salvation?
Therefore, we should give the most earnest heed to the things which we have heard, otherwise at any time we may let them slip.
For if the angels' spoken word was steadfast, and every disobedient transgression received a just reward as compensation.
How can we escape if we neglect such a great salvation, that the Lord first began to be speak, which was confirmed to us by those who heard him.
God also bears witness with both signs and wonders to them, with various gifts and miracles from the Holy Spirit according to his will?
For he has not subjected the angels to the world to come, about which we have spoken.
But in one certain place it was testified and said, "What is it about a man that makes you think of him, and what is it about the son of man that makes you visit him?"
You made him a little lower than the angels, you crowned him with glory and honor and set him over the works of your hands.

You have put all things under his feet. For in that he has subjected all things under him, and there is nothing that he did not put under him. But now we still do not see all things that are under him.
But we see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels to suffer death. He was crowned with glory and honor, so that by the grace of God he would taste death for every man.
For death became him, for whom and by whom all things all things exist, to bring many sons to glory, to make the captain of their salvation perfect through suffering.
For both the one who sanctifies, and those who are sanctified are all part of the one and only Jesus, who is not ashamed to call them brothers.
And Jesus says, "`I will declare your name and sing praises to my brothers in the middle of the church.´"
And behold once again Jesus says, "`I will put my trust in God, and I am here with the children which God has given me.´"
For as much as the children partake of flesh and blood, Jesus also took part in the same flesh, so that through death he could destroy the devil who held the power of death.
And deliver those who fear death from their lifetime subjected to bondage.
For surely did not take the nature of angels upon himself, but he took the seed of Abraham upon himself.

Therefore, Jesus took it upon himself to be made just like his brothers in all things, so that he could be a merciful and faithful high priest in everything that pertains to God, to make reconciliation for the sins of the people.
For Jesus himself has suffered; and when he was tempted, he can help those who are also tempted.
Therefore holy brothers, who share the heavenly calling, consider the apostle and the high priest of our profession, Jesus Christ.
Who was faithful to the one who appointed him, just as Moses was also faithful in all of God's house.
For Jesus was counted worthy of more glory than Moses, since the one who has built the house has more honor than the house itself.
For every house is built by some man, but God is the one who builds all things.
And Moses was truly faithful as a servant throughout God's house, as a testimony of those things which were to be spoken of later.
But Christ is a faithful son over his own house and we are his house, if we hold firmly to the confidence and rejoiceful hope until the end.
Therefore, as the Holy Spirit says, "Today, if you hear the Holy Spirit's voice.
Do not harden your hearts, as you did when you were provoked on the day of temptation in the wilderness.
When your fathers tempted and tested me and saw my works for forty years.
Which caused me great grief with that generation and I said, 'They always err in their heart, and they have not known my ways.'
So I swore in my anger, that they would not enter my rest."
Take heed brothers, otherwise there could be an evil heart of disbelief in any one of you, that may cause you to depart from the living God.
But encourage one another daily, while it is called today, otherwise any one of you could be hardened through the deceitfulness of sin.
For we are made to share in Christ, if we hold steadfastly in our confidence as it was in the beginning until the end.
And as it has been said before, "Today if you hear God's voice, do not harden your hearts, as you did in the provocation."
For some who heard God's voice were provoked, and they were led out of Egypt by Moses.
But was God not grieved by them for forty years? Was God not grieved by those who had sinned, whose bodies fell in the wilderness?
And to whom did he sware that they would not enter into his rest? Was it not those who did not believe?
So we see that they could not enter because of their unbelief.
Therefore let us fear, otherwise many of you may fall short of the promise he has left us of entering into his rest.
For the gospel was preached both to us as well as them, but the word that was preached did not profit them, because their faith was not mixed in with those who heard it.

For we who believe enter into that rest, and it is just as God has said, "As I have sworn an oath in my anger, they shall never enter into my rest, even though God's works have been finished since the foundation of the world."
For God spoke in some place about the seventh day of this wisdom, and God rested on the seventh day from all his works.
And God spoke in this place again and said, "If they enter into my rest.
Since some must still enter into my rest there, and those to whom it was first preached did not enter because of their disbelief.
Again, God declared a certain day and spoke through David and said, "Today, after such a long time, as it is said, 'If you hear his voice today, do not harden your hearts. (Psalms 95:7-8)"
For if Jesus had given them rest, then would God not have spoken of another day afterward.
Therefore, there remains a place of rest for the people of God.
For whoever enters God's rest, has also ceased his own work, just as God rested from his work.
So, let us labor to enter into that rest, otherwise someone may follow their same example of disbelief.

For the word of God is quick and powerful, and sharper than any double-edged sword, which even pierces and divides the soul and spirit, the joints and marrow, and God recognizes the thoughts and intents of the heart.
There is no creature that is not manifested in God's sight, but everything is laid naked and opened to the eyes of God to whom we must appear.
Since then, we have had a great high priest who has passed into the heavens, which is Jesus the son of God, so let us hold fast to our profession.
For we do not have a high priest who cannot feel our infirmities, but he was tempted by everything with which we are tempted, yet he did not sin.
Therefore, let us come boldly to the throne of grace, so that we may obtain mercy and find grace to help us in our time of need.
For every high priest taken from among men who is ordained to represent men in things pertaining to God, and to offer both gifts and sacrifices for sins.
Who can have compassion for the ignorant and those who are misguided, for he himself is also surrounded by infirmity.
And that's why he should offer sacrifices for his sins as well as for the sins of the people.
And no man takes this honor upon himself, but he is called by God just as Aaron was.
So Christ also did not glorify himself to be made a high priest, but he was called by the one who said to him, "You are my son, and today I have become your father. (Psalm 5:5)"
And as God also says in another place, "You are a priest forever in the order of Melchizedek. (Psalm 110:4)"
During the days that Jesus lived in the flesh he offered up strong prayers and pleas with crying and tears to the one who could save him from death, and he was heard because he feared.
Even though Jesus was a son, he learned obedience through the things that he suffered.
And having been made perfect, Jesus became the author of eternal salvation for all of those who obey him.
And Jesus was called by God as a high priest in the order of Melchisedec.
We have much to say about Jesus, but it is hard to explain since you are dull of hearing.

For when the time comes when you should become teachers, you need someone to teach you again about the first principles of the oracles of God, for you will have need of milk and not solid meat at this time.
For those who need milk are unskilled babes in the word of righteousness.
But solid meat belongs to those who are mature and full of age, even those who are experienced and have used and exercised their senses to recognize both good and evil.
Therefore, after leaving the principles of the doctrine of Christ, let us go on to perfection, and let us not lay the foundation of repentance from dead works again, but of faith in God.
And the doctrine of baptism and the laying on of hands, and the resurrection of the dead and eternal judgment.
And we will do this, if God permits.
For it is impossible for those who were once enlightened, who have tasted the heavenly gift and have partaken of the Holy Spirit.
And who have tasted the good word of God and the powers of the world to come.
And if they have fallen away, only to be renewed to repentance again, since they themselves crucify the son of God and openly shame him once again.
For the earth which drinks in the rain that often falls on it and produces herbs meant for those who tend them and receive the blessing from God.
But the land which bears thorns and briers is rejected, and it is nearly a curse which will end up being burned.
My beloved, we are persuaded of better things about you and the things that accompany salvation, even though we speak this way.
For God is not unrighteous and he will not forget your work and labor of love, which you have shown toward his name, since you have ministered and still do minister to the saints.
And we desire that every one of you show the same diligence in full assurance of hope to the very end.
So that you are not dull and lazy, but you follow those who have the faith and patience to inherit the promises.
For when God made his promise to Abraham, since there was no one greater than him, God swore by his own name.
And God said, "I will surely bless you and multiply your descendants. (Genesis 22:17)"
So, after Abraham waited and patiently endured, he obtained the promise.
For men honestly swear by someone greater than themselves, and they swear an oath of confirmation to end all conflict.
In which God was more abundantly willing to show to the heirs of the promise of God's unchanging counsel, which he confirmed with an oath.
That by two unchanging things in which it is impossible for God to lie, so that we who have fled to refuge might be strongly comforted to take hold of the hope set before us.
We hold this hope both sure and steadfast like an anchor of the soul, which enters into that which is behind the veil.
Where our forerunner Jesus has entered behind the veil and was forever made a high priest in the order of Melchisedec.
For Melchisedec was the king of Salem and a priest of the most-high God. And Melchisedec met Abraham returning from the slaughter of the kings and blessed him.

Abraham also gave Melchisedec a 1/10th part of everything. The first interpretation of the title King Melchisedec means he is the king of righteousness, and after that it also means he is the "king of Salem",which means "king of peace".
We have no information about his father, mother, or ancestors nor do we know his birthday or the date of his death, but he was made like the son of God, who continuously endures as a priest.
Now consider how great this man was, to whom even the patriarch Abraham gave 1/10th of the spoils.
And truly Levi's sons, who are in the priesthood, are ordered to take tithes from the people in accordance with the law, even though they also come from Abraham's descendants.
But Melchisedec who is not a Levite descendant received tithes from Abraham and blessed the one who had the promises.
And without contradiction, the less is blessed by the better.
And here men who die receive the tithes, but there Melchisedec receives them, for it is witnessed that he still lives.
And if I may say so, Levi, who also receives tithes, paid tithes through Abraham.
For Levi was still in the loins of his father, when Melchisedec met Abraham.

Therefore, if perfection could be received through the Levitical priesthood, for under the priesthood people received the law. Which is why there was a further need for another priest to rise in the order of Melchisedec, and no need for one in the order of Aaron?
Because since the priesthood had changed, it was necessary for the law to also change.
For the one about whom these things are said belonged to another tribe, from which no man had ever attended to the altar.
For it is evident that our Lord Jesus descended from Juda, a tribe of which Moses said nothing about belonging to the priesthood.
And yet this is far more evident, because if another priest like Melchisedec rises.
Who was not made priest by the law of a carnal commandment, but by the power of an endless life.
