For it is testified about Jesus, "You are a priest forever in the order of Melchisedec."
For the previous commandment is truly cancelled, for it was weak and unprofitable.
For the law made nothing perfect, but bringing a better hope which draws us nearer to God brought perfection.
And Jesus was made a priest by God's oath.
For those priests were made without an oath, but with an oath by the one who said to Jesus, "The Lord swore an oath and he will not repent, you are a priest forever in the order of Melchisedec.
By this oath Jesus was made the guarantee of a better testament.
And there were truly many priests, because they did not suffer and continue because they died.
But this man Jesus has an unchangeable priesthood, because he lives forever.
Therefore Jesus can save those who are the furthest from God through himself, since he lives forever to make intercession for them.
For such a high priest who is holy, innocent, clean, separate from sinners, and made higher than the heavens became like us.
Unlike the other high priests, Jesus does not need to offer up daily sacrifices first for his own sins, and then for the sins of the people, because he did this once when he offered up himself.
For the law makes men who have infirmities the high priests, but the word of God's oath, which came after the law, makes the son, who has been declared sacred forever.
Now this is the sum of all those things of which we have spoken. We have such a high priest, who sat at the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens.
A minister of the sanctuary and the true tabernacle tent, which was pitched by the Lord and not man.
For every high priest is ordained to offer gifts and sacrifices, because it was necessary for this man Jesus to also have something to offer.
Because if Jesus were here on earth, he would not be a priest, since there are priests who offer gifts in accordance with the law.

The place where they serve is a shadow of the heavenly things. And just as Moses was warned by God when he was about to build the tabernacle when he said, "See to it that you make everything according to the pattern you were shown on the mountain."
But now Jesus has obtained a much more excellent ministry, through which he is also the mediator of a much better covenant, which was established on better promises.
For if that first covenant had been faultless, then there would have been no place sought for a second covenant.
For God found fault with them and the Lord said, "Behold the day has come, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and the house of Judah."

And the Lord said, "It will not be like the covenant I made with their fathers on the day that I took them by the hand and led them out of Egypt, because they did not continue in my covenant, so I did not regard them."

And the Lord said, "For this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, I will put my laws into their mind and write them in their hearts, and I will be their God and they will be my people.
And each man will no longer teach his neighbor and his brother and say, 'Know the Lord,' because they will all know me, from the least to the greatest.
For I will be merciful to their unrighteousness, and I will no longer remember their sins and wickedness."
In that new covenant God said that he has made the first covenant old. And now that covenant which has grown old, decays and it is ready to vanish away.
The first true covenant also had legal decrees of divine service, and a worldly sanctuary.
For a tabernacle was built, and its first room which was called the sanctuary, held the lampstand, table, and the priest's bread offering.
And behind the second veil was the tabernacle called the Most Holy Place.
Which held the golden censer and the gold covered Ark of the Covenant, where the golden pot of manna was kept, along with Aaron's budded staff and the covenant tablets.
The cherubim of glory were above the ark and overshadowed the mercy seat, which we can no longer discuss in detail.
After these things were ordained, the priests always went into the first tabernacle to perform the services of God.
But the high priest was the only one who went into the second tabernacle once per year, but he never entered without a blood offering, which he offered for himself and for the errors of the people.
This was how the Holy Spirit signified that the way into the Most Holy Place had not yet been revealed, since the first tabernacle was still standing.
Which was a present figure at that time, and a place where both gifts and sacrifices were offered, but it still could not make the one who performed the services have a perfect conscience.
Which stood only in meats, drinks, diverse washings, and carnal ordinances imposed on the people until the time of reformation.
But when Christ came as the high priest of the good things to come, through a greater and more perfect tabernacle, that was not made with hands and was not part of this first building.
Christ did not enter by the blood of goats and calves, but he entered the Most Holy Place by shedding his own blood once and for all and obtained eternal redemption for us all.
For if the blood of bulls and goats and the ashes of a heifer sprinkled on those who are unclean, sanctifies and purifies the flesh.

Then how much more will the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself as an unblemished sacrifice to God, purge your consciousness of the works of the dead to serve the living God?

Therefore Christ is the mediator of the new testament through his death, for the redemption of the transgressions that were under the first testament, so that those who are called can receive the promise of the eternal inheritance.
For where there is a testament, the death of the testator (one who makes a will) is also necessary.
For a testament is only enforced after men die, because it has no strength at all while the testator lives.
So, the first testament was not dedicated without blood.

For when Moses had spoken every precept to all the people in accordance with the law, he took the blood of calves and goats, along with water, scarlet wool, and hyssop and sprinkled it both on the book and all the people.
And Moses said, "This is the blood of the testament, which God has encouraged you to keep."
Furthermore, he sprinkled blood both on the tabernacle and on all the vessels used in the ministry.
And by the law, almost all things are purged with blood, and there is no remission of sin without the shedding of blood.
Therefore, it was necessary for the copies of the heavenly things to be purified with these blood sacrifices, but the heavenly things themselves offer better sacrifices than these.
For Christ has not entered the holy places made with hands, which are just copies of the true, but he has now entered into heaven itself to appear in the presence of God for us.
Nor did he have to offer himself often, as the high priest must enter into the Most Holy Place every year with the blood of others.
For Christ would have had to suffer often since the foundation of the world, but now he has appeared only once at the end of the world to put away sin by the sacrifice of himself.
And it is appointed unto men to die only once, but after this the judgment.
So Christ was also offered only once to bear the sins of many, and to those who look for him, he will appear a second time without sin to bring them into salvation.

For the law was a shadow of the good things to come, and not the very image of the coming things. The law can never make perfect those who come to it through the sacrifices which they continuously offered year after year.
If it could, would they not have ceased making those offerings? Because once the worshippers are purged, they would no longer have a sinful conscience.
But those sacrifices are an annual reminder of sins once again.
For it is not possible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins.
Therefore when Christ came into the world, he said, "`Sacrifice and offering God did not want, but God prepared a body for me.´
`In burnt offerings and sin sacrifices, God has had no pleasure.´
`Then I said, 'O God look, in the volume of the book it is written of me, that I have come to do your will.'´"(Psalms 40:6-8)

In the above passages Christ said, "`You did not desire sacrifice and offerings, you have opened my ears, and you did not require burnt offerings and sin offerings.´" Even though they are offered by the law.
Then the Lord said, "`O God look, I have come to do your will.´" Jesus takes away the first testament, so that he may establish the second.
By which we are sanctified through Jesus Christ offering up his body one time for us all.
And every priest stands every day ministering and often offering the same sacrifices all over again, which can never take away sins.
But this man Jesus, after he offered his one sacrifice for all sins forever, sat down at the right hand of God.
And from now on he expects and waits for his enemies to be made his footstool.
For through his one offering he has forever made perfect those who are sanctified.
Furthermore the Holy Spirit is also a witness to us, because after that he had said before.
And the Lord said, "This is the covenant that I will make with them after those days, I will put my law in their hearts, and I will write them in their minds.
And I will no longer remember their sins and wickedness."
Now where these sins are in remission, sin offerings are no longer needed.
Therefore brothers, boldly enter into the Most Holy Place by the blood of Jesus.
By a new and living way, which Jesus has declared sacred for us through the veil of his flesh.
And since we have a high priest over the house of God.
Let us draw near with a true heart fully assured of faith, having our hearts sprinkled to save us from an evil conscience and our bodies washed with pure water.
Let us unwaveringly hold fast and profess our faith, because God who promised is faithful.
And let us consider how to inspire one another to love and do good works.
Let us not forsake assembling ourselves together as some do, but encourage one another and so much more, as you see the day approaching.
For if we willfully sin after we have received the knowledge of truth, there remains no more sacrifice for sins.
But a certain fearful expectation of judgment and fiery indignation that will devour the adversaries.
Whoever despised the law of Moses, died without mercy under the testimony of two or three witnesses.

How much more severe do you suppose the punishment will be for the one thought to be worthy, who has trampled on the son of God. The one who has counted on the blood of the covenant, that sanctified him as an unholy thing, and has done this to spite the spirit of grace?
For we know the God who has said, "Vengeance is Mine, I will repay!" And again, the Lord says, "The Lord will judge his people!"
It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.
But remember the former days when you were illuminated, and you endured a great fight of afflictions.
Partly because you were made a spectacle through both disrespect and afflictions, and partly because you became companions of those who were so used.
For you had compassion for me in my bondage, and joyfully accepted the seizure of your goods, knowing that you yourselves have a better and enduring substance in heaven.
Therefore, do not throw away your confidence which has great reward for compensation.
For you need patience, so that after you have done the will of God, you might receive the promise.
For in just a little while, Jesus will come and he will not delay.
Now the just will live by faith, but if a man draws back, my soul will take no pleasure in him.
But we are not of those who draw back to damnation, but of those who believe in the saving of their soul.
Now faith is the substance of the things we hope for, and the evidence of the unseen things.
For through faith the elders obtained a good report.
Through faith we understand that the worlds were framed by God's word, so that the things which are seen were not made from things that are seen.

By faith, Abel offered God a better sacrifice than Cain, through which Abel obtained God's testimony that he was righteous when God testified of his gifts. And through faith Abel still speaks even though he is dead.
By faith, Enoch was translated and he did not see death, and he could not be found because God had translated him. For before his translation his testimony was that he pleased God.
But without faith it is impossible to please God, because whoever comes to God must believe that he is God, and that God rewards those who diligently seek him.

By faith, Noah was warned by God of things not yet seen, and he was moved by fear to prepare an ark to save his household. By faith, Noah condemned the world and became the heir of righteousness which comes by faith.
By faith, after Abraham was called to leave and go to a place where he would later receive an inheritance. So he obeyed and left not knowing where he was going.

By faith, Abraham traveled in the promised land as a stranger in a strange country. He made his home in tabernacles just as Isaac and Jacob did, who along with Abraham were the heirs of the same promise.
For Abraham looked for a city with foundations designed and built by God.
Through faith, Sara also received strength to conceive and deliver a child when she was past her childbearing years, because she judged God to be faithful as well as his promise.
Therefore, even though Abraham was as good as dead, so many descendants sprang forth from him that were as numerous as the stars of the sky, and as endless as the sand on the seashore.

All these people died in faith without receiving the promises, but they saw them from far away. They were persuaded and embraced the promises that were made to them, and they confessed that they were strangers and pilgrims on the earth.
For those who say such things plainly declare that they are seeking their own country.
And truly, if they had been thinking of the country they had left, they might have had an opportunity to return.
But now they desire a better more heavenly country. Therefore, God is not ashamed to be called their God, for he has prepared a city for them.
By faith, when Abraham was tested, he offered up Isaac. The one who had received the promises offered up his only son.
Of whom God had said, "Through Isaac your descendants will be called."
Abraham even believed that God could raise Isaac up from the dead, and Isaac did return from the dead, as a figure of speech.
By faith, Isaac blessed his sons Jacob and Esau about the things to come.
By faith, when Jacob was dying, he blessed both of Joseph's sons and worshipped God leaning on his staff.
By faith, Joseph spoke about the Israelis exodus from Egypt and gave them a commandment about his bones.
By faith, when Moses was born, he was hidden for three months by his parents, because they saw he was a beautiful child, and they were not afraid of the king's commandment.
By faith, when Moses became an adult, he refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter.
Moses chose to suffer affliction with God's people, rather than enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season.
Mose felt that the disrespect of Christ offered greater riches than all the treasures in Egypt, because he had respect for the reward as his compensation.
By faith, Moses had forsaken Egypt, and he did not fear the king's anger, and he endured because he saw God who is invisible.
Through faith, Moses kept the Passover and the sprinkling of blood, otherwise the one who destroyed the firstborn would touch Israel's firstborn,
By faith, the people passed through the Red Sea by walking on dry land, but when the Egyptians attempted to do so, they were drowned.
By faith, the walls of Jericho fell down after they were surrounded for about seven days.
By faith, Rahab the prostitute did not perish with those who did not believe, after she had received the spies with peace.
So what more can I say? For time does not allow me to tell of Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthae, David, Samuel, and the prophets.
Who through faith subdued kingdoms, worked righteousness, obtained promises, and shut the mouths of lions.
They quenched the violent fire, escaped the edge of the sword, and from weakness they were made strong and grew courageous in battle, and turned the alien armies to flight.
Women received their dead who were returned and raised back to life. Others were tortured and they would not accept deliverance, so that they might obtain a better resurrection.
And others had trials of cruel mocking and scourging, and even bondage and imprisonment.
They were stoned, sawn apart, and tempted. They were killed with the sword and wandered around in sheepskin and goatskin. They were destitute, afflicted, and tormented.
The world was not worthy to have the people who wandered in the deserts, mountains, and lived in the earth's dens and caves.
And all of these people have obtained a good report through faith, but they did not receive the promise.
God has provided something better for us, so that those without us would not be made perfect.
Therefore, since we are surrounded by such a great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside all the weight of the sin which so easily plagues us, and let us patiently run the race set before us.

Looking to Jesus the author and finisher of our faith, who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross. Jesus despised the shame of the cross and he has now sat down at the right hand of God's throne.
So consider the one who endured such a contradiction of sinners against himself, otherwise you may grow weary and faint in your minds.
You have not yet resisted to the point of bloodshed, struggling against sin.
And you have forgotten the encouragement which speaks to you as children and says, "My son, do not despise the Lord's disciplining, nor faint when you are reprimanded by him.
For the Lord loves the one he disciplines, and he scourges every son he receives.
If you endure discipline, God deals with you as sons. For what son does the father not discipline?
But if you are without chastisement of which everyone else partakes, then are you bastards and not sons.
Furthermore, we all have earthly fathers who corrected us and we respect them. Should we not submit much more to our spiritual father and live?
For earthly fathers honestly chastened us for a few days as they thought best, but God disciplines us for our own profit, so that we might share in his holiness.
Now no discipline at the present time seems to be a joyous thing, but it is grievous. Nevertheless, afterward it yields the peaceful fruit of righteousness to those who have been trained that way.
Therefore, lift up your limp hands and feeble knees.
And make a straight path for your feet, so that, that which is lame may not disabled; but rather let it be healed.
Pursue peace and holiness with everyone, otherwise no one will see the Lord.
Diligently see that no one falls from the grace of God, and that no root of bitterness springs up to trouble you and defile many.
Otherwise there may be an adulterer or profane person such as Esau, who sold his inheritance for one morsel of meat.
For you know that afterward, he wanted to inherit the blessing, but he was rejected because he found no place for repentance, even though he carefully sought it with tears.
For you have not come to a physical mountain that can be touched and burned with fire, nor to a black, dark, and violent windy storm.
And the sound of a trumpet and the voice of words, which those who heard pleaded that the word would not be spoken to them anymore.
Because they could not endure what was commanded when they heard, "If even so much as a beast touches the mountain, it will be stoned or thrust through with a spear."
And so terrible was the sight, that Moses said, "I am quaking in fear."
But you have come to Mount Zion and Jerusalem the heavenly city of the living God, with an endless company of angels.
You have come to the general assembly and church of the firstborn, which are written in heaven. You have come to God the Judge of all, and to the spirits of righteous men made perfect.
And to Jesus the mediator of the new covenant, and to the sprinkling of blood, that speaks better things than the blood of Abel.

See that you do not refuse Jesus the one who speaks. For if we did not escape from the one whom we refused when he spoke on earth, how much more will we not escape, if we turn away from the one who speaks from heaven.
Whose voice shook the earth, but now he has promised and said, "Once more I will shake not only the earth, but heaven as well."
And this word once more, signifies the removal of those things that can be shaken which are the things that are made, so that those things which cannot be shaken may remain.
Therefore we are receiving a kingdom which cannot be moved, so let us have grace, so that we may serve God acceptably with reverence and godly fear.
For our God is a consuming fire.
Let brotherly love continue.
Do not forget to entertain strangers, because in doing so some have unknowingly entertained angels.
Remember those who are in bondage as if you were bound with them, and those who suffer adversity, as if you yourselves were also in their body.
Marriage is honorable to all and the bed must be kept clean, but God will judge the whoremongers and adulterers.
Let your conversations be without covetousness, and be content with the things that you have, because God has said, "I will never leave you, nor forsake you."
So that we may boldly say, "The Lord is my helper, and I will not fear what man can do to me."
Remember your leaders who have spoken the word of God to you, whose faith you follow, and you consider their conversations later.
Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever.

Do not get carried away with different strange doctrines. For it is a good thing for the heart to be established with grace, not with meats, which have not profited those who have been occupied by them.
We have an altar from which those who serve in the tabernacle have no right to eat.
For the bodies of the beasts whose blood is brought into the sanctuary by the high priest for sin, are burned outside the camp.
Therefore, Jesus also suffered outside the gate., so that he might sanctify the people with his own blood,
Therefore let us go to him outside the camp, bearing his disgrace.
For we have we no continuing city here, but we seek the one to come.
Therefore, through Jesus let us continually offer the sacrifice of praise to God, that is the fruit of our lips giving thanks to his name.
But do not forget to do good and to communicate, because God is well pleased by such sacrifices.

Obey your leaders and submit yourselves to them, because they watch over your souls, as those who must give an account. So that they may lead with joy and not with grief, for that is unprofitable for you.
Pray for us, because we trust that we have a good conscience in all things, and we are willing to live honestly.
But I beg you to do this, so that I may be restored to you the sooner.
Now may the God of peace, who brought our Lord Jesus from dead, who is the great shepherd of the sheep, through the blood of the everlasting covenant.
Make you perfect in every good work to do his will. And may God work in you everything that is well pleasing in his sight, through Jesus Christ. And the glory is his forever and ever. Amen!
And I beg you brothers, to suffer the word of encouragement, for I have written a letter of few words to you.
Know you that our brother Timothy has been set free. If he comes soon, then I will see you soon.
Greet all of your leaders and the saints. Those from Italy send you their salutations.
Grace be with you all. Amen!
I James, a servant of God and the Lord Jesus Christ, send my greetings to the twelve tribes of Israel which are scattered abroad.
My brothers, consider it to be joy when you fall into different kinds of temptation.
For you know that the testing of your faith brings patience.
But let patience have her perfect work, so that you may be perfect and complete, wanting for nothing.
If any of you lack wisdom, then let him ask God who gives liberally to all men and he does not severely criticize, and it will be given him.
But let him ask in faith, without wavering. For the one who wavers is like an ocean wave driven and tossed by the wind.
For do not let that man think that he will receive anything from the Lord.
A double minded man is unstable in all his ways.
But the brother of low degree should rejoice in the fact that he is glorified.
But the one who is rich is made low, because he will pass away like a flower in the field.
For the sun has no sooner risen with burning heat, when the grass begins to wither, and its flower falls off, and the grace of its beauty perishes. So also, the rich man will fade away in his ways.
Blessed is the man who endures temptation, because when he is tested, he will receive the crown of life, which the Lord has promised to those who love him.
Let no man say when he is tempted, "I have been tempted by God." Because God cannot be tempted by evil, nor does he tempt anyone.
But every man is tempted when he is tempted and drawn away by his own lust.
Then after lust has conceived, it brings forth sin, and sin, when it is finished, brings forth death.
Do not err, my beloved brothers.
For every good and perfect gift is from above, and comes down from the father of lights, with whom there is no fickle nor turning shadow.
Of his own will he fathered us with the word of truth, so that we would be a kind of first fruits of his creatures.
My beloved brothers, everyone must be swift to hear, slow to speak, and slow to anger.
For the wrath of man does not do the work of God's righteousness.
So remove all the filthiness and superfluous naughtiness and humbly receive the word grafted within you, which can save your souls.
But be one of those who does what the word says, and not one of those who only hears the word but deceives themselves.
For if anyone hears the word and does not do what it says, is like a man who sees his natural face in a mirror.
For he sees himself and goes away and immediately forgets what he has seen.
But whoever looks into the perfect law of liberty and continues in it because he is not a forgetful listener, but he is someone who does the work. This man will be blessed by his deeds.
If any man among you seems to be religious, and does not bridle his tongue, but he deceives his own heart and his religion is vain.
Pure and clean religion before God the father is this; visit the fatherless and the widows in their affliction and keep yourself unpolluted by the world.
My brothers, do not have faith in our glorious Lord Jesus Christ based on the respect of people.
For if a man comes to your assembly with a gold ring wearing goodly apparel, and a poor man also comes in wearing vile clothes.
And you have respect for the one who wears gay clothing, and you say to him, "Sit here in a good place." And you say to the poor man, "Stand there, or sit here under my footstool."
Are you not then showing partiality among yourselves, and have you not become judges of evil thoughts?
Listen, my beloved brothers; has not God chosen the poor of this world to be rich in faith, and heirs of the kingdom which he has promised to those who love him?
But you have despised the poor. Do not rich oppress you, and bring you before the judgment seats?
Do they not blaspheme the worthy name by which you have been called?
If you fulfill the royal law in the scripture, you will love your neighbor as yourself, and you will do well.
But if you respect people by their status, you commit a sin and by law you are convicted as transgressors.
For whoever keeps the whole law but offends in only one point is guilty of it all.
For God said, "Do not commit adultery." But he also said, "Do not kill." Now if you do not commit adultery, but you kill, you have become a transgressor of the law.
So speak and do as those who will be judged by the law of liberty.
For those who judge without mercy will be shown no mercy, and mercy rejoices over judgment.
My brothers, what does it profit a man who says he has faith, and he has no works? Can his faith save him?
If a brother or sister is naked and without daily food.
And one of you says to them, "Go in peace; stay warm and well fed," but you did not give them the things which their body needs, what does it profit you?
Even so, faith alone with no works is dead.
Yes, a man may say, "You have faith and I have works." Show me your faith without your works, and I will show you my faith by my works.
You believe that there is one God. Good for you, the demons also believe and tremble.
O vain man, how will you know, that faith without works is dead?
Was not our father Abraham justified by works, when he offered up his son Isaac on the altar?
See how faith worked with his works, and by his works his faith was made perfect?
And the scripture was fulfilled which says, Abraham believed God, and because of that God recognized his righteousness, and he was called a Friend of God. (Genesis 15:6 - Isaiah 41:8)
So as you can see, a man is justified by his works and not only by his faith.
Likewise, Rahab the prostitute was also justified by her works, when she received the messengers, and helped them escape and sent them out in a different direction?
For just as the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without works is also dead.
My brothers, do not have many teachers, because you know that we who teach will be judged more harshly.
For we all offend in many ways. If a man's word does not offend, then he is a perfect man, able to bridle the whole body.
Behold, we put bits in a horse's mouth, so that they will obey us, and we make them turn their whole body.
Look at the ships also, which even though they are so large and they are driven by fierce winds, yet they are turned around with a very small helm, wherever the pilot wants to go.
Even so the tongue is a small part of the body, but it boasts of great things. Behold, how something so small, kindles such a great fire!
And the tongue is a fire, that kindles a world of immorality among our members. It defiles the whole body, and sets the course of nature on fire, and is itself set on fire by hell.
For every kind of beast, bird, serpent, and things in the sea, are tamed and have been tamed by mankind.
But the tongue cannot be tamed by man, it is an unruly evil, full of deadly poison.
With the tongue we bless our Lord and Father, and we use it to curse men, who are made in God's likeness.
Out of the same mouth proceeds blessing and cursing. My brothers, these things should not be!
Does sweet and bitter water flow from the same fountain?
My brothers, can a fig tree produce olives? Will a grapevine produce figs? So no fountain can yield both fresh and salt water.
Who is a wise and understanding among you? Let him show it by his good conversation and works with humility that comes from wisdom.
But if you have bitter envy and conflict in your hearts, do not glorify it and do not lie against the truth.
This wisdom does not descend from above, but it is earthly, sensual, and devilish.
For wherever there is envy and conflict is, there is also confusion and every evil work.
But the wisdom that is from above is first of all pure, then peaceful, gentle, easy to accommodate, full of mercy and good fruits, and without partiality or hypocrisy.
And the fruit of righteousness is sown in the peace of those who make peace.
Where do wars and fights among you come from? Do they not come from your lusts that are at war within your members?
You lust after what you do not have, you kill and desire what you cannot obtain. You fight and war, but you do not have because you do not ask.
You ask and do not receive, because you ask inappropriately, just so you can consume it in your lusts.
You adulterers and adulteresses, do you not know that friendship with the world is hostility to God? Therefore, whoever is a friend of the world is an enemy of God.
Do you think that the scripture vainly states, "The spirit that lives within us lusts with envy?"
But God gives us more grace. Which is why he says, "God resists the proud but gives grace to the humble. (Proverbs 3:34)"
Therefore, submit yourselves to God. Resist the devil and he will flee from you.
Draw near to God and he will draw near to you. You double minded sinners, cleanse your hands and purify your hearts.
Be afflicted, mourn, and weep. Let your laughter turn to mourning and your joy to sadness.
Humble yourselves in sight of the Lord, and he will lift you up.

Brothers, do not speak evil of each other. Whoever speaks evil of his brother and judges his brother, speaks evil of the law and judges the law. But if you judge the law, you are not one who does what the law says, but you are a judge.
There is only one lawgiver who can save and destroy, who are you to judge one another?
Go now, you who say, "Today or tomorrow we will go into a city and stay there for a year buying and selling and grow.
But the fact is, you do not even know what will happen tomorrow. For what is your life? It is a vapor, that appears for a short time and then vanishes.
For that you ought to say, "If the Lord is willing, we will live and do this or that."
But now you rejoice in your boasts. All such rejoicing is evil.
Therefore, whoever knows to do good and they do not do good is guilty of sin.
Go now, you rich men, weep and howl for your miseries that will come upon you.
Your riches are corrupted and your garments are motheaten.
Your gold and silver is cankered, and their rust will be a witness against you and it will eat your flesh as if it were fire. You have hoarded treasure for the last days.
Behold, the laborers you hired who have reaped your fields, whose wages you have kept through fraud, cry out. And the cries of those who have reaped have entered the ears of the Lord of Sabaoth.
You have lived in wanton pleasure on the earth. You have nourished your hearts, as on a day of slaughter.
You have condemned and killed the righteous, who did not resist you.
Therefore brothers, be patient until the Lord comes. Behold, the farmer waits for the earth's precious fruit, and he waits patiently until he receives the spring and harvest rain.
You must also be patient and establish your hearts, because the Lord's coming draws near.
Brothers, do not hold a grudge against one another, otherwise you will be condemned. For behold the judge is standing before the door.
Take my brothers the prophets, who have spoken in the Lord's name as an example of suffering, affliction, and patience.
Behold, we count those who endure as happy. You have heard of the patience of Job, and you have seen that the Lord's ending was very pitiful, but still, he is full of tender mercy.
But above all things, my brothers, do not swear by heaven, nor by the earth, nor by any other oath, but let your yes mean yes and your no mean no, otherwise you will fall into condemnation.
Is anyone among you afflicted? Let him pray. Is anyone among you merry? Let him sing psalms.
Is anyone among you sick? Let him call for the elders of the church, and let them pray over him, and anoint him with oil in the Lord's name.
And the faithful prayer will save the sick, and the Lord will raise him up, and he will be forgiven if he has committed sins.
Confess your faults to one another, and pray for one another, so that you may be healed. The successful fervent prayer of a righteous man will profit many.
Elijah was a man subject to passions just like us. He prayed earnestly that it would not rain, and it did not rain on the earth for three years and six months.
And Elijah prayed again, and the heavens gave rain, and the earth brought forth her fruit.
Brothers, if any of you err from the truth, and someone converts him.
Let him know, that whoever converts a sinner from the error of his way will save a soul from death, which will hide a multitude of sins.
Peter, an Apostle of Jesus Christ, wrote this letter to the exiles scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia.

And to the elect, chosen through the prior knowledge of God the father, through sanctification of the Spirit for obedience and the sprinkling of the blood of Jesus Christ: "May your grace and peace be multiplied.
Blessed be the God and father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who with his abundant mercy has let us be born again to a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead.
To a clean and incorruptible inheritance, that does not fade, which is reserved in heaven for you.
You who are protected through faith, by God's power until salvation is ready to be revealed in the last time.
In this you greatly rejoice, even though, if need be, for a while, you may have been saddened by many temptations.
So that the trial of your faith, is much more precious than gold that perishes. Even though it is tested by fire, it may be found to praise, honor, and glory at the appearance of Jesus Christ.
Whom even though you have not seen him, you love and believe in him, and you rejoice full of glory with unspeakable joy.
By receiving the final outcome of your faith, which is the salvation of your souls.
This salvation, about which the prophets have inquired and diligently searched for, who prophesied of the grace that would come to you.

Who searched for, what and when the Spirit of Christ which was within them signified, when the Spirit of Christ testified beforehand about the sufferings of Christ, and the glory that would follow later.

To whom it was revealed that they were not ministering to themselves, but they ministered these things to us. Now we report these things to you through those who have preached the gospel to you with the Holy Spirit, which was sent down from heaven. For even the angels desire to look into these things.
Therefore fasten this belt to the loins of your mind. Be sober, and hope until the end for the grace that will be brought to you at the revelation of Jesus Christ.
As obedient children, do not fashion yourselves to conform to the lusts of your former ignorance.
But just as the one who called you is holy, so you must also be holy in all types of conversation.
For it is written, 'Be holy to me, because I am holy.' (Leviticus 11:44)
And if you call on the father, who impartially judges people according to their works, then pass the time you spend here living in the fear of God.
For you know that you were not redeemed with corruptible things such as silver and gold, from your vain conversation that you traditionally received from your fathers.
But with the precious blood of Christ, as a lamb without blemish or spot.
Who was truly predestined before the foundation of the world but was revealed in these last times for you.
Through him you believe in God, who raised him up from the dead and glorified him, so that your faith and hope would be in God.
Since you have purified your souls by your obedience to the truth through the Holy Spirit to the true love of your brothers. So see that you passionately love one another with a pure heart.
For you have been born again, not of corruptible seed but of the incorruptible, through the word of God, which lives and endures forever.
For all flesh is like grass, and all the glory of man is like the flowering grass. The grass withers, and its flower fall away.
But the Lord's word of endures forever. And this word is the gospel which was preached to you."

Peter, an Apostle of Jesus Christ, continued writing this letter to the elect and exiles scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia which said, "Therefore, set aside all malice, deceit, hypocrisy, envy, and evil sayings.
As newborn babies, desire the sincere milk of the word, so that you may grow in your faith
If you have tasted that the Lord is gracious.
To whom you come as if to a living stone, rejected by men but chosen by God and precious in his sight.
You also, are like living stones which are being built up as a spiritual house to be a holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ.
For it is also contained in the scripture: 'Behold, I lay a chief, elect, and precious corner stone in Zion, and the one who believes in him will not be confounded.'
Therefore, Christ is precious to those of you who believe. But to those who are disobedient it is written, 'The stone which the builders rejected, has become the main cornerstone. (Psalm 118:22)
But Christ is also a stumbling stone and a rock of offense.' (Isaiah 8:14) They stumble in the word, because they are disobedient to that which they were appointed.
But you are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, and a peculiar people, so that you could reveal the praises of God who has called you out of darkness into his marvelous light.
Which in times past, you were not a people, but you are now God's people; who had at one time not obtained mercy, but who now have obtained mercy.
Dearly beloved, I beg you as strangers and pilgrims, to abstain from fleshly lusts which are at war against the soul.
Have your honest conversations among the Gentiles, even though they speak against you as evildoers, so that they may see your good works and glorify God on his day of visitation.
Submit yourselves to every ordinance of man for the Lord's sake; whether it is to the king as the supreme authority.
Or to the governors as those who are sent by him to punish the evildoers, and to praise those who do well.
For it is God's will, that by doing well you may silence the ignorance of foolish men.
Live as free men, but do not use your liberty as a cloak to conceal malicious intent; but live as servants of God.
Honor all men and love your brothers. Fear God and honor the king.
Servants, submit to your masters with fear, not only to those who are good and gentle, but also to those who are stubborn.
For a man is worthy of gratitude, if he endures grief and wrongfully suffers because he is conscious of God's presence.
For what glory do you deserve if you are battered when you are at fault, and you patiently endure it? But God finds you acceptable, if you suffer for doing good and you patiently endure it.
For you were called to this, because Christ also suffered for us and he left us an example, so that you could follow in his footsteps.
Christ committed no sin, nor was there any deceit found in his mouth.
When Christ was reviled, he did not revile in return. When Jesus suffered, he did not threaten anyone, but he committed himself to God who judges righteously.
Christ himself bore our sins in his own body on the tree, so that we who were dead in our sins, could live in righteousness, for it is written, 'By his stripes you were healed.' (Isaiah 53:5)
For it is said, 'We are all like sheep that have gone astray,' (Isaiah 53:6) but now you have returned to the shepherd and bishop of your souls."

Peter, an Apostle of Jesus Christ, continued writing this letter to the elect and exiles scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia which said, "Likewise wives, you must submit yourselves to your husbands, so that those who are outside of the word and do not obey the word, may also be won through the conversation of their wives.
When they see your chaste conversations coupled with fear.
And your beauty which does not come from outward adornment such as braided hair or wearing gold jewelry and fine clothes.
But let it come from what is hidden in a man's heart, and that which is in an incorruptible, meek, and quiet spirit, which is precious in God's sight.
For this is how the holy women in times past, who also trusted in God, adorned themselves and were submissive to their own husbands.
Just as Sara obeyed Abraham and called him Lord, whose daughters you are as long as you do well, and you are not amazed by fear.
Husbands you must also be understanding with your wives, and honor your wife as the weaker vessel, and live together as heirs of the gracious gift of life, so that your prayers are not hindered.
Finally, you must all be of one mind and have compassion for one another, love each other as brothers and be pitiful and courteous.
Do not give evil for evil, or shouting for shouting, but to the contrary, give blessings knowing that you are called to this, so that you could inherit a blessing.
For it is written, 'What kind of man desires life, and loves to see many good days? Keep your tongue and lips from speaking evil and deceit.
Depart from evil and do good things, seek and pursue peace.
For the Lord's eyes are on the righteous, and his ears are open to their cries. The Lord's face is against those who do evil, and he will remove the memory of them from the earth.' (Psalms 34:12-26)
And who can harm you, if you follow that which is good?
But even if you suffer for the sake of righteousness, you are happy. For it is written, 'Do not be afraid of the terror that they fear, nor should you be troubled.' (Isaiah 8:12)
But sanctify the Lord God in your hearts and always be ready to answer anyone who asks you for your reason for the hope that is within you with meekness and fear.
Have a good conscience, so that, if they in fact speak evil of you as they do of evildoers, they may be ashamed of their false accusations for your good conversation in Christ.
For, if it is God's will, it is better that you suffer for well doing, than it is for doing evil.
For Christ also once suffered for the sins of the just and for the unjust, so he could bring us to God. For Christ was put to death in the flesh but returned to life by the Holy Spirit.
By which he also went and preached to the spirits in prison.
Who were sometimes disobedient, when the long suffering God once waited patiently during Noah's days, while the ark was being prepared, in which only eight souls were saved through water.
The water by which baptism even now also saves us, not by removing the filth of the flesh, but it answers with a good conscience toward God, through the resurrection of Jesus Christ.
Who has gone into heaven and sits at the right hand of God, where angels, authorities, and powers are made subject to him."

Peter, an Apostle of Jesus Christ, continued writing this letter to the elect and exiles scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia which said, "Therefore, since Christ has suffered for us in the flesh, you must arm yourselves with the same determination, because anyone who has suffered in the flesh is finished with sin.
So that he no longer lives his remaining time in the flesh for the lusts of men, but for the will of God.
For in times past, our life may have been satisfied by doing he works of the Gentiles, when we walked in lasciviousness, lust, drunkenness, reveling, banquets, and abominable idolatries.
In which they think it is strange that you do not run with them in the same excess uproar they speak evil of you.
Who will give an account to God who is ready to judge the living and the dead.
For this reason, the gospel was also preached to the dead, so that they may also be judged as men in the flesh, but they live in accordance with God's spirit.
But the end of all things is at hand, therefore stay sober so that you may watch and pray.
And above all else, be charitable to one another, because charity will cover a multitude of sins.
Be hospitable to one another and do not hold grudges.
Just as every man has received a gift, they must use that same gift to minister to one another, as good managers of God's many graces.

If a man speaks, let him speak as the oracle of God. If a man ministers, let him minister with the abilities God has given him, so that God may be glorified through Jesus Christ in all things, to whom belongs the praise and authority forever and ever. Amen.
Beloved, do not think the fiery trial that has come to try you is some strange thing that has happened to you.
But you should rejoice, since you share in the sufferings of Christ, so that when his glory is revealed you may also be exceptionally glad and joyous.
If you are insulted for the name of Christ, be happy because God's spirit of glory rests on you. For on their part, he was spoken evil of, but on your part, he is glorified.
But none of you should suffer as a murderer, thief, evildoer, or a busybody who meddles in other men's affairs.
But if you suffer as a Christian, do not be ashamed but glorify God because of this.
For the time has come for judgment to begin in the house of God, and if it first begins with us, what will be the end for those who do not obey the gospel of God?
And if the righteous are scarcely saved, where will the ungodly and the sinner appear?
So let those who suffer in accordance with God's will commit their souls to doing well for their faithful Creator to keep."

Peter, an Apostle of Jesus Christ, continued writing this letter to the elect and exiles scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia which said, "I am an elder and a witness of Christ's sufferings who shares in the glory to be revealed, and I encourage the elders among you.
Feed the flock of God who are among you and willingly watch over them, not because you are forced to and not for dirty money but with an eager mind.
Not as someone who lords over God's heritage, but as someone who is an example to the flock.
And when God's chief shepherd appears, you will receive a crown of glory that does not fade.
Your younger people should also submit themselves to your elders. Yes, all of you should serve one another and be clothed with humility, for God resists the proud and gives grace to the humble.
Therefore, humble yourselves under God's mighty hand, so that he may glorify you in due time.
Cast all of your cares on God because he cares for you.
Be sober and vigilant, because your adversary the devil walks around like a roaring lion looking someone to devour.
Resist the devil and stand steadfast in the faith, knowing that your brothers all over the world are suffering the same afflictions as you.
But after you have suffered for a while, the God of all grace who has called us to his eternal glory through Jesus Christ, will make you perfect and he will establish, strengthen, and settle you.
To God be the glory and authority forever and ever. Amen.
Through Silvanus, whom I think of as your faithful brother, I have briefly written to you to encourage and testifying that this is the true grace of God in which you stand.
The church in Babylon, which was elected along with you, sends you their greetings and so does my son Marcus.
Greet one another with a kiss of charity. Peace be with you all who are in Jesus Christ. Amen!"

Simon Peter, a servant and an apostle of Jesus Christ, wrote this letter to those who have obtained the same precious faith as us through the righteousness of God and our savior Jesus Christ which said,
"Grace and peace be multiplied to you through the knowledge of God and our Lord Jesus.
His divine power has given us everything we need for life and Godliness, through the knowledge of Christ who has called us to his glory and goodness.

By which we are given extremely great and precious promises, so that through these promises you may share in the divine nature, since you have escaped the corruption that is in the world through lust.
And besides this, you must diligently add to your virtuous faith and knowledge.
And to knowledge add temperance, and to temperance add patience, and to patience add Godliness.
And to Godliness add brotherly kindness, and to brotherly kindness add charity.
For if these things abound in you, they will make you neither barren nor unfruitful in the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.
But whoever lacks these things is blind and nearsighted and has forgotten that his old sins have been purged.
Therefore brothers, strive to make your calling and election sure, because if you do these things, you will never fall.
For such an entrance will abundantly minister you into the everlasting kingdom of our Lord and savior Jesus Christ.
So, I will not be negligent to remind you of these things, even though you know them and you are already established in the present truth.
Yes, I think that it is correct to stir up your memory as long as I am in this tabernacle.
Because I know that I must shortly be removed from my tabernacle, just as our Lord Jesus Christ has shown me.
Furthermore, I will endeavor to make sure that you always remember these things after I am deceased.
For we did not follow cunningly devised fables when we made known to you the power and coming of our Lord Jesus Christ but were eyewitnesses of his majesty.
For Jesus received honor and glory from God the father, when the voice came to him from God's excellent glory that said, 'This is my beloved son, in whom I am well pleased.'
And we heard this voice that came from heaven, when we were with him on the holy mountain.

We also have a more confident word of prophecy, of which you would do well to heed and pay attention to as if it were a light that shines in a dark place until the morning dawn, and the day star rises in your hearts.
First knowing that no prophecy of the scripture has ever come from a private interpretation.
For the ancient prophecies did not come through the will of any man, but through holy men of God who only spoke as they were moved by the Holy Spirit."

Simon Peter, a servant and an apostle of Jesus Christ, continued writing this letter to the believers which said, "But there were also false prophets among the people, just as there will be false teachers among you. They will privately bring damnable heresies; they will even deny the Lord who bought them and bring swift destruction down on themselves.
Many will follow their destructive ways, and because of them evil will be spoken about the way of truth.
Through their greed, they will exploit you with insincere deceptive words and make merchandise of you. And now their judgment does not linger for long, and their damnation does not sleep.
For if God did not spare the angels who sinned but threw them into hell and put them in chains of darkness to be held for judgement.
And God did not spare the old world. But he did save Noah a righteous preacher who was one of only eight people saved when God brought the flood on the world of the ungodly.
God condemned, overthrew, and turned the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah into ashes, and made them an example to those who lived ungodly lives.
God delivered only Lot from Sodom and Gomorrah, because he was frustrated with the filthy conversations of the wicked.
For Lot was a righteous man whose soul was tormented while he was living among the wicked, because he saw and heard their unlawful deeds every day.
The Lord knows how to deliver the godly from temptations, and he knows how to hold the unrighteous for punishment on the day of judgment.

But the Lord especially knows how to deal with those who chase after the flesh in the lust of uncleanliness and despise government. They are overconfident, stubborn, and unafraid to speak evil of honor and self-respect.
Whereas angels who are greater in power and mightier than men, do not dare to scream accusations against them before the Lord.

But these men are like natural brute beasts, that were made to be captured and destroyed. They speak evil about things that they do not understand, and they will completely perish in their own corruption.

They will receive the reward of unrighteousness, just as those who take pleasure in rioting in the daytime. They are like spots and blemishes, and they revel in their own deceptive practices while they feast with you.
Their eyes are full of adultery that cannot refrain from sin, and they beguile unstable souls. They have exercised their heart with covetous practices, and they are cursed children.
Who have forsaken the righteous way and gone astray, following the way of Balaam son of Bosor, who loved the wages of unrighteousness.
But Balaam was rebuked for his iniquity, for speaking to a dumb donkey that spoke with a man's voice to stop the prophet from beating him and prevent the prophet's madness.
These men are wells without water, clouds that are carried by a violent storm, to whom the mist of darkness is reserved forever.
For when they speak great swollen words of vanity, they appeal to the lusts of the flesh through much promiscuity, but those who were clean escaped from those who live in error.
While they promise liberty, they themselves are the servants of corruption. Because a man will be overcome by the same things that have brought him into bondage.

For if after they have escaped the world's pollution through the knowledge of our Lord and savior Jesus Christ, only to be entangled and overcome again, then their final end is worse than it was in the beginning.
For they would have been better off not knowing the way of righteousness than to have known it and turn away from the holy commandment that was delivered to them.
But these proverbs are a true for them, 'A dog always returns to his own vomit, and a washed sow always returns to wallowing in her own mud.'"

Simon Peter, a servant and an apostle of Jesus Christ, continued writing this letter to the believers which said, "My beloved this is my second letter, that I Peter now write to you. Both of which I write to stir up the pure memories of your mind.
So that you may be reminded of the words which were spoken before by the holy prophets, and of the commandment of we who are the apostles of our Lord and savior.
First knowing that scoffers will come in the last days walking after their own lusts.
And they will say, 'Where is the promise of his coming? For since our fathers fell asleep, everything has continued as it has been since the beginning of the creation.'
For they are willingly ignorant of this, that by God's word the heavens were old, and the earth was formed out of water and in the water.
Through which the world back then overflowed with water and perished.
But today's heavens and the earth through that same word are kept in store and reserved for fire until the day of judgment and perdition of ungodly men.
But beloved do not be ignorant of this one thing, that one day with the Lord is like a thousand years, and a thousand years is like one day.
The Lord is not slack about his promise, as some men understand slackness, but is long suffering toward us, not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance.

But the Day of the Lord will come like a thief in the night, in which the heavens will pass away with a great noise, and the elements will melt with fervent heat, and the earth and its works will also be burned up.
Since all of these things will be dissolved, what kind of people should you be in all holy conversation and Godliness.
Looking for and hasting the coming of the day of God, in which the heavens will be dissolved by fire, and the elements will melt with fervent heat?
Nevertheless, through God's promise we look forward to new heavens and a new earth where righteousness lives.
Therefore beloved, since you look forward to such things, be diligent so that God may find you in peace, spotless and blameless.
And consider that the long suffering of our Lord brings salvation, just as our beloved brother Paul has written to you with the wisdom God gave him.

Paul also writes this way in all his letters about these things, in which some things are hard to understand, which those who are uneducated and unstable wrestle with, just as they do with the other scriptures, to their own destruction.
Therefore beloved, since you already know these things, beware, otherwise you may also be led away by the error of the wicked and fall from your own steadfastness.
But grow in grace, and in the knowledge of our Lord and savior Jesus Christ. To him be glory both now and forever. Amen."
That which was from the beginning, which we have heard, which we have seen with our eyes, which we have looked upon, and our hands have handled, is the word of life.
For this life was manifested, and we have seen it and testified about it, and we have shown you that eternal life, which was with the father and was revealed to us.
We have declared that which we have seen and heard to you, so that you may also have fellowship with us. And truly our fellowship is with God the father and his son Jesus Christ.
And we write these things to you, so that your joy may be full.
This then is the message which we have heard from Jesus and declare to you: God is light, and there is no darkness in him at all.
If we say that we have fellowship with Jesus Christ, but we walk in darkness, then we lie and do not tell the truth.
But if we walk in the light, just as Jesus is in the light, then we have fellowship with one another, and the blood of God's son Jesus Christ cleanses us from all sin.
If we say that we have no sin, then we deceive ourselves and the truth is not in us.
If we confess our sins, God is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
If we say that we have not sinned, we make God a liar and his word is not in us.
My little children, I am writing these things to you so that you do not sin. But if a man does sin, we have an advocate with God the father who is the righteous Jesus Christ.
Jesus is the atonement not only for our sins, but also for the sins of the whole world.
And we will know that we know Christ, if we keep his commandments.
Anyone who says, "I know Jesus!" But does not keep the commandments of Christ, is a liar and the truth is not in him.
But whoever keeps the word of Jesus, then the love of God is truly perfected in him, and this is how we know that we are in him.
Whoever says that they abide in him, must also walk as Jesus walked.
Brothers, I am not writing a new commandment to you, but an old one which has been with you from the beginning. This old commandment is the word which you have heard from the very beginning.
But again, I am also writing a new commandment to you, which is true in Jesus and also in you. Because the darkness is in the past and the true light now shines.
Anyone who says he is in the light but hates his brother, is still in darkness.
Whoever loves his brother remains in the light, and there is nothing in him that will cause him to stumble.
But whoever hates his brother is in darkness and walks in darkness. He does not know where he is going, because the darkness has blinded his eyes.
I am writing to you little children, because your sins have been forgiven through your faith in Christ's name.

I am writing to you fathers, because you have known Christ who is from the beginning. I am writing to you young men, because you have overcome the wicked one. I am writing to you little children, because you have known God the father.

I have written to you fathers, because you have known Christ who is from the beginning. I have written to you young men, because you are strong and the word of God abides in you, and you have overcome the wicked one.
Do not love the world nor the things in the world. If a man loves the world, the love of God the father is not in him.
Because everything in the world including the lust of the flesh, the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life, is not from the father but it is from the world.
The world passes away along with its lust, but whoever does the will of God remains forever.
Little children, this is the last time and as you have heard the antichrist is coming, but even now are there many antichrists. And this is how we know that this is the last time.
They left us, but they were not one of us. For if they had been one of us, they would not have left. But they left us, so it was obvious to us that they were not one of us.
But you have been anointed by the Holy One, and you know all things.
I have not written to you because you do not know the truth, but because you know the truth, and you know that no lie comes from the truth.
The one who is a liar, is the one that denies that Jesus is the Christ? The antichrist is the one that denies the father and the son.
Whoever denies the son, does not have the father within them, but whoever acknowledges the son also has the father.

Therefore, you should let what you have heard from the beginning endure within you. If what you have heard from the beginning remains in you, you will also continue in Jesus the son and God the father.
This is the promise of eternal life that God has made to us.
I have written to you about these things to warn you about those who want to seduce you.

But the anointing you have received from Christ endures within you, and you do not need anyone to teach you. But being anointed by Jesus teaches you the truth about everything, and he does not lie. So remain in Christ as you have been taught!
So now little children, remain in Christ so that when Jesus appears we will not be ashamed when he comes.
If you know that Jesus Christ is righteous, then you know that anyone who is righteous is born within him.
Behold, what kind of love has God the father bestowed on us, that we should be called the sons of God. Therefore, the world does not know us because it did not know Christ.
Beloved, now are we the sons of God, and it has not yet been revealed what we will be, but we know that when Christ appears, we will be like him because we will see him as he is.
And every man that has this hope in Jesus purifies himself, just as Christ is pure.
Whoever commits sin also transgresses against the law, because sin is lawlessness.
And you know that Christ was manifested to take away our sins, and in Jesus there is no sin.
Whoever endures in Christ does not sin, whoever sins has not seen him and does not know him.
Little children, let no one deceive you, whoever does righteousness is righteous, just as Christ is righteous.
Whoever commits sin is of the devil, because the devil sins from the very beginning. God's son was revealed to destroy the works of the devil.
Whoever is born of God does not commit sin, because God's seed remains in him and he cannot sin, because he is born of God.
This way the differences between the children of God and the devil's children are revealed, whoever does no righteousness is not from God, nor is the one who does not love his brother.
For this message that you have heard from the beginning, is that we should love one another.
Not like Cain, who was from the wicked one and killed his brother. And why did Cain slay him? Because Cain's works were evil, and his brother's acts were righteous.
My brothers, do not be surprised if the world hates you.
We know that we have passed from death to life, because we love the brothers. Whoever does not love his brother remains in death.
Whoever hates his brother is a murderer, and you know the eternal life does not live within a murderer.
This is how we know the love of God, because Jesus laid down his life for us, and we should lay down our lives for our brothers.
But whoever has goods from this world and sees that his brother is in need, and withholds his bowels of compassion from him, how can the love of God live in him?
My little children, let us not love in only in word and speech, but in deeds and truth.
And this is how we know that we are of the truth and will assure our hearts before God.
For even if our heart condemns us, God is greater than our heart and he knows all things.
Beloved, if our heart does not condemn us, then have we confidence toward God.
And we will receive whatever we ask from him, because we keep his commandments, and do those things that are pleasing in his sight.
And God's commandment, is that we should believe in the name of his son Jesus Christ and love one another, just as he has commanded us.
And whoever keeps God's commandments lives in God, and God lives in him. And we know that God remains in us, by the Holy Spirit which Christ has given us.
Beloved, do not believe every spirit, but test the spirits to know whether they are from God, because many false prophets have gone out into the world.
This is how you will know the Spirit of God, every spirit that confesses that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is from God.

And every spirit that confesses that Jesus Christ has not come in the flesh is not from God. But this is the spirit of the antichrist, which you have heard would come, and even now it is already in the world.
O little children, you are from God, and you have overcome them, because greater is Christ who is in you, than the one who is in the world.
They are of the world: Therefore, they speak of the world and the world listens to them.
We are of God, and whoever knows God listens to us; whoever is not of God does not listen to us. This is how we know the spirit of truth, and the spirit of error.
Beloved, let us love one another, for love comes from God, and everyone who loves is born of God and knows God.
Whoever does not love does not know God, because God is love.
This is how God's love was revealed to us, for God sent his only begotten son Jesus Christ into the world, so that we might live through him.
And this is love; it is not that we loved God, but that he first loved us, and sent his son Jesus Christ to be the atoning sacrifice for our sins.
Beloved, if God loved us so much, then we should also love one another.
No man has ever seen God. But if we love one another, God lives in us, and his love is perfected in us.
This is how we know that we live in God, and God lives in us, because he has given love to us from his Spirit.
And we have seen and we can testify that God the father sent his son Jesus to be the savior of the world.
Whoever confesses that Jesus is the son of God, then God lives in him, and he lives in God.
And we have known and believed in the love that God has for us. God is love, and whoever lives in love lives in God, and God lives in him.
This is how our love has been made perfect, so that we may be bold on the day of judgment, because we are just like him in this world.
There is no fear in love, but perfect love casts out fear, because fear comes with torment. The one who fears, has not been made perfect in love.
We love God, because God first loved us.
If a man says, "I love God!" And he hates his brother, then he is a liar. For someone who does not love his brother whom he has seen, cannot love God whom he has not seen.
And we have this commandment from God: Whoever loves God must also love his brother.
Whoever believes that Jesus is the Christ is born of God, and everyone who loves God the father, also loves those born of God.
We know that we love the children of God, when we love God, and keep his commandments.
For this is the love of God, that we keep his commandments, and his commandments are not grievous.
For whatever is born of God overcomes the world, and our faith is the victory that overcomes the world.
Who overcomes the world, but those who believe that Jesus is the son of God?
Jesus Christ is the one who came by water and blood, but not just by water only, but by water and blood, and it is the Holy Spirit that testifies, because the Holy Spirit is truth.
For there are three that testify in heaven, God the father, the Word, and the Holy Spirit, and these three are one God.
And there are three who testify on earth, the Holy Spirit, the water, and the blood, and these three agree as one.
Even if we receive the witness of men, the witness of God is greater. For this is God's testimony which he has testified about his son Jesus.

Whoever believes in God's son Jesus Christ has this witness within himself, but whoever does not believe God has made him a liar, because he does not believe the testimony that God has given about his son Jesus.
And this is God's testimony; God has given us eternal life, and this life is in his son Jesus Christ.
Whoever has God's son Jesus has life, and whoever does not have the son of God does not have life.
I have written these things to those of you who believe in the name of God's son Jesus Christ, so that you may know that you have eternal life, and that you may believe in the name of the son of God.
And this is the confidence that we have in God, that if we ask anything within his will, God hears us.
And if we know that God hears whatever we ask, we know that we already have what we desired from him.

If a man sees his brother commit a nondeadly sin, he should ask and God will give him life for those who do not sin to death. There is sin that leads to death, and I am not saying that he should pray for sin that leads to death.
All unrighteousness is sin, but there is a sin does not lead to death.
We know that whoever is born of God does not sin, but whoever is begotten of God keeps himself, and the wicked one does not touch him.
And we know that we are of God, and the whole world lies in wickedness.

And we know that Jesus the son of God has come and given us understanding, so that we may know who is true, and we are in the one who is true which is God's son Jesus Christ. This is the true God and eternal life.
Little children, keep yourselves from idols. Amen.
From the elder, to the chosen lady and her children whom I love in the truth, and not only me, but also all of those who have known the truth.
For the truth's sake, which lives in us and will be with us forever.
Grace be with you, mercy and peace from God the father, and from the Lord Jesus Christ, the son of God the father in truth and love.
I was overjoyed to find your children walking in truth, just as God the father commanded us.
And now I beg you lady, not as if I wrote you a new commandment, but one that we have had from the beginning; that we must love one another.
And this is love, that we walk in God's commandments. This is the commandment, that as you have heard about from the beginning, you should walk in love.
For many deceivers have entered the world, who do not confess that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh. This type of person is a deceiver and an antichrist.
Watch yourselves, so that we do not lose those things for which we have worked, but that we receive a full reward.
Whoever transgresses, and does not remain in the doctrine of Christ, does not have God. Whoever remains in the doctrine of Christ, has both God the father and his son Jesus Christ.
If anyone comes to you, and does not bring this doctrine, do not receive him into your home, nor bid him God speed.
For whoever bids him God speed shares in his evil deeds.
I have many things to write to you about, but I would prefer not to write with paper and ink. But I trust I will come to you and speak face to face, so that our joy may be full.
The children of your elect sister send you greetings. Amen.
From the elder to the beloved Gaius, whom I love in the truth.
Beloved, I wish above all else, that you may prosper and be in health, just as your soul prospers.
For I rejoiced greatly, when the brothers came and testified about the truth that is in you, as you walk in the truth.
I have no greater joy than to hear that my children walk in truth.
Beloved, you are faithful in whatever you do for the brothers and strangers.
Who have testified of your charity before the church, and you would do well to send them on their journey in a manner worthy of God.
Because, for the sake of God's name they left, taking nothing from the Gentiles.
Therefore, we should receive such men, so that we may be fellow helpers in the truth.
I wrote to the church about this, but Diotrephes, who loves to feel superior among them, did not receive us.

Therefore, if I come, I will remind them of his deeds, foolishly talking against us with malicious words. And not content with that, he does not receive the brothers and forbids those who would and throws them out of the church.
Beloved, do not follow that which is evil, but follow that which is good. Whoever does good is of God, but whoever does evil has not seen God.
Demetrius has been given a good report from all men, and from the truth itself. Yes, we also testify for him, and you know that our record is true.
I had many things to write, but I will not write to you with pen and ink.
But I trust I will see you shortly, and we will speak face to face. Peace be with you. Our friends salute you. Greet the friends by name.
Jude, the servant of Jesus Christ and brother of James, wrote this letter to those who are sanctified by God the father, and called and protected in Jesus Christ.
Mercy, peace, and love be multiplied to you.

Beloved, when I diligently tried to write to you about our common salvation, it was necessary for me to write to you and encourage you, so that you could earnestly contend for the faith which was once delivered to the saints.

For certain ungodly men have crept in unnoticed, who were long ago ordained for condemnation. They turn the grace of our God into lasciviousness, and deny the only Lord God, and our Lord Jesus Christ.
Therefore, I will remind you, even though you once knew this, how the Lord had saved the people from the land of Egypt, and later destroyed those who did not believe.
And the angels who did not keep their first estate but left their own home have been reserved in everlasting chains under darkness until the great day of judgement.
Just as Sodom and Gomorrah and the cities around them also gave themselves over to fornication, and pursuing strange flesh, are set forth as an example, suffering the vengeance of eternal fire.
Likewise the filthy dreamers who defile the flesh, despise authority, and speak evil of dignity.
Yet when Michael the archangel dealt with the devil and argued about the body of Moses, he did not dare to bring screaming accusations against him, but said, "The Lord rebuke you."
But these men speak evil against those things which they do not understand, but like brute beasts they naturally do what they know, and they corrupt themselves in those things.
Woe unto them! For they have gone in the way of Cain and greedily ran after the error of Balaam for reward and perished in Korah's rebellion. (Numbers 16)

These men are spots in your feasts of charity, when they feast with you and fearlessly feed themselves, they are clouds without water, carried around by the winds. Trees whose fruit withers and fruitless trees, twice dead and torn out by their roots.
Raging waves of the sea, foaming from their own shame, wandering stars, to whom is reserved the black darkness forever.
Enoch, who was Adam's seventh son had a prophesy about the people and said, "Behold, the Lord is coming with tens of thousands of his saints."

To execute judgment on everyone, and to convince all who are ungodly among them of all their ungodly deeds which they have ungodly committed. And of all their hard speeches which the ungodly sinners have spoken against God.
These men are murmurers and complainers, who chase after their own lusts, and their mouth speaks great swelling words, admiring and flattering others for their own advantage.
But beloved, remember the words previously spoken about the apostles of our Lord Jesus Christ.
How they told you that there would be mockers in the last times, who would chase after their own ungodly lusts.
These are the ones who separate themselves, for they are sensual and have no Holy Spirit.
But you beloved, build yourselves up on your most holy faith and praying in the Holy Spirit.
Keep yourselves in the love of God, looking for the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ to secure eternal life.
And make a difference for some by having compassion.
And save others with fear, by pulling them out of the fire, hating even the clothing stained by the flesh.
Now to God who can keep you from falling and present you as blameless before God's glorious presence with exceptional joy.
